That is, intellect is not intelligence, because we find many people who are intelligent but do not take heed through the Qurʾān. So we do not call these people "intellectuals" (ʿuqalāʾ). But what has been removed from them of intellect: is it the intellect of perception or the intellect of conduct?
* The students: Conduct.
* The Shaykh: The intellect of conduct and right judgment. As for perception, they do perceive, and that is why the proof (ḥujjah) is established against them.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: among the Qurʾān is that whose interpretation (taʾwīl) none knows except Allah, according to the reading that pauses at ﴿but Allah﴾: ﴿And none knows its interpretation except Allah﴾ (Āl ʿImrān 3:7). If someone asks, "What is the benefit of sending down something whose interpretation is not known?" we say: The benefit is testing the servants by their good manners toward Allah, exalted is He, whether they try to reach something their intellects cannot grasp or stop at the limits of what their intellects can grasp. For some people go ahead and presume to try to comprehend what the intellect cannot reach, while others act with good manners, and when they reach what the intellect cannot attain, they stop.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the vastness of Allah's knowledge, exalted is He, based on His saying: ﴿And none knows its interpretation except Allah﴾, according to the reading that pauses there.
* And among its benefits also: the speech of Allah, exalted is He, is varied. Among it is the clear (muḥkam), among it is the ambiguous (mutashābih), among it is the command, among it is the prohibition, among it is the report, among it is the interrogative, and other types that none can enumerate except Allah. This is contrary to those who say that the speech of Allah is a single type, and that the difference of surahs or forms does not indicate its variety and diversity, such as the Ashʿarites (al-Ashāʿirah). For the Ashʿarites hold that the speech of Allah is the meaning subsisting in the self (al-maʿnā al-qāʾim bi-al-nafs), and that it is one thing: if it is expressed in Arabic it becomes the Qurʾān, if it is expressed in Hebrew it becomes the Torah, if it is expressed in Syriac it becomes the Gospel, and if it comes in the form of a prohibition it becomes a prohibition, and so on. Or, if it is expressed in the form of a prohibition it becomes a prohibition, and if it is expressed in the form of a command it becomes a command; otherwise it is one thing. There is no doubt that this is a view that both reason and revelation refute.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verse 8 (part 1 of 2):

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us﴾ [Al 'Imran 8]. The apparent meaning is that this is part of the speech of those firmly grounded in knowledge, who say: ﴿We believe in it; all is from our Lord﴾, and they also say: ﴿Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us﴾. Supplication is generally introduced with "Lord" (Rabb), because supplication necessarily requires a response, and response is an act, and acts are more closely related to Lordship (rububiyyah) than to divinity (uluhiyyah). For this reason most supplications begin with "Rabbana" (our Lord). As for ﴿Rabbana﴾, it is in the accusative by the elided vocative particle (ya), and the original phrase is: "Ya Rabbana," but the ya was omitted for lightness and for the blessing of beginning with the name of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

﴿Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate﴾. ﴿Do not let deviate﴾ (la tuzigh) is a supplicatory sentence, even though it is in the form of a prohibition, because a prohibition cannot come from a created being to the Creator; a prohibition is a demand to refrain issued from a position of superiority, and a created being can never demand that his Lord refrain in a manner of superiority. It has already passed with us that when a demand is directed from a lower to a higher party, it is called (du'a') (supplication). So we say: the (la) is supplicatory, not prohibitive (nahiyah), because there is no prohibition from a creature to the Creator.

﴿Do not let our hearts deviate﴾: tuzigh means tumil (incline, turn away), as in "zaghat al-shams" (the sun declined), meaning it moved away from the middle of the sky. Tuzigh means tumil: you incline it. Away from what? The following clause clarifies it: ﴿do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us﴾, meaning: do not let them deviate from guidance, but guide them with the guidance of direction and the guidance of success (tawfiq).

The verb is attached to the heart because the heart is the axis on which action turns, due to the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Verily, in the body there is a piece of flesh; if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt. Verily, it is the heart"[[A hadith agreed upon (Bukhari 52; Muslim 1599/107) from the hadith of al-Nu'man ibn Bashir radiyallahu 'anhu.]]. The heart is this organ situated in the chest, due to the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿For indeed, it is not the eyes that are blinded, but blinded are the hearts which are within the breasts﴾ [al-Hajj 46], and by this heart intellect exists, due to His saying: ﴿Have they not traveled through the earth so that they would have hearts by which to reason?﴾ [al-Hajj 46]. Based on these proofs it becomes clear that intellect is in the heart, not in the brain. Scholars have differed, anciently and in modern times, over whether intellect is in the brain or in the heart.

What the Qur'an indicates is that it is in the heart, and the Qur'an is the speech of the Creator, and the Creator, Mighty and Majestic, knows best what He has created. So intellect is with the heart; but the intellect of the heart is the intellect of direction and management, not the intellect of perception and conception. The intellect of perception and conception is in the brain: the brain conceives and comprehends, and it is like a secretary to the heart, explaining what it wishes to raise to the heart, then it raises it to the heart, then the heart issues the orders. And who conveys the orders to the subjects? The brain is what conveys the orders, and for this reason all the muscles become active with the activity of the brain. So the matter becomes a chain: that which conceives, perceives, and in which the intellect of perception resides is the brain.

As for the intellect of management, direction, rectitude and corruption, it is the intellect of the heart. The brain conceives, perceives things, examines them, then raises them written so that the heart may endorse them; they come back to the heart, and the heart commands and forbids, but the heart does not directly deal with things; it is itself too exalted to directly address these soldiers. It sends the matter to whom? To the brain again, and the brain directs the orders, saying: "The King commands you to such and such," and you comply with the orders. For this reason the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Verily, in the body there is a piece of flesh..." [[A hadith agreed upon (Bukhari 52; Muslim 1599/107) from the hadith of al-Nu'man ibn Bashir radiyallahu 'anhu.]] And then the apparent problem disappears and the textual and sensory evidences come together. So where is the perceptive intellect located?
* The students: The brain.
* The Shaykh: And the intellect of direction, which is the basis of guidance and corruption, is the heart.

He, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate﴾, and when the hearts are upright and do not incline, the limbs are upright in belief, speech and action.

His saying: ﴿after You have guided us﴾: this clause is not intended as self-admiration; rather it is intended as seeking means (tawassul) by previous blessings to subsequent blessings. It is as if they are saying: "Our Lord, You have bestowed upon us guidance first, so we ask You to bestow upon us the permanence of this guidance, so do not let it deviate." In this supplication there is praise of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for what? For the previous guidance. Had they said only "Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate," it would have sufficed; but they said "after You have guided us" to seek means through Allah's previous blessings to His subsequent blessings, and to praise Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for His previous blessings, and that He, Mighty and Majestic, is deserving of bounty and bestowal. ﴿after You have guided us﴾: is it guidance of direction or of success?
* The students: Direction, and success.
* The Shaykh: Or both?
* The students: Both.
* The Shaykh: Yes, both. The believers were guided by Allah with the guidance of success and the guidance of direction; the guidance of direction is that He made the truth clear to them, and the guidance of success is that He enabled them to follow the truth. Among people some are deprived of both guidances, and some are deprived of the second guidance; I do not think anyone is deprived of the second only, meaning I do not think anyone is given the first guidance without the third, since success cannot be attained except after knowledge.
Among people, some are deprived of both guidances, so they have neither the guidance of direction nor the guidance of success, like the Christians, who are astray: they did not know the truth and did not act upon it. Among people, some are deprived of the guidance of success, like the Jews: the Jews knew but did not act. Among people, some are granted both guidances, like the believers whom Allah has favored. Here ﴿guided us﴾ means the guidance of direction and the guidance of success: they were guided to the truth by its indication, and they were guided to the truth by success. Can you bring evidence for the guidance of direction alone?
* A student: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And as for Thamud, We guided them, but they preferred blindness over guidance﴾ [Fussilat 17].
* The Shaykh: Yes, ﴿And as for Thamud, We guided them, but they preferred blindness over guidance﴾. Is this the guidance of success?
* A student: ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills﴾ [al-Qasas 56].
* The Shaykh: Yes, meaning you cannot grant the success of guidance, but Allah guides whom He wills. As for the guidance of direction, there is no doubt that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ guided people and pointed them to the way: ﴿And indeed, you guide to a straight path﴾ [al-Shura 52]. After You have guided us.

﴿And grant us from Yourself mercy﴾ [Al 'Imran 8]. "Hab" (grant) means "a'ti" (give), and a gift (hibah) is giving without compensation, and its perfection is without reproach (minnah); giving without compensation is a gift, and its perfection is that it is not accompanied by reproach. Allah, glorified and exalted, has the favor over us, as He said: ﴿Rather, Allah confers favor upon you that He guided you to faith﴾ [al-Hujurat 17]. Here the form is for what? For command or for supplication?
* The students: For supplication.
* The Shaykh: Yes, for supplication. ﴿And grant us﴾ means give us ﴿from Yourself﴾, i.e., from You. They attributed this gift to Allah so that no one else would have a favor over them; this is one aspect, and because if it is from Allah, the Most Generous of the generous, it becomes a great gift, since giving is according to the status of whom?
* The students: The giver.
* The Shaykh: According to the giver. For this reason they said: ﴿Grant us from Yourself﴾, meaning a gift that no one else can claim as a favor upon us, and a great gift, because it comes from You. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ said to Abu Bakr when he asked him to teach him a supplication to recite in his prayer: "Say: O Allah, I have wronged myself greatly, and none forgives sins but You, so forgive me a forgiveness from You and have mercy on me"[[A hadith agreed upon (Bukhari 7387; Muslim 2705/48) from the hadith of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq radiyallahu 'anhu.]]. He said: ﴿and grant us from Yourself mercy﴾, mercy. We have previously mentioned repeatedly that mercy is one of the attributes of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and it is applied to His blessings, since they are among the effects of His mercy, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And it is He who sends down rain after they had despaired, and spreads His mercy﴾ [al-Shura 28]. Allah the Exalted said to Paradise: "You are My mercy; I show mercy through you to whom I will"[[A hadith agreed upon (Bukhari 4850; Muslim 2846/34) from the hadith of Abu Hurairah radiyallahu 'anhu.]]. Among its usage is His saying: ﴿As for those whose faces will be whitened, they will be in the mercy of Allah, wherein they will abide forever﴾ [Al 'Imran 107]. So mercy is applied to both this and that. Which of the two types is in this verse: ﴿grant us from Yourself mercy﴾?
* The students: The second mercy.
* The Shaykh: The second, which is the blessings, and they are among the effects of His mercy. ﴿grant us from Yourself mercy﴾, and by mercy the desired is attained and a person is saved from what is feared. If it is combined with forgiveness, then by mercy the desired is attained, and by forgiveness salvation from what is feared.

﴿Indeed, You are the Bestower﴾ [Al 'Imran 8]. The sentence here is resumptive, giving the reason and a means (tawassul): meaning that we only asked You for the gift, a gift of mercy, because You are the Bestower. It consists of (inna), its noun and its predicate: its noun is the kaf (you), and its predicate is "al-Wahhab" (the Bestower). The pronoun "anta" (you) is called a pronoun of separation (damir al-fasl), and the pronoun of separation has three benefits; who knows them?
* A student: (...) emphasis of meaning.
* The Shaykh: Emphasis.
* The student: Separation between the predicate and the attribute.
* The Shaykh: Separation between the predicate and the attribute; you have changed from the first?
* The student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Okay, and emphasis.
* The student: And restriction.
* The Shaykh: And restriction. Okay, these are three things; that is, it has three benefits:
First: separation between the attribute and the predicate.
Second: what? Emphasis.
Third: restriction. We give an example to make the matter clear: if you say "Zayd al-fadil" (Zayd the virtuous), the word al-fadil may be a predicate or an attribute with the predicate omitted, the estimate being: "Zayd the virtuous is present." But if you say "Zayd huwa al-fadil" (Zayd is he the virtuous), it becomes specifically a predicate. Also, if you say "Zayd al-fadil," it may be that someone else is also virtuous; but if you say "Zayd huwa al-fadil," it is restriction.
* A student: Restriction.
* The Shaykh: This is restriction, a restriction in its wording: meaning no one else is virtuous, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And indeed, Our soldiers will surely be the victorious﴾ [al-Saffat 173]. Third: emphasis, for when you say "Zayd al-fadil" you ascribe virtue to him, but when you say "huwa al-fadil" you add emphasis. Here ﴿Indeed, you are the Bestower﴾ fits this. So we say: "anta" is a pronoun of separation for emphasis, restriction, and determining that what follows is a predicate, not what?
* The students: Not an attribute.
* The Shaykh: Not an attribute. As for His saying ﴿Indeed, You are the Bestower﴾: al-Wahhab means one who gives abundantly. Can it be a relative attribute (nisbah)?
* A student: It can be.
* The Shaykh: It can be; it can be for attribution, and it can be for intensification (mubalaghah), and we may say it is both together. He is al-Wahhab, meaning the abundant giver, and this is a permanent attribute of His; and He is also one who gives abundantly, meaning those whom Allah gives are countless and cannot be counted. The Prophet ﷺ said: "The hand of Allah is full, pouring continuously night and day; have you considered what He has spent since He created the heavens and the earth? Verily it has not diminished what is in His right hand"[[A hadith agreed upon (Bukhari 4684; Muslim 993/37) from the hadith of Abu Hurairah radiyallahu 'anhu.]]. See how?
* A student: It has not decreased.
* The Shaykh: Yes, it has not decreased. And Allah the Exalted said in the hadith qudsi: "O My servants, if your first and last, your humans and your jinn, stood in one open place and asked Me, and I gave each person his request, that would not decrease what is with Me except as a needle decreases when dipped in the sea"[[Narrated by Muslim (2577/55) from the hadith of Abu Dharr radiyallahu 'anhu.]]. Does this diminish the sea at all? No. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is never counted in His gifts; even you yourself cannot count Allah's gifts to you: ﴿And if you should count the favors of Allah, you could not enumerate them﴾ [al-Nahl 18]. ﴿Indeed, You are the Bestower﴾. In this verse there are several benefits:
First: the legitimacy of supplicating in this form, since it is the supplication of those firmly grounded in knowledge and people of understanding.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the legitimacy of beginning supplication with the name "Lord" ﴿Rabbana﴾.
* Among its benefits: that a person does not control his own heart; therefore you ask Allah not to let your heart deviate, so do not be deceived by yourself that you are a believer, for many a believer has slipped, may Allah protect us, but always ask Allah to keep you firm and not let your heart deviate. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, informed: "Verily the hearts are between two of the fingers of the Most Merciful; if He wills He causes them to deviate, and if He wills He guides them; He turns them as He wills"[[Narrated by Muslim (2654/17) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn 'Amr radiyallahu 'anhuma.]].
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: an indication that when the heart is sound, the whole body is sound, since they said: ﴿Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate﴾ [Al 'Imran 8].
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the heart has two states: a state of uprightness and a state of deviation, and a person is compelled to ask Allah, Exalted and Mighty, not to let his heart deviate, so that it remains upright.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: seeking means to Allah through His blessings, by their saying: ﴿after You have guided us﴾ [Al 'Imran 8].
Among them: praise of these masters, since they acknowledged to Allah the blessing in their saying, what?
* The students: ﴿after You have guided us﴾.
* The Shaykh: ﴿after You have guided us﴾. This falls under His saying: ﴿And as for the blessing of your Lord, proclaim it﴾ [al-Duha 11].
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that clearing (takhliyah) comes before adornment (tahliyah).
* The Shaykh: Is this statement known?
* The students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Clearing comes before adornment; that is, the place is emptied of impurities and harm, then it is purified. From where is this taken? ﴿Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate﴾, then He said: ﴿And grant us﴾, ﴿grant us from Yourself﴾ [Al 'Imran 8].
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that a person is compelled to his Lord in repelling and in attracting; and if you wish, say: in bringing benefit and warding off harm. Because they asked what? That He not let their hearts deviate after He had guided them, and they asked that He grant them mercy from Himself. Is their supplication that He not let their hearts deviate a supplication for repelling or for raising?
* A student: For repelling.
* The Shaykh: Pay attention: "do not let deviate after You have guided us" is then a supplication for raising (i.e., preservation of what is had). "Grant us from Yourself mercy" is for repelling: meaning grant us from Yourself mercy by which we repel evil; and "do not let our hearts deviate" means do not remove from us the guidance after we have been guided.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that giving is according to the status of the giver, by His saying: ﴿grant us from Yourself mercy﴾. Can we consider this as seeking means through the state of the one being called upon, or do we say that this is seeking means through the attributes of Allah, Mighty and Majestic?
This second is clearer, since it has passed with us that tawassul is divided into six categories.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: seeking means through Allah's names, by His saying: ﴿Indeed, You are the Bestower﴾, for it is among the requirements of His being the Bestower that He grant us mercy from Himself.

Among its benefits as well: a person is in need of the mercy of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. For this reason, they ask Allah to grant them mercy from Him.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verse 9 (part 1 of 2):

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Our Lord, You are the gatherer of the people for a Day about which there is no doubt. Indeed, Allah does not fail in His promise.﴾ [Al 'Imran 9]. In this, they say: ﴿Our Lord, You are the gatherer of the people﴾. As for the grammatical analysis (i'rab) of ﴿Our Lord﴾, it is as we said in the analysis of what came before.

And His saying: ﴿You are the gatherer of the people for a Day about which there is no doubt.﴾ ﴿Gatherer﴾ (jami') is an active participle (ism fa'il), and here it does not govern its object because it is in a construct phrase (idafa). Were it not for the idafa, it would say: "Our Lord, You are a gatherer of the people (an-nas)," with the noun in the accusative. But with the idafa, it only takes the genitive. And His saying: ﴿for a Day about which there is no doubt﴾ means: He gathers them for this time, so the lam here indicates a specific time (lil-tawqit). It is like His saying: ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun﴾ [al-Isra' 78], meaning at the time of its decline, or like His saying: ﴿When you divorce women, divorce them for their waiting period﴾ [at-Talaq 1], meaning at the time of their waiting period. So Allah the Exalted gathers the people for this time, ﴿for a Day about which there is no doubt﴾, meaning there is no uncertainty. However, "rayb" is more emphatic than "shakk" (doubt), although their meanings are close, because rayb includes additional unease and agitation along with doubt, while shakk is free of that. For this reason the word "rayb" was used, as its literal meaning indicates that there is a kind of anxiety and turmoil arising from doubt. Some doubts do not produce worry, distress, agitation, or concern in a person, while other doubts occupy a person, agitate him, and make him anxious, such as these great matters reported in the news about the Last Day, since a person must be completely reassured.

As for His saying: ﴿there is no doubt about it﴾, its grammatical analysis is: "la" is the particle of absolute negation (la li-nafy al-jins), "rayb" is its noun, and "fihi" is a prepositional phrase (jar and majrur) functioning as a predicate attached to an omitted predicate.

﴿Indeed, Allah does not fail in His promise﴾: this sentence is an affirmation of what came before, that He, the Exalted, gathers the people for a Day about which there is no doubt. In this verse, Allah the Exalted says about these noble people: after they have supplicated to Allah with what preceded, they report this statement which expresses their faith and certainty that they believe Allah gathers the people for a Day about which there is no doubt. Therefore they asked Allah not to let their hearts deviate and to grant them mercy from Him, because they believe that there is a Day on which Allah will gather people and recompense them for their deeds. Allah the Mighty and Majestic then says, reporting about these people, that they affirm this Last Day, and that Allah the Exalted will gather people, first and last, as He said: ﴿Say: Indeed, the former and the latter (49) will surely be gathered to the appointed time of a known day﴾ [al-Waqi'a 49-50]. He also said: ﴿That is a Day on which people will be gathered, and that is a Day witnessed﴾ [Hud 103]. How many are the people who preceded us, and how many are those who will come after us, and Allah knows best. Yet all of these people will be gathered in one plain: the caller will make them hear, and the sight will reach them. The caller makes them hear because nothing stands between them and his voice, neither tree, nor wall, nor mountains, nor valleys. Likewise, sight reaches them because they will be on an extended, non-spherical earth, so the eye sees the farthest of them just as it sees the nearest. This is evident: if the whole earth is spread out like a leather hide, as the Prophet ﷺ informed, then its farthest part will be like its nearest. But in its present spherical shape, whenever a thing recedes, part of it disappears from you; the lowest part disappears first, then it keeps disappearing little by little until you no longer see it. Allah the Exalted will gather all people on that Day, from the first of them to the last. Will He gather others besides them too? Yes, He will gather the jinn. And others? Yes: what are they? The wild beasts and the cattle: ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾ [at-Takwir 5], ﴿And when the pregnant camels are neglected﴾ [at-Takwir 4]. And others? Yes: the angels: ﴿On the Day when the Spirit and the angels stand in ranks, none will speak﴾ [an-Naba' 38], ﴿and your Lord comes with the angels, rank upon rank﴾ [al-Fajr 22]. So this Day is a great Day, a great Day; every intelligent person should prepare for it and ask Allah the Exalted to protect him from its evil.

﴿For a Day about which there is no doubt﴾ [Al 'Imran 9]: there is no doubt in it; the believer does not doubt it. Why? Because revelation (al-sam') indicates it, reason ('aql) indicates it, and innate nature (fitra) indicates it. Do we say that the consensus of the Muslims indicates it? Yes, the consensus of the Muslims indicates it, and of the Jews, the Christians, and every religious person. No proofs are as unanimously agreed upon as belief in the Last Day. For this reason He said: ﴿there is no doubt about it﴾. The Book indicates it; I think the indication of the Book is clear: it indicates it in countless verses. The Sunnah also indicates it in countless hadiths. Reason indicates it too, not merely its possibility but its necessity, and this is what is meant here. How does it indicate its necessity? ﴿Indeed, He who has imposed upon you the Qur'an will surely bring you back to a return﴾ [al-Qasas 85]: the One who imposed the Qur'an upon you and obligated it on you must certainly return you to a return (ma'ad), so He cannot leave you neglected. For what is the benefit of a Qur'an that is sent down, messengers who are sent, and blood that is shed against those who oppose, with the result being nothing? Thus there is no benefit. Therefore there must be a Day on which people will be recompensed for these deeds. Reason indicates that we must be gathered to Allah the Mighty and Majestic, and be recompensed for our deeds, and that it is impossible for the heavens and earth to be created, messengers to be sent, and books to be revealed, with the outcome and purpose being that we are buried in the earth and never return. There must be a return. For this reason we say that reason indicates what? The existence of the Last Day, its occurrence, and that it must certainly occur.

* The Shaykh: And what else does it indicate?
* A student: Innate nature (fitra).
* The Shaykh: Indeed, a person, if left to his innate nature, would know that he has a Lord who will recompense him, and that recompense occurs in the Hereafter and also in this world. It is indicated by consensus, the consensus of the Muslims, which is a matter transmitted with certainty and known necessarily from the religion. Even the consensus of the Jews and Christians: the Jews and Christians believe in the Last Day. For this reason, to this day, when one of them dies, they pray over him and supplicate for him for mercy and forgiveness, because they believe in the Day of Reckoning. But in any case, they believed and were deprived of the benefit of faith, since they did not believe in the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so their belief in this Day became a proof against them and not a proof in their favour.
* A student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan. ﴿Our Lord, You are the gatherer of the people for a Day about which there is no doubt. Indeed, Allah does not fail in His promise (9). Indeed, those who disbelieve, their wealth and their children will not avail them against Allah at all, and they are the fuel of the Fire (10). [They are] like the custom of the people of Pharaoh and those before them; they denied Our signs, so Allah seized them for their sins, and Allah is severe in punishment (11). Say to those who disbelieve: You will be overcome and gathered to Hell, and wretched is the resting place﴾ [Al 'Imran 9-12].
* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Shaytan. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us, and grant us from Yourself mercy. Indeed, You are the Bestower﴾ [Al 'Imran 8]. How is this sentence connected to what precedes it?
* A student: This sentence is connected to what precedes it as part of the supplication of those firm in knowledge.
* The Shaykh: Yes, it is part of the supplication of those firm in knowledge, meaning: ﴿They say: We believe in it﴾ [Al 'Imran 7], and they say: ﴿Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us﴾.
* The Shaykh: What is the meaning of zaygh (deviation)?
* The student: Zaygh is inclination.
* The Shaykh: And from it?
* The student: "Zaghat al-shams" (the sun declined).
* The Shaykh: Meaning?
* The student: It inclined.
* The Shaykh: From the middle of the sky. Their saying: ﴿after You have guided us﴾, what is its connection to what precedes it?
* A student: (...) its connection to what precedes it?
* The Shaykh: Yes, ﴿Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate﴾?
* The student: In what respect?
* The Shaykh: Its connection to what precedes it. Meaning, is its presence and absence the same, or does its presence have a benefit?
* A student: It has a benefit, which is seeking a means to Allah by mentioning that Allah has guided them.
* The Shaykh: Yes, seeking a means to Allah through His guidance of them, that He would not let them deviate?
* The student: That He would not let their hearts deviate afterward.
* The Shaykh: After the guidance. Well done. That is one. What is the second benefit?
* A student: Praise of Allah.
* The Shaykh: Correct, praise of Allah for His guidance, which is a form of speaking of the blessings of Allah the Mighty and Majestic. What is the benefit of His saying: ﴿from Yourself﴾?
* The student: That is, mercy when it comes from Him is great, and we do not want it from anyone else.
* The Shaykh: Yes, meaning sincerity, and that this mercy is great because it comes from Allah. Is there a parallel to it in the Sunnah?
* A student: The Prophet ﷺ taught Abu Bakr, who said:
* The Shaykh: "Teach me a supplication to make in my prayer."
* The student: "Teach me a supplication to make in my prayer." He said:
* The Shaykh: "Say: O Allah, indeed I have wronged myself greatly."
* The student: "O Allah, indeed I have wronged myself greatly, so forgive me."
* The Shaykh: "And none forgives sins."
* The student: "Except You, so forgive me with forgiveness from Yourself, indeed You are."
* The Shaykh: "And have mercy upon me."
* The student: "And have mercy upon me, indeed You are."
* The Shaykh: "The Forgiving, the Merciful"[[A hadith agreed upon (muttafaq 'alayh); al-Bukhari (7387) and Muslim (2705/48), from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him).]], yes.
* The Shaykh: His saying: ﴿al-Wahhab﴾ is one of the names of Allah. Does its coming in this form (sigha) indicate intensity of meaning (mubalagha), or attribution (nisba), or both?
* The student: Both.
* The Shaykh: Both. Explain that.
* The student: (...) it is a state (hal).
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* The student: Secondly, that it indicates intensity.
* The Shaykh: No, it is intensity due to the great number of those to whom He grants, for none can count those who receive His gifts except Allah the Mighty and Majestic.

His saying: ﴿You are the gatherer of the people for a Day about which there is no doubt﴾ [Al 'Imran 9]: what is meant by this Day?
* The student: The Day of Resurrection.
* The Shaykh: The Day of Resurrection. And what is the meaning of ﴿about which there is no doubt﴾?
* The student: That is, there is no doubt in it.
* The Shaykh: That is, there is no doubt in it. So rayb is synonymous with shakk. Is there a difference between them?
* The student: Yes, rayb is hesitation between doubt and anxiety.
* The Shaykh: Doubt with anxiety.
* The Shaykh: And shakk?
* The student: Doubt.
* The Shaykh: Doubt without anxiety. That is, one may be hesitant but without psychological anxiety. But this, because the matter is important, involves anxiety about what one doubts. Yet the believers do not doubt it, they have no rayb about it.

﴿Indeed, Allah does not fail in His promise﴾ [Al 'Imran 9]: this sentence's position relative to what precedes it is for emphasis, emphasizing the occurrence of that Day. The reason is: Allah promised it, and He does not fail in His promise, meaning He does not fail to fulfil what He, the Mighty and Majestic, promised of the occurrence of this Day. When you reflect on this sentence, you will find that it differs from what precedes it in its context: what precedes it is addressed in the second person, ﴿Our Lord, You are the gatherer of the people for a Day about which there is no doubt﴾ [Al 'Imran 9], while in this sentence the context is third person, ﴿Indeed, Allah does not fail in His promise﴾, and it did not say ﴿Indeed You do not fail in the promise﴾. Is this a case of iltifat (shift of pronoun) with the speech from one speaker, or is it a new resumed statement (isti'naf) from Allah and not from the speech of those firm in knowledge?

There are two opinions among the exegetes. Some say that ﴿Indeed, Allah does not fail in His promise﴾ is the speech of Allah, and on this reading there is no iltifat. Others say it is the speech of those firm in knowledge, and on this reading there is iltifat. Each has a preferred view. Whoever prefers the first says: iltifat is a departure from the usual form of speech, and the default is its absence, so the speech is from Allah. Whoever says it is the speech of those firm in knowledge with iltifat says: the default is that speech comes from one speaker, especially as part of it is linked to another part: ﴿You are the gatherer of the people﴾, ﴿You do not fail in the promise﴾, so part of it is connected to part. On reflection, this second view is the more preferred. The benefit of the iltifat is, first: alerting the addressee. When speech is in one uniform style, a person remains absorbed and does not notice, and things pass by while he is walking along. But when the style of speech changes and the manner shifts, then he becomes alert: alert to what changed, and why it changed. So there is a benefit: alerting the addressee. As for meaning, the coming of the form of the third person is more eloquent in magnifying, as if the Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, who is Allah, were a great king, and He, glory be to Him, is a great King, spoken of in the third person for exaltation and magnification, as a king who magnifies himself says to his soldiers: "The king commands you to such and such," or a commander says: "The commander orders you to such and such," instead of saying: "I command you." In any case, the attribute here is of what kind? Of the attributes of negation (salbiyya) or of affirmation (thubutiyya)?
* The students: Negative (salbiyya).
* The Shaykh: ﴿Indeed, You do not fail in the promise﴾ is negative, because it is an attribute of negation. It has passed with us that there is no purely negative attribute in the attributes of Allah, and that the negation found in an attribute of Allah entails the affirmation of the perfection of its opposite, and that because of the perfection of its opposite this thing does not exist. So here "He does not fail in the promise": the opposite of not failing in the promise is what?
* The students: Failing in the promise.
* The Shaykh: Failing in the promise. Failing in a promise happens either because the promiser lies or because he is incapable. Anyone who promised you and failed you did so for one of two reasons: either because he is a liar who makes promises and then fails, or because he is incapable. Is it clear?
A man said: "I will come to you tomorrow," and did not come. Why? It may be that he is a liar who promised and failed, yes? Or he is incapable: he was truthful that he would come, but he was prevented, by illness or something else, and did not come. So the negation of Allah's failing in His promise is due to the perfection of His truthfulness and the perfection of His power, the Mighty and Majestic. Because of the perfection of His truthfulness and power, He does not fail in the promise. I told you this sentence serves as emphasis for what preceded: ﴿Our Lord, You are the gatherer of the people for a Day about which there is no doubt﴾, because You do not fail in the promise, and whoever does not fail in a promise must certainly fulfil and accomplish what he promised.

Benefits:
In this verse ﴿Our Lord, You are the gatherer of the people for a Day about which there is no doubt﴾ there are benefits, among them: that the Day of Resurrection is coming, with no doubt, by His saying: ﴿for a Day about which there is no doubt﴾.
Among them: the completeness of Allah's power, the Glorified and Exalted, in gathering all people on this Day; yet this gathering needs no period of time: ﴿It will be but a single shout, and at once they will be on the surface of the earth﴾ [an-Nazi'at 13-14].
Among them: the wisdom of Allah the Mighty and Majestic in gathering people for this Day, because this gathering has consequences after it, which is the recompense of each doer for what he did, as He said: ﴿The Day He gathers you for the Day of Gathering, that is the Day of mutual loss and gain. And whoever believes in Allah and does righteousness, He will remove from him his misdeeds and admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. That is the great achievement. But those who disbelieved and denied Our signs, those are the companions of the Fire, abiding therein forever, and wretched is the destination﴾ [at-Taghabun 9-10]. So this gathering has a wisdom: the recompense of the doer for his deed, good if good and evil if evil.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: it is obligatory upon us to believe in this Day with certainty without any doubt. If anyone doubts it or denies it, he is not a believer; he is a disbeliever.

Among people in this station there are three categories, or if you wish, say four: a believer whose faith is free of any doubt; a doubter; a disbelieving denier; and a disbelieving disputant. That is, a person who is a denier may also argue and contend. The Quraysh disbelievers, which of these types were they? They were of the fourth type, the denier who disputes. Among people there is also one who denies but does not dispute, yet he is a denier in his own heart, not affirming the truth. Among people there is one who wavers in doubt. And among people there is one who believes with certainty, as though he sees it with his own eyes in his heart.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the negation of the attribute of breaking a promise from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, based on His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not fail in His promise﴾. The negation of this attribute implies His perfection in two things: truthfulness and power. Because of the perfection of Allah's truthfulness and the perfection of His power, He does not break His promise; rather, what He has promised must necessarily come to pass.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verse 10–11 (part 1 of 2):

Then the Exalted said, explaining the state of the disbelievers on that Day: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve, their wealth will not avail them, nor their children, against Allah at all. And they are the fuel of the Fire﴾ [Ali 'Imran 10]. ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve﴾ means: those who disbelieve in what it is obligatory to believe in. So whether they disbelieve in Allah, or in the Last Day, or in the angels, or in the Books, or in the Prophets, or in predestination (al-qadar), whoever disbelieves in any one of these six matters is a disbeliever, a disbeliever, because faith (iman) is not divisible, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And they say, "We believe in some and disbelieve in others," and they intend to adopt a way in between. Those are the disbelievers in truth﴾ [An-Nisa' 150-151]. And the Exalted said: ﴿Do you believe in part of the Book and disbelieve in part? Then what is the recompense of those who do that among you except disgrace in the life of this world; and on the Day of Resurrection they will be sent back to the severest punishment﴾ [Al-Baqarah 85].

So, "those who disbelieve" — in what? In what it is obligatory to believe in, namely the six pillars that the Messenger ﷺ explained in answer to Jibril when he asked him about faith (iman), saying: what is it? Come on.

* The student: "That you believe in Allah, His angels, His Books, His Messengers, the Last Day, and you believe in predestination, its good and its evil." [[Reported by Muslim (8/1) from the hadith of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) with this wording.]]

* The Shaykh: Yes. Whoever disbelieves in any one of these is a disbeliever. The disbelievers have wealth and they have children, and perhaps Allah gives them more children and wealth than He gives the believers. So do they benefit from this? Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Their wealth will not avail them, nor their children, against Allah at all.﴾ The word ﴿yughni﴾ (avail) has two meanings: it can mean "to prevent" or "to repel." So these wealths and children do not prevent anything from these disbelievers, nor do they repel anything from them. If some punishment of Allah befalls them, these children or this wealth cannot lift it from them; and if Allah decrees something against them, they cannot prevent or repel it. Thus ﴿will not avail﴾ means: they will not prevent, will not repel, and will not lift ﴿their wealth nor their children against Allah at all.﴾ Does ﴿their children﴾ include males or females?

* The students: It includes both.

* The Shaykh: It includes both, because the word "walad" (child), when used without qualification, includes the male and the female. What is the evidence that "walad" includes male and female?

* The students: ﴿Allah instructs you concerning your children: for the male, what is equal to the share of two females﴾.

* The Shaykh: ﴿Allah instructs you concerning your children: for the male, what is equal to the share of two females﴾ [An-Nisa' 11]. ﴿Their wealth nor their children will avail them against Allah at all﴾, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter. That is why you find one of them possessing great and abundant wealth, but if the Angel of Death comes to him, that wealth does not prevent him; his wealth does not prevent him. He has many children, retinue and servants, but they avail him nothing.

﴿And they are the fuel of the Fire﴾ [Ali 'Imran 10]. We seek refuge in Allah. Let us first look at the grammar so we understand the meaning: ﴿Ula'ika﴾ (those) is a subject (mubtada'), ﴿hum﴾ (they) is a second subject or a pronoun of separation (damir fasl), and ﴿waqud﴾ (fuel) is a predicate (khabar), either for the second subject or for the first subject. If you take ﴿hum﴾ as a second subject, then ﴿waqud﴾ is the predicate of the second subject; and if you take ﴿hum﴾ as a pronoun of separation, then ﴿waqud﴾ is the predicate of the first subject. The "waqud" with an opening vowel on the waw (waqūd, فَعُول-type noun) is that by which something is kindled, like "tahur" is that by which one purifies, "sahur" is that by which one takes the pre-dawn meal, and "fatur" is that by which one breaks the fast. This is in contrast to the form with a dammah: fuṭūr, suḥūr, ṭuhūr and wuḍū', which are the acts. That is, there is a difference between waḍū' and wuḍū', ṭahūr and ṭuhūr, saḥūr and suḥūr. Suḥūr with a dammah on the sin means the act of eating the pre-dawn meal. Saḥūr (with fatḥah) is that with which one takes the pre-dawn meal. So if a person brings dates at the end of the night, what do we call these dates? Saḥūr. If he eats them, we call it suḥūr. If he brings water to perform wudu' with, it is waḍū'. If he does it, washing his face and hands, wiping his head and washing his feet, we call it wuḍū'. Apply this to everything else.

Here He says ﴿waqud﴾, meaning that with which the fire is kindled, like firewood. Firewood is the fuel of the fire. These disbelievers are the fuel of the Fire. It has another fuel; what is it?

* The students: Stones.

* The Shaykh: Stones, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿O you who have believed, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is men and stones﴾ [At-Tahrim 6]. So these are the fuel of the Fire, and if they are—may Allah protect us—its fuel, then it is kindled by them, or set ablaze by them, and at the same time it burns them. We ask Allah for well-being.

He said: ﴿the fuel of the Fire﴾. "The Fire" is one of the names of Hell, the abode that Allah the Exalted prepared for those who denied His Messengers. Its heat is intense, and in it is the freezing cold (zamharir) of intense cold, we seek refuge in Allah. Concerning its heat, the Prophet ﷺ said: "Indeed it has been given preference over your fire by sixty-nine parts" [[A hadith agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3265) and Muslim (2843/30) from the hadith of Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him).]]. We seek refuge in Allah. What is its measure?

* The students: Seventy.

* The Shaykh: Seventy. Seventy, meaning in comparison to the fire of this world, it is seventy times more intense.

﴿Like the custom of the people of Pharaoh and those before them﴾ [Ali 'Imran 11]. The word ﴿ka-da'bi﴾ (like the custom of): the kaf is for comparison, and the prepositional phrase is the predicate of a fronted subject; that is, the custom (da'b) of these people is like the custom of the people of Pharaoh. The word "da'b" is used to mean "matter/affair" and it is also used to mean "habit." So in this verse, ﴿like the custom of the people of Pharaoh﴾ means like their situation. And when you say, "So-and-so, this is his da'b," it means this is his habit. ﴿Like the custom of the people of Pharaoh﴾, meaning their followers. "Fir'awn" is a proper name for every ruler of Egypt who was a disbeliever; every ruler of Egypt who was a disbeliever is called "Pharaoh," just as every ruler of Rome is called "Caesar" and every ruler of Persia is called "Khosrow."

﴿The people of Pharaoh and those before them﴾. Before the people of Pharaoh there were nations. The people of Abraham came before them, or not?

* The students: Yes.

* The Shaykh: And the people of Lot came before them, the people of Noah came before them, the people of Hud came before them, and 'Ad came before them. That is, there were nations before them. That is why He said ﴿and those before them﴾. What was their custom? He explained it with His saying: ﴿They denied Our signs﴾, meaning they denied everything that indicates them, of the cosmic signs and the legislative signs. Most often they deny the legislative signs, because few deny the cosmic signs, which are Allah's creation, and few deny that the Creator is Allah. But it is the legislative signs, which are the revelation that the Messengers brought, that is where denial occurs. The people of Pharaoh denied the signs of Allah. And what did Pharaoh say to Musa? He said to him: "Indeed, your messenger who has been sent to you is mad." [Ash-Shu'ara' 27]. He also said he was a sorcerer, described him with grave descriptions, and threatened him: ﴿He said, "If you take a deity other than me, I will surely make you among the imprisoned."﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara' 29]. He used to slaughter the sons of the Children of Israel and spare their women, and he would say to his people: "I am your Lord, the Most High." He said: ﴿Am I not better than this one who is contemptible and can hardly speak clearly? Then why not bracelets of gold be bestowed upon him or angels accompany him in succession?﴾ [Az-Zukhruf 52-53]. Allah the Exalted mentioned his story in His Book many times, for the sake of the Jews who were in Medina, and for the sake of the Ansar who had received much of the knowledge of the Jews.

He says: ﴿And those before them denied Our signs, so Allah seized them for their sins﴾ [Ali 'Imran 11]. ﴿Seized them﴾ means: destroyed them. ﴿For their sins﴾ means: because of their sins. A sin is an act of disobedience, and all the disobedience of these people was disbelief, we seek refuge in Allah; that is why they were seized. And with what did Allah seize Pharaoh and his people? He was seized by drowning, destroyed by what he used to boast of. He used to say to his people: ﴿Is not the dominion of Egypt mine, and these rivers flowing beneath me?﴾ [Az-Zukhruf 51]. So he was destroyed by what? By the water that flowed beneath him, which had been his pride. Allah the Mighty and Majestic destroyed him with water. The story is well known: Pharaoh gathered all the people of the cities in order to scheme against Musa. Musa left Egypt with his people and, by Allah's command, headed toward the Sea of Qulzum, which is the well-known Red Sea separating the continents of Africa and Asia on the side of Jeddah. When they reached the sea, the companions of Musa said: ﴿Indeed, we are overtaken!﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara' 61]. How? Because the sea was before them and Pharaoh and his people were behind them, so they were doomed in every case: if they went into the sea they would perish in it, and if they stayed they would perish by Pharaoh and his soldiers. Then Musa, peace be upon him, said: ﴿No!﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara' 62], meaning you will not be overtaken, and he gave the reason with his saying: ﴿Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara' 62]. Allah is Greatest! See how faith is at times of hardship: he sees the sea before him and Pharaoh and his soldiers behind him, and his companions, with whatever faith they had, said: ﴿Indeed, we are overtaken!﴾ But he said: ﴿No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me.﴾ Allah is Greatest! Then Allah revealed to him that he should strike the sea with his staff, and he struck the sea with his staff and it split. After how many days?

* The students: Immediately.

* The Shaykh: Immediately, in an instant. What is the evidence that it was in an instant? Because He said: ﴿So it parted﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara' 63]. ﴿Strike with your staff the sea, so it parted﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara' 63]. See how Allah omitted even the action by which the parting occurred; when Allah commanded Musa to strike it, the sea was prepared to part, and by that one strike that landed on it, it split. And how many were there? There were twelve dry paths. They became dry at once, and they walked on them on foot, and the waters were like mountains of rock. Some exegetes mentioned in the account of the Children of Israel that Allah placed windows in these masses of water so that they could see one another, so that each could be reassured about the others. When Musa and his people had fully exited, behold, Pharaoh and his people entered, and the Lord the Exalted commanded the sea and it closed over him at once, and they all drowned to the last one. When Pharaoh realized he was drowning, ﴿he said, "I believe that there is no deity except that in whom the Children of Israel have believed"﴾ [Yunus 90]. When he saw the punishment and witnessed it, he believed ﴿that there is no deity except that in whom the Children of Israel have believed,﴾ but that did not benefit him, as Allah the Exalted said about such cases: ﴿So when they saw Our punishment, they said, "We have believed in Allah alone and disbelieved in what we used to associate with Him." But their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our punishment﴾ [Ghafir 84-85]. That is why it was said to Pharaoh: ﴿Now?﴾ [Yunus 91], meaning: now you believe that there is no deity except that in whom the Children of Israel have believed, ﴿while you had disobeyed before and were among the corrupters?﴾ This interrogation means rebuke against him and the negation of his benefit from that faith. But Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So today We will save you in your body﴾ [Yunus 92], not for your benefit, but so that you would be a sign for those who come after you. Who are those who come after him?

The Children of Israel. Because Pharaoh had terrified the Children of Israel, and if his body had not been shown to them upon the surface of the water, they would have doubted, perhaps he had not perished with his people, perhaps he had escaped. So Allah preserved his body: ﴿So today We will save you in your body﴾, only the body, not your soul. Why? ﴿So that you may be a sign for those who come after you﴾ [Yunus 92], so that they would know that you had indeed died.

Do you see any greater retribution, may Allah protect us, against this tyrant man? No, it is an extreme retribution. He gathered his people and displayed the appearance of might in order to finish off Musa and his people, and Allah seized them with the seizure of the Mighty, the All-Powerful: ﴿And there had certainly come to the people of Pharaoh warnings. They denied all of Our signs, so We seized them with the seizure of an Mighty, Omnipotent One﴾ [Al-Qamar 41-42]. The Mighty: the Overpowering who cannot be overcome; the Omnipotent who is never incapable, glorified and exalted is He. They were destroyed by this water in which Pharaoh used to take pride. That is why He said: ﴿So Allah seized them for their sins﴾ [Ali 'Imran 11]. The "ba'" here is causal in one respect and compensatory in another respect. How so? It is causal, meaning that it is because of their sins, since Allah does not wrong people at all, but people wrong themselves, and Allah seizes no one except for a sin. And it is compensatory from another angle: He did not wrong them, rather He made their recompense of the same kind as their deeds: ﴿Whoever comes with a good deed will have ten times its like, and whoever comes with an evil deed will not be recompensed except with the like thereof﴾ [Al-An'am 160].

﴿And Allah is severe in punishment﴾ [Ali 'Imran 11]. Ending the verse with this attribute is highly appropriate, because those who were seized for their sins were seized with what? With the severe punishment, than which there is none more severe. I do not think that anyone, up to our present day, can destroy his enemy as Allah destroyed Pharaoh. Can the greatest state in the world now withdraw the water so quickly that the enemy enters and then the water closes over them? No, it is impossible. But the Severe in Punishment, the Exalted, the Lord the Exalted who sends down His punishment upon His enemies for a wisdom, is able to do so in an instant: ﴿So strike for them a dry path in the sea, not fearing being overtaken, and not being afraid﴾ [Ta-Ha 77]. ﴿And Allah is severe in punishment.﴾

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve, their wealth will not avail them, nor their children﴾ [Ali 'Imran 10], and so on to the end.

* From this noble verse is derived: that the disbelievers do not benefit from their wealth or their children. Among its benefits: the wealth and children of the disbelievers will not avail them anything against Allah.

* And among its benefits: the believers may benefit from their wealth and children, and so it is. The believer gives charity from his wealth and benefits, and his child prays for him during his life and after his death and he benefits; but the disbeliever does not benefit even if his child prays for him. Is that not so?

* The students: Indeed.

* The Shaykh: And is it permissible for his child to pray for him?

* The students: It is not permissible.

* The Shaykh: No, except if he is alive, then it is permissible to pray for him to be guided. As for praying for him after his death, that is not possible.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the disbeliever owns property. Do you see? [Your question appears garbled; I have rendered the text as it stands.]

His saying: ﴿their wealth﴾ attributes the wealth to them, which is evidence that the disbeliever owns his wealth. The scholars differed concerning the apostate who disbelieves after his Islam: does his ownership of what is in his possession cease or not?

Some scholars said: when a person apostatizes, his ownership of what is in his possession ceases, and therefore his dispositions over it are not valid. But the preponderant view is that his ownership does not cease unless he dies in his apostasy, in which case his property does not pass to his heirs but to the public treasury (bayt al-mal). It is well known that if we said that the apostate's ownership ceases, a great difficulty would arise in our time, namely: some people do not pray, and whoever does not pray is an apostate. If we say that the apostate's ownership ceases, it follows that every transaction made with his property by one who does not pray is invalid: if they sell something, the sale is not valid; if they buy something, the purchase is not valid; if they hire something, the hiring is not valid; if they lease something, the leasing is not valid. Although some scholars held this view, the preponderant view is that his ownership of his property remains until he dies. When he dies, we direct his property to the public treasury, and none of his heirs inherits from him, based on the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "A Muslim does not inherit from a disbeliever, nor does a disbeliever inherit from a Muslim." [[A hadith agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6764) and Muslim (1614/1) from the hadith of Usamah ibn Zayd (may Allah be pleased with them both).]]

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verses 10–11 (part 2 of 2):**

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the demonstration of the power of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and that neither wealth nor children avail anything against Allah, based on His saying: ﴿Their wealth and their children will not avail them at all against Allah﴾. And apart from Allah? Do they avail or not?
* Students: No.
* Shaykh: No, they avail. Apart from Allah they avail. It is possible for someone to pay some of his wealth and be spared from being killed, is that not so?
* Students: Yes.
* Shaykh: And it is possible that he has brave children who defend him if someone intends him harm. But against Allah, neither wealth nor child avails.
And among them, * one of the benefits of the verse: encouraging the hearts of the believers against the disbelievers. What is its basis? That their wealth and their children do not avail anything against Allah. So if we are victorious through Allah, then what they have of (...), and stockpiles, and wealth, and children, will not avail them anything against Allah, is that not so? Yes, it is so. For this reason, if Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, willed to nullify everything they have done, He would nullify it. I think you do not forget the earthquakes that destroy much of what they have built, and you do not forget either that what they have made may be corrupted by their own hands. How many explosions have occurred in stores of atomic and nuclear bombs, and much evil has thereby befallen them and those around them! If Allah, glorified and exalted, willed, He would only cause the atmosphere to be darkened with fog, and they would be unable to do anything, because the power and might of Allah, glorified and exalted, cannot be overcome by anything.
The atomic and nuclear bombs, and much evil has thereby befallen them and those around them. If Allah, glorified and exalted, willed, He would only cause the atmosphere to be darkened with fog, and they would be unable to do anything, because the power and might of Allah, glorified and exalted, cannot be overcome by anything. For this reason He said: ﴿Their wealth and their children will not avail them at all against Allah﴾ [Al 'Imran 10].
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the disbelievers are in the Fire, based on His saying: ﴿And those are the fuel of the Fire﴾ [Al 'Imran 10]. But do we testify that every disbeliever is in the Fire? No. Do we testify that a specific disbeliever, by name, is in the Fire? The answer is no. Rather, we testify in a general sense and say: every disbeliever is in the Fire, just as we say: every believer is in Paradise, but we do not testify for any specific individual that he is in Paradise. So there is a difference between the general and the particular.
And in the verse there is also the affirmation of the Fire, based on His saying: ﴿the fuel of the Fire﴾ (...).
* * *
* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed. ﴿Like the custom of the people of Pharaoh and those before them, who denied Our signs, so Allah seized them for their sins; and Allah is severe in punishment. (11) Say to those who disbelieve: "You will be overcome and gathered into Hell, and wretched is the resting place." (12) There has already been a sign for you in the two armies that met: one fighting in the way of Allah, and another disbelieving, seeing them twice their number by sight. And Allah strengthens with His victory whom He wills. Indeed in that is a lesson for those of vision. (13) Beautified for people is the love of desires: women, sons, heaped-up piles of gold and silver, branded horses, cattle, and tilth. That is the enjoyment of the worldly life, and with Allah is the best return﴾ [Al 'Imran 11–14].
* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from Satan the accursed. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve—neither their wealth nor their children will avail them at all against Allah﴾. His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve—neither their wealth nor their children will avail them at all against Allah﴾. Is what is meant by "those who disbelieve" a specific people, or is it general?
* Student: General.
* Shaykh: Rather, general.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: And he has wealth and children, so these wealth and children—?
* Student: Will not avail him against Allah at all.
* Shaykh: Is the negation of availing here in this world or in the Hereafter?
* Student: In the Hereafter.
* Shaykh: And in this world?
* Student: It is possible that they avail them in this world.
* Shaykh: Against Allah?
* Student: No, against people.
* Shaykh: I want to say: they will not avail them against Allah.
* Student: In the Hereafter they will not avail them.
* Shaykh: And in this world?
* Student: Against Allah?
* Shaykh: Yes indeed.
* Student: They do not avail them.
* Shaykh: Are you certain?
* Student: Not avail them, certainly.
* Shaykh: Neither in this world nor in the Hereafter. Do you agree with this? Yes. "Will not avail them against Allah at all," based on the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And when Allah intends harm for a people, there is no turning it away﴾ [Ar-Ra'd 11]. His saying: ﴿And those are the fuel of the Fire.﴾ "Fuel of the Fire" means that by which it is kindled, i.e., they are the ones with whom the Fire is kindled. Does anyone share with them in that?
* Student: No one shares with them in it except those who disbelieved in His messengers.
* Shaykh: They are the disbelievers, yes.
* Student: The hypocrites.
* Shaykh: The hypocrites are disbelievers.
* Student: Or the Jews?
* Shaykh: No, no.
* Student: The stones.
* Shaykh: The stones, ﴿its fuel is people and stones﴾. His saying: ﴿like the custom of the people of Pharaoh﴾, what does it mean?
* Student: It means like the people of Pharaoh.
* Shaykh: The word "da'b" means what?
* Student: Like the people.
* Shaykh: It means ﴿like the custom of the people of Pharaoh﴾, i.e., like the example of the people of Pharaoh?
* Student: Like their habit and their condition.
* Shaykh: Like their habit and their condition. And what is the i'rab (grammatical analysis) position of this phrase, or this word?
* Student: Its i'rab position?
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: That is, (da'b) is a subject, (the people of Pharaoh) is the predicate.
* Shaykh: No, no.
* Student: The da'b (...) like it.
* Shaykh: No.
* Student: This is not its i'rab.
* Shaykh: No, that is not its i'rab.
* Student: (Ka-da'b) is a prepositional phrase functioning as a fronted predicate.
* Shaykh: A fronted predicate of what?
* Student: Of an implied subject.
* Shaykh: A fronted predicate of an implied subject? A fronted predicate, as long as the subject is implied, you have the choice (...) you put it after (...) you put it before. So now you are saying: a predicate of an implied subject, delayed such-and-such?
* Student: I retracted from the delayed one.
* Shaykh: You retracted from the delayed one? So, a predicate of an implied subject, and the implied element is?
* Student: The implied element: their custom.
* Shaykh: Their custom is like the custom of the people of Pharaoh. What is meant by "the people of Pharaoh" here?
* Student: Pharaoh?
* Shaykh: "The people of Pharaoh."
* Student: Pharaoh himself and those who followed him, or those among his people who disbelieved.
* Shaykh: Those who followed him. Why do we not say: those who followed him?
* Student: Those among his people who disbelieved, or those who followed him.
* Shaykh: Those who followed him. That is, he and his followers. ﴿Those before them﴾, like whom?
* Student: Like the people of Noah.
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: And 'Ad.
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: And Thamud.
* Shaykh: Yes, and the people of Abraham, the people of Lot, and the companions of Madyan, many. The clause: ﴿they denied Our signs﴾, ﴿they denied Our signs, so Allah seized them﴾, what is its i'rab position?
* Student: A resumptive explanatory clause.
* Shaykh: Yes, a resumptive clause explaining this custom. What is meant by "signs" here?
* Student: The cosmic and the legislated.
* Shaykh: And the legislated. How can one deny legislated signs?
* Student: They denied what Moses brought.
* Shaykh: Yes, or their messengers, because He says: ﴿and those before them﴾.
* Student: The messengers all, what their messengers brought.
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: And likewise regarding the cosmic signs.
* Shaykh: Regarding the cosmic signs, they denied them either by attributing them to other than Allah, or by claiming that Allah has a partner in them or a helper. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿so Allah seized them for their sins﴾. The letter "ba'" (in bi-dhunubihim) means what?
* Student: The "ba'" here is causal.
* Shaykh: The "ba'" here is causal: Allah seized them because of their sins. And is there another meaning that is valid?
* Student: Exchange.
* Shaykh: Exchange. That is, their recompense is of the same kind as their deeds and in exchange for them. ﴿And Allah is severe in punishment.﴾ Let us now take the benefits.
* Among the benefits of these verses, first, the first verse: that disbelievers may be provided with wealth and children.
* Student: We have taken it.
* Shaykh: You have taken it?
* Student: Yes.
* Shaykh: * Among the benefits of the noble verse: ﴿like the custom of the people of Pharaoh and those before them﴾, which is the second verse. * Among its benefits: that later disbelievers are like earlier disbelievers, because Allah's way with creation is one, since He, the Mighty and Majestic, has no kinship with creation that He observes and favors toward whoever is connected to Him. People are equal before Allah, the Exalted; the most noble of them before Allah is the most pious, based on His saying: ﴿like the custom of the people of Pharaoh﴾, to the end.
* And among the benefits of the noble verse: that Pharaoh and his household were punished in this world, just as they will be punished in the Hereafter, based on His saying: ﴿so Allah seized them for their sins﴾.
* And among its benefits: the refutation of those who claim that Pharaoh became Muslim and that his Islam benefited him, because Allah, the Exalted, mentioned that in the manner of censure and punishment. Had he been a penitent whose repentance would benefit him, his sin would not have been mentioned without mention of his repentance, since Allah, the Exalted, is just and does not mention anyone for a sin from which he repented unless He clarifies his repentance. Adam, peace be upon him, when he ate from the tree and what happened to him occurred, and he repented to Allah: ﴿Then Adam received from his Lord words, and He accepted his repentance﴾ [Al-Baqarah 37]. Allah mentioned his disobedience and mentioned that he repented, and mentioned that after repentance he was better than he was before it: ﴿Then his Lord chose him, and accepted his repentance and guided him﴾ [Ta-Ha 122].
* And among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of the signs (ayat) of Allah, which are the indicators pointing to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to His existence, and to what these signs contain of His attributes. For example, the descent of mercy and the descent of rain is a sign of mercy, a sign of Allah's mercy, of His existence and His mercy. The descent of punishments is a sign of Allah's existence and of His wrath. And so every sign that indicates the existence of Allah, glorified and exalted, and what that sign requires of attributes, whether it is a sign of mercy or a sign of punishment.
* And among the benefits of the noble verse: that Allah does not wrong people at all, but rather seizes them for their sins, ﴿so Allah seized them for their sins﴾. A parallel to this is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And whatever affliction strikes you is because of what your hands have earned, and He pardons much﴾ [Ash-Shura 30].
* And among the benefits of the noble verse: the refutation of the Jabriyya (the determinist sect) who do not attribute the act of the servant to him, based on His saying: ﴿for their sins﴾, where He attributed the sins to them. An act is attributed only to the one who truly performs it, while the Jabriyya say that an act is not attributed to a human in the true sense.
* And among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of the attribute of severity of punishment for Allah, based on His saying: ﴿And Allah is severe in punishment﴾.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verse 10–11 (part 1 of 2):

Then the Exalted said, explaining the state of the disbelievers on that Day: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve, their wealth will not avail them, nor their children, against Allah at all. And they are the fuel of the Fire﴾ [Ali 'Imran 10]. ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve﴾ means: those who disbelieve in what it is obligatory to believe in. So whether they disbelieve in Allah, or in the Last Day, or in the angels, or in the Books, or in the Prophets, or in predestination (al-qadar), whoever disbelieves in any one of these six matters is a disbeliever, a disbeliever, because faith (iman) is not divisible, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And they say, "We believe in some and disbelieve in others," and they intend to adopt a way in between. Those are the disbelievers in truth﴾ [An-Nisa' 150-151]. And the Exalted said: ﴿Do you believe in part of the Book and disbelieve in part? Then what is the recompense of those who do that among you except disgrace in the life of this world; and on the Day of Resurrection they will be sent back to the severest punishment﴾ [Al-Baqarah 85].

So, "those who disbelieve" — in what? In what it is obligatory to believe in, namely the six pillars that the Messenger ﷺ explained in answer to Jibril when he asked him about faith (iman), saying: what is it? Come on.

* The student: "That you believe in Allah, His angels, His Books, His Messengers, the Last Day, and you believe in predestination, its good and its evil." [[Reported by Muslim (8/1) from the hadith of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) with this wording.]]

* The Shaykh: Yes. Whoever disbelieves in any one of these is a disbeliever. The disbelievers have wealth and they have children, and perhaps Allah gives them more children and wealth than He gives the believers. So do they benefit from this? Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Their wealth will not avail them, nor their children, against Allah at all.﴾ The word ﴿yughni﴾ (avail) has two meanings: it can mean "to prevent" or "to repel." So these wealths and children do not prevent anything from these disbelievers, nor do they repel anything from them. If some punishment of Allah befalls them, these children or this wealth cannot lift it from them; and if Allah decrees something against them, they cannot prevent or repel it. Thus ﴿will not avail﴾ means: they will not prevent, will not repel, and will not lift ﴿their wealth nor their children against Allah at all.﴾ Does ﴿their children﴾ include males or females?

* The students: It includes both.

* The Shaykh: It includes both, because the word "walad" (child), when used without qualification, includes the male and the female. What is the evidence that "walad" includes male and female?

* The students: ﴿Allah instructs you concerning your children: for the male, what is equal to the share of two females﴾.

* The Shaykh: ﴿Allah instructs you concerning your children: for the male, what is equal to the share of two females﴾ [An-Nisa' 11]. ﴿Their wealth nor their children will avail them against Allah at all﴾, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter. That is why you find one of them possessing great and abundant wealth, but if the Angel of Death comes to him, that wealth does not prevent him; his wealth does not prevent him. He has many children, retinue and servants, but they avail him nothing.

﴿And they are the fuel of the Fire﴾ [Ali 'Imran 10]. We seek refuge in Allah. Let us first look at the grammar so we understand the meaning: ﴿Ula'ika﴾ (those) is a subject (mubtada'), ﴿hum﴾ (they) is a second subject or a pronoun of separation (damir fasl), and ﴿waqud﴾ (fuel) is a predicate (khabar), either for the second subject or for the first subject. If you take ﴿hum﴾ as a second subject, then ﴿waqud﴾ is the predicate of the second subject; and if you take ﴿hum﴾ as a pronoun of separation, then ﴿waqud﴾ is the predicate of the first subject. The "waqud" with an opening vowel on the waw (waqūd, فَعُول-type noun) is that by which something is kindled, like "tahur" is that by which one purifies, "sahur" is that by which one takes the pre-dawn meal, and "fatur" is that by which one breaks the fast. This is in contrast to the form with a dammah: fuṭūr, suḥūr, ṭuhūr and wuḍū', which are the acts. That is, there is a difference between waḍū' and wuḍū', ṭahūr and ṭuhūr, saḥūr and suḥūr. Suḥūr with a dammah on the sin means the act of eating the pre-dawn meal. Saḥūr (with fatḥah) is that with which one takes the pre-dawn meal. So if a person brings dates at the end of the night, what do we call these dates? Saḥūr. If he eats them, we call it suḥūr. If he brings water to perform wudu' with, it is waḍū'. If he does it, washing his face and hands, wiping his head and washing his feet, we call it wuḍū'. Apply this to everything else.

Here He says ﴿waqud﴾, meaning that with which the fire is kindled, like firewood. Firewood is the fuel of the fire. These disbelievers are the fuel of the Fire. It has another fuel; what is it?

* The students: Stones.

* The Shaykh: Stones, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿O you who have believed, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is men and stones﴾ [At-Tahrim 6]. So these are the fuel of the Fire, and if they are—may Allah protect us—its fuel, then it is kindled by them, or set ablaze by them, and at the same time it burns them. We ask Allah for well-being.

He said: ﴿the fuel of the Fire﴾. "The Fire" is one of the names of Hell, the abode that Allah the Exalted prepared for those who denied His Messengers. Its heat is intense, and in it is the freezing cold (zamharir) of intense cold, we seek refuge in Allah. Concerning its heat, the Prophet ﷺ said: "Indeed it has been given preference over your fire by sixty-nine parts" [[A hadith agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3265) and Muslim (2843/30) from the hadith of Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him).]]. We seek refuge in Allah. What is its measure?

* The students: Seventy.

* The Shaykh: Seventy. Seventy, meaning in comparison to the fire of this world, it is seventy times more intense.

﴿Like the custom of the people of Pharaoh and those before them﴾ [Ali 'Imran 11]. The word ﴿ka-da'bi﴾ (like the custom of): the kaf is for comparison, and the prepositional phrase is the predicate of a fronted subject; that is, the custom (da'b) of these people is like the custom of the people of Pharaoh. The word "da'b" is used to mean "matter/affair" and it is also used to mean "habit." So in this verse, ﴿like the custom of the people of Pharaoh﴾ means like their situation. And when you say, "So-and-so, this is his da'b," it means this is his habit. ﴿Like the custom of the people of Pharaoh﴾, meaning their followers. "Fir'awn" is a proper name for every ruler of Egypt who was a disbeliever; every ruler of Egypt who was a disbeliever is called "Pharaoh," just as every ruler of Rome is called "Caesar" and every ruler of Persia is called "Khosrow."

﴿The people of Pharaoh and those before them﴾. Before the people of Pharaoh there were nations. The people of Abraham came before them, or not?

* The students: Yes.

* The Shaykh: And the people of Lot came before them, the people of Noah came before them, the people of Hud came before them, and 'Ad came before them. That is, there were nations before them. That is why He said ﴿and those before them﴾. What was their custom? He explained it with His saying: ﴿They denied Our signs﴾, meaning they denied everything that indicates them, of the cosmic signs and the legislative signs. Most often they deny the legislative signs, because few deny the cosmic signs, which are Allah's creation, and few deny that the Creator is Allah. But it is the legislative signs, which are the revelation that the Messengers brought, that is where denial occurs. The people of Pharaoh denied the signs of Allah. And what did Pharaoh say to Musa? He said to him: "Indeed, your messenger who has been sent to you is mad." [Ash-Shu'ara' 27]. He also said he was a sorcerer, described him with grave descriptions, and threatened him: ﴿He said, "If you take a deity other than me, I will surely make you among the imprisoned."﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara' 29]. He used to slaughter the sons of the Children of Israel and spare their women, and he would say to his people: "I am your Lord, the Most High." He said: ﴿Am I not better than this one who is contemptible and can hardly speak clearly? Then why not bracelets of gold be bestowed upon him or angels accompany him in succession?﴾ [Az-Zukhruf 52-53]. Allah the Exalted mentioned his story in His Book many times, for the sake of the Jews who were in Medina, and for the sake of the Ansar who had received much of the knowledge of the Jews.

He says: ﴿And those before them denied Our signs, so Allah seized them for their sins﴾ [Ali 'Imran 11]. ﴿Seized them﴾ means: destroyed them. ﴿For their sins﴾ means: because of their sins. A sin is an act of disobedience, and all the disobedience of these people was disbelief, we seek refuge in Allah; that is why they were seized. And with what did Allah seize Pharaoh and his people?
