He was seized by drowning, destroyed by what he used to boast of. He used to say to his people: ﴿Is not the dominion of Egypt mine, and these rivers flowing beneath me?﴾ [Az-Zukhruf 51]. So he was destroyed by what? By the water that flowed beneath him, which had been his pride. Allah the Mighty and Majestic destroyed him with water. The story is well known: Pharaoh gathered all the people of the cities in order to scheme against Musa. Musa left Egypt with his people and, by Allah's command, headed toward the Sea of Qulzum, which is the well-known Red Sea separating the continents of Africa and Asia on the side of Jeddah. When they reached the sea, the companions of Musa said: ﴿Indeed, we are overtaken!﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara' 61]. How? Because the sea was before them and Pharaoh and his people were behind them, so they were doomed in every case: if they went into the sea they would perish in it, and if they stayed they would perish by Pharaoh and his soldiers. Then Musa, peace be upon him, said: ﴿No!﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara' 62], meaning you will not be overtaken, and he gave the reason with his saying: ﴿Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara' 62]. Allah is Greatest! See how faith is at times of hardship: he sees the sea before him and Pharaoh and his soldiers behind him, and his companions, with whatever faith they had, said: ﴿Indeed, we are overtaken!﴾ But he said: ﴿No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me.﴾ Allah is Greatest! Then Allah revealed to him that he should strike the sea with his staff, and he struck the sea with his staff and it split. After how many days?

* The students: Immediately.

* The Shaykh: Immediately, in an instant. What is the evidence that it was in an instant? Because He said: ﴿So it parted﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara' 63]. ﴿Strike with your staff the sea, so it parted﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara' 63]. See how Allah omitted even the action by which the parting occurred; when Allah commanded Musa to strike it, the sea was prepared to part, and by that one strike that landed on it, it split. And how many were there? There were twelve dry paths. They became dry at once, and they walked on them on foot, and the waters were like mountains of rock. Some exegetes mentioned in the account of the Children of Israel that Allah placed windows in these masses of water so that they could see one another, so that each could be reassured about the others. When Musa and his people had fully exited, behold, Pharaoh and his people entered, and the Lord the Exalted commanded the sea and it closed over him at once, and they all drowned to the last one. When Pharaoh realized he was drowning, ﴿he said, "I believe that there is no deity except that in whom the Children of Israel have believed"﴾ [Yunus 90]. When he saw the punishment and witnessed it, he believed ﴿that there is no deity except that in whom the Children of Israel have believed,﴾ but that did not benefit him, as Allah the Exalted said about such cases: ﴿So when they saw Our punishment, they said, "We have believed in Allah alone and disbelieved in what we used to associate with Him." But their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our punishment﴾ [Ghafir 84-85]. That is why it was said to Pharaoh: ﴿Now?﴾ [Yunus 91], meaning: now you believe that there is no deity except that in whom the Children of Israel have believed, ﴿while you had disobeyed before and were among the corrupters?﴾ This interrogation means rebuke against him and the negation of his benefit from that faith. But Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So today We will save you in your body﴾ [Yunus 92], not for your benefit, but so that you would be a sign for those who come after you. Who are those who come after him?

The Children of Israel. Because Pharaoh had terrified the Children of Israel, and if his body had not been shown to them upon the surface of the water, they would have doubted, perhaps he had not perished with his people, perhaps he had escaped. So Allah preserved his body: ﴿So today We will save you in your body﴾, only the body, not your soul. Why? ﴿So that you may be a sign for those who come after you﴾ [Yunus 92], so that they would know that you had indeed died.

Do you see any greater retribution, may Allah protect us, against this tyrant man? No, it is an extreme retribution. He gathered his people and displayed the appearance of might in order to finish off Musa and his people, and Allah seized them with the seizure of the Mighty, the All-Powerful: ﴿And there had certainly come to the people of Pharaoh warnings. They denied all of Our signs, so We seized them with the seizure of an Mighty, Omnipotent One﴾ [Al-Qamar 41-42]. The Mighty: the Overpowering who cannot be overcome; the Omnipotent who is never incapable, glorified and exalted is He. They were destroyed by this water in which Pharaoh used to take pride. That is why He said: ﴿So Allah seized them for their sins﴾ [Ali 'Imran 11]. The "ba'" here is causal in one respect and compensatory in another respect. How so? It is causal, meaning that it is because of their sins, since Allah does not wrong people at all, but people wrong themselves, and Allah seizes no one except for a sin. And it is compensatory from another angle: He did not wrong them, rather He made their recompense of the same kind as their deeds: ﴿Whoever comes with a good deed will have ten times its like, and whoever comes with an evil deed will not be recompensed except with the like thereof﴾ [Al-An'am 160].

﴿And Allah is severe in punishment﴾ [Ali 'Imran 11]. Ending the verse with this attribute is highly appropriate, because those who were seized for their sins were seized with what? With the severe punishment, than which there is none more severe. I do not think that anyone, up to our present day, can destroy his enemy as Allah destroyed Pharaoh. Can the greatest state in the world now withdraw the water so quickly that the enemy enters and then the water closes over them? No, it is impossible. But the Severe in Punishment, the Exalted, the Lord the Exalted who sends down His punishment upon His enemies for a wisdom, is able to do so in an instant: ﴿So strike for them a dry path in the sea, not fearing being overtaken, and not being afraid﴾ [Ta-Ha 77]. ﴿And Allah is severe in punishment.﴾

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve, their wealth will not avail them, nor their children﴾ [Ali 'Imran 10], and so on to the end.

* From this noble verse is derived: that the disbelievers do not benefit from their wealth or their children. Among its benefits: the wealth and children of the disbelievers will not avail them anything against Allah.

* And among its benefits: the believers may benefit from their wealth and children, and so it is. The believer gives charity from his wealth and benefits, and his child prays for him during his life and after his death and he benefits; but the disbeliever does not benefit even if his child prays for him. Is that not so?

* The students: Indeed.

* The Shaykh: And is it permissible for his child to pray for him?

* The students: It is not permissible.

* The Shaykh: No, except if he is alive, then it is permissible to pray for him to be guided. As for praying for him after his death, that is not possible.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the disbeliever owns property. Do you see? [Your question appears garbled; I have rendered the text as it stands.]

His saying: ﴿their wealth﴾ attributes the wealth to them, which is evidence that the disbeliever owns his wealth. The scholars differed concerning the apostate who disbelieves after his Islam: does his ownership of what is in his possession cease or not?

Some scholars said: when a person apostatizes, his ownership of what is in his possession ceases, and therefore his dispositions over it are not valid. But the preponderant view is that his ownership does not cease unless he dies in his apostasy, in which case his property does not pass to his heirs but to the public treasury (bayt al-mal). It is well known that if we said that the apostate's ownership ceases, a great difficulty would arise in our time, namely: some people do not pray, and whoever does not pray is an apostate. If we say that the apostate's ownership ceases, it follows that every transaction made with his property by one who does not pray is invalid: if they sell something, the sale is not valid; if they buy something, the purchase is not valid; if they hire something, the hiring is not valid; if they lease something, the leasing is not valid. Although some scholars held this view, the preponderant view is that his ownership of his property remains until he dies. When he dies, we direct his property to the public treasury, and none of his heirs inherits from him, based on the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "A Muslim does not inherit from a disbeliever, nor does a disbeliever inherit from a Muslim." [[A hadith agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6764) and Muslim (1614/1) from the hadith of Usamah ibn Zayd (may Allah be pleased with them both).]]

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verses 10–11 (part 2 of 2):**

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the demonstration of the power of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and that neither wealth nor children avail anything against Allah, based on His saying: ﴿Their wealth and their children will not avail them at all against Allah﴾. And apart from Allah? Do they avail or not?
* Students: No.
* Shaykh: No, they avail. Apart from Allah they avail. It is possible for someone to pay some of his wealth and be spared from being killed, is that not so?
* Students: Yes.
* Shaykh: And it is possible that he has brave children who defend him if someone intends him harm. But against Allah, neither wealth nor child avails.
And among them, * one of the benefits of the verse: encouraging the hearts of the believers against the disbelievers. What is its basis? That their wealth and their children do not avail anything against Allah. So if we are victorious through Allah, then what they have of (...), and stockpiles, and wealth, and children, will not avail them anything against Allah, is that not so? Yes, it is so. For this reason, if Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, willed to nullify everything they have done, He would nullify it. I think you do not forget the earthquakes that destroy much of what they have built, and you do not forget either that what they have made may be corrupted by their own hands. How many explosions have occurred in stores of atomic and nuclear bombs, and much evil has thereby befallen them and those around them! If Allah, glorified and exalted, willed, He would only cause the atmosphere to be darkened with fog, and they would be unable to do anything, because the power and might of Allah, glorified and exalted, cannot be overcome by anything.
The atomic and nuclear bombs, and much evil has thereby befallen them and those around them. If Allah, glorified and exalted, willed, He would only cause the atmosphere to be darkened with fog, and they would be unable to do anything, because the power and might of Allah, glorified and exalted, cannot be overcome by anything. For this reason He said: ﴿Their wealth and their children will not avail them at all against Allah﴾ [Al 'Imran 10].
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the disbelievers are in the Fire, based on His saying: ﴿And those are the fuel of the Fire﴾ [Al 'Imran 10]. But do we testify that every disbeliever is in the Fire? No. Do we testify that a specific disbeliever, by name, is in the Fire? The answer is no. Rather, we testify in a general sense and say: every disbeliever is in the Fire, just as we say: every believer is in Paradise, but we do not testify for any specific individual that he is in Paradise. So there is a difference between the general and the particular.
And in the verse there is also the affirmation of the Fire, based on His saying: ﴿the fuel of the Fire﴾ (...).
* * *
* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed. ﴿Like the custom of the people of Pharaoh and those before them, who denied Our signs, so Allah seized them for their sins; and Allah is severe in punishment. (11) Say to those who disbelieve: "You will be overcome and gathered into Hell, and wretched is the resting place." (12) There has already been a sign for you in the two armies that met: one fighting in the way of Allah, and another disbelieving, seeing them twice their number by sight. And Allah strengthens with His victory whom He wills. Indeed in that is a lesson for those of vision. (13) Beautified for people is the love of desires: women, sons, heaped-up piles of gold and silver, branded horses, cattle, and tilth. That is the enjoyment of the worldly life, and with Allah is the best return﴾ [Al 'Imran 11–14].
* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from Satan the accursed. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve—neither their wealth nor their children will avail them at all against Allah﴾. His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve—neither their wealth nor their children will avail them at all against Allah﴾. Is what is meant by "those who disbelieve" a specific people, or is it general?
* Student: General.
* Shaykh: Rather, general.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: And he has wealth and children, so these wealth and children—?
* Student: Will not avail him against Allah at all.
* Shaykh: Is the negation of availing here in this world or in the Hereafter?
* Student: In the Hereafter.
* Shaykh: And in this world?
* Student: It is possible that they avail them in this world.
* Shaykh: Against Allah?
* Student: No, against people.
* Shaykh: I want to say: they will not avail them against Allah.
* Student: In the Hereafter they will not avail them.
* Shaykh: And in this world?
* Student: Against Allah?
* Shaykh: Yes indeed.
* Student: They do not avail them.
* Shaykh: Are you certain?
* Student: Not avail them, certainly.
* Shaykh: Neither in this world nor in the Hereafter. Do you agree with this? Yes. "Will not avail them against Allah at all," based on the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And when Allah intends harm for a people, there is no turning it away﴾ [Ar-Ra'd 11]. His saying: ﴿And those are the fuel of the Fire.﴾ "Fuel of the Fire" means that by which it is kindled, i.e., they are the ones with whom the Fire is kindled. Does anyone share with them in that?
* Student: No one shares with them in it except those who disbelieved in His messengers.
* Shaykh: They are the disbelievers, yes.
* Student: The hypocrites.
* Shaykh: The hypocrites are disbelievers.
* Student: Or the Jews?
* Shaykh: No, no.
* Student: The stones.
* Shaykh: The stones, ﴿its fuel is people and stones﴾. His saying: ﴿like the custom of the people of Pharaoh﴾, what does it mean?
* Student: It means like the people of Pharaoh.
* Shaykh: The word "da'b" means what?
* Student: Like the people.
* Shaykh: It means ﴿like the custom of the people of Pharaoh﴾, i.e., like the example of the people of Pharaoh?
* Student: Like their habit and their condition.
* Shaykh: Like their habit and their condition. And what is the i'rab (grammatical analysis) position of this phrase, or this word?
* Student: Its i'rab position?
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: That is, (da'b) is a subject, (the people of Pharaoh) is the predicate.
* Shaykh: No, no.
* Student: The da'b (...) like it.
* Shaykh: No.
* Student: This is not its i'rab.
* Shaykh: No, that is not its i'rab.
* Student: (Ka-da'b) is a prepositional phrase functioning as a fronted predicate.
* Shaykh: A fronted predicate of what?
* Student: Of an implied subject.
* Shaykh: A fronted predicate of an implied subject? A fronted predicate, as long as the subject is implied, you have the choice (...) you put it after (...) you put it before. So now you are saying: a predicate of an implied subject, delayed such-and-such?
* Student: I retracted from the delayed one.
* Shaykh: You retracted from the delayed one? So, a predicate of an implied subject, and the implied element is?
* Student: The implied element: their custom.
* Shaykh: Their custom is like the custom of the people of Pharaoh. What is meant by "the people of Pharaoh" here?
* Student: Pharaoh?
* Shaykh: "The people of Pharaoh."
* Student: Pharaoh himself and those who followed him, or those among his people who disbelieved.
* Shaykh: Those who followed him. Why do we not say: those who followed him?
* Student: Those among his people who disbelieved, or those who followed him.
* Shaykh: Those who followed him. That is, he and his followers. ﴿Those before them﴾, like whom?
* Student: Like the people of Noah.
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: And 'Ad.
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: And Thamud.
* Shaykh: Yes, and the people of Abraham, the people of Lot, and the companions of Madyan, many. The clause: ﴿they denied Our signs﴾, ﴿they denied Our signs, so Allah seized them﴾, what is its i'rab position?
* Student: A resumptive explanatory clause.
* Shaykh: Yes, a resumptive clause explaining this custom. What is meant by "signs" here?
* Student: The cosmic and the legislated.
* Shaykh: And the legislated. How can one deny legislated signs?
* Student: They denied what Moses brought.
* Shaykh: Yes, or their messengers, because He says: ﴿and those before them﴾.
* Student: The messengers all, what their messengers brought.
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: And likewise regarding the cosmic signs.
* Shaykh: Regarding the cosmic signs, they denied them either by attributing them to other than Allah, or by claiming that Allah has a partner in them or a helper. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿so Allah seized them for their sins﴾. The letter "ba'" (in bi-dhunubihim) means what?
* Student: The "ba'" here is causal.
* Shaykh: The "ba'" here is causal: Allah seized them because of their sins. And is there another meaning that is valid?
* Student: Exchange.
* Shaykh: Exchange. That is, their recompense is of the same kind as their deeds and in exchange for them. ﴿And Allah is severe in punishment.﴾ Let us now take the benefits.
* Among the benefits of these verses, first, the first verse: that disbelievers may be provided with wealth and children.
* Student: We have taken it.
* Shaykh: You have taken it?
* Student: Yes.
* Shaykh: * Among the benefits of the noble verse: ﴿like the custom of the people of Pharaoh and those before them﴾, which is the second verse. * Among its benefits: that later disbelievers are like earlier disbelievers, because Allah's way with creation is one, since He, the Mighty and Majestic, has no kinship with creation that He observes and favors toward whoever is connected to Him. People are equal before Allah, the Exalted; the most noble of them before Allah is the most pious, based on His saying: ﴿like the custom of the people of Pharaoh﴾, to the end.
* And among the benefits of the noble verse: that Pharaoh and his household were punished in this world, just as they will be punished in the Hereafter, based on His saying: ﴿so Allah seized them for their sins﴾.
* And among its benefits: the refutation of those who claim that Pharaoh became Muslim and that his Islam benefited him, because Allah, the Exalted, mentioned that in the manner of censure and punishment. Had he been a penitent whose repentance would benefit him, his sin would not have been mentioned without mention of his repentance, since Allah, the Exalted, is just and does not mention anyone for a sin from which he repented unless He clarifies his repentance. Adam, peace be upon him, when he ate from the tree and what happened to him occurred, and he repented to Allah: ﴿Then Adam received from his Lord words, and He accepted his repentance﴾ [Al-Baqarah 37]. Allah mentioned his disobedience and mentioned that he repented, and mentioned that after repentance he was better than he was before it: ﴿Then his Lord chose him, and accepted his repentance and guided him﴾ [Ta-Ha 122].
* And among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of the signs (ayat) of Allah, which are the indicators pointing to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to His existence, and to what these signs contain of His attributes. For example, the descent of mercy and the descent of rain is a sign of mercy, a sign of Allah's mercy, of His existence and His mercy. The descent of punishments is a sign of Allah's existence and of His wrath. And so every sign that indicates the existence of Allah, glorified and exalted, and what that sign requires of attributes, whether it is a sign of mercy or a sign of punishment.
* And among the benefits of the noble verse: that Allah does not wrong people at all, but rather seizes them for their sins, ﴿so Allah seized them for their sins﴾. A parallel to this is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And whatever affliction strikes you is because of what your hands have earned, and He pardons much﴾ [Ash-Shura 30].
* And among the benefits of the noble verse: the refutation of the Jabriyya (the determinist sect) who do not attribute the act of the servant to him, based on His saying: ﴿for their sins﴾, where He attributed the sins to them. An act is attributed only to the one who truly performs it, while the Jabriyya say that an act is not attributed to a human in the true sense.
* And among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of the attribute of severity of punishment for Allah, based on His saying: ﴿And Allah is severe in punishment﴾.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verse 12–13 (part 1 of 3):

Then He, Exalted is He, says: ﴿Say to those who disbelieve: "You will be overcome and gathered to Hell, and wretched is the resting place."﴾ The address "Say" (qul) is to the Prophet (ﷺ). Know that the address directed to the Prophet (ﷺ) is sometimes inclusive of him and the Ummah by the explicit text accompanying that address, sometimes specific to him, and sometimes general to him and the Ummah by virtue of his being the imam (leader) of the Ummah. That is, there is no wording in the address that indicates generality, but because he is the imam of the Ummah, the address is directed to him, and its ruling includes him and the Ummah. An example of the first is the address directed to the Prophet (ﷺ) accompanied by something that indicates it is general to him and the Ummah, the words of the Exalted: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them at their prescribed time﴾ [at-Talaq 1]. He said, "O Prophet," then He said, "when you (plural) divorce," and did not say "when you (singular) divorce." This indicates that this address is directed to him and his Ummah. An example of the general address that has no accompanying text indicating its generality is that most of the addresses directed to the Messenger (peace be upon him) are of this category, such as this verse: ﴿Say to those who disbelieve﴾, which includes him and the Ummah; even we say to those who disbelieve: "You will be overcome and gathered to Hell." The third example is the words of the Exalted: ﴿Did We not expand for you your breast?﴾ [ash-Sharh 1], ﴿Did He not find you an orphan and give you shelter?﴾ [ad-Duha 6]; this is specific to the Messenger (peace be upon him).

God, Exalted is He, says: ﴿Say to those who﴾, meaning: say, O Muhammad, and his Ummah also says this to the disbelievers, following him and emulating him. Say to them: ﴿You will be overcome and gathered﴾. In another reading (a canonical reading): ﴿They will be overcome and gathered﴾. ﴿You will be overcome﴾: by whom will they be overcome? They will be overcome by the believers, as God, Exalted is He, says: ﴿Honour belongs to God, His Messenger, and the believers﴾ [al-Munafiqun 8], and God, Exalted is He, says: ﴿God has decreed: "I and My messengers will surely prevail. Indeed, God is Strong and Mighty"﴾ [al-Mujadila 21]. But which believer will prevail? The believer who prevails is the one who truly believed and performed righteous deeds; faith is not merely the statement of the tongue. ﴿And among the people are those who say, "We believe in God and the Last Day," but they are not believers﴾ [al-Baqarah 8]. There must be sincere faith attested by action, so that it is righteous. And God, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Indeed, We will surely support Our messengers and those who believe in the worldly life and on the Day when the witnesses stand﴾ [Ghafir 51]. So those who believed with true faith, confirmed by action, will certainly prevail without doubt; they will overcome the disbelievers.

But if someone says: What do you say about the Islamic Ummah today, which is overpowered, and the disbelievers subjugate it to utmost humiliation and fight it from every direction with every kind of weapon? Our answer is: I say about the Islamic Ummah that what applies to each individual among them applies to the masses: they have from Islam only its name, and from the Qur'an only its outward form. For this reason you find one of them venerating the Qur'an in a manner that transgresses the limits of the Shari'ah, yet it is a merely formal veneration: he kisses the Qur'an, loves it, and places it on his forehead, but he acts upon what is in it only rarely. He may even do that while associating partners with God, calling upon other than God. Where is acting by the Qur'an? There is no acting by the Qur'an. If you look carefully at the Muslim world today, you will find that it does not truly represent Islam. You will find in worship many kinds of shirk, with the dead and the living; you will find many kinds of innovation in belief and in practice; you will find many kinds of breaking covenants, treachery, deceit, lying and cheating. So where is Islam? It is nothing but its name. Therefore we have not overcome those who disbelieve; rather, those who disbelieve have overcome us in reality, and they are the ones who hold dominance now, dominance over the world economically, politically and militarily. Yes.

So if someone asks: how does this verse hold true, or how does its meaning apply, in light of what we see today? The answer: we have not been truthful to God so that victory might be ours. ﴿But if they had been truthful to God, it would have been better for them﴾ [Muhammad 21]. Yes.

﴿You will be overcome and gathered to Hell﴾: in this world you will be overcome; in the Hereafter you will be gathered to Hell, and we seek refuge with God, they will be assembled toward it, enter it and abide in it forever. So these disbelievers will have lost both this world and the Hereafter: they lost this world by being overcome and humbled, and they lost the Hereafter by being gathered to Hell. This is like the words of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth to avert [people] from the way of God. They will spend it; then it will become for them a regret; then they will be overcome. And those who disbelieve will be gathered to Hell﴾ [al-Anfal 36]. This verse is a parallel to this verse.

His words: ﴿and wretched is the resting place﴾: this is a disparagement of the Fire, and we seek refuge with God, that it is a wretched resting place, meaning a wretched bed that a person prepares for himself, like one who lays out his bedding and wraps himself in his covering. ﴿They will have above them layers of Fire and below them layers﴾ [az-Zumar 16]; we seek refuge with God. ﴿On the Day the punishment will cover them from above them and from beneath their feet, and it will be said: "Taste what you used to do"﴾ [al-'Ankabut 55]. ﴿For them from Hell is a bed, and above them are coverings﴾ [al-A'raf 41], meaning: something that envelops and covers them of the punishment. So they, we seek refuge with God, are in a state that a person cannot imagine because of its magnitude and severity, and they abide in it forever.

﴿There has already been for you a sign in two companies that met﴾. The words ﴿there has already been﴾ may be part of the statement that preceded, in His words: ﴿Say to those who disbelieve: "You will be overcome and gathered to Hell, and wretched is the resting place. There has already been for you﴾, so it is part of what is said, meaning: say to them, take heed by an example I set forth for you. ﴿There has been for you a sign﴾, that is, a indication that you will be overcome, because "ayah" in the language means a sign: a sign that you will be overcome. ﴿In two companies that met﴾, meaning, for battle between them, and "fi'ah" means a group.

Is the meaning of the two companies two real, actual groups, or is it by way of example? Most of the exegetes hold that they are two real groups in an actual matter. Some exegetes said that this is by way of illustration, meaning: let us suppose that there are two groups in this manner, one group fighting in the way of God and another disbelieving.

If we say they are two groups in an actual event, then those who hold this view say: the intended two are the group of disbelievers and the group of believers at Badr. They are two groups: one fighting in the way of God, namely the Prophet (ﷺ) and those with him, and another disbelieving group fighting in the way of the Taghut, as God, Exalted is He, says: ﴿Those who believe fight in the way of God, and those who disbelieve fight in the way of Taghut﴾ [an-Nisa' 76]. God is greatest. ﴿So fight against the allies of Satan﴾: to whom is the address? To the believers. ﴿So fight against the allies of Satan; indeed, the plot of Satan is ever weak﴾ [an-Nisa' 76]. Glory be to God: if we took this verse and we, being truly believers, fought in the way of God, these people would be before us like moths, but the matter is as you know.

His words: ﴿a sign in two companies﴾, meaning: two groups of people, ﴿that met﴾, meaning some of them encountered others. ﴿One company fighting in the way of God﴾: ﴿one company﴾ is the subject (mubtada'), and ﴿fighting﴾ is its predicate. It is permissible for the subject to be indefinite because it is for division (taqsim), and it has already been mentioned that when there is a division, it is permissible to begin with an indefinite noun. Among that is the poet's verse:

One day is against us, and one day for us,
And one day we are troubled, and one day we are gladdened.

So he began with the indefinite for the sake of division. Here he said: ﴿one company fighting﴾, beginning with the indefinite because the context is one of division. ﴿Fighting in the way of God﴾: ﴿in the way of God﴾ means in His path. Fighting in the way of God includes several matters. First: sincerity of intention for God. Second: that it conform to the command of God. Third: that the prohibitions of God be avoided in it. For this reason the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever fights so that the word of God is the highest, he is in the way of God." [Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (123) and Muslim (1904/149) from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari.]

The first: that it be intended for the Face of God, and that His word be the highest. This is sincerity. A person does not intend by his fighting to seize control of the world, to own the earth, to take booty and to enslave the offspring. If he intends this, then his fighting is not in the way of God.

The second: that the fighting be within the limits of His Shari'ah, such that there is no aggression against anyone. If there is aggression against anyone in it, then it is not in the way of God.

An example: that there be a covenant between us and the polytheists, and then we break it and fight. This is forbidden, and this fighting is not in the way of God; rather it is disobedience to God, Mighty and Majestic, because God, Exalted is He, said: ﴿So as long as they remain upright toward you, remain upright toward them﴾ [at-Tawbah 7]. He forbade us to fight during a covenant, and said: ﴿And if you fear from a people treachery, then throw back to them [their treaty] on equal terms﴾ [al-Anfal 58]. That is, even if you have made a covenant with a people of the disbelievers and fear that they will betray it, it is not permissible for you to break the covenant; rather, ﴿throw back to them on equal terms﴾, meaning: tell them, "There is no covenant between us and you," ﴿on equal terms﴾, until you are (...) on equal terms, meaning with knowledge that the covenant has been annulled. As for fighting while the covenant stands, this is not in the way of God.

The third matter: that you avoid in it what? The prohibitions of God. If you do not avoid the prohibitions of God in it, then although its origin is in the way of God, victory and triumph will not be realized in it, as evidenced by what befell the Muslims at the Battle of Uhud. At the beginning of the day in the Battle of Uhud, the matter was in the hands of the Muslims and the upper hand was theirs, but they disobeyed the Messenger (peace be upon him) and were forsaken, so the reversal came upon the polytheists. God, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Until, when you lost courage and disputed about the matter and disobeyed after He had shown you what you love﴾ [Al 'Imran 152]; meaning, defeat occurred. ﴿Among you are those who desire this world, and among you are those who desire the Hereafter. Then He turned you away from them﴾ [Al 'Imran 152]. God is greatest! God, Exalted is He, turned the Muslims away from them so that they did not fight them. ﴿That He might test you; and He has already pardoned you﴾ [Al 'Imran 152]. Observe that after this rebuke and reproach, from which whoever comes after them takes warning, He said after it: ﴿And He has already pardoned you.﴾ And if we did as they did, could we be sure that God would pardon us? No. But the Companions, may God pardon them, were pardoned, and what they did became as though it had not been. The point is that we say: in the way of God there must be conditions; there must be conditions. What do you say about a people who fight for nationalism: is that in the way of God? It is not in the way of God. For this reason the Prophet (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who fights out of bravery, a man who fights out of zeal, and a man who fights to be seen in his place: which of these is in the way of God? He said: "Whoever fights so that the word of God is the highest, he is in the way of God." [Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (123) and Muslim (1904/149) from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari.] That is, all of these are not in the way of God. The man who fights out of bravery is brave, and the brave person loves to fight, because bravery and boldness are part of his nature, so he loves this. The second fights out of zeal and affection for his people, and the third fights out of showing off and reputation, so that his place may be seen. Which of these is in the way of God? He said: "Whoever fights so that the word of God is the highest, he is in the way of God."

The other company is disbelieving. God, Mighty and Majestic, did not say "fighting in the way of such-and-such." This is from the device of mentioning one attribute and omitting the other. In the first He said: ﴿one company fighting﴾ and did not say "a believing company fighting in the way of God," and in the second He said: ﴿and another disbelieving﴾ and did not say "fighting in the way of Taghut." So from the first He omitted what corresponds to what was mentioned in the second, namely "believing," whose counterpart is "disbelieving," and from the second He omitted the opposite of what was mentioned in the first, so He omitted "in the way of Taghut," while in the first "in the way of God" was mentioned. This is from the device of mentioning one of two attributes in place of the other, and it is a form of concise eloquence. He said: ﴿and another disbelieving﴾, meaning: fighting in the way of Taghut.

﴿They see them as twice their number with their own eyes﴾. In a canonical reading: ﴿You see them as twice your number with your own eyes﴾. Here we consider who the seer is: are they the fighters in the way of God, or the disbelievers? The fact is the pronoun suits both, but ﴿You see them as twice your number with your own eyes﴾ clearly refers to the disbelievers: you see the fighters, the company fighting in the way of God, as twice the disbelievers, but it is only a vision and not real. ﴿When God showed them to you in your dream as few; and had He shown them to you as many, you would have lost courage and disputed about the matter; but God saved [you]. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts﴾ [al-Anfal 43]. ﴿And when He showed them to you, when you met, as few in your eyes and made you appear few in their eyes, that God might accomplish a matter already destined﴾ [al-Anfal 44].

﴿They see them as twice their number with their own eyes﴾, meaning they observe with their eyes that they are twice their number, whether they are believers or disbelievers. If they are believers who see the disbelievers as twice their number, then it is clear that the small company is the believing one. If the disbelievers see them as twice their number with their own eyes, there is a difficulty: if the disbelievers see the believers with their own eyes as twice their number, then the victory goes to whom?

* Student: To the believers.

* The Shaykh: Yes, but (...). The victory goes to the greater number. But they said: their seeing them as twice their number is by way of God's showing them so, even though in reality it was less than that, if in reality it was less than that.

In any case, the closer view is that the seers are the believing group, and the two multiples are the disbelieving group. That is, the believing group sees the disbelieving group as twice their number, and realizes that these disbelievers reach double their own number. Two times the number: if the believers are one hundred, the disbelievers would be two hundred.

If we say this verse concerns an actual event, which is the day of Badr, then a great difficulty arises regarding His words ﴿twice their number﴾. Why? Because the number of the believers at Badr was three hundred and some odd men, and the number of the disbelievers was between nine hundred and a thousand. Are nine hundred or a thousand twice three hundred and some odd men? Yes, roughly three times, three times or more. So some scholars held that they saw them as twice their number, though in reality they were more.

Other scholars held that the intended meaning of "twice" here is "more," and they took the meaning of His words ﴿they see them as twice their number﴾ to be: they see them as more than themselves. This is if we say that the verse concerns an actual event, which is the event of Badr.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verses 12–13 (part 2 of 3):

As for if we say that it is a parable (ḍarb mathal), is there a difficulty in it or not? There is no difficulty in it, if we say that it is of the type of parable, and that when the believers are half of the disbelievers, they will overcome them. This is what matches the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Now Allah has lightened your burden, and He knows that among you is weakness. So if there are among you one hundred steadfast, they will overcome two hundred; and if there are among you one thousand, they will overcome two thousand﴾ [al-Anfal 66]. Here, a group overcomes twice its number. Is that not so? A group of one hundred overcomes two hundred, and a thousand overcomes two thousand.

Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿They see them twice their number with their own eyes﴾. ﴿With their own eyes﴾ (ra'y al-'ayn) is an emphatic infinitive (maṣdar mu'akkid) for the verb: ﴿they see them﴾ or ﴿tara-wnahum﴾ (you see them), if we take the seeing to be what? Visual. If we take it to be cognitive, meaning they know them to be twice their number with certainty (ra'y al-'ayn), then it is also a case of emphasis of meaning (at-tawkid al-ma'nawi), meaning they know them with certain knowledge as if they were seeing them with their own eyes.

﴿And Allah supports with His victory whom He wills﴾. ﴿Yu'ayyid﴾ means "strengthens." The ba' here is the ba' of means (ba' al-wasilah), meaning: He strengthens by means of His victory whom He wills. I have said that the ba' of means is like when one says: "I slaughtered with the knife," and "I struck with the stick." So victory is the means of support, and He, the Mighty and Majestic, strengthens by His victory whom He wills. ﴿Whom He wills﴾ means whom wisdom requires to be given victory, or whom wisdom requires to be strengthened. We must restrict every verse that comes with the wording of will (mashī'ah), or that is linked to will, by wisdom, due to the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And you will not will except that Allah wills. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾ [al-Insan 30].

﴿And Allah supports with His victory whom He wills. Indeed in that is a lesson for those who have vision﴾. ﴿In that﴾ refers to what has preceded of the mention of this matter. That is, indeed in what has been mentioned is a lesson ('ibrah), meaning a consideration (i'tibar). And i'tibar is crossing over from one thing to another, derived from crossing over from one thing to another. It is as if a person crosses over with his mind from what is mentioned to what is understood. Here, a story has been related to us, and we take from it a lesson: by what? That a small group overcomes a large group. In this there is confirmation of the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Say to those who disbelieve, "You will be overcome"﴾. So when the disbelievers boast of their numbers, we say to them: your numbers will not avail you anything. This is a group fighting in the cause of Allah, and another that is disbelieving, and yet victory went to whom? To the one fighting in the cause of Allah.

﴿Indeed in that is a lesson for those who have vision﴾. "Al-abṣār" (vision) is the plural of "baṣar," like "asbāb" is the plural of "sabab." But what is meant here by "al-abṣār"? Is it the vision of physical sight, or the vision of the mind, or does it include both? It includes both, since they see them with their own eyes, so there is a lesson in it for those who have vision, meaning those who saw with their eyes. Likewise it is a lesson for those who have vision with their minds, with their intellects, even if they did not see it with their own eyes, because when they hear of it, they take heed. When they hear, they take heed, so in that there is a lesson for them.

* Student: Does it not apply to the Muslims today that they are "like the foam of the torrent" (ghuthā' ka-ghuthā' as-sayl)?
* Shaykh: Yes, indeed. It applies to the Muslims today that they are like the foam of the torrent, because the nations have gathered against them as diners gather around their dish.

* Student: ﴿A group fighting in the cause of Allah﴾. This group represents every (...), and this is from the perspective of (...). Likewise, in terms of eloquence (balāghah), if you remove one of the two descriptions, the other description is lost.
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: It is possible (...) a group.
* Shaykh: He says that it is permissible to make ﴿a group fighting in the cause of Allah﴾ the predicate of an omitted subject, the estimate being: "one of them is a group fighting." This is correct. What he mentioned is one of the possible grammatical analyses (i'rab) of the verse, meaning it is permissible to make ﴿a group﴾ the predicate of an omitted subject whose estimate is "one of them." However, the scholars have established a rule: if the speech can be understood without estimating an omission, that is preferable. We studied this previously in what? In grammar (nahw) and also in the principles of jurisprudence (uṣūl al-fiqh): that speech is to be understood without omission whenever possible.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: No, no. If you say: "A people sell and a people rent out," this is a division. These are divided into this, and those into that.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: Is this a disparagement (qadh)?
* Shaykh: Yes, yes, it is a disparagement of their resting place (mihād).
* Student: In Hell...
* Shaykh: In the resting place, yes.
* Student: (...), three categories. Then we said: it may be specific to the Prophet ﷺ, and we gave the example of the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Did We not expand for you your breast?﴾ [ash-Sharh 1]. (Did We not expand for you your breast?) This is general; does every individual, when he is guided, have his breast expanded for Islam?
* Shaykh: No, because this interrogative is for affirmation (taqrir). ﴿And We raised for you your mention﴾ [ash-Sharh 4], ﴿And We removed from you your burden﴾ [ash-Sharh 2]. This is specific to the Messenger.

* Student: What is the position regarding a mujahid who fights alongside people who disobey Allah, whether it is a disobedience that does not take one out of the religion, or some acts of disobedience that take them out of the religion, such as acts of shirk?
* Shaykh: In any case, these people do not deserve victory. Those who disobey Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, do not deserve victory, because disobedience is a cause of abandonment. However, they may be given victory because of the oppression of their adversary. Sometimes a wrongdoer is given victory over another wrongdoer in order to humiliate the second, as Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And thus We make some of the wrongdoers allies of others for what they used to earn﴾ [al-An'am 129]. So the victory of the Jews, for example, over the people of Palestine is of this type. Otherwise, the people of Palestine are more deserving of victory than the Jews if they are Muslims, since the Muslim is more deserving of victory than the disbeliever. But a Muslim may have many acts of disobedience which necessitate that he be humiliated by the disbeliever.

We say: this is the secret of prostration (sujud): complete servitude to Allah and humility before Him. For this reason, the reward of the one who prostrates is that he is nearest to his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, because he humbled himself before Allah and lowered himself, so Allah raised him and he became nearest to his Lord. It has been related in a hadith: "Allah has forbidden the Fire to consume the limbs of prostration," concerning those among the sinning believers who enter the Fire. This is because the sinning believers, if Allah does not forgive them and they have no good deeds that outweigh their bad deeds, will be punished in the Fire in proportion to their sins. But the limbs of prostration are held in honor; the Fire does not consume them and does not affect them. For this reason, one of them said:

O Lord, You have freed the limbs of prostration
By Your abundant grace, and You are the Everlasting.
And freedom ... so bestow upon the perishing
Freedom from the Everlasting.

Meaning: he seeks means to Allah through the freeing of these limbs, until the freedom spreads to the entire body. The author, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "Even if there is a barrier, that is not one of the limbs of prostration." He said: "He keeps his forearms away from his sides (yujāfī 'adadayhi 'an janbayhi)." Yujāfī: who is the subject? The praying person who prostrates keeps his forearms away from his sides, meaning he distances them.

* * *

* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿Say to those who disbelieve, "You will be overcome and gathered to Hell, and wretched is the resting place." There has already been for you a sign in the two armies which met: one fighting in the cause of Allah and another disbelieving, seeing them twice their number with their own eyes. And Allah supports with His victory whom He wills. Indeed in that is a lesson for those who have vision. Adorned for people is the love of that which they desire: of women and sons and heaped-up sums of gold and silver and branded horses and cattle and tillage. That is the enjoyment of the worldly life, but Allah has with Him the best return﴾ [Al 'Imran 12–14].
* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Say to those who disbelieve, "You will be overcome and gathered to Hell, and wretched is the resting place."﴾ This verse begins with "Say," which indicates that Allah commanded His Messenger ﷺ to convey it to the disbelievers. What does the prefacing of some rulings or reports with "Say" convey? That is, that Allah commands His Prophet ﷺ with a specific command to convey this matter: what does that indicate?
* Student: It indicates its importance.
* Shaykh: Its importance, and that he was commanded to convey it with a specific command, although the Messenger ﷺ was commanded to convey the entire Qur'an. But this indicates that it is given special attention, like: ﴿Say to My servants who have believed: establish prayer﴾ [Ibrahim 31], ﴿Say to the believing men that they should lower their gaze﴾ [an-Nur 30]. Examples of this are many.

As for His saying: ﴿You will be overcome﴾, there are two recitations.
* Student: ﴿Sa-tughlabūn﴾.
* Shaykh: Yes, and ﴿sa-yughlabūn﴾. His saying: ﴿and gathered to Hell﴾.
* Student: ﴿Tuḥsharūn﴾ and ﴿yuḥsharūn﴾.
* Shaykh: And ﴿yuḥsharūn﴾. And what is the meaning of ḥashr (gathering)?
* Student: Collecting.
* Shaykh: Collecting. His saying: ﴿There has already been for you a sign in two armies﴾: a sign of what? Yes, a sign, meaning an indication, but of what?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Of the fact that they will be overcome, that the disbeliever is defeated. What is meant by "two armies" in His saying ﴿fi'atayn﴾?
* Student: According to the author's view that...
* Shaykh: We have no author here; this is the Qur'an.
* Student: Some exegetes said it is the battle of Badr.
* Shaykh: Yes, it is a reference to the Battle of Badr, and this is what the majority hold. And some scholars said what?
* Student: Something else.
* Shaykh: Example, example. The meaning of "sign" (āyah) includes the people of Badr and others. If we say they are the people of Badr, that it refers to the people of Badr, how do we reconcile the reality with His saying: ﴿They see them twice their number with their own eyes﴾?
* Student: "Twice their number" means that the abundance was taken into account (...).
* Shaykh: Mere increase, and that does not indicate duality, like His saying: ﴿Then return the vision twice﴾ [al-Mulk 4]. We say: what is meant by "two times" is an increase, regardless of whether it is one time and one time, because it is well known that the Muslims at Badr were three hundred and some odd men, and the polytheists were between nine hundred and a thousand. Is there another opinion?
* Student: "Twice their number" means more than them.
* Shaykh: This has been said.
* Student: That is, even though they were more than you, they see them as twice your number.
* Shaykh: ﴿They see them twice their number﴾, meaning they were made to appear few in their eyes. And what confirms this? What confirms it?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: No, we want it from the Qur'an.
* Student: (...) Allah, when you met, in their eyes, but He made them appear few in your eyes.
* Shaykh: Yes: ﴿And when He showed them to you when you met in your eyes as few﴾. And why did He specify "twice" when in the verse of al-Anfal He said only ﴿few﴾?
* Student: Because of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Now Allah has lightened your burden, and He knows that among you is weakness. So if there are among you one hundred steadfast, they will overcome two hundred; and if there are among you one thousand, they will overcome two thousand﴾ [al-Anfal 66].
* Shaykh: Correct. Allah showed them (...) twice their number, because the believer must endure against two, the believers must endure against twice their number, so they were shown twice their number. These are two opinions.

There is a third opinion that I came across today: that what is meant by "twice" (mithlayn) is "two times" (ḍi'fayn). According to this, it matches the reality, because "the doubling of a thing" means its multiplication twice. So if it is two times, it becomes its multiplication three times. The polytheists were between nine hundred and a thousand, and the Muslims were three hundred and some odd men.

His saying: ﴿They see them twice their number with their own eyes﴾. Who is the subject? Who is the subject of ﴿they see them twice their number﴾?
* Student: The believers.
* Shaykh: The believers. And the object?
* Student: What do you mean?
* Shaykh: ﴿They see them﴾.
* Student: The polytheists.
* Shaykh: Yes, it refers to the disbelievers, meaning the believers see the disbelievers. The pronoun in ﴿mithlayhim﴾ (twice their number) refers to whom?
* Student: To the believers.
* Shaykh: To the believers, meaning the believers see the disbelievers as twice the number of the believers. There is a reading here.
* Student: In ("tarawna")?
* Shaykh: In ﴿yarawnahum﴾.
* Student: In the reading "tarawna."
* Shaykh: ﴿Tarawnahum﴾. On this basis, the address in His saying ﴿tarawnahum﴾ would refer to the believers, or refer to the disbelievers based on the referent of ("lakum") in ﴿there has already been for you a sign﴾.

In His saying: ﴿a group fighting in the cause of Allah and another disbelieving﴾, there is what is known as the omission of one of two contrasting terms because the other indicates it by contrast.
* Student: The omission of the believers: ﴿a group fighting in the cause of Allah﴾.
* Shaykh: And what was omitted from it?
* Student: The counterpart.
* Shaykh: And what is the counterpart?
* Student: The believers. The omission of the counterpart of those who fight in the cause of the false deity (ṭāghūt).
* Shaykh: No.
* Student: The omission of the disbelievers and polytheists, the omission of the believers.
* Shaykh: And what is the estimate?
* Student: A group of believers and another disbelieving.
* Shaykh: The estimate is: a believing group fighting in the cause of Allah, and another disbelieving group fighting in the cause of the false deity. For the disbelievers, He mentioned "disbelieving" (kāfirah) and said ﴿another disbelieving﴾, but He did not mention what they fight for. For the believers, He mentioned what they fight for but did not mention the description of faith. So if someone says: what is the evidence for this division that you have mentioned?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: The saying of Allah: ﴿Those who believe...﴾.
* Student: ﴿Those who believe fight in the cause of Allah, and those who disbelieve fight in the cause of the false deity﴾ [an-Nisa' 76].
* Shaykh: Yes, correct. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And Allah supports with His victory whom He wills﴾. Is the will (mashī'ah) in the phrase ﴿whom He wills﴾ unrestricted?
* Student: Restricted.
* Shaykh: Restricted, by what? By wisdom. Every text linked to will is restricted by wisdom. What is your evidence?
* Student: ﴿And you will not will except that Allah wills. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾ [al-Insan 30].
* Shaykh: ﴿And you will not will except that Allah wills. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.﴾ This is evidence that the will of Allah follows His knowledge and wisdom. And His saying: ﴿Indeed in that is a lesson for those who have vision﴾. What is the lesson?
* Student: The lesson is admonition.
* Shaykh: Admonition. Its linguistic root is what one crosses over from one thing to another. From it comes the "ʿabbārah" among people, which is a ferry that carries water from one side to another. A person crosses from this state to that state. And who takes a lesson?
* Student: Those who have vision.
* Shaykh: Is the vision with the eye or the vision of the heart?
* Student: The vision of the heart.
* Shaykh: The heart? What is your evidence?
* Student: ﴿Indeed in that is a lesson for one who fears﴾ [an-Nazi'at 26]. The one who fears is the heart.
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: ﴿For indeed, it is not eyes that are blinded, but blinded are the hearts which are within the breasts﴾ [al-Hajj 46].
* Shaykh: Yes, ﴿For indeed, it is not eyes that are blinded, but blinded are the hearts which are within the breasts.﴾

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Say to those who disbelieve, "You will be overcome and gathered to Hell, and wretched is the resting place."﴾ In this verse: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is a servant to whom commands are directed, as shown by His saying ﴿Say﴾. He is a servant who is not worshipped and a messenger who is not denied.

It also contains: the importance of this command or this report which Allah commanded His Prophet to convey to the disbelievers.

* Among its benefits also: strengthening the believers, since it is said to their enemies, the disbelievers: "You will be overcome in this world, and you will have no outcome in the Hereafter, for you will be gathered to Hell."

* Among its benefits also: instilling terror in the disbelievers and warning them, by His saying: ﴿You will be overcome and gathered to Hell﴾.

* Among the benefits of the verse is also that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, combines two punishments for the disbelievers: the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter. The punishment of this world is in His saying: ﴿You will be overcome﴾, even if they spend large amounts of wealth. ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth to averter from the way of Allah; so they will spend it, then it will become a regret for them; then they will be overcome﴾. The second punishment is His saying: ﴿And you will be gathered to Hell﴾. As for the believer, when Allah punishes him in this world, He does not punish him in the Hereafter; Allah will not combine two punishments for him. ﴿And whatever affliction strikes you is because of what your hands have earned, and He pardons much﴾.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse is good news for us in this era: if we were truthful to Allah, the Exalted, with faith, the disbelievers would be overcome. ﴿Say to those who disbelieve: You will be overcome﴾. And who overcomes? ﴿Allah has decreed: Indeed I and My messengers will prevail﴾, and ﴿Indeed, We will help Our messengers and those who believe in the worldly life﴾. So if we returned truly to faith in belief, speech, action, morals, manners, and everything related to the Islamic Sharia, the disbelievers would be overcome before us. This reality that occurred in the early generations of this Ummah confirms this, when they ruled the eastern and western parts of the earth.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of the punishment of the Fire, based on His saying: ﴿And you will be gathered to Hell﴾. This is established by the Book, the Sunnah, and the consensus of the Muslims, and whoever denies it has disbelieved.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that sin is ruinous, and indeed the ultimate end of sin is the Fire, based on His saying: ﴿And wretched is the resting place﴾.

As for His saying: ﴿There has already been for you a sign in two armies that met﴾, among its benefits: the coining of parables with actual events, because that is more eloquent in conveying conviction and tranquility. It follows from this that the preacher and the caller to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, should present examples to those he addresses from actual events, because that is more eloquent. For instance, if he wants to call to abandoning evil deeds and performing obligations, he says: Look at such-and-such city, which was called, not long ago, the flower of the Middle East, and everyone who sought pleasure from the Middle East, from Europe, and from elsewhere would go to this city, because he would find the utmost of pleasure. It has now become rivers flowing with blood; Allah has sent their violence among them until they fled from their homes. Instead of their city exceeding a million, it now has only two hundred thousand and some change; that is, more than three-quarters of the city's people have gone because of trials and calamities. So when you present this actual example to those whom you warn against falling into luxury and thus perishing, it becomes a lesson. This is why Allah struck this example with His saying: ﴿There has already been for you a sign in two armies that met﴾.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that however truthful a person may be, the presentation of actual events makes his speech the certainty of truth (ḥaqq al-yaqīn). The levels, as we have previously mentioned, are three: knowledge of certainty (ʿilm al-yaqīn), eye of certainty (ʿayn al-yaqīn), and truth of certainty (ḥaqq al-yaqīn). Knowledge of certainty is the report of the truthful; eye of certainty is what you see with your eye directly; and truth of certainty is what you perceive with your senses. So if someone says to you: "This is an apple," or "I have an apple, in my pocket there is an apple," and he is a truthful man, how do you know that an apple exists? You know it through knowledge of certainty. If he takes it out and you look at it, this is eye of certainty. If you eat it, this is truth of certainty, because that is the reality. So we say: a person, however much trust people place in him, should present examples to people so that they become convinced of his words; for we do not doubt that the truest speech is the speech of Allah, and Allah, the Exalted, has said: ﴿Say to those who disbelieve: You will be overcome﴾, and then He struck a real example that the disbelievers were defeated although they were more numerous than the believers.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that victory is not by the abundance of numbers nor the strength of equipment, but it is from Allah; because when Allah struck this example He said: ﴿And Allah supports with His help whom He wills﴾. But if it is asked: what is the real means to the victory of Allah by which support comes? The answer is what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, mentioned in His saying: ﴿Allah has promised those of you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will surely grant them succession upon the earth, as He granted succession to those before them, and that He will surely establish for them their religion which He has approved for them, and that He will surely substitute for them, after their fear, security﴾ [an-Nur 55]. Up to this point the cause of victory has not yet come; He said: ﴿They worship Me, not associating anything with Me﴾ [an-Nur 55]. This is one: sincerity of worship to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is one of the causes of victory. There are also other causes mentioned by Allah in His saying: ﴿And Allah will surely support those who support Him. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Mighty. [They are] those who, if We establish them in the land, establish prayer, give zakah, enjoin what is right, and forbid what is wrong﴾ [al-Hajj 40–41].

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that fighting is not a cause of victory except if it is for the sake of Allah. For the sake of Allah, with sincerity, and what else?

* The students: Conformity with the Sharia.

* The Shaykh: And following the Sharia, conformity with the Sharia.

* The students: And avoiding the prohibitions.

* The Shaykh: And avoiding the prohibitions. When these three matters are fulfilled: sincerity, that it conforms to the Sharia, and that one avoids the prohibitions and sins in it, then this is what is "in the way of Allah."

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that there is no harmony between believers and disbelievers, based on His saying: ﴿One company fighting in the way of Allah and another disbelieving﴾. Whoever tries to unite believers and disbelievers has tried to combine fire and water, and this is impossible. It is not possible for the friends of Allah to be in harmony with the enemies of Allah, and whoever tries to reconcile the friends of Allah with the enemies of Allah, it means he will end up eliminating the allegiance to Allah; based on the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿O you who believe, do not take the Jews and Christians as allies; they are allies of one another. And whoever is an ally to them among you is [one] of them. Indeed, Allah guides not the wrongdoing people﴾ [al-Ma'idah 51]. And how can a person who says he is among the friends of Allah and believes in Allah be allied with the enemies of Allah, the disbelievers in Allah? This is not possible. This is why we find that the conflict between the followers of the messengers and the enemies of the messengers is constant and ongoing, either by speech or by action; by speech: ﴿If they overcome you, they will be to you enemies and extend against you their hands and tongues with evil﴾ [al-Mumtahanah 2], and either by armed conflict as is well known.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that Allah, the Exalted, may show the fighters the matter as it is, or contrary to its reality, for a wisdom, as the verse of al-Anfal bears witness: ﴿And [remember] when He showed them to you as few when you met them, and He made you few in their eyes﴾; because when a person sees his enemy as few, he becomes energized to fight, and when he sees him as many, he becomes discouraged. So Allah, glorified and exalted, showed the believers the disbelievers as few, and showed the disbelievers the believers as few, so that each one would advance to fight.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of the act, or the affirmation of the acts of Allah, based on His saying: ﴿And Allah supports with His help whom He wills﴾.

* Among its benefits also: a refutation of the Jabriyyah (determinists), in His saying: ﴿fighting in the way of Allah﴾, where He attributed the act to them. The Jabriyyah say that the act is not attributed to the agent except figuratively, as you say: "The fire consumed the firewood," whereas in truth a person does not act by his own choice but is compelled to his action.

* Among the benefits of the verse: the affirmation of Allah's will, based on His saying: ﴿whom He wills﴾.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that only people of insight take heed of matters, based on His saying: ﴿Indeed in that is a lesson for those of insight﴾.

* Among its benefits: if you find in yourself a lack of taking heed and admonition from what occurs, know that you are weak in insight, because when Allah affirms the lesson for those of insight, the absence of the lesson indicates weakness of insight or its total absence.

* Among the benefits of the verse: praise of people of insight, because the context is one of praise, so it contains praise of people of insight and condemnation of the blind of heart.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verse 12–13 (part 1 of 3):

Then He, Exalted is He, says: ﴿Say to those who disbelieve: "You will be overcome and gathered to Hell, and wretched is the resting place."﴾ The address "Say" (qul) is to the Prophet (ﷺ). Know that the address directed to the Prophet (ﷺ) is sometimes inclusive of him and the Ummah by the explicit text accompanying that address, sometimes specific to him, and sometimes general to him and the Ummah by virtue of his being the imam (leader) of the Ummah. That is, there is no wording in the address that indicates generality, but because he is the imam of the Ummah, the address is directed to him, and its ruling includes him and the Ummah. An example of the first is the address directed to the Prophet (ﷺ) accompanied by something that indicates it is general to him and the Ummah, the words of the Exalted: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them at their prescribed time﴾ [at-Talaq 1]. He said, "O Prophet," then He said, "when you (plural) divorce," and did not say "when you (singular) divorce." This indicates that this address is directed to him and his Ummah. An example of the general address that has no accompanying text indicating its generality is that most of the addresses directed to the Messenger (peace be upon him) are of this category, such as this verse: ﴿Say to those who disbelieve﴾, which includes him and the Ummah; even we say to those who disbelieve: "You will be overcome and gathered to Hell." The third example is the words of the Exalted: ﴿Did We not expand for you your breast?﴾ [ash-Sharh 1], ﴿Did He not find you an orphan and give you shelter?﴾ [ad-Duha 6]; this is specific to the Messenger (peace be upon him).

God, Exalted is He, says: ﴿Say to those who﴾, meaning: say, O Muhammad, and his Ummah also says this to the disbelievers, following him and emulating him. Say to them: ﴿You will be overcome and gathered﴾. In another reading (a canonical reading): ﴿They will be overcome and gathered﴾. ﴿You will be overcome﴾: by whom will they be overcome? They will be overcome by the believers, as God, Exalted is He, says: ﴿Honour belongs to God, His Messenger, and the believers﴾ [al-Munafiqun 8], and God, Exalted is He, says: ﴿God has decreed: "I and My messengers will surely prevail. Indeed, God is Strong and Mighty"﴾ [al-Mujadila 21]. But which believer will prevail? The believer who prevails is the one who truly believed and performed righteous deeds; faith is not merely the statement of the tongue. ﴿And among the people are those who say, "We believe in God and the Last Day," but they are not believers﴾ [al-Baqarah 8]. There must be sincere faith attested by action, so that it is righteous. And God, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Indeed, We will surely support Our messengers and those who believe in the worldly life and on the Day when the witnesses stand﴾ [Ghafir 51]. So those who believed with true faith, confirmed by action, will certainly prevail without doubt; they will overcome the disbelievers.

But if someone says: What do you say about the Islamic Ummah today, which is overpowered, and the disbelievers subjugate it to utmost humiliation and fight it from every direction with every kind of weapon? Our answer is: I say about the Islamic Ummah that what applies to each individual among them applies to the masses: they have from Islam only its name, and from the Qur'an only its outward form. For this reason you find one of them venerating the Qur'an in a manner that transgresses the limits of the Shari'ah, yet it is a merely formal veneration: he kisses the Qur'an, loves it, and places it on his forehead, but he acts upon what is in it only rarely. He may even do that while associating partners with God, calling upon other than God. Where is acting by the Qur'an? There is no acting by the Qur'an. If you look carefully at the Muslim world today, you will find that it does not truly represent Islam. You will find in worship many kinds of shirk, with the dead and the living; you will find many kinds of innovation in belief and in practice; you will find many kinds of breaking covenants, treachery, deceit, lying and cheating. So where is Islam? It is nothing but its name. Therefore we have not overcome those who disbelieve; rather, those who disbelieve have overcome us in reality, and they are the ones who hold dominance now, dominance over the world economically, politically and militarily. Yes.

So if someone asks: how does this verse hold true, or how does its meaning apply, in light of what we see today? The answer: we have not been truthful to God so that victory might be ours. ﴿But if they had been truthful to God, it would have been better for them﴾ [Muhammad 21]. Yes.

﴿You will be overcome and gathered to Hell﴾: in this world you will be overcome; in the Hereafter you will be gathered to Hell, and we seek refuge with God, they will be assembled toward it, enter it and abide in it forever. So these disbelievers will have lost both this world and the Hereafter: they lost this world by being overcome and humbled, and they lost the Hereafter by being gathered to Hell. This is like the words of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth to avert [people] from the way of God. They will spend it; then it will become for them a regret; then they will be overcome. And those who disbelieve will be gathered to Hell﴾ [al-Anfal 36]. This verse is a parallel to this verse.

His words: ﴿and wretched is the resting place﴾: this is a disparagement of the Fire, and we seek refuge with God, that it is a wretched resting place, meaning a wretched bed that a person prepares for himself, like one who lays out his bedding and wraps himself in his covering. ﴿They will have above them layers of Fire and below them layers﴾ [az-Zumar 16]; we seek refuge with God. ﴿On the Day the punishment will cover them from above them and from beneath their feet, and it will be said: "Taste what you used to do"﴾ [al-'Ankabut 55]. ﴿For them from Hell is a bed, and above them are coverings﴾ [al-A'raf 41], meaning: something that envelops and covers them of the punishment. So they, we seek refuge with God, are in a state that a person cannot imagine because of its magnitude and severity, and they abide in it forever.

﴿There has already been for you a sign in two companies that met﴾. The words ﴿there has already been﴾ may be part of the statement that preceded, in His words: ﴿Say to those who disbelieve: "You will be overcome and gathered to Hell, and wretched is the resting place. There has already been for you﴾, so it is part of what is said, meaning: say to them, take heed by an example I set forth for you. ﴿There has been for you a sign﴾, that is, a indication that you will be overcome, because "ayah" in the language means a sign: a sign that you will be overcome. ﴿In two companies that met﴾, meaning, for battle between them, and "fi'ah" means a group.

Is the meaning of the two companies two real, actual groups, or is it by way of example? Most of the exegetes hold that they are two real groups in an actual matter. Some exegetes said that this is by way of illustration, meaning: let us suppose that there are two groups in this manner, one group fighting in the way of God and another disbelieving.

If we say they are two groups in an actual event, then those who hold this view say: the intended two are the group of disbelievers and the group of believers at Badr. They are two groups: one fighting in the way of God, namely the Prophet (ﷺ) and those with him, and another disbelieving group fighting in the way of the Taghut, as God, Exalted is He, says: ﴿Those who believe fight in the way of God, and those who disbelieve fight in the way of Taghut﴾ [an-Nisa' 76]. God is greatest. ﴿So fight against the allies of Satan﴾: to whom is the address? To the believers. ﴿So fight against the allies of Satan; indeed, the plot of Satan is ever weak﴾ [an-Nisa' 76]. Glory be to God: if we took this verse and we, being truly believers, fought in the way of God, these people would be before us like moths, but the matter is as you know.

His words: ﴿a sign in two companies﴾, meaning: two groups of people, ﴿that met﴾, meaning some of them encountered others. ﴿One company fighting in the way of God﴾: ﴿one company﴾ is the subject (mubtada'), and ﴿fighting﴾ is its predicate. It is permissible for the subject to be indefinite because it is for division (taqsim), and it has already been mentioned that when there is a division, it is permissible to begin with an indefinite noun. Among that is the poet's verse:

One day is against us, and one day for us,
And one day we are troubled, and one day we are gladdened.

So he began with the indefinite for the sake of division. Here he said: ﴿one company fighting﴾, beginning with the indefinite because the context is one of division. ﴿Fighting in the way of God﴾: ﴿in the way of God﴾ means in His path. Fighting in the way of God includes several matters. First: sincerity of intention for God. Second: that it conform to the command of God. Third: that the prohibitions of God be avoided in it. For this reason the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever fights so that the word of God is the highest, he is in the way of God." [Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (123) and Muslim (1904/149) from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari.]

The first: that it be intended for the Face of God, and that His word be the highest. This is sincerity. A person does not intend by his fighting to seize control of the world, to own the earth, to take booty and to enslave the offspring. If he intends this, then his fighting is not in the way of God.

The second: that the fighting be within the limits of His Shari'ah, such that there is no aggression against anyone. If there is aggression against anyone in it, then it is not in the way of God.

An example: that there be a covenant between us and the polytheists, and then we break it and fight. This is forbidden, and this fighting is not in the way of God; rather it is disobedience to God, Mighty and Majestic, because God, Exalted is He, said: ﴿So as long as they remain upright toward you, remain upright toward them﴾ [at-Tawbah 7]. He forbade us to fight during a covenant, and said: ﴿And if you fear from a people treachery, then throw back to them [their treaty] on equal terms﴾ [al-Anfal 58]. That is, even if you have made a covenant with a people of the disbelievers and fear that they will betray it, it is not permissible for you to break the covenant; rather, ﴿throw back to them on equal terms﴾, meaning: tell them, "There is no covenant between us and you," ﴿on equal terms﴾, until you are (...) on equal terms, meaning with knowledge that the covenant has been annulled. As for fighting while the covenant stands, this is not in the way of God.

The third matter: that you avoid in it what? The prohibitions of God. If you do not avoid the prohibitions of God in it, then although its origin is in the way of God, victory and triumph will not be realized in it, as evidenced by what befell the Muslims at the Battle of Uhud. At the beginning of the day in the Battle of Uhud, the matter was in the hands of the Muslims and the upper hand was theirs, but they disobeyed the Messenger (peace be upon him) and were forsaken, so the reversal came upon the polytheists. God, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Until, when you lost courage and disputed about the matter and disobeyed after He had shown you what you love﴾ [Al 'Imran 152]; meaning, defeat occurred. ﴿Among you are those who desire this world, and among you are those who desire the Hereafter. Then He turned you away from them﴾ [Al 'Imran 152]. God is greatest! God, Exalted is He, turned the Muslims away from them so that they did not fight them. ﴿That He might test you; and He has already pardoned you﴾ [Al 'Imran 152]. Observe that after this rebuke and reproach, from which whoever comes after them takes warning, He said after it: ﴿And He has already pardoned you.﴾ And if we did as they did, could we be sure that God would pardon us? No. But the Companions, may God pardon them, were pardoned, and what they did became as though it had not been. The point is that we say: in the way of God there must be conditions; there must be conditions. What do you say about a people who fight for nationalism: is that in the way of God? It is not in the way of God. For this reason the Prophet (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who fights out of bravery, a man who fights out of zeal, and a man who fights to be seen in his place: which of these is in the way of God? He said: "Whoever fights so that the word of God is the highest, he is in the way of God." [Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (123) and Muslim (1904/149) from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari.] That is, all of these are not in the way of God. The man who fights out of bravery is brave, and the brave person loves to fight, because bravery and boldness are part of his nature, so he loves this. The second fights out of zeal and affection for his people, and the third fights out of showing off and reputation, so that his place may be seen. Which of these is in the way of God? He said: "Whoever fights so that the word of God is the highest, he is in the way of God."

The other company is disbelieving. God, Mighty and Majestic, did not say "fighting in the way of such-and-such." This is from the device of mentioning one attribute and omitting the other.
