In the first He said: ﴿one company fighting﴾ and did not say "a believing company fighting in the way of God," and in the second He said: ﴿and another disbelieving﴾ and did not say "fighting in the way of Taghut." So from the first He omitted what corresponds to what was mentioned in the second, namely "believing," whose counterpart is "disbelieving," and from the second He omitted the opposite of what was mentioned in the first, so He omitted "in the way of Taghut," while in the first "in the way of God" was mentioned. This is from the device of mentioning one of two attributes in place of the other, and it is a form of concise eloquence. He said: ﴿and another disbelieving﴾, meaning: fighting in the way of Taghut.

﴿They see them as twice their number with their own eyes﴾. In a canonical reading: ﴿You see them as twice your number with your own eyes﴾. Here we consider who the seer is: are they the fighters in the way of God, or the disbelievers? The fact is the pronoun suits both, but ﴿You see them as twice your number with your own eyes﴾ clearly refers to the disbelievers: you see the fighters, the company fighting in the way of God, as twice the disbelievers, but it is only a vision and not real. ﴿When God showed them to you in your dream as few; and had He shown them to you as many, you would have lost courage and disputed about the matter; but God saved [you]. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts﴾ [al-Anfal 43]. ﴿And when He showed them to you, when you met, as few in your eyes and made you appear few in their eyes, that God might accomplish a matter already destined﴾ [al-Anfal 44].

﴿They see them as twice their number with their own eyes﴾, meaning they observe with their eyes that they are twice their number, whether they are believers or disbelievers. If they are believers who see the disbelievers as twice their number, then it is clear that the small company is the believing one. If the disbelievers see them as twice their number with their own eyes, there is a difficulty: if the disbelievers see the believers with their own eyes as twice their number, then the victory goes to whom?

* Student: To the believers.

* The Shaykh: Yes, but (...). The victory goes to the greater number. But they said: their seeing them as twice their number is by way of God's showing them so, even though in reality it was less than that, if in reality it was less than that.

In any case, the closer view is that the seers are the believing group, and the two multiples are the disbelieving group. That is, the believing group sees the disbelieving group as twice their number, and realizes that these disbelievers reach double their own number. Two times the number: if the believers are one hundred, the disbelievers would be two hundred.

If we say this verse concerns an actual event, which is the day of Badr, then a great difficulty arises regarding His words ﴿twice their number﴾. Why? Because the number of the believers at Badr was three hundred and some odd men, and the number of the disbelievers was between nine hundred and a thousand. Are nine hundred or a thousand twice three hundred and some odd men? Yes, roughly three times, three times or more. So some scholars held that they saw them as twice their number, though in reality they were more.

Other scholars held that the intended meaning of "twice" here is "more," and they took the meaning of His words ﴿they see them as twice their number﴾ to be: they see them as more than themselves. This is if we say that the verse concerns an actual event, which is the event of Badr.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verses 12–13 (part 2 of 3):

As for if we say that it is a parable (ḍarb mathal), is there a difficulty in it or not? There is no difficulty in it, if we say that it is of the type of parable, and that when the believers are half of the disbelievers, they will overcome them. This is what matches the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Now Allah has lightened your burden, and He knows that among you is weakness. So if there are among you one hundred steadfast, they will overcome two hundred; and if there are among you one thousand, they will overcome two thousand﴾ [al-Anfal 66]. Here, a group overcomes twice its number. Is that not so? A group of one hundred overcomes two hundred, and a thousand overcomes two thousand.

Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿They see them twice their number with their own eyes﴾. ﴿With their own eyes﴾ (ra'y al-'ayn) is an emphatic infinitive (maṣdar mu'akkid) for the verb: ﴿they see them﴾ or ﴿tara-wnahum﴾ (you see them), if we take the seeing to be what? Visual. If we take it to be cognitive, meaning they know them to be twice their number with certainty (ra'y al-'ayn), then it is also a case of emphasis of meaning (at-tawkid al-ma'nawi), meaning they know them with certain knowledge as if they were seeing them with their own eyes.

﴿And Allah supports with His victory whom He wills﴾. ﴿Yu'ayyid﴾ means "strengthens." The ba' here is the ba' of means (ba' al-wasilah), meaning: He strengthens by means of His victory whom He wills. I have said that the ba' of means is like when one says: "I slaughtered with the knife," and "I struck with the stick." So victory is the means of support, and He, the Mighty and Majestic, strengthens by His victory whom He wills. ﴿Whom He wills﴾ means whom wisdom requires to be given victory, or whom wisdom requires to be strengthened. We must restrict every verse that comes with the wording of will (mashī'ah), or that is linked to will, by wisdom, due to the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And you will not will except that Allah wills. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾ [al-Insan 30].

﴿And Allah supports with His victory whom He wills. Indeed in that is a lesson for those who have vision﴾. ﴿In that﴾ refers to what has preceded of the mention of this matter. That is, indeed in what has been mentioned is a lesson ('ibrah), meaning a consideration (i'tibar). And i'tibar is crossing over from one thing to another, derived from crossing over from one thing to another. It is as if a person crosses over with his mind from what is mentioned to what is understood. Here, a story has been related to us, and we take from it a lesson: by what? That a small group overcomes a large group. In this there is confirmation of the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Say to those who disbelieve, "You will be overcome"﴾. So when the disbelievers boast of their numbers, we say to them: your numbers will not avail you anything. This is a group fighting in the cause of Allah, and another that is disbelieving, and yet victory went to whom? To the one fighting in the cause of Allah.

﴿Indeed in that is a lesson for those who have vision﴾. "Al-abṣār" (vision) is the plural of "baṣar," like "asbāb" is the plural of "sabab." But what is meant here by "al-abṣār"? Is it the vision of physical sight, or the vision of the mind, or does it include both? It includes both, since they see them with their own eyes, so there is a lesson in it for those who have vision, meaning those who saw with their eyes. Likewise it is a lesson for those who have vision with their minds, with their intellects, even if they did not see it with their own eyes, because when they hear of it, they take heed. When they hear, they take heed, so in that there is a lesson for them.

* Student: Does it not apply to the Muslims today that they are "like the foam of the torrent" (ghuthā' ka-ghuthā' as-sayl)?
* Shaykh: Yes, indeed. It applies to the Muslims today that they are like the foam of the torrent, because the nations have gathered against them as diners gather around their dish.

* Student: ﴿A group fighting in the cause of Allah﴾. This group represents every (...), and this is from the perspective of (...). Likewise, in terms of eloquence (balāghah), if you remove one of the two descriptions, the other description is lost.
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: It is possible (...) a group.
* Shaykh: He says that it is permissible to make ﴿a group fighting in the cause of Allah﴾ the predicate of an omitted subject, the estimate being: "one of them is a group fighting." This is correct. What he mentioned is one of the possible grammatical analyses (i'rab) of the verse, meaning it is permissible to make ﴿a group﴾ the predicate of an omitted subject whose estimate is "one of them." However, the scholars have established a rule: if the speech can be understood without estimating an omission, that is preferable. We studied this previously in what? In grammar (nahw) and also in the principles of jurisprudence (uṣūl al-fiqh): that speech is to be understood without omission whenever possible.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: No, no. If you say: "A people sell and a people rent out," this is a division. These are divided into this, and those into that.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: Is this a disparagement (qadh)?
* Shaykh: Yes, yes, it is a disparagement of their resting place (mihād).
* Student: In Hell...
* Shaykh: In the resting place, yes.
* Student: (...), three categories. Then we said: it may be specific to the Prophet ﷺ, and we gave the example of the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Did We not expand for you your breast?﴾ [ash-Sharh 1]. (Did We not expand for you your breast?) This is general; does every individual, when he is guided, have his breast expanded for Islam?
* Shaykh: No, because this interrogative is for affirmation (taqrir). ﴿And We raised for you your mention﴾ [ash-Sharh 4], ﴿And We removed from you your burden﴾ [ash-Sharh 2]. This is specific to the Messenger.

* Student: What is the position regarding a mujahid who fights alongside people who disobey Allah, whether it is a disobedience that does not take one out of the religion, or some acts of disobedience that take them out of the religion, such as acts of shirk?
* Shaykh: In any case, these people do not deserve victory. Those who disobey Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, do not deserve victory, because disobedience is a cause of abandonment. However, they may be given victory because of the oppression of their adversary. Sometimes a wrongdoer is given victory over another wrongdoer in order to humiliate the second, as Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And thus We make some of the wrongdoers allies of others for what they used to earn﴾ [al-An'am 129]. So the victory of the Jews, for example, over the people of Palestine is of this type. Otherwise, the people of Palestine are more deserving of victory than the Jews if they are Muslims, since the Muslim is more deserving of victory than the disbeliever. But a Muslim may have many acts of disobedience which necessitate that he be humiliated by the disbeliever.

We say: this is the secret of prostration (sujud): complete servitude to Allah and humility before Him. For this reason, the reward of the one who prostrates is that he is nearest to his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, because he humbled himself before Allah and lowered himself, so Allah raised him and he became nearest to his Lord. It has been related in a hadith: "Allah has forbidden the Fire to consume the limbs of prostration," concerning those among the sinning believers who enter the Fire. This is because the sinning believers, if Allah does not forgive them and they have no good deeds that outweigh their bad deeds, will be punished in the Fire in proportion to their sins. But the limbs of prostration are held in honor; the Fire does not consume them and does not affect them. For this reason, one of them said:

O Lord, You have freed the limbs of prostration
By Your abundant grace, and You are the Everlasting.
And freedom ... so bestow upon the perishing
Freedom from the Everlasting.

Meaning: he seeks means to Allah through the freeing of these limbs, until the freedom spreads to the entire body. The author, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "Even if there is a barrier, that is not one of the limbs of prostration." He said: "He keeps his forearms away from his sides (yujāfī 'adadayhi 'an janbayhi)." Yujāfī: who is the subject? The praying person who prostrates keeps his forearms away from his sides, meaning he distances them.

* * *

* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿Say to those who disbelieve, "You will be overcome and gathered to Hell, and wretched is the resting place." There has already been for you a sign in the two armies which met: one fighting in the cause of Allah and another disbelieving, seeing them twice their number with their own eyes. And Allah supports with His victory whom He wills. Indeed in that is a lesson for those who have vision. Adorned for people is the love of that which they desire: of women and sons and heaped-up sums of gold and silver and branded horses and cattle and tillage. That is the enjoyment of the worldly life, but Allah has with Him the best return﴾ [Al 'Imran 12–14].
* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Say to those who disbelieve, "You will be overcome and gathered to Hell, and wretched is the resting place."﴾ This verse begins with "Say," which indicates that Allah commanded His Messenger ﷺ to convey it to the disbelievers. What does the prefacing of some rulings or reports with "Say" convey? That is, that Allah commands His Prophet ﷺ with a specific command to convey this matter: what does that indicate?
* Student: It indicates its importance.
* Shaykh: Its importance, and that he was commanded to convey it with a specific command, although the Messenger ﷺ was commanded to convey the entire Qur'an. But this indicates that it is given special attention, like: ﴿Say to My servants who have believed: establish prayer﴾ [Ibrahim 31], ﴿Say to the believing men that they should lower their gaze﴾ [an-Nur 30]. Examples of this are many.

As for His saying: ﴿You will be overcome﴾, there are two recitations.
* Student: ﴿Sa-tughlabūn﴾.
* Shaykh: Yes, and ﴿sa-yughlabūn﴾. His saying: ﴿and gathered to Hell﴾.
* Student: ﴿Tuḥsharūn﴾ and ﴿yuḥsharūn﴾.
* Shaykh: And ﴿yuḥsharūn﴾. And what is the meaning of ḥashr (gathering)?
* Student: Collecting.
* Shaykh: Collecting. His saying: ﴿There has already been for you a sign in two armies﴾: a sign of what? Yes, a sign, meaning an indication, but of what?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Of the fact that they will be overcome, that the disbeliever is defeated. What is meant by "two armies" in His saying ﴿fi'atayn﴾?
* Student: According to the author's view that...
* Shaykh: We have no author here; this is the Qur'an.
* Student: Some exegetes said it is the battle of Badr.
* Shaykh: Yes, it is a reference to the Battle of Badr, and this is what the majority hold. And some scholars said what?
* Student: Something else.
* Shaykh: Example, example. The meaning of "sign" (āyah) includes the people of Badr and others. If we say they are the people of Badr, that it refers to the people of Badr, how do we reconcile the reality with His saying: ﴿They see them twice their number with their own eyes﴾?
* Student: "Twice their number" means that the abundance was taken into account (...).
* Shaykh: Mere increase, and that does not indicate duality, like His saying: ﴿Then return the vision twice﴾ [al-Mulk 4]. We say: what is meant by "two times" is an increase, regardless of whether it is one time and one time, because it is well known that the Muslims at Badr were three hundred and some odd men, and the polytheists were between nine hundred and a thousand. Is there another opinion?
* Student: "Twice their number" means more than them.
* Shaykh: This has been said.
* Student: That is, even though they were more than you, they see them as twice your number.
* Shaykh: ﴿They see them twice their number﴾, meaning they were made to appear few in their eyes. And what confirms this? What confirms it?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: No, we want it from the Qur'an.
* Student: (...) Allah, when you met, in their eyes, but He made them appear few in your eyes.
* Shaykh: Yes: ﴿And when He showed them to you when you met in your eyes as few﴾. And why did He specify "twice" when in the verse of al-Anfal He said only ﴿few﴾?
* Student: Because of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Now Allah has lightened your burden, and He knows that among you is weakness. So if there are among you one hundred steadfast, they will overcome two hundred; and if there are among you one thousand, they will overcome two thousand﴾ [al-Anfal 66].
* Shaykh: Correct. Allah showed them (...) twice their number, because the believer must endure against two, the believers must endure against twice their number, so they were shown twice their number. These are two opinions.

There is a third opinion that I came across today: that what is meant by "twice" (mithlayn) is "two times" (ḍi'fayn). According to this, it matches the reality, because "the doubling of a thing" means its multiplication twice. So if it is two times, it becomes its multiplication three times. The polytheists were between nine hundred and a thousand, and the Muslims were three hundred and some odd men.

His saying: ﴿They see them twice their number with their own eyes﴾. Who is the subject? Who is the subject of ﴿they see them twice their number﴾?
* Student: The believers.
* Shaykh: The believers. And the object?
* Student: What do you mean?
* Shaykh: ﴿They see them﴾.
* Student: The polytheists.
* Shaykh: Yes, it refers to the disbelievers, meaning the believers see the disbelievers. The pronoun in ﴿mithlayhim﴾ (twice their number) refers to whom?
* Student: To the believers.
* Shaykh: To the believers, meaning the believers see the disbelievers as twice the number of the believers. There is a reading here.
* Student: In ("tarawna")?
* Shaykh: In ﴿yarawnahum﴾.
* Student: In the reading "tarawna."
* Shaykh: ﴿Tarawnahum﴾. On this basis, the address in His saying ﴿tarawnahum﴾ would refer to the believers, or refer to the disbelievers based on the referent of ("lakum") in ﴿there has already been for you a sign﴾.

In His saying: ﴿a group fighting in the cause of Allah and another disbelieving﴾, there is what is known as the omission of one of two contrasting terms because the other indicates it by contrast.
* Student: The omission of the believers: ﴿a group fighting in the cause of Allah﴾.
* Shaykh: And what was omitted from it?
* Student: The counterpart.
* Shaykh: And what is the counterpart?
* Student: The believers. The omission of the counterpart of those who fight in the cause of the false deity (ṭāghūt).
* Shaykh: No.
* Student: The omission of the disbelievers and polytheists, the omission of the believers.
* Shaykh: And what is the estimate?
* Student: A group of believers and another disbelieving.
* Shaykh: The estimate is: a believing group fighting in the cause of Allah, and another disbelieving group fighting in the cause of the false deity. For the disbelievers, He mentioned "disbelieving" (kāfirah) and said ﴿another disbelieving﴾, but He did not mention what they fight for. For the believers, He mentioned what they fight for but did not mention the description of faith. So if someone says: what is the evidence for this division that you have mentioned?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: The saying of Allah: ﴿Those who believe...﴾.
* Student: ﴿Those who believe fight in the cause of Allah, and those who disbelieve fight in the cause of the false deity﴾ [an-Nisa' 76].
* Shaykh: Yes, correct. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And Allah supports with His victory whom He wills﴾. Is the will (mashī'ah) in the phrase ﴿whom He wills﴾ unrestricted?
* Student: Restricted.
* Shaykh: Restricted, by what? By wisdom. Every text linked to will is restricted by wisdom. What is your evidence?
* Student: ﴿And you will not will except that Allah wills. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾ [al-Insan 30].
* Shaykh: ﴿And you will not will except that Allah wills. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.﴾ This is evidence that the will of Allah follows His knowledge and wisdom. And His saying: ﴿Indeed in that is a lesson for those who have vision﴾. What is the lesson?
* Student: The lesson is admonition.
* Shaykh: Admonition. Its linguistic root is what one crosses over from one thing to another. From it comes the "ʿabbārah" among people, which is a ferry that carries water from one side to another. A person crosses from this state to that state. And who takes a lesson?
* Student: Those who have vision.
* Shaykh: Is the vision with the eye or the vision of the heart?
* Student: The vision of the heart.
* Shaykh: The heart? What is your evidence?
* Student: ﴿Indeed in that is a lesson for one who fears﴾ [an-Nazi'at 26]. The one who fears is the heart.
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: ﴿For indeed, it is not eyes that are blinded, but blinded are the hearts which are within the breasts﴾ [al-Hajj 46].
* Shaykh: Yes, ﴿For indeed, it is not eyes that are blinded, but blinded are the hearts which are within the breasts.﴾

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Say to those who disbelieve, "You will be overcome and gathered to Hell, and wretched is the resting place."﴾ In this verse: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is a servant to whom commands are directed, as shown by His saying ﴿Say﴾. He is a servant who is not worshipped and a messenger who is not denied.

It also contains: the importance of this command or this report which Allah commanded His Prophet to convey to the disbelievers.

* Among its benefits also: strengthening the believers, since it is said to their enemies, the disbelievers: "You will be overcome in this world, and you will have no outcome in the Hereafter, for you will be gathered to Hell."

* Among its benefits also: instilling terror in the disbelievers and warning them, by His saying: ﴿You will be overcome and gathered to Hell﴾.

* Among the benefits of the verse is also that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, combines two punishments for the disbelievers: the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter. The punishment of this world is in His saying: ﴿You will be overcome﴾, even if they spend large amounts of wealth. ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth to averter from the way of Allah; so they will spend it, then it will become a regret for them; then they will be overcome﴾. The second punishment is His saying: ﴿And you will be gathered to Hell﴾. As for the believer, when Allah punishes him in this world, He does not punish him in the Hereafter; Allah will not combine two punishments for him. ﴿And whatever affliction strikes you is because of what your hands have earned, and He pardons much﴾.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse is good news for us in this era: if we were truthful to Allah, the Exalted, with faith, the disbelievers would be overcome. ﴿Say to those who disbelieve: You will be overcome﴾. And who overcomes? ﴿Allah has decreed: Indeed I and My messengers will prevail﴾, and ﴿Indeed, We will help Our messengers and those who believe in the worldly life﴾. So if we returned truly to faith in belief, speech, action, morals, manners, and everything related to the Islamic Sharia, the disbelievers would be overcome before us. This reality that occurred in the early generations of this Ummah confirms this, when they ruled the eastern and western parts of the earth.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of the punishment of the Fire, based on His saying: ﴿And you will be gathered to Hell﴾. This is established by the Book, the Sunnah, and the consensus of the Muslims, and whoever denies it has disbelieved.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that sin is ruinous, and indeed the ultimate end of sin is the Fire, based on His saying: ﴿And wretched is the resting place﴾.

As for His saying: ﴿There has already been for you a sign in two armies that met﴾, among its benefits: the coining of parables with actual events, because that is more eloquent in conveying conviction and tranquility. It follows from this that the preacher and the caller to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, should present examples to those he addresses from actual events, because that is more eloquent. For instance, if he wants to call to abandoning evil deeds and performing obligations, he says: Look at such-and-such city, which was called, not long ago, the flower of the Middle East, and everyone who sought pleasure from the Middle East, from Europe, and from elsewhere would go to this city, because he would find the utmost of pleasure. It has now become rivers flowing with blood; Allah has sent their violence among them until they fled from their homes. Instead of their city exceeding a million, it now has only two hundred thousand and some change; that is, more than three-quarters of the city's people have gone because of trials and calamities. So when you present this actual example to those whom you warn against falling into luxury and thus perishing, it becomes a lesson. This is why Allah struck this example with His saying: ﴿There has already been for you a sign in two armies that met﴾.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that however truthful a person may be, the presentation of actual events makes his speech the certainty of truth (ḥaqq al-yaqīn). The levels, as we have previously mentioned, are three: knowledge of certainty (ʿilm al-yaqīn), eye of certainty (ʿayn al-yaqīn), and truth of certainty (ḥaqq al-yaqīn). Knowledge of certainty is the report of the truthful; eye of certainty is what you see with your eye directly; and truth of certainty is what you perceive with your senses. So if someone says to you: "This is an apple," or "I have an apple, in my pocket there is an apple," and he is a truthful man, how do you know that an apple exists? You know it through knowledge of certainty. If he takes it out and you look at it, this is eye of certainty. If you eat it, this is truth of certainty, because that is the reality. So we say: a person, however much trust people place in him, should present examples to people so that they become convinced of his words; for we do not doubt that the truest speech is the speech of Allah, and Allah, the Exalted, has said: ﴿Say to those who disbelieve: You will be overcome﴾, and then He struck a real example that the disbelievers were defeated although they were more numerous than the believers.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that victory is not by the abundance of numbers nor the strength of equipment, but it is from Allah; because when Allah struck this example He said: ﴿And Allah supports with His help whom He wills﴾. But if it is asked: what is the real means to the victory of Allah by which support comes? The answer is what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, mentioned in His saying: ﴿Allah has promised those of you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will surely grant them succession upon the earth, as He granted succession to those before them, and that He will surely establish for them their religion which He has approved for them, and that He will surely substitute for them, after their fear, security﴾ [an-Nur 55]. Up to this point the cause of victory has not yet come; He said: ﴿They worship Me, not associating anything with Me﴾ [an-Nur 55]. This is one: sincerity of worship to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is one of the causes of victory. There are also other causes mentioned by Allah in His saying: ﴿And Allah will surely support those who support Him. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Mighty. [They are] those who, if We establish them in the land, establish prayer, give zakah, enjoin what is right, and forbid what is wrong﴾ [al-Hajj 40–41].

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that fighting is not a cause of victory except if it is for the sake of Allah. For the sake of Allah, with sincerity, and what else?

* The students: Conformity with the Sharia.

* The Shaykh: And following the Sharia, conformity with the Sharia.

* The students: And avoiding the prohibitions.

* The Shaykh: And avoiding the prohibitions. When these three matters are fulfilled: sincerity, that it conforms to the Sharia, and that one avoids the prohibitions and sins in it, then this is what is "in the way of Allah."

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that there is no harmony between believers and disbelievers, based on His saying: ﴿One company fighting in the way of Allah and another disbelieving﴾. Whoever tries to unite believers and disbelievers has tried to combine fire and water, and this is impossible. It is not possible for the friends of Allah to be in harmony with the enemies of Allah, and whoever tries to reconcile the friends of Allah with the enemies of Allah, it means he will end up eliminating the allegiance to Allah; based on the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿O you who believe, do not take the Jews and Christians as allies; they are allies of one another. And whoever is an ally to them among you is [one] of them. Indeed, Allah guides not the wrongdoing people﴾ [al-Ma'idah 51]. And how can a person who says he is among the friends of Allah and believes in Allah be allied with the enemies of Allah, the disbelievers in Allah? This is not possible. This is why we find that the conflict between the followers of the messengers and the enemies of the messengers is constant and ongoing, either by speech or by action; by speech: ﴿If they overcome you, they will be to you enemies and extend against you their hands and tongues with evil﴾ [al-Mumtahanah 2], and either by armed conflict as is well known.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that Allah, the Exalted, may show the fighters the matter as it is, or contrary to its reality, for a wisdom, as the verse of al-Anfal bears witness: ﴿And [remember] when He showed them to you as few when you met them, and He made you few in their eyes﴾; because when a person sees his enemy as few, he becomes energized to fight, and when he sees him as many, he becomes discouraged. So Allah, glorified and exalted, showed the believers the disbelievers as few, and showed the disbelievers the believers as few, so that each one would advance to fight.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of the act, or the affirmation of the acts of Allah, based on His saying: ﴿And Allah supports with His help whom He wills﴾.

* Among its benefits also: a refutation of the Jabriyyah (determinists), in His saying: ﴿fighting in the way of Allah﴾, where He attributed the act to them. The Jabriyyah say that the act is not attributed to the agent except figuratively, as you say: "The fire consumed the firewood," whereas in truth a person does not act by his own choice but is compelled to his action.

* Among the benefits of the verse: the affirmation of Allah's will, based on His saying: ﴿whom He wills﴾.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that only people of insight take heed of matters, based on His saying: ﴿Indeed in that is a lesson for those of insight﴾.

* Among its benefits: if you find in yourself a lack of taking heed and admonition from what occurs, know that you are weak in insight, because when Allah affirms the lesson for those of insight, the absence of the lesson indicates weakness of insight or its total absence.

* Among the benefits of the verse: praise of people of insight, because the context is one of praise, so it contains praise of people of insight and condemnation of the blind of heart.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verse 14 (part 1 of 4):

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Beautified for people is the love of desires: women and children, heaped-up piles of gold and silver, branded horses, cattle and tilled land.﴾ How many are these? ﴿women and children, heaped-up piles of gold and silver, branded horses, cattle and tilled land﴾: seven, unless you wish to make gold and silver one item; gold and silver are two.

﴿Beautified for people﴾, meaning: this thing was made attractive in their hearts. Who is it that beautified? Is the one who beautifies Allah, Mighty and Majestic, or is the one who beautifies Satan? The one who beautifies is Allah, and Allah has attributed beautification to Himself in several verses: ﴿Thus We made attractive to every community its deeds﴾ [al-An'am 108], ﴿Indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter – We have made attractive to them their deeds﴾ [an-Naml 4].

He also attributed beautification to Satan: ﴿And Satan made attractive to them their deeds and averted them from the way﴾ [an-Naml 24]. But Satan's beautification was only with respect to these people's deeds; that is, he made their deeds appear attractive to them. As for created things, it is Allah, Mighty and Majestic, who beautifies them.

﴿Beautified for people﴾: that is, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, beautified them in their hearts as a trial and a test. For were it not for the beautification of these things in people's hearts, the true believer would not be recognised. If a person did not care for such matters, there would be nothing to turn him away from the religion of Allah. But when love for these desires is cast into his heart, if his faith is strong, he does not prefer them over the love of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Have you not considered the words of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him: "A man whom a woman of rank and beauty invites, and he says: 'Indeed I fear Allah'"? [Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (1423) and Muslim (1031 / 91) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.] This is one of those whom Allah shades under His shade on a day when there is no shade but His shade. The woman of rank and beauty is among the most attractive things to a man among women: rank and beauty. Yet he said: "Indeed I fear Allah." She invited him in a secluded place where no one was present, for if anyone had been present he would have said: "There is someone with us, how can you say these words?" But he said: "Indeed I fear Allah." The place was empty, so the obstacles were absent, and the causes of immorality were present and abundant, yet he said: "Indeed I fear Allah." So we say that this beautification is a trial and a test from Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

He said: ﴿the love of desires from women﴾, and did not say "the love of women," meaning that a person marries a woman merely for desire and not for some other reason. For this reason, does the Messenger of Allah ﷺ fall under this? Is it said that he was among those for whom the love of desires was made attractive? No. For he, peace and blessings be upon him, did not marry a virgin, and had he wished merely for desire he would have chosen beautiful virgins, and nothing would have prevented him from that. But he said: "Women and perfume have been made beloved to me from your world" [related by an-Nasa'i (3939) from the hadith of Anas]; this is because of the great benefits in his choosing women, such as his connection with people and the tribes of the Arabs, and likewise the spreading of knowledge through women, especially the household knowledge that only women are aware of, along with other benefits. The point is that the verse says ﴿the love of desires from women﴾ and does not say "the love of women," because the beautification of love for women when it is not merely for desire may be praiseworthy for a person, but when it is merely for desire, this is from temptation. For this reason He said ﴿the love of desires from women﴾.

Second: ﴿the children﴾. Likewise, a person loves children not so that they may be a help to him in obeying Allah, but so that he may boast of them. In the Jahiliyyah they used to boast of sons and disliked daughters. When one of them was given the good news of a female, what would his state be? ﴿His face becomes dark, and he is filled with suppressed grief (58). He hides himself from the people (59)﴾ [an-Nahl 58–59]: he hides from them out of fear of disgrace. Then he deliberates and considers: ﴿Should he keep it despite contempt, or bury it in the dust?﴾ [an-Nahl 59]; that is, should he keep this newborn female in humiliation and oppression of her rights, or bury her alive in the dust? Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Unquestionably, evil is what they decide﴾ [an-Nahl 59]. The point is that there is no doubt that many people have had the love of children made attractive to them as a desire, and not the sexual desire, but the desire for pride, honour and prestige: "My children are ten, I have twenty children," and the like.

﴿And heaped-up piles of gold and silver﴾: "heaped-up piles" (al-qanatir al-muqantarah). Qanatir is the plural of qintar. What is meant by a qintar? It is said: it means a thousand mithqals of gold. A thousand mithqals of gold; so when they become qanatir, they are thousands. Muqantarah: cared for and preserved. It is also said that a qintar is what fills the hide of an ox, meaning an ox-hide of gold, which is more than a thousand mithqals? Indeed, yes. In any case, Allah the Exalted mentioned these large amounts of gold and silver, because generally the more wealth there is, the more a person is tempted by it. Whenever it increases, a person is tempted by it. So when there are heaped-up piles of gold, the temptation by them becomes stronger. ﴿of gold and silver﴾: He specified these two because they are the most valuable of wealth, and therefore people's desires are attached to these two jewels, gold and silver. Even if there are precious jewels, you will not find hearts attached to them as they are attached to gold and silver. Nowadays they counterfeit gold and silver, bringing things coated in a yellow colour imitating gold, while they are not gold, because they know that souls rush strongly toward gold and have a strong desire for it. And the poet says:

"I have seen people go to the one who has gold,
and I have seen people go to the one who has wealth."

He says: ﴿of gold and silver﴾. Gold is the well-known metal of yellow colour. Recently what people call "white gold" has become famous, but this is not gold, even though they consider it equal to gold in expense and in attaching souls to it. Yet it is not the gold meant in this verse. Silver is also a well-known metal and familiar jewel, but it is less than gold.

* Student: Shaykh, you mentioned that the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, did not marry a virgin?
* Shaykh: No, he generally did not marry a virgin; the only one was 'Aishah. He married her while she was a virgin.
* Student: We said that the believers must not take the disbelievers as allies, but in the case of da'wah, meaning inviting them, how can a person combine not taking them as allies with wanting to encourage them toward Islam?
* Shaykh: Taking them as allies means supporting and aiding them. That is taking them as allies, not seeking closeness to them for the sake of calling them.
* Student: So if we draw close to them for the sake of calling them?
* Shaykh: Do we not give them from the zakat? We give them money to win their hearts to Islam. I do not draw close to him because I love to be close to him personally; I draw close to him so that he may draw close to Islam. And here I feel within myself that I am not truly his ally. Whoever takes a Christian, or a disbeliever in general, as an ally, supports him, aids him and helps him, this is the one who has taken them as allies.
* Student: So if we go to invite them, do we begin with the greeting of peace and so on?
* Shaykh: No, we do not begin them with the greeting of peace. We do not begin with the salam; we begin with a greeting such as "good morning" or "how are you." As for handshaking: if they extend their hands, shake hands with them; otherwise, no.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Yes, but (...).
* * *
* Student: ﴿Beautified for people is the love of desires: women and children, heaped-up piles of gold and silver, branded horses, cattle and tilled land. That is the enjoyment of the worldly life, and with Allah is the best return﴾ [Al 'Imran 14].
* Shaykh: Well done. I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Beautified for people is the love of desires: women and children﴾ to the end. His saying ﴿beautified﴾: by whom is it beautified?
* Student: By Allah, Glorified and Exalted, originally.
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: Then to Satan...
* Shaykh: Why did He beautify them?
* Student: Allah, Glorified and Exalted, beautified them to be good news for the servants in this world.
* Shaykh: Good news?
* Student: To be a test for the servants.
* Shaykh: Yes, He beautified them as a test for the servants: will they prefer these desires, or what pleases Allah, Mighty and Majestic? His saying ﴿for people﴾: does it include the believer and the disbeliever? Yes, it includes both the believer and the disbeliever, because when it says "people," we say it is general; when it says "the believers," it is specific.
His saying ﴿the love of desires from women﴾ to the end: why did He not say "the love of women," but said "the love of desires"?
* Student: Because love of women without desire may be praiseworthy.
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: But love of women for desire (...).
* Shaykh: Yes. Why did He single out sons over daughters?
* Student: Because they used to boast of sons and used to dislike daughters.
* Shaykh: Yes, because this is the point of pride among the Arabs, and people to this day still prefer sons over daughters.
﴿heaped-up piles (al-qanatir al-muqantarah)﴾: qanatir is the plural of?
* Student: Qintar.
* Shaykh: And what is the qintar?
* Student: A thousand mithqals.
* Shaykh: Yes, many thousands; according to the preponderant view, they are many thousands of dinars. ﴿muqantarah﴾: what does it mean?
* Student: Cared for.
* Shaykh: Yes, cared for, which its owners tend, guard and count, and sometimes even bury out of fear for them.
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿of gold and silver﴾. Gold and silver are the two well-known metals for which all of mankind has desire; all children of Adam have their desire attached to gold and silver more than to anything else. For this reason gold and silver became the measure of value for all things; all things are sold for gold and silver. You will never find other wealth serving as the price with which things are sold. Did you sell your house? For what, for what thing? For gold and silver. You sold your car for gold and silver, you sold your book for gold and silver. Everything has gold and silver as its equivalent. Therefore they are the object of people's desire, and for this He said ﴿of gold and silver﴾. Gold is that reddish metal, and silver is the well-known white metal. But if gold is transformed and becomes white, does it retain the ruling of red gold, so that it becomes forbidden for men to wear it, or does the ruling change with the change of state? We hear that there is white gold, but the gold specified is red gold. If it is converted into white gold, then if it is merely a matter of colour, this is in my view open to consideration: does it count as gold, so that its nisab for zakat is the nisab of gold, it is forbidden for men, and selling it for red gold in unequal amounts is forbidden? Or do we say it has changed and taken the ruling of silver? This requires us to know what the chemists say about this matter: does it change by the substance added to it that makes it white, or does it not change?

And His saying ﴿of gold and silver and branded horses﴾: horses are these well-known animals. They were named "khayl" because their owner is generally afflicted with arrogance (khuyala), since they are the most prestigious mounts, so the rider has arrogance in his heart; or because they strut in their gait, and so you see horses in their walk are not like others, you feel in them a haughtiness and strutting. Some said: or because it seems to them that nothing rivals them. We do not know about this, except what appears as an effect, such as their strutting in their gait. In any case, horses are well known, and their owners undoubtedly see themselves as above people, since they were the finest mounts at that time and still are. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Good is tied to the forelocks of horses until the Day of Resurrection" [Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (2850) and Muslim (1873 / 98) from the hadith of 'Urwah al-Bariqi]. It is well known that the verse here is in the context of one who loves horses for desire, meaning he has taken them as an object of desire; this is the blameworthy beautification. As for one who takes them to strive in the way of Allah, this is good, and undoubtedly it is good for him. Just as one who loves gold and silver, not for desire and accumulating wealth, but for the benefits that follow from wealth, this is praiseworthy.

The Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, divided horses into three categories: one who keeps them for boasting and arrogance, or to oppose the Muslims with them, this one bears a burden (wizr). Second: one who keeps them to strive upon them in the way of Allah, this one has a reward. Third: one who keeps them for riding, breeding and benefiting from them, these are a covering for him, neither sin nor reward.

The Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, divided them into three categories: boasting and arrogance, or to oppose the Muslims with them, this one bears a burden. Second: one who keeps them to strive upon them in the way of Allah, this one has a reward. Third: one who keeps them for riding, breeding and benefiting from them, these are a covering for him, neither reward nor burden.

And His saying ﴿branded﴾ [Al 'Imran 14]: it is said the meaning of "musawwamah" is one that is left to pasture, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿and from it is a tree in which you pasture [your herds]﴾ [an-Nahl 10]. It is also said: "musawwamah" means one marked with markings for beauty and pride, such as having ostrich feathers placed on it or other things that beautify it.

We now have branded cars, do we not? They put decoration on them: trim, rims and other things; they brand them. Some people even dress up cheap cars in the clothing of expensive ones, putting a Mercedes rim on them, while you might find it is a Mazda or worse than a Mazda. In any case, branding of mounts is still a known matter among people to this day.

Among people, the branded is more expensive than the others, because it is only branded because it is good and of good origin, so it is branded and taken care of more.

﴿and cattle and tilled land﴾: "cattle" (al-an'am) is the plural of ni'am, like asbab is the plural of sabab, and they are camels, cattle and sheep. These kinds of animals are also objects of people's desire. Most people keep camels, cattle and sheep; you will not find them keeping gazelles or the like of animals, but they take care to keep these three kinds: camels, cattle and sheep, in the desert and in the settled areas, though they are more numerous in the desert.

The most valuable of these kinds are the red camels, and for this they are used as a proverb for value and love. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to 'Ali ibn Abi Talib when he sent him to Khaybar: "Proceed calmly, then invite them to Islam. By Allah, for Allah to guide one man through you is better for you than red camels" [Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (3009) and Muslim (2406 / 34) from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd ibn Malik, with a similar wording].

﴿and tilled land﴾: "harth" means cultivation, tilling the land for farming.

These are seven things: women, children, heaped-up piles of gold and silver, branded horses, cattle, and tilled land.

If you searched the general desires of people in this world, you would find that for the most part they do not go beyond these seven things. Otherwise there are other things that are objects of desire for people, such as lofty palaces. Lofty palaces: some people are also infatuated with them; they love them, cultivate them, and want their house or palace to be luxurious without equal.

The point is that these are the desires of people.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verse 14 (part 2 of 4):

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿That is the enjoyment of the worldly life﴾. "That" (dhalika): why did He say "dhalika" in the masculine singular when the things referred to are plural? Plurals of rational beings take "ha'ulaa'" (these), and plurals of non-rational beings take "hadhihi" (this)?

The answer, and Allah knows best, is that He returned the demonstrative to a masculine singular with the sense of "that which has been mentioned." So He omitted the mention of all seven of these things, referred to them collectively, and alluded to them by the phrase "that which has been mentioned." This is because of their insignificance in comparison with the bounties of the Hereafter.

As for His saying: ﴿That is the enjoyment of the worldly life﴾, it means: the enjoyment that people enjoy in the worldly life. Its end is cessation. Either it departs from you, or you depart from it. As for it remaining for you or you remaining for it, that is impossible. You must either part from it or it parts from you. This is a matter that needs no proof. These things, even if they were all gathered for a person, are nothing but the enjoyment of the worldly life, which a person enjoys and then parts from, or which parts from him.

His saying: ﴿the worldly life﴾ implies that there is a worldly life and another life. What is the true life? Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And indeed, the Last Abode—that is the [true] life﴾ [al-'Ankabut 64]. It is the true life, yes. As for this world, it is a simple life, not worth anything. The Prophet ﷺ said: «The place of a whip of one of you in Paradise is better than the world and everything in it»[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (2892), and Ahmad in his Musnad (15563), from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd ibn Malik; the wording is Ahmad's.]]. Allahu akbar, the place of a whip! A whip is about a meter. "...in Paradise is better than the world and everything in it." Which world? The world from the time it was created until the Day of Resurrection, with all its bounties. This is because the bounties of this world are, in reality, like dreams, like our dreams.

Consider the matter by what has passed of your life. All that has passed of your life is as if it were a dream, is it not? It is not as if it were something that actually happened, because it has gone. There is no difference between what you did while awake yesterday and what you saw in your sleep last night; all of it has gone. For this reason He called it the "worldly life." "Dunya" is the feminine of "adna" (nearer, lower), and it was described with this description because of the nearness of its rank in relation to the Hereafter, the nearness of its rank in relation to the Hereafter. So it is nothing in comparison with the Hereafter, as you have heard in the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad.

Likewise, it was called "dunya" because it is nearer (adna) than the Hereafter in terms of chronological order. ﴿And the Hereafter is better for you than the first (life)﴾ [al-Duha 4]. Thus it is first in terms of chronological order. So the "dunya" is near to people.

﴿That is the enjoyment of the worldly life.﴾ So, since we know that this is the enjoyment of the worldly life, let us look at these things not with a gaze of desire, but with a gaze of seriousness. If that benefits us in the Hereafter, then looking at it is good and beneficial, and it becomes part of the good of this world and the Hereafter. But if we look at it merely with the gaze of desire, then a person is in danger of desire overcoming the side of truth. For this reason Allah lowered the rank of these things and placed them where He said: ﴿That is the enjoyment of the worldly life.﴾ Then He said: ﴿and with Allah is the best of destinations﴾, meaning the best place of return. Return to what? In the Hereafter, because every person's return is to the Hereafter, either to Paradise or to the Fire, and there is no third abode. All people, jinn… indeed all jinn and mankind, their final destination in the Hereafter is either Paradise or the Fire, and there is no other abode. So with Allah is the best destination, meaning the best place of return.

* In this verse there are several benefits:
* First: the wisdom of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in testing people by making the love of desires attractive to them in these seven matters. The wisdom is this: were it not for these desires which contend with a person in his turning towards his Lord, there would be no benefit in the test in religion. Pay attention: that is, if this love had not been planted in a person's heart or in his nature, there would be no benefit in the test in religion. The reason: because submission to religion, if it has no competitor, is easy and smooth. For this reason, who was the first to respond to the messengers?
The poor, who were deprived of the world, because nothing contends with them, neither wealth nor leadership nor anything else. So this is from the wisdom of Allah, that He made the love of desires attractive in the hearts of people.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that one who loves these things, not in this manner (i.e., not with love of desire), is not blamed. For when the love of these things is made attractive to him not for the sake of desire, it is not a cause of turning him away from the religion of Allah. Because what most tempts a person is desire. If there is no doubt (shubha), then if there is doubt and desire combined upon him, both trials are produced for him.
What also indicates this is that the Prophet ﷺ said: «Women and perfume have been made beloved to me from your world»[[Narrated by al-Nasa'i in al-Sughra (3939), from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik.]].
Also indicating this: the Prophet ﷺ encouraged marriage and urged it, and commanded it to the youth.
And among what indicates this: the Prophet ﷺ urged marrying the woman who is "waluud". The waluud is one who bears many children; and if she is fertile, her offspring increase, and among her offspring are sons.
The point is that love of these things, not for the sake of desire, is a matter for which a person is not blamed.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the strength of Qur'anic expression, and that it is the highest type of speech in perfection. For this reason He said: ﴿love of desires﴾, and did not say: love of women, or love of sons, or love of heaped-up treasures; rather He said: love of desires from these things. So He attached the love to what? To the desires, not to these things. Because love of these things may be praiseworthy, as you have learned.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: giving precedence to the most dangerous. For this reason He placed women first, because the trial of the desire for women is the greatest trial. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ said: «I have not left after me a trial more harmful to men than women»[[Agreed upon; narrated by al-Bukhari (5096) and Muslim (2740/96), from the hadith of Usama ibn Zayd.]]. For this reason He began with it, saying: ﴿from women﴾.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that sons may be a trial; and the saying of Allah the Exalted witnesses to this: ﴿Your wealth and your children are only a trial﴾ [al-Taghabun 15]. "Children" is more general than "sons."
* Among the benefits of the noble verse also: that gold and silver are among the most dangerous wealth for a person. For this reason He placed them before the rest of the wealth, saying: ﴿and heaped-up quintars of gold and silver, and branded horses, and cattle, and tilth﴾, because they are the greatest wealth in trial, especially those described with this description: that they are heaped-up quintars.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the more wealth increases, the more the trial in its desire increases. From where do we take this? From His saying: ﴿and heaped-up quintars of gold and silver﴾.
For this reason we find some of the poor giving away all their wealth, while the rich do not give away all their wealth; rather some of the rich—we ask Allah for well-being—are tested: the more their wealth increases, the more their stinginess and withholding intensifies.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: horses are the greatest mounts for pride. For this reason He said: ﴿and branded horses﴾, especially when they are branded, that is, marked and well cared for, or branded and let loose in pasture, well cared for in their grazing; for they are then the greatest mounts in trial.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse also: the trial of cattle—camels, cows and sheep—is less than the trial of horses, according to the order; and the order in this verse is from the highest to the lowest.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse also: that among people there are those who are tested in tilth, that is, farming. They are tested by it and cultivate it in a lawful and unlawful manner, and this is so, especially in our time, when agriculture has flourished, so people—we seek refuge in Allah—go to every extreme in it and commit prohibited acts: such as lying to the government and betrayal. Yes, and despite this they see no harm in it. You find a person, for example, selling his produce to a person for cash, then giving him his name so that the buyer may take from the government a higher price. He buys it from the farmer, for example, at a riyal and a half per kilo and sells it to the government at two riyals, and lies, and takes the farmer's name; so the farmer becomes a betrayer and the other a liar, and from this results the consumption of wealth by falsehood. When they are asked, "Surely this is haram," they say, "We need money, so we sell it to the merchant." If you need money, do you lie and scheme? Be patient, or else sell it to him and don't give him your name. Sell him the produce and don't give him your name, if the government permits its sale. But people have been afflicted with this matter.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that all these things are nothing but the enjoyment of the worldly life; because of His saying: ﴿That is the enjoyment of the worldly life.﴾
* Among its benefits: discouraging attachment to these things; because of His saying: ﴿That is the enjoyment of the worldly life.﴾ Whatever belongs to this world, a person should not let his soul follow it, because it is passing. Do not let your soul follow anything of this world except what you use to aid you in obedience to Allah, so that it benefits you; and you will attain from it what whoever follows his soul in the enjoyment of the worldly life attains, for the world. For example, a man who eats dinner: some people eat it in order to preserve their body, eating it in compliance with the command of Allah, eating it as aid for obedience to Allah, eating it enjoying the blessings of Allah, and he is rewarded for that. Others eat it merely for desire, to fill their stomach, and so this reward is denied them, because they intended merely desire.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the belittling of this life; because of His saying: ﴿the worldly life﴾. By Allah, it is indeed deficient: a home where a person does not know the length of his stay, a home whose purity is nothing but turbid with murkiness, a home in which there is rancor, enmity and hatred among people, and other troubles, is indeed a lowly world. None of us in this world can guarantee that he will remain even for a single moment, is that not so? Then how can we say: this is a life? How can we say that this is a life? It is indeed the life of this world. And a person, in truth, by the wisdom of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has been tested by what is in it of these things that Allah mentioned. But the intelligent person looks to the outcome and the end.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that what is with Allah is better than this world; because of His saying: ﴿and with Allah is the best of destinations﴾.
And among them: what some have pointed out, that whoever is attached to these things with the attachment of desire, his end will not be praiseworthy; because when Allah mentioned attachment to these things in the manner of desire, He said: ﴿and with Allah is the best of destinations﴾, as if He were saying: there is no good destination for this one attached to these things; that is, his end is not praiseworthy. Thus did some of them mention it. But there is something in the soul about it, and what appears to me is that the verse was concluded with this, ﴿and with Allah is the best of destinations﴾, in order to encourage a person toward what is with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and that he not be attached to the enjoyment of the worldly life.
What supports what I have mentioned is His saying: ﴿Say: Shall I inform you of something better than that?﴾ [Al 'Imran 15]. The address in ﴿Say﴾ is to the Prophet ﷺ. We have mentioned earlier that when Allah begins a statement with "Say" (qul), this is evidence of Allah's care for it, and that He commanded His Messenger ﷺ with a particular command, and that He commanded His Messenger ﷺ to convey it specifically. Otherwise, the entire Qur'an was addressed to the Messenger ﷺ: ﴿O Messenger, convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾ [al-Ma'idah 67]. But sometimes Allah mentions something that He introduces with "Say" to indicate care for it.
Let us consider that the care for what is mentioned came from more than one aspect. First: because Allah began it with "Say." Second: He began it with an interrogative: ﴿Shall I inform you of something better than that?﴾, meaning: shall I tell you of something better than that, i.e., the thing indicated in the preceding verse. The interrogative conveys alerting the addressee and attentiveness to what will be conveyed to him. It is like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, shall I guide you to a transaction that will save you from a painful punishment?﴾ [al-Saff 10].
Then in this interrogative there is also a meaning other than alerting, namely arousing eagerness: ﴿Shall I inform you of something better than that?﴾, meaning: after Allah related to us the enjoyment of the worldly life, He commanded His Prophet to say to the people: ﴿Shall I inform you of something better than that?﴾, in order to make them eager for that good.
And His saying: ﴿Shall I inform you of something better than that?﴾ — He said ﴿unabbi'ukum﴾ and did not say "a'ukhbirukum" (shall I inform you), because "naba'" is used only for important matters: ﴿About what are they asking each other? About the great news﴾ [al-Naba' 1-2]. For this reason the Prophet was called "Nabi" and was not called "Mukhbir"; this is an important matter that needs to be announced.
And His saying: ﴿something better than that﴾ — He did not say "than that" (min dhalika) because the addressee is plural; the addressee is all people.
Here we pause to remember: what is observed regarding the demonstrative combined with the kaf?
The demonstrative combined with the kaf comprises a pointed-to thing and an addressee: the demonstrative agrees with the thing pointed to, and the kaf agrees with the addressee.
First: how do we say when we address a masculine singular and point to a masculine singular? We say "dhalika" (that): "dha" is the demonstrative for the masculine singular, and the kaf is for the masculine addressee. What do we say when we point to a masculine dual and address a masculine singular? We say "dhanika"; Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So those two are proofs from your Lord﴾ [al-Qasas 32]. We say "dhaanika."
What do we say when we address a masculine singular and point to a feminine dual? We say "tanika" ("those two women are standing").
What do we say when we point to a feminine singular and address a masculine singular? We say "tilka," or we say "tiika," especially with the particle ha, like "haatika."
What do we say when we point to masculine plurals, or to plurals in general, while addressing a masculine singular? We say "ulaaika" (those).
Now we have counted how many forms? Several forms, and the kaf has not changed. Why? Because the addressee is masculine singular.
How do we say when the pointed-to thing is masculine singular and the addressee is dual? "Dhalikuma"; Allah the Exalted said: ﴿That is of what my Lord has taught me﴾ [Yusuf 37].
When it is feminine singular and the addressee is dual?
Have you learned the first rule? In the previous examples we mentioned when the pointed-to thing differs while the addressee is one masculine singular. Now, when the addressee is dual and the pointed-to thing is feminine singular?
* Student: "Tilkuma."
* The Shaykh: "Tilkuma," correct.
How do we say when the addressee is dual and the pointed-to thing is feminine dual? The pointed-to thing is feminine dual and the addressee is dual?
* Student: "Tanikuma."
* The Shaykh: "Tanikuma."
How do we say when the addressee is a group of women and the pointed-to thing is masculine singular? The pointed-to thing is masculine singular and the addressee is a group of women?
* Student: "Dhalikunna."
* The Shaykh: "Dhalikunna," [Yusuf 32]: "She said: That is the one you blamed me for." Is that right? Good. The meaning is clear; we do not need to continue, because it is a matter of illustration that requires patience.
The demonstrative follows what?
* Student: The pointed-to thing.
* The Shaykh: The pointed-to thing. The kaf follows?
* Student: The addressee.
* The Shaykh: The addressee. Thus at times each of them is masculine singular, at times each is feminine singular, at times each is a plural of males, at times each is a plural of females, and at times the situation differs between the pointed-to thing and the addressee.
The kaf of the addressee: I told you it follows whom?
* Student: The addressee.

**Shaykh:** The addressee. In it there is a dialect: that it be for the masculine with an open *kaf* (ك), whatever the masculine is, whether dual, plural, or singular. Note: when it is for the masculine, it is open, fixed on the *fatḥa*; for the feminine it is fixed on the *kasra*, and it is singular in both cases. That is, there is a dialect among the dialects of the Arabs in which they keep the *kaf* in the singular form always open for the masculine and always open for the feminine. There is a third dialect: they keep the *kaf* open and singular for the masculine, the feminine, the dual, the plural, and the singular. So they say, for example, *dhalika* (ذلكَ), whether they are addressing a man or a woman, or two men or two women, or men or women. I think this dialect is suitable, because it is easier.

**Student:** Easier.

**Shaykh:** Because it is easier.

**Student:** (...) more eloquent.

**Shaykh:** We say: our rule is that when the grammarians disagree, we adopt the easier view; but when the dialects differ, we adopt the more eloquent one.

When the dialects differ, take the more eloquent. When the grammarians differ, take the easier. Is that right? And when the jurists differ, take the more cautious. Right? These are three rules.

**Student:** I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. ﴿Alif, Lam, Meem. Allah – there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence. He has sent down upon you, [O Muhammad], the Book in truth, confirming what was before it. And He revealed the Torah and the Gospel, Before, as guidance for the people. And He revealed the Criterion. Indeed, those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah will have a severe punishment, and Allah is Exalted in Might, the Lord of Retribution. Indeed, nothing is hidden from Allah on the earth or in the heaven. He is the One who forms you in the wombs however He wills. There is no deity except Him, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.﴾ [Āl ʿImrān 1–6]

**Shaykh:** What do you say about His saying: ﴿Alif, Lam, Meem. Allah – there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer﴾?

**Student:** We say: these are letters with which Allah, glorified and exalted, began, and He brought them as a challenge (*taḥaddī*).

**Shaykh:** He began some of the surahs with them.

**Student:** Yes.

**Shaykh:** And do they have a meaning or not?

**Student:** It has been said that they have no meaning and that their knowledge is with Allah. The correct view is that they have a meaning.

**Shaykh:** No. If you say their knowledge is with Allah, you cannot then say they have no meaning and also have no meaning. The one who entrusts the matter to Allah affirms and does not negate.

**Student:** And the correct view is that Allah, glorified and exalted, brought them as a challenge.

**Shaykh:** The question is: do they have a meaning? We do not mean: do they have a purpose? Do they have a meaning in themselves or not?

**Student:** We say: they have no meaning that we know.

**Shaykh:** The preponderant view is that they have no meaning, neither known nor unknown. Is that right or not? Good. What is the evidence that this is the preponderant view?

**Student:** Because the meanings of these letters have not been reported, neither in the Book nor in the Sunnah.

**Shaykh:** No.

**Student:** Because the Arabs do not speak with these letters; they have no meaning.

**Shaykh:** Because the Qur'an was revealed in a clear Arabic tongue, and these letters, as they are, combined in this way, have no meaning in the Arabic language. Therefore, by the requirement that the Qur'an is in the Arabic tongue, we say: they have no meaning. Now, if we say they have no meaning, does that make them vain? And Allah, mighty and majestic, is free of vanity.

**Student:** The correct thing is to say that they have a purpose (...), and it is the challenge to the Arabs (...) these letters (...) the challenge to the Arabs.

**Shaykh:** They have a purpose, which is the challenge to the Arabs, since this Qur'an did not come in a new language, so that they could say, "By Allah, we do not know this language." Rather, it came in the Arabic tongue, which is made up of the familiar letters they know. Despite that, they were unable (to produce its like).

Good. What supports the consideration of this purpose? What testifies to or supports the view of this purpose?

**Student:** (...)

**Shaykh:** Correct. Generally, when these alphabetic letters are mentioned, the Qur'an is mentioned after them, such as: ﴿Alif, Lam, Meem. That is the Book﴾ [al-Baqarah 1–2], and ﴿Alif, Lam, Meem. Allah – there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer. He has sent down upon you the Book﴾ [Āl ʿImrān 1–3], and so on to the end.

**Student:** I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿It is He who has sent down to you the Book. In it are verses that are clear (*muḥkamāt*), which are the foundation of the Book, and others that are ambiguous (*mutashābihāt*). As for those in whose hearts is deviation, they follow that of it which is ambiguous, seeking discord and seeking its interpretation (*ta'wīl*). But none knows its interpretation except Allah. And those firm in knowledge say, "We believe in it; all of it is from our Lord." And none will be reminded except those of understanding. Our Lord, let not our hearts deviate after You have guided us, and grant us from Yourself mercy. Indeed, You are the Bestower. Our Lord, indeed You will gather the people for a Day about which there is no doubt. Indeed, Allah does not fail in (His) promise.﴾ [Āl ʿImrān 7–9]

**Shaykh:** His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿the Book﴾. What is meant by it?

**Student:** The Qur'an.

**Shaykh:** And why was it called a book?

**Student:** (...) The first matter: it is written in the Preserved Tablet (*al-Lawḥ al-Maḥfūẓ*). The second matter: it is written in the people's scrolls.

**Shaykh:** And the third matter?

**Student:** The third matter: it is written with the angels.

**Shaykh:** In the scrolls that are in the hands of the angels: ﴿So whoever wills will remember it, in honored scrolls, raised and purified, by the hands of scribes﴾ [ʿAbasa 12–15].

Good. His saying: ﴿in it are verses that are clear﴾. What is meant by "clear"?

**Student:** The clear ones are those perfected in their rulings and in their reports.

**Shaykh:** So does it mean that some of the Qur'an is not perfected?

**Student:** No, this is general perfection; that is, the whole Qur'an is true.

**Shaykh:** ﴿In it are verses that are clear﴾. What is the meaning of "clear" alone? Define it.

**Student:** That is, there is no ambiguity in them; they are apparent and evident.

**Shaykh:** Well said. That is, apparent and evident, with no ambiguity. Good.

And the ambiguous ones?

**Student:** The opposite.

**Shaykh:** The opposite. That is, they contain obscurity which only those of understanding or those firm in knowledge can grasp.

Good. As for His saying: ﴿and none knows its interpretation except Allah﴾, there are two readings among the early scholars. The first reading: stopping at ﴿except Allah﴾. The second reading: continuing. What is the justification for each of the two readings?

**Student:** The justification for stopping at ﴿except Allah﴾ is that the meaning of interpretation (*ta'wīl*) is that none knows it except Allah.

**Shaykh:** And what is the meaning of interpretation according to the stopping reading?

**Student:** (...) the ambiguous (...)

**Shaykh:** No.

**Student:** The outcome.

**Shaykh:** The outcome and the reality to which this ambiguous thing points; none knows it except Allah.

Good. And according to the continuing reading? Does the meaning become "interpretation"?

**Student:** (...)

**Shaykh:** What is the meaning of interpretation in this reading, the continuing reading?

**Student:** Explanation.

**Shaykh:** Explanation. Its meaning is explanation. That is, the explanation of the ambiguous verses is known only to Allah and those firm in knowledge. As for those whose knowledge is superficial, they do not know the interpretation of these ambiguous things.

Good. Among the ambiguous verses are those whose apparent meaning is contradictory, such as?

**Student:** Such as His saying: ﴿Allah has sent down the best statement as a Book, consistent and repeating (*mathānī*)﴾ [al-Zumar 23].

**Shaykh:** No.

**Student:** An example of the ambiguous?

**Shaykh:** Verses whose apparent meaning is contradictory, which become confusing for some people, so they suppose that there is contradiction in the Qur'an. They follow that ambiguity and mislead people with it. But those firm in knowledge know the reconciling aspect of these verses, and there is no contradiction in them.

**Student:** Such as His saying: ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all, about what they used to do﴾ [al-Ḥijr 92–93], and here He said: ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all﴾. And in Surat al-Raḥmān He said: ﴿So on that Day, no one will be asked about his sin, neither man nor jinn﴾ [al-Raḥmān 39]. Such things may confuse those of limited knowledge who reflect, so they suppose there is contradiction, since He affirmed questioning in one place and negated it in another.

**Shaykh:** Well said. Those firm in knowledge understand the way of this, so they interpret each verse in a way that does not contradict the other verse.

There are also many subtle verses in it. There are many verses which Shaykh Muḥammad al-Amīn al-Shanqīṭī, may Allah have mercy on him, pointed to in his book which he titled *Daf' Īhām al-Iḍṭirāb ʿan Āyāt al-Kitāb* (Removing the Illusion of Contradiction from the Verses of the Book). It is a good and beneficial book for the student of knowledge.

**Student:** I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve, their wealth will not avail them, nor their children, against Allah at all. And they are the fuel of the Fire. [Their condition is] like the custom of the people of Pharaoh and those before them. They denied Our signs, so Allah seized them for their sins, and Allah is severe in punishment. Say to those who disbelieve: "You will be overcome and gathered to Hell, and wretched is the resting place."﴾ [Āl ʿImrān 10–12]

**Shaykh:** Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿you will be overcome and gathered﴾. Is there a second reading for it?

**Student:** A reading (...) ﴿they will be overcome and gathered﴾ with the *yā'*.

**Shaykh:** A reading with the *yā'*: ﴿they will be overcome and gathered﴾.

Here Allah, glorified and exalted, mentioned the condition of these disbelievers in this world and their condition in the Hereafter. What is their condition in this world?

**Student:** (...) And in the Hereafter (...).

**Shaykh:** Well said. So they are in loss in this world and in the Hereafter. Is there anything in the Qur'an that supports this verse, that the outcome of those who disbelieve is to be overcome in this world and the Fire in the Hereafter?

**Student:** ﴿If Allah helps you, no one can overcome you﴾ [Āl ʿImrān 160].

**Shaykh:** No.

**Student:** (...) connected with one another.

**Shaykh:** A verse similar to this one, if not identical to it, in meaning, though the wording differs somewhat.

**Student:** (...).

**Shaykh:** Well said. There is a verse in Surat al-Anfāl exactly like this one: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth to avert [people] from the way of Allah. They will spend it; then it will be a regret for them; then they will be overcome. And those who disbelieve will be gathered to Hell﴾ [al-Anfāl 36].

Good. If a disbeliever boasts of the strength, wealth, and children he has, with what does the believer respond to this boasting?

**Student:** They will not avail them against Allah at all. But in this world they may avail them, not from Allah but from people, meaning (...).

**Shaykh:** We say: these will not avail you against Allah at all, yes. And if Allah, mighty and majestic, willed, He would have given victory over you. But Allah tests His servants by means of one another. Is that clear? What do you say?

**Student:** Yes.

**Shaykh:** Thus. As for looking at their wealth and children with admiration, esteem, and awe, so that we become humbled and say, "It is impossible for us to reach what they have reached," and then become their tails following them, this is not the state of the believer. The believer looks at them as though they were bats, but he strives for what will bring victory over them: faith in Allah, righteous deeds, preparing strength, and other means.

**Student:** I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿There has already been for you a sign in the two armies that met: one fighting in the way of Allah, and another disbelieving, who saw them [the believers] as twice their number by sight. **Shaykh:** His, mighty and majestic, saying: ﴿who saw them as twice their number by sight﴾. Are there two readings in it?

**Student:** ﴿they see them as twice their number﴾ has a reading with the *tā'* and a reading with the *yā'*.

**Shaykh:** ﴿yarawnahum﴾ and ﴿taraunahum﴾.
