These four types flow beneath these lofty palaces and luxuriant trees that delight the beholders, gladdening the beholders; they gladden the heart. A person cannot imagine the bliss within them.

He says: ﴿beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever﴾. This too is part of the perfection of bliss: eternity. ﴿They do not taste therein death﴾ [Ad-Dukhan 56]. Rather, it is said to them: "Eternity, with no death" [Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (6545) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, and by Muslim (2849/40) from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri], so they are gladdened. Rather, it is said to them: "Indeed, for you is that you will enjoy and never be miserable, that you will be healthy and never be sick, that you will be youthful and never grow old, and that you will live and never die forever" [Related by Muslim (2837/22) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah]. All the afflictions of this world that spoil bliss are removed from them. For this reason He said ﴿abiding therein forever﴾.

﴿and purified spouses﴾ is conjoined to ﴿gardens﴾: gardens and spouses. Its conjunction to them is because the type of pleasure differs: pleasure from the gardens is the pleasure of the appetite of the belly, while pleasure from spouses is another pleasure, of another kind. For this He said ﴿spouses﴾, including the spouses from the Houris (al-hur al-'in) and the women of this world.

A person who has a wife in this world will remain his wife in the Hereafter. If she had two husbands, she will be given the choice between them. If a person did not have a wife in this world, then in Paradise there are women who had no husbands in this world; this one will be married to one of them. There are also spouses of another kind, namely the Houris, and the Houris are also included in His saying ﴿and purified spouses﴾.

His saying, the Exalted, ﴿purified﴾: from what? From every filth, physical or moral. Purified from every filth, physical or moral: the physical, such as urine, feces, menstruation, foul sweat, and mucus, and the like; the moral, such as rancor, hatred, immorality, and aversion to the husband, and the like.

The essential point: Allah stated it absolutely, saying ﴿purified﴾ without saying "from such and such," in order to convey generality, because among the well-known rules is that omitting the object indicates the generality of the verb. This is a well-known principle among them: that omitting the object indicates the generality of the verb.

There are many examples of this. For instance, His saying to the Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿Did He not find you an orphan and give you refuge? And He found you lost and guided you? And He found you poor and made you self-sufficient?﴾ [Ad-Duha 6–8]. He said, ﴿Did He not find you an orphan﴾, and did not say "and sheltered you"; ﴿and He found you lost﴾, and did not say "and guided you," although the address is to him; ﴿and He found you poor﴾, and did not say "and made you self-sufficient," but omitted the object to indicate the generality of the verb.

So the Messenger (ﷺ) was found by his Lord as an orphan and He gave him refuge; but He did not give him refuge alone: He gave him refuge and gave refuge through him, until He made him a stronghold for every believer. Lost, and He guided him; or did He guide him and guide through him? He guided him and guided through him. Poor, and He made him self-sufficient and made self-sufficiency through him. From where did the Arabs obtain these enormous spoils, which they never thought to seize? How would the Arabs, shepherds of sheep and camels, conquer the lands of Persia and Rome, except by means of the Prophet (ﷺ) and his religion?

The essential point is that this is an established, well-known principle: that omitting the object indicates the generality of the verb.

So then ﴿spouses, purified﴾ does not mention the object, which indicates that they are purified from every filth, physical or moral.

His saying ﴿spouses, purified﴾: He did not say "purified" in the feminine plural. Why?

Because the adjective of a plural noun may be in the plural or the singular, except that the sound feminine plural must be in the plural. For example, you say: "I passed by believing women" and "believing women" (in the feminine plural form), and you say: "I passed by righteous Muslim women," and do not say "righteous Muslim women" in the singular. Here "spouses" is a plural, a sound feminine plural or a broken plural? It is a broken plural (jam' taksir), so its adjective may be singular or plural. It is permissible to say: azwaj mutahharah and azwaj mutahharat.

Ibn Malik said:
"And Allah decrees with abundant gifts..."
Had he said "wafirat" (abundant), it would have been correct.

﴿and purified spouses and the pleasure of Allah﴾: Allah is greatest! This is the greatest thing: ﴿the pleasure of Allah﴾, that Allah the Exalted alights upon them His pleasure, so He will never be displeased with them afterward; He will never be angry with them. This is the greatest that can be, as Allah the Exalted said when enumerating the bliss of the people of Paradise: ﴿And the pleasure of Allah is greater﴾ [At-Tawbah 72]. It is greater than all of this, because when the one you love, whom you have sought to reach since you knew and since you discerned, is pleased with you, this is the greatest aim of a person: to attain the pleasure of Allah the Mighty and Majestic. Greater than that is looking at the Face of Allah the Exalted, as Allah said: ﴿For those who have done good is the best [reward] and an increase﴾ [Yunus 26]. There is nothing more delightful, more pleasant, or more beautiful for the people of Paradise than looking at the Face of Allah the Exalted.

So the highest thing is looking at the Face of Allah; the pleasure follows it; the bodily enjoyments of Paradise come after this. For this reason He said ﴿and the pleasure of Allah﴾, singling it out for mention, because it is bliss of the heart, whereas what preceded it is bliss of the body and flesh. This, however, is bliss of the heart. For this Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: "Indeed, I have made My pleasure lawful for you, so I will never be displeased with you after it, ever" [Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (6549) and Muslim (2829/9) from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, without the word "innI"].

He said: ﴿and the pleasure of Allah. And Allah is Seeing of the servants﴾, the Exalted. Allah is Seeing of the servants who desire this world and the servants who desire the Hereafter; He is seeing of them. Seeing by sight of observation or seeing by knowledge? It includes both. He is seeing of the servants by sight of observation: nothing escapes His sight; He is seeing of them by knowledge: ﴿Not an atom's weight escapes Him in the heavens or on the earth, nor anything smaller than that or greater, but it is in a clear register﴾ [Saba' 3].

His saying ﴿of the servants﴾: what is meant by them? What kinds of worship are meant: general or specific?

General. So the servitude here is general servitude.

He is seeing of all the servants: their believers and their disbelievers, their righteous and their wicked, their mindful and their disobedient; of all the servants Allah the Exalted is seeing.

He, the Exalted, is seeing of who deserves to be among the mindful and who deserves to be among the disobedient. Disobedience is by His wisdom, and obedience is by His grace: disobedience by His wisdom and justice, and obedience by His mercy and grace.

Then the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Those who say, "Our Lord, indeed we have believed"﴾. This is an explanation of ﴿for those who are mindful﴾, not of the servants in general, because all the servants do not possess these attributes; rather, the mindful among them are the ones who possess these attributes: ﴿those who say, "Our Lord, indeed we have believed."﴾

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on Surah 3, verses 15–19 (part 2 of 6)**

His saying: ﴿They say﴾. He means by this saying with the tongue and belief with the heart. When Allah the Exalted mentions saying "we believe" without anything following it, what is meant is saying with the tongue and conviction in the heart. The evidence for this is the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And among the people are those who say, "We believe in Allah and the Last Day," but they are not believers﴾ [al-Baqarah 8]. Because the intended meaning of this saying is only the tongue, He said: ﴿but they are not believers﴾. But when Allah mentions a person's saying "I have believed," He means by it saying with the tongue and conviction in the heart.

For this reason He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Say, "We believe in Allah"﴾ [al-Baqarah 136]. He does not mean that we should say it with our tongues only, but with our tongues and our hearts. ﴿Say, "We believe in Allah"﴾ [Al 'Imran 84]: He does not mean that we should say it with the tongue only, but with the tongue and the heart. So then, ﴿those who say, "Our Lord, indeed we have believed"﴾: believed in what? With their tongues only? No. With their tongues in utterance and with their hearts in conviction, meaning belief.

His saying: ﴿those who say, "Our Lord"﴾. Look how they sought nearness to Allah through His Lordship, to report their state of faith in Him. It is as if they are saying: "Our Lord, we have believed, but we did not reach faith except through Your Lordship over us, that particular Lordship which entails complete care." They say: ﴿Our Lord, indeed we have believed﴾. Pay attention. If He had said "those who say: we have believed," the sentence would have been sound without doubt. But when they say: ﴿Our Lord, indeed we have believed﴾, this is like an indication that they did not reach faith except by the requirement of this particular Lordship that entails complete care.

﴿Those who say, "Our Lord, indeed we have believed"﴾. In ﴿indeed we have believed﴾, how many emphasizing particles are there in the sentence?

* Student: One.

* Shaykh: One, and it is (*innana*), because the second (*na*) is a pronoun. ﴿Indeed we have believed﴾: they emphasize their faith. ﴿Indeed we have believed, so forgive us﴾.

Good. We believed in what? In everything that it is obligatory to believe in.

Jibril asked the Prophet ﷺ: "What is faith?" He said: "That you believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and you believe in divine decree, both its good and its evil."[^1] And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The Messenger believes in what has been revealed to him from his Lord, and so do the believers. Each one believes in Allah and His angels and His books and His messengers. We make no distinction between any of His messengers﴾ [al-Baqarah 285].

So faith here includes belief in everything that it is obligatory to believe in, and it is six kinds: belief in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and divine decree, both its good and its evil.

Good. Faith is not merely *tasdiq* (affirmation of truth). It is not merely affirmation, because mere affirmation is not faith. For this reason it is said "*amantu bihi*" (I believed in him), and it is said "*amantu lahu*" (I believed for him), and there is a difference between them. And it is said "*saddaqahu*" (he affirmed him), and there is a difference between these too.

Faith must be accompanied by acceptance and submission. That is, he affirms, then he accepts, then he submits. This is faith. For this reason it is said "*amantu bihi*" (I believed in him), and not "*amantuhu*" (I believed him). If faith were synonymous with affirmation, it would be correct to say "*amantuhu*" just as one says "*saddaqtuhu*" (I affirmed him). So faith includes a meaning beyond mere affirmation; rather it is affirmation that includes what? Acceptance and submission. For this reason, we all know, according to what history has transmitted, that Abu Talib affirmed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, affirmed him, and saw that what he reported was like the sun. Indeed he acknowledged this in his poems, saying:

*They have known that our son is not a liar among us, nor is he concerned with false speech.*

He says: he is not one who is called a liar, nor is he concerned with false speech. So he was an affirmer. And he says:

*And I have indeed known that the religion of Muhammad is of the best religions of mankind as a religion. Were it not for blame or fear of disgrace, you would have seen me clearly declaring it.*

So he was an affirmer, but his affirmation did not include acceptance and submission. He did not accept and did not submit. Shall we say he is a believer? No. Therefore faith necessarily requires acceptance and submission.

﴿Those who say, "Our Lord, indeed we have believed, so forgive us our sins"﴾ [Al 'Imran 16]. The *fa'* here is for causation. That is: because of our faith, forgive us. For there is no doubt that faith is a means to forgiveness, and whenever faith strengthens, the causes of forgiveness strengthen, to the point that when a person sincerely makes his faith pure, his good deeds remove his bad deeds. Good. For this reason He said: ﴿so forgive us﴾, meaning: because of faith, forgive us. This is from the category of seeking nearness through obedience to make supplication accepted.

He said: ﴿So forgive us our sins and protect us from the punishment of the Fire﴾. In ﴿اغْفِرْ لَنَا ذُنُوبَنَا﴾ (*ighfir lana dhunubana*, forgive us our sins), *ighfir* is a verb of supplication, not a verb of command. Why?

* Student: Because it is directed to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

* Shaykh: We do not say "*ighfir lana*" is an imperative verb, because Allah is not commanded. The servant does not command Allah; he supplicates to Him. So every verb in the imperative form that is directed to Allah is a supplicative verb, called a verb of supplication, and not called an imperative verb. Forgiveness is derived from *al-ghafr*, which is covering together with protection. From it comes *al-mighfar*, the helmet that the fighter wears on his head to cover the head and protect it from arrows. So forgiveness is not merely covering, but covering and protection. For this reason we say: the forgiveness of sins is covering them from people and pardoning their punishments. What proves this is that Allah, glorified and exalted, will meet His believing servant on the Day of Resurrection, and will make him acknowledge his sins, saying: "You did such and such, and you did such and such, and you did such and such," until he confesses. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: "I have covered them for you in the world, and I forgive them for you today."[^2] That is, I will not recompense you for them. And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, covers sins over His servants. By Allah, were it not for this, many people would be disgraced. It is said that among the Children of Israel, whoever committed a sin would wake up to find his sin written on his door[^3], and we seek refuge in Allah, that is disgrace. As for this Ummah, Allah has covered it, praise be to Allah, but He has opened for it the doors of repentance wide, as they say. ﴿Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah; indeed Allah forgives all sins"﴾ [al-Zumar 53]. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gives respite to the human being, gives him respite and bears patiently with him. If he is granted success, he admonishes himself by himself. He himself thinks: what have I done, and what have I done? So he feels shame before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and fears that Allah will disgrace him. Because if a person dares against his Lord in secret, perhaps He will disgrace him openly if he does not repent to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. If he repents, Allah accepts his repentance and replaces his bad deeds with good deeds.

﴿So forgive us our sins﴾. The sins are acts of disobedience, and they are either grave or less than that, and all of them need forgiveness. A person seeks forgiveness for all of them. Do not think that minor sins, when they are expiated by good deeds, are like sins expiated by repentance. There is a great difference between them. When sins are expiated by repentance, the bad deeds are replaced by good deeds. When they are expiated by acts of worship, they are only erased, but they are not replaced by good deeds. Allah says: ﴿Indeed, good deeds remove bad deeds﴾ [Hud 114], and He says: ﴿Except for one who repents and believes and does righteous work, for those Allah will replace their bad deeds with good deeds﴾ [al-Furqan 70]. There is a difference between the two matters: between a bad deed being removed by a good deed, and a bad deed being replaced with a good deed. Is that not so? So do not rely on good deeds expiating bad deeds, saying: "My bad deeds are expiated by my good deeds." No. Furthermore, in reality, we hope that our good deeds will clear our obligations, meaning they are not strong enough to expiate. Do not think that every prayer expiates. No. There may be a prayer that does not clear the obligation except, as they say, "like a tambourine," because it is a prayer that a person performs out of habit, and then when he enters into it he begins to calculate his money if he is a merchant, begins to leaf through his ledgers if he is a student, begins to look at his plane and saw if he is a carpenter, and so on. The whisperings increase only when he enters the prayer. When he finishes, these whisperings fly away, and his heart becomes present for the remembrance that comes after the prayer. As for the prayer itself, he wanders everywhere. When he closes one door, Satan opens a distant door that had never occurred to him. When he tries to close it, another door is open, and so on, so that Satan may come between a person and his Lord. Because Satan knows that this connection between Allah and the servant, that is, his connection with Allah in prayer, has a great importance and a great role in the reform of the servant. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing﴾ [al-'Ankabut 45]. Do you want anything greater than this? That there should be within you a deterrent that forbids you from immorality and wrongdoing. This is what enrages Satan, so Satan wants to come between you and this by casting whisperings into your prayer, until you leave your prayer with a dry, parched heart, just as you entered it. For this reason, I ask Allah to help me and you to reform this great act of worship, because if it is reformed, all acts of worship are reformed, all acts of worship. But if it is dry, from where will the trees of deeds be watered? They are not watered except with water.

* Student: A person commits sins and does not remember them. How is repentance? There are many sins.

* Shaykh: Yes. If he repents a general repentance, that is sufficient.

* Student: So it is valid if he says: "I seek forgiveness from Allah, the Mighty"?

* Shaykh: Yes. And if he also says the well-known istighfar: "O Allah, I seek Your forgiveness for what I do not know," this is also good.

* Student: So this expiates?

* Shaykh: It expiates. Yes. If releasing a debtor from a right of a human being that is vague and unknown is permissible, and he is cleared by it, then what about the right of Allah?

* Student: But he does not remember it.

* Shaykh: No, he does not remember, but he says "I seek forgiveness from Allah from every sin." Seeking forgiveness from Allah from every sin is sufficient.

* Student: Would a person who is approached by Satan during prayer and whispered to be in contradiction with the saying of Allah: ﴿Indeed, you have no authority over My servants﴾ [al-Hijr 42; al-Isra 65]?

* Shaykh: No. This authority is of two types: an authority by which he misguides them and they are not guided. This cannot be over the sincere servants of Allah. And an authority by which Satan overpowers a person, but Allah grants him repentance, so He erases and demolishes whatever Satan has built. His authority in this case is in reality an increase of grief for him, for Satan. For this reason, Satan is never seen more humiliated or smaller than on the Day of 'Arafah, because of what he sees of the descent of mercy. Satan may overpower a person, but if he seeks forgiveness and is forgiven, his grief increases.

* Student: Shaykh, the saying: ﴿and purified spouses﴾ [Al 'Imran 15]: does it include the women of this world as well?

* Shaykh: Yes. Even the women of this world in Paradise are purified from this.

* Student: Can we say that this verse, ﴿Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves"﴾, is for all (...) servants, meaning the disbelievers and the believers?

* Shaykh: Yes. Everyone who repents to Allah, Allah will forgive his sin. This verse was revealed concerning those who repent. As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him﴾ [al-Nisa' 116], this was revealed concerning those who do not repent. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾: this is concerning those who do not repent. As for ﴿Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves"﴾, this is concerning those who repent.

* Student: Is repentance accepted from one sin and not from another?

* Shaykh: This requires us to ask about the conditions of repentance. Do you know some of them?

* Student: To abandon the sin, and to resolve never to return to it.

* Shaykh: First, that we be sincere to Allah. Sincerity to Allah.

* Student: Sincerity to Allah.

* Shaykh: Regret.

* Student: Regret for what you did, abandoning the sin, resolving not to return, and if it is a matter involving a human being, to be released from it.

* Shaykh: The fifth.

* Student: That he be released from it, if it is a right of a human being.

* Shaykh: No. What you are saying is included in his saying: abandonment.

* Student: That it be within the time.

* Shaykh: Yes, that it be within the time in which it is accepted. Five conditions. If these conditions are present, the repentance is valid. And among these conditions is not that one is not persisting in another sin. For this reason, the correct view is that repentance is valid from one sin while one persists in another. But what is problematic is whether repentance is valid from one sin while one persists in its kind. This is what is under consideration. As for if it is of a different kind, there is no doubt that it is accepted, because this is what justice requires. But a person repents to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, from looking at forbidden women, yet he kisses women. Do we say that his repentance from looking is accepted, and he is punished only for kissing, or is it not valid?

* Student: This is one type and that is another type.

* Shaykh: There is disagreement about it. The kind is one. This is a matter of uncertainty for us.

* Student: Is kissing not greater than looking?

* Shaykh: It is greater. But if he repents from looking, is he punished for looking and kissing, or for kissing only? We say this is a matter of consideration. And Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, in *Madarij al-Salikin*, when he examined this, said: this matter has a deep depth. That is, it may be considered: is this repentance a reform of the heart? If his repentance is a reform of the heart, then he must avoid kissing, because how can one who repents from looking kiss?

* Student: He does not kiss except after looking.

* Shaykh: No, not at all. He may not chase women with his gaze, but if he encounters a woman, he kisses her.

* Student: It necessitates, O Shaykh. A woman he kisses, he looks at her.

* Shaykh: May Allah guide us and you. But he does not look at others. Here there are people whose concern is looking at women, he takes pleasure in looking at them and does not kiss and does not think of kissing. And there is a person whose concern is to find a woman with her face uncovered so he may kiss her.

* Student: Shaykh, what are the signs of acceptance of repentance?

* Shaykh: The signs of acceptance of repentance are that the person finds comfort and tranquility, aversion to sin, and turning towards Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

* * *

* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿Those who say, "Our Lord, indeed we have believed, so forgive us our sins and protect us from the punishment of the Fire." The patient, the truthful, the obedient, those who spend, and those who seek forgiveness in the hours before dawn. Allah bears witness that there is no deity except Him, and so do the angels and those of knowledge, standing in justice. There is no deity except Him, the Mighty, the Wise﴾ [Al 'Imran 16–18].

* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say, "Shall I inform you of something better than that? For those who fear Allah, with their Lord are gardens beneath which rivers flow"﴾ [Al 'Imran 15], and so on to the end. What is meant by the interrogative here in His saying ﴿Shall I inform you﴾ (*a-unabbi'ukum*)? What is meant by the interrogative?

* Student: To arouse eagerness.

* Shaykh: To arouse eagerness. Does it have a parallel? We want another example. Bring another example from the Quran.

* Student: The saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, shall I direct you to a commerce that will save you from a painful punishment?﴾ [al-Saff 10].

* Shaykh: Well done. His saying ﴿for those who fear Allah, with their Lord﴾: what is the position of this sentence in relation to what precedes it in meaning?

* Student: Explanation.

* Shaykh: Explanation of what?

* Student: Of the good which is better than what came before.

* Shaykh: Well done. An explanation of who deserves this good, which is better than what preceded. His saying ﴿with their Lord﴾: what does this "with" (*'indahum*) convey?

* Student: It conveys glorification.

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verses 15–19 (part 3 of 6):**

* **Shaykh:** Ta'zim (veneration) and what else? Tashrif (honour). Because what is with Allah is undoubtedly close to Him, and so this is an honour for it. What is meant by *rububiyyah* (lordship) here?
* **Student:** This is a *rububiyyah khassah* (specific lordship).
* **Shaykh:** The specific one. So *rububiyyah* is divided into two types.
* **Student:** A general *rububiyyah* that encompasses all servants, and a specific *rububiyyah* that belongs to the believers, and a more specific one that belongs to the prophets and messengers.
* **Shaykh:** Excellent. Now, can you bring us an example that combines both meanings?
* **Student:** The words of Allah the Exalted, relating the account of Pharaoh and Moses: ﴿Pharaoh said, "And what is the Lord of the worlds?" (23) [Moses] said, "Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, if you were certain."﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara' 23–24].
* **Shaykh:** This?
* **Student:** General *rububiyyah*.
* **Shaykh:** Yes.
* **Student:** The specific *rububiyyah* is like this verse.
* **Student (another):** Yes, what combines them is the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿They said, "We have believed in the Lord of the worlds (121), the Lord of Moses and Aaron."﴾ [Al-A'raf 121–122].
* **Shaykh:** Yes, correct. The words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Beneath which rivers flow﴾ [Al 'Imran 15]. What is the meaning of His words ﴿beneath it (min tahtiha)﴾?
* **Student:** They flow over its surface and between its trees.
* **Shaykh:** How "over its surface" when He says ﴿min tahtiha (from beneath it)﴾?
* **Student:** They flow from beneath its trees.
* **Shaykh:** Its trees and its palaces. Good. What are these rivers that flow? What are their types?
* **Student:** Four types: ﴿of water unaltered (ghayru asin)﴾.
* **Shaykh:** Do you know what *asin* means?
* **Student:** It means unchanging.
* **Shaykh:** Do you know what *asin* means?
* **Student:** *Asin* is that which changes.
* **Shaykh:** So *ghayru asin* means "unchanging." Good.
* **Student:** And rivers of milk, ﴿delicious to those who drink﴾.
* **Shaykh:** No, its taste has not changed. And the third?
* **Student:** And rivers of wine, ﴿delicious to those who drink﴾.
* **Shaykh:** Of wine (*khamr*), delicious to those who drink.
* **Student:** And rivers of honey, ﴿clarified﴾.
* **Shaykh:** Excellent. These are four. Now, ﴿purified spouses (azwajun mutahharah)﴾. Purified from what?
* **Student:** Purified from the impurity of the outward and the impurity of the inward.
* **Shaykh:** *Rijs* (impurity), sensory and non-sensory. The sensory is like what?
* **Student:** Menstruation, sweat, and mucus.
* **Shaykh:** And urine and feces. Good. And the inward?
* **Student:** Like spite, rancour, and envy.
* **Shaykh:** Good. Does this include the spouses of this world?
* **Student:** Yes, it includes them.
* **Shaykh:** It includes them.
* **Student:** (...).
* **Shaykh:** Yes, meaning that the spouses from the people of this world will be purified on the Day of Resurrection. The words ﴿*ridwan*﴾: there are two readings for it?
* **Student:** Kasrah of the *ra'* and its dammah.
* **Shaykh:** There is *ridwan* with a kasrah on the *ra'* and *ruḍwan* with a dammah. Good. Which is greater: this blessing enumerated, or *ridwan*?
* **Student:** *Ridwan* is undoubtedly superior. The pleasure of Allah, glorified and exalted, with the believers is superior.
* **Shaykh:** What is the evidence?
* **Student:** The words of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, in the hadith: «I bestow My pleasure upon you, so I will never be displeased with you»[[Agreed upon hadith; al-Bukhari (6549), and Muslim (183/302), from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri.]].
* **Shaykh:** Is there nothing in the Qur'an?
* **Student:** ﴿Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him﴾ [Al-Bayyinah 8].
* **Shaykh:** No, what do you say?
* **Student:** The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And approval from Allah is greater﴾ [At-Tawbah 72].
* **Shaykh:** The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And approval from Allah is greater.﴾ Excellent. ﴿Those who say, "Our Lord, indeed we have believed."﴾ Does ﴿say (yaqulun)﴾ mean with the heart or with the tongue?
* **Student:** Both: their hearts and their tongues.
* **Shaykh:** Good. Is the tongue alone sufficient?
* **Student:** It is not sufficient.
* **Shaykh:** The evidence?
* **Student:** We said, "Abu Talib..."
* **Shaykh:** The evidence?
* **Student:** Evidence from the Qur'an, you mean?
* **Shaykh:** From the Qur'an, yes.
* **Student:** ﴿Those who say, "Our Lord, we have believed."﴾
* **Student (another):** The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And among the people are those who say, "We believe in Allah and the Last Day," but they are not believers﴾ [Al-Baqarah 8].
* **Shaykh:** So the meaning of their words ﴿they say, "Our Lord, indeed we have believed"﴾ is not saying with the tongue alone. Rather, it means saying with the tongue and the heart.
* **Student:** Is there anything more explicit than this verse?
* **Shaykh:** Do I not know it? Don't we know it?
* **Student:** ﴿They say with their mouths what is not in their hearts﴾ [Al 'Imran 167].
* **Shaykh:** Yes, and this also benefits, but my verse is more explicit. He says: ﴿and they are not believers.﴾ Good. His words: ﴿So forgive us our sins﴾?
* **Student:** The *fa'* is for causation (...) forgiveness together with removal of sins.
* **Shaykh:** What is *maghfirah* (forgiveness)?
* **Student:** *Maghfirah* is derived from falling into concealment.
* **Shaykh:** Concealment?
* **Student:** Concealment together with forgiveness.
* **Shaykh:** We are asking for forgiveness now. We cannot say: forgiveness is concealment together with forgiveness. We are asking now about forgiveness.
* **Student:** Concealing the sin and overlooking it.
* **Shaykh:** So, concealment and protection. What indicates from the language that forgiveness includes both meanings, concealment and protection?
* **Student:** The meaning of *maghfirah* is..
* **Shaykh:** We know its meaning: concealing the sin and protecting from it by overlooking it.
* **Student:** From it comes *mighfar*, the helmet worn by a warrior.
* **Shaykh:** It is derived from the *mighfar* with which the warrior covers his head. Good. Now the benefits from His words: ﴿Protect us from the punishment of the Fire.﴾
I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And protect us from the punishment of the Fire﴾. *Qina*: the *qaf* is a verb of supplication, correct?
* **Students:** Correct.
* **Shaykh:** The *qaf* is a verb of supplication. Wrong. We say *(qi)* is a verb of supplication. We do not say "the *qaf*." Good. "The money belongs to Zayd," what do we say? We say *(li)* is a preposition (*harf jarr*). Or is *al-lam* a preposition? *Al-lam* is a preposition. What is the difference between (*li*-Zayd) and (*qi*)?
* **Student:** (*Qi*) is an imperative verb.
* **Shaykh:** Good.
* **Student:** That one is of one letter and this one is of two letters.
* **Shaykh:** *Qi* is one letter. What is its colour? Its origin is of three letters. We say: because the *lam* is a particle, and *qi* is a verb. For this reason, if you write *qaf* as an alphabetic letter you would say "qaf." So *qi* is an imperative verb. Its morphological pattern (*wazn sarfi*)?
* **Student:** (*fi*).
* **Shaykh:** No.
* **Student:** (*'i*).
* **Shaykh:** (*'i*). Its morphological pattern is (*'i*), because its first radical and its last radical were deleted. Its origin is from (*waqa*): *waw*, *qaf*, *alif*. If the first radical and last radical are deleted, what remains? The middle radical remains, so *qi* is on the pattern of *'i*. Make a person from *wa'a* (to memorize) say it.
* **Students:** (*'i*).
* **Shaykh:** (*'i*), its morphological pattern?
* **Students:** (*'i*).
* **Shaykh:** (*'i*). From *wafa*?
* **Students:** (*fi*).
* **Shaykh:** (*fi*), its morphological pattern?
* **Students:** (*'i*).
* **Shaykh:** (*'i*). *Washa*?
* **Students:** (*shi*).
* **Shaykh:** (*shi*). I think al-Khudari, in his commentary on Ibn 'Aqil, mentions about twenty verbs of this type, meaning imperative verbs whose first and last radicals were deleted and which took the pattern (*'i*).

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿*Qina* 'adhaba al-nar﴾ come from *al-wiqaya* (protection). That is, "protect us from it." Does this mean: protect us from the punishment when we deserve it, or protect us from the punishment so that we do not do the deed that leads to it, or both together? Apparently the intended meaning is both together. These noble ones have supplicated that Allah protect them from the punishment of the people of the Fire, and supplicated that Allah, glorified and exalted, protect them from the Fire if they do the deeds of its people. But how would He protect them if they do the deeds of its people? He protects them through multiple means. The scholars have mentioned the causes of forgiveness of sins, and they reached about ten causes. Among them: that a person is granted repentance. When a person repents from a sin, Allah protects him from the punishment of that sin. ﴿Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins"﴾ [Az-Zumar 53].
Among them: righteous deeds, charity, the supplication of the believers, and other things. The point is that they mentioned about ten causes, all of them causes of protection from the punishment of the Fire. So their supplication for protection from the punishment of the Fire includes two meanings. The first meaning: that He protects them from the deeds of the people of the Fire. The second: that He protects them from the punishment after committing a deed that makes punishment obligatory, after the deed that makes it obligatory, by facilitating for them the causes of repentance and the erasure of these sins, even if by His will, glorified and exalted. Thus ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ [An-Nisa' 48].

His words: ﴿the punishment of the Fire﴾: this is general, but it is detailed in many verses. Allah, glorified and exalted, has clarified the punishment of the people of the Fire, and that it is a punishment by which hearts are torn and by which hearts are broken. ﴿Indeed, in that is a reminder for whoever has a heart, or gives ear while he is present﴾ [Qaf 37].

Then Allah the Exalted described these noble ones by His words: ﴿*as-sabirin* (the patient)﴾. This is an adjective of His words ﴿for those who fear Allah with their Lord﴾, and of ﴿those who say, "Our Lord, indeed we have believed"﴾, and of ﴿the patient﴾, and so on. *As-sabir* is an active participle from *as-sabr* (patience). Linguistically it originally means restraint. Its legal meaning is restraining the self from what Allah has forbidden. Its types are three: patience upon Allah's painful decrees, patience in refraining from Allah's disobedience, and patience in obeying Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Three types: patience in obedience to Allah, patience in refraining from disobedience to Allah, and patience upon Allah's painful decrees.

As for patience in obedience, a person finds from it great difficulty, because when he intends to obey, he finds his commanding self (*nafs ammarah*) and Satan trying to turn him away from obeying Allah. You find him in a struggle with his commanding self, until, if Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, helps him, he overcomes these two enemies, Satan and the commanding self, and does what Allah has made obligatory, or what Allah has commanded. As for patience in refraining from disobedience, especially when the causes that call to it are present, you find a person in a fierce struggle with himself, especially when the call to it is strong and there is no opposition. For when the call to disobedience is strong and there is no opposition, no one is saved from it except whom Allah protects. For this reason the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, among those whom Allah will shade in His shade on the day when there is no shade but His, "A man whom a woman of rank and beauty invited, and he said: 'Indeed I fear Allah'»[[Agreed upon hadith; al-Bukhari (1423), and Muslim (1031/91), from Abu Hurayrah.]].

This man exercised this great patience in refraining from the prohibitions of Allah while the call was strong and there was no... what? Opposition. This man did not say, "By Allah, I have no desire." No. The man had desire. The woman was not ugly, not one to be disdained; rather she was beautiful. The woman was not of the common people who have no good in them; rather she was of rank and honour. She invited him. There was no one present to oppose reaching the goal, because he did not say, "There is someone around us whom we fear." Rather there was one thing: fear of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. This is patience in refraining from what? From the disobedience of Allah. Patience in refraining from the disobedience of Allah. There is no doubt that in this there is great hardship. A young man, in an empty place, has desire, and a woman of rank and beauty invites him, she invites him for herself. Many people do not control themselves if a young beautiful woman speaks to them, so how much more when she is inviting them? Yet he says, "Indeed I fear Allah." This is great patience. From it is the patience of Yusuf, peace be upon him, when the wife of the ruler invited him, and she was his mistress. Undoubtedly she adorned herself for him, and she did all the means of enticement, or all the enticements, to reach her goal. But he, peace be upon him, saw the proof of his Lord; otherwise the matter would have been completed. ﴿She desired him, and he would have desired her, had he not seen the proof of his Lord﴾ [Yusuf 24]. At the last moment Allah protected him, and this is the strongest form of chastity and the most powerful form of chastity. Have you not considered the Israelite man who «was pursuing his cousin, seeking her, and she refused him. Then a year of hardship struck her; she came to him and gave herself to him. When he sat between her thighs as a man sits with his wife, at the height of readiness, she said to him: "Fear Allah, and do not break the seal except by right." And what happened? He got up from her, though she was the most beloved of people to him»[[Agreed upon hadith; al-Bukhari (3465), and Muslim (2743/99), from Abdullah ibn Umar.]]. He did not hate her; his self still desired her. But when she reminded him of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, he feared Allah. So I say: this is patience in refraining from the disobedience of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

The third: patience upon Allah's painful decrees. This is common. Among examples is Ayyub, peace be upon him, who was greatly patient. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, We found him patient. An excellent servant; indeed he was a frequent returner [to Allah]﴾ [Sad 44]. He was patient upon the harm that befell him, a great patience. Patience also upon Allah's painful decrees that result from obedience to Allah is greater in reward. So the patience of the messengers in the face of people's harm for the sake of calling to Allah, because these endured the harmful decrees that result from what? From a voluntary act on their part, which is obedience to Allah by conveying His message. Let us give an example of the patience of the master of creation, peace and blessings be upon him, Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. He was greatly patient, a patience no one else could bear, along with forbearance, deliberation, pardon, and tolerance. When he went out to the people of Ta'if calling them to Allah, calling them to the Oneness of Allah, calling them to Paradise, saving them from the Fire, what happened? They lined up in two rows, their fools lined up in two rows, and they said: "Strike Muhammad with stones!" They began striking him with stones until his heels bled. He did not regain consciousness except at Qarn al-Tha'alib, peace and blessings be upon him. Then the angel of the mountains came to him in this state, in which he could have taken revenge on his enemies, and said to him: "Indeed Allah sent me to you, and commanded me to close the two mountains upon them, if you wish." He could have said, "Close them upon them," because the One who sent him is the One who says to a thing, "Be," and it is. Glorified and exalted is He. But he said: «No. I hope that Allah will bring forth from their loins one who worships Allah and associates nothing with Him»[[Agreed upon hadith; al-Bukhari (3231), and Muslim (1795/111), from Aisha.]]. Allah is greatest! Allah brought forth from their loins one who worships Allah and does not associate anything with Him. Through them Allah supported Islam and opened the eastern and western regions of the earth. So look at the outcome of patience, forbearance, and deliberation.

One day, peace and blessings be upon him, was praying beneath the House of Allah, in the safest place on the face of the earth, prostrating to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. The fools of his people came, and they sent one of them to the slaughter of the Banu so-and-so. He brought its entrails, its blood, and placed them on the back of the Prophet ﷺ while he was prostrating. Prostrating to Allah in the safest place, in the place where the polytheist unbeliever feels safe, safe from the evil of Quraysh. And Muhammad, Messenger of Allah ﷺ, was not safe from their harm until his young daughter Fatimah came and removed the harm from his back»[[Agreed upon hadith; al-Bukhari (240), and Muslim (1794/107), from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud.]]. Yet he endured and persevered, and he did not leave Makkah except after Allah permitted him. His people emigrated, but he refused, and he did not emigrate until he was permitted, peace and blessings be upon him. So he was a servant of Allah in residence and a servant of Allah in migration, peace and blessings be upon him.

The point is that patience is a great rank. Allah praises the patient, and makes clear that the patient will be given their reward without reckoning. It is a high rank that is not attained except through something one must be patient with. Do not think that patience is a simple matter; there must be something you endure. For this reason, the people of knowledge bear a responsibility in which they must endure people's harm more than others. Everyone whom Allah has entrusted with knowledge, his being entrusted with that knowledge is a covenant and pact between him and his Lord that he convey it to the people and call people by it. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And [mention] when Allah took the covenant of those who were given the Scripture: "You must make it clear to the people and not conceal it"﴾ [Al 'Imran 187]. From what did He take it? Has any one of you now been given the Book by Allah? Has any of you felt that Allah took the covenant and pact from him?

* **Student:** No.

* Shaykh: No, rather, Allah's teaching you is a covenant and a pact. Allah has singled you out with knowledge from among the rest of the ignorant. This is the covenant and the pact. That is, it is not a physical pledge of allegiance that people witness in the mosques or in the open wilderness. Rather, it is a blessing that Allah bestows upon a person. So whenever Allah bestows knowledge upon someone, this is the covenant and pact that Allah has taken. If the students of knowledge who exist today would convey some of their knowledge, not all of it, you would find knowledge widely spread among people. But most of them, or many of the students of knowledge, are more beneficial to people than copies of books, because their knowledge does not go beyond their chests. Indeed, they sometimes disgrace themselves through their actions and words, showing their ignorance as if they had no knowledge at all. This includes shortcomings in worship, shortcomings in dealings, bad character, and failure to fulfill the rights of people. You find that the student of knowledge's treatment is worse than that of the ignorant layman. So do we say that this man is patient? No, he is not patient, because when is one praised for patience? When one conveys knowledge and is harmed for it. If you reflect now, you will see that the most knowledgeable people and the leaders in religion are those who have suffered the most harm from people. Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, what was done to him? He was dragged by a mule through the markets and beaten with whips until he lost consciousness. He was the Imam of Ahl al-Sunnah (the People of the Sunnah). Yet this harm did not weaken his resolve to say the truth. He was not asked for much. He was only asked to say, "The Qur'an is created," nothing more, and still he refused. He said, "The Qur'an is revealed, uncreated," (...).

The magicians said: ﴿We will never prefer you over the clear proofs that have come to us and over the One who created us. So decide whatever you are going to decide. You can only decide concerning this worldly life.﴾ [Ta-Ha 72]. Imam Ahmad said, "I do not care, and I would die in jihad for spreading the sound creed." If Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, had said, even by way of interpretation, "The Qur'an is created," nations would have gone astray. But as some scholars said, Allah granted victory to Islam through him on the day of the trial (al-Mihna, the inquisition), just as He granted victory to Islam through Abu Bakr on the day of apostasy (al-Ridda). What happened to Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah? He was harmed. He was imprisoned several times and died in prison. He would write while in prison and spread knowledge in prison. They prevented him from having ink and paper, so he began writing knowledge on the walls of the prison. He wrote whatever Allah opened to him. He mentioned about himself that Allah opened great knowledge to him because he devoted himself to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. His companions would come to him and take what he had written. What did his enemies do? They prevented his companions from reaching him. They said, "Do not enter upon this man to take his knowledge." Yet he remained patient and devoted himself to reciting the Qur'an. His brother was with him, reviewing the Qur'an with him, until he completed the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and rivers, in a seat of truth, in the presence of a Sovereign, Omnipotent.﴾ [al-Qamar 54-55]. Then his soul departed, may Allah have mercy on him. Allah is greatest! A conclusion, a good conclusion. We ask Allah to join us, you, and him with the righteous. The point is that patience is a high rank. You, with what Allah has bestowed upon you of knowledge, and praise be to Allah, and His having preferred you over many of His believing servants, must convey knowledge and be patient with the harm that comes with it.

Therefore we say: patience has three types: patience in obeying Allah, patience in refraining from what Allah has forbidden, and patience in the painful decrees of Allah. Which of these types is best? The best is patience in obeying Allah, then patience in refraining from the disobedience of Allah, then patience in the decrees of Allah. This is in principle. However, a person may struggle with patience in the decrees more than with patience in commands, so he is rewarded in that respect because of the hardship. And he may struggle with patience in refraining from what Allah has forbidden more than with patience in obeying Allah, so he is greater in reward in that respect because of the hardship. Do you understand? But in terms of the categories themselves, the best without doubt is patience in obeying Allah, because patience in obeying Allah combines two matters: restraining the inner self to do this act and restraining the outward body to do this act. Obedience is an action, and action requires first resolve and second deed. So it involves two matters. But patience in refraining from disobedience involves only inner action, which is restraining the self from acting. There is no physical hardship in it. There is no bowing, no prostration, no standing, no sitting, no spending of wealth, nothing. It is only restraint. So it involves only inner struggle, and therefore it is of a lower rank. Patience in decrees involves neither of these, because it is not by your choice. If a person is struck by an accident and his leg or hand breaks, was that by his choice? No, it was not by his choice. He will either be patient with the patience of the noble, or he will forget it like animals do. There is nothing else. Therefore it is of a lower rank than the first two types, because the first two types are from a person's own action and choice.

﴿The patient and the truthful﴾. Truthfulness (al-Sidq) is conformity with reality. Conformity with reality is called truthfulness. So the truthful person is one whose report conforms with reality, and the liar is the opposite. Truthfulness can be in speech, in action, with Allah, and with the servants of Allah. How many categories are there? Four: it is in speech, in action, with Allah, and with the servants of Allah. As for truthfulness in speech, it is the conformity of speech with reality. If he says to you, "Zayd came," and Zayd had come, then it conforms with reality, so it is truthfulness. Truthfulness is one of the characteristics of believers, and lying is one of the characteristics of hypocrites. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, urged truthfulness and said: «Adhere to truthfulness, for truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise. A man continues to speak the truth and strive for truthfulness until he is recorded with Allah as a *siddiq*»[[Hadith agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6094), and Muslim (2607 / 105), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud.]]. And *al-Siddiqiyyah* (the state of being a *siddiq*, one of exceptional truthfulness) is not a low rank. Rather, it is the rank that follows the rank of the prophets. Therefore, al-Siddiqiyyah is in the second rank among ﴿those upon whom Allah has bestowed favor: of the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous﴾ [an-Nisa' 69]. This is truthfulness in speech. Truthfulness in action is that action conforms with the heart. This is truthfulness in action: that action conforms with the heart. A man shows you affection while his heart hates you. Is this truthful?

* Students: No.

* Shaykh: A man shows that he is a believer, prays, gives charity, and attends gatherings of knowledge, but his heart harbors disbelief, may Allah protect us. Is this truthful? No, this is a liar in action. He showed the opposite of what he concealed. The two examples now: one with the servants and one with Allah. The hypocrite is a liar with Allah, and the one who shows you friendliness while he hates you is a liar with people; he was not truthful with you. So in His saying ﴿the truthful﴾, it includes both of these: truthfulness in speech and action with Allah and with the servants of Allah. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded truthfulness in His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and be with the truthful﴾ [at-Tawbah 119]. The Prophet ﷺ urged it with a great urging, which grammarians call what? *al-Igharah* (urging by way of stirring up, an exhortation to take hold of something), which is a demand with intensity and urgency. He said: «Adhere to truthfulness».

The outcome of the truthful is not hidden from you. Even if there were nothing from it except that unique example, as far as we know, that occurred with Ka'b ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, and Hilal ibn Umayyah, and Murarah ibn al-Rabi', when they stayed behind from the Battle of Tabuk without an excuse. When the Messenger ﷺ came back to Madinah, the superficial hypocrites came to the Messenger ﷺ apologizing, and he excused them, because he, may the peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, does not know the unseen and only takes people by their outward appearance. He excused them, asked forgiveness for them, and they turned away thinking they had gained something. They thought they were the clever ones who had combined appeasing the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, with appeasing the disbelievers. So they became brothers to the Muslims outwardly and brothers to the disbelievers inwardly. ﴿When they meet those who have believed, they say, "We believe"; but when they are alone with their devils, they say, "Indeed, we are with you"﴾ [al-Baqarah 14]. They did not say, "We have disbelieved." They said, ﴿Indeed, we are with you﴾ [al-Baqarah 14]. That is, disbelief plus more, meaning they are disbelievers and assist the disbelievers.

As for Ka'b ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, he had been given eloquence, argument, and skill in that. But before whom was he? He was not before a human being whom he could escape by a trick. Rather, he was before the Knower of the unseen, Mighty and Majestic, who, if he lied today, would expose him tomorrow. As happened with the hypocrites, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿They will swear by Allah to you when you return to them, that you may leave them alone. So leave them alone. Indeed, they are impure, and their refuge is Hell as recompense for what they used to earn﴾ [at-Tawbah 95]. Do you want something more severe than this blame and this punishment? ﴿Indeed, they are impure﴾: this is blame and condemnation. The punishment: ﴿and their refuge is Hell as recompense for what they used to earn﴾. But he, may Allah be pleased with him, said: I will not escape today by a trick or an excuse, lest Allah, Mighty and Majestic, expose me tomorrow. He informed the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, of the truth, with truthfulness. So success came from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, through the testing of these three. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, boycotted them and commanded that they be boycotted. After forty nights had passed, he commanded them to separate from their wives. When the messenger of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to Ka'b, may Allah be pleased with him, commanding him to separate from his wife, he said: "Should I divorce her?" He said: "No, but separate from her." Did he say, "By Allah, this is my wife, with whom I sleep tonight?" Or did he say, "Go back to your family"? "Go back to your family." He said, "I hear and obey." So they endured this great patience: first in truthfulness, and second in this boycott. Ka'b, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "I would greet the Prophet ﷺ, and I did not know whether he moved his lips to return the greeting or not." Allah is greatest! The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was the best of people in character, the greatest in cheerfulness, and the best in returning greetings. Ka'b would greet him and not know whether he returned the greeting. And he would greet Abu Qatadah, his cousin, who was the most beloved person to him, and Abu Qatadah would not return the greeting. Abu Qatadah, may Allah be pleased with him. Even if you came today in tribal zeal, would one leave his cousin over such matters? Never, and Allah knows best, one would not. But Abu Qatadah, may Allah be pleased with him, did not return Ka'b's greeting. Ka'b said: "I said to him, 'I beseech you by Allah, do you know that I love Allah and His Messenger?'" He stayed silent for a moment and then said, "Allah knows best." He did not answer with a yes or no. He said, "Allah knows best." And Allah knows best that Abu Qatadah did not intend by that a reply to Ka'b. He intended to inform that Allah, Glorified and Exalted, is more knowing than anyone. But after this great patience, what was the result? The result was the revelation of verses recited concerning them until the Day of Resurrection. Their remembrance will never be forgotten. Perhaps someone better than them among the Companions may be forgotten, but these will not be forgotten. And how can we match the great reward for this patience? ﴿And [He turned in forgiveness to] the three who were left behind﴾ [at-Tawbah 118]. That is, He turned in forgiveness to the three who were left behind. ﴿Until, when the earth constricted for them despite its vastness and their souls confined them, and they were certain that there is no refuge from Allah except in Him. Then He turned to them so they might repent. Indeed, Allah is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful﴾ [at-Tawbah 118]. Then He commanded the believers to do likewise, to be like them, saying: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and be with the truthful﴾. The point is that truthfulness is a great, lofty, elevated character that none attains except one who is granted success, until he is in the second rank among those upon whom Allah has bestowed favor. «A man continues to speak the truth and strive for truthfulness until he is recorded with Allah as a *siddiq*»[[Hadith agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6094), and Muslim (2607 / 105), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud.]].

* * *

* Student: I seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿The patient, the truthful, the devout, the spenders, and those who seek forgiveness before dawn﴾ (17). ﴿Allah bears witness that there is no deity except Him, and the angels and those of knowledge, [that He is] standing in justice. There is no deity except Him, the Almighty, the Wise﴾ (18). ﴿Indeed, the religion in the sight of Allah is Islam. And those who were given the Scripture did not differ except after knowledge had come to them, out of jealousy among themselves. And whoever disbelieves in the signs of Allah – indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning﴾ (19) [Aal Imran 17-19].

* Shaykh: I seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, the Exalted, said in describing those who fear their Lord: ﴿For those who fear Allah are gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide eternally, and purified spouses, and approval from Allah. And Allah is Seeing of His servants﴾ [Aal Imran 15].

﴿الصَّابِرِينَ﴾ in the rest of their attributes. ﴿الصَّابِرِينَ﴾ (the patient). The discussion of patience (sabr), its meaning linguistically and in the Sharia, has already preceded. It is divided into three categories: patience in obedience to Allah, patience in refraining from disobedience to Allah, and patience in the painful decrees of Allah. Then He said: ﴿وَالْقَانِتِينَ﴾ (and the devout). Al-qanitin (the devout) is the active participle from al-qunut (constant obedience). ﴿وَالصَّادِقِينَ﴾ (and the truthful). The discussion of truthfulness (sidq) has also preceded, and we explained that it is truthfulness in speech, action, and belief, and that it is truthfulness toward Allah and truthfulness toward the servants of Allah. Then He said: ﴿وَالْقَانِتِينَ﴾ (and the devout). This is also one of their attributes, qunut. Qunut is applied to several meanings, and the most fitting of them for this verse is that qunut here means the continuance of obedience together with humility and submission to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, such that a person is constant in obedience to Allah and turns devotedly toward Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, in his obedience. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿حَافِظُوا عَلَى الصَّلَوَاتِ وَالصَّلَاةِ الْوُسْطَى وَقُومُوا لِلَّهِ قَانِتِينَ﴾ [Al-Baqarah 2:238] ("Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer, and stand before Allah devoutly obedient"), meaning: humbly submissive. For this reason, when this verse was revealed, they were commanded to be silent and forbidden to speak (during prayer). So the qanit is one who constantly obeys Allah, with humility and presence of heart, and who is committed to turning toward Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. ﴿وَالْمُنْفِقِينَ﴾ (and the spenders). Al-munfiqin is from anfaqa, meaning to expend. Nafaqah is the spending of wealth. Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, has stated spending here without specifying it, but in other verses He mentioned the measure for spending and mentioned what is spent on or for whom. He said: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ إِذَا أَنْفَقُوا لَمْ يُسْرِفُوا وَلَمْ يَقْتُرُوا وَكَانَ بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ قَوَامًا﴾ [Al-Furqan 25:67] ("And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor stingy, but are ever between that [being moderate]"). He, the Glorified and Exalted, also said: ﴿وَلَا تَجْعَلْ يَدَكَ مَغْلُولَةً إِلَى عُنُقِكَ وَلَا تَبْسُطْهَا كُلَّ الْبَسْطِ﴾ [Al-Isra 17:29] ("And do not make your hand chained to your neck, nor extend it completely open"). This is the measure of spending: that a person should be neither stingy nor extravagant. If we take this as the measure, it varies according to circumstances, times, and places. Spending may be extravagance for one person and not extravagance for another. The spending of the poor is not like the spending of the rich. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿لِيُنْفِقْ ذُو سَعَةٍ مِنْ سَعَتِهِ وَمَنْ قُدِرَ عَلَيْهِ رِزْقُهُ فَلْيُنْفِقْ مِمَّا آتَاهُ اللَّهُ﴾ [At-Talaq 65:7] ("Let a man of wealth spend from his wealth, and he whose provision is restricted – let him spend from what Allah has given him"). The spending of the middle-income person is between them. Likewise, it varies with time. Sometimes the time is a time of general prosperity in this society, so extravagance in a society that is less prosperous is not extravagance with regard to this society. It also varies with times: at some times wealth is abundant and available, so spending much of it is not extravagance, and at other times the situation is the reverse. In any case, Allah has mentioned spending here in the verse without qualification, and He mentioned its measure in several verses, among them in Surah al-Furqan: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ إِذَا أَنْفَقُوا لَمْ يُسْرِفُوا وَلَمْ يَقْتُرُوا وَكَانَ بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ قَوَامًا﴾. As for what it is spent on or for whom? Allah, the Glorified, said: ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ مَاذَا يُنْفِقُونَ قُلْ مَا أَنْفَقْتُمْ مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَلِلْوَالِدَيْنِ وَالْأَقْرَبِينَ وَالْيَتَامَى وَالْمَسَاكِينِ وَابْنِ السَّبِيلِ﴾ [Al-Baqarah 2:215] ("They ask you what they should spend. Say: Whatever good you spend is for parents, relatives, orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer"). So the channels of expenditure: each channel is one in which there is need, or in which the Muslims have need of it. Either it is in need, or the Muslims are in need of it. So spending in the way of Allah is for whose need? It is for the need of the Muslims for jihad in the way of Allah, because in jihad in the way of Allah is the elevation of the word of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and the preservation of His Sharia. Spending on the poor is for whose need? It is for the need of the poor, not for the need of the Muslims; rather, it is for the need of the poor. So you always see that spending is either to relieve the need of a needy person, or to relieve the need of the Muslims in general, that is, in public interests. The main point is that these are spenders; those who are among the people of Paradise are spenders, but their spending is governed by Sharia controls.

﴿وَالْمُسْتَغْفِرِينَ بِالْأَسْحَارِ﴾ (and those who seek forgiveness at dawn). ﴿الْمُسْتَغْفِرِينَ﴾ (those who seek forgiveness): those who ask Allah for forgiveness. Maghfirah (forgiveness) is the concealment of a sin and overlooking it, derived from al-ghafr, which is covering with protection. From it comes al-mighfar (the helmet) that is placed on the head during war, for it combines covering and protection. That is, they ask for forgiveness.

As for His saying: ﴿بِالْأَسْحَارِ﴾ (at dawn). The bā' here indicates time (zarfiyyah), meaning "in," and al-asḥār is the plural of saḥar, which is the last part of the night. That is, they ask for forgiveness at this time of the night, at its end. Why? First: because it is the time when Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, descends to the lowest heaven. "Indeed Allah, the Exalted, descends to the lowest heaven when the last third of the night remains, and He says: Who calls upon Me, that I may answer him? Who asks of Me, that I may give him? Who seeks forgiveness from Me, that I may forgive him?"[[A hadith agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1145) and Muslim (758/168) from Abu Hurairah.]] Second: it is the time when they finish the tahajjud (night prayer) and their work, and a person, when he finishes worship, is required to seek forgiveness from Allah. For this reason, it is prescribed for us to seek Allah's forgiveness three times after the prayer. And Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, commanded us to seek forgiveness during Hajj. When?

* Student: ﴿فَإِذَا قَضَيْتُمْ مَنَاسِكَكُمْ﴾ ("When you have completed your rites").
* Shaykh: ﴿ثُمَّ أَفِيضُوا مِنْ حَيْثُ أَفَاضَ النَّاسُ وَاسْتَغْفِرُوا اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ [Al-Baqarah 2:199] ("Then depart from where the people depart, and seek forgiveness of Allah. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful"). Likewise, also at the end of the night, after tahajjud, the one who performs tahajjud asks Allah for forgiveness. This asking for forgiveness after finishing worship contains complete humility before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and that a person does not become conceited about his deed but fears falling short in it. Therefore he seeks forgiveness for whatever deficiency and shortcoming occurred in this worship.

Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿شَهِدَ اللَّهُ أَنَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ وَأُولُو الْعِلْمِ قَائِمًا بِالْقِسْطِ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ﴾ [Aal 'Imran 3:18] ("Allah bears witness that there is no deity except Him, and [so do] the angels and those of knowledge – standing in justice. There is no deity except Him, the Almighty, the Wise"). ﴿شَهِدَ اللَّهُ﴾ (Allah bears witness). Testimony (shahadah) may be by speech and may be by action. Allah's testimony for Himself of His sole divinity is like His testimony for His Messenger (ﷺ) that He sent down the Book to him. Here He said: ﴿شَهِدَ اللَّهُ أَنَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ﴾, and He said: ﴿لَكِنِ اللَّهُ يَشْهَدُ بِمَا أَنْزَلَ إِلَيْكَ أَنْزَلَهُ بِعِلْمِهِ وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ يَشْهَدُونَ﴾ [An-Nisa 4:166] ("But Allah bears witness to what He has sent down to you; He sent it down with His knowledge, and the angels bear witness"). Here He said: ﴿شَهِدَ اللَّهُ أَنَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ﴾. So His testimony for Himself of oneness, and His testimony for His Prophet (ﷺ) of prophethood, along with the angels. Testimony, as I said, is verbal, as in this verse, and as in the verse of An-Nisa: ﴿لَكِنِ اللَّهُ يَشْهَدُ بِمَا أَنْزَلَ إِلَيْكَ﴾, and it is practical, which is what Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, shows of His signs. What He shows of His signs is testimony to His oneness. All creation bears witness to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, of His oneness, either by the tongue of speech or by the tongue of state. Likewise, His supporting the Prophet (ﷺ) with victory and making the final outcome his is a testimony that he is truly the Messenger of Allah. So Allah's testimony for Himself of oneness, I say, is by speech and is by action. In the noble verse, is the testimony by speech or by action? By speech: ﴿شَهِدَ اللَّهُ﴾, that is, He informed about Himself that He bears witness that there is no deity except Him, the Glorified and Exalted. ﴿لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ﴾ (there is no deity except Him). We have encountered this many times, and every Muslim must know its meaning and know its requirement as well. Its meaning is that there is no worshipped one with true right except Allah. This is the meaning of the verse. Everything worshipped besides Allah is false, and even if it is called a deity, its divinity is merely a name. It does not deserve divinity, even if those people worshipped it and took it as a god. But the one worshipped besides Allah is not in himself a god. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿مَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ إِلَّا أَسْمَاءً سَمَّيْتُمُوهَا أَنْتُمْ وَآبَاؤُكُمْ مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ بِهَا مِنْ سُلْطَانٍ﴾ [Yusuf 12:40] ("You worship not besides Him except names you have named, you and your fathers, for which Allah has sent down no authority"). And are they names that correspond to reality, when they are false deities? This is impossible. So ﴿لَا إِلَهَ﴾ means: there is no worshipped one with true right except Allah. As for a false worshipped one, it exists, as Allah the Exalted named the idols "gods" in His saying: ﴿وَاتَّخَذُوا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ آلِهَةً لَعَلَّهُمْ يُنْصَرُونَ﴾ [Ya-Sin 36:74] ("And they have taken gods besides Allah, hoping they would be helped"), and He said: ﴿فَمَا أَغْنَتْ عَنْهُمْ آلِهَتُهُمُ الَّتِي يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ لَمَّا جَاءَ أَمْرُ رَبِّكَ﴾ [Hud 11:101] ("So their gods, which they invoked besides Allah, did not avail them at all when the command of your Lord came"), and He said: ﴿إِنَّكُمْ وَمَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ حَصَبُ جَهَنَّمَ﴾ [Al-Anbiya 21:98] ("Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are fuel for Hell"). The verses on this are many. And He said: ﴿فَلَا تَدْعُ مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلَهًا آخَرَ فَتَكُونَ مِنَ الْمُعَذَّبِينَ﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara 26:213] ("So do not invoke with Allah another deity, or you will be among those punished"), and ﴿وَلَا تَدْعُ مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلَهًا آخَرَ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ كُلُّ شَيْءٍ هَالِكٌ إِلَّا وَجْهَهُ﴾ [Al-Qasas 28:88] ("And do not invoke with Allah another deity. There is no deity except Him. Everything will perish except His Face"). All these worshipped things are called gods, but is this name correspondent to reality? No. So the meaning of "There is no deity except Allah" is: there is no worshipped one with true right except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. It follows that whoever is the one worshipped must be the Lord, just as it follows that whoever is the Lord must be worshipped alone. So His oneness in divinity includes His oneness in lordship. For this reason Allah built the oneness of divinity upon the oneness of lordship in His saying: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اعْبُدُوا رَبَّكُمُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ وَالَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ﴾ [Al-Baqarah 2:21] ("O mankind, worship your Lord, who created you and those before you").

As for His saying: ﴿أَنَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ﴾ (that there is no deity except Him, and [so do] the angels), it is conjoined to the Name of Majesty, "Allah": that is, the angels also bear witness that there is no deity except Allah. The third: ﴿وَأُولُو الْعِلْمِ﴾ (and those of knowledge), the people of knowledge whom Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, has granted knowledge, also bear witness that there is no deity except Allah. No one is more certain or stronger in faith than the people of knowledge. For this reason they are the people of awe, as He said: ﴿إِنَّمَا يَخْشَى اللَّهَ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ الْعُلَمَاءُ﴾ [Fatir 35:28] ("Only those among His servants who have knowledge fear Allah"). What is meant here by "those of knowledge" is not worldly knowledge, nor knowledge of the natures of things, nor knowledge of the secrets of the universe, but rather the knowledge of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Those of knowledge of Allah, who knew Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, through His cosmic and legislative signs, are those who testified to His oneness.

﴿قَائِمًا بِالْقِسْطِ﴾ (standing in justice). ﴿قَائِمًا﴾ (standing) is a circumstantial state (ḥāl) of ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ (Allah), meaning: while He is standing in justice, that is, in justice: in justice in His legislative rulings, and justice in His judicial and retributive rulings. He is just in His legislative rulings; there is no oppression in the legislative rulings of Allah, the Exalted. All of them are justice. Moreover, while they are justice, they include grace, pardon, and beneficence. For this reason Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا﴾ [Al-Baqarah 2:286] ("Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity"), and He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿أُولَئِكَ يُسَارِعُونَ فِي الْخَيْرَاتِ وَهُمْ لَهَا سَابِقُونَ (٦١) وَلَا نُكَلِّفُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا﴾ [Al-Mu'minun 23:61–62] ("Those hasten toward good deeds, and they are foremost in them. And We do not burden a soul except [with what it can bear]"). This is an addition beyond justice, because it includes pardon and forgiveness. Likewise in recompense: He is just in His recompense, He never wrongs anyone at all, but He is also one of grace in His recompense, for He rewards a good deed tenfold up to seven hundred times and to many multiples, and rewards an evil deed with its like or pardons it, except for one who is a disbeliever and not deserving of pardon, so he is not pardoned. So ﴿قَائِمًا بِالْقِسْطِ﴾ is in His legislative rulings and in His judgment. Likewise He is standing in justice by separating between His servants. Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, judges for the oppressed against the oppressor, either by answering the supplication of the oppressed if he prays against his oppressor in this world, as the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said to Mu'adh ibn Jabal when he sent him to Yemen: "Beware of their most precious possessions, and fear the supplication of the oppressed, for there is no barrier between it and Allah."[[A hadith agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1496) and Muslim (19/29) from Ibn 'Abbas.]] Or by taking from the oppressor from his good deeds on the Day of Resurrection, as the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whom do you count as bankrupt among you?" They said: "One who has neither dirham nor goods." Or they said: "Nor dinar." He said: "The bankrupt is one who comes on the Day of Resurrection with good deeds like mountains, but he has wronged this one, struck that one, reviled this one, and taken the wealth of this one. So this one takes from his good deeds, and that one takes from his good deeds, and this one takes from his good deeds. If some of his good deeds remain, [well]; otherwise, their sins are taken and cast upon him, and he is cast into the Fire."[[Narrated by Muslim (2581/59) from Abu Hurairah, with the wording "Do you know who is the bankrupt?"]] So there must be justice among the servants. For this reason the scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, said: the rights between the servants are from the register from which Allah leaves nothing out, so the oppressed must be avenged against the oppressor. If a sayer says: Are not people afflicted with calamities of fear, hunger, loss of wealth, lives, and fruits? The answer: Yes. If they say: Is this not oppression? The answer: No, it is not oppression, because this is by what the hands of people have earned: ﴿ظَهَرَ الْفَسَادُ فِي الْبَرِّ وَالْبَحْرِ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ أَيْدِي النَّاسِ لِيُذِيقَهُمْ بَعْضَ الَّذِي عَمِلُوا لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ﴾ [Ar-Rum 30:41] ("Corruption has appeared on land and sea by [reason of] what the hands of people have earned, that He may let them taste part of [the consequence of] what they have done that they might return"). So these calamities are a grace, because their purpose is the discipline of creation and deterring them so that they return to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. This is not oppression at all; rather it is recompense for deeds, for a praiseworthy end, which is people's return from their oppression. And Allah, the Exalted, has said: ﴿وَلَوْ يُؤَاخِذُ اللَّهُ النَّاسَ بِمَا كَسَبُوا مَا تَرَكَ عَلَى ظَهْرِهَا مِنْ دَابَّةٍ وَلَكِنْ يُؤَخِّرُهُمْ إِلَى أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى﴾ [Fatir 35:45] ("If Allah were to impose blame on the people for what they have earned, He would not leave upon it [the earth] a creature, but He defers them to an specified term").

The difference between qist and iqsat has passed us, and we said that qasata means "jara" (acted unjustly), and aqsata means "adala" (acted justly). Here He said: ﴿قَائِمًا بِالْقِسْطِ﴾, because qist itself is justice, but qasata as a verb means "jara" (oppressed), and aqsata means "adala" (was just), that is, it established justice, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿وَنَضَعُ الْمَوَازِينَ الْقِسْطَ لِيَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ﴾ [Al-Anbiya 21:47] ("And We will set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection").

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verses 15–19 (part 6 of 6):

﴿Standing firm in justice; there is no god but Him.﴾ This is a judgment that follows the testimony. God bore witness for Himself that there is no god but Him, and He also passed judgment for Himself that there is no god but Him. Thus testimony and judgment are combined in His speech, He being a witness for Himself and a judge over Himself in regard to divinity. This sentence, ﴿there is no god but Him﴾, is therefore both a judgment and a confirmation, because what is known in legal hearings and proceedings is that testimony is given first and then the verdict is issued. God, exalted is He, first bore witness and informed of who bore witness with Him, and secondly He passed judgment, saying: ﴿there is no god but Him﴾.

It has already been noted that the theologians (al-mutakallimun) explain this great sentence as meaning what? The one capable of creating (al-qadir 'ala al-ikhtira'). They interpreted it in terms of what the polytheists acknowledge, though they were not monotheists (muwahhidun). The polytheists affirm that God is the One capable of everything, that God is the Creator, the Provider, the One who gives life and causes death, the One who manages all affairs. Yet are they monotheists? No. Rather, they are polytheists whom the Messenger ﷺ fought, because they did not realize the meaning of "there is no god but Allah." It is astonishing that these polytheists should understand the meaning of "there is no god but Allah" better than these theologians. Many of the later scholars as well, when you read their books, you find that their discussion of divinity revolves only around establishing lordship (rububiyyah). This is a great deficiency.
