He informed the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, of the truth, with truthfulness. So success came from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, through the testing of these three. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, boycotted them and commanded that they be boycotted. After forty nights had passed, he commanded them to separate from their wives. When the messenger of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to Ka'b, may Allah be pleased with him, commanding him to separate from his wife, he said: "Should I divorce her?" He said: "No, but separate from her." Did he say, "By Allah, this is my wife, with whom I sleep tonight?" Or did he say, "Go back to your family"? "Go back to your family." He said, "I hear and obey." So they endured this great patience: first in truthfulness, and second in this boycott. Ka'b, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "I would greet the Prophet ﷺ, and I did not know whether he moved his lips to return the greeting or not." Allah is greatest! The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was the best of people in character, the greatest in cheerfulness, and the best in returning greetings. Ka'b would greet him and not know whether he returned the greeting. And he would greet Abu Qatadah, his cousin, who was the most beloved person to him, and Abu Qatadah would not return the greeting. Abu Qatadah, may Allah be pleased with him. Even if you came today in tribal zeal, would one leave his cousin over such matters? Never, and Allah knows best, one would not. But Abu Qatadah, may Allah be pleased with him, did not return Ka'b's greeting. Ka'b said: "I said to him, 'I beseech you by Allah, do you know that I love Allah and His Messenger?'" He stayed silent for a moment and then said, "Allah knows best." He did not answer with a yes or no. He said, "Allah knows best." And Allah knows best that Abu Qatadah did not intend by that a reply to Ka'b. He intended to inform that Allah, Glorified and Exalted, is more knowing than anyone. But after this great patience, what was the result? The result was the revelation of verses recited concerning them until the Day of Resurrection. Their remembrance will never be forgotten. Perhaps someone better than them among the Companions may be forgotten, but these will not be forgotten. And how can we match the great reward for this patience? ﴿And [He turned in forgiveness to] the three who were left behind﴾ [at-Tawbah 118]. That is, He turned in forgiveness to the three who were left behind. ﴿Until, when the earth constricted for them despite its vastness and their souls confined them, and they were certain that there is no refuge from Allah except in Him. Then He turned to them so they might repent. Indeed, Allah is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful﴾ [at-Tawbah 118]. Then He commanded the believers to do likewise, to be like them, saying: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and be with the truthful﴾. The point is that truthfulness is a great, lofty, elevated character that none attains except one who is granted success, until he is in the second rank among those upon whom Allah has bestowed favor. «A man continues to speak the truth and strive for truthfulness until he is recorded with Allah as a *siddiq*»[[Hadith agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6094), and Muslim (2607 / 105), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud.]].

* * *

* Student: I seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿The patient, the truthful, the devout, the spenders, and those who seek forgiveness before dawn﴾ (17). ﴿Allah bears witness that there is no deity except Him, and the angels and those of knowledge, [that He is] standing in justice. There is no deity except Him, the Almighty, the Wise﴾ (18). ﴿Indeed, the religion in the sight of Allah is Islam. And those who were given the Scripture did not differ except after knowledge had come to them, out of jealousy among themselves. And whoever disbelieves in the signs of Allah – indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning﴾ (19) [Aal Imran 17-19].

* Shaykh: I seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, the Exalted, said in describing those who fear their Lord: ﴿For those who fear Allah are gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide eternally, and purified spouses, and approval from Allah. And Allah is Seeing of His servants﴾ [Aal Imran 15].

﴿الصَّابِرِينَ﴾ in the rest of their attributes. ﴿الصَّابِرِينَ﴾ (the patient). The discussion of patience (sabr), its meaning linguistically and in the Sharia, has already preceded. It is divided into three categories: patience in obedience to Allah, patience in refraining from disobedience to Allah, and patience in the painful decrees of Allah. Then He said: ﴿وَالْقَانِتِينَ﴾ (and the devout). Al-qanitin (the devout) is the active participle from al-qunut (constant obedience). ﴿وَالصَّادِقِينَ﴾ (and the truthful). The discussion of truthfulness (sidq) has also preceded, and we explained that it is truthfulness in speech, action, and belief, and that it is truthfulness toward Allah and truthfulness toward the servants of Allah. Then He said: ﴿وَالْقَانِتِينَ﴾ (and the devout). This is also one of their attributes, qunut. Qunut is applied to several meanings, and the most fitting of them for this verse is that qunut here means the continuance of obedience together with humility and submission to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, such that a person is constant in obedience to Allah and turns devotedly toward Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, in his obedience. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿حَافِظُوا عَلَى الصَّلَوَاتِ وَالصَّلَاةِ الْوُسْطَى وَقُومُوا لِلَّهِ قَانِتِينَ﴾ [Al-Baqarah 2:238] ("Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer, and stand before Allah devoutly obedient"), meaning: humbly submissive. For this reason, when this verse was revealed, they were commanded to be silent and forbidden to speak (during prayer). So the qanit is one who constantly obeys Allah, with humility and presence of heart, and who is committed to turning toward Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. ﴿وَالْمُنْفِقِينَ﴾ (and the spenders). Al-munfiqin is from anfaqa, meaning to expend. Nafaqah is the spending of wealth. Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, has stated spending here without specifying it, but in other verses He mentioned the measure for spending and mentioned what is spent on or for whom. He said: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ إِذَا أَنْفَقُوا لَمْ يُسْرِفُوا وَلَمْ يَقْتُرُوا وَكَانَ بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ قَوَامًا﴾ [Al-Furqan 25:67] ("And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor stingy, but are ever between that [being moderate]"). He, the Glorified and Exalted, also said: ﴿وَلَا تَجْعَلْ يَدَكَ مَغْلُولَةً إِلَى عُنُقِكَ وَلَا تَبْسُطْهَا كُلَّ الْبَسْطِ﴾ [Al-Isra 17:29] ("And do not make your hand chained to your neck, nor extend it completely open"). This is the measure of spending: that a person should be neither stingy nor extravagant. If we take this as the measure, it varies according to circumstances, times, and places. Spending may be extravagance for one person and not extravagance for another. The spending of the poor is not like the spending of the rich. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿لِيُنْفِقْ ذُو سَعَةٍ مِنْ سَعَتِهِ وَمَنْ قُدِرَ عَلَيْهِ رِزْقُهُ فَلْيُنْفِقْ مِمَّا آتَاهُ اللَّهُ﴾ [At-Talaq 65:7] ("Let a man of wealth spend from his wealth, and he whose provision is restricted – let him spend from what Allah has given him"). The spending of the middle-income person is between them. Likewise, it varies with time. Sometimes the time is a time of general prosperity in this society, so extravagance in a society that is less prosperous is not extravagance with regard to this society. It also varies with times: at some times wealth is abundant and available, so spending much of it is not extravagance, and at other times the situation is the reverse. In any case, Allah has mentioned spending here in the verse without qualification, and He mentioned its measure in several verses, among them in Surah al-Furqan: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ إِذَا أَنْفَقُوا لَمْ يُسْرِفُوا وَلَمْ يَقْتُرُوا وَكَانَ بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ قَوَامًا﴾. As for what it is spent on or for whom? Allah, the Glorified, said: ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ مَاذَا يُنْفِقُونَ قُلْ مَا أَنْفَقْتُمْ مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَلِلْوَالِدَيْنِ وَالْأَقْرَبِينَ وَالْيَتَامَى وَالْمَسَاكِينِ وَابْنِ السَّبِيلِ﴾ [Al-Baqarah 2:215] ("They ask you what they should spend. Say: Whatever good you spend is for parents, relatives, orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer"). So the channels of expenditure: each channel is one in which there is need, or in which the Muslims have need of it. Either it is in need, or the Muslims are in need of it. So spending in the way of Allah is for whose need? It is for the need of the Muslims for jihad in the way of Allah, because in jihad in the way of Allah is the elevation of the word of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and the preservation of His Sharia. Spending on the poor is for whose need? It is for the need of the poor, not for the need of the Muslims; rather, it is for the need of the poor. So you always see that spending is either to relieve the need of a needy person, or to relieve the need of the Muslims in general, that is, in public interests. The main point is that these are spenders; those who are among the people of Paradise are spenders, but their spending is governed by Sharia controls.

﴿وَالْمُسْتَغْفِرِينَ بِالْأَسْحَارِ﴾ (and those who seek forgiveness at dawn). ﴿الْمُسْتَغْفِرِينَ﴾ (those who seek forgiveness): those who ask Allah for forgiveness. Maghfirah (forgiveness) is the concealment of a sin and overlooking it, derived from al-ghafr, which is covering with protection. From it comes al-mighfar (the helmet) that is placed on the head during war, for it combines covering and protection. That is, they ask for forgiveness.

As for His saying: ﴿بِالْأَسْحَارِ﴾ (at dawn). The bā' here indicates time (zarfiyyah), meaning "in," and al-asḥār is the plural of saḥar, which is the last part of the night. That is, they ask for forgiveness at this time of the night, at its end. Why? First: because it is the time when Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, descends to the lowest heaven. "Indeed Allah, the Exalted, descends to the lowest heaven when the last third of the night remains, and He says: Who calls upon Me, that I may answer him? Who asks of Me, that I may give him? Who seeks forgiveness from Me, that I may forgive him?"[[A hadith agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1145) and Muslim (758/168) from Abu Hurairah.]] Second: it is the time when they finish the tahajjud (night prayer) and their work, and a person, when he finishes worship, is required to seek forgiveness from Allah. For this reason, it is prescribed for us to seek Allah's forgiveness three times after the prayer. And Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, commanded us to seek forgiveness during Hajj. When?

* Student: ﴿فَإِذَا قَضَيْتُمْ مَنَاسِكَكُمْ﴾ ("When you have completed your rites").
* Shaykh: ﴿ثُمَّ أَفِيضُوا مِنْ حَيْثُ أَفَاضَ النَّاسُ وَاسْتَغْفِرُوا اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ [Al-Baqarah 2:199] ("Then depart from where the people depart, and seek forgiveness of Allah. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful"). Likewise, also at the end of the night, after tahajjud, the one who performs tahajjud asks Allah for forgiveness. This asking for forgiveness after finishing worship contains complete humility before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and that a person does not become conceited about his deed but fears falling short in it. Therefore he seeks forgiveness for whatever deficiency and shortcoming occurred in this worship.

Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿شَهِدَ اللَّهُ أَنَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ وَأُولُو الْعِلْمِ قَائِمًا بِالْقِسْطِ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ﴾ [Aal 'Imran 3:18] ("Allah bears witness that there is no deity except Him, and [so do] the angels and those of knowledge – standing in justice. There is no deity except Him, the Almighty, the Wise"). ﴿شَهِدَ اللَّهُ﴾ (Allah bears witness). Testimony (shahadah) may be by speech and may be by action. Allah's testimony for Himself of His sole divinity is like His testimony for His Messenger (ﷺ) that He sent down the Book to him. Here He said: ﴿شَهِدَ اللَّهُ أَنَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ﴾, and He said: ﴿لَكِنِ اللَّهُ يَشْهَدُ بِمَا أَنْزَلَ إِلَيْكَ أَنْزَلَهُ بِعِلْمِهِ وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ يَشْهَدُونَ﴾ [An-Nisa 4:166] ("But Allah bears witness to what He has sent down to you; He sent it down with His knowledge, and the angels bear witness"). Here He said: ﴿شَهِدَ اللَّهُ أَنَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ﴾. So His testimony for Himself of oneness, and His testimony for His Prophet (ﷺ) of prophethood, along with the angels. Testimony, as I said, is verbal, as in this verse, and as in the verse of An-Nisa: ﴿لَكِنِ اللَّهُ يَشْهَدُ بِمَا أَنْزَلَ إِلَيْكَ﴾, and it is practical, which is what Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, shows of His signs. What He shows of His signs is testimony to His oneness. All creation bears witness to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, of His oneness, either by the tongue of speech or by the tongue of state. Likewise, His supporting the Prophet (ﷺ) with victory and making the final outcome his is a testimony that he is truly the Messenger of Allah. So Allah's testimony for Himself of oneness, I say, is by speech and is by action. In the noble verse, is the testimony by speech or by action? By speech: ﴿شَهِدَ اللَّهُ﴾, that is, He informed about Himself that He bears witness that there is no deity except Him, the Glorified and Exalted. ﴿لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ﴾ (there is no deity except Him). We have encountered this many times, and every Muslim must know its meaning and know its requirement as well. Its meaning is that there is no worshipped one with true right except Allah. This is the meaning of the verse. Everything worshipped besides Allah is false, and even if it is called a deity, its divinity is merely a name. It does not deserve divinity, even if those people worshipped it and took it as a god. But the one worshipped besides Allah is not in himself a god. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿مَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ إِلَّا أَسْمَاءً سَمَّيْتُمُوهَا أَنْتُمْ وَآبَاؤُكُمْ مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ بِهَا مِنْ سُلْطَانٍ﴾ [Yusuf 12:40] ("You worship not besides Him except names you have named, you and your fathers, for which Allah has sent down no authority"). And are they names that correspond to reality, when they are false deities? This is impossible. So ﴿لَا إِلَهَ﴾ means: there is no worshipped one with true right except Allah. As for a false worshipped one, it exists, as Allah the Exalted named the idols "gods" in His saying: ﴿وَاتَّخَذُوا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ آلِهَةً لَعَلَّهُمْ يُنْصَرُونَ﴾ [Ya-Sin 36:74] ("And they have taken gods besides Allah, hoping they would be helped"), and He said: ﴿فَمَا أَغْنَتْ عَنْهُمْ آلِهَتُهُمُ الَّتِي يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ لَمَّا جَاءَ أَمْرُ رَبِّكَ﴾ [Hud 11:101] ("So their gods, which they invoked besides Allah, did not avail them at all when the command of your Lord came"), and He said: ﴿إِنَّكُمْ وَمَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ حَصَبُ جَهَنَّمَ﴾ [Al-Anbiya 21:98] ("Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are fuel for Hell"). The verses on this are many. And He said: ﴿فَلَا تَدْعُ مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلَهًا آخَرَ فَتَكُونَ مِنَ الْمُعَذَّبِينَ﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara 26:213] ("So do not invoke with Allah another deity, or you will be among those punished"), and ﴿وَلَا تَدْعُ مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلَهًا آخَرَ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ كُلُّ شَيْءٍ هَالِكٌ إِلَّا وَجْهَهُ﴾ [Al-Qasas 28:88] ("And do not invoke with Allah another deity. There is no deity except Him. Everything will perish except His Face"). All these worshipped things are called gods, but is this name correspondent to reality? No. So the meaning of "There is no deity except Allah" is: there is no worshipped one with true right except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. It follows that whoever is the one worshipped must be the Lord, just as it follows that whoever is the Lord must be worshipped alone. So His oneness in divinity includes His oneness in lordship. For this reason Allah built the oneness of divinity upon the oneness of lordship in His saying: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اعْبُدُوا رَبَّكُمُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ وَالَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ﴾ [Al-Baqarah 2:21] ("O mankind, worship your Lord, who created you and those before you").

As for His saying: ﴿أَنَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ﴾ (that there is no deity except Him, and [so do] the angels), it is conjoined to the Name of Majesty, "Allah": that is, the angels also bear witness that there is no deity except Allah. The third: ﴿وَأُولُو الْعِلْمِ﴾ (and those of knowledge), the people of knowledge whom Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, has granted knowledge, also bear witness that there is no deity except Allah. No one is more certain or stronger in faith than the people of knowledge. For this reason they are the people of awe, as He said: ﴿إِنَّمَا يَخْشَى اللَّهَ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ الْعُلَمَاءُ﴾ [Fatir 35:28] ("Only those among His servants who have knowledge fear Allah"). What is meant here by "those of knowledge" is not worldly knowledge, nor knowledge of the natures of things, nor knowledge of the secrets of the universe, but rather the knowledge of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Those of knowledge of Allah, who knew Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, through His cosmic and legislative signs, are those who testified to His oneness.

﴿قَائِمًا بِالْقِسْطِ﴾ (standing in justice). ﴿قَائِمًا﴾ (standing) is a circumstantial state (ḥāl) of ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ (Allah), meaning: while He is standing in justice, that is, in justice: in justice in His legislative rulings, and justice in His judicial and retributive rulings. He is just in His legislative rulings; there is no oppression in the legislative rulings of Allah, the Exalted. All of them are justice. Moreover, while they are justice, they include grace, pardon, and beneficence. For this reason Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا﴾ [Al-Baqarah 2:286] ("Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity"), and He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿أُولَئِكَ يُسَارِعُونَ فِي الْخَيْرَاتِ وَهُمْ لَهَا سَابِقُونَ (٦١) وَلَا نُكَلِّفُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا﴾ [Al-Mu'minun 23:61–62] ("Those hasten toward good deeds, and they are foremost in them. And We do not burden a soul except [with what it can bear]"). This is an addition beyond justice, because it includes pardon and forgiveness. Likewise in recompense: He is just in His recompense, He never wrongs anyone at all, but He is also one of grace in His recompense, for He rewards a good deed tenfold up to seven hundred times and to many multiples, and rewards an evil deed with its like or pardons it, except for one who is a disbeliever and not deserving of pardon, so he is not pardoned. So ﴿قَائِمًا بِالْقِسْطِ﴾ is in His legislative rulings and in His judgment. Likewise He is standing in justice by separating between His servants. Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, judges for the oppressed against the oppressor, either by answering the supplication of the oppressed if he prays against his oppressor in this world, as the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said to Mu'adh ibn Jabal when he sent him to Yemen: "Beware of their most precious possessions, and fear the supplication of the oppressed, for there is no barrier between it and Allah."[[A hadith agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1496) and Muslim (19/29) from Ibn 'Abbas.]] Or by taking from the oppressor from his good deeds on the Day of Resurrection, as the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whom do you count as bankrupt among you?" They said: "One who has neither dirham nor goods." Or they said: "Nor dinar." He said: "The bankrupt is one who comes on the Day of Resurrection with good deeds like mountains, but he has wronged this one, struck that one, reviled this one, and taken the wealth of this one. So this one takes from his good deeds, and that one takes from his good deeds, and this one takes from his good deeds. If some of his good deeds remain, [well]; otherwise, their sins are taken and cast upon him, and he is cast into the Fire."[[Narrated by Muslim (2581/59) from Abu Hurairah, with the wording "Do you know who is the bankrupt?"]] So there must be justice among the servants. For this reason the scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, said: the rights between the servants are from the register from which Allah leaves nothing out, so the oppressed must be avenged against the oppressor. If a sayer says: Are not people afflicted with calamities of fear, hunger, loss of wealth, lives, and fruits? The answer: Yes. If they say: Is this not oppression? The answer: No, it is not oppression, because this is by what the hands of people have earned: ﴿ظَهَرَ الْفَسَادُ فِي الْبَرِّ وَالْبَحْرِ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ أَيْدِي النَّاسِ لِيُذِيقَهُمْ بَعْضَ الَّذِي عَمِلُوا لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ﴾ [Ar-Rum 30:41] ("Corruption has appeared on land and sea by [reason of] what the hands of people have earned, that He may let them taste part of [the consequence of] what they have done that they might return"). So these calamities are a grace, because their purpose is the discipline of creation and deterring them so that they return to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. This is not oppression at all; rather it is recompense for deeds, for a praiseworthy end, which is people's return from their oppression. And Allah, the Exalted, has said: ﴿وَلَوْ يُؤَاخِذُ اللَّهُ النَّاسَ بِمَا كَسَبُوا مَا تَرَكَ عَلَى ظَهْرِهَا مِنْ دَابَّةٍ وَلَكِنْ يُؤَخِّرُهُمْ إِلَى أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى﴾ [Fatir 35:45] ("If Allah were to impose blame on the people for what they have earned, He would not leave upon it [the earth] a creature, but He defers them to an specified term").

The difference between qist and iqsat has passed us, and we said that qasata means "jara" (acted unjustly), and aqsata means "adala" (acted justly). Here He said: ﴿قَائِمًا بِالْقِسْطِ﴾, because qist itself is justice, but qasata as a verb means "jara" (oppressed), and aqsata means "adala" (was just), that is, it established justice, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿وَنَضَعُ الْمَوَازِينَ الْقِسْطَ لِيَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ﴾ [Al-Anbiya 21:47] ("And We will set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection").

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verses 15–19 (part 6 of 6):

﴿Standing firm in justice; there is no god but Him.﴾ This is a judgment that follows the testimony. God bore witness for Himself that there is no god but Him, and He also passed judgment for Himself that there is no god but Him. Thus testimony and judgment are combined in His speech, He being a witness for Himself and a judge over Himself in regard to divinity. This sentence, ﴿there is no god but Him﴾, is therefore both a judgment and a confirmation, because what is known in legal hearings and proceedings is that testimony is given first and then the verdict is issued. God, exalted is He, first bore witness and informed of who bore witness with Him, and secondly He passed judgment, saying: ﴿there is no god but Him﴾.

It has already been noted that the theologians (al-mutakallimun) explain this great sentence as meaning what? The one capable of creating (al-qadir 'ala al-ikhtira'). They interpreted it in terms of what the polytheists acknowledge, though they were not monotheists (muwahhidun). The polytheists affirm that God is the One capable of everything, that God is the Creator, the Provider, the One who gives life and causes death, the One who manages all affairs. Yet are they monotheists? No. Rather, they are polytheists whom the Messenger ﷺ fought, because they did not realize the meaning of "there is no god but Allah." It is astonishing that these polytheists should understand the meaning of "there is no god but Allah" better than these theologians. Many of the later scholars as well, when you read their books, you find that their discussion of divinity revolves only around establishing lordship (rububiyyah). This is a great deficiency. Lordship is affirmed even by the polytheists, and the Messenger ﷺ did not make them monotheists by it, nor did he make this acknowledgment something that removes them from disbelief, nor a protection for their blood and property, nor a means of salvation from the Fire. Rather, he fought them, made their blood and property lawful, and took their women and offspring captive, while they were saying: "Our Lord is Allah." When they were asked who created the heavens and the earth, they said: "Allah." When they were asked who created them, they said: "Allah." When they were asked who gives life and causes death, they said: "Allah." When they were asked who manages the affair, they said: "Allah." Yet this faith did not benefit them. Acknowledging that God is the Creator of the universe, its manager, and the one who disposes of it is not sufficient for tawhid at all. Whoever dies upon this, without believing that there is no true object of worship except Allah, has not died upon tawhid.

As for His saying ﴿the Mighty, the Wise﴾: ﴿al-'Aziz﴾ means the Possessor of might (al-'izzah). Might is explained in three meanings: might of rank (izzat al-qadr), might of overpowering (izzat al-qahr), and might of inaccessibility (izzat al-imtina'). As for might of rank, it means that God, exalted is He, possesses great rank, sovereignty, honour, and majesty, along with other meanings of rank and elevation. The second is might of inaccessibility, meaning that He is beyond harm reaching Him. From this is the saying about hard, firm land: "ardun 'izaz," meaning strong and firm, nothing reaches it. The third is might of overpowering, meaning He is the one who prevails over everything. From it is His saying: ﴿He said, "Commit her to my care, and he has overpowered me in speech."﴾ [Sad 23], meaning he overcame me. These three kinds of might belong to God, exalted is He, in every respect. He is the One of great rank; He is the One of inaccessibility, to whom no deficiency can attach in any way; and He is the Overpowering One whom nothing overpowers. The pre-Islamic poet said:

"Where is the escape, when the Seeker is God?
And the one with the split lip is the defeated, not the victor."

So God, exalted is He, overpowers everything. As for ﴿the Wise﴾, it derives from judgment (hukm) and perfection (ihkam). He possesses judgment and perfection. Judgment divides into cosmic (kawni) and legislative (shar'i). Perfection means excellence, and excellence entails wisdom (hikmah), which is placing things in their proper places. Wisdom in turn divides into two kinds: formal wisdom, meaning that a thing in this form is in accordance with wisdom (and if we wish, we may say "formal" instead, lest a corrupt meaning be understood), and wisdom of state and wisdom of end. The wisdom of state is what the thing is in its present condition; the wisdom of end is what the thing leads to. Likewise, wisdom exists in cosmic rulings and in legislative rulings. On this basis, if you multiply two by two in terms of wisdom, you reach four: wisdom of state in the cosmic ruling, wisdom of state in the legislative ruling, wisdom of end in the cosmic ruling, and wisdom of end in the legislative ruling. Is that right? What did we say?

* Student: Wisdom of state in the legislative ruling and in the cosmic ruling.
* The Shaykh: That is two.
* Student: And wisdom of end in the legislative ruling and in the cosmic ruling.
* The Shaykh: Correct, that is four. Good. So ﴿the Wise﴾ is from judgment and perfection. We mentioned that judgment is cosmic and legislative. Since this division has already passed over us, it only remains for us to recall it, so let us seek an example of cosmic judgment, a verse that mentions cosmic judgment?
* Student: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Had Allah willed, we would not have associated [others with Him]﴾ [al-An'am 148].
* The Shaykh: No.
* Student: ﴿So I will not leave this land until my father permits me or Allah judges for me, and He is the best of judges﴾ [Yusuf 80].
* The Shaykh: Yes, ﴿So I will not leave this land until my father permits me or Allah judges for me, and He is the best of judges.﴾ Good. The legislative one?
* Student: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That is the judgment of Allah; He judges between you, and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾ [al-Mumtahanah 10].
* The Shaykh: And where is it in it?
* Student: In the surah of the women emigrants (al-Mumtahanah).
* The Shaykh: When He mentioned the ruling concerning the women emigrants and what relates to them, He said: ﴿That is the judgment of Allah; He judges between you, and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.﴾ Good. We said that the legislative ruling contains a wisdom of state and a wisdom of end?
* Student: The legislative ruling has a wisdom of state and a wisdom of end, such as prayer. The wisdom of state is the bowing and prostration.
* The Shaykh: That means their being in this specific form.
* Student: Their being in this specific form which the Law required. The wisdom of end is abstaining from evil deeds and from things which...
* The Shaykh: That means what results from them of praiseworthy effects and great reward, correct? Good. In cosmic matters, what is the wisdom of state?
* Student: For example, rain has a wisdom of state and a wisdom of end. The descent of rain in this manner, descending in this particular way, is formal wisdom or wisdom of state, and what results from it of plant growth in the earth and the revival of the land is wisdom of end.
* The Shaykh: Did you hear?
* The students: No.
* The Shaykh: You did not hear. He says: the descent of rain in this way, in drops, does not harm people, their livestock, or their buildings, and it covers both the high ground and the low. This is what kind of wisdom? State wisdom. The wisdom of end is what results from this rain (...) great, so that is wisdom of end. Thus the sum is that God is Wise in these respects. He says: ﴿the Mighty, the Wise﴾. Combining the two has a benefit, God willing, which you will mention in the lessons.

Let us take the lessons. God, exalted is He, says: ﴿Say, "Shall I inform you of something better than that?"﴾ to the end. Among the lessons of this verse: the importance of this news, and this is from two aspects: its introduction with "Say" (qul), and its being in the form of a question, which indicates what? Excitement and anticipation. As for the first, we have said that everything God introduces with "Say" is a command to convey it specifically, and this indicates special attention to it. Otherwise, the whole Qur'an was commanded by God to be said by the Prophet ﷺ to the community.

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: the Prophet ﷺ is a servant who is commanded and forbidden, by God's saying: ﴿Say, "Shall I inform you"﴾, and he has no share in lordship at all. He does not give life, cause death, provide sustenance, or repel harm from himself or from others, and he does not know the unseen. He is distinguished from people by what?
* The students: By prophethood.
* The Shaykh: By prophethood. ﴿Say, "I am only a human being like you, to whom it is revealed"﴾ [al-Kahf 110]. This is a distinction, and what an excellent distinction it is. He, ﷺ, also personally possesses a readiness to bear the burdens of prophethood that no one else has, as God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Allah knows best where to place His message﴾ [al-An'am 124].
* Among the lessons of this noble verse: God's care for His creation. When He mentioned what had been made attractive to people of desires among the seven matters, it was feared that people would turn toward these desires. So, out of God's care for them, He commanded His Messenger ﷺ to inform them of what is better than that.
* Among the lessons of this noble verse: the goodness of the method of teaching and calling, and that a person in the position of calling should use words that arouse attention, because when a person is told: "Shall I inform you of such and such?", he will become eager and attentive, saying: "What is it you want to inform me of?" This differs from if the speech came plainly without such a preface.
* Among the lessons of this noble verse: the permissibility of comparing two things between which there is a great difference, by His saying: ﴿something better than that﴾. It is known that everything mentioned of the seven desires is not worth anything at all in comparison with the reward of the Hereafter. The Prophet ﷺ said: "The place of a whip of one of you in Paradise is better than the world and everything in it" [narrated by al-Bukhari (3250) from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd]. Has a similar form come in the Qur'an, a comparison between two things with a great difference between them?
* Student: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The companions of Paradise on that Day are better in resting place and finer in resting-place﴾ [al-Furqan 24].
* The Shaykh: ﴿The companions of Paradise on that Day are better in resting place and finer in resting-place,﴾ correct? Indeed, God said, speaking in the manner of conceding to the opponent's claim: ﴿Is Allah better, or what they associate?﴾ [al-Naml 59].
* Among the lessons of this noble verse: that this good, which God made His servants eager for, is established for the God-fearing, by His saying: ﴿for those who have taqwa with their Lord﴾, and the meaning of taqwa has already been mentioned.
* Among the lessons of this noble verse: that this good belongs to these believers in the most honourable neighbourhood, which is the neighbourhood of the Lord of the worlds, by His saying: ﴿with their Lord are gardens﴾. The people closest to God are the companions of Paradise, and for this reason God placed them near Him, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who are near your Lord do not disdain His worship, and they exalt Him, and to Him they prostrate﴾ [al-A'raf 206].
* Among the lessons of this noble verse: the greatness of these gardens, because they are with God in His neighbourhood, exalted is He.
* Among its lessons: the reward of these God-fearing people is this great abode, comprising a bliss without parallel, by His saying: ﴿gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾. We have already mentioned the kinds of rivers.
* Among the lessons of this noble verse: exhortation to fear God, since mentioning the reward of the God-fearing contains an exhortation to taqwa.
* Among the lessons of this noble verse: God's care, exalted is He, for these people, by His saying: ﴿with their Lord﴾. And lordship here is what?
* The students: Special.
* The Shaykh: Special.
* Among the lessons of this noble verse: that these noble people enjoy every kind of bliss in God's reward: eating, drinking, and marriage. Eating and drinking are in His saying: ﴿gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾, so from the gardens they eat, and from the rivers they drink. As for marriage, He said: ﴿and purified spouses﴾. These are the foundations of the bodily pleasures: eating, drinking, and marriage.
* Among the lessons of this noble verse: the excellence of the spouses in Paradise through their being purified, ﴿and purified spouses﴾, and we have already explained that purification is both sensory and spiritual.
* Among the lessons of this noble verse: that the completion of these people's bliss is in God's good pleasure, by His saying: ﴿and good pleasure from Allah﴾. God has explained in Surah al-Tawbah that this good pleasure is the greatest bliss, saying: ﴿and good pleasure from Allah is greater﴾ [al-Tawbah 72].
* Among its lessons: affirmation of the attribute of good pleasure (ridwan) for God, by His saying: ﴿and good pleasure from Allah﴾. Is good pleasure one of the essential attributes or the active attributes?
* The students: The active.
* The Shaykh: The active, because it is connected to His will; whenever the cause of pleasure exists, pleasure exists. And every attribute that is linked to a cause is among what attributes?
* The students: The active.
* The Shaykh: The active.
* Among the lessons of this noble verse: God's encompassing of His servants with knowledge and sight, by His saying: ﴿and Allah is Seeing of the servants﴾.
* Among the lessons of this noble verse: the demonstration of God's wisdom, exalted is He, in that He divided people into two categories: the God-fearing and the disobedient. From where do we derive this? From His saying: ﴿for those who have taqwa with their Lord﴾ after His saying: ﴿Beautified for people is the love of desires﴾. This indicates that people are of two kinds: a God-fearing kind and a non-God-fearing, disobedient kind.
* Among its lessons: God, exalted is He, is Wise in that He placed taqwa with its people. By His saying: ﴿and Allah is Seeing of the servants﴾, from His sight of His servants is that He made these God-fearing and the others disobedient, and these have reward of Paradise while those have reward of the Fire. There is no doubt that this is part of God's wisdom, exalted is He, for just as He knows best where to place His message, He knows best where to place the inheritance of His message, and the inheritance of His message is knowledge, the knowledge that includes calling to God and worship.
* Among the lessons of this noble verse: that all creation are servants of God. From where do we take this?
* Student: ﴿and Allah is Seeing of the servants﴾.
* The Shaykh: What is the point of evidence?
* Student: That God, exalted is He, is Seeing of His servants.
* The Shaykh: The point of evidence is that it is general.
* Student: Because He said: ﴿of the servants﴾.
* The Shaykh: Good. Together with His saying: ﴿for those who have taqwa with their Lord are gardens﴾, this indicates that He is Seeing of all the servants: the God-fearing and the non-God-fearing.
* Among its lessons: a warning against opposing His command, because whenever a person knows that God sees him, he will refrain, or will restrain himself from opposing his Lord, since if he opposes his Lord, God sees him and will requite him according to his opposition.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verse 20:

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And if they argue with you, say: "I have submitted myself entirely to Allah, and so have those who follow me."﴾ In this verse there is evidence that the Prophet ﷺ had those among his enemies who would argue with him, and so it was. They argued with him about the foundations of the religion and its branches, they mocked him, and they raised many doubts from the time he was sent until this day of ours. People raise doubts about the Islamic religion, but Allah refuses except to perfect His light, because they want to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, while Allah perfects His light.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: those who argue with the Messenger ﷺ do not require great effort (to refute), because they argue over a matter that is clear. For this reason Allah commanded him to expose their foolishness and to say: ﴿I have submitted myself entirely to Allah, and so have those who follow me.﴾ That is: if you submit, it is for your benefit, and if you do not submit, the consequence falls upon you. It follows from this that if you know that someone is arguing with you only intending to support his position, even if it is false, you may turn away from him and say: "This is what I worship Allah with, and this is what I submit to," and leave him. Why? Because this person is obstinate and arrogant, and he is not worthy of your entering into argument or dispute with him, for he does not want the truth. If he wanted the truth, no argument would have taken place.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the followers of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ follow his example in submitting themselves to Allah and entrusting the matter to Him, based on His saying: ﴿I have submitted myself entirely to Allah, and so have those who follow me.﴾

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the face is the most honoured of the limbs, and it is the means by which submission and non-submission take place, based on His saying: ﴿I have submitted myself entirely to Allah.﴾ For the submission of the face is what constitutes compliance. For this reason, a person is at his most humble before his Lord when he is prostrating, and closest to his Lord when he is prostrating, because this is the utmost humility: that you place your most honoured limb upon the place where feet tread on the earth.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the Prophet ﷺ is one who is followed, not one who follows, based on His saying: ﴿and so have those who follow me.﴾ It follows from this that it is obligatory upon the one to whom the truth has become clear to adopt it, if he wishes to be among the followers of the Messenger ﷺ. As for the one who twists the necks of texts to fit his own saying, this is not a true follower. For some people, when they say a statement and a Qur'anic or Prophetic text comes that contradicts their statement, they try to twist the neck of the text and distort the text so that it agrees with their statement, and this is forbidden, because you are a follower, not one who is followed.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: it is not possible for the saying of any one of the people of knowledge to be a proof upon others. Why? Because all are followers, not ones who are followed. Whoever wants people to be followers of himself and not of the truth has made himself a partner in the Message. What is obligatory is that when you call to the truth, you do not want people to follow you because you are so-and-so, the son of so-and-so, but rather that people follow your statement because it is the statement indicated by the evidence.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the denouncing of foolishness and simplemindedness upon whoever argues and opposes without submitting to Allah, based on His saying: ﴿Say﴾: ﴿Have you submitted?﴾ And if we take it as a command, then the command is clear.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the demonstration of the great favour of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, upon the Arabs through the sending of the Messenger ﷺ. The evidence for this is that He said: ﴿to those who were given the Scripture and to the unlettered﴾. He distinguished between the two descriptions: between those who were given the Scripture and the unlettered one who neither reads nor writes. Those who were given the Scripture are people of knowledge and people of a book, while the unlettered are people of ignorance. But with the sending of the Messenger ﷺ, they became in truth the People of the Book. This is because the Book that was sent down upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was described by Allah as confirming what is before it of the Scripture and as a guardian over it. Thus, by the praise of Allah, these unlettered people became the true People of the Book. In this there is a great demonstration of the favour of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, upon the Arabs through the sending of the Messenger ﷺ, for they were at first unlettered and ignorant, and afterwards they became People of the Book and purified: ﴿Allah has certainly conferred favour upon the believers when He sent among them a messenger from themselves, reciting to them His verses, purifying them, and teaching them the Book and wisdom, although they were before in clear error﴾ [Al 'Imran 164].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the obligation of submission to Allah, whether we say that the interrogative is to rebuke those people and to reproach them, or we say that it is a command, for it indicates the obligation of submission and surrender to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the people of guidance are the Muslims, based on His saying: ﴿If they submit, then they have been guided.﴾ And among its benefits also: whoever does not submit is astray; and if he had known the truth, he is among those who are astray and upon whom is anger, because everyone who knows the truth and does not follow it is one upon whom is anger.

He, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿But if they turn away, then upon you is only the conveyance (of the message)﴾. In this sentence there is a warning to the one who turns away after being called. His saying: ﴿And Allah is Seeing of the servants﴾ undoubtedly warns them against opposing Him, because the Messenger ﷺ has conveyed.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that there is no obligation upon one who has conveyed except conveyance; as for guidance, it is up to Allah, based on His saying: ﴿Upon you is only the conveyance﴾. Among its benefits: the obligation of conveyance upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, based on His saying: ﴿Upon you is only the conveyance﴾. And among its benefits also, which is a branch of what precedes it: that whoever has been given knowledge of this revelation by Allah is obliged to convey it, as a successor to whom? To the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: an indication that a person is not questioned about the deeds of others; he is to do what is obligatory upon him, and as for others, their affair is with Allah, based on His saying: ﴿But if they turn away, then upon you is only the conveyance﴾, and He did not say: "Upon you is their sin," but ﴿upon you is the conveyance﴾, and you are free of their sin. This verse is the basis from which many issues branch out, among them what the Prophet ﷺ indicated when a people said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, some people bring us meat and we do not know whether they mentioned the name of Allah over it or not?" He said to them: "Mention the name of Allah yourselves and eat"[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (2057), and Ibn Majah (3174), and the wording is his, from the hadith of 'Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her.]]. This is an indication that you are only held accountable for your own action, and the action of another is nothing to do with you. He did not say: "Verify whether they mentioned it or not." He said: "Mention it yourselves." Now, this mention of the name that the Messenger ﷺ commanded, is it upon the action of the slaughterers or upon the action of the eaters?

* The students: Upon the eaters.

* A student: Upon the slaughterers.

* The Shaykh: Good. If it is upon the action of the slaughterers, as one of you said, then this is a mention upon a prior action. Does it have any benefit?

* The students: It has no benefit.

* The Shaykh: It has no benefit. The benefit is that you mention it upon a subsequent action. Accordingly, His saying: "Mention it" means at the time of eating, because the slaughter was undertaken by others, and they are the ones questioned about it. As for you, the obligation of mentioning the name falls upon you at the time of eating. This is one of the favours of Allah. If we were commanded to investigate the actions of others, we would fall into a hardship without end. For example, if a person served us meat, we would say: "Come, who slaughtered it? So-and-so? Did he mention the name or not? From whom did he buy this sheep? Did he seize it by force or steal it?" It may have been stolen. If he says: "He bought it from so-and-so," then from where did so-and-so buy it? Or did he steal it, or how? If we were commanded to search into the actions of others, then when the imam came forward we would say: "Come, are you in a state of ablution or not? Are you in a state of major impurity or not? Is there impurity on your garment or is it pure? Is it usurped or lawful?" It would be a problem. But by the favour of Allah, we are not questioned about the actions of others. Whoever performs an action and is qualified to do so, we do not ask about it, and asking about it is excessive scrupulosity and burdening oneself with what one has not been burdened with. For this reason He said: ﴿But if they turn away, then upon you is only the conveyance﴾. You perform your action, and they will be called to account for their actions. For this reason He said: ﴿And Allah is Seeing of the servants﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of the name "the Seeing" for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and it may be that what is meant by "the Seeing" here is the attribute, because He restricted it by saying: ﴿Seeing of the servants﴾, whereas the unrestricted name of Allah is like His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Seeing﴾ [al-Hajj 61] and what resembles it.

* And among its benefits also: the comprehensiveness of the knowledge of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, based on His saying: ﴿Seeing of the servants﴾, that is, of all their conditions.

And among the benefits of the verse: the warning against opposing Allah. How? If Allah is Seeing of me, then every person feels shame and is embarrassed to do what Allah has forbidden him or to leave what Allah has commanded him, because he knows that Allah sees him and will punish him.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verse 21–25 (part 1 of 5):

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah and kill the prophets without right and kill those who enjoin justice among the people – give them tidings of a painful punishment.﴾ In this verse there are two recitations in two words. First: ﴿an-Nabiyyin﴾ has a reading ﴿an-Nabi'in﴾. Second: ﴿wa-yaqtulun﴾ has a reading ﴿wa-yuqatilun﴾, so that it reads ﴿and they fight those who enjoin justice among the people﴾.

He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah﴾ – they disbelieve in the signs of Allah, whether the cosmic (kawniyyah) or the legislative (shar'iyyah). The word ᾱyāt (signs) is the plural of āyah, which linguistically means a sign or indicator. These cosmic signs that we witness, which mankind cannot create the like of, are a sign of Allah, a sign showing that the Creator is one, with no partner, and that nothing resembles Him. For if all of mankind gathered together to create a single mountain, they would not be able to do it, or to create a single animal, they would not be able to do it: ﴿Indeed, those whom you invoke besides Allah will never create a fly, even if they gathered together for it﴾ [al-Hajj 73]. The legislative signs of Allah, too, mankind cannot produce the like of: ﴿Say: If mankind and the jinn gathered together to produce the like of this Qur'an, they would not produce its like﴾ [al-Isra' 88]. So the legislative signs are the indicators that the One who sent down these signs is one God, and that He is perfect in wisdom. Those who disbelieve in these signs – after He mentioned multiple conjoined items, the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿so give them tidings of a painful punishment﴾. But how can there be disbelief in the signs of Allah? We say, first: the cosmic signs?

* Student: (...) by denying that the Creator, glorified and exalted is He, created them.

* The Shaykh: By claiming that someone other than Allah created them; this is one.

* The Student: Or by attributing a partner to Him in their creation.

* The Shaykh: Or by holding that He has a partner in His creation.

* The Student: Or by attributing a helper to Him in their creation.

* The Shaykh: Or by holding that He has a helper in His creation; three things. Good. And disbelief in the legislative signs?

* Student: Either by denial or by arrogance, and we seek refuge with Allah.

* The Shaykh: Yes, either by denying and rejecting them, or by arrogance and obstinacy. And among rejecting them or turning arrogantly away from them is distorting the texts (taḥrīf al-nuṣūṣ), for distorting the texts is a kind of disbelief without doubt. He says: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah and kill the prophets without right﴾ – they kill the prophets whom Allah sent to them, without right. The word "prophets" here includes the messengers and those prophets who were not sent as messengers. This attribute is found most among the Jews, for the Jews are the most stubborn opponents of the messengers and the harshest of them, we seek refuge with Allah. Some of them killed prophets without right and worshipped the taghut. Here He says: ﴿the prophets without right﴾. This qualifier is not intended to exclude what opposes it; rather, it is intended to state the reality and to indicate that this killing was transgression. So it serves two purposes:
First: to state the reality, that they killed them while they were not justified, meaning they did not kill them in retaliation (qiṣāṣ), for example, but killed them through aggression and injustice.
Second: that their killing was with falsehood, without right; for there is no killing that is rightful for any of the prophets.

﴿And they kill the prophets without right and kill those who enjoin justice among the people﴾. In one reading: ﴿they fight﴾. Who are those who enjoin justice among the people? Messengers and non-messengers: the scholars enjoin justice among the people, the rightly guided caliphs enjoin justice among the people, the prophets enjoin justice among the people. Thus its conjunction to "the prophets" is by way of conjoining the general to the specific, but He singled out the prophets because killing them is greater than killing others, for there is no killing greater in crime than killing the prophets without right. ﴿And they kill those who enjoin justice among the people﴾ – ﴿justice﴾ means fairness; ﴿among the people﴾ includes the prophets and others. We have already encountered the question: when the general is conjoined to the specific, or the specific to the general, does this indicate that the specific is excluded from the general ruling, or that it is stated explicitly because of its importance, so that it is mentioned twice?
* The Students: The second.
* The Shaykh: The second is closer to the truth: it is mentioned twice, once by way of generality and once by way of specificity, but it was singled out from among the other individuals, or the ruling was restated concerning it among the other individuals, out of concern for it and emphasis upon it. ﴿So give them tidings of a painful punishment﴾. The address is either to the Messenger ﷺ or to everyone who may be addressed. ﴿Give them tidings﴾: inform them. ﴿A painful punishment﴾: the punishment is the retribution, and "painful" means causing pain. Is this tidings meant sarcastically toward these people? Or is it the comparison of glad tidings to that which causes distress, on the basis that in both the complexion is affected and changes?
* Students: The first includes.
* Student: The second.
* The Shaykh: Both are possible. But if we say it is sarcasm, then this adds to the pain of those who are given these tidings, like His saying: ﴿Seize him and drag him into the midst of the Hellfire. Then pour over his head some of the torment of boiling water. Taste! Indeed, you were the mighty, the noble!﴾ [ad-Dukhan 47–49], meaning: say to him, "Taste!" Indeed this word or sentence will undoubtedly reach his heart to the utmost; for he will remember: where is the might? Where is the nobility? Where is the might by which he overcame, and the generosity by which he was bountiful? So the impact will be more severe and his regret greater that he has lost this attribute which in the world he regarded himself as belonging to.
* Student: The statement of the author of al-Jalalayn that the Jews killed forty-three prophets?
* The Shaykh: No, I do not know it well. There is no doubt that they killed prophets without right, but whether they were forty-three, four hundred, more or fewer, Allah knows best.
* Student: If a country imports meat, known to come from a communist country.
* The Shaykh: What?
* The Student: It imports meat from a state that is atheist, not believing in God, communist; most of its imports, or nearly all of them. And there is local meat in the country, but nobody buys it because of its high price, or few buy it. And you know that this man who invited you, he always buys or mostly buys from this meat. If he invites you, O Shaykh, or gives you meat, would you be scrupulous that you do not know where it is from? Most of his purchases from it, he always buys, does he not buy local?
* The Shaykh: First: communist states may have Muslims in them. Have you not heard of the uproar that took place in Yugoslavia these days?
* The Student: No.
* The Shaykh: There are many Muslims there. It has been said that most of those who run the slaughterhouses are Muslims, because they are poor in that place. So the slaughterer may well be a Muslim. But even so, the scholars say: if a slaughtered animal is found in a country most of whose people are of those whose slaughter is lawful, it is lawful, out of regard for the majority and the prevailing condition, and as facilitation for the community. So one looks: if it is said, "By Allah, most of the slaughterhouses in this communist country are run by Muslims," then what is imported from it is lawful. If it is said, "most of them are non-Muslims," then what is imported is unlawful, even if it is assumed to be a land of Jews or Christians; and if it is known that most of those who perform slaughter are neither Jews nor Christians, their slaughter is not lawful.
* Student: Shaykh, so if a person goes there, for example, and there is a great quantity of chickens that come from abroad, O Shaykh, and we are certain they were not named over, because they do not know the naming at all; suppose people went there and said that they eat them?
* The Shaykh: I do not know, because He said: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned﴾ [al-An'am 121], and He did not say, "do not eat of what you do not know." He said: ﴿of that which has not been mentioned﴾, meaning if we are certain that the name of Allah was not mentioned over it.
* Student: Is this like being certain, Shaykh, because I know they do not name?
* The Shaykh: If something is certain, do not eat it. But as long as you are not certain, then eating is permitted to you.
* Student: If we are certain, we do not eat?
* The Shaykh: It is known that if we are certain, eating is not permitted.
* Student: The benefit we have taken is that whoever Allah has given knowledge in this time has the duty of conveying it, or it is obligatory upon him to convey (...)?
* The Shaykh: Yes, the scholar is obligated to convey the Sharia.
* Student: Revelation, Shaykh, what is the meaning of revelation?
* The Shaykh: Yes, revelation (...). The Qur'an is revelation.
* Student: (...)
* The Shaykh: No, there is no prophet after Muhammad.
* Student: Shaykh, the statement of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve﴾, this is conjoined to every relative clause as the predicate of "inna." ﴿So give them tidings of a painful punishment﴾ is the predicate, and this is the subject. Where does the fa' of the conditional come from?
* The Shaykh: Did you understand his question?
* Student: Repeat.
* The Shaykh: This man understood it very well, and you were born here in the Arab land, and did you not understand that? Yes?
* Student: Yes indeed.
* The Shaykh: He says: the fa' occurring in the predicate of the subject like this; what brought it here? Is it not a conditional particle? The scholars say: the relative pronoun resembles the conditional noun in generality. ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah﴾ is like his saying: "Indeed, whoever disbelieves in the signs of Allah."
* Student: Meaning it includes the meaning of a condition.
* The Shaykh: Yes, the relative pronoun includes the meaning of a condition. He says: when you say, "Whoever comes to me, for him is a dirham," it means the same as your saying, "Whoever comes to me, for him is a dirham." Understood?
* Student: Shaykh, the Exalted says: ﴿And if they argue with you, say: I have submitted my face to Allah﴾. If it is said that the intended meaning of "face" here is the essence, meaning I have submitted my whole essence to Allah, the Exalted, then what would His saying be: ﴿nearer to him﴾ [Qaf 16]?
* The Shaykh: Whoever submits his face has submitted himself. Now, for example, someone speaks to you while (...) and I say I am listening to you, and you say what, will people believe you? They will not believe you.
* Student: I say, Shaykh, that the scholars' disagreement in understanding a text, sometimes some scholars give an understanding of the text that differs from one scholar to another, is this a difference of variety or of contradiction?
* The Shaykh: We do not know. If the two statements can be reconciled, it is a difference of variety. For example, some scholars said concerning His saying: ﴿and the night when it turns its back﴾ [at-Takwir 17], that it means it withdraws; and others said: ﴿and the night when it turns its back﴾ means it approaches. There is no contradiction in this; it is a difference of variety. But if the two statements cannot be reconciled, like His saying: ﴿And divorced women shall wait by themselves for three periods﴾ [al-Baqarah 228], some of them said the intended meaning of "qur'" is menstruation, and others said the intended meaning of "qur'" is purity; this cannot be reconciled, so this is a difference of contradiction. Likewise the Hanafis said: the time of 'Asr enters when the shadow of everything is twice its length. Others said: the time of 'Asr leaves when the shadow of everything is twice its length.
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: It cannot be reconciled; this is a difference of contradiction (...).
* Student: Shaykh, Allah the Mighty and Majestic commanded the Prophet ﷺ, when disputing, to say: ﴿I have submitted my face to Allah﴾. What is the ruling on disputation if it occurs between Muslims and the People of the Book?
* The Shaykh: Yes, this disputation: if their obstinacy has become evident, then say this. As long as they are not obstinate but seek the truth, then argue with them until the truth becomes clear. But if their obstinacy has become clear now, then we say: either we strike your necks, or you give the jizyah willingly while you are humbled. This is the duty upon the Muslims when they are able. As for when they are not able at the present time, this is a matter (...).
* * *
* Student: I seek refuge with Allah from Satan the accursed: ﴿Those are the ones whose deeds have become void in this world and the Hereafter, and they will have no helpers. Have you not considered those who were given a portion of the Book? They are invited to the Book of Allah to judge between them; then a faction of them turns away while they are refusing. That is because they say, "The Fire will not touch us except for a few numbered days," and their fabrications have deluded them in their religion. So how will it be when We gather them for a Day about which there is no doubt, and every soul is paid in full for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged? Say: O Allah, Owner of sovereignty, You give sovereignty to whom You will and You take sovereignty away from whom You will; You honor whom You will and You humble whom You will. In Your hand is all good. Indeed, You are Competent over all things. You cause the night to enter the day and You cause the day to enter the night, and You bring the living out of the dead and You bring the dead out of the living, and You provide for whom You will without account﴾ [Al 'Imran 22–27].
* The Shaykh: I seek refuge with Allah from Satan the accursed. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And if they argue with you, say: I have submitted my face to Allah, and so have those who follow me﴾. This is the beginning of the lesson, the discussion.
* Student: If they submit inwardly through faith.
* The Shaykh: Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And if they submit, then they have been guided; but if they turn away, upon you is only the conveyance, and Allah is Seeing of the servants.﴾ Where is the answer to the condition in His saying: ﴿And if they submit﴾?
* Student: ﴿then they have been guided﴾.
* The Shaykh: ﴿then they have been guided﴾. Why is it joined with the fa'?
* Student: Because the past tense with "qad" requires the fa' when it is with "qad."
* The Shaykh: Excellent, exactly. Is there a famous verse about the sentences that must be linked with the fa' when they occur as an answer to a condition?
* Student:
Nominal, imperative,
and with mā, qad, and lan,
and with the negation of the future (tanfīs).
* The Shaykh: This is "qad." Good. He says: ﴿if they submit, then they have been guided﴾. What is meant by guidance here?
* Student: Guidance of success (tawfīq).
* The Shaykh: Guidance of success. Can you bring me an example that contains both guidance of indication (dalālah) and guidance of success?
* Student: ﴿And as for Thamud, We guided them, but they preferred blindness over guidance﴾ [Fussilat 17].
* The Shaykh: ﴿And as for Thamud, We guided them, but they preferred blindness over guidance﴾: this is guidance of what?
* Student: Indication.
* The Shaykh: Guidance of indication. Is it derived from this verse that the Messenger ﷺ is not responsible for guiding the people?
* Student: Because of His saying: ﴿and if they turn away, upon you is only the conveyance﴾.
* The Shaykh: ﴿and if they turn away, upon you is only the conveyance﴾. Does this ruling extend to those scholars who inherited from the Prophet ﷺ?
* Student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Then the conveyance is upon them, without the guidance of success. Some scholars used this verse to support the well-known principle in the legal theory (uṣūl al-fiqh): it is not permissible to delay clarification beyond the time of need. How is that?
* Student: His saying: ﴿upon you is only the conveyance﴾; this is restrictive, it indicates restriction.
* The Shaykh: Good, but what is the aspect of its indication for their claim that it is not permissible to delay clarification beyond the time of need?
* Student: ﴿upon you﴾, and (upon) is clearly for obligation, and conveyance is obligatory when this matter appears (...) His saying: ﴿upon you is the conveyance﴾.
* The Shaykh: Meaning, if he did not clarify at the time of need, he would not have conveyed, and he would have neglected this obligation; is that clear? Good. If the Prophet ﷺ remained silent about a condition, and the need called for its clarification, had it been a condition, can we use that to argue that it is not a condition? For example, a matter that some scholars made a condition for the validity of worship, and the Prophet ﷺ remained silent about it in a situation where need called for its explanation, had it been obligatory: can we use this to argue that it is not a condition?
* Student: Yes.

* **The Shaykh:** Which verse is this?
* **The Student:** Which verse is this?
* **The Shaykh:** This verse, because if it were a condition, the Prophet ﷺ would have conveyed it. His saying ﴿and Allah is Seeing of the servants﴾: is the intended meaning sight of vision or sight of knowledge?
* **Student:** The verse intends sight of knowledge.
* **The Shaykh:** Sight of knowledge. Why did you restrict it to sight of knowledge in this verse?
* **The Student:** Because His saying ﴿Seeing of the servants﴾ (...) what they do.
* **The Shaykh:** Good. Could He not be seeing of their deeds in the sense of seeing them?
* **The Student:** (...) this context (...).
* **The Shaykh:** What is the aspect of the context?
* **The Student:** He said: ﴿and Allah is Seeing of the servants﴾ (...).
* **The Shaykh:** So it includes both sight of vision and sight of knowledge. Now, is there evidence that Allah sees with a sight of vision?
* **Student:** The saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "His veil is light; were He to remove it, the glories of His Face would burn away whatever of His creation His sight reaches."
* **The Shaykh:** "His veil is light; were He to remove it, the glories of His Face would burn away whatever of His creation His sight reaches"[[Reported by Muslim (179 / 293) from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him.]]. So it affirms for Allah a sight by which He, Mighty and Majestic, sees. Good. What does this sentence, which came as the answer to His saying ﴿but if they turn away﴾, convey?
* **Student:** A threat.
* **The Shaykh:** A threat, and that since He is Seeing of them, He will requite them for their turning away. His, Exalted is He, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah and kill the prophets without right, and kill those who enjoin justice among the people﴾. In the second ﴿يَقْتُلُونَ﴾ (they kill), are there two recitations?
* **Student:** ﴿يُقَاتِلُونَ﴾ (they fight) and ﴿يَقْتُلُونَ﴾ (they kill).
* **The Shaykh:** ﴿يَقْتُلُونَ﴾ and ﴿يُقَاتِلُونَ﴾. Good. Can both recitations be acted upon? Is there a contradiction between them?
* **The Student:** There is no contradiction between them.
* **The Shaykh:** Yes, because they kill those among the people who enjoin justice, killing the one who does not fight them, and fighting the one who fights them. In ﴿النَّبِيِّينَ﴾ (the prophets), are there also two recitations?
* **The Student:** ﴿النَّبِيِّينَ﴾ and ﴿النَّبِيئِينَ﴾.
* **The Shaykh:** ﴿النَّبِيِّينَ﴾ and ﴿النَّبِيئِينَ﴾. I think it has passed us that when two recitations come in one verse, the better course is for a person to recite with this one at one time and with that one at another time, just as if the Sunnah came with two forms of an act of worship, the better course is for a person to do this at one time and that at another. Likewise the two recitations, but a person must make sure of the recitation. If he is certain that it is one of the canonical seven readings (qira'a sab'iyya), then the better course is to recite with this at one time and that at another, because all of it is Sunnah. Now, His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿and kill the prophets without right﴾. Is there killing of prophets with right? Because He made the seat of the blood the killing of the prophets without right. So is there killing of prophets with right?
* **Student:** Like retaliation (qisas), Shaykh?
* **The Shaykh:** (...).
* **The Student:** (...) of the prophets are intended by this.
* **The Shaykh:** Good. Is the one killed in retaliation blamed, and his killer blamed? So the verse is laid out in the manner of blame?
* **Student:** Shaykh? This verse is to state the reality.
* **The Shaykh:** To state the reality, correct. This verse is to state the reality and to censure them: to state the reality that they kill the prophets without right, rather in falsehood, and to censure these people, since they kill these noble ones without right. Yes, Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So give them good tidings of a painful punishment﴾. How did He use good tidings for punishment, when good tidings are only ever of good?
* **Student:** Either as a mockery of them.
* **The Shaykh:** And is praise or description with goodness mentioned in a context of mockery? Can a beloved thing be mentioned in a context of mockery?
* **The Student:** (...)
* **The Shaykh:** Bring an example you cite to strengthen your view.
* **Student:** His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Taste it, indeed you are the mighty, the noble﴾ [al-Dukhan 49].
* **The Shaykh:** Its example is His saying: ﴿Taste it, indeed you are the mighty, the noble﴾. Good. This is one aspect. The second aspect? The first aspect is that it is by way of mocking them. What is the second?
* **Student:** The good tidings appear on their faces.
* **The Shaykh:** That good tidings were used in the context of a warning, because it is the sign of news that appears on the skin, so the complexion changes, just as the complexion changes with what pleases. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Those are the ones whose deeds have become void in this world and the Hereafter, and they will have no helpers﴾. ﴿Those﴾ refers to those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah, kill the prophets without right, and kill those among the people who enjoin justice, who are the people of goodness, the ones who enjoin right and forbid wrong. Those in whom these attributes are found are the ones whose deeds have become void. Habt (voiding) of a thing means its going away, its disappearance, and not benefiting from it. So their deeds have become void in this world and the Hereafter. As for the Hereafter, it is clear, because they will not benefit from their deeds, even if they were good. Even the disbelieving person, if he does good in this world, such as kindness to people, especially or generally, that does not benefit him in the Hereafter, by His saying: ﴿And We will turn to what they did of deeds and make them scattered dust﴾ [al-Furqan 23]. But how were their deeds voided in this world? Their deeds were voided in this world because, since they did not benefit from them, they became as though they had not done them, so their deeds did not benefit them. The evidence for this is His saying: ﴿Say: Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Unquestionably, that is the manifest loss﴾ [al-Zumar 15].

He said: ﴿and they will have no helpers﴾. This sentence, as we all know, is a negated sentence with ﻣﺎ (ma). I ask here: is this ﻣﺎ acting like ﻟﻴﺲ (laysa) or not?
* **Student:** It is not acting like laysa.
* **The Shaykh:** Why?
* **The Student:** Because the predicate came first.
* **The Shaykh:** Because the predicate came first. Do you have a witness from the words of the scholars for what you said?
* **The Student:** From the Alfiyya?
* **The Shaykh:** From the Alfiyya, if it is slightly altered, it does not matter.
* **Student:** A grammatical rule says: (...) acts with what resembles laysa.
* **The Shaykh:** No, I want it from the words of Ibn Malik.
* **The Student:** And I have the words of Ibn al-Hajib.
* **Student:**
"The operation of laysa is given to ma without inna, while the negation remains and the order is kept."
* **The Shaykh:** Good, but here there is a difficulty: His saying ﴿from helpers﴾. How do we parse it (i'rab, grammatical analysis)?
* **Student:** ﴿مِنْ نَاصِرِينَ﴾: the مِنْ is a superfluous preposition, a superfluous, superfluous particle.
* **The Shaykh:** A superfluous, superfluous preposition, like that?
* **The Student:** Yes indeed.
* **The Shaykh:** What is "superfluous, superfluous"? Explain it to the brothers.
* **The Student:** Superfluous in its i'rab and superfluous in its wording.
* **The Shaykh:** In meaning. That is, superfluous in the i'rab, and it adds to the meaning.
* **The Student:** And ﻧَاصِرِينَ is the noun of ﻣَا (ma), in the nominative.
* **The Shaykh:** The noun of ma, and Muhammad says: what does ma do? How do we say "the noun of ma"? Do you have anything other than this?
* **Student:** The predicate.
* **The Shaykh:** No, the predicate, that is not correct.
* **Student:** The subject, and لَهُمْ is the predicate.
* **The Shaykh:** Yes, but complete the i'rab of nāṣirīn: subject.
* **The Student:** (nāṣirīn) the active participle, genitive in form and nominative in meaning, subject. And لَهُمْ.
* **The Shaykh:** Wait, complete it, complete it.
* **The Student:** Subject, that is, nominative in form (at the end, correct), (nāṣirīn) the active participle, the sound masculine plural, and its nominative is with the wāw, the letter before it being damma, and its accusative and genitive are with the yā', the letter before it being kasra, genitive in form and nominative in position, subject, and ma is negating.
* **The Shaykh:** What is the sign of its nominative? The implied wāw.
* **The Student:** And ma is negating, and لَهُمْ is an adverbial complement related to an omitted element.
* **The Shaykh:** A prepositional phrase related to an omitted element.
* **The Student:** And the omitted element is the predicate.
* **The Shaykh:** The important thing now: we understood from his words that the wāw is implied in the place of the yā', its appearance being prevented by the place being occupied by a vowel?
* **The students:** The preposition.
* **The Shaykh:** The superfluous preposition. That is, those whose deeds have become void in this world and the Hereafter have no one to help them. And He, glorified and exalted, emphasized the negation here, He emphasized it with the superfluous مِنْ, meaning they have no one to help them, neither collectively nor individually, because the superfluous مِنْ, when it enters, makes the negation explicit in generality, like the negating لَا of genus.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Have you not considered those who were given a portion of the Scripture? They are invited to the Book of Allah to judge between them; then a faction of them turns away, while they are refusing﴾. ﴿Have you not considered﴾: the interrogative here is for amazement, because every intelligent person is amazed at this condition. And ﴿ترَ﴾ (consider) may be a sight of the eye, and may be a sight of knowledge, and the second is better, because it is more comprehensive, and because it relates to a condition, and a condition is known, not seen with the eye, meaning: have you not known about these people?
﴿Those who were given a portion of the Scripture﴾ means they were given a portion of knowledge. The one who gave them the portion is Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and He omitted it because it is known, since Allah, Exalted is He, is the one who gives knowledge. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿He gives wisdom to whom He wills, and whoever is given wisdom has certainly been given much good﴾ [al-Baqarah 269], and He, Exalted, said: ﴿And We taught him from Us a knowledge﴾ [al-Kahf 65]. So the one who gives the portion of knowledge is Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
And His saying: ﴿a portion of the Scripture﴾: does it indicate minimization or maximization? It may be that the intended meaning is that they were given a large portion of the Scripture, such that it would have led them to guidance, but they, may Allah protect us, were arrogant. And it may be that they have nothing but a little knowledge, and that even if it were supposed that they had much knowledge, this knowledge did not benefit them, so they became like the one given a small portion of knowledge.
And His saying: ﴿They are invited to the Book of Allah﴾ is the place of amazement: that is, despite the knowledge they have, they are invited to the Book of Allah. The one inviting them is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and whoever calls with his call until the Day of Resurrection. These are invited to the Book of Allah ﴿to judge between them﴾. The attribution of judgment here may be to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that Allah judges between them by His Book, and it may be to the Book, and judgment is attributed to it because the judgment comes through it, and a thing is often attributed to its cause. In any case, whether we say the pronoun in ﴿يَحْكُمَ﴾ (judge) refers to Allah or we say it refers to the Book, these people are invited to the Book of Allah to judge between them, but they do not accept this. That is why He said: ﴿then a faction of them turns away, while they are refusing﴾. A faction of them turns away, not all of them, because some of them have been guided. Some of these who were given a portion of the Scripture have been guided by Allah, and they are many. But a faction of them turned away, and along with their turning away they are refusing, may Allah protect us, having no acceptance either outwardly or inwardly. Rather, they are turning away and refusing. He said ﴿while they are refusing﴾, which is a circumstantial clause from ﴿faction﴾. He said that because a person may turn away due to a passing cause, but there remains in his heart some acceptance. As for these, they are turning away, and they have been filled with aversion from the Book of Allah to judge between them. And here He says: ﴿a faction of them turns away, while they are refusing﴾. How is a circumstantial clause valid from an indefinite noun?
* **Student:** The circumstantial (hal) is what describes the state of the doer.
* **The Shaykh:** Yes.
