Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Have you not considered those who were given a portion of the Scripture? They are invited to the Book of Allah to judge between them; then a faction of them turns away, while they are refusing﴾. ﴿Have you not considered﴾: the interrogative here is for amazement, because every intelligent person is amazed at this condition. And ﴿ترَ﴾ (consider) may be a sight of the eye, and may be a sight of knowledge, and the second is better, because it is more comprehensive, and because it relates to a condition, and a condition is known, not seen with the eye, meaning: have you not known about these people?
﴿Those who were given a portion of the Scripture﴾ means they were given a portion of knowledge. The one who gave them the portion is Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and He omitted it because it is known, since Allah, Exalted is He, is the one who gives knowledge. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿He gives wisdom to whom He wills, and whoever is given wisdom has certainly been given much good﴾ [al-Baqarah 269], and He, Exalted, said: ﴿And We taught him from Us a knowledge﴾ [al-Kahf 65]. So the one who gives the portion of knowledge is Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
And His saying: ﴿a portion of the Scripture﴾: does it indicate minimization or maximization? It may be that the intended meaning is that they were given a large portion of the Scripture, such that it would have led them to guidance, but they, may Allah protect us, were arrogant. And it may be that they have nothing but a little knowledge, and that even if it were supposed that they had much knowledge, this knowledge did not benefit them, so they became like the one given a small portion of knowledge.
And His saying: ﴿They are invited to the Book of Allah﴾ is the place of amazement: that is, despite the knowledge they have, they are invited to the Book of Allah. The one inviting them is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and whoever calls with his call until the Day of Resurrection. These are invited to the Book of Allah ﴿to judge between them﴾. The attribution of judgment here may be to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that Allah judges between them by His Book, and it may be to the Book, and judgment is attributed to it because the judgment comes through it, and a thing is often attributed to its cause. In any case, whether we say the pronoun in ﴿يَحْكُمَ﴾ (judge) refers to Allah or we say it refers to the Book, these people are invited to the Book of Allah to judge between them, but they do not accept this. That is why He said: ﴿then a faction of them turns away, while they are refusing﴾. A faction of them turns away, not all of them, because some of them have been guided. Some of these who were given a portion of the Scripture have been guided by Allah, and they are many. But a faction of them turned away, and along with their turning away they are refusing, may Allah protect us, having no acceptance either outwardly or inwardly. Rather, they are turning away and refusing. He said ﴿while they are refusing﴾, which is a circumstantial clause from ﴿faction﴾. He said that because a person may turn away due to a passing cause, but there remains in his heart some acceptance. As for these, they are turning away, and they have been filled with aversion from the Book of Allah to judge between them. And here He says: ﴿a faction of them turns away, while they are refusing﴾. How is a circumstantial clause valid from an indefinite noun?
* **Student:** The circumstantial (hal) is what describes the state of the doer.
* **The Shaykh:** Yes.
* **The Student:** Whether the doer is indefinite or definite.
* **The Shaykh:** No, no.
* **The Student:** It describes the state of the doer.
* **The Shaykh:** Yes, but the doer must be definite, or indefinite with a reason.
* **Student:** Because it is qualified.
* **The Shaykh:** Because it is qualified: ﴿a faction of them﴾. When an indefinite noun is qualified, it becomes specified, and so it resembles the definite.
﴿Then a faction of them turns away, while they are refusing. That is because they said: "The Fire will not touch us except for numbered days"﴾. ﴿That﴾ refers to the turning away and refusing. Because they deceived themselves and said: ﴿The Fire will not touch us﴾, meaning it will not reach us, ﴿except for numbered days﴾, meaning a few days; because everything numbered is few. The evidence for this is His saying: ﴿And We do not delay it except for a limited term﴾ [Hud 104], and He said: ﴿Say: The enjoyment of this world is little﴾ [al-Nisa' 77]. So everything numbered is few, because a thing that passes by counting, one, two, three, four, must end. These people say: ﴿The Fire will not touch us except for numbered days﴾. Then who will succeed them after that? Who will succeed them in it? They claim that the one who succeeds them will be the Prophet ﷺ and his companions. These are the Jews. They said, by their own assumption and a rejected claim: they will enter the Fire, but will not remain in it except for numbered days, and then the Prophet ﷺ and his companions will succeed them in it forever and ever. They lied in that. They will indeed be touched by the Fire and will remain in it forever and ever. But they deceived themselves and deluded their common folk with this false, fabricated saying: ﴿That is because they said: The Fire will not touch us except for numbered days. And their fabrications deceived them in their religion﴾. ﴿Deceived them﴾: deluding and deception are close in meaning. That is, these people were deceived, or were taken in, regarding their religion, since they thought they were upon the truth. And some of them opposed the truth while knowing it, a fabricator and a liar. ﴿And their fabrications deceived them in their religion﴾, that is, what they used to fabricate, and among it their saying: ﴿The Fire will not touch us except for numbered days﴾.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verses 21–25 (part 3 of 5):

﴿So how will it be when We gather them for a Day about which there is no doubt, and every soul will be paid in full what it earned, and they will not be wronged?﴾ That is, how will their condition be? How will their condition be at that time, when We gather them for a Day about which there is no doubt? The interrogative here is for magnifying the matter, meaning: how great will their condition be on that Day, and how intense will their regret be! ﴿when We gather them for a Day about which there is no doubt﴾: that is, We gather them for this Day, meaning in it. The *lam* (ل) always carries the sense of (في, "in"), and grammarians call it *lam al-tawqit* (the lam of time). From it is the Almighty's saying: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them for their waiting period﴾ [al-Talaq 1], meaning: at the beginning of their waiting period, in anticipation of it. So "the Day about which there is no doubt" means they are gathered for this Day, that is, in it, and it is the Day of Resurrection.

As for His saying ﴿about which there is no doubt﴾, it may be an informative statement with the meaning of a prohibition, meaning: "Do not doubt it." Or it may be a statement on its literal sense, meaning that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, informs about this Day that there is no doubt about it, that is, no doubt about its occurrence. This Day is established by the Book, the Sunnah and reason. As for the Book, how many are the verses that affirm the Last Day, and how many are the parables that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sets forth to establish this Day, the resurrection of creatures. As for the Sunnah, it also affirms this Day abundantly. As for reason, it necessarily indicates that this creation must have a return (ma'ad) at which it will be called to account for what it was commanded to do. For it is not reasonable that Allah should create the creation, command and forbid it, send messengers to it, reveal books to it, permit the blood of those who do not submit to these books and do not follow these messengers, and then the outcome be that this humanity dies and is not resurrected, becoming dust. If such an act were committed by anyone, it would be said that this is among the most foolish of foolishness. If a person made a garment, sewed it, perfected it, made it as good as possible, and in the end burned it and destroyed it so that no trace remained, all people would regard this as foolishness. How much more so, then, with this creation which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, created, revealed books to, and sent messengers to, and whose blood and property He permitted for those who did not submit to these books or follow these messengers, only for the outcome to be that this creation is destroyed without any punishment or any reckoning. Therefore, the Book, the Sunnah, the consensus (ijma', the agreement of the scholars) and reason all point to the establishment of this Day, about which Allah said: ﴿So how will it be when We gather them for a Day about which there is no doubt, and every soul will be paid in full what it earned, and they will not be wronged?﴾

*Wuffiyat* (وُفِّيَتْ) means "was given," and from it comes the saying "waffaahu haqqahu," meaning he gave him his right in full.

As for His saying ﴿every soul﴾: does it refer to humans only, or to others as well? It refers to humans and jinn, meaning those who are accountable (mukallafun), who were commanded and forbidden. They are the ones who will be paid their rewards in full. As for those to whom no command or prohibition was addressed, they will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection, but they have no deeds for which they will be recompensed. Therefore His saying ﴿and every soul will be paid in full what it earned﴾ does not include them. What then will be the condition of those who turned away and were averse? It will be the worst condition, and we seek refuge in Allah, because they will look at people who have been rewarded with a great reward, and at themselves who have been requited with humiliating punishment. Their deeds will become sources of regret for them, and we seek refuge in Allah, on the Day of Resurrection, and they will benefit neither in their worldly life nor in their Hereafter.

His saying ﴿what it earned﴾ means good or evil, as shown by the generality of the word "what" (ما). But how is it paid in full? As for good, the doer of a good deed is repaid tenfold, up to seven hundred times, up to many multiples. As for evil, the evil deed is repaid with its like, unless Allah pardons it. Allah may pardon it, or he may have righteous deeds that expiate these sins. Thus the recompense and full payment of deeds by Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, moves between grace (fadl) and justice ('adl): grace toward the people of good, and justice toward the people of evil.

As for the third category, which is oppression and injustice, this is impossible for Allah, and therefore He said: ﴿and they will not be wronged﴾, meaning none will be diminished in his good deeds or increased in his evil deeds. We know that whoever gives another his due has only three possible states: he gives it either out of grace, or out of justice, or out of injustice. But Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, gives His due only between justice and grace, while injustice and oppression are impossible for Him, as in His saying: ﴿And your Lord does not wrong anyone﴾ [al-Kahf 49]; ﴿And your Lord is not ever unjust to the servants﴾ [Fussilat 46]; ﴿And whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer will not fear injustice or diminution﴾ [Taha 112]. In a hadith qudsi (a hadith in which Allah speaks in the first person), Allah the Exalted said: "O My servants, I have forbidden injustice to Myself and have made it forbidden among you, so do not wrong one another." [Narrated by Muslim (2577/55) from Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him).]

Now let us return to the lessons of the verse we mentioned. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah and kill the prophets without right﴾ up to the end [Al 'Imran: 21]. Among the lessons in this verse: it is fitting that these disbelievers be informed of what Allah has commanded us to announce to them: ﴿give them tidings of a painful punishment﴾. Without doubt, the Prophet (ﷺ), whenever there was wisdom in giving these people the tidings of a painful punishment, gave them these tidings. Likewise, whoever inherits the Prophet (ﷺ) in knowledge and da'wah (calling to Islam) should give every disbeliever in the signs of Allah the tidings of a painful punishment, but this must follow wisdom. It may not be wise, when you invite a man to Islam, to say: "Come, you are a disbeliever?" If he says "Yes," and you say, "Rejoice in the painful punishment," and then go on to invite him. Is this proper? It is not appropriate. But every situation has its own speech. If you invite him and he is obstinate and arrogant, then it is appropriate to say: "If you remain as you are, then rejoice in a painful punishment." Or if a man comes to you praising these disbelievers, saying: "So-and-so, and so-and-so, and so-and-so," you say: "My brother, give them the tidings of a painful punishment." What benefit will this bring them on the Day of Resurrection?

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: the obligation of faith in the signs of Allah, because Allah threatened these disbelievers who rejected them with a painful punishment. Faith in the cosmic signs (al-ayat al-kawniyyah) has one meaning, and faith in the legislative signs (al-ayat al-shar'iyyah) has another. Faith in the legislative signs, as we have said, is: affirming the reports, acting upon the rulings, and not subjecting them to tahrif (distortion), three things. And faith in the cosmic signs is: not believing that Allah has any partner in them, or any helper, or any independent authority over His dominion.

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: the prohibition of killing the prophets, and that it is wrongful regardless of circumstances, based on His saying: ﴿and kill the prophets without right﴾. Although killing the prophets without right is itself part of disbelief, it was explicitly mentioned because of its extreme heinousness, and we seek refuge in Allah.

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: the prohibition of, or the heinousness of, anyone who kills or fights those among the people who enjoin justice. Who are those who enjoin justice among the people? We have said they are scholars and rulers: the scholars explain the Shari'ah, and the rulers implement the Shari'ah. So if someone kills them, he falls under this verse, if they were enjoining justice.

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: the establishment of punishment for those who possess these attributes, based on His saying: ﴿so give them tidings of a painful punishment﴾.

* Among its lessons: the punishment that they are given tidings of is not a light punishment that can be borne, but a painful torment.

Among the lessons of the verse that follows: those who disbelieved in the signs of Allah, killed His prophets, and killed those who enjoin justice among the people, their deeds have become void in this world and the Hereafter, so they gain no benefit from them. As for the Hereafter, this is clear. As for this world, they did not benefit from their deeds, so it is as if they never existed.

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: disbelief nullifies deeds, based on His saying: ﴿These are the ones whose deeds have become void in this world and the Hereafter﴾. This is also indicated by His saying: ﴿And whoever of you reverts from his religion and dies while he is a disbeliever, those are the ones whose deeds have become void in this world and the Hereafter, and they are the companions of the Fire, wherein they will abide eternally﴾ [al-Baqarah 217].

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: these disbelievers have no helpers: ﴿and they will have no helpers﴾. But is the meaning that they have no helper in this world and the Hereafter, or only in the Hereafter? It means in the Hereafter. As for this world, someone of their kind may help them. But they and those who help them are destined for humiliation and abandonment, because Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Allah has decreed: "I will surely prevail, I and My messengers." Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might﴾ [al-Mujadila 21].

* Student: His saying ﴿for a limited number of days﴾: why the distinction between ﴿ma'dudah﴾ [al-Baqarah 80] and ﴿ma'dudat﴾? (...)

* * *

* Student: ﴿Say, "O Allah, Owner of sovereignty, You give sovereignty to whom You will and You take sovereignty away from whom You will. You honor whom You will and You humble whom You will. In Your hand is [all] good. Indeed, You are over all things competent"﴾ [Al 'Imran 26].

* Shaykh: (...) ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah and kill the prophets without right and kill those who enjoin justice among the people—give them tidings of a painful punishment. Those are the ones whose deeds have become void in this world and the Hereafter, and for them there are no helpers﴾. ﴿their deeds have become void in this world and the Hereafter﴾. As for the Hereafter, the voiding of their deeds is clear, because they do not benefit from their deeds in the Hereafter. But in this world, how are their deeds made void?

* Student: They are defeated.

* Shaykh: How are they defeated?

* Student: That is, they kill the prophets, and in the end they are defeated; they have no power over the Muslims.

* Shaykh: So the meaning is that in the end their deeds are voided, meaning their honor and pride. This is a good explanation. Is there anything else?

* Student: Their deeds are not beneficial to them, even their righteous deeds.

* Shaykh: Since they did not benefit from them, they became void, and even if they benefited from them in this world, because they were not beneficial to them in the Hereafter, they became lost, as Allah said: ﴿Say, "Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection"﴾ [al-Zumar 15].

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Have you not considered those who were given a portion of the Book, being invited to the Book of Allah﴾. Who is addressed by ﴿Have you not considered﴾?

* Student: The address is to the Messenger (ﷺ).

* Shaykh: To the Prophet (ﷺ). Is there no other interpretation?

* Student: To the People of the Book.

* Shaykh: No.

* Student: To everyone who can be addressed.

* Shaykh: To everyone who can be addressed, meaning everyone who is fit to be addressed, Allah addresses him with "Have you not considered." This statement is more general than the first. Who are they meant to be?

* Student: They are the People of the Book.

* Shaykh: Who?

* Student: The Jews and the Christians.

* Shaykh: The Jews and the Christians. Now, ﴿a portion﴾ here is indefinite. Does it indicate few or many?

* Student: ﴿a portion﴾ indicates a small amount, though it may occasionally indicate a large amount.

* Shaykh: Which is intended here?

* Student: It means a small amount.

* Shaykh: That is, they were given?

* Student: They were given a small share of knowledge among them, a little among them.

* Shaykh: Now, what is the connection? If you say the meaning is a small amount, they might say: "By Allah, we only have little knowledge, and we do not know whether the Book of Allah is true or not." 

* Student: What is the connection?

* Shaykh: I am saying now: if you say the meaning is a small amount, how can they be blamed when they have only a little knowledge, by which they cannot distinguish truth from falsehood?

* Student: The meaning is that they were given a portion, that is, a little knowledge, which is not enough for them in matters of their religion and their worldly life.

* Shaykh: Now, when these people are called to Allah, they say: "By Allah, we do not know the truth by it, so we should not be blamed for turning away from it"?

* Student: We say: ﴿a portion﴾ may mean a great deal of knowledge, but they were arrogant when called to the Book of Allah. And it may mean a small amount of knowledge.

* Shaykh: Now, each meaning has its justification. If we say "a small amount," the basis for blaming them is that, since they were given only a little knowledge, it was obligatory for them to take up the knowledge to which they were called, so that they might increase in knowledge. But if we say "a large amount," the basis is: how can they fail to know the truth, when if they were given much knowledge or a great portion of the Book, among its contents is that they recognize Muhammad (ﷺ)? How then can they be given much knowledge by which the proof is established, and yet be arrogant toward it? So the verse is suitable for both meanings together.

Now, His saying: ﴿they are called to the Book of Allah that it may judge between them﴾. Who is the subject of "yahkum" (it judges)?

* Student: In "yahkum" the subject is the name of Allah and the Book, both.

* Shaykh: That is, it may refer both to Allah and to the Book, is that right?

* Student: Yes.

* Shaykh: Because the Book judges, and likewise Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, judges among His servants. Now, why do they turn away while being averse? What is the cause that led them to that?

* Student: Arrogance.

* Shaykh: No.

* Student: The cause is in His saying: ﴿That is because they said, "The Fire will not touch us except for a limited number of days"﴾.

* Shaykh: Yes, that is what led them to it: delusion, and that their own selves deceived them, so they said: "The Fire will not touch us except for a limited number of days," and then, after that, you, O Muhammad, and your companions will be left in it. That is why He said: ﴿Their own invention deceived them in their religion﴾. Now, what is meant by the interrogative in His saying: ﴿So how will it be when We gather them for a Day about which there is no doubt﴾?

* Student: To magnify this Day; that is, how terrible will this Day be when We gather them? Or how will their condition be on this Day when they are gathered?

* Shaykh: It includes magnifying that Day and threatening these people. So it is for magnifying that Day and for threatening these people. What is meant by "this Day"?

* Student: The Day of Resurrection.

* Shaykh: Now, Allah said: ﴿about which there is no doubt﴾?

* Student: That is, there is no doubt about it.

* Shaykh: Why is there no doubt about it, when it is an unseen matter?

* Student: The one who informs about it is truthful; it is Allah who informed about it.

* Student: The Book, the Sunnah and reason indicate it.

* Shaykh: Because each of the Book, the Sunnah and reason indicates this Day, and that people will be resurrected. We want evidence from the Qur'an for the establishment of this Day, other than the verse we have before us.

* Student: His saying: ﴿Say, "Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection"﴾ [al-Zumar 15].

* Shaykh: That is possible, but is there no verse indicating that people will be gathered on that Day, so that the meaning is complete?

* Student: ﴿Those who disbelieve claim that they will never be resurrected. Say, "Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected; then you will surely be informed of what you did"﴾ [al-Taghabun 7].

* Shaykh: Yes. Is there no evidence for the gathering itself?

* Student: His saying: ﴿The Day He gathers you for the Day of Gathering—that is the Day of loss and gain﴾ [al-Taghabun 9].

* Shaykh: Good, correct, yes. And in Surah Hud: ﴿That is a Day for which the people will be gathered, and that is a Day witnessed﴾ [Hud 103]. Now, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿and every soul will be paid in full what it earned, and they will not be wronged﴾. What is the meaning of ﴿every soul has been paid in full﴾?

* Student: Yes, its meaning is that every soul was given its due.

* Shaykh: In full. Well done. The clause ﴿and they will not be wronged﴾: what is its place in i'rab (grammatical analysis)?

* Student: It is a predicate (khabar).

* Shaykh: No.

* Student: It is a circumstantial clause (hal).

* Shaykh: A circumstantial clause of what?

* Student: A circumstantial clause of ﴿and every soul has been paid in full﴾.

* Shaykh: Of ﴿every soul﴾?

* Student: No, of the...

* Shaykh: Of the whole world, the verb and its subject.

* Student: The soul that paid it in full, from the subject.

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on Surah 3, Verses 21–25 (Part 4 of 5)**

* **Shaykh:** We do not have a *fā'il* (subject); what we have is a *nā'ib fā'il* (deputy subject, the grammatical term for a passive verb's subject), because وُفِّيَ (wuffiya, "was paid in full") is a past-tense verb in the passive voice (*fi'l māḍī mabnī lil-majhūl*).
* **Student:** The *nā'ib fā'il*.
* **Shaykh:** The *nā'ib fā'il* is His saying: ﴿every soul﴾. Good. What is the meaning of the injustice (...)? The injustice that is negated here, or what is meant by it?
* **Student:** Non-oppression. The injustice here means non-oppression, because the full payment of a person's due has three states; either he is given his due...
* **Shaykh:** No, we only want to know the negation of injustice. Injustice occurs either by reducing some of one's good deeds or by increasing one's sins. As for how the payment is made, that is what you are asking about. The payment has three categories: justice, grace, and oppression. Oppression is negated, while justice and grace are affirmed.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture?﴾ [Aal 'Imran 23], and so on to the end.

Several benefits are derived from this noble verse:

* The first: Not everyone who is given knowledge is granted the success to act upon it, by His saying: ﴿they are called to the Book of Allah﴾ ﴿then a faction of them turns away﴾ [Aal 'Imran 23].
* Another benefit of this noble verse: It expresses amazement at the state of these people. How astonishing it is that Allah gives them knowledge, and yet afterward they do not turn to the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
* Another benefit: These people have had the proof established against them by being called to it. This is the point of blame. As for those who were never called and never learned the truth, they are not blamed for that, provided they did not neglect seeking the truth.
* Another benefit of this noble verse: It is obligatory to refer disputes to the Book of Allah, by His saying: ﴿they are called to the Book of Allah, that it may judge between them﴾ [Aal 'Imran 23].
* Another benefit: There is no judgment except the judgment of Allah as revealed in His Book. No ruler can legislate rulings that contradict the rulings of Allah. Whoever legislates rulings that contradict the rulings of Allah and imposes them upon the servants is a disbeliever in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, a disbeliever. The exception is if he is excused by a valid interpretation; this may remove him from disbelief, but his act, considered in itself, leads to disbelief.
* Another benefit of this noble verse: Judgment in the Book of Allah applies to everything: in acts of worship, transactions, morals, and deeds, everything. Since He did not restrict it, He said: ﴿that it may judge between them﴾, meaning in every matter.

From this benefit there follows a refutation of those who say that the Shariah came only to regulate acts of worship, while transactions are left to people. They cite as evidence that when the Prophet (ﷺ) arrived in Madinah, he saw people pollinating the date palms (*yu'abbirūna al-nakhl*, meaning fertilizing them). He said, peace and blessings be upon him: "I do not think that this benefits anything," or words to that effect. So they left off pollination, and the fruit was spoiled, because when a palm is not pollinated it is ruined. When the harvest came, they came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him. He said: "You are more knowledgeable about the affairs of your worldly life." They said: So he entrusted the knowledge of worldly affairs to them, and even made them more knowledgeable than him in this matter. Accordingly, worldly affairs are not subject to the Shariah. But this is a mistaken understanding, a false understanding. That is because worldly affairs are of two kinds: either they are legal rulings, such as what is permitted and what is prohibited, and these are referred back to the Shariah; or they are technical matters that are known through experience and learning, and these are referred back to the people of expertise. How many a scholar with vast and wide knowledge of the matters of the Shariah cannot make a door or a needle, while an ignorant man, one of the most ignorant of people, can make a door of the finest quality and a needle of the finest quality. Is that not so?

* **Students:** Yes indeed.
* **Shaykh:** And the matter of the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) regarding pollination, is it a legal ruling or a technical matter? It is technical, without doubt, known through experience. And the Prophet (ﷺ), as we know, was born in Makkah, and Makkah does not have date palms, so he knew nothing of this. Thus the people of Madinah, who had practiced this through experience, became more knowledgeable than him in this. As for the legal rulings of the Shariah, there is no doubt that Allah and His Messenger are the most knowledgeable. The point is: to whom does judgment belong? To Allah. It is not permissible for judgment to belong to anything other than Allah. If someone says: Do you not refer to custom (*'urf*) in many matters?

The answer is: Yes. But who directed us to custom? The Shariah. We have referred to custom by His saying: ﴿live with them in kindness﴾ [An-Nisa' 19], ﴿retain them in kindness or release them in kindness﴾ [At-Talaq 2]. So the Shariah is what commanded us to refer to custom, and when it commands us to refer to custom, we refer to it and make it the arbiter. For this reason, when a husband and wife dispute the amount of maintenance, we do not go to this book or that book, such as al-Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud, or the like. We do not refer to these. To whom do we refer? To the people of expertise in custom, in every time and place according to its circumstances. So judgment in matters referred to custom belongs to whom? To the Shariah.

* **Student:** To the Shariah and the people of expertise.
* **Shaykh:** No. Judgment belongs to the Shariah, which is what commanded us to refer to custom; so the people of custom are the ones who judge.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: Those who were called to the Book of Allah, from among those who were given a portion of the Scripture, did not all turn away. Rather, a faction of them turned away. And indeed, many Jews and Christians embraced Islam, their Islam was sound, and they had a sure standing in Islam.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: Condemnation of one who turns away with aversion, by His saying: ﴿a faction of them turns away while they are refusing﴾ [Aal 'Imran 23], because turning away, as we mentioned in the tafsir, may be out of aversion and may be out of other than aversion. Turning away is blameworthy in every case, but when it is out of aversion and indifference, it is more severe.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿That is because they said, "The Fire will not touch us except for a few numbered days"﴾ [Aal 'Imran 24].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: The falsehood of wishful thinking, and that the soul may wish for a person things that will not happen. These people were deceived by their souls when they said: ﴿The Fire will not touch us except for a few numbered days﴾.

* Another benefit: A warning against relying on wishful thinking, because this is the practice of the Jews and Christians. Many common people today fall into sins and wish for forgiveness. If one of them commits a sin, you say to him: "Brother, fear Allah, do not disobey Allah," and he says: "Allah is Forgiving and Merciful, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful." Is that correct?

* **Students:** Yes, indeed.

* **Shaykh:** It is true that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. But Allah said: ﴿Inform My servants that I am the Forgiving, the Merciful, and that My punishment is the painful punishment﴾ [Al-Hijr 49–50]. And He said: ﴿Know that Allah is severe in punishment and that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 98]. When He commanded His Prophet to inform, He began with forgiveness. When He told about Himself, He began with punishment, because the context is one of sovereignty and exaltedness, so He said: ﴿Know that Allah is severe in punishment and that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

So what do we say to this one who says, "Allah is Forgiving and Merciful"? We say: And Allah is also severe in punishment. Some disobedient people entertain wishful thinking and say: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ [An-Nisa' 48]. He wants to commit adultery, steal, drink wine, and do everything short of associating partners with Allah, and then he says: "Allah says, ﴿He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾." This is a report, a report from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and He is the most truthful of speakers. So what do we say?

We say: Read the verse. Do not be blind or one-eyed; you are looking with only one eye. He forgives what is less than that absolutely, for whom He wills, and whoever He does not will, He does not forgive. So do you assert that you are among those whom Allah wills to forgive?

Certainly not. You do not assert it, neither this nor that. So you are in danger. You are in danger, and the one who treats sin lightly and deceives himself and others may be among those whom Allah does not will to forgive. We seek refuge in Allah, because this person is reckless and disdainful.

So those who wish wishful things from Allah while persisting in disobedience resemble whom? The Jews and Christians. For this reason, a hadith says: "The intelligent one is he who holds himself accountable (that is, reckons with it) and works for what comes after death, and the incapable one is he who follows his soul's desires and wishes things from Allah." (Narrated by al-Tirmidhi, 2459, and Ibn Majah, 4260, from Shaddad ibn Aws al-Ansari.)

* Another benefit of this noble verse: These people believed in the Resurrection, but their faith did not benefit them. From where do we take this? From their saying: ﴿The Fire will not touch us except for a few numbered days﴾.

It follows from this that belief in the existence of Allah and the Last Day is not sufficient for faith unless that faith entails acceptance and submission. Mere assent is not considered faith. Acceptance and submission are necessary. The evidence for this includes many texts, among them that Abu Talib, the uncle of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), used to affirm that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was true, and he would say:

*They surely know that our son is not a liar among us,*
*nor is he concerned with vain speech.*

And he would say:

*I have known that the religion of Muhammad*
*is among the best religions of mankind, in religion.*

Nevertheless, this affirmation did not benefit him, because it was not accompanied by acceptance and submission. He ended, may Allah protect us, by saying: "I am upon the creed of 'Abd al-Muttalib." But because of his defense of Islam, Allah the Mighty and Majestic permitted His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) to intercede for him, so he interceded, and he was in a shallow part of the Fire, with two sandals whose heat boils his brain forever and ever. (Agreed upon; narrated by al-Bukhari, 3883, and Muslim, 209/357, from al-'Abbas.) We seek refuge in Allah: forever and ever. And this is the least punished of the people of the Fire. May Allah protect me and you from it.

We do not know of any disbeliever for whom intercession benefited absolutely, in the sense that he was saved from punishment forever. We do not know of any disbeliever whose punishment was lightened by intercession except Abu Talib. So we say: Belief in the Last Day, and that there is a Fire, is not sufficient for faith. Acceptance and submission are necessary.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: A person may be deceived by the religion he is upon. He may be deceived by his religion, by His saying: ﴿and what they used to invent deceived them in their religion﴾ [Aal 'Imran 24]. He becomes deceived that he prays, pays zakah, fasts, and performs Hajj, and then says to himself: "I will not be punished." This is a deficiency in reasoning, because the matter is not merely that you pray, pay zakah, fast, or perform Hajj. The whole matter is that this deed is accepted from you. How many a worker has nothing from his work except fatigue, because of a nullifier that precedes it or follows it. A preceding nullifier is such as the absence of sincerity, for example. A following nullifier is such as being impressed with one's deed and boasting of it before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and a person considering himself to have a right over his Lord. This may nullify the deed. So your deed is surrounded by dangers before it and after it. For this reason, do not be deceived by the religion you are upon. Rather, always ask your Lord for success and acceptance. Success comes first, and acceptance comes after. A person may even want good and love good, but be afflicted by innovation. How many people love good, have a desire and love for Allah and His Messenger, yet are afflicted by ignorance and innovate in the religion of Allah what is not part of it? Is their deed then destroyed or accepted? It is destroyed, because one of the conditions for accepting a deed is that it conform to what the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) brought, based on the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever does a deed that is not in accordance with our matter, it is rejected." (Agreed upon; al-Bukhari, 2697, and Muslim, 1718/17, the wording is Muslim's.)

Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿How then will it be when We gather them for a Day about which there is no doubt, and every soul will be paid in full for what it earned, and they will not be wronged?﴾ [Aal 'Imran 25].

In this verse there is evidence of the greatness of that Day, by His saying: ﴿How then will it be when We gather them﴾ ﴿and every soul will be paid in full﴾.

There is also in it evidence of a summons to lament for those who will have nothing on that Day but loss and ruin. For this reason He said: How will their state be on that Day?

The answer is: their state will be the most wretched state, the most wretched state of all, may Allah protect us, because they will have nothing. They have lost their religion and their worldly life.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: Affirmation of the Last Day, by His saying: ﴿for a Day about which there is no doubt﴾.

* Another benefit: Whoever disbelieves in the Last Day or doubts it is a disbeliever, because he is denying the saying of the Exalted: ﴿about which there is no doubt﴾. Allah has informed that this Day is beyond doubt; it is a reality, and you will surely, surely be gathered with your father, mother, brother, and sister on that Day. Yet you will flee from them, ﴿The Day a man will flee from his brother, and his mother and his father, and his wife and his children. For each man among them, that Day will be a matter sufficient for him﴾ [Abasa 34–37], until people settle in their abodes. When people settle in their abodes, and one gathers with them in Paradise, this is the utmost of desires. ﴿And those who believed, and whose descendants followed them in faith, We will join with them their descendants, and We will not deprive them of anything of their deeds﴾ [At-Tur 21]. As for young children who died without having descendants to join their fathers so that they might be gathered with them, would the higher be lowered to the lower, or the reverse?

The reverse: the lower is raised to the higher. As for one who has children, he has his own independent rank, because he has descendants. In any case, in His saying: ﴿How then will it be when We gather them for a Day about which there is no doubt﴾ there is evidence that whoever doubts this Day or denies it is a disbeliever, because he is denying Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: The Day of complete payment is the Day of Resurrection, by His saying: ﴿and every soul will be paid in full for what it earned﴾. I said "complete payment" because a person may be paid something for his deeds in this world. Is that not so? Yes, he may be paid in this world, but he is also paid in the Hereafter. Souls are paid for what they did. He may be paid in this world, but what is paid in this world?

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out and provide for him from where he does not expect﴾ [At-Talaq 2–3]: a way out from every hardship, and abundance in provision, and provision from where he does not expect. This is in this world, and it is a reward. There is another reward, greater and more beneficial, which is guidance. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and gives them their righteousness﴾ [Muhammad 17]. Guidance and righteous deeds are better than wealth, better than wealth, because when Allah increases a person in guidance, his chest expands, his heart is illuminated, and he becomes at peace. Then piety becomes easier for him than anything else, and righteous deeds become the gardens of his heart and the joy of his soul. For this reason the Messenger of Allah (may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him) said: "The coolness of my eyes has been placed in prayer." (Narrated by al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan, 3939, from Anas.) And the believer, for all righteous deeds, finds coolness of the eyes, because in every righteous deed he feels two great matters. The first: that he worships Allah through the righteous deed, and so he increases in humility before his Lord, in love for Him, and in turning to Him in repentance. The second: that by it he follows the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). So when he performs the act of worship, he feels that his leader is Muhammad (ﷺ), and so his love for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) increases, and his veneration for his words grows, and even for his guidance and his *sunnah* (the way and practice). This is the greatest gain: that this matter be attained for you in worship and piety.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: The negation of injustice from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, because His saying: ﴿was paid in full﴾ and ﴿and they will not be wronged﴾. The doer of the payment is known: who pays in full? Allah. And He does not wrong. But is the negation of injustice from Allah, Glorified and Exalted, one of the affirmative attributes, or one of the negative attributes that they call "negative" (*salbiyyah*)?

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on Surah 3, verses 21–25 (part 5 of 5):**

The second point. However, we say: "He does not wrong" means that there is not the least wrong in His recompense. So the negation of wronging indicates the perfection of justice. Wronging may be complete or partial. It may be complete, in that a person is given none of the due recompense for his deeds. It may be partial, in that he is given some of it. When Allah negates wronging from Himself, this necessarily implies the perfection of justice. Likewise, ﴿And We created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, and no fatigue touched Us﴾ [Qaf 38]. Lughub (fatigue) means weariness and exhaustion. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, and no lughub (fatigue), that is, no weariness or exhaustion, touched Him. Why? Because of the perfection of His power and might, Mighty and Majestic. A human performs a work and becomes tired, but the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, because of the perfection of His power and strength, created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in a few days, six days, and no fatigue touched Him. From this we derive a useful principle concerning the attributes: every attribute that Allah negates from Himself is intended to establish the perfection of its opposite. The opposite of wronging is justice, so when wronging is negated, it indicates the perfection of justice. The opposite of power and strength is weariness, so when weariness is negated, the perfection of power and strength is established. Apply this to others as well.

*Student:* Shaykh, regarding His words ﴿So how will it be when We gather them for a Day about which there is no doubt﴾ and His words ﴿Your relatives and your children will not benefit you on the Day of Resurrection; He will judge between you﴾ [al-Mumtahanah 3], how is it that He "will separate between you"?

*Shaykh:* It is not accepted from him.

[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2697) and Muslim (1718/17), and the wording is Muslim's.] However, he is rewarded only for his good intention. *Student:* Yes?

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verse 21–25 (part 1 of 5):

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah and kill the prophets without right and kill those who enjoin justice among the people – give them tidings of a painful punishment.﴾ In this verse there are two recitations in two words. First: ﴿an-Nabiyyin﴾ has a reading ﴿an-Nabi'in﴾. Second: ﴿wa-yaqtulun﴾ has a reading ﴿wa-yuqatilun﴾, so that it reads ﴿and they fight those who enjoin justice among the people﴾.

He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah﴾ – they disbelieve in the signs of Allah, whether the cosmic (kawniyyah) or the legislative (shar'iyyah). The word ᾱyāt (signs) is the plural of āyah, which linguistically means a sign or indicator. These cosmic signs that we witness, which mankind cannot create the like of, are a sign of Allah, a sign showing that the Creator is one, with no partner, and that nothing resembles Him. For if all of mankind gathered together to create a single mountain, they would not be able to do it, or to create a single animal, they would not be able to do it: ﴿Indeed, those whom you invoke besides Allah will never create a fly, even if they gathered together for it﴾ [al-Hajj 73]. The legislative signs of Allah, too, mankind cannot produce the like of: ﴿Say: If mankind and the jinn gathered together to produce the like of this Qur'an, they would not produce its like﴾ [al-Isra' 88]. So the legislative signs are the indicators that the One who sent down these signs is one God, and that He is perfect in wisdom. Those who disbelieve in these signs – after He mentioned multiple conjoined items, the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿so give them tidings of a painful punishment﴾. But how can there be disbelief in the signs of Allah? We say, first: the cosmic signs?

* Student: (...) by denying that the Creator, glorified and exalted is He, created them.

* The Shaykh: By claiming that someone other than Allah created them; this is one.

* The Student: Or by attributing a partner to Him in their creation.

* The Shaykh: Or by holding that He has a partner in His creation.

* The Student: Or by attributing a helper to Him in their creation.

* The Shaykh: Or by holding that He has a helper in His creation; three things. Good. And disbelief in the legislative signs?

* Student: Either by denial or by arrogance, and we seek refuge with Allah.

* The Shaykh: Yes, either by denying and rejecting them, or by arrogance and obstinacy. And among rejecting them or turning arrogantly away from them is distorting the texts (taḥrīf al-nuṣūṣ), for distorting the texts is a kind of disbelief without doubt. He says: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah and kill the prophets without right﴾ – they kill the prophets whom Allah sent to them, without right. The word "prophets" here includes the messengers and those prophets who were not sent as messengers. This attribute is found most among the Jews, for the Jews are the most stubborn opponents of the messengers and the harshest of them, we seek refuge with Allah. Some of them killed prophets without right and worshipped the taghut. Here He says: ﴿the prophets without right﴾. This qualifier is not intended to exclude what opposes it; rather, it is intended to state the reality and to indicate that this killing was transgression. So it serves two purposes:
First: to state the reality, that they killed them while they were not justified, meaning they did not kill them in retaliation (qiṣāṣ), for example, but killed them through aggression and injustice.
Second: that their killing was with falsehood, without right; for there is no killing that is rightful for any of the prophets.

﴿And they kill the prophets without right and kill those who enjoin justice among the people﴾. In one reading: ﴿they fight﴾. Who are those who enjoin justice among the people? Messengers and non-messengers: the scholars enjoin justice among the people, the rightly guided caliphs enjoin justice among the people, the prophets enjoin justice among the people. Thus its conjunction to "the prophets" is by way of conjoining the general to the specific, but He singled out the prophets because killing them is greater than killing others, for there is no killing greater in crime than killing the prophets without right. ﴿And they kill those who enjoin justice among the people﴾ – ﴿justice﴾ means fairness; ﴿among the people﴾ includes the prophets and others. We have already encountered the question: when the general is conjoined to the specific, or the specific to the general, does this indicate that the specific is excluded from the general ruling, or that it is stated explicitly because of its importance, so that it is mentioned twice?
* The Students: The second.
* The Shaykh: The second is closer to the truth: it is mentioned twice, once by way of generality and once by way of specificity, but it was singled out from among the other individuals, or the ruling was restated concerning it among the other individuals, out of concern for it and emphasis upon it. ﴿So give them tidings of a painful punishment﴾. The address is either to the Messenger ﷺ or to everyone who may be addressed. ﴿Give them tidings﴾: inform them. ﴿A painful punishment﴾: the punishment is the retribution, and "painful" means causing pain. Is this tidings meant sarcastically toward these people? Or is it the comparison of glad tidings to that which causes distress, on the basis that in both the complexion is affected and changes?
* Students: The first includes.
* Student: The second.
* The Shaykh: Both are possible. But if we say it is sarcasm, then this adds to the pain of those who are given these tidings, like His saying: ﴿Seize him and drag him into the midst of the Hellfire. Then pour over his head some of the torment of boiling water. Taste! Indeed, you were the mighty, the noble!﴾ [ad-Dukhan 47–49], meaning: say to him, "Taste!" Indeed this word or sentence will undoubtedly reach his heart to the utmost; for he will remember: where is the might? Where is the nobility? Where is the might by which he overcame, and the generosity by which he was bountiful? So the impact will be more severe and his regret greater that he has lost this attribute which in the world he regarded himself as belonging to.
* Student: The statement of the author of al-Jalalayn that the Jews killed forty-three prophets?
* The Shaykh: No, I do not know it well. There is no doubt that they killed prophets without right, but whether they were forty-three, four hundred, more or fewer, Allah knows best.
* Student: If a country imports meat, known to come from a communist country.
* The Shaykh: What?
* The Student: It imports meat from a state that is atheist, not believing in God, communist; most of its imports, or nearly all of them. And there is local meat in the country, but nobody buys it because of its high price, or few buy it. And you know that this man who invited you, he always buys or mostly buys from this meat. If he invites you, O Shaykh, or gives you meat, would you be scrupulous that you do not know where it is from? Most of his purchases from it, he always buys, does he not buy local?
* The Shaykh: First: communist states may have Muslims in them. Have you not heard of the uproar that took place in Yugoslavia these days?
* The Student: No.
* The Shaykh: There are many Muslims there. It has been said that most of those who run the slaughterhouses are Muslims, because they are poor in that place. So the slaughterer may well be a Muslim. But even so, the scholars say: if a slaughtered animal is found in a country most of whose people are of those whose slaughter is lawful, it is lawful, out of regard for the majority and the prevailing condition, and as facilitation for the community. So one looks: if it is said, "By Allah, most of the slaughterhouses in this communist country are run by Muslims," then what is imported from it is lawful. If it is said, "most of them are non-Muslims," then what is imported is unlawful, even if it is assumed to be a land of Jews or Christians; and if it is known that most of those who perform slaughter are neither Jews nor Christians, their slaughter is not lawful.

* The Shaykh: I do not know, because He said: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned﴾ [al-An'am 121], and He did not say, "do not eat of what you do not know." He said: ﴿of that which has not been mentioned﴾, meaning if we are certain that the name of Allah was not mentioned over it.

* The Shaykh: If something is certain, do not eat it. But as long as you are not certain, then eating is permitted to you.

* The Shaykh: It is known that if we are certain, eating is not permitted.

* The Shaykh: Yes, the scholar is obligated to convey the Sharia.

* The Shaykh: Yes, revelation (...). The Qur'an is revelation.
* Student: (...)
* The Shaykh: No, there is no prophet after Muhammad.
* Student: Shaykh, the statement of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve﴾, this is conjoined to every relative clause as the predicate of "inna." ﴿So give them tidings of a painful punishment﴾ is the predicate, and this is the subject. Where does the fa' of the conditional come from?
* The Shaykh: Did you understand his question?
* Student: Repeat.
* The Shaykh: This man understood it very well, and you were born here in the Arab land, and did you not understand that? Yes?
* Student: Yes indeed.
* The Shaykh: He says: the fa' occurring in the predicate of the subject like this; what brought it here? Is it not a conditional particle? The scholars say: the relative pronoun resembles the conditional noun in generality. ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah﴾ is like his saying: "Indeed, whoever disbelieves in the signs of Allah."
* Student: Meaning it includes the meaning of a condition.
* The Shaykh: Yes, the relative pronoun includes the meaning of a condition. He says: when you say, "Whoever comes to me, for him is a dirham," it means the same as your saying, "Whoever comes to me, for him is a dirham." Understood?
* Student: Shaykh, the Exalted says: ﴿And if they argue with you, say: I have submitted my face to Allah﴾. If it is said that the intended meaning of "face" here is the essence, meaning I have submitted my whole essence to Allah, the Exalted, then what would His saying be: ﴿nearer to him﴾ [Qaf 16]?

* Student: I say, Shaykh, that the scholars' disagreement in understanding a text, sometimes some scholars give an understanding of the text that differs from one scholar to another, is this a difference of variety or of contradiction?
* The Shaykh: We do not know. If the two statements can be reconciled, it is a difference of variety. For example, some scholars said concerning His saying: ﴿and the night when it turns its back﴾ [at-Takwir 17], that it means it withdraws; and others said: ﴿and the night when it turns its back﴾ means it approaches. There is no contradiction in this; it is a difference of variety. But if the two statements cannot be reconciled, like His saying: ﴿And divorced women shall wait by themselves for three periods﴾ [al-Baqarah 228], some of them said the intended meaning of "qur'" is menstruation, and others said the intended meaning of "qur'" is purity; this cannot be reconciled, so this is a difference of contradiction. Likewise the Hanafis said: the time of 'Asr enters when the shadow of everything is twice its length. Others said: the time of 'Asr leaves when the shadow of everything is twice its length.
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: It cannot be reconciled; this is a difference of contradiction (...).

* The Shaykh: Yes, this disputation: if their obstinacy has become evident, then say this. As long as they are not obstinate but seek the truth, then argue with them until the truth becomes clear. But if their obstinacy has become clear now, then we say: either we strike your necks, or you give the jizyah willingly while you are humbled. This is the duty upon the Muslims when they are able. As for when they are not able at the present time, this is a matter (...).

Nominal, imperative,
and with mā, qad, and lan,
and with the negation of the future (tanfīs).

His, Exalted is He, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah and kill the prophets without right, and kill those who enjoin justice among the people﴾. In the second ﴿يَقْتُلُونَ﴾ (they kill), are there two recitations?

* **The Shaykh:** (...).

* **Student:** The good tidings appear on their faces.
* **The Shaykh:** That good tidings were used in the context of a warning, because it is the sign of news that appears on the skin, so the complexion changes, just as the complexion changes with what pleases. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Those are the ones whose deeds have become void in this world and the Hereafter, and they will have no helpers﴾. ﴿Those﴾ refers to those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah, kill the prophets without right, and kill those among the people who enjoin justice, who are the people of goodness, the ones who enjoin right and forbid wrong. Those in whom these attributes are found are the ones whose deeds have become void. Habt (voiding) of a thing means its going away, its disappearance, and not benefiting from it. So their deeds have become void in this world and the Hereafter. As for the Hereafter, it is clear, because they will not benefit from their deeds, even if they were good. Even the disbelieving person, if he does good in this world, such as kindness to people, especially or generally, that does not benefit him in the Hereafter, by His saying: ﴿And We will turn to what they did of deeds and make them scattered dust﴾ [al-Furqan 23]. But how were their deeds voided in this world? Their deeds were voided in this world because, since they did not benefit from them, they became as though they had not done them, so their deeds did not benefit them. The evidence for this is His saying: ﴿Say: Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Unquestionably, that is the manifest loss﴾ [al-Zumar 15].

He said: ﴿and they will have no helpers﴾. This sentence, as we all know, is a negated sentence with ﻣﺎ (ma). I ask here: is this ﻣﺎ acting like ﻟﻴﺲ (laysa) or not?
* **Student:** It is not acting like laysa.
* **The Shaykh:** Why?
* **The Student:** Because the predicate came first.
* **The Shaykh:** Because the predicate came first. Do you have a witness from the words of the scholars for what you said?
* **The Student:** From the Alfiyya?
* **The Shaykh:** From the Alfiyya, if it is slightly altered, it does not matter.
* **Student:** A grammatical rule says: (...) acts with what resembles laysa.
* **The Shaykh:** No, I want it from the words of Ibn Malik.
* **The Student:** And I have the words of Ibn al-Hajib.
* **Student:**
"The operation of laysa is given to ma without inna, while the negation remains and the order is kept."
* **The Shaykh:** Good, but here there is a difficulty: His saying ﴿from helpers﴾. How do we parse it (i'rab, grammatical analysis)?
* **Student:** ﴿مِنْ نَاصِرِينَ﴾: the مِنْ is a superfluous preposition, a superfluous, superfluous particle.
* **The Shaykh:** A superfluous, superfluous preposition, like that?
* **The Student:** Yes indeed.
* **The Shaykh:** What is "superfluous, superfluous"? Explain it to the brothers.
* **The Student:** Superfluous in its i'rab and superfluous in its wording.
* **The Shaykh:** In meaning. That is, superfluous in the i'rab, and it adds to the meaning.
* **The Student:** And ﻧَاصِرِينَ is the noun of ﻣَا (ma), in the nominative.
* **The Shaykh:** The noun of ma, and Muhammad says: what does ma do? How do we say "the noun of ma"? Do you have anything other than this?
* **Student:** The predicate.
* **The Shaykh:** No, the predicate, that is not correct.
* **Student:** The subject, and لَهُمْ is the predicate.
* **The Shaykh:** Yes, but complete the i'rab of nāṣirīn: subject.
* **The Student:** (nāṣirīn) the active participle, genitive in form and nominative in meaning, subject. And لَهُمْ.
* **The Shaykh:** Wait, complete it, complete it.
* **The Student:** Subject, that is, nominative in form (at the end, correct), (nāṣirīn) the active participle, the sound masculine plural, and its nominative is with the wāw, the letter before it being damma, and its accusative and genitive are with the yā', the letter before it being kasra, genitive in form and nominative in position, subject, and ma is negating.
* **The Shaykh:** What is the sign of its nominative? The implied wāw.
* **The Student:** And ma is negating, and لَهُمْ is an adverbial complement related to an omitted element.
* **The Shaykh:** A prepositional phrase related to an omitted element.
* **The Student:** And the omitted element is the predicate.
* **The Shaykh:** The important thing now: we understood from his words that the wāw is implied in the place of the yā', its appearance being prevented by the place being occupied by a vowel?
* **The students:** The preposition.
* **The Shaykh:** The superfluous preposition. That is, those whose deeds have become void in this world and the Hereafter have no one to help them. And He, glorified and exalted, emphasized the negation here, He emphasized it with the superfluous مِنْ, meaning they have no one to help them, neither collectively nor individually, because the superfluous مِنْ, when it enters, makes the negation explicit in generality, like the negating لَا of genus.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Have you not considered those who were given a portion of the Scripture? They are invited to the Book of Allah to judge between them; then a faction of them turns away, while they are refusing﴾. ﴿Have you not considered﴾: the interrogative here is for amazement, because every intelligent person is amazed at this condition. And ﴿ترَ﴾ (consider) may be a sight of the eye, and may be a sight of knowledge, and the second is better, because it is more comprehensive, and because it relates to a condition, and a condition is known, not seen with the eye, meaning: have you not known about these people?
﴿Those who were given a portion of the Scripture﴾ means they were given a portion of knowledge. The one who gave them the portion is Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and He omitted it because it is known, since Allah, Exalted is He, is the one who gives knowledge. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿He gives wisdom to whom He wills, and whoever is given wisdom has certainly been given much good﴾ [al-Baqarah 269], and He, Exalted, said: ﴿And We taught him from Us a knowledge﴾ [al-Kahf 65]. So the one who gives the portion of knowledge is Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
And His saying: ﴿a portion of the Scripture﴾: does it indicate minimization or maximization? It may be that the intended meaning is that they were given a large portion of the Scripture, such that it would have led them to guidance, but they, may Allah protect us, were arrogant. And it may be that they have nothing but a little knowledge, and that even if it were supposed that they had much knowledge, this knowledge did not benefit them, so they became like the one given a small portion of knowledge.
And His saying: ﴿They are invited to the Book of Allah﴾ is the place of amazement: that is, despite the knowledge they have, they are invited to the Book of Allah. The one inviting them is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and whoever calls with his call until the Day of Resurrection. These are invited to the Book of Allah ﴿to judge between them﴾. The attribution of judgment here may be to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that Allah judges between them by His Book, and it may be to the Book, and judgment is attributed to it because the judgment comes through it, and a thing is often attributed to its cause. In any case, whether we say the pronoun in ﴿يَحْكُمَ﴾ (judge) refers to Allah or we say it refers to the Book, these people are invited to the Book of Allah to judge between them, but they do not accept this. That is why He said: ﴿then a faction of them turns away, while they are refusing﴾. A faction of them turns away, not all of them, because some of them have been guided. Some of these who were given a portion of the Scripture have been guided by Allah, and they are many. But a faction of them turned away, and along with their turning away they are refusing, may Allah protect us, having no acceptance either outwardly or inwardly. Rather, they are turning away and refusing. He said ﴿while they are refusing﴾, which is a circumstantial clause from ﴿faction﴾. He said that because a person may turn away due to a passing cause, but there remains in his heart some acceptance. As for these, they are turning away, and they have been filled with aversion from the Book of Allah to judge between them. And here He says: ﴿a faction of them turns away, while they are refusing﴾. How is a circumstantial clause valid from an indefinite noun?
* **Student:** The circumstantial (hal) is what describes the state of the doer.
* **The Shaykh:** Yes.
* **The Student:** Whether the doer is indefinite or definite.
* **The Shaykh:** No, no.
* **The Student:** It describes the state of the doer.
* **The Shaykh:** Yes, but the doer must be definite, or indefinite with a reason.
* **Student:** Because it is qualified.
* **The Shaykh:** Because it is qualified: ﴿a faction of them﴾. When an indefinite noun is qualified, it becomes specified, and so it resembles the definite.
﴿Then a faction of them turns away, while they are refusing. That is because they said: "The Fire will not touch us except for numbered days"﴾. ﴿That﴾ refers to the turning away and refusing. Because they deceived themselves and said: ﴿The Fire will not touch us﴾, meaning it will not reach us, ﴿except for numbered days﴾, meaning a few days; because everything numbered is few. The evidence for this is His saying: ﴿And We do not delay it except for a limited term﴾ [Hud 104], and He said: ﴿Say: The enjoyment of this world is little﴾ [al-Nisa' 77]. So everything numbered is few, because a thing that passes by counting, one, two, three, four, must end. These people say: ﴿The Fire will not touch us except for numbered days﴾. Then who will succeed them after that? Who will succeed them in it? They claim that the one who succeeds them will be the Prophet ﷺ and his companions. These are the Jews. They said, by their own assumption and a rejected claim: they will enter the Fire, but will not remain in it except for numbered days, and then the Prophet ﷺ and his companions will succeed them in it forever and ever. They lied in that. They will indeed be touched by the Fire and will remain in it forever and ever. But they deceived themselves and deluded their common folk with this false, fabricated saying: ﴿That is because they said: The Fire will not touch us except for numbered days. And their fabrications deceived them in their religion﴾. ﴿Deceived them﴾: deluding and deception are close in meaning. That is, these people were deceived, or were taken in, regarding their religion, since they thought they were upon the truth. And some of them opposed the truth while knowing it, a fabricator and a liar. ﴿And their fabrications deceived them in their religion﴾, that is, what they used to fabricate, and among it their saying: ﴿The Fire will not touch us except for numbered days﴾.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verses 21–25 (part 3 of 5):

﴿So how will it be when We gather them for a Day about which there is no doubt, and every soul will be paid in full what it earned, and they will not be wronged?﴾ That is, how will their condition be? How will their condition be at that time, when We gather them for a Day about which there is no doubt? The interrogative here is for magnifying the matter, meaning: how great will their condition be on that Day, and how intense will their regret be! ﴿when We gather them for a Day about which there is no doubt﴾: that is, We gather them for this Day, meaning in it. The *lam* (ل) always carries the sense of (في, "in"), and grammarians call it *lam al-tawqit* (the lam of time). From it is the Almighty's saying: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them for their waiting period﴾ [al-Talaq 1], meaning: at the beginning of their waiting period, in anticipation of it. So "the Day about which there is no doubt" means they are gathered for this Day, that is, in it, and it is the Day of Resurrection.

As for His saying ﴿about which there is no doubt﴾, it may be an informative statement with the meaning of a prohibition, meaning: "Do not doubt it." Or it may be a statement on its literal sense, meaning that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, informs about this Day that there is no doubt about it, that is, no doubt about its occurrence. This Day is established by the Book, the Sunnah and reason. As for the Book, how many are the verses that affirm the Last Day, and how many are the parables that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sets forth to establish this Day, the resurrection of creatures. As for the Sunnah, it also affirms this Day abundantly. As for reason, it necessarily indicates that this creation must have a return (ma'ad) at which it will be called to account for what it was commanded to do. For it is not reasonable that Allah should create the creation, command and forbid it, send messengers to it, reveal books to it, permit the blood of those who do not submit to these books and do not follow these messengers, and then the outcome be that this humanity dies and is not resurrected, becoming dust. If such an act were committed by anyone, it would be said that this is among the most foolish of foolishness. If a person made a garment, sewed it, perfected it, made it as good as possible, and in the end burned it and destroyed it so that no trace remained, all people would regard this as foolishness. How much more so, then, with this creation which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, created, revealed books to, and sent messengers to, and whose blood and property He permitted for those who did not submit to these books or follow these messengers, only for the outcome to be that this creation is destroyed without any punishment or any reckoning. Therefore, the Book, the Sunnah, the consensus (ijma', the agreement of the scholars) and reason all point to the establishment of this Day, about which Allah said: ﴿So how will it be when We gather them for a Day about which there is no doubt, and every soul will be paid in full what it earned, and they will not be wronged?﴾

*Wuffiyat* (وُفِّيَتْ) means "was given," and from it comes the saying "waffaahu haqqahu," meaning he gave him his right in full.

As for His saying ﴿every soul﴾: does it refer to humans only, or to others as well? It refers to humans and jinn, meaning those who are accountable (mukallafun), who were commanded and forbidden. They are the ones who will be paid their rewards in full. As for those to whom no command or prohibition was addressed, they will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection, but they have no deeds for which they will be recompensed. Therefore His saying ﴿and every soul will be paid in full what it earned﴾ does not include them. What then will be the condition of those who turned away and were averse? It will be the worst condition, and we seek refuge in Allah, because they will look at people who have been rewarded with a great reward, and at themselves who have been requited with humiliating punishment. Their deeds will become sources of regret for them, and we seek refuge in Allah, on the Day of Resurrection, and they will benefit neither in their worldly life nor in their Hereafter.

His saying ﴿what it earned﴾ means good or evil, as shown by the generality of the word "what" (ما). But how is it paid in full? As for good, the doer of a good deed is repaid tenfold, up to seven hundred times, up to many multiples. As for evil, the evil deed is repaid with its like, unless Allah pardons it. Allah may pardon it, or he may have righteous deeds that expiate these sins. Thus the recompense and full payment of deeds by Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, moves between grace (fadl) and justice ('adl): grace toward the people of good, and justice toward the people of evil.

As for the third category, which is oppression and injustice, this is impossible for Allah, and therefore He said: ﴿and they will not be wronged﴾, meaning none will be diminished in his good deeds or increased in his evil deeds. We know that whoever gives another his due has only three possible states: he gives it either out of grace, or out of justice, or out of injustice. But Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, gives His due only between justice and grace, while injustice and oppression are impossible for Him, as in His saying: ﴿And your Lord does not wrong anyone﴾ [al-Kahf 49]; ﴿And your Lord is not ever unjust to the servants﴾ [Fussilat 46]; ﴿And whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer will not fear injustice or diminution﴾ [Taha 112]. In a hadith qudsi (a hadith in which Allah speaks in the first person), Allah the Exalted said: "O My servants, I have forbidden injustice to Myself and have made it forbidden among you, so do not wrong one another." [Narrated by Muslim (2577/55) from Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him).]

Now let us return to the lessons of the verse we mentioned. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah and kill the prophets without right﴾ up to the end [Al 'Imran: 21]. Among the lessons in this verse: it is fitting that these disbelievers be informed of what Allah has commanded us to announce to them: ﴿give them tidings of a painful punishment﴾. Without doubt, the Prophet (ﷺ), whenever there was wisdom in giving these people the tidings of a painful punishment, gave them these tidings. Likewise, whoever inherits the Prophet (ﷺ) in knowledge and da'wah (calling to Islam) should give every disbeliever in the signs of Allah the tidings of a painful punishment, but this must follow wisdom. It may not be wise, when you invite a man to Islam, to say: "Come, you are a disbeliever?" If he says "Yes," and you say, "Rejoice in the painful punishment," and then go on to invite him. Is this proper? It is not appropriate. But every situation has its own speech. If you invite him and he is obstinate and arrogant, then it is appropriate to say: "If you remain as you are, then rejoice in a painful punishment." Or if a man comes to you praising these disbelievers, saying: "So-and-so, and so-and-so, and so-and-so," you say: "My brother, give them the tidings of a painful punishment." What benefit will this bring them on the Day of Resurrection?

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: the obligation of faith in the signs of Allah, because Allah threatened these disbelievers who rejected them with a painful punishment. Faith in the cosmic signs (al-ayat al-kawniyyah) has one meaning, and faith in the legislative signs (al-ayat al-shar'iyyah) has another. Faith in the legislative signs, as we have said, is: affirming the reports, acting upon the rulings, and not subjecting them to tahrif (distortion), three things. And faith in the cosmic signs is: not believing that Allah has any partner in them, or any helper, or any independent authority over His dominion.

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: the prohibition of killing the prophets, and that it is wrongful regardless of circumstances, based on His saying: ﴿and kill the prophets without right﴾. Although killing the prophets without right is itself part of disbelief, it was explicitly mentioned because of its extreme heinousness, and we seek refuge in Allah.

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: the prohibition of, or the heinousness of, anyone who kills or fights those among the people who enjoin justice. Who are those who enjoin justice among the people? We have said they are scholars and rulers: the scholars explain the Shari'ah, and the rulers implement the Shari'ah. So if someone kills them, he falls under this verse, if they were enjoining justice.

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: the establishment of punishment for those who possess these attributes, based on His saying: ﴿so give them tidings of a painful punishment﴾.

* Among its lessons: the punishment that they are given tidings of is not a light punishment that can be borne, but a painful torment.

Among the lessons of the verse that follows: those who disbelieved in the signs of Allah, killed His prophets, and killed those who enjoin justice among the people, their deeds have become void in this world and the Hereafter, so they gain no benefit from them. As for the Hereafter, this is clear. As for this world, they did not benefit from their deeds, so it is as if they never existed.

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: disbelief nullifies deeds, based on His saying: ﴿These are the ones whose deeds have become void in this world and the Hereafter﴾. This is also indicated by His saying: ﴿And whoever of you reverts from his religion and dies while he is a disbeliever, those are the ones whose deeds have become void in this world and the Hereafter, and they are the companions of the Fire, wherein they will abide eternally﴾ [al-Baqarah 217].

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: these disbelievers have no helpers: ﴿and they will have no helpers﴾. But is the meaning that they have no helper in this world and the Hereafter, or only in the Hereafter? It means in the Hereafter. As for this world, someone of their kind may help them. But they and those who help them are destined for humiliation and abandonment, because Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Allah has decreed: "I will surely prevail, I and My messengers." Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might﴾ [al-Mujadila 21].

* Student: His saying ﴿for a limited number of days﴾: why the distinction between ﴿ma'dudah﴾ [al-Baqarah 80] and ﴿ma'dudat﴾? (...)

* * *

* Student: ﴿Say, "O Allah, Owner of sovereignty, You give sovereignty to whom You will and You take sovereignty away from whom You will. You honor whom You will and You humble whom You will. In Your hand is [all] good. Indeed, You are over all things competent"﴾ [Al 'Imran 26].

* Shaykh: (...) ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah and kill the prophets without right and kill those who enjoin justice among the people—give them tidings of a painful punishment. Those are the ones whose deeds have become void in this world and the Hereafter, and for them there are no helpers﴾. ﴿their deeds have become void in this world and the Hereafter﴾.
