* The student: Yes, because we say this relates to the soul, not the body, and this..
* Another student: Shaykh, we said that what the brain sends, it prepares the thing and forms an image of it, then sends it to the heart, and then the heart orders its execution.
* The Shaykh: According to what reaches it. Did you understand? For example, this man's brain has not changed and his conceptions have not changed, and the heart sends and commands according to what reaches it of conceptions. So if this man is upright and righteous, what reaches the heart that was transplanted into him, the righteous thing, it commands it. Or do they say: "It is placed," I think this is an artificial heart.
* A student: (...) Is there no problem with faith?
* The Shaykh: No, it is not a problem at all, it is not a difficulty, because this heart has valves and other things that Allah the Mighty and Majestic created in the form that they manufacture, or they manufacture them in the form that Allah created, so it is not problematic.
* A student: Shaykh, regarding His words, the Exalted: ﴿instead of the believers﴾, its restriction is that it is not (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed, we discussed this: this is to clarify the most abhorrent form of allegiance. Otherwise there is another verse that indicates the prohibition of taking them as allies absolutely.
* A student: Shaykh, does Satan know what whispers in a person's soul?
* The Shaykh: What do you say?
* Students: He is the one who whispers; essentially, he is the one who whispers.
* The Shaykh: Satan, without doubt, probes the heart, testing it, because he runs through the son of Adam like blood. Then if he sees that the heart is strong, meaning he is unable to overcome it, unable to overcome it, just as Satan used to flee from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him: "Satan never takes a path except that 'Umar takes a different path"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3294) and Muslim (2396/22) from the hadith of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas.]]. And if he finds softness and laxity in the heart, he increases it in softness and laxity. And if he finds strength in it, he tries to increase it toward extremism and excess.
* A student: But Shaykh, if, for example, my soul speaks to itself about something, does this speaking become known?
* The Shaykh: Allah knows best, but there is no doubt that He tests the hearts.
* The student: But Allah, glorified and exalted, alone possesses this knowledge.
* The Shaykh: But Allah may make others aware of it.
* * *
* A student: ﴿On the Day every soul will find what it has done of good present, and what it has done of evil, it will wish that between it and that were a great distance. And Allah warns you of Himself, and Allah is Kind to the servants﴾ (30). ﴿Say: If you should love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you and forgive you your sins. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (31). ﴿Say: Obey Allah and the Messenger; but if they turn away, then indeed, Allah does not love the disbelievers﴾ (32) [Ali 'Imran 30–32].
* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿On the Day every soul will find what it has done of good present﴾.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Say: Whether you conceal what is in your breasts or reveal it, Allah knows it.﴾

This verse also refutes the Jabriyyah (those who hold that man is compelled in his actions and has no will of his own). The refutation is that Allah attributes the act to man, saying ﴿if you conceal﴾ and ﴿or reveal it﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: Allah encompasses everything in knowledge, even what lies within a person's ribs (the innermost thoughts). Because of His words ﴿if you conceal﴾ and ﴿or reveal it, Allah knows it﴾, nothing that is in a person's soul is hidden from Him. Moreover, He knows what a person has not yet spoken to himself about, that he will think about it at a specific time and place. Is this clear?

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: a warning against a person harboring in his soul what does not please Allah. Allah only told us of His knowledge of this as a warning to us against concealing in our breasts what He does not approve.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the comprehensiveness of Allah's knowledge, in His words ﴿and He knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth﴾. The verses about knowledge vary: sometimes they are general and sometimes detailed, and sometimes they concern the actions of man and sometimes the actions of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. When a person believes in the attribute of knowledge, it brings him two matters:
The first: fleeing from disobedience to Allah, so that Allah does not find him where He has forbidden him, that is, Allah does not find him where He has forbidden him.
The second: profit in obeying Allah, so that Allah does not miss him where He has commanded him; for he knows that Allah, glorified and exalted, believes that Allah, glorified and exalted, knows him.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of the heavens, and that the word is plural. Allah has stated in His Book that they are seven, saying: ﴿Say: Who is the Lord of the seven heavens and the Lord of the Mighty Throne?﴾ [al-Mu'minun 86]. As for the earth, it comes in the singular and is not mentioned in the Qur'an in the plural, but it is mentioned in the plural in the Sunnah. In the Qur'an there is an indication that there are seven of them, in the words of the Exalted: ﴿Allah is He who created seven heavens and of the earth the like thereof﴾ [at-Talaq 12]. The likeness here cannot be in the manner (of their creation), since that is impossible, and when likeness in manner is impossible, it necessarily means likeness in number, just as you say: "Glory be to Allah as many as the number of His creation, and praise be to Allah the like thereof," meaning as many as the number of His creation.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of Allah's power, the Mighty and Majestic, in His words ﴿and Allah is over all things competent﴾, and the comprehensiveness of this power in His words ﴿over all things competent﴾.

* Among its benefits: guiding a person to attach himself to his Lord. For when you know that Allah is over all things competent, nothing will prevent you from turning to Allah, glorified and exalted, by asking for whatever you want. Do not consider anything too far-fetched. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said, alerting to this matter: ﴿It may be that Allah will bring about affection between you and those of them with whom you have enmity﴾ [al-Mumtahanah 7]. It is well known that enmity between the believers and the disbelievers is a established matter, and a person may consider it far-fetched that Allah would place affection in his heart for this disbeliever on account of his faith. So Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿It may be that Allah will bring about affection between you and those of them with whom you have enmity, and Allah is Competent, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. ﴿Competent﴾ in regard to turning hearts, the Mighty and Majestic. ﴿Forgiving﴾ in that He makes it easy for these disbelievers to embrace Islam and forgives them. Did this happen or not? It happened. It happened, for a people of the disbelievers embraced Islam in the year of the Conquest and before the year of the Conquest, and enmity in the hearts of the believers toward them turned into affection.

In sum: when you know the power of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, this brings you to attach yourself to your Lord, glorified and exalted, and not to consider anything you ask of Him as too far-fetched.

Then the Most High said: "On the Day every soul will find what it has done of good present (before it)." The phrase "the Day" (yawma) is a time adverb. The well-known rule among the grammarians (ahl al-nahw) is that an adverb of time or place and a prepositional phrase must have something they depend on (mut'alliq), because they are like a direct object, or like a predicate when they occur as a predicate, or like a relative clause complement when they occur as one. The point is that they cannot stand on their own; they need a governing element ('amil), as the author of al-Jumal said:

"The preposition must have something it depends on,
a verb or its meaning, such as 'murtaqi' (ascending).
Exempt every superfluous particle that has no governing effect,
such as the ba', min, and kaf, and also la'alla."

So every original (non-superfluous) preposition must have something it depends on.

As for His saying "the Day every soul will find": since "yawma" is a time adverb, it must have something it depends on. Where is its dependent? The dependent is omitted, and its estimated form is: "Remember the Day when...", i.e., remember people with it and warn them of this great Day. "Every soul will find what it has done of good present." "Every soul" here means all accountable souls, namely humans and jinn, for these are charged with worshipping God, as the Most High said: "I did not create the jinn and humankind except that they should worship Me" [al-Dhariyat 56]. As for animals, they will not find what they have done, but retribution will be made for them if they were wronged, as the Prophet (ﷺ) informed: that "the hornless sheep will be given retribution from the horned sheep on the Day of Resurrection."[[Recorded by Muslim (2582/60) from Abu Hurayra.]] As for animals themselves, they are not accountable, and their deeds go nowhere. "On the Day every soul will find": so "every soul" is restricted by what? By being accountable: every accountable soul, which is commanded and forbidden.

"What it has done of good present": "ma" here is a relative pronoun functioning as the first object, "muhdaran" is the second object, and "min khayr" is a prepositional phrase explaining "ma" in His saying "what it has done." The clause "'amilat" is the relative clause, and the returning pronoun of the relative is omitted; the estimated form is: "what it has done of good, present." His saying "what it has done" includes everything it has done, whether little or much. The Most High said: "Whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it" [al-Zalzala 7]. (Everything it has done.)

As for His saying "present," who presents it? God the Most High presents it, either by His word, or His angels present it, or He commands and it is presented. The word "present" may suggest to the mind that the deed will become a body, presented as dirhams are presented to one who collects them. If this is what God the Most High intends, it is not strange that deeds, which are an abstract matter, be made into bodies. This is apparent in the Qur'an, where deeds are weighed, and weighing is only for a dense body. Deeds are placed in the pans of good deeds and bad deeds. This is not strange to the power of God, glorified and exalted. Likewise death, which is an attribute, the cessation of life, will be represented on the Day of Resurrection as a ram, and it will be stopped between Paradise and Hellfire, and it will be said: "O people of the Fire, O people of Paradise," and they will look, and it will be said to them: "Do you recognize this?" They will say: "Yes, this is death." It will be slaughtered, and it will be said: "O people of Paradise, eternity without death; and O people of the Fire, eternity without death." Then the people of Paradise will increase in joy upon their joy, and the people of the Fire in sorrow upon their sorrow.[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4730) and Muslim (2849/40) from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri.]] And we seek God's refuge.

As for His saying "and what it has done of evil it wishes": the "wa" here may be resumptive (isti'nafiyya), so that "ma" is the subject (mubtada'), or it may be coordinating ('atifa), so that "ma" is conjoined with the first "ma," meaning: what it has done of good, present, and what it has done of evil, present likewise. On the first reading, "ma" is the subject, and "tawaddu" (it wishes) with "law anna bayniha wa baynahu amadan ba'idan" (if only there were between it and it a far distance) is the predicate. On the second reading, "ma" is conjoined with the first "ma 'amilat," and there is an ellipsis in the sentence, estimated as: "and what it has done of evil, present, it wishes that between it and it there were a far distance." But the first meaning is more apparent, because the original state is the absence of ellipsis, and resumption is common in the Arabic language. It is also more eloquent, because what one has done of evil may be presented, and a person may be made to confess it without it being presented. Here the statement is general, including believers and disbelievers. A believer's evil deed is not presented to him; rather he is made to confess his sins when God the Most High meets him privately and makes him confess, saying: "Did you do such-and-such? Did you do such-and-such?" He says, "Yes." God says to him: "I concealed it for you in this world, and today I forgive it for you."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2441) and Muslim (2768/52) from Abdullah ibn Umar ibn al-Khattab.]]

As for disbelievers, their deeds are presented. The Most High said: "The Book will be placed, and you will see the criminals fearful of what is in it, and they will say: 'Woe to us! What is this book that leaves nothing small or great but has counted it?' And they will find what they did present" [al-Kahf 49]. For the evil deeds of disbelievers are not erased; they are presented and they will be called to account for them. Thus it becomes clear that the reading in which "wa" is resumptive and "ma" is the subject is more apparent than that in which it is coordinating and "ma" is conjoined with what preceded. So "what it has done of evil" does not please it, "it wishes that between it and it there were a far distance," meaning a long time or a distant place. It wishes it had not done it, and was not reminded of it, and that it had not been presented to it, if it is among those to whom evil deeds are presented. "Wudd" is pure love, so it loves with intense love, with its whole heart, that between it and it there were a far distance.

"Law anna bayniha wa baynahu amadan ba'idan": How do we parse "law" here? Do we say it is a masdar (verbal particle)?

* A student: It is a particle of prohibition for prohibition.

* The Shaykh: No, it is not a particle of prohibition for prohibition. Do we say it is a verbal particle (masdariyya), or that it is superfluous (za'ida)? For "law" after "wadda" is masdariyya, as in His saying: "They wish you would compromise, so they would compromise" [al-Qalam 9], meaning they wish that you would compromise. "Many of the People of the Book wish they could turn you back" [al-Baqara 109], i.e., that they would turn you back. But here there is a difficulty, which is that "anna" following it is masdariyya. However, the objection can be avoided by saying that "law" governs an omitted verb, estimated as: "if it were established that between it and it there is a far distance," or "if it occurred," so it wishes that if it occurred that between it and it there were a far distance. In that case it is masdariyya and the verb following it is omitted; the estimate is: "if it occurred that between it and it there were a far distance." Otherwise we say it is superfluous, and the estimate is: "it wishes that between it and it there were a far distance." If you removed "law" in other than the Qur'an and said "it wishes that between it," the sentence would be correct. So for its parsing we have two interpretations: the first, that it is superfluous for emphasis or stress; the second, that it is masdariyya and the verb is omitted, estimated as: "if it occurred that between it and it there were a far distance."

As for His saying "anna bayniha wa baynahu amadan ba'idan," "amadan" is in the accusative as the postponed subject of "anna."

The Most High said: "And God warns you of Himself." This is repeated because the context requires it; the context requires warning, so beware of God, the Most High. Beware lest God afflict you with His punishment if you disobey Him and oppose His command. The first "God warns you of Himself" concerns action, namely in allying with disbelievers, and the second concerns recompense, because He mentions it after mentioning the recompense that will occur on the Day of Resurrection. Then He said: "And God is Kind to the servants." There are two readings: the first reading is "ra'ūf," and the second is "ra'uf" without the waw. "Ra'uf" is an intensive form (fa'ūl) from "ra'fa" (tenderness), which is the most intense mercy and the most tender mercy, because tenderness contains more softness and gentleness than mercy does. His saying "bil-'ibad" is the plural of "'abd" (servant), and by it is meant the creation; it is from general servitude.

Some scholars objected to His saying "And God is Kind to the servants" coming after "And God warns you of Himself," and said: the context would have required that it say, "And God warns you of Himself, and God is severe in punishment," because the context of warning calls for threat. This was answered: it is among His kindness toward the servants that He warned them of Himself and informed them that the matter is great, for informing a person of the true state of affairs is undoubtedly a form of kindness toward him. Otherwise it is not appropriate to threaten a person with warning and then say: "And you have tenderness and mercy." Rather, they said: the kindness toward the servants returns to what? To informing the servants of the true state of the matter and warning them of its consequence. This is undoubtedly a good and fine explanation.

* A student: As for His saying "And God is Kind to the servants" (...), that it is specific to believers, because this context is the Day of Resurrection, so God, glorified and exalted, is kind to the believing servants, bringing out whoever had an atom's weight in his heart.

* The Shaykh: No, because we said: what is meant by kindness in the warning? The kindness is in the informing, because if people were left to what they have, they would go astray.

* The student: May God reward you with good regarding "amadan": is it not in the accusative as an adverb of time?

* The Shaykh: No.

* The student: "a long time."

* The Shaykh: No, because it is affected by governing elements, so one says "ila amadin ba'idin" (to a far term), "ila amadin qarib" (to a near term), and one says "amaduhu amadun tawil" (its term is a long term).

* A student: Regarding "the Day every soul will find what it has done of evil present," could it not be that the records are brought and it is seen before it, and this is the presenting of deeds?

* The Shaykh: It is possible, it is possible, and that is why we said there are two interpretations, but the closer one is that it is resumptive.

* A student: Shaykh, the Most High's saying "and what it has done of evil present": does it include major and minor sins?

* The Shaykh: Yes indeed, everything that has not been pardoned.

Our Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, said: "On the Day every soul will find what it has done of good present."

* Among the benefits of this verse: warning and reminder of this great Day on which a person will find what he has done of good or evil.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the obligation, or at least the recommendation, of a person's remembrance of this Day; because "remember" (udhkur) includes both verbal remembrance and mental remembrance, meaning reflection in the heart.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the establishment of recompense for every soul. Is this general? Or is whoever is not accountable excluded? It is possible: if we look at the generality of the wording, we say it is inclusive, and the non-accountable one has good recorded for it but not evil recorded against it, so what it has done of evil is lifted from it. It is also possible that what is meant is the souls to whom recompense applies as punishment or honor, namely the accountable souls. There is no doubt that it is not general regarding animals, for animals do not find this.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the perfection of God's power in presenting what a person has done, whether little or much. From where do we derive that it is little and much? From the relative "ma," which conveys generality.

* Among its benefits: the perfection of His watchfulness, glorified and exalted, that nothing escapes Him; everything a person has done he will find. So you, and yourself! See what you have sent forward for this Day, of good or of its opposite.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of the Last Day, the Day of recompense, which is known.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that evil harms its doer. From where is this derived? Because His saying "and what it has done of evil" is parallel to His saying "of good," and the requirement of the parallelism would have been that He say "and what it has done of evil," since He said "of good," whose opposite is evil. But He expressed evil by its consequence, the harm, because evil harms its doer: "Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own soul, and whoever does evil, it is against it" [Fussilat 46].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of consciousness on that Day, from His saying "wudd," because affection is pure love, and it is a branch of awareness of a thing.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the evildoer's aversion to what he has done on that Day, and that he loves that between him and it there be what is between the east and the west, from His saying "it wishes that between it and it there were a far distance." Likewise a person wishes that between him and his evil deed there were a far distance, and between him and an evil companion a far distance. The Most High said: "And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We appoint for him a devil, and he is his companion. And indeed they hinder them from the way, while they think they are guided. Until, when he comes to Us, he says: 'Oh, would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts! Wretched is the companion!'" [al-Zukhruf 36-38]. In this world they are friends, but in the Hereafter they are enemies.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: God's mercy toward His servants by warning them of Himself, so that they do not fall into His punishment and wrath, from His saying "And God warns you of Himself."

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that one should use the style suited to the situation. God, the Most High, said in this verse: "God warns you of Himself," while in many verses He shows affection and kindness to His servants, because the situation we are in is what? A situation of warning and threat. The situation of warning and threat should be addressed with suitable styles. For this reason it is said that the utmost eloquence is the speech shaped to suit the situation. This is the utmost of eloquence: that speech be fashioned to match what the situation calls for. For if it were shaped otherwise, it would be considered incoherent. If a truthful friend came and said: "So-and-so has arrived, by God, he has arrived, by God, he has arrived, by God Who there is no god but Him, he has arrived," would this be eloquence or not? It is not eloquence, because you would say to him: "Stop, brother, I did not ask you to swear; until now I have not said you are lying, so that you swear!" Thus producing speech that matches the situation is undoubtedly the utmost of eloquence, as in this verse.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of kindness to God, indeed the affirmation of the Name and attribute in His saying "ra'ūf." Kindness is the most intense and most tender mercy. Consider His saying about Himself: "And God is Kind to the servants," and His saying about His Prophet: "Kind and merciful to the believers" [al-Tawba 128]. The kindness of God is general, while the kindness of the Prophet (ﷺ) is specific to the believers. The disbelievers and hypocrites are not shown kindness: "O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be harsh with them. Their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination" [al-Tawba 73]. This is God's instruction to His Prophet concerning disbelievers and hypocrites. In the flogging of the adulterer, God the Most High said: "And let not kindness toward them take hold of you in the religion of God" [al-Nur 2]. But the Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, is Kind to the servants; His forbearance, mercy, well-being, and provision encompass them.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that a person should know his own worth in relation to his Lord. What is his standing relative to his Lord? He is a servant, and the Lord is the Lord. The servant must be submissive to the command of his Lord, and humble before Him, glorified and exalted, in law as he is humbled before Him by decree. All people are humbled before God by decree; they cannot oppose His decree. The greatest person in the world and the most arrogant will fall ill and die. This is submission to what? To the decreed lordship. But one who is not a believer is not submissive to the legislated lordship. "And God is Kind to the servants."

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verse 31 (part 1 of 2):

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: If you should love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you and forgive you your sins. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ Some of the early scholars (al-salaf) called this verse the verse of trial (ayat al-mihna), meaning the verse of testing and examination. The reason is that some people claimed that they loved Allah, so Allah commanded His Prophet to challenge them with this criterion. The criterion is that if they are truthful, then let them follow the Messenger ﷺ, whether they were from the Jews, the Christians, or the hypocrites. The point is that whoever claims to love Allah, this is the criterion. ﴿And the Jews and the Christians said: We are the children of Allah and His beloved ones﴾ [al-Ma'idah 18]. If they are truthful, then let them follow the Messenger. As for mere claim:

"Everyone claims a bond with Layla, but Layla does not acknowledge them in that."

Everyone claims that he loves Allah, because claiming is easy. But the matter rests on proof, for the burden of proof lies on the claimant. If they truly love Allah, then let them follow the Prophet ﷺ so that they may attain something greater than their claim, which is Allah's love for them. For this reason He said: ﴿Say: If you should love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you.﴾ The matter is not that you love, the matter is that you are loved; this is the fruit. As for you loving without being loved, that is enmity. Look at Barirah and Mughith: Barirah disliked Mughith, while Mughith loved her, and he was tormented by his love for her. Was he tormented or not? Yes, he was tormented. When she was freed, the Prophet ﷺ gave her the choice, saying: "Choose yourself." She said: "By Allah, I do not desire the man," meaning her husband, "but I have been freed, so I request the option for myself, and the Sharia enables her to do so." So her husband would weep behind her in the market, in the alleys of Madinah, asking her not to choose. He came to the Prophet ﷺ, peace be upon him, and said: "Intercede for me, O Messenger of Allah, with her." So the Prophet ﷺ spoke to her, and said: "Return to Mughith." She said: "O Messenger of Allah, if you are commanding me, then I hear and obey, (may Allah bless her), but if you are advising me, then I have no need of him." [Al-Bukhari (5283) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]

"If you are commanding me, then I hear and obey (may Allah bless her), but if you are advising me, then I have no need of him." He said: "Rather, I am advising." She said: "I have no need of him." [Al-Bukhari (5283) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, with something similar in wording.] That is, she did not accept even the intercession of the Prophet ﷺ, and she did not show mercy to the man who walked behind her weeping in the markets. So, is the matter that a person should be a lover, or that he should be beloved?
* The students: Beloved.
* The Shaykh: That he should be beloved. For this reason the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Then follow me; Allah will love you﴾ [Al 'Imran 31]. He did not say: "Follow me so that you may be truthful in your claim of love." He said: ﴿Follow me; Allah will love you.﴾

We say: ﴿Say: If you should love Allah﴾. The address is to the Messenger ﷺ. It has passed us more than once that when (say) is directed to the Prophet ﷺ in the Qur'an, it is an indication of the importance of this statement which he was commanded to say, because this is a command to convey this particular statement specifically. As for the whole Qur'an, he was commanded to say all of it, but some matters are singled out, and it is said "say," such as: ﴿Say to the believing men that they lower their gaze﴾ [al-Nur 30], ﴿And say to the believing women that they lower their gaze﴾ [al-Nur 31], ﴿Say: O mankind, I am the Messenger of Allah to you all﴾ [al-A'raf 158], and similar. This is a command to convey this specific matter, so it contains emphasis and a sign of its importance. There is no doubt that this must be taken care of. A person comes and says: "By Allah, I love Allah, I am the beloved of Allah," and deceives the common people. It is said: "Praise be to Allah, let us examine." Just as some people now claim to be friends of Allah. But whoever claims to be among the friends of Allah, we test him. We say to him: "Do you wish for death?" No, this was said to the Jews: ﴿Say: O you who have become Jews, if you claim that you are friends of Allah to the exclusion of other people, then wish for death﴾ [al-Jumu'ah 6]. But we test him with what is less than that. We look: is he a believer, pious? Then he is what?
* The students: Truthful.
* The Shaykh: Truthful. Or is he a disobedient, wicked, deceiver who wants to associate others with Allah in love and obedience? Then he is an enemy and not a friend, because Allah said about the criterion for the friends: ﴿Surely the friends of Allah, no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve (62)﴾ [Yunus 62]. Who are they?
* The students: ﴿Those who believe﴾.
* The Shaykh: ﴿Those who believe and used to be pious﴾ [Yunus 63].

﴿If you should love Allah﴾: there is no doubt that the address here, ﴿if you were﴾, does not identify a specific person; the addressee is not identified individually, but is known in meaning. The meaning is derived from what follows ﴿if you should love Allah﴾. That is: say to whoever claims that he loves Allah, what? ﴿If you should love Allah, then follow me.﴾

He said: ﴿If you should love Allah, then follow me.﴾ The sentence here is conditional, the conditional verb is ﴿you were﴾, and its response is ﴿then follow me﴾. The fa' (then) came in the response because the response clause is imperative, and when the response clause is imperative, it must be joined by the fa'.

﴿Follow me; Allah will love you.﴾ Follow me in what? In the Sharia that I am upon, in belief, speech, action, and abstention. How many items are there?
* A student: Belief, speech, action, and abstention.
* The Shaykh: How many?
* The student: Four.
* The Shaykh: Four. Whoever follows the Messenger ﷺ in these four is truthful in his following, and whoever opposes him is not truthful.

Belief: that his belief be as the Messenger ﷺ and his companions were upon, without distortion (tahrif), without denial of attributes (ta'til), without modality (takyif), without likening (tamthil), without doubt, without wavering, a complete faith free from all impurities. Speech: he neither exceeds nor falls short of what the Sharia has brought of statements. Action: likewise, he neither exceeds nor falls short. Abstention: that he abstains from what the Messenger, peace be upon him, did not do. Whatever the Messenger did not worship Allah by, he must not worship Allah by. If he worships Allah by it, even if he says he loves the Messenger, then his claim is false. If he worships Allah by performing something that the Messenger left off worshipping Allah by, he has not worshipped Allah by it, and yet he says: "By Allah, I love the Messenger," and worships Allah by this matter out of love for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, we say: your claim is false. If you truly loved him, you would truly follow him, in belief, speech, action, and abstention. But as for introducing into his religion what is not from it, where is your love for him? We find that a human being, if he loves someone other than the Messenger, follows his footsteps, admires him, imitates him, watches what he does and does, even if the act is bad, in the eyes of the beloved, it becomes good?
* The students: Good.
* The Shaykh: Good, as it has been said:

"The eye of contentment is blind to every fault, / just as the eye of anger reveals the faults."

This is a proven matter.

The summary is that Allah said to the Messenger ﷺ: ﴿Say: If you should love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you.﴾ ﴿Will love you﴾ is the form with the idgham removed, which is why the sukun appears on it. Outside the Qur'an, if it were said "yuhibbakumu Allah," it would be correct, because idgham here is permissible, and removing the idgham is also permissible.

﴿Allah will love you and forgive you your sins﴾ (Allahu akbar). ﴿Allah will love you﴾ is the fruit and result which every person strives for: to be beloved in the presence of Allah, glorified and exalted. Second: ﴿and forgive you your sins.﴾ Look (Allahu akbar): two great benefits, Allah's love for you and the forgiveness of your sins.

﴿Forgive you your sins﴾ means: all the sins you have committed will be forgiven for you. But do we say that He forgives even if the person does not seek forgiveness for it, because the good deed of following erases this sin, and Allah's love for the person requires that he not be punished? Or do we say: ﴿forgive you your sins﴾ means He makes the means of forgiveness easy for you, if He would not forgive without a cause? Allah knows best. It is possible that He, glorified and exalted, intends that He forgives sins because of this following and love, or that even if the person does what he does, He makes the means of forgiveness easy for him by returning from disobedience of Allah to His obedience. Allah knows best. But in any case, the promise here is certain, which is the forgiveness of sins, either because of a cause from the servant or merely by Allah's grace.

As for His words ﴿your sins﴾: sin (dhanb) is disobedience. As you see, it is a plural construct in the definite form (jam' mudaf li-ma'rifah), and a plural construct attached to a definite noun conveys what? It conveys generality.

﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ The sentence here is nominal and contains three of Allah's names: Allah, al-Ghafur, and al-Rahim.

As for the meaning of (Allah): it has been mentioned to us many times that it means al-ma'luh, that is, the one worshipped with love and veneration, and that the origin of Allah is al-Ilah. The hamza was dropped for lightness due to frequent use, just as it was dropped from (al-nas), (shar), and (khayr).

As for al-Ghafur: al-Ghafur here may be an intensive form (sigha mubalaghah) and may be an adjective of quality (sifah mushabbahah), and the two meanings do not contradict, so it is both an adjective of quality and an intensive form. It is an adjective of quality because Allah has always been and always will be Forgiving, and an intensive form because of the multitude of those He forgives and the multitude of sins He forgives.

Forgiveness (maghfirah) is covering the sin and overlooking it, and not merely covering, for two reasons: linguistic and textual. The linguistic reason: forgiveness is derived from al-mighfar, the helmet with which a warrior covers his head and protects himself from arrows, and the mighfar combines covering and protection. The textual reason: what has been reported about how Allah calls His believing servant to account, that He takes him aside and makes him acknowledge his sins, saying: "I covered them for you in the world, and I forgive them for you today." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2441), Muslim (2768/52) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Umar.] Is it clear, brothers?

As for al-Rahim: He is the possessor of mercy, and it is also suitable to be an adjective of quality or an intensive form. Mercy is an attribute that entails tenderness and kindness toward the one shown mercy.

The combination of the two, al-Ghafur and al-Rahim, is for a great benefit, which is combining protection and care. Through forgiveness, Allah, glorified and exalted, protects you from the evil of sins, and care, by what? 
* A student: By mercy.
* The Shaykh: By mercy. Allah cares for you, so He makes you easy for ease, and protects you from?
* A student: Hardship.
* The Shaykh: Hardship. So the combination of the two for this great benefit is a combination of what?
* The students: Protection and care.
* The Shaykh: Protection and care. Forgiveness contains protection from sins, and mercy contains care for the servant until Allah makes him easy for ease and protects him from hardship.

* From the benefits of this noble verse: Allah commanded His Prophet ﷺ to challenge those who claim His love with this just criterion, which is their following of the Messenger, peace be upon him.
* And among its benefits: it is permissible to address the claimant with a challenge, because this is the truth. Do not be shy before a person who claims what he does not possess, for if he knew himself, he would not claim to possess a quality he does not have. He is the one who has humbled himself in reality, so do not fear him; challenge him so that he establishes proof and evidence for his claim.
* And among the benefits of the noble verse: it confirms the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "The burden of proof is on the claimant" [al-Tirmidhi in al-Jami' (1341) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As]. Although this was in claims between people, in reality it is a general principle: every claimant must establish proof for his claim.
* And among the benefits of the noble verse: the love of Allah, the Exalted, is an aim for all people, even a non-believer says: "I love Allah," is that so? Because of His words: ﴿If you should love Allah, then follow me.﴾
* And among the benefits of the noble verse: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is truly the Messenger of Allah. What is the proof? That Allah made following him a cause of Allah's love for the servant.
* And among the benefits of the noble verse: whenever a person's following of the Messenger ﷺ is stronger, he is stronger in proof of the truthfulness of his love for Allah. This is a sign of a person's love for his Lord. So when you see a person who is very strict in following the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, know that he is very loving toward Allah. Everyone who follows the Messenger, what does he want? He wants to reach Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and nothing is sought to be reached unless it is beloved to the person. What you hate, you do not strive to reach; you strive to flee from it and keep away from it.
* And among the benefits of the noble verse: following the Prophet ﷺ is a cause of Allah's love for the servant, because of His words: ﴿Follow me; Allah will love you.﴾
* And among the benefits of the noble verse: a person should answer another with more than what he asked, if he needs it and the need calls for it, because He did not say "follow me so that you may love Allah," but said ﴿Allah will love you﴾, and no one is loved by Allah except one who loves Allah, for when you love Allah you act, so Allah loves you. Therefore He brought the important fruit, which is Allah's love for the servant.
* And among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of love between the servant and the Lord from both sides, because He said ﴿you love Allah﴾, affirming that the person loves Allah, and ﴿Allah will love you﴾, affirming that Allah loves the person, and it is a true love, unlike those who interpreted it saying: ﴿you love Allah﴾ means: you love His reward; ﴿Allah will love you﴾ means: Allah will reward you. This is distortion.

The cause of this distortion is the false principle, refuted by both revelation and reason, which is: subjecting what is affirmed and negated about Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to the judgment of the intellect. Some people claimed rationalism and said: "We are the ones who judge about Allah what is obligatory for Him, permissible, or impossible, and it is not what Allah reported about Himself that judges between us," (we seek refuge in Allah). This is the necessary implication of their statement, even if they do not openly say it. When it is said: Allah said about Himself that He loves, they say: No, Allah does not love, but He rewards. When He says about Himself that He is loved, they say: No, who loves Allah? The one who is loved is the reward. ﴿So Allah will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him﴾ [al-Ma'idah 54]. Whom does He love?
* The students: He rewards them.
* The Shaykh: He rewards them. ﴿Who love Him﴾: they love His reward. (Subhan Allah.) By Allah, a person finds a taste in the love of Allah like nothing else. (Allahu akbar.) And the love of Allah is not the love of reward. When the love of Allah enters your heart, you forget everything, even Paradise and everything else. You love Allah Himself, the Mighty and Majestic. You see that everything fades away and becomes a servant of Allah before you. So the love is true love for Allah. This is why there came in a hadith, though there is weakness in it: "Love Allah for the blessings He nourishes you with." All blessings come from where?
* The students: From Allah.
* The Shaykh: ﴿And whatever blessing you have is from Allah﴾ [al-Nahl 53]. The greatest blessing upon a person, by Allah, is that He guides him to Islam: ﴿Today I have perfected your religion for you and completed My favor upon you﴾ [al-Ma'idah 3]. The person whom Allah guided to Islam has no equal in blessing except one upon whom Allah has bestowed it. So in reality you love Allah Himself for His essence and for the blessings He has bestowed upon you. The love of Allah is not like the love of a wife, the love of food, the love of drink, the love of clothing, the love of a home, the love of a car. No, it is a love that nothing resembles. Try it and you will find out. Make your heart clear for a day of your life, pray, and be connected to Allah in your prayer, and you will find something that cannot be expressed in the mind, and you will find something whose effect lasts a long time, and you remember that moment in which you were connected to your Lord, the Mighty and Majestic.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verse 31 (part 2 of 2):

So the conclusion is that we say: No one denies the love of Allah Himself except one who has been deprived of it. By Allah, if we believed that we love Allah's reward without Allah Himself, we would not strive so hard at righteous deeds, even though we fall short and do little. But we say, meaning, that a person does a righteous deed for Allah, and that does not mean we do not take the reward into account. No, we do take the reward into account. We are not Sufis who say: "Whoever works for reward is working for dust." We say: We love Allah and we love His reward. But what is the origin?
* Student: The love of Allah.
* The Shaykh: The love of Allah. This is why Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿For those who do good is the best reward, and more﴾ [Yunus 26]. What is ﴿the best reward﴾? Paradise in its entirety with all its bliss. ﴿And more﴾ is looking at the Face of Allah. So He made looking at the Face of Allah an addition, an additional matter beyond the bliss; because a person, may Allah make me and you among those who look upon Him, when he looks at his Lord, this is the most perfect pleasure and delight he can find (...). Therefore we say: the love of Allah is truly love for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and there is no barrier to it.
They say: Love exists only between those who are compatible, and there is no compatibility between the Creator and the created. What do we say to them?
* Student: A claim.
* The Shaykh: A claim, a false claim refuted by reality. Do you not love your homes, your clothes, and your mounts? A man has a camel that is extremely unruly, which the bridle cannot restrain, and a camel that is docile, smooth in its gait, a pacer. Which of the two do you love more?
* Student: The second.
* The Shaykh: Or the first? The one you love, you say: "Go and bring my camel." He brings the unruly camel and you say: "No, go and return it, bring the second." Why? Because the second is more beloved to him. Who says that love exists only between those who are compatible or similar? Who says this? It is established love.
Then, supposing this occurs among creatures, it is not so between the Creator and the created. Allah, and He knows best, has affirmed that the Creator and the created love and are loved.
So in this verse there is a refutation of those who deny what? The love of Allah, the love between the human being and the Lord.
And people on this matter are of three categories: One category said: there is no love between the Lord and the servant from either side. Another category said: No, rather love is established between the Lord and the servant from both sides. And a third said: Allah loves but does not love in return. The Qur'an and the Sunnah refute two groups and affirm one group. Whoever negates love between the two parties, his saying is false; and whoever contradicts himself by affirming it on the side of the servant but not the Lord has also contradicted himself. The first's saying is false but consistent; his saying is consistent, but it is false. The second's saying is contradictory and false. Whoever affirms it between the servant and the Lord, this is the one who is upon the truth, because Allah has affirmed that.
* Student: Shaykh, if a person realizes the four matters by which he follows the Prophet ﷺ, belief, speech, and action, does that conflict with it? Does his committing sins, his mixing with some minor sins, prevent the love of Allah?
* The Shaykh: No, it may not prevent it, but it certainly diminishes it (...).
In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Bestower of Mercy. * Among the benefits of this noble verse: the magnificent fruit of following the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, which is the love of Allah.
* Among the benefits of the verse also: it is fitting for a person, when he performs a deed, to feel within himself, or to sense, that he is following the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in it; because this intention is important. A person, when performing an act of worship, should have two intentions: The first intention: sincerity to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that he did not do it except in obedience to Allah and seeking His pleasure. The second: that he feels he is following the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so that he perfects the deed; because if he is sincere to Allah and sincere to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ by following him, he perfects his worship more and more.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the reward is of the same kind as the deed; from His saying: ﴿Follow me﴾, where He made it a proof of the truthfulness of the claim of love, and made the reward of the same kind: that Allah loves the servant.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that following the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is a cause for Allah's forgiveness of sins; from His saying: ﴿And He will forgive you your sins﴾. This is evident: that following the Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, is among the causes of forgiveness. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿If you avoid the major sins which you are forbidden, We will remove from you your misdeeds﴾ [An-Nisa 31], and He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds﴾ [Hud 114].
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the perfection of Allah's, glorified and exalted is He, beneficence by rewarding the deed more than it deserves; because the one who follows the Messenger attains the love of Allah and forgiveness of sins. This bounty becomes clear to you in that the One who bestowed upon you the deed first is Allah, then He bestowed upon you a second time by rewarding it with more. This is why how great is Allah's thanks to the servant, where He says: ﴿Is the reward of good anything but good?﴾ [Ar-Rahman 60], although the servant's goodness was only by Allah's goodness to him. Is that not so?
* The students: Yes indeed.
* The Shaykh: So Allah, exalted is He, benefits you with the deed first and second: first by enabling it for you, and second by rewarding it: ﴿Indeed, this has been for you a reward, and your effort has been appreciated﴾ [Al-Insan 22]. See the great grace: as if the matter were from us, ﴿and your effort has been appreciated﴾, although the enabling is from Allah, glorified and exalted is He.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of these two names and what they include of attributes. His saying: ﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. In them is the affirmation of the names for Allah in these two names, and the second is the affirmation of the attribute they include. It is well known that each name of Allah indicates its own specific meaning, but the combination of the two names indicates a third meaning, which is: the combination of forgiving faults and mercy through care for virtues; because forgiveness corresponds to sins, and mercy corresponds to Allah's care for the human being, that Allah, exalted is He, has mercy on the human being. From the combination of these two names arises a third attribute: the Lord, glorified and exalted is He, combines beneficence and care, and protection from sins and their effects through forgiveness.
Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say: Obey Allah and the Messenger﴾. ﴿Say⦆..
* Student: A benefit.
* The Shaykh: A benefit? What is it?
* The Student: That a Sunnah of the Messenger ﷺ should not be abandoned even if the common people dislike the People of the Sunnah, and Allah, exalted is He, loves the People of the Sunnah.
* The Shaykh: No, that is not possible, this is not possible; because it has come (...) the superior does not make the inferior... and this is a well-known principle among the scholars of knowledge, and harmonizing among the Muslims is something legislatively required. Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, has stated that if abandoning the Sunnah results in bringing the worshippers together, then harmony must be given greater consideration, as he said: If he leads a people who do not hold the qunut in the witr prayer, he should not perform qunut. And he said: If he follows a person who performs qunut in the Fajr prayer, let him follow him and say "Amin" to his supplication. "Rather, the Prophet ﷺ abandoned rebuilding the Ka'bah on the foundations of Ibrahim out of fear of fitnah"[[Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (1583) and Muslim (1333 / 399) from the hadith of 'A'ishah.]]. This principle is one that students of knowledge should pay attention to, namely: that the lesser matter may come to be better than the greater one. If you reflect on the Sharia according to its general principles, you will find that everything that causes discord and enmity among Muslims is forbidden, such as selling over the sale of a Muslim, deception, and the like, all of this because it causes discord and enmity among the Muslims.
A person can reconcile between performing the Sunnah and harmonizing: he performs the Sunnah within himself, in a place where people are not repelled by it, then he calls people to it by speech first and explains it to them first. When people become at ease with it, it becomes easy to apply it to himself and to them. The most important thing is to persuade those who do not understand; when they are at ease, he applies the Sunnah with them in a manner that involves no repulsion.
In any case, the consideration of interests in the Islamic Sharia is a known matter, and the repelling of harms is a known matter.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verse 32 (part 1 of 2):

﴿Say: Obey Allah and the Messenger﴾. The address in His words ﴿Say﴾ is to the Messenger ﷺ. As for ﴿Obey Allah﴾, what is obedience (ta'ah)? Obedience is an expression for submission and compliance, whether it is in doing or in refraining. If it is a command, then obedience is doing what is commanded; and if it is a prohibition, then obedience is avoiding what is prohibited. This is obedience.

His words ﴿Obey Allah and the Messenger﴾ use the conjunction "wa" (and), which indicates joining. The obedience of the Messenger ﷺ in what he commands of the Shari'ah is part of the obedience of Allah. His obedience in what he commands of the Shari'ah is obedience to Allah. As for what he does not command of the Shari'ah, there is no doubt that he is the person with the greatest right over us, but he may indicate a thing without it being binding, or he may intercede for a thing without his obedience in intercession being obligatory, as passed with us in the story of Barirah when she said: "O Messenger of Allah, if you command me, then I hear and obey; if you only advise me, then I have no need of it."[[Already takhrij passed.]]

As for the obedience of the Messenger in what he commands of the Shari'ah of Allah, it is equal to the obedience of Allah. So when he, peace and blessings be upon him, commands something, his obedience is obedience to Allah the Glorified and Exalted. For this reason the conjunction "wa" came in ﴿Obey Allah and the Messenger﴾. Consider also the legal usage even in giving: ﴿And if they had been content with what Allah and His Messenger gave them﴾ [at-Tawbah 59], and He did not say "then His Messenger," because this is a legal giving, not a divine-decree giving. In matters of divine decree, the Messenger cannot be joined with Allah by "wa"; in legal matters he is joined, because the Prophet ﷺ legislates only by the legislation of Allah. For this reason He said: ﴿Obey Allah and the Messenger﴾.

His words ﴿the Messenger﴾: the "al" (the definite article) here is for previous reference (al-'ahd), not for totality (al-istighraq). Who is the one referred to?
* Student: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
* The Shaykh: The one referred to is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Muhammad son of 'Abdullah, and this reference is mental (dhihni), not present (huduri) nor mentioned (dhikri), because references are of three kinds: mentioned (dhikri), mental (dhihni), and present (huduri). If you say: "Honor this man"?
* The students: Present.
* The Shaykh: This is present. If you say: "I saw a man, so I called the man"?
* The students: Mentioned.
* The Shaykh: This is mentioned. If you say: "The judge came"?
* The students: Mental.
* The Shaykh: This is mental. Yes.

He says: ﴿Obey Allah and the Messenger﴾, and who is the Messenger? According to the majority of scholars, the Messenger is one to whom a Shari'ah is revealed and who is commanded to convey it, while the Prophet (nabi) is one to whom a Shari'ah is revealed by which he worships, but who is not commanded to convey it. Adam was a prophet, because a Shari'ah was revealed to him, but he was not a messenger, because he was not obligated to convey it. However, his offspring at that time followed him, because they were few and had not multiplied, so disputes did not arise among them, and worldly life had not deceived them; they followed their father in what they worshipped of Allah's Shari'ah. When people multiplied and differed, Allah sent the prophets, as He said: ﴿Mankind were one community, then Allah sent the prophets as bearers of good tidings and warners﴾ [al-Baqarah 213]. Thus the messenger became more specific than the prophet. Accordingly we say: every messenger is a prophet, but not every prophet is a messenger. However, the prophets mentioned in the Qur'an with the term "prophethood" are both prophets and messengers, by His saying: ﴿And We indeed sent messengers before you; of them are those We have related to you and of them are those We have not related to you﴾ [Ghafir 78]. The noble verse indicates that everyone Allah has related to us in the Qur'an is a messenger, even if his mention came only with the term "prophethood."

He says: ﴿Say: Obey Allah and the Messenger; but if they turn away﴾, meaning: they turned away from obedience, did not comply with it, and did not submit. ﴿But if they turn away, then Allah does not love the disbelievers﴾. If they turn away from the obedience of Allah, then this is disbelief, disbelief on their part; but it may be expulsive from Islam and it may not be expulsive. How? If it is total disbelief in everything they were commanded, then it is disbelief that expels from Islam. If it is disbelief restricted to some of the commands, then it is a lesser disbelief that does not expel from Islam. The criterion in this is the texts: whatever the texts indicate to be disbelief, turning away from it is expulsive disbelief from the religion; whatever the texts indicate to be disobedience, it is a disbelief that does not expel from the religion.

As for His words ﴿Then Allah does not love the disbelievers﴾, how is the negation of love explained here? Some of them explained it as meaning: He does not reward them. But this is distortion (tahrif). The correct view is that He does not love them, and if He does not love them He will not reward them; this is the negation of Allah's love for them.

His words ﴿the disbelievers﴾ are an explicit noun in place of a pronoun. The context required saying: "then Allah does not love them," but He used the explicit noun for two benefits: one is verbal and the other is meaningful, and the meaningful one includes three benefits. The verbal benefit is observing the rhyme-endings (fawasil) of the verses. If He had said "then Allah does not love them," this ending would not have matched the endings before and after it. Observing the rhyme-endings is part of eloquence. Have you not seen His saying in Surah Ta-Ha: ﴿They said: We have believed in the Lord of Harun and Musa﴾ [Ta-Ha 70], although in the other verse He puts Musa first, and Musa is without doubt more excellent and more deserving of precedence; but He placed Harun before Musa in this verse (the verse of Ta-Ha) for the sake of observing the rhyme-endings. Without doubt the Qur'an is at the peak of eloquence, so observing rhyme-endings is part of eloquence.

As for the meaningful benefit: His saying ﴿Allah does not love the disbelievers﴾ is an explicit noun in place of a pronoun, which has three meaningful benefits:
* The first benefit: recording disbelief upon these people, meaning ruling on them that they are disbelievers. If He had said "then He does not love them," this benefit of their being disbelievers would not have been achieved.
* The second benefit: generalization, so that the negation of Allah's love applies to every disbeliever. If He had said "He does not love them," the negation of love would be restricted to these people only.
* The third benefit: causation (ta'lil), because when a ruling is attached to a description, it indicates that this description is its cause.
﴿Indeed Allah does not love the disbelievers﴾. Why? Because of their disbelief. So attaching the ruling to the description indicates the causation of that description in the ruling; that is, its reason is this description. If you say: "Honor the diligent (mujtahid)." Why?
* The students: For his diligence.
* The Shaykh: For his diligence. So honor was attached to a description, namely diligence, and this indicates that diligence is the cause. Thus the explicit noun in place of the pronoun has three meaningful benefits and one verbal benefit. But the verbal benefit may not be established or achieved in every place; in this place it is achieved. The verbal benefit here?
* Student: Observing the rhyme-endings.
* The Shaykh: Good. The meaningful one?
* Student: Recording disbelief upon them.
* The Shaykh: That is, ruling on them as disbelievers.
* Student: And generalization.
* The Shaykh: Generalization.
* Student: And causation.
* The Shaykh: And causation. Is it clear, everyone?
* Student: I have a fourth.
* The Shaykh: And what is it?
* The student: Worship through recitation.
* The Shaykh: No, because if He had said "He does not love them," we would still worship by reciting it.
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: That means every verse of the Qur'an would need to be longer, and you would say it is deficient. This is not appropriate.

So we say: in this verse there are benefits.
First: the great care of Allah the Glorified and Exalted for His obedience and the obedience of His Messenger. What is its direction?
* Student: Because He said: ﴿Say: Obey Allah and the Messenger; but if they turn away﴾, meaning they did not obey.
* The Shaykh: No.
* Student: Yes, Shaykh; because He joined the polytheists with "wa."
* The Shaykh: Yes?
* Student: Two reasons, Shaykh. First: the opening of the verse with the command.
* The Shaykh: With "Say."
* Student: With "Say." Second: placing it after the verse of love.
* The Shaykh: Yes, because it has passed with us that when a verse begins with "Say," it is a specific command to convey it, although the Messenger was commanded to say the whole Qur'an. The second connection: it was mentioned with love, after the verse of love, as an indication that obedience to Allah and His Messenger is a cause of that.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the obligation of obeying the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, by His saying: ﴿and the Messenger﴾, and this is repeated in many verses.
* Among its benefits: the refutation of those who say: "The Sunnah is acted upon only if it agrees with the Qur'an." What is its direction? Allah said: ﴿Obey Allah and the Messenger﴾, and it is known that if we said the Messenger ﷺ is obeyed only in what Allah commanded, there would be no benefit in the command to obey him; because everyone who is commanded with what Allah commanded is obeyed, obeyed not for his command but for Allah's command. So obedience to the Messenger by his command is an independent obedience.

Furthermore, we say: the one who says "he does not act upon the Sunnah except what agrees with the Qur'an" is self-contradictory. What is its direction? His saying "except what agrees with the Qur'an" is a judgment that is not valid, because there is nothing in the Sunnah that contradicts the Qur'an; the Qur'an commanded acting upon the Sunnah, so acting upon it is agreement with the Qur'an, not contradiction. Thus this is a contradiction.

I heard that some people denied the argument from His saying: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it﴾ [al-Hashr 7], and said: this is in the section on fay' (spoils). It is true that the verse is in the section on fay', but if we are obligated to accept what the Messenger ﷺ distributed of fay' and to refrain from what he forbade, then what about legal matters? Is not our acceptance of what he brought in the Shari'ah more fitting than our acceptance of what he distributed as wealth?
* The students: Indeed.
* The Shaykh: There is no doubt. Even if we grant for argument's sake, and it is a reality, that it is about fay', it indicates that if we accept his distribution of wealth, then we must accept what he ruled in Allah's Shari'ah.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of the Prophet's ﷺ messengerhood, by His saying: ﴿Obey Allah and the Messenger﴾.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the obligation of obedience, by His saying: ﴿but if they turn away, then Allah does not love the disbelievers﴾.

Know that if abandoning compliance with obedience is caused by disliking what the Messenger ﷺ brought, then this is disbelief that expels from the religion, as He said: ﴿That is because they disliked what Allah sent down, so He made their deeds fruitless﴾ [Muhammad 9]. If it is laziness and disliking this act itself, not because the Messenger brought it, then this does not expel from the religion. This is a matter that must be watched for and noticed, because some people, when they see that a person disliked someone for applying the Sunnah, say: "This one disliked what Allah sent down, so he is a disbeliever." This is a great error. Disbelief is not an easy coin you give to whomever you wish and withhold from whomever you wish; its matter is very grave. It is not permissible to declare takfir except on one whom we are certain has truly been described as a disbeliever. For this reason a person may dislike this act from one person and not dislike it from another. So he does not dislike the act because it is Sunnah, but he may dislike this man himself because he practiced it.

This is a common thing that is observed. If one of the people trusted by the common folk did this act, you would find them saying: "Do you see this as Sunnah? I do not know that it is Sunnah," so they adopt it, or at least do not object to it. But if one untrustworthy person did it, what do you find?
* Student: They object to it.
* The Shaykh: They object to it and dislike it, and this (...) poor man, and they hurl every calamity at him.

So the point, my brothers, is that these are matters in which we must distinguish between one who dislikes the act because it is the Shari'ah of Allah, which there is no doubt in his disbelief, ﴿That is because they disliked what Allah sent down, so He made their deeds fruitless﴾ [Muhammad 9]; and the sign of that is that if it came from outside the Shari'ah of Allah he would accept it. This is disbelief. As for one who dislikes the act because it is an act, this does not reach the level of disbelief, but his situation is examined. May Allah bless you, we have applied these matters to many whom some people hasten to judge the doer as a disbeliever, not knowing that "whoever calls a man 'disbeliever' or says 'O enemy of Allah' when it is not so, it returns upon him," [[Recorded by Muslim (61/112) from the hadith of Abu Dharr with the wording: "unless it reverts upon him." As will come after.]] and the one who said this is the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him. The meaning of "it returns upon him" is that he will be declared a disbeliever; he will become a disbeliever, because he said "unless it reverts upon him," and did not say "unless it is about to revert upon him." He said "unless it reverts upon him," meaning that you will become a disbeliever today or tomorrow, unless Allah bestows upon you repentance. All this is to protect the religions of people. If the Shari'ah protects people's honor by making whoever slanders a person liable to the hadd punishment of eighty lashes, it also protects their religions: by saying of a person "disbeliever" or "O enemy of Allah," it returns upon you, even if you say "O enemy of Allah" regarding what makes him a sinner; it returns upon you and you are afflicted with sin, and we seek refuge in Allah.

So the point, my brothers, is that we must not hasten in these matters, and know that the matter is grave, grave beyond what a person can imagine. But praise be to Allah, what the Shari'ah of Allah the Mighty and Majestic indicates suffices you: whoever Allah and His Messenger declared a disbeliever, declare him so; but you must be certain, you must be certain that this particular man is ruled as a disbeliever. Just as we do not testify for a particular believer that he is in Paradise, even though he is included in the general category of believers, so we do not testify for a man that he is a disbeliever even though he is included in the general category of disbelievers. That is, if a text says "whoever does such and such is a disbeliever," we do not apply this ruling to everyone who does it individually. Just as the texts state that believers enter Paradise, do we rule that every believer individually enters Paradise? No; we do not testify to Paradise for a specific person except one whom the Messenger ﷺ testified for. Likewise, the rulings of disbelief are like the rulings of faith exactly.

Know that if you rule someone a disbeliever, you have made his wealth and blood permissible, you have forbidden him Paradise and made the Fire obligatory for him, you have made obligatory the annulment of his marriage to his wives, that he inherits from none of his relatives, that no prayer is offered over him, and that he is not buried among the Muslims. The rulings of disbelief are not light, to be on everyone's tongue. Yes indeed.
* Student: Some people dislike the Sunnah. For example, a person wears a garment not in accordance with the Sunnah, and they do not dislike this. But if they know it is Sunnah they dislike it, or his beard, or like this; do we inform them?
* The Shaykh: In any case, as I told you: whoever dislikes it because it is the Shari'ah of Allah, this is disbelief.
* Student: (...) a person; but (...) they say: this is excessive strictness and rigidity (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, correct, they see it as (...)?
* Student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: So they dislike the person himself. Therefore, what you mentioned now, add a third: if the one whom people trust in knowledge and religion does it, they do not dislike it; so they dislike the person himself. And that sinner who lifts his garment does not dislike it nor like it, because he says: "Glory be to Allah, perhaps Allah has guided him." Yes.
* Student: (...) if this person who did this Sunnah, and there are other Muslims who did not do the Sunnah as the Prophet ﷺ brought it, they do it for the sake of people and dislike it for the sake of applying the correct Sunnah; what is their ruling, Shaykh?
* The Shaykh: I have given you a rule; apply it to all people: whoever dislikes the man because of disliking the Sunnah, or dislikes the act because it is Sunnah and Shari'ah, he is a disbeliever; and whoever dislikes him for the sake of this person himself, then it is because of disliking the person, and as I told you, our brother Ghanim added a third category.
* Student: The observance of the rhyme-endings of verses. If someone says: Allah the Glorified and Exalted is able to make all the verses follow one pattern, ﴿Lord of Harun and Musa﴾ [Ta-Ha 70]; can Allah the Glorified and Exalted make all verses (...)?
* The Shaykh: And what is the wording?
* Student: Allah the Glorified and Exalted is able to make...
* The Shaykh: We do not judge Allah, my brother; it is Allah who judges us.
* Student: But the observance of the rhyme-endings?
* The Shaykh: Yes, this is well known, and the scholars have mentioned it, and it is true that observing rhyme-endings sometimes leads to a word that is somewhat unusual in the Arabic language for this reason, such as: ﴿By the night when it turns its back (17), and by the morning when it breathes﴾ [at-Takwir 17, 18], and many things of this kind, because this is what eloquence requires.

* Student: May Allah reward you well, Shaykh. 'Uthman (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "What is my concern that I should not curse what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cursed?"[[Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (5931) and Muslim (2125 / 120), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud.]] And in the Book of Allah (...).
* The Shaykh: Well said.
* The student: Can a ruling be derived from this?
* The Shaykh: He did not curse a specific person. Even if it is supposed that he cursed a specific person, the intended meaning is the category, as in the saying of the Messenger (ﷺ): "The one who cups has broken his fast." When he passed by two men who were cupping in al-Baqi', he said: "The one who cups and the one who is cupped have broken their fast."[[Related by Abu Dawud in his Sunan (2367), from the hadith of Thawban.]] The Shaykh al-Islam (Ibn Taymiyyah) said: He does not mean that these two broke their fast because they were ignorant. Rather, the intended meaning is that the category broke its fast, i.e., the category of this practitioner. Yes, indeed.

**Student:** I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿Indeed, Allah chose Adam, Noah, the family of Abraham, and the family of ʿImran over the worlds, (33) offspring, one descended from another. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing. (34) When the wife of ʿImran said: "My Lord, I have dedicated to You what is in my womb, as a devoted servant, so accept it from me. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing." (35) And when she gave birth to her, she said: "My Lord, I have given birth to a female," and Allah knew best what she had delivered, "and the male is not like the female. I have named her Maryam, and I seek refuge for her in You and for her offspring from the accursed Satan."﴾ [Ali ʿImran 3:33–36].

**Shaykh:** I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, Allah chose Adam, Noah, the family of Abraham, and the family of ʿImran over the worlds.﴾

First: I think we have completed the earlier benefits (fawa'id), and nothing remains.

Allah says: ﴿Indeed, Allah chose Adam and Noah.﴾ This sentence, as we see, is emphasized with (inna), because the context requires it, since the purpose is to explain that Allah the Exalted chooses whom He wills from among people. ﴿Allah chooses messengers from among the angels and from among mankind.﴾ [al-Hajj 22:75], meaning: and from among mankind. So Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, Allah chose Adam.﴾ Adam is the father of mankind. Allah created him as a separate creation, and not evolved from another kind or species before him, as the atheists claim. Whoever claims this has disbelieved in Allah, because Allah the Exalted informed us in His Book in several places that Allah created Adam from earth: ﴿from clay like pottery﴾ [al-Rahman 55:14], ﴿from clay﴾ [Sad 38:71]. He created him with His own hand, breathed into him from His spirit, and commanded His angels to prostrate to him. Whoever claims otherwise is a disbeliever, a believer in other than Allah and a denier of Allah, may Allah protect us. Moreover, no one can speak about Adam and the beginning of his creation and how he was created without relying on revelation, and his words are not accepted. Why? Because he did not witness it. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿I did not make them witnesses to the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor to the creation of themselves.﴾ [al-Kahf 18:51]. Allah the Exalted also says: ﴿Has there not come to you the report of those before you: the people of Noah, ʿAd, Thamud, and those after them, whom none knows except Allah?﴾ [Ibrahim 14:9]. Whoever claims to know anything about those who came before is a liar, unless he has proof. And Adam, as we know, is separated from us by very long periods of time, so we cannot accept any statement about him except through sound revelation.

Adam was named, it is said, after his ʾudmah (complexion), meaning that his color was neither pure white nor deep black, but between the two. Allah created him in His image, that is, in the image of Allah the Exalted, as an honor to him. Being created in the image of Allah does not necessarily mean that he resembles Him, because Allah says: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the Hearing, the Seeing.﴾ [al-Shura 42:11]. We must believe in all the texts: we believe that He created him in His image, and we believe that there is nothing like Him.

If you say: How can he be in His image and not like Him?

The answer is: This is possible. It is possible in the created, so what about the Creator? The Prophet ﷺ informed us that: "The first group to enter Paradise will be in the form of the full moon on its night." [Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (3246) and Muslim (2834/14) from Abu Hurayrah]. It is known that resemblance is not required. That is, their form is not exactly like the form of the full moon, but in general terms of beauty and radiance, like the moon on the night of the full moon. Moreover, the Qur'an and the Sunnah do not contradict one another. If it is possible for created things to share a likeness without resembling one another, that is, for one thing to be in the form of another without being identical to it, then it is more fitting that this is possible between the Creator and the created, because there is nothing like Him. As for his saying: "and Allah created him in His image," and "He commanded His angels to prostrate to him," it is an honor for him. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My spirit, fall down in prostration to him.﴾ [al-Hijr 15:29]. He commanded them to prostrate, so He commanded the angels to prostrate to him as an honor.

Adam, peace be upon him, received revelation, as stated in the Noble Qur'an. There is no doubt that revelation came to him also by reason, because he cannot independently know how to worship Allah except through revelation from Allah, and he was created for worship: ﴿I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me.﴾ [al-Dhariyat 51:56]. So both the transmitted texts and reason indicate that he received revelation.

But was he a messenger? No, he was not a messenger, according to the evidence of the Book and the Sunnah. As for the Book, it is in His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him.﴾ [al-Nisa 4:163]. He made the prophets come after Noah. And He said: ﴿And We sent Noah and Abraham and placed in their offspring prophethood and the Scripture.﴾ [al-Hadid 57:26]. As for the Sunnah, in the authentic long hadith of intercession: "People will come to Noah and say to him: You are the first messenger whom Allah sent to the people of the earth." [Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (3340) and Muslim (194/327) from Abu Hurayrah]. Accordingly, Adam was a prophet to whom revelation was sent with a law (shariʿah), and by which he worshiped Allah. The people remained upon this law because they were few, and no disagreement arose among them. When they disagreed: ﴿Allah sent the prophets as bringers of good tidings and warners, and sent down with them the Book in truth to judge between people concerning that over which they differed.﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:213].

As for His saying: ﴿Adam and Noah.﴾ Allah mentioned Noah after Adam because he is the second father of mankind. When his people denied him, except for a few, Allah destroyed them by drowning, and made his offspring the remaining ones, as in Surah al-Saffat: ﴿And We made his descendants the survivors.﴾ [al-Saffat 37:77]. So he became the second father of mankind, and he was the first messenger Allah sent to the people of the earth. He remained among his people for a thousand years minus fifty years, calling them to Allah, and only a few believed with him. A thousand years, and only a few believed with him! When we call ten people and they hesitate a little, and then one of the ten responds, we say: "Our call was not accepted," and we grow weary of calling to Allah and despair. This was a messenger who remained a thousand years minus fifty years among his people, and only a few believed with him. Yet Allah said in His Book: ﴿There was certainly in their stories a lesson for those of understanding.﴾ [Yusuf 12:111].

﴿And the family of Abraham and the family of ʿImran over the worlds.﴾ The family of Abraham: there is no doubt that Abraham is included among them, with even greater priority, but the family was specified because of the large number of messengers among them, especially since the best of messengers, Muhammad ﷺ, is among them. Muhammad ﷺ is from the family of Abraham.
