* Student: ﴿So We sent to her Our Spirit, and it appeared before her as a man in complete form﴾.
* The Shaykh: Yes, that is Jibril (Gabriel).
* Student: O, dear Shaykh, they raise questions to us and we cannot..., we want a decisive proof, Shaykh, against these people.
* The Shaykh: We ask Allah. May Allah help you. What do you have?
* Student: The sending. ﴿It appeared before her as a man in complete form﴾ [Maryam 17]. They say this.
* The Shaykh: Right, correct. We say this: Jibril, peace be upon him, appeared to her as a man in complete form in order to test her.
* Student: A man?
* The Shaykh: A man, a man. Do you understand? Therefore she said: ﴿I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you are God-fearing﴾ [Maryam 18]. And what did he say to her? ﴿I am only the messenger of your Lord, to give you a pure boy﴾ [Maryam 19]. The verses are continuous. It is not that a man came and she became pregnant; he made clear that he was a messenger of Allah.
* Student: The difficulty they raise is that this is a human being, a man (...), they may say that she conceived from him or something like that.
* Another student: Shaykh, this statement (...).
* The Shaykh: They said this. Therefore they said from the very beginning when she came to them: ﴿O sister of Harun, your father was not a man of evil, nor was your mother unchaste﴾ [Maryam 28]. What is the meaning of this? This is an insinuation that she was an adulteress. They are saying: how did you come with fornication when your father was not a man of evil and your mother was not unchaste? If this were hereditary, we would not have been surprised. If your father were a man of evil, or your mother were an adulteress, may Allah protect us, we would say: she is like her parents. This is an insinuation. But what happened? She pointed to him. Look at the verse. So he defended himself.
* Student: Shaykh, there is a sending, Shaykh? Is there a difficulty?
* The Shaykh: There is no difficulty, brother, there is no difficulty. This man, this is Jibril, peace be upon him, whom Allah the Exalted sent to test her. Therefore she sought refuge in Allah: ﴿I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you are God-fearing (18). He said, I am only the messenger of your Lord﴾. There is no difficulty.
* Student: Shaykh, may Allah reward you with good. You said: you presented three opinions about the name of the Messiah. When he wipes the blind person, he is cured?
* The Shaykh: One with an affliction.
* Student: One with an affliction is cured, and that he wipes the earth (...).
* * *
* Student: ﴿When the angels said: O Maryam, indeed Allah gives you good news of a word from Him, whose name is the Messiah, 'Isa son of Maryam, distinguished in this world and the Hereafter and among those brought near (45). And he will speak to the people in the cradle and in maturity, and he will be among the righteous (46). She said: My Lord, how can I have a son when no man has touched me? He said: Thus Allah creates what He wills; when He decrees a matter, He only says to it "Be," and it is (47). And He will teach him the Book and wisdom, and the Torah and the Gospel (48). And a messenger to the Children of Israel: "Indeed I have come to you with a sign from your Lord: that I create for you from clay the likeness of a bird, then breathe into it and it becomes a bird by Allah's permission. And I heal the blind and the leper, and I bring the dead to life by Allah's permission. And I inform you of what you eat and what you store in your houses. Indeed in that is a sign for you if you are believers"﴾ [Al 'Imran 45–49].
* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿When the angels said: O Maryam, indeed Allah gives you good news of a word from Him, whose name is the Messiah, 'Isa son of Maryam, distinguished in this world and the Hereafter and among those brought near﴾. And this we have read.
He said: ﴿And he will speak to the people in the cradle﴾. "Wa" (and) is a conjunction particle, and the clause is conjoined to what preceded.
﴿And he will speak to the people in the cradle﴾, that is, in childhood. The origin of "mahd" or "mihad" is a bed placed for a person, on which he treads and rests.
His saying ﴿in the cradle﴾ means on the bed while he is small. This is one of the signs of Allah the Exalted, because the custom by which Allah the Exalted made humans is that no one speaks except at a particular age. In the cradle, only three have spoken, among them the Messiah 'Isa son of Maryam. He spoke words among the most eloquent speech when his people brought her carrying him: ﴿They said: O Maryam, you have certainly come with an amazing thing (27). O sister of Harun, your father was not a man of evil, nor was your mother unchaste (28). So she pointed to him﴾ [Maryam 27–29]. They said: how can we speak to one who is in the cradle as a child? ﴿He said﴾, that is, when he heard them: ﴿Indeed I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet (30). And He has made me blessed wherever I am, and enjoined upon me prayer and zakah as long as I remain alive (31). And dutiful to my mother, and He has not made me a domineering wretch (32). And peace is upon me the day I was born, and the day I die, and the day I am raised alive﴾ [Maryam 30–33]. Words from the most eloquent and grandest speech, while he was in the cradle. This is one of the signs of Allah the Exalted indicating His power. Therefore all the signs of 'Isa revolve around this matter, around extraordinary events in cosmic affairs. He himself is a sign: created without a father. He spoke to the people in the cradle, and this is one of the signs. He makes from clay the likeness of a bird, then breathes into it, and it becomes a bird. He heals the blind and the leper, whom none of the physicians can heal. He brings the dead to life and brings them out of their graves.
The scholars said: because he was sent in a time when medicine had advanced enormously, he came with signs of the kind of works they practised, so that this would be more conclusive in miraculousness, just as Musa, peace be upon him, came with the staff and the hand that nullified the magic of the magicians, and magic in his time had increased and spread. And just as Muhammad (ﷺ) came with speech most eloquent and most fluent, because eloquence had spread in his time and era, so that these eloquent people would be unable to match it, and it would become clear that it is not the speech of humans.
He said: ﴿And he will speak to the people in the cradle and in maturity﴾, that is, he will speak to them in maturity, from thirty-one to forty. He will speak to them in this state. In this state, it is not strange that he speaks to people. But he mentioned it for a benefit, which is that his speech in the cradle was like his speech in maturity. That is, it was not like the speech of a child who speaks in the cradle ("Papa, Mama") and the like, but eloquent speech, among the most eloquent, as he speaks in maturity. And what is he?
* Student: Mature.
* The Shaykh: He is mature. ﴿And among the righteous﴾, also among the righteous. That is, he is among the righteous. We have previously said that the righteous one is the one whose inner and outer nature is sound, meaning his outward and inward: his outward by sincerity to Allah and freedom from every shirk, hypocrisy, doubt, rancour and hatred toward the believers, and the like. His outward, by what? By following the Messenger, peace be upon him, and not innovating. So he, peace be upon him, is among the righteous whose outward and inward are sound. If you wish, say: their secrets and their openness.
﴿She said: My Lord, how can I have a son when no man has touched me?﴾ ﴿She said: My Lord, how can it be?﴾ She is now addressing Allah, whereas those who had been addressing her were the angels or Jibril. But when they said: ﴿Indeed Allah gives you good news﴾ [Al 'Imran 45], and she knew the matter was from Allah, she directed the address to Him, Glorified and Exalted. She said: ﴿My Lord, how can I have a son?﴾ Consider this entreaty from her: she said: ﴿My Lord﴾. It is known that the word ﴿Rabb﴾ here is attached to the first person pronoun "ya" (my), which was dropped for lightness, and its original form is: "Rabbi, how can I have a son?"
Her saying ﴿How can I have a son?﴾ is an interrogative, meaning: from where can I have a son when no man has touched me? This question is not out of doubt, nor out of considering it unlikely, but for seeking assurance and additional tranquillity, like the saying of Ibrahim: ﴿My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead﴾ [al-Baqarah 260]. Otherwise she had no doubt.
Her saying ﴿and no man has touched me﴾ is a circumstantial clause: that is, while no man has touched me. That is, no man has had intercourse with me, because "mass" (touching) is used for intercourse; it is a euphemism for intercourse, as the Exalted said: ﴿There is no blame upon you if you divorce women as long as you have not touched them﴾ [al-Baqarah 236], that is, not had intercourse with them. ﴿And no man has touched me﴾, meaning neither in marriage nor outside marriage. So from where would a child come?
﴿He said: Thus﴾. Who said? Allah, Mighty and Majestic, because she addressed Allah: ﴿My Lord, how can I have a son?﴾ ﴿He said: Thus﴾, meaning: the matter is so. The prepositional phrase is the predicate of an omitted subject whose estimated form is "the matter." On this basis, it is good to stop here, that is, it is good for you to pause: you say ﴿Thus﴾, then begin: ﴿Allah creates what He wills﴾.
This construction has parallels in the Qur'an, such as His saying: ﴿Thus, and We wed them to wide-eyed houris﴾ [al-Dukhan 54]. This form comes for affirmation and confirmation, meaning the matter is exactly as it happened.
His saying ﴿Allah creates what He wills﴾, Glorified and Exalted, ﴿Allah﴾ is the subject, and ﴿creates﴾ with its clause is the predicate, meaning that Allah, Glorified and Exalted, creates what He wills, whether in accordance with the customary way or against it. 'Isa, peace be upon him, came against the customary way. But his likeness with Allah is ﴿like the likeness of Adam: He created him from dust﴾ [Al 'Imran 59], that is, He created Adam from dust, ﴿then said to him "Be," and he was﴾ [Al 'Imran 59]. And Allah is over all things competent.
The scholars have mentioned that among humans, some were created without mother or father, some from a mother without a father, some from a father without a mother, and most of creation is from mother and father. The one created without mother or father is Adam. From a father without a mother: Hawwa', the wife of Adam. From a mother without a father: 'Isa. And all the rest of people are from a mother and a father.
﴿Allah creates what He wills﴾, that is, He creates what He wills in quantity and quality, both by a known cause and by an unknown cause. Allah, Glorified and Exalted, cannot be questioned about His judgement; He creates what He wills. We said: in quantity and quality, and known and unknown cause, and also in kind. How numerous are the kinds of creation that a human cannot count, let alone their individuals! How numerous is creation! If you wanted to count the creatures, you would not be able to. Allah, Exalted, has counted them, provided for them, sustained them, and prepared every creature for what it was created. Pharaoh said: ﴿Who is your Lord, O Musa? (49) He said: Our Lord is He who gave everything its creation, then guided [it]﴾ [Ta-Ha 49–50]. He gave everything its suitable creation, then guided it, guided it to what it was created for. Look: sometimes you examine a book, you review the book, and you find in it an animal that the eye can only perceive with difficulty, an animal inside this book that the eye can only perceive with difficulty. Who created it? Allah. And who prepared it for provision? Allah. And who sustained it with its suitable provision? He, Allah, Mighty and Majestic. So what about the vast creation that is far greater than this? The point is that Allah, Exalted, creates what He wills in quantity, quality and kind, by a customary cause and by an unusual cause. There is no fault in Allah, Mighty and Majestic, who creates what He wills and does what He wills. He said: ﴿Thus Allah creates what He wills﴾ [Al 'Imran 47]. ﴿When He decrees a matter, He only says to it "Be," and it is﴾. ﴿When He decrees﴾, decrees, that is, a universal decree, because decree has two meanings: universal and legislative. An example of the legislative is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And your Lord has decreed that you not worship except Him﴾ [al-Isra' 23]. That is a legislative decree. An example of the universal is this verse, and the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And We decreed to the Children of Israel in the Scripture that you would cause corruption in the land twice and would become exceedingly arrogant﴾ [al-Isra' 4]. Did We decree it legislatively or universally?
* The students: Universally.
* The Shaykh: It is not valid legislatively?
* The students: No.
* The Shaykh: Because Allah never legislatively decrees corruption. He does not love corruption. But it is a universal decree. What is the difference between the universal and legislative decrees?
The difference between them is that the legislative decree concerns what Allah loves: performing what is commanded or abandoning what is forbidden.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verses 42–51 (part 4 of 7):

Second: The legislative decree (al-qada' al-shar'i) may or may not take effect, and it may or may not take effect on the one it is decreed upon. The cosmic decree (al-qada' al-kawni) concerns what Allah loves and what He does not love. The cosmic decree must necessarily take effect on the one it is decreed upon. So what is the difference?
* Students: Two aspects.
* The Shaykh: Four aspects or two?
* Students: Two.
* The Shaykh: Two. When we mention a thing and its opposite, they become four.

The verse of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Then when We decreed death for him, nothing showed them his death except a creature of the earth﴾ [Saba' 14]?
* Students: Cosmic.
* The Shaykh: Is this cosmic or legislative?
* Students: Cosmic.
* The Shaykh: Cosmic. The verse: ﴿And the water was made to subside, and the matter was decided﴾ [Hud 44]?
* Students: Cosmic.
* The Shaykh: Cosmic. ﴿And Allah judges with truth﴾ [Ghafir 20]?
* Students: Legislative.
* A student: Comprehensive.
* The Shaykh: Legislative, or comprehensive?
* Students: Comprehensive.
* The Shaykh: Comprehensive. That is, even the cosmic decree that Allah decrees, even if it is evil, but in terms of the things decreed. As for the decree itself, it is truth.

Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿When He decrees a matter﴾. The word (amran), is it singular? Its plural is (umur) or (awamir)?
* Students: Umur.
* The Shaykh: Umur. The meaning of (amr) here is affair (sha'n), that is, when He decrees an affair, any affair among affairs, ﴿He only says to it, "Be," and it is﴾. It requires no work, no tools, and no cause. All creation submits to Allah the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And to Him submits whoever is in the heavens and the earth﴾ [Al 'Imran 83]. They await the commands. When the command proceeds from Allah the Mighty and Majestic, the one commanded obeys. The cosmic command says "Be" only, and ﴿it is﴾.

Allah the Exalted said about the resurrection, the resurrection of all creation: ﴿It will be but one shout, and at once they will be on the surface of the earth﴾ [al-Nazi'at 13–14]. Allah the Exalted explained in Surah al-Qamar how this command is: does it repeat? Does the one commanded delay? He said: ﴿And Our command is but one, like a glance of the eye﴾ [al-Qamar 50]. There is no repetition; it is one. Does the one commanded delay? What?
* Students: ﴿Like a glance of the eye﴾.
* The Shaykh: ﴿Like a glance of the eye.﴾ That is, if our Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, wills that this earth and whoever is on it cease to exist in an instant, ﴿Be, and it is﴾. This is the complete, great power, to which the power of creatures cannot be compared.

﴿When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ The particle (fa') here indicates sequence, and if you wish, say it indicates causation. If you say it indicates causation, then read it in the accusative (fayakuna). If you say it indicates sequence, then read it in the nominative (fayakunu). Both readings are sound and recognized among the seven readings: that ﴿He says to it "Be," fayakuna﴾ and that ﴿He says to it "Be," fayakunu﴾. On the nominative reading, the clause is resumptive (isti'nafiyyah), and the fa' is conjunctive, indicating sequence and immediacy: "Be," and it is immediately. On the accusative reading, the fa' indicates causation, as if the existence is caused by the saying. It is known that the effect comes alongside its cause. On the accusative reading, (kun) is the cause and (fayakuna) is the effect. It is known that the effect follows the cause immediately, because it is its cause, and the cause is simultaneous with its effect. Accordingly, each of the two readings conveys a meaning different from the other, but the two meanings are mutually implicated.

﴿Be, and it is.﴾ Fine. Allah the Exalted did not mention what the thing should be like. He only says ﴿Be,﴾ and the thing occurs according to Allah's will. Or must He say ﴿Be,﴾ and specify what it will be?
* Students: The first.
* The Shaykh: Fine, the first.
* A student: The second.
* The Shaykh: The first, the second, the first, the second. When Allah created the pen, He said to it: "Write." Did it write or did it not write?
* Students: It wrote.
* The Shaykh: No, it did not write. "He said: My Lord, what shall I write? He said: Write what will exist until the Day of Resurrection." [Narrated by al-Tabarani in Musnad al-Shamiyyin (1572), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Umar.] So in that moment it ran with what will exist until the Day of Resurrection. Allahu akbar!

So the apparent view, and Allah knows best, is that when Allah says "Be" to a thing, He must specify what it will be, based on the hadith of the pen. However, when He specifies what will be, the thing must be as He specified. The pen did not know the unseen, but when the Lord the Mighty and Majestic said to it, "Write what will exist until the Day of Resurrection," it wrote what will exist until the Day of Resurrection, because Allah informed it. He informed it, so it wrote.

So "Be, [such and such]." The specification of the general command is necessary; it is necessary. This is the apparent view. If Allah the Mighty and Majestic commands it by saying "Be," it is in accordance with Allah's will, and this is not strange to Allah's power as well: that Allah makes this thing submit to His command which He wills, even if He has not informed it of that. But what appears more likely to me, based on the hadith of the pen, is that Allah the Mighty and Majestic commands it to be, and specifies what it will be like. ﴿Be, and it is.﴾

﴿And He will teach him the Book and wisdom﴾. The pronoun in (yu'allimuhu) refers to Jesus, and the subject is Allah the Mighty and Majestic.

﴿He will teach him the Book﴾, because Jesus, like other human beings, knows only what Allah taught him. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The Knower of the unseen; He does not disclose His unseen to anyone, except to whom He approves of the messengers﴾ [al-Jinn 26–27].

﴿He will teach him the Book, wisdom, the Torah, and the Gospel.﴾ (Al-Kitab) means the written. Is the meaning that He teaches him writing, that is, to write well, or the meaning is that He teaches him the earlier scriptures?
* Students: The second.
* The Shaykh: The second. Both are not mutually exclusive: He taught him writing, so he wrote, and He taught him the earlier scriptures, and taught him the Torah and the Gospel. (Al-Tawrah) is mentioned by way of specific after general, because of its nobility. As for (al-Injil), it was not revealed to anyone before Jesus.

As for His saying ﴿and wisdom﴾, this means the Sharia, because the Sharia is from Allah, and everything from Allah contains wisdom. Allah the Exalted said to Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿And Allah has sent down to you the Book and wisdom and taught you what you did not know. And the bounty of Allah upon you has been great﴾ [al-Nisa' 113].

So wisdom is the Sharia. This agrees with those who interpret it as the Sunnah, because the Sunnah of the Prophet (ﷺ) is his Sharia, his legislation which he brought from Allah. So Allah the Mighty and Majestic taught him wisdom. The (al-) in (al-hikmah) here is the mental definite article (al-'ahd al-dhihni), meaning the Sharia which Allah legislated for Jesus, not all wisdom, but the wisdom that was legislated for him.

﴿The Torah and the Gospel.﴾ The Torah is the Book Allah revealed to Moses. The Gospel is the Book Allah revealed to Jesus. Allah wrote the Torah by writing: ﴿And We wrote for him on the tablets of everything﴾ [al-A'raf 145]. For this reason the scholars of the early generations said: Allah planted the Garden of Eden with His own hand, created Adam with His own hand, and wrote the Torah with His own hand, glorified and exalted is He. So the Torah is written by Allah, written by His own hand, glorified and exalted is He, and it was sent down on tablets to Moses, containing what the benefit, need, and necessity of that time required. As for the Gospel, it is the Book of Allah that Allah the Exalted revealed to Jesus. In relation to the Torah, it is as a completion of it, as Allah the Exalted said later in the verses: ﴿And to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you﴾ [Al 'Imran 50]. So it is like a completion of the Torah, because in reality it was sent down to the Children of Israel to whom the Torah was revealed. It is known that the state of the Children of Israel changed from the time of Moses to the time of Jesus, so the Gospel contained matters of modification or addition. In short, it is a completion of the Torah.

Then He said: ﴿And a messenger to the Children of Israel﴾. (Wa) is a conjunctive particle, and (rasulan) is conjoined with the whole preceding clause, meaning: He sends him as a messenger to the Children of Israel.

The messenger (rasul) is one to whom a law is revealed and who is commanded to convey it. If he is not commanded to convey it, he is a prophet (nabi). This is the view famous among the majority of scholars, may Allah have mercy on them.

It was said: the prophet is not revealed a law; rather he was a confirmer of a law before him, meaning he is revealed to confirm the law that came before him. Thus the prophets before were like scholars in this nation. This view, though it has a basis, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which is guidance and light. By it the prophets who submitted judged for those who were Jews﴾ [al-Ma'idah 44]. He said ﴿by it,﴾ that is, by this Torah, ﴿the prophets who submitted judged for those who were Jews, and the rabbis and scholars, by what they were entrusted of the Book of Allah and were witnesses over it.﴾ But this view is undermined by the case of Adam, for Adam was a prophet, yet he was not a renewer of a previous law, since no law was revealed to humanity before Adam, peace be upon him. For this reason, the definition of the majority regarding the prophet and the messenger is preferred. If we say the prophet is one to whom a law is revealed, this does not preclude that the law revealed to the prophet is the law of one before him, revealed to him for confirmation and affirmation.

He said: ﴿And a messenger to the Children of Israel.﴾ "Banu Isra'il" (the sons of Israel): is it the name of a tribe, or the name of specific individuals?
* Students: The name of a tribe.
* The Shaykh: The name of a tribe, as one says "Banu Tamim." The scholars, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on them, distinguish between "ibn" (son) and "banu" (sons) when it is the name of a tribe and also the name of a specific person. When they discuss this in the chapter on endowments (waqf), and derive rulings from it: if you say, "This is an endowment for the Banu so-and-so," meaning a tribe, such as the Banu Tamim for example, does it include all of them? Does it include males and females?
They said: Yes, it includes all of them and includes males and females, but universal inclusion is not obligatory. Universal inclusion is not obligatory. So I may distribute this endowment among only three of the Banu Tamim, and I may give it to only three women, because it is not restricted to men, but includes males and females, and because it does not necessarily require universal inclusion. But if you say, "This is an endowment for the Banu so-and-so," a specific individual, then it is obligatory to include all of them, excluding the females. Include whom? The males, excluding the females, because the son is not the daughter. And because the specified Banu so-and-so are limited and can be enumerated, it is obligatory to include all of them, treat them equally, and exclude the women among them. So the Children of Israel: which of the two categories are they? The first: a tribe.
Israel is Ya'qub ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim. They are cousins of the Banu Isma'il. For this reason, when the Prophet (ﷺ) was sent to his cousins, the Banu Isma'il, the Jews were jealous of that and denied him. They had previously sought victory over the disbelievers, saying: A prophet will be sent, and we will follow him and overpower you and defeat you, thinking that he would be from the Children of Israel. This was not a genuine assumption; it was a delusion, because they knew the Prophet (ﷺ) as they know their own sons, and they knew he would be sent in Mecca. But they imagined this, their false selves deluded them. When he was sent from the Banu Isma'il, they denied and rejected him.
What is the meaning of Israel? In Syriac, they said its meaning is, or in Hebrew: "servant of God," meaning "servant of God." Now the Jewish state is called Israel (...).

* * *

A student: ﴿And a messenger to the Children of Israel: "Indeed, I have come to you with a sign from your Lord: that I will create for you from clay the form of a bird, then I will breathe into it and it will be a bird by the permission of Allah. And I will heal the blind and the leper, and I will bring the dead to life by the permission of Allah. And I will inform you of what you eat and what you store in your houses. Indeed in that is a sign for you, if you are believers." And confirming what was before me of the Torah and to make lawful for you some of that which was forbidden to you. And I have come to you with a sign from your Lord, so fear Allah and obey me. Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path﴾ [Al 'Imran 49–51].
* The Shaykh: (...) ﴿Allah creates what He wills﴾. Here He used the word "creates" (yakhluqu), while in the story of Zakariyya He used the verb "does" (yaf'alu) [Al 'Imran 40]. Here He said (yakhluqu). Is there a point to this, or is it a difference of expression, which is part of variety in expression, as they say?
* A student: A difference of expression.
* The Shaykh: A difference of expression, fine.
* A student: Here there is a subtle point.
* The Shaykh: And what is it?
* The student: When the angel gave the good news to the one who spoke with Allah (Kalim Allah), a thing that is strange, which is not (...), whereas with Maryam it is entirely strange, outside the norm, and she had no husband.
* A student: Shaykh, the state is the existence of the affirmation (...), but here (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, this is close to it. Apparently it is a difference of wording.
* A student: Shaykh, perhaps in the story of Zakariyya, when Allah the Mighty and Majestic informed him with the verb, He informed him with the verb, because creating is an agent in origin.
* The Shaykh: What?
* The student: That creating would be from its origin. But here, creating may not be expected, because.
* The Shaykh: A difference of expression.
* The student: Shaykh, this woman gave birth while no human had touched her, a young woman, and no human had touched her, which is more surprising than an aged barren woman giving birth.
* The Shaykh: A difference of expression.
* A student: As they say: even (...).
* The Shaykh: No, in any case they say that what you mentioned is close to what the scholars said, and it is correct: that Jesus, peace be upon him, was created without the usual course, created in a manner for which there was no precedent at all. So it suits the expression "creation," which indicates origination. For this reason it is said: Allah created the heavens, and it is not said: Allah did (fa'ala) the heavens, although creation is His action. But creation contains a kind of origination, and therefore He said "created."
The second aspect: a refutation of the doubts of the Christians who say that Jesus is God, and God is the third of three. So there is in it an explicit statement that he is created, and this cuts off their claim at its root. So there is in it: a cosmic point and a legislative point, meaning wisdom: legislative and cosmic. I think I have not mentioned it (...).
His saying ﴿and a messenger﴾: (rasulan), what made it accusative?
* A student: A circumstantial accusative (hal).
* The Shaykh: A circumstantial accusative, a (hal), from a non-derived noun?!
* A student: Yes, it is conjoined.
* The Shaykh: Yes, conjoined to what?
* A student: To (musaddiqan) and (rasulan).
* The Shaykh: It does not fit, nor is it there. Is it (musaddiqan) there? ﴿He will teach him the Book, wisdom, the Torah, the Gospel, and a messenger.﴾
* A student: Yes, conjoined to ﴿the Gospel﴾, and (musaddiqan) conjoined to what came before the Gospel.
* The Shaykh: So, "and He will teach him the Book, wisdom, the Torah, and the Gospel, and will teach him as a messenger"?
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No, wait, let me examine it. One should not speak conjecturally like this. Answer: does the meaning hold?
* The student: It does not hold.
* The Shaykh: Then.
* The student: It is conjoined to "and the Gospel."
* The Shaykh: By God, the help is sought! It does not fit.
* A student: Shaykh, it is in the accusative by a verb omitted, its estimated form being "He sends him as a messenger."
* The Shaykh: Correct, "and He sends him as a messenger." Who are the Children of Israel?
* A student: The Children of Israel are the twelve sons of Ya'qub.
* The Shaykh: The twelve sons of Ya'qub. So Israel is?
* The student: Ya'qub, peace be upon him.
* The Shaykh: Ya'qub is the son of?
* The student: The son of Ishaq.
* The Shaykh: The son of Ibrahim, so? ﴿Indeed, I have come to you﴾. ﴿That I will create for you from clay the form of a bird﴾. There are two readings. We informed you of them, or not?
* Students: No (...).
* The Shaykh: There is a reading with the hamza of (anni) pronounced with a kasra and with a fatha, and with a fatha on the ya' together with a fatha on the hamza: three readings: ﴿anniya﴾, ﴿anni﴾, ﴿inni﴾.
His saying ﴿I will heal the blind and the leper.﴾ ﴿Then I will breathe into it and it will be a bird by the permission of Allah.﴾ "Then it will be a bird by the permission of Allah": this thing will become a bird.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verses 42–51 (part 5 of 7):

And His saying: ﴿I will create for you from clay the likeness of a bird﴾, meaning, its like and its form. Then I will breathe into it and it will become a bird. In the recitation of the seven readers: ﴿and it will become a bird by Allah's permission﴾. Each of the two recitations has a meaning that completes the other. His saying ﴿it becomes a bird﴾ means a living bird, after it had been in the form of a bird but without a soul. His saying ﴿it becomes a flier﴾ means that it flies, which you witness flying in reality. So we have three stages: the shaping in the form of a bird; second, a bird that has a soul, according to the reading ﴿it becomes a bird﴾; third, a bird that actually flies, according to the reading ﴿a flier by Allah's permission﴾. Accordingly, he creates something in the form of a bird, breathes into it so that it receives a soul, and then it flies.

And His saying ﴿by Allah's permission﴾ means by His permission that is both cosmic (kawni) and legislative (shar'i). This is because his shaping something that resembles the creation of Allah requires legislative permission, since the basic principle is that it is not permitted for anyone to shape images in imitation of the shaping of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Allah the Exalted said: "And who is more unjust than one who attempts to create like My creation?" [Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (5953) and Muslim (2111/101) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.] However, Allah the Exalted permitted 'Isa, peace be upon him, for a wisdom. This is according to the interpretation "by Allah's permission". What is the permission? 
* Students: Legislative.
* Shaykh: Legislative. Likewise the cosmic permission. That is, "by Allah's permission" is cosmic permission, because the creation of this bird so that it flies happens by Allah's cosmic permission, or legislative? 
* Students: Cosmic.
* Shaykh: Cosmic. That is: it flies by Allah's permission, a cosmic permission. So 'Isa, peace be upon him, creates the likeness of a bird by Allah's legislative permission, and it becomes a bird when he breathes into it, and it flies by Allah's cosmic permission.

And His saying ﴿by Allah's permission﴾ is for the sake of establishing tawhid (monotheism, the affirmation of Allah's oneness), so that no one supposes that he creates independently. For were it not for this restriction "by Allah's permission", the Christian and others would imagine that 'Isa, peace be upon him, creates just as Allah created Adam from clay in His form, then breathed into him the soul, so he became a human. Thus one might think that 'Isa creates like the creation of Allah. Therefore he, peace be upon him, used to say: "by Allah's permission."

﴿And I heal the blind and the leper﴾. Ubri' (I heal) means I cure. Al-bur' (healing) originally derives from al-bara'ah (freedom), and al-bara'ah from a thing means safety from it. From this comes "bari'a min dayniHi", meaning he was free from his debt, i.e., safe from its harm and its burden. Thus healing from illness means safety from it and recovery from it.

And His saying ﴿al-akmah﴾ (the blind). It has been said: it is one who cannot see at night but can see by day. It has also been said: one who sees at night but cannot see by day. It has also been said: one who sees only with difficulty. And it has been said: one born without eyes. If the word akmah in the Arabic language can bear all these meanings, then it carries all of them. If it can bear only one meaning, then the closest of the sayings is that the akmah is one born without eyes, because this is more emphatic in showing power, and whatever is more emphatic in power is greater as a sign. So we say: if the Arabic language applies akmah to everything that has been said, then let the verse be inclusive. If it bears only one meaning, then the closest of them is that the akmah is one born without eyes, because this is more emphatic in power. As for al-abras (the leper), he is one who has baras (leprosy). Baras is a defect that appears on a person from skin defects, and it may affect general health in the body, and it may not. But baras has no cure, it has no cure. Therefore He said: "I heal the leper by Allah's permission."

And His saying ﴿I heal the blind and the leper, and I bring the dead to life by Allah's permission﴾: "I bring the dead to life by Allah's permission." The dead here are not specific dead persons; rather it refers to the category. Thus any of the dead on whom this matter could happen. As for the saying of one who said that he revived Sam bin Nuh, or revived so-and-so or so-and-so, this is among the Isra'iliyyat (narrations taken from Jewish and Christian sources). But the verse means that he revives the dead: any dead person he stands over and commands, he comes to life by Allah's permission.

﴿And I bring the dead to life by Allah's permission, by Allah's permission, and I inform you of what you eat and what you store in your houses﴾. Unabbi'ukum (I inform you): I tell you what you eat today and what you store for tomorrow in your houses, without anyone coming to inform him of that. This contains some of the knowledge of the unseen, some of the knowledge of the unseen. He informed them that among his signs is that he tells a person: "You ate today such and such, and stored for tomorrow or the day after such and such," even though he had sent no one to observe what is in the house. This cannot happen except by revelation from Allah. If there is no human who informs him of what is in the houses, then it is from the revelation of Allah. It may also be through the jinn, for the jinn sometimes serve humans: they go to distant places, or climb walls and report what is in houses. But jinn of this kind it is not permitted to benefit from or to be in contact with. Why?

Because their knowledge of people's affairs is injustice and aggression, and it is not permitted for a person to seek help from an oppressor in his oppression. Therefore this assumption is ruled out with respect to whom? With respect to 'Isa, peace be upon him.

That is to say: if someone said that those who seek help from the jinn may come to know what is eaten and stored in houses, we say: this does not apply to 'Isa, because benefiting from the jinn in this way is forbidden, due to the aggression and injustice in it. But 'Isa could not possibly do this. Thus it is clear that it comes to him through revelation.

The wisdom of informing them of this is to make them know that revelation from Allah comes to him concerning specific matters, specific matters in their houses. The second, and Allah knows best, is to warn them against eating something forbidden to them. This is why he will later say to them: ﴿and to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you﴾ [Ali 'Imran 50]. For if they knew that he knows what they eat and what they store in their houses, they would stop from the forbidden thing. And if they stopped from the forbidden thing, Allah might facilitate for them that it be made lawful for them.

* * *

* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan: ﴿And a messenger to the Children of Israel: "I have come to you with a sign from your Lord: I shall create for you from clay the likeness of a bird, then I breathe into it and it becomes a bird by Allah's permission. And I heal the blind and the leper, and I bring the dead to life by Allah's permission. And I inform you of what you eat and what you store in your houses. Indeed in that is a sign for you, if you are believers" (49). "And confirming what is before me of the Torah, and to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you. And I have come to you with a sign from your Lord, so fear Allah and obey me. Indeed Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path"﴾ [Ali 'Imran 49–51].
* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And a messenger to the Children of Israel: "I have come to you with a sign from your Lord: I shall create for you from clay the likeness of a bird, then I breathe into it and it becomes a bird by Allah's permission. And I heal the blind and the leper, and I bring the dead to life by Allah's permission﴾, and we have read all of these. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And confirming what is before me of the Torah﴾. ﴿Indeed in that is a sign for you, if you are believers﴾. "Indeed in that": the referent is what was mentioned earlier of several matters: His saying ﴿I shall create for you from clay the likeness of a bird, then I breathe into it and it becomes a bird by Allah's permission. And I heal the blind and the leper, and I bring the dead to life by Allah's permission. And I inform you of what you eat and what you store in your houses﴾. These are three signs, each of which indicates the truthfulness of 'Isa, peace be upon him, and that he is truly the messenger of Allah, because the like of this is not within the capacity of a human. The signs of the prophets that came are proofs of their truthfulness, which no human can produce the like of. For if it were possible for a human to produce the like of it, it would not be a sign, since every person could do such a thing. And His saying ﴿if you are believers﴾ means that it is a sign under this condition, i.e., if you are believers. As for one who is not a believer, he does not benefit from the signs, and the sign is not a sign for him. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And signs and warnings do not avail a people who do not believe﴾ [Yunus 101], because their hearts are hardened and sealed, and we seek refuge in Allah; good does not reach them, and they do not soften through punishments and warnings, because they are hard. The believer is the one who benefits from the signs. Indeed the non-believer sees these great signs as "tales of the ancients": ﴿when Our verses are recited to him, he says: "Tales of the ancients"﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 13]. This is because of the darkness of sins upon his heart, and we seek refuge in Allah, as He says: ﴿No! Rather, what they used to earn has covered over their hearts﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 14]. Iman (faith) we have explained many times: it is affirmation that necessarily entails acceptance and submission, not mere affirmation. Evidence for this is that it does not take the same complement that tasdiq (affirmation) takes: one does not say "I iman-ed him," but one says "I believed him (saddaqtuhu)." Rather it includes acknowledgment, confession, submission and surrender. Whoever affirms but does not accept or submit is not a believer. Abu Talib, the uncle of the Prophet ﷺ, affirmed his message, but he did not accept or submit, so he was not a believer. Otherwise he affirmed what the Prophet said in his poetry and in his conduct, yet he, we seek refuge in Allah, was not a believer. So iman is a meaning beyond tasdiq, and is not merely tasdiq.

He said: ﴿And confirming what is before me of the Torah﴾. This is coordinated with what preceded, meaning it is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause: "And I have come to you confirming what is before me of the Torah." "What is before me" refers to what came before him. "Before the hands" is also used for what will come. So "between the hands" applies to the past and is also used for the future. If it is paired with "behind," then it refers to the future; otherwise it is suitable for both future and past. In His saying ﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them﴾ [al-Baqarah 255], which is meant?
* Students: The future.
* Shaykh: The future, because of His saying ﴿and what is behind them﴾. In this verse, ﴿confirming what is before me﴾ means what preceded me of the Torah. His confirmation of the Torah has two aspects:
First: he establishes its truth and says it is a true book.
Second: he affirms what it reported. If it reported something, and then he was sent, he confirms what is in it.

His saying ﴿of the Torah﴾: it is the book that Allah revealed to Musa, peace be upon him, and it is the origin of the scriptures revealed to the Children of Israel and the greatest of them. Indeed it is, as far as we know, the greatest of books after the Qur'an.

﴿And to make lawful for you﴾: meaning, "I have also come to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you." His saying ﴿to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden﴾: he did not say "all." What was forbidden to them is mentioned by Allah in His saying: ﴿And for those who were Jews We forbade every animal with claws, and of cattle and sheep We forbade them their fat, except what their backs or entrails carry, or what is mixed with bone﴾ [al-An'am 146]. And He said: ﴿For the wrongdoing of those who were Jews, We forbade them good things that had been made lawful for them﴾ [al-Nisa' 160]. Since these good things were forbidden to them because of their wrongdoing and aggression, and Allah sent 'Isa, peace be upon him, he made lawful for them some of what had been forbidden to them. The explanation of this "some" is not mentioned in the Qur'an, so it remains on its general application. If there were any benefit for us in specifying it, Allah would have made it clear.

His saying ﴿some of what was forbidden to you﴾: the verb here is in the passive voice, but its agent is known. Who is it?
* Students: Allah, Glorified and Exalted.
* Shaykh: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, as He said: ﴿And for those who were Jews We forbade every animal with claws﴾ [al-An'am 146].

﴿And I have come to you with a sign from your Lord﴾: he repeats this after His saying ﴿Indeed in that is a sign for you﴾. Either it can be said that the sign mentioned here, ﴿And I have come to you with a sign﴾, is limited to his confirmation of what was before him of the Torah and his making lawful some of what was forbidden to them, and then there is no repetition in the verse. Or it can be said that His saying ﴿And I have come to you with a sign﴾ includes all the signs that came, and it is for emphasis and for establishing proof against them, so he repeated his coming with signs as an argument against them for what they had denied.

He said: ﴿So fear Allah and obey me﴾. "Fear Allah" means take a shield against His punishment. Taqwa (God-consciousness, piety) is derived from what? 
* Students: From protection (wiqayah).
* Shaykh: From protection. So by what is protection from His punishment achieved? It is achieved by doing His commands and avoiding His prohibitions. This is the comprehensive meaning of taqwa when used alone. When taqwa is paired with birr (righteousness), it means avoiding the prohibited, as in His saying: ﴿And cooperate in righteousness and taqwa﴾ [al-Ma'idah 2]. The scholars have defined taqwa in several ways, but what unites them is what we mentioned: taking protection from Allah's punishment by doing His commands and avoiding His prohibitions.

He said: ﴿and obey me﴾: obey me in what I command you and in what I forbid you. Obeying him is undoubtedly part of taqwa, but it is mentioned explicitly because it is a specific taqwa regarding what 'Isa brought. For taqwa is enjoined on every person, and when he says "obey me," it becomes a specific taqwa in obeying this messenger who was sent to his people.

The scholars said in explaining obedience (ta'ah): it is conformity with the command, avoiding what is forbidden and doing what is commanded. Whoever avoids the prohibition intending thereby to comply with the command is obedient. Whoever does the command intending thereby to comply with the command is also obedient. As for one who abandons the prohibition, or more precisely, what is prohibited, out of inability, he is not obedient. Rather, if he strives toward its causes until he is unable, he is like one who did it, due to the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "When two Muslims meet with their swords, the killer and the killed are in the Fire." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, this is the killer, but what about the killed?" He said: "Because he was eager to kill his companion." [Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (31) and Muslim (2888/16) from the hadith of Abu Bakrah Nufay' ibn al-Harith.]

Then he said: "Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him." When He commanded them to fear Allah, He mentioned what is, in effect, the reason for that, saying: "Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord." Al-rabb (the Lord) is the Creator, the Owner, the One who disposes of affairs. To affirm Allah's Lordship (tawhid al-rububiyyah) is to believe that there is no creator, no owner, and no manager except Allah, glory be to Him and exalted is He. Whatever is attributed to other than Allah in terms of creation, ownership, or management is attributed in a deficient manner, deficient in its comprehensiveness and in its scope of action. For example, creation is attributed to other than Allah, and we have already passed, recently, that 'Isa said: "I create for you from clay" [Ali 'Imran 49], while Allah the Exalted said: "So blessed is Allah, the best of creators" [al-Mu'minun 14]. And Allah said in the hadith qudsi: "And who is more unjust than one who goes to create like My creation?"[[Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (5953) and Muslim (2111/101) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]] And the Prophet ﷺ said: "The people who will suffer the most punishment on the Day of Resurrection are the makers of images, who imitate the creation of Allah."[[Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (5950) and Muslim (2109/98) from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud.]] He, peace and blessings be upon him, also said: "It will be said to them: Give life to what you have created."[[Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (2105) and Muslim (2107/96) from the hadith of 'A'ishah.]] However, creation attributed to other than Allah the Mighty and Majestic is deficient creation; it is not true bringing-into-existence but rather a change of form. For example, a person makes a door from wood: did he create the wood? And from iron he makes a car: did he create the iron? Never. Rather, he changed it, transformed it from one state to another, and so this became a creation, but he is not the one who brought the iron or the wood into existence, such that it could be said that his creation is like the creation of Allah. Likewise, the creation of a human being, or of humankind in general, is not comprehensive or all-encompassing, because every person creates only what he makes; what he does not make is not of his creation. Likewise ownership: "And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth" [Ali 'Imran 189]. "Say: In whose hand is the dominion of all things?" [al-Mu'minun 88]. The verses establishing ownership for Allah alone are many. Nevertheless, Allah attributed ownership to others in His saying: "except over their wives or what their right hands possess" [al-Mu'minun 6], and in His saying: "or that whose keys you possess" [al-Nur 61]. Do we say that this ownership is like Allah's ownership? No, neither in comprehensiveness nor in scope of action. As for comprehensiveness, every person owns no more than what is under his control; therefore you do not own my book, and I do not own your book. But Allah's ownership is general and all-encompassing. As for scope of action, the ownership of other than Allah is limited, because a person does not have absolute disposal as he wishes; rather he acts according to what the Shari'ah of Allah requires and what Allah permits. If a person wanted to tear up his book, would he have the right to do so? * Student: He does not have that right.
* Shaykh: He does not own that right; it is forbidden for him, and he sins. And if he wanted to tear up someone else's book, it would be forbidden on two counts: the count of wasting property, and the count of transgression against another. So the summary is that a person's ownership is limited in two respects, namely:
* Student: Ownership (...).
* Shaykh: No, a person's ownership is limited.
* Student: Yes, the ownership of a person, yes (...).
* Shaykh: Yes, it is limited in its scope of action.
* Student: In terms of comprehensiveness.
* Shaykh: So it is limited in comprehensiveness. Good. As for management, it is likewise: the third meaning of lordship is management. Management also belongs to other than Allah, but it is deficient management, both in comprehensiveness and in scope of action. A person does not manage everything; he manages only what he has the right to manage. Yet his management is deficient, in accordance with what the Shari'ah requires. If he wanted to manage his camel in a way that would cause it hardship, making it walk through mud or over fire or the like, would that be permitted? * The students: It is not permitted.
* Shaykh: It is not permitted, so it is deficient. If he wanted to send upon it a blaze of fire, does he own that?
* The students: He does not own that.
* Shaykh: He does not own that, but Allah the Mighty and Majestic owns it. He owns all of this, is that not so?
* The students: Indeed.
* Shaykh: And no one opposes Him. The point is that lordship is Allah's sole possession of creation, ownership, and management, and this does not mean that no one shares with Him in creation, ownership, or management; but it is in a manner that does not resemble what is established for the Creator in that regard. A person may create, and it is said that he created; it is said that he owns, and it is said that he manages; but, as you have heard, it is deficient.
His saying: "my Lord and your Lord" begins with himself, so that he is the first to submit to this Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, because the Lord is Creator, Owner, and Manager; so he began with himself so that he would be the first to submit and yield to this Lord.
He said: "so worship Him." The fa' here is conjunctive and indicates causation; that is: because He is Lord, therefore worship Him. For this reason we say that affirming tawhid al-rububiyyah entails affirming tawhid al-uluhiyyah (the oneness of worship), and whoever affirms tawhid al-rububiyyah but denies tawhid al-uluhiyyah has contradicted himself. For this reason Allah rebuked the polytheists who used to affirm tawhid al-rububiyyah and then deny tawhid al-uluhiyyah, saying: "How are they turned away?" [Ghafir 69], "How are you turned away?" [Yunus 32], "How are they deluded?" [al-Ma'idah 75], and the like, which shows that it is foolish for a person to affirm that Allah alone is the Creator, Owner, and Manager, and then worship other than Him! So we say, for example, to the polytheist: Do you not believe in Allah? He will say: Yes. That He is the Creator? Yes. That He is the Owner? Yes. That He is the Manager? Yes. That there is no creator with Him, no owner, and no manager? Yes, I believe all of this. Then how do you make a god with Him that you worship? And whoever is other than Allah is either worshipped or a worshipper?
* The students: A worshipper.
* Shaykh: A worshipper, one who is managed; he is a servant managed by Allah the Mighty and Majestic. How then do you make him an object of worship alongside Allah?! For this reason He said: "so worship Him." So the fa' is conjunctive and indicates causation: because He is my Lord and your Lord, worship Him alone.

What is worship? Worship ('ibadah) is derived from servitude (ʿabada), meaning humbling oneself (dhalla), and from it comes the saying "a paved road" (tariq mu'abbad), meaning one made smooth for its travelers. Its root is humility, but in relation to Allah the Mighty and Majestic it is humility combined with love and exaltation. Every act of worship directed to Allah is combined with these two matters: love and exaltation. By love comes seeking, and by exaltation comes fleeing; when a person loves something he seeks it, and when he exalts something he is awed by it and flees from it and fears it. For this reason worship is built upon hope and fear.

Worship is sometimes used in this sense that we have mentioned, as a verbal noun (masdar); what is that which we mentioned? Humbling oneself to Allah together with love and exaltation. It is sometimes used to denote the object (ism al-maf'ul), or the thing by which one worships; in that case we say it is a comprehensive term for everything that Allah loves and is pleased with, of statements and deeds, outward and inward. So, for example, prayer?
* The students: Worship.
* Shaykh: Worship. Zakat is worship, fasting is worship, Hajj is worship, kindness to parents is worship, maintaining ties of kinship is worship, and so on. So sometimes it is used of the act, and sometimes of the object. Regarding the act, we explain it as: humbling oneself to Allah the Mighty and Majestic in love and exaltation. And regarding what is done or the object, it is a comprehensive term for everything Allah loves and is pleased with, of what He and His Messenger have commanded.

He said: "So worship Him. This is a straight path." The demonstrative "this" refers either to the nearest thing mentioned or to everything that preceded it, from His saying: "So fear Allah and obey me. [50] Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This" — that is: fearing Allah, obeying His Messenger, and fulfilling worship to Him, is a straight path. A path is called a sirat (a path that is wide and straight) only when it combines breadth and moderation, because it is derived from al-sarṭ, which means swallowing quickly, or, if you prefer, from al-zarṭ, which means swallowing quickly. A wide, straight road swallows its travelers quickly, because people do not walk in a narrow place except how?
* The students: Slowly.
* Shaykh: Gradually, slowly. A path that is not straight does not reach its goal except slowly, whether its deviation is to the right or to the left, or in terms of ascent and descent; when it rises and falls, it tires the traveler, does it not?
* The students: Yes indeed.
* Shaykh: So if we assume, for example, that a mountain is fifty meters long and fifty meters wide, how far is it from one of its width to its other width?
* The students: (...).
* Shaykh: No, a person climbs it, climbs it.
* The students: A hundred.
* Shaykh: No, a hundred and fifty, a hundred and fifty. Its width is fifty, its length is fifty, and its height upward into the sky: that makes a hundred and fifty. The ascent is fifty, the descent is fifty, and the flat part is fifty. So if the path is straight, without deviations to right or left and without rising or falling, it shortens the way. Likewise, if we assume that the goal can be reached by a straight path in thirty meters, but this path has bends, each bend ten meters, and there are ten bends, how far does one travel to reach the goal per meter?
[Hundred], so the summary is that the scholars said: a path is not a sirat unless it is wide and straight, and it is derived from al-sarṭ or al-zarṭ. You know the meaning of al-zarṭ from eating: you give someone a morsel and he puts it in his mouth and swallows it right away; what does one say?
* A student: Izrutuha (swallow it).
* Shaykh: One says: izrutha. "Straight" (mustaqim): straight, meaning there is no crookedness in it. Describing it as straight after we said that the path is the wide, straight one with no crookedness is by way of emphasis, as you say: "He is a man, a man." How is "a man, a man"? What is the meaning of "a man, a man"? It means one who combines all the meanings of manhood. Likewise, "a straight path" combines every meaning of a path. This is the straight path.

Allah the Exalted said: "When the angels said..." [Ali 'Imran 42]. Allah the Exalted said: "And when the angels said: O Maryam, indeed Allah has chosen you and purified you." Among the benefits of this verse: the magnification of the status of Maryam, peace be upon her, in that Allah commanded His Prophet to mention her story to this nation. We said that "idh qalat" (when she said) is the object of a verb omitted in the sentence, its estimated form being: "Remember when she said."
* Among its benefits: the virtue of Maryam, in that the angels addressed her, saying: "Indeed Allah has chosen you," and so on to the end.
Among its benefits, according to what some scholars have held: that Maryam was a prophetess, because the angels conveyed revelation to her and said: "Indeed Allah has chosen you," and so on. But there is room for scrutiny in this inference, because it is not explicit that she was given prophethood; the mere address of the angels to her does not establish her prophethood, since prophethood belongs only to one to whom revelation is given with a Shari'ah, not to one to whom revelation is given with praise or with preparation for what is to come. Rather, prophethood belongs to one to whom revelation is given with a law, and she was not given revelation with a law, so the matter is not explicit. We have a verse indicating that no prophet is sent from among women: Allah the Exalted said: "And We sent before you only men to whom We revealed, from the people of the towns" [Yusuf 109]. The word "only" (illa) indicates restriction, so it shows that it is impossible for any woman to be a prophetess. Likewise the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, when he was informed that the Persians had appointed the daughter of Chosroes as their ruler, said: "A people will never prosper who entrust their affairs to a woman."[[Related by al-Bukhari (4425) from the hadith of Abu Bakrah Nufay' ibn al-Harith.]] And if a people will not prosper when they choose, then it is they who chose her and appointed her, so how could Allah send a woman so that people might prosper through her?!
It is true that a woman may be a scholar and a caller to Allah, as the reality shows; but that she be a prophetess to whom revelation is given so that she may assume authority, as they call it, the legislative and executive, is far-fetched. So the correct view is that Maryam is among the righteous, devoutly obedient women, and not among the prophets and messengers.
* Among the benefits of the noble verses: that Allah the Exalted chooses whom He wills from among people, as in His saying: "Indeed Allah has chosen you," meaning He selected you with a selection in which no one shared with her, for she became a servant of Bayt al-Maqdis (the Holy House), even though among them only men serve it. This is a kind of election.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the innocence of Maryam from what the Jews claimed, that she was a prostitute, by His saying: "and purified you."
Another benefit of the noble verse: the innocence of Maryam from what the Jews claimed, that she was a prostitute; by His saying: "and purified you." The Jews, may Allah curse them, wronged Maryam and her son. They said of Maryam that she was a prostitute, and of her son 'Isa that he was a child of fornication, and they denied him, and they killed him in a sense that is not real: how did they kill him in a sense that is not real? Because they carried out this matter, believing that they had killed 'Isa and crucified him, and they said: "Indeed we killed the Messiah, 'Isa son of Maryam, the messenger of Allah." Allah the Exalted said: "And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them" [al-Nisa' 157]. So they were killers in a sinful sense, not in reality, because 'Isa is still alive.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that Maryam is preferred and chosen above the women of the worlds. But does this encompass the women of the worlds until the Day of Resurrection, or the women of the worlds in her own time? It admits both meanings. Either the intended meaning is the women of the worlds in her time, and the saying of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, "Many men have reached perfection, but among women only Asiya the wife of Pharaoh, Maryam daughter of 'Imran, and Khadijah daughter of Khuwaylid have reached perfection"[[Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (3411) and Muslim (2431/70) from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, without the phrase "and Khadijah daughter of Khuwaylid." As for her hadith, it is agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (3432) and Muslim (2430/69) from the hadith of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, with the wording: "The best of her women is Maryam daughter of 'Imran, and the best of her women is Khadijah daughter of Khuwaylid."]] is of what Allah made His Prophet aware of, and the angels were not informed of this; the angels conveyed to Maryam only what they conveyed.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the repetition, or the permissibility of repeating virtues, because whenever attributes of perfection are repeated, there appears from the perfection of the one described what was not known before. Is it clear?
From this benefit we move to a benefit related to the attributes of Allah the Mighty and Majestic: most of what Allah describes Himself with are the affirmative attributes that He affirms for Himself. As for the attributes that He negates from Himself, His description with them is few compared to His description with affirmative attributes, because affirmative attributes are perfection, perfections, while negative attributes are deficiencies; they are negated not for their own sake but to affirm the perfection of their opposite, though they are also actually negated.
Then He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: "O Maryam, be devoutly obedient to your Lord, prostrate yourself, and bow down with those who bow."
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the explanation that whenever Allah bestows something upon a person, the demand upon him for worship increases, because when the angels said: "Indeed Allah has chosen you, purified you, and chosen you above the women of the worlds," they commanded her with what? With devout obedience, prostration, and bowing. This shows that a person should, whenever Allah's blessings increase upon him, increase in thanks by devout obedience to Allah, bowing, prostration, and all other acts of worship.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the virtue of devout obedience (qunut) to Allah. But what is qunut? Constant obedience, humility, and occupation with obedience to the exclusion of everything else. For this reason, when the verse "Guard the prayers, and the middle prayer, and stand before Allah in devout obedience" [al-Baqarah 238] was revealed, they were commanded to be silent and forbidden to speak, so that they would occupy themselves with obedience to the exclusion of anything else. So qunut is constant obedience together with occupation with it to the exclusion of others.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse also: the virtue of prostration and bowing, by His saying: "prostrate yourself, and bow down with those who bow," even though it falls under qunut; but because of their excellence, they were specifically mentioned.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the permissibility of not following the order (tartib) for the sake of a benefit or for the sake of observing something else, namely His saying: "prostrate yourself and bow down," where prostration is mentioned before bowing.

Could someone say: perhaps in their time prostration was placed before bowing, while in this law bowing is placed before prostration? You say: the original order is the opposite, but He mentioned prostration first because it is more expressive of humility (qunut, devout obedience) than bowing, as we noted during the commentary.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: men who worship are more numerous than women who worship. Its address to the men is more numerous, based on His words: ﴿Bow with those who bow﴾. He did not say "with the women who bow," indicating that perfection lies in men, and that the abundance of good deeds is more evident in men than in women. For this reason women are the majority of the people of the Fire, as is established in the authentic hadith from the Prophet ﷺ[[A hadith agreed upon (Muttafaqun 'alayh): al-Bukhari (304) and Muslim (80), from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him), with the wording: "O women, give charity, for I have been shown that most of the people of the Fire are women."]].
