The second reason: therein the witnesses will stand. The messengers will bear witness against their nations, and this nation will bear witness against the previous nations. God Most High said: ﴿Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believe in the worldly life and on the Day when the witnesses will stand﴾ [Ghafir 51]. The third reason: justice is established therein. God Most High said: ﴿And We will set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be wronged at all﴾ [al-Anbiya' 47]. So justice is established therein. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ), who was truthful, righteous, and believed in, swore an oath and said (peace be upon him): "By God, rights will certainly be returned to their people, until the hornless sheep will be avenged against the horned sheep." [Narrated by Muslim (2582/60) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.] This is justice, the greatest justice. So the Day of Resurrection is named for these three reasons. Recite them to us.

A student: The Day of Resurrection.

The Shaykh: Yes. The Day of Resurrection is named for how many reasons?

The student: Justice is established therein.

The Shaykh: Justice is established therein.

The student: So that people are avenged, and therefore it is called the Day of Resurrection.

The Shaykh: Yes, and the second?

A student: People stand therein.

The Shaykh: For what?

The student: People stand before God, Lord of the worlds.

The Shaykh: The evidence?

The student: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿The Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds﴾.

The Shaykh: Good...?

A student: The Day when the witnesses stand.

The Shaykh: The witnesses stand therein. The evidence?

The student: The saying of God, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believe in the worldly life and on the Day when the witnesses will stand﴾.

The Shaykh: The evidence for the first? The evidence for the first that our brother mentioned, that justice is established therein?

A student: His saying, Glory be to Him and Exalted: ﴿The Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds﴾. And the second reason: justice is established therein.

The Shaykh: Justice is established therein. What is the evidence?

The student: ﴿And We will set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection﴾.

The Shaykh: Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Then to Me is your return﴾. That is, then after this, dominance in the world, or contention in the world, so that some of you are above others afterwards. ﴿To Me is your return﴾, that is, your final destination. All destinations lead to God, Mighty and Majestic, in this world and in the Hereafter. God Most High said: ﴿And that to your Lord is the finality﴾ [an-Najm 42], and ﴿Whatever you differ over, its judgment is with God﴾ [ash-Shura 10]. The matter belongs to God, first and last. But the manifestation of this return will only occur on the Day of Resurrection, when it becomes clear to all people that the return to God, Glorified and Exalted, will recompense every soul for what it has done. For this reason He said: ﴿Then to Me is your return, and I will judge between you concerning that over which you used to differ﴾ [Al 'Imran 55]. God is greatest! How just is this judgment! ﴿I will judge between you﴾. Between whom? Between the creatures concerning what they used to differ over. Do people differ over anything? Yes: ﴿Among you is a disbeliever and among you is a believer﴾ [at-Taghabun 2]. This is a great difference. So God, Mighty and Majestic, judges between these and those, and He also judges between the messengers and their followers. The messengers establish proof that they conveyed the message, and the followers of the messengers may deny it, but their aim is not achieved. So the judgment on the Day of Resurrection between people concerning what they differed over belongs to God. As for His saying: ﴿I will judge﴾, this is a present-tense verb. Can a name of God be derived from it? The rule is that a name is not derived from a verb, but a name has been found without returning to this verb, which is al-Hakim (the Wise). Al-Hakim is derived from al-hukm (judgment) and al-hikmah (wisdom). Among God's names is al-Hakam (the Judge), as the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Indeed God is al-Hakam, and to Him belongs judgment." [Narrated by Abu Dawud (4955) and an-Nasa'i (5387), from the hadith of Hani' ibn Yazid.] This is from al-hukm. So God is the Judge to whom people return in their disputes. Know that the judgment belongs to God and is divided into two parts, which will come, God willing, in the explanation.

A student: The attribute of cunning (...). A person says: O best of (...)?

The Shaykh: "O best of the schemers," if the occasion calls for it, for example if you fear the scheming of a person, there is no harm. But do not say "O best of the schemers, forgive me," as that is not appropriate, because God says: ﴿And to God belong the most beautiful names, so call upon Him by them﴾ [al-A'raf 180]. You do not call upon God by a name that you want to be a means of obtaining your request unless it is suitable. Suppose someone said: "O Severe in punishment, forgive me." Is it suitable?

The people: No.

The Shaykh: And what is suitable?

The people: "O Forgiving."

The Shaykh: Or he says: "O Severe in punishment, punish me." No one has said it like that.

A student: May God be good to you, our shaykh. If someone said regarding ﴿And those who follow you above those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection﴾ that he (peace be upon him) was sent to the Children of Israel, and the Jews are those who disbelieved in him, then the present reality is that the Christians are above the Jews. Is that not possible?

The Shaykh: No, we have explained that this is not possible, because the Christians now have not followed him, and the Qur'an speaks only the truths. Now, do you see that the Jews are above the Christians, or the Christians above the Jews?

The students: The Jews.

A student: The Jews, in an indirect way.

The Shaykh: We now hear that the Jews hold the reins of economic and political affairs, that they manage the world, and culture.

A student: But in an indirect way.

The Shaykh: Yes, in an indirect way.

A student: As for the one who rules, it is the Christians.

The Shaykh: Yes, that is correct, but do you not see that the Christians are above these, meaning that they fear them and seek their favor?

A student: Shaykh, may God pardon you, there are now those who raise media studies claiming that the Jews and the Christians are our brothers, and they do not allow (...) among them?

The Shaykh: But look, may God bless you, can you prevent them from this? Can you prevent them from this?

The student: I cannot.

The Shaykh: Because if they say, "We are their brothers," we say to them, "May God bless you in them. You are their brothers, and you will be gathered with them in the Fire."

The student: They will deceive people with them, Shaykh.

The Shaykh: No one will be deceived by them.

The student: (...)

The Shaykh: Not at all. Let no one think that he is deceived into saying that a disbeliever is his brother, whether Christian, Jewish, or other, and God says: ﴿The believers are but brothers, so make reconciliation between your brothers﴾ [al-Hujurat 10].

A student: Shaykh, what about the young people who go to their countries, even saying, "They are our brothers," and they really say that (...)

The Shaykh: No, not at all, no. I do not think that a person with faith in his heart would call them brothers, and God, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies﴾ [al-Mumtahanah 1]. Where is the brotherhood?

A student: Shaykh, may God bless you, how did Jesus ascend from the earth to the heaven? With whom?

The Shaykh: God knows best, whether it was in the company of Gabriel or otherwise; God knows best. Or God said "Be" and it was.

A student: Shaykh, (...) ﴿Indeed, I will take you in death and raise you to Myself﴾. Is it possible that the death and the raising happened on the Day of Resurrection?

The Shaykh: Is there resurrection on the Day of Resurrection? That is not death.

The student: I mean, on the day of his death after he descends to the world?

The Shaykh: That is, in the future?

The student: Yes.

The Shaykh: Yes.

The student: Does this agree with the world?

The Shaykh: This does not agree, because the raising comes after death: ﴿I will take you in death and raise you﴾, and the death you mean can only be after the raising.

The student: (...)?

The Shaykh: When? Meaning at the end of time? No, he will be buried in the earth.

A student: Shaykh, we said that God, Glorified and Exalted, spoke to him with an audible voice. Why did we not say that He spoke to him by revelation?

The Shaykh: We will come to it in the benefits, God willing.

A student: Shaykh, may God pardon you, we know it is not permitted to approach God's names with any denial (ta'til), anthropomorphism (tamthil), or distortion (tahrif). Cunning is an attribute of created beings, so how can it be an attribute of God? That is, is it like the face by which we describe the Creator?

The Shaykh: Yes. We say that it is cunning befitting Him. It is not like my cunning or the cunning of Zayd and 'Ubayd. Like hearing and sight and other attributes, they are affirmed for God, but in a manner that does not resemble the created.

A student: Shaykh, may God reward you with good. When the Messenger (ﷺ) was taken on the Night Journey, he saw Jesus, greeted him, and spoke with him. So is it only sleep in the case of the raising?

The Shaykh: What do you mean? No, he saw him in the heaven.

The student: No, my intention is that God, Glorified and Exalted, said: ﴿And raising you to Myself﴾, meaning ﴿taking you in death﴾. We said that taking in death is sleep, so it is only in the case of the raising?

The Shaykh: In the case of the raising, yes.

The student: When he reached the heaven, meaning he awoke?

The Shaykh: Yes, this is the apparent meaning.

A student: Shaykh, may God be good to you. Is it permissible to say "friends of the disbelievers"?

The Shaykh: By God, if it is merely a verbal statement, meaning a friend in the sense that he has not shown enmity, it may be tolerated, because some disbelievers, as you know, show enmity and openly wage hostility, while between us and others there is a treaty. For this reason, the tribe of Khuza'ah, before it embraced Islam, was described as being a trusted confidant of sincere counsel to the Messenger (peace be upon him), though they were disbelievers.

The student: (...) says: "O friend, friend."

The Shaykh: No, now the word "friend" has become a term by which everyone who is not Arab is addressed.

The student: "Comrade."

The Shaykh: Yes, "comrade" is one of the titles of the Communists: "Comrade so-and-so."

I seek refuge with Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from Satan the accursed. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Then to Me is your return, and I will judge between you concerning that over which you used to differ.﴾ ﴿I will judge between you﴾: judgment belongs to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, both in the cosmic (kawni) and the legislative (shar'i) sense. He is the Judge in the cosmic sense and He is the Judge in the legislative sense. As for the cosmic judgment, it is enforced upon everyone, and no one can escape it or oppose it. As for the legislative judgment, it depends on the choice of the one judged: ﴿And say, "The truth is from your Lord, so whoever wills let him believe, and whoever wills let him disbelieve"﴾ [al-Kahf 29]. So Allah's judgment is divided into two parts: cosmic and legislative. The cosmic judgment is what Allah decrees upon His servants, which cannot be deviated from, and it relates to what He loves and what He does not love. He judges cosmically by the occurrence of acts of obedience, which He loves, and He judges cosmically by the occurrence of sins and disobedience, which He does not love; yet He, Mighty and Majestic, judges by it cosmically for wisdom and great benefits. As for the legislative judgment, it is what He has prescribed among the servants by law, and it is what the messengers brought; its basis is commands and prohibitions: "Do this, do not do that." The occurrence of what is legislated does not necessarily follow from the legislative judgment; rather, many people may deviate from it. Here are the messengers, whom Allah sends, and some few people follow them and many people follow them. Indeed, the Prophet ﷺ said: "I saw a prophet with a group, and a prophet with one man or two men, and a prophet with no one with him"[[Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (5705) and Muslim (220 / 374) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, and the wording is his.]], so the legislative judgment is not carried out. As for the retributive judgment: some scholars said that there is a third kind of judgment, which is the retributive judgment, in which Allah judges with recompense upon whoever acts: if good, then good, and if evil, then evil. Upon this His saying here is understood: ﴿so I will judge between you concerning that over which you used to differ﴾, meaning I will judge between you with a retributive judgment, and He judges between them with a retributive judgment, and the outcome of this judgment follows, either to Paradise or to the Fire.

﴿So I will judge between you concerning that over which you used to differ.﴾ He says: ﴿As for those who disbelieved﴾. The fa' here is a conjunction connecting to what precedes it, a fa' of consequence (tafri'): what follows it is a branch of what precedes it, meaning this judgment will be in this manner: ﴿As for those who disbelieved, I will punish them﴾. And (amma) here is a conditional of detailing (tafsil), meaning it conveys detail, as in His saying: ﴿As for he who gives and fears Allah﴾ [al-Layl 5], ﴿And as for he who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient﴾ [al-Layl 8]. And here He says: ﴿As for those who disbelieved﴾ and ﴿As for those who believed﴾.

As for His saying: ﴿As for those who disbelieved, I will punish them﴾, disbelieved in whom? That is, they disbelieved in Allah and His messengers. Kufr (disbelief) linguistically means covering, and from it is named the al-kufra (the sheath of the date palm blossom), which in colloquial language is called al-kafur. So those who disbelieved covered over what Allah had bestowed upon them of the blessing of intellect, the blessing of wealth, health, and other things, since the effects of these things did not appear upon them. The effect of intellect is that a person does what benefits him and leaves what harms him; these are the effects of intellect. From this, intellect is called hijr (restraint), because it restrains its possessor from what harms him. But those who disbelieved covered over what intellect requires of good conduct, which is belief in Allah and His messengers. Therefore they were named kuffar (disbelievers), that is, what? Those who cover over what Allah has bestowed upon them of the blessing of intellect, whose requirement is belief in Allah and His messengers.

He says: ﴿I will punish them with a severe punishment﴾. ﴿I will punish them﴾: 'adhab (punishment) is doing what involves hardship, or the occurrence of what involves hardship, whether it is due to a sin or not, as the Prophet ﷺ said: "Travel is a piece of punishment"[[Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (1804) and Muslim (1927 / 179) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]], and he said: "The deceased is punished by the weeping of his family over him"[[Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (1304) and Muslim (931 / 25) from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar.]]. This means punishment of hardship, and from the punishment of hardship is the punishment of retribution, because it is hard for the one punished; and here the meaning of punishment is the hardship of retributive punishment. ﴿I will punish them with a severe punishment﴾: shadid (severe) means strong and great.

﴿In this world and the Hereafter﴾. As for "in this world," the scholars said: the punishment in this world is what befalls their hearts of constriction, distress, anxiety, regret, and other things, and what befalls them at the hands of the believers of killing, captivity, jizyah, and other things. So their punishment is through their inner pain and their bodily pain. For this reason He said: ﴿I will punish them with a severe punishment in this world﴾. As for their punishment in the Hereafter, it is clear: they are punished in the Hereafter with what? With the Fire; they are punished in the Hereafter with the Fire. And the two punishments do not pass them by, or one of them: that is, either both of these will befall them, which is the more common, or the punishment of the Hereafter will necessarily befall them. But the apparent meaning of the noble verse: ﴿in this world and the Hereafter﴾ is that the punishment befalls them in both abodes.

He says: ﴿in this world and the Hereafter﴾. The dunya (world) is this life we live, and it is described by that for two reasons. The first reason is its nearness (dunuww), since it precedes the Hereafter, so it is near (dani). The second reason is the lowness of its rank, as it is said: dunya and 'ulya (lower and higher). So the world is lower in rank than the Hereafter, however far its bliss reaches; however far its bliss reaches, it is lower than the Hereafter, because the bliss of this world, when it is attained, is mixed with turbidity, as the poet said:

A day for us and a day against us, and a day we are made to suffer, and a day we are made to be happy.

And the second said:

There is no pleasure in life while it is embittered; its delights are with the remembrance of death and old age.

So however much a person is given bliss in this world, its bliss is near (dani), and for this it is described as the dunya. As for the bliss of the Hereafter, Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Therein is whatever the souls desire and whatever the eyes delight in, and you therein will abide eternally﴾ [al-Zukhruf 71], and He the Exalted said: ﴿No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for their eyes as reward for what they used to do﴾ [al-Sajdah 17]. So the dunya is described by that for two reasons. The first? 
* Student: The first: its nearness, because it occurs before the Hereafter.
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: The second: that it is near (dani), meaning lower in rank than the Hereafter.
* Shaykh: The nearness of its rank and station. As for His saying: ﴿and the Hereafter﴾, it is described by that because it comes later, later in time, not in rank; it is above the dunya in rank, but later in time. He says: ﴿and they will have no helpers﴾, meaning this severe punishment that Allah inflicts upon them, they will find no one to help them against it, that is, no one who repels this punishment from them: not family, not wealth, not a friend, not a relative, nor anyone among the people. ﴿The criminal would wish to ransom himself from the punishment of that Day by his children, and his wife and his brother, and his kinsfolk who shelter him, and all those on earth, then it would save him. No! ﴾ [al-Ma'arij 11–15]. As for His saying: ﴿and they will have no helpers﴾, the mā here is negating. Is it Hijazi?
* Student: No.
* Shaykh: Why?
* Student: The Hijazi (mā) requires the order (tartib).
* Shaykh: What is the meaning of tartib?
* Student: Its subject comes first, then its predicate, yes.
* Shaykh: And here?
* Student: Here its predicate precedes its subject.
* Shaykh: Because ﴿lahum﴾ is a preposed predicate. Good. (min) is a superfluous prepositional particle, superfluous in i'rab, and ﴿nasirin﴾ is a postponed subject, raised by the yā'? Or by the wāw? Some—
* Students: By the yā'.
* Student: Accusative.
* Another student: Genitive.
* Shaykh: Do we have something that is raised by the yā', O people?
* Students: No.
* Shaykh: Nothing in the whole world is raised by the yā' except it is a non-Arabic language, we don't know. It is raised by the wāw presumed to exist, its place being the yā', and its appearance is prevented by the occupation of the position by the suitable letter, or the one brought for the superfluous prepositional particle. Were it not for (min), it would be (nasirun), and they would have "nasirun."

Then he brought the second division, saying: ﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds﴾. ﴿Those who believed and did righteous deeds﴾: they believed with their hearts and did righteous deeds with their limbs. The Lord, Mighty and Majestic, always repeats this in the Qur'an, combining belief and righteous deeds, because there is no belief without deeds, nor deeds without belief; rather both are necessary. ﴿Believed﴾: here the object of belief is omitted, so we estimate it in its most general form and say: they believed in what must be believed in, which is belief in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and the decree, its good and its evil. ﴿Did righteous deeds﴾: that is, they did righteous deeds, and righteous deeds are those that are for Allah and in Allah, meaning they are sincere to Allah and within the bounds of the sharia of Allah, meaning sincere and correct, as al-Fudayl ibn 'Iyad, may Allah have mercy on him, said: sincere to Allah and correct, meaning in accordance with the Sunnah. This is righteous deeds; if it is not sincere, it is not a righteous deed, but rather it is rejected upon its doer, because of the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord﴾ [al-Kahf 110]. And in the hadith qudsi, Allah the Exalted said: "I am the most self-sufficient of partners from association; whoever does a deed in which he associates others with Me, I leave him and his association."[[Related by Muslim (2985 / 46) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]] As for conformity or correctness, as al-Fudayl said, it is because of the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Whoever does a deed that is not upon our command, it is rejected"[[Related by Muslim (1718 / 18) from the hadith of 'A'ishah.]], so no deed is accepted except with conformity to the sharia. ﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, He will give them their rewards in full﴾ [al-Nisa' 173]. The fa' falls in the response to (amma), the conditional. And ﴿yuwaffihim﴾ has two readings: ﴿nuwaffihim﴾ and ﴿yuwaffihim﴾. As for the reading ﴿fa-yuwaffihim﴾, there is a shift (iltifat) from the first person to the third person, right? Because he said earlier: ﴿fa-u'adhdhibuhum﴾, and here he said: ﴿fa-yuwaffihim﴾, which is third person. As for the reading with nūn: ﴿fa-nuwaffihim﴾, there is a kind of shift from singular pronoun to plural pronoun: ﴿fa-u'adhdhibuhum﴾, and here he said: ﴿fa-nuwaffiyahum﴾. And what do you have with you?
* Student: The Jalalayn.
* Shaykh: Look, what does it say?
* Student: It says: ﴿fa-yuwaffihim﴾ with yā' and nūn.
* Shaykh: With yā' and nūn, look at the margin?
* Student: It says: with yā' and nūn, both are canonical (sab'iyyatan).
* Shaykh: Yes. In any case, the copy of the Qur'an I have does not write the second reading, but (...) it needs to be written. Good. He said: ﴿fa-nuwaffihim﴾, ﴿fa-yuwaffihim﴾. In any case, whether ﴿yuwaffihim﴾ or ﴿nuwaffihim﴾, there is some shift in it, and we mentioned earlier that the shift has benefits, or a benefit. Among them?
* Student: Alerting the listener.
* Shaykh: Alerting the listener how?
* Student: Because the listener, if he is reading in one rhythm and then it changes.
* Shaykh: When the speech is in one pattern,
* Student: Then this pattern changes so he becomes alert.
* Shaykh: He becomes attentive. Is this correct?
* Students: Yes.
* Shaykh: Yes indeed. The ways of alerting the listener are many. Among them: if you are speaking, you raise your voice on certain words, or lower your voice, or the like; this is a kind of alerting. Likewise, the shift from one pronoun to another necessitates the alertness of the listener. As for the second benefit: when he says ﴿fa-yuwaffihim ajurahum﴾ or ﴿yuwaffihim ajurahum﴾, there is in it some glorification of the one who gives in full, because the speaker referring to himself with the third-person form may suggest glorification, as a king says: "The king orders such-and-such," meaning himself; this has some glorification. There is also in it some honoring of those who did righteous deeds, honoring those who did righteous deeds, so He gives them in full. How so? Because mentioning Allah's favor upon them in the first-person form is greater than mentioning the favor in the third-person form; that is, this contains some honoring for them. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Is the reward for good anything but good?﴾ [al-Rahman 60], so He made it as if they were the ones who did good, although the one who does good is Allah, who does good to them in the deed and in its reward. And He the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, this has been for you a reward, and your effort has been appreciated﴾ [al-Insan 22]. So for the sake of honoring these people, Allah did not address them with explicit favor by saying "fa-nuwaffikum" or "fa-uwaffikum," but He said: ﴿fa-yuwaffihim﴾. So there are two benefits: glorification of the speaker himself, and second, honoring the one rewarded. As for the reading with nūn, the glorification in it is clear: ﴿fa-nuwaffihim﴾, because a plural pronoun attributed to Allah, or one intended to refer to Allah, we know with certainty that it is not meant as plurality in number, but what is meant by it is?
* Students: Glorification.
* Shaykh: Glorification. There is also in it honoring of the one rewarded (with nūn), the honoring of the one rewarded, because when his honor appears in the form of glorification, the reward coming from the Glorious is glorious, it is great. On this basis, in both readings there are three benefits: the shift, in both readings, has three benefits. The first?
* Students: Alerting.
* Student: And this is general.
* Shaykh: Alerting, and this is general. The second?
* Students: Glorification.
* Shaykh: Glorification of the one who gives in full. The third?
* Students: Honoring.
* Shaykh: Honoring of the one who is given in full.
He said: ﴿fa-yuwaffihim ajurahum﴾. Why was "ajurahum" put in the accusative when the verb had already completed its object?
* Student: It is the second object of the verb ﴿yuwaffihim﴾. ﴿fa-yuwaffihim ajurahum﴾, "ajurahum" is the second object of "yuwaffihim."
* Shaykh: (Yuwaffi) takes two objects? Are their origins a subject and predicate? Are their origins a subject and predicate?
* Student: Yes, both objects originally are subject and predicate.
* Shaykh: No, sir, this is one of the most false rules.
* Student: No, it is not subject and predicate.
* Shaykh: What?
* Student: "Hum" is its first object and "ajurahum" is its second object.
* Shaykh: Yes, but are the origins of the two objects a subject and predicate or not?
* Student: No.
* Shaykh: Then you have invalidated the rule.
* Student: Yes, I said it could be like "kana" (its subject and its predicate).
* Shaykh: No.
* Student: It slipped from me.
* Shaykh: Yes. If you say: "I considered Zayd understanding," this is where the origins are subject and predicate, because "zanna" (to consider) and its sisters take two objects whose origin is subject and predicate. Good. There are other words that take two objects whose origin is not subject and predicate; they call it the category of "kasa" (to clothe), and some say from "kasa wa-a'ta" (clothed and gave). This is from the category of?
* Students: "Kasa wa-a'ta."
* Shaykh: "Kasa wa-a'ta" take two objects whose origin is not subject and predicate. ﴿fa-yuwaffihim ajurahum﴾: "ajurahum" means the recompense of their deeds. O Allah, to You be praise. Look at this favor: as if these were workers who deserve a wage, necessarily, since Allah named their recompense a wage ('ajr), and a wage from the employer is a right that must be paid; but this is from the grace and generosity of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, because the one who made the wage obligatory upon Himself is who?
* Students: Allah.

**The Shaykh:** Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is the One who made that obligatory upon Himself. No one made it obligatory upon Him. Had He willed, He would have commanded and forbidden us, and we would have been bound to obey Him without any recompense, because He is our Lord and Creator. Whatever we do does not match even one of the millions of His blessings. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "No one will enter Paradise by his deeds." They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Not even I, unless Allah covers me with His mercy."[[Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (5673) and Muslim (2816/75) from Abu Hurayrah.]] So these rewards, which are the recompense for deeds and which Allah called a wage (ajr), are like the fixed wage owed by an employer. Yet no one made them obligatory upon Allah. Rather, He is the One who made this wage obligatory upon Himself. Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

*For the servants there is no right upon Him that is obligatory;*
*it is He who made obligatory the great reward.*
*Nay, no deed of theirs is lost before Him*
*if it is done with sincerity and excellence.*
*If they are punished, it is by His justice;*
*if they are blessed, it is by His grace, and grace belongs to the Bestower.*

O Allah, to You be all praise. The conclusion, then, is that we have no obligatory right upon Allah: ﴿Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy: whoever among you does evil in ignorance, then repents after it and makes amends, indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-An'am 54]. O Allah, to You be all praise. Good. ﴿So He will pay them their wages﴾, that is, the recompense for their deeds. It is called a wage, like the wage of a hired worker which is obligatory upon the employer. But who made it obligatory?

**The students:** Allah.

**The Shaykh:** Allah. He said: ﴿And Allah does not love the wrongdoers.﴾ Ending the verse with this is appropriate. Since He had explained that those who believe and do righteous deeds will be paid their wages in full, He clarified that these people have fulfilled what was required of them and that they did not wrong themselves. For this reason Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, granted them this great reward. And Allah, glorified and exalted, does not love the wrongdoers. Had they wronged themselves, they would not deserve this reward, as He said, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, association [with Allah] is a great wrong﴾ [Luqman 13]. Had they associated others with Allah, what they had done would have been nullified and their deeds would have been void. But they were sincere to Allah. Had they innovated in the religion of Allah, He would not have accepted it from them, but they followed the Sharia of Allah. Thus wrongdoing was negated from them, both in sincerity and in action, and they were worthy of the honour of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. As for those who disbelieved and deserved punishment, they wronged themselves and obtained the wrath of Allah, His punishment, and His non-love, we seek refuge in Allah. Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿That﴾.

**A student:** The verse is not clear.

**The Shaykh:** Yes: ﴿That We recite to you from the signs and the wise reminder﴾. ﴿That﴾ refers to everything mentioned earlier of the Surah of the Family of ʿImran, from ﴿Indeed, Allah chose Adam and Noah and the family of Abraham﴾ and so on to the end [Ali ʿImran 33]. All of this is what Allah recited to His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ). His saying ﴿We recite it to you﴾ means We recite it to you in sequence, one part following another, but through the medium of Jibril, peace be upon him, as He said: ﴿And indeed, it is the revelation of the Lord of the worlds. The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down upon your heart, that you may be among the warners, in a clear Arabic tongue﴾ [al-Shuʿara 192–195].

His saying ﴿We recite it to you from the signs﴾: the word ﴿from﴾ here (min). Some of them said it is bayaniyya (explanatory), explaining what is referred to by ﴿That﴾. Others said it is tab'idiyya (partitive), meaning "some of the signs." The correct view is the first, and that everything Allah recited to His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) is signs. The word ʾāyāt (signs) is the plural of āyah, which linguistically means a sign or indication. A sign of a thing is called an āyah, as He said: ﴿Is it not a sign for them that the scholars of the Children of Israel know it?﴾ [al-Shuʿara 197]. And He said: ﴿And a sign for them is the night: We strip from it the day﴾ [Ya-Sin 37], meaning a sign of Our power, and similar verses. When the Prophet (ﷺ) sent a man to his agent in Khaybar, instructing him to give him wasqs of dates, he said: "If he asks you for a sign (āyah), or he said, a mark (amārah), then place your hand on his trachea (tarquwah)."[[Related by Abu Dawud in his Sunan (3632) from Jabir ibn ʿAbdullah.]] In this sense, it is as if the Prophet (ﷺ) said to the agent: when I send you a messenger, the sign of his truthfulness is that he places his hand on his trachea.

He said: ﴿from the signs and the reminder﴾. The reminder (dhikr): what is meant by what Allah recited of the signs is the Quran, and likewise the reminder. Dhikr is used with several meanings, among them honour, as He said: ﴿And indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people﴾ [al-Zukhruf 44], meaning a great honour. From this is His saying: ﴿And We raised high your remembrance﴾ [al-Sharh 4], meaning We raised your honour. Dhikr is also used for that by which reflection is achieved, so good speech containing admonition is called dhikr. Allah said: ﴿So remind, if the reminder benefits﴾ [al-Aʿla 9], meaning the reminder. Dhikr is also used for the remembrance of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, as He said: ﴿And when you have finished the prayer, remember Allah standing, sitting, and lying on your sides﴾ [al-Nisaʾ 103].

What is meant by dhikr in this verse are the first two meanings: honour, and that by which remembrance is achieved. Undoubtedly this Quran is an honour for whoever holds fast to it and fulfils its rights. He attains the honour of this world and the Hereafter, and the happiness of this world and the Hereafter. The Arabs were not honoured, nor did they attain happiness, victory, and prominence, except when they held fast to it. For this reason, when they abandoned it, the quality of honour, prominence and victory left them, and they became what you see. Their former glory will not return to them, however much they boast of Arabism, nationalism and the like, unless they return to Islam. However far they go in propaganda concerning nationalism, Arabism and the like, it will not benefit them. It will only increase them in destruction, like those who ﴿sought refuge with men from the jinn, and they increased them in distress﴾ [al-Jinn 6]. It will only increase them in humiliation, unless they return to the religion of Allah through which they were victorious before.

Now, this Quran is also a reminder in terms of admonition. It is a reminder in terms of honour, and a reminder in terms of admonition, because every person who reads the Quran with a present heart will inevitably be affected by it: ﴿Indeed, in that is a reminder for whoever has a heart, or gives ear while he is a witness﴾ [Qaf 37]. He will inevitably be reminded by it. It is a great admonition even for non-believers: when they hear it while they understand its verses, that is, their meanings, they will be admonished by it. What happened to some of the Arabs in this regard is a famous matter in history. It is reported that when the Prophet (ﷺ) recited to them: ﴿But if they turn away, say: I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of ʿAd and Thamud﴾ [Fussilat 13], they said: "Stop," or, they stopped him and placed their hands over his mouth.[[Related by al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (539) from Jabir ibn ʿAbdullah.]] This was because of how greatly they understood these great meanings.

His saying ﴿the Wise﴾: al-Hakim means the one possessing wisdom. The entire Quran is wisdom. The word ḥakīm is a form of faʿīl used in the sense of mufʿal, and also in the sense of fāʿil. As faʿīl in the sense of mufʿal, it means muḥkam, precise and perfected. As faʿīl in the sense of fāʿil, it means ḥākim (judging), because the Quran undoubtedly judges between people: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you﴾ [al-Nisaʾ 105]. But does faʿīl come in the sense of mufʿal?

**A student:** "Amin rayhānati al-dāʿī al-samīʿ" (from the fragrance of the caller who hears).

**The Shaykh:** Here it is in the sense of musmiʿ (one who causes to hear).

**A student:** It is faʿīl in the sense of mufʿil.

**The Shaykh:** How "in the sense of mufʿil"? It is in the sense of muḥkim (precise). This (the word in the verse) is in the sense of muḥkam (made precise). It is like jarīḥ in the sense of majrūḥ (wounded), qatīl in the sense of maqtūl (killed). That is, faʿīl comes in the sense of mafʿūl and mufʿal, that is, what has not named its doer. So the Quran is muḥkam, and the Quran is also ḥākim.

**A student:** In His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And they have no helpers﴾, we said that (mā) here is the Hijazi mā, which requires word order. Here the predicate is a prepositional phrase. Is it valid for it to be Hijazi?

**The Shaykh:** And if the predicate is a prepositional phrase, is it valid for it to be Hijazi?

**The student:** Yes, is it not so?

**The Shaykh:** No, it is not so. Where did you get this statement from?

**The student:** They say: word order is necessary, unless the predicate is an adverb of place or time, or a prepositional phrase.

**The Shaykh:** Who said that?

**The student:** Ibn Malik said it.

**The Shaykh:** No, read what Ibn Malik said.

**The student:** In his saying:

*And the precedence of a prepositional phrase or an adverb, as in "mā bī anta maʿniyyan" (what you are concerned with in me), the scholars have permitted.*

**The Shaykh:** He means that the object of the predicate (maʿmūl al-khabar) is what is fronted. For this reason, in "mā bī anta maʿniyyan," the word order is normal: anta is its subject (ism), and maʿniyyan is the predicate (khabar). As for bī, it is the object of the predicate. That is, it is permissible for the complement of the predicate to precede it if it is an adverb or a prepositional phrase. This is the meaning of Ibn Malik's statement. Do you understand, or not?

**The student:** Yes, I understand.

**A student:** What is the third meaning of dhikr? Does it refer to this verse being a remembrance of Allah?

**The Shaykh:** No, that is far-fetched.

**The student:** Is the Quran itself a remembrance from Allah, Glorified and Exalted?

**The Shaykh:** Yes, but the remembrance of Allah that we mean is the one Allah mentioned in the Quran: ﴿So when you have finished the prayer, remember Allah﴾ [al-Nisaʾ 103].

**The student:** No, I mean, can these verses not be a remembrance?

**The Shaykh:** No, they cannot. For this reason, one does not say of someone who recites the Quran that he is remembering Allah, except in the general sense, because every act of worship is a remembrance of Allah. But the specific remembrance is: "Subḥān Allāh" (Glory be to Allah), "al-ḥamdu lillāh" (praise be to Allah), "lā ilāha illā Allāh" (there is no god but Allah), "Allāhu akbar" (Allah is greatest), and the like.

**The student:** The Quran is not a remembrance?

**The Shaykh:** The specific remembrance is a remembrance in the general sense.

**A student:** May Allah reward you well, O our Shaykh. Yesterday the polytheists came to the Messenger (ﷺ), and with him was a brother. They said to him: "Hold back." Does this indicate that their certainty in the punishment of this world is greater than their certainty in the punishment of the Hereafter?

**The Shaykh:** Yes, they fear, because some of them know that the Messenger is truthful, but they have obstinacy, we seek refuge in Allah.

**The student:** Yes, but they fear the punishment of this world, and their certainty in the punishment of the Hereafter is small?!

**The Shaykh:** But: ﴿Have you seen him who has taken his own desire as his god, and Allah has misguided him knowingly, and sealed his hearing and his heart, and placed over his sight a covering? Then who will guide him after Allah?﴾ [al-Jathiyah 23].

**A student:** Shaykh, ﴿That We recite to you from the signs﴾: do the signs refer only to what was mentioned about ʿIsa and the Family of ʿImran?

**The Shaykh:** Yes.

**The student:** If the address is to the Prophet (ﷺ), is it restricted to what was mentioned about ʿIsa? We said ﴿that﴾ means...

**The Shaykh:** The referent now is restricted to these narratives.

**The student:** Can we not say, O Shaykh, that ﴿that﴾ means that, referring to the story of ʿIsa and others?

**The Shaykh:** We estimate its referent as possibly in this story.

**A student:** Shaykh, we took from the benefits of iltifat (the shift in grammatical person) the removal of boredom and tedium from the listener, and also prompting him to reflect on the meaning. Shall we add these to the benefits of iltifat?

**The Shaykh:** It is possible, but prompting reflection may be from the category of alerting, though it does not contradict. These are two benefits that escaped us, and they are two correct benefits.

**A student:** Shaykh, the saying of Allah, Exalted is He: ﴿As for those who disbelieved, I will punish them with a severe punishment in this world and the Hereafter﴾. Does this mean that the punishment of this world is sensory and also a specific meaning, or not?

**The Shaykh:** Apparent and non-apparent.

**The student:** How?

**The Shaykh:** Apparent, like a trace, and non-apparent, which is in the heart.

**A student:** (...)

**The Shaykh:** Perhaps, perhaps, in a distant sense.

**The reader:** I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿And as for those who believed and did righteous deeds, He will pay them their wages in full. And Allah does not love the wrongdoers (57). That We recite to you from the signs and the wise reminder (58). Indeed, the example of ʿIsa with Allah is like the example of Adam; He created him from dust, then said to him, "Be," and he was (59). The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters﴾ [Ali ʿImran 57–60].

**The Shaykh:** I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And they plotted, and Allah plotted, and Allah is the best of plotters﴾ [Ali ʿImran 54]. From this noble verse it is derived that the enemies of the messengers scheme against them and plot against them, as indicated by His saying ﴿and they plotted﴾. From this we move to the point that the enemies of the messengers also plot against the followers of the messengers, because the enemies of the messengers do not plot against the messengers, or scheme against them, for the sake of individuals, but for the sake of their call. If the scholars inherit that call after them, then those who plotted against the messengers will scheme against the followers of the messengers and the heirs of the messengers. From this benefit it follows that the people of knowledge must take complete precaution against the enemies of the messengers who lie in wait for them, and must guard against their evil as much as they can, lest they plot against them. Plotting, its means and its methods are many, but the wise and intelligent person remains alert. For this reason Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said to the Messenger (ﷺ) regarding the hypocrites: ﴿They are the enemy, so beware of them﴾ [al-Munafiqun 4]. He made clear that they are the true enemy, and commanded caution against them.

* From the benefits of this verse: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is described with plotting, but He is not described with it in an absolute sense. Rather, it is said that Allah is a plotter against whoever plots against Him, so that plotting becomes a quality of perfection. Because plotting, when mentioned absolutely, can carry the connotation of deficiency. But when it is restricted, by saying that Allah, exalted is He, is a plotter against those who plot against Him and against His allies, it becomes a quality of perfection, indicating the might of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and the comprehensiveness of His knowledge, and that His knowledge is more subtle than the knowledge of those plotters who employ hidden means and crooked methods to bring the servants of Allah into evil. Thus Allah, glorified and exalted, is stronger than them in this respect, stronger than them in this matter, when they plot, He plots against them. It is not permissible to name Allah "the Plotter" absolutely. Is He named "the Plotter"? No. Is He described as "the Plotter" in an absolute sense? No. He is described as "the Plotter" in a restricted sense. We have already noted that Allah described Himself with plotting, scheming, mockery, deception and ridicule, but He never described Himself with treachery, because treachery is always a quality of blame: ﴿And if they intend to betray you, they have already betrayed Allah before, so He gave you power over them﴾ [al-Anfal 71]. He did not say "He betrayed them," because treachery is deception in a position of trust, and deception in a position of trust is a quality of blame and deficiency.

* From the benefits of the noble verse: permissibility of comparing the Creator and the creation in attributes, as He said: ﴿and Allah is the best of plotters﴾. Here "best" (khayr) is an ism al-tafḍīl (comparative/superlative form). It is permissible to compare between the Creator and the created, because this corresponds to reality completely. Allah, exalted is He, is more perfect than every possessor of perfection. Do you understand?

From this a rule branches out, namely that some scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, erred in interpreting the ism al-tafḍīl attributed to Allah as an ism al-fāʿil (active participle). For example, they say of His saying ﴿Allah knows best where He places His message﴾ [al-Anʿam 124]: "Allah is knowing where He places His message." They did not realize that when they say "Allah is knowing," this does not prevent others from sharing in knowledge with equality. But when they say "Allah is more knowing" (aʿlam), what? It prevents others from sharing with Him in the knowledge in which He is more knowing than others.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verses 54–55 (part 5 of 5):

﴿And Allah is the best of planners.﴾ Then the Exalted said: ﴿When Allah said: "O Jesus, I will take you and raise you to Me"﴾ [Al 'Imran 55], and so on. In this noble verse there is a reminder that we should remind people of the circumstances of the earlier prophets. The reason is that we estimated ﴿when Allah said﴾ to be governed by what? By "mention when Allah said." So a person should remind people of the circumstances of the earlier prophets, because in that there is love for them, praise of them, knowledge of their circumstances, the preservation of their remembrance, and other great benefits.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation that Allah speaks, and that His speech is with letters and with audible sounds, as shown by ﴿O Jesus, I will take you﴾. This is an address to one who hears. Then, is it words made of letters, or without letters? It is made of letters. For this reason, the position of Ahl al-Sunnah wa'l-Jama'ah (the People of the Sunnah and the Community) is that Allah speaks with an audible speech, with letter and sound.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the refutation of those who say that the speech of Allah is the inner meaning (al-ma'na al-nafsi, the meaning existing within the self), the meaning subsisting in His essence. This is not called "saying" (qawl). If it is called "saying," it must be qualified, as in His words: ﴿And they say within themselves: "Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?"﴾ [al-Mujadilah 8]. When He intended inner speech, what qualified it? ﴿They say within themselves.﴾ But when the word "saying" comes unqualified, what is meant by it is what is heard. In this there is a refutation of the Ash'ariyyah (followers of al-Ash'ari), who say that the speech of Allah is the inner speech subsisting in His essence, that it is eternal, does not occur anew, and that one part of it does not precede another, because it is a meaning subsisting in the soul. In reality, the content of this view is the denial of the speech of Allah. For this reason, one of their fair-minded ones said: "There is no difference between us and the Mu'tazilah, because we all say that this Qur'an which is in the mushaf is created." The Ash'ariyyah say that Allah the Exalted does not speak with what is heard, but He creates a speech through which He expresses what is in His self. On this basis, what is heard, what is recited, and what is written is created. So the Mu'tazilah and the Ash'ariyyah agree. Indeed, the Mu'tazilah are better than them in terms of attribution, because they say: "This is the speech of Allah," whereas those say: "This is an expression of the speech of Allah, an expression of the speech of Allah and not the speech of Allah." The point is that this verse and its like contain a refutation of whom? Of the Ash'ariyyah.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the virtue and distinction of Jesus, due to Allah addressing him. Whoever Allah addresses, that is without doubt a source of honor for him, especially since He said to him: ﴿I will take you and raise you to Me﴾, and so on.

* Among its benefits: that Allah, glorified and exalted be He, raised Jesus bodily, as shown by ﴿and raise you﴾. The address is to Jesus, who is composed of a body and a soul. So his raising was with what? With his body.

* Among its benefits: the affirmation of a distinction for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. That is because the Prophet ﷺ was taken by night journey (isra') to the seven heavens, until he passed through all of them while awake, whereas Jesus was raised only while asleep. This is because His words ﴿I will take you﴾ mean "I will cause you to sleep" (munimuk), according to one of the opinions, and it is the closest of them. It is well known that the steadfastness of the heart of one who experiences a thing while awake is stronger than the steadfastness of one who experiences it while asleep. Is this clear? For this reason, you find some people, when they hear loud thunder and a flashing lightning, close their eyes and put their two fingers in their ears so as not to hear, and say: "I wish I had slept before this." But the steadfast person who says: "Nothing will befall us except what Allah has decreed for us," you find that it does not concern him. The point is that the Messenger ﷺ was taken by night journey while awake, with his spirit and body, whereas when Allah wished to raise Jesus, He caused him to sleep.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: another distinction for Jesus, in that He said: ﴿raise you to Me﴾, "to Me." He attributed his raising to Himself, glorified and exalted be He. Without doubt this is a distinction, that Allah took him to Himself and raised him to Himself, so that he would be closer to Him than if he had remained on earth.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that Allah, glorified and exalted be He, protected Jesus from the harm that the disbelievers could inflict on him, as He said: ﴿purifying you from those who disbelieved﴾ [Al 'Imran 55]. This was by defending him. The disbelievers said that he was born of adultery, may Allah destroy them, so Allah purified him, Allah purified him, when they said: ﴿O Mary, you have certainly come with a monstrous thing. O sister of Harun, your father was not a man of evil, nor was your mother unchaste﴾ [Maryam 27–28]. Where did the adultery come from? Where did they get adultery from? Because this is an insinuation: they say, "Your father was not a man of evil, rather he was pure, and your mother likewise, so where did the adultery come from?" Look, I seek refuge in Allah: she did not answer them. ﴿She pointed to him﴾ [Maryam 29]. "Ask the child?" ﴿They said: "How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?"﴾ [Maryam 29]. He answered them before they asked him, and what did he say? ﴿He said: "Indeed, I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Book"﴾ [Maryam 30] and so on. This is a great purification for him and for his mother, may Allah be pleased with her.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that everyone who accuses Jesus of this evil is a disbeliever, because He did not say "purifying you from those who slandered you." He said: ﴿from those who disbelieved﴾. From this we derive, first, the disbelief of those people, and second, that everyone who accuses him of that is a disbeliever.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that supporting the followers is supporting the one they follow. From where? ﴿And I will make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve﴾. Were it not that he rejoices in this and is gladdened, Allah would not have given him this good news. But it is well known that every person who guides to guidance, when his followers prevail, it is certain that he will rejoice, because whenever his followers prevail, the guidance that led people to it becomes strong, and his reward increases. Indeed, whoever guides to good has a reward like that of its doer.[[Narrated by Muslim (133/1893) from the hadith of Abu Mas'ud al-Ansari, with the wording: "Whoever guides to good."]]

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the followers of Jesus will be victorious until the Day of Resurrection, because of His words: ﴿above those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection﴾. We have previously mentioned who his followers are?
* Student: Those who believed in him.
* Shaykh: After the mission of the Messenger ﷺ, they are the community of Muhammad. Whoever disbelieves in Muhammad has not followed Jesus. We have mentioned another aspect: that the Christians will be above others among the disbelieving communities. But Islam is above all of them. But when will Islam be above all? When the Muslims return to Islam in truth. As for when they do not return to Islam in truth, it is feared that the Christians will be above them. And the reality?
* Students: It bears witness to this.
* Shaykh: The reality now, unfortunately, bears witness to this.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of the Day of Resurrection, because of His words: ﴿until the Day of Resurrection﴾. The Day of Resurrection is the day when people will be raised for recompense: if good, then good; if evil, then evil. Why is it called the Day of Resurrection?
* Student: Because people stand up on it.
* Shaykh: That is one. Complete it?
* Student: The witnesses stand on it.
* Shaykh: The witnesses stand on it. Complete it?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: What?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Justice is established on it.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the application of "above" to a metaphorical superiority.
* Student: ﴿above those who disbelieve﴾.
* Shaykh: Does its meaning mean that they will be on a ceiling above their heads?
* Students: No, a metaphorical elevation?
* Shaykh: No, it is a physical superiority; a metaphorical superiority. Correct. So the affirmation of metaphorical superiority is like physical superiority.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the return of all creatures is to their Lord, glorified and exalted be He, who began their creation, and the end will be to Him, because of His words: ﴿Then to Me is your return﴾. It is certain. For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿O mankind, indeed you are laboring toward your Lord with labor, and you will meet it﴾ [al-Inshiqaq 6]. "Mankind" is addressed; every person, not only the believer, every person. ﴿Indeed, you are laboring toward your Lord with labor, and you will meet it﴾. "Laboring toward Him" (ila) indicates the ultimate end: the end is to Allah. Then He confirmed this end with His words ﴿and you will meet it﴾, meaning: prepare for this meeting.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of Allah's judgment in this world and the Hereafter. ﴿So I will judge between you﴾ refers to the Hereafter. In this world: ﴿And whatever you differ over, its judgment is with Allah﴾ [al-Shura 10]. So all judgment returns to Allah, glorified and exalted be He, and Allah the Exalted is the Judge in this world and in the Hereafter.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the good news to the believers that their dispute with the disbelievers will be decided by the hand of the One, the Irresistible. He will judge between you concerning what you used to differ about. Allah, glorified and exalted be He, has informed us that the disputants, the prevailing party, are the believers. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection﴾ [al-Nisa' 141]. And what follows it? ﴿And Allah will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers﴾ [al-Nisa' 141]. Praise be to Allah. Look: ﴿sabilan (a way)﴾ is an indefinite noun in the context of what?  An indefinite noun in the context of what?
* Student: The context of negation.
* Shaykh: Negation. Whenever an indefinite noun occurs, it is in the context of negation?
* Student: Yes.
* Shaykh: Wrong, wrong, that is not correct, it is not so. The point is that this is an indefinite noun in the context of negation, so it includes every way, any way, whether little or much. This is good news: any adversary in this world is told: you will prevail in every case. That is, a judge says to the litigant: "Look, you are litigating before me, and you are the victor in every case." Has such a dispute ever occurred? Never. But our disputes with the disbelievers, praise be to Allah, the judgment in them is in our favor in advance. ﴿So Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection, and Allah will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers﴾. Yes, praise be to Allah.
* Student: (...) Allah (...) to Him.
* Shaykh: Yes, correct, yes.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of Allah's exaltedness in His essence, because of His words: ﴿and raise you to Me﴾. Raising is known to be ascending upward. When He says ﴿to Me﴾, it is known with certainty that Allah is above, glorified and exalted be He, and so He is, above everything in His essence. This does not contradict what is established: that He, glorified be He, descends every night to the lowest heaven when the last third of the night remains. He is descending and He is high. Nor does it contradict that He is with His creation, as He, glorified be He, said: ﴿And He is with you wherever you are﴾ [al-Hadid 4]. He is with the creation and He is above them, as Shaykh al-Islam (Ibn Taymiyyah) said in al-Wasitiyyah: "High in His nearness, near in His highness." Nor does it contradict that He comes on the Day of Resurrection to judge between the servants. He comes, but He is above everything. Nor does it contradict that He draws near on the evening of 'Arafah, boasting before the angels about the people of the standing place.

If someone says: "How can this not contradict? I cannot imagine that something could be high and descending at the same time?" We say: Woe to you! You cannot imagine this regarding whom? Regarding the created being. But regarding the Creator, everything that Allah has informed about Himself is true, true and not contradictory, and there is nothing in it that is impossible. If you say "it is impossible," it means that you will not believe the reports of Allah and His Messenger unless they agree with your desire, and otherwise not. For this reason, whoever among people went astray in such matters went astray, saying: "This is not possible, and this is not possible," and they built their creed upon their desires. If you want to build your creed upon your desire, what is the benefit of the messengers? There is no benefit from the messengers. If you want to build the creed upon what you desire, and when the messengers bring words that oppose what you have, you go about distorting them, then there is no benefit from the messengers. For this reason I advise you always and forever, and I repeat that you should accept everything that came in the Book and the Sunnah about the attributes of Allah, glorified and exalted be He, and about the attributes of the Last Day as well. For in the Last Day there are things that do not exist in this world: the nearness of the sun to people by the distance of a mile on the Day of Resurrection. If that were in this world, the earth and everyone on it would burn. But in the Hereafter it is something else. The people being in light and others in darkness while the place of standing is one. In this world it is impossible; if the smallest lamp were brought with you, the one beside you would benefit from it. In this world it is possible. In the Hereafter, people sweat according to their deeds: some are bridled by their sweat, and others reach to their ankles, while the place of standing is one. In this world, is it possible or not? It is not possible. So all the matters of the Hereafter, the matters of the unseen, it is not permissible for you to measure them by what you witness in this world, because the analogy here is impossible; it is an analogy between things that differ. This is especially so regarding the attributes of the Creator, glorified and exalted be He, for the difference between the attributes of the Creator and the attributes of the created is a vast difference. Therefore, beware of measuring what Allah has affirmed for Himself of attributes by what you know of the attributes of created beings, for you will go astray.

* * *

* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿Indeed, the likeness of Jesus to Allah is like that of Adam. He created him from dust; then He said to him, "Be," and he was. The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters. Whoever argues with you about it after knowledge has come to you, say: "Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves; then let us invoke earnestly and invoke the curse of Allah upon the liars."  Indeed, this is the true narration. And there is no deity except Allah, and indeed Allah is the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾ [Al 'Imran 59–62].
* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan.
* Student: The benefits. We took the affirmation of Allah's exaltedness, because of His words: ﴿and raise you to Me﴾.
* Shaykh: * Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the return of all creatures is to Allah, as an end and as a judgment; for people will be presented to their Lord on the Day of Resurrection for a judgment that will judge between them.

* Among its benefits: the affirmation of recompense, because of the Exalted's words: ﴿So I will judge between you﴾, and this is a judgment of recompense.

* Among its benefits: that disputing occurs between believers and disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection, because of His words: ﴿So I will judge between you﴾. It may be said that this is a judgment whose dispute began in this world, where the disbelievers and hypocrites used to dispute. But the first is closer, and it is supported by the Exalted's words: ﴿Indeed, you will die, and indeed they will die. Then indeed, on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord you will dispute﴾ [al-Zumar 30–31].

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the disagreement between Muslims and disbelievers is a fundamental disagreement, which Allah will judge between these and those on the Day of Resurrection. As for disagreement among Muslims over matters whose source is ijtihad (independent reasoning), they will not be judged between, because the mujtahids, although they differ in the ruling, have not differed in the truth; for each of them excuses the other and does not regard him as opposing him. Even if he opposes him in statement and opinion, he has not opposed him in method and approach. Each of them seeks the truth, but they differ over how to reach it.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of Allah's knowledge, because of His words: ﴿So I will judge between you﴾, since there is no judgment except after knowledge. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ said: "I only judge according to what I hear."[[Agreed upon; narrated by al-Bukhari (6967) and Muslim (4/1713) from the hadith of Umm Salamah.]]

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verse 54–55 (part 1 of 5):

Student: I seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿And they schemed, and Allah schemed, and Allah is the best of schemers (54). When Allah said: "O 'Isa, indeed I will take you in death and raise you to Me and purify you from those who disbelieve, and I will make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection. Then to Me is your return, and I will judge between you concerning that wherein you used to differ (55). As for those who disbelieve, I will punish them with a severe punishment in this world and the Hereafter, and they will have no helpers (56). As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, He will give them their rewards in full. And Allah does not love wrongdoers (57). That which We recite to you of the verses and the wise Reminder (58).﴾ [Al 'Imran 54–58].

The Shaykh: I seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And they schemed, and Allah schemed, and Allah is the best of schemers﴾. ﴿They schemed﴾: the pronoun refers to those who disbelieved in 'Isa. Makr (scheming) is to reach the avenging of one's opponent by means that are unexpected, that is, by hidden means: one takes revenge on one's opponent and adversary by hidden means. It resembles deception (khida'), for a person reaches the avenging of his opponent from a direction he does not perceive, by hidden means. His saying: ﴿And they schemed, and Allah schemed﴾ means that Allah the Glorified and Exalted schemed against them when they schemed against 'Isa. ﴿And Allah is the best of schemers﴾ means: the most powerful of them in scheming, the most intense, and the most knowing of the means that surround His enemies.

If someone asks: what shows us that the pronoun in His saying ﴿they schemed﴾ refers to those who disbelieved in 'Isa? The answer to this is easy, because His saying ﴿And they schemed, and Allah schemed﴾ cannot proceed from a people who said: ﴿We believe in Allah, and bear witness that we are Muslims﴾ [Al 'Imran 52], and who said: ﴿Our Lord, we believe in what You have sent down and we follow the Messenger﴾ [Al 'Imran 53]. This is impossible. Rather, it proceeds only from a people who disbelieved, and that is His saying: ﴿But when 'Isa perceived disbelief from them﴾ [Al 'Imran 52].

If it is said: what is this scheming that they schemed? The answer is that they schemed against 'Isa when they conspired to kill him, and Allah saved him from them, and He schemed against them by making his likeness fall upon a man, either from among them, from those who came to kill him, or from among the companions of 'Isa. Allah cast his likeness upon one of them and he was killed. The point is that these people conspired to kill and came to 'Isa, peace be upon him, and entered upon him without letting him know that they intended to kill him, so that he would not seek help from anyone or defend himself, and similar things. But Allah the Mighty and Majestic cast his likeness upon one of them, or upon one of his disciples, the Hawariyyun. There are two opinions of the exegetes on this. Some said: Allah cast his likeness upon one of them, who was their leader. Allah made the likeness of 'Isa fall upon this man, so when they wanted to kill him he said: "I am your companion." They said: "You are lying; you are not our companion, rather you are 'Isa." So they killed him and crucified him. Is this scheming or not? It is a great scheme, greater than their scheme, because this man who came claiming to lead these people to kill 'Isa became the one killed. This opinion is stronger in that it contains a great scheme against these people. As for the second opinion, they say: when 'Isa, peace be upon him, perceived that they had entered upon him to kill him, he said to one of his companions: "Who will agree to have my likeness cast upon him, and I guarantee him Paradise?" One of them volunteered for this, and Allah cast his likeness upon him. It was also said: rather, Allah cast his likeness upon all who were with 'Isa, so that when these people entered, each one would say: "Which of you is 'Isa? Which of you is 'Isa? Which of you is 'Isa?" They did not recognize him. These are two principal opinions. The first opinion: upon whom was the likeness cast?

Students: The leader.

The Shaykh: Yes, upon the leader of the people who came to kill him, and he was killed. The second opinion is that it was cast upon a man of 'Isa's companions. Then, was the likeness cast upon all of them so that it became confused for those who entered? Or was it cast upon one of them? On this too there are two opinions. The matter has no explicit text from the infallible Prophet, peace be upon him, and Allah knows best. But His saying the Exalted: ﴿And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them﴾ [An-Nisa' 157] may support the last opinion, that every one of those with 'Isa came to resemble 'Isa, so it became confused for them who 'Isa was. The point is that this is their scheme: they came to 'Isa, peace be upon him, to kill him in a manner that he would not perceive. As for Allah's scheme against them, it is that He cast the likeness either upon one of them or upon one of 'Isa's followers, so they killed him, and they thought they had killed 'Isa, and they began to announce: "We killed 'Isa, the son of Maryam, the Messenger of Allah," and "they crucified him," while they did not kill him and did not crucify him.

In the saying of Allah the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And they schemed, and Allah schemed﴾ there is, among the attributes of Allah, the affirmation of scheming to Allah the Mighty and Majestic. The discussion of this: first, is scheming in its true sense? Or is it an expression for requiting a scheme, so that the requital of a scheme is called a scheme by way of verbal correspondence and not semantic correspondence? It is like His saying: ﴿So whoever transgresses against you, transgress against him in like manner﴾ [Al-Baqarah 194]. The one who takes retribution for himself is not called a transgressor, but it resembles it in wording, by verbal correspondence and not semantic correspondence. Or is it a true scheme, because Allah's treatment of them is a scheme, since the one killed was one of them according to one opinion, or the matter was confused for them according to the second opinion? The correct view in this is that Allah the Exalted is described by what He described Himself with, and we do not know Allah better than He knows Himself. He is more knowing of Himself, more truthful in speech, and better in discourse. But He must be exempted from every deficiency. Is scheming among the attributes of deficiency absolutely, meaning that there is no praise in it at all? Or is it a deficiency in some circumstances and not in others? The second is the truth: scheming in its proper place is praiseworthy and an attribute of perfection, while scheming out of its proper place is an attribute of deficiency, because scheming out of its proper place is treachery, and treachery is a blameworthy attribute. For this reason Allah did not describe Himself with it, nor in the correspondence that follows: ﴿And if they intend treachery against you, then they have already betrayed Allah before﴾ [Al-Anfal 71]?

Students: ﴿So He gave you power over them﴾.

The Shaykh: ﴿So He gave you power over them﴾ [Al-Anfal 71], and He did not say: "so He betrayed them," because treachery is a blameworthy attribute absolutely. In contrast, ﴿And they schemed, and Allah schemed﴾, where Allah answered their scheme with a scheme and did not answer their treachery with treachery. So it follows that we must describe Allah with what He described Himself with of scheming in the circumstance in which Allah described Himself with scheming, and that is in response to the scheming of His enemies. So we say: Allah schemes against whom?

Students: They scheme against Him.

The Shaykh: They scheme against Him, against His messengers, and against His signs. But as for describing Allah with scheming absolutely, so that we say: "Allah is a schemer" without qualification, this is not permissible. Why? Because of the possibility of deficiency, since scheming, as we said, is not perfection in every circumstance nor deficiency in every circumstance. When it is stated absolutely, it becomes capable of being a deficiency. When it is restricted to the circumstance in which it is perfection, it does not admit of being a deficiency. So we say: scheming is attributed to Allah not absolutely, but in the circumstance in which Allah described Himself with it. For this reason it came in the hadith: "War is deception"[[Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (3029) and Muslim (1740/18) from Abu Hurayrah.]]. Everyone knows that deception in war is perfection or deficiency?

Students: Perfection.

The Shaykh: Perfection. And it is reported of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, that when 'Amr ibn Wudd came out to him to duel, and you know what a duel is? When the two lines meet, the combatants ask for a duel: who will come out against so-and-so? A duel is a cause of conquest or defeat, because when two men duel and one of them prevails, whose spirits are strengthened?

Students: His companions'.

The Shaykh: His companions', and the spirits of the others are weakened. When he came out to duel 'Amr ibn Wudd, 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, came out to him and cried out to him, saying: "I did not come out to duel two men." So 'Amr ibn Wudd thought that someone from his people had followed him, so he turned to look whether anyone had reached him. When he turned, 'Ali struck him with the sword until his head rang. Is this a deception or not?

Students: A deception.

The Shaykh: Praiseworthy or not praiseworthy?

Students: Praiseworthy.

The Shaykh: Praiseworthy, because he came to kill him. He came to kill 'Ali, so he rid himself of him by this deception. This is counted as a virtue of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib and an attribute of perfection. Then we say: scheming in its proper place is praise and perfection. Now, He says: ﴿And Allah is the best of schemers﴾. This is a fixed, absolute attribute; it does not need a qualifier, because it is described with perfection. What is the perfection? ﴿the best﴾. ﴿And Allah is the best of schemers﴾: meaning that no one schemes except that Allah's scheming is above it and better than it. Is scheming among the essential attributes or the active attributes?

Students: The active.

The Shaykh: The active, because it relates to His will, and every attribute that has a cause is related to His will, since every attribute of Allah that has a cause is related to His will, because the one who determines the cause is Allah; when He determines the cause, He has willed it, and what follows from it of attributes follows.

﴿And they schemed, and Allah schemed, and Allah is the best of schemers (54). When Allah said: "O 'Isa, indeed I will take you in death﴾. It is possible that (idh) is connected to ﴿Allah schemed﴾, meaning: and Allah schemed when Allah said: "O 'Isa, indeed I will take you in death, and raise you to Me, and purify you from those who disbelieve." It is also possible that it is connected to an omitted element whose estimate is: "Mention, O Muhammad, extolling the virtue of 'Isa, when Allah said: 'O 'Isa, indeed I will take you in death and raise you to Me and purify you from those who disbelieve.'" ﴿When Allah said: "O 'Isa, indeed I will take you in death"﴾. Did He say it with an audible speech or an inaudible one?

Students: Audible.

The Shaykh: With audible speech, which 'Isa heard. He spoke with audible speech because He was addressing him: ﴿O 'Isa, indeed I will take you in death﴾. He says: ﴿indeed I will take you in death﴾. So what is the meaning of this death? In it the scholars have three opinions. The first opinion: "I will receive you," meaning: "I will take you," derived from the expression "tawaffa al-da'in dayna-hu," meaning he received his debt. 'Isa was taken by Allah to Himself in heaven, and raised until he descends at the end of time. The second opinion: ﴿mutawaffika﴾ is death of sleep, meaning "I will make you sleep," because the sleeper is one who is taken in death. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that have not died during their sleep﴾ [Az-Zumar 42]. And He said: ﴿And it is He who takes you in death by night, and knows what you have committed by day; then He resurrects you therein﴾ [Al-An'am 60]. The third opinion: it is an actual death; Allah caused him to die a real death, and will bring him back to life at the end of time and he will descend to the world. The correct view is that it is death of sleep, and that when Allah the Mighty and Majestic wished to raise him to heaven, He made him sleep to make the passage from earth to heaven easy for him, because passing from earth to heaven is not an easy matter, due to the length and distance of the journey, and the terrors seen between heaven and earth and within the heavens as well. So Allah made him sleep and then raised him while asleep until he reached heaven. However, this opinion does not contradict the first opinion, which means "I will receive you," because their end is one. As for the third opinion, that it is death in the sense of dying, it is a weak view, weakened by His saying the Exalted: ﴿And there is none of the People of the Book but that he will surely believe in him before his death﴾ [An-Nisa' 159], "before his death," meaning 'Isa's death, and this indicates that he has not died. Also, Allah the Exalted has not raised anyone after death so that he remains as in the descent of 'Isa, peace be upon him, at the end of time. And also, the application of "death" (tawaffi) to sleep is frequent in the Qur'an; it is not a strange meaning such that we would say it cannot be applied to it. Rather, it is a meaning with much frequency in the Qur'an.

He says: ﴿I will take you in death and raise you to Me﴾. ﴿raising you to Me﴾: ﴿raising you﴾ is in construct with the pronoun "ka" just as ﴿taking you in death﴾ is in construct with the pronoun "ka." So how do you parse the "ka" in both? Is it in a genitive position or an accusative position?

Some students: An accusative position.

Other students: A genitive position.

The Shaykh: Is it not the direct object?

Student: Yes.

The Shaykh: "Mutawaffa" and "marfu'"? So is it in an accusative position or a genitive position?

Students: In a genitive position.

The Shaykh: It is in a genitive position, because the action of the noun on it is stronger than the action of the meaning. That is, the action of the noun, which is the word, is stronger than the action of the meaning. It is well known that the noun is always construed with its agent and construed with its object. Then He said: ﴿and raise you to Me﴾. ﴿to Me﴾: to what place? To heaven, because raising is from a lower place, so the meaning of ﴿raising you to Me﴾ is: in heaven.
