That is, they came from the lands of al-Sham because they knew that the emigration place of this Prophet would be Medina, according to what the Torah says about him. So they said: "We will go there to be with him." ﴿And before this they used to seek victory over those who disbelieved, but when there came to them what they recognized, they disbelieved in it﴾ [Al-Baqarah 89].

﴿The People of the Book⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠ are Jews and Christians, and the majority of them are Jews.

﴿Wish they could (law yudillunakum)⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠: here "law" is masdariyyah, meaning "that" (an). The rule regarding "law" is that when it follows something that expresses wish and love, it is masdariyyah. ﴿They wished you would soften, so they would soften﴾ [Al-Qalam 9]: that is, they wished that you would soften. ﴿Many of the People of the Book wish they could return you to disbelief after your belief﴾ [Al-Baqarah 109]: that is, they wish that they would return you. Here it is masdariyyah. It is known that "law" also comes as a conditional particle of impossibility for impossibility, like: "If Zayd had come, I would have honored you." Here my honoring you was impossible because Zayd's coming was impossible.

He, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿wish they could lead you astray﴾, meaning they wish to lead you astray. Misguidance (idlal) means being turned away from the truth; that is, they wish to take you out of guidance into error. What is the kind of error they wished for the Muslims? It may be explained by the second verse in al-Baqarah: ﴿Many of the People of the Book wish they could return you to disbelief after your belief, out of envy from themselves﴾ [Al-Baqarah 109].

He, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿but they lead astray none but themselves﴾ [Al 'Imran 69], meaning: by their attempt and this wish of theirs, they lead none but themselves astray. And how do they lead themselves astray? The well-known view of most exegetes is that the meaning is: they destroy none but themselves. This is because when they wish misguidance for you, they incur sin for that, and so they become like the ones who are astray. It has also been said: rather, the meaning of ﴿they lead astray none but themselves﴾ is that when they busy themselves with trying to mislead you, they busy themselves away from what would guide them. This is what actually happens: when a person wants to reject the truth and lead others astray, he busies himself with trying to mislead others instead of trying to guide his own self. So the meaning is: they lead none but themselves astray, because they busied themselves with trying to mislead you away from—what? From seeking their own guidance. For the habit is that when a person busies himself with trying to mislead others, you find him knocking on every door and taking every path, trying to mislead others, and forgetting himself. He forgets himself. This happens often, even among students of knowledge at times: a person wants to defend himself and his opinion even if it is mistaken, so you find him seeking excuses, distortions, and interpretations, and turning texts away from their apparent meaning in order to make them agree with his view, forgetting that it is obligatory for him, when he is opposed, to seek the truth and to review himself, lest the correct view lies with others. This often happens when a person adopts an opinion or states one, and then, when it is reviewed, it becomes clear to him that the correct view is contrary to what he believed at first. So, ﴿but they lead astray none but themselves﴾ has two opinions:

The first opinion: ﴿they lead astray none but themselves﴾ by destruction and abundant punishment, since they tried to turn people away from the religion of Allah.

The second: ﴿they lead astray none but themselves﴾ by busying themselves with trying to mislead you away from seeking the guidance of their own selves.

Some exegetes said: this second is preferable, because a threat of what will happen to them in the Hereafter would be pointless in this context, since they do not in fact believe in the one who warned of this, so as to be told that they destroy none but themselves. But the reality is that this is not the point; that is, Allah is speaking about the actual situation. So the verse allows both meanings. The first meaning, the well-known one among most exegetes, is that they lead themselves astray by what? By their destruction through the sins and transgressions they earn. The second meaning: they lead themselves astray by wasting themselves and busying themselves with what becomes a cause of your misguidance.

﴿But they lead astray none but themselves, and they do not perceive﴾: meaning they do not perceive that they have wasted their time in trying to mislead you and have forgotten themselves. For a person, in the heat of the desire for victory, or the love of victory and the intoxication of love for prominence, forgets and does not perceive that time has been lost to him. These people do not perceive that time has been lost to them by busying themselves with seeking, or trying, to mislead you. And perception (shu'ur) is the inner meaning that a person perceives within himself, sometimes as reproach and regret, or the opposite of that, as relief and optimism.

* In this noble verse: a declaration of the enmity of the People of the Book toward the Muslims, since they wish misguidance for them. And the group of a people generally has the same drink as the rest of the people, so if this group wishes this, others are like them.

* Among the benefits of the verse: a warning about the People of the Book, and that they try to turn the Muslims away from their religion, just like the polytheists. Each of the two groups wishes misguidance for the Muslims. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿They wish you would disbelieve as they disbelieved, so that you would be alike﴾ [An-Nisa' 89], and He the Exalted said about the polytheists of Quraysh: ﴿and they wished that you would disbelieve﴾ [Al-Mumtahanah 2]. So all polytheists, all atheists, and everyone who claims to possess a scripture all wish that the Muslims would disbelieve and go astray after their guidance and faith.

And if this is so, it is obligatory for us to be cautious of them and to believe that they are bitter enemies who wish to destroy us and our religion overnight.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the transgressor is repaid with the like of his aggression and is afflicted with the like of what he inflicted on others, based on His saying: ﴿but they lead astray none but themselves﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: consoling the Muslims regarding what these people intend for them of misguidance. It is as if Allah said: "Do not fear them, for misguidance returns only to them." But this applies truly to the believers who believe fully in their religion, take pride in it, and honor it, not to those who make their religion mere words on the tongue or letters on paper, while in reality they follow others and exalt others in their souls. Such people may be harmed by the filth of these disbelievers who wish to mislead them.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: a person may be blind to falsehood even while practicing it, based on the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿but they lead astray none but themselves, and they do not perceive﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the comprehensive knowledge of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, of what is in the hearts of creatures, based on His saying: ﴿a group wished﴾, for wudd has its seat in the heart, and none knows what is in the hearts except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: we refute everyone who claims, or imagines, that the disbelievers wish good for the Muslims, because we say to him: "You do not know what is in their hearts. Listen to the Knower of the Unseen, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: ﴿A group of the People of the Book wish they could lead you astray﴾." So you do not know, and do not be deceived by their flattery, their deception, and their cunning.

Then Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿O People of the Book, why do you disbelieve in the signs of Allah while you bear witness? O People of the Book, why do you mix truth with falsehood and conceal the truth while you know?﴾ This is an address from Allah to the People of the Book in the manner of rebuke. ﴿O People of the Book⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠: Jews and Christians, and especially the Jews. ﴿Why (lima)⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠: "ma" is an interrogative noun whose alif has been dropped because the preposition has entered upon it, and the interrogation here is for rebuke. ﴿Why do you disbelieve in the signs of Allah﴾: "signs" (ayat) is the plural of "ayah," which is the sign indicating Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Every sign of Allah's signs indicates one of His attributes. So retribution is a sign indicating anger, and the expansion of provision, when a person is not in disobedience to Allah, is a sign indicating good pleasure and mercy.

So the signs vary according to what they relate to. These people disbelieved in the signs of Allah. The legislative signs are what the messengers brought. So what are the signs these people disbelieved in? They are the signs that were revealed to their messengers and to Muhammad ﷺ. The Jews disbelieved in the signs of Allah, which is the Torah; and the Christians disbelieved in the signs of Allah, which is the Gospel (Injil). They disbelieved in them. How did they disbelieve in both? Because Allah, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, whom they find written with them in the Torah and the Gospel, who enjoins upon them what is right and forbids them what is wrong, makes lawful for them the good things and prohibits for them the evil things, and relieves them of their burden and the shackles that were upon them﴾ [Al-A'raf 157]. This description exists. And He, the Exalted, says: ﴿Those to whom We gave the Book recognize him as they recognize their own sons﴾ [Al-Baqarah 146]. He did not say "their children" or "their daughters," because a person's knowledge of his son is stronger than his knowledge of his daughter, due to the intensity of his attachment to him; he does not ignore anything about him. So they recognize the Messenger ﷺ as they recognize their sons, because his description is present with them in the Torah and the Gospel. But they disbelieved in the signs of Allah: ﴿When there came to them what they recognized, they disbelieved in it﴾ [Al-Baqarah 89]. So "the signs of Allah" includes the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur'an. They disbelieved in all three.

﴿While you bear witness⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠: He did not say "while you know," because witnessing is stronger, since witnessing requires that the knower be like one who sees the thing with his senses, and seeing with the senses is stronger than seeing with the mind or knowing with the mind. They witness the signs and know them, and yet they disbelieve in these signs.

﴿O People of the Book, why do you mix the truth with falsehood﴾ [Al 'Imran 71]: they, in their disbelief, are deceivers, mixing truth with falsehood. The meaning of mixing truth with falsehood is blending truth with falsehood. They bring falsehood and disguise it as truth. The reason is that if they had brought falsehood openly, it would not have been accepted, would it not?

* Students: Yes.

* The Shaykh: But they bring it mixed with some truth, in order to disguise it for those who do not know the realities. This is part of the deception and cunning of every falsifier who disguises truth with falsehood.

Among this is that a person brings a general expression that may bear both truth and falsehood, but he intends falsehood by it, while the one who hears it may take it to mean the truth. This too is mixing truth with falsehood, and it will come, Allah willing, in the benefits.

He said: ﴿Why do you mix the truth with falsehood and conceal the truth﴾. "Conceal the truth": you hide it. Here someone may say: how does He say ﴿you mix the truth with falsehood and conceal the truth﴾? Is there not a contradiction in this? The answer: no, there is no contradiction, because they conceal the clear truth and bring it mixed and disguised with falsehood. Nor is their intention, when they bring the truth mixed with falsehood, the truth; their intention is—what? Falsehood. And this truth which they bring is like a garment that hides a defect beneath the clothes.

﴿And conceal the truth while you know﴾: know what? You know the truth, and you know your own state, that you are mixing truth with falsehood. They know both matters: they know the clear truth, and they know that they have mixed the truth with falsehood. This is especially true of the Jews, because the Jews disobeyed Allah while knowing that they were disobeying Him; they disobeyed Allah with insight.

* Among the benefits of these two verses: a rebuke of the People of the Book for their disbelief in the signs of Allah.

* Among the benefits of the first verse: this rebuke is directed at its proper target, since they disbelieved in the signs of Allah while they were witnessing them.

* Among the benefits of the verse: a clear ruling that admits of no interpretation, that the People of the Book who did not believe in Muhammad ﷺ are disbelievers. ﴿Why do you disbelieve in the signs of Allah﴾: one is not rebuked except for an actual matter. Disbelief in the signs of Allah is disbelief in Allah, and by this we know that even if they claim to believe in Allah, they are disbelievers in Him, clear and pure disbelievers.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: these disbelievers disbelieved with knowledge and witness, based on His saying: ﴿while you bear witness﴾.

In the second verse, among the benefits: these disbelievers from the People of the Book used to deceive and scheme, by what? By mixing truth with falsehood. How often do they disguise the noble Qur'an to support the falsehood of what they have adopted! Such as His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who believe, and those who are Jews, Christians, and Sabians, whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day and does righteous deeds, will have their reward with their Lord, and no fear will be upon them, nor will they grieve﴾ [Al-Baqarah 62]. So they say: ﴿those who believe﴾ are the Muslims; ﴿those who are Jews and Christians﴾ are the Jews and Christians; ﴿the Sabians﴾ are the Sabians. Whoever among them believes in Allah and the Last Day, they will have their reward with their Lord. So they put us and you in one row: the believer among us in Allah and the Last Day has the reward, and if we were opposed to you, we would have no reward. And they say that Jesus, son of Mary, gave glad tidings of a messenger who would come after him named Ahmad, and he has not yet come, since the one who came was named Muhammad. ﴿Muhammad is only a messenger; messengers have passed away before him﴾ [Al 'Imran 144]; ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those with him﴾ [Al-Fath 29]. So we are awaiting Ahmad. Thus they mix truth with falsehood and deceive. But whoever Allah has given knowledge and understanding will see clearly that they are mixing. And the scholars of the Muslims, praise be to Allah, have composed works explaining their falsehood and refuting their arguments, works that are like the sun in illumination and light, whose brightness hides every other brilliance. The first verse, for example: with what did Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, restrict the reward of these categories? ﴿whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day and does righteous deeds﴾ [Al-Baqarah 62]. So you, by the explicit text of this verse, ﴿Why do you disbelieve in the signs of Allah while you bear witness?﴾, are disbelievers. You were believers while the message of the Prophet was in force, the Prophet who was sent to you was in force. But now that it has been abrogated (nusikha), if you remain upon it, then you are disbelievers.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verses 69–74 (part 2 of 5):

As for His saying: ﴿And a messenger coming after me, whose name is Ahmad﴾ [al-Saff 6], there is no objection to one referent having several names. Ahmad has indeed come to you. This is why God, exalted is He, said in the same verse: ﴿But when he brought them the clear proofs, they said, "This is plain magic"﴾. So Ahmad has come to you, and we do not know of any prophet who came after 'Isa except Muhammad ﷺ. Accordingly, this deception should not be hidden from a person whom God has given knowledge and insight. Shaykh al-Islam (Ibn Taymiyyah), may God have mercy on him, wrote a book in two volumes titled *al-Jawab al-sahih li-man baddala din al-Masih* (The Correct Response to Those Who Altered the Religion of the Messiah). The refutations of the Christians by the leading scholars of the Muslims are numerous.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: one must be wary of the people of falsehood when they mix truth with falsehood, and we must not be deceived by them, for they come with ornate speech to delude. Among this is what happens with the innovators (*mubtadi'ah*) of this Ummah. When you hear their words, you say, "I would not exchange this for anything; this is the truth, and I will not go beyond it." But it is as was said:

*Arguments that crumble like glass; you think them true,*
*yet every one is a broken, shattered one.*

Their arguments are all fragile, having nothing to hold them upright, let alone to make them attack. They cannot defend themselves, let alone attack others. Yet they still deceive. Much of this has come up for us in the book of 'Aqidah, of their deception, their trickery, and their ornate speech. So a person must guard against those who mix truth with falsehood.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: rebuke, or the rebuke of whoever follows this course. The rebuke directed at the People of the Book is not restricted to particular individuals; it applies to the category, the kind, and the attribute. Anyone who is of their likeness deserves this rebuke.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the obligation to make the truth clear to one who knows it, or upon one who knows it. The obligation to make the truth clear falls on the one who knows it, because of His saying: ﴿while you conceal the truth though you know﴾. As for one who does not know, his excuse is evident. But whoever knows is obligated to make the truth clear. Furthermore, know that making the truth clear is obligatory when one is asked about it, either by the tongue of speech or by the tongue of circumstance. Asking by the tongue of speech is when a person comes to you and says, "What is the ruling on such-and-such?" Asking by the tongue of circumstance is when people fall into disobedience and need to be shown the truth. Do not say, "Since people have not come to me, I am not responsible." You are responsible. You must make it clear. Do not conceal it.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And a group of the People of the Book said, "Believe in what has been revealed to those who believe at the beginning of the day, and disbelieve at its end, that perhaps they may return."﴾ [Al 'Imran 72], to the end of the verse. When God mentioned their scheming with words, He mentioned their scheming with practical stratagems. The words were that they mix truth with what? With falsehood. The practical stratagems: this crafty trick, ﴿A group of the People of the Book said, "Believe in what has been revealed to those who believe at the beginning of the day, and disbelieve at its end"﴾. ﴿Believe in what has been revealed to those who believe﴾ means the Qur'an, or if you wish, the whole Shari'ah. ﴿At the beginning of the day﴾ means its first part. The evidence that "the beginning of the day" means its first part is His saying: ﴿and disbelieve at its end﴾. This is one of the methods by which the meanings of words in the noble Qur'an are known: a word's meaning is known by mentioning its counterpart, as in His saying: ﴿So go forth in separate groups or go forth all together﴾ [al-Nisa' 71]. If someone asked you, "What is the meaning of *thubat* (separate groups)?", we look at its counterpart: ﴿or go forth all together﴾. So *infiru thubat* means go forth separately, individually.

Here, if someone asks, "What tells us that 'the face of the day' is its beginning? Why isn't it its middle?", we say: His saying ﴿and disbelieve at its end﴾ shows this. ﴿That perhaps they may return﴾: the pronoun refers to the believers, ﴿they may return﴾ meaning return from their religion. Because you are People of the Book, if you believe at the beginning of the day and then turn back, people will say, "Had they not known their religion to be false, they would not have turned back." Look at the scheme! Enter with them at the beginning of the day, pray as they pray, attend their gatherings of remembrance, and if there is weeping, weep. Be entirely with them. Then at the end of the day, disbelieve; say, "We have disbelieved in this religion." For when you do this, people will say, "Had this religion not been false, these people would not have disbelieved after believing, for when a person believes in a religion and it is true, he remains steadfast and does not turn back." The evidence for this is: Heraclius asked Abu Sufyan when he met him in Syria about the companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ, asking, "Does anyone among them turn back from his religion after entering it?" He said, "No, no one turns back." He said, "Thus is faith when its delight has mingled with the hearts; it does not turn back."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4553) and Muslim (1773/74) from the hadith of Abu Sufyan.]] Or words to that effect. The point is that these people deceive others by their action, so people say, "Had they not known it to be false, they would not have turned away from it," for by nature a person does not turn back from what? From the religion of truth. ﴿That perhaps they may return.﴾

﴿And do not believe except in one who follows your religion﴾ [Al 'Imran 73]. This is part of the speech of the group; that is, "Believe, and do not believe." ﴿And do not believe except in one who follows your religion﴾ means: do not reveal what you are upon except to one who follows your religion, for if you showed the Muslims that you believed and then turned back in order to corrupt their religion, they would neither accept this from you nor turn back. But if you tell this scheme and deception to one who follows your religion, the matter is settled for you. It is as though they are saying: keep this method hidden except from one who follows your religion. To one who follows your religion, you may tell it; there is no objection. But do not tell others.

God, glorified and exalted is He, said: ﴿Say: "Indeed, guidance is the guidance of God"﴾. This is a parenthetical clause, but it is perfectly fitting in its place. Since the purpose of this deceitful act was to lead people astray from their religion, it is entirely appropriate that this scheme be nullified by making clear that guidance and success are in whose hand? In the hand of God. That is, say: this scheme and trickery will not benefit you, for guidance is the guidance of God. Even if you carry out this crafty, deceptive method, it will not harm the Muslims in the slightest, because guidance is the guidance of God. From this we learn that this parenthetical clause has great benefit in this context. Why? Because this scheme is a great deception that deceives, but whoever knows that guidance is in the hand of God, exalted is He, will not be concerned with this scheme and this deception.

Then He said: ﴿that anyone be given the like of what you were given﴾. His saying ﴿that anyone be given the like of what you were given﴾ has greatly puzzled the exegetes and the grammarians (*al-mu'rabin*, those who analyze i'rab, grammatical case). But let us look at the context of the noble verse: ﴿that anyone be given the like of what you were given﴾. The most apparent thing we can say about it is that it is connected to His saying ﴿and do not believe﴾. That is: and do not believe except in one who follows your religion, lest anyone be given the like of what you were given; that is, do not tell anyone that someone will be given the like of what we were given, for if you told people that they will be given the like of what we were given of the Book and virtues and other things, [they would not follow you]. For God gave the Children of Israel books; indeed He gave them the Torah, in which is guidance and light, and He gave them virtues: He shaded them with clouds, sent down upon them manna and quail, and destroyed their fierce enemy until they witnessed it, and so on.

He says: do not believe that anyone will be given the like of what you were given, except to one who follows your religion, for if you told people that this Islamic Ummah would be given the like of the virtues and laws we were given, that would be an incitement to them to hold fast to their religion.

It is also said that the meaning is: ﴿and do not believe except in one who follows your religion﴾, that is, do not tell anyone about this scheme and deception, that you believe at the beginning of the day and disbelieve at its end, so that the Muslims may turn back from their religion. ﴿And do not believe except in one who follows your religion﴾ means: do not tell anyone except one who follows your religion that someone is given the like of what you were given of this scheme and this deception.

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿or that they may argue with you before your Lord﴾. That is, also do not believe that they will argue with you before God, for if you believed that on the Day of Resurrection these people would argue against you before God, none of you would accept this stratagem. So the verse becomes: ﴿that anyone be given the like of what you were given, or that they may argue with you before your Lord﴾, connected to what? To His saying ﴿and do not believe﴾, that is, do not believe anyone; rather, conceal it from him. ﴿that anyone be given the like of what you were given, or that they may argue with you before your Lord﴾.

Why did they say: do not believe except in one who follows your religion? Because one who follows their religion knows that God will make Muhammad ﷺ prevail, and he will have Shari'ah and virtues equal to or greater than theirs. They also believe that they will argue with them before God, as He said: ﴿Then, on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord, you will dispute with one another﴾ [al-Zumar 31], and He said: ﴿Indeed, those who believe, and those who are Jews, and the Sabians, and the Christians, and the Magians, and those who associate others with God—God will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection﴾ [al-Hajj 17]. So you do not tell people this except one who follows your religion. Thus they believe that the Muslims will argue against them before God on the Day of Resurrection.

God said: ﴿Say: "Indeed, bounty is in the hand of God; He gives it to whom He wills, and God is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing"﴾. So as for those who said: do not believe that anyone will be given the like of what you were given, God said: ﴿Say: "Indeed, bounty is in the hand of God"﴾. Even if you try to hide the bounties God bestows upon this Ummah, that will not prevent what has happened, for bounty is in the hand of God; He gives it to whom He wills. God has given this Ummah, praise be to Him, virtues far exceeding those given to the Children of Israel.

﴿And God is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing﴾: all-encompassing in all His attributes, vast in knowledge, vast in mercy, vast in wisdom, vast in power, in all attributes; all-knowing of who deserves bounty, exalted is He. He gives His bounty to whom He wills, with knowledge and wisdom.

﴿He singles out for His mercy whom He wills﴾ [Al 'Imran 74]. *Yakhtassu* means He specifies for mercy whom He wills. Yet He, mighty and majestic, singles out for His mercy the one who is worthy of mercy, as He said: ﴿God knows best where to place His message﴾ [al-An'am 124]. We have already learned the principle that every act of God that is linked to His will (*mashi'ah*) follows His wisdom, and we cited for this His saying: ﴿And you do not will except that God wills; indeed God is ever All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾ [al-Insan 30]. So He, glorified and exalted is He, is All-Knowing and All-Wise; He gives His bounty to whom He wills among those who deserve it.

﴿He singles out for His mercy whom He wills, and God is the Possessor of Immense Bounty﴾. *Dhu al-fadl* means the possessor of great bounty, that is, abundant and vast. There is no bounty greater than the bounty of God, mighty and majestic. Look at what God has bestowed upon His servants from the beginning of the world to its end, and none of that has diminished what is with God in the slightest. God said in a sacred hadith (*hadith qudsi*): "If the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were to stand in one open plain and ask Me, and I gave each person what he asked, that would not diminish what is with Me any more than a needle diminishes the sea when it is dipped into it."[[Narrated by Muslim (2577/55) from the hadith of Abu Dharr.]] Dip a needle in the sea and then take it out: does the sea lose anything because of the drop the needle carried? Not at all, not in the slightest. Thus every bounty God, mighty and majestic, bestows, even if it were supposed to be outside His dominion, and it is not outside it, but is within it, nonetheless, were it supposed to be outside His dominion, it would not diminish God's dominion in the slightest, any more than a needle diminishes when dipped in the sea, and that does not diminish the needle either.

* * *

* Student: I seek refuge in God from the accursed Satan. ﴿Among the People of the Book is one who, if you entrust him with a heap of gold, will return it to you; and among them is one who, if you entrust him with a single dinar, will not return it to you unless you keep standing over him. That is because they say, "There is no blame upon us regarding the unlettered," and they speak falsehood against God while they know. Yes, whoever fulfils his covenant and fears God—indeed God loves those who fear Him. Indeed, those who sell the covenant of God and their oaths for a small price—those will have no share in the Hereafter, and God will not speak to them, nor look at them on the Day of Resurrection, nor purify them, and for them is a painful punishment﴾ [Al 'Imran 75–77].

* Shaykh: I seek refuge in God from the accursed Satan. God, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿A group of the People of the Book wished to lead you astray, but they lead astray none but themselves, and they do not perceive﴾.

In this verse, among the benefits: the explanation of the enmity of the People of the Book toward the believers, and that...

* Student: After: ﴿And a group of the People of the Book said, "Believe in what has been revealed to those who believe"﴾.

* Shaykh: What is written in your notes? What did you write last?

* Student: The explanation of the enmity of the People of the Book toward the Muslims, since they want to lead them astray.

Warning against the People of the Book, and that they try to turn the Muslims away from their religion.

Third: that the aggressor is repaid with the like of his aggression, because of His saying: ﴿but they lead astray none but themselves﴾.

Fourth: consolation to the Muslims regarding what these people intend for them of misguidance.

Fifth: that a person may be blind to falsehood even while practicing it, because of His saying: ﴿and they do not perceive﴾.

Sixth: the all-encompassing knowledge of God regarding what is in the hearts of creatures, because of His saying: ﴿wished﴾.

Seventh: that we refute every person who claims that the disbelievers want good for the Muslims.

* Shaykh: What is this benefit?

* Student: That we refute every person who claims that the disbelievers want good for the Muslims, by this verse.

* Shaykh: Yes, it must be by this verse.

* Student: Then we also mentioned: ﴿O People of the Book, why do you mix truth with falsehood?﴾, and we mentioned its benefits as well. We stopped at ﴿And a group said﴾.

* Shaykh: God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And a group of the People of the Book said, "Believe in what has been revealed to those who believe at the beginning of the day, and disbelieve at its end, that perhaps they may return."﴾

In this verse: the explanation of the scheming of the disbelievers against the Muslims, through following various kinds of stratagems, for they said: ﴿Believe in what has been revealed to those who believe at the beginning of the day, and disbelieve at its end, that perhaps they may return.﴾

* Among its benefits also: that the People of the Book may include hypocrites, because of His saying: ﴿Believe in what has been revealed to those who believe at the beginning of the day, and disbelieve at its end﴾, for a truly believing person must have faith firmly settled in his heart, and he does not disbelieve and turn back.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the believer may be deceived by such a trick, when his enemy pretends to agree with him and then disavows him in the end, because of His saying: ﴿Believe in what has been revealed to those who believe at the beginning of the day, and disbelieve at its end, that perhaps they may return﴾. They want the Muslims to turn back from their religion because these people turned back. What has been said in its interpretation already makes this entirely clear.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the zealotry of the People of the Book for their religion despite their misguidance, because of His saying: ﴿And do not believe except in one who follows your religion﴾.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verses 69–74 (part 3 of 5):

* Among its benefits also: the Muslim repels the schemes of these people by declaring that guidance is the guidance of Allah. However much they try to turn us away from our religion, if Allah has willed our guidance, that will not harm us. From this benefit follows that the servant should rely on his Lord in seeking guidance and not rely on himself, for whoever relies on himself is forsaken, however much intelligence and cunning he has.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: those who devised this deception revealed and made clear that what moved them to it was envy, as shown by their saying: ﴿that anyone should be given the like of what you were given﴾. The Jews are among the most distinguished of people for envy: ﴿Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty?﴾ [An-Nisa 54]. ﴿Many of the People of the Scripture wish they could turn you back to disbelief after your belief, out of envy from themselves﴾ [Al-Baqarah 109].
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the People of the Scripture believe in the Resurrection and the Reckoning, as shown by His saying: ﴿or they might argue with you before your Lord﴾. For this reason, the three religions, Judaism, Christianity and the religion of Islam, agree on belief in the Resurrection. But not everyone who believes in the Resurrection works for it. The Jews and Christians, as long as they remain in their disbelief in Muhammad (ﷺ), have not worked for this Resurrection, for if they had worked for it, they would have believed in the Messenger (ﷺ).
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: affirming that giving is the giving of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and that when Allah bestows a bounty on anyone, no one can prevent it, as shown by His saying: ﴿Say: Indeed, bounty is in the hand of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills﴾.
* Among its benefits: affirming that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has a hand, as shown by His saying: ﴿in the hand of Allah﴾. This hand is a real hand with which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, grasps, seizes and takes, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They did not appraise Allah with His true appraisal, while the earth entirely will be His handful on the Day of Resurrection﴾ [Az-Zumar 67]. The Prophet (ﷺ) also informed: «Indeed Allah, the Exalted, extends His hand at night so that the one who sinned during the day may repent, and He extends it during the day so that the one who sinned at night may repent»[[Recorded by Muslim (2759/31) from the hadith of Abu Musa.]].
He (ﷺ) also informed: «Indeed, when a person gives in charity the equivalent of a date (i.e., an amount equal to a date) from good earnings, and Allah accepts only the good, Allah takes it with His right hand and nurtures it as one of you nurtures his foal», and the hadith continues[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1410) and Muslim (1014/64) from the hadith of Abu Hurairah.]]. Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah (the people of the Sunnah and the community) believe that this is true in its literal sense, because Allah the Exalted informed of it concerning Himself, and He knows Himself best and knows others best. He informed of it concerning Himself in eloquent, clear speech that admits no doubt.
Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And who is more truthful in statement than Allah?﴾ [An-Nisa 87], and He informed of it concerning Himself with a report that is the most truthful of reports, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And who is more truthful in statement than Allah?﴾ [An-Nisa 122]. So Allah's report is the most truthful of reports. He informed of it concerning Himself so that people may be guided by it, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿By it Allah guides those who pursue His approval to the ways of peace﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 16], and He said: ﴿Allah makes clear to you so that you do not go astray﴾ [An-Nisa 176], and He said: ﴿Allah wants to make clear to you and guide you to the ways of those before you﴾ [An-Nisa 26]. So these are four attributes that characterize Allah's report concerning Himself. What is the first attribute?
* Student: First: that it is most truthful.
* Shaykh: The first attribute?
* Student: The first attribute is that it is the best speech.
* Shaykh: The first attribute?
* Student: Truthful.
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: "Allah wants."
* Shaykh: No, the first attribute of His speech.
* Student: "And who is better than Allah in speech?"
* Shaykh: No, we want the first attribute. Shall I arrange them?
* Student: Knowledge.
* Shaykh: That it is a report issuing from knowledge, right? Indeed Allah knows Himself and others. That is one. The second attribute?
* Student: "And who is better than Allah in speech?"
* Shaykh: How "who is better than Allah"? What does it look like?
* Student: That the speech of Allah is the best speech.
* Shaykh: Good, that the speech of Allah is the best speech, meaning in eloquence, clarity and explicitness. The third?
* Student: That the report that issues from Allah is the most truthful.
* Shaykh: Good, that Allah's report concerning Himself is the most truthful report. The fourth?
* Student: That He wants to clarify for Himself. Allah wants to make clear to you.
* Shaykh: Good, that Allah the Exalted, by what He reports concerning Himself, wants people to be guided by it so that they do not go astray. When these four attributes are combined in a speech, no trace of doubt remains in it, and it is impossible to say that it is among the ambiguous (mutashabih) texts. This is contrary to those who claim that the verses about the attributes are ambiguous, and so they say that they are ambiguous, and that if we are to recite such verses we should pass them over without considering their meaning. This, as we have often noted, is an error. Rather, we recite the verses about the attributes, we consider their meaning, and we ask about their meaning, but we do not ask about their modality (kayfiyyah). That is, we ask: What is the meaning of "istawa"? We ask, since there is no obstacle to it: What is the meaning of "He istawa upon the Throne"? But how He istawa, we do not say, nor do we ask. Here, the hand of Allah: we ask, what is this hand? Is it sensory or figurative? The answer is that it is sensory, with which He, the Mighty and Majestic, takes and grasps. But we do not ask about its modality. We do not say: How is this hand? Is the palm of the Most Merciful, the Mighty and Majestic, like the palm of a human or not? We do not say this.
If someone says: It has come in the hadith from the Prophet (ﷺ): «Indeed Allah created Adam in His image»[[Recorded by Muslim (2612/115) from the hadith of Abu Hurairah.]], and in another narration: «in the image of the Most Merciful»[[Recorded by at-Tabarani in al-Kabir (13580) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Umar.]]. This would require that the attributes of Allah be like the attributes of the created. So His face is like the face of the created, His hand like the hand of the created, His eye like the eye of the created, His leg like the leg of the created, and His foot like the foot of the created. What is the answer?
The answer to that is: this cannot be the intended meaning of the hadith, for if it were, it would contradict His saying: ﴿There is nothing like Him﴾ [Ash-Shura 11]. The report of Allah and His Messenger does not contradict itself; rather, part of it confirms the other part. If that is so, what is the meaning of the hadith? The answer is that we say: It does not follow from Adam's being in the image of Allah that he resembles Him. Something may be in the image of another in general, not in detail. This is supported by the fact that the Prophet (ﷺ) informed that «the first group to enter Paradise will be in the image of the moon on the night of the full moon»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3246) and Muslim (2834/14) from the hadith of Abu Hurairah.]]. Does it follow that they will be like the moon? Never. Rather, in general they will be in the image of the moon. Otherwise, the moon has no nose, no eyes, and no mouth, while the people of Paradise have noses, eyes and mouths. But it is in general. This is a very strong answer, and it leaves the text on its apparent meaning.
The second answer: We say that Allah created Adam in the image of the Most Merciful, that is, in the form He chose, in His image, in the form He chose. It is like when you say: This door is the work of so-and-so, meaning he is the one who made it. So Allah is the One who fashioned Adam, and attributing Adam's form to Allah indicates honour. For this reason, this statement came in some hadiths as a reason for the prohibition of striking the face and disparaging the face, because Adam was created in the image of the Most Merciful. If you strike the face that Allah created and chose this form for, that blow may harm and alter it. And if you disparage the face, saying: How ugly this face is! This too is a disparagement of the form that Allah created and chose for this face.
Accordingly, the attribution of "image" to Allah is an attribution of the created to its Creator, like His saying: "the she-camel of Allah," "the house of Allah," "the mosques of Allah," "the houses of Allah," and the like. Then the texts remain, praise be to Allah, sound, not contradicting or conflicting. The hand is affirmed for Allah in the manner befitting Him, without likeness. We are certain and know with certainty that there is no likeness between the attributes of the Creator and the attributes of the created.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: a person should hang his hope on Allah, with fear and with desire, as shown by His saying: ﴿Say: Indeed, bounty is in the hand of Allah﴾. When you know that bounty is in the hand of Allah, from whom do you seek bounty? From Allah. And when you know that bounty is in the hand of Allah, of whom are you afraid that he will withhold bounty from you? Allah. Therefore, the believer should attach his heart to Allah, the Exalted, in hope and in fear, and indeed it is obligatory upon him.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: affirming that voluntary actions subsist in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. What does this statement mean? What is the meaning of this? The meaning is that Allah the Exalted is described by attributes of actions related to His will, as shown by His saying: ﴿He gives it to whom He wills﴾. Giving is an action connected to His will. So we affirm that Allah the Exalted has actions that He performs and brings into being, which are connected to His will. This is a refutation of the Mu'attilah (those who deny divine attributes), who said that Allah the Exalted is not described by voluntary actions, since for them there is no attribute of Allah connected to His will. All attributes are eternal, and there are no attributes that come into being by the will of Allah. This verse refutes them. Why do they say that Allah does not act? They say that Allah does not istawa over the Throne in an active sense, does not descend to the lowest heaven, and does not come to judge among His servants. Why? They said: Because events subsist only in an event, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is not an event. Allah is eternal and everlasting, glorified and exalted. So if you affirm for Him voluntary actions connected to His will, you affirm that an event subsists in Him, and an event subsists only in an event. What is the answer to this?
The answer: This proposition, or this ruling, is a rational ruling that contradicts the text, because it entails rejecting every text that indicates that voluntary actions subsist in Allah. Whatever entails rejecting texts is false, because whatever entails rejecting the truth is false.
Second, we say: This proposition or principle you have mentioned is a false principle. Actions come after the agent, and it does not follow that they must be as eternal as he is, nor that he must be as originated as they are. For this reason, we eat today, and we ate yesterday and the day before. Does it follow, if we ate today, that we only came into existence today?
* Students: No, it does not follow.
* Shaykh: That is, our existence precedes our actions. Likewise, the voluntary actions of Allah: the existence of Allah precedes them. It does not follow that if we affirm originated actions, we have affirmed that the agent himself is originated. So this rational implication is false in itself, and it is also false because it conflicts with what? With the texts.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: affirming the will of Allah, as shown by His saying: ﴿whom He wills﴾. No one denies that Allah has will concerning His acts, that they follow His will and occur only by His will. But the community differed about whether the acts of the servant occur by the will of Allah or not. Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah said: They occur by the will of Allah, while affirming the servant's own will. Are you with us?
* Students: Yes.
* Shaykh: The act of the servant occurs by the will of Allah, with the affirmation of the servant's will for it. But the Qadariyyah, the Magians of this community, held that the act of the servant does not occur by the will of Allah, and that the servant is free to do what he wills, and there is no connection between the will and volition of Allah and his act. For this reason they were called the Magians of this community, because they believed that the servant is independent in what he brings about. So they made two creators for events: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, regarding His own act, and the human regarding his own act as well. Allah is the creator of His acts and the human is the creator of his acts. Allah wills His acts and the human wills his acts, and the will of Allah has no connection to the act of the servant.
Another group opposed them, saying: The acts of the servant occur by the will of Allah, and the servant has no will in them. Do you understand? These are the Jabriyyah. They said: The acts of the servant occur by the will of Allah, and the servant has no will in them at all. If he stands, he is compelled; if he sits, he is compelled; if he descends from the roof by the stairs, he is compelled; if he rolls down against his will, he is compelled; if he dies, he is compelled; if he drinks, he is compelled. It is all compulsion, with no choice. These people also contradicted reason, transmitted evidence and sensory experience. If one of them stood before us and said: The human is compelled in his act, and one of us stood up and slapped him and said: By Allah, this was forced upon me, I am compelled to slap you. What would he say? He would not accept it. If he said: No, why are you attacking me? We would say: Now you have invalidated your own principle.
For this reason it is reported that Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) was brought a thief, and he ordered that his hand be cut off. He said: Cut off his hand, "And as for the thief, male or female, cut off their hands" [Al-Ma'idah 38]. The man said: Gently, O Commander of the Faithful. By Allah, I only stole by the decree of Allah, meaning it was forced upon me. Umar said: And we only cut off your hand by the decree of Allah. So he refuted him with his own argument. The Commander of the Faithful cuts off the hand of the thief by the decree of Allah and the legislation of Allah, while the thief steals by what? By the decree of Allah, not by the legislation of Allah, since Allah forbids him from stealing. In short, affirming the will of Allah in the verses is abundant, and it encompasses His act and the acts of created beings.
Here we say: Is the will of Allah absolute? That is, does He will what wisdom requires and not will what wisdom does not require, or is it restricted by wisdom?
The answer: It is restricted by wisdom. Whenever a verse affirming will comes to you, it is restricted by wisdom. The evidence for this is His saying: ﴿And you do not will except that Allah wills. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾ [Al-Insan 30]. His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾ indicates that the will of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is accompanied by knowledge and wisdom, and so it is. He, glorified and exalted, does not will anything except for a wisdom. But the wisdom may be made clear to us, or it may be hidden from us, because our minds are limited. We may think, for example, that the rain falling at this time is harmful, when it is not harmful. We may think that withholding rain from us is harmful, when it is not harmful. So we believe that nothing that Allah, glorified and exalted, causes to take place happens except for a wisdom, but the wisdom may be hidden from us and may be manifest to us.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: affirming two of the names of Allah: Wasi' (All-Encompassing) and 'Alim (All-Knowing). Wasi' in what sense? In all of His attributes. All His attributes, glorified and exalted, are encompassing. His mercy encompasses all things, His knowledge encompasses all things, His dominion includes all things, and His power is over all things. He is All-Encompassing in every sense of the word. Allah said: ﴿Wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah. Indeed, Allah is All-Encompassing and All-Knowing﴾ [Al-Baqarah 115]. Wherever you turn your face toward, Allah is in front of you. When you are praying, Allah, the Exalted, is conversing with you and He is in front of you, as the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «When one of you stands to pray, indeed Allah is in front of his face»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (406) and Muslim (547/50) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Umar.]]. Any person: those who face east are like those who are west of Makkah, those who face west are like those who are east of Makkah, those who face south are like those who are north of it, and those who face north are like those who are south of it. All of them, wherever they turn, the Face of Allah is there, because Allah is All-Encompassing and All-Knowing. But do not think that Allah, glorified and exalted, is on the earth in front of your face while you pray. Rather, He is in front of your face while He is in the heaven, because Allah is not like anything in all His attributes. If a created being, while being created, can be in the sky and in front of your face, how much more so the Creator? If you face the sun at its rising, where would it be? In front of your face, and where is it? In the sky. Likewise at sunset, it is in front of your face while it is in the sky. In sum, Allah the Exalted is All-Encompassing in all His attributes and in everything this word carries of meaning.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verses 69–74 (part 4 of 5):

* Among the benefits of the verse is the affirmation of God's knowledge in His saying: ﴿All-Knowing﴾ (ʿAlīm). The knowledge of God in His saying ﴿All-Knowing﴾. So what is knowledge (ʿilm)? Knowledge is the perception of a thing as it actually is. Whoever does not perceive a thing is not knowledgeable, and whoever perceives it contrary to how it actually is also is not knowledgeable. The first is simple ignorance (al-jahl al-basīt), and the second is compound ignorance (al-jahl al-murakkab). If someone asked us, "When was the Conquest (ghazwat al-fath)?" and it was said to him, "It was in the third year of the Hijrah," then the speaker is in compound ignorance. But if someone asked us, "When was the Conquest?" and it was said to him, "God knows best," then the speaker is ignorant, but his ignorance is simple. Which of them is greater blindness? The first is greater blindness, because he is ignorant and does not know that he is ignorant. For this reason it is said that compound ignorance is more ugly than simple ignorance. A scholar who does not benefit from his knowledge is more sinful than the ignorant person, because the scholar who does not benefit from his knowledge has knowledge, but, God forbid, he does not act upon it.
If someone asked us, "When was the Conquest?" and it was said to him, "In the eighth year, in Ramadan," then he would be knowledgeable. Therefore God, exalted is He, is All-Knowing, perceiving things as they actually are, and His knowledge, glorified and exalted is He, is complete in every respect, eternally and everlastingly. He has always been knowing, knowing what will be. And when He knows, and He is knowing, mighty and majestic, He does not forget, as Moses, peace be upon him, said: ﴿My Lord neither errs nor forgets﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:52].

Is God described as ʿārif (one who has ma'rifah)?
* Students: No.
* The Shaykh: The scholars said: God is not described as ʿārif. Why? Because ma'rifah is discovery after obscurity, discovery after concealment. Let me put it better for you: ma'rifah is discovery after concealment. This is why, when you teach a child, you say to him, "Did you understand (ʿarafta)?" and he says, "What?" Yes, meaning that after it was hidden from him, it has now become known to him. Because it is discovery after concealment, it is not valid to apply it to God, since God has always been and still is All-Knowing.
Second: ma'rifah is applied to both knowledge and conjecture. This is why, when we say, "Knowledge is the recognition of the truth by its proof," this definition includes conjecture, since knowable things are either certain or conjectural. For this reason it is not valid to describe God as ʿārif.
If someone says: How do you say this when it is authentically reported from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Get to know God in ease, and He will know you in hardship" [Ahmad, al-Musnad (2803), from Ibn ʿAbbās]. "He will know you" — and this is an action? The answer to this is that this is a special ma'rifah that entails care: care for the one who got to know God beforehand. The proof that it is not the ma'rifah of knowledge, but the ma'rifah of care, is that he said "get to know God," although God knows you whether you worship Him or not. He knows you, mighty and majestic is He, He knows you whether you worship Him or not. But when you worship Him, you have become acquainted with Him, and when you become acquainted with Him in ease, He knows you in hardship.
Then God, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿He singles out for His mercy whomever He wills, and God is the Possessor of great bounty﴾.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: God, mighty and majestic, may show a special mercy to some servants, as indicated by His saying: ﴿He singles out for His mercy whomever He wills﴾. God clarifies in other verses that He shows mercy to whoever deserves it, that is, whoever exposes himself to the causes of mercy, such as His saying: ﴿By it God guides whoever follows His pleasure to the ways of peace﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 5:16]. And whoever is the opposite has not done what calls for mercy, and so he is not deserving of it. God said: ﴿My mercy encompasses all things, so I will decree it for those who fear Me﴾ [Al-A'raf 7:156]. For whom? ﴿For those who fear (Me)﴾. And He, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿So when they deviated, God caused their hearts to deviate, and God does not guide the defiant people﴾ [As-Saff 61:5].
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: there is no objection against God in His singling out Zayd with His mercy and withholding His mercy from ʿAmr, because the matter is His. It is bounty: if He wills, He withholds it, and if He wills, He gives it.
* Following from this benefit: those who were deprived of God's bounty have not been wronged in any way, because God gives His bounty to whom He wills and singles out with His mercy whom He wills. (...) If there were ten men before you, and you gave one of them ten, another nine, another eight, another seven, another six, another five, another four, another three, another two, and another one, would you have wronged the one to whom you gave only one dirham? No, you did not wrong him, because this is your bounty. It cannot be said that you wronged the one to whom you gave one dirham, because you gave the first ten dirhams.
But if you hired ten laborers for ten dirhams each day, and they all did the work, and you gave one of them ten dirhams because he worked a full day, and the second, who had also worked a full day, you gave nine, the third eight, and so on decreasing, you would be considered unjust, because it is not justice for everyone to do what you hired them for and then give some of them and deprive others. The difference between this and the previous example is that the first is bounty and kindness, pure bounty and kindness, while this second case is justice, and justice requires that every person be given his due right.
﴿He singles out for His mercy whomever He wills, and God is the Possessor of great bounty﴾.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: it is permissible to describe other than God as ʿazīm (great), from His saying: ﴿the Possessor of great bounty﴾. Because "bounty" here may mean God's bounty, that is, His giving, or it may mean the thing bestowed, which is what? The thing given. On the second meaning there is no difficulty in deriving the benefit we mentioned, that greatness may be attributed to other than God. On the first meaning, if we say that bounty is the very act of God, then describing it as great is not problematic, why? Because it is one of God's attributes.
The Shaykh: ﴿He singles out for His mercy whomever He wills, and God is the Possessor of great bounty﴾ [Ali ʿImran 3:74].
* Among the benefits of these noble verses: it is permissible to describe other than God as great, from His saying: ﴿the Possessor of great bounty﴾, because "bounty" here may refer to God's bounty, that is, His giving, or it may refer to the thing bestowed, which is the bestowed thing itself. On the second meaning, there is no difficulty in deriving the benefit we mentioned: that greatness may be attributed to other than God. On the first meaning: if we say that bounty is the very act of God, then describing it as great is not problematic, why? Because it is one of God's attributes, and God's attributes, like His essence, are great. If someone says: As long as both possibilities remain, there is no proof that greatness may be attributed to anyone other than God, since we say that bounty here may be God's attribute, and God's attributes are great like His essence.
The answer to this is: If you are not convinced by this, then read God's saying: ﴿And she has a great throne﴾ [An-Naml 27:23]. Here the throne is described as great, even though her throne is created. So it is valid for us to say, "This act is great," "This man is great," "This car is great," "This house is great," and similar things, and there is no harm in it, just as it is valid to say, "So-and-so is mighty," "So-and-so is strong." Is that acceptable?
* Students: Yes...
* The Shaykh: Yes, so-and-so is strong, and there is no blame in that. But we must know that what we describe created things with, of the attributes of God, does not resemble God's attributes, nor even approach them, because the attribute of each described thing suits it.
* A student: Is there any comparison here between the hypocrites among the Muslims and the People of the Book?
* The Shaykh: How?
* A student: Is there a comparison in action between the Muslims and the hypocrites of the People of the Book?
* The Shaykh: Muslims and hypocrites.
* The student: The hypocrites... Can the hypocrites of the time of the Prophet (ﷺ) be compared with the hypocrites of the People of the Book?
* The Shaykh: No. The verses that have passed us, they are hypocrites not all the time. They are hypocrites by deception at the beginning of the day and disbelieve at its end.
* A student: O Shaykh, the hadith "He will know you in hardship," is it "He will know you in hardship"?
* The Shaykh: What?
* The student: The hadith "He will know you in hardship": "Get to know God in ease, and He will know you in hardship" [Ahmad (2803); ʿAbd ibn Humayd (635); al-Hakim, al-Mustadrak (6436, 6437), from Ibn ʿAbbās].
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* A student: Does the attribute of ʿirfān (knowing/recognizing) mean we establish it for God as an active attribute?
* The Shaykh: What?
* A student: Do we affirm that God is ʿārif as an active attribute?
* The Shaykh: Yes. If we say the meaning is care, not scholarly knowledge, because God has always been knowing, from before hardship exists in Him. But if we say the ma'rifah whose requirement is care is of this type, then yes.
* A student: So is it valid to say that the one who does not benefit from his knowledge has a characteristic of the Jews, because they had knowledge?
* The Shaykh: How? Yes, there is no doubt.
* A student: A two-part question. Regarding God, some people describe Him, they say: God is eternal (qadīm)?
* The Shaykh: Yes?
* The student: Some people among the sects describe Him, they say: God is eternal, or everlasting, or such. Where did these terms come from?
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* The student: Which sects said this?
* The Shaykh: These came from the theologians (mutakallimūn), without doubt. They were not known in the time of the Messenger (ﷺ) or the Companions, although it was reported: "I seek refuge in God the Mighty, in His noble face, and in His eternal authority" [Abu Dawud (466), from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs], as a description of the authority, not of God. But their meaning according to what they intend is correct, because according to them, the eternal (al-qadīm) is the one who has no beginning, that is, the one who has always existed and still exists. They do not mean "eternal" in its linguistic sense, because in language qadīm applies to a thing that is originated and preceded something else, as in His saying: ﴿until it became like the old, withered palm stalk﴾ [Ya-Sin 36:39]. We have already learned that what is said about God is either something God has told about Himself, or something God has not told about Himself but does not contradict His perfection, or something God has not told about Himself and which contradicts His perfection. The first is clearly permissible, the third is clearly impermissible, and the second is permissible. So it is permissible to inform about God what does not contradict His perfection, but it is not permissible to inform about God what contradicts His perfection. Some scholars even say: It is not permissible for you to go into detail about God's creation by saying, for example, that God created donkeys, dogs, filth, and stench, and similar things, because this involves some kind of disrespect. Rather, say: He created everything. Then, if someone denied it and said, "God did not create donkeys," say: No, He did create donkeys, in response to the denial.
In any case, whatever is stated as a report about God is either something God has reported about Himself, in which case its status is clear, or something God has not reported but which contradicts His perfection, in which case its status is also clear. The first is clearly permissible, and the second is clearly impermissible. Or it may be something God has not reported about Himself but which does not contradict His perfection, and this is not objectionable. For this reason we say: God is Willing (murīd), Speaking (mutakallim), Creator (ṣāniʿ), even though these derivative names were not reported as names of God, and God did not report them about Himself in this wording.
* A student: O Shaykh, Jahm ibn Safwan, when he passed with a group of students, went with them to the places of those afflicted with diseases, and said to them: "Look, is this God's mercy, that people are afflicted this way?"
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* The student: How do we respond to this statement?
* The Shaykh: We respond that this is from God's mercy.
* The student: That they are afflicted with this...
* The Shaykh: Yes, that they are afflicted. ﴿So that He may let them taste part of what they have done﴾ [Ar-Rum 30:41], what? ﴿So that they may return﴾. If they do not benefit, others benefit, because you do not know the value of God's blessing upon you except when you are afflicted with its opposite, or you see someone afflicted with its opposite. Let us review. Come on, let us hear, may God reward you with good. His saying: ﴿The disciples said﴾ [Ali ʿImran 3:52]. What is the meaning of al-Hawariyyun (the disciples)?
* A student: Al-hawar is derived from al-hawar, and al-hawar is whiteness.
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* The student: And their hearts were free from...
* The Shaykh: Pure and clean.
* The student: From disbelief and polytheism.
* The Shaykh: Well said. So they were called disciples (al-Hawariyyun) because of the purity of their hearts.
* The student: Because of the purity of their hearts.
* The Shaykh: Because of the purity of their hearts. Good, well said. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they schemed, and God schemed﴾ [Ali ʿImran 3:54]. How is God described as scheming?
* The student: Because when scheming is in response to an adversary, it is described of God, blessed and exalted is He, and it is a perfection. When it is not in response to another, it is a deficiency. That is, God is only described as scheming in response to an adversary.
* The Shaykh: Well said. And then it would be?
* The student: It would be in response to the scheming of the polytheists...
* The Shaykh: It would be a perfection.
* The student: Yes...
* The Shaykh: A perfection, because it indicates that He is stronger than that one, than His enemy. His saying: ﴿Indeed, this is the true narrative﴾ and ﴿Indeed, this is the Mighty﴾, in them there are two readings.
* A student: (Lahuwa) with the ha vowelled and with it sukūn.
* The Shaykh: With the ha vowelled and with sukūn: ﴿lahuwa﴾ and ﴿lahwa﴾.

Good. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, the likeness of Jesus before God is like the likeness of Adam; He created him from dust﴾. The pronoun in ﴿created him﴾ (khalaqahu), the object, refers to what?
* A student: ﴿Indeed, the likeness of Jesus before God﴾.
* The Shaykh: ﴿like the likeness of Adam, He created him from dust﴾.
* A student: That is, Adam.
* The Shaykh: It refers to Adam. What is the purpose of this verse? To refute whom?
* A student: To refute those who said: Jesus is the son of God.
* The Shaykh: To refute the Christians who said: Jesus is the son of God, and they said: How could he come without a father? His father is God. Good. Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, the likeness of Jesus...﴾
* The student: ﴿before God﴾.
* The Shaykh: That is, his case is like the case of Adam; God created him from dust, ﴿then He said to him, "Be," and he was﴾.
Good. This verse is distinguished by something. What is the thing this verse is distinguished by: ﴿Say: O People of the Scripture, come to a word...﴾?
* A student: (...)
* The Shaykh: It has a specific distinction, a particular one, eh?
* The student: (...)
* The Shaykh: That the Prophet (ﷺ) used to recite it in the second rak'ah of the Sunnah...?
* The student: The Fajr prayer.
* The Shaykh: The Fajr prayer. And in the first rak'ah he recites?
* The student: ﴿Say: We believe in God﴾ [Al-Baqarah 2:136].
* The Shaykh: ﴿Say: We believe in God﴾, which is in Surat al-Baqarah.
Good. His saying: ﴿to a word that is equitable between us and you﴾. What does it mean?
* The student: ﴿Say: Come to a word...﴾
* The Shaykh: ﴿equitable between us and you﴾?
* The student: That is, it would be a separator...
* The Shaykh: ﴿equitable between us and you﴾.
* The student: That is, it would be a separator between us and you.
* The Shaykh: How?
* A student: It is the word of monotheism (kalimat al-tawhid).
* The Shaykh: What kind of separator is this?
* The student: That is, we and you would make it the judge between us...
* The Shaykh: Yes. But what is meant by ﴿equitable (sawāʾ)﴾?
* A student: Just.
* The Shaykh: Just. That is one meaning. What is the other meaning?
* A student: Level (mustawiyan).
* The Shaykh: Level.
* The student: It is from the active participle form.
* The Shaykh: Yes, meaning that it is complete, a complete word, because it includes justice.

Good. His saying: ﴿and that some of us should not take others as lords besides God﴾. How did some of them take others as lords besides God?
* A student: It means that some of them call on others (...).
* The Shaykh: They call on one another.
* A student: That is, some of them take others; that is, some worship others.
* The Shaykh: But is the hadith of ʿAdī ibn Hatim that they worship one another?
* The student: He said with an exception (...).
* The Shaykh: He said: "We do not worship them."
* The student: But he said: "We call upon them." He said: "That is their worship" [al-Tirmidhi (3095); al-Bayhaqi, al-Sunan (10/116); al-Tabarani, al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (218), (17/92), from ʿAdī ibn Hatim].
* The Shaykh: No, he did not say that they call upon them.
* A student: They follow them in forbidding what is lawful and permitting what is unlawful.
* The Shaykh: Yes, they follow them in permitting what is unlawful and forbidding what is lawful.

Ibn 'Uthaymin said: Alright, did you take this portion of the Qur'an? You?

* Student: Me?
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: I took some of it.
* Shaykh: Did you memorize its beginning or not? From where did you memorize it?
* Student: From these verses.
* Shaykh: From these verses. Come on, let us hear it. ﴿O People of the Scripture, why do you argue about Abraham...﴾ Recite it to us from memory.
* Student: I did not memorize it.
* Shaykh: What is the benefit then? Yes.
* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿O People of the Scripture, why do you argue about Abraham when the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed until after him? Then will you not reason? (65) Here you are—you argued about that of which you had knowledge; so why do you argue about that of which you have no knowledge? And Allah knows, while you know not.﴾ [Ali 'Imran 65–66].
* Shaykh: Well done. The words of Allah, ﴿Here you are﴾ (hā antum), have two readings.
* Student: With a damma on the mim...
* Shaykh: What?
* Student: "Hā antum-u"?
* Shaykh: No. Did you forget, or did you not memorize it?
* Student: I did not know.
* Shaykh: There are two readings.
* Student: ﴿hā antum﴾ and ﴿ha'antum﴾ with simplification (tashil).
* Shaykh: ﴿hā antum﴾ with the madd (prolongation), and ﴿ha'antum﴾ without the madd.

Alright. As for His words, ﴿why do you argue about Abraham﴾: what is meant by the interrogative here?

* Student: Denunciation (inkar).
* Shaykh: Denunciation. Meaning?
* Student: Meaning he denounces the disbelievers (...).
* Shaykh: Is there not another meaning?
* Student: Rebuke (tawbikh) and denunciation. What is meant by it is rebuke and denunciation.
* Shaykh: Rebuke.
* Student: And denunciation.
* Shaykh: And amazement (ta'ajjub). Huh. How is the verse? What is the meaning of the verse? What is the story?
* Student: The story is that they claimed they were upon the creed (millah) of Abraham, so Allah denounced them and was amazed at them. How can you say that you are upon the creed of Abraham?!
* Shaykh: Meaning they claimed that Abraham was upon the creed of the Torah, for example, and the creed of the Gospel.
* Student: Yes.
* Shaykh: Alright. And that they follow him. What is the basis of the denunciation against them?
* Student: Because the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed except after Abraham.
* Shaykh: Yes. So how could it be?
* Student: How could Abraham be upon their creed?!
* Shaykh: Upon the creed of something that was not revealed except after him, right? Alright, yes.
* Student: There is another meaning.
* Shaykh: Another meaning.
* Student: And it is that they are upon the creed of Abraham.
* Shaykh: That they are...
* Student: They claim that they are upon the creed of Abraham.
* Shaykh: Yes, and that they are the most entitled people to him. Alright. In His words, ﴿Then will you not reason?﴾, is there evidence for making reason the judge in legal matters (shar'i)?
* Student: What is meant by reason here is the reason of right guidance...
* Shaykh: That is, the reason of right guidance. Fine. But is there evidence in it for returning to the reason of right guidance for legal matters? Or here the rebuke is directed at their own act, namely their claim that Abraham followed the Torah, or that they are upon the creed of Abraham while they oppose him?
* Student: Rather, it is a denunciation of them.
* Shaykh: It is not about a legal matter. Is there a parallel? Did Allah denounce a people for setting aside their reason, opposing what reason requires? Yes. Who knows? ﴿Do you order the people to righteousness and forget yourselves while you recite the Scripture? Then will you not reason?﴾ [al-Baqarah 44]. Alright, come on.
* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was a hanif, a Muslim, and he was not of the polytheists. (67) Indeed, the most worthy of Abraham among people are those who followed him and this Prophet and those who believed. And Allah is the Ally of the believers. (68) A faction of the People of the Scripture wish they could mislead you, but they mislead none except themselves, and they perceive not.﴾ [Ali 'Imran 67–69].
* Shaykh: Well done. The words of Allah, ﴿Abraham was not a Jew﴾: this is a refutation of whom?
* Student: Whom do you mean?
* Shaykh: ﴿Abraham a Jew﴾.
* Student: Yes.
* Shaykh: A refutation of whom?
* Student: Of the Jews and Christians.
* Shaykh: All of the Jews and Christians?
* Student: Of the Christians.
* Shaykh: ﴿Abraham was not a Jew﴾, just this part. We read this as a refutation of whom?
* Student: Of the Jews.
* Shaykh: ﴿Nor a Christian﴾?
* Student: Of the Christians.
* Shaykh: A refutation of the Christians. Because each group among them claims that it is upon his creed and that he was upon their creed.

Alright. As for His words, ﴿Indeed, the most worthy of Abraham among people are those who followed him and this Prophet﴾: why did He begin with ﴿those who followed him﴾ before mentioning the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, when the Prophet is more honorable than them? Huh, come on?

* Student: Because following (ittiba') only comes first through affirming the Book of Allah, then the words of the Prophet ﷺ.
* Shaykh: No.
* Student: Because they are the first in creation.
* Shaykh: Huh.
* Student: Because they are the first in creation.
* Shaykh: Earlier in time.
* Student: Earlier in time than the Prophet.
* Shaykh: Because they are earlier in time. That is one. A second reason?
* Student: That Allah, Mighty and Majestic, honored the Messenger, so He said: ﴿and this﴾, joining him...
* Shaykh: Joining him?
* Student: He pointed...
* Shaykh: He placed him later. The problem is not the delay. But the brother wants to say: because those who followed him are earlier in time. Another thing?
* Student: Apparently, and Allah knows best, these Jews and Christians who claim that Abraham is of their creed, and they did not follow him and have nothing to do with him, Allah made clear to them that the most worthy of Abraham are those who followed him, and these did not follow him; they only claim to follow him by name.
* Shaykh: Yes, but the Messenger ﷺ is more honorable than those who followed him, so why did He put them first? Yes.
* Student: Because they followed him in his sharia (divine law) (...) the foundations of religion (usul al-din).
* Shaykh: What?
* Student: The sharia of the Messenger is Islam, but each prophet has his own specific sharia. He said: they followed him in his specific sharia (...).
* Shaykh: Yes, correct. Because those who followed him followed him completely. As for the Prophet ﷺ, he has a method (minhaj) that differs from the method of Abraham in matters related to the public interests: ﴿For each of you We have made a law and a method﴾ [al-Ma'idah 48]. Since those who followed him held to the foundations of his sharia, its branches, its details, and its major matters, He placed them first.

Alright. As for His words, ﴿lalladhina ittaba'uhu﴾ (la-lladhina ittaba'uhu): what is this lam, and what does it mean?

* Student: Causal (ta'lil).
* Shaykh: No. Not every lam is causal. Not every white thing is fat.
* Student: A particle of preposition (harf jarr).
* Shaykh: Nor is it a preposition. The preposition is a kasra-vowelled noun with a relative pronoun... Yes.
* Student: For emphasis (tawkid).
* Shaykh: The brother...
* Student: For emphasis.
* Shaykh: For emphasis: ﴿Indeed, the most worthy of Abraham among people are those who followed him﴾. Alright. As for His words, ﴿And Allah is the Ally of the believers﴾, and in some verses, ﴿Then they are returned to Allah, their true Master﴾ [al-An'am 62]. So He affirmed His wilayah (guardianship/lordship) over the disbelievers. What is the reconciliation?

* Student: Follow the Messenger ﷺ.
* Shaykh: But here Allah said, ﴿And Allah is the Ally of the believers﴾, and in some verses He affirmed His wilayah for non-believers.
* Student: Yes, because the wali (ally) of the believers is by following the Messengers.
* Shaykh: No.
* Student: What is meant is the specific wilayah, Shaykh.
* Shaykh: What is meant here is the specific wilayah. And Allah's wilayah over non-believers is what kind?
* Students: General.
* Shaykh: The general. Alright.
* Student: In the sense of love, Shaykh?
* Shaykh: Yes?
* Student: In the sense of love, the general wilayah?
* Shaykh: No, no. The general wilayah means conveyance (tabligh) and authority, the governing of affairs. Alright. Brother... read.
* Student: (...) the enemies of the Muslims.
* Shaykh: The warning...
* Student: Against allying with disbelievers.
* Shaykh: Yes. The warning against the Jews and Christians, because they want us to... to mislead us. Alright, how did He say, ﴿but they mislead none except themselves﴾? What is the aspect of their misleading none but themselves?
* Student: Because by this misleading they are themselves astray in origin, and by this misleading they increase in error, so they mislead themselves.
* Shaykh: Well done, exactly.

He said: ﴿of the verses and the Wise Reminder﴾.
Why was the Qur'an called a reminder (dhikr)? Huh, come on (...). Now, its arrow is with you.
