Who knows? ﴿Do you order the people to righteousness and forget yourselves while you recite the Scripture? Then will you not reason?﴾ [al-Baqarah 44]. Alright, come on.
* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was a hanif, a Muslim, and he was not of the polytheists. (67) Indeed, the most worthy of Abraham among people are those who followed him and this Prophet and those who believed. And Allah is the Ally of the believers. (68) A faction of the People of the Scripture wish they could mislead you, but they mislead none except themselves, and they perceive not.﴾ [Ali 'Imran 67–69].
* Shaykh: Well done. The words of Allah, ﴿Abraham was not a Jew﴾: this is a refutation of whom?
* Student: Whom do you mean?
* Shaykh: ﴿Abraham a Jew﴾.
* Student: Yes.
* Shaykh: A refutation of whom?
* Student: Of the Jews and Christians.
* Shaykh: All of the Jews and Christians?
* Student: Of the Christians.
* Shaykh: ﴿Abraham was not a Jew﴾, just this part. We read this as a refutation of whom?
* Student: Of the Jews.
* Shaykh: ﴿Nor a Christian﴾?
* Student: Of the Christians.
* Shaykh: A refutation of the Christians. Because each group among them claims that it is upon his creed and that he was upon their creed.

Alright. As for His words, ﴿Indeed, the most worthy of Abraham among people are those who followed him and this Prophet﴾: why did He begin with ﴿those who followed him﴾ before mentioning the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, when the Prophet is more honorable than them? Huh, come on?

* Student: Because following (ittiba') only comes first through affirming the Book of Allah, then the words of the Prophet ﷺ.
* Shaykh: No.
* Student: Because they are the first in creation.
* Shaykh: Huh.
* Student: Because they are the first in creation.
* Shaykh: Earlier in time.
* Student: Earlier in time than the Prophet.
* Shaykh: Because they are earlier in time. That is one. A second reason?
* Student: That Allah, Mighty and Majestic, honored the Messenger, so He said: ﴿and this﴾, joining him...
* Shaykh: Joining him?
* Student: He pointed...
* Shaykh: He placed him later. The problem is not the delay. But the brother wants to say: because those who followed him are earlier in time. Another thing?
* Student: Apparently, and Allah knows best, these Jews and Christians who claim that Abraham is of their creed, and they did not follow him and have nothing to do with him, Allah made clear to them that the most worthy of Abraham are those who followed him, and these did not follow him; they only claim to follow him by name.
* Shaykh: Yes, but the Messenger ﷺ is more honorable than those who followed him, so why did He put them first? Yes.
* Student: Because they followed him in his sharia (divine law) (...) the foundations of religion (usul al-din).
* Shaykh: What?
* Student: The sharia of the Messenger is Islam, but each prophet has his own specific sharia. He said: they followed him in his specific sharia (...).
* Shaykh: Yes, correct. Because those who followed him followed him completely. As for the Prophet ﷺ, he has a method (minhaj) that differs from the method of Abraham in matters related to the public interests: ﴿For each of you We have made a law and a method﴾ [al-Ma'idah 48]. Since those who followed him held to the foundations of his sharia, its branches, its details, and its major matters, He placed them first.

Alright. As for His words, ﴿lalladhina ittaba'uhu﴾ (la-lladhina ittaba'uhu): what is this lam, and what does it mean?

* Student: Causal (ta'lil).
* Shaykh: No. Not every lam is causal. Not every white thing is fat.
* Student: A particle of preposition (harf jarr).
* Shaykh: Nor is it a preposition. The preposition is a kasra-vowelled noun with a relative pronoun... Yes.
* Student: For emphasis (tawkid).
* Shaykh: The brother...
* Student: For emphasis.
* Shaykh: For emphasis: ﴿Indeed, the most worthy of Abraham among people are those who followed him﴾. Alright. As for His words, ﴿And Allah is the Ally of the believers﴾, and in some verses, ﴿Then they are returned to Allah, their true Master﴾ [al-An'am 62]. So He affirmed His wilayah (guardianship/lordship) over the disbelievers. What is the reconciliation?

* Student: Follow the Messenger ﷺ.
* Shaykh: But here Allah said, ﴿And Allah is the Ally of the believers﴾, and in some verses He affirmed His wilayah for non-believers.
* Student: Yes, because the wali (ally) of the believers is by following the Messengers.
* Shaykh: No.
* Student: What is meant is the specific wilayah, Shaykh.
* Shaykh: What is meant here is the specific wilayah. And Allah's wilayah over non-believers is what kind?
* Students: General.
* Shaykh: The general. Alright.
* Student: In the sense of love, Shaykh?
* Shaykh: Yes?
* Student: In the sense of love, the general wilayah?
* Shaykh: No, no. The general wilayah means conveyance (tabligh) and authority, the governing of affairs. Alright. Brother... read.
* Student: (...) the enemies of the Muslims.
* Shaykh: The warning...
* Student: Against allying with disbelievers.
* Shaykh: Yes. The warning against the Jews and Christians, because they want us to... to mislead us. Alright, how did He say, ﴿but they mislead none except themselves﴾? What is the aspect of their misleading none but themselves?
* Student: Because by this misleading they are themselves astray in origin, and by this misleading they increase in error, so they mislead themselves.
* Shaykh: Well done, exactly.

He said: ﴿of the verses and the Wise Reminder﴾.
Why was the Qur'an called a reminder (dhikr)? Huh, come on (...). Now, its arrow is with you.

* Student: It was called a reminder because in it is the remembrance of Allah. Also, dhikr is used for three meanings.
* Shaykh: For three groups?!
* Student: For three meanings.
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: ﴿And We raised high your remembrance﴾ [al-Sharh 4]. And ﴿remember your Lord standing and sitting﴾. This dhikr, the Qur'an, contains the remembrance of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. Also, dhikr is used for uttering (talaffuz), and also there are words in it.
* Shaykh: You have overwhelmed us, Shaykh. Yes.
* Student: ...
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: Because in it is the mention of those before us and those after us.
* Shaykh: What?
* Student: Because in it is the mention of those before us and the mention of those after us from the generations.
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: As the Prophet ﷺ said...
* Shaykh: Alright, and what else?
* Student: The hadith...
* Shaykh: Yes?
* Student: As the Prophet ﷺ said...
* Shaykh: Alright, come on!
* Student: I do not memorize it.
* Student: Because it is in the scriptures of the earlier ones.
* Shaykh: No.
* Student: Because one is reminded by it.
* Shaykh: Correct, because one is reminded by it. Alright.
* Student: Dhikr in the sense of honor. He, Exalted, says: ﴿And indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people﴾ [al-Zukhruf 44].
* Shaykh: Excellent!
* Student: And because He is remembered by it, Mighty and Majestic.
* Shaykh: Because it is a reminder...
* Student: For Allah, Mighty and Majestic...
* Shaykh: For whoever follows it. ﴿And indeed, it is a reminder for you﴾, meaning honor, ﴿and for your people﴾. Alright, come on... "the Wise" is a description of the Qur'an. Is it from ḥukm (judgment), because the Qur'an judges among people, or from iḥkam (firmness), because the Qur'an is muhkam?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: From both meanings together: the Qur'an is muhkam and ḥākim. Alright, is this description for the whole Qur'an?
* Student: Yes. Disagreement is reported in it (...). Yes, it is a description of the whole Qur'an.
* Shaykh: For the whole Qur'an.
* Student: Yes.
* Shaykh: Alright. Does not the saying of Allah, Exalted, present an objection to this: ﴿He is the one who has sent down to you the Book; in it are verses that are definitive, which are the foundation of the Book, and others unspecific﴾ [Ali 'Imran 7]? Why did Allah not make the whole Qur'an muhkam?
* Student: Because the mutashabihat (ambiguous verses) are with respect to Allah, glorified is He (...), and the mutashabihat with respect to the common people are not wise.
* Shaykh: So the ambiguity is relative?
* Student: Yes.
* Shaykh: Yes. Do you agree with this? And when the mutashabih is referred back to the muhkam, everything becomes muhkam. Go ahead.
* Student: ﴿And among them is one who, if you entrust him with a certain amount of gold, will not return it to you unless you continually stand over him. That is because they say, "There is no blame upon us concerning the unlettered." And they speak falsehood about Allah while they know. (75) Yes, whoever fulfills his covenant and fears Allah—indeed, Allah loves those who fear Him. (76) Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price—those will have no share in the Hereafter, and Allah will not speak to them or look at them on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them, and for them is a painful punishment.﴾ [Ali 'Imran 75–77].

Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Among the People of the Book is one who, if you entrust him with a qintar, he will return it to you; and among them is one who, if you entrust him with a dinar, he will not return it to you unless you constantly stand over him.﴾

When Allah, glorified and exalted is He, mentioned the treachery of the People of the Book in religious matters, their distortion of the truth with falsehood, their obstinacy, their hypocrisy, and their altering of things for the believers, He mentioned their condition in worldly matters, regarding wealth, and divided them by Allah the Exalted into two categories. He said: ﴿Among the People of the Book﴾. This includes the Jews and the Christians, and they were called "People of the Book" because they are the ones who possess remnants of the religion revealed to the prophets: the Jews have remnants of the Torah, and the Christians have remnants of the Gospel.

﴿مَنْ إِنْ تَأْمَنْهُ﴾ Here it is necessary to pronounce the hamza clearly, because the hamza is a hamzat qat' (cutting hamza), so one says ﴿مَنْ إِنْ﴾, unlike what is said by some people, even some imams of mosques, who say (مَنِ انْ تأمنْه). This is an error, because if one says (مَنِ انْ تأمنه), one makes the hamza a hamzat wasl (linking hamza), whereas it is a hamzat qat', since it is (إن), the conditional particle. ﴿مَنْ إِنْ تَأْمَنْهُ﴾: the address in ﴿إِنْ تَأْمَنْهُ﴾ returns to the addressee; that is, "one who, if you, O addressee, entrust him..." ﴿بِقِنْطَارٍ﴾: that is, with a qintar. ﴿يُؤَدِّهِ إِلَيْكَ﴾: The qintar is an expression for a large amount of gold. Some defined it as a thousand dinars, and some as the filling of a bull's hide (مَسْك الثور, i.e., the bull's skin) with dinars. In any case, the meaning is: one who, if you entrust him with a large amount of gold, will return it to you, i.e., he will give it back to you without alteration or deficiency. Al-adaa' (الأداء) is the delivery of a thing, as in "adaa' al-hadith" (conveying a narration), and "adaa' al-amanat" (delivering trusts), i.e., delivering them to their rightful owner. So ﴿يُؤَدِّهِ إِلَيْكَ﴾ means: he will give it to you whole, free of any deficiency. This is a trustworthy person.

In the phrase ﴿يُؤَدِّهِ إِلَيْكَ﴾ there are two readings: one with a kasra on the ha' ﴿يُؤَدِّهِ إِلَيْكَ﴾, and another with sukun ﴿يُؤَدِّهْ إِلَيْكَ﴾.

As for the second category, the treacherous one who cannot be trusted: ﴿مَنْ إِنْ تَأْمَنْهُ بِدِينَارٍ لَا يُؤَدِّهِ إِلَيْكَ﴾. Regarding ﴿لَا يُؤَدِّهِ﴾ we say about it what we said about ﴿يُؤَدِّهِ﴾: ﴿لَا يُؤَدِّهِ إِلَيْكَ﴾ and ﴿لَا يُؤَدِّهِ إِلَيْكَ﴾.

﴿مَنْ إِنْ تَأْمَنْهُ بِدِينَارٍ﴾: The dinar is the unit of gold currency, which is what we call the "junayh" (guinea). ﴿إِنْ تَأْمَنْهُ بِدِينَارٍ لَا يُؤَدِّهِ إِلَيْكَ﴾: that is, he will not return it to you intact; rather he will diminish it and betray it. ﴿إِلَّا مَا دُمْتَ عَلَيْهِ قَائِمًا﴾: that is, unless you remain standing over him, watching him and observing his affairs; then you will be safe from his treachery. But if you become negligent even slightly, he will betray you. So Allah, mighty and majestic, has now divided the People of the Book into two categories: a trustworthy category, which, if you entrust it with a large amount, does not diminish it at all, and if you entrust it with a small amount, it will not diminish it all the more, since if it does not diminish a large amount at all, while a small portion taken from a large amount would not be noticed, then entrusting it with a small amount is all the more so.

The second category: one who, if you entrust him with the smallest amount, one single coin, will not return it to you, unless you stand over him, watching him; then you are safe from his evil. Otherwise, he may diminish even one dinar. And if you entrust him with less than a dinar...

* Students: He will not return it.
* Shaykh: Likewise he will not return it. And for more?
* Students: All the more so.
* Shaykh: All the more so.

Now, grammatically, in this verse, first the phrase ﴿مَنْ إِنْ تَأْمَنْهُ بِقِنْطَارٍ﴾: what is the grammatical position of ﴿مَنْ﴾ in ﴿وَمِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ مَنْ إِنْ تَأْمَنْهُ﴾...

* Student: A predicate.
* Shaykh: A subject, a delayed subject (mubtada' mu'akhkhar). ﴿وَمِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ﴾ is a fronted predicate (khabar muqaddam). ﴿مَنْ﴾ is a relative pronoun and requires a relative clause (silah). Where is its silah? Its silah is the conditional sentence ﴿إِنْ تَأْمَنْهُ بِقِنْطَارٍ يُؤَدِّهِ﴾; that is, the relative clause is not complete unless the condition and its response come. So ﴿إِنْ﴾ is conditional, ﴿تَأْمَنْهُ﴾ is the conditional verb, and ﴿يُؤَدِّهِ﴾ is the response of the condition. And the sentence?

* Students: The relative clause.
* Shaykh: The relative clause; the sentence is the silah of the relative pronoun. Good. And we also say of the second sentence ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ إِنْ تَأْمَنْهُ بِدِينَارٍ لَا يُؤَدِّهِ إِلَيْكَ﴾, except that in the second sentence we say: ﴿لَا﴾ is a negation particle, ﴿لَا يُؤَدِّهِ﴾ is not a prohibition; it is a negation with a fatha, and ﴿يُؤَدِّهِ﴾ is the response of the condition. Now, the response of the condition requires jazm (apocopation), and here ﴿يُؤَدِّهِ﴾ has a kasra on the dal and is not jussive?

We say it is...

* Student: Because of two consecutive sukuns (iltiqa' al-sakinayn).

* Shaykh: No, there is no meeting of two sukuns. We say: this verb ends in a weak letter, and a verb ending in a weak letter is jussived by deleting the weak letter. The original form of ﴿يُؤَدِّهِ﴾ is (يؤدِّيه), so the yaa' was deleted for the sake of jazm. And in ﴿إِلَّا مَا دُمْتَ عَلَيْهِ قَائِمًا﴾, how is ﴿قَائِمًا﴾ parsed?

* Students: A circumstantial accusative (hal).

* Shaykh: No, my brothers!

* Students: A predicate, the predicate of (دام).

* Shaykh: The predicate of (دام), because dāma is among the sisters of kāna: it raises the subject and puts the predicate in the accusative. The ta' is its subject, the ta' is its subject, and its predicate...

* Students: ﴿قَائِمًا﴾.

* Shaykh: ﴿قَائِمًا﴾. Then Allah, mighty and majestic, said, explaining their betrayal of trust: ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾: that is, the aforementioned betrayal ﴿بِأَنَّهُمْ قَالُوا لَيْسَ عَلَيْنَا﴾.

The bā' here is causal (lil-sababiyyah); that is, their not being trustworthy, indeed their untrustworthiness, is due to their saying, i.e., because of their saying: ﴿لَيْسَ عَلَيْنَا فِي الْأُمِّيِّينَ سَبِيلٌ﴾. ﴿لَيْسَ عَلَيْنَا فِي الْأُمِّيِّينَ﴾: the ummiyyun are the Arabs, and they were called ummiyyin in reference to "umm" (mother). An ummi person is one who neither reads nor writes. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ أُمِّيُّونَ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ الْكِتَابَ إِلَّا أَمَانِيَّ﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:78]; that is, they know it only by recitation. As for the ummi in origin, he is the one who neither reads nor writes; that is why the Arabs did not read or write until after the Messenger ﷺ was sent, and then they acquired reading and writing. So, ﴿فِي الْأُمِّيِّينَ﴾ refers to whom?

* Student: The Arabs.

* Shaykh: The Arabs, and they were called ummiyyin because they neither read nor write. Some exegetes said: what is meant by the ummiyyin is anyone other than the People of the Book, so the ummi means one who has no scripture. These Jews and Christians would then be saying: everyone other than the People of the Book, we have no responsibility toward them; we may wrong them, take their wealth, kill them, enslave their women, because we are the chosen ones before Allah and others are our servants, and a master may do what he wishes with his servants. That is why the Jews say: "We are the chosen people of God." Indeed, but God chose them over the worlds of their time, yet they did not give thanks for this blessing. So, they said: ﴿لَيْسَ عَلَيْنَا فِي الْأُمِّيِّينَ سَبِيلٌ﴾: is ﴿فِي الْأُمِّيِّينَ﴾ concerning their wealth, or concerning their wealth, their lives, and all their affairs?

* Students: (...)

* Shaykh: Yes. Whoever looks at the context of the verse, that it is in the context of trusteeship over wealth, restricts this to: there is no responsibility on us toward the ummiyyin regarding what?

* Students: Wealth.

* Shaykh: Wealth. And whoever looks at the generality says it includes their claim that there is no way against them regarding the ummiyyin in their wealth and their lives, and this meaning is more general; and when the meaning is more general and the wording does not contradict it, the preference is what?

* Students: The more general.

* Shaykh: That you take the more general, because the more general includes the more specific and not vice versa. So ﴿لَيْسَ عَلَيْنَا فِي الْأُمِّيِّينَ سَبِيلٌ﴾ means neither in their wealth nor in their lives. Their word ﴿سَبِيلٌ﴾: sabil originally means a path, and here it means blame; that is, there is no way of blame upon us, or no path to blame; in other words, we are not blamed, not censured, and not sinful regarding whom?

* Students: The ummiyyin.

* Shaykh: Regarding the ummiyyin. Now, this statement they make, they do not attribute it to themselves, as though they themselves permitted for themselves the aggression against the ummiyyin; rather they make it a law from Allah, saying: Allah has permitted us this and did not place any way upon us regarding the ummiyyin. That is why Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾, ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾: that is, they lie against Allah and fabricate against Allah, and claim this as a law from Allah, while they know that Allah has forbidden them to consume people's wealth unjustly, and their blood and honor; they know this, yet they lie against Allah.

Grammar: ﴿ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ﴾: we said that the bā' is...

* Students: Causal.

* Shaykh: Causal. And ﴿لَيْسَ عَلَيْنَا فِي الْأُمِّيِّينَ سَبِيلٌ﴾: ﴿سَبِيلٌ﴾ is nominative...

* Students: The subject of laysa.

* Shaykh: As the subject of laysa. ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ﴾: ﴿الْكَذِبَ﴾ is the object of ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾. It has also been said that it is an adjective of an omitted verbal noun, whose estimate is?

* Student: The saying.

* Shaykh: The saying, the lie: they say against Allah the lying saying. ﴿عَلَى اللَّهِ﴾ is a prepositional phrase related to ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾, but we say: when it is related to ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾, then ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ here is implicitly carrying the meaning of (يفترون, "they fabricate"), so ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ means: they fabricate against Allah the lie. This kind of expression occurs often in the Qur'an, such as ﴿يَفْتَرُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ﴾ [an-Nisa' 4:50].

Now, implicit transference (at-tadmin) has passed over us, I think, and I do not know whether you recall it or not: that transference is disputed, whether we make the verb carry a meaning suitable to its complement, or we make the transference in the particle, for example. And it has previously been said that the preferred view is that we make the verb carry a meaning suitable to the particle, and among the most prominent examples of this is the Almighty's saying: ﴿عَيْنًا يَشْرَبُ بِهَا عِبَادُ اللَّهِ﴾ [al-Insan 76:6].

* Shaykh: Are you with me?

* Student: Yes.

* Shaykh: Among the most prominent examples of this is the Almighty's saying: ﴿عَيْنًا يَشْرَبُ بِهَا عِبَادُ اللَّهِ﴾. Is the spring drunk with it, or is it drunk from a cup?

* Students: From a cup.

* Shaykh: From a cup. Hm, or from the spring itself?

* Students: From a cup.

* Shaykh: From a cup. When a person sits by a river and drinks, he does not lift the river; he drinks from it with a cup, is that not so?

* Students: Indeed.

* Shaykh: Now, some scholars said: the bā' in ﴿يَشْرَبُ بِهَا عِبَادُ اللَّهِ﴾ means (مِن, "from"), i.e., they drink from it, and according to this view ﴿يَشْرَبُ﴾ is on its literal meaning of drinking. Others said: rather ﴿يَشْرَبُ﴾ means "to be quenched" (يَرْوَى), and according to this the bā' is causal and not in the sense of "from"; that is, a spring by which the servants of God are quenched. This meaning is more correct, because when ﴿يَشْرَبُ﴾ carries the meaning of "to be quenched," quenching only comes after drinking, only after drinking. According to this, the verb "to be quenched" indicates the meaning of drinking. And what else?

* Students: And an addition.

* Shaykh: And an addition. But if you say ﴿يَشْرَبُ﴾ on its literal meaning and the bā' in the sense of (مِن), we would not derive this benefit, which is quenching. Yes indeed. So then ﴿يَقُولُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ﴾: we say, ﴿عَلَى اللَّهِ﴾ is related to what? To ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾, with ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ carrying the meaning of (يفترون, "they fabricate"). And their saying ﴿يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ is a circumstantial clause (hal) from the waw in ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾; that is, they say it while they know that they are lying, so their saying is worse than one who says a lie without knowing it is a lie. Then Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿بَلَى﴾. Bala: a particle of refutation in this context, or in this context, against what they said, which is ﴿لَيْسَ عَلَيْنَا فِي الْأُمِّيِّينَ سَبِيلٌ﴾; that is: yes, there is a way against them, because if they betray a trust, then there is a way against them. Everyone who betrays his trust?

* Student: There is a way against him.

* Shaykh: So there is a way against him, they or others. So his saying ﴿بَلَى﴾ is a particle brought to refute what they claimed in their saying:

* Students: ﴿لَيْسَ عَلَيْنَا فِي الْأُمِّيِّينَ سَبِيلٌ﴾...

* Shaykh: ﴿لَيْسَ عَلَيْنَا فِي الْأُمِّيِّينَ سَبِيلٌ﴾. Then He said: ﴿مَنْ أَوْفَى بِعَهْدِهِ وَاتَّقَى﴾: this sentence is resumptive (isti'nafiyyah), and its parsing will come at the end of the discussion of the verse. ﴿مَنْ أَوْفَى بِعَهْدِهِ وَاتَّقَى﴾: ﴿أَوْفَى﴾ means "completed," so it is a past verb and not a superlative; that is, he completed with his covenant, i.e., with what he covenanted with another, and feared Allah in this fulfillment: ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُتَّقِينَ﴾. Now, His saying ﴿مَنْ أَوْفَى بِعَهْدِهِ﴾: we said ﴿بِعَهْدِهِ﴾ means: by the contract he contracted. Is a contract a covenant? Yes, a contract is a covenant, for each of the two contracting parties pledges to the other to complete what the contract was made upon, even if the covenant is not mentioned verbally; but this is what the contract implies. The implication of a contract is that if I contract with you, I will fulfill to you what the contract was made upon, so every contract is what?

* Students: A covenant.

* Shaykh: A covenant.

Now He said: ﴿بَلَى مَنْ أَوْفَى بِعَهْدِهِ﴾; that is, by what he covenanted with another, of contracts and others, and among them is trust: if I entrust you with something, I have covenanted with you to guard it. And His saying ﴿وَاتَّقَى﴾: feared whom?

* Students: Feared Allah.

* Shaykh: Feared Allah, by fulfilling the covenant; and among fearing Allah is fearing treachery, that he not betray. Taqwa is derived from wiqaya (protection), and it is a comprehensive term for doing what Allah commanded and avoiding what He forbade; this is taqwa, a comprehensive term for doing what Allah commanded. Complete it.

* Students: And avoiding what He forbade...

* Shaykh: And avoiding what He forbade. If it is mentioned alongside piety (birr), it is restricted to the prohibitions, and piety is restricted to the commands, like His saying: ﴿تَعَاوَنُوا عَلَى الْبِرِّ وَالتَّقْوَى﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:2]; that is, cooperate in doing the commands and avoiding the prohibitions. But when taqwa is mentioned alone, it includes doing the commands and avoiding the prohibitions. So taqwa is a comprehensive term for doing what Allah commanded and avoiding what He forbade, and its wording indicates this, because it is derived from wiqaya, and there is no protection from the punishment of Allah except by doing His commands and avoiding His prohibitions; this is taqwa.

Some scholars said: taqwa is to act in obedience to Allah, upon light from Allah, hoping for the reward of Allah; thus he combined knowledge, action, and seeking reward: to act in obedience to Allah, this is what? Action. Upon light from Allah?

* Students: Knowledge.

* Shaykh: Knowledge. Hoping for the reward of Allah?

* Students: Seeking reward.

* Shaykh: Seeking reward. And to abandon what Allah forbade, upon light from Allah, fearing the punishment of Allah; also combining knowledge, action, and seeking reward. Others said in defining taqwa:

Leave sins, both the small of them and the great, that is taqwa.
And act like one walking over a field of thorns, watchful of what he sees.
Do not belittle any small sin, for mountains are made of pebbles.

This too does not contradict what preceded; it is only a difference of expression.

Now, His saying ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُتَّقِينَ﴾: here He said ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ and did not say "indeed Allah loves him." Such an expression is called ishar fi mawdi' al-idmar (explicit noun in place of pronoun), and it has benefits, among them:

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verses 75–76 (part 2 of 3):

Alerting the addressee (tanbih al-mukhatab). The reason for this is that when speech follows one uniform pattern, nothing in it calls for attention, correct? For this reason the listener or speaker goes on without anything in the speech calling for attention. But when the style changes and a noun is used explicitly in place of a pronoun, a person pays attention to what is said: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves him﴾. Isn't that so?

Second: using an explicit noun in place of a pronoun gives the reason for the ruling that comes with it. His saying ﴿Indeed, Allah loves him﴾ does not state the cause in the way His saying ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who are mindful of Him﴾ does. For when He says ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who are mindful of Him﴾, why? Because of their piety. So it conveys the cause.

Third: it conveys generality, meaning that everyone covered by this explicit form is included. Read the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Whoever is an enemy to Allah and His angels and His messengers and Jibril and Mika'il, then indeed Allah is an enemy to the disbelievers﴾ [al-Baqarah 98]. He did not say "indeed Allah is an enemy to him," so that it would include every disbeliever, whether his disbelief consists of this enmity or of something else. Thus the ruling is generalized.

Alright, ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who are mindful of Him﴾. We take the benefits from these verses:

Alright, from these verses is the explanation that the People of the Book were divided in respect of trustworthiness into two groups.

* A student: The i'rab (grammatical analysis), sir?
* The Shaykh: Yes, yes, the i'rab. Alright: ﴿Yes! Whoever fulfils his covenant and is mindful of Allah﴾. ﴿Whoever fulfils his covenant﴾: ﴿man﴾ here is a conditional noun of firm conditioning (ism shart jazim), and ﴿awfa﴾ is
* The students: The conditional verb (fi'l al-shart).
* The Shaykh: The conditional verb. ﴿wa-ittaqa﴾ is conjoined to it, and the clause ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who are mindful of Him﴾...
* A student: The response of the condition (jawab al-shart).
* The Shaykh: The response of the condition. But you may ask: why is the response of the condition joined with the particle fa, when the condition in His saying ﴿Of them is one who, if you entrust him with a qintar, will return it to you﴾ and ﴿does not return it to you﴾ has no fa? The answer is that we say: when the response of the condition cannot be a verb for the condition, it must be joined with fa. Do you understand?
* A student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: When the response of the condition cannot be a verb for the condition, it must be joined with fa. Ibn Malik said:
"Join with fa, necessarily, a response that, if it were made the condition for (in) or others, would not be made a condition."
This is the rule: when the response of the condition cannot be a verb for the condition, it must be joined with fa. This is the rule, and its detailed explanation is in the well-known line:
"Nominal, imperative, with a fixed (past) verb, with mā, with lan, with qad, and with negation by tanfis."
These are seven cases. When the response of the condition is one of these seven, it must be joined with fa. Here the clause is ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who are mindful of Him﴾. Is it imperative?
* The students: Nominal.
* The Shaykh: Nominal, correct, because ﴿Allah loves those who are mindful of Him﴾ is a subject and predicate, but it is abrogated (mansukh) by (inna), so the clause here is nominal.

From the benefits of these verses:

First: the explanation that the People of the Book are divided into two groups: trustworthy and treacherous. Just as they are divided into two groups, believers and disbelievers. For example, 'Abdullah ibn Salam (may Allah be pleased with him) was among the rabbis of the Jews, and Allah blessed him with Islam, so he embraced it, is that so? And Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf was among the nobles of the Jews, but he remained in his disbelief and did not believe. So just as they are divided into disbeliever and believer, they are also divided into treacherous and trustworthy.

Alright. The Prophet (ﷺ) also made a transaction with the Jews, and he (ﷺ) died while his armour was pledged with a Jew. [Reported by al-Bukhari (2916) from the hadith of 'A'isha.] This shows that among the Jews there is one who is trustworthy, for otherwise, how would the Messenger (ﷺ) pledge his armour, which is one of the instruments of war, with this Jewish man? He was trustworthy.

* From the benefits of the verse: it is obligatory to be cautious of the People of the Book, the Jews and the Christians, because as long as they are divided into two groups, we do not know, when we deal with them, which of the two groups these people belong to. So we must be cautious, especially when it becomes clear to us that they are treacherous, people of betrayal, and that they never strive for our interests, as is the reality. In the present time, the reality is that the Jews and the Christians never strive for the good of the Muslims, but rather they strive...
* The students: For the belittling of the Muslims...
* The Shaykh: For the deception of the Muslims and corrupting them, so much so that when they see a state among the Muslim states heading towards Islam, they try to topple it and to restrict it economically, militarily and politically. This is something that everyone who reflects and considers current events knows.

So it is obligatory for us to be extremely cautious of the Jews and the Christians, and to know that each of the Jews and the Christians is an ally of the other, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿O you who believe, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies; they are allies of one another﴾ [al-Ma'idah 51]. However long the period, they are allies against a common enemy, and they are?
* The students: The Muslims.
* The Shaykh: The Muslims, yes indeed.
* And from the benefits of this verse: the permissibility of limiting oneself to an example so that what resembles it can be analogized to it, for He said: a qintar and a dinar. Alright, and if you entrusted him with a car or a child's toy, what is its like?
* The students: Like it, of course.
* The Shaykh: Yes. Among the People of the Book is one who, if you entrust him with a child's toy, will not return it to you unless you stand over him, and among them is one who, if you entrust him with a car, yes, and returns it to you safe. But Allah mentioned the dinar and the qintar by way of example.
* And from the benefits of these verses: the self-admiration of the People of the Book and their contempt for others, for they said: ﴿There is no blame upon us regarding the unlettered﴾, and this indicates self-conceit and contempt for others.
* And from their benefits: the People of the Book do not confine themselves to injustice and transgression and attribute it to their own whims, but rather they attribute it to the law of Allah. The proof of this is His saying the Exalted: ﴿and they speak falsehood about Allah﴾. So they speak falsehood about Allah in this and in other matters.
* And from the benefits of these verses: whoever fabricates lies about Allah concerning what he issues as a legal opinion (fatwa) or what he rules between people, there is a resemblance to whom? To the Jews and the Christians. There is a resemblance to the Jews and the Christians. Fabricating lies about Allah has occurred in this ummah too, whether in judging between people or in fatwas that are not rulings but are reports about the Shari'ah.
* And from the benefits of the noble verse: whoever fabricates lies about Allah knowingly is more sinful and more transgressive than one who does not know, and although each of them is in error, the deliberate one is not like the one who is not deliberate. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever lies about me deliberately, let him take his seat in the Fire." [Reported by al-Bukhari (1291) and Muslim (4/4) in the introduction, from the hadith of al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba.]
* And from the benefits of that: an indication that compound ignorance (al-jahl al-murakkab) is worse than simple ignorance. What is the reason for this? * The students: (...).
* The Shaykh: Because the one who lies while knowing is worse than the one who lies without knowing. The compound ignorant person who advances on a matter while knowing that he has no knowledge of it is worse than the person who thinks that this is knowledge.
* And from the benefits of the verses: praise for those who fulfil their covenants, as in His saying: ﴿Yes! Whoever fulfils his covenant and is mindful of Allah, then indeed Allah loves those who are mindful of Him﴾.
* And from their benefits: fulfilling the covenant is among the causes of Allah's love, because of His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who are mindful of Him﴾.
* And from their benefits also: that piety towards Allah in general is a cause of what? Of His love.
* And from the benefits of the verses: a refutation of the Ash'arites and others among the people of negation (ahl al-ta'til) who deny Allah's love, and who said: it is not permissible to affirm that Allah loves; if you affirm that Allah loves, you have attributed to Allah deficiency and defect, because this is a characteristic of created things; and because love exists only between two things that are similar. So how can you affirm that Allah loves? He affirmed it for Himself. They said: the intended meaning of affirming love is not love itself; what is meant is its necessary consequence, which is reward. So the meaning of ﴿He loves those who are mindful of Him﴾ is that He rewards the mindful. As for His loving them, no, not at all. The reason? They said:
* A student: Love is between two things...
* The Shaykh: Love exists only between two things that are similar; and because love is a attribute of created things, so it does not befit Allah, glory be to Him. But we say: this is distorting the words from their places, for the texts affirming Allah's love, that He loves and is loved, are almost countless: ﴿So Allah will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him﴾ [al-Ma'idah 54]. And love is other than reward. When Allah loves a servant, He rewards him; so reward is a necessary consequence of love. As for their saying that it exists only between similar things, this is not correct; for it has been established from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said about Uhud: "A mountain that loves us and we love it." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1481) and Muslim (1392/503) from the hadith of Abu Humayd al-Sa'idi; and al-Bukhari (3367) and Muslim (1365/462) from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik.] And where is the similarity between humans and a mountain? And it has been established by observable reality that some animals love humans. The she-camel loves her owner and comes to him from among the people and kneels beside him, yes. If anyone other than her owner came, she would strike him with her leg or bite him with her mouth. But her owner, she yearns for him and sits near him, and when she hears his voice even if she does not see him, she yearns. Likewise the rest of the animals, which is something observed, and this is love. Now the cat loves some members of the household and not others. If one of the household members she does not love comes, she runs away and hisses at him, yes. And if the one she loves comes, she approaches him and starts rubbing against him. This is something observed. What made her rub against this one and seek his affection, while she flees from the other and rebukes him?
* A student: Love.
* The Shaykh: Love. There is no doubt about it; this is something observed. So their claim that love exists only between two things is refuted by both hearing and reality. Hearing, by the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) about Uhud: "A mountain that loves us and we love it." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1481) and Muslim (1392/503) from the hadith of Abu Humayd al-Sa'idi; and al-Bukhari (3367) and Muslim (1365/462) from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik.] And reality needs no proof, for everyone knows it.

﴿Yes! Whoever fulfils his covenant and is mindful of Allah, then indeed Allah loves those who are mindful of Him﴾. Then He said: ﴿Indeed, those who sell﴾. Is the time up?
* A student: In His saying the Exalted: ﴿And among the People of the Book﴾, is this for diminution (taqlil)?
* The Shaykh: Eh?
* The student: For diminution, this?
* The Shaykh: No, this is for partitive (tab'id).
* The student: That is, some of them...
* The Shaykh: Some of them, yes. And the other part is ﴿Of them is one who, if you entrust him with a dinar, will not return it to you﴾. Alright, there is in fact a benefit in the verse: that one should monitor the treacherous person and keep watch over him. So if you give your wealth to someone who is not trustworthy, it is neither prudence nor resolve to leave him, but rather be on guard against him. And if this applies to entrusting wealth, entrusting honour is even more so. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) warned against entering upon women and said: "Beware of entering upon women." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, what about the in-law (al-hamu)?" He said: "The in-law is death." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5232) and Muslim (2172/20) from the hadith of 'Uqba ibn 'Amir al-Juhani.]
So whatever you fear may lead to the loss of trust, be keen to keep watch over it and to stand guard over it. For this reason He said: ﴿except as long as you stand over him﴾.
* A student: Now some calls come to illiteracy; they take their children out of schools and so on, and they argue from the "unlettered" (ummiyyin). Is this what is mentioned in the Qur'an?
* The Shaykh: What do you mean?
* The student: I mean there are calls to this, not widespread and not strong. Regarding arguing from illiteracy: we are an unlettered nation. Is this praise?
* The Shaykh: No, it is not praise. Illiteracy is a defect, which Allah the Exalted mentioned in a disparaging way, saying: ﴿And among them are unlettered people who know not the Book except wishful fancies﴾. He also alluded to it in His saying: ﴿It is He who raised among the unlettered a messenger from among themselves, who recites to them His verses and purifies them and teaches them the Book and wisdom, though before that they were in clear error﴾ [al-Jumu'ah 2]. Error is not seen by anyone as praise. But for the Messenger (ﷺ) it is a purification, because his being unlettered, yet bringing this great Book, shows that he is truthful, for an unlettered person could not produce a book like this, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And you did not recite any scripture before it, nor write it with your right hand; otherwise the falsifiers would have doubted﴾ [al-'Ankabut 48]. And we are "an unlettered nation," as the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) said, but after Allah opened to us and gave us knowledge and wisdom, we became a scholarly nation, not an unlettered nation.
If someone says: this contradicts you, since the Messenger said: "We are an unlettered nation," in Medina, after the Book had been revealed to him? We say: yes, he said it with regard to the crescent (hilal), with regard to the crescent. And with regard to the crescent, even after the conquests, we are an unlettered nation; we do not know the calculation of the lunar phases and do not know them. Yes indeed.
* A student: The second meaning, the interpretation of "unlettered" (ummiyyin), the second meaning you mentioned, does it have a basis?
* The Shaykh: It has a basis, because His saying the Exalted: ﴿And among them are unlettered people﴾ speaks of the People of the Book, for they do not know the Book except as wishful fancies, that is, mere recitation. And this, note well, contains a rebuke of those who attend to the wording of the Qur'an and neglect its meaning. Some people are so careful with the words of the Qur'an that you find them reaching the point of obsession in pronouncing certain letters, based on the idea that they want to articulate them according to tajwid, or according to the rules of tajwid as they understand them, but in meaning...
* The students: They do not know it...
* The Shaykh: They do not know it; they do not attend to it at all, so they are unlettered. For this reason Shaykh al-Islam (may Allah have mercy on him) denounced those who exaggerate in articulating letters and the qualities of letters while being heedless of the meanings of the Qur'an.
* * *

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verses 75–76 (part 3 of 3):**

* Student: ﴿Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price, those will have no share in the Hereafter. Allah will not speak to them, nor look at them on the Day of Resurrection, nor purify them, and for them is a painful punishment (77). And indeed, among them is a group who distort their tongues with the Scripture so that you may think it is from the Scripture, but it is not from the Scripture. They say, "It is from Allah," but it is not from Allah. And they speak falsehood about Allah while they know it (78). It is not for a human that Allah should give him the Scripture, the judgment and prophethood, and then he say to the people, "Be servants to me instead of Allah." Rather, [he would say], "Be devoted worshippers of the Lord by what you teach of the Scripture and by what you study" (79). Nor would He order you to take the angels and the prophets as lords. Would He order you to disbelief after you have submitted [to Him]? (80) And [mention] when Allah took the covenant of the prophets: "Whatever I have given you of Scripture and wisdom, and then there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you must believe in him and support him." He said, "Do you affirm and accept My commitment on this condition?" They said, "We affirm it." He said, "Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses" (81).﴾ [Al 'Imran 77–81].
* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price, those will have no share in the Hereafter. Allah will not speak to them, nor look at them on the Day of Resurrection, nor purify them, and for them is a painful punishment.﴾
I think we have already taken the benefits of what came before?
* Students: Yes, we have not finished, O Shaykh.
* Shaykh: We have not finished? Up to what?
* Students: (...) It is obligatory to punish the traitor. This is the last benefit.
* Shaykh: Yes indeed. Alright. Among the benefits of the previous verses, which is His saying the Exalted: ﴿And among the People of the Book is one who, if you entrust him with a great amount, will return it to you; and among them is one who, if you entrust him with a single dinar, will not return it to you unless you constantly stand over him.﴾
* Among its benefits: that these treacherous Jews have what they use to dress up their falsehood in their saying: ﴿That is because they say, "There is no blame upon us concerning the unlettered."﴾
* Among its benefits: the clarification of the Jews' conceit in themselves and their contempt for the servants of Allah.
* Among its benefits: that these Jews speak falsehood about Allah, fabricating it while knowing it is false, and this is worse than one who speaks falsehood while being ignorant.
* Among its benefits: that the Jews and others are equal in that whoever wrongs someone is liable to be held to account. For this reason, the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿and they speak falsehood about Allah﴾, and this indicates that the unlettered and others are equal in the prohibition of wronging them.
* Among the benefits of the two verses: that these Jews are liable to be held to account regarding the unlettered, whether they wrong their lives, their wealth or their honor, based on His saying the Exalted: ﴿Yes﴾; i.e., they are liable to be held to account regarding the unlettered, just as they are liable if some of them wrong others.
* Among its benefits: that fulfilling the covenant and piety are among the causes of the love of Allah, based on His saying: ﴿Yes, whoever fulfills his covenant and fears Allah, indeed Allah loves the righteous.﴾ Among its benefits: the affirmation of Allah's love, based on His saying: ﴿indeed Allah loves the righteous﴾. If Allah the Exalted loves the righteous, then another benefit follows from this, which is: the encouragement to fear Allah, because every person loves that Allah the Mighty and Majestic should love him. So if you want that, there is nothing for you but to establish the fear of Allah.

The love of Allah the Exalted is connected to the doer, connected to the deed, connected to time, and connected to place. It is connected to the doer, as in this verse: ﴿He loves the righteous﴾, and as in His saying the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in a row, as if they were a compact structure﴾ [As-Saff 4], and as in His saying: ﴿And do good; indeed, Allah loves the good-doers﴾ [Al-Baqarah 195].

It is connected to the deed: "The most beloved of deeds to Allah is prayer at its proper time"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (527) and Muslim (85/139), from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud.]].

It is connected to time: "There are no days in which righteous deeds are more beloved to Allah than these ten days"[[Narrated by Abu Dawud (2438), al-Tirmidhi (757), and Ibn Majah (1727), from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, and its origin is in al-Bukhari (969).]]. It may be said that this is connected to the deed and not to time.

It is connected to place: like the love of Allah the Exalted for Makkah, as reported from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said about it: "Indeed, you are the most beloved of the lands to Allah"[[Narrated by al-Bazzar (4690, 5095), from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, with the wording: "Indeed, you are the most beloved land of Allah to Allah," and its origin is in al-Tirmidhi (3926).]].

So the love of Allah is connected to the doer, the deed, the time, and the place.

Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Among the People of the Book is one who, if you entrust him with a qintar, he will return it to you; and among them is one who, if you entrust him with a dinar, he will not return it to you unless you constantly stand over him.﴾

When Allah, glorified and exalted is He, mentioned the treachery of the People of the Book in religious matters, their distortion of the truth with falsehood, their obstinacy, their hypocrisy, and their altering of things for the believers, He mentioned their condition in worldly matters, regarding wealth, and divided them by Allah the Exalted into two categories. He said: ﴿Among the People of the Book﴾. This includes the Jews and the Christians, and they were called "People of the Book" because they are the ones who possess remnants of the religion revealed to the prophets: the Jews have remnants of the Torah, and the Christians have remnants of the Gospel.

﴿مَنْ إِنْ تَأْمَنْهُ﴾ Here it is necessary to pronounce the hamza clearly, because the hamza is a hamzat qat' (cutting hamza), so one says ﴿مَنْ إِنْ﴾, unlike what is said by some people, even some imams of mosques, who say (مَنِ انْ تأمنْه). This is an error, because if one says (مَنِ انْ تأمنه), one makes the hamza a hamzat wasl (linking hamza), whereas it is a hamzat qat', since it is (إن), the conditional particle. ﴿مَنْ إِنْ تَأْمَنْهُ﴾: the address in ﴿إِنْ تَأْمَنْهُ﴾ returns to the addressee; that is, "one who, if you, O addressee, entrust him..." ﴿بِقِنْطَارٍ﴾: that is, with a qintar. ﴿يُؤَدِّهِ إِلَيْكَ﴾: The qintar is an expression for a large amount of gold. Some defined it as a thousand dinars, and some as the filling of a bull's hide (مَسْك الثور, i.e., the bull's skin) with dinars. In any case, the meaning is: one who, if you entrust him with a large amount of gold, will return it to you, i.e., he will give it back to you without alteration or deficiency. Al-adaa' (الأداء) is the delivery of a thing, as in "adaa' al-hadith" (conveying a narration), and "adaa' al-amanat" (delivering trusts), i.e., delivering them to their rightful owner. So ﴿يُؤَدِّهِ إِلَيْكَ﴾ means: he will give it to you whole, free of any deficiency. This is a trustworthy person.

In the phrase ﴿يُؤَدِّهِ إِلَيْكَ﴾ there are two readings: one with a kasra on the ha' ﴿يُؤَدِّهِ إِلَيْكَ﴾, and another with sukun ﴿يُؤَدِّهْ إِلَيْكَ﴾.

As for the second category, the treacherous one who cannot be trusted: ﴿مَنْ إِنْ تَأْمَنْهُ بِدِينَارٍ لَا يُؤَدِّهِ إِلَيْكَ﴾. Regarding ﴿لَا يُؤَدِّهِ﴾ we say about it what we said about ﴿يُؤَدِّهِ﴾: ﴿لَا يُؤَدِّهِ إِلَيْكَ﴾ and ﴿لَا يُؤَدِّهِ إِلَيْكَ﴾.

﴿مَنْ إِنْ تَأْمَنْهُ بِدِينَارٍ﴾: The dinar is the unit of gold currency, which is what we call the "junayh" (guinea). ﴿إِنْ تَأْمَنْهُ بِدِينَارٍ لَا يُؤَدِّهِ إِلَيْكَ﴾: that is, he will not return it to you intact; rather he will diminish it and betray it. ﴿إِلَّا مَا دُمْتَ عَلَيْهِ قَائِمًا﴾: that is, unless you remain standing over him, watching him and observing his affairs; then you will be safe from his treachery. But if you become negligent even slightly, he will betray you. So Allah, mighty and majestic, has now divided the People of the Book into two categories: a trustworthy category, which, if you entrust it with a large amount, does not diminish it at all, and if you entrust it with a small amount, it will not diminish it all the more, since if it does not diminish a large amount at all, while a small portion taken from a large amount would not be noticed, then entrusting it with a small amount is all the more so.

The second category: one who, if you entrust him with the smallest amount, one single coin, will not return it to you, unless you stand over him, watching him; then you are safe from his evil. Otherwise, he may diminish even one dinar. And if you entrust him with less than a dinar...

* Students: He will not return it.
* Shaykh: Likewise he will not return it. And for more?
* Students: All the more so.
* Shaykh: All the more so.

Now, grammatically, in this verse, first the phrase ﴿مَنْ إِنْ تَأْمَنْهُ بِقِنْطَارٍ﴾: what is the grammatical position of ﴿مَنْ﴾ in ﴿وَمِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ مَنْ إِنْ تَأْمَنْهُ﴾...

* Student: A predicate.
* Shaykh: A subject, a delayed subject (mubtada' mu'akhkhar). ﴿وَمِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ﴾ is a fronted predicate (khabar muqaddam). ﴿مَنْ﴾ is a relative pronoun and requires a relative clause (silah). Where is its silah? Its silah is the conditional sentence ﴿إِنْ تَأْمَنْهُ بِقِنْطَارٍ يُؤَدِّهِ﴾; that is, the relative clause is not complete unless the condition and its response come. So ﴿إِنْ﴾ is conditional, ﴿تَأْمَنْهُ﴾ is the conditional verb, and ﴿يُؤَدِّهِ﴾ is the response of the condition. And the sentence?

* Students: The relative clause.
* Shaykh: The relative clause; the sentence is the silah of the relative pronoun. Good. And we also say of the second sentence ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ إِنْ تَأْمَنْهُ بِدِينَارٍ لَا يُؤَدِّهِ إِلَيْكَ﴾, except that in the second sentence we say: ﴿لَا﴾ is a negation particle, ﴿لَا يُؤَدِّهِ﴾ is not a prohibition; it is a negation with a fatha, and ﴿يُؤَدِّهِ﴾ is the response of the condition. Now, the response of the condition requires jazm (apocopation), and here ﴿يُؤَدِّهِ﴾ has a kasra on the dal and is not jussive?

We say it is...

* Student: Because of two consecutive sukuns (iltiqa' al-sakinayn).

* Shaykh: No, there is no meeting of two sukuns. We say: this verb ends in a weak letter, and a verb ending in a weak letter is jussived by deleting the weak letter. The original form of ﴿يُؤَدِّهِ﴾ is (يؤدِّيه), so the yaa' was deleted for the sake of jazm. And in ﴿إِلَّا مَا دُمْتَ عَلَيْهِ قَائِمًا﴾, how is ﴿قَائِمًا﴾ parsed?

* Students: A circumstantial accusative (hal).

* Shaykh: No, my brothers!

* Students: A predicate, the predicate of (دام).

* Shaykh: The predicate of (دام), because dāma is among the sisters of kāna: it raises the subject and puts the predicate in the accusative. The ta' is its subject, the ta' is its subject, and its predicate...

* Students: ﴿قَائِمًا﴾.

* Shaykh: ﴿قَائِمًا﴾. Then Allah, mighty and majestic, said, explaining their betrayal of trust: ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾: that is, the aforementioned betrayal ﴿بِأَنَّهُمْ قَالُوا لَيْسَ عَلَيْنَا﴾.

The bā' here is causal (lil-sababiyyah); that is, their not being trustworthy, indeed their untrustworthiness, is due to their saying, i.e., because of their saying: ﴿لَيْسَ عَلَيْنَا فِي الْأُمِّيِّينَ سَبِيلٌ﴾. ﴿لَيْسَ عَلَيْنَا فِي الْأُمِّيِّينَ﴾: the ummiyyun are the Arabs, and they were called ummiyyin in reference to "umm" (mother). An ummi person is one who neither reads nor writes. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ أُمِّيُّونَ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ الْكِتَابَ إِلَّا أَمَانِيَّ﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:78]; that is, they know it only by recitation. As for the ummi in origin, he is the one who neither reads nor writes; that is why the Arabs did not read or write until after the Messenger ﷺ was sent, and then they acquired reading and writing. So, ﴿فِي الْأُمِّيِّينَ﴾ refers to whom?

* Student: The Arabs.

* Shaykh: The Arabs, and they were called ummiyyin because they neither read nor write. Some exegetes said: what is meant by the ummiyyin is anyone other than the People of the Book, so the ummi means one who has no scripture. These Jews and Christians would then be saying: everyone other than the People of the Book, we have no responsibility toward them; we may wrong them, take their wealth, kill them, enslave their women, because we are the chosen ones before Allah and others are our servants, and a master may do what he wishes with his servants. That is why the Jews say: "We are the chosen people of God." Indeed, but God chose them over the worlds of their time, yet they did not give thanks for this blessing. So, they said: ﴿لَيْسَ عَلَيْنَا فِي الْأُمِّيِّينَ سَبِيلٌ﴾: is ﴿فِي الْأُمِّيِّينَ﴾ concerning their wealth, or concerning their wealth, their lives, and all their affairs?

* Students: (...)

* Shaykh: Yes. Whoever looks at the context of the verse, that it is in the context of trusteeship over wealth, restricts this to: there is no responsibility on us toward the ummiyyin regarding what?

* Students: Wealth.

* Shaykh: Wealth. And whoever looks at the generality says it includes their claim that there is no way against them regarding the ummiyyin in their wealth and their lives, and this meaning is more general; and when the meaning is more general and the wording does not contradict it, the preference is what?

* Students: The more general.

* Shaykh: That you take the more general, because the more general includes the more specific and not vice versa. So ﴿لَيْسَ عَلَيْنَا فِي الْأُمِّيِّينَ سَبِيلٌ﴾ means neither in their wealth nor in their lives. Their word ﴿سَبِيلٌ﴾: sabil originally means a path, and here it means blame; that is, there is no way of blame upon us, or no path to blame; in other words, we are not blamed, not censured, and not sinful regarding whom?

* Students: The ummiyyin.

* Shaykh: Regarding the ummiyyin. Now, this statement they make, they do not attribute it to themselves, as though they themselves permitted for themselves the aggression against the ummiyyin; rather they make it a law from Allah, saying: Allah has permitted us this and did not place any way upon us regarding the ummiyyin. That is why Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾, ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾: that is, they lie against Allah and fabricate against Allah, and claim this as a law from Allah, while they know that Allah has forbidden them to consume people's wealth unjustly, and their blood and honor; they know this, yet they lie against Allah.

Grammar: ﴿ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ﴾: we said that the bā' is...

* Students: Causal.

* Shaykh: Causal. And ﴿لَيْسَ عَلَيْنَا فِي الْأُمِّيِّينَ سَبِيلٌ﴾: ﴿سَبِيلٌ﴾ is nominative...

* Students: The subject of laysa.

* Shaykh: As the subject of laysa. ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ﴾: ﴿الْكَذِبَ﴾ is the object of ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾. It has also been said that it is an adjective of an omitted verbal noun, whose estimate is?

* Student: The saying.

* Shaykh: The saying, the lie: they say against Allah the lying saying. ﴿عَلَى اللَّهِ﴾ is a prepositional phrase related to ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾, but we say: when it is related to ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾, then ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ here is implicitly carrying the meaning of (يفترون, "they fabricate"), so ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ means: they fabricate against Allah the lie. This kind of expression occurs often in the Qur'an, such as ﴿يَفْتَرُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ﴾ [an-Nisa' 4:50].

Now, implicit transference (at-tadmin) has passed over us, I think, and I do not know whether you recall it or not: that transference is disputed, whether we make the verb carry a meaning suitable to its complement, or we make the transference in the particle, for example. And it has previously been said that the preferred view is that we make the verb carry a meaning suitable to the particle, and among the most prominent examples of this is the Almighty's saying: ﴿عَيْنًا يَشْرَبُ بِهَا عِبَادُ اللَّهِ﴾ [al-Insan 76:6].

* Shaykh: Are you with me?

* Student: Yes.

* Shaykh: Among the most prominent examples of this is the Almighty's saying: ﴿عَيْنًا يَشْرَبُ بِهَا عِبَادُ اللَّهِ﴾. Is the spring drunk with it, or is it drunk from a cup?

* Students: From a cup.

* Shaykh: From a cup. Hm, or from the spring itself?

* Students: From a cup.

* Shaykh: From a cup. When a person sits by a river and drinks, he does not lift the river; he drinks from it with a cup, is that not so?

* Students: Indeed.

* Shaykh: Now, some scholars said: the bā' in ﴿يَشْرَبُ بِهَا عِبَادُ اللَّهِ﴾ means (مِن, "from"), i.e., they drink from it, and according to this view ﴿يَشْرَبُ﴾ is on its literal meaning of drinking. Others said: rather ﴿يَشْرَبُ﴾ means "to be quenched" (يَرْوَى), and according to this the bā' is causal and not in the sense of "from"; that is, a spring by which the servants of God are quenched. This meaning is more correct, because when ﴿يَشْرَبُ﴾ carries the meaning of "to be quenched," quenching only comes after drinking, only after drinking. According to this, the verb "to be quenched" indicates the meaning of drinking. And what else?

* Students: And an addition.

* Shaykh: And an addition. But if you say ﴿يَشْرَبُ﴾ on its literal meaning and the bā' in the sense of (مِن), we would not derive this benefit, which is quenching. Yes indeed. So then ﴿يَقُولُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ﴾: we say, ﴿عَلَى اللَّهِ﴾ is related to what? To ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾, with ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ carrying the meaning of (يفترون, "they fabricate"). And their saying ﴿يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ is a circumstantial clause (hal) from the waw in ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾; that is, they say it while they know that they are lying, so their saying is worse than one who says a lie without knowing it is a lie. Then Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿بَلَى﴾. Bala: a particle of refutation in this context, or in this context, against what they said, which is ﴿لَيْسَ عَلَيْنَا فِي الْأُمِّيِّينَ سَبِيلٌ﴾; that is: yes, there is a way against them, because if they betray a trust, then there is a way against them. Everyone who betrays his trust?

* Student: There is a way against him.

* Shaykh: So there is a way against him, they or others. So his saying ﴿بَلَى﴾ is a particle brought to refute what they claimed in their saying:

* Students: ﴿لَيْسَ عَلَيْنَا فِي الْأُمِّيِّينَ سَبِيلٌ﴾...

* Shaykh: ﴿لَيْسَ عَلَيْنَا فِي الْأُمِّيِّينَ سَبِيلٌ﴾. Then He said: ﴿مَنْ أَوْفَى بِعَهْدِهِ وَاتَّقَى﴾: this sentence is resumptive (isti'nafiyyah), and its parsing will come at the end of the discussion of the verse. ﴿مَنْ أَوْفَى بِعَهْدِهِ وَاتَّقَى﴾: ﴿أَوْفَى﴾ means "completed," so it is a past verb and not a superlative; that is, he completed with his covenant, i.e., with what he covenanted with another, and feared Allah in this fulfillment: ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُتَّقِينَ﴾. Now, His saying ﴿مَنْ أَوْفَى بِعَهْدِهِ﴾: we said ﴿بِعَهْدِهِ﴾ means: by the contract he contracted. Is a contract a covenant? Yes, a contract is a covenant, for each of the two contracting parties pledges to the other to complete what the contract was made upon, even if the covenant is not mentioned verbally; but this is what the contract implies. The implication of a contract is that if I contract with you, I will fulfill to you what the contract was made upon, so every contract is what?

* Students: A covenant.

* Shaykh: A covenant.

Now He said: ﴿بَلَى مَنْ أَوْفَى بِعَهْدِهِ﴾; that is, by what he covenanted with another, of contracts and others, and among them is trust: if I entrust you with something, I have covenanted with you to guard it. And His saying ﴿وَاتَّقَى﴾: feared whom?

* Students: Feared Allah.

* Shaykh: Feared Allah, by fulfilling the covenant; and among fearing Allah is fearing treachery, that he not betray. Taqwa is derived from wiqaya (protection), and it is a comprehensive term for doing what Allah commanded and avoiding what He forbade; this is taqwa, a comprehensive term for doing what Allah commanded. Complete it.

* Students: And avoiding what He forbade...

* Shaykh: And avoiding what He forbade. If it is mentioned alongside piety (birr), it is restricted to the prohibitions, and piety is restricted to the commands, like His saying: ﴿تَعَاوَنُوا عَلَى الْبِرِّ وَالتَّقْوَى﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:2]; that is, cooperate in doing the commands and avoiding the prohibitions. But when taqwa is mentioned alone, it includes doing the commands and avoiding the prohibitions. So taqwa is a comprehensive term for doing what Allah commanded and avoiding what He forbade, and its wording indicates this, because it is derived from wiqaya, and there is no protection from the punishment of Allah except by doing His commands and avoiding His prohibitions; this is taqwa.

Some scholars said: taqwa is to act in obedience to Allah, upon light from Allah, hoping for the reward of Allah; thus he combined knowledge, action, and seeking reward: to act in obedience to Allah, this is what? Action. Upon light from Allah?

* Students: Knowledge.

* Shaykh: Knowledge. Hoping for the reward of Allah?

* Students: Seeking reward.

* Shaykh: Seeking reward. And to abandon what Allah forbade, upon light from Allah, fearing the punishment of Allah; also combining knowledge, action, and seeking reward. Others said in defining taqwa:

Leave sins, both the small of them and the great, that is taqwa.
And act like one walking over a field of thorns, watchful of what he sees.
Do not belittle any small sin, for mountains are made of pebbles.

This too does not contradict what preceded; it is only a difference of expression.

Now, His saying ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُتَّقِينَ﴾: here He said ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ and did not say "indeed Allah loves him." Such an expression is called ishar fi mawdi' al-idmar (explicit noun in place of pronoun), and it has benefits, among them:

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verses 75–76 (part 2 of 3):

Alerting the addressee (tanbih al-mukhatab). The reason for this is that when speech follows one uniform pattern, nothing in it calls for attention, correct? For this reason the listener or speaker goes on without anything in the speech calling for attention. But when the style changes and a noun is used explicitly in place of a pronoun, a person pays attention to what is said: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves him﴾. Isn't that so?

Second: using an explicit noun in place of a pronoun gives the reason for the ruling that comes with it. His saying ﴿Indeed, Allah loves him﴾ does not state the cause in the way His saying ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who are mindful of Him﴾ does. For when He says ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who are mindful of Him﴾, why? Because of their piety. So it conveys the cause.

Third: it conveys generality, meaning that everyone covered by this explicit form is included. Read the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Whoever is an enemy to Allah and His angels and His messengers and Jibril and Mika'il, then indeed Allah is an enemy to the disbelievers﴾ [al-Baqarah 98]. He did not say "indeed Allah is an enemy to him," so that it would include every disbeliever, whether his disbelief consists of this enmity or of something else. Thus the ruling is generalized.

Alright, ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who are mindful of Him﴾. We take the benefits from these verses:

Alright, from these verses is the explanation that the People of the Book were divided in respect of trustworthiness into two groups.

* A student: The i'rab (grammatical analysis), sir?
* The Shaykh: Yes, yes, the i'rab. Alright: ﴿Yes! Whoever fulfils his covenant and is mindful of Allah﴾. ﴿Whoever fulfils his covenant﴾: ﴿man﴾ here is a conditional noun of firm conditioning (ism shart jazim), and ﴿awfa﴾ is
* The students: The conditional verb (fi'l al-shart).
* The Shaykh: The conditional verb. ﴿wa-ittaqa﴾ is conjoined to it, and the clause ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who are mindful of Him﴾...
* A student: The response of the condition (jawab al-shart).
* The Shaykh: The response of the condition. But you may ask: why is the response of the condition joined with the particle fa, when the condition in His saying ﴿Of them is one who, if you entrust him with a qintar, will return it to you﴾ and ﴿does not return it to you﴾ has no fa? The answer is that we say: when the response of the condition cannot be a verb for the condition, it must be joined with fa. Do you understand?
* A student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: When the response of the condition cannot be a verb for the condition, it must be joined with fa. Ibn Malik said:
"Join with fa, necessarily, a response that, if it were made the condition for (in) or others, would not be made a condition."
This is the rule: when the response of the condition cannot be a verb for the condition, it must be joined with fa. This is the rule, and its detailed explanation is in the well-known line:
"Nominal, imperative, with a fixed (past) verb, with mā, with lan, with qad, and with negation by tanfis."
These are seven cases. When the response of the condition is one of these seven, it must be joined with fa. Here the clause is ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who are mindful of Him﴾. Is it imperative?
* The students: Nominal.
* The Shaykh: Nominal, correct, because ﴿Allah loves those who are mindful of Him﴾ is a subject and predicate, but it is abrogated (mansukh) by (inna), so the clause here is nominal.

From the benefits of these verses:

First: the explanation that the People of the Book are divided into two groups: trustworthy and treacherous. Just as they are divided into two groups, believers and disbelievers. For example, 'Abdullah ibn Salam (may Allah be pleased with him) was among the rabbis of the Jews, and Allah blessed him with Islam, so he embraced it, is that so? And Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf was among the nobles of the Jews, but he remained in his disbelief and did not believe. So just as they are divided into disbeliever and believer, they are also divided into treacherous and trustworthy.

Alright. The Prophet (ﷺ) also made a transaction with the Jews, and he (ﷺ) died while his armour was pledged with a Jew. [Reported by al-Bukhari (2916) from the hadith of 'A'isha.] This shows that among the Jews there is one who is trustworthy, for otherwise, how would the Messenger (ﷺ) pledge his armour, which is one of the instruments of war, with this Jewish man? He was trustworthy.

* From the benefits of the verse: it is obligatory to be cautious of the People of the Book, the Jews and the Christians, because as long as they are divided into two groups, we do not know, when we deal with them, which of the two groups these people belong to. So we must be cautious, especially when it becomes clear to us that they are treacherous, people of betrayal, and that they never strive for our interests, as is the reality. In the present time, the reality is that the Jews and the Christians never strive for the good of the Muslims, but rather they strive...
* The students: For the belittling of the Muslims...
* The Shaykh: For the deception of the Muslims and corrupting them, so much so that when they see a state among the Muslim states heading towards Islam, they try to topple it and to restrict it economically, militarily and politically. This is something that everyone who reflects and considers current events knows.

So it is obligatory for us to be extremely cautious of the Jews and the Christians, and to know that each of the Jews and the Christians is an ally of the other, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿O you who believe, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies; they are allies of one another﴾ [al-Ma'idah 51]. However long the period, they are allies against a common enemy, and they are?
* The students: The Muslims.
* The Shaykh: The Muslims, yes indeed.
* And from the benefits of this verse: the permissibility of limiting oneself to an example so that what resembles it can be analogized to it, for He said: a qintar and a dinar. Alright, and if you entrusted him with a car or a child's toy, what is its like?
* The students: Like it, of course.
* The Shaykh: Yes. Among the People of the Book is one who, if you entrust him with a child's toy, will not return it to you unless you stand over him, and among them is one who, if you entrust him with a car, yes, and returns it to you safe. But Allah mentioned the dinar and the qintar by way of example.
* And from the benefits of these verses: the self-admiration of the People of the Book and their contempt for others, for they said: ﴿There is no blame upon us regarding the unlettered﴾, and this indicates self-conceit and contempt for others.
* And from their benefits: the People of the Book do not confine themselves to injustice and transgression and attribute it to their own whims, but rather they attribute it to the law of Allah. The proof of this is His saying the Exalted: ﴿and they speak falsehood about Allah﴾. So they speak falsehood about Allah in this and in other matters.
* And from the benefits of these verses: whoever fabricates lies about Allah concerning what he issues as a legal opinion (fatwa) or what he rules between people, there is a resemblance to whom? To the Jews and the Christians. There is a resemblance to the Jews and the Christians. Fabricating lies about Allah has occurred in this ummah too, whether in judging between people or in fatwas that are not rulings but are reports about the Shari'ah.
* And from the benefits of the noble verse: whoever fabricates lies about Allah knowingly is more sinful and more transgressive than one who does not know, and although each of them is in error, the deliberate one is not like the one who is not deliberate. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever lies about me deliberately, let him take his seat in the Fire." [Reported by al-Bukhari (1291) and Muslim (4/4) in the introduction, from the hadith of al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba.]
* And from the benefits of that: an indication that compound ignorance (al-jahl al-murakkab) is worse than simple ignorance. What is the reason for this? * The students: (...).
* The Shaykh: Because the one who lies while knowing is worse than the one who lies without knowing. The compound ignorant person who advances on a matter while knowing that he has no knowledge of it is worse than the person who thinks that this is knowledge.
* And from the benefits of the verses: praise for those who fulfil their covenants, as in His saying: ﴿Yes! Whoever fulfils his covenant and is mindful of Allah, then indeed Allah loves those who are mindful of Him﴾.
* And from their benefits: fulfilling the covenant is among the causes of Allah's love, because of His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who are mindful of Him﴾.
* And from their benefits also: that piety towards Allah in general is a cause of what? Of His love.
* And from the benefits of the verses: a refutation of the Ash'arites and others among the people of negation (ahl al-ta'til) who deny Allah's love, and who said: it is not permissible to affirm that Allah loves; if you affirm that Allah loves, you have attributed to Allah deficiency and defect, because this is a characteristic of created things; and because love exists only between two things that are similar. So how can you affirm that Allah loves? He affirmed it for Himself. They said: the intended meaning of affirming love is not love itself; what is meant is its necessary consequence, which is reward. So the meaning of ﴿He loves those who are mindful of Him﴾ is that He rewards the mindful. As for His loving them, no, not at all. The reason? They said:
* A student: Love is between two things...
* The Shaykh: Love exists only between two things that are similar; and because love is a attribute of created things, so it does not befit Allah, glory be to Him. But we say: this is distorting the words from their places, for the texts affirming Allah's love, that He loves and is loved, are almost countless: ﴿So Allah will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him﴾ [al-Ma'idah 54]. And love is other than reward. When Allah loves a servant, He rewards him; so reward is a necessary consequence of love. As for their saying that it exists only between similar things, this is not correct; for it has been established from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said about Uhud: "A mountain that loves us and we love it." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1481) and Muslim (1392/503) from the hadith of Abu Humayd al-Sa'idi; and al-Bukhari (3367) and Muslim (1365/462) from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik.] And where is the similarity between humans and a mountain? And it has been established by observable reality that some animals love humans. The she-camel loves her owner and comes to him from among the people and kneels beside him, yes. If anyone other than her owner came, she would strike him with her leg or bite him with her mouth. But her owner, she yearns for him and sits near him, and when she hears his voice even if she does not see him, she yearns. Likewise the rest of the animals, which is something observed, and this is love. Now the cat loves some members of the household and not others. If one of the household members she does not love comes, she runs away and hisses at him, yes. And if the one she loves comes, she approaches him and starts rubbing against him. This is something observed. What made her rub against this one and seek his affection, while she flees from the other and rebukes him?
* A student: Love.
* The Shaykh: Love. There is no doubt about it; this is something observed. So their claim that love exists only between two things is refuted by both hearing and reality. Hearing, by the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) about Uhud: "A mountain that loves us and we love it." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1481) and Muslim (1392/503) from the hadith of Abu Humayd al-Sa'idi; and al-Bukhari (3367) and Muslim (1365/462) from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik.] And reality needs no proof, for everyone knows it.

﴿Yes! Whoever fulfils his covenant and is mindful of Allah, then indeed Allah loves those who are mindful of Him﴾. Then He said: ﴿Indeed, those who sell﴾. Is the time up?
* A student: In His saying the Exalted: ﴿And among the People of the Book﴾, is this for diminution (taqlil)?
* The Shaykh: Eh?
* The student: For diminution, this?
* The Shaykh: No, this is for partitive (tab'id).
* The student: That is, some of them...
* The Shaykh: Some of them, yes. And the other part is ﴿Of them is one who, if you entrust him with a dinar, will not return it to you﴾. Alright, there is in fact a benefit in the verse: that one should monitor the treacherous person and keep watch over him. So if you give your wealth to someone who is not trustworthy, it is neither prudence nor resolve to leave him, but rather be on guard against him. And if this applies to entrusting wealth, entrusting honour is even more so. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) warned against entering upon women and said: "Beware of entering upon women." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, what about the in-law (al-hamu)?" He said: "The in-law is death." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5232) and Muslim (2172/20) from the hadith of 'Uqba ibn 'Amir al-Juhani.]
So whatever you fear may lead to the loss of trust, be keen to keep watch over it and to stand guard over it. For this reason He said: ﴿except as long as you stand over him﴾.
* A student: Now some calls come to illiteracy; they take their children out of schools and so on, and they argue from the "unlettered" (ummiyyin). Is this what is mentioned in the Qur'an?
* The Shaykh: What do you mean?
* The student: I mean there are calls to this, not widespread and not strong. Regarding arguing from illiteracy: we are an unlettered nation. Is this praise?
* The Shaykh: No, it is not praise. Illiteracy is a defect, which Allah the Exalted mentioned in a disparaging way, saying: ﴿And among them are unlettered people who know not the Book except wishful fancies﴾. He also alluded to it in His saying: ﴿It is He who raised among the unlettered a messenger from among themselves, who recites to them His verses and purifies them and teaches them the Book and wisdom, though before that they were in clear error﴾ [al-Jumu'ah 2]. Error is not seen by anyone as praise.
