But for the Messenger (ﷺ) it is a purification, because his being unlettered, yet bringing this great Book, shows that he is truthful, for an unlettered person could not produce a book like this, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And you did not recite any scripture before it, nor write it with your right hand; otherwise the falsifiers would have doubted﴾ [al-'Ankabut 48]. And we are "an unlettered nation," as the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) said, but after Allah opened to us and gave us knowledge and wisdom, we became a scholarly nation, not an unlettered nation.
If someone says: this contradicts you, since the Messenger said: "We are an unlettered nation," in Medina, after the Book had been revealed to him? We say: yes, he said it with regard to the crescent (hilal), with regard to the crescent. And with regard to the crescent, even after the conquests, we are an unlettered nation; we do not know the calculation of the lunar phases and do not know them. Yes indeed.
* A student: The second meaning, the interpretation of "unlettered" (ummiyyin), the second meaning you mentioned, does it have a basis?
* The Shaykh: It has a basis, because His saying the Exalted: ﴿And among them are unlettered people﴾ speaks of the People of the Book, for they do not know the Book except as wishful fancies, that is, mere recitation. And this, note well, contains a rebuke of those who attend to the wording of the Qur'an and neglect its meaning. Some people are so careful with the words of the Qur'an that you find them reaching the point of obsession in pronouncing certain letters, based on the idea that they want to articulate them according to tajwid, or according to the rules of tajwid as they understand them, but in meaning...
* The students: They do not know it...
* The Shaykh: They do not know it; they do not attend to it at all, so they are unlettered. For this reason Shaykh al-Islam (may Allah have mercy on him) denounced those who exaggerate in articulating letters and the qualities of letters while being heedless of the meanings of the Qur'an.
* * *

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verses 75–76 (part 3 of 3):**

* Student: ﴿Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price, those will have no share in the Hereafter. Allah will not speak to them, nor look at them on the Day of Resurrection, nor purify them, and for them is a painful punishment (77). And indeed, among them is a group who distort their tongues with the Scripture so that you may think it is from the Scripture, but it is not from the Scripture. They say, "It is from Allah," but it is not from Allah. And they speak falsehood about Allah while they know it (78). It is not for a human that Allah should give him the Scripture, the judgment and prophethood, and then he say to the people, "Be servants to me instead of Allah." Rather, [he would say], "Be devoted worshippers of the Lord by what you teach of the Scripture and by what you study" (79). Nor would He order you to take the angels and the prophets as lords. Would He order you to disbelief after you have submitted [to Him]? (80) And [mention] when Allah took the covenant of the prophets: "Whatever I have given you of Scripture and wisdom, and then there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you must believe in him and support him." He said, "Do you affirm and accept My commitment on this condition?" They said, "We affirm it." He said, "Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses" (81).﴾ [Al 'Imran 77–81].
* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price, those will have no share in the Hereafter. Allah will not speak to them, nor look at them on the Day of Resurrection, nor purify them, and for them is a painful punishment.﴾
I think we have already taken the benefits of what came before?
* Students: Yes, we have not finished, O Shaykh.
* Shaykh: We have not finished? Up to what?
* Students: (...) It is obligatory to punish the traitor. This is the last benefit.
* Shaykh: Yes indeed. Alright. Among the benefits of the previous verses, which is His saying the Exalted: ﴿And among the People of the Book is one who, if you entrust him with a great amount, will return it to you; and among them is one who, if you entrust him with a single dinar, will not return it to you unless you constantly stand over him.﴾
* Among its benefits: that these treacherous Jews have what they use to dress up their falsehood in their saying: ﴿That is because they say, "There is no blame upon us concerning the unlettered."﴾
* Among its benefits: the clarification of the Jews' conceit in themselves and their contempt for the servants of Allah.
* Among its benefits: that these Jews speak falsehood about Allah, fabricating it while knowing it is false, and this is worse than one who speaks falsehood while being ignorant.
* Among its benefits: that the Jews and others are equal in that whoever wrongs someone is liable to be held to account. For this reason, the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿and they speak falsehood about Allah﴾, and this indicates that the unlettered and others are equal in the prohibition of wronging them.
* Among the benefits of the two verses: that these Jews are liable to be held to account regarding the unlettered, whether they wrong their lives, their wealth or their honor, based on His saying the Exalted: ﴿Yes﴾; i.e., they are liable to be held to account regarding the unlettered, just as they are liable if some of them wrong others.
* Among its benefits: that fulfilling the covenant and piety are among the causes of the love of Allah, based on His saying: ﴿Yes, whoever fulfills his covenant and fears Allah, indeed Allah loves the righteous.﴾ Among its benefits: the affirmation of Allah's love, based on His saying: ﴿indeed Allah loves the righteous﴾. If Allah the Exalted loves the righteous, then another benefit follows from this, which is: the encouragement to fear Allah, because every person loves that Allah the Mighty and Majestic should love him. So if you want that, there is nothing for you but to establish the fear of Allah.

The love of Allah the Exalted is connected to the doer, connected to the deed, connected to time, and connected to place. It is connected to the doer, as in this verse: ﴿He loves the righteous﴾, and as in His saying the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in a row, as if they were a compact structure﴾ [As-Saff 4], and as in His saying: ﴿And do good; indeed, Allah loves the good-doers﴾ [Al-Baqarah 195].

It is connected to the deed: "The most beloved of deeds to Allah is prayer at its proper time"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (527) and Muslim (85/139), from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud.]].

It is connected to time: "There are no days in which righteous deeds are more beloved to Allah than these ten days"[[Narrated by Abu Dawud (2438), al-Tirmidhi (757), and Ibn Majah (1727), from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, and its origin is in al-Bukhari (969).]]. It may be said that this is connected to the deed and not to time.

It is connected to place: like the love of Allah the Exalted for Makkah, as reported from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said about it: "Indeed, you are the most beloved of the lands to Allah"[[Narrated by al-Bazzar (4690, 5095), from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, with the wording: "Indeed, you are the most beloved land of Allah to Allah," and its origin is in al-Tirmidhi (3926).]].

So the love of Allah is connected to the doer, the deed, the time, and the place.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verse 77 (part 1 of 2):

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, those who sell the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price﴾. This verse is connected to what precedes it, for this act is of the same kind as the previous act of those who "devour the wealth of people falsely." So this verse also contains a form of devouring the wealth of people falsely.

His saying: ﴿yashtaruna bi-'ahdi Allah wa-aymanihim thamanan qalilan﴾. It is said: yashtaruna, and it is said: yashru. What is the difference between them?
* Student: Yashtaruna?
* Shaykh: Yes, what is the difference between "yashtaruna" and "yashruna"?
* Student: In meaning?
* Shaykh: Yes, in meaning!
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Is there no difference between them? No, is there a difference?
* Student: Yashruna, meaning: they sell.
* Shaykh: Yashruna means they sell, and yashtaruna?
* Student: They buy.
* Shaykh: Yes. So the seller gives and the buyer takes. The evidence for this from the Qur'an is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So let those fight in the way of Allah who sell the life of this world for the Hereafter﴾ [an-Nisa' 74]. That is, they sell the life of this world for the Hereafter. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And among the people is one who sells himself seeking the pleasure of Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah 207], that is, he sells himself. As for ishtira' in the sense of taking, it is in verses like this one: ﴿Indeed, those who sell the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price﴾, meaning they take a small price in exchange for the covenant of Allah, so they break the covenant of Allah after its ratification and swear false oaths for the sake of worldly gain. His saying: ﴿bi-'ahdi Allah﴾ may mean what they covenanted with Allah upon, and it may mean what they covenanted with the creation upon. As for the first, i.e., what they covenanted with Allah upon, it is clear from the verse, because Allah intended the covenant made to Him. An example of it is that a scholar conceals his knowledge for the sake of some worldly gain, for Allah made a covenant with the scholars that they should make knowledge clear: ﴿And when Allah took the covenant of those who were given the Scripture, [saying], "You must make it clear to the people and not conceal it"﴾ [Al 'Imran 187]. If someone says: How did Allah take a covenant from the scholars when we do not know that any scholar concluded a covenant transaction with Allah? Have you known any scholar to have concluded a covenant transaction with Allah? No. But when Allah gave the scholars knowledge, their receiving it was a covenant that they would do what? Spread it and proclaim it among the creation. So if they do not do that, they have not fulfilled the covenant of Allah.

The second opinion: ﴿yashtaruna bi-'ahdi Allah﴾, i.e., with their covenant with people, and Allah attributed it to Himself as "the covenant of Allah" because He commanded its fulfillment. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And fulfill the covenant of Allah when you have taken it, and do not break oaths after their confirmation﴾ [an-Nahl 91]. So Allah called the covenant that believers make with others a covenant of what? A covenant to Him: ﴿And fulfill the covenant of Allah when you have taken it﴾, although they did not covenant with Allah but covenanted with the creation; yet He attributed it to Himself because He commanded its fulfillment, so it is correct to say: ﴿Fulfill the covenant of Allah﴾.

Therefore, ﴿Indeed, those who sell the covenant of Allah﴾ includes both meanings together: what they covenanted with Allah upon, or what they covenanted with the creation upon. On the first meaning, the sense is..
* Students: Clear..
* Shaykh: Clear and evident, with no difficulty. On the second there is some difficulty, since the covenant of created beings is called a covenant of Allah; but the answer to it is to say: Allah attributed it to Himself because He commanded its fulfillment.

His saying: ﴿wa-aymanihim﴾, meaning: they also sell, with their oaths, for a small price. The aymān are the plural of yamin, and it is swearing by Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. So they sell with the oath a small price, such as swearing to deny a right that is obligatory upon him, or swearing to claim a right that is not his. Understood? He swears to deny a right that is obligatory upon him, or swears to claim a right that is not his while lying. This is the yamin ghamus about which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever swears an oath in which he is a wicked liar, by which he takes the wealth of a Muslim man, will meet Allah while He is angry with him."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2356, 2357) and Muslim (138 / 220) from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud in a similar wording.]] I seek refuge in Allah! "He will meet Allah while He is angry with him." His saying: "wicked liar in it" means a liar. So this one has sold with the oath a small price. An example of an oath for a claim that is not his: that he claims against a person that he is owed one hundred riyals in his liability, and the person says: "I have nothing"; so the judge says to the claimant: "Do you have evidence?" He says: "No"; so the judge says to the denier: "Swear!" He says: "I will not swear; let him swear, and if he swears I will give it to him." So the claimant swears that Fulan owes him one hundred riyals while he is lying. This is swearing to what? To what thing?
* Student: A false claim.
* Shaykh: To a claim of what is not his. He swore that Fulan owes me one hundred riyals and was judged in his favor. This one has sold with the oath what?
* Students: A small price.
* Shaykh: A small price. Good. Swearing to deny what is obligatory upon him, such as? That he claims against a person that he is owed one hundred dirhams in his liability, and the defendant denies it while knowing that he owes Fulan one hundred dirhams, and swears that he owes him nothing. This is swearing to what? To denying what is obligatory upon him. In such a case, does the judge acquit the defendant? Yes, he acquits him and releases him, because he swore. So both men have sold with their oath a small price.

What is the small price in the example?
* Student: What you mentioned.
* Shaykh: Huh?
* Student: Did you mention it?
* Shaykh: How?
* Student: Did you mention the small price?
* Shaykh: What is the small price in the examples we mentioned?
Where did you reach? And where did you go?
* Student: It's there, I didn't go..
* Shaykh: How?
* Student: I say: it's there, I didn't go.
* Shaykh: And the heart?
* Student: It's there..
* Shaykh: In the chest?
* Shaykh: Good.. are you his neighbor?
* Student: A small price.
* Shaykh: Yes, in the two examples we mentioned?
* Student: In the first example, one hundred riyals..
* Shaykh: And the second?
* Student: And the second, one hundred riyals.
* Shaykh: May Allah make it easy for us that someone completes it; one who has nothing, one who has half; who has the whole? Yes.
* Student: In the first example one hundred riyals, and in the second example one hundred dirhams.
* Shaykh: Well done, excellent! In the first example one hundred riyals and the second one hundred dirhams, is it clear? Each of them sold with his oath a small price.
Good. Consider if someone said: Consider if I sold with this oath a large price, if he swore on a million?
* Students: It is small..
* Shaykh: Yes?
* Students: It is small..
* Shaykh: Either we say: it is small, because Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say: The enjoyment of this world is little﴾ [an-Nisa' 77]. Say: the enjoyment of the whole world is little. Yes. Or we say: whoever sells a little for a small price, likewise whoever sells for much; the point is that he has violated the sanctity of the oath for something of this world.

Good. He said: ﴿Those will have no share in the Hereafter﴾. ﴿Those﴾ refers to those who sold the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price. His saying: ﴿they will have no share in the Hereafter﴾, i.e., they have no portion in the Hereafter, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And he has in the Hereafter no share﴾ and ﴿Among the people is he who says, "Our Lord, give us in this world," and he has in the Hereafter no share﴾, i.e., portion; ﴿And among them is he who says, "Our Lord, give us in this world [that which is] good and in the Hereafter [that which is] good and protect us from the punishment of the Fire." Those will have a share﴾ [al-Baqarah 201, 202]. He said: ﴿Those will have a share﴾ in contrast to His saying ﴿no share﴾, which indicates that khalaq is portion. ﴿They will have no share in the Hereafter﴾, meaning in the Last Abode, which is the Day of Resurrection. The Day of Resurrection was called the last abode because it is the final stage of mankind, indeed of creation. A person has stages in this world: in the mother's womb, in the world, in the barzakh, and in the Hereafter. How many abodes?
* Students: Four..
* Shaykh: Four stages. In the first abode he has two states: a state of life and a state of death; before the soul is breathed into him he is dead, and after the soul is breathed into him he is alive. The final stage is what? The Hereafter: either to Paradise or to the Fire. Therefore He said: ﴿They will have no share in the Hereafter﴾. And in this world? It is possible that they have a share, it is possible that they have a portion of what they acquired; this small price they acquired may be a portion for them. Do you see, if he swore to a claim of a million riyals, there would come to him what? A million riyals; this is a portion in this world, but by Allah, it is a wretched portion.

If the world were worth the wing of a mosquito, He would not give to the disbeliever a drop of it.
But by Allah, it is more worthless to Him than the wing of a mosquito that cannot fly far.
All of the world is nothing.

﴿And Allah will not speak to them﴾, meaning and those also, Allah will not speak to them with speech of pleasure, but He may speak to them with speech of humiliation; for Allah, glorified and exalted, says to the people of the Fire: ﴿Remain in it and do not speak to Me﴾ [al-Mu'minun 108]. This is speech from Allah, but it is speech of rebuke, censure and humiliation; and what is negated is the speech of pleasure. ﴿And Allah will not speak to them or look at them﴾, meaning nor look at them with a look of mercy, compassion and tenderness; this is because they are not worthy of mercy. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿My mercy encompasses all things, so I will decree it﴾ for whom? ﴿For those who fear Me and give zakah﴾ [al-A'raf 156]. As for others, they have no share in the mercy of Allah in the Hereafter.

﴿Nor look at them on the Day of Resurrection﴾. The Day of Resurrection is the Day of Raising, and it was called the Day of Resurrection for three reasons. The first?
* Student: The rising of people from their graves.
* Shaykh: The rising of people from their graves; and the second?
* Student: The second is the day the witnesses stand.
* Shaykh: The day the witnesses stand; and the third?
* Student: The rising of the..
* Shaykh: Justice is established in it: ﴿And We will set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be wronged at all﴾ [al-Anbiya' 47].

﴿Nor purify them﴾, meaning He will not cleanse them from the effects of their filth with which they were defiled in the world; their sins remain, not forgiven, and we seek refuge in Allah! So there is no purification for them with Allah, because they are not worthy of purification.
﴿And He will not look at them﴾ [Al 'Imran 77], meaning nor look at them with a look of mercy, compassion and tenderness; this is because they are not worthy of mercy. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿My mercy encompasses all things, so I will decree it﴾ for whom? ﴿For those who fear Me and give zakah﴾ [al-A'raf 156]. As for others, they have no share in the mercy of Allah in the Hereafter.
﴿Nor look at them on the Day of Resurrection﴾. The Day of Resurrection is the Day of Raising, and it was called the Day of Resurrection for three reasons: The first?
* Student: The rising of people from their graves.
* Shaykh: The rising of people from their graves, and the second?
* Student: The day the witnesses stand.
* Shaykh: The day the witnesses stand, and the third?
* Student: The standing of the scale.
* Shaykh: Justice is established in it: ﴿And We will set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be wronged at all﴾ [al-Anbiya' 47].
﴿Nor purify them﴾ [Al 'Imran 77], meaning He will not cleanse them from the effects of their filth with which they were defiled in the world; their sins remain, not forgiven, and we seek refuge in Allah; so there is no purification for them with Allah, because they are not worthy of purification. This is why on the Day of Resurrection the wrongdoers will be called out: ﴿These are the ones who lied against their Lord. Unquestionably, the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers﴾ [Hud 18], meaning expulsion and removal from His mercy.

﴿And for them is a painful punishment﴾ [Al 'Imran 77]. ﴿For them is a punishment﴾: al-'adhab means retribution and punishment. ﴿Painful﴾ means causing pain; for fa'il in Arabic comes in several forms: it comes in the sense of fa'il (active), it comes in the sense of maf'ul (passive), and it comes in the sense of mufil (causative). Three. An example of its meaning as fa'il?
* Student: Rahim, sami', from (...).
* Shaykh: Sami', basir, rahim, all in the sense of fa'il. An example of its meaning as maf'ul?
* Student: Jarih.
* Shaykh: Qatil, jarih, dhabih and what resembles them. An example of its meaning as mufil is this verse: ﴿alim﴾ means mu'lim (painful). And from it is the saying of the poet:
Is it from Rayhana the caller, the one who hears, that keeps me awake, while my companions are asleep?
The evidence is his saying?
* Students: al-Sami'.
* Shaykh: al-Sami'. It does not mean the caller who hears, but the caller who makes hear, i.e., the caller who makes one hear. Yu'arriqni: it drives sleep away from me, while my companions are asleep.

So ﴿alim﴾ means mu'lim (painful). This is the meaning of the verse in its words. Now let us return to the grammatical analysis. We have a sentence emphasized with inna, and inna, as we know, puts the subject in the accusative and raises the predicate. So where is its noun? Its noun is alladhina, a relative pronoun, and its predicate is a sentence: ﴿Those will have no share in the Hereafter﴾. Ula'ika (those) is a subject; where is the predicate of ula'ika? The sentence: ﴿la khalaqa lahum fi al-akhirah﴾. So we now have a subject whose predicate is a sentence, and the predicate of that predicate, which is also a sentence, is correct? And His saying: ﴿la khalaqa lahum﴾, what put khalaq in the accusative?
* Student: La, the negation of the genus.
* Shaykh: The noun of la; la here is a negation of the genus, and its noun following it, if it is singular, is built on what it takes as accusative. Why do we not say it is built on fatha? Because it may be built on other than fatha; it may be built on ya', it may be built on kasra; so we say: on what it takes in the accusative. If you say: la rajulayni fi al-bayt, this is built on what?
* Students: On ya'.
* Shaykh: On ya', built on ya'. And if you say: la muslimat fi al-dar, this is built on what?
* Students: On kasra.
* Shaykh: On kasra, not on fatha. And if you say: la muslimin fi al-balad.
* Students: On ya'.
* Shaykh: On ya'. So we say: "on what it takes in the accusative" is better than saying "built on fatha." I said: if its noun is singular; how then is my statement correct when I gave the examples muslimin, muslimin and muslimat?

We say: the grammarians, like the jurists, have terminologies, each in its own context. The singular in the chapter of la is what is not idafa and not resembling idafa, so even if it is plural or dual; and in the chapter of i'rab, the singular is what is not dual and not plural, just as "rich" in the jurists' terminology differs: in zakat it has one definition, and in giving zakat it has another definition, and so on.

Regarding the readings of His saying: ﴿wa-la yanzuru ilayhim﴾ [Al 'Imran 77], there is a reading: ﴿ilayhum﴾, ﴿wa-la yanzuru ilayhum﴾. I have a rule on this written in my mushaf that we look at. It says: these are general regulations for the readings across the whole Qur'an: the pronoun huwa and hiya, the first with a dammah on the ha' and the second with a kasrah, huwa; it is said hiya according to the majority of reciters absolutely; al-Kisa'i, Qalun and Abu 'Amr made the ha' quiescent after waw, fa', and lam, like: fahuwa, fahiya, huwa, lahiya; ﴿Lahuwa al-Ghaniyyu﴾ [al-Hajj 64], ﴿Lahiya al-hayawan﴾ [al-'Ankabut 64]. So, by the grace of Allah, it is eloquent: ﴿And indeed the Last Abode, that is the Life﴾; the reading of the seven is permissible, and we say, according to the opinion of the majority: what?
* Students: ﴿lahiya﴾.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verse 77 (part 2 of 2):

* The Shaykh: ﴿لَهِيَ﴾ with a kasra on the ha'. Al-Kisa'i and Qalun also read it with a sukun in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿ثُمَّ هْوَ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ مِنَ الْمُحْضَرِينَ﴾ [al-Qasas: 61] ﴿ثُمَّ هْوَ﴾. The pronoun in (عليهِم) (ʿalayhim), (إليهِم) (ilayhim), (لديهِم) (ladayhim) has a kasra on the ha'. Hamzah read it with a damma on the ha': (عليهُم), (إليهُم), (لديهُم). Is the ha' kasra or not?* The students: (...).
* The Shaykh: ﴿غَيْرِ الْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ [al-Fatihah: 7], yes. ﴿وَمَا كُنْتَ لَدَيْهِمْ﴾ [Al 'Imran: 44] [Yusuf: 102], ﴿وَلَا يَنْظُرُ إِلَيْهِمْ﴾. He says: Hamzah read it with a damma on the ha'. Among that is His saying here: ﴿وَلَا يَنْظُرُ إِلَيْهُمْ﴾, ﴿غَيْرِ الْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهُمْ﴾, ﴿وَمَا كُنْتَ لَدَيْهُمْ إِذْ أَجْمَعُوا أَمْرَهُمْ وَهُمْ يَمْكُرُونَ﴾ [Yusuf: 102].
* Among the benefits of this verse: a warning to those who sell the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price. This applies to the scholars who conceal what Allah has revealed, out of flattery, out of deference, or for the sake of wealth, for they have sold the covenant of Allah for a small price, because Allah made a covenant with the scholars that they should make knowledge clear. We have already passed that scholars are of three types. Scholar of what?
* The student: Scholar of the world, scholar of the community, scholar of the religion.
* The Shaykh: Scholar of the religion, scholar of the world, and scholar of the community. Yes indeed, this is from your own pocket!
* A student: Scholar of the state, scholar of the community, and scholar of the faith-community (milla).
* The Shaykh: Correct. This is it: scholar of the community, scholar of the state, and scholar of the milla. The scholar of the milla does not sell the covenant of Allah for a small price; he makes the milla clear and does not care. The scholar of the state sells the signs of Allah for a small price, so that he may have standing with the state and perhaps be given wealth. The scholar of the community is the one who considers the community: he looks at what the community desires, and issues rulings accordingly or says what it wants to hear. What the community does not desire, he remains silent about. When he sees the community doing something not permissible in the Shari'ah, he remains silent about it; and if they ask him for something not permissible in the Shari'ah but he thinks it will please them, he agrees with them on it.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the prohibition of the perjurious oath (al-yamin al-ghamus), by His saying: ﴿وَأَيْمَانِهِمْ﴾ [Al 'Imran: 77].
* Among its benefits: that the perjurious oath and failing to fulfil the covenant of Allah are among the major sins (kaba'ir al-dhunub). That this is among the major sins is an additional matter beyond its being prohibited, because the major sin is greater than mere prohibition. What is the basis for its being a major sin? Because a threat is attached to it, and every sin to which a threat is attached is a major sin.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: whoever fulfils the covenant of Allah and swears truthfully will not be deprived of a share in the Hereafter. The reasoning: if the one who sells the covenant of Allah or his oath for a small price has no share (khalaq) in the Hereafter, then its opposite has a share. We took this line of inference from the saying of al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, regarding His saying: ﴿كَلَّا إِنَّهُمْ عَنْ رَبِّهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ لَمَحْجُوبُونَ﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 15]. He said: in this verse is evidence for the believers seeing Allah. How so? Because when these were veiled in a state of anger, it is evidence that the others will be seen in a state of pleasure.
* Among the benefits of the verse: the affirmation of the Hereafter, by His saying: ﴿لَا خَلَاقَ لَهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ﴾ [Al 'Imran: 77].
* Among its benefits: a person should make the Hereafter his aim, his goal and what he seeks. This is why He said: ﴿لَا خَلَاقَ لَهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ﴾ and did not say "in this world," because they may have a share in this world, but there is no good in it.
* Among the benefits of the verse: the affirmation of speech for Allah. The affirmation of speech for Allah, by His saying: ﴿وَلَا يُكَلِّمُهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ [Al 'Imran: 77]. The reasoning: if Allah did not speak, the negation of speech to these people would have no meaning. Were it not that He speaks, His not speaking to them would not be a punishment. Is that clear?
* Among its benefits: the speech of Allah is among His voluntary actions which He performs whenever He wills, because this speech which Allah negated He negated at a specific time, which is what? The Day of Resurrection. This shows that speech is among Allah's voluntary actions, which occur by His will, glorified and exalted is He.
* Among the benefits of the verse: that among the punishments of these people, along with their deprivation of a share in the Hereafter, is that Allah does not speak to them. This is among the greatest punishments, and we seek refuge with Allah. This is why looking at the Face of Allah is among the best, greatest and highest of rewards, indeed the ultimate of reward and virtue.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of Allah's seeing, by His saying: ﴿وَلَا يَنْظُرُ﴾ ﴿وَلَا يَنْظُرُ إِلَيْهِمْ﴾.
It is also evidence for the affirmation of the eye for Allah. Do you agree with this?
* Students: Yes.
* Other students: No.
* The Shaykh: No, you should not agree.
* Students: It does not necessarily follow.
* The Shaykh: Because seeing does not necessarily imply an eye, as we have said: we affirm Allah's hearing, and we do not affirm an ear. This is a matter you must be alert to, because speech does not necessarily imply the existence of a tongue and lips, hearing does not necessarily imply ears, and seeing does not necessarily imply eyes. Have you understood?
* The student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: On the Day of Resurrection the earth will relate its news. Does it have a tongue and lips? No. The pebbles glorified Allah in the presence of the Messenger ﷺ. Did they have a tongue and lips? No. Does the earth hear or not?
* Students: It hears.
* A student: It does not hear.
* The Shaykh: It hears.
* The student: Now?!
* The Shaykh: Now it hears, because it relates its news. Were it not hearing, it would not have spoken. When Allah said to the heavens and the earth: ﴿ائْتِيَا طَوْعًا أَوْ كَرْهًا﴾ [Fussilat: 11], they were addressed. Did they hear or not?
* Students: They heard.
* The Shaykh: They said: ﴿أَتَيْنَا طَائِعِينَ﴾. Do they have ears?
* Students: No.
* The Shaykh: They have no ears. Do they see or not?
* Students: They see.
* A student: They do not see.
* The Shaykh: ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ تُحَدِّثُ أَخْبَارَهَا﴾ [al-Zalzalah: 4], meaning: what was done upon it, as the early scholars said, what was done upon it of good and evil. What is done on the earth is either speech that is heard or action that is seen. So it sees. Nevertheless, we do not say it has two eyes. Therefore, affirming Allah's seeing does not necessarily entail affirming an eye, but the eye is established by other texts, for Allah has two eyes which do not resemble the eyes of creation. The evidence for this is His saying: ﴿وَلِتُصْنَعَ عَلَى عَيْنِي﴾ [Taha: 39], His saying: ﴿وَاصْبِرْ لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ فَإِنَّكَ بِأَعْيُنِنَا﴾ [al-Tur: 48], His saying: ﴿تَجْرِي بِأَعْيُنِنَا﴾ [al-Qamar: 14], and the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: «Indeed your Lord is not one-eyed»[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (4402) from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar.]]. So the affirmation of the two eyes is not from this verse, but from other evidences.
* A student: O Shaykh, here Allah negated speech.
* The Shaykh: What?
* The student: I mean: He negated speaking to these people. In another verse: ﴿قَالَ اخْسَئُوا فِيهَا وَلَا تُكَلِّمُونِ﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 108]. So here He speaks and here He negates speech? How do we reconcile them?
* The Shaykh: Have we reconciled them, O people?
* Students: Yes, we have.
* The Shaykh: We have reconciled them, but it seems that what happened to you has happened. Yes, ask now. What do you say? How do you reconcile ﴿وَلَا يُكَلِّمُهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ [al-Baqarah: 174] with another verse in which He said: ﴿اخْسَئُوا فِيهَا﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 108], so He spoke to them?
* The student: That speaking here means speaking of pleasure.
* The Shaykh: And there is the speaking of anger and rebuke, which is why He said: ﴿اخْسَئُوا فِيهَا﴾.
* The student: You mentioned, O Shaykh, you mentioned two real eyes.
* The Shaykh: What?
* The student: You affirmed two eyes for Allah, and Allah mentioned in the verses we cited ﴿تَجْرِي بِأَعْيُنِنَا﴾. How do we reconcile them?
* The Shaykh: The hadith. We brought the hadith so that the doubt you mentioned would be removed.
* The student: The reconciliation?
* The Shaykh: The plural is for glorification, like His saying: ﴿مِمَّا عَمِلَتْ أَيْدِينَا أَنْعَامًا﴾ [Ya Sin: 71], although Allah has only two hands.
* A student: O Shaykh, (...) does it refer to the angels?
* The Shaykh: What?
* The student: (أَعْيُننا) refers to the eyes of the angels?
* The Shaykh: By Allah, I do not know. If you say to someone: "I saw you with my eye," does that mean you saw with the eye of a seer?
* The student: No. ﴿بِأَعْيُنِنَا﴾ is the plural.
* The Shaykh: Or "with our eyes": ﴿تَجْرِي بِأَعْيُنِنَا﴾ is the eye of Allah, mighty and majestic.
* A student: O Shaykh, does this threat include one who swears regarding a commodity he has sold, regarding the price (...)?
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed. What do you say? If he swears that he bought this commodity for a hundred, and he is lying, does it fall under this? Yes, it does. This is why the Prophet ﷺ said in the hadith of Abu Dharr, narrated by Muslim: «Three whom Allah will not speak to on the Day of Resurrection, nor look at them, nor purify them, and for them is a painful punishment» — he repeated it three times — he said: "Who are they, O Messenger of Allah? They are ruined and lost." He said: «The one who lets his garment trail, the one who reminds of his giving, and the one who sells his goods by a false oath»[[Narrated by Muslim (106/171) from the hadith of Abu Dharr.]]. This, and we seek refuge with Allah, is included.
* A student: Is it permissible to entrust disbelievers with trusts?
* The Shaykh: What?
* The student: Is it permissible to entrust disbelievers with trusts?
* The Shaykh: By Allah, among them is the trustworthy and among them is the treacherous. But state affairs should not be entrusted to them. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَتَّخِذُوا بِطَانَةً مِنْ دُونِكُمْ لَا يَأْلُونَكُمْ خَبَالًا وَدُّوا مَا عَنِتُّمْ قَدْ بَدَتِ الْبَغْضَاءُ مِنْ أَفْوَاهِهِمْ وَمَا تُخْفِي صُدُورُهُمْ أَكْبَرُ قَدْ بَيَّنَّا لَكُمُ الْآيَاتِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ﴾ [Al 'Imran: 118]. For this reason, when Abu Musa wrote to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, saying: "We have a Christian man who is skilled in writing and accounts, and I want to make him in charge of the treasury (bayt al-mal)." He said: "Do not make him so. How would you entrust someone whom Allah has branded a traitor?" He wrote to him a second time, saying: "O Commander of the Believers, the man is skilled and we are in need of him." 'Umar replied: "From the servant of Allah, the Commander of the Believers 'Umar ibn al-Khattab: Peace be upon you. The Christian has died. Peace." [[Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (20409) from the hadith of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, in similar wording.]] "The Christian has died." If he dies, will you revive him so that he can write for you? Do not revive him; assume he has died and it is over. For this reason Shaykh al-Islam mentioned in several places in his books that it is not permissible for non-Muslims to be entrusted with the secrets of the Muslims, that this is betrayal, and that this is a danger to the Islamic state. I think in the twentieth volume he mentioned wondrous things, may Allah have mercy on him, about the danger of these people to the Islamic community if they are given charge of state secrets. He was truthful, there is no doubt about this; there is no doubt they are enemies, whatever their circumstances.
* A student: May Allah reward you well, O Shaykh. What about training on some weapons, meaning that only some disbelievers know them?
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed. This does not fall under the matter, because these are sensory and known matters. This does not fall under it. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ hired a polytheist man to guide him on the path during the migration.
* * *
I seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَشْتَرُونَ بِعَهْدِ اللَّهِ وَأَيْمَانِهِمْ ثَمَنًا قَلِيلًا أُولَئِكَ لَا خَلَاقَ لَهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ وَلَا يُكَلِّمُهُمُ اللَّهُ وَلَا يَنْظُرُ إِلَيْهِمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ وَلَا يُزَكِّيهِمْ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾ [Al 'Imran: 77].
* We have mentioned among the benefits of this noble verse: that those who sell the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price, Allah will not look at them on the Day of Resurrection. What is meant is the special look; as for the general look, nothing is hidden from His sight.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of the Day of Resurrection, and that it is true, by His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ﴾.
* Among its benefits: the affirmation of what this attribute includes, namely that justice will be established on that day, that people will stand from their graves before the Lord of the worlds, and that witnesses will be brought forward.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse also: that those who sell the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price, Allah will not purify them, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter. This is why the phrase ﴿وَلَا يُزَكِّيهِمْ﴾ came after His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ﴾. Allah does not purify them in this world; rather He makes their defects manifest and exposes them in this world until people know them, and know the fall of their integrity and the loss of their good standing. Likewise, Allah will not purify them on the Day of Resurrection; He will not accept from them any repentance or ransom.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of punishment by His saying: ﴿وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾. Punishment may be in this world or in the Hereafter, and that which occurs in this world may be by the act of Allah, or by the act of the servants of Allah who are His party.
Among examples of what occurs at the hands of the servants of Allah is His saying: ﴿قَاتِلُوهُمْ يُعَذِّبْهُمُ اللَّهُ بِأَيْدِيكُمْ﴾ [al-Tawbah: 14], and what befell the disbelievers at the Battle of Badr and others.
Among what is by the act of Allah is what happened on the day of the Confederates (al-Ahzab), when the confederates dispersed from Madinah not by the act of the Messenger ﷺ and his Companions, but by the wind and the armies that Allah sent against them.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that buying a small price with the covenant of Allah and an oath is among the major sins, for this oath is the perjurious oath (al-yamin al-ghamus), which plunges its swearer into sin, and then into the Fire.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on Surah 3, verses 78–80 (part 1 of 3):

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And indeed, among them is a group who distort their tongues with the Book﴾ [Aal 'Imran 78].

﴿And indeed, among them﴾: The pronoun refers to the People of the Book, because the verses share one context. At the beginning of the verses He said: ﴿And among the People of the Book is one who, if you entrust him with a qintar, will return it to you﴾ [Aal 'Imran 75]. Here He said: ﴿And indeed, among them is a group who distort their tongues with the Book﴾. Al-layy (لَيّ) means turning or twisting, as in "layy al-habl" (twisting the rope). So ﴿they distort their tongues﴾ means they turn them aside. The layy here includes both verbal layy and meaningful layy.

Verbal layy: Sometimes they bring speech of their own and recite it in the manner of revealed Scripture, so that whoever hears it among the people imagines that it is from the revealed Book. That is, they inflect the speech the way the Qur'an is inflected, so the listener thinks it is from Allah. This is one type.

The second type of verbal layy is tahrif (distortion) of the words themselves, as some innovators distorted the saying of Allah: ﴿And Allah spoke to Musa with direct speech﴾ [an-Nisa' 164], by reading it as "wa kallama Allaha Musa taklima" (and Allah was spoken to by Musa with direct speech), intending that the speaking be from Musa to Allah. As for meaningful tahrif, it is interpreting the speech with other than what Allah intended by it. One says, "The meaning of the verse is such-and-such," contrary to what Allah intended.

So layy has three divisions. The first is layy in wording that does not affect the revealed Book itself, but rather produces speech of one's own that is chanted as if it were revealed Scripture, so that the listener thinks it is from Allah.

The second is verbal layy that involves altering the form of the revealed Book, which is called verbal tahrif.

The third is meaningful layy, where one says, "The meaning of the verse is such-and-such." There is no doubt that this is layy of the tongue. ﴿They distort their tongues with the Book﴾, because the Book means such-and-such while they say, "What is meant is such-and-such."

Who is this group? We say they are the distorters who alter words from their places.

﴿They distort their tongues with the Book so that you may think it is from the Book﴾ [Aal 'Imran 78]. The lam here may be the lam of causation (lam at-ta'lil) or the lam of consequence (lam al-'aqibah). The difference is that the lam of causation indicates the motive for the action, while the lam of consequence indicates the outcome of the action. For example, if you say, "I came to read," the lam is for what?

* Students: For consequence.
* A student: For causation.
* The Shaykh: The lam is for causation, meaning that what motivated my coming was reading. And if you say, "I hunted this game to become a torment for me."
* Students: For consequence.
* The Shaykh: That is a consequence. From this is the saying of Allah: ﴿So the family of Pharaoh picked him up, that he might become for them an enemy and a grief﴾ [al-Qasas 8]. The family of Pharaoh did not pick him up for this reason at all. Had they known he would become an enemy and a grief to them, they would not have picked him up.

Here, ﴿so that you may think﴾. Does the meaning mean that they distort their tongues with the Book in order to mislead you, so that you think it is from Allah? Or that they distort their tongues with the Book without intending it, so that you think it is from Allah?

The apparent meaning is the first: they do this in order to make the people imagine that it is from Allah. ﴿so that you may think it is from the Book﴾, that is, so that you may suppose it is from the revealed Book, while it is from the distorted Book in which layy and alteration have occurred.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And it is not from the Book﴾ [Aal 'Imran 78]. This is a refutation of what they intended by their twisting of their tongues with the Book, since the one who hears might think it is from the Book. So Allah said: ﴿And it is not from the Book﴾.

Which Book is referred to here? It is the Torah if this layy comes from the Jews, and the Gospel if this layy comes from the Christians. "Kitab" (the Book), as you know, is a generic noun that applies to both.

﴿And they say, "It is from Allah"﴾. The pronoun in ﴿it﴾ refers to what they twisted their tongues with from the Book. ﴿They say: it is from Allah.﴾ Allah refuted this claim by saying: ﴿And it is not from Allah﴾ [Aal 'Imran 78].

Therefore it is good for the reader to pause and say, for example, ﴿so that you may think it is from the Book﴾, then say, ﴿And it is not from the Book﴾, and ﴿And they say it is from Allah﴾, then pause and say, ﴿And it is not from Allah﴾.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And they say about Allah what is false﴾ [Aal 'Imran 78]. They also say about Allah what is false, whether through verbal distortion or meaningful distortion.

His saying, ﴿they say about Allah what is false﴾, has a parallel that we have mentioned before. We said that ﴿they say﴾ here is implicitly taken to mean "they fabricate" (yaftaruna), which is why it takes ʿalā (about/against). ﴿They say about Allah what is false﴾ means they say falsehood about Allah in His rulings, in His actions, in His names, in His attributes, and in everything related to Him, glory be to Him. For example, they said, "The hand of Allah is chained," and they lied. They said, "Allah is poor," and they lied. They said, "Allah became tired and rested," and they lied. Whatever they attributed to Allah that is unbefitting of Him, they are liars in it.

His saying, ﴿while they know﴾ [Aal 'Imran 78], is a circumstantial clause (jumlah haliyyah), a ḥāl from the waw in ﴿they say﴾. That is, they say falsehood while knowing it is false. This makes their sin greater than that of one who says falsehood without knowing it is false.

Grammatical analysis (i'rab) of this verse: First, His saying ﴿And indeed, among them is a group﴾ [Aal 'Imran 78]: this sentence is emphasized. Emphasized by how many emphasizers?

* A student: The lam.
* The Shaykh: And what else?
* The student: Inna.
* The Shaykh: Inna. ﴿a group﴾: what put "fariqan" in the accusative?
* A student: The lam, Shaykh.
* The Shaykh: The lam? It does not put things in the accusative, I suppose you are not one of the sons of Sibawayh! Alright, go on.
* The student: It is accusative because it is the delayed ism of inna.
* The Shaykh: The delayed ism of inna, correct. And His saying ﴿so that you may think it﴾: why was the nun deleted?
* A student: Because the preposition lam is followed by a verb, and there must be an implied an before it, to be interpreted as a verbal noun, and an (the subjunctive particle) when it enters a present-tense verb, and there is something at the end, then after it the verb takes the accusative by deleting the nun.
* The Shaykh: That was long!
* The student: Because it is an (the particle "an") in the accusative...
* The Shaykh: So, because it is in the accusative.
* The student: In the accusative.
* The Shaykh: The nun was deleted because it is in the accusative, its governor being the implied an after the lam. Is that right?
* The student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: What kind of verb is this?
* The student: A verb with something before its last letter.
* The Shaykh: No.
* The student: A present-tense verb, a present-tense verb.
* The Shaykh: ﴿tahsabuhu﴾.
* The student: A present-tense verb.
* The Shaykh: Yes, of what type of verb?
* The student: Of the pattern "hasiba - yahsibu."
* The Shaykh: No.
* The student: Of the pattern of the ifti'al form.
* Another student: One of the five verbs.
* The Shaykh: One of the five verbs.
* The student: I had thought it was something else.
* The Shaykh: That is why the nun was deleted. It has two readings: ﴿litahsibuhu﴾ and ﴿litahsabuhu﴾. His saying ﴿And it is not from the Book﴾: what is this "ma"?
* The student: Negative.
* The Shaykh: And it has a specific name among the grammarians. What is it?
* The student: "Ma" is negative.
* The Shaykh: What is it?
* A student: Ma al-Hijaziyyah (the Hijazi ma).
* The Shaykh: Yes, "ma" is Hijazi. Where is its ism?
* The student: Its ism is a pronoun.
* The Shaykh: Where is it? Is it hidden? A pronoun is only hidden in a verb or what is equivalent to one.
* A student: Huwa.
* The Shaykh: Where is it?
* The student: ﴿And it is not﴾, "huwa".
* The Shaykh: ﴿And it is not huwa﴾, well done. His saying ﴿And they say, "It is from Allah," and it is not from Allah﴾: the sentence ﴿it is from Allah﴾ has what place in grammar?
* The student: What?
* The Shaykh: ﴿And they say, "It is from Allah"﴾.
* The student: In the accusative position as the object of the saying (maqul al-qawl).
* The Shaykh: In the accusative position as the object of the saying. ﴿falsehood﴾: in ﴿And they say about Allah falsehood﴾, what is its place in grammar?
* The student: Accusative.
* The Shaykh: As what?
* The student: As an object of "yaftaruna" (fabricate).
* The Shaykh: We do not have "yaftaruna" here.
* The student: Because it is the object of the saying, in the accusative position as the object of (...).
* The Shaykh: The object of ﴿they say﴾?
* The student: Yes, because it implies the meaning of saying.
* The Shaykh: Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿It is not for any human that Allah should give him the Book and the wisdom and prophethood, and then he would say to the people, "Be servants to me rather than Allah." Rather, [he would say], "Be masters (rabbaniyyin) by what you teach of the Book and by what you study"﴾ to the end [Aal 'Imran 79].

His saying ﴿It is not for any human﴾: the phrase "ma kana" (it is not) is used for something impossible. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And your Lord was not forgetful﴾ [Maryam 64]. This is something impossible for Him to forget, impossible by law and impossible by decree. So His saying ﴿It is not for any human that Allah should give him the Book and the wisdom and prophethood, and then he would say...﴾ is impossible by law and by decree. ﴿And your Lord was not forgetful﴾ is impossible by decree, indeed impossible as an attribute, since it is inconceivable that decree would bring it about; it is impossible for Allah to be forgetful or to forget. ﴿And Allah would not punish them while you are among them﴾ [al-Anfal 33] is impossible by law. Even if He willed to punish them while you were among them, He would punish them, but it is impossible by law.

Here, ﴿It is not for any human﴾: we said it is impossible by law and by decree. "Bashar" (human) means a person from the children of Adam. He was named bashar because of the visibility of his skin (bashrah), since the human skin is apparent and exposed, without hair, wool, fur, feathers, or fins. It is also said he was named bashar because the trace of good news (bushra) appears on him when he is informed of something that pleases him. There is no barrier to the word having been named for both reasons. The wisdom in Allah making the human's skin exposed is so that the human knows he needs physical clothing, and then moves from that to knowing that he needs spiritual clothing, which is piety, and that he needs to take the means that cover him inwardly just as he takes the means that cover him outwardly. This is from the wisdom of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

He says: ﴿It is not for any human﴾, meaning for any one of mankind, any person, ﴿that Allah should give him the Book and the wisdom and prophethood﴾. ﴿That Allah should give him the Book﴾, that is, give it to him, a legislative giving, and likewise a decreed giving. Then ﴿and the wisdom﴾: wisdom meaning judgment by what he has been given of the Book, just as Allah said to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: ﴿And judge between them by what Allah has revealed﴾ [al-Ma'idah 49].

﴿And prophethood﴾ means the reporting of revelation. The reason He said "and prophethood" along with "that Allah should give him the Book" is that giving the Book is sometimes applied to those to whom it was sent, not to the one who was sent with it, as in the saying of Allah: ﴿Those to whom We gave the Book recognize it as they recognize their own sons﴾ [al-Baqarah 146], and ﴿Those to whom We gave the Book recite it with its true recitation; they believe in it﴾ [al-Baqarah 121]. So those who were given the Book here, are they prophets? It is a known matter, or is it a foreign question? ﴿Those to whom We gave the Book recognize it as they recognize their own sons﴾: are they prophets?

* The students: They are not prophets.
* The Shaykh: Then it does not follow that whoever is given the Book is a prophet. That is why He said "and prophethood", lest someone imagine that those given the Book are those to whom it was sent. The one given the Book here is the one who was sent with the Book, not the one to whom it was sent, rather the one who was sent with the Book to others.

His saying ﴿prophethood﴾ with a shaddah on the waw: either it is from (nabwah), meaning elevation, and in that case the waw is original, because the rank of the prophet is the highest of created beings. Allah said: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger, those are with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor of the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous﴾ [an-Nisa' 69]. Or the waw is a softened hamza, and the original is "nubu'ah," in which case it is derived from (naba'), meaning news. This is because the Messenger is one who is informed (munba') by Allah the Mighty and Majestic, and one who informs (munbi') those to whom he is sent, telling them, giving them good news, and warning them.

﴿It is not for any human that Allah should give him the Book and the wisdom and prophethood﴾: the sentence has not ended yet, but the impossible thing is ﴿then he would say to the people, "Be servants to me rather than Allah"﴾ [Aal 'Imran 79]. This is the impossible thing, and it is what the negation falls upon. That is: it is not for any human that Allah should give him the Book with the message, and the judgment among people by this Book, and prophethood and exaltation, and then after all this he would say to the people, "Be servants to me rather than Allah." That is, "Be worshippers of me, worship me rather than Allah, worship me by obedience, prostrate to me, bow to me, sacrifice to me," and the like. This is impossible, because the one whom Allah has given the Book, wisdom, and prophethood came for the opposite of these things, to eradicate this matter, not to call people to it.

His saying ﴿Be servants to me rather than Allah﴾: if someone asks, does it mean "worship me and do not worship Allah," or does it mean "worship me even if you also worship Allah"?

* Students: It includes both.
* The Shaykh: Because a person is either one who worships Allah alone, or one who worships other than Him, or one who worships Allah along with another. Do you understand? As for the one who worships Allah alone, this is sincere. And the one who worships other than Allah, rather than Allah, what is this?
* Students: A polytheist.
* The Shaykh: A polytheist. Or we say: one who is arrogant toward worshipping Allah and devoted to another. And the one who worships Allah and another, this is a polytheist. So we say: whoever calls people to worship himself alone, rather than Allah, has called them to worship himself rather than Allah. This is clear. And whoever calls people to worship himself and does not forbid them from worshipping Allah, the reality of his call is that he has called people to worship him rather than Allah. How so? Because Allah is free of need for the worship of these people. So if they associate others with Allah, worship becomes purely for whom? For other than Allah. It becomes purely for other than Allah.

Because of the saying of Allah in the sacred hadith: "I am the most self-sufficient of partners in regard to partnership. Whoever does a deed in which he associates another with Me, I abandon him and his association." [Narrated by Muslim (2985/46) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.] With this, the difficulty in His saying ﴿Be servants to me rather than Allah﴾ is removed. We say: has anyone said to people, "Worship me and do not worship Allah"? Or is this the meaning intended by this verse? We say: no, it is not specific. The verse includes both aspects: it includes whoever calls to the worship of himself and that Allah not be worshipped, and whoever calls to the worship of himself even if Allah is worshipped alongside him. The first is clear, as he says, "Worship me and do not worship Allah." The second: it follows from association that worship is not for Allah, because when a person associates anyone with Allah, his worship of Allah is void, whether it exists or not. And it is possible that the meaning of "dun" (rather than/besides) here is "siwa" (other than): ﴿servants to me rather than Allah﴾, meaning "from other than Him," and the intent is not to prohibit combining, but rather "from other than Him" meaning "along with Him." If this interpretation is correct, there is no difficulty. If it is not correct, you have known the difficulty and its answer.

He said: ﴿But rather, be masters (rabbaniyyin)﴾ [Aal 'Imran 79]. This "but" is a corrective conjunction (istidrak) that stands in contrast to the negation with which the verse opens: ﴿It is not for any human that Allah should give him...﴾ ﴿and then he would say...﴾ ﴿But rather...﴾. Therefore there must be an omission, and its implied form is: "But rather he would say to the people: be masters." That is, he would say to people: be masters, be masters in a legislative manner or in a decreed manner?

* Students: Legislative.

Sheikh: Legally (shar'iyyan), because he does not have the power to say to them "Be" in the sense of divine decree (kawnan qadariyyan), but he has the power to command them legally to be rabbaniyyin. "Rabbaniyyin" is a nisba to the Lord (rabb) and a nisba to upbringing (tarbiyah). So the rabbani is one who is a servant of the Lord, Mighty and Majestic; the rabbani is one who trains people upon the law of God through knowledge, calling to God, worship and conduct. Thus the rabbani is attributed both to lordship (rububiyyah) and to upbringing (tarbiyah). So, considering it as attached to God?

Students: Lordship (rububiyyah).

Sheikh: Lordship. And considering it as attached to reform?

Students: Upbringing (tarbiyah).

Sheikh: Upbringing. "But be rabbaniyyin" means: sincere devotees of the Lord, worshipping Him. And "be rabbaniyyin" means: trainers of people according to what the Sharia requires.

"Because you have been teaching the Book" (Al 'Imran 79). The "ba'" here indicates causation; i.e., because of your teaching of the Book. "Because you have been teaching the Book": the one who teaches the Book is a trainer, and for this reason, whenever a person's students multiply, his training of people increases; because it is expected of the teacher that he not be a teacher of people in a merely theoretical, argumentative way, since that can be grasped from books. Rather, he should teach them both theoretically and through training. This is the guidance of the Prophet (ﷺ) with his companions. If you look at the Prophetic biography (sirah), you will find how the Messenger (ﷺ) taught people in a manner joined with and accompanied by training. If you contemplate the biographies of the Rightly Guided Caliphs, you will find them likewise. Look, for example, at 'Umar ibn al-Khattab raising the punishment for wine to eighty to deter people, and preventing the one who divorces three times from returning to his wife in order to deter people. The truth is that the scholar is not the one who fills people's minds with knowledge, or the teacher is not the one who fills people's minds with knowledge; rather, the one who fills their thoughts or minds with knowledge and their character with training.

* * *

Student: "It is not for a human being that Allah should give him the Book, the wisdom and the prophethood and then he should say to the people, 'Be servants of me rather than of Allah.' But rather, [he will say], 'Be rabbaniyyin by what you have been teaching of the Book and by what you have been studying' (79). And He would not order you to take the angels and the prophets as lords. Would He order you to disbelieve after you have submitted [to Him]? (80). And [mention] when Allah took the covenant of the prophets: 'Whatever I have given you of Book and wisdom and then there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you must believe in him and support him.' He said, 'Do you acknowledge and accept My commitment upon that?' They said, 'We acknowledge it.' He said, 'Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses.' (81). So whoever turns away after that — those are the defiantly disobedient.' [Al 'Imran 79–82]

Sheikh: We seek refuge in Allah from Satan, the accursed. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: "And indeed, among them is a party who distort their tongues with the Book so that you may think it is from the Book" (Al 'Imran 78). The pronoun in His saying "minhum" (among them) refers to?

Student: To the People of the Book.

Sheikh: To the People of the Book. What is the evidence?

Student: Because they are the ones who altered the Book.

Sheikh: But is there nothing in the context that indicates it?

Student: At the beginning of the verses He said: "And among the People of the Book is one who, if you entrust him with a qintar..." (Al 'Imran 75)?

Sheikh: "And among the People of the Book is one who, if you entrust him..." Yes, correct. What made "fariqan" accusative?

Student: Inna.

Sheikh: (Inna) as what? (Inna) what does it do?

Student: It makes the subject accusative and the predicate nominative.

Sheikh: Then as what?

Student: Accusative, subject.

Sheikh: How is it a subject if it were a nominative subject?

Student: It makes the subject accusative; the noun of (inna) is delayed.

Sheikh: Yes, as the delayed noun of (inna). His saying: "yalwuna alsinatahum bil-kitab" — what is this twisting (layy)? Or what is this layy?

Student: Layy is divided into two kinds: we said it is verbal layy and semantic layy.

Sheikh: Then what is meant by semantic layy?

Student: It is twisting: that they twist the verses of the Book with their tongues.

Sheikh: What?

Student: We said they change the meanings of the Book.

Sheikh: Changing the meaning; Allah called changing the meaning "layy" because it turns the speech away from what is intended by it.

Sheikh: Now, verbal change?

Student: It is changing the wording itself.

Sheikh: That is, it has only one aspect?

Student: Yes, no, layy of the wording includes the meaning.

Sheikh: No.

Student: Verbal layy may be by producing a sound like the Qur'an's, chanting it, deceiving the listener.

Sheikh: And the speech is from his own (words).

Student: And the speech is from his own, and it deceives the listener into thinking it is the speech of Allah, Glorified and Exalted; or perhaps he changes the very wording, altering it and changing another word, and says: this is from Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Sheikh: Correct. So at times layy means he brings speech from himself and attributes it to Allah, and at times he brings layy with the Book itself but distorts its wording, substituting and altering. The "lam" in His saying "li-tahsabuhu" — what is this lam?

Student: The lam of causation.

Sheikh: Of causation. And in "tahsabuhu," is there a reading?

Student: "Li-tahsabuhu," the second reading?

Sheikh: Yes.

Student: (...).

Sheikh: No.

Student: (tahsibuhu).

Sheikh: (tahsibuhu) with kasra; i.e., with the sin vowelled with kasra, and what?

Student: And with fatha.

Sheikh: And with fatha on the sin. His saying: "It is not for a human being that Allah should give him the Book, the wisdom and the prophethood and then he should say to the people..." (Al 'Imran 79) — on what does the prohibition fall?

Student: On those who have knowledge.

Sheikh: On the first, or the second, or both together?

Student: On those who (...) Allah, Mighty and Majestic (...).

Sheikh: That is, is what is impossible that a human says to people, "Be servants of me besides Allah," or that Allah gives them the Book, wisdom and prophethood, or that he says to the people, "Be servants of me" while being given wisdom and prophethood?

Student: The last.

Sheikh: The last. So the prohibition falls on the combination of both states. Are you all understanding, O people?

Students: Yes.

Sheikh: His saying: "But be rabbaniyyin" — the sentence "wa-lakin kunu rabbaniyyin" — what is its grammatical position?

Student: "Kunu rabbaniyyin," its grammatical position is conjoined...

Sheikh: "Kunu rabbaniyyin" alone — what is its grammatical position?

Student: In the accusative position as the object of the saying.

Sheikh: Where is the saying?

Student: "Wa-lakin yaqulu" (but he says), with an implied element: "but they say: be rabbaniyyin."

Sheikh: Yes, "but he says: be rabbaniyyin." Who is the rabbani?

Student: The rabbani is sometimes attributed to Allah and sometimes to the trainer. If it is attributed to Allah, the person is rabbani by his obedience to Allah and his worship; and if it is attributed to training, i.e., they train people by the law of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Sheikh: Yes, so rabbani is either from lordship or from training. If it is from lordship, what is its meaning?

Student: If from lordship, they are servants of Allah, sincere, obedient to Him, acting by His law.

Sheikh: And if from training?

Student: That is, they train people by the law of Allah.

Sheikh: Correct. And His saying: "Because you have been teaching the Book": He said, "bima kuntum tu'allimuna" — the "ba'" here is causal and "ma" is masdariyyah, i.e., "by your being teachers." If someone asks: what is the sign of masdariyyah "ma"? We say: its sign is that what follows it can be converted into a verbal noun; it and what follows it are preceded by a verbal noun, so what follows is a verbal noun. So "bima kuntum" means "by your being," and "tu'allimuna" has two readings: one is "tu'allimuna," i.e., you teach others, from teaching; and another reading: "bima kuntum ta'lamuna," i.e., you know yourselves. Which is more general, "tu'allimuna" or "ta'lamuna"?

Students: "Tu'allimuna."

Sheikh: "Tu'allimuna," because one teaches only one who knows; yet nevertheless we say that each of the two readings indicates a meaning necessarily implied by the other, so the meaning is "by what you knew and taught."

And His saying: "al-Kitab" is an object with the doubled form; i.e., "tu'allimuna," but it is a single object and the second object is omitted, i.e., "by what you taught people the Book." As for the reading "ta'lamuna," "al-Kitab" is the sole object and it does not take two objects.

And His saying: "tu'allimuna al-Kitab": what is meant by "al-Kitab" is the genus, to include the Torah and the Gospel, part of them and all of them.

"Wa-bima kuntum tadrusuna": i.e., by what you used to read; by what you knew and studied, you read it. So for you there is verbal knowledge of the Book and semantic knowledge; verbal knowledge comes through study, and semantic knowledge through knowledge and teaching. And regarding "bima kuntum tadrusuna," we say what we said about what precedes it: the "ba'" is causal and "ma" is masdariyyah.

Then He said: "wa-la yamurakum" (Al 'Imran 80). There are two readings: "wa-la yamurukum" and "wa-la yamurakum."

As for the accusative reading "wa-la yamurakum," it is conjoined to His saying: "thumma yaqulu lil-nas" (79), meaning: it is not for a human that Allah give him the Book, wisdom and prophethood, then He commands you to take the angels as lords. So it is conjoined to "thumma yaqulu lil-nas."

As for the reading with sukun, the fatha is presumed on it, because the sukun here is not an inflectional sukun but a sukun of lightening, lightening of pronunciation; because the saying "wa-la yamurkum" is lighter than "wa-la yamurakum." Do you agree with this?

Students: Yes.

Sheikh: "Wa-la yamurkum" is lighter than "wa-la yamurakum," so the sukun here is not inflectional but lightening. Hence we say: it is accusative in both readings, but in the fatha reading it is accusative by the original fatha, and in the sukun reading by a presumed fatha on its end, and it is made sukun for lightness.

"Wa-la yamurakum an tattakhidhu al-mala'ikata wal-nabiyyina arbaban" (80): meaning, it is not for him to command you to take the angels and prophets as lords, just as he does not say to you, "Be servants of me," for this is utterly impossible: that Allah bestow upon someone the Book and wisdom, then command people to worship him, or say: worship the angels and prophets, take them as lords. This is utterly impossible.

As for "al-mala'ikah": angels is the plural of (malak), and its origin is (ma'lak) from (al-alukah), which means message. It became, by morphological alteration, (ma'lak): the hamza was moved to the place of the lam and the lam was moved to the place of the hamza. The origin of (al-alukah) is message, and for this Allah said: "Who makes the angels messengers" (Fatir 1).

A second time we say: angels is the plural of (malak), originally from (al-alukah), meaning message; so its origin is (ma'lak). Then the hamza was transposed to the place of the lam and the lam to the place of the hamza, so it became (ma'lak), and the plural of ma'lak is mala'ik, and the ta' is the verbal feminine marker. Then (ma'lak) was also lightened by deleting the hamza, so it became malak.

The angels are an unseen world, created by Allah, Mighty and Majestic, from light; they neither eat, nor drink, nor reproduce, but are honored servants of Allah: "They do not precede Him in speech, and they act by His command" (al-Anbiya 27), and they have deeds and attributes which we have already discussed sufficiently, so there is no need to repeat them.

He said: "wal-nabiyyin": there is a reading "wal-nabi'in" with the hamza realized.

"Arbaban": plural of (rabb), i.e., lords worshipped and sought besides Allah; this is impossible to occur from one whom Allah has given the Book, wisdom and prophethood.

Allah, Exalted, said: "Would He order you to disbelieve after you have submitted?" (Al 'Imran 80). The interrogative here is for negation: i.e., it is impossible that He would command you to disbelieve after you have submitted.

In His saying "ya'murukum" there are two readings: "ya'murkum" with lightening, and "ya'murukum" in the original form. His saying "ba'da idh antum muslimun" means: after your submission has been established and confirmed, He cannot command you to disbelieve.

Allah, Exalted, said: "And indeed, among them is a party who distort their tongues with the Book."

From the benefits of this verse and what follows: a party of the People of the Book distort words, either in wording or in meaning.

* And from the benefits of the verses: the evil intent of those who twist their tongues with the Book. What is the intent? To mislead people so they think it is from the Book.

* And from its benefits: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, loves guidance for His servants and that they be guided; hence He said: "and it is not from the Book" (Al 'Imran 78), so that people are not deceived by this twisting that occurred from them.

* And from the benefits of this verse: caution against disbelievers and against the deceptive speech that comes from them, for they mix truth with falsehood and wish to mislead people.

* And also from the benefits of this verse: caution against those in this Ummah who share their characteristics and begin to twist their tongues with the Book. We say this because the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "You will surely follow the ways of those before you"[[Recorded by Ahmad (21897) from the hadith of Abu Waqid al-Laythi; the origin of the hadith is in al-Bukhari (3456) and Muslim (2669/6) from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri.]] So if among the People of the Book there are those who twist their tongues with the Book, there will also be in this Ummah those who twist their tongue with the Book.

* And also from the benefits of this noble verse: among the People of the Book are those who fabricate lies against Allah. Among these is their lying about the punishment of the married adulterer; for the punishment of the married adulterer among them is stoning until death. But when adultery became common among their nobles, they deviated from this and said: "How can we kill our nobles? Then what shall we do?" They said: we blacken his face and parade him, him and the woman he committed adultery with, on a donkey, with the back of each facing the back of the other, both riding the donkey, and we parade them among the tribes among the people, then the matter ends. So they distorted and concealed: they distorted when they claimed this was the punishment for the married adulterer, and concealed when they said: there is no stoning in the Torah. For this reason, when they denied that stoning was in the Torah, the Prophet (ﷺ) asked them to bring the Torah. They brought it, and the reader began to read and placed his hand over the verse of stoning, for what? To conceal it. But he was commanded to lift his hand; when he lifted it, the verse of stoning appeared clear and manifest. The Prophet (ﷺ) then commanded that they be stoned, i.e., the adulterer and the adulteress. The conclusion is that among the methods of the People of the Book is that they say about Allah what is false while they know it.

Then Allah, Exalted, said: "It is not for a human being that Allah should give him the Book, the wisdom and the prophethood" (Al 'Imran 79), and so on to the end.

* From the benefits of this verse: a refutation of the Christians who claim that Jesus, peace be upon him, has the right to be worshipped besides Allah. For this reason Allah will say to him on the Day of Resurrection: "Did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah?'" (al-Ma'idah 116). He will say: "Glory be to You," meaning it is impossible for me to say this. The Christians claim that their religion is Trinitarian, i.e., that Allah is the third of three.

* And from the benefits of this noble verse: whoever Allah has blessed with beneficial knowledge cannot possibly call people to worship himself, saying: "Be servants of me besides Allah."

* Among its benefits: whoever compels people, or wants them, to follow his word whatever it may be, has in effect commanded them to take him as a lord, and has indeed made them his worshippers; for obeying a person is a form of worship, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿They took their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah﴾ [Ali 'Imran 79]. 'Adi ibn Hatim said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, we do not worship them." He said: "Do they not make lawful what Allah has made unlawful, and you make it lawful, and make unlawful what Allah has made lawful, and you make it unlawful?" He said: "Yes." He said: "That is their worship."[[Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (218) and al-Bayhaqi in al-Madkhal ila al-Sunan al-Kubra (261), from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri.]] A person may not say to people, "Worship me, bow to me, and prostrate to me," but he may say, "Adhere to what I say," and this is a kind of worship.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: whoever Allah has blessed with the Book, wisdom, judgment and prophethood will command only good, because of His saying: ﴿But be godly (rabbaniyyin)﴾ [Ali 'Imran 79].

* Also among the benefits of this noble verse: an indication that a person should be a godly teacher (mu'allim rabbani), because of His saying: ﴿But be godly (rabbaniyyin)﴾. As for what occurs among some people, namely that one is a teacher but not godly, his knowledge is deficient, very deficient; for the benefit and fruit of knowledge is action and adherence to the manners of knowledge. So if this man fills students' minds with knowledge but there is no conduct, morals, deeds or worship in him, then his teaching is very incomplete. Hence He said: ﴿But be godly (rabbaniyyin)﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: a refutation of those who deny causes, because of His saying: ﴿by what you used to teach of the Book﴾, where the "bi" (by) denotes causation. There is no doubt that causes are established, but they are not independent in bringing things into existence or annihilating them; rather they have effect by the power Allah has placed in them. With this we repel the doubt of those who deny causes, arguing that affirming causes entails affirming a creator besides Allah. We say to them: we affirm causes, but what are they?
* Student: They do not have an effect by themselves.
* The Shaykh: They do not have an effect by themselves, but by the power Allah has placed in them. The proof of this is that when Abraham, peace be upon him, was thrown into the fire, Allah said to the fire: ﴿O fire, be cool and safe for Abraham﴾ [al-Anbiya' 69], and it became cool and safe for him; it did not harm him although it is burning. The scholars said: had Allah said, "Be cool," without saying "and safe," it would have killed him with cold, because it obeys the command of Allah the Mighty and Majestic.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that a teacher of people may rightly be called rabbani, because He said: ﴿But be godly (rabbaniyyin) by what you used to teach of the Book﴾ [Ali 'Imran 79]. This is why we find in the biographies of the scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, that they frequently describe a scholar as "the godly scholar" (al-'alim al-rabbani).

* Among the benefits of this noble verse, in His saying: ﴿Nor would he command you to take the angels and the prophets as lords﴾ [Ali 'Imran 80]: an affirmation of the angels, and belief in them is one of the six pillars of faith, so a servant's faith is not complete until he believes in the angels.

* Also among its benefits: that the one whom Allah has blessed with the Book, judgment and prophethood cannot possibly command others to take the angels and prophets as lords, just as he would not call people to worship himself.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that whoever commands another to become his servant has commanded disbelief, and whoever commands that the angels and prophets be taken as lords has commanded disbelief, because of Allah's saying: ﴿Would he command you to disbelief after you have submitted [to Allah]?﴾ [Ali 'Imran 80].

* Among its benefits: that this disbelief expels one from the religion (millah), because of His saying: ﴿after you have submitted [to Allah]﴾.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on Surah 3, verses 78–80 (part 1 of 3):

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And indeed, among them is a group who distort their tongues with the Book﴾ [Aal 'Imran 78].

﴿And indeed, among them﴾: The pronoun refers to the People of the Book, because the verses share one context. At the beginning of the verses He said: ﴿And among the People of the Book is one who, if you entrust him with a qintar, will return it to you﴾ [Aal 'Imran 75]. Here He said: ﴿And indeed, among them is a group who distort their tongues with the Book﴾. Al-layy (لَيّ) means turning or twisting, as in "layy al-habl" (twisting the rope). So ﴿they distort their tongues﴾ means they turn them aside. The layy here includes both verbal layy and meaningful layy.

Verbal layy: Sometimes they bring speech of their own and recite it in the manner of revealed Scripture, so that whoever hears it among the people imagines that it is from the revealed Book. That is, they inflect the speech the way the Qur'an is inflected, so the listener thinks it is from Allah. This is one type.
