Thus when the Messengers said that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah who is sent in the manner Allah described, enjoining right and forbidding wrong, and he came in conformity with what they reported, he became a confirmation of them.
﴿confirming what is with you﴾, i.e., of what is with you, from what? From the earlier scriptures they brought.
﴿you shall believe in him﴾ [Aal-i-Imran 81]: this is the place of the covenant, meaning: if this Messenger confirming what is with you comes to you, then My covenant upon you is ﴿you shall believe in him and you shall support him﴾ [Aal-i-Imran 81]. ﴿you shall believe in him﴾ means you shall believe that he is true. ﴿and you shall support him﴾ means you shall help him in spreading his message and in fighting his enemies, because support here includes support by knowledge and by weapons.
﴿He said: Do you acknowledge and accept My burden upon that?﴾ They said: "We acknowledge it." [Aal-i-Imran 81]. When He had informed that He took from them the covenant and pact, He made them confirm this: ﴿He said: Do you acknowledge and accept My burden upon that? They said: We acknowledge it﴾.
His saying: ﴿Do you acknowledge﴾ means: do you admit and commit yourselves to that. His saying: ﴿accept My burden upon that﴾ means: you accepted the heavy covenant, because al-isr, whose plural is (aṣār), means heavy things, so ﴿My burden﴾ means My heavy covenant.
﴿They said: We acknowledge it﴾: there is a reading among us, ﴿He said: Do you acknowledge﴾, in which it is read ﴿آأَقْرَرْتُمْ﴾ with the first alif lengthened. ﴿They said: We acknowledge it. He said: Then bear witness﴾ [Aal-i-Imran 81]. ﴿They said: We acknowledge it﴾ means: we admitted and committed ourselves to believe in him and support him. ﴿He said: Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses﴾.
﴿Bear witness﴾ means: let some of you bear witness against others, and let all of you bear witness to the covenant between Me and you. ﴿And I am with you among the witnesses﴾, and Allah suffices as a witness. So He made them witnesses against themselves, and He, Mighty and Majestic, bore witness against them of what took place.
Now we return to the grammar. We said: ﴿Idh akhadha Allah﴾ is the object of an omitted verb, its estimated form being: (remember when Allah took).
His saying: ﴿لَمَا آتَيْتُكُمْ﴾ has two readings: ﴿لَمَا﴾ and ﴿لِمَا﴾. On the reading ﴿لِمَا﴾ the lam is causal (lam al-ta'lil), and ma is a relative pronoun, i.e., for that which I gave you of Scripture and wisdom, ﴿you shall believe in him﴾. So the cause precedes the thing caused. The estimate on this basis is: And when Allah took the covenant of the Prophets, that you shall believe in this Messenger, because of what I have given you of Scripture and wisdom. So the lam is then causal. As for the reading with fatha, the lam is said to be the lam of initiation (lam al-ibtida'): ﴿And when Allah took the covenant of those given the Scripture﴾ [Aal-i-Imran 187], for that which I gave you, meaning it, of Scripture and wisdom, ﴿then there came to you a Messenger confirming what is with you, you shall believe in him﴾ [Aal-i-Imran 81], i.e., in this Messenger, so ma is a relative pronoun as in the first case.
The Shaykh: ﴿Akhadha Allah﴾ is the object of an omitted verb; its estimate is?
* A student: "Remember."
* The Shaykh: Remember when Allah took.
His saying: ﴿لَمَا آتَيْتُكُمْ﴾ has two readings: ﴿لَمَا﴾ and ﴿لِمَا﴾. On the reading ﴿لِمَا﴾ the lam is causal, and ma is a relative pronoun, i.e., for that which I gave you of Scripture and wisdom, ﴿you shall believe in him﴾; so the cause precedes the caused. The estimate: And when Allah took the covenant of the Prophets, that you believe in this Messenger because of what I gave you of Scripture and wisdom; so the lam is causal.
As for the reading with fatha, the lam is the lam of initiation; and when Allah took the covenant of those given the Scripture, surely that which I gave you of Scripture and wisdom; ﴿then there came to you a Messenger confirming what is with you, you shall believe in him﴾, i.e., in this Messenger; so ma is a relative pronoun as in the first case. But the lam is for initiation. It was also said: rather, the lam is the answer to the covenant (mithaq), because mithaq means 'ahd (covenant), and a covenant is treated like an oath, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Allah had certainly taken the covenant of the Children of Israel, and We raised among them twelve leaders. And Allah said: Indeed I am with you, if you establish prayer﴾ and so on [al-Ma'idah 12]. So the covenant is answered with what an oath is answered with. On this basis the lam in His saying ﴿لَمَا﴾ falls in the answer of an oath, since the covenant has that meaning. Then ﴿لَتُؤْمِنُنَّ بِهِ﴾ is also a preparatory lam (muwatti'ah) for another omitted oath; the estimate: "By Allah, you shall believe in him." The clause ﴿لَتُؤْمِنُنَّ بِهِ﴾ is in the place of nominative predicate of ma in His saying ﴿لَمَا آتَيْتُكُمْ مِنْ كِتَابٍ وَحِكْمَةٍ﴾. There is also a third point in the grammar: ﴿لَتُؤْمِنُنَّ بِهِ﴾: tu'min is a verb of what?
* The students: Imperfect.
* The Shaykh: Imperfect. The scholars say that when the imperfect verb is joined to the emphatic nun, it must be built on fatha, as in His saying: ﴿Certainly he will be thrown into the crushing one﴾ [al-Humazah 4]. Is it "liyunbadhanna" or "liyunbadhunn"?
* The students: ﴿لَيُنْبَذَنَّ﴾.
* The Shaykh: ﴿لَيُنْبَذَنَّ﴾, ﴿لَنَسْفَعَنْ بِالنَّاصِيَةِ﴾ [al-'Alaq 15], ﴿لَيُسْجَنَنَّ﴾ [Yusuf 32], which end in a nun, and ﴿وَلَيَكُونَنْ مِنَ الصَّاغِرِينَ﴾ [Yusuf 32]. Here the verb was not built on fatha: ﴿لَتُؤْمِنُنَّ﴾, and it is not said "لتؤمنَن". So how is the answer to this difficulty? They say: the nun here does not directly adjoin the verb, and the verb is built only when it directly adjoins the emphatic nun; when there is no direct adjoining, it is not built. Because its original form is: لتؤمنونن. How many nuns do we have?
* The students: Three.
* The Shaykh: Three nuns. They say: one of them is deleted to avoid the succession of identical elements; three identical letters in a row cannot stand, so it must be deleted. Now which do you want to delete? They say: I delete the nun of the verb. Which is the nun of the verb?
* The students: The first.
* The Shaykh: The first: لتؤمنونن. I delete the nun of the verb. Why not delete the emphatic nun? They say: because the emphatic nun was brought to convey a meaning. What is the meaning it conveys?
* The students: Emphasis.
* The Shaykh: Emphasis. And the nun of the nominative (nun al-raf') is often deleted. When is it deleted?
* A student: In the accusative.
* The Shaykh: In the accusative and jussive cases. We have learned that the five verbs take the accusative by deleting the nun and take the jussive by deleting the nun, and sometimes it is deleted without a governing or jussive particle, merely for lightening, as in the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "By Allah, you will not enter Paradise until you believe" [narrated by Muslim (54/93) and Ahmad in al-Musnad (10650), the wording of the latter, from Abu Hurayrah ra]. He said: "لا تدخلوا", whereas the original is to say: لا تدخلون. So what was deleted from لتؤمنونن? Which letter was deleted?
* The students: The nun of the verb.
* The Shaykh: The nun of the nominative. It was deleted. Someone may ask: where did the waw go? Where did the waw go in لتؤمنونن? We say: it was deleted, and why was it deleted? Because what follows it is quiescent, and when the letter before a quiescent letter is a soft letter (harf layn), it is deleted, in accordance with the words of Ibn Malik:
If two quiescent letters meet, vowel the first with kasra;
and if it is a soft letter, its deletion is deserved.
Shall I repeat the verse?
If two quiescent letters meet, vowel the first with kasra;
and if it is a soft letter, its deletion is deserved.
The soft letters are known: waw, ya and alif. Ibn Malik means: if two quiescent letters meet and the first is sound, vowel the first with kasra; and if it is a soft letter, delete the soft letter. So in (لتؤمنُونَنَّ) the waw is a soft letter, delete it, and the emphatic nun comes to directly adjoin the verb's nun? Is it clear? So this is the explanation of His saying: ﴿لَتُؤْمِنُنَّ بِهِ﴾. The clause ﴿لَتُؤْمِنُنَّ بِهِ﴾ is the answer to an oath, either a presumed oath or the earlier oath. The discussion of grammar is finished.
* A student: Meeting of two quiescents is permitted in its proper form and not permitted outside it; so in a form like ضالِّين...
* The Shaykh: What?
* The student: ضالّين, especially, for example; here too the meeting of two quiescents is in its proper form, because some of it...
* The Shaykh: Some of it what?
* The student: Some of it has a vowel consistent with the waw, for example: لتؤمنونن?
* The Shaykh: Yes, but there is a difference between them. (ضالّين) is in one word; if you delete the alif of (الضالّين) the meaning changes and the word is broken. But this waw is separate from the verb, separate; it is a pronoun. That is the difference.
* A student: We said: when the waw was deleted, the last nun directly adjoined the verb's nun, although we determined earlier that the verb's nun was deleted.
* The Shaykh: The nun of the nominative?
* The student: The nun of the nominative, yes (...)?
* The Shaykh: What is the problem?
* The student: If we decided it was deleted, how did it directly adjoin?
* The Shaykh: When it was deleted, the nun became the doubled emphatic nun whose first element is quiescent, and the waw?
* The student: Quiescent.
* The Shaykh: Quiescent. What do we do?
* The student: We delete the waw.
* The Shaykh: We delete the waw, so now the nun, the verb's nun, has not directly adjoined the emphatic nun in terms of estimation, or has the wording directly adjoined? It has directly adjoined only in estimation, not in estimation... in estimation it has not directly adjoined.
* * *
* A student: ﴿فَمَنْ تَوَلَّى بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْفَاسِقُونَ (٨٢) أَفَغَيْرَ دِينِ اللَّهِ يَبْغُونَ وَلَهُ أَسْلَمَ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ طَوْعًا وَكَرْهًا وَإِلَيْهِ يُرْجَعُونَ (٨٣) قُلْ آمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ وَمَا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْنَا وَمَا أُنْزِلَ عَلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ وَالْأَسْبَاطِ وَمَا أُوتِيَ مُوسَى وَعِيسَى وَالنَّبِيُّونَ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ لَا نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِنْهُمْ وَنَحْنُ لَهُ مُسْلِمُونَ﴾ [Aal-i-Imran 82–84].
* The Shaykh: I seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Shaytan. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿And when Allah took the covenant of the Prophets, that which I have given you of Scripture and wisdom...﴾ [Aal-i-Imran 81] to the end.
What is meant by the mithaq?
* A student: That which is between the two contracting parties by covenant.
* The Shaykh: That which is between two parties by a contract.
* A student: From the covenant.
* The Shaykh: Derived from where?
* A student: From wathuqa al-shay' (to be secure in something).
* The Shaykh: From al-wathaq, which is the rope.
* A student: The tie.
* The Shaykh: With which a thing is tied.
His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿لَمَا آتَيْتُكُمْ مِنْ كِتَابٍ وَحِكْمَةٍ ثُمَّ جَاءَكُمْ رَسُولٌ مُصَدِّقٌ لِمَا مَعَكُمْ لَتُؤْمِنُنَّ بِهِ﴾: how is the grammar of this verse on the fatha of the lam?
* A student: On the fatha of the lam there are two lines of analysis. The first: the lam is the lam of initiation, and ma is a relative noun as subject, with the predicate the clause ﴿لَتُؤْمِنُنَّ بِهِ﴾. Another analysis: the lam is with kasra in the other reading.
* The Shaykh: No, no, fatha.
* The student: The lam falls in the place of the answer to an oath, because the covenant has the meaning of an oath.
* The Shaykh: Yes, since it includes the meaning of an oath, the lam is preparatory for the oath, and ma is a conditional noun of jazm, ﴿لَتُؤْمِنُنَّ بِهِ﴾ is the answer to the oath. In truth we have not completed its grammar in its proper place; on this, the lam is preparatory for the oath and ma is conditional, ﴿آتَيْتُكُمْ﴾ is the conditional verb, and the answer of the condition is omitted, and ﴿لَتُؤْمِنُنَّ بِهِ﴾ is the answer to the oath, following the words of Ibn Malik, may Allah have mercy on him:
When the condition and the oath come together, omit the answer of whichever is placed later; it is then obligatory.
So the answer in ﴿لَتُؤْمِنُنَّ بِهِ﴾ is the answer to the oath, while the answer of the condition, which is ma, is omitted; the clause of the condition and its answer has no place in grammar, being the answer of the oath contained in the covenant.
His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ جَاءَكُمْ رَسُولٌ﴾: who is meant by the Messenger here?
* A student: Muhammad ﷺ.
* The Shaykh: Muhammad ﷺ.
His saying: ﴿مُصَدِّقٌ لِمَا مَعَكُمْ﴾?
* A student: ﴿مُصَدِّقٌ﴾ has two meanings: confirming what came before him, this is one meaning, and confirming what he reported...
* The Shaykh: That is, that he...
* The student: That he reported about the Messengers who came before him.
* The Shaykh: That is, that he fell as a confirmation of what they said.
* The student: As you said.
* The Shaykh: That is one; and the second, that he?
* The student: That he confirms them.
* The Shaykh: He confirms the earlier scriptures; that is, he informs that they are truth.
His saying: ﴿إِصْرِي﴾: what is meant by my burden? ﴿وَأَخَذْتُمْ عَلَى ذَلِكُمْ إِصْرِي﴾?
* A student: Al-isr in the language is the heavy burden; that is, the covenant.
* The Shaykh: The covenant, and it was called isr because fulfilling it is heavy, and a person bears it.
Good. ﴿قَالَ فَاشْهَدُوا﴾: do we stop here, I think, or have we completed the verse?
* A student: We have completed the verse.
* The Shaykh: ﴿قَالَ فَاشْهَدُوا﴾... bear witness against whom?
* A student: Bear witness, referring to themselves.
* The Shaykh: And likewise some of them...
* A student: Against one another, some of them bearing witness against others, witnesses bearing witness against them...
* The Shaykh: He commanded them: bear witness against yourselves and some of you against others.
His saying: ﴿وَأَنَا مَعَكُمْ مِنَ الشَّاهِدِينَ﴾: the companionship here?
* A student: We stop here.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verse 81–83 (part 2 of 5):

* The Shaykh: Good. ﴿He said: "Then bear witness."﴾ That is, some of you bear witness against others, and you also bear witness against yourselves, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants and made them testify concerning themselves, [saying], "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we have testified."﴾ [Al-A'raf 172]. Likewise, Allah made the prophets bear witness concerning themselves that they would believe in Muhammad ﷺ, because this description applies to none but them.
And some scholars said: the intended "Messenger" is the Messenger who comes after them confirming what is with them, because every messenger confirms the one before him: 'Isa confirms Musa, and Muhammad confirms both of them and all the prophets.
But the correct view is the first: that what is intended is Muhammad ﷺ.
As for His saying: ﴿And I am with you among the witnesses﴾, this is a special companionship. This is a special accompaniment (mu'iyyah), a companionship in this testimony, because He said: ﴿And I am with you among the witnesses.﴾ The accompaniment of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is of two kinds: a general accompaniment that encompasses all creation, and a special accompaniment restricted to or specified for some of creation. In His saying the Exalted: ﴿There is no secret conversation between three but that He is their fourth, nor between five but that He is their sixth, nor less than that or more but that He is with them wherever they are﴾ [Al-Mujadila 7], is this an accompaniment?
* The students: General.
* The Shaykh: General. And His saying: ﴿He it is who created the heavens and the earth in six days and then established Himself above the Throne. He knows what enters into the earth and what emerges from it, what descends from the sky and what ascends therein. And He is with you wherever you are. And Allah, of what you do, is Seeing﴾ [Al-Hadid 4]. Is this also?
* The students: General.
* The Shaykh: A general accompaniment for all creation. And His saying the Exalted: ﴿Be patient, for indeed Allah is with the patient﴾ [Al-Anfal 46].
* The students: Special.
* The Shaykh: This is special, specific to the patient. And His saying to His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿When he said to his companion, "Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us"﴾ [At-Tawba 40]. This is also special, special in essence and place.
Now, the general accompaniment entails: knowledge and encompassment of creation in power, authority, governance and other things; these are among its implications, because all creation is under Allah's power, authority and governance. The special accompaniment entails: support, victory, aid, strengthening and similar things, and what determines these implications is the context.
If someone says: Does Allah's accompaniment contradict His being above? The answer: No, it does not contradict it. He is with creation while being above the Throne, because nothing among His creatures resembles Him, or nothing among His creatures is like Him. For this reason Allah combined the two in the verse we recited last: ﴿He it is who created the heavens and the earth in six days and then established Himself above the Throne. He knows what enters into the earth and what emerges from it, what descends from the sky and what ascends therein. And He is with you﴾ [Al-Hadid 4]. So He combined His being above with what? 
* The students: And His accompaniment.
* The Shaykh: And His accompaniment. There is no contradiction between them. The Prophet ﷺ said: «Indeed Allah descends to the lowest heaven»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1145) and Muslim (758/168), with the wording «Allah descends to the lowest heaven», from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah may Allah be pleased with him.]] and yet His descent is real while He is upon His Throne; so His descent does not contradict His elevation. If you wish, let us mention an example that brings this closer to you: look at the moon. Its place is in the sky, and it is with the human being. If we are in the town, it is with us; if we are traveling, it is with us. It is with the people of 'Unayzah, the people of Riyadh, the people of Makkah, the people of Madinah, and everyone on the surface of the earth in regard to the moon. The Arabs say: "We kept travelling and the moon was with us." Yet all creation knows that the moon is in the sky. If there is no contradiction between elevation and accompaniment, which is companionship among created things, then what about the Creator? For this reason, you must not think that the speech of Allah contradicts itself at all; the speech of Allah confirms one part of it with another: ﴿And if it had been from other than Allah, they would have found within it much contradiction﴾ [An-Nisa 82]. But the implications of this accompaniment, as you know, differ; its implication for generality is not like its implication for specificity.
Now, He said: ﴿And I am with you among the witnesses.﴾ ﴿Among the witnesses﴾ here: "witness" is an attribute shared by the Creator and the created, so He said ﴿among the witnesses﴾ and made Himself, the Mighty and Majestic, one of the witnesses. But does this sharing in testimony necessitate similarity?
* The students: No.
* The Shaykh: No, just as sharing in life does not necessitate similarity: ﴿He brings the living out of the dead﴾ [Al-An'am 95], He affirmed the created living; ﴿Allah — there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence﴾ [Al-Baqarah 255], He affirmed that His name is the Living. So the sharing of the Creator and the created in life does not entail what?
* The students: Similarity.
* The Shaykh: Similarity. Therefore, that Allah is among the witnesses does not entail that His witnessing is like the witnessing of creation. The witnessing of Allah is an established, true witnessing, not preceded by ignorance nor followed by forgetfulness; the witnessing of the created is the opposite, preceded by ignorance and followed by forgetfulness. So there is a difference between them.
﴿Then whoever turns away after that, those are the defiantly disobedient﴾. ﴿Whoever turns away after that﴾: that is, after this explanation and clarification that was mentioned, and that Muhammad ﷺ was taken as a covenant from all the prophets to believe in him and to support him. What is taken from the leader is taken from the follower too; that is, what was taken from the prophets is taken from their followers as well. So if it is obligatory upon the prophets to believe in him and support him, it is obligatory upon their followers to believe in him and support him. For this reason, when the Prophet ﷺ saw with 'Umar ibn al-Khattab some of the Torah, he became angry and said: «Have I not brought it to you white and pure? Had my brother Musa been alive, he would have had no choice but to follow me»[[Narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad (15156) from the hadith of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab may Allah be pleased with him, with the wording «Are you bewildered in it, O son of al-Khattab? By Him in whose hand my soul is, I have come to you with it white and pure. Do not ask them about anything, lest they inform you of truth and you deny it, or of falsehood and you affirm it. By Him in whose hand my soul is, if Musa were alive, he would have had no choice but to follow me.»]] How can you bring the Torah? The Qur'an is sufficient in itself over every book; whatever beneficial is in the books of this world is present in the Qur'an, and there is no need for them, especially since they are now not the books sent down from heaven, but contain alteration, substitution and concealment which only Allah knows. So we say: ﴿Whoever turns away after that﴾ after what? After this clarification and explanation that Allah the Mighty and Majestic made clear, and that Allah took the covenant of all the prophets, that when a messenger comes to them confirming what is with them, they must believe in him and support him. Would the one who turns away turn away after that? No: ﴿Whoever turns away after that, those are the defiantly disobedient.﴾ ﴿They﴾: a pronoun of separation (damir fasl). ﴿The defiantly disobedient (al-fasiqun)﴾: those who have departed from the level of justice, from the level of manhood, and from the level of faith; they departed from obedience, turned away, and withdrew. These are the defiantly disobedient. And what is meant by fisq (defiant disobedience) here is the fisq of disbelief, because fisq is applied both to the fisq of sins and to the fisq of disbelief. From the first is His saying the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, if a defiantly disobedient person brings you news, verify it﴾ [Al-Hujurat 6]; this is the fisq of sin. From the second is His saying the Exalted: ﴿Is one who was a believer like one who was defiantly disobedient? They are not equal. As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, for them are the Gardens of Refuge as a lodging, because of what they used to do. But as for those who defied, their refuge is the Fire. Every time they wish to get out of it, they are returned to it﴾ [As-Sajdah 18–20]. So here, what is meant by fisq? The fisq of disbelief, because it comes in opposition to faith; it came as the counterpart of faith, and the counterpart of a thing is other than the thing. As for His saying the Exalted: ﴿And whoever does not rule by what Allah has revealed, those are the defiantly disobedient﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 47], is it the fisq of disbelief or the fisq of sin?
* The students: The fisq of sin.
* The Shaykh: It is said: sin; it is said: disbelief; and it is said: it is to be distinguished in detail.
Good. Regarding the grammar of this verse: there is a condition and an answer. The condition?
* A student: ﴿Whoever turned away﴾.
* The Shaykh: ﴿Whoever turned away﴾. The answer?
* The student: ﴿Defiantly disobedient﴾?
* The Shaykh: No.
* The students: ﴿Those﴾?
* The Shaykh: ﴿Then those﴾; the answer here is a nominal clause; for this reason it is joined with the fa' (fa'). ﴿Fa-ulaika﴾: because when a clause is not suitable to directly follow the conditional particle, it must be joined with fa'. Ibn Malik said:
وَاقْــرِنْ بِفَــا حَتْمًــا جَوَابًــا لَــوْجُعِــــلْ ∗∗∗ شَرْطًا لِـ(إِنْ) أَوْ غَيْرِهَا لَمْيَنْجَعِلْ
This is the rule:
وَاقْــرِنْ بِفَــا حَتْمًــا جَوَابًــا لَــوْجُعِــــلْ ∗∗∗ شَرْطًا لِـ(إِنْ) أَوْ غَيْرِهَا لَمْيَنْجَعِلْ
meaning "it did not become"; this is a general statement by Ibn Malik that was detailed by the saying of the poet:
اسْمِيّــــــــــــَةٌ طَلَبِيَّــــــــــــةٌوَبِجَامِــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــدٍ ∗∗∗ وَبِمَــــا وَقَــــدْ وَبِـ(لَــــــــــــنْ)وَبِالتَّنْفِيــــــــسِ
How many is this?
* The students: Seven.
* The Shaykh: Seven. Have you memorized them?
* A student: Some of them, not all.
* The Shaykh: Good, recite what you have memorized?
* The student:
اسْمِيّــــــــــــَةٌ طَلَبِيَّــــــــــــةٌ............ ∗∗∗ ............................
* The Shaykh: The versifier?
The student: (...) repeat three times!
* The Shaykh: Good, let us repeat three times.
اسْمِيّــــــــــــَةٌ طَلَبِيَّــــــــــــةٌوَبِجَامِــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــدٍ ∗∗∗ وَبِمَــــا وَقَــــدْ وَبِـ(لَــــــــــــنْ)وَبِالتَّنْفِيــــــــسِ
Whoever did not memorize it before, let him recite it to me. Did you memorize it before? Continue?
* A student:
اسْمِيّــــــــــــَةٌ طَلَبِيَّــــــــــــةٌوَبِجَامِــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــــدٍ ∗∗∗ وَبِمَــــا وَقَــــدْ وَبِـ(لَــــــــــــنْ)وَبِالتَّنْفِيــــــــسِ
* The Shaykh:
............................ ∗∗∗ وَبِمَــــا وَقَــــدْ...................
* The student:
............................ ∗∗∗ وَبِمَــــــــــا وَقَــــــــــــــــدْوَبِالتَّنْفِيــــــــــــــــــــــــــسِ
* The Shaykh:
............................ ∗∗∗ وَبِمَــــا وَقَــــدْ وَبِـ(لَــــــــــــنْ)وَبِالتَّنْفِيــــــــسِ
These are seven things: when they occur as the answer to the condition, the condition must be joined with fa'. Which of the clauses is present with us now?
* The students: Nominal.
* The Shaykh: ﴿Ulaika hum al-fasiqun﴾ is a nominal clause, right? Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Then those are the defiantly disobedient.﴾

Then He said: ﴿Do they then seek other than the religion of Allah?﴾ ﴿Other than the religion of Allah﴾: "religion" (din) is applied both to recompense and to the law; that is, to the action and its recompense. It is sometimes applied to the action that is the law of Allah, and sometimes to recompense. From its application to recompense is the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in pleasure, and indeed, the wicked will be in Hellfire. They will burn therein on the Day of Recompense, and they will not be absent from it. And what can make you know what is the Day of Recompense? Then what can make you know what is the Day of Recompense? The Day when no soul will possess for another anything, and the command, that Day, belongs to Allah﴾ [Al-Infitar 13–19].
And Allah said in Surah al-Fatihah: ﴿Sovereign of the Day of Recompense﴾ [Al-Fatihah 4]. Here "din" means?
* The students: Recompense.
* The Shaykh: Recompense. And from the use of din to mean action and law is His saying: ﴿For you is your religion, and for me is my religion﴾ [Al-Kafirun 6], and His saying: ﴿And I have approved for you Islam as a religion﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 3]; that is, a law. Here, ﴿Do they then seek other than the religion of Allah?﴾: the religion of Allah means His law, which He prescribed for His servants, and He attributed it to Himself to show its importance and that it is the just and beneficial law without which creation cannot stand; because it is the law of Allah, it is the most perfect of laws. He also attributed it to Himself because He is the one who prescribed it. Sometimes din is attributed to the one who acts upon it, like the saying of Allah: ﴿For you is your religion, and for me is my religion﴾; originally "my religion" (dini); it is attributed to the doer, in consideration that he took it and adhered to it; and it is attributed to Allah in consideration that He prescribed it and established it for His servants.
Now, His saying: ﴿yabghun﴾: that is, they seek. This interrogative is for denunciation and rebuke; it denounces those who seek other than the religion of Allah and rebukes them. There is a reading: ﴿tabghun﴾, ﴿Do you then seek other than the religion of Allah?﴾, the reading of the seven. On this basis, it is good that we sometimes recite ﴿tabghun﴾ and sometimes ﴿yabghun﴾, except when we are in the presence of common people; then we do not recite both readings, but recite to them what they know. For if you recited two readings before the common people, they would be emboldened against you on one hand, and the standing of the Qur'an would diminish in their eyes on the other hand, and they would rise against you with horses and men and say: "Nothing remains for you but to change the Qur'an," and they would be after you night and day. So do not recite other than what they know. As for between you and Allah, recite this sometimes and that sometimes, on condition that you are certain of that reading, because this is the speech of Allah, and you must be certain.
He said: ﴿Do they then seek other than the religion of Allah, while to Him has submitted whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or by compulsion?﴾ The "wa" here is for the state (hal); that is, the state being that to Him submitted whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly and unwillingly. Did He submit in legislative submission or cosmic submission?
* The students: Legislative.
* The Shaykh: Cosmic submission, not legislative submission; because legislative submission has no compulsion, and because legislative submission does not encompass whoever is in the heavens and the earth. It encompasses whoever is in the heavens, true, but whoever is on the earth: no. His saying: ﴿And to Him has submitted﴾: that is, He submitted in cosmic obedience. He said ﴿And to Him has submitted﴾ after His saying ﴿Do they seek other than the religion of Allah?﴾ to establish the proof against those who did not submit to Allah legislatively and did not follow His religion, as if it were said: "You have submitted to Allah cosmically, so you must submit to Him legislatively, because the Lord who governs creation as He wills, whether they wish it or dislike it, is the One upon whose law we must conduct ourselves." So this serves as a proof for what preceded.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verse 81–83 (part 3 of 5):

His saying: ﴿Whoever is in the heavens and the earth has submitted to Him﴾. He used "man" (مَنْ), which denotes rational beings, giving precedence to the rational ones. For if we were to count those in the heavens and the earth, the majority would be rational beings, because "there is not a place of four fingers in the heavens except that there is an angel standing before Allah, or bowing, or prostrating"[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (2312) and Ibn Majah (4190) from the hadith of Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him), and its wording is: "It is right that it should creak; there is not a place of four fingers in it except that there is an angel placing his forehead in prostration to Allah."]]. The heaven is extremely vast, and none knows its vastness except Allah: ﴿And the heaven We built with might, and indeed, We are expanding it﴾ [adh-Dhariyat 47]. The lowest heaven is far vaster than the earth, the second heaven is far vaster than the lowest, and so on: every heaven is vaster than what is beneath it.

His saying: ﴿and the earth﴾. "Earth" is singular, but it is intended as a genus, so it includes the earths. The earths are seven, according to the apparent meaning of the Qur'an and the explicit Sunnah. The apparent meaning of the Qur'an is His saying: ﴿Allah is He who created seven heavens and of the earth the like of them﴾ [at-Talaq 12]. The likeness here is not in form, is it not so?
* The students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: And it is not in quantity. By quantity I mean weight: the heaven is greater than the world, but in number they are alike. He said ﴿willingly or unwillingly﴾...
* The students: And the explicit Sunnah, O Shaykh?
* The Shaykh: Very well, the explicit Sunnah: his saying ﷺ: "Whoever usurps a span of the earth (meaning unjustly), it will be hung around his neck on the Day of Resurrection from seven earths"[[Narrated by Muslim (1610/137) from the hadith of Sa'id ibn Zayd ibn 'Amr ibn Nufayl (may Allah be pleased with him).]]. In this hadith is evidence that the seven are layered, one inside the other, because he says: "it will be hung around his neck from seven earths," and he only seized it from the upper, visible one. Therefore the second is within it, the third within the second, and so on; they are layered. By this we know that whoever says the seven refers to the seven continents has erred, for if they were seven continents, what would be the connection of the second and third earths and what follows them to the earth in which the usurpation took place?

His saying: ﴿willingly or unwillingly﴾. ﴿Willingly﴾ may be a verbal noun in the accusative, described as an adjective of an omitted verbal noun, the sense being: submission willingly; or it may be an accusative verbal noun functioning as a circumstantial state, interpreted as an active participle. Yes, a state of whom? Of the one in His saying ﴿whoever﴾: ﴿has submitted whoever﴾, meaning: and to Him have submitted whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willing and unwilling, willing and unwilling. Willingly is what is done by choice, and unwillingly is what is done without choice. He said: ﴿and to Him you will be returned﴾, and in one reading: ﴿you will be returned﴾, based on the reading in ﴿they seek﴾; meaning, these who are submitting to Allah will surely return to Allah, the Exalted, and He will inform them of what they did and will call them to account for what the messengers were sent to them with.

As for the grammar, we say: ﴿Is it other than the religion of Allah that they seek?﴾ Here there is an interrogative followed by a conjunction. We have mentioned for scholars two opinions regarding such a construction. The first view: the hamzah is interrogative, and the conjunction after it links what follows to an implied element between it and the hamzah, which the context specifies.
The second view: the hamzah is interrogative, and the fa' is a conjunction linking to what precedes, but it has been postponed so that the interrogative may have precedence. The sense on this view is: "So is it other than the religion of Allah that they seek?" We mentioned earlier that this view is better than the first. Why?
* The students: It needs no estimation.
* The Shaykh: Because it needs no estimation. And because the first, which needs an estimation, may sometimes leave you unable to find something to estimate that suits the context. For example, ﴿Have they not travelled in the land?﴾ [Yusuf 109]: if we say it is conjoined to an omitted element, one estimates: "Were they heedless, so they did not travel in the land?" Here, ﴿Is it other than the religion of Allah that they seek?﴾: "Have they gone astray, so is it other than the religion of Allah that they seek?" Because whoever seeks other than the religion of Allah is... what?
* A student: Astray.
* The Shaykh: So he is astray.
* A student: What is the evidence in His saying, ﴿Is it other than the religion of Allah that they seek, while to Him has submitted...﴾? We said here the will is cosmic (kawni) here.
* The Shaykh: The will is cosmic?
* The student: The submission, I mean, is cosmic here, and in reality not everyone on earth has submitted?
* The Shaykh: Cosmically?
* The student: They did not submit cosmically.
* The Shaykh: They did not submit cosmically?! Who can oppose Allah in His decree?
* The student: Now the atheists, the atheists now oppose Allah, the Exalted, rather they deny Him.
* The Shaykh: No, Glory be to Allah!
* The student: The atheists now say: there is no god!
* The Shaykh: If Allah, the Exalted, willed that one of them become ill, he would say: "By Allah, we do not accept illness." If He decreed death for him, he would say: "No, we do not accept death." Or does he submit and agree?
* The student: That is, he submits.
* The Shaykh: Very well, that is it.
* The student: But now, is what is meant here submission (istislam) or Islam itself?
* The Shaykh: Islam, because He said: "I have submitted" (aslamtu), and aslama means istaslama.
* A student: Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And when Allah took the covenant of the prophets﴾. How did He take it, may He be exalted? In a book that was revealed, or how?
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed, this is a problem, a problem, and perhaps we passed over it in the tafsir, and perhaps it will come in the benefits. When did Allah take the covenant from the prophets? When? Some scholars said: He took it from them as He took it from the children of Adam generally: ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins﴾ [al-A'raf 172], based on the soundness of the hadith in which Allah, the Exalted, extracted the offspring of Adam from his loins like specks, and took the covenant from them[[Narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad (21232) from the hadith of Ubayy ibn Ka'b (may Allah be pleased with him).]]. And it was said: Allah took the covenant from them by what He gave them of revelation; that is, He revealed this matter to them, and Allah's revelation of a thing is a covenant, as we said regarding His saying: ﴿And when Allah took the covenant of those who were given the Scripture, that you shall make it clear to the people and not conceal it﴾ [Al 'Imran 187]. (...) Does any of us feel that he has made a covenant with Allah over something? What is the answer?
* A student: Directly?
* The Shaykh: No, but when Allah gives a person knowledge, that is the covenant.
* A student: Does the connection of the state, O Shaykh, mean which of the two expressions is better? Do we say: Allah is with us by His knowledge, established by His essence, or do we say: Allah is with us and established upon His Throne?
* The Shaykh: It is best to affirm as Allah affirmed and not restrict. But if a layman addresses you and understands by His being with us that He is in the earth, say: "by His knowledge," so as to add the meaning, since the addressees differ. For this reason, "by His knowledge" was only used much after the doctrine of the Jahmiyyah spread that Allah is with us by His essence in the earth, and the scholars began to use it often. Although it is reported from Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him), or from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said: Ibn Mas'ud said: He is knowing of them, regarding ﴿and He is with them﴾ [an-Nisa 108]: He is knowing of them.
* A student: Is it other than Allah...
* The Shaykh: ﴿Is it other than the religion of Allah﴾.
* The student: ﴿Is it other than the religion of Allah﴾, the people who seek other than it...
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* The student: And it is placed before it...
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* The student: For the sake of restriction?
* The Shaykh: Yes, because whoever seeks other than the religion of Allah, it will not benefit him even if he holds to the religion of Allah. Look, if a man says: "I seek other than the religion of Allah in some matters, and I seek the religion of Allah in others," will the religion of Allah benefit him in this state?
* The student: No.
* The Shaykh: It will not benefit him, because whoever disbelieves in part of the Book has disbelieved in all of the Book.
* A student: May Allah reward you with good. Regarding one who recites other readings, may he recite one verse in one reading and another verse in another reading, as here: he says ﴿Is it other than the religion of Allah that they seek﴾ and in another verse he says ﴿to Him you will be returned﴾, so the meaning changes?
* The students: The same verse.
* The Shaykh: The scholars differed on this issue. They said: for example, if the reciters differ over a verse, may you recite its beginning in one reader's reading and its end in another reader's reading? Some scholars said: yes, it is valid, because all are transmitted; but the reader who transmitted it remains upon what he transmitted, whereas I have received it from others, and it is established that the Messenger recited the beginning of a verse in one way and the end of it in another, so I may recite it in both ways. This is the choice of Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, and it is the correct view. Others said: No, if you recite in one reader's reading, do not recite in the second reader's reading at the end of the verse. Do you understand? For example, in the verse before us: ﴿Is it other than the religion of Allah that you seek, while to Him has submitted whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly and unwillingly, and to Him you will be returned﴾ is valid, with "you will be returned" following... Then the whole verse with "to Him they will be returned" [in the third person]: ﴿Is it other than the religion of Allah that they seek...and to Him they will be returned﴾; and ﴿Is it other than the religion of Allah that you seek...and to Him you will be returned﴾, O you to whom the Qur'an was revealed, the addressees in both verbs together.
* A student: May Allah be good to you. Suppose there is another verse other than this one in which one of the two words differs from the other, and if you recite with this reading and then recite with the other reading, the meaning changes. Should I leave the reading in this case, even according to the view of Shaykh al-Islam?
* The Shaykh: No, you may recite both of them.
* The student: And even if the meaning differs?
* The Shaykh: Even if the meaning differs, because difference in meaning means added meaning; the verse indicates both meanings by the text. Yes.
* A student: Regarding "tawalla" (turning away), O Shaykh, does the meaning of tawalla mean (...)?
* The Shaykh: "A'rada", turning away.
* The student: That is, he does not turn away from the gatherings of the Qur'an...
* The Shaykh: Not at all. Turning away is with the body and with the heart: with the heart it is aversion, and with the body it is walking away and abandoning.
* The student: (...)
* The Shaykh: We say: that is not correct. The Arabic language says: so-and-so turned away, whether with his heart or with his body.
* A student: May Allah be good to you, the hadith (...) of the messengers, that after Allah took the covenant from them, one of them turns away until the threat applies to him: "Then whoever turns away, those are the defiantly disobedient"?
* The Shaykh: Glory be to Allah! What did you understand from the explanation of this?
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: What did you understand? That whoever turns away among the people after this clarification is defiantly disobedient; it is not "whoever turns away after the messengers upon whom the covenant was taken." When he mentioned this clarification, that the covenant was taken from the messengers that they should believe in Muhammad ﷺ, he said: "whoever turns away after what We have made clear," that is, from the messengers. For this reason I indicated this by my saying: what is taken from the one who is followed is taken from the follower.
* A student: May Allah bless you. The evidence that the earths are layered, one above another?
* The Shaykh: We mentioned it.
* The student: I did not hear it.
* The Shaykh: "Whoever usurps a span of earth, it will be hung around his neck on the Day of Resurrection from seven earths."
* The student: (...)
* The Shaykh: For example, you entered my land and took from it a span; you will be encircled on the Day of Resurrection with seven earths, because I own the surface of the earth you took and I own what is beneath it down to the seventh earth; therefore you were unjust to me down to the seventh earth.
* The student: That means the earth beneath, is there inhabitance on it, or...?
* The Shaykh: Allah knows best. We do not know whether there are inhabitants on it or nothing is on it; that is not within my knowledge.

In this noble verse, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Is it other than the religion of Allah that they seek, while to Him has submitted whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly...﴾; that is, whoever is in the heavens and the earth has submitted to Him. ﴿willingly or unwillingly﴾: a cosmic, decreed submission, from surrender, not a legislated submission; for not all who are on the earth have submitted to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in the legislated sense.

His saying: ﴿and to Him you will be returned﴾; that is, just as He has complete authority over us in this world, so too they will return to Him in the Hereafter. The placing of the complement before the verb indicates restriction, for the complement is the object of the verb, and fronting the object conveys exclusivity: they will return to Allah and not to other than Him, and He will inform them of what they did when they return to Him.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And when Allah took the covenant of the prophets...﴾ to the end. Among the benefits of this noble verse: the prophets, peace be upon them, are servants and worshippers of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, just as others are; the proof from the verse is that Allah took the covenant from them with obligation, which shows that they, like others, are servants and worshippers of Allah as others worship Him.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: establishing that the covenant may be by what Allah gave them of the Book and wisdom, according to the second reading: ﴿for what I have given you of Book﴾. As for the reading in the Mushaf, ﴿lamā﴾, a benefit is derived from it: that Allah, the Exalted, gave them the covenant, or took from them the covenant and pledge, by what He gave them of the Book and wisdom; that is, because they were given the Book and wisdom they became fit for this great covenant, and whatever they were given, they must believe in this Messenger.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: what Allah bestowed upon the prophets of the Book and wisdom. From this benefit follows that whoever inherits this Book and wisdom has taken a generous share of what Allah bestowed upon the prophets. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ said: "The scholars are the heirs of the prophets"[[Narrated by Abu Dawud (3641), al-Tirmidhi (2682) and Ibn Majah (223) from the hadith of Abu al-Darda' (may Allah be pleased with him).]]. So when Allah makes them heirs to the knowledge of the prophets, they must stand in the place of the prophets in calling to Allah, spreading knowledge, and striving in His path; whoever among them is negligent in this has fallen short.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: the excellence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, since Allah took from all the prophets the covenant and pledge that they would believe in him. If someone says: the word "messenger" (rasul) is indefinite, so what makes you apply it to the Prophet ﷺ? The principle with an indefinite noun is that it is a common generic noun not specific to one over another? The answer to that is: this attribute by which Allah described this messenger applies perfectly to whom?
* The students: The Prophet ﷺ.
* The Shaykh: To the Prophet ﷺ. This is supported by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saying to 'Umar: "If my brother Musa were alive, he would have no choice but to follow me." Also supporting this: when the Prophet ﷺ was gathered with the prophets on the night of the Mi'raj, he became their imam, and thus he was the one followed, not the follower, upon him be peace.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the message of the Prophet ﷺ encompasses the affirmation of all the messages; as in His saying: what?
* The students: ﴿confirming what is with you﴾...
* The Shaykh: ﴿confirming what is with you﴾. For this reason this Ummah, by the grace of Allah, and I ask Allah to make me and you among them, is the one that fully confirms all the messengers, and this is a distinction not given to any other.

The Shaykh's commentary on the Quran, surah 3, verses 81–83 (part 4 of 5):

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: it is obligatory upon the prophets to believe in this Messenger who comes to them confirming what they already have, and to support him, based on His words: ﴿You shall surely believe in him and you shall surely support him.﴾ If this is obligatory upon the prophets, it is obligatory upon their nations, because what is obligatory upon the leader is obligatory upon his follower. Therefore all nations must believe in Muhammad (ﷺ) and support him. Whoever is not like this has disbelieved in his Messenger, because his Messenger has taken this covenant from Allah, and it is well known that if they are truthful in following their Messenger, they must follow what their Messenger has committed to.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: it is permissible, indeed prescribed, in important matters, for the one who has taken the covenant to be questioned until he acknowledges and confirms it, in addition to the original contract that took place between him and the one he made the covenant with. This is based on His words: What? (The Shaykh asks the students.)
* Students: (...)
* The Shaykh: ﴿Do you acknowledge and accept My covenant on this condition?﴾ This occurs in great and important matters. A comparable example in some respects is that when the Prophet (ﷺ) questioned the one who had confessed to adultery, he asked him: "Did you do such-and-such? Did you do such-and-such?" until he said to him: "Did you have intercourse with her?" He did not use euphemism. He said: "Yes." He said: "Like the rope disappearing into the well and the kohl-stick into the kohl-pot?" He said: "Yes."[[Reported by al-Bukhari (6824) in abridged form from the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbas, and by Abu Dawud (4428) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "Like the kohl-stick disappearing into the kohl-pot, and the rope into the well?"]] All of this is for the sake of confirmation.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse also: the affirmation that the speech of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is connected to His will, based on His words: ﴿He said: Do you acknowledge?﴾ ﴿They said: We acknowledge. He said: Then bear witness.﴾ All of this shows that His speech, glorified and exalted is He, is audible and connected to His will. This contains a refutation of the Ash'arites (a school of kalam theology) who said that the speech of Allah is the meaning that subsists in His essence, and that it is not connected to His will.
* Student: (...)
* The Shaykh: Complete it?
* Students: (...)
* The Shaykh: It is not connected to His will, because it is an attribute inseparable from Him, like knowledge and life.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: it is permissible for a person to call witnesses against himself, if we say that ﴿He said: Then bear witness﴾ is addressed to each individual separately. If we say it means "bear witness against one another," the verse contains no evidence for that. But bearing witness against oneself is something the Sharia has brought, based on His words: ﴿O you who believe, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for Allah, even if it be against yourselves﴾ [An-Nisa' 135].
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the strengthening of this covenant through these confirmations and attestations, sealed by His words: ﴿and I am with you among the witnesses.﴾ How great is the witnessing of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in any matter! All of this adds to the excellence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that such a covenant, confirmed with these affirmations, was taken for the sake of believing in him (ﷺ) and supporting him.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: if it is obligatory upon the prophets and the earlier nations to believe in the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and support him, then our belief in him and our support for him is all the more binding, because we are affiliated with him, belong to him, and believe him to be our leader, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him. Thus it is obligatory upon us to support him. It is well known that supporting him during his lifetime means fighting alongside him side by side. Supporting him after his death means supporting his Sunnah (the way of the Prophet), spreading it, explaining it to people, defending it, and striving (jihad) for its support. All of this is obligatory upon the Muslim nation. Based on this, the Muslim nation must reject everything that comes to it from the enemies of Allah if it opposes the Sunnah. Everything that comes to us from the disbelievers, whether beliefs, morals, deeds, dealings, or otherwise, if it opposes the Sunnah of the Messenger (ﷺ), then the least that can be said about supporting him is what? That this thing be rejected, that it be thrown back in the face of the one who brought it, and that it have no place among the Muslim nation. For how could it be support when we import from the enemies of this support what contradicts it? Whoever claims that is a liar, for his action contradicts his claim. And if his claim were true, the first thing he would do in supporting the law of Allah is to reject what? Everything that opposes the law of Allah.
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Whoever turns away after that, those are the defiantly disobedient.﴾ ﴿Whoever turns away after that, those are the defiantly disobedient.﴾ That is, from among the nations of these prophets. This conditional sentence does not apply to the prophets, because the prophets, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them, bore witness against themselves and Allah bore witness with them. Rather, this conditional sentence applies to whom?
* Students: Their followers.
* The Shaykh: To their followers. That is, whoever among the followers of the prophets turns away after being reminded of this great covenant is defiantly disobedient.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that defiant disobedience (fisq) is applied to disbelief (kufr). Evidence for this is what we mentioned in the lesson: ﴿Is he who was a believer like one who is defiantly disobedient? They are not equal. As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, for them are gardens of refuge as hospitality for what they used to do. And as for those who defied, their refuge is the Fire﴾ [As-Sajdah 18–20].
* Among the benefits of the verse: whoever turns away before the proof has been established against him is not judged as defiantly disobedient, based on His words: ﴿Whoever turns away after that.﴾
* A significant point follows from this: legal obligations do not bind before knowledge. Legal obligations do not bind before knowledge. This is a great matter, a very great matter on which the scholars have differed at great length. But whoever reflects on the texts of the Book and the Sunnah, and also reflects on the great attributes of Allah, will conclude that legal obligations do not bind before knowledge, because Allah has prescribed for Himself that His mercy precedes His wrath. If we said that legal obligations bind before knowledge, wrath would precede mercy, because we would be obligating a person with something he does not know. However, perhaps the person is negligent in asking, meaning he does not ask. In that case we may obligate him even before he knows, because of what? Because of his negligence. But if he was not negligent, such as a person who grew up in the desert, knows nothing of religion, has no scholar around him, and never occurred to him [the need to learn], so he prayed in a state of major impurity without doing ghusl and continued like this for ten years or more, then came and asked. What do we tell him?
* Student: This is an ignorant person who does not know.
* The Shaykh: We say: there is nothing upon you, because you did not know that ghusl from major impurity is obligatory. But if he were in a town where he could hear and ask, perhaps we would obligate him to make up what he missed. Among examples: many women who reach puberty while young, reach it through menstruation while still young, but they do not fast, on the basis that they are young and that fasting is only obligatory once they have completed fifteen years. Then they come and ask. If we know from their circumstances that they are excused by ignorance, we do not obligate them to make up the fasts they missed, because they are excused. This applies to one who is affiliated with Islam: we excuse him, judge him to be a Muslim, and pray over him when he dies. But as for one who is not affiliated with Islam, that person is a disbeliever, a disbeliever in this world. As for the Hereafter, his knowledge is with Allah. So the people to whom the call did not reach, and who are disbelievers, are disbelievers in this world. If they die, we do not pray over them nor supplicate for them. But in the Hereafter, the correct view is that their affair is with Allah, and that Allah, Exalted is He, tests them with whatever He wills of obligations. Whoever obeys among them enters Paradise, and whoever disobeys enters the Fire. Please pay attention to this matter. As for one who is affiliated with Islam but is in a state that would make him a disbeliever by abandoning an obligation or committing a prohibited act, while the Sharia has not reached him, the preponderant view is that he is not judged as a disbeliever, because he is excused. For this reason you find that the texts of the Book and the Sunnah, all or most of them, are restricted to the conveying of the message, to knowledge, to clarification, and similar matters. And this, as I have told you, is the requirement of the attribute of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, namely that His mercy precedes His wrath. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds. This is why He says: ﴿Whoever turns away after that.﴾
As for one who says that ﴿after that﴾ is a qualification intended to emphasize the severity of the reproach against them, and that whoever turns away even if the matter has not been made clear to him is defiantly disobedient, but He restricted it with "after" to emphasize the severity of the reproach against them, this goes against the principle. Because the principle is that whatever is qualified by an attribute, the attribute returns to it itself and not to something else. Here, what was qualified by "after" is what? The turning away. So if he turns away after knowledge has reached him, then he is defiantly disobedient.
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Do they seek other than the religion of Allah, while to Him submits whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or by compulsion, and to Him they will be returned?﴾
* In this verse: a severe denunciation of those who seek other than the religion of Allah.
* Among its benefits: whoever seeks other than the religion of Allah, even in regulation and what is called law, deserves this great reproach. This is shown by His words, Exalted is He, in Surah al-Ma'idah, which is the last or among the last to be revealed: ﴿Is it the judgment of the time of ignorance that they seek? And who is better than Allah in judgment for a people who are certain?﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 50]. And what is the judgment of the time of ignorance? Everything that opposes the judgment of the Sharia is judgment of ignorance, because the judgment of the Sharia is based on knowledge, and whatever else is based on ignorance. This is the utmost in reproach and rebuke: that you seek a judgment of ignorance and abandon the judgment of whom? The judgment of the All-Knowing, the All-Aware. ﴿And who is better than Allah in judgment for a people who are certain?﴾ By this we know that whoever seeks a judgment other than the judgment of Allah is among the most misguided of the servants of Allah, the most foolish of the servants of Allah, and the most losing of the servants of Allah, and that his affairs will not be set right, neither his religious affairs nor his worldly affairs. We seek refuge in Allah!
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: a condition for the validity and acceptance of an act of worship is that it conform to the law of Allah. Why? Because Allah denounced those who seek a religion other than the religion of Allah. Therefore, sincerity to Allah and conformity to the law of Allah are conditions of worship.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the honoring of this religion which Allah has legislated, because Allah attributed it to Himself, saying: ﴿Do they seek other than the religion of Allah?﴾
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the establishment of proof that it is not fitting for a person to seek a religion other than the religion of Allah while he is a servant owned by Allah, based on His words: ﴿while to Him submits whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or by compulsion.﴾ It has passed in our explanation that this clause may be a circumstantial clause (ḥāliyyah) or a new independent clause (isti'nāfiyyah).
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the generality of the dominion and authority of Allah. From where is this derived?
* Students: (...)
* The Shaykh: ﴿while to Him submits whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or by compulsion.﴾ This is the completeness of authority and dominion: that everyone in the heavens and the earth is submitting to Allah, whether obediently or under compulsion. Therefore no one can deviate or resist the decree of Allah. If the most arrogant of Allah's creation came wanting to resist what Allah, Exalted is He, has decreed, could he do that? Never. Pharaoh was a tyrant, obstinate, and he was drowned by the very thing he boasted of: ﴿He said: O my people, is not the dominion of Egypt mine, and these rivers flowing beneath me? Then do you not see?﴾ [Az-Zukhruf 51]. By what was he destroyed?
* Students: By water.
* The Shaykh: By the water he had boasted of. And ʿĀd were arrogant upon the earth, saying ﴿Who is mightier than us in strength?﴾ [Fussilat 15], so by what were they destroyed? By the wind, air, air that Allah subjected against them until it destroyed them: ﴿They became such that nothing could be seen except their dwellings﴾ [Al-Ahqaf 25]. This is the completeness of strength and power. Today, when the weak in faith are told: return to your religion and you will be victorious over your enemies, they say: how will we be victorious over our enemies, and what can we do? We cannot even thread a needle! How can we resist the people of missiles, the people of cannons, and the people of guided bombs? They did not know that the matter is in the hand of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and that if He wills, He flattens the earth over them completely, and they are swallowed down to the seventh layer with a single word. If we were truthful with Allah, Allah would be truthful with us. But in reality we have neglected the command of Allah, so when we forgot Allah, Allah forgot us, He abandoned us. I heard some years ago that Allah sent upon Washington, the capital of America, is it the capital or almost the capital? Students: It is the capital. The Shaykh: He sent upon it thunderbolts, thunderbolts from those clouds like cotton, thunderbolts, meaning they nearly destroyed it, to the point that the electric wires were cut, the lights went out, and this great capital, one of the largest capitals in the world, became plunged in darkness, and there was massive looting of hotels and commercial shops, and there were lootings and other things. And these thunderbolts, meaning from the smallest thing: an earthquake strikes the earth and in one instant destroys hundreds of cities and villages, hundreds of cities and villages. And by what did this earthquake happen? By one word, which is what?
* Students: Be.
* The Shaykh: (Be), only, (Be), and the top of the earth was turned to its bottom and all the features of the earth were changed. So if we are truthful with Allah, Allah is truthful with us.
It is related that Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas, while pursuing the Persians from city to city until he reached the Tigris: when he reached the Tigris, the Persians had moved to al-Mada'in on the other side of the Tigris to the east. They had sunk the boats and broken the bridges so the Muslims could not cross to them. Saʿd stopped, having with him only camels, horses, and foot soldiers, and could not proceed. He called out to Salman al-Farisi, may Allah be pleased with him, and said: O Salman, give us from your, meaning from your military planning, because he was the one who advised the Prophet (ﷺ) to dig the trench. He said: By Allah, O Saʿd, there is no reinforcement now, there is no strategy except the fear of Allah. But let me look at the army. If they are in the fear of Allah, then He who split the sea for Musa will make the crossing easy for us over this river, because this nation is better than the nation of Musa. Allahu Akbar, look at the faith!
So Salman went and looked at the army (...). What did he see? At night they spend the night before their Lord, prostrating and standing in prayer, and by day they attend to the affairs of war and what is needed for war. He returned to him after three days and said: By Allah, they are in the best condition, but seek help from Allah and cross. So Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas called out to the people and said: We are crossing, if Allah wills. But I will stand and say: In the name of Allah, and I will say Allahu Akbar three times. When I say the third takbir, cross. He did so, saying: In the name of Allah, then he said Allahu Akbar three times. When he said the third, the people crossed walking upon the water, and the river was throwing up its foam, flowing and moving. You know the river is not like the sea, which stands still; it flows. The historians say that even when a Persian horse grew tired, Allah caused a mound of earth to rise for it, and the horse stood on it to rest, until they had crossed the Tigris. When the Persians saw them, they cried out and shouted, saying: You are only fighting jinn, you have no power against these people. Flee! So they fled and left al-Mada'in, and they were defeated, praise be to Allah, under the banner of tawhid and jihad that was founded on piety, so that the word of Allah would be supreme, not seeking martyrdom, nor for the sake of nationalism, tribalism, or homeland. Their only concern was that the word of Allah be supreme, and that this Qur'an be the law for the people of the earth.
The people of al-Mada'in fled from it, the capital, the capital of Persia. The Muslims came, conquered it, and gained such wealth as only the Lord of the servants knows, just as the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Their treasures, the treasures of Khosrow and Caesar, will surely be spent in the way of Allah."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3618) and Muslim (2918/75) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]] And they took the crown, the crown of Khosrow, on which he would sit, above his head, adorned with pearls and gold and whatever else of the adornments of this world, as Allah willed. They wanted to carry it but found only two large camels that could carry it from al-Mada'in to Medina.

At that time there were no large ships or large cars. So they carried him on two camels from al-Mada'in to Madinah, and they placed him before the Commander of the Faithful 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him. And what would you know of 'Umar, who was just, so they were just, and who was secure, so they were secure! He said, while looking at it: "By Allah, a people who delivered this are trustworthy!" The Commander of the Faithful 'Ali ibn Abi Talib said: "Yes, O Commander of the Faithful, they are trustworthy, because you were trustworthy. Had you indulged yourself, they would have indulged themselves."[[Narrated in al-Kamil fi al-Tarikh by Ibn al-Athir (2/362), and al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, Hajar edition (10/17).]]

Allahu Akbar! This is the crown of Khosrow from al-Mada'in, being distributed among the Muslims in Madinah. Who gave them victory until they crossed the river with their horses and their men on foot, if not Allah, the Mighty and Majestic? Why do we not believe in this? By Allah, we are weak in faith! Why do we not believe? Does not the Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, who is the most truthful of speakers and the most capable of doers, say: ﴿Allah will surely help those who help Him. Indeed, Allah is Strong and Mighty. Those who, if We establish them in the land, establish prayer, give zakah, enjoin what is right, and forbid what is wrong. And with Allah is the outcome of all affairs﴾ [al-Hajj 40–41].

These are emphatic assurances, both verbal and substantive, from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. If we had true faith, we would be the first to act upon this verse. Let us see: with what do we help Allah? Because Allah made a condition: ﴿Allah will surely help those who help Him﴾. With what do we help Allah, so that we may see? Now calamities come upon the Muslims in various forms, various calamities. We see hardly anyone, except a rare few, saying: "O people, return to your religion; the affliction is from you. Who has spoken and said: the error is our error, the injustice is our injustice, so let us return to our Lord so that these wrongdoers are not set over us?" For Allah says: ﴿And thus We make some of the wrongdoers allies of others, because of what they used to earn﴾ [al-An'am 129].

Calamities come as though they were merely material events unconnected with religion, even though we are Muslims. And for a Muslim, these events occur only because of his own deeds. The disbeliever may be given in this world whatever he desires, because his good things have been hastened to him in the life of this world. He is given more luxury in this world than the Muslim is given, but when he passes to the Hereafter the punishment upon him will be more severe, because he has passed from what to what?
* A student: From bliss...
* The Shaykh: From bliss to punishment, from bliss to punishment. So he loses what he used to enjoy in this world, and it will be more severe upon him, more severe and greater. Therefore my advice to you in such circumstances is that you make people aware. Say: this which has befallen us is not a material event, a dispute over money or the economy or borders or land or the like. No, it is a divine decree, by which some of us have been set over others, because we have neglected the command of Allah. ﴿Whatever affliction befalls you is because of what your hands have earned, and He pardons much﴾ [al-Shura 30]. As for our remaining as we are, as if nothing has happened, when nothing has happened: the merchant in his lying and his cheating, the employee in his betrayal and his failure to do the work, each person in what he is engaged in, as if nothing has happened. This undoubtedly indicates the death of hearts and their hardness, and that they do not take heed, and that affairs and events are likely to develop and change for the worse. For Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, brings about such things so that perhaps we may turn in repentance. As the Messenger (ﷺ) said concerning the eclipse: «Indeed Allah, the Exalted, causes it so that perhaps His servants will turn to Him in repentance»[[Narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad (20178) from the hadith of Samurah ibn Jundub, with the wording «But they are signs of Allah by which His servants take warning. So He sees who among them turns to Him in repentance.»]]. But where are the attentive hearts? We ask Allah to make us and you attentive.
* The students: Amin.
* The Shaykh: The conclusion: Allah rebukes those who seek other than the religion of Allah, and says: how can you seek other than the religion of Allah when the whole matter belongs to Allah? ﴿And to Him has submitted whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly﴾?!

From the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of the heavens and that they are a number, and the evidences indicate that they are seven. Likewise the earth is seven, but Allah the Exalted did not explicitly state this in the Qur'an; rather He said: ﴿and of the earth, the like thereof﴾ [al-Talaq 12], and the explicit statement about it came in the Sunnah.
* From the benefits of this noble verse: that the return is to Allah, ﴿and to Him they will be returned﴾. They return in this world and they return in the Hereafter. As for this world, the return is to Allah in rulings: the judgment belongs to Allah, the worship belongs to Allah, the command belongs to Allah, the prohibition belongs to Allah. We return to Him, to His law, not to the opinion of so-and-so, nor to the law of so-and-so, nor to the system of so-and-so, but we return to Allah. Likewise we return to Him in the Hereafter, the return to Allah in the Hereafter, and every person will be held accountable for what he did: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾ [al-Zalzalah 7–8].
* From the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of the permanence of Allah, because if the return of all creation is to Him, it follows that He, the Mighty and Majestic, will endure, so that He may be the place of return for all creation.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verse 81–83 (part 1 of 5):

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And when Allah took the covenant of the Prophets﴾ [Aal-i-Imran 81]. (Idh) is the object of a verb that is omitted, its estimated form being: (remember). ﴿And when Allah took the covenant of the Prophets﴾ means: remember, O Muhammad, to those to whom We sent you, this covenant and pact. ﴿Allah took the covenant of the Prophets﴾. Al-mithaq is al-'ahd (the covenant), and it is called mithaq (covenant) because each of the two parties to the agreement is bound to the other by it, like al-wathaq (the bond), the rope with which a person is tied.
His saying: ﴿the Prophets﴾ includes the Messengers, because every Messenger is also a Prophet.
His saying: ﴿that which I have given you of Scripture and wisdom﴾ [Aal-i-Imran 81] has three readings: ﴿لَمَا آتَيْتُكُمْ﴾, ﴿لِمَا آتَيْتُكُمْ﴾, and ﴿لَمَا آتَيْنَاكُمْ﴾. In all the readings there is a shift (iltifat). From where?
* A student: From the third person (ghaybah).
* The Shaykh: From the third person to the second person (hudur).
His saying: ﴿لَمَا آتَيْتُكُمْ﴾: concerning the lam there are two readings: kasra, and the second, fatha.
His saying: ﴿آتَيْتُكُمْ﴾ means: I gave you. The giving here refers to what Allah gave the Prophets of the matters of the Sharia, and for this He said: ﴿of Scripture and wisdom﴾. The Scripture is well known, such as the Torah and the Gospel. Wisdom: judging between people and attaining what is correct, because judging between people and attaining what is correct is placing things in their proper places, and this is wisdom.
﴿Then there came to you a Messenger confirming what is with you, you shall believe in him and you shall support him﴾ [Aal-i-Imran 81] means: what I have given you of Scripture and wisdom, when a Messenger comes to you confirming what is with you, you will believe in him and support him.
His saying: ﴿confirming what is with you﴾ has two meanings:
The first meaning: he confirms the scriptures that preceded him, saying for example that the Torah is true, and the Gospel is true, and similar things.
The second meaning: he comes as a fulfilment (muṣādaqah) of what the earlier scriptures foretold, because the scriptures informed about him; when he comes in conformity with what they informed of, what does he become? He becomes a confirmation of them. So on this aspect he is a testimony that this Book is true, and on the first aspect he is a testimony that the earlier scriptures are true. The difference between the two meanings is therefore clear. ﴿confirming what is with you﴾: we said it has two meanings:
One of them: that the Prophet ﷺ testified to the truth of what preceded him of the scriptures.
The second: that his message was what? A fulfilment of what the earlier scriptures had informed of; because Allah the Exalted says concerning the Prophet ﷺ: ﴿Whom they find written with them in the Torah and the Gospel, who enjoins upon them what is right and forbids them what is wrong﴾ [al-A'raf 157]. So when he came in the description that the Torah and the Gospel brought, he became a fulfilment of them, because they informed of a thing and this thing came, so he is confirmed. Do you see? If one of the people said: so-and-so will arrive today after noon, and he arrived, then the one who arrived has become a confirmation of what was reported. Thus when the Messengers said that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah who is sent in the manner Allah described, enjoining right and forbidding wrong, and he came in conformity with what they reported, he became a confirmation of them.
﴿confirming what is with you﴾, i.e., of what is with you, from what? From the earlier scriptures they brought.
﴿you shall believe in him﴾ [Aal-i-Imran 81]: this is the place of the covenant, meaning: if this Messenger confirming what is with you comes to you, then My covenant upon you is ﴿you shall believe in him and you shall support him﴾ [Aal-i-Imran 81]. ﴿you shall believe in him﴾ means you shall believe that he is true. ﴿and you shall support him﴾ means you shall help him in spreading his message and in fighting his enemies, because support here includes support by knowledge and by weapons.
﴿He said: Do you acknowledge and accept My burden upon that?﴾ They said: "We acknowledge it." [Aal-i-Imran 81]. When He had informed that He took from them the covenant and pact, He made them confirm this: ﴿He said: Do you acknowledge and accept My burden upon that? They said: We acknowledge it﴾.
His saying: ﴿Do you acknowledge﴾ means: do you admit and commit yourselves to that. His saying: ﴿accept My burden upon that﴾ means: you accepted the heavy covenant, because al-isr, whose plural is (aṣār), means heavy things, so ﴿My burden﴾ means My heavy covenant.
﴿They said: We acknowledge it﴾: there is a reading among us, ﴿He said: Do you acknowledge﴾, in which it is read ﴿آأَقْرَرْتُمْ﴾ with the first alif lengthened. ﴿They said: We acknowledge it. He said: Then bear witness﴾ [Aal-i-Imran 81]. ﴿They said: We acknowledge it﴾ means: we admitted and committed ourselves to believe in him and support him. ﴿He said: Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses﴾.
﴿Bear witness﴾ means: let some of you bear witness against others, and let all of you bear witness to the covenant between Me and you. ﴿And I am with you among the witnesses﴾, and Allah suffices as a witness. So He made them witnesses against themselves, and He, Mighty and Majestic, bore witness against them of what took place.
Now we return to the grammar. We said: ﴿Idh akhadha Allah﴾ is the object of an omitted verb, its estimated form being: (remember when Allah took).
His saying: ﴿لَمَا آتَيْتُكُمْ﴾ has two readings: ﴿لَمَا﴾ and ﴿لِمَا﴾. On the reading ﴿لِمَا﴾ the lam is causal (lam al-ta'lil), and ma is a relative pronoun, i.e., for that which I gave you of Scripture and wisdom, ﴿you shall believe in him﴾. So the cause precedes the thing caused. The estimate on this basis is: And when Allah took the covenant of the Prophets, that you shall believe in this Messenger, because of what I have given you of Scripture and wisdom. So the lam is then causal.
