............................ ∗∗∗ wa-bimā wa-qad wa-bilan wa-bi-t-tanfīs
This is lan; the fa' is the linking particle for the response: ﴿then it will never be accepted from him﴾, meaning that religion will not be accepted. And His saying ﴿fa-lan yuqbala﴾: He did not say "then Allah will not accept," He said ﴿fa-lan yuqbala minhu﴾, to encompass rejection and refusal from Allah the Mighty and Majestic, from the Messenger, and from the Muslims; therefore it is not permissible for Muslims to allow anyone to follow a religion other than the sharī'ah of the Messenger (peace be upon him); it is not permissible for them to do so. ﴿Lan yuqbala minhu﴾. And in His saying ﴿fa-lan yuqbala minhu﴾, is the acceptance meant here complete acceptance or acceptance of validity?
* The students: Validity..
* The Shaykh: Acceptance of validity. The evidence for that is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ, narrated by the two Shaykhs from 'Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her), that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever does an action that is not in accordance with our command, it is rejected" [[Agreed upon; narrated by al-Bukhari (2697) and Muslim (1718/18), the wording being his, from the hadith of 'Aisha.]] rejected; so whoever follows a religion other than Islam, whether in its root or in its branches, his religion is rejected and refused, ﴿fa-lan yuqbala minhu﴾. And will he be given reward in the Hereafter for his deed?
No; therefore He said: ﴿and he, in the Hereafter, will be among the losers﴾, and this, by Allah, is the great loss: that a person lives in this world as long as Allah wills him to live, then he does not earn what benefits him in the Hereafter; when he comes before his Lord he will find nothing, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage in a qī'ah﴾ [an-Nur 39]. Do you know the mirage in a qī'ah? Qī'ah means a level, wide plain. In such land, in intense heat, it appears to a person from afar that there is water; that is the mirage, it is called the mirage. When a thirsty person comes and finds this mirage which seems like water of the sea, he rejoices and hastens toward it, until when he reaches it he finds nothing, and so disappointment comes after strong hope; and this is the most severe regret for a person, that his disappointment comes at the height of his hope; because if a person had not hoped in the first place it would not have troubled him, but the problem is that he hopes and then is overturned, and this is worse. We ask Allah for well-being!
﴿Until when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing, and finds Allah with him, and He will pay him his account in full. And Allah is swift in reckoning﴾ [an-Nur 39]. Everyone who does not adopt Islam as his religion will be a loser in the Hereafter. ﴿And We will turn to what they did of deeds and make them scattered dust﴾ [al-Furqan 23]; and His saying ﴿and he, in the Hereafter, will be among the losers﴾ includes the loss of the self, the loss of wealth, and the loss of family. As for the loss of the self, he will gain nothing from his deeds. As for the loss of wealth, even if he spends all his wealth on what benefits people, he will not benefit from it in the Hereafter; meaning, if he repairs roads, builds mosques, and builds schools, it will not benefit him. I suppose you do not expect that this would come from an outright disbeliever, building mosques and schools; but it would come from an apostate disbeliever. For example, a man who does not pray but is a man of good who builds mosques, builds schools, repairs roads, and feeds the needy; does he benefit from any of this deed? No; because he is a disbeliever, and a disbeliever's deeds will never benefit him on the Day of Resurrection.
Alright, as for the loss of wealth, we have just mentioned that if he spends it he gains nothing; as for the loss of family, they also do not benefit him in this world; if they make supplication for him, he will not benefit from that, if they make supplication for him he will not benefit from that; because Allah says: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believed to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were relatives, after it has become clear to them that they are the companions of the Blazing Fire﴾ [at-Tawbah 113], and they do not benefit from supplication. Likewise in the Hereafter they do not benefit from their families, because each one is separated from the other in the fire of Hell. Unlike the believers, for Allah says: ﴿And those who believed and whose descendants followed them in faith – We will join them with their descendants, and We will not deprive them of anything of their deeds. Every person is held in pledge for what he has earned﴾ [at-Tur 21]. If you have offspring who are in the fifth rank while you are in the seventh rank, the offspring are elevated from the fifth to the seventh, and you are not lowered at all. It is not said: "Descend a rank while they ascend a rank, and you will be in which one?" In the sixth? The offspring are in the fifth and the fathers in the seventh; the offspring are raised from the fifth to the seventh and the fathers are not lowered from the seventh to the sixth. That is, if someone says: this rises a rank and that falls a rank, is this justice? But we say: Allah deals with bounty, the Mighty and Majestic; therefore He said: ﴿and We did not deprive them﴾; because someone might suppose that if the offspring are raised, the reward of the fathers is diminished, so He said: ﴿and We will not deprive them of anything of their deeds﴾. Why? ﴿Every person is held in pledge for what he has earned﴾. And if we lowered the fathers, the doer would not be held in pledge for what he earned. Yes indeed.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿How will Allah guide a people who disbelieved after their belief﴾; (how): an interrogative meaning deep improbability; meaning it is very far, if not impossible, that Allah should guide a people who disbelieved after their belief; meaning they apostatized after they believed and knew the truth, so their guidance is far off; and that is because whoever knows the truth and then turns away from it is greater in crime than one who did not know the truth and did not enter it and remained in his disbelief. Therefore we say: the apostate disbeliever is greater than the original disbeliever, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter. In this world the original disbeliever is left in his religion and is not compelled to leave it, but the apostate is not allowed to remain in his apostasy; rather he is compelled to return to Islam or be killed, due to the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Whoever changes his religion, kill him" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari (3017) from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas.]]. So Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: it is far that Allah should guide a people who disbelieved after their belief; as for those who were upon disbelief from the start, how many have been guided after having been upon disbelief. ﴿And they testified that the Messenger is true﴾; the ﴿al-Rasul﴾ here is the al- of mental familiarity (al-'ahd al-dhihni), because it has not been previously mentioned but is known in the mind. Incidentally, we say: the definite al- of familiarity is divided into three types: mental familiarity, mentioned familiarity, and present familiarity. Three types:
Mentioned familiarity: when it is prefixed to what has already been mentioned.
Present familiarity: when it is prefixed to something present.
Mental familiarity: when it is prefixed to something known in the mind. For example, His saying ﴿and they testified that the Messenger is true﴾ means the Messenger of Allah Muhammad ﷺ; because His saying ﴿How will Allah guide a people who disbelieved after their belief﴾ means that guidance is expected for them, and this is not possible after the revelation of the Qur'an except if the Messenger is Muhammad ﷺ; and you say, for example, while you are in the city: "The judge has come"; which judge? The well-known judge of the city.
Mentioned familiarity is when it is prefixed to what was previously mentioned, such as His saying: ﴿As We sent to Pharaoh a messenger (15). But Pharaoh disobeyed the messenger﴾ [al-Muzzammil 15, 16]. Who is meant by the first messenger?
* The students: Moses.
* The Shaykh: The first messenger, who was sent to Pharaoh, is Moses, and here the familiarity is mentioned.

**The presential definite article (al-ʿahd al-ḥuḍūrī, the "I mean this one, which is present" use of *al-*):** This is most common with *al-* that follows a demonstrative noun for something present, because the demonstrative points to a referent and that referent is present. For example, you say: "هذا اليوم شديد الحر" (*hādhā al-yawm shadīd al-ḥarr*, "This day is very hot"). Which day? The present one: "يومنا هذا، اليوم الحاضر" ("today, the present day"). Similarly, Allah says: ﴿الْيَوْمَ أَكْمَلْتُ لَكُمْ دِينَكُمْ﴾ [al-Mā'ida 3], "Today I have perfected your religion for you," where *al-yawm* means the present day.

There is a second *al-* that is the counterpart of the presential *al-*, namely the generic *al-* (al-jinsiyya). The generic *al-* indicates the reality of a kind, and indicates the encompassing of that reality. If you say: "الرجال أكمل من النساء" (*al-rijāl akmal min al-nisāʾ*, "Men are more complete than women"), this is the generic *al-* indicating the reality of the category: the category of men is superior to the category of women. It does not mean that every man is more complete than every woman. Among women are those who are better than many men. Is this clear? Good. The generic *al-* may also indicate totality, as in Allah's words: ﴿إِنَّ الْإِنْسَانَ لَفِي خُسْرٍ﴾ [al-ʿAṣr 2], "Indeed, mankind is in loss." That is, every person is in loss. Its sign is that *kull* (كلّ, "every," with a doubled *lām*) can take its place. Here: ﴿وَشَهِدُوا أَنَّ الرَّسُولَ حَقٌّ﴾, "and they had testified that the Messenger was true," meaning: established truth, truthful in what he reported, just in what he judged (ﷺ). ﴿وَجَاءَهُمُ الْبَيِّنَاتُ﴾, "and the clear proofs had come to them," meaning the clear signs that demonstrate the truthfulness of what the Messenger (ﷺ) brought. *Al-bayyināt* is feminine, yet its verb is not feminine (*jāʾahum*, not *jāʾathum*), for two reasons:

The first reason: its feminine marking is not real (ḥaqīqī).

The second reason: a separation has been made between it and the verb. It has also come in the Qur'an in the feminine form: ﴿جَاءَتْهُمُ الْبَيِّنَاتُ﴾ [al-Baqara 213]. This is permissible, and so is that.

﴿وَاللَّهُ لَا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾, "And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people." The clause is resumptive (isti'nāfiyya), and in meaning it is like a reason (ta'līl) for what precedes it. It is as if He says: Allah does not guide them because they are wrongdoers, *al-ẓālimīn*: those who wronged themselves, since the truth became manifest to them and its face became clear, yet they disbelieved nonetheless.

Then He, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿أُولَئِكَ جَزَاؤُهُمْ أَنَّ عَلَيْهِمْ لَعْنَةَ اللَّهِ وَالْمَلَائِكَةِ وَالنَّاسِ أَجْمَعِينَ﴾, "Those—their recompense is that upon them is the curse of Allah, and of the angels, and of mankind, all together."

I have not parsed the first verse. His words ﴿كَيْفَ يَهْدِي اللَّهُ قَوْمًا كَفَرُوا بَعْدَ إِيمَانِهِمْ وَشَهِدُوا﴾, "How will Allah guide a people who disbelieved after their belief and had testified," the word ﴿وَشَهِدُوا﴾ is conjoined (*maʿṭūfa*) to ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾. However, it may bear another meaning, namely that it is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), i.e., "while they had testified that the Messenger is true." They disbelieved after their belief, while they had testified that the Messenger is true. This is because if its conjunction is to ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾, then "they disbelieved after their belief and testified," disbelief in which there is testimony would be a disbelief in which testimony does not benefit.

Then He said: ﴿أُولَئِكَ جَزَاؤُهُمْ أَنَّ عَلَيْهِمْ لَعْنَةَ اللَّهِ وَالْمَلَائِكَةِ وَالنَّاسِ أَجْمَعِينَ﴾. *Ulāʾika* refers to those indicated, who disbelieved after their belief, testified that the Messenger is true, and the clear proofs came to them. He used the demonstrative in the form of distance, indicating the lowness of their rank. The demonstrative of distance may be used for a near referent to indicate the elevation of rank, and it may be used to indicate the lowness of rank. Here it indicates the lowness of their rank, so because of their lowly rank they are treated as distant and are pointed to with the distance demonstrative. ﴿جَزَاؤُهُمْ﴾, "their recompense," meaning their repayment for their deeds. ﴿أَنَّ عَلَيْهِمْ لَعْنَةَ اللَّهِ﴾: here *ʿalayhim* (على, "upon") indicates that the curse came upon them as something deserved, and from a lofty command, because it is a curse. The curse of Allah is His expulsion and distancing of someone from His mercy. That is, He, glorified and exalted, expelled them and distanced them from the mercy of Allah.

﴿وَالْمَلَائِكَةِ﴾, meaning: and the curse of the angels. *Al-malāʾika* is the plural of *malak*, and its origin is *ma'lak*, from *al-ʾalūka*, which is "message." However, there is an inversion (iʿlāl bil-qalb) in it, meaning a transposition of the place (qalb al-makān), not a change of the letter. This happened by placing the *lām* before and the *hamza* after, so it became *maʾlak*. The plural of *maʾlak* is *malāʾika*. Then it was eased, and it is said that *malak* replaced *maʾlak*.

The angels are a kind of created beings, an unseen world, whom Allah created from light and made *ṣumud* (solid, not eating or drinking). Since they do not eat or drink, they do not urinate or defecate. This is why Allah described them as purified, saying: ﴿إِنَّهُ لَقُرْآنٌ كَرِيمٌ (٧٧) فِي كِتَابٍ مَكْنُونٍ (٧٨) لَا يَمَسُّهُ إِلَّا الْمُطَهَّرُونَ﴾ [al-Wāqiʿa 77–79], "Indeed, it is an honorable Qur'an, in a Book protected, which none touches except the purified."

﴿وَالنَّاسِ أَجْمَعِينَ﴾: *al-nās* are the children of Adam. Its origin is *ʾanās*, and the *hamza* was dropped for ease because of frequent usage. As for His words ﴿أَجْمَعِينَ﴾, it is an emphatic (tawkīd) for what precedes it. Is it an emphatic directly for what precedes it, or for what precedes it and what precedes that?

* Student: Yes, for all of them.
* Shaykh: For all of them: the angels all together and mankind all together.

Good. ﴿خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا﴾, "abiding therein." It is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), meaning abiding in this curse, remaining in it either eternally or for a long stay. Because *al-khulūd*, as the linguists said, is used for a long stay and is also used for a perpetual stay. But here, does it mean a long stay or a perpetual one? It means the perpetual one, because these are disbelievers, and disbelievers abide forever in punishment. ﴿لَا يُخَفَّفُ عَنْهُمُ الْعَذَابُ﴾, "the punishment will not be lightened for them." *Al-takhfīf* is the opposite of *al-tathqīl* (making heavy); that is, the punishment cannot be made easier for them even for one day. This is why ﴿قَالَ الَّذِينَ فِي النَّارِ لِخَزَنَةِ جَهَنَّمَ ادْعُوا رَبَّكُمْ يُخَفِّفْ عَنَّا يَوْمًا مِنَ الْعَذَابِ﴾ [Ghāfir 49], "Those in the Fire will say to the keepers of Hell, 'Call upon your Lord to lighten for us a day of the punishment.'" Look: (may Allah protect us) they asked the angels to call on Allah on their behalf, so that they would be intermediaries between them and Allah. Yet even so, they did not say "Call upon our Lord," they said ﴿ادْعُوا رَبَّكُمْ﴾, "Call upon your Lord," out of their extreme shame and humiliation before Allah. Then they said ﴿يُخَفِّفْ عَنَّا يَوْمًا مِنَ الْعَذَابِ﴾, "lighten for us a day of the punishment," and they did not seek deliverance from punishment absolutely, nor did they ask that the punishment be lightened permanently, because they knew that they were in error, indeed sinners. Therefore they asked that the punishment be lightened for one day, but that will not happen. This is why He said: ﴿لَا يُخَفَّفُ عَنْهُمُ الْعَذَابُ﴾, "the punishment will not be lightened for them." *Al-ʿadhāb* means the punishment. ﴿وَلَا هُمْ يُنْظَرُونَ﴾, "nor will they be reprieved," meaning they will not be given respite or delayed; rather they will be hastened to punishment.

Consider, may Allah bless you, His words about the people of the Fire: ﴿وَسِيقَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إِلَى جَهَنَّمَ زُمَرًا حَتَّى إِذَا جَاءُوهَا فُتِحَتْ أَبْوَابُهَا وَقَالَ لَهُمْ خَزَنَتُهَا أَلَمْ يَأْتِكُمْ رُسُلٌ مِنْكُمْ﴾ [al-Zumar 71], "And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups, until when they reach it, its gates will be opened, and its keepers will say to them, 'Did there not come to you messengers from among you?'" And He said about the people of Paradise: ﴿وَسِيقَ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا رَبَّهُمْ إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ زُمَرًا حَتَّى إِذَا جَاءُوهَا وَفُتِحَتْ أَبْوَابُهَا﴾ [al-Zumar 73], "And those who feared their Lord will be driven to Paradise in groups, until when they reach it and its gates are opened." ﴿جَاءُوهَا وَفُتِحَتْ﴾, "they reach it and its gates are opened." So there is a difference between these and those. The people of the Fire, (may Allah protect us), are hastened by its opening, so the punishment confronts them as soon as they approach it. As for the people of Paradise, when they reach Paradise they are made to stop at a bridge between Paradise and the Fire, and retribution is taken among them for one another, a special retribution different from the first one that occurs on the plains of Resurrection, so that what is in their hearts of rancor and hatred is removed, until they enter Paradise in the purest state of affection: ﴿إِخْوَانًا عَلَى سُرُرٍ مُتَقَابِلِينَ﴾ [al-Ḥijr 47], "as brothers, on couches facing one another."

This is why we say about the *wāw* here: it is conjoined (ʿāṭifa) to the omitted response of the conditional, meaning: "until when they reach it, such-and-such occurs, and its gates are opened." It is not extra (zāʾida), as some have claimed, nor is it the "eighth *wāw*" (wāw al-thamāniya), as some have also claimed. Rather it is a conjunctive *wāw* in the usual manner, and the thing conjoined to is omitted.

So ﴿لَا هُمْ يُنْظَرُونَ﴾ means they will not be given respite, and the punishment will not be delayed from them; rather they will be hastened into it. Indeed they will be hastened into it before the Hour arrives, as Allah said to the family of Pharaoh: ﴿النَّارُ يُعْرَضُونَ عَلَيْهَا غُدُوًّا وَعَشِيًّا وَيَوْمَ تَقُومُ السَّاعَةُ أَدْخِلُوا آلَ فِرْعَوْنَ أَشَدَّ الْعَذَابِ﴾ [Ghāfir 46], "The Fire, they are exposed to it morning and evening, and on the day the Hour is established: 'Admit the family of Pharaoh into the severest punishment.'" Indeed they will be hastened into punishment before they die: ﴿وَلَوْ تَرَى إِذْ يَتَوَفَّى الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا الْمَلَائِكَةُ يَضْرِبُونَ وُجُوهَهُمْ وَأَدْبَارَهُمْ وَذُوقُوا عَذَابَ الْحَرِيقِ﴾ [al-Anfāl 50], "If only you could see when the angels take those who disbelieved, striking their faces and their backs, 'Taste the punishment of the burning.'" And they will be rebuked before they die: ﴿وَلَوْ تَرَى إِذِ الظَّالِمُونَ فِي غَمَرَاتِ الْمَوْتِ وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ بَاسِطُو أَيْدِيهِمْ أَخْرِجُوا أَنْفُسَكُمُ الْيَوْمَ تُجْزَوْنَ عَذَابَ الْهُونِ بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَقُولُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ غَيْرَ الْحَقِّ وَكُنْتُمْ عَنْ آيَاتِهِ تَسْتَكْبِرُونَ﴾ [al-Anʿām 93], "If only you could see when the wrongdoers are in the agonies of death, and the angels are extending their hands, 'Release your souls! Today you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation for what you used to say about Allah other than the truth, and for being arrogant toward His signs.'" Consider His words: ﴿أَخْرِجُوا أَنْفُسَكُمُ﴾, "release your souls." By Allah, they are greedy with these souls, stingy. The soul, when given the good news of punishment, recoils, shrinks, and retreats into the body. So they say: ﴿أَخْرِجُوا أَنْفُسَكُمُ﴾, "give us your souls." For what? For punishment: ﴿الْيَوْمَ تُجْزَوْنَ عَذَابَ الْهُونِ﴾, "Today you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation." So what about you, (may Allah protect us), with this evil, ugly glad tidings at the time of departing from the world and parting from family, wealth, and homeland? It is indeed a critical hour, (may Allah protect us), and we ask Allah to make our end good and yours! A critical state, in which they are not given respite and not reprieved in punishment from the moment death comes to them until eternity, forever, (may Allah protect us). We ask Allah for well-being for us and for you!

He says: ﴿إِلَّا الَّذِينَ تَابُوا مِنْ بَعْدِ ذَلِكَ وَأَصْلَحُوا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān 89], "Except those who repent after that and reform, for indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful." O Allah, to You belongs all praise. The mercy of Allah precedes His anger. Those who disbelieved after their belief, and testified that the Messenger is true, and the clear proofs came to them, and the proof was established against them from every direction: if they turn back to Allah, Allah turns to them in forgiveness. ﴿إِلَّا الَّذِينَ تَابُوا مِنْ بَعْدِ ذَلِكَ وَأَصْلَحُوا﴾: *tābū*, meaning they returned to Allah. Repentance (*tawba*) is the return to Allah from His disobedience to His obedience, and from fleeing from Him to taking refuge at His door.

Repentance has five conditions, which I will recite to you and require of you:

The first condition: sincerity to Allah (al-ikhlāṣ). That is, a person intends by his repentance the face of Allah, and that He accept it from him and pardon him, not that he intends by his repentance to show off to people or to seek any worldly matter. This is because a repentant person may want to show off to people, so that people know he has repented and returned, and they praise him for that. This repentance is of no benefit to him and is not accepted from him. Or he intends by his repentance some worldly matter: he hears that Allah says ﴿وَمَنْ يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ يَجْعَلْ لَهُ مِنْ أَمْرِهِ يُسْرًا﴾ [al-Ṭalāq 4], "And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him ease in his affair," while he wants a wife, and says: "Perhaps I will fear Allah so that Allah makes a wife easy for me." This fear or this repentance is very weak. This is why Shaykh al-Islam Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhab, may Allah have mercy on him, said in *Kitāb al-Tawḥīd*: "Chapter: Among shirk is a person's intention in his deed to seek the worldly life." This is a lowly intention, but it is not like the first one. The first wants to draw near to people through what he draws near to Allah with, and this is a great matter: making what belongs to Allah serve creation. As for this one, no, he did not intend this. He intended to draw near to Allah in order that some worldly matter be made easy for him, and in the Hereafter he is heedless of it. So this one who intended by repentance one of two things: his repentance is rejected in comparison to the first, the one who sought showing off; and very weak in comparison to the second, the one who lacks sincerity to Allah.

The second condition of repentance: regret for what one has done of sin. Regret has become problematic for some people. They say: How can a person regret? A person cannot make himself regret. But in reality there is no problem with it at all, no problem whatsoever. Because the meaning of regret is that a person feels grief over what he has done, not that the act and its absence are the same to him. That is, he feels now that he is aggrieved, as common people say: "I am aggrieved, how did this thing slip from me?"

The third: that he desist from the disobedience. He must desist from the disobedience immediately. If it was against Allah, then it is either abandoning an obligation or committing a prohibited act. If it was committing a prohibited act, he must desist from it and leave it, even if a sip of wine is in his mouth; it is obligatory upon him to spit it out. If it was against a created being, then he must either give that person his right or seek his pardon for it, whether it was financial, physical, or a matter of honor known to its owner. Physical, like beating. Financial, like taking money or denying money owed to a person. Honor-related, like backbiting. If the person harmed knows of the backbiting, then he must seek his pardon. If he does not know, there is no need to inform him and then seek his pardon, because perhaps if he knows he will not pardon. Rather, in place of soiling his reputation in a gathering, he praises him in that same gathering for what he has in him, because ﴿الْحَسَنَاتِ يُذْهِبْنَ السَّيِّئَاتِ﴾ [Hūd 114], "good deeds erase bad deeds." If it is a right of a created being, then what is required?

* Student: Seeking his pardon.
* Shaykh: Seeking his pardon, if it was physical, financial, or honor-related and he knows of it. If it was for Allah, we say: if it was committing a prohibited act, he must desist from it immediately. If it was abandoning an obligation, he must make up for it if making it up is possible, and if it is not possible, it lapses. What do you say about (...) a man who usurped land and planted crops in it, and during his occupation of it he repented to Allah. What does he do?

* Students: He returns it.

* Shaykh: He will return it, but now he is in control of it. His walking from its middle to its edge is walking in disobedience, and if he remains there he is in disobedience. So what does he do?

* Students: He leaves.

* Shaykh: The scholars said: his leaving here is not disobedience, because it is leaving to free himself from disobedience, and freeing oneself from a thing is not given the ruling of that thing. This is why, if the one in *iḥrām* was smeared with perfume and wanted to wash it off, he must touch it while washing. Is that permissible or forbidden? Permissible, because he wants to free himself from it. Likewise *istinjāʾ* (cleansing after relieving oneself): a person who wants to cleanse himself touches the filth with his hand, and this touching of filth with the hand is permissible, because it is for the sake of freeing himself from this filth and removing it. Similarly, this one who repented from usurped land, was in the middle of the land, and walked: we say this walking is an act of obedience, because you only walked for the sake of freeing yourself. How many conditions is this?

* Students: Three.

* Shaykh: Three.

The fourth condition: that he resolve never to return. If he repents without resolving not to return, his repentance is not valid. Like a man whose habit was to stay up drinking wine in the bars, bars that serve wine (may Allah protect us). One night the sky was raining, and he came to the bar, and it was closed, so he said: "I repent." But his intention is that when the next night is clear and the bars open, he will come and drink wine. What do you say about this? This is not a repentant person. His repentance is closest to being a mockery. Like a man who wanted to repent from backbiting, while he is with his companions who bring in servants of Allah and place them among them, and turn sharp knives on them, tearing their flesh. One of them said: "I seek Allah's forgiveness and repent to Him." ﴿رَبَّنَا ظَلَمْنَا أَنْفُسَنَا وَإِنْ لَمْ تَغْفِرْ لَنَا وَتَرْحَمْنَا لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْخَاسِرِينَ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf 23], "Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers." "O so-and-so, what are you saying about so-and-so?" He backbites. Is this repentance valid? No, because he did not desist. Even if he desisted at the time of saying "I seek Allah's forgiveness and repent to Him," he did not resolve never to return, as evidenced by the fact that as soon as he said these words, he said: "Come on, bring so-and-so, what do you say about him?" We say: this man did not repent a true repentance. We say: is it resolution not to return, or the condition not to return?

* Students: Resolution not to return.

The fourth condition: that he resolve not to return. If he repents without resolving not to return, his repentance is not valid. Like a man whose habit was to stay up drinking wine in the bars, bars that serve wine (may Allah protect us). One night the sky was raining, and he came to the bar, and it was closed, so he said: "I repent." But his intention is that when the next night is clear and the bars open, he will come and drink wine. What do you say about this?

* Students: His repentance is not valid.

**The Shaykh:** This is not a repentance-maker. His repentance is closest to mockery, like a man who wants to repent from backbiting while he sits with companions who bring up the servants of Allah among themselves and set blunt knives upon them, tearing their flesh. One of them says, "I seek Allah's forgiveness and turn to Him," and then, "O so-and-so, what do you say about so-and-so?" (…) Is his repentance valid?

**The students:** It is not valid.

**The Shaykh:** No, because he did not give it up. Even if he gave it up at the moment he said, "I seek Allah's forgiveness and turn to Him," he had not resolved never to return to it. The proof is that from the moment he said these words, he said, "Come on, bring so-and-so, what do you all say about him?" We say that this man did not truly repent. We ask: is the condition the resolve not to return, or the condition is not to return?

**The students:** The resolve not to return.

**The Shaykh:** The resolve not to return. That means that if he resolved not to return, but his soul later tempted him and he returned, does the first repentance become void or not?

**The students:** It does not become void.

**The Shaykh:** The first repentance is not void, but he needs a new repentance for the last relapse. As for the first repentance, it is complete. For this reason we say: the condition is the resolve not to return, not the fact of not returning. Is that clear?

If he returned to it and repented sincerely, and then returned again? He repents, then returns and repents again. The Prophet (ﷺ) reported: "A man used to commit a sin and then repented from it. Then he committed another sin and repented from it. Then he committed a sin and repented. Allah the Exalted said: 'My servant knows that he has a Lord who forgives sins and punishes for them. I have forgiven My servant, so let him do whatever he wishes.'"[[Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (7507) and Muslim (2758/29) from Abu Hurayrah.]]

This man was sincere. But this, as Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah said, does not apply to every penitent. The Messenger (ﷺ) only informed us about a man for whom this happened, and it does not happen for every penitent.

**The fifth condition:** That the repentance occurs within the time of acceptance. If the time of acceptance has ended, there is no repentance. The ending of the time of acceptance is of two kinds: general and specific. The specific is the arrival of the appointed term for each individual person. The general is the rising of the sun from its west. When the appointed term arrives, repentance does not benefit, due to the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And repentance is not for those who do evil deeds until, when death approaches one of them, he says, "Indeed, I have repented now."﴾ [An-Nisa 18]

If this condition is established, what does this indicate that repentance is obligatory upon?

**The students:** Immediately.

**The Shaykh:** Because no one knows when death will come to him. If you do not know when death will come to you, it follows that you must hasten to repentance, and that it should always be on your mind that you are repenting to your Lord and returning to Him, so that if it is decreed that the appointed term comes upon you suddenly, you are fully prepared. We ask Allah to protect us and you from the heedlessness of hearts. Hearts are heedless and do not reckon with this matter. What is obligatory is that a person reckons with this matter, always remembering repentance. For this reason, "Our Prophet (ﷺ) used to seek Allah's forgiveness more than seventy times a day and turn to Him in repentance more than seventy times."[[Related by al-Bukhari (6307) from Abu Hurayrah.]]

As for the general ending, it is the rising of the sun from its west. The sun moves by Allah's permission from the time Allah created it until Allah permits it to stop. Remarkably, it neither advances nor delays! Consider its rising today, for example, on the second day of the constellation Virgo, it rises at such-and-such hour and minute. On this very day of hundreds of years before, it rose at the same hours and minutes. These do not differ. If you counted them since people recorded history, you would find that they have not differed. It rises on this day from the constellation Virgo at such-and-such hour and minute until the Day of Resurrection. When it sets, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said, and he is the truthful and the one believed, who does not speak from desire: "When it sets, it prostrates beneath the Throne, glorifying Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and it asks permission: will it come out or return? Either it is permitted, or it is said: 'Return from where you came.' So it returns from where it came, and rises from its west. When people see it, they all will believe."[[Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (3199) and Muslim (159/250) from Abu Dharr.]] They will all believe, because at that time they will know that it has a Lord who manages it. Now, one supposes that it is merely nature, a natural law that governs the universe in this order. But if the order is disrupted and the sun returns from the west, they will all believe, the believer and the disbeliever alike. However, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith if it had not believed before or earned good through its faith.﴾ [Al-An'am 158] Faith will not benefit them, because these people believe like the faith of those who were overtaken by the punishment. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So when they saw Our might, they said, "We believe in Allah alone and disbelieve in what we used to associate with Him." But their faith did not benefit them when they had seen Our might. This is the way of Allah which has preceded among His servants. And the disbelievers were lost therein.﴾ [Ghafir 84-85]

So the point is that the conditions of repentance are five. Some scholars have said they are three, so they dropped sincerity and dropped that it must be within the time of acceptance. But these two conditions are necessary: sincerity is necessary, and it must be within the time of acceptance.

**A student:** Shaykh, does it become void when it rises from the west, or does it return?

**The Shaykh:** By Allah, I know nothing about this. I do not know anything about this. Does it return always, or only when it has come out upon the people and they have all seen it, and it has circled for twenty-four hours? Because it must circle for twenty-four hours so that it comes out upon all the people. That is, it must circle for twenty-four hours, and when it reaches its end, then it returns. We do not know whether it continues or not. Allah knows best.

**A student:** Shaykh, regarding Allah's saying ﴿abiding therein﴾: abiding in the curse of the angels and people, or abiding in the Fire of Hell?

**The Shaykh:** The curse, because "therein" refers to the curse.

**The student:** So this means it is not an eternal abiding.

**The Shaykh:** Why?

**The student:** Because people die, for example.

**The Shaykh:** No, no. It means that people curse them, not only with the tongue of speech but even with the tongue of state.

**A student:** Shaykh, may Allah be good to you. It is known, Shaykh, that a person may fall into great sins and may not know, that is, about these specific sins. For example, he shouts and becomes angry and does not know that this is a sin. So how is his repentance from these sins that he does not know?

**The Shaykh:** You mean to ask: is repentance valid in general terms?

**The student:** Yes.

**The Shaykh:** Yes, it is valid, because a person may not encompass all his sins. For this reason he said: "O Allah, forgive me what I have done before and what I have done later, what I have concealed and what I have made public, and what You know better than I."

**The student:** Shaykh, may Allah reward you with good. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Men are in charge of women﴾ [An-Nisa 34]. Is the "al-" here for the genus?

**The Shaykh:** Yes.

**The student:** Alright, is it true for the genus or for each individual?

**The Shaykh:** No, no, it is for the genus.

**The student:** Is it not true of each individual?

**The Shaykh:** It is not true of each individual.

**The student:** So it exists.

**The Shaykh:** It means there are foolish men over whom women are in charge, and there are men without intellect over whom women are in charge.

**A student:** O Shaykh, Allah the Exalted mentioned the curse of the angels and people, and did not mention the curse of the jinn, even though the jinn are responsible, having obligations as people do. How is this?

**The Shaykh:** Allah knows best. Allah knows best that since most jinn are devils who lead people astray, He mentioned those among them who are more complete, namely humans and angels.

**A student:** Shaykh, some exegetes mentioned regarding Allah's saying ﴿How will Allah guide a people who disbelieved after their belief﴾ that its occasion of revelation was that a man apostatized after his Islam, then embraced Islam again, and sent to his people to ask the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), meaning, what should he do, is his Islam valid? So Allah revealed His saying ﴿How will Allah guide a people﴾. I do not know if this is sound?

**The Shaykh:** Then Allah revealed: ﴿except for those who repent after that and reform﴾. This is sound, but the consideration is the generality of the wording, not the specific occasion.

**A student:** Shaykh, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The first of the signs to appear is—" that is, "the rising of the sun from its west." So this means it will come before the emergence of the Dajjal and Jesus son of Mary?

**The Shaykh:** Nothing prevents that the meaning is the great signs, the major signs. Otherwise there is no doubt that there are signs that occur before the sun rises from its west.

**A student:** Shaykh, in Al 'Imran Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And what was given to Musa and 'Isa and the prophets﴾ [Al 'Imran 84], and in Al-Baqarah: ﴿And what was given to the prophets﴾ [Al-Baqarah 136]. What is (...)?

**The Shaykh:** You mean that He repeated the agent there and did not repeat it here? Apparently, and Allah knows best, I do not know, unless it is a difference of expression like ﴿revealed to us﴾ [Al-Baqarah 91] and ﴿revealed to us﴾ [Al-Baqarah 136] with one meaning. Or, when He said there, "Say: We believe in Allah" [Al-Baqarah 136], and the address turned directly to people, it became necessary that they explicitly affirm belief in what was given to the prophets. Allah knows best.

**A student:** Shaykh, is there a sign that repentance has been accepted?

**The Shaykh:** Yes, how? A sign. Because sins affect the living heart. Sins affect the living heart, and you find that it constricts and the person's chest tightens. When he repents, his chest expands. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So is he whose chest Allah has opened to Islam and who is upon a light from his Lord [like one who is hardened]? Woe to those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of Allah. Those are in obvious error.﴾ [Az-Zumar 22]

**A student:** Shaykh, whenever...

**The Shaykh:** Also among its signs: instead of lethargy in obedience, the person finds in himself vigor in obedience. Because Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And Adam disobeyed his Lord and erred. Then his Lord chose him, accepted his repentance, and guided him.﴾ [Ta-Ha 121-122] So a person grows more energetic in obedience when Allah accepts his repentance.

**A student:** O Shaykh, does it mean that whenever he sees (...) in his heart, it is from the effect of sins?

**The Shaykh:** No, not in every case. Someone may strike him or push him and his chest tightens. But if the person, in the ordinary way, finds constriction, then it is from the effects of sins. As the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, there comes over my heart a veil, and indeed I seek Allah's forgiveness more than seventy times."[[Related by Muslim (2702/41) from al-Aghharr al-Muzani.]]

**A student:** ﴿Except for those who repent after that and reform﴾ [Al 'Imran 89]. Is this an exception from "who disbelieved," meaning from those who disbelieved?

**The Shaykh:** From what preceded.

**The student:** From "those who disbelieved"?

**The Shaykh:** Yes, ﴿disbelieved after their belief﴾.

**The student:** And its case is the accusative?

**The Shaykh:** Its case is what?

**The student:** That is, the exception is in the accusative case? Its position?

**The Shaykh:** Yes, because what precedes it is a complete affirmative sentence.

How is the answer to this?

**The Shaykh:** What?

**The student:** The Prophet (ﷺ) did not mention repentance in the hadith. How is the answer, then?

**The Shaykh:** The answer: the many verses show that when a person repents, it is lifted from him, and the texts of the Qur'an and Sunnah show that when he repents, he returns to his former state. But the matter of requesting repentance is a separate question.

**The student:** So we say: specified by the Sunnah.

**The Shaykh:** Yes, specified by the Sunnah and the Qur'an. The requesting of repentance is what the scholars disagreed about: is it obligatory, or is he killed without being asked to repent? If he repents, there is no problem. The question is whether we must first ask him to repent, and if he repents we leave him, or do we kill him and his account is with Allah? The correct view is that requesting repentance is subject to the opinion of the ruler.

Sometimes the sword is placed on his neck, then the heirs of the slain say, "We pardon," and if they say, "We pardon," the sword must be lifted.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verse 85–89 (part 1 of 3):

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion﴾. "Man" (مَن) is conditional (شرطية, a conditional particle). How close we are to the conditional "man." But ﴿yabtaghi﴾ has departed from what is apparent in its i'rab (grammatical inflection), because it was not jussive by sukun. The ﴿yabtaghi﴾ I have here is kasra-ended, jussive by what?
* The students: By deleting the yā'.
* The Shaykh: By deleting the weak letter, the yā', by deleting the yā'; because its original form is yabtaghī. And His saying ﴿man yabtaghi ghayra al-Islāmi dīnan﴾: ﴿ghayra﴾ is the object of ﴿yabtaghi﴾, and ﴿dīnan﴾ may be a second object; meaning, whoever seeks it as a religion; and it may be a tamyīz (specifier) for the ambiguous ghayr, since ghayr is an ambiguous noun. Alright, in any case ﴿yabtaghi﴾ means seeks. And His saying ﴿ghayra al-Islām﴾: what is meant by Islam here is the particular Islam, which is what Muhammad ﷺ brought, although Islam in its origin applies to submission to Allah in every time and place, as you know, what Allah mentioned about the earlier prophets, that they used the term Islam: ﴿She said: My Lord, I have wronged myself, and I submit with Solomon to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ [an-Naml 44]. And the verses on this are many, that the messengers and their followers are Muslims; but this is the general Islam. After the mission of the Messenger (peace be upon him), whatever is called Islam is only what the Messenger ﷺ brought. So ﴿ghayra al-Islām﴾ means what? Other than the sharī'ah of Muhammad ﷺ; because we say: what is meant by Islam here is what?
* The students: The particular Islam..
* The Shaykh: The particular Islam, which is the sharī'ah of Muhammad ﷺ. ﴿Dīnan﴾: meaning a deed by which one submits to Allah and hopes to be recompensed for it with reward from Allah; because dīn applies to both the deed and the recompense. In His saying ﴿For you is your religion, and for me is my religion﴾ [al-Kafirun 6] it means the deed, and in His saying ﴿And what will make you know what the Day of Religion is? Then what will make you know what the Day of Religion is?﴾ [al-Infitar 17, 18]..
* The students: The recompense..
* The Shaykh: The recompense; and in His saying here ﴿And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion﴾ what is meant?
* The students: A deed..
* The Shaykh: The deed. Alright, but dīn is only in a deed for which a person hopes for reward, meaning he hopes to be recompensed by it; for this it is said: "As you judge, so you will be judged" [[Narrated by Ma'mar in al-Jami' (20262), and al-Bayhaqi in az-Zuhd al-Kabir (710), from the hadith of Abu Qilabah.]]. And His saying ﴿then it will never be accepted from him﴾: the fa' in its i'rab, according to what passed with us last night, is what? A linking particle for the response, is it not so?
* The students: Yes.
* The Shaykh:
............................ ∗∗∗ wa-bimā wa-qad wa-bilan wa-bi-t-tanfīs
This is lan; the fa' is the linking particle for the response: ﴿then it will never be accepted from him﴾, meaning that religion will not be accepted. And His saying ﴿fa-lan yuqbala﴾: He did not say "then Allah will not accept," He said ﴿fa-lan yuqbala minhu﴾, to encompass rejection and refusal from Allah the Mighty and Majestic, from the Messenger, and from the Muslims; therefore it is not permissible for Muslims to allow anyone to follow a religion other than the sharī'ah of the Messenger (peace be upon him); it is not permissible for them to do so. ﴿Lan yuqbala minhu﴾. And in His saying ﴿fa-lan yuqbala minhu﴾, is the acceptance meant here complete acceptance or acceptance of validity?
* The students: Validity..
* The Shaykh: Acceptance of validity. The evidence for that is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ, narrated by the two Shaykhs from 'Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her), that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever does an action that is not in accordance with our command, it is rejected" [[Agreed upon; narrated by al-Bukhari (2697) and Muslim (1718/18), the wording being his, from the hadith of 'Aisha.]] rejected; so whoever follows a religion other than Islam, whether in its root or in its branches, his religion is rejected and refused, ﴿fa-lan yuqbala minhu﴾. And will he be given reward in the Hereafter for his deed?
No; therefore He said: ﴿and he, in the Hereafter, will be among the losers﴾, and this, by Allah, is the great loss: that a person lives in this world as long as Allah wills him to live, then he does not earn what benefits him in the Hereafter; when he comes before his Lord he will find nothing, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage in a qī'ah﴾ [an-Nur 39]. Do you know the mirage in a qī'ah? Qī'ah means a level, wide plain. In such land, in intense heat, it appears to a person from afar that there is water; that is the mirage, it is called the mirage. When a thirsty person comes and finds this mirage which seems like water of the sea, he rejoices and hastens toward it, until when he reaches it he finds nothing, and so disappointment comes after strong hope; and this is the most severe regret for a person, that his disappointment comes at the height of his hope; because if a person had not hoped in the first place it would not have troubled him, but the problem is that he hopes and then is overturned, and this is worse. We ask Allah for well-being!
﴿Until when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing, and finds Allah with him, and He will pay him his account in full. And Allah is swift in reckoning﴾ [an-Nur 39]. Everyone who does not adopt Islam as his religion will be a loser in the Hereafter. ﴿And We will turn to what they did of deeds and make them scattered dust﴾ [al-Furqan 23]; and His saying ﴿and he, in the Hereafter, will be among the losers﴾ includes the loss of the self, the loss of wealth, and the loss of family. As for the loss of the self, he will gain nothing from his deeds. As for the loss of wealth, even if he spends all his wealth on what benefits people, he will not benefit from it in the Hereafter; meaning, if he repairs roads, builds mosques, and builds schools, it will not benefit him. I suppose you do not expect that this would come from an outright disbeliever, building mosques and schools; but it would come from an apostate disbeliever. For example, a man who does not pray but is a man of good who builds mosques, builds schools, repairs roads, and feeds the needy; does he benefit from any of this deed? No; because he is a disbeliever, and a disbeliever's deeds will never benefit him on the Day of Resurrection.
Alright, as for the loss of wealth, we have just mentioned that if he spends it he gains nothing; as for the loss of family, they also do not benefit him in this world; if they make supplication for him, he will not benefit from that, if they make supplication for him he will not benefit from that; because Allah says: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believed to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were relatives, after it has become clear to them that they are the companions of the Blazing Fire﴾ [at-Tawbah 113], and they do not benefit from supplication. Likewise in the Hereafter they do not benefit from their families, because each one is separated from the other in the fire of Hell. Unlike the believers, for Allah says: ﴿And those who believed and whose descendants followed them in faith – We will join them with their descendants, and We will not deprive them of anything of their deeds. Every person is held in pledge for what he has earned﴾ [at-Tur 21]. If you have offspring who are in the fifth rank while you are in the seventh rank, the offspring are elevated from the fifth to the seventh, and you are not lowered at all. It is not said: "Descend a rank while they ascend a rank, and you will be in which one?" In the sixth? The offspring are in the fifth and the fathers in the seventh; the offspring are raised from the fifth to the seventh and the fathers are not lowered from the seventh to the sixth. That is, if someone says: this rises a rank and that falls a rank, is this justice? But we say: Allah deals with bounty, the Mighty and Majestic; therefore He said: ﴿and We did not deprive them﴾; because someone might suppose that if the offspring are raised, the reward of the fathers is diminished, so He said: ﴿and We will not deprive them of anything of their deeds﴾. Why? ﴿Every person is held in pledge for what he has earned﴾. And if we lowered the fathers, the doer would not be held in pledge for what he earned. Yes indeed.
