He did not command His servants to worship in order to benefit from it, as in the hadith qudsi, the long hadith of Abu Dharr al-Ghifari: "O My servants, you will never reach My benefit so as to benefit Me, nor will you reach My harm so as to harm Me. O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were upon the most wicked heart of one man among you, that would not decrease anything of My dominion."[[Narrated by Muslim (2577/55) from the hadith of Abu Dharr.]] So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is free of need from us. He only commanded and forbade us so that our affairs would be set right and our conditions improved, and that we would be happy in this world and the Hereafter. As for if we were upon the most wicked heart of a man among people, that would not harm Allah in the least. But since the children of Adam were given intellect, by which they deserve to be addressed with commands and prohibitions, they became fit for commands and prohibitions. For this reason commands and prohibitions are not directed at beasts, because they were not given intellects. So giving intellect to the children of Adam means, or entails, binding them to obligations so that they attain happiness in this world and the Hereafter. As for beasts, their final state is that they will become dust, resurrected on the Day of Resurrection, and retribution will be exacted from some of them for others, and then it will be said: "Become dust," and they will become dust.

Among the benefits of these two verses: if Allah is free of need from the worlds, it follows that the worlds are in need of Him, and they have no independence from Allah. And so it is. The creation is in need of Allah, the Exalted, in the utmost degree of need. For this reason, it is befitting for you to ask your Lord, in the tongue of your state or the tongue of your speech, in all your affairs. Seek help from Allah in all your affairs: ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾ [al-Fātiḥah 5]. Let your attachment to Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, not leave your mind in anything. There has come in a hadith: "Let one of you ask his Lord even for the strap of his sandal."[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (3604/m 8) from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik.]] Even the cheap sandal strap, which is worth nothing, should not be neglected in asking Allah for it, either by the tongue of one's state or by the tongue of one's speech.

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Say: "O People of the Scripture, why do you disbelieve in the signs of Allah?"﴾ [Al 'Imran 98]. Here Allah commanded His Messenger ﷺ to rebuke those among the People of the Scripture. In an earlier verse the address came from Allah directly: ﴿O People of the Scripture, why do you disbelieve in the signs of Allah while you witness [their truth]?﴾ [Al 'Imran 70]. So here is a command from Allah to the Messenger ﷺ to say to them: ﴿O People of the Scripture, why do you disbelieve in the signs of Allah?﴾ The interrogative (li-ma) here is for rebuke. The lam is a particle of genitive (harf jarr), and (ma) is interrogative, but its alif has been dropped, because when the interrogative (ma) is preceded by a particle of genitive, its alif is dropped, as in (limma, 'ammа, fīmа, 'alāma), and similar forms. That is, if you say: "'ala ma tadribuni" (on what are you striking me), it is not permissible to say it that way; rather you say: "'alāma tadribunī" (on what are you striking me). Is "limā tadribunī" permissible? No; you say: "lima tadribuni," and so on.

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Why do you disbelieve in the signs of Allah?﴾ (takfurūn) means: you deny them, neglect them, and turn a blind eye to them. By "the signs" here are meant both the cosmic (kawniyyah) and the legislated (shar'iyyah) signs. Disbelief in the cosmic signs involves three matters: first, that one denies that Allah created them; second, that one believes that Allah has a partner in bringing them into being; third, that one believes that Allah has a helper in them. These are three matters. How many things does disbelief in Allah's cosmic signs involve?

* Student: Three matters... I was about to say three matters and I forgot.

* Shaykh: That is the problem.

* Student: That one believes Allah did not create them, that one believes Allah has a helper in creating them, and that one believes there is a partner with Allah in creating them.

* Shaykh: Yes. That one denies Allah's creation of them, meaning he denies that Allah created these beings. Second: that one believes Allah has a partner in them, for example, that Allah created the heavens and someone else created the earth, for instance. Third: that one believes Allah has a helper in them, saying: they belong to Allah, but there is someone who assisted Him. This is disbelief in the cosmic signs. Disbelief in the legislated signs is denying them, by denying that they came from Allah, or denying their reports, or opposing them. If the opposition is complete, it is major disbelief (kufr akbar); if the opposition is incomplete, it is minor disbelief (kufr asghar), which is what is called wickedness (fusuq). So disbelief in the cosmic signs is how many things? Three things. And the legislated are two: denial and opposition. Denial may concern their origin, by saying: this was not sent down from Allah; or it may deny their reports, meaning that if one denies any report in them, it is denial of all of them, because one cannot believe in part of the Book and disbelieve in part. The second is what? Opposition. Then, if the opposition is complete, it is major disbelief; if it is not complete, it is minor disbelief, which is expressed as lesser disbelief (kufr duna kufr) or wickedness (fusuq).

* Student: Shaykh, may Allah reward you well. There is a hadith: "Whoever dies without performing Hajj, dies either as a Jew or a Christian" [Narrated by al-Darimi (1826) from the hadith of Abu Umamah.]. Do you endorse this hadith, that it is major disbelief?

* Shaykh: Yes. If this were authentically reported from the Messenger ﷺ, it would support it; it would indicate it clearly.

* Student: Shaykh, may Allah pardon you, one who believes that Allah, glorified and exalted, created the cosmic signs in vain, would that be disbelief?

* Shaykh: This would be denying wisdom; this would be denying the wisdom of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

* Student: So he would be a disbeliever in this case?

* Shaykh: It appears that he is a disbeliever, because this includes mocking Allah and denying Allah. ﴿Did you think that We created you in vain?﴾ [al-Mu'minun 115]. ﴿And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them as play﴾ [al-Dukhan 38].

* Student: Shaykh, may Allah reward you well. We said: killing within the Sacred Precinct (haram) is not permissible?

* Shaykh: What?

* Student: Killing in the haram is not permissible?

* Shaykh: Yes.

* Student: Killing in justice, the hudud (prescribed punishments), and so on?

* Shaykh: Killing in justice: if the disobedient one who deserves death committed his sin within the haram, he is killed, because he violated the sanctity of the haram, so he has no sanctity, as in His saying: ﴿If they fight you, then kill them﴾ [al-Baqarah 191]. If he committed a hadd offense outside the haram and then sought refuge in the haram, the correct view is that the hadd is not carried out on him and he is not killed, but he is restricted: he is not to be dealt with in food, drink, or trade, until he finds no one to trade with, eat with, or drink with. If he has food and drink, they will run out, and then he will be forced to leave. This is the correct view.

* Student: Shaykh, what is your opinion on asking people for needs, such as cars, books, and other things?

* Shaykh: Asking them for needs?

* Student: Does it include the pledge of the Companions to the Prophet ﷺ that they would not ask people for anything?

* Shaykh: Is this included in our reading?

* Student: You mentioned that a servant must ask Allah in all matters, even for the strap of his sandal?

* Shaykh: Yes, that is the matter of independence from Allah, that one is not independent of Allah. Asking people is without doubt either forbidden or disliked; either forbidden or disliked. This is the basic ruling. It may deviate from this basic ruling if necessity or need calls for it, in which case one may ask. As for asking for the benefit of wealth, such as 'ariyyah (loan of an item) and qard (loan of money), and similar things, there is no harm in it. But asking for the wealth itself is what is either forbidden or disliked.

* Student: Shaykh, if someone is found committing legal violations in the haram, should he be rebuked severely, whether he is a sinner (fasiq) or an innovator (mubtadi')?

* Shaykh: Such as?

* Student: For example, if he is a sinner who, say, touches women during the circumambulation?

* Shaykh: Yes, the punishment is multiplied for him.

* Student: As for me, for example, is it (...) severe?

* Shaykh: Yes, yes. Sin within the haram is more grave than sin outside the haram, and therefore his discipline (ta'zir) must be more severe.

* Student: Shaykh, may Allah reward you well. We mentioned that Makkah was the qiblah of all people, then when distortion occurred they turned away from it. Shaykh, the Prophet's ﷺ affirmation in (...)?

* Shaykh: Yes. This affirmation was for the sake of agreeing with the Jews, because the Jews believed they were upon the truth; so if they had been told "you are upon falsehood," they would have fled. Yes.

* * *
* Student: ﴿Say: "O People of the Scripture, why do you bar from the way of Allah those who believe, seeking to make it crooked, while you are witnesses? And Allah is not unaware of what you do."﴾ (99) ﴿O you who have believed, if you obey a faction of those who were given the Scripture, they will return you, after your belief, to disbelief.﴾ (100) ﴿And how can you disbelieve while the verses of Allah are recited to you and His Messenger is among you? And whoever holds firmly to Allah has been guided to a straight path.﴾ (101) [Al 'Imran 99-101]
* Shaykh: Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say: "O People of the Scripture, why do you disbelieve in the signs of Allah while Allah is Witness over what you do?"﴾. The beginning of this verse has already been discussed: Allah rebukes the People of the Scripture, indeed He commands the Prophet ﷺ to rebuke them: why do they disbelieve in the signs of Allah?

As for His saying: ﴿And Allah is Witness over what you do﴾, (shahid) means witness. It is in the form of intensive or the attributive adjective, because Allah, glorified and exalted, is a witness over their deeds, and their deeds are many; when the things witnessed are many, the testimony is great. His saying: ﴿And Allah is Witness over what you do﴾ may be included within the rebuke in His saying: ﴿why do you disbelieve﴾, so the meaning would be: why do you disbelieve in the signs of Allah while you know that Allah is Witness over what you do. It may also be that the waw is for resumption, and the rebuke ends at His saying: ﴿why do you disbelieve in the signs of Allah?﴾, and then He resumes: ﴿And Allah is Witness over what you do﴾, in which case it is a warning to those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah: a warning by what? By Allah being a witness over what they do; and if He is a witness over what they do, He will recompense them for it in this world and the Hereafter according to what they deserve.

From the lessons of this noble verse: the command to the Prophet ﷺ to rebuke the People of the Scripture for their disbelief in the signs of Allah, and this ruling extends to others. From this lesson follows that everyone who disbelieves in the signs of Allah deserves rebuke, and we have already explained that disbelief in the signs of Allah includes the cosmic and the legislated, and we clarified the types of disbelief in both.

* Among the lessons of this noble verse: the affirmation that Allah, glorified and exalted, witnesses everything the children of Adam do, from His saying: ﴿And Allah is Witness over what you do﴾, and (ma) is a relative pronoun conveying generality.

* Among its lessons: a warning to those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah, because such a phrase as ﴿And Allah is Witness over what you do﴾ is meant to rebuke whoever does what does not please Allah, Mighty and Majestic, by informing him that Allah is witness over him and will count his deeds and then recompense him for them.

* Among the lessons of the verse: the all-encompassing knowledge of Allah, the Exalted, over everything, and that He is Vast in scope over everything, from His saying: ﴿over what you do﴾. Whoever counts the children of Adam, from the People of the Scripture and others, and counts their deeds, yet Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is All-Encompassing and All-Knowing, who counts everything, and nothing from the deeds of the children of Adam is hidden from Him.

Perhaps it may be derived from this verse, from His saying: ﴿Witness over what you do﴾, that a servant is not held accountable for what he merely thinks of in himself, as is authentically reported from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in his saying: "Indeed Allah has overlooked for my nation what its souls whisper about, as long as they do not act upon it or speak it" [Agreed upon; narrated by al-Bukhari (5269) and Muslim (127 / 201) from the hadith of Abu Hurairah.]. Thus, the whisperings of the soul, which are the suggestions that occur in the breast, are not held against a person unless he acts upon them, inclines to them, believes in them, and makes them among the deeds of the heart, in which case he is then held accountable for them; or he utters them with his tongue; or he acts in accordance with them with his limbs, in which case he is then held accountable for them.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verse 99:

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say: O People of the Scripture, why do you avert [people] from the way of Allah﴾. This is another command to the Prophet ﷺ from his Lord, that he rebuke the People of the Scripture for their transgression against others. The first rebuke, ﴿Why do you disbelieve in the signs of Allah﴾, is a rebuke for their deed that is limited to themselves. The second, ﴿Say: O People of the Scripture, why do you avert [people] from the way of Allah﴾, is a rebuke for their transgression against others, in that they bar [people] from the way of Allah. He said: ﴿Why do you avert [people] from the way of Allah﴾, meaning: for what reason, and by what proof, ﴿do you avert﴾, i.e., turn away, ﴿from the way of Allah﴾, i.e., from His religion and His law. The religion is called "the way of Allah" because it leads to Him. It is attributed to Allah for two reasons. The first: Allah is the One who set it as a way for creation to walk upon. The second: it is, what? It leads to Allah, so whoever follows the way that Allah has set for the servants will reach Allah, Mighty and Majestic. So what is meant by "the way of Allah"? What is meant by it is His religion, because it is the path that leads to Him. As for His saying ﴿those who believe﴾, the word "those" (man) here is the object of ﴿you avert﴾, meaning: you turn away those who believe from the way of Allah. This is the practice of the Children of Israel, the Jews and Christians, who bar from the way of Allah those who believe. He mentioned "those who believe" even though they also bar those who have not believed: they bar the believer until he apostatizes from his faith, and they bar the non-believer so that he does not enter into faith. This is because barring those who believe is a greater transgression than barring those who have not believed, since they bar the believer so that he becomes an apostate, whereas they bar the non-believer from the way of Allah in order that he remain in his disbelief, and remaining in disbelief is easier than apostasy, as is evident. His saying ﴿those who believe﴾ includes men and women, but the addresses of the Qur'an are mostly to men, because the man is the basis and is the leader over the woman: ﴿Men are in charge of women by [right of] what Allah has given one over the other﴾ [an-Nisa' 34].

﴿Seeking to make it crooked﴾. The phrase ﴿seeking it﴾ is a circumstantial clause (hal) from the waw in His saying ﴿you avert﴾, meaning: while you seek the way of Allah, i.e., you seek it. ﴿Crooked﴾, i.e., for the sake of crookedness, so it is an object of purpose (maf'ul min ajlihi). It may also be an object (maf'ul bihi), meaning: you seek it crooked, i.e., you make it crooked. Crookedness (al-'iwaj) is the opposite of straightness. It is said: 'iwaj in meanings and 'awaj in physical things. For example, you say: "This stick is 'awaj," because it is a physical thing; and you say: "This statement is 'iwaj," because it is a meaning. So in meanings it is with a kasra on the 'ayn, and in tangible things with a fatha. The root of 'iwaj is inclination, and its opposite is uprightness. Crookedness from the law of Allah includes two meanings. The first concerns the commands, and the second the prohibitions. As for the commands, their crookedness is either by treating them lightly and neglecting them, or by exceeding in them and extremism. Thus people with regard to Allah's commands are of three categories: a moderate category, a negligent category, and an excessive category, meaning extremist, going beyond the limit. The moderate is the straight one, the negligent is crooked, and the excessive is also crooked. This concerns the commands. As for the prohibitions, crookedness in them is violating and committing them, and this is crookedness, because the straight path regarding prohibitions is to leave them and to refrain from them; so if you do them and violate them, this is the crookedness in them. So these Jews and Christians, the People of the Scripture, want people to be crooked in the commands and in the prohibitions: in the commands, by what? By negligence and laxity, or by extremism and excess; and in the prohibitions, by violating them and treating them lightly.

﴿Seeking it crooked while you are witnesses﴾. The waw here is circumstantial, meaning: and the situation is that you are witnesses over what you do. You know that by this deed you bar from the way of Allah; you know this and bear witness to it. The basis of this is that it is found in their scriptures that Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ﷺ will be sent, that he is the Messenger of Allah, and that he is the one whom 'Isa foretold. But they distort the words from their places in order to bar people from believing in Muhammad ﷺ, so they came to bar from the way of Allah while they are witnesses who testify to the truth. But, may Allah protect us, they were arrogant toward it. ﴿While you are witnesses﴾: witnesses to what? To the fact that you bar from the way of Allah, because you know that what Muhammad ﷺ brought is the way of Allah. ﴿And Allah is not unaware of what you do﴾: meaning, Allah has negated that He is unaware of their deeds, small or great. Here we find that this attribute is one of the negative attributes, since the attributes of Allah, as we have passed, are of two kinds: affirmative and negative, meaning something affirmed for Allah and something negated from Him. Here the attribute is negative. What has been negated of Allah? Heedlessness. The principle among the People of the Sunnah is that negative attributes contain two things. The first: the negation of that attribute which Allah has negated of Himself. The second: the affirmation of perfection in its opposite, because it is negated only because He is perfect. So His saying ﴿And Allah is not unaware of what you do﴾ includes the negation of heedlessness from Allah, and the second, the affirmation of perfect watchfulness, because one who has perfect watchfulness has no heedlessness. So this verse affirms for Allah, the Exalted, perfect watchfulness, as He said: ﴿And Allah is ever, over all things, Watchful﴾ [al-Ahzab 52], and the negation of heedlessness from Him. The sentence conveys a threat to those who bar from the way of Allah those who believe and seek to make it crooked.

Among the benefits of this verse:
- The Prophet ﷺ was commanded to rebuke the People of the Scripture for their transgression against others, namely by barring from the way of Allah.
- Among its benefits: whoever bars Muslims from the way of Allah shares in a resemblance to the Jews and Christians. So if someone discourages you from doing good or encourages you to do evil, there is in him a resemblance to the Jews and Christians, because this is their path.
- Among the benefits of this verse: the affirmation that the devils are not only the devils of the jinn. Just as the jinn have devils who bar from the way of Allah, so too among mankind there are devils who bar from the way of Allah. To this Allah, blessed and exalted, refers in Surat al-An'am: ﴿And thus We have made for every prophet an enemy: devils of mankind and jinn, inspiring one another with decorated speech as deception﴾ [al-An'am 112].
- Among the benefits of this verse: the exhortation to adhere to the Sharia, because it is the way of Allah, and every sensible person strives to reach Allah, Mighty and Majestic, since He is the ultimate goal, and there is no reaching Allah except by following His law, His way that leads to Him.
- Among the benefits of this verse: whoever bars from the way of Allah one who believes in Him is at the utmost degree of transgression, and he is greater than one who bars from the way of Allah one who has not believed, because this is elevation and the former is prevention, and elevation is more severe. Removing good is a greater punishment and a greater crime than preventing it.
- Among the benefits of this verse: the evil intention of the People of the Scripture, in that they wish the way of Allah to be crooked. This description of the People of the Scripture still applies to them today. The Christians have missionaries who proselytize people and exert every effort to bar those who believe from the way of Allah, because they want people to follow the crooked way, not the straight way. They still do so to this day, and they have special radio stations calling people to Christianity, may Allah protect us, the false Christianity which 'Isa, peace be upon him, opposed, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And when Allah says, "O 'Isa, son of Maryam, did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as two deities besides Allah?'" He will say, "Exalted are You! It was not for me to say that to which I have no right. If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is within myself, and I do not know what is within Yourself. Indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen. I did not tell them except what You commanded me: 'Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord.'"﴾ [al-Ma'idah 116-117]. They now claim that the religion of 'Isa, peace be upon him, is the doctrine of the Trinity, and they say: "God is the third of three." Then they deceive themselves and the people, saying: "Three in one, three in one." Is this reasonable? But this is from the misguidance of the Christians, for the Christians are astray; they do not even find their way to rational matters. How can it be three in one? This is impossible. In any case, they have wanted to mislead people from the time of the Messenger ﷺ until our day. Therefore, it is obligatory upon the Muslims to be cautious of them, to be wary of them, and to expose them so that people are repelled from them, and to confront their atheistic, disbelieving call with the call to monotheism and sincerity. Sincerity and monotheism agree with the sound nature, if someone presents them in a true, appealing manner. But, regrettably, the Muslims are heedless. You find few of the Muslims who are upon the truth who are callers to the truth, and even few of them in their own lands. As for those missionary Christians, they roam the eastern and western parts of the earth, enticing people with money and good manners until people are deceived by them.
- Among the benefits of this verse: the People of the Scripture who bar from the way of Allah know that they are upon falsehood and that the truth lies opposite to them, as shown by His saying ﴿while you are witnesses﴾. But what prevents them is arrogance.
- Among the benefits of this verse: the affirmation of Allah's encompassing of everything in knowledge and watchfulness, as shown by His saying ﴿And Allah is not unaware of what you do﴾.
- Among its benefits: that among the attributes of Allah are negative ones, meaning negated, and this is abundant in the Qur'an. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾ [ash-Shura 11], ﴿Do you know of any similar to Him?﴾ [Maryam 65].

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verses 100–101 (part 1 of 3):

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿O you who have believed, if you obey a faction of those who were given the Scripture, they will return you, after your belief, to disbelief.﴾

﴿O you who have believed, if you obey﴾. First, this ruling is introduced with the vocative ﴿O you who have believed﴾, and introducing a ruling with the vocative indicates attentiveness to it and care for it, because the vocative contains an alert to the one addressed, and an alert is only given for an important matter that deserves care. Then the address to those who have believed becomes an incitement (ighra'), since describing them with faith requires that they carry out what this address demands of them. It is like when you say to a person: "O man, do such-and-such," meaning: what does your manhood require? That you do this. So when you say: "O believer, do this," the meaning is that it is among the requirements of your faith that you do this. ﴿O you who have believed﴾, meaning: it is among the requirements of your faith that you pay attention to what will be cast upon you. For this reason Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "When you hear Allah say, 'O you who have believed,' then give it your full hearing, for it is either a good thing you are commanded to do or an evil thing you are forbidden from doing."[[Narrated by Sa'id ibn Mansur in his Tafsir (50).]] Moreover, the address with the description of faith requires that compliance with it is among the requirements of faith, and it also requires that opposing it is a deficiency in faith, because a believer's faith requires that he carry out what he is commanded and avoid what he is forbidden.

* Student: Sheikh, there are people who love to do good and the Sunnah, and they say: (...) the customs of people object to me (...), and perhaps when they do them people shun them. Do we say that doing them is a form of obstructing (sadd)?
* The Shaykh: No, it is not possible. That is, some people do Sunnahs that people do not know, and they object to them. Do we say that doing them is obstructing from the way of Allah? No, we do not say it is obstruction; but we may say that leaving them, for the sake of reconciling hearts (ta'lif), is part of the way of Allah, just as the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, left rebuilding the Ka'bah on the foundations of Ibrahim, because people were recently in disbelief, out of fear of tribulation for them.
* Student: We said that Islam is the religion of Allah in (...), and it is in accordance with the fitrah. Now we see that the other creeds and desires, the other sects (niHal), people are quicker to enter them. What is the reason for that?
* The Shaykh: What?
* Student: That is, we see that religions other than Islam, people enter them more quickly, such as communism, socialism and Christianity, and other things, to the point that Muslim lands have been entered. What is the reason?
* The Shaykh: The reason for that is that these...
* The Student: This is opposed to the fitrah.
* The Shaykh: Yes, this is opposed to the fitrah, because there exists a strong drive that overpowers the fitrah, as the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Every child is born upon the fitrah, then his parents make him a Jew, or a Christian, or a Magian."[[Agreed upon; narrated by al-Bukhari (1359) and Muslim (2658) from Abu Hurairah.]] So these people, you find that they lived in the embrace of communism, for example, or studied its opinions and ideas, or lived in the embrace of the West and studied its opinions and ideas, so this obstacle became a barrier between them and the requirement of the fitrah. Otherwise, if people were left to themselves, they would be upon the fitrah.
* Student: Sheikh, Allah's address to the People of the Book: ﴿O People of the Book, why do you obstruct...﴾ Is it addressed to the scholars of the People of the Book, or does it include all of them?
* The Shaykh: The verse includes everyone who obstructs, everyone who obstructs from the way of Allah, whether he is from the scholars or from the fanatics.
* Student: How do they obstruct, Sheikh?
* The Shaykh: Yes, the layman; there are laymen now who argue while being laymen. Sometimes they argue using the actions of Muslims. They say: "Look, Islam among you is lying, deceit, treachery and fraud," and similar things, and so he argues.
* Student: May Allah be good to you, Sheikh. The Crusader and Christian organizations, Sheikh, have now raised a slogan, that is: "Take off Islam" – they say: "We will strip you of the garment of poverty and hunger," openly like that. Do some Muslims still, Sheikh, flatter them?
* The Shaykh: By Allah, that people flatter them and remain silent in the face of these people is without doubt a weakness of faith, without doubt it is a weakness of faith. And it is obligatory upon the Muslims, and upon the rulers first, those able to spread Islam against these people, that they stand up for the sake of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to obstruct these people, and that they form committees in the Islamic nation to repel this evil.
* Student: Sheikh, may Allah pardon you, if the People of the Book disbelieved in the signs of Allah and obstruct from the way of Allah, why does Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, call them "People of the Book" when they disbelieved in it?
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed, this is from establishing the proof against them and from severe rebuke of them. That is, you are People of the Book, you have knowledge and understanding, and despite that you obstruct. So this is from the severity of blame and rebuke for them.
* Student: Is there no praise in it for them, Sheikh?
* The Shaykh: No, not at all. This is an emphasis of blame in a form resembling praise.
* Student: The Prophet's ﷺ saying to the Companions: "O People of the Qur'an, observe the witr (odd prayer)," and "Observe the witr, O People of the Qur'an" [[Narrated by Abu Dawud (1416) and al-Tirmidhi (453) from Ali ibn Abi Talib.]] – is that praise?
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed; because the People of the Qur'an hold fast to it, but these are People of the Book who opposed it, so this is more severe.
* Student: May Allah be good to you. What is the best response to their saying of the Trinity?
* The Shaykh: The best response is that we say: your Prophet said, ﴿I did not say to them except what You commanded me: "Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord."﴾ [al-Ma'idah 117]. And these two deities they claim are created: the Messiah is created and his mother Mary is created, so how can this be a god? This is from the standpoint of reason. As for the standpoint of the Shari'ah, this is their Prophet, peace be upon him, denouncing this against them.
* Student: Some callers (du'at) wish to call their family and children and the people of their neighbourhood, and some wish to travel the lands east and west, and when it is said to him, "Call your family and neighbours," he says he wishes to call those who are outside the country. Which of them is correct, Sheikh?
* The Shaykh: Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And warn your closest kindred﴾ [ash-Shu'ara' 214]. So a person begins with his family. But a person may wish to call those from outside, because his family are upon the Shari'ah, and they have nothing but sins less grave than disbelief. He says: "I call people to enter Islam, but my family have nothing except sins and do not need strong persuasion; all that is needed is (...) from sin until they call to it."
* Student: Some people, if they leave some Sunnahs for the sake of reconciling hearts (...) the correct Islam (...)?
* The Shaykh: We say: leaving is of two kinds: leaving by neglect (ta'til) and leaving for reconciliation (ta'lif). Leaving for reconciliation, we defer this until a later time after it is explained to the people and clarified for them that this (...), until they are reassured. As for leaving by neglect, where one says: "I neglect the Sunnahs because people do not act upon them," this is not correct.
* Student: May Allah be good to you. An expression that Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, has attributes that are negative and privative (...) if they are negative (...) Allah (...)?
* The Shaykh: No, they are among His attributes, because a description is either affirmation or negation. If you say: "So-and-so does not wrong people," or "So-and-so is not ignorant," this is praise, he does not wrong because of his perfect justice. Yes, it is affirmative; there is no pure negation in it. That is, the attributes of Allah contain no pure negation at all.
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed. We say: affirmative and negative; and a negative attribute is not praise unless its perfection is complete.
* * *

﴿a faction of those who were given the Scripture, they will return you, after your belief, to disbelief.﴾

Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, and it has been repeated to us many times that whatever is preceded by the vocative is given special attention, because introducing a matter with the vocative indicates its importance, since the vocative necessitates attentiveness. Then the address with the phrase ﴿O you who have believed﴾, and in directing the address with this description there is an incitement to accept what follows, as affirmation if it is a report, and as compliance if it is a demand, whether a command or a prohibition. It is as if He says: "O you who have believed, if you are truly believers, the matter is such-and-such," so there is an incitement to accept what comes after it, just as if you said: "O man, do such-and-such," meaning that by the requirement of your manhood you do such-and-such. And in introducing it with this description, or in choosing this description, is evidence that what comes next must be accepted as among the requirements of faith, as affirmation if it is a report and as compliance if it is a demand. And there is also in it that not accepting it contradicts faith. So these are four matters. The first: when the address is introduced with the vocative, it is evidence of?
* Student: Evidence of faith.
* The Shaykh: No, when the address is introduced with the vocative, it is evidence of what?
* Student: Of care for the one addressed.
* The Shaykh: Of care for it and its importance. What is the reasoning behind that?
* Student: The reasoning is that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic (...).
* The Shaykh: The vocative necessitates attentiveness, just as when I call you, you pay attention, is that not so?
* Student: Indeed.
* The Shaykh: Second: the choice of faith. Choosing the vocative with the description of faith necessitates what is intended by it: what?
* Student: So that it is softer to their hearts, with the like of (...).
* The Shaykh: No.
* Student: That they carry out what they were commanded, by the requirement of their faith.
* The Shaykh: That is, the incitement and urging; because calling a person by his quality necessitates that he attend to the matter. Yes. Third: the choice of the description of faith?
* Student: He addressed them by faith to urge them to (...).
* The Shaykh: This incitement we have finished with.
* Student: Compliance if it is a command, and avoidance if it is a prohibition, are among the requirements of faith.
* The Shaykh: And affirmation if it is a report is among the requirements of faith. Complete. These are three. The fourth?
* Student: Not turning away from it, or denying it, or not complying with it, is a deficiency in faith.
* The Shaykh: And that turning away from it is rejection, that is, it is among the things that diminish faith.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿O you who have believed, if you obey a faction of those who were given the Scripture﴾. "Faction" (fariq) means a group, and ﴿those who were given the Scripture﴾ are the Jews and the Christians. The Scripture of the Jews is the Torah, and the Scripture of the Christians is the Gospel. His saying ﴿a faction of those who were given the Scripture﴾ means: not all of them, because some of the People of the Book do not have this description; some of them believed. Among the Christians, an-Najashi believed, and among the Jews, Abdullah ibn Salam believed, and these are among the best of the believers. But a faction of them, He says: ﴿they will return you, after your belief, to disbelief﴾, meaning: they will cause you to apostatize after faith, whether that is by fighting among yourselves, as it is mentioned that a Jewish man sowed discord between the Aws and the Khazraj and reminded them of the days of ignorance, so they rose up, that is, some of them rose against others and became angry. This cause or meaning that has been mentioned may be weak, but whatever the matter, among the People of the Book are those who want us to renounce faith, and Allah has declared this in other verses: ﴿Many of the People of the Book wish they could return you to disbelief after your belief﴾ [al-Baqarah 109], ﴿A faction of the People of the Book wish they could mislead you﴾ [Al 'Imran 69]. So the People of the Book wish this, and you know that whoever wishes something strives to obtain it. Therefore we know that the People of the Book strive with all they can to turn the Muslims away from their religion, whether by preventing people from entering the religion of Islam or by removing them from it after they have entered it. The discussion of this will come, Allah willing, at length in the mention of the benefits.

His saying: ﴿they will return you, after your belief﴾. Apostasy after belief is greater than preventing belief from the outset, because it is a removal from faith into disbelief, and it is well known that a person will not leave faith for disbelief except through severe attempts; for whoever has not entered into a thing, keeping him away from it is easier than for whom? Than for one who has entered it and believed in it. For this reason He said: ﴿after your belief﴾. And His saying ﴿disbelievers﴾ refers to disbelief that removes one from the religion. However, they may not be able to remove us from faith entirely, but gradually, by placing before us obstacles to the perfection of faith, until faith dissolves little by little and nothing remains in the hearts, and then it becomes pure disbelief.

Then He, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿if you obey a faction﴾, a conditional sentence. Where is the answer? ﴿they will return you, after your belief﴾. And there is a difficulty here, because it is known that the conditional particle ﴿in﴾ (if) apocopates two verbs: the first is the verb of the condition and the second is the answer of the condition. Here we find no apocopation in ﴿tuti'u﴾ nor in ﴿yaruddukum﴾?
* Student: By deleting the nun, Sheikh.
* The Shaykh: This is apocopated by deleting the nun. Why is it apocopated by deleting the nun?
* Student: Because it is one of the five verbs.
* The Shaykh: Because it is one of the five verbs. Can you list them for us?
* Student: The five verbs?
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: Taf'alu, yaf'alu, and taf'alani, yaf'alani, and...
* The Shaykh: Give the fifth: yaf'alani, taf'alani, yaf'aluna, taf'aluna.
* Student: And taf'alina.
* The Shaykh: And taf'alina. Correct.
Now, His saying ﴿kafirin﴾ is a circumstantial clause (hal) from the waw in His saying ﴿yaruddukum﴾, meaning: they will return you while you are disbelievers.
* Student: ﴿yaruddukum﴾, Sheikh, the apocopation?
* The Shaykh: The apocopation by deleting the nun, because it is one of the five verbs.

﴿And how can you disbelieve while the verses of Allah are recited to you and among you is His Messenger?﴾ The word "how" (kayfa) may carry two meanings, since it is now interrogative, but it may carry two meanings. The first meaning: disapproval as improbable (istib'ad). The second meaning: wonder (ta'ajjub). If we look at their situation, that the verses of Allah are recited to them and among them is His Messenger, we say: their apostasy is what? Improbable. It is improbable that they would turn back on their heels while the Book of Allah is recited to them and His Messenger is among them, seeing the Prophet ﷺ morning and evening, and hearing the verses that descend upon him, so their apostasy is remote. For this reason apostasy did not occur except after the death of the Messenger, peace be upon him, and apostasy during his lifetime was very rare. The second meaning: that it is for wonder, so this is a wonder at the state of one who could apostatize, for whoever apostatizes while the verses of Allah are recited to him and the Messenger is among him, his state is without doubt astonishing; for if a person apostatized without having seen the Messenger ﷺ or heard the verses descend day by day, he would have some excuse. But in this state, hearing the verses of Allah and seeing the Messenger ﷺ, he has no excuse whatsoever. So the interrogative is for what? For wonder: how amazing is your state if you disbelieved! Thus, in the verse, on both meanings, there is a dispelling of hope for the People of the Book, that they will attain their aim from the believers through attempting to make them apostatize. On what meaning? Istib'ad: that is, however much they try, it is impossible. On the second meaning, it is a rebuke to whoever attempts to apostatize: how can you do this, while the verses of Allah are recited to you and His Messenger is among you!

He said: ﴿And how can you disbelieve while the verses of Allah are being recited to you and His Messenger is among you?﴾ ﴿Are recited (tutla)﴾ means: are read to you. The word tilawah comes to mean recitation (qira'ah). When it is used with a subject in the form talā, it has two meanings. The first is recitation, and the second is following (ittiba'). In the Almighty's saying ﴿Those to whom We have given the Book recite it as it should be recited; those believe in it﴾ [al-Baqarah 121], "yatlūnahu" means they read it and follow it, they read it and follow it. So here ﴿the verses of Allah are recited to you﴾ means they are read, and the one who reads them to them is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The chain is: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, from Jibril, from Allah. ﴿And indeed, it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds. The trustworthy Spirit has brought it down, upon your heart﴾ [ash-Shu'ara 192–194]. So it is recited to them through the Messenger ﷺ.

His saying ﴿verses of Allah (āyāt Allāh)﴾ is the plural of āyah, which means a sign. Here it refers to the Qur'an. The Qur'an consists of verses, and each verse is evidence for the One who spoke it, who is Allah, the Exalted, with the attributes that necessitate those verses. For this reason, every verse of the Qur'an is a miracle, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Then let them produce a discourse like it﴾ [at-Tur 34]. "Ḥadīth" here means one verse, or ten verses, or a surah, or ten surahs, or the whole Qur'an. All of it is miraculous.

As for His saying ﴿and His Messenger is among you﴾, the verses of Allah here refer to the legislative verses (āyāt shar'iyyah). Is that so, or not? Is it required, or is it permissible that the cosmic verses (āyāt kawniyyah) are also meant?

* The students: It is required.
* The Shaykh: It is required that they be the legislative verses, because cosmic verses are not recited. But one may speak about them, i.e., report about them. ﴿And among His signs are the night and the day and the sun and the moon﴾ [Fussilat 37]. These are signs of what? Cosmic ones. Is it required or not? It is required. The night, the day, the sun and the moon are cosmic signs and nothing else.

﴿And you are being recited to, the verses of Allah, and among you is His Messenger﴾. The particle "fī" is for location. "Fīkum" means: in your society. "Fīkum" means: in your community, and not that he was residing among them, peace and blessings be upon him, but he was in their community. As Ḥassān ibn Thābit said:

"And among us is the Messenger of Allah, reciting His Book..." [remainder of the verse not given]

The Messenger ﷺ was in their community. They saw him morning and evening. He would visit them in their gatherings, visit them when they were sick, and visit them in their homes ﷺ. He taught them the Book and the wisdom. So, for one who was in this state, is it possible for a small group of the People of the Book to turn him away from his religion? No.

﴿And whoever holds fast to Allah has been guided to a straight path﴾ [Ali 'Imran 101]. ﴿Whoever holds fast (ya'taṣim)﴾ means: whoever clings firmly and seeks protection in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has been guided to a straight path. His saying ﴿holds fast to Allah﴾ includes holding fast to Him in reliance (tawakkul) upon Him, and holding fast to Him in worship (ta'abbud) to Him, because in each of them there is protection. ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾ [al-Fatihah 5]. So whoever holds fast to Allah in worship and seeking help, ﴿has been guided to a straight path﴾. Here the past tense verb ﴿has been guided (hudiya)﴾ is used, indicating that guidance has been established for him previously and in reality: previously in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), and in the writing that occurs when the soul is breathed into him in his mother's womb; and in reality, because he has held fast to Allah. His saying ﴿has been guided to a straight path﴾ omits the agent, because there are many ways of guidance. Who is the highest of the guides? Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Then the Messenger, peace be upon him. Then the heirs of the Messenger, who are the scholars. So the agent is omitted here to include all guides, and the first of them is Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿He guides whom He wills to a straight path﴾ [al-Baqarah 142]. Then the Messenger ﷺ: ﴿And indeed, you guide to a straight path﴾ [ash-Shura 52]. Then the heirs of the Messenger, who are the scholars: ﴿And We made from among them leaders guiding by Our command when they were patient and were certain of Our signs﴾ [as-Sajdah 24]. So ﴿has been guided﴾: the first guidance is from Allah, then the Messenger, then the people of knowledge. But the guidance of divine enabling (tawfiq) is specific to Allah. If all of creation gathered to guide someone with the guidance of tawfiq, they would not be able to do so. Rather, they can point out, urge, and encourage.

His saying ﴿to a straight path (ṣirāṭ mustaqīm)﴾ has two readings: with sīn and with ṣād, "sirāṭ" and "ṣirāṭ", because the ṣād and sīn alternate constantly. His saying ﴿ṣirāṭ (path)﴾: the ṣirāṭ is the wide road. A wide road is called ṣirāṭ, and its root is from al-zarṭ (with zāy), which means swallowing quickly, because people enter a wide road and leave it quickly, unlike a narrow one, where people crowd and can barely exit except with difficulty. His saying ﴿mustaqīm﴾ means not crooked, i.e., not curved, but straight. It includes straightness in descent and ascent, and straightness in deviation and moderation. So it is moderate, with no descent or ascent. Because a path that has a deviation is not straight. If there is a deviation, it is not straight. Is that correct? Yes. Does it increase the distance or not? It increases the distance; the distance becomes longer and arrival at the goal is delayed. Likewise, if it varies in descent and ascent, it is not straight, except that the distance becomes longer and hardship occurs upon ascent and upon descent. Does hardship occur upon descent? Yes.

* The students: Perhaps.
* The Shaykh: No, greatly. If the descent is a steep descent, a person becomes exhausted restraining himself from rushing downward. In any case, we say that the straight is the moderate in deviation, straightness, height and descent.

In these verses there are several benefits. First: a warning to the believers against obeying the disbelievers; by His saying ﴿If you obey a group of those who were given the Book, they will turn you back﴾.

Second: the disbelievers, even if they are People of the Book, try to the utmost extent to turn the believers from their faith to disbelief. The One who says this is Allah, who knows what is in their breasts. They may show us peace and flattery, and claim they are allies and friends, but in their hearts is hatred and rancor, and a desire that we should revert to disbelief. From where do we know this about what is in their hearts while they show us affection, friendship and love? From the Qur'an. If someone says: Allah says ﴿a group of those given the Book﴾, and "group" is indefinite. We do not know; perhaps some of them are otherwise. When possibility exists, the deduction is invalidated. So one cannot specify a sect of the People of the Book and say: these love that we revert to disbelief. One cannot specify, as long as Allah says ﴿a group﴾. "Group" is indefinite. If you say: they are these, we say: no, rather those. So what is the criterion then? Yes?

* A student: We say to them: ﴿a group﴾, O Shaykh, is an indefinite used to indicate generality.
* The Shaykh: No, that does not work, because ﴿a group﴾ clearly indicates part of them. Yes, it indicates an indefinite, that there is a group.
* A student: Shaykh, may Allah be gracious to you, we say: there are other verses that clarified that all Jews and Christians want to lead the Muslims astray, such as the Exalted's saying: ﴿The Jews and the Christians will never be pleased with you until you follow their religion﴾ [al-Baqarah 120].
* The Shaykh: Yes, and this is general.
* The student: Yes, this is general.
* The Shaykh: Good. Then for this there are two answers. The first answer: Allah mentioned in other verses that all disbelievers wish us to disbelieve, and this includes the People of the Book and others: ﴿They wish you would disbelieve as they disbelieved, so that you would be alike﴾ [an-Nisa' 89]; ﴿and they wish you would disbelieve﴾ [al-Mumtahanah 2]; ﴿Many of the People of the Book wish they could return you to disbelief after your belief, out of envy from themselves﴾ [al-Baqarah 109]; ﴿A group of the People of the Book wished to mislead you﴾.
* A student: Many.
* The Shaykh: Many. So we say: there are verses showing that all disbelievers, including the People of the Book, wish this of us. The second answer: we say that this indefinite group is clarified by reality, which is that among the People of the Book are those who believed, and whoever believed cannot wish others to disbelieve. Then we say: what is meant by the group here is those among them who did not believe. Everyone who did not believe is included in this group.

* From the benefits of this noble verse: these groups from the People of the Book do not accept from us anything short of disbelief, unless it is a means to disbelief, because the end is stated: ﴿they will turn you back, after your belief, into disbelievers﴾. The methods of the People of the Book in misleading the Muslims are numerous, very numerous and varied. Among them: opening the doors of desires for them, because the door of desires is wide, and the narrow of the doors of desires widens quickly. The proof of this is the Prophet's ﷺ saying: "I have left after me no trial more harmful to men than women." [Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (5096) and Muslim (2740/96) from Usamah ibn Zayd.] For this reason, may Allah curse them, the curse of Allah be upon the Jews and Christians altogether, they strive earnestly to give women what they call freedom, which in reality is slavery, not freedom. Because when a woman goes beyond the limits of Allah, she leaves the slavery of religion, which is true slavery because it is servitude to Allah, for the slavery of Satan. She leaves the slavery of religion for the slavery of Satan. When she goes out to the slavery of Satan and Satan enslaves her, she becomes his slave; she is ruined and ruins others. Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

"They fled from the slavery for which they were created, so they were tested with the slavery of the self and Satan."

Fled from the slavery for which they were created. What is the slavery for which we were created? The worship of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. "Bulū" means Allah tested them with the slavery of the self and Satan. For this reason you find them focusing on women, so that she deteriorates and becomes free from the servitude of Allah in order to fall into the servitude of Satan, because they know that the most severe trial for men is women. They strive with all their effort that she mingle with men and share in their work, that her shoulder be pressed against his shoulder and her leg against his leg, that he feel her warmth and she feel his warmth, that he smell her breath and she smell his breath, that she shake his hand and perhaps embrace him. Because they know that when a person reaches this level, he remains animalistic, bestial, with no aim except to satisfy his instinct, may Allah protect us, and then he forgets the religion and what is beyond religion, and returns afterward to what? To disbelief. They cannot tell the Muslims: disbelieve! Because if they said "disbelieve," they would not disbelieve. They would say: yes, we disbelieve in the false deity and believe in Allah, and we will strike your head. But they bring these methods which necessitate that people slide into immorality, and immorality is the courier of disbelief.

Second: they throw corrupt, atheistic, disbelieving ideas among the Muslims under the name: "people are free, let everyone adopt what he wishes, let everyone say what he wishes, do not enslave people, for their mothers bore them free," and similar resounding phrases which, when a person hears them, he says: this is the religion. Then people become lax and each one acts as he wishes. But what is the path by which they reach this? The path is that they strike at enjoining good and forbidding evil, and they make people neither enjoin good nor forbid evil, because they know that when good is commanded, good stands, and when evil is forbidden, evil disappears. So they try to reduce and weaken this prohibiting force until people remain with no one enjoining or forbidding, each rides whatever he wishes.

Also, another thing they strike at is the matter of the hudud (prescribed punishments) and the ta'zirat (discretionary punishments). They distort Islam by saying it cuts off the hand of the thief and stones the adulterer. They distort this so as to weaken this aspect. It is well known that when faith weakens, the deterrent of authority is necessary. If faith weakens and the deterrent of authority is absent, the matter becomes chaos. Each one ... does as he wishes: he disbelieves, commits adultery, steals, drinks wine, and it does not matter, because there are no effective punishments, and faith is weak, on the basis that they say: make every person free in himself. People become lax in religion by such methods. That is, casting corrupt ideas into the Muslims is one of the methods of the Jews and Christians by which they mislead people and turn them back into disbelievers after their belief.

Likewise, among their methods by which they turn people from disbelief is that they make the love of wealth and the collection of wealth attractive to people by any means, lawful or unlawful. They make attractive to them the gains of usury (ribā) in its various forms, and the gains of gambling (maysir) in its various forms. Usury is well known. Gambling is represented in insurance and the like. Insurance is undoubtedly a form of maysir, because the contract of the insurer and the insured revolves between what and what? Between gain and loss. This is exactly maysir. When the soul becomes accustomed to it, it forgets everything; its greatest concern becomes to acquire wealth through usury, because usury causes the wealth to increase steadily and the injustice to increase steadily. The increase of wealth goes to whom? To the one who takes usury, and the injustice goes to the one who gives it. So the soul is seized by greed, stinginess and love of wealth, and forgets what it was created for. Likewise gambling (qimar): at the head of gambling, two gamblers sit in a session, each having five million in wealth, and a game of gambling takes place. Then one of them acquires all of the other's wealth, five million, so this one has ten million, and the other has nothing but his clothes. He leaves the gambling hall with nothing but his clothes. He may gamble over his clothes, and say: buy them from me. If he defeats him in gambling for his clothes and takes his clothes, he says: I will sell them to you; I am not sending you out naked, but buy them from me. In any case, such methods that the Jews and Christians and their likes throw among the Muslims must be guarded against by the Muslims, because Allah says: ﴿If you obey a group of those who were given the Book, they will turn you back after your belief into disbelievers﴾. The Muslims must draw their life and their way from what? From the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger ﷺ.

I am fully certain that if they rely on the Book and the Sunnah in this, they will trample the necks of these disbelievers, because Allah says: ﴿It is He who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to make it prevail over all religion﴾ [as-Saff 9]. This is the word of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. The word of Allah, who is capable of everything. It is a promise from Allah, the Capable, truthful in His promise. If that is the case, why do we not hold firmly to our religion? Why do we not hold firmly with complete firmness and make the Islamic nation rise again, anew, holding to its religion in text and spirit, not in text only? Because holding to religion in text only, without spirit, is nothing. It is an outward attachment that vanishes when calamities occur. But holding to it in text and spirit is what benefits a person in his worldly life and his hereafter. So we must beware of the plots of those who were given the Book and the plot of every disbeliever, because Allah says about the disbelievers: ﴿They wish you would disbelieve as they disbelieved, so that you would be alike﴾ [an-Nisa' 89], and He said in Surat al-Mumtahanah: ﴿and they wish you would disbelieve﴾. So we must take these guidelines to which Allah the Exalted has guided us, and walk our path guided by the guidance of Allah, following the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so that victory, happiness, honor and dignity may be attained for us in this world and the hereafter.

* A student: Shaykh, regarding this, we see clear effects of enjoining good and forbidding evil in the Islamic world, but some committed young people place the full burden on certain bodies and say: they have not performed their full role, and so on. What is your opinion?

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verse 100–101 (part 3 of 3):

* The Shaykh: My opinion on this is that everyone is at fault; not everyone has fulfilled the duty incumbent upon him. Every individual among the Muslim peoples and the rulers of the Muslims is at fault in not fulfilling the duty. We should not confine the fault to a particular group or a particular body; we are all at fault. Now, among the people themselves: if a person sees an evil from his brother, does he say, "O brother, come, this that you see is forbidden and not permissible, fear Allah"? No. Yet no one is prohibited from doing this; nobody has been forbidden from it, and still you find only a rare few who do it. Indeed, I recall that someone said: "I came out of the mosque one day and saw a man with his garment hanging long, so I said, 'O brother, this is not permissible, this is forbidden.' He said: 'Bidinna (what is this)? How is this a form of address? Bidinna, meaning from now on you are going to enjoin good and forbid evil?'" Yet the man says: "I spoke to him in the gentlest and most pleasant manner, but he..." So I say: If people were accustomed to enjoining good and forbidding evil, this word would not have come from this common man; he would have known that this is the concern of all Muslims: "You must certainly enjoin what is good and you must certainly forbid what is evil"[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (2169) from the hadith of Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman.]]. And enjoining good does not require that it be a particular group appointed by the rulers; everyone enjoins good and forbids evil, but with wisdom. I always say: enjoining good is not the same as changing evil. Enjoining good and forbidding evil is not the same as changing evil; changing evil requires authority, but enjoining does not require authority. Everyone enjoins and forbids. We have mentioned that there are three things that are confused by some people, and they are different: da'wah (calling to Islam), enjoining good and forbidding evil, and change (of evil by force). They are different, and many people think they are one and the same, but they are not.
* A student: May Allah reward you well. For example, there is a doubt among some Muslims, namely that they say: Do not apply these words of enmity to some Christians; they regard them as friends and apply to them the word of friendship, and they cite the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And you will surely find the nearest of them in affection to those who believe the ones who say, "We are Christians." That is because among them are priests and monks, and because they are not arrogant﴾ [al-Ma'idah 82]. What is your view?
* The Shaykh: Our statement is that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿You will surely find the most intense of the people in enmity toward those who believe to be the Jews and those who associate others with Allah; and you will find the nearest of them in affection to those who believe to be those who say, "We are Christians"﴾. Here Allah divided the non-Muslims into three categories: the Jews, the polytheists, and the Christians. And here He said: ﴿those who say, "We are Christians"﴾, and did not say "and the Christians". ﴿Those who say, "We are Christians"﴾, so notice the difference. Then we find that Allah said in another verse: ﴿O you who believe, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies; they are allies of one another﴾ [al-Ma'idah 51], and He said in another verse: ﴿And those who disbelieve, some of them are allies of others. If you do not do so, there will be fitnah (turmoil) in the land and great corruption﴾ [al-Anfal 73]. These are three verses. So those who say, "We are Christians," are not the Christians who are allies of the Jews and of the disbelievers. Those are a specific people whom Allah described with a description not found among the rest of the Christians, when He said: ﴿those who say, "We are Christians." That is because among them are priests and monks, and because they are not arrogant. And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of what they have recognized of the truth. They say, "Our Lord, we have believed, so register us among the witnesses"﴾ [al-Ma'idah 82–83]. So this group of Christians is the one whose affection toward those who believe is nearest. As for the group which, when it hears what was revealed to the Messenger, recoils and strives with all its might (...) this group, by Allah, is not nearer in affection than the Jews and the polytheists; they are on an equal footing.
* * *
﴿O you who believe, if you obey a party of those who were given the Scripture﴾. Regarding His saying: ﴿O you who believe, if you obey a party﴾, where is the answer to the conditional in this sentence?
* A student: ﴿yaruddukum﴾.
* The Shaykh: Is it in the accusative or the jussive?
* The student: Jussive.
* The Shaykh: By what?
* The student: By the deletion of the nun.
* The Shaykh: Jussive by the deletion of the nun. Good. The Exalted's saying: ﴿if you obey a party of those who were given the Scripture﴾ — why did He express it with ﴿a party﴾ and not say "if you obey those among the People of the Book"?
* The student: Because some of the People of the Book believed, such as Abdullah ibn Salam and the King of Abyssinia and others who believed, so not all of them mislead the believers; rather, a party of them does.
* The Shaykh: Yes; because among the People of the Book some believed, some made peace, and some attacked: three categories. Those who believed, such as Abdullah ibn Salam from the Jews and al-Najashi from the Christians; those who made peace; and those who attacked and kept attacking the Muslims and wanting to lead them astray. In the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And how can you disbelieve?﴾, what is the interrogation here?
* A student: The interrogation here is for denial of likelihood.
* The Shaykh: For denial of likelihood, and also for wonder.
* The student: It may carry two meanings: denial of likelihood and wonder.
* The Shaykh: Yes. What is the explanation of that?
* The student: That is, what is their state while the verses of Allah are recited to them and His Messenger is among them? It is unlikely that they would disbelieve.
* The Shaykh: That whoever is in such a state, to whom the verses of Allah are recited and among whom is His Messenger, it is very unlikely that he would disbelieve. But if they do disbelieve, then their state is to be wondered at. This is on the basis that the interrogation is for wonder.

The Exalted's saying: ﴿Whoever holds fast to Allah has certainly been guided﴾. ﴿Whoever holds fast to Allah has certainly been guided to a straight path﴾. What is the meaning of "holds fast to Allah"?
* A student: That is, he adheres to the law of Allah, Glorified and Exalted, and to what has come of the truth.
* The Shaykh: Because in adhering to that there is protection. Good. Why is the answer of the conditional joined with the particle fa' in His saying: ﴿fa-qad hudiya (then he has certainly been guided)﴾?
* A student: It is a nominal sentence.
* The Shaykh: A nominal sentence? A nominal sentence and ﴿qad﴾ enters upon it?
* A student: A demand sentence.
* The Shaykh: A demand sentence, and ﴿fa-qad hudiya﴾ is a statement?!!
* The student: Let me read.
* The Shaykh: What are you reading?
* The student: ﴿qad﴾ has entered upon it.
* The Shaykh: Yes; because the answer was joined with ﴿qad﴾. And it has been said in this regard:
A nominal, a demand, and an inflected (?) sentence, / with what, with qad, with lan, and with the tanfis (future particle).
The Exalted's saying: ﴿to a straight path﴾. What is the ﴿path (sirat)﴾?
* A student: The clear road; it is said: the wide one. Its origin is with sin (s), and it was changed to sad (ṣ); that is, in the language it is with sin, and it is derived from al-zirt, which is the wide road, because it is the opposite of narrow.
* The Shaykh: It encompasses everything that is traveled upon. As for "straight" (mustaqim), it is the opposite of crooked. We have said that the crooked is either? 
* The student: Either a deviation to the right or the left, or a rising and a lowering.
* The Shaykh: Excellent. Now let us take the benefits.
* A student: We have taken three.
* The Shaykh: What are they?
* The student: The liberation of the believers from obedience to the disbelievers; that the disbelievers try to turn the believers back from their faith after they have entered it; that they do not accept anything short of disbelief except what is a means to disbelief; and their methods of enticing the believers are many.
* The Shaykh: Yes. In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful. And among the benefits of this verse: that obeying the disbelievers contradicts faith, from His saying: ﴿O you who believe﴾; so their obedience contradicts perfect faith, and may reach the negation of faith altogether.
* And among its benefits also: that the eagerness of the disbelievers for this is for the sake of our faith. On the basis of this, we apply the earlier principle that whatever is attached to an attribute increases with the increase of that attribute and its strength. So be certain that whenever the believers grow in adherence to their religion, the disbelievers will grow in harshness in turning them away from their religion. Do you understand this? As long as the attribute is faith, whenever we grow in adherence to faith, the disbelievers grow in harshness in turning us away from faith. Similarly obedience and disobedience: whenever people grow in turning to Allah and adhering to His guidance, the wrongdoers grow in harshness in trying to eliminate this strength in obedience.
And among the benefits of this verse: that obeying the disbelievers contradicts faith, from His saying: ﴿O you who believe﴾ [Al 'Imran 100]; so their obedience contradicts perfect faith, and may reach the negation of faith altogether.
* And among its benefits also: that the eagerness of the disbelievers for this is for the sake of our faith; on this basis we apply the earlier principle that whatever is attached to an attribute increases with the increase of that attribute and its strength. So be certain that whenever the believers grow in adherence to their religion, the disbelievers will grow in harshness in turning them away from their religion. As long as the attribute is faith, whenever we grow in adherence to faith, the disbelievers grow in harshness in turning us away from faith. Similarly obedience and disobedience: whenever people grow in turning to Allah and adhering to His guidance, the wrongdoers grow in harshness in trying to eliminate this strength in obedience.
* Among the benefits of this verse: that some of the People of the Book do not try to lead us astray from our religion; this is taken from His saying: ﴿if you obey a party of those who were given the Scripture﴾, and we have now mentioned that the People of the Book, with respect to this matter, are of three categories.
Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And how can you disbelieve﴾ to the end [Al 'Imran: 101].
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the denial of likelihood that a believer would apostatize into disbelief while the Book of Allah is recited to him and His Messenger is among them; and reality bears witness to this, which is why apostasy did not occur until after the death of the Messenger ﷺ.
* And among the benefits of this noble verse: that the Book of Allah, the Sunnah of His Messenger ﷺ, and turning to them both are the greatest barrier preventing disbelief. From where is this taken? From His saying: ﴿And how can you disbelieve﴾, meaning: disbelief is far from you while the verses of Allah are recited to you and His Messenger is among you. The verses of Allah are recited to us now; His Messenger is not among us, but his Sunnah is among us. From this we derive that whenever we hold fast to the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger, that will be an impregnable fortress against disbelief.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the establishment that the Noble Qur'an is a sign (ayah) from the signs of Allah; from His saying: ﴿the signs of Allah﴾.
* Branching from this benefit: since it is a sign from the signs of Allah, it is impossible for anyone to bring its like, for the sign is the indicator that specifies what it signifies; and if anyone could bring the like of this Qur'an, it would not be a sign of Allah.
* Among the benefits of this verse: we may say that the Qur'an is a legal sign (ayah shar'iyyah), and it also contains cosmic signs (ayat kawniyyah), through what Allah has deposited in it of great allusions to the signs in the universe, so that we make the signs of Allah encompass the legal and what this legal sign points to of cosmic signs. Otherwise there is no doubt that what is recited is the legal, but it contains cosmic signs that it indicates, such as His saying: ﴿And the sun runs toward its stationary point; that is the decree of the Almighty, the Knowing. And the moon—We have determined for it phases until it returns like the old dried curved stalk of a palm. It is not for the sun to reach the moon, nor does the night overtake the day; and each, in an orbit, is swimming﴾ [Ya-Sin 38–40], and many other cosmic signs to which Allah has pointed. And like His saying: ﴿And the horses, the mules, and the donkeys, for you to ride and as adornment. And He creates that which you do not know﴾ [al-Nahl 8]; this verse, in its final phrase, encompasses everything on which one can ride until the Day of Resurrection. And like His saying: ﴿And there is no creature on the earth, nor bird that flies with its wings, but that they are communities like you﴾ [al-An'am 38]; according to some scholars, His saying ﴿with its wings﴾ excludes what flies by mechanical power, such as these iron airplanes, for they are not among the communities that are like us.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the exhortation to hold fast to Allah; from His saying: ﴿And whoever holds fast to Allah has certainly been guided﴾.
* Among its benefits: the glad tidings to whoever is granted success in holding fast to Allah that he is guided; and this is one instance of the many glad tidings which, when a person reflects upon them, leads him to praise Allah, Glorified and Exalted, for His blessing that He has guided him and bestowed favor upon him.
* Among the benefits of this verse: that the religion of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is a straight religion; from His saying: ﴿to a straight path﴾, and the path of Allah is straight in everything. If you look at the rights, you find it straight in them, without injustice. We have rights before Allah, we have rights over ourselves, we have rights over our family, we have rights over our visitor, and everyone has a right over another. The Prophet ﷺ said to Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As: "Give every one who has a right his right"[[Narrated by Ibn Hibban (320) and Abu Ya'la (898) from the hadith of Abu Juhayfah.]]. So this is justice, meaning: there is no bias (janaf) in it, nor in the right of the Creator, Mighty and Majestic; even the right of the Creator, we must have rights that do not wrong ourselves nor those who have a right over us. This is among the uprightness of this religion. But we have already drawn attention earlier to a matter: that some people say the religion of Islam is a religion of equality, and we explained that this is a mistake; rather, the religion of Islam is a religion of justice, because most of what is in the Qur'an is the negation of equality, not its affirmation: ﴿Say, "Are those who know equal to those who do not know?"﴾ [al-Zumar 9]; ﴿Say, "Are the blind and the seeing equal, or are the darknesses and the light equal?"﴾ [al-Ra'd 16], and many verses in which there is negation of equality: that this and that are not equal.
But justice: ﴿Indeed, Allah orders justice﴾ [al-Nahl 90]. We mentioned that this phrase includes those who say that man and woman are made equal, and the scholar and the ignorant, and every person with another, despite the differences in attributes and each one being distinguished from another by his attributes. This is without doubt an error, and Islam does not come with it. Islam comes with justice: that you give every person with a right his right.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verses 100–101 (part 1 of 3):

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿O you who have believed, if you obey a faction of those who were given the Scripture, they will return you, after your belief, to disbelief.﴾

﴿O you who have believed, if you obey﴾. First, this ruling is introduced with the vocative ﴿O you who have believed﴾, and introducing a ruling with the vocative indicates attentiveness to it and care for it, because the vocative contains an alert to the one addressed, and an alert is only given for an important matter that deserves care. Then the address to those who have believed becomes an incitement (ighra'), since describing them with faith requires that they carry out what this address demands of them. It is like when you say to a person: "O man, do such-and-such," meaning: what does your manhood require? That you do this. So when you say: "O believer, do this," the meaning is that it is among the requirements of your faith that you do this. ﴿O you who have believed﴾, meaning: it is among the requirements of your faith that you pay attention to what will be cast upon you. For this reason Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "When you hear Allah say, 'O you who have believed,' then give it your full hearing, for it is either a good thing you are commanded to do or an evil thing you are forbidden from doing."[[Narrated by Sa'id ibn Mansur in his Tafsir (50).]] Moreover, the address with the description of faith requires that compliance with it is among the requirements of faith, and it also requires that opposing it is a deficiency in faith, because a believer's faith requires that he carry out what he is commanded and avoid what he is forbidden.

* Student: Sheikh, there are people who love to do good and the Sunnah, and they say: (...) the customs of people object to me (...), and perhaps when they do them people shun them. Do we say that doing them is a form of obstructing (sadd)?
* The Shaykh: No, it is not possible. That is, some people do Sunnahs that people do not know, and they object to them. Do we say that doing them is obstructing from the way of Allah? No, we do not say it is obstruction; but we may say that leaving them, for the sake of reconciling hearts (ta'lif), is part of the way of Allah, just as the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, left rebuilding the Ka'bah on the foundations of Ibrahim, because people were recently in disbelief, out of fear of tribulation for them.
* Student: We said that Islam is the religion of Allah in (...), and it is in accordance with the fitrah. Now we see that the other creeds and desires, the other sects (niHal), people are quicker to enter them. What is the reason for that?
* The Shaykh: What?
* Student: That is, we see that religions other than Islam, people enter them more quickly, such as communism, socialism and Christianity, and other things, to the point that Muslim lands have been entered. What is the reason?
* The Shaykh: The reason for that is that these...
* The Student: This is opposed to the fitrah.
* The Shaykh: Yes, this is opposed to the fitrah, because there exists a strong drive that overpowers the fitrah, as the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Every child is born upon the fitrah, then his parents make him a Jew, or a Christian, or a Magian."[[Agreed upon; narrated by al-Bukhari (1359) and Muslim (2658) from Abu Hurairah.]] So these people, you find that they lived in the embrace of communism, for example, or studied its opinions and ideas, or lived in the embrace of the West and studied its opinions and ideas, so this obstacle became a barrier between them and the requirement of the fitrah. Otherwise, if people were left to themselves, they would be upon the fitrah.
* Student: Sheikh, Allah's address to the People of the Book: ﴿O People of the Book, why do you obstruct...﴾ Is it addressed to the scholars of the People of the Book, or does it include all of them?
