The leader has four options regarding captives: killing, enslavement, releasing them freely, or releasing them in exchange for ransom. Four things. In any case, these matters should be left to the rulers. For example, if we saw someone in a land with Muslim rulers, and we knew that he was an apostate disbeliever, we would leave this matter to the rulers, because it would cause fitnah. But if he is in lands of disbelief, then yes, there is no harm in killing him, because the lands of disbelief do not rule by the Book and the Sunnah.
* **Student:** Shaykh, in our country some of the "sayyids," who are from the families of the soothsayers or sayyids and so on, people come to them, they spit on them and believe in healing, relying on the ruling that the Prophet (ﷺ) several times spat on some Companions and prayed for them and they were healed. He says this is blessing, not (...), but Allah is the Healer, and this blessing has evidence...
* **Shaykh:** But is the blessing of this charlatan the blessing of the Messenger?! Subhan Allah! I say: is the blessing of this charlatan the blessing of the Messenger (ﷺ)? And notice, everyone, that these are the allies of the devils. Notice that the devils may assist them in what they want; they may assist them, so the common people think this is from sainthood, and they are deceived by them.

* * *

* **Student:** ...our master Muhammad and his family and all his companions. Ibn al-Qayyim (may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him) said in Zad al-Ma'ad:

**Section on the Battle of Uhud:**
When Allah killed the nobles of Quraysh at Badr, and they were struck by a calamity the like of which they had never suffered, and Abu Sufyan ibn Harb became their leader because their great men had perished, he came, as we have mentioned, to the outskirts of Madinah in the Ghazwat al-Sawiq. He did not attain what was in his heart, so he began to incite against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims and gathered the troops. He assembled nearly three thousand from Quraysh, their allies and the Ahabish, and they brought their women so that they would not flee and so that they would defend them. Then he advanced with them toward Madinah and camped near Mount Uhud, at a place called 'Aynayn, in Shawwal of the third year. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) consulted his Companions: should he go out to them or remain in Madinah? His opinion was that they should not go out of Madinah and should fortify themselves in it. If they entered it, the Muslims would fight them at the mouths of the alleys, and the women from the top of the houses. 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy agreed with this opinion, and it was the correct one. But a group of excellent Companions who had missed going out on the day of Badr hastened to him, advised him to go out, and insisted on it. 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy advised remaining in Madinah, and some of the Companions agreed with him. Those men insisted to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so he rose, entered his house, put on his armour and came out to them. Their resolve had weakened, and they said: "We forced the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to go out." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, if you wish to remain in Madinah, then do so." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It is not fitting for a Prophet, once he has put on his armour, to take it off until Allah judges between him and his enemy."[[Narrated by Ahmad (14787) and al-Darimi (2205) from the hadith of Jabir.]]

He went out with a thousand Companions and appointed Ibn Umm Maktum over Madinah with those who remained in it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had seen a dream while in Madinah: he saw that there was a notch in his sword, that cows were being slaughtered, and that he had put his hand into a strong coat of mail. He interpreted the notch in his sword as a man of his family who would be struck, the cow as a group of his companions who would be killed, and the coat of mail as Madinah.

He set out on Friday, and when he reached al-Shawt between Madinah and Uhud, 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy withdrew with about a third of the army and said: "You disobeyed me and listened to someone else." 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn Haram, the father of Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, followed them, rebuking them and urging them to return, saying: "Come, fight in the way of Allah or defend yourselves." They said: "If we knew that you would be fighting, we would not return." So he turned away from them and cursed them. Some of the Ansar asked the Messenger (ﷺ) to seek help from their Jewish allies, but he refused and took the path of Harrat Banu Harithah, and said: "Who is a man who will lead us against the people by a short route?"...

* **Shaykh:** Some of the Ansar asked him to seek help from their Jewish allies, and he refused. That was because there was no need for it. Moreover, the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) knew that the Jews were a treacherous people and that they could not be trusted. For this reason it is not permissible to seek help from a disbeliever when there is no need, and we do not seek help from one whom we cannot trust, whom we cannot trust with our secrets, or whom we fear will abandon us in battle. The point is that the Messenger (ﷺ) forbade these people to seek help from their Jewish allies for this reason.

* * *

* **Student:** He took the path of Harrat Banu Harithah and said: "Who is a man who will lead us against the people by a short route?" Some of the Ansar led him by a path through an orchard of one of the hypocrites, who was blind. He stood up and threw dust in the faces of the Muslims, saying: "I do not permit you to enter my orchard if you are the Messenger of Allah." The people rushed to kill him, but the Messenger (ﷺ) said: "Do not kill him, for he is blind in heart and blind in sight."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) proceeded until he descended into the ravine of Uhud, at the side of the valley, with his back to Uhud. He forbade the people to fight until he commanded them. When morning came, on Saturday, he arranged the army for battle; he had seven hundred men, including fifty horsemen. He appointed 'Abdullah ibn Jubayr over the archers, who numbered fifty, and ordered him and his companions to remain at their post and not to leave it even if they saw birds snatching the army. They were behind the army, and he ordered them to shoot arrows at the polytheists so that they would not come upon the Muslims from behind. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then...

* **Shaykh:** Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And when you departed from your family in the morning to position the believers at their stations for battle﴾. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) arranged them and positioned them at their places on the morning of Saturday. Some scholars said it was on the eleventh, others said it was on the sixth of Shawwal, and they agreed that it was in Shawwal.

[The author's speech has been abbreviated due to its great length.]

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verse 118–122 (part 1 of 8):

Student: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take as intimates (bitanah) those other than your own, who will not spare you [any] ruin. They wish you would suffer; hatred has appeared from their mouths, but what their breasts conceal is greater. We have certainly made clear to you the signs, if you use reason.﴾ ﴿Here you are—you love them, but they do not love you, and you believe in the entire Scripture. And when they meet you, they say, "We believe." But when they are alone, they bite their fingertips at you out of rage. Say, "Die in your rage. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what is within the breasts." If good touches you, it distresses them; and if disaster strikes you, they rejoice at it. But if you are patient and fear Allah, their plot will not harm you at all. Indeed, Allah is encompassing of what they do.﴾ [Ali 'Imran 118–120]

The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take as intimates (bitanah) those other than your own﴾. We have mentioned previously the negation of injustice from Allah, and that is due to the perfection of His justice.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take as intimates those other than your own﴾. It recurs before us many times that address of this kind:

First: Opening it with the call (nida') indicates its importance and the need to be alert to it.

Second: Directing it to the believers has three benefits:

First: Encouragement to comply, as if He says: If you are a believer, do such-and-such; if you are a believer, do not do such-and-such; if you are a believer, affirm the report. So in directing it to the believers there is encouragement to what? To compliance.

Second: That complying with it is among the requirements of faith. For one is not addressed by a description and then given a ruling connected to that description except that this is evidence that complying with this ruling is among the requirements of faith, since it is not valid to address a wicked person with a word that concerns the believer.

The third benefit: That neglecting it is a deficiency in faith. When Allah directs the address to the believers, this is evidence that neglecting it is a deficiency in faith.

Moreover, there must be a great benefit when Allah directs the address to the believers; as 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "When you hear Allah say, ﴿O you who have believed﴾, then lend it your hearing—that is, listen to it—for it is either good that you are commanded to, or evil that you are forbidden from."[[Narrated by Ibn al-Mubarak in al-Zuhd (36), and Sa'id ibn Mansur in al-Sunan (50), from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud.]]

The third benefit: That neglecting it is a deficiency in faith. When Allah directs the address to the believers, this is evidence that neglecting it is a deficiency in faith.

* Moreover, there must be a great benefit: when Allah directs the address to the believers, as 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "When you hear Allah say:" ﴿O you who have believed﴾ "then lend it your hearing—that is, listen to it—for it is either good that you are commanded to, or evil that you are forbidden from"[[Narrated by Sa'id ibn Mansur in al-Tafsir (50), from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud.]].

In this verse He says: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take as intimates those other than your own﴾. This is a prohibition; (lā) is the prohibitive particle, and for this reason it has jussed the verb, so He says: ﴿do not take﴾.

The meaning of bitanah is: the people who are close to a person, derived from the lining of a garment (bitanat al-thawb), because it is closer to the body or the flesh than its outer surface. The garment has a lining and has an outer surface; the lining is closer. So the meaning is: do not take as close people, to whom you confide secrets and inform of your circumstances and of what you intend to do.

His saying ﴿those other than your own﴾ means: other than you, as in His saying the Exalted: ﴿And they have taken besides Allah gods, that they might be helped﴾ [Ya-Sin 74], meaning: other than Him. So the meaning of ﴿other than your own﴾ is: other than you—in what respect? In religion, or in aim, or in what?

We say: What is meant is everyone who differs from you in any of the matters. This varies: it may be in religion, for example, and it may be in worldly affairs. If the matter concerns religion, then we do not take the disbelievers as allies other than the believers, and we do not take the hypocrites as allies other than the believers, because they are other than us. If it concerns trade, we do not take anyone as an intimate who deceives us in our trade, because he differs from us in this direction. And this, in reality, is a principle directed at every believer, and it is valid even for the disbeliever: even the disbeliever, for example, should not take as an intimate someone other than himself—that is, other than his own kind—who would harm him by taking him as an intimate.

His saying: ﴿do not take as intimates those other than your own, who will not spare you [any] ruin. They wish you would suffer; hatred has appeared from their mouths, but what their breasts conceal is greater﴾ these are four sentences. ﴿who will not spare you [any] ruin﴾ is one. ﴿They wish you would suffer﴾ how many?

* Students: Two.

* Shaykh: ﴿hatred has appeared from their mouths﴾, ﴿but what their breasts conceal is greater﴾. These sentences: are they descriptions of the intimates—that is, intimates characterized by these attributes—or are they explanatory sentences giving the reason for the prohibition: that is, do not take intimates other than your own, for they will not spare you ruin and wish you would suffer... to the end?

In this there are two possibilities. It may be that these sentences are descriptions, do you understand? And it may be that they are resumptive explanatory sentences, to clarify the reason: that is, do not take intimates other than your own because they will not spare you ruin... to the end. According to the first view, the meaning of the verse is: do not take intimates other than your own of this description; that is, intimates other than your own who will not spare you ruin, wish you would suffer... to the end. If we say these sentences are descriptions, then His saying ﴿other than your own﴾ is considered a fifth description, because ﴿other than your own﴾, the prepositional phrase, is a description of what? Of intimates. Accordingly, Allah has forbidden us to take as intimates those who are characterized by these five attributes: that they are other than us, that they do not spare us ruin, that they wish us suffering, that hatred has appeared from their mouths, and that what their breasts conceal is greater.

Now we return to the words:

His saying: ﴿who will not spare you [any] ruin﴾. (ya'lu) means to exert effort; that is, they do not spare any effort in your ruin. That is, they exert every effort in your ruin. Khabal (ruin) is corruption of opinion and intellect; for this reason people say of a man whose mind and opinion are corrupt: he is khibl. So the meaning of ﴿who will not spare you [any] ruin﴾ is: they do not spare any effort in your ruin; they exert every effort to corrupt your affairs, because they are a people who are not of you, and they are distant from you, ﴿intimates other than your own﴾.

And their saying: ﴿They wish you would suffer﴾. ﴿Wadd﴾ is pure love; that is, they love with all their hearts that you suffer; that is, what troubles you. It is possible that (mā) is a verbal-noun particle, meaning: they wish your suffering ('anat). And 'anat means hardship and severity, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And if Allah had willed, He would have caused you distress﴾ [al-Baqarah 220], meaning: He would have inflicted hardship upon you. And He said: ﴿Your suffering grieves him﴾ [al-Tawbah 128], meaning: what is hard for you.

The meaning, then, is that these intimates spare no effort in corrupting our affairs, and they wish with all their hearts for suffering and hardship upon us, intellectual, physical and financial suffering; everything that could afflict us with hardship, they wish for it.

The third description: ﴿hatred has appeared from their mouths﴾. ﴿Badat﴾ means: became manifest. ﴿from their mouths﴾: (min) indicates the place of manifestation, so it is for the starting point; that is, it became manifest from their mouths. It is as though they wish to conceal this hatred, but it appears; it must be understood from their speech, even if they do not intend this. For this reason He did not say: "they have displayed hatred from their mouths," but said: ﴿has appeared﴾, and this is evidence that it came out of their mouths as a slip; otherwise they conceal it. They conceal their hatred in order to attain their aims in taking as what? 

* Students: Intimates.

* Shaykh: Intimates. But hatred must appear from their mouths.

﴿but what their breasts conceal is greater﴾: that is, beyond what appears from their mouths; that is, they have much more hatred in their hearts than the tongues express. These people characterized by these attributes, Allah has forbidden us to take them as intimates, and the prohibition on taking them as intimates entails keeping them far from you, being wary of them, and not inclining toward them.

Then He said: ﴿We have certainly made clear to you the signs﴾: that is, We have made them manifest until they became clear like the break of dawn. And ﴿the signs﴾ means: the indicators. Is what is meant the indicators by which these people were described, or is it more general, encompassing everything Allah has made clear to us? It is better to take it as general: we say, Allah the Exalted has made clear to us the indicators that point to truth and to falsehood in this matter and in others.

His saying: ﴿We have certainly made clear to you the signs﴾ indicates that He, glorified and exalted, has a special care for the believers: He makes clear to them the signs that might be hidden from them, indeed that are hidden from them.

His saying: ﴿if you use reason﴾ means that our making the signs clear benefits only one who has reason by which he reasons about himself and his desire. As for one who lacks reason, he does not benefit: ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has come into effect will not believe, even if every sign should come to them until they see the painful punishment﴾ [Yunus 96–97]. It is possible that the condition ﴿We have certainly made clear to you the signs, if you use reason﴾ refers back to His saying ﴿do not take as intimates those other than your own﴾, and the meaning on this reading is: if you use reason, do not take intimates other than your own. As for the first view, the sense is: if you use reason, then We have certainly made the signs clear to you, so reason them out. We have previously noted that when a verse can bear two meanings that do not contradict each other, it is better to carry it on both; so it is part of reason not to take them as intimates, and part of reason to clarify what Allah has made clear to us of the signs.

* * *

He said: ﴿Here you are—you love them﴾ [Ali 'Imran 119]. In His saying ﴿Here you are﴾ there are two readings: with the madd, ﴿Ha antum﴾, and with the qasr, ﴿Ha'antum ulaa'i tuhibbunahum﴾. Both are recognized Sab'i readings. It is fitting for the reciter to recite with this sometimes and with that sometimes, that is, with this at times and with that at times, except before the common people. Before the common people one should recite only in the reading of the mushaf that is in their hands, because if you recite with a reading other than the mushaf in their hands, they will accuse you of error or doubt what?

* Students: In the Qur'an.

* Shaykh: In the Qur'an. They doubt the Qur'an: how can the Qur'an's verses change?! And if they are common and ignorant masses, they might even strike you, saying: you have altered the Book of Allah, because the ignorant masses are a problem; they cannot distinguish. So ﴿Ha antum﴾ is one reading, and the second is ﴿Ha'antum﴾.

﴿Ha antum﴾: (ha) is for alerting. It is said that it has been moved from its place and that the original is: antum ha'ulaa' tuhibbunahum. And it is said: rather it is for alerting and it is in its place, because alerting should be at the beginning of the words, so it is in its place.

His saying: ﴿ulaa'i﴾: ﴿ulaa'i﴾ is a vocative, and its origin is: ya ha'ulaa' (O you).

﴿tuhibbunahum﴾: that is, you love these intimates who spare you no ruin, who wish you suffering, whose hatred has appeared from their mouths, and whose breasts conceal something greater; you love them. That is because believers are predominantly characterized by soundness and purity of heart and by not suspecting others of evil, and these people would show affection to them and claim that they wished them well, so the believers love them, based on what? On their deceiving them.

﴿wa la yuhibbunakum﴾: that is, while they do not love you, though you love them. And how would they love us when hatred has appeared from their mouths?

His saying ﴿tuhibbunahum﴾ is known to us, but ﴿wa la yuhibbunakum﴾ is not known to us; yet Allah has given us indicators for it, namely what their what reveals? Their mouths. So if they do not love you, how can you love them?! The sensible, decisive person treats one who has this characteristic in the same manner as he is.

﴿wa tu'minuna bil-kitabi kullihi﴾: "the Book" here is a generic noun encompassing all books. ﴿bil-kitab﴾ the Qur'an; ﴿bil-kitab﴾ the Torah; ﴿bil-kitab﴾ the Gospel; ﴿bil-kitab﴾ the Psalms; ﴿bil-kitab﴾ the scrolls of Ibrahim. You believe in all of this, and they do not believe in it.

Now, who are these? This applies to the Jews, the Christians and the hypocrites; all of them are described this way by us. But the Jews claim that they believe in the Torah, and the Christians claim that they believe in the Gospel, while the hypocrites believe in nothing.

﴿wa idha laqukum qalu amanna﴾: in hypocrisy and flattery; they say with their mouths what is not in their hearts. For this reason He said: ﴿but when they are alone﴾, that is, by themselves or with their devils, ﴿they bite their fingertips at you out of rage﴾: that is, out of intense rage. But out of intense rage at what they see of Allah's blessing upon you, or out of rage at your not following them, or out of both together. Indeed, we might even say it includes what they claimed, that they spent time with the Muslims without being able to attain their aims.

His saying ﴿they bite their fingertips at you﴾: the fingertips (anamil) are the ends of the fingers, and biting them expresses intense regret and grief, and it also expresses intense rage. Sometimes the one who threatens you is seen biting his fingertips, nodding his head, and saying: "Perhaps I will catch you, perhaps I will catch you," so as to threaten you; we say: this is biting his fingertips out of rage. And the second: his car broke down so he bites his finger; this is out of intense regret. But here Allah the Mighty and Majestic explained that they bite the fingertips out of intense rage, wishing that you were between their teeth so they could chew you up.

﴿wa idha khalaw 'addu 'alaykumu al-anamila min al-ghayz﴾: are the fingertips that are bitten the tips of the fingers or the middle of the fingers?

* Students: The middle of the fingers.

* Other students: The tips of the fingers.

* Shaykh: That is, the upper part? In any case, it appears that it differs according to people's customs: one bites the upper part, and some people bite the middle.

* Student: Because the middle one can bear it.

* Shaykh: And is that your view?

* Student: The fingertips.

* Shaykh: The fingertips, yes, I think we have the middle here.

* Student: The middle one, sir, can bear it more than the upper.

* Shaykh: No, leave aside "can bear it or cannot bear it"; this is a custom, customs are not justified by reasons. Some people bite the middle of the finger and some bite the tip; the point is that all of them indicate intensity, either intensity of grief or intensity of rage.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say, "Die in your rage."﴾ ﴿Say﴾: the address is to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, or to whoever can be addressed, and this is the closer view, since he was addressing the believers at the beginning: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, ﴿Here you are—you love them﴾. So the meaning is: say, O believer, to these people: ﴿Die in your rage﴾. This command is for humiliation and to show indifference toward them.

As for ﴿Die in your rage﴾, the bi ("in") is said to be for the limit and accompaniment: that is, remain in your rage until you die. And it is said to be causal: that is, die because of your rage, for it does not concern us. The second is closer. The first is a supplication against them that their rage remain until death; the second is a supplication against them that death be hastened by their rage. Thus this is closer to correctness and more intense in defiance and in distancing oneself from them.

"Say: Die in your rage. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what is within the breasts." The sentence is a resumptive clause in which Allah, the Exalted, states that He is Knowing of *dhat al-sudur*, meaning the one who possesses the breasts, namely the hearts. This is because the heart is the seat of reason, perception, and the direction of the body. We say that *dhat al-sudur* means the hearts because of the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿For indeed, it is not the eyes that are blinded, but blinded are the hearts which are within the breasts﴾ [al-Hajj 46]. The heart is the place of reason and the place of direction. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ said: "Indeed, in the body there is a piece of flesh; if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt. Indeed, it is the heart."[[Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (52) and Muslim (1599 / 107) from the hadith of al-Nu'man ibn Bashir.]] It is also the place of intention and will, for the Prophet ﷺ said: "Actions are only by intentions."[[Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (1) and Muslim (1907 / 155) from the hadith of Umar ibn al-Khattab, and the wording is that of al-Bukhari.]]

So, ﴿Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾ means: of the hearts, of the one who possesses the breasts. This is a literal explanation, and what is meant is the hearts.
* * *
Then He said: ﴿If good touches you, it distresses them﴾ [Ali 'Imran 120]. ﴿If it touches you﴾: to whom is the address? To the believers. Here He used the plural form, and He used the singular form in His words ﴿Say: Die in your rage﴾, and He had previously used the plural form. This is a variation in address (*al-tafannun fi al-khitab*), and one of its benefits is attentiveness: when the style changes for a person, he becomes attentive, unlike when the style is of one uniform pattern.

﴿If good touches you, it distresses them﴾. "Good": what kind of good? Religious or worldly, physical, financial, or familial?
* Students: General.
* The Shaykh: General. The scope is that *hasanah* is indefinite, and an indefinite noun in the context of a conditional expresses generality. So any good that reaches the believers distresses them, because they are enemies, whether this good is in wealth, body, family, victory, or any other good. Indeed, these people are distressed by good when it touches you.

As for His words ﴿And if an evil befalls you, they rejoice at it﴾: the evil here is what distresses you; that is, if there befalls you what distresses you, in body, family, wealth, or religion, ﴿they rejoice at it﴾, meaning joy reaches them because of it.

Here He says: ﴿If it touches you﴾ regarding good, and ﴿if it befalls you﴾ regarding evil. Is this a difference of expression, or is there a difference in meaning?
Some scholars said: This is a difference of expression, and the meaning of His words ﴿If good touches you﴾ is: if good befalls you. They said: the evidence for this is the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Whatever good reaches you is from Allah, and whatever evil reaches you is from yourself﴾ [al-Nisa' 79].

Other scholars said: Rather, there is a difference between them, because *al-mass* is lighter than *al-isabah*. Based on this, they are distressed by good even if it is very little, and they rejoice at evil if it strikes and causes pain.

This difference regarding His words ﴿If good touches you﴾ is sound, but regarding His words ﴿And if an evil befalls you, they rejoice at it﴾, if we say this difference, their rejoicing at evil would only occur if it were...?
* Student: Severe.
* The Shaykh: Severe. This, as appears, contradicts their condition. Based on this, the view that *massa* and *asaba* have the same meaning is preferred. Is that right?
* Student: One meaning.
* The Shaykh: One meaning, but the expression varies for a benefit, which is alerting, because when the style varies, the addressed person must become attentive, unlike when it is of one uniform pattern.

As for His words ﴿And if an evil befalls you﴾, does their defeat in jihad enter into this?
* Students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Yes, it enters. This is shown by the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And indeed among you is he who lingers. So if a disaster strikes you, he says: "Allah has blessed me, since I was not a witness with them." And if bounty comes to you from Allah, he would surely say, as if there had never been between you and him any affection: "Oh, I wish I had been with them so I could have achieved a great achievement."﴾ [al-Nisa' 72, 73].

As for His words ﴿And if you are patient and fear Allah, their plot will not harm you at all. Indeed, Allah is encompassing of what they do﴾: if you are patient over what reaches you from them and fear Allah in how you deal with them, because the person is required, regarding these disbelievers, to do two things. The first: patience over what they do. The second: that he fear Allah in what he does to them.

﴿If you are patient and fear Allah, their plot will not harm you at all﴾. ﴿Their plot﴾: *al-kayd* is *al-makr* (deceit), and *al-makr* is reaching the goal of striking the opponent by hidden means. By our saying "reaching by hidden means," what is excluded is when one reaches by a known matter to strike his opponent; this is not called *makr*. For example, if he comes to him openly and kills him. But if he comes to him in a hidden way and kills him, we say: this is *makr* and *kayd*.

As for His words ﴿will not harm you at all﴾: ﴿at all﴾ is indefinite in a negative context, so it includes anything whatsoever. So if we deal with the disbelievers with patience and piety, they will never harm us in any way.
﴿Indeed, Allah is encompassing of what they do﴾.
* Student: We see among believers that there are rabble and scum. Are all People of the Book whom Allah warns us about at this level, and that among the believers there are those who seek only their pleasures and desires, and do not defend the religion of Allah or support it..?
* The Shaykh: This, in any case, brings benefits.
* Student: May Allah reward you, O Shaykh. How can the disbelievers take as intimates some from among them, when they are disbelievers? Any intimate among them is a disbeliever.
* The Shaykh: How?
* Student: That is, their whole community is one.
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed.
* Student: So we said that if the second group is treacherous, they should not be taken as intimates. The disbelievers are one community. How?
* The Shaykh: Yes, but some of them may betray one another for their worldly interests; ﴿The Jews say: The Christians are not upon anything, and the Christians say: The Jews are not upon anything﴾ [al-Baqarah 113].
* Student: May Allah reward you. If a man bites his fingertips out of rage, is this considered imitation?
* The Shaykh: No, no, it is not imitation, because this is a natural thing.
* Student: He mentioned it as one of the attributes of the hypocrites.
* The Shaykh: No, He mentioned it because they bite their fingertips over them. For the believer to do it, yes, that is imitation.
* Student: But the act itself is not imitation.
* The Shaykh: No, no, a bare act is not.
* Student: How is one to distinguish (ālā) which means oath from (ālā) which means falling short?
* The Shaykh: The one meaning falling short is (alā), not (ālā); the one meaning oath is (ālā).
* Student: And in the plural?
* The Shaykh: The plural? Say: the verbal noun. (Ala ila) which means falling short, and (ālā) its verbal noun is *īlā'*.
* Student: Shaykh, may Allah reward you, we mentioned that this may refer to the Jews, the Christians, or the hypocrites. May Allah reward you, we must not love them in any case, whether they love us or hate us..
* The Shaykh: Yes, this comes under the benefits.
* Student: Shaykh, may Allah reward you, He said: ﴿And you believe in the Scripture, all of it﴾ [Ali 'Imran 119], and did not say: "And they do not believe in the Scripture, all of it," though He said: ﴿You love them, but they do not love you﴾ [Ali 'Imran 119]?
* The Shaykh: Yes, because they may believe in some of their scripture.
* Student: Well, faith, Shaykh, is not divisible, because one who believes in some of the Scripture is not described as a believer.
* The Shaykh: No, I mean, some of the books; that is, "al-kitab" is a generic noun.
* Student: Even if he believes in it?
* The Shaykh: And also even the hypocrites believe in the Scripture when it serves their interest.
* Student: But it is not truly called faith.
* The Shaykh: Yes, but it is said that he believes in it; ﴿And if the right is theirs, they come to it willingly﴾ [al-Nur 49].
* Student: May Allah reward you. If he believed in the Torah (...) and believed in the Qur'an and denied the Torah..?
* The Shaykh: The reality is that whoever disbelieves in Muhammad ﷺ after his mission is a disbeliever even in the Torah. This is the reality, even in the Gospel.
* Student: I say, O Shaykh: (...) ﴿Here you are, you love them﴾. For example, now the hypocrites in this age, as if Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is pointing with this verse, meaning we should keep away from this...
* The Shaykh: This will come to us in the benefits, God willing (...).
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: They are concomitants, but is the meaning: if you understand these verses we have explained, or: if you understand, then do not take them as intimates? So among the causes of lacking reason is taking them as intimates outright, which is not necessary. And there is a difference between the indication of entailment and the indication of inclusion.
* * *
* Student: ﴿When two groups among you were about to lose heart, while Allah was their ally. And upon Allah let the believers rely. And Allah had already given you victory at Badr, while you were humble. So fear Allah that you may be grateful﴾ [Ali 'Imran 122, 123].
* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan.

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿If good touches you, it distresses them; and if an evil befalls you, they rejoice at it. And if you are patient and fear Allah, their plot will not harm you at all. Indeed, Allah is encompassing of what they do﴾.

We have spoken about the beginning of this verse, and we said: those who are other than the believers and whom they have taken as intimates, when good touches the Muslims it distresses them. What is meant by good here is worldly good: provision, well-being, spoils, and others, and likewise victory over enemies. If an evil befalls them, that is, what distresses them such as humiliation, loss of wealth, calamities, or other things, they are delighted by it.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And if you are patient and fear Allah, their plot will not harm you at all﴾: you are patient over what reaches you from them. It is known that the patient one awaits relief, because he will be patient over the harm he has received in this specific time, but he awaits relief.

﴿And fear Allah﴾: by committing to the fear of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in dealing with these people and in other matters.

﴿Their plot will not harm you at all﴾: that is, even if they harm you, it will not harm you. We have already mentioned that *kayd* is reaching the striking of the opponent by hidden causes, and it means deceit and trickery. It is established for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; that is, Allah is described with *makr*, deception, and *kayd* in their proper places, unlike treachery, for Allah is not described by it, because it is a dispraised attribute in every case.

He says: ﴿will not harm you﴾. In ﴿will not harm you﴾ there are two readings: one is ﴿lā yadurrukum﴾, and the second is ﴿lā yadirrukum﴾, from *al-ḍayr*. *Al-ḍayr* means harm and also means injustice; it is harm with injustice. From this is what came in the hadith about seeing Allah, the Exalted: "Indeed, you will see your Lord as you see the moon on the night of the full moon; you will not be harmed (*la taḍārrūn*)" and "la tuḍārūn,"[[Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (4581) and Muslim (183 / 302) from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri.]] meaning: no harm (*ḍayr*) will reach you. Here He says: ﴿will not harm you their plot﴾, and the reading ﴿lā yaḍirrukum﴾, so each of the two readings conveys a meaning other than the other, because general harm is less than *ḍayr*; *ḍayr* is more severe. So they will not reach us with harm or with *ḍayr*.

His words ﴿at all﴾ are indefinite in a negative context, so they are general: that is, whatever it may be. But will they cause some harm to them?

The answer is yes, by the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿You will surely be tried in your possessions and in your persons, and you will surely hear from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associate others with Allah much hurtful speech﴾ [Ali 'Imran 186]. But harm does not necessarily follow from hurt. For this reason Allah said in the sacred hadith: "O My servants, indeed you will never reach My harm so as to harm Me,"[[Related by Muslim (2577 / 55) from the hadith of Abu Dhar.]] and He affirmed that the children of Adam hurt Him, saying: "The son of Adam hurts Me; he reviles time,"[[Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (4826) and Muslim (2246 / 2) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]] and He said: ﴿Indeed, those who hurt Allah and His Messenger, Allah has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter﴾ [al-Ahzab 57].

﴿Indeed, Allah is encompassing of what they do﴾. The encompassing here is the encompassing of knowledge, power, and authority; He encompasses them as a wall encompasses those within it; that is, they cannot escape the decree, knowledge, authority, and power of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

His words ﴿of what they do﴾: *mā* here is a relative pronoun, so it expresses generality. We have learned in grammar that every relative noun needs a returning pronoun (*'ā'id*) to refer back to it, so that it becomes clear the clause after it is its relative clause; for we cannot know that the clause is related to what precedes it except through a link or returning pronoun. In the chapter on the subject, they call it a link (*rābit*); in the chapter on the relative, they call it a returning pronoun (*'ā'id*). So where is the returning pronoun in His words ﴿of what they do is encompassing﴾?
* Students: It is omitted.
* The Shaykh: The returning pronoun is omitted; that is, "of what they do, He is encompassing."
* * *
Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And [remember] when you set out from your family﴾ [Ali 'Imran 121]. From here to near the end of the surah is all about the Battle of Uhud and what relates to it. His words ﴿and when you set out﴾: ﴿idh﴾ is an adverbial clause, and its governing element is omitted, its estimate being: remember when you set out. ﴿Ghadawta﴾ means you went out in the morning (*ghudwa*), that is, at the beginning of the day, as the matter was indeed so; for the Prophet ﷺ went out to the Battle of Uhud at the beginning of Saturday, which corresponds to the eleventh of Shawwal in the third year after the Hijrah. On that day the Prophet ﷺ set out from his family.

His words ﴿from your family﴾: ﴿min﴾ is for starting point; that is, the starting point of this morning departure was from his family, from Medina. The Prophet, peace be upon him, went out in the morning toward Uhud after he consulted the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, on whether he should go out or not.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verse 118–122 (part 3 of 8):

The cause of this expedition was that Quraysh, after those of their chieftains who were killed at Badr were slain (and it has already passed us in the reading of the Asr prayer that those of them who were killed were seventy men of their leaders, and seventy men of them were taken captive), wanted to avenge themselves upon the Prophet ﷺ. So they set out toward the Prophet (ﷺ), intending to fight him, and they were three thousand, with abundant equipment, intending to attack the Prophet ﷺ to finish him off, and they encamped around Madinah. When this reached the Prophet ﷺ, he consulted the Companions on whether they should go out to them or not. As for the young Companions who had not attended Badr, they advised the Prophet ﷺ to go out, and they said: "Let us go out and fight them." As for some of the Companions, they remained silent. As for the hypocrites, they said: "We will not go out, we will not go out to them; rather, let us leave them. If they remain, they will remain in the worst state, and if they grow weary they will return to Makkah, and if they enter Madinah we will fight them: we will fight them with swords, and the women and children will fight them with stones and from the rooftops." This is what the hypocrites said; not out of sincere counsel to Allah and His Messenger, but out of cowardice, weakness, deception and deceit. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) entered his house, put on his armour, and prepared himself (ﷺ). Some of the Companions said: "Perhaps we have compelled the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to go out," meaning they regretted and said: "Would that we had not spoken this." When he went out, having put on his armour, meaning that which is placed upon the head, and having prepared himself, they said: "O Messenger of Allah, if you wish that we not go out, we will do so." He said: «It is not fitting for a Prophet who has put on his armour to take it off until Allah judges between him and his enemy»[[Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (1142) in a similar wording.]] So he proceeded. He went out of Madinah with a thousand fighters. Along the way, 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy, the chief of the hypocrites, turned back with about a third of the army, and they said: ﴿Had we known there would be fighting, we would certainly have followed you﴾. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They were nearer to disbelief that day than to faith﴾ [Aal 'Imran 167]. So they withdrew. But the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, because of their steadfastness and faith, were not harmed by that at all; they continued until they reached Uhud. When they arrived, the Prophet (ﷺ) arranged them in the best formation and drew up their ranks, and he chose fifty men from the archers and appointed 'Abdullah ibn Jubayr over them, and said to them: «Do not leave your position». He placed them at the foot of the mountain, on a pass of it, and said: «Do not leave your position, whether we are victorious or defeated»[[Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (1142) in a similar wording.]]. So they remained protecting the backs of the Muslims. The fighting took place at the beginning of the day, and the advantage was with the polytheists, so they turned their backs, and the Muslims began gathering the spoils. When the people of the mountain saw the state of the Muslims, and that the polytheists had turned their backs and the Muslims were gathering the spoils, they said: "Let us descend to help our brothers in gathering the spoils, the battle is over." Their commander reminded them of the words of the Prophet ﷺ: «Do not leave your position, whether we are victorious or defeated»[[Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (1142) in a similar wording.]], but they insisted and descended. When the cavalry of Quraysh saw that the gap was empty and that there was no one left to protect the Muslims from behind, they charged at them from behind with their horses and entered. At their head were two great leaders: Khalid ibn al-Walid and Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, may Allah be pleased with them, before their Islam. The people became mixed with the Muslims from behind, and there occurred what Allah had decreed and willed for a great wisdom. Seventy men of the Muslims were killed, the Prophet (ﷺ) was wounded, his lower front tooth was broken, and his face was split open, and his daughter Fatimah would come with a mat, burn it and sprinkle its ash on the wound of the Prophet ﷺ, but the blood kept flowing. In sum, there occurred of trial and testing what Allah the Exalted had decreed and predestined for a great wisdom, so that people would know that judgment belongs to Allah and the final end is to Him, and so that people would know that there is never victory with disobedience. They disobeyed the Prophet (ﷺ) in the legal sense, and they neglected what was incumbent upon them in the predestined sense. They disobeyed the Messenger in the legal sense and neglected what was incumbent upon them in the predestined sense. How so? They disobeyed the Prophet (ﷺ) because he said to them: «Do not leave your position», and they abandoned what was incumbent upon them in the predestined sense, which is protecting the Muslims from behind; for this is among the beneficial means. Abandoning beneficial means is foolishness of mind and deficiency in religion, because Allah the Exalted commanded us to take the means, the greatest of which is reliance upon Allah; but we must indeed do the material, physical means. So they, may Allah be pleased with them and pardon them, experienced what they experienced, and the great calamity resulted. The martyrs, may Allah be pleased with them, their families carried them to Madinah to bury them in al-Baqi', but the Prophet ﷺ ordered that they be returned to their places of death and buried there at Uhud, and they did so. The wisdom behind this, and Allah knows best, is that the one killed in the way of Allah will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection with his wound flowing blood: its colour is the colour of blood and its scent is the scent of musk. He is not washed, lest this blood be removed from their bodies, and he is not shrouded, but is buried in the clothes in which he was killed. All of this is so that his rising on the Day of Resurrection from the place where he fell, and in the state in which he fell, may be realized. In sum, Allah the Exalted reminds His Prophet ﷺ of this great expedition, in which there are such secrets and wisdoms that make clear that this was indeed the right course and the best choice for the believers.

And the Hafiz Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned in his book Zad al-Ma'ad of the wisdoms in this expedition what you will not find in any other book, so refer to it, for it is beneficial.

He says: ﴿When you went out early from your family to station the believers at their positions for the fight﴾. ﴿tubawwi'u﴾: this clause is circumstantial; meaning: while you were stationing. The meaning of (tubawwi'u) is "you cause to descend," and tabawwu' means descending, as in the authentic hadith: «Whoever lies about me deliberately, let him take his seat in the Fire»[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (1291), and Muslim in the Introduction (4/4), from the hadith of al-Mughirah.]], meaning: let him bring himself down into a seat in the Fire. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And those who had settled the abode and the faith﴾ [al-Hashr 9], meaning: who had made it their home.

He says: ﴿tubawwi'u al-mu'minina maqa'ida lil-qital﴾. ﴿al-mu'minin﴾: who is the believer?
The believer is one who affirms what must be believed in, with acceptance and submission, and with this, a testimony from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, of the most complete kind, that these who witnessed this battle are what? Believers.
﴿maqa'ida lil-qital﴾: Allah is greatest! ﴿maqa'ida lil-qital﴾, and they remain firm and sit as one who remains seated in his sitting. For this reason He said ﴿maqa'id﴾ and did not say "manazil." Why? So that these places where they were positioned would be a place of steadiness like the steadiness of one seated in his assembly. It does not mean that the Messenger ﷺ placed them in these positions and said: "Sit down." No, they move as suits the interest of the war, but they were called maqa'id because of steadiness in them.
﴿lil-qital﴾: meaning for fighting the enemies. And you know that the fighter will not remain in his place constantly; rather he advances and retreats as the interest requires.
﴿wallahu sami'un 'alim﴾: sami' 'alim, meaning: Hearing what you say to them, Knowing your conditions.
It may be said that the word ﴿sami'un﴾ is more general than being what He hears them say when arranging them and stationing them, so it is more comprehensive, and this is the better view, because whenever the wording is more comprehensive it is better and more general.
﴿'alim﴾: meaning: knowing what occurs of speech, action, state, present and future.

Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿When two groups among you were about to lose heart, though Allah was their ally﴾. ﴿idh﴾ here, the exegetes or grammarians said: it is a substitute for the first (idh), meaning the estimation is: remember when two groups among you were about to lose heart.
﴿hammat﴾: hamm is applied to mere inner speech of the self, and hamm is also applied to resolve, that is, a person may have hamm: he speaks to himself whether to do or not to do, one says: "this is a hamm," and it is applied to a firm resolve that is carried out if no obstacle exists.
Here the two groups, namely Banu Salamah and Banu Harithah, were about to lose heart, and loss of heart here means cowardice and fear; that is, there fell into their hearts the thought of retreat, and its cause was what the hypocrite 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy did, who withdrew and abandoned with about a third of the army. You know that when a third of the army withdraws or abandons, this is a great breach in the army. So these two tribes were about to lose heart, to be cowardly and turn back, but Allah made them firm, and for this He said: ﴿and Allah is their ally﴾. So Allah, Exalted, made them firm, and they did not do what they had resolved upon.
His saying ﴿and Allah is their ally﴾ is a particular guardianship, and Allah's guardianship is divided into general and particular. The guardianship that means management, the management of affairs, is a general guardianship; and that which means care, that is, which entails special care, is a particular guardianship. This guardianship is undoubtedly particular, because when a person is about to commit a sin or a wrong, and then something from Allah prevents him from it, this is undoubtedly a particular guardianship. Often a person is inclined to a sin or to leaving an obligation, meaning a sin of doing a forbidden act or leaving an obligatory act; he finds in his heart, when he intends the forbidden act, a loosening of this resolve and a turning away from it; this is a guardianship from Allah. Or sometimes he intends to leave an obligation, and Allah brings someone to help him to do it. This too is a particular guardianship. So when these two tribes were about to lose heart, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, took them under His care, so they did not lose heart and remained with the army. Some of these two groups said joyfully: "It was indeed"—meaning from their good fortune—"that Allah, Exalted, informed about them with this report, because He reported that they were about to lose heart, and He reported another joyful report and a distinction for them, which is that Allah is their ally; so this was with that."

﴿And upon Allah let the believers rely﴾. ﴿'ala Allah﴾ is connected to ﴿yatawakkal﴾, and it was placed first to indicate exclusivity, meaning: upon Allah, not upon other than Him, let them rely.

The people of knowledge said tawakkul is: sincere dependence upon Allah in bringing benefits and warding off harms, together with trust in Him and doing the means He commanded. This definition is long but comprehensive; sincere dependence upon Allah in bringing benefits and warding off harms, together with trust in Him, and doing the means He commanded. I will repeat it a third time: sincere dependence upon Allah in bringing benefits and warding off harms, together with trust in Him, and doing the means He commanded.

Repeat it to us.

* Student: It is sincere dependence upon Allah in warding off harms and bringing benefits together with dependence.
* The Shaykh: Together with trust in Him.
* The Student: Together with trust in Him.
The Shaykh: And doing the means He commanded.
* The Shaykh: Good. So it is not enough that your dependence upon Allah be sincere until there is in your heart trust that Allah will help you and suffice you, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And whoever relies upon Allah, He is sufficient for him﴾ [al-Talaq 3]. Nor is it enough to depend upon Allah and trust Him until you do the means He commanded, for if you do not do the means He commanded, you are one who leaves matters to chance (mutawakkil), not one who truly relies (mutawakkil). It is mentioned that "the Commander of the Believers 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, was told: Some people from Yemen came as pilgrims without provisions, and they said: 'We are the ones who rely upon Allah.' He said: 'They are not those who rely upon Allah, but those who leave matters to chance'"[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (1523) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]]. Meaning they are negligent and neglectful. If someone said: "I will depend upon Allah in obtaining provision, that Allah will provide for me," while he is able to do the means but does not do them, we say: you are neglectful and leave matters to chance; do the means. ﴿It is He who made the earth subservient to you, so walk in its tracts and eat of His provision﴾ [al-Mulk 15]. He may say: "Perhaps a relative of mine will die and I will inherit, and this is from Allah's provision." We say: And if he does not die? Will you kill him? Even if he killed him to take his wealth, he would be deprived of inheritance, because one who kills intentionally does not inherit. In sum, for the soundness of tawakkul there must be doing the means Allah commanded; as for means Allah did not command, it is not permissible for a person to engage in them.

His saying ﴿so let the believers rely﴾ is a command to the believers to rely upon Allah, because tawakkul cannot be realized except by the believer, for tawakkul is among the requirements of faith, and true faith is among the causes of reliance upon Allah.

Now let us return to take the benefits, lest we go far afield. What was the last benefit we wrote down?
* Students: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, Allah the Exalted said: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take as intimates those other than yourselves, who will not spare you [any] ruin﴾ and so on to its end.
* In this noble verse: the prohibition of taking intimates who are not of us, because of His saying ﴿do not take﴾, and the original state of a prohibition is prohibition.
* Among its benefits: this warning is not specific to rulers; rather every person is not permitted to take intimates other than his own kind. Even a single individual among us may not take intimates other than his own kind, meaning those who are not on his path or his method. If a Muslim man befriended a disbeliever and took him as an intimate to whom he confides matters, we would say: this is forbidden for him. This is supported by His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies, showing them affection, while they have disbelieved in what has come to you of the truth, having driven out the Messenger and yourselves...﴾ up to His saying: ﴿you confide to them with affection, and I am most knowing of what you conceal and what you declare﴾ [al-Mumtahanah 1].
* Among its benefits: avoiding evil intimates is among the requirements of faith, because to whom was the address directed?
* The students: To the believers.
* The Shaykh: To the believers.
* Among its benefits: taking evil intimates is among the deficiencies of faith, correct? Based on the principle we established earlier: whatever faith requires, its absence is a deficiency in faith.
Would it be among the nullifiers of faith; among the nullifiers, or among the deficiencies?
* The students: It may be.
* The Shaykh: It may be; perhaps it is among the nullifiers of faith. If he took such intimates in matters that take one out of Islam, that would be among the nullifiers of faith.
* Among the benefits of this verse: that those other than us will not spare us ruin. This is based on the sentence being what? Resumptive, giving the reason. I mentioned to you in the tafsir that some scholars said it is a qualifier of what precedes, and that if those other than us do not spare us ruin, then there is no harm in taking them as intimates. But the apparent meaning is the first: that the sentence is resumptive giving the reason, meaning that those other than us do not spare us ruin.
Let us give an example of believers taking intimates from among the disbelievers: the disbelievers, without doubt, do not fall short in seeking ruin for us. Now: "It is mentioned that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, was sent to by Abu Musa, wanting him to appoint a Christian scribe over the treasury, because he, that is this Christian scribe, was good at accounting. 'Umar wrote to him not to do so, and ordered him to dismiss him. He repeated the request a second time, asking him to keep him as scribe, and 'Umar wrote to him: The Christian has died, and peace."[[Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-Kubra (9/204) and Shu'ab al-Iman (8939) from the hadith of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, in a similar wording.]] What is the meaning?
* The students: (...).
* The Shaykh: Meaning, if he died, does this mean the treasury or its accounting would be halted? Suppose he died. As for entrusting him with the treasury of the Muslims after he has betrayed Allah and His Messenger, that is impossible.
By this we know that it is not permissible for our enemies, whether disbelievers or others, to be entrusted with the secrets of our affairs, for if we entrust them with the secrets of our affairs, we have taken them as intimates.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verse 118–122 (part 4 of 8):

* Among the benefits of this verse: it shows the care of Allah, glorified and exalted, for His believing servants, in that He warns them against matters that may remain hidden from them, namely taking bad intimates (bitanat, "inner circle").
* Among the benefits of this verse: our enemies wish for us what distresses us, as His saying shows: ﴿They love that you should suffer hardship﴾.
Here is a question: do they wish for what distresses us in worldly matters or in religious matters?
* The students: It includes both.
* The Shaykh: It includes both. They wish to destroy our armies, they wish to destroy our economy, they wish to destroy our knowledge, they wish to destroy our religion. The apparent view to me, and Allah knows best, is that the most important thing to them is the destruction of religion, because they know that if our religion grows strong, it becomes a destruction for them. But if our economy grows strong, it is not a destruction for them, because they are stronger than us economically, stronger than us militarily, and stronger than us in equipment. Rather, it is religion that destroys them. Therefore we say: everything that distresses us, in matters of religion and of worldly life, they seek. They wish to harass us in religion as much as they can, they wish to harass us in the economy as much as they can, they wish to harass us in weapons as much as they can. They send us weapons that have been left behind by time, weapons whose usefulness has ceased in the present age, and which, compared to the weapons of the present age, are like a knife or a club compared to weapons; that is, they have no benefit. But they do not care; they want to complete their economy and keep their factories running, and they do not mind whether we benefit or are harmed.
* Among the benefits of this verse: if a person reflects on the state of our enemies, he finds the breath of hatred coming from their mouths, as His saying shows: ﴿Hatred has already appeared from their mouths﴾ by what they say. Sometimes hatred also appears in their actions, through harassment; so sometimes they show it from their mouths, and sometimes from their deeds, through threats and the like, actual threats rather than verbal ones.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: what is in the hearts of the enemies of enmity, hatred, rancor, and fury is greater than what appears. This is a matter that none knows except Allah, glorified and exalted, and He is the One who informed us of it: ﴿And what their breasts conceal is greater﴾, greater than what their mouths reveal.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: it shows that intrinsic or acquired attributes vary in degree, as His saying shows: ﴿greater﴾. He spoke of hatred, and hatred is an intrinsic attribute of the heart that a person cannot know except through its effects. So here He made clear that hatred varies in degree, and likewise love varies in degree. There is no doubt about love; everyone accepts it, because it came in the Qur'an and the Sunnah: ﴿Say: If your fathers, your sons, your brothers...﴾ until His saying: ﴿more beloved to you than Allah and His Messenger﴾ [at-Tawbah 24]. The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: «None of you believes until I am more beloved to him than his child, his father, and all people»[[Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (15) and Muslim (44 / 70) from the hadith of Anas.]].
But does hatred also vary? We say: yes, even hatred varies; some of it is greater than other.
* Among the benefits of this verse: the favour of Allah, glorified and exalted, upon us in making His signs clear, as His saying shows: ﴿We have already made the signs clear to you﴾. The signs that Allah has made clear are of two kinds: cosmic signs and legislative signs. His making them clear is either through sensory observation or through rational reflection. Legislative signs are through rational reflection, and cosmic signs through sensory observation, which may also lead to rational reflection.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the more intellect a person has, or the stronger his intellect, the better he understands the signs of Allah. Is this derived? 
* A student: From His saying, exalted is He: ﴿if you use your reason﴾.
* The Shaykh: ﴿We have already made the signs clear to you, if you use your reason﴾. Therefore, the more intelligent a person is, the clearer and more evident the signs are to him.
Then Allah, exalted, said: ﴿Here you are﴾. Do you have questions? Good.
* A student: O Shaykh, is it better for a sick person to seek treatment, or to rely upon Allah and ask Allah to heal him?
* The Shaykh: This is a matter of difference among the scholars. Some said that leaving medicine is better; some said that medicine is better; and some said that if the benefit of medicine predominates, then it is better. The Prophet, peace be upon him, commanded treatment, and Allah commanded the preservation of the self. The most correct view is that if this medicine is known to cure this disease, then it is better to take it, because this is one of Allah's blessings, just as a person takes food and drink obligatorily. Likewise, if it is strongly believed that there is benefit, then it is better to seek treatment.
* The student: The hadith of the woman who used to uncover herself, and the Prophet ﷺ said: «If you are patient, you will have Paradise»[[Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (5652) and Muslim (2576 / 54) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]]. They prefer not to be treated and to remain upon..
* The Shaykh: Yes, that was a specific case. Perhaps the Messenger, peace be upon him, understood that her condition might change if she were completely cured, and for this reason, sometimes illness is better for a person in religious terms.
* A student: May Allah reward you well. We mentioned that it is not permissible to entrust our secrets to the enemies of Allah. But, may Allah reward you well, sometimes the country needs that, for example technology?
* The Shaykh: No, no. These are not secrets of industry. In industry they know more than us; that is, they are the ones who conceal their secrets from us, because they have access to things we do not. But our secrets are: what we intend to do in arranging our armies, in the interests of our peoples, in our own interests. If it is specific, that is the matter. As for industry, at present they are ahead, and perhaps a day will come when we are better than them. But at present, they are the ones who conceal their secrets from us.
* A student: The number of disbelievers at the battle of Uhud and Badr was three times the number of the Muslims. So was it not right for the Prophet ﷺ to seek help from someone, O Shaykh, from one of the tribes?
* The Shaykh: The disbelievers, you mean? And the question?
* The student: I mean, did the Prophet ﷺ not seek help from anyone?
* The Shaykh: Yes, he was not compelled to do so. The Messenger was not compelled to do this.
* The student: Their number was three times.
* The Shaykh: Yes, perhaps. ﴿How often has a small company overcome a large company by Allah's permission﴾ [al-Baqarah 249]. But if there is no suitable occasion at all, there is no suitable occasion. What do they do? If there is no suitable occasion, for example if we know with certainty that in confronting them, or in their aggression against us, we cannot defend ourselves at all; but three against nine, for example, there is possibility, there is possibility of victory.
* A student: O Shaykh, regarding hospitals for example, the director might be a Christian (...), meaning..
* The Shaykh: What do you mean?
* The student: (...) the secrets of the Muslims?
* The Shaykh: Hospitals.
* The student: The hospital director might be a Christian, for example.
* The Shaykh: And the hospital is Islamic or..?
* The student: It is in a Muslim country.
* The Shaykh: In a Muslim country, no, this is not permissible. It is not permissible to entrust the secrets of the Muslims to them, and women are uncovered, and one is not safe, because the Christians in the countries of Africa tell us that they give patients medicine, and the patient thinks it is a cure, but it is a medicine of sterility. They sterilize women, may Allah curse them, so I was told, and Allah knows best. But we cannot trust the disbelievers; how can we trust them?! They may give us injections that destroy us over the long term. Yes.
* A student: (...) Arab medicines or medicines, meaning (...)?
* The Shaykh: By Allah, if natural medicines are possible, they are better, because most modern medicines contain chemical substances that may be harmful to a person. Therefore, this medicine may harm one man while benefiting another, according to its ingredients.
* A student: (...) meaning, there was no occasion for the Prophet ﷺ to seek help from the polytheists. And it is established that he turned away a polytheist when he went out to fight with him. Also, in one of the battles the Romans were nine-tenths of the Muslims in the expedition, and he also did not seek help from polytheists.
* The Shaykh: Yes, correct.
* The student: How could it be nine-tenths..
* The Shaykh: Like what is nine-tenths? In which battle?
* The student: The Romans, in the battle of 'Ayn Jalut roughly, the battle of... the battle of Mu'tah, O Shaykh.
* The Shaykh: I understand that 'Ayn Jalut was not in the time of the Messenger, peace be upon him.
* The student: Mu'tah, O Shaykh, Mu'tah.
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* The student: And al-Qadisiyyah also.
* The Shaykh: Yes. First: he himself did not campaign at Mu'tah; he sent an army against the Romans, and it happened that the Romans gathered. The Muslims did not think they would gather in such numbers, and for this reason Khalid ibn al-Walid led them to the mountain, and Allah granted victory.
* The student: Therefore he did not seek help (...).
* The Shaykh: Come on, in the name of Allah, we place our trust in Allah.
* A student: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and prayers and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad and upon his family and all his companions. Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, said in Zad al-Ma'ad:
Chapter on the Great Battle of Badr.
When it was the month of Ramadan of that year, news reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ of the caravan coming to Quraysh from Syria, accompanied by Abu Sufyan. It was the caravan they had gone out to pursue when it left Makkah. They were about forty men, and it contained great wealth for Quraysh. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called people to go out to it, and ordered those who had mounts to ride out. He did not make a great preparation for it, because he went out quickly with three hundred and some men. There were no horses with them except two horses: a horse for al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam and a horse for al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad al-Kindi. They had seventy camels, and two or three men would take turns riding one camel. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, 'Ali, and Marthad ibn Abi Marthad al-Ghanawi took turns on one camel; Zayd ibn Harithah and his son and Kabshah, the freed slaves of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, took turns on one camel; Abu Bakr, 'Umar, and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf took turns on one camel. He appointed Ibn Umm Maktum over Madinah and over the prayer. When they reached al-Rawha, he sent back Abu Lubabah ibn 'Abd al-Mundhir and appointed him over Madinah.
* The Shaykh: I have here (bi-l-Rawha): al-Rawha, with a fatha on the ra' and a sukun on the waw: a village about forty miles from Madinah. Yes.
* * *
* The student: When they reached al-Rawha, he sent back Abu Lubabah ibn 'Abd al-Mundhir and appointed him over Madinah, and he gave the banner to Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr, and the single flag to 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, and the other, which belonged to the Ansar, to Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, and he placed Qays ibn Abi Sa'sa'ah over the rear guard, and he proceeded. When he drew near to al-Safra, he sent Basbas ibn 'Amr al-Juhani and 'Adi ibn Abi al-Zaghba' to Badr to spy out news of the caravan.
As for Abu Sufyan, news reached him of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ's departure and his intention toward it, so he hired Damdam ibn 'Amr al-Ghifari to go to Makkah as a crier seeking help from Quraysh, calling them to rush to their caravan to protect it from Muhammad and his companions. The cry reached the people of Makkah, and they rose quickly and turned out in full force. None of their nobles stayed behind except Abu Lahab, who sent in his place a man who owed him a debt. They mobilized those around them from the tribes of the Arabs, and no branch of Quraysh stayed behind except the Banu 'Adi, and none of them went out with them. They left their homes, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿boastfully and to be seen by people, and to bar from the way of Allah﴾ [al-Anfal 47]. They advanced, as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «With their sharpness and their iron; you oppose Him and oppose His Messenger»[[Zad al-Ma'ad (3 / 172). See al-Maghazi of al-Waqidi (1 / 95), and the Sirah of Ibn Hisham (1 / 621) with the wording: «O Allah, this is Quraysh, who have come with their arrogance and pride, opposing You and denying Your Messenger».]], and they came with determination, capable, with zeal, anger, and rage against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his companions, because of what they intended: to seize their caravan and kill those in it. They had struck 'Amr ibn al-Hadrami and the caravan that was with him the day before. Allah gathered them without prior appointment, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Even if you had made an appointment, you would have differed concerning the appointment; but that Allah might accomplish a matter that was to be done﴾ [al-Anfal 42].
"When the news of Quraysh's departure reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he consulted his companions. The Muhajirun spoke and spoke well. Then he consulted them a second time, and the Muhajirun spoke and spoke well. Then he consulted them a third time, and the Ansar understood that he meant them. Sa'd ibn Mu'adh hastened to say: 'O Messenger of Allah, it seems you are hinting at us.' He was indeed meaning them, because they had pledged to him to protect him against red and black in their homes. When he resolved to go out, he consulted them to know what they had. Sa'd said to him: 'Perhaps you fear that the Ansar regard it as a right upon them that they should not help you except in their own homes. I speak on behalf of the Ansar and answer for them. Go wherever you wish, join whomever you wish, sever whomever you wish, take from our wealth what you wish, give us what you wish, and what you take from us is dearer to us than what you leave. Whatever you command, our affair follows your command. By Allah, if you were to travel until you reached Barak al-Ghimad, we would travel with you. By Allah, if you were to lead us into this sea, we would plunge into it with you.'"
"Al-Miqdad said to him: 'We will not say to you what the people of Musa said to Musa: ﴿Go, you and your Lord, and fight; we will sit here﴾, but we will fight on your right and your left, before you and behind you.' The face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ shone"[[Related by al-Bukhari (3952) from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud in abridged form, and Ibn Jarir in his tafsir (11 / 41) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas in full.]].
* The Shaykh: First: the Muhajirun spoke and spoke well, even though they were going to fight their own people from Quraysh. Then the Ansar spoke, this wonderful speech that shows the strength of faith, the strength of their obedience to the command of the Prophet ﷺ, and their protection of him, and that whatever he does, they follow him, may Allah be pleased with them. This, my brothers, is what truly represents Islam and truly represents the Muslims: when Allah and His Messenger command a matter, they have no choice in their affair, and they follow the Messenger, peace be upon him, ransoming him with their selves, their wealth, and their children. Likewise, we must ransom, to the extent we can, the Book of our Lord and the Sunnah of our Prophet ﷺ, with our selves, our wealth, and our children, because these are the dearest things we have in this world. Therefore I want us to take a lesson from this and keep in mind what they said to him in that great statement: "If you were to lead us into this sea, we would plunge into it with you," even though plunging into the sea is destruction. But they would follow the Prophet ﷺ in everything. May Allah be pleased with them and content them. Yes.
* * *
* The student: «The face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ shone, and he was delighted by what he heard from his companions, and said: "Proceed and rejoice, for Allah has promised me one of the two groups, and I have seen the places where the people will fall."»[[Mentioned by Ibn Hisham in al-Sirah (1 / 615), and Ibn Jarir in his tafsir (11 / 41) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]]. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ proceeded toward Badr, and Abu Sufyan turned aside and reached..
* The Shaykh: "Proceed and rejoice": it is as if victory were in his hand, peace be upon him, as if he were holding it, because Allah, exalted, is the One who promised him: ﴿And when Allah promised you one of the two groups, that it would be yours﴾ [al-Anfal 7]. The first group was Abu Sufyan and the caravan; the second was Quraysh. ﴿And you wished that the one without thorns would be yours﴾ [al-Anfal 7], and the one without thorns was who? The caravan. ﴿And Allah wished to establish the truth by His words and cut off the last of the disbelievers﴾ [al-Anfal 7]. Praise be to Allah. Yes.
Then he says: "I have seen the places where the people will fall." This is also good news, so rejoice. Or "I have seen the places where the people will fall" is literal; that is, it is certain knowledge and the truth of certainty, because the vision of the Prophet ﷺ is revelation.
* * *

*Student:* The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set out for Badr. Abu Sufyan veered off and reached the coast, and when he saw that he had escaped and secured the caravan, he wrote to the Quraysh: "Turn back, for you only went out to protect your caravan." The news reached them while they were at al-Juhfah, and they resolved to return. Abu Jahl said: "By Allah, we will not turn back until we reach Badr, stay there, feed those who attend us from among the Arabs, and the Arabs will fear us after this." Al-Akhnas ibn Shariq advised them to return, but they disobeyed him, so he returned with the Banu Zuhrah, and no one from Zuhrah attended Badr. Afterwards the Banu Zuhrah took pride in al-Akhnas's opinion, and he remained among them obeyed and honoured. The Banu Hashim wished to return, but Abu Jahl pressed them hard and said: "This band shall not leave us until we return." So they went on. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) marched until he halted in the evening at the nearest of the waters of Badr and said: "Advise me on the place to stop." Al-Hubab ibn al-Mundhir said: "O Messenger of Allah, I know this place and its wells. If you see fit, let us go to a well we know, which has abundant sweet water, and let us stop there, get ahead of the people to it, and fill in the other water sources." [Cited by Ibn Hisham in al-Sirah (1/620).]

The polytheists advanced hastily, seeking water. The Prophet (ﷺ) sent ʿAli, Saʿd and al-Zubayr to Badr to seek news. They came back with two servants of the Quraysh, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was standing in prayer. His Companions asked them: "Who are you?" They said: "We are water-carriers for the Quraysh." The Companions disliked this and wished that they had been from Abu Sufyan's caravan. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) finished the prayer, he said to them: "Tell me where the Quraysh are." They said: "Behind this sand dune." He said: "How many are the people?" They said: "We do not know." He said: "How many camels do they slaughter each day?" They said: "One day ten, and one day nine." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The people are between nine hundred and a thousand." [Cited by al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il (965) from the hadith of Yazid ibn Ruman.] Then Allah sent down a single rain that night. It was a heavy downpour upon the polytheists which prevented them from advancing, while for the Muslims it was a light rain by which He purified them, removed from them the defilement of Satan, firmed the ground, hardened the sand, made their feet steady, prepared the place of encampment, and strengthened their hearts. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions reached the water first and camped beside it in the middle of the night. They made cisterns and filled in the other water sources. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions stopped at the cisterns. A shelter (ʿarish) was built for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), where he would stand on a hill overlooking the battlefield. He walked over the place of battle and began pointing with his hand: "This is the place where so-and-so will fall, and this is the place where so-and-so will fall, if Allah wills." [Muslim (2873/76) from the hadith of ʿUmar.]

*Student:* The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions stopped at the cisterns, and a shelter was built for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) where he would stand on a hill overlooking the battlefield. He walked over the place of battle and began pointing with his hand: "This is the place where so-and-so will fall, and this is the place where so-and-so will fall, and this is the place where so-and-so will fall, if Allah wills." [Muslim (2873/76) from the hadith of ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab.] None of them went beyond the place he had pointed to.

When the polytheists came into view and the two hosts faced each other, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Allah, these are the Quraysh; they have come with their arrogance and pride, they have come to oppose You and to deny Your Messenger." He stood, raised his hands, and sought victory from his Lord, saying: "O Allah, fulfil for me what You promised me. O Allah, I implore You by Your covenant and Your promise."
