The meaning of (tubawwi'u) is "you cause to descend," and tabawwu' means descending, as in the authentic hadith: «Whoever lies about me deliberately, let him take his seat in the Fire»[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (1291), and Muslim in the Introduction (4/4), from the hadith of al-Mughirah.]], meaning: let him bring himself down into a seat in the Fire. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And those who had settled the abode and the faith﴾ [al-Hashr 9], meaning: who had made it their home.

He says: ﴿tubawwi'u al-mu'minina maqa'ida lil-qital﴾. ﴿al-mu'minin﴾: who is the believer?
The believer is one who affirms what must be believed in, with acceptance and submission, and with this, a testimony from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, of the most complete kind, that these who witnessed this battle are what? Believers.
﴿maqa'ida lil-qital﴾: Allah is greatest! ﴿maqa'ida lil-qital﴾, and they remain firm and sit as one who remains seated in his sitting. For this reason He said ﴿maqa'id﴾ and did not say "manazil." Why? So that these places where they were positioned would be a place of steadiness like the steadiness of one seated in his assembly. It does not mean that the Messenger ﷺ placed them in these positions and said: "Sit down." No, they move as suits the interest of the war, but they were called maqa'id because of steadiness in them.
﴿lil-qital﴾: meaning for fighting the enemies. And you know that the fighter will not remain in his place constantly; rather he advances and retreats as the interest requires.
﴿wallahu sami'un 'alim﴾: sami' 'alim, meaning: Hearing what you say to them, Knowing your conditions.
It may be said that the word ﴿sami'un﴾ is more general than being what He hears them say when arranging them and stationing them, so it is more comprehensive, and this is the better view, because whenever the wording is more comprehensive it is better and more general.
﴿'alim﴾: meaning: knowing what occurs of speech, action, state, present and future.

Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿When two groups among you were about to lose heart, though Allah was their ally﴾. ﴿idh﴾ here, the exegetes or grammarians said: it is a substitute for the first (idh), meaning the estimation is: remember when two groups among you were about to lose heart.
﴿hammat﴾: hamm is applied to mere inner speech of the self, and hamm is also applied to resolve, that is, a person may have hamm: he speaks to himself whether to do or not to do, one says: "this is a hamm," and it is applied to a firm resolve that is carried out if no obstacle exists.
Here the two groups, namely Banu Salamah and Banu Harithah, were about to lose heart, and loss of heart here means cowardice and fear; that is, there fell into their hearts the thought of retreat, and its cause was what the hypocrite 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy did, who withdrew and abandoned with about a third of the army. You know that when a third of the army withdraws or abandons, this is a great breach in the army. So these two tribes were about to lose heart, to be cowardly and turn back, but Allah made them firm, and for this He said: ﴿and Allah is their ally﴾. So Allah, Exalted, made them firm, and they did not do what they had resolved upon.
His saying ﴿and Allah is their ally﴾ is a particular guardianship, and Allah's guardianship is divided into general and particular. The guardianship that means management, the management of affairs, is a general guardianship; and that which means care, that is, which entails special care, is a particular guardianship. This guardianship is undoubtedly particular, because when a person is about to commit a sin or a wrong, and then something from Allah prevents him from it, this is undoubtedly a particular guardianship. Often a person is inclined to a sin or to leaving an obligation, meaning a sin of doing a forbidden act or leaving an obligatory act; he finds in his heart, when he intends the forbidden act, a loosening of this resolve and a turning away from it; this is a guardianship from Allah. Or sometimes he intends to leave an obligation, and Allah brings someone to help him to do it. This too is a particular guardianship. So when these two tribes were about to lose heart, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, took them under His care, so they did not lose heart and remained with the army. Some of these two groups said joyfully: "It was indeed"—meaning from their good fortune—"that Allah, Exalted, informed about them with this report, because He reported that they were about to lose heart, and He reported another joyful report and a distinction for them, which is that Allah is their ally; so this was with that."

﴿And upon Allah let the believers rely﴾. ﴿'ala Allah﴾ is connected to ﴿yatawakkal﴾, and it was placed first to indicate exclusivity, meaning: upon Allah, not upon other than Him, let them rely.

The people of knowledge said tawakkul is: sincere dependence upon Allah in bringing benefits and warding off harms, together with trust in Him and doing the means He commanded. This definition is long but comprehensive; sincere dependence upon Allah in bringing benefits and warding off harms, together with trust in Him, and doing the means He commanded. I will repeat it a third time: sincere dependence upon Allah in bringing benefits and warding off harms, together with trust in Him, and doing the means He commanded.

Repeat it to us.

* Student: It is sincere dependence upon Allah in warding off harms and bringing benefits together with dependence.
* The Shaykh: Together with trust in Him.
* The Student: Together with trust in Him.
The Shaykh: And doing the means He commanded.
* The Shaykh: Good. So it is not enough that your dependence upon Allah be sincere until there is in your heart trust that Allah will help you and suffice you, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And whoever relies upon Allah, He is sufficient for him﴾ [al-Talaq 3]. Nor is it enough to depend upon Allah and trust Him until you do the means He commanded, for if you do not do the means He commanded, you are one who leaves matters to chance (mutawakkil), not one who truly relies (mutawakkil). It is mentioned that "the Commander of the Believers 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, was told: Some people from Yemen came as pilgrims without provisions, and they said: 'We are the ones who rely upon Allah.' He said: 'They are not those who rely upon Allah, but those who leave matters to chance'"[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (1523) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]]. Meaning they are negligent and neglectful. If someone said: "I will depend upon Allah in obtaining provision, that Allah will provide for me," while he is able to do the means but does not do them, we say: you are neglectful and leave matters to chance; do the means. ﴿It is He who made the earth subservient to you, so walk in its tracts and eat of His provision﴾ [al-Mulk 15]. He may say: "Perhaps a relative of mine will die and I will inherit, and this is from Allah's provision." We say: And if he does not die? Will you kill him? Even if he killed him to take his wealth, he would be deprived of inheritance, because one who kills intentionally does not inherit. In sum, for the soundness of tawakkul there must be doing the means Allah commanded; as for means Allah did not command, it is not permissible for a person to engage in them.

His saying ﴿so let the believers rely﴾ is a command to the believers to rely upon Allah, because tawakkul cannot be realized except by the believer, for tawakkul is among the requirements of faith, and true faith is among the causes of reliance upon Allah.

Now let us return to take the benefits, lest we go far afield. What was the last benefit we wrote down?
* Students: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, Allah the Exalted said: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take as intimates those other than yourselves, who will not spare you [any] ruin﴾ and so on to its end.
* In this noble verse: the prohibition of taking intimates who are not of us, because of His saying ﴿do not take﴾, and the original state of a prohibition is prohibition.
* Among its benefits: this warning is not specific to rulers; rather every person is not permitted to take intimates other than his own kind. Even a single individual among us may not take intimates other than his own kind, meaning those who are not on his path or his method. If a Muslim man befriended a disbeliever and took him as an intimate to whom he confides matters, we would say: this is forbidden for him. This is supported by His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies, showing them affection, while they have disbelieved in what has come to you of the truth, having driven out the Messenger and yourselves...﴾ up to His saying: ﴿you confide to them with affection, and I am most knowing of what you conceal and what you declare﴾ [al-Mumtahanah 1].
* Among its benefits: avoiding evil intimates is among the requirements of faith, because to whom was the address directed?
* The students: To the believers.
* The Shaykh: To the believers.
* Among its benefits: taking evil intimates is among the deficiencies of faith, correct? Based on the principle we established earlier: whatever faith requires, its absence is a deficiency in faith.
Would it be among the nullifiers of faith; among the nullifiers, or among the deficiencies?
* The students: It may be.
* The Shaykh: It may be; perhaps it is among the nullifiers of faith. If he took such intimates in matters that take one out of Islam, that would be among the nullifiers of faith.
* Among the benefits of this verse: that those other than us will not spare us ruin. This is based on the sentence being what? Resumptive, giving the reason. I mentioned to you in the tafsir that some scholars said it is a qualifier of what precedes, and that if those other than us do not spare us ruin, then there is no harm in taking them as intimates. But the apparent meaning is the first: that the sentence is resumptive giving the reason, meaning that those other than us do not spare us ruin.
Let us give an example of believers taking intimates from among the disbelievers: the disbelievers, without doubt, do not fall short in seeking ruin for us. Now: "It is mentioned that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, was sent to by Abu Musa, wanting him to appoint a Christian scribe over the treasury, because he, that is this Christian scribe, was good at accounting. 'Umar wrote to him not to do so, and ordered him to dismiss him. He repeated the request a second time, asking him to keep him as scribe, and 'Umar wrote to him: The Christian has died, and peace."[[Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-Kubra (9/204) and Shu'ab al-Iman (8939) from the hadith of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, in a similar wording.]] What is the meaning?
* The students: (...).
* The Shaykh: Meaning, if he died, does this mean the treasury or its accounting would be halted? Suppose he died. As for entrusting him with the treasury of the Muslims after he has betrayed Allah and His Messenger, that is impossible.
By this we know that it is not permissible for our enemies, whether disbelievers or others, to be entrusted with the secrets of our affairs, for if we entrust them with the secrets of our affairs, we have taken them as intimates.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verse 118–122 (part 4 of 8):

* Among the benefits of this verse: it shows the care of Allah, glorified and exalted, for His believing servants, in that He warns them against matters that may remain hidden from them, namely taking bad intimates (bitanat, "inner circle").
* Among the benefits of this verse: our enemies wish for us what distresses us, as His saying shows: ﴿They love that you should suffer hardship﴾.
Here is a question: do they wish for what distresses us in worldly matters or in religious matters?
* The students: It includes both.
* The Shaykh: It includes both. They wish to destroy our armies, they wish to destroy our economy, they wish to destroy our knowledge, they wish to destroy our religion. The apparent view to me, and Allah knows best, is that the most important thing to them is the destruction of religion, because they know that if our religion grows strong, it becomes a destruction for them. But if our economy grows strong, it is not a destruction for them, because they are stronger than us economically, stronger than us militarily, and stronger than us in equipment. Rather, it is religion that destroys them. Therefore we say: everything that distresses us, in matters of religion and of worldly life, they seek. They wish to harass us in religion as much as they can, they wish to harass us in the economy as much as they can, they wish to harass us in weapons as much as they can. They send us weapons that have been left behind by time, weapons whose usefulness has ceased in the present age, and which, compared to the weapons of the present age, are like a knife or a club compared to weapons; that is, they have no benefit. But they do not care; they want to complete their economy and keep their factories running, and they do not mind whether we benefit or are harmed.
* Among the benefits of this verse: if a person reflects on the state of our enemies, he finds the breath of hatred coming from their mouths, as His saying shows: ﴿Hatred has already appeared from their mouths﴾ by what they say. Sometimes hatred also appears in their actions, through harassment; so sometimes they show it from their mouths, and sometimes from their deeds, through threats and the like, actual threats rather than verbal ones.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: what is in the hearts of the enemies of enmity, hatred, rancor, and fury is greater than what appears. This is a matter that none knows except Allah, glorified and exalted, and He is the One who informed us of it: ﴿And what their breasts conceal is greater﴾, greater than what their mouths reveal.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: it shows that intrinsic or acquired attributes vary in degree, as His saying shows: ﴿greater﴾. He spoke of hatred, and hatred is an intrinsic attribute of the heart that a person cannot know except through its effects. So here He made clear that hatred varies in degree, and likewise love varies in degree. There is no doubt about love; everyone accepts it, because it came in the Qur'an and the Sunnah: ﴿Say: If your fathers, your sons, your brothers...﴾ until His saying: ﴿more beloved to you than Allah and His Messenger﴾ [at-Tawbah 24]. The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: «None of you believes until I am more beloved to him than his child, his father, and all people»[[Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (15) and Muslim (44 / 70) from the hadith of Anas.]].
But does hatred also vary? We say: yes, even hatred varies; some of it is greater than other.
* Among the benefits of this verse: the favour of Allah, glorified and exalted, upon us in making His signs clear, as His saying shows: ﴿We have already made the signs clear to you﴾. The signs that Allah has made clear are of two kinds: cosmic signs and legislative signs. His making them clear is either through sensory observation or through rational reflection. Legislative signs are through rational reflection, and cosmic signs through sensory observation, which may also lead to rational reflection.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the more intellect a person has, or the stronger his intellect, the better he understands the signs of Allah. Is this derived? 
* A student: From His saying, exalted is He: ﴿if you use your reason﴾.
* The Shaykh: ﴿We have already made the signs clear to you, if you use your reason﴾. Therefore, the more intelligent a person is, the clearer and more evident the signs are to him.
Then Allah, exalted, said: ﴿Here you are﴾. Do you have questions? Good.
* A student: O Shaykh, is it better for a sick person to seek treatment, or to rely upon Allah and ask Allah to heal him?
* The Shaykh: This is a matter of difference among the scholars. Some said that leaving medicine is better; some said that medicine is better; and some said that if the benefit of medicine predominates, then it is better. The Prophet, peace be upon him, commanded treatment, and Allah commanded the preservation of the self. The most correct view is that if this medicine is known to cure this disease, then it is better to take it, because this is one of Allah's blessings, just as a person takes food and drink obligatorily. Likewise, if it is strongly believed that there is benefit, then it is better to seek treatment.
* The student: The hadith of the woman who used to uncover herself, and the Prophet ﷺ said: «If you are patient, you will have Paradise»[[Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (5652) and Muslim (2576 / 54) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]]. They prefer not to be treated and to remain upon..
* The Shaykh: Yes, that was a specific case. Perhaps the Messenger, peace be upon him, understood that her condition might change if she were completely cured, and for this reason, sometimes illness is better for a person in religious terms.
* A student: May Allah reward you well. We mentioned that it is not permissible to entrust our secrets to the enemies of Allah. But, may Allah reward you well, sometimes the country needs that, for example technology?
* The Shaykh: No, no. These are not secrets of industry. In industry they know more than us; that is, they are the ones who conceal their secrets from us, because they have access to things we do not. But our secrets are: what we intend to do in arranging our armies, in the interests of our peoples, in our own interests. If it is specific, that is the matter. As for industry, at present they are ahead, and perhaps a day will come when we are better than them. But at present, they are the ones who conceal their secrets from us.
* A student: The number of disbelievers at the battle of Uhud and Badr was three times the number of the Muslims. So was it not right for the Prophet ﷺ to seek help from someone, O Shaykh, from one of the tribes?
* The Shaykh: The disbelievers, you mean? And the question?
* The student: I mean, did the Prophet ﷺ not seek help from anyone?
* The Shaykh: Yes, he was not compelled to do so. The Messenger was not compelled to do this.
* The student: Their number was three times.
* The Shaykh: Yes, perhaps. ﴿How often has a small company overcome a large company by Allah's permission﴾ [al-Baqarah 249]. But if there is no suitable occasion at all, there is no suitable occasion. What do they do? If there is no suitable occasion, for example if we know with certainty that in confronting them, or in their aggression against us, we cannot defend ourselves at all; but three against nine, for example, there is possibility, there is possibility of victory.
* A student: O Shaykh, regarding hospitals for example, the director might be a Christian (...), meaning..
* The Shaykh: What do you mean?
* The student: (...) the secrets of the Muslims?
* The Shaykh: Hospitals.
* The student: The hospital director might be a Christian, for example.
* The Shaykh: And the hospital is Islamic or..?
* The student: It is in a Muslim country.
* The Shaykh: In a Muslim country, no, this is not permissible. It is not permissible to entrust the secrets of the Muslims to them, and women are uncovered, and one is not safe, because the Christians in the countries of Africa tell us that they give patients medicine, and the patient thinks it is a cure, but it is a medicine of sterility. They sterilize women, may Allah curse them, so I was told, and Allah knows best. But we cannot trust the disbelievers; how can we trust them?! They may give us injections that destroy us over the long term. Yes.
* A student: (...) Arab medicines or medicines, meaning (...)?
* The Shaykh: By Allah, if natural medicines are possible, they are better, because most modern medicines contain chemical substances that may be harmful to a person. Therefore, this medicine may harm one man while benefiting another, according to its ingredients.
* A student: (...) meaning, there was no occasion for the Prophet ﷺ to seek help from the polytheists. And it is established that he turned away a polytheist when he went out to fight with him. Also, in one of the battles the Romans were nine-tenths of the Muslims in the expedition, and he also did not seek help from polytheists.
* The Shaykh: Yes, correct.
* The student: How could it be nine-tenths..
* The Shaykh: Like what is nine-tenths? In which battle?
* The student: The Romans, in the battle of 'Ayn Jalut roughly, the battle of... the battle of Mu'tah, O Shaykh.
* The Shaykh: I understand that 'Ayn Jalut was not in the time of the Messenger, peace be upon him.
* The student: Mu'tah, O Shaykh, Mu'tah.
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* The student: And al-Qadisiyyah also.
* The Shaykh: Yes. First: he himself did not campaign at Mu'tah; he sent an army against the Romans, and it happened that the Romans gathered. The Muslims did not think they would gather in such numbers, and for this reason Khalid ibn al-Walid led them to the mountain, and Allah granted victory.
* The student: Therefore he did not seek help (...).
* The Shaykh: Come on, in the name of Allah, we place our trust in Allah.
* A student: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and prayers and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad and upon his family and all his companions. Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, said in Zad al-Ma'ad:
Chapter on the Great Battle of Badr.
When it was the month of Ramadan of that year, news reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ of the caravan coming to Quraysh from Syria, accompanied by Abu Sufyan. It was the caravan they had gone out to pursue when it left Makkah. They were about forty men, and it contained great wealth for Quraysh. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called people to go out to it, and ordered those who had mounts to ride out. He did not make a great preparation for it, because he went out quickly with three hundred and some men. There were no horses with them except two horses: a horse for al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam and a horse for al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad al-Kindi. They had seventy camels, and two or three men would take turns riding one camel. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, 'Ali, and Marthad ibn Abi Marthad al-Ghanawi took turns on one camel; Zayd ibn Harithah and his son and Kabshah, the freed slaves of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, took turns on one camel; Abu Bakr, 'Umar, and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf took turns on one camel. He appointed Ibn Umm Maktum over Madinah and over the prayer. When they reached al-Rawha, he sent back Abu Lubabah ibn 'Abd al-Mundhir and appointed him over Madinah.
* The Shaykh: I have here (bi-l-Rawha): al-Rawha, with a fatha on the ra' and a sukun on the waw: a village about forty miles from Madinah. Yes.
* * *
* The student: When they reached al-Rawha, he sent back Abu Lubabah ibn 'Abd al-Mundhir and appointed him over Madinah, and he gave the banner to Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr, and the single flag to 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, and the other, which belonged to the Ansar, to Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, and he placed Qays ibn Abi Sa'sa'ah over the rear guard, and he proceeded. When he drew near to al-Safra, he sent Basbas ibn 'Amr al-Juhani and 'Adi ibn Abi al-Zaghba' to Badr to spy out news of the caravan.
As for Abu Sufyan, news reached him of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ's departure and his intention toward it, so he hired Damdam ibn 'Amr al-Ghifari to go to Makkah as a crier seeking help from Quraysh, calling them to rush to their caravan to protect it from Muhammad and his companions. The cry reached the people of Makkah, and they rose quickly and turned out in full force. None of their nobles stayed behind except Abu Lahab, who sent in his place a man who owed him a debt. They mobilized those around them from the tribes of the Arabs, and no branch of Quraysh stayed behind except the Banu 'Adi, and none of them went out with them. They left their homes, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿boastfully and to be seen by people, and to bar from the way of Allah﴾ [al-Anfal 47]. They advanced, as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «With their sharpness and their iron; you oppose Him and oppose His Messenger»[[Zad al-Ma'ad (3 / 172). See al-Maghazi of al-Waqidi (1 / 95), and the Sirah of Ibn Hisham (1 / 621) with the wording: «O Allah, this is Quraysh, who have come with their arrogance and pride, opposing You and denying Your Messenger».]], and they came with determination, capable, with zeal, anger, and rage against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his companions, because of what they intended: to seize their caravan and kill those in it. They had struck 'Amr ibn al-Hadrami and the caravan that was with him the day before. Allah gathered them without prior appointment, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Even if you had made an appointment, you would have differed concerning the appointment; but that Allah might accomplish a matter that was to be done﴾ [al-Anfal 42].
"When the news of Quraysh's departure reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he consulted his companions. The Muhajirun spoke and spoke well. Then he consulted them a second time, and the Muhajirun spoke and spoke well. Then he consulted them a third time, and the Ansar understood that he meant them. Sa'd ibn Mu'adh hastened to say: 'O Messenger of Allah, it seems you are hinting at us.' He was indeed meaning them, because they had pledged to him to protect him against red and black in their homes. When he resolved to go out, he consulted them to know what they had. Sa'd said to him: 'Perhaps you fear that the Ansar regard it as a right upon them that they should not help you except in their own homes. I speak on behalf of the Ansar and answer for them. Go wherever you wish, join whomever you wish, sever whomever you wish, take from our wealth what you wish, give us what you wish, and what you take from us is dearer to us than what you leave. Whatever you command, our affair follows your command. By Allah, if you were to travel until you reached Barak al-Ghimad, we would travel with you. By Allah, if you were to lead us into this sea, we would plunge into it with you.'"
"Al-Miqdad said to him: 'We will not say to you what the people of Musa said to Musa: ﴿Go, you and your Lord, and fight; we will sit here﴾, but we will fight on your right and your left, before you and behind you.' The face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ shone"[[Related by al-Bukhari (3952) from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud in abridged form, and Ibn Jarir in his tafsir (11 / 41) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas in full.]].
* The Shaykh: First: the Muhajirun spoke and spoke well, even though they were going to fight their own people from Quraysh. Then the Ansar spoke, this wonderful speech that shows the strength of faith, the strength of their obedience to the command of the Prophet ﷺ, and their protection of him, and that whatever he does, they follow him, may Allah be pleased with them. This, my brothers, is what truly represents Islam and truly represents the Muslims: when Allah and His Messenger command a matter, they have no choice in their affair, and they follow the Messenger, peace be upon him, ransoming him with their selves, their wealth, and their children. Likewise, we must ransom, to the extent we can, the Book of our Lord and the Sunnah of our Prophet ﷺ, with our selves, our wealth, and our children, because these are the dearest things we have in this world. Therefore I want us to take a lesson from this and keep in mind what they said to him in that great statement: "If you were to lead us into this sea, we would plunge into it with you," even though plunging into the sea is destruction. But they would follow the Prophet ﷺ in everything. May Allah be pleased with them and content them. Yes.
* * *
* The student: «The face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ shone, and he was delighted by what he heard from his companions, and said: "Proceed and rejoice, for Allah has promised me one of the two groups, and I have seen the places where the people will fall."»[[Mentioned by Ibn Hisham in al-Sirah (1 / 615), and Ibn Jarir in his tafsir (11 / 41) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]]. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ proceeded toward Badr, and Abu Sufyan turned aside and reached..
* The Shaykh: "Proceed and rejoice": it is as if victory were in his hand, peace be upon him, as if he were holding it, because Allah, exalted, is the One who promised him: ﴿And when Allah promised you one of the two groups, that it would be yours﴾ [al-Anfal 7]. The first group was Abu Sufyan and the caravan; the second was Quraysh. ﴿And you wished that the one without thorns would be yours﴾ [al-Anfal 7], and the one without thorns was who? The caravan. ﴿And Allah wished to establish the truth by His words and cut off the last of the disbelievers﴾ [al-Anfal 7]. Praise be to Allah. Yes.
Then he says: "I have seen the places where the people will fall." This is also good news, so rejoice. Or "I have seen the places where the people will fall" is literal; that is, it is certain knowledge and the truth of certainty, because the vision of the Prophet ﷺ is revelation.
* * *

*Student:* The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set out for Badr. Abu Sufyan veered off and reached the coast, and when he saw that he had escaped and secured the caravan, he wrote to the Quraysh: "Turn back, for you only went out to protect your caravan." The news reached them while they were at al-Juhfah, and they resolved to return. Abu Jahl said: "By Allah, we will not turn back until we reach Badr, stay there, feed those who attend us from among the Arabs, and the Arabs will fear us after this." Al-Akhnas ibn Shariq advised them to return, but they disobeyed him, so he returned with the Banu Zuhrah, and no one from Zuhrah attended Badr. Afterwards the Banu Zuhrah took pride in al-Akhnas's opinion, and he remained among them obeyed and honoured. The Banu Hashim wished to return, but Abu Jahl pressed them hard and said: "This band shall not leave us until we return." So they went on. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) marched until he halted in the evening at the nearest of the waters of Badr and said: "Advise me on the place to stop." Al-Hubab ibn al-Mundhir said: "O Messenger of Allah, I know this place and its wells. If you see fit, let us go to a well we know, which has abundant sweet water, and let us stop there, get ahead of the people to it, and fill in the other water sources." [Cited by Ibn Hisham in al-Sirah (1/620).]

The polytheists advanced hastily, seeking water. The Prophet (ﷺ) sent ʿAli, Saʿd and al-Zubayr to Badr to seek news. They came back with two servants of the Quraysh, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was standing in prayer. His Companions asked them: "Who are you?" They said: "We are water-carriers for the Quraysh." The Companions disliked this and wished that they had been from Abu Sufyan's caravan. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) finished the prayer, he said to them: "Tell me where the Quraysh are." They said: "Behind this sand dune." He said: "How many are the people?" They said: "We do not know." He said: "How many camels do they slaughter each day?" They said: "One day ten, and one day nine." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The people are between nine hundred and a thousand." [Cited by al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il (965) from the hadith of Yazid ibn Ruman.] Then Allah sent down a single rain that night. It was a heavy downpour upon the polytheists which prevented them from advancing, while for the Muslims it was a light rain by which He purified them, removed from them the defilement of Satan, firmed the ground, hardened the sand, made their feet steady, prepared the place of encampment, and strengthened their hearts. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions reached the water first and camped beside it in the middle of the night. They made cisterns and filled in the other water sources. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions stopped at the cisterns. A shelter (ʿarish) was built for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), where he would stand on a hill overlooking the battlefield. He walked over the place of battle and began pointing with his hand: "This is the place where so-and-so will fall, and this is the place where so-and-so will fall, if Allah wills." [Muslim (2873/76) from the hadith of ʿUmar.]

*Student:* The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions stopped at the cisterns, and a shelter was built for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) where he would stand on a hill overlooking the battlefield. He walked over the place of battle and began pointing with his hand: "This is the place where so-and-so will fall, and this is the place where so-and-so will fall, and this is the place where so-and-so will fall, if Allah wills." [Muslim (2873/76) from the hadith of ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab.] None of them went beyond the place he had pointed to.

When the polytheists came into view and the two hosts faced each other, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Allah, these are the Quraysh; they have come with their arrogance and pride, they have come to oppose You and to deny Your Messenger." He stood, raised his hands, and sought victory from his Lord, saying: "O Allah, fulfil for me what You promised me. O Allah, I implore You by Your covenant and Your promise." Abu Bakr al-Siddiq came up behind him, embraced him, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, be of good cheer. By the One in whose hand is my soul, Allah will surely fulfil for you what He has promised you." [Al-Bukhari (2915) from the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbas, and Muslim (1763/58) from the hadith of ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab.]

The Muslims also sought help from Allah and implored Him, sincerely devoted themselves to Him, and humbled themselves before Him. So Allah revealed to His angels: ﴿I am with you; so strengthen those who believe. I will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve﴾ [al-Anfal 12]. And He revealed to His Messenger: ﴿I will reinforce you with a thousand angels following one another﴾ [al-Anfal 9]. It has been recited with a kasrah and with a fathah on the dal. It is said the meaning is that they follow you (ridf lakum), and it is said that some of them follow others in successive groups; they did not come all at once.

*Student:* Here it is mentioned that He reinforced them with a thousand, while in Surat Al ʿImran He says: ﴿When you said to the believers, "Is it not enough for you that your Lord reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?" (124) Yes, if you are steadfast and fear Allah, and they come upon you suddenly, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels, marked out﴾ [Al ʿImran 124–125]. How then can these be reconciled?

It is said that there is disagreement about this reinforcement of three thousand and the one of five thousand, and there are two opinions:

The first: it was on the day of Uhud, and it was a reinforcement conditional upon a stipulation. When the stipulation was not fulfilled, the reinforcement was not realised. This is the view of al-Dahhak and Muqatil, and one of the two reports from ʿIkrimah.

The second: it was on the day of Badr. This is the view of Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid and Qatadah, and the other report from ʿIkrimah. A group of exegetes chose it.

The argument of these people is that the context indicates this, for He, glorified is He, said: ﴿Allah had already given you victory at Badr when you were weak. So fear Allah that you may be grateful (123) when you said to the believers, "Is it not enough for you that your Lord reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down? Yes, if you are steadfast and fear Allah"﴾ [Al ʿImran 123–125], up to His saying: ﴿And Allah made it not but as good tidings for you and that your hearts might be assured thereby﴾ [Al ʿImran 126], meaning this reinforcement.

These people said: When they sought His help, He reinforced them with three thousand in full, then He reinforced them with five thousand in full when they were steadfast and feared Allah. This gradual approach and continued reinforcement had a better effect and was stronger for their souls and more comforting to them than if it had come all at once. It is like the successive sending and revelation of the Qur'an, one after another.

The first group said: The story is in the context of Uhud, and the mention of Badr was introduced as a digression within it. For He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And when you departed from your family in the morning to station the believers at their posts for battle; and Allah is Hearing, Knowing (121) when two parties among you were about to lose heart, though Allah was their ally; and upon Allah let the believers rely﴾ [Al ʿImran 121–122]. Then He said: ﴿Allah had already given you victory at Badr when you were weak, so fear Allah that you may be grateful﴾, reminding them of His favour upon them when He gave them victory at Badr while they were weak. Then He returned to the story of Uhud and reported the words of His Messenger to them: ﴿Is it not enough for you that your Lord reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?﴾ Then He promised them that if they were steadfast and feared Allah, He would reinforce them with five thousand. So this is from the words of the Messenger, whereas the reinforcement at Badr was from the words of the Exalted. The one at Badr was a thousand, and this one was five thousand. This one is conditional, while that one is unconditional. The story in Surat Al ʿImran is the story of Uhud in full and at length, and Badr is mentioned in it as a digression. The story in Surat al-Anfal is the story of Badr in full and at length. So the context of Al ʿImran differs from the context of al-Anfal.

What clarifies this is that His saying ﴿and they come upon you suddenly﴾ [Al ʿImran 125] has been said by Mujahid to refer to the day of Uhud. This requires that the reinforcement mentioned in it be (also at Uhud). So it is not correct to say that the reinforcement with this number was on the day of Badr, while their coming suddenly was on the day of Uhud. And Allah knows best.

*Section:* The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spent the night praying toward the trunk of a tree...

*Shaykh:* ...these two opinions, and he did not decide which of them is more correct. ﴿When you said to the believers, "Is it not enough for you that your Lord reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?" (124) Yes, if you are steadfast and fear Allah, and they come upon you suddenly, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels, marked out﴾. If we take the reinforcement of three thousand and five thousand to be at Uhud, there is no difficulty. If we take it to be at Badr, there is a difficulty, because Allah said about the story of Badr: ﴿When you sought help from your Lord, and He responded to you: "I will reinforce you with a thousand angels following one another." (9) And Allah made it not but as good tidings﴾ [al-Anfal 9–10]. But if we take it to be at Badr, the difficulty is: how can three thousand and five thousand and one thousand be reconciled?

Some answered that Allah reinforced them with a thousand, then with three thousand, then with five thousand. But if you reflect on the context, you find that it differs, and that the reinforcement at Uhud was only conditional: that they be steadfast and fear Allah, and steadfastness did not come from them. Rather, some of them disobeyed. It is known that what is conditional is not realised except when its condition is present. This supports that this conditional reinforcement was at Uhud, and since the condition was not fulfilled, what was conditioned was not fulfilled.

On this basis, the reinforcement at Badr was with a thousand angels following one another or being followed, and the reinforcement at Uhud was with three or five thousand, but conditioned upon a condition that was not fulfilled. And when the condition is not fulfilled, what was conditioned is not fulfilled. On this basis, the angels did not fight at Uhud, and the Muslims were not reinforced with any of them at Uhud. We will come, God willing, in the course of the tafsir, to what shows that the sounder view is this one.

\* \* \*

*Student:* Section: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spent the night praying toward the trunk of a tree there, and that was the night of Friday, the seventeenth of Ramadan in the second year. When morning came, the Quraysh advanced in their battalions and the two sides lined up. Hakim ibn Hizam and ʿUtbah ibn Rabiʿah went among the Quraysh asking them to return and not to fight. But Abu Jahl refused, and there took place between him and ʿUtbah a dispute which I will recall (ahfazahu).

*Shaykh:* He had some anger; it angered him. "Ahfazahu" means it angered him, meaning it stirred his anger, and it is a metaphor for provoking and enraging him.

*Student:* Abu Jahl ordered the brother of ʿAmr ibn al-Hadrami to demand vengeance for his brother ʿAmr. He uncovered his backside and cried out: "Wa-ʿamraah!" So the people became incited, and the war broke out. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) arranged the ranks, then returned to the shelter with Abu Bakr alone, while Saʿd ibn Muʿadh with a group of the Ansar stood at the door of the shelter guarding the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

ʿUtbah and Shaybah, the sons of Rabiʿah, and al-Walid ibn ʿUtbah came out seeking single combat. Three men from the Ansar came out against them: ʿAbdullah ibn Rawahah, ʿAwf and Muʿawwidh, the sons of ʿAfra. They asked them: "Who are you?" They said: "From the Ansar." They said: "You are noble equals, but we want our cousins." Then ʿAli, ʿUbaydah ibn al-Harith and Hamzah advanced against them. ʿAli killed his opponent al-Walid, Hamzah killed his opponent ʿUtbah, and it is said Shaybah. ʿUbaydah and his opponent exchanged two blows; then ʿAli and Hamzah attacked the opponent of ʿUbaydah and killed him. They carried ʿUbaydah, whose leg had been cut off, and he remained gravely wounded until he died at al-Safra.

ʿAli used to swear by Allah that this verse was revealed concerning them: ﴿These two adversaries dispute concerning their Lord﴾ [al-Hajj 19].

*Shaykh:* Now, the Quraysh had the zeal of the Jahiliyyah. What incited them to fight? It was the seeking of vengeance when this man shouted, uncovered his backside, and began wailing for his brother, saying: "Wa-ʿamraah!" Second, when three men from the Ansar came out against them, they refused to fight them out of pride and arrogance, saying: "You are noble equals, but we want our cousins," meaning the Quraysh.

Three came out against them: ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him; second, ʿUbaydah ibn al-Harith; and third, Hamzah ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib.

Single combat is practised in war because it strengthens the ranks: if their companion kills his opponent, this strengthens their spirits, and if it goes the other way, it weakens their spirits. For this reason the scholars said: if the enemy seeks single combat, it is not permitted for the commander of the army to allow anyone to engage in it unless he knows (that is, with a strong probability) that this challenger will overcome his opponent. But with mere possibility it is not permitted, because if he were defeated, it would break the hearts of the Muslims.

These three, may Allah be pleased with them, as you have seen: ʿAli killed his opponent al-Walid, Hamzah killed his opponent ʿUtbah or Shaybah, depending on the disagreement, and ʿUbaydah ibn al-Harith killed his opponent, either ʿUtbah or Shaybah. But ʿAli and Hamzah attacked when ʿUbaydah and his opponent had exchanged two blows, each striking the other, and these two had finished with their companions; so they turned against the companion of ʿUbaydah and killed him.

This is evidence for the permissibility of killing the opponent when such a single combat takes place. Do not say: why did they kill him when he had not come out against them? We say: because he had come out with his companion, and because his blood is forfeit, since he is a combatant.

\* \* \*

*Student:* Then the fighting grew fierce, the millstone of war turned, the battle intensified, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) began supplicating and entreating his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, until his cloak fell from his shoulders. Abu Bakr put it back on him and said: "Enough of your pleading with your Lord, for He will surely fulfil for you what He has promised you."

Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) dozed off briefly, and drowsiness overcame the people in the midst of battle. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) raised his head and said: "Be of good cheer, O Abu Bakr, this is Jibril, upon his front teeth is the dust of battle." [Dala'il al-Nubuwwah of al-Bayhaqi (979) from the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbas and Hakim ibn Hizam.]

Victory came; Allah sent down His hosts, strengthened His Messenger and the believers, and granted them the necks of the polytheists, taking them captive and killing them. They killed seventy of them and captured seventy.

Section: When they resolved to set out, they mentioned the enmity that existed between them and the Banu Kinanah. Iblis appeared to them in the form of Suraqah ibn Malik al-Mudlaji, who was one of the nobles of the Banu Kinanah, and said to them: "No one among the people will overcome you today, and I am a protector for you against Kinanah bringing you anything you dislike." So they set out, with the Devil as their protector, never leaving them. When they drew up for battle, and the enemy of Allah saw the hosts of Allah descending from the sky, he turned back and fled backwards. They said: "Where are you going, O Suraqah? Did you not say that you were a protector for us and would not leave us?" He said: "I see what you do not see. I fear Allah, and Allah is severe in punishment."

He spoke truly in saying "I see what you do not see," and he lied in saying "I fear Allah."

It has been said that his fear was for his own self, lest he perish with them. This is more evident.

*Shaykh:* Correct. The second is the more evident: the Devil's saying "I fear Allah" is not fear of worship; rather he feared destruction, not punishment. This is like His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Like the Devil when he says to man, "Disbelieve." But when he disbelieves, he says, "Indeed, I am free of you; indeed, I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds"﴾ [al-Hashr 16]. This is not fear of worship, for if he feared Allah with the fear of worship, he would have worshipped Him and not been arrogant toward His worship. Rather, this is the fear of destruction, as a man fears a wolf. This is not the fear of worship. So the correct view is what Ibn al-Qayyim said: that it is more evident.

\* \* \*

*Student:* When the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease saw the small number of Allah's party and the great number of its enemies, they thought that victory comes only through numbers, and they said: ﴿These people have been deluded by their religion﴾ [al-Anfal 49]. So He, glorified is He, informed that victory comes through reliance upon Him, not through multitude or number, and Allah is Mighty and cannot be overcome, Wise, who gives victory to whoever deserves it, even if he is weak. His might and wisdom necessitated the victory of the party that relies upon Him.

When the enemy drew near and the two sides faced each other...

*Shaykh:* (...) ﴿These people have been deluded by their religion﴾. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And whoever relies upon Allah, then indeed Allah is Mighty and Wise﴾ [al-Anfal 49]. But as we said before, reliance upon Allah includes taking the legally prescribed means that one has been commanded to take, so as to prepare the ground for victory. For whoever says "I rely upon Allah" and does not prepare anything with which to fight, his reliance is not valid. Rather, this is a kind of mockery and ridicule of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for Allah, exalted is He, has joined things to their causes. But when a person does what he is able to do while observing the legal command, and realises reliance, he will be given victory.

\* \* \*

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verse 118–122 (part 6 of 8):

* The student: When the enemy drew near and the two sides faced each other, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood among the people and exhorted them, reminding them of what they would gain through patience and steadfastness: swift victory and triumph, and Allah's reward in the Hereafter. He informed them that Allah had made Paradise obligatory for whoever is martyred in His cause. Then 'Umayr ibn al-Hammam stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, is it a Paradise whose breadth is the heavens and the earth?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Bakh, bakh (well done, well done), O Messenger of Allah!" He said: "What prompts you to say 'bakh, bakh'?" He said: "No, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah, only the hope of being among its people." He said: "Indeed, you are among its people." He said: "So he took out some dates from his quiver and began eating them. Then he said: 'If I live until I finish eating these dates of mine, it would be a long life.' He then threw away the dates he had with him, and fought until he was killed."[[Narrated by Muslim (1901 / 145) from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik.]] He was the first to be killed.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took a handful...
* The shaykh: This is faith. Look at this man, may Allah be pleased with him. When the Prophet ﷺ informed him that it is a Paradise whose breadth is the heavens and the earth, no doubt at all remained in him; he was certain of it as if he were seeing it with his own eyes. This is why, when he took out the dates and began eating, he said: "If I live until I finish eating these dates of mine, it would be a long life." Then he threw them away and fought until he was killed. Allahu Akbar, subhan Allah al-'Azim.
* * *
* The student: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took a handful of pebbles, threw them at the faces of the enemy, and there was not a single man among them whose eyes were not filled with it. They were occupied with the dust in their eyes, and the Muslims were occupied with killing them. Allah revealed concerning this throw to His Messenger: ﴿And you did not throw when you threw, but it was Allah who threw﴾ [al-Anfal 17].
Some people thought that the verse indicates the negation of the act from the servant and its affirmation to Allah, and that He alone is the true doer. This is an error on their part for several reasons, mentioned in other places. The meaning of the verse is that Allah, glorified is He...
* The shaykh: Who are these people?
* A student: The Ash'aris.
* The shaykh: No.
* The students: The Jabriyya.
* The shaykh: The Jabriyya, no. The Jabriyya are the opposite of this. The Jabriyya say that the human being is not the doer, that the human being is merely an instrument; so he is not the one who fasts, nor the one who pays zakat, nor the one who performs Hajj, nor the one who throws: ﴿And you did not throw when you threw, but it was Allah who threw﴾. Here He said: ﴿you did not throw when you threw﴾. How is this? Someone may say: this is contradictory: ﴿you did not throw when you threw﴾. Someone may say: rather, he threw when he threw. But we say: throwing is an act, and bringing the projectile to its target is something other than the act. For example, a person may throw and a strong wind may come and turn the arrow back, or he may throw while there is a wind behind the arrow carrying it further. So the throwing which is the act is from whom?
* The students: From the Messenger ﷺ.
* The shaykh: And the throwing which is the hitting is from Allah. So His saying ﴿but it was Allah who threw﴾ means He brought this dust to their eyes. Had the matter been by your own power, it would not have reached their eyes; it would have reached the nearest of them, if at all. But to reach the eyes of each one of them, when they were between nine hundred and a thousand, this was not within the capacity of the Prophet ﷺ.
* * *
* The student: The meaning of the verse is that Allah, glorified is He, affirmed for His Messenger the initiation of the throw, and negated from him the reaching of the projectile, which did not occur by his throw. Thus "throwing" refers to both launching and reaching; He affirmed launching for His Prophet and negated reaching from him.
At that time the angels were hastening the Muslims to kill their enemies. Ibn 'Abbas said: While a man from among the Muslims that day was pursuing a man from the polytheists ahead of him, he heard the sound of a whip above him and the voice of a rider above him saying: "Advance, Hayzum!" Then he looked at the polytheist ahead of him lying on his back; he looked at him and found that his nose had been slit and his face split like the mark of a whip, and all of it had turned green. The Ansari came and related this to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "You have spoken the truth; that was from the reinforcement of the third heaven."[[Narrated by Muslim (1763 / 58) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]]
Abu Dawud al-Mazini said: "Indeed..."
* The shaykh: In my copy it says: (Narrated by Muslim in al-Jihad). So the hadith is sound. Thus it becomes clear here that the angels fought alongside the Muslims, and this fighting is one whose effect is known, because the man heard the voice of the rider saying: "Advance, Hayzum!" This is the name of the angel who struck the polytheist, and the effect of the blow appeared on this polytheist.
* * *
* The student: Abu Dawud al-Mazini said: "Indeed, I was pursuing a man from the polytheists to strike him, when his head fell before my sword could reach him. I knew that someone other than me had killed him."
A man from the Ansar brought al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib as a captive. Al-'Abbas said: "By Allah, this man did not capture me. Rather, a man bald-headed, of the most handsome face, on a piebald horse, whom I do not see among the people, captured me." The Ansari said: "I captured him, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Be silent, for Allah has supported you with a noble angel."[[Narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad (948) from the hadith of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib.]]
Three from the Banu 'Abd al-Muttalib were taken captive: al-'Abbas, 'Aqil, and Nawfal ibn al-Harith.
Al-Tabarani mentioned in his al-Mu'jam al-Kabir, from Rifa'a ibn Rafi', who said: When Iblis saw what the angels were doing to the polytheists on the day of Badr, he feared that the killing would reach him. Al-Harith ibn Hisham clung to him, thinking he was Suraqa ibn Malik, so he pushed Al-Harith in the chest and threw him down, then fled until he threw himself into the sea, raised his hands, and said: "O Allah, I ask You for Your respite for me." And he feared that the killing would reach him. Then Abu Jahl ibn Hisham came forward and said: "O people, let not the desertion of Suraqa, who abandoned you, defeat you; for he was in agreement with Muhammad. And let not the killing of 'Utba, Shayba, and al-Walid frighten you; for they were hasty. By al-Lat and al-'Uzza, we will not return until we bind them with ropes, and I will not find any man among you who has killed a man of them, but seize them alive until we make them know the evil of their deeds."
Abu Jahl sought victory that day and said: "O Allah, whichever of us is more severed from kinship and brought what we do not know, destroy him this morning. O Allah, whichever of us is more beloved to You and more pleasing in Your sight, give him victory today." Then Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿If you seek a decision, then the decision has come to you. And if you desist, it is better for you. And if you return, We will return. And your company will not avail you at all, even if it is numerous, and that Allah is with the believers﴾ [al-Anfal 19].
When the Muslims set their hands upon the enemy, killing and capturing, Sa'd ibn Mu'adh was standing at the door of the tent in which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was, the 'Arish, girded with his sword among some of the Ansar. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw aversion in Sa'd ibn Mu'adh's face at what the people were doing. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "It seems you dislike what the people are doing?" He said: "Yes, by Allah. It was the first battle which Allah brought upon the polytheists, and inflicting heavy slaughter was dearer to me than sparing the men."[[See Tafsir al-Tabari (16320).]]
When the war cooled and the people turned fleeing, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said...
* The shaykh: This is what the Qur'an brought, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿It is not for a Prophet to have captives until he inflicts a great slaughter in the land. You desire the commodities of this world, but Allah desires the Hereafter﴾ [al-Anfal 67]. Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, as you know, was the chief of the Aws, may Allah be pleased with him; he wished that they be killed and not taken captive. But the opinion of the Prophet ﷺ and the opinion of Abu Bakr was that they should be taken captive and ransom taken from them without killing. The story is mentioned in Surat al-Anfal.
* * *
* The student: When the war cooled and the people turned fleeing, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Who will look for us what Abu Jahl did?" Ibn Mas'ud set out and found him struck by the two sons of 'Afra' until he was cooled, and he took hold of his beard and said: "Are you Abu Jahl?" He said: "To whom does the victory belong today?" He said: "To Allah and His Messenger. Has Allah disgraced you, O enemy of Allah?" He said: "Is there anything above a man whom his own people have killed?"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3962) and Muslim (1800 / 118), from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik.]] Then 'Abdullah killed him and came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "I have killed him." He said: "By Allah, the One besides whom there is no god?" He repeated it three times. **Section on the Battle of Uhud:**
When Allah killed the nobles of Quraysh at Badr, and they were struck by a calamity the like of which they had never suffered, and Abu Sufyan ibn Harb became their leader because their great men had perished, he came, as we have mentioned, to the outskirts of Madinah in the Ghazwat al-Sawiq. He did not attain what was in his heart, so he began to incite against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims and gathered the troops. He assembled nearly three thousand from Quraysh, their allies and the Ahabish, and they brought their women so that they would not flee and so that they would defend them. Then he advanced with them toward Madinah and camped near Mount Uhud, at a place called 'Aynayn, in Shawwal of the third year. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) consulted his Companions: should he go out to them or remain in Madinah? His opinion was that they should not go out of Madinah and should fortify themselves in it. If they entered it, the Muslims would fight them at the mouths of the alleys, and the women from the top of the houses. 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy agreed with this opinion, and it was the correct one. But a group of excellent Companions who had missed going out on the day of Badr hastened to him, advised him to go out, and insisted on it. 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy advised remaining in Madinah, and some of the Companions agreed with him. Those men insisted to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so he rose, entered his house, put on his armour and came out to them. Their resolve had weakened, and they said: "We forced the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to go out." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, if you wish to remain in Madinah, then do so." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It is not fitting for a Prophet, once he has put on his armour, to take it off until Allah judges between him and his enemy."[[Narrated by Ahmad (14787) and al-Darimi (2205) from the hadith of Jabir.]]

He went out with a thousand Companions and appointed Ibn Umm Maktum over Madinah with those who remained in it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had seen a dream while in Madinah: he saw that there was a notch in his sword, that cows were being slaughtered, and that he had put his hand into a strong coat of mail. He interpreted the notch in his sword as a man of his family who would be struck, the cow as a group of his companions who would be killed, and the coat of mail as Madinah.

He set out on Friday, and when he reached al-Shawt between Madinah and Uhud, 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy withdrew with about a third of the army and said: "You disobeyed me and listened to someone else." 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn Haram, the father of Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, followed them, rebuking them and urging them to return, saying: "Come, fight in the way of Allah or defend yourselves." They said: "If we knew that you would be fighting, we would not return." So he turned away from them and cursed them. Some of the Ansar asked the Messenger (ﷺ) to seek help from their Jewish allies, but he refused and took the path of Harrat Banu Harithah, and said: "Who is a man who will lead us against the people by a short route?"...

* **Shaykh:** Some of the Ansar asked him to seek help from their Jewish allies, and he refused. That was because there was no need for it. Moreover, the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) knew that the Jews were a treacherous people and that they could not be trusted. For this reason it is not permissible to seek help from a disbeliever when there is no need, and we do not seek help from one whom we cannot trust, whom we cannot trust with our secrets, or whom we fear will abandon us in battle. The point is that the Messenger (ﷺ) forbade these people to seek help from their Jewish allies for this reason.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verse 123–128 (part 1 of 5):

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And Allah had already given you victory at Badr when you were humble﴾ [Al 'Imran 123].

Allah, may He be glorified and exalted, says, clarifying His favour upon the Prophet (ﷺ) and his Companions, and indeed upon the whole Ummah; for the victory of the Prophet (ﷺ) and his Companions is a victory for the entire Ummah until the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, the victory of the earlier Messengers is a victory for the believers until the Day of Resurrection. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) fasted on 'Ashura', giving thanks to Allah for His favour in saving Musa and his people and destroying Fir'awn and his people, and he said to the Jews: "We have a greater right to Musa than you do" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3943) and Muslim (1130 / 127) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]].

He says, may He be glorified: ﴿And Allah had already given you victory at Badr﴾. This sentence is emphasised by three things: first, the implied oath; second, the lam; third, qad; for the sense is: "By Allah, Allah had certainly given you victory."

Victory (nasr) is that Allah makes dominance belong to these people over those people; whoever Allah grants dominance to, He has given them victory.

Victory has five causes (asbab, pl. of sabab, "cause"):

First: sincerity to Allah, based on the saying of Allah: ﴿Allah has promised those of you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will surely make them successors upon the earth, just as He made successors those before them, and that He will surely establish for them their religion which He has approved for them, and that He will surely replace their fear with security, [provided] they worship Me, not associating anything with Me﴾ [An-Nur 55].

Second: establishing the prayer; third: giving zakat; fourth: enjoining what is good; fifth: forbidding what is evil, based on the saying of Allah: ﴿Allah will surely support those who support Him. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might. [They are] those who, if We give them authority in the land, establish prayer and give zakat and enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong﴾ [Al-Hajj 40, 41]. So the causes are five:

* Student: Sincerity to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and its evidence: ﴿Allah has promised those of you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will surely make them successors upon the earth, just as He made successors those before them﴾ up to the end of the verse.
* Shaykh: We want the point, up to His saying:
* Student: ﴿they worship Me, not associating anything with Me﴾.
* Student: The second: establishing the prayer; the third: giving zakat; the fourth: enjoining what is good; and the fifth: forbidding what is evil, based on the saying of Allah: ﴿[They are] those who, if We give them authority in the land, establish prayer and give zakat and enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong﴾ [Al-Hajj 41].
* Shaykh: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And Allah had already given you victory at Badr﴾. The ba' here means "in" (fi), indicating place (zarfiyyah). There is nothing strange in ba' being used for place, as in the saying of the Most High: ﴿And indeed, you pass by them in the morning (137) and at night﴾ [As-Saffat 137, 138], meaning: "and at night." So His saying ﴿bi-Badrin﴾ means "at Badr."

Badr is a well-known place, and it is still known today between Makkah and Madinah.

The cause of this expedition was that when the Prophet (ﷺ) heard of a caravan of Quraysh coming from Syria, he called upon his Companions to go out to seize it, because the Quraysh had expelled the Prophet (ﷺ) and his Companions from their homes and their wealth, and they were at war against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ); so their wealth was lawful spoil for the Messenger (ﷺ). He called his Companions to go out against them, and they went out in a small number and with weak equipment: they went out with about three hundred and some men, on seventy camels and only two horses, which they took in turns: two men on a camel, and three on a camel, intending only the caravan. But Abu Sufyan, who was the commander of the caravan, took it along the coast, the seaside, and not by the well-known route, and he sent a shout to the people of Makkah calling for their help to protect their caravan. Then, when he escaped, he sent to them that he had escaped, that the caravan had got away; but they had already prepared to go out to fight the Prophet (ﷺ), so they went out with their chiefs and leaders in the manner that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, described: they went out ﴿insolent and showing off to the people and barring [others] from the way of Allah﴾ [Al-Anfal 47]. Shaytan said to them: ﴿No one among the people can overcome you today, and I am your protector﴾ [Al-Anfal 48], but he betrayed them: ﴿So when the two armies sighted each other, he turned back on his heels﴾ [Al-Anfal 48].

They went out numbering between one thousand and nine hundred, and they brought the women with them, so that their fighting would intensify out of fear for their women, since they had brought the women and placed them behind.

The battle took place between the Prophet (ﷺ) and these polytheists. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) and his Companions were few, few in number and in equipment, but Allah, may He be glorified and exalted, gave them victory; for this reason He said: ﴿And Allah had already given you victory at Badr when you were humble﴾. "Adhillah" is the plural of "dhalil," just as "a'izzah" is the plural of "'azeez."

Good. In what respect were they humble? In terms of number and in terms of equipment: three hundred and some men compared with nine hundred to one thousand, meaning less than a third; and what they had in terms of equipment was nothing: seventy camels and two horses. But Allah gave them victory, may He be glorified and exalted.

He said: ﴿So fear Allah that you may be grateful﴾ [Al 'Imran 123]. Fear Allah. The fa' here is for consequence (tafri'): meaning, in return for this victory which Allah granted you, it is obligatory upon you to fear Allah, and not to make victory a cause of arrogance and insolence, as those who have no faith do: when they triumph over their enemy, they make this a cause of arrogance and insolence, and they enter the town singing and merry. Yes, as was mentioned of some Arab broadcasters during their war with the Jews, who said: "Tomorrow Umm Kulthum will sing in Tel Aviv." Subhan Allah! Is this the reward for a blessing?!

As for the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him), he entered Makkah in the year of the Conquest, which is among the greatest victories, with his head bowed in submission to Allah, may He be glorified and exalted. This is how it should be: when a person is victorious, he should not make this victory a cause of arrogance and insolence, but should regard it as a blessing from Allah, may He be glorified and exalted, and fear Allah. For this reason He said: ﴿So fear Allah﴾.

Taqwa is taking a shield against the punishment of Allah. With what does the shield come? What protects you from the punishment of Allah? With what is the protection?

* Student: By doing what is commanded and avoiding what is forbidden.
* Shaykh: Yes, doing what is commanded and avoiding what is forbidden. So if someone asks us, "What is taqwa?" we say: it is doing what is commanded and abandoning what is forbidden, because when you do what is commanded and abandon what is forbidden, you have taken the protection from the punishment of Allah, may He be glorified and exalted.

His saying ﴿that you may be grateful﴾: here "la'alla" indicates purpose (ta'lil), meaning: in order that you may attain the gratitude of Allah. Taqwa is in reality gratitude to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; that is, so that you may attain gratitude, i.e., the rank of the grateful.

And how is gratitude for a blessing expressed?

* Student: Righteous deeds and avoiding evil deeds.
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: Ibn al-Qayyim said: gratitude to Allah consists of three matters: gratitude with the heart, with the tongue, and by spending it in obedience to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
* Shaykh: It is with the heart, the tongue and the limbs. Gratitude is with the heart, the tongue and the limbs.

As for gratitude of the heart, it is that you believe these blessings are from Allah, by His grace and favour, and that you have nothing from them except doing the means that were permitted to you; but their reality is from Allah, and you believe in that. Do not be like the one who said: ﴿I was only given it on account of knowledge I have﴾ [Al-Qasas 78]; rather say: "I was given it by the grace and mercy of Allah," even if it came through your own effort.

As for when it comes from the action of Allah, it is clear that every person attributes it to Allah; yet some people do not attribute to Allah what comes from His action: when rain falls they say, "We have been given rain by such-and-such a star." For this reason Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) led us in prayer at al-Hudaybiyah following a rain that had fallen during the night, i.e., after rain. When he finished, he turned to us and said: 'Do you know what your Lord said?' They said: 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' He said: 'He said: Some of My servants have awakened as believers in Me and some as disbelievers. As for the one who said: We have been given rain by the grace and mercy of Allah, that is a believer in Me and a disbeliever in the star; and as for the one who said: We have been given rain by such-and-such a star, that is a disbeliever in Me and a believer in the star.'" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (846) and Muslim (71 / 125) from the hadith of Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani.]]. So you must believe in your heart that the blessing is from whom?

* Student: From Allah, glorified be He.
* Shaykh: From Allah, and that whatever you do to bring about this blessing is only a means permitted by Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Second: the tongue, that you praise Allah with it, not that you say it boastfully over the servants of Allah, but that you praise Him by saying: "All praise is due to Allah who gave me such-and-such," based on the saying of Allah: ﴿And as for the blessing of your Lord, proclaim it﴾ [Ad-Duha 11].

Third: that you act with your limbs in obedience to Allah, especially regarding this particular blessing. It is not gratitude, if Allah provides you with wealth, to spend it on buying tobacco that you smoke, since this is using Allah's blessing to disobey Allah; nor to buy with it an instrument of amusement by which you divert yourself; this is not gratitude. Rather, gratitude is that you make the blessing a helper for you in obedience to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. One of the poets said:

The blessings have benefited you from me in three ways: ∗∗∗ my hand, my tongue, and the veiled conscience.

"My hand": these are the limbs; "my tongue": speech, praising Allah for the blessing; "the veiled conscience": belief.

﴿So fear Allah that you may be grateful﴾.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿[Remember] when you said to the believers, "Is it not sufficient for you that your Lord reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?" (124) Yes, if you are patient and fear Allah, and they come at you [in] their rage at this very moment, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels marked [for battle]﴾ [Al 'Imran 124, 125].

First: in this verse, His saying ﴿munzilin﴾ has a Sab'i reading: ﴿munazzilin﴾, with the zay doubled. And His saying ﴿musawwimin﴾ also has a Sab'i reading: ﴿musawwamin﴾, in the passive form.

He says: ﴿[Remember] when you said to the believers﴾. The address is to the Prophet (ﷺ), and this is among the addresses that are specific to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). It has already passed with us that the addresses directed at the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) are divided into three categories:

The first: what evidence shows is specific to him.

The second: what evidence shows is general to the Ummah.

The third: what no evidence indicates either way.

What evidence shows is specific to him is specific to him, such as this verse: ﴿[Remember] when you said to the believers, "Is it not sufficient for you"﴾; and ﴿And [remember] when you said to him on whom Allah bestowed favour and you bestowed favour﴾ [Al-Ahzab 37] — this is specific; ﴿Did We not expand for you your breast?﴾ [Ash-Sharh 1] — this is specific; ﴿O Messenger, convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 67] — this too is specific, although the Ummah is obligated to convey from another angle.

The second: what evidence shows is general, as in the saying of Allah: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them at their waiting period﴾ [At-Talaq 1]. This is clearly general, for He first addressed the Prophet (ﷺ) and then generalised the ruling by saying: ﴿when you divorce﴾.

The third: what no evidence indicates either way is general; it is general without doubt, its ruling is general. But is the address general in terms of its wording or not?

What appears is that it is general even in wording, because an address to the imam is an address to those who follow him.

For this reason, if a minister said, for example, to the commander: "Go to such-and-such a place," that would be an address to him and to those under his command.

Likewise, when the address is directed to the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) and no evidence shows that it is specific to him, it includes him and the whole Ummah.

Some scholars said: it does not include the Ummah; the address is to him alone, but the Ummah must follow.

If you reflect, you will find that the disagreement is close to a verbal one; for they agree that the ruling is general, but the question is whether the Ummah is included within this address or is addressed by another address, since it is commanded to follow. This is the point of disagreement, and in truth, when you examine it, you will find it is close to a verbal disagreement.

* Student: May Allah bless you, Shaykh. Some people overindulge in permissible things to the point that extravagance is feared for them; when you advise them, they say: ﴿And as for the blessing of your Lord, proclaim it﴾?
* Shaykh: Yes indeed. We say to him: ﴿And do not be wasteful; indeed, He does not like the wasteful﴾ [Al-An'am 141]. We are not saying to you, if you are wealthy: go out in the clothes of the poor, and eat only what the poor eat; we say: eat what the wealthy eat and wear what the wealthy wear, but do not be wasteful.
* Student: Two groups of Muslims fought, and one of them seized weapons from the other. Is it lawful for the other to take booty in the same way?
* Shaykh: I did not understand.
* Student: Are the wealth of the Muslims not to be taken as booty?
* Shaykh: Not to be taken as booty?
* Student: I mean during fighting.
* Shaykh: One looks at what the fighting is. If it is for partisanship or leadership, there is no doubt that it is oppression and not permissible, and neither property nor lives become lawful thereby. But if it is rebellion (baghy), then the rebel must be fought until he returns from his rebellion, as Allah the Mighty and Majestic said.
* Student: But is his weapon taken?
* Shaykh: Certainly his weapon is taken, because if we fight him and are able to take the weapon but do not take it, he will turn it against us. So we take it. Then whether it becomes booty or not depends on whom we are fighting: if the one we fight is a disbeliever, it is booty; if he is not a disbeliever, this is a matter for consideration.
* Student: Shaykh, may Allah be good to you: is the prohibition on giving disbelievers authority in general matters, or in particular matters?
* Shaykh: No, in leadership matters. As for non-leadership matters, such as construction or the like, like a worker with you, there is nothing wrong with that. Except in this Arabian Peninsula, it is not appropriate to bring disbelievers into it, because the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) commanded their expulsion from the Arabian Peninsula, and said: "Woe to the Arabs from an evil that has drawn near; today an opening the size of this has been made in the barrier of Gog and Magog," [and he made a circle with his thumb and forefinger]. Zaynab said: "O Messenger of Allah, will we be destroyed while the righteous are among us?" He said: "Yes, when wickedness increases" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3346) and Muslim (2880 / 1) from the hadith of Zaynab bint Jahsh.]]. Here "khabath" (wickedness) includes personal wickedness and practical wickedness. If wickedness increases among Muslims, Allah is near to destroying them; and if wickedness increases among non-Muslim individuals, that is, disbelievers come into the land, Allah is likewise near to seizing them.
* Student: Are there matters that we do not have knowledge or experience in, while they have experience, so we must give them some leadership so that we may learn from them or they may assist us in something?
* Shaykh: These matters may be incidental and not permanent. Therefore we are not forbidden to learn from them what they teach us, or for example to take from their experience; there is benefit for us in this.
* Student: Is it permissible, Shaykh, to appoint some people of misguided sects who harbour hatred against Ahl al-Sunnah wal-Jama'ah, such as the Rafidah and others, to leadership positions?
* Shaykh: ﴿O you who believe, do not take as intimates other than your own, who will not spare you [from] ruin﴾ [Al 'Imran 118]. "Min dunikum" means other than you. Every person whom we know does not advise us sincerely, it is not permissible for us to appoint him.

* Student: The words of Allah the Exalted, ﴿And Allah will surely help those who help Him﴾ [al-Hajj 40], and His words ﴿those who, if We establish them in the land﴾ [al-Hajj 41]. Some people say, meaning: the apparent sense of the verse is that if We establish them in the land, they establish prayer. Meaning, after being empowered, they establish prayer?

* Shaykh: Yes, this is among the causes of victory, without doubt. When Allah knows that these people intend, if they are empowered in the land, to establish prayer, this is one of the causes of victory.
