* Student: A cause object (mafʿūl li-ajlihi), or a second object of (ja'ala). If (ja'ala) means (ṣayyara, "made into"), it is a second object. If it does not mean (ṣayyara), it is a cause object.

* Shaykh: Is it not valid as an exception?

* Student: No.

* Shaykh: Why?

* Student: The excepted-from is not mentioned, because it is a restrictive particle.

* Shaykh: Because the governing word has not completed its complement.

He said: ﴿and so that your hearts would be at rest through it﴾ [Ali ʿImran 126]. ﴿wa-li-taṭma'inna qulūbukum bihi﴾: tranquility (iṭmi'nān) means settling and the absence of anxiety. There is no doubt that the tranquility of the heart brings rest to the soul, opens the door to optimism and hope, and provides steadfastness in the matter. Contrast this with a person whose heart is not at rest, for you find him always in anxiety and constriction. But when his heart is at rest, this helps him to endure, to stand firm, and to be patient. For this reason He said: ﴿and so that your hearts would be at rest through it﴾. In the chapter of al-Anfal the context differs. There He said: ﴿Allah did not make it except as good news, and so that your hearts would be at rest through it﴾ [al-Anfal 10], omitting the words "for you," and placing the prepositional phrase before the subject: ﴿and so that your hearts would be at rest through it﴾ in Surat al-Anfal. But here it is ﴿and so that your hearts would be at rest through it﴾. This supports that the two verses are not about the battle of Badr. Rather, the verse of al-Anfal is about the battle of Badr, and this one is about the battle of Uhud, and the reinforcement did not occur, because of the unmet condition, as you have understood.

Then He said: ﴿Victory is only from Allah﴾. This means that even if you were reinforced with three thousand or five thousand angels, victory is not due to them. Rather, victory is from Allah, who prepares the causes of victory. So do not rely on anyone other than Allah the Exalted, even on what Allah has made a cause of victory.

He said: ﴿only from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise﴾. "Al-ʿAzīz" means: the one possessing might. The might of Allah the Exalted has three kinds: might of rank, might of subjugation, and might of inaccessibility. Might of rank means nobility, lordship and excellence, such as when you say: "This thing is rare in its existence," meaning it is unique in its complete attributes compared to others. Might of subjugation means dominance, meaning He is overpowering, and from it is His saying: ﴿He said, "Give it to me, and he has overpowered me in speech"﴾ [Sad 23], meaning he overcame me in it. Allah the Exalted has dominance, as He said: ﴿They say﴾, meaning the hypocrites: ﴿If we return to Medina, the mightier will surely expel the meaner from it﴾ [al-Munafiqun 8], and Allah affirmed for them that the mightier expels the meaner. But to whom does might belong?

* Students: Might belongs to Allah, and to His Messenger.

* Shaykh: ﴿But might belongs to Allah, to His Messenger, and to the believers, but the hypocrites do not know﴾ [al-Munafiqun 8]. So, might of subjugation means dominance, that He is dominant, dominant over everything. And from pre-Islamic poetry:

Where is the escape, when the Pursuing God is seeking you? / The cut-nosed one is overcome; he is not the victor.

He says: the third: might of inaccessibility, meaning that harm or deficiency cannot reach Him, glorified and exalted is He. It is derived from their saying (ʿarḍ ʿazāz), meaning a hard, strong land on which the tools do not leave an impression. So the might which Allah is described by has three kinds. Mention them.

* Student: Might of rank, might of subjugation, and might of inaccessibility.

* Shaykh: Yes. And what is the meaning? What is the meaning of might of rank?

* Student: The might of nobility and status.

* Shaykh: Yes, and lordship. Good. And might of subjugation?

* Student: Meaning the might of dominance.

* Shaykh: The might of dominance: meaning He is dominant, nothing overcomes Him. The evidence that might can mean dominance?

* Student: Yes, the saying of Allah the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿and he has overpowered me in speech﴾, meaning dominance.

* Shaykh: In the sense of dominance. The third: might of inaccessibility, what is its meaning?

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verses 123–128 (part 3 of 5):**

* Student: That Allah, glory be to Him, is exempt from being touched by any evil or deficiency.
* The Shaykh: Or deficiency.
* The Student: From this is their saying: "land 'azaz" (ʿazāz), meaning firm, hard.
* The Shaykh: Yes. As for His words ﴿the All-Wise﴾, al-Hakim is derived from al-hukm (judgment) and al-ihkam (perfecting). Hukm means decision, and ihkam means perfection. We know that Allah's judgment is divided into two kinds: a kawni (cosmic, existential) judgment, which whatever it governs cannot fail to occur, and a shar'i (legislative) judgment, which may be disobeyed. The kawni judgment never fails. From it is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So I will not leave this land until my father permits me or Allah decides for me﴾ [Yusuf 80]. Is this decision a legislative judgment or a cosmic judgment?
* Student: Cosmic.
* The Shaykh: A cosmic judgment. As for the legislative judgment, an example is His saying in Surah al-Mumtahanah: ﴿That is the judgment of Allah; He judges between you, and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾ [al-Mumtahanah 10]. From it is also His saying: ﴿Do they seek the judgment of the Jahiliyyah? And who is better than Allah in judgment for a people who are certain?﴾ [al-Ma'idah 50].
So judgment is divided into?
* Students: Two kinds.
* The Shaykh: Cosmic and legislative. Moreover, there is wisdom (hikmah) in each of them. That is, every judgment, whether cosmic or legislative, is accompanied by wisdom, because we have said that the word is derived from judgment and perfecting. So the cosmic judgment must have a wisdom, and the legislative judgment must have a wisdom. Then wisdom may mean that the occurrence of a thing in this particular form is wise, and its purpose is also wise. So wisdom is in the form of the thing, and a second wisdom is in its purpose. For instance, the prayers being in this particular form is a wisdom related to the form of the act, and their purpose is a wisdom related to the intended aim of the act. So when we say that wisdom is either in the cosmic or the legislative judgment, and either in the form of the thing or in its end, we have many divisions, and all of them are included in His saying: ﴿the All-Wise﴾.

Joining "might" (al-ʿizzah) with "wisdom" (al-hikmah) conveys a third meaning, distinct from the meaning conveyed by "might" alone or "wisdom" alone. This is because the mighty may be overcome by his might so that he behaves with recklessness and foolishness, as Allah says: ﴿And when it is said to him, "Fear Allah," pride takes him to sin﴾ [al-Baqarah 206]. But the might of Allah, mighty and majestic is He, does not depart from wisdom, although He possesses absolute might. This might does not depart from wisdom. He does nothing in a manner of foolishness; He does it in a manner of wisdom.

Then Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿That He might cut off a part of those who disbelieve﴾.

Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿And Allah had already given you victory at Badr when you were humiliated﴾ and so on to the end [Al 'Imran 123].

* In this verse: Allah, glory be to Him, bestows favor upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his companions by granting them victory at Badr. Their victory is a victory for the ummah until the Day of Resurrection.
* Among the benefits of the verse: a person cannot achieve victory without the help of Allah. If the soldiers of Allah, who are the greatest soldiers on the face of the earth, namely the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and those with him, did not win by themselves but by the victory of Allah, then whoever is other than them is even more so.
* A branch of this benefit: we do not attribute victory to anyone but Allah, the Exalted. We do not attribute victory to our strength or to the strength of anyone supporting us. We attribute victory to Allah alone, and we consider these material things through which victory is achieved to be means (asbab) whose results may fail to follow, because victory comes from Allah alone.
* Among the benefits of this verse: the more a person is humble before Allah, the closer he is to Allah's victory, and the more a person is self-sufficient without Allah, the further he is from victory. This is due to His saying: ﴿while you were humiliated﴾. When a person sees himself as mighty, exalts himself and becomes proud, he is forsaken. Allah says: ﴿Indeed, man transgresses, when he sees himself self-sufficient﴾ [al-'Alaq 6–7].
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: victory does not come through the multitude of numbers or the strength of equipment, but it is from Allah, glory be to Him. Yet the multitude of numbers and the strength of equipment are things Allah commanded us to have, and He made them a means to victory. As Allah says: ﴿And prepare against them whatever you are able of power and of steeds of war by which you may frighten the enemy of Allah and your enemy and others besides them whom you do not know. Allah knows them﴾ [al-Anfal 60]. Therefore, the rulers of the Islamic ummah must prepare the greatest weapon that devastates the enemies, so that if they need it they can attack the enemy, or defend if anyone aggresses against them. As for conventional weapons, which in our present time are like donkeys compared to horses in the past, these are not sufficient, except when a person is unable, in which case he is excused. But if he is able, it is obligatory for him to equip himself with all the strength he can, because the enemies of Islam lie in wait for it and want to eliminate the Muslims by every means. If we do not have weapons to humiliate and disgrace them with, then we have not fulfilled what Allah has obligated us: ﴿And prepare against them whatever you are able of power﴾. Here He says: ﴿So fear Allah﴾.
* From its benefits: whoever Allah has bestowed a blessing upon, that blessing should be a reason for fearing Allah. Victory is a cause of piety, humility before Allah, submission to Him, and prostration before Him, just as the Prophet ﷺ did when he conquered Makkah: he entered with his head bowed, reciting the Book of Allah, mighty and majestic. This is contrary to what many people today, or some people, do when they achieve victory: they make it a cause of arrogance, excess, entertainment, songs, and other sins. Indeed, after victory they may become more corrupt than before the war. This contradicts what Allah has commanded, because Allah said: ﴿And Allah had already given you victory﴾ ﴿So fear Allah﴾. He commanded piety after victory, lest a person lift his nose in pride and exalt himself over his Lord because of his triumph, and so return to the exultation, excess, and insolence he was in before.
* Among the benefits of this verse: fearing Allah, the Exalted, is a form of gratitude. Fearing Allah is gratitude to Allah, due to His saying: ﴿so that you may be grateful﴾. There is no doubt that piety is gratitude; indeed, it is gratitude in reality, because piety (taqwa) is taking a shield against the punishment of Allah by doing His commands and avoiding His prohibitions. Gratitude (shukr) is performing the obedience of the Bestower with the heart, the tongue, and the limbs. Do you understand? What is gratitude?
* Student: It is performing the obedience of Allah with the heart, the tongue, and the limbs.
* The Shaykh: Yes, performing the obedience of the Bestower with the heart, the tongue, and the limbs.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿When you said to the believers, "Is it not enough for you that your Lord should aid you with three thousand angels sent down?"﴾ and so on to the end [Al 'Imran 124].

* Among its benefits: the Prophet's ﷺ manner in dealing with his companions, by instilling hope in their hearts at times of severe crisis. This is the sound method, because when you give people hope, they become energetic and forget the worry and distress they are in. But some people do the opposite: you find them opening to people the door of pessimism, terrifying news, and frightening things. Whenever we say that these terrifying things have ended, something even more frightening comes. This is without doubt contrary to the legislative policy (siyasah shar'iyyah), and even contrary to reason. Matters that necessity requires and that cause fear are unavoidable. But as for what there is no need or necessity for, open the door of hope to people. The Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, when they feared that the polytheists would reinforce one another, said to them this statement: ﴿Is it not enough for you that your Lord should aid you with three thousand angels sent down?﴾ [Al 'Imran 124]. When he was informed that the Banu Qurayzah had broken the covenant during the year of al-Ahzab, he sent someone to verify the news and said to the messengers: "If you come, speak to me in code (fa-ilhanu li lahnan)," "Speak to me in code." What does "yulhinu" mean? It means inform me of this by a sign, which we now call a code (shifrah), a special code he informed them with. Because when they came and found that the Jews had broken the covenant, then if the Messenger announced it openly before the people, panic and fear would overtake them. So he said: "Speak to me in code." When they returned to the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, and informed him that the Banu Qurayzah had broken the covenant, but not in explicit words, rather in the code he had guided them to, he said: "Rejoice, rejoice."[[Recorded by al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (1373) from the hadith of 'Asim ibn 'Umar ibn Qatadah.]] If he had been like some of our leaders, one would expect him to say: "By Allah, this is a calamity; a new enemy has come upon us," and then fill the hearts with terror. But the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Rejoice." When they were digging the trench and encountered a hard rock (kudyah), a rock too hard for them, they came to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him. He came, descended into the trench, took a pickaxe, and struck it a blow, from which a spark flashed. In the first strike he said: "The palaces of Kisra or Caesar were illuminated by it." In the second: "The palaces of Kisra or Caesar." In the third: "The palaces of Yemen," Sana'a. Then he said: "Rejoice."[[Recorded by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (20/223) from the hadith of 'Awf al-Muzani, and Ahmad in al-Musnad (18694) from the hadith of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib with nearly this wording. Its origin is in al-Bukhari (4101) from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah.]] Yet Allah said of them in that situation: ﴿When they came at you from above you and from below you, and when eyes shifted and hearts reached the throats, and you assumed about Allah assumptions﴾ [al-Ahzab 10]. Now, for example, in these events we find that the tyrant has become unstable and his defects have appeared, and there is no doubt about this. Then some people come and say: "No, he has a great strength stored up, which he will unleash at the end." Allahu akbar! Allah, glory be to Him, has already given you good news indicating that Allah will suffice the Muslims against his evil, and then you come and terrify the people, saying: "No, he has, he has a strength, but he will release it at the end of the matter." Who told you this? If that is a possibility, the first is more probable. There is no doubt that it is more probable, because no person can ever pretend to be defeated before his enemy. For this reason, we should open the door of hope and that what is decreed will happen to people, whether we open the door of hope that energizes them, brings joy to them, and makes them forget their sorrows, or we open upon them the door of terror and constriction, so that a person's intestines dry up in his belly. This is not correct. You open the door of hope, and what Allah wills will happen. However, I say: opening the door of hope is only appropriate when the heart is attached to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and one's resources are cut off except from Allah, glory be to Him.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: affirming the special lordship (rububiyyah khassah), due to His saying: ﴿that your Lord should aid you﴾.
Lordship is of two kinds: general and specific. In His saying: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Fatihah 2], this is general. In His saying here: ﴿your Lord﴾, it is specific. Both kinds are combined in His saying about the magicians of Pharaoh whom Allah blessed with faith: ﴿They said, "We have believed in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Musa and Harun"﴾ [al-A'raf 121–122]. The first is general, the second is specific.
* Student: There is a report in some hadiths that some angels fought alongside the Muslims at the Battle of Uhud. How (...)?
* The Shaykh: No, but that is if those hadiths are authentic. Some scholars have declared them weak and said: the angels only fought at Badr, and at Uhud they came only to strengthen the Muslims. But if they are authentic, then that was a special case, when the companions abandoned the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and only a small group remained with him.
* Student: Shaykh, some people in current events are truly not optimistic. I said to one of them: "Be optimistic, my brother, and think well [of Allah]." He said: "By Allah, our situation is not pleasing." I do not know what he means.
* The Shaykh: Yes, there is no doubt that our situation is weak, but our hope in Allah and His pardon is greater than our bad opinion of ourselves.
* Student: Shaykh, what is the meaning of His words: ﴿from their immediate rush﴾?
* The Shaykh: Have we not explained it?
* Student: We have explained it, Shaykh.
* The Shaykh: ﴿from their immediate rush﴾ means at the present time, that is, from the direction in which they came at you. When they departed, the disbelievers had defeated the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, and his companions, and what happened to them happened, and then they departed. Allah, mighty and majestic, said: if they come at you in this very rush and return against you, Allah will reinforce you.
* Student: Shaykh, ﴿and that their hearts may be assured﴾ is conjoined with what?
* The Shaykh: What do you say?
* Students: We did not hear.
* Student: The question, Shaykh.
* The Shaykh: He asks: ﴿and that their hearts may be assured﴾ is conjoined with what?
* Student: With ﴿glad tidings﴾, Shaykh.
* The Shaykh: With ﴿glad tidings﴾.
* The Student: If it is conjoined with ﴿glad tidings﴾, then (...) it is a direct object.
* The Shaykh: And this supports that it is a purpose clause (maf'ul min ajlih).
* The Student: If it is a direct object?
* The Shaykh: And if it is a direct object, the verb is to be assumed.
* The Student: The verb is assumed.
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed. That is: "And Allah informed you so that your hearts might be assured by it."
* The Student: Shaykh, may I ask a second question?
* The Shaykh: You may! On condition that the brothers agree. Do you agree?
* The Student: Allah, blessed and exalted, sent three thousand angels with the companions, although one angel, Jibril, would suffice for all of (...)?
* The Shaykh: Yes, no, say: a thousand. Because we mentioned that the reinforcement did not occur, since the condition was not fulfilled according to the correct opinion. But a thousand angels at Badr; one angel is undoubtedly sufficient, and a single word from Allah suffices instead of the angels and humans as well. Is that not so?
* Students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: For this reason Allah said: ﴿And if Allah had willed, He would have taken vengeance upon them, but [He ordained fighting] to test some of you by means of others. And those who are killed in the cause of Allah — He will never waste their deeds. He will guide them and amend their condition. And He will admit them into Paradise, which He has made known to them﴾ [Muhammad 4–6]. This benefit is lost. Is it clear?
* Student: Regarding the conditions of victory: if they are fulfilled, victory is achieved. But does the descent of angels continue to our day? Do angels descend?
* The Shaykh: Perhaps, yes. Perhaps angels descend to strengthen the believers, and if the fighting is truly jihad in the cause of Allah, they may fight, because Allah, the Exalted, supports His religion.
* Student: Shaykh, could the adverbial phrase (idh) be linked to (udhkur) or (tadhakkar)?
* The Shaykh: Which one?
* Student: ﴿When you said to the believers﴾. Is it appropriate?
* The Shaykh: It is appropriate if there is no other option, because the original principle is that it is not assumed. Assumption requires deletion, and the original principle is non-deletion. So if it can be linked to something existing, it is not assumed. But if it cannot, it is assumed.
* Student: Shaykh, what is the more correct opinion regarding the pronoun in His words: ﴿and Allah did not make it﴾?
* The Shaykh: It refers to the statement of the Messenger. This is the correct opinion, although most exegetes say it refers to Allah's report. But the closer view is that it refers to the statement of the Messenger and his promise to them.
* * *
* Student: ﴿or He will turn to them in forgiveness or punish them, for indeed, they are wrongdoers. And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [Al 'Imran 128–129].
* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿When you said to the believers, "Is it not enough for you that your Lord should aid you with three thousand angels sent down?"﴾ [Al 'Imran 124].
We have taken up: among the benefits of this verse: it is appropriate to convey glad tidings to the fighters, as the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, did.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verses 123–128 (part 4 of 5):

* Among its benefits also: the specific lordship (al-rububiyya al-khassa) in His saying: ﴿that your Lord would reinforce you﴾. The specific lordship entails, along with the general meaning, which is management and sovereignty, the granting of steadfastness, assistance, and restraining from evils and similar things, because it is specific.
* Among its benefits: that the angels are bodies that can be counted by number, due to His saying: ﴿with three thousand angels﴾.
* Among its benefits also: that the abode of the angels is the heavens, and this is the original state, due to His saying: ﴿sent down﴾. Descent only occurs from above to below, so when these angels are described as "sent down," this indicates that their place is in the heavens. This is the original state, but they descend to the earth frequently according to the command of Allah, the Exalted.
* Among its benefits: the angels did not fight, without doubt. But were they reinforced? We have mentioned that the matter has two opinions among the scholars. If it refers to Badr, then they were reinforced; and if it refers to Uhud, then they were not reinforced, because that was conditioned upon patience and piety.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Yes, if you are patient and fear Allah﴾, to the end.

* Among the benefits of this verse: patience and piety are two causes of victory, due to His saying: ﴿if you are patient and fear Allah﴾, meaning: be patient in obeying the commands and avoid the prohibitions. Its explanation has already been mentioned.
* Among its benefits also: Allah, the Exalted, increased them beyond what the Messenger (ﷺ) had given them good news of. He increased them by two thousand if they were patient and feared Allah.
* Among its benefits: these angels by whom they would be reinforced, if the believers were patient and feared Allah, were ﴿marked﴾ or ﴿distinguished﴾ according to the two readings. As for ﴿marked﴾ (musawwamin), it means they had a sign specific to them, as previously mentioned. As for ﴿distinguished﴾ (musawwamin), it means they made a sign for themselves, on what had been granted to them of horses, according to what the narrations have reported.
* Among the benefits of this verse and the one before it: it is one of Allah's blessings upon the servant that the one under whose guardianship the angels are placed, because the angels make a person steadfast upon goodness, unlike the devils, who make a person steadfast upon evil.

From this benefit it follows that when the angels refrain from entering a house, this is a kind of punishment, as in the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Indeed, the angels do not enter a house in which there is an image."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (3224) from the hadith of 'Aisha, and Muslim (2106/85) from the hadith of Abu Talha Zayd ibn Sahl.]]

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And Allah did not make it except as good news for you﴾, to the end.

* Among its benefits also: whether this promise from Allah was good news or from the Messenger is a matter of difference among the scholars, and the difference on this is minor; the matter is simple, whether what He made, meaning the words of the Messenger, or what He made, meaning the words of Allah to them, ﴿except as good news﴾.
* Among its benefits: that supporting a person with what helps him is a cause of his joy and good tidings, due to His saying: ﴿And Allah did not make it except as good news﴾, and a cause of the tranquility of his heart, his steadfastness, and his calm, due to His saying: ﴿and that your hearts may be reassured thereby﴾.
* Among its benefits: however great the means may be, if Allah does not support a person with victory, he will never be victorious, due to His saying after mentioning this reinforcement: ﴿And victory is only from Allah﴾.
* Among its benefits: it is obligatory for a person, while taking the means, to rely upon his Lord and to hope for victory from Him, the Exalted.
* Among its benefits: victory is part of the requirement of His name, the Mighty, the Wise.
* Among its benefits: Allah will not grant victory except to whom wisdom requires that He grant victory, due to His saying: ﴿the Mighty, the Wise﴾. It is not objected to this that Allah, the Exalted, granted the polytheists victory in the Battle of Uhud, because we say: this victory contained a great benefit for the Muslims, so it is wisdom. The victory of the polytheists at Uhud is undoubtedly a wisdom from which great benefits follow, which will be mentioned, if Allah wills, in the verses.

Among them is His saying: ﴿that He might cut off a portion of those who disbelieved﴾. The lam here indicates purpose. The subject of ﴿cut off﴾ refers to Allah, the Exalted, and what is meant by "cutting off" here is destruction, meaning: that He may destroy a portion. The prepositional phrase (the lam) is attached either to His saying: ﴿And Allah had already given you victory at Badr﴾, but this is weak because it is distant, meaning that many verses separate the governing element from what it governs, and there is no parallel to this. Or it is attached to an omitted element whose estimated meaning is: "He did that in order to cut off a portion," and this view is more correct, so the lam is attached to a verb that is omitted and estimated in an appropriate manner.

His saying: ﴿that He might cut off a portion of those who disbelieved﴾ means: that He might destroy them. But is this when they are victorious over the Muslims, or when the Muslims are victorious over them, or both?

The correct view is that it applies to both situations. If the Muslims are victorious and defeat them, then a portion of them has been destroyed. If they are victorious over the Muslims, then pride and the intoxication of victory will overtake them, and then they will repeat the attack a second time, and at that point they will be finished. So both outcomes occur, whether they overcome or are overcome.

As for His saying: ﴿a portion of those who disbelieved﴾, "a portion" (tarf) of a thing is its extremity, either from below or from above. So is what is meant by "a portion" here the part that is nearest to the Muslims?

The answer: yes, what is meant is the part nearest to the Muslims, because the Muslims are obligated to fight those disbelievers who are near them, until they conquer the lands of the disbelievers city by city: ﴿O you who have believed, fight those of the disbelievers who are near to you, and let them find in you harshness﴾ [at-Tawba 123]. This is both a legislated sunnah of Allah and also in accordance with human nature, because it is not wisdom to go far away to fight an enemy while leaving the near one, since in such a case the near enemy may become an ambush, meaning that it could cut you off from returning to your land.

His saying: ﴿or He will subdue them﴾ means: He will humiliate them and disgrace them, even if no killing occurs among them.

﴿So they will turn back defeated﴾. Turn back to whom? They turn back to their lands defeated, meaning they did not obtain any good. This is what happened in the Battle of the Confederates (al-Ahzab), for the confederates in the Battle of the Confederates returned defeated without fighting, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And Allah repelled those who disbelieved in their rage, not having obtained any good. And Allah sufficed the believers in battle﴾ [al-Ahzab 25]. So there was no fighting; Allah repelled them with the wind and with soldiers that we did not see.

﴿You have no part in the matter﴾. Regarding ﴿You have no part﴾, some scholars said that the meaning is: "It is not up to you in the matter," like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Our Lord, indeed we have heard a caller calling to faith﴾ [Al 'Imran 193], meaning calling to faith. But the apparent meaning is that the lam retains its original meaning and is not with the sense of "to," and the meaning is that you do not possess anything. It does not mean that nothing is returned to you; rather the meaning is that you do not possess anything. So the lam remains as it is, and the address in His saying: ﴿You have no part in the matter﴾ is to the Prophet (ﷺ).

His saying: ﴿in the matter﴾ means the cosmic command (al-amr al-kawni). As for the legislative command (al-amr al-shar'i), the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) does have a part in it, due to His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah﴾ [an-Nisa 80]. As for the cosmic command, he does not.

The narrations differed regarding the occasion of revelation of this verse. In some narrations, its cause was that the Prophet (ﷺ) invoked curses upon a group of disbelievers, such as Abu Sufyan, Suhayl ibn 'Amr, Safwan ibn Umayya, and al-Harith ibn Hisham. These four were the ones the Messenger (ﷺ) would curse, when he prayed the dawn prayer in the last rak'ah, he would invoke curses upon them, saying: "O Allah, curse so-and-so, and so-and-so, and so-and-so,"[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (4070) from the hadith of Salim ibn 'Abdullah, and Ahmad in al-Musnad (5997) from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar.]] by their names. So Allah revealed: ﴿You have no part in the matter﴾, and so the matter is up to Allah.

There is also another authentic narration regarding this: that when they wounded the face of the Prophet (ﷺ) at Uhud, he began wiping the blood from his face and saying: "How will a people prosper who have wounded the face of their prophet while he is calling them to Allah?"[[Narrated by Muslim (1791/104) from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik.]] So Allah revealed: ﴿You have no part in the matter﴾.

The principle regarding the occasions of revelation is that when preference between them cannot be established, there is no objection to the cause being multiple, so the verse may have two causes; meaning it was revealed after both of them together. So the two matters are two causes for the revelation of the verse. First: his (ﷺ) rejection of those people and his saying: "How will they prosper?", expressing his disbelief that they would prosper. Second: his cursing of these four. There is no prohibition in this, for a verse may have two causes for its revelation.

His saying: ﴿or He will accept their repentance﴾. It has been said that it is joined to ﴿He will cut off﴾, and it has been said that ﴿or﴾ means "until" (ila), meaning: until He accepts their repentance.

According to the first view, there is no difficulty in the verse, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has mentioned four outcomes for these disbelievers: He will cut off a portion of those who disbelieved, or He will subdue them, or He will accept their repentance, or He will punish them. This interpretation, as you see, is a good one, and there is nothing in it except the parenthetical sentence in His saying: ﴿You have no part in the matter﴾, and this does no harm. There are parenthetical sentences in the Qur'an between things close in meaning, and indeed there are verses like that. For example, His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Guard over the prayers, and the middle prayer, and stand before Allah devoutly obedient﴾ [al-Baqarah 238] was mentioned in the middle of verses about the 'idda (waiting period), and a person does not see the connection clearly, but Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knows better than us. Likewise here, we say: it does no harm that there be a parenthetical sentence, although we will, if Allah wills, explain the connection in it.

As for the second view, which says that ﴿or﴾ means "until," they say that there is an omission in the verse, and the estimated meaning is: "You have no part in the matter, so be patient until Allah accepts their repentance." They estimate a verb, which is "be patient," meaning: do not invoke curses upon them, be patient until Allah accepts their repentance. You know that ﴿or﴾ comes with the meaning of "until" and comes with the meaning of "unless that" (illa an), meaning "until that" and "unless that." So if someone says: "I will kill the disbeliever, or he becomes Muslim," it means "unless that," and it is not correct to take it to mean "until that." And if someone says: "I will hold on to the debtor until he pays me my debt," it means "until that."

His saying: ﴿or He will accept their repentance﴾ means: by guiding them to Islam, because the discussion is now about disbelievers, and Allah's accepting the repentance of a disbeliever is that He guides him to Islam, and His accepting the repentance of a sinner is that He turns him away from sin to obedience.

Allah's acceptance of the servant's repentance has two types: a prior repentance and a subsequent repentance, and the servant's repentance lies between them. This is mentioned in Surat at-Tawba. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Allah has already accepted the repentance of the Prophet and the Muhajirin and the Ansar who followed him in the hour of difficulty, after the hearts of a faction of them had almost deviated. Then He accepted their repentance. Indeed, He is to them Kind and Merciful. And [He also accepted the repentance of] the three who were left behind, until the earth closed in on them in spite of its vastness and their souls confined them and they were certain that there is no refuge from Allah except in Him. Then He turned to them so that they might repent﴾ [at-Tawba 117–118].

﴿He turned to them so that they might repent﴾: this is the prior repentance, and the prior repentance means the granting of success (tawfiq) to repent, while the subsequent repentance means the acceptance of repentance. The servant's repentance occurs... what? 

* Students: between them.
* The Shaykh: between them, yes. ﴿or He will accept their repentance﴾, meaning: He will make it easy for them to move from disbelief to Islam.

* Student: Shaykh, regarding the Messenger, he was forbidden, meaning Allah forbade the Messenger (ﷺ) from naming names in his curse, perhaps while he was in prostration, (...) someone (...) for example.
* The Shaykh: No, no, he was forbidden from cursing them. Do not curse, but invoke destruction upon him, there is no objection. Invoke that Allah tighten His grip upon him.
* The Student: By his name?
* The Shaykh: By his name there is no objection, but not cursing, because cursing means expulsion and removal from the mercy of Allah. You do not know, perhaps this disbelieving, aggressive, wrongdoing person may one day become a supporter of Islam. Was not Khalid ibn al-Walid the one who fought the Messenger (ﷺ) at Uhud? He fought him, and then became one of the knights of Islam. And 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, and 'Amr ibn al-'As said: "By Allah, I wish I could get the opportunity to get at the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)," so that I could kill him. He wished for that, but when Allah granted him Islam, he said: "By Allah, I could not even raise my eyes to look at him out of reverence for him."[[Narrated by Abu 'Awana in his Musnad (200) from the hadith of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Shamasa al-Mahri from 'Amr ibn al-'As.]] Allahu Akbar! Hearts are not known except by the hand of Allah.

* Student: ﴿You have no part in the matter, or He will accept their repentance﴾. Is it correct to join it to "part"? If "or" means "unless that," is joining it to "part" better?
* The Shaykh: No, no, the meaning does not hold that way, because if you say: "until He accepts their repentance," the meaning becomes: "if He accepts their repentance, then you have a part in the matter"?
* The Student: "You have no part in the matter."
* The Shaykh: "Until He accepts their repentance."
* The Student: "Allah has a part in the matter, what is it?"
* The Shaykh: No, for Allah, that is a second point. But if we say the verse means: "You have no part in the matter until He accepts their repentance," then the meaning of the verse becomes: "If He accepts their repentance, then you have a part in the matter." For this reason Ibn Jarir rejected this meaning and said: this is not correct, because the command belongs to Allah whether He accepts their repentance or not, and the Messenger has no part in the matter whether Allah accepts their repentance or not.

* * *

* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿You have no part in the matter, or He will accept their repentance, or He will punish them, for indeed they are wrongdoers﴾ (128). ﴿And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (129). ﴿O you who have believed, do not consume interest, doubled and multiplied, and fear Allah that you may be successful﴾ (130). ﴿And fear the Fire, which has been prepared for the disbelievers﴾ (131). ﴿And obey Allah and the Messenger that you may receive mercy﴾ (132) [Al 'Imran 128–132].

* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿that He might cut off a portion of those who disbelieved or subdue them, so that they will turn back defeated﴾.

﴿You have no part in the matter﴾: the discussion of the explanation of this verse has already passed, and we said that the preponderant view is that His saying ﴿You have no part in the matter﴾ is a parenthetical sentence. On this basis, His saying ﴿or He will accept their repentance﴾ is joined to His saying ﴿that He might cut off﴾. ﴿Or He will accept their repentance﴾, meaning: He will prepare for them the means of repentance until they repent. We have explained that Allah, the Exalted, has two kinds of repentance toward His servant: the repentance of granting success (tawfiq), and the repentance of acceptance, and we cited as evidence His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And [He also accepted the repentance of] the three who were left behind﴾, to His saying: ﴿Then He turned to them so that they might repent. Indeed, Allah is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful﴾ [at-Tawba 118].

He said: ﴿or He will punish them﴾, joined also to ﴿that He might cut off﴾, and this is the fourth condition. And the three?

* Student: That He might cut off a portion, and that He might accept their repentance, and subdue them.
* The Shaykh: Or subdue them. He said: ﴿or He will punish them﴾, meaning: He will punish them with a punishment from Him. This is like His saying: ﴿Say, "Do you await for us except one of the two good things? And we await for you that Allah will afflict you with punishment from Him or at our hands"﴾ [at-Tawba 52], meaning: or He will punish them with a punishment from Him, so He will send upon them a defilement or a plague, through disease, plague, earthquakes, and other things, because Allah, the Exalted, is over all things competent.

Part 5 of the commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin on Surah Al 'Imran, verses 123–128

﴿So they are wrongdoers﴾. The position of this sentence in relation to what precedes it is that it gives the reason for it; that is, they deserve one of these matters because they are wrongdoers. The exception is repentance, for when Allah accepts their repentance, their attribute of wrongdoing is removed. The four whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to invoke against were all forgiven by Allah and they embraced Islam. In this there is an indication, as has already been mentioned, that a person should not invoke curse upon anyone, however far he has gone in disbelief and tyranny. Rather, it is not permissible to invoke a curse upon him, because cursing (la'nah) means expulsion and removal from the mercy of Allah. It is not right for you to restrict the mercy of Allah, for Allah may bestow His grace upon this disbelieving criminal so that he repents, just as He, glorified and exalted, may bestow His grace upon the sinner who has not reached the level of disbelief, so that he becomes upright and his condition is set right.

* Among the benefits of this verse: ﴿That He may cut off a part﴾ affirms the wisdom of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in His actions and legislation, because the lam here indicates causation (ta'lil), and causation is wisdom (hikmah).

* Among the benefits of this verse: Allah, glorified and exalted, empowers the believers over the disbelievers in order to cut off a part of those who disbelieved, not all of them, because it is part of Allah's wisdom that faith and disbelief remain in conflict perpetually until the sincere believer is distinguished from others.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the outcome of the disbelievers is one of these four matters. The first is their destruction. The second is their humiliation, by His saying: ﴿or He will subdue them, so that they return frustrated﴾.

* Among the benefits of this verse: kabt (subjugation), which is humiliation and abandonment, is frustration, by His saying: ﴿so that they return frustrated﴾.

Is there a parallel to this? Yes, the story of the confederates (al-Ahzab), for Allah, glorified and exalted, turned them back on their heels, frustrated.

Then He said: ﴿You have no part in the affair at all﴾, to the end of the verse.

* Among the benefits of this verse: the Prophet (ﷺ) does not possess any part of the affair, meaning which affair? The universal (kawni) affair. This sentence is also a refutation of those who attach themselves to the Messenger (ﷺ) in supplication and seeking help, even after his death. Today you find them at the noble grave calling upon the Messenger (ﷺ) openly. Indeed, when they supplicate, even if they are far away, they turn toward the grave and not toward the qiblah, and this is from their foolishness.

* Among the benefits of this verse, or rather of this sentence: the Prophet (ﷺ) is under obligation (mukallaf); Allah commands him and forbids him. Accordingly, this is a refutation of the claim of those who say that when a person reaches a certain state of servitude, the obligations fall from him. This is the view of a group of Sufis, who say that when a person advances in certainty until he reaches the highest rank, the obligation falls from him, and everything forbidden becomes lawful for him, and everything obligatory is no longer obligatory upon him. Thus they do not require him to pray, nor do they forbid him from fornication or drinking wine, because the man has reached the ultimate goal. In their view, these obligations are nothing but a means and a path: once a person reaches the goal, the means falls away. They say: if you travel to a city and arrive there, do you still need a road to walk along? No. This is what they say. Worship is a path by which you reach a certain goal; once you have reached it, it falls away from him.

It is said to them: if the Prophet (ﷺ), who is the most noble of creation, does not attain this rank, then what of those below him?

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: Allah, exalted is He, may accept the repentance of the most rebellious of people and the most intense in disbelief, by the generality of His saying: ﴿or He will accept their repentance﴾.

* Among its benefits also: Allah may punish the disbelievers with a punishment in which the believers have no hand, but which comes from Allah alone, by His saying: ﴿or He will punish them﴾.

* Among the benefits of this verse: Allah does not punish except for a sin, by His saying: ﴿for they are wrongdoers﴾, and the wrongdoer deserves to be punished by Allah, because Allah, exalted is He, does not love wrongdoing. Indeed, He said in the sacred hadith: "Indeed I have forbidden injustice to Myself, and I have made it forbidden among you, so do not wrong one another." [Narrated by Muslim (2577/55) from the hadith of Abu Dharr.]

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verse 123–128 (part 1 of 5):

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And Allah had already given you victory at Badr when you were humble﴾ [Al 'Imran 123].

Allah, may He be glorified and exalted, says, clarifying His favour upon the Prophet (ﷺ) and his Companions, and indeed upon the whole Ummah; for the victory of the Prophet (ﷺ) and his Companions is a victory for the entire Ummah until the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, the victory of the earlier Messengers is a victory for the believers until the Day of Resurrection. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) fasted on 'Ashura', giving thanks to Allah for His favour in saving Musa and his people and destroying Fir'awn and his people, and he said to the Jews: "We have a greater right to Musa than you do" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3943) and Muslim (1130 / 127) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]].

He says, may He be glorified: ﴿And Allah had already given you victory at Badr﴾. This sentence is emphasised by three things: first, the implied oath; second, the lam; third, qad; for the sense is: "By Allah, Allah had certainly given you victory."

Victory (nasr) is that Allah makes dominance belong to these people over those people; whoever Allah grants dominance to, He has given them victory.

Victory has five causes (asbab, pl. of sabab, "cause"):

First: sincerity to Allah, based on the saying of Allah: ﴿Allah has promised those of you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will surely make them successors upon the earth, just as He made successors those before them, and that He will surely establish for them their religion which He has approved for them, and that He will surely replace their fear with security, [provided] they worship Me, not associating anything with Me﴾ [An-Nur 55].

Second: establishing the prayer; third: giving zakat; fourth: enjoining what is good; fifth: forbidding what is evil, based on the saying of Allah: ﴿Allah will surely support those who support Him. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might. [They are] those who, if We give them authority in the land, establish prayer and give zakat and enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong﴾ [Al-Hajj 40, 41]. So the causes are five:

* Student: Sincerity to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and its evidence: ﴿Allah has promised those of you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will surely make them successors upon the earth, just as He made successors those before them﴾ up to the end of the verse.
* Shaykh: We want the point, up to His saying:
* Student: ﴿they worship Me, not associating anything with Me﴾.
* Student: The second: establishing the prayer; the third: giving zakat; the fourth: enjoining what is good; and the fifth: forbidding what is evil, based on the saying of Allah: ﴿[They are] those who, if We give them authority in the land, establish prayer and give zakat and enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong﴾ [Al-Hajj 41].
* Shaykh: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And Allah had already given you victory at Badr﴾. The ba' here means "in" (fi), indicating place (zarfiyyah). There is nothing strange in ba' being used for place, as in the saying of the Most High: ﴿And indeed, you pass by them in the morning (137) and at night﴾ [As-Saffat 137, 138], meaning: "and at night." So His saying ﴿bi-Badrin﴾ means "at Badr."

Badr is a well-known place, and it is still known today between Makkah and Madinah.

The cause of this expedition was that when the Prophet (ﷺ) heard of a caravan of Quraysh coming from Syria, he called upon his Companions to go out to seize it, because the Quraysh had expelled the Prophet (ﷺ) and his Companions from their homes and their wealth, and they were at war against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ); so their wealth was lawful spoil for the Messenger (ﷺ). He called his Companions to go out against them, and they went out in a small number and with weak equipment: they went out with about three hundred and some men, on seventy camels and only two horses, which they took in turns: two men on a camel, and three on a camel, intending only the caravan. But Abu Sufyan, who was the commander of the caravan, took it along the coast, the seaside, and not by the well-known route, and he sent a shout to the people of Makkah calling for their help to protect their caravan. Then, when he escaped, he sent to them that he had escaped, that the caravan had got away; but they had already prepared to go out to fight the Prophet (ﷺ), so they went out with their chiefs and leaders in the manner that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, described: they went out ﴿insolent and showing off to the people and barring [others] from the way of Allah﴾ [Al-Anfal 47]. Shaytan said to them: ﴿No one among the people can overcome you today, and I am your protector﴾ [Al-Anfal 48], but he betrayed them: ﴿So when the two armies sighted each other, he turned back on his heels﴾ [Al-Anfal 48].

They went out numbering between one thousand and nine hundred, and they brought the women with them, so that their fighting would intensify out of fear for their women, since they had brought the women and placed them behind.

The battle took place between the Prophet (ﷺ) and these polytheists. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) and his Companions were few, few in number and in equipment, but Allah, may He be glorified and exalted, gave them victory; for this reason He said: ﴿And Allah had already given you victory at Badr when you were humble﴾. "Adhillah" is the plural of "dhalil," just as "a'izzah" is the plural of "'azeez."

Good. In what respect were they humble? In terms of number and in terms of equipment: three hundred and some men compared with nine hundred to one thousand, meaning less than a third; and what they had in terms of equipment was nothing: seventy camels and two horses. But Allah gave them victory, may He be glorified and exalted.

He said: ﴿So fear Allah that you may be grateful﴾ [Al 'Imran 123]. Fear Allah. The fa' here is for consequence (tafri'): meaning, in return for this victory which Allah granted you, it is obligatory upon you to fear Allah, and not to make victory a cause of arrogance and insolence, as those who have no faith do: when they triumph over their enemy, they make this a cause of arrogance and insolence, and they enter the town singing and merry. Yes, as was mentioned of some Arab broadcasters during their war with the Jews, who said: "Tomorrow Umm Kulthum will sing in Tel Aviv." Subhan Allah! Is this the reward for a blessing?!

As for the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him), he entered Makkah in the year of the Conquest, which is among the greatest victories, with his head bowed in submission to Allah, may He be glorified and exalted. This is how it should be: when a person is victorious, he should not make this victory a cause of arrogance and insolence, but should regard it as a blessing from Allah, may He be glorified and exalted, and fear Allah. For this reason He said: ﴿So fear Allah﴾.

Taqwa is taking a shield against the punishment of Allah. With what does the shield come? What protects you from the punishment of Allah? With what is the protection?

* Student: By doing what is commanded and avoiding what is forbidden.
* Shaykh: Yes, doing what is commanded and avoiding what is forbidden. So if someone asks us, "What is taqwa?" we say: it is doing what is commanded and abandoning what is forbidden, because when you do what is commanded and abandon what is forbidden, you have taken the protection from the punishment of Allah, may He be glorified and exalted.

His saying ﴿that you may be grateful﴾: here "la'alla" indicates purpose (ta'lil), meaning: in order that you may attain the gratitude of Allah. Taqwa is in reality gratitude to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; that is, so that you may attain gratitude, i.e., the rank of the grateful.

And how is gratitude for a blessing expressed?

* Student: Righteous deeds and avoiding evil deeds.
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: Ibn al-Qayyim said: gratitude to Allah consists of three matters: gratitude with the heart, with the tongue, and by spending it in obedience to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
* Shaykh: It is with the heart, the tongue and the limbs. Gratitude is with the heart, the tongue and the limbs.

As for gratitude of the heart, it is that you believe these blessings are from Allah, by His grace and favour, and that you have nothing from them except doing the means that were permitted to you; but their reality is from Allah, and you believe in that. Do not be like the one who said: ﴿I was only given it on account of knowledge I have﴾ [Al-Qasas 78]; rather say: "I was given it by the grace and mercy of Allah," even if it came through your own effort.

As for when it comes from the action of Allah, it is clear that every person attributes it to Allah; yet some people do not attribute to Allah what comes from His action: when rain falls they say, "We have been given rain by such-and-such a star." For this reason Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) led us in prayer at al-Hudaybiyah following a rain that had fallen during the night, i.e., after rain. When he finished, he turned to us and said: 'Do you know what your Lord said?' They said: 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' He said: 'He said: Some of My servants have awakened as believers in Me and some as disbelievers. As for the one who said: We have been given rain by the grace and mercy of Allah, that is a believer in Me and a disbeliever in the star; and as for the one who said: We have been given rain by such-and-such a star, that is a disbeliever in Me and a believer in the star.'" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (846) and Muslim (71 / 125) from the hadith of Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani.]]. So you must believe in your heart that the blessing is from whom?

* Student: From Allah, glorified be He.
* Shaykh: From Allah, and that whatever you do to bring about this blessing is only a means permitted by Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Second: the tongue, that you praise Allah with it, not that you say it boastfully over the servants of Allah, but that you praise Him by saying: "All praise is due to Allah who gave me such-and-such," based on the saying of Allah: ﴿And as for the blessing of your Lord, proclaim it﴾ [Ad-Duha 11].

Third: that you act with your limbs in obedience to Allah, especially regarding this particular blessing. It is not gratitude, if Allah provides you with wealth, to spend it on buying tobacco that you smoke, since this is using Allah's blessing to disobey Allah; nor to buy with it an instrument of amusement by which you divert yourself; this is not gratitude. Rather, gratitude is that you make the blessing a helper for you in obedience to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. One of the poets said:

The blessings have benefited you from me in three ways: ∗∗∗ my hand, my tongue, and the veiled conscience.

"My hand": these are the limbs; "my tongue": speech, praising Allah for the blessing; "the veiled conscience": belief.

﴿So fear Allah that you may be grateful﴾.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿[Remember] when you said to the believers, "Is it not sufficient for you that your Lord reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?" (124) Yes, if you are patient and fear Allah, and they come at you [in] their rage at this very moment, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels marked [for battle]﴾ [Al 'Imran 124, 125].

First: in this verse, His saying ﴿munzilin﴾ has a Sab'i reading: ﴿munazzilin﴾, with the zay doubled. And His saying ﴿musawwimin﴾ also has a Sab'i reading: ﴿musawwamin﴾, in the passive form.

He says: ﴿[Remember] when you said to the believers﴾. The address is to the Prophet (ﷺ), and this is among the addresses that are specific to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). It has already passed with us that the addresses directed at the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) are divided into three categories:

The first: what evidence shows is specific to him.

The second: what evidence shows is general to the Ummah.

The third: what no evidence indicates either way.

What evidence shows is specific to him is specific to him, such as this verse: ﴿[Remember] when you said to the believers, "Is it not sufficient for you"﴾; and ﴿And [remember] when you said to him on whom Allah bestowed favour and you bestowed favour﴾ [Al-Ahzab 37] — this is specific; ﴿Did We not expand for you your breast?﴾ [Ash-Sharh 1] — this is specific; ﴿O Messenger, convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 67] — this too is specific, although the Ummah is obligated to convey from another angle.

The second: what evidence shows is general, as in the saying of Allah: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them at their waiting period﴾ [At-Talaq 1]. This is clearly general, for He first addressed the Prophet (ﷺ) and then generalised the ruling by saying: ﴿when you divorce﴾.

The third: what no evidence indicates either way is general; it is general without doubt, its ruling is general. But is the address general in terms of its wording or not?

What appears is that it is general even in wording, because an address to the imam is an address to those who follow him.

For this reason, if a minister said, for example, to the commander: "Go to such-and-such a place," that would be an address to him and to those under his command.

Likewise, when the address is directed to the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) and no evidence shows that it is specific to him, it includes him and the whole Ummah.

Some scholars said: it does not include the Ummah; the address is to him alone, but the Ummah must follow.

If you reflect, you will find that the disagreement is close to a verbal one; for they agree that the ruling is general, but the question is whether the Ummah is included within this address or is addressed by another address, since it is commanded to follow. This is the point of disagreement, and in truth, when you examine it, you will find it is close to a verbal disagreement.

* Student: May Allah bless you, Shaykh. Some people overindulge in permissible things to the point that extravagance is feared for them; when you advise them, they say: ﴿And as for the blessing of your Lord, proclaim it﴾?
* Shaykh: Yes indeed. We say to him: ﴿And do not be wasteful; indeed, He does not like the wasteful﴾ [Al-An'am 141]. We are not saying to you, if you are wealthy: go out in the clothes of the poor, and eat only what the poor eat; we say: eat what the wealthy eat and wear what the wealthy wear, but do not be wasteful.
* Student: Two groups of Muslims fought, and one of them seized weapons from the other. Is it lawful for the other to take booty in the same way?
* Shaykh: I did not understand.
* Student: Are the wealth of the Muslims not to be taken as booty?
* Shaykh: Not to be taken as booty?
* Student: I mean during fighting.
* Shaykh: One looks at what the fighting is. If it is for partisanship or leadership, there is no doubt that it is oppression and not permissible, and neither property nor lives become lawful thereby. But if it is rebellion (baghy), then the rebel must be fought until he returns from his rebellion, as Allah the Mighty and Majestic said.
* Student: But is his weapon taken?
* Shaykh: Certainly his weapon is taken, because if we fight him and are able to take the weapon but do not take it, he will turn it against us. So we take it. Then whether it becomes booty or not depends on whom we are fighting: if the one we fight is a disbeliever, it is booty; if he is not a disbeliever, this is a matter for consideration.
* Student: Shaykh, may Allah be good to you: is the prohibition on giving disbelievers authority in general matters, or in particular matters?
* Shaykh: No, in leadership matters. As for non-leadership matters, such as construction or the like, like a worker with you, there is nothing wrong with that. Except in this Arabian Peninsula, it is not appropriate to bring disbelievers into it, because the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) commanded their expulsion from the Arabian Peninsula, and said: "Woe to the Arabs from an evil that has drawn near; today an opening the size of this has been made in the barrier of Gog and Magog," [and he made a circle with his thumb and forefinger]. Zaynab said: "O Messenger of Allah, will we be destroyed while the righteous are among us?" He said: "Yes, when wickedness increases" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3346) and Muslim (2880 / 1) from the hadith of Zaynab bint Jahsh.]]. Here "khabath" (wickedness) includes personal wickedness and practical wickedness. If wickedness increases among Muslims, Allah is near to destroying them; and if wickedness increases among non-Muslim individuals, that is, disbelievers come into the land, Allah is likewise near to seizing them.
* Student: Are there matters that we do not have knowledge or experience in, while they have experience, so we must give them some leadership so that we may learn from them or they may assist us in something?
* Shaykh: These matters may be incidental and not permanent. Therefore we are not forbidden to learn from them what they teach us, or for example to take from their experience; there is benefit for us in this.
* Student: Is it permissible, Shaykh, to appoint some people of misguided sects who harbour hatred against Ahl al-Sunnah wal-Jama'ah, such as the Rafidah and others, to leadership positions?
* Shaykh: ﴿O you who believe, do not take as intimates other than your own, who will not spare you [from] ruin﴾ [Al 'Imran 118]. "Min dunikum" means other than you. Every person whom we know does not advise us sincerely, it is not permissible for us to appoint him.

* Student: The words of Allah the Exalted, ﴿And Allah will surely help those who help Him﴾ [al-Hajj 40], and His words ﴿those who, if We establish them in the land﴾ [al-Hajj 41]. Some people say, meaning: the apparent sense of the verse is that if We establish them in the land, they establish prayer. Meaning, after being empowered, they establish prayer?

* Shaykh: Yes, this is among the causes of victory, without doubt. When Allah knows that these people intend, if they are empowered in the land, to establish prayer, this is one of the causes of victory.

* Student: Meaning, even if their state (...) is from the state they were in before victory?

* Shaykh: Because the one whose intention is this before victory, he will undoubtedly remain upon it.

* Student: Shaykh, may Allah reward you with good. Regarding the words of Allah the Exalted, ﴿so that you may be grateful﴾, some of them, O Shaykh, say that this (la'alla, "perhaps/so that") also admits the sense of hope (tarajji), but with reference to the addressees?

* Shaykh: (...) Because you... for hope with reference to the addressees, you have diverted it from its apparent meaning.

* Student: So it remains in its original sense, (la'alla) for hope, and it is with reference to the addressee?

* Shaykh: No, never. It is for causation (ta'lil). It is for causation, and that is stronger. Meaning, that piety being a cause of gratitude is stronger, without doubt.

* Student: Meaning it is wrong..

* Shaykh: Yes, this is wrong.

* Student: When is it permissible to attribute rain to a time period?

* Shaykh: When you attribute rain to a time period by treating it as a container for it (zarf), not as its cause. For example, if you say: "We were rained upon during the nawʾ of such-and-such," meaning, for example, "We were rained upon during the nawʾ of al-Shawla," this is fine. In the nawʾ of al-Naʿaim, which among us they call al-Shabt, there is no harm. For this reason the scholars said: it is forbidden to say "We were rained upon by the nawʾ of such-and-such" (bi-nawʾ), and it is permissible to say "We were rained upon in the nawʾ of such-and-such" (fi nawʾ). But the common people among us make the bāʾ mean (fī), so they say: "We were rained upon in Shubat," "We were rained upon in al-Mirbaʿaniyya," and they put the bāʾ: "bi-al-Mirbaʿaniyya," "bi-al-mawsim." That is because the bāʾ means (fī) for them. The matter is judged by intention.

* Student: ﴿When you were saying to the believers﴾ (idh) is connected to victory, or is it connected to something else?

* Shaykh: This is based on whether this is at Badr or at Uhud?

* Student: I think it is at Badr, after (...).

* Shaykh: There is a disagreement which we will mention, Allah willing. Some scholars say: it is at Badr, and some say: at Uhud. Those who said it is at Badr said: the verse ﴿And Allah had already helped you at Badr when you were weak﴾ is an interjected verse within the narrative, because His words ﴿And when you set out from your family﴾ [Ali ʿImran 121] are by agreement about the battle of Uhud.

* Student: If we make the disbeliever a ruler, he will have in his own mind a sense of power by which he will exalt himself over the Muslims, and he does not give (...) because he is spiteful. How do we appoint him?

* Shaykh: No, we do not appoint him. If we fear this, we do not appoint him. If we fear this prohibited outcome, we do not appoint him.

* * *

* Student: ﴿When you were saying to the believers: "Is it not enough for you that your Lord reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?" (124) "Yes. If you are patient and mindful of Allah, and they come upon you suddenly from this very moment, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels, marked (for battle)." (125) Allah did not make it except as good news for you, and so that your hearts would be at rest through it. Victory is only from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise. (126) That He may cut off a part of those who disbelieve, or subdue them so that they turn back defeated. (127) You have no say in the matter: whether He turns to them in forgiveness or punishes them, for they are wrongdoers.﴾ [Ali ʿImran 124–128].

* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿When you were saying to the believers, "Is it not enough for you that your Lord reinforce you..."﴾ and so on to the end.

His words, ﴿idh﴾: this is an adverb of time (ẓarf). The rule in Arabic grammar is that an adverb of time and a prepositional phrase must have something they depend on (mutaʿallaq), because an adverb of time and a prepositional phrase occupy the position of a direct object, and whatever occupies the position of a direct object must have a governing word upon which it depends.

As for His words ﴿idh taqūlu﴾: if we say that it needs something it depends on, where is what it depends on? It has been said that what it depends on is His words ﴿And Allah had already helped you at Badr﴾: "He helped you at Badr when you were saying to the believers..." But this is a weak view.

The second view: it is a substitute (badal) for His words ﴿And when you set out from your family, settling the believers in their positions for battle﴾. The meaning: "And when you were saying to the believers, 'Is it not enough for you...'" The construction: "when you were saying to the believers: 'When you set out, when you were saying to the believers.'" This is closer.

Then His words ﴿when you were saying to the believers﴾: the address in it is to the Prophet ﷺ, and this is a specific address to him which does not extend to the community.

His words ﴿to the believers﴾ mean the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them. He described them with faith rather than companionship, because the description of faith (by which I mean the attribute of faith) is the basis of victory at every time, even after the Companions, for Allah helps those who believe.

﴿Is it not enough for you﴾: this is the content of the speech, meaning: when you were saying to them these words: ﴿Is it not enough for you that your Lord reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?﴾ The people of knowledge said: the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, learned that the polytheists had begun to support one another in fighting the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions. So the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, said to them: "Is it not enough for you" (that is, will this matter not suffice you) "that your Lord reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?"

﴿with three thousand angels﴾: the angels are an unseen world whom Allah the Exalted created from light. He assigned them acts of worship and deeds which they perform. They do not disobey Allah in them, and they do what they are commanded. There is no arrogance in them that would lead to disobedience, and no incapacity in them that would prevent the act. Rather, they are obedient, listening, and able to carry out Allah's command. This contrasts with humans, for in them there is arrogance, so they disobey Allah, and in them there is incapacity, so they cannot carry out Allah's command. As for the angels, they have a strength by which they are never unable to comply with Allah's command, and they have complete submission, so they do not disobey Allah, glorified and exalted is He.

His words ﴿with three thousand angels sent down﴾: sent down from where? From heaven, because the basic place of the angels is heaven. But there are angels who are with a person, such as the honorable scribes and the guardians who succeed one another over a person, angels by night and angels by day. Otherwise, the basic position is that they are in heaven.

His words ﴿sent down (munzilīn)﴾: there are two readings: ﴿munazzalīn﴾ and ﴿munzilīn﴾. On the reading with lightening (takhfīf), it is from (anzala). On the reading with emphasis (tashdīd), it is from (nazzala). The meaning is one, and the one who sends them down is Allah the Exalted, because they descend by His command.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Yes (balā)﴾: balā here is for affirmation, or to confirm the interrogative: ﴿Is it not enough for you?﴾ Yes, meaning: it is enough for you that your Lord reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down.

He says: "Yes," meaning this reinforcement is sufficient for you, but on a condition: if you are patient and mindful of Allah, and they come upon you suddenly from this very moment, your Lord will reinforce you with more than what you were told. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Is it not enough for you that He reinforce you with three thousand?" But if you are patient and mindful of Allah, Allah will reinforce you with more. For this reason He said: ﴿your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand﴾.

So here there are two things: three thousand angels, which was promised by the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him. Five thousand angels, beyond the three thousand, which Allah guaranteed, but on the condition of patience and piety.

His words ﴿and they come upon you suddenly from this very moment (min fawrihim hādhā)﴾ [Ali ʿImran 125] mean: they come upon you from the direction from which they came to you, at an immediate time. Because al-fawr means hastening toward something. The meaning is that if they surprise you and come upon you from their immediate moment, then your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels, marked.

So the conditions are three: patience. The second?

* Students: Piety.

* Shaykh: And the third: that they come upon them from this very moment. For Allah will reinforce them with five thousand angels, not merely sent down, but marked (musawwamīn), meaning distinguished with the sign of jihad and the sign of fighting. This is more eloquent than mere sending down. Allah the Exalted guaranteed an increase, and this relates to quantity, and He guaranteed strength and bravery, and this relates to quality.

His words ﴿marked (musawwamīn)﴾ [Ali ʿImran 125] mean: marked with the signs of combat, because it is customary for brave warriors to have signs upon them, in the form of distinctive war-gear, so that the brave man can be recognized from others.

As for this reinforcement, the people of knowledge disagreed over whether it was at Badr or at Uhud. If it was at Badr, there is a difficulty, because Allah mentioned that He reinforced them at Badr with one thousand angels, saying: ﴿When you sought help from your Lord, and He answered you: "I will reinforce you with a thousand angels, following one another"﴾ [al-Anfal 9]. Here He said three thousand and five thousand. But they reconciled the two by saying there is no obstacle to Allah answering them and reinforcing them with one thousand angels, then increasing them to three thousand, then increasing them to five thousand if the conditions are fulfilled.

Based on this view, His words ﴿idh taqūlu﴾ are connected to "helped" (naṣara).

The second view: this verse is about Uhud and not about Badr, because the matter at Badr was not conditional: ﴿When you sought help from your Lord, and He answered you: "I will reinforce you with a thousand angels, following one another"﴾, whereas this one is conditional. The condition was not fulfilled, so the conditioned matter was not realized. That is, the Muslims at the battle of Uhud did not fulfill the condition Allah set, which is piety and patience, because there was dispute, failure, and disobedience among them, so they were not in the state that would merit what Allah had conditioned for them.

This view is more correct and closer to the truth: that what is meant is the battle of Uhud, and that the reinforcement did not occur, because the reinforcement was conditioned on a condition that was not met. On this basis, no contradiction remains between the two verses, because each verse was revealed concerning a different battle.

Furthermore, we must know that what the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, promised them is different from what Allah promised them. The speech is not from one speaker, but from the Prophet ﷺ and from Allah the Exalted. The Messenger said: ﴿Is it not enough for you that He reinforce you?﴾ And Allah said: ﴿Yes. If you are patient and mindful of Allah, and they come upon you suddenly from this very moment, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels, marked﴾.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Allah did not make it except as good news for you﴾. The pronoun in (ja'alahu, "He made it") is said to refer to the reinforcement, or to the promise of it with the three conditions. It has also been said that it refers to the Messenger's words ﴿when you were saying to the believers﴾, meaning that Allah did not make the Messenger's statement except as good news for you. Good news is information that brings joy. There is no doubt this is good news, for when the fighter knows that Allah the Exalted will reinforce him with angels, he becomes energized, strong, and hopeful of victory, unlike when this has not happened for him.

His words ﴿except as good news for you﴾ [Ali ʿImran 126]: do you know the grammatical analysis (iʿrāb) of bushrā (good news)?

* Student: A second object.

* Shaykh: A second object of what?

* Student: Of (ja'ala, "made").

* Shaykh: Of (ja'ala), or is it in the accusative by exception?

* Student: A cause object (mafʿūl li-ajlihi), or a second object of (ja'ala). If (ja'ala) means (ṣayyara, "made into"), it is a second object. If it does not mean (ṣayyara), it is a cause object.

* Shaykh: Is it not valid as an exception?

* Student: No.

* Shaykh: Why?

* Student: The excepted-from is not mentioned, because it is a restrictive particle.

* Shaykh: Because the governing word has not completed its complement.

He said: ﴿and so that your hearts would be at rest through it﴾ [Ali ʿImran 126]. ﴿wa-li-taṭma'inna qulūbukum bihi﴾: tranquility (iṭmi'nān) means settling and the absence of anxiety. There is no doubt that the tranquility of the heart brings rest to the soul, opens the door to optimism and hope, and provides steadfastness in the matter. Contrast this with a person whose heart is not at rest, for you find him always in anxiety and constriction. But when his heart is at rest, this helps him to endure, to stand firm, and to be patient. For this reason He said: ﴿and so that your hearts would be at rest through it﴾. In the chapter of al-Anfal the context differs. There He said: ﴿Allah did not make it except as good news, and so that your hearts would be at rest through it﴾ [al-Anfal 10], omitting the words "for you," and placing the prepositional phrase before the subject: ﴿and so that your hearts would be at rest through it﴾ in Surat al-Anfal. But here it is ﴿and so that your hearts would be at rest through it﴾. This supports that the two verses are not about the battle of Badr. Rather, the verse of al-Anfal is about the battle of Badr, and this one is about the battle of Uhud, and the reinforcement did not occur, because of the unmet condition, as you have understood.

Then He said: ﴿Victory is only from Allah﴾. This means that even if you were reinforced with three thousand or five thousand angels, victory is not due to them. Rather, victory is from Allah, who prepares the causes of victory. So do not rely on anyone other than Allah the Exalted, even on what Allah has made a cause of victory.

He said: ﴿only from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise﴾. "Al-ʿAzīz" means: the one possessing might. The might of Allah the Exalted has three kinds: might of rank, might of subjugation, and might of inaccessibility. Might of rank means nobility, lordship and excellence, such as when you say: "This thing is rare in its existence," meaning it is unique in its complete attributes compared to others. Might of subjugation means dominance, meaning He is overpowering, and from it is His saying: ﴿He said, "Give it to me, and he has overpowered me in speech"﴾ [Sad 23], meaning he overcame me in it. Allah the Exalted has dominance, as He said: ﴿They say﴾, meaning the hypocrites: ﴿If we return to Medina, the mightier will surely expel the meaner from it﴾ [al-Munafiqun 8], and Allah affirmed for them that the mightier expels the meaner. But to whom does might belong?

* Students: Might belongs to Allah, and to His Messenger.

* Shaykh: ﴿But might belongs to Allah, to His Messenger, and to the believers, but the hypocrites do not know﴾ [al-Munafiqun 8]. So, might of subjugation means dominance, that He is dominant, dominant over everything. And from pre-Islamic poetry:
