A person should not fear anyone among the creation in implementing Allah's command. If he fears anyone among the creation, then he is not a believer. The evidence for this is His saying: ﴿It is only Satan who frightens his allies, so do not fear them, but fear Me, if you are believers﴾ [Al 'Imran 175]. ﴿He frightens his allies﴾: that is, he causes fear to fall upon his allies? 
* Student: No.
* The Shaykh: Yes. For this reason we say that His saying ﴿his allies﴾ is the second object of "yukhawwif" (he frightens), and the first object is omitted. The meaning of the sentence is: he frightens you with his allies, that is, he places fear in your hearts from his allies. Is it clear? He the Exalted said: ﴿so do not fear them, but fear Me, if you are believers﴾. ﴿Those to whom people said, "Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them."﴾ So what did they say? They said: ﴿Sufficient for us is Allah, and He is the best Disposer of affairs﴾ [Al 'Imran 173]. So if Satan frightens his allies, who are the disbelievers, it is not permissible for us to fear them. It is not permissible for us to fear them; rather, we do what Allah has commanded us. However, Allah's command to us to fight the disbelievers applies only when we have a strength with which we can fight them. As for fighting them with weapons that are not theirs and far less than theirs, this is considered recklessness. For this reason the believers were not commanded to wage jihad until they had might and power. As for when they did not have it, then no. But this entails that it is obligatory upon us to arm ourselves to fight them until the religion is for Allah. The address here, regarding the obligation to arm oneself, is to those in authority, not to individuals, because individuals cannot undertake this. But the rulers of the Muslims must establish a vast, armed army with the most modern weapons, in order to fight ﴿those who do not believe in Allah or in the Last Day, and do not forbid what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, and do not adopt the religion of truth from those who were given the Scripture, until they give the jizyah (poll tax) willingly while they are humbled﴾ [At-Tawbah 29]. But unfortunately, today we have lost even the weapon of da'wah (calling to Islam). We do not find anyone calling as he should, while we see the Christians in full force in calling to the falsehood they hold. They spend great sums of money and risk themselves in unknown places, on roads, in deserts. The priest among them carries a piece of bread and a jug of water and travels through wastelands in order to call one Muslim to become Christian. As for us, unfortunately, we do not carry this moral strength in our souls, even though when we call to the truth, our religion, praise be to Allah, if it is presented correctly in da'wah and correctly in practice, that alone is sufficient for people to enter the religion of Allah in multitudes. But if we call to truthfulness, for example, and we are among the biggest liars of Allah's servants, what is this? Is this da'wah?
* The students: No.
* The Shaykh: Why? How can you call to truthfulness while you lie? If we call to fulfilling covenants while we are among the most treacherous people, yes, this is deception. If we call to safeguarding trusts while we are among the most dishonest people, this is not right. If our religion forbids usury (riba) and some of us practice usury, how is the da'wah? Where is the da'wah? If da'wah is not embodied by the state of the caller, in complete practice to the best of his ability, then it will diminish people's acceptance to the degree that its practice has decreased. What is it? From its practice. For this reason we say: Allah made a condition: ﴿you are the superior ones if you are believers﴾, and Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth. Is the Islamic nation today the superior one?
* The students: No.
* The Shaykh: No? You know the word "no," what does it mean? Is the Islamic nation today the superior one? No. Why? Because faith is deficient, and making the nation superior is conditioned on faith. So if faith is not present, we will be behind, and whoever among others has material strength will be the superior one. I tell you: when a person has faith and does what is required of him in material preparation, as the Messenger and his Companions, peace and blessings be upon him, did, they will be given victory over their enemy with a strength that neither they nor their enemy have. But on condition that they exert effort with two weapons: the weapon of faith and the material weapon to the best of their ability. If you want an example, look at the Battle of the Trench (Ghazwat al-Khandaq). The Battle of the Trench: ten thousand fighters from various Arab tribes gathered against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was in Medina, with the strongest weapons, and with a great power in material terms that the Muslims could not match. The Muslims did everything they could to defend themselves, to the extent that they dug a trench. They fulfilled their duty, yet they were besieged for nearly a month. So what happened? Allah the Mighty and Majestic brought a power against which neither the disbelievers nor the Muslims had any means; they had no power to resist it. What was it? The wind, a severe cold wind, which is the east wind (al-sabā), about which the Prophet ﷺ said: "I have been given victory with the east wind, and 'Ad were destroyed with the west wind (al-dabūr)."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1035), and Muslim (900/17), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Abbas.]] A severe, cold wind, and hosts of angels cast terror into the hearts of those people until they departed between sunset and sunrise. The wind overturned their cooking pots, destroyed their tents, and disturbed them with immense unrest. Even Abu Sufyan, who was the commander of the army at that time, was warming himself at the fire, even though the fire was unstable because of the intensity of the wind. Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman was near him and said: "If I wished, I could have shot him with an arrow until he died." But the Prophet ﷺ had told him: "Do not do anything."[[Narrated by Muslim (1788/99), and Ahmad (23334), and the wording is his, from the hadith of Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman.]] See, if one of these young men had been there, Allah would have enabled him to shoot him. But obedience to the command of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, which is wisdom, restrained him, otherwise killing him would have been easy. "Abu Sufyan said: 'Let each of you look at the one sitting beside him, to see who he is.'" He feared that someone from outside the army might be among them. "Hudhayfah said: 'I grasped the hand of a man close to me and said: Who are you?'"[[Narrated by Muslim (1788/99), and Ahmad (23334), from the hadith of Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman.]] This is from his cleverness. Why? So that the other would not get ahead and ask Hudhayfah: "Who are you?" In any case, I say: if the Muslims exert what they can of moral strength, which is faith, and material strength, which is what they were commanded to prepare against the disbelievers, then they will be given victory with a strength that these people cannot withstand. Do you understand?

A man heard someone reciting: ﴿Allah will surely support those who support Him. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Mighty. Those who, if We establish them in the land, establish prayer, give zakah, enjoin what is right, and forbid what is wrong. And to Allah belongs the outcome of all matters﴾ [Al-Hajj 40–41]. He said: These four attributes: ﴿they establish prayer, give zakah, enjoin what is right, and forbid what is wrong﴾. How can these attributes confront atomic, hydrogen, and chemical bombs and other such things? What should we answer? The verse concludes: ﴿And to Allah belongs the outcome of all matters.﴾ Who possesses the outcomes of matters? Who possesses the outcomes of matters? Allah the Mighty and Majestic. For this reason He placed the predicate first: ﴿to Allah belongs the outcome of all matters﴾. If the One who possesses the outcome of matters is Allah, how easy are these weapons for Allah the Mighty and Majestic! He is capable, the Exalted, of shaking their land beneath them and their weapons, with a quake that will annihilate them to the last one. Floods will destroy them, winds will carry them away as they carried the people of Hud. So a person must know that if he exerts what must be exerted of faith and material strength, as he was commanded, he will be victorious, whatever the circumstances. But unfortunately, our certainty is weak, indeed our faith is weak. We have lost faith, righteous deeds, and wisdom, and we have fallen behind to this extent. Is it clear, O brothers?

So: ﴿you are the superior ones﴾ when? ﴿if you are believers.﴾

* Benefits: Allah the Exalted forbids His believing servants from weakness in acting in the future, and from grieving over what has passed. This is because, in reality, just as it contradicts the Sharia, it contradicts reason. Why? Because grieving over what has been lost does not bring back what is lost. Is that not so? If you grieve night and day over what has passed, you will change nothing. What has passed has happened and will not change. For this reason it is part of wisdom that a person should not grieve over anything that has passed, but should say: "Allah decreed it, and He does what He wills." Likewise, weakness and feebleness toward the future, as they contradict the Sharia, contradict reason too, because reason requires that matters be faced with earnestness and resolve. In a hadith: "The intelligent one is he who holds himself accountable and works for what comes after death, and the incapable one is he who follows his desires and wishes vainly upon Allah."[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (2459), and Ibn Majah (4260), from the hadith of Shaddad ibn Aws.]]

* Among the benefits of this verse: a person, in matters other than war and jihad, should be strong of resolve, not weak nor cowardly. How many a person has been weak and cowardly and thereby lost much good, which he would have gained had he advanced, because you do not know what the outcome of the future will be.

* Among the benefits of this verse: this nation is the superior one on condition that it believes, based on His saying: ﴿and you are the superior ones if you are believers.﴾

* Among its benefits: a subtle rebuke when weakness or grief occurs, especially if we say that the "waw" here is the waw of circumstance (waw al-ḥāl), meaning: how does it befit you to weaken and grieve while you are the superior ones? For the superior one does not befit weakness or grief.

* Among the benefits of this verse: the more the faith of the nation increases, the more its supremacy increases. From where is this derived? Because He attached supremacy to faith, and what is attached to a thing increases with its increase and decreases with its decrease. A verse close to this is His saying: ﴿It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, to make it prevail over all religion﴾ [At-Tawbah 33]. "To make it prevail" (liyuzhirahu): what does it mean? It means to make it clear and raise it high. From it comes the saying "he prevailed over the mountain," meaning he rose above it. From it also comes "the back (ẓahr) of an animal," which is its highest part. So ﴿to make it prevail over all religion﴾ means to raise it high. So if you want to rise above people, then hold fast to this religion, because this religion must be the religion that is high above everything.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verses 138–139 (part 1 of 2):

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿This is a clear statement for mankind, and a guidance and an admonition for those who are mindful of Allah﴾ [Al 'Imran 138]. Does this "this" refer to the Qur'an, or to what was mentioned in His words: ﴿And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord﴾ up to the end [Al 'Imran 133]?

On this there are two opinions among the exegetes (mufassirun). Some said: it refers to the Qur'an, because this usage is frequent in the Book of Allah, such as His words, blessed and exalted: ﴿And this is a blessed reminder which We have sent down﴾ [al-Anbiya' 50], and similar verses in which the demonstrative refers to the Qur'an itself. So "this" – that is, the Qur'an – is a clear statement for mankind.

Others said: it refers to the nearest thing mentioned, because both the demonstrative and the pronoun refer to the nearest antecedent. But the preferable view is the first: that it refers to the whole Qur'an, and this verse is part of it. If we make "this" refer to the whole Qur'an, then what was mentioned in His words ﴿And hasten to forgiveness﴾ up to the end is included within it.

As for His words ﴿a clear statement (bayan) for mankind﴾: bayan is a verbal noun (masdar), or rather an ism al-masdar (a noun of the verbal action), from bayyana, yubayyinu, whose masdar is tabyin, just as baddala, yubaddilu has tabdil, and as kallama, yukallimu has taklim, while bayan is an ism al-masdar, and ism al-masdar is a kalam. When we say that "this is a bayan" and treat it as an ism al-masdar, then he has expressed the one described as "clear statement" by the noun of the action which is bayan. This is of the category of hyperbole (mubalaghah), where the described thing itself is made to be the attribute. Pay attention: when we express the described thing by the attribute, this is of the category of hyperbole, as if we have negated its being described by it, until we make it the very attribute itself. This is why they say: the saying of the speaker "so-and-so is justice (adl)" is more emphatic than their saying "so-and-so possesses justice (dhu adl)", as if he made the described thing itself the attribute. So the Qur'an does not contain clarity; rather, it is itself the clarity.

"A clear statement for mankind": who is mankind? All of mankind. Everyone who recites the Qur'an has what it indicates made clear to him. But does everyone to whom this becomes clear become guided? No. This is why He said: ﴿and a guidance and an admonition for those who are mindful of Allah﴾. Guidance (huda) here means a sign by which the mindful one is led to conclusions; admonition (mawizah) means compliance (imtithal), because admonition is the softening of hearts by mentioning what is feared or mentioning what is desired. So it is guidance, meaning indication, and admonition, meaning compliance.

Allah described the Qur'an with three attributes: a general attribute, and two specific ones. The general attribute is that it is a clear statement for mankind; the two specific ones are guidance and admonition, for none are guided by it except the mindful, and none are admonished by it except the mindful. As for those who are not like that, it is a blindness upon them – we seek refuge with Allah – a blindness upon them, and they do not increase in admonition by it. Rather Allah, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿And as for those in whose hearts is a disease, it adds to their filth upon their filth﴾, meaning filth added to their impurity, ﴿and they die while they are disbelievers﴾ [al-Tawbah 125]. Glory be to Allah! One speech has this divergent effect: for a people it is guidance and admonition, and upon another people it is blindness and filth. This is because hearts are like lands. Among lands there is good land which accepts water, grows pasture, and from which people benefit. Among them is hard ground which does not drink water but holds water, so people benefit from it. And among them is salty, barren flat land which drinks water but does not grow anything, so water only increases its harm; for when it is dry, it is possible to walk on it, but when it is wet it is not possible to walk on it, for it becomes slippery and treacherous, and yet people do not benefit from it, neither by water it retains nor by plants it produces. Likewise is the Qur'an. In relation to people, some benefit from it and increase in guidance and piety, and some do not benefit from it but increase only in blindness and misguidance, because whenever they deny a verse, their sin and punishment increase.

﴿And do not be weak, nor grieve, and you will be superior, if you are believers﴾ [Al 'Imran 139]. The (la) here is a prohibitive particle (nahiyah), and the verb after it is in the jussive mood by dropping the nun: (tahinu), whose original is (tahinuna); the nun was dropped because of the jussive. ﴿And do not be weak﴾: the address is to this community, headed by our Prophet ﷺ and his companions. Wahn means weakness, meaning: do not become weak, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And do not be weak in pursuing the enemy﴾ [al-Nisa' 104], do not become weak and cowardly. ﴿Nor grieve﴾ over what has befallen you. ﴿And you will be superior﴾. So Allah, glorified and exalted, mentioned their state of advancing and their state of retreating. In their state of advancing He forbade them from weakness, and this gives them strength and boldness. In their state of retreating He forbade them from grief, and this gives them the disposition to turn away from what lies behind them and not to look back at it. It is well known that grief occurs over what is distressing, and grieving over what has passed does not benefit a person; rather it weakens resolve, disturbs peace, and gains nothing. Therefore the Prophet ﷺ forbade them from what hinders them in the state of advancing and from what hinders them in the state of retreating. How so? I say: ﴿Do not be weak﴾ – this is what hinders in the state of advancing and boldness, so he forbade them from weakness, meaning: advance, do not be cowardly, do not hold back. ﴿Do not grieve﴾ over what would cause them to halt in the state of retreating, because when a person grieves over what has passed, he remains anxious and cannot act well. So He forbade them from this and that.

Then He said: ﴿and you will be superior﴾. The exegetes have differed over whether the waw here is a circumstantial waw (hal) or a resumptive waw (isti'nafiyyah). What do you think? If we say it is a circumstantial waw, then this prohibition is restricted to the community as long as it is superior; meaning, if it is brought low, then it may be weak and may grieve, because it is weak and cannot advance, nor can it console itself over what has passed, for with what would it console itself? Do you know what follows if we make it circumstantial? If we make the waw resumptive, so that the meaning is "do not be weak and do not grieve; you are the superior," then in it there is encouragement for the community not to become weak and not to grieve, because they are the superior, so that even if they are struck by what they are struck with, in accordance with what Allah's wisdom requires by the alternation of days among people, the final outcome is theirs. On this basis, this second view is closer to the correct, although the first view is also possible.

His words ﴿and you will be superior﴾ present a difficulty from the standpoint of grammatical inflection (i'rab). For it is known that the waw of the masculine plural is preceded by a damma, so one says: muslimun, and one does not say: muslimaun. Here He said: ﴿and you will be superior﴾ and did not say: wa antum al-a'lunu?

* A student: The waw which is preceded by a damma was dropped, because its original form is a'lawun, and after it the waw was dropped; then the first waw was changed into an alif, and the alif was dropped because of the meeting of two sukun, and the lam is fatha, which indicates the dropped waw. Therefore it becomes a'lawn.

* The Shaykh: Did you hear? He says that (al-a'lawn) originally was (al-a'la). The alif was dropped because of the meeting of two sukun, so the alif is sakin and the waw is sakin. When the alif is dropped because of the meeting of two sukun, the vowel that precedes it must remain as it is, and what is the vowel before it? A fatha. For if you made it a damma, it would not be clear that there is a dropped alif; if you made the lam a damma (al-a'lun), it would not be clear that there is a dropped alif. So the fatha must remain, to indicate the dropped alif because of the meeting of two sukun. So the difficulty is removed. Is that correct? ﴿and you will be superior﴾.

* A student: The words of the Exalted: ﴿So travel through the earth﴾. Some people derive from this verse the gathering of the traces of earlier peoples, and they spend money on relics and travel (...)?

* The Shaykh: He says that the words of the Exalted ﴿So travel through the earth﴾ are used as evidence by some who are infatuated with collecting relics, who take an ancient piece that is not worth a qirsh for many dirhams. Does this fall under it? The answer is: no, it does not fall under it. Even those who collect relics do not intend by them consideration (i'tibar) and that the end of those who were of that condition is destruction and ruin; rather they are things their souls incline toward, just as we have heard and hear often that some people collect (...) or postage stamps, to the extent that one buys a stamp worth five qurush for perhaps fifty riyals.

* The student: Millions of pounds sterling, if the stamp differs from... the complete one, I mean, sixty million pounds sterling, Shaykh.

* The Shaykh: There is no power nor strength except with Allah! Well, in any case, what we see is that if there is a legitimate benefit in it, then there is no harm; otherwise, leaving it is better.

* A student: Shaykh, may Allah be good to you, what is the difference between tourism (siyahah) and travel (sayr)?

* The Shaykh: There is no difference between them.

* The student: Tourism is travel?

* The Shaykh: Yes, tourism on the earth means travelling in it.

* The student: So there is no restriction to four months if it is the same thing?

* The Shaykh: No, no, as I say: travel in the earth for four months.

* The student: Shaykh, may Allah be good to you, one who travels in the earth for a legitimate purpose, such as treatment for example, but his companion is doing something forbidden, is he prevented from travelling?

* The Shaykh: If he cannot travel for treatment except by committing this forbidden act, then it becomes forbidden, because treatment by means of what is forbidden is forbidden. Treatment by means of what is forbidden is forbidden, because committing a forbidden act is a certain harm, while recovery from illness is an expected benefit that is not certain. Were it not so, we would say: whoever needs to eat pork for treatment may eat it, although it is not permitted. This is the difference between the permissibility of eating pork out of hunger and eating pork for seeking a cure: the second is forbidden and the first is permitted, because eating meat in hunger certainly benefits, for it removes hunger and sustains a person's life, but treating by the forbidden may succeed or may not succeed. So he commits a certain corruption for the sake of an anticipated benefit that is imagined; and if you wish, say it is also a preponderant benefit, but the preponderant is not like the certain. This is why it has come in the hadith: "Indeed Allah has not placed your cure in what He has forbidden to you" [Narrated by 'Abd al-Razzaq (17097) and Ibn Abi Shaybah (23839), from the saying of Ibn Mas'ud], and this is true. But suppose some medicines contain some pork, yet it has no effect on taste or smell; is it permissible or not?

* A student: It is permissible.

* The Shaykh: It is permissible?

* A student: Does one know that these medicines contain pork? It is not permissible.

* The Shaykh: Yes, one knows, one knows, but it is a small part that has no effect. Is it absolutely not permissible in any circumstances?

* A student: It is permissible.

* A student: This medicine is not eaten; it is used as valves for the heart; it is only placed, not eaten.

* The Shaykh: Yes, you mean the impure substance.

* The student: This is what we know regarding pork: it is used for treatment only, meaning tissue for a valve, which is merely placed, not eaten. That is, there is no medicine into which food is placed.

* The Shaykh: I gave it as an example. Let us suppose a medicine contains alcohol. Leave aside pork; this alcohol shows neither its effect nor its taste. Is it permissible? We say: yes, and we take as evidence for this the words of the Prophet ﷺ: "Indeed water is pure; nothing makes it impure except what changes its taste, colour, or smell" [Narrated by Abu Dawud (66) and al-Tirmidhi (66), from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri without the final sentence containing the exception; the exception was narrated by Ibn Majah (521) from the hadith of Abu Umamah al-Bahili]. Although this exception is weak, the scholars agree upon its ruling: that water is pure and is not made impure except by what alters its smell. If water is not made impure and it is permissible for you to perform ablution with it and drink it, then so too is other than it. But using pork meat or pork fat in a manner that does not reach the body, meaning one does not eat it, is it permissible? We say: yes, it is permissible. So if it were stipulated that a person be prescribed to anoint himself with pork fat, and he anointed with it, but when he wishes to pray he washes it off, then that is permissible. Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, stated this explicitly in his Fatawa, and it is correct, because it does no harm, like greasing ships with impure fat and what resembles it.

* * *

I seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, glorified and exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, there have passed before you precedents, so travel through the earth﴾. What is meant by "precedents" (sunan) here?

* A student: Sunan means what Allah has established... the Messenger ﷺ.

* The Shaykh: Sunan means, for example, voluntary prayer and voluntary fasting.

* A student: The earlier nations.

* The Shaykh: The earlier nations; meaning sunan is applied to nations. That is one opinion. The second opinion?

* Students: The ways.

* The Shaykh: The ways. That is, the ways of Allah, mighty and majestic, passed on those who denied the messengers.

His words: ﴿travel through the earth﴾: is what is meant the travel of the feet or the travel of the heart?

* A student: Both.

* The Shaykh: Yes, both: the travel of the heart and the travel of the feet. Well, is it derived from this verse that a person should read history?

* The student: Yes.

* The Shaykh: Yes, because reading history is in reality travel through the earth. Now, His words ﴿travel through the earth﴾: (fi) here means what?

* A student: It means (ala, upon).

* The Shaykh: It means (ala, upon), or is (fi) used for location?

* The student: For location, but the exegetes agreed that it means (ala), because it is not possible to travel inside the earth.

* The Shaykh: So it is originally for location, and it comes for other than location according to context.

What do you say about his ﷺ words: "A woman entered the Fire because of a cat which she confined"? [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3318) and Muslim (2242/151), from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar.]

* The student: For the sake of.

* The Shaykh: For causation?

* A student: Yes.

* A student: It differs according to context.

* The Shaykh: Correct.

His words, exalted: ﴿Then see how was the end of those who denied﴾. Where is the object of (see)?

* A student: The clause (how was).

* The Shaykh: The clause (how), and where is the predicate of (was)?

* The student: The predicate of (was) is placed before it.

* The Shaykh: Where is it?

* The student: (How).

* The Shaykh: (How) is placed first. Is this fronting obligatory or permissible here?

* The student: Obligatory.

* The Shaykh: Obligatory. Why?

* The student: Because (how) is an interrogative particle, and interrogative particles hold the front position.

* The Shaykh: Yes, correct: the predicate of (how) is fronted obligatorily, because it is an interrogative, and interrogation has the front of the sentence.

His words, exalted: ﴿This is a clear statement for mankind﴾. (This) – what does the demonstrative refer to?

* A student: The Qur'an.

* The Shaykh: The Qur'an. Is there another opinion?

* A student: There is another opinion that what preceded is the statement, and the first opinion is that it is the Qur'an in general.

* The Shaykh: The Qur'an in general. Which of them is preferable?

* The student: The nearer, the Qur'an.

* The Shaykh: It is preferable to say: the Qur'an, because it is more general; whenever something is more general, it is preferable, because it is more comprehensive. Well, why did He distinguish with His words: ﴿a clear statement for mankind, and a guidance and an admonition for those who are mindful of Allah﴾?

* A student: Because clarity is a general attribute, so it is for the believer and for the non-believer. But whomever Allah guides, for him it is guidance and admonition, and whomever He does not guide, for him it is clarity.

* The Shaykh: Yes, meaning it is a clarification for all, but none are guided by it and admonished by it except the mindful.

Here He stated "clear statement" without restriction: ﴿This is a clear statement for mankind﴾. If we say it is the Qur'an, in what is there clarity? Is it in every matter, or only in matters of worship?

* A student: In all things: in narratives, in rulings, and in creed.

* The Shaykh: In everything. Do you have evidence from the Qur'an that it is general in everything?

* The student: Yes.

* A student: The words of the Exalted: ﴿And We have sent down to you the Book as an explanation of all things﴾ [al-Nahl 89].

* The Shaykh: The words of the Exalted: ﴿And We have sent down to you the Book as an explanation of all things﴾ – clear.

Well, Allah the Exalted said: ﴿This is a clear statement for mankind, and a guidance and an admonition for those who are mindful of Allah﴾.

* Benefitting from this noble verse: that the Qur'an is a clear statement for mankind in every matter. It is general in terms of clarification and general in terms of the one to whom clarification is made. We take the generality of the recipients from His words ﴿for mankind﴾, and the comprehensiveness of the clarification from the omission of the object of the verb, and omission of the object indicates generality: this is a clear statement for mankind in everything. This is supported by the verse we mentioned earlier, His words: ﴿And We have sent down to you the Book as an explanation of all things﴾.

* Among its benefits: that the Qur'an is suitable for guidance for both believer and disbeliever, as in His words ﴿for mankind﴾, which includes both believer and disbeliever.

* Among its benefits also: it is a guidance only for the God-fearing (al-muttaqin), meaning that only the God-fearing benefit from it, due to His saying: ﴿and a guidance and an admonition for the God-fearing﴾.

* And among its benefits also: whoever is not admonished by the Qur'an should suspect himself. From where is this derived? From His saying: ﴿for the God-fearing﴾. So if you are not admonished by the Qur'an, then suspect yourself, for there is a trial within you. Likewise, whoever is not restrained by his prayer from indecency and wrongdoing should suspect himself, for his prayer is deficient. This is because the One who informed us that prayer restrains from indecency and wrongdoing is Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and His report is true and corresponds to reality. So if a person knows from the reality of his own self that his prayer does not restrain him from indecency and wrongdoing, then he should suspect himself, because Allah's report cannot be doubted. For this reason, one of the early generation (al-salaf) said: "Whoever is not restrained by his prayer from indecency and wrongdoing, his prayer only increases him in distance from Allah."[[Narrated by Sa'id ibn Mansur in his Tafsir (1705), and Abu Dawud in al-Zuhd (134), from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud.]] We ask Allah for well-being, and we ask Allah to help us.
Here, if you are not admonished by the Qur'an, then suspect yourself of not being God-fearing, because the God-fearing person must be admonished by the Qur'an.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the virtue of taqwa (God-consciousness), and that it is a cause of being guided and of being admonished by the Qur'an.

* Among its benefits: the more a person increases in taqwa, the more guidance and admonition he gains. Why? Because a ruling attached to a description grows stronger with its strength and weakens with its weakness. So since guidance and admonition are attached to taqwa, they must increase and grow stronger with taqwa, and weaken and decrease with its absence. Is it clear?

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And do not weaken, nor grieve, for you will be the superior ones if you are believers.﴾

* In this verse: a prohibition to the believers from weakness (al-wahn). ﴿And do not weaken, nor grieve, for you will be the superior ones.﴾ A human being is in reality between two times: a past time and a future time. If good has escaped him or evil has befallen him in the past, his state is grief; he grieves over what has passed. In the future, if he becomes weak and cowardly, he loses good in proportion to his weakness and cowardice. For this reason He said: ﴿do not weaken﴾, meaning from acting in the future, ﴿nor grieve﴾ over what befell you in the past. So do not grieve over what befell you in the past, because you are the superior ones, and whoever is superior, the outcome will be his. Whatever is in the future, do not be weak in it nor be cowardly in it, for the outcome belongs to you, since you are the superior ones.

His saying: ﴿do not weaken, nor grieve, for you will be the superior ones﴾: we have mentioned that this sentence may be a circumstantial clause (ḥāliyyah), meaning: while you are the superior ones, because the superior one does not befit weakness or grief. We have also mentioned that it may be a new independent statement (isti'nāfiyyah) in which Allah affirms the supremacy of the believers. When their supremacy is established, their state requires what? That they should not weaken and should not grieve. The two meanings are interrelated, for whoever believes that he is the superior one will not be cowardly nor grieve, and whoever's state is superiority will likewise not weaken nor grieve.

His saying: ﴿if you are believers﴾: this is a condition for superiority. That is: you are the superior ones while being believers. Faith, as you know, is more specific than Islam, because Islam can be found in the hypocrite and in the one whose faith is weak, whereas faith exists only in one whose faith is complete, the true believer. For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The Bedouins say, "We have believed."﴾ See, the desert Bedouins say "We have believed." ﴿Say, "You have not believed, but say, 'We have submitted,'"﴾ Why? He said: ﴿and faith has not yet entered your hearts﴾ [Al-Hujurat 14]. Until now faith has not entered the heart. You have Islam, but you do not have faith yet, though faith is near to you, because His saying "lamma" (not yet) is a negation particle that indicates the nearness of what is negated. That is, faith will soon enter your hearts, but not yet.

So we say: this nation is the superior one on a condition, what is it? The condition of faith. As for if it does not have faith, it has no covenant with Allah for victory, because the binding covenant between Allah and His servants regarding victory is that victory is reciprocal: ﴿O you who believe, if you support Allah, He will support you and make firm your feet﴾ [Muhammad 7], and ﴿Allah will surely support those who support Him. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Mighty﴾ [Al-Hajj 40]. But if there is no support of Allah the Mighty and Majestic from us, then Allah's support may be withheld; that is, it is not guaranteed.

Alright, then you are the superior ones if you are believers. The signs of faith are many, among them: that a person does not fear anyone among the creation in implementing the command of Allah. A person should not fear anyone among the creation in implementing Allah's command. If he fears anyone among the creation, then he is not a believer. The evidence for this is His saying: ﴿It is only Satan who frightens his allies, so do not fear them, but fear Me, if you are believers﴾ [Al 'Imran 175]. ﴿He frightens his allies﴾: that is, he causes fear to fall upon his allies? 
* Student: No.
* The Shaykh: Yes. For this reason we say that His saying ﴿his allies﴾ is the second object of "yukhawwif" (he frightens), and the first object is omitted. The meaning of the sentence is: he frightens you with his allies, that is, he places fear in your hearts from his allies. Is it clear? He the Exalted said: ﴿so do not fear them, but fear Me, if you are believers﴾. ﴿Those to whom people said, "Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them."﴾ So what did they say? They said: ﴿Sufficient for us is Allah, and He is the best Disposer of affairs﴾ [Al 'Imran 173]. So if Satan frightens his allies, who are the disbelievers, it is not permissible for us to fear them. It is not permissible for us to fear them; rather, we do what Allah has commanded us. However, Allah's command to us to fight the disbelievers applies only when we have a strength with which we can fight them. As for fighting them with weapons that are not theirs and far less than theirs, this is considered recklessness. For this reason the believers were not commanded to wage jihad until they had might and power. As for when they did not have it, then no. But this entails that it is obligatory upon us to arm ourselves to fight them until the religion is for Allah. The address here, regarding the obligation to arm oneself, is to those in authority, not to individuals, because individuals cannot undertake this. But the rulers of the Muslims must establish a vast, armed army with the most modern weapons, in order to fight ﴿those who do not believe in Allah or in the Last Day, and do not forbid what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, and do not adopt the religion of truth from those who were given the Scripture, until they give the jizyah (poll tax) willingly while they are humbled﴾ [At-Tawbah 29]. But unfortunately, today we have lost even the weapon of da'wah (calling to Islam). We do not find anyone calling as he should, while we see the Christians in full force in calling to the falsehood they hold. They spend great sums of money and risk themselves in unknown places, on roads, in deserts. The priest among them carries a piece of bread and a jug of water and travels through wastelands in order to call one Muslim to become Christian. As for us, unfortunately, we do not carry this moral strength in our souls, even though when we call to the truth, our religion, praise be to Allah, if it is presented correctly in da'wah and correctly in practice, that alone is sufficient for people to enter the religion of Allah in multitudes. But if we call to truthfulness, for example, and we are among the biggest liars of Allah's servants, what is this? Is this da'wah?
* The students: No.
* The Shaykh: Why? How can you call to truthfulness while you lie? If we call to fulfilling covenants while we are among the most treacherous people, yes, this is deception. If we call to safeguarding trusts while we are among the most dishonest people, this is not right. If our religion forbids usury (riba) and some of us practice usury, how is the da'wah? Where is the da'wah? If da'wah is not embodied by the state of the caller, in complete practice to the best of his ability, then it will diminish people's acceptance to the degree that its practice has decreased. What is it? From its practice. For this reason we say: Allah made a condition: ﴿you are the superior ones if you are believers﴾, and Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth. Is the Islamic nation today the superior one?
* The students: No.
* The Shaykh: No? You know the word "no," what does it mean? Is the Islamic nation today the superior one? No. Why? Because faith is deficient, and making the nation superior is conditioned on faith. So if faith is not present, we will be behind, and whoever among others has material strength will be the superior one. I tell you: when a person has faith and does what is required of him in material preparation, as the Messenger and his Companions, peace and blessings be upon him, did, they will be given victory over their enemy with a strength that neither they nor their enemy have. But on condition that they exert effort with two weapons: the weapon of faith and the material weapon to the best of their ability. If you want an example, look at the Battle of the Trench (Ghazwat al-Khandaq). The Battle of the Trench: ten thousand fighters from various Arab tribes gathered against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was in Medina, with the strongest weapons, and with a great power in material terms that the Muslims could not match. The Muslims did everything they could to defend themselves, to the extent that they dug a trench. They fulfilled their duty, yet they were besieged for nearly a month. So what happened? Allah the Mighty and Majestic brought a power against which neither the disbelievers nor the Muslims had any means; they had no power to resist it. What was it? The wind, a severe cold wind, which is the east wind (al-sabā), about which the Prophet ﷺ said: "I have been given victory with the east wind, and 'Ad were destroyed with the west wind (al-dabūr)."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1035), and Muslim (900/17), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Abbas.]] A severe, cold wind, and hosts of angels cast terror into the hearts of those people until they departed between sunset and sunrise. The wind overturned their cooking pots, destroyed their tents, and disturbed them with immense unrest. Even Abu Sufyan, who was the commander of the army at that time, was warming himself at the fire, even though the fire was unstable because of the intensity of the wind. Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman was near him and said: "If I wished, I could have shot him with an arrow until he died." But the Prophet ﷺ had told him: "Do not do anything."[[Narrated by Muslim (1788/99), and Ahmad (23334), and the wording is his, from the hadith of Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman.]] See, if one of these young men had been there, Allah would have enabled him to shoot him. But obedience to the command of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, which is wisdom, restrained him, otherwise killing him would have been easy. "Abu Sufyan said: 'Let each of you look at the one sitting beside him, to see who he is.'" He feared that someone from outside the army might be among them. "Hudhayfah said: 'I grasped the hand of a man close to me and said: Who are you?'"[[Narrated by Muslim (1788/99), and Ahmad (23334), from the hadith of Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman.]] This is from his cleverness. Why? So that the other would not get ahead and ask Hudhayfah: "Who are you?" In any case, I say: if the Muslims exert what they can of moral strength, which is faith, and material strength, which is what they were commanded to prepare against the disbelievers, then they will be given victory with a strength that these people cannot withstand. Do you understand?

A man heard someone reciting: ﴿Allah will surely support those who support Him. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Mighty. Those who, if We establish them in the land, establish prayer, give zakah, enjoin what is right, and forbid what is wrong. And to Allah belongs the outcome of all matters﴾ [Al-Hajj 40–41]. He said: These four attributes: ﴿they establish prayer, give zakah, enjoin what is right, and forbid what is wrong﴾. How can these attributes confront atomic, hydrogen, and chemical bombs and other such things? What should we answer? The verse concludes: ﴿And to Allah belongs the outcome of all matters.﴾ Who possesses the outcomes of matters? Who possesses the outcomes of matters? Allah the Mighty and Majestic. For this reason He placed the predicate first: ﴿to Allah belongs the outcome of all matters﴾. If the One who possesses the outcome of matters is Allah, how easy are these weapons for Allah the Mighty and Majestic! He is capable, the Exalted, of shaking their land beneath them and their weapons, with a quake that will annihilate them to the last one. Floods will destroy them, winds will carry them away as they carried the people of Hud. So a person must know that if he exerts what must be exerted of faith and material strength, as he was commanded, he will be victorious, whatever the circumstances. But unfortunately, our certainty is weak, indeed our faith is weak. We have lost faith, righteous deeds, and wisdom, and we have fallen behind to this extent. Is it clear, O brothers?

So: ﴿you are the superior ones﴾ when? ﴿if you are believers.﴾

* Benefits: Allah the Exalted forbids His believing servants from weakness in acting in the future, and from grieving over what has passed. This is because, in reality, just as it contradicts the Sharia, it contradicts reason. Why? Because grieving over what has been lost does not bring back what is lost. Is that not so? If you grieve night and day over what has passed, you will change nothing. What has passed has happened and will not change. For this reason it is part of wisdom that a person should not grieve over anything that has passed, but should say: "Allah decreed it, and He does what He wills." Likewise, weakness and feebleness toward the future, as they contradict the Sharia, contradict reason too, because reason requires that matters be faced with earnestness and resolve. In a hadith: "The intelligent one is he who holds himself accountable and works for what comes after death, and the incapable one is he who follows his desires and wishes vainly upon Allah."[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (2459), and Ibn Majah (4260), from the hadith of Shaddad ibn Aws.]]

* Among the benefits of this verse: a person, in matters other than war and jihad, should be strong of resolve, not weak nor cowardly. How many a person has been weak and cowardly and thereby lost much good, which he would have gained had he advanced, because you do not know what the outcome of the future will be.

* Among the benefits of this verse: this nation is the superior one on condition that it believes, based on His saying: ﴿and you are the superior ones if you are believers.﴾

* Among its benefits: a subtle rebuke when weakness or grief occurs, especially if we say that the "waw" here is the waw of circumstance (waw al-ḥāl), meaning: how does it befit you to weaken and grieve while you are the superior ones? For the superior one does not befit weakness or grief.

* Among the benefits of this verse: the more the faith of the nation increases, the more its supremacy increases. From where is this derived? Because He attached supremacy to faith, and what is attached to a thing increases with its increase and decreases with its decrease. A verse close to this is His saying: ﴿It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, to make it prevail over all religion﴾ [At-Tawbah 33]. "To make it prevail" (liyuzhirahu): what does it mean? It means to make it clear and raise it high. From it comes the saying "he prevailed over the mountain," meaning he rose above it. From it also comes "the back (ẓahr) of an animal," which is its highest part. So ﴿to make it prevail over all religion﴾ means to raise it high. So if you want to rise above people, then hold fast to this religion, because this religion must be the religion that is high above everything.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verse 140 (part 1 of 2):

Then Allah the Exalted said, consoling the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, with His words: ﴿If a wound touches you, a similar wound has touched the people﴾ [Al 'Imran 140]. ﴿If a wound touches you﴾. In this word there is a reading, ﴿qurh﴾ (with a *damma* on the *qaf*), in both places: ﴿a similar qurh has touched the people﴾. It has been said that the two readings have the same meaning, and that *qarh* and *qurh* both mean a wound. It has also been said that *qurh* is the wound and *qarh* is the pain of the wound. And even if we say that the two words differ in meaning, the two opinions are mutually necessary, because *qarh* is a necessary consequence of the wound, which is *qurh*. The person who is wounded must be in pain. The meaning is: if you are struck by wounds and pain, then the people have been struck by a similar wound and pain.

Allah the Exalted said in the same context of the verses: ﴿Why, when a calamity struck you, though you had struck (the enemy with) twice as much, did you say, "How is this?" Say, "It is from yourselves"﴾ [Al 'Imran 165]. So if a calamity struck you, you had struck them with twice as much at Uhud: seventy of you were killed. But at Badr, seventy of your enemy were killed and seventy were taken prisoner. That is double. Here He says: ﴿a similar wound has touched the people﴾. In this there is consolation for the believers, because when a person knows that his enemy has been struck with the same as what struck him, the calamity becomes easier for him to bear. Al-Khansa', mourning her brother Sakhr, said:

*Were it not for the great number of those weeping around me over their brothers,*
*I would have killed myself.*
*They do not weep as I weep for my brother, but I console myself about him*
*through consolation (by comparison).*

To this Allah pointed in the Qur'an when He said: ﴿And it will not benefit you today, since you did wrong, that you are sharing in the punishment﴾ [Az-Zukhruf 39]. Sharing in the punishment did not benefit them, and did not lighten their pain. But Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says to the believers: if you have been struck by a wound, your enemy has been struck by a similar wound. Moreover, in another verse Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And do not weaken in pursuit of the people﴾ [An-Nisa' 104]. Look how great the consolation is. ﴿Do not weaken in pursuit of the people﴾, meaning in seeking them out: do not be weak in pursuing them. Seek them out and kill them. ﴿If you are suffering pain, then they suffer pain as you suffer pain﴾ [An-Nisa' 104]. Allah has spoken the truth. Is that not so? What more? ﴿and you hope﴾. This is a subtle point: ﴿and you hope from Allah for what they do not hope﴾ [An-Nisa' 104]. This is the great benefit. They hope for nothing; they only want exaltation and arrogance. They went out from their homes insolently and to be seen by people. But what do you hope for? You hope for Paradise and for martyrdom. For this reason He said: ﴿you hope from Allah for what they do not hope﴾. And what did the Companions say to Abu Sufyan at Uhud when he said: "A day for a day: Badr, and war is (a matter of) turns"? That is, one time for us and one time against us. They said: "No, they are not equal. Our slain are in Paradise and your slain are in the Fire"[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (3039), and Ahmad (2609), and the wording is his, from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Abbas.]]. We seek refuge with Allah.

So the believers do not think that their enemy is not struck with pain, or with a wound. He is struck. The believers are not dismayed by his false propaganda, that he will do this and do that and do that. No, they are not dismayed. If one of them is killed, they feel the pain of that one who was killed, just as if one of us were killed, we would feel his pain. But we hope from Allah for what they do not hope. For this reason He said: ﴿If a wound touches you, a similar wound has touched the people﴾. This is an exchange for that.

Then He said: ﴿And those days We alternate among the people﴾. ﴿Those﴾ is a demonstrative noun (*ism ishara*). The meaning: these days, We alternate them among the people. That is, We make them turns (*duwal*): sometimes one party prevails over another, and sometimes that party prevails over this one. Look at His words ﴿We alternate them﴾, which came in the form of the first-person plural of majesty (*nun al-'azama*), indicating that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in the perfection of His authority and greatness, causes people to prevail over one another. So sometimes the days belong to these, and sometimes the days belong to those. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is the One in whose hand is the command. Even the dominance may at times go to His enemies over His allies, for a wisdom He intends. He explained this with His words: ﴿and that Allah may know those who believe﴾, to its end.

* Student: Regarding the jihad against the disbelievers in our time. For example, Saudi Arabia and Senegal are (two) countries. If the government of a country wants to fight the disbelievers, other countries oppose them. Why do you tire yourself (...)? If it were one nation, for example one state, with all Muslims having one leader, it would be possible for them to agree on jihad. But now their agreement on jihad is very difficult?
* The Shaykh: Do you have an Islamic nation now according to what Allah wants from it? I ask you now: do you have a nation according to what Allah wants from it?
* Student: Except those whom Allah has mercy on.
* The Shaykh: Answer. You mentioned the exception without the thing excepted.
* Student: As for the rulers, no.
* The Shaykh: No, not even the peoples. Do you not know that there are people who claim to be Muslims in other lands, and they say about the scholars of Saudi Arabia what they say? So the disagreement is not only among the rulers. It is even among the scholars, even among the principles. Now the one who calls to monotheism (*tawhid*) is called a strict, rigid, obstinate, extremist Wahhabi. Well, where is the Islamic nation? It is feared that war will break out among the Islamic nation. This is a problem. The matter needs treatment at its roots. How good it would be if the scholars of the Muslims gathered with sincere intention, sincerity, and counsel to Allah, to His Book, to His Messenger, to the leaders of the Muslims and their common folk, and studied the conditions of the Muslims.
* Student: And they make the leader one only.
* Another student: May Allah be good to you. Shaykh, we find that jihad has died in people's hearts. The common people do not know that jihad was prescribed for this nation as an obligation. They rarely hear about jihad; it is as if it were fictional stories. Because, O Shaykh, we see that the scholars do not stir the people, and they also do not call for the obligation of jihad as they call for the other obligations. So why this great distance from jihad, and from explaining it..?
* The Shaykh: There is no doubt that it must be made clear that the disbelievers are enemies to us, that we must prepare for them, that we must fear their evil, and that they sometimes conceal poison in honey. Indeed, often. But unfortunately we do not have this spirit. The rulings of jihad about which the jurists, may Allah have mercy on them, wrote books, composed works, are not known to the general body of students of knowledge. They do not know them. And had it not been for the Gulf crisis, the Gulf crisis, people began to feel something of jihad, a matter or two. Yes indeed.
* Student: O Shaykh, why do the scholars call for (...), like..
* The Shaykh: By Allah, I say: I ask Allah to set right our bellies first, bellies in which there is decay. We ask Allah for safety.
* Student: May Allah pardon you, O Shaykh. You mentioned that it is recklessness and throwing oneself into destruction for us to confront our enemies when we do not have strength like their strength. How do we reconcile, O Shaykh, this with our being told to prepare for them, when we will not be able to reach the level of technology they have reached?
* The Shaykh: But we have not even thought about this. Even until now, I say, even some Arab countries that form armies and weapons, I do not think it occurs to them that these are for fighting the disbelievers.
* Student: There is no doubt.
* The Shaykh: There is no doubt. So the foundation itself is ruined. If you built a wall of mud over a pond, a body of water, would it stand firm for the roof built upon the wall? No. You cannot know (...) the mud and the water. Would it collapse? Yes indeed. It requires intention. If you asked many of the Arab leaders now, or if you wish, the leaders of the Muslims, "Why do you form an army?", he would say: "I fear my neighbors," or "he fears that his people will rise up against him, and he wants to remain in power."
* Student: What should we do? Should we despair and surrender to this?
* The Shaykh: No, we do not despair. Praise be to Allah, there is now an opening. In this Gulf war there are people, praise be to Allah, from the Saudis and from non-Saudi Gulf sons, of whom we hear that they do not ride (vehicles) except in the name of Allah, and they do not fight except in the name of Allah, and that they pray before they board the airplanes, for example, or before they board the ships. All of this is good. There is now a good awakening.
* Student: Shaykh, may Allah be good to you. The Qur'an was revealed in the language of the Arabs, and Allah, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿This is an explanation for mankind﴾, all people. As for the non-Arabs, who are not Arabs, what are the aspects (...) that it should be an explanation for them?
* The Shaykh: The answer to this, and it is a proper difficulty, is said: how was the Qur'an, being in Arabic, an explanation for all people, including the non-Arabs who do not know the language of the Arabs? We say: because Allah will appoint for them someone who conveys it to them. For this reason, many of the Muslim scholars now who have a true standing in knowledge and religion, many of them are non-Arabs. If you wish, be amazed that the sole reference for most people in the Arabic language was the work composed by the non-Arab al-Fayruzabadi, *al-Qamus al-Muhit*. *al-Qamus al-Muhit* is the reference to which most people now turn in language. In grammar, who is the imam of the Basrans? Sibawayh. Sibawayh, in the non-Arabic language: "the smell of apples." Is that right? Yes indeed. So the conclusion is that, praise be to Allah, the non-Arabs have been reached by the Qur'an through an intermediary. It is not necessary that they take from the Qur'an itself. Some of them became Arabized, and their tongue became Arabic.
* Student: May Allah reward you with good. We mentioned in the context of the verses that the Muslims should not fight until they prepare with the strength of faith and material strength. Meanwhile we have heard that jihad in Afghanistan began with a small few, meaning four people, who achieved very striking results. How is this matter?
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed, there is no problem. Because these people, you know from the fighting of the Afghans, have readiness and strength. The nature of their land is suitable for guerrilla warfare, and they began this way. Then they began taking a little at a time, on the mountain peaks, in the caves, in the trees, and elsewhere, and they obtained much good.
* Student: Is it not a starting point, O Shaykh, in jihad for the general Ummah?
* The Shaykh: The starting points are many, but we ask Allah to make easy the one who sets out. *MunTaLaq* with a *fatha* on the *lam* is found (one who is able), but *munTaLiq* with a *kasra* on the *lam* is one whose wing is broken. God willing, it will be so, God willing.
* Student: Shaykh, the Prophet ﷺ says, if it is established: "Twelve thousand will not be defeated for lack of numbers"[[Narrated by Abu Dawud (2611), and al-Tirmidhi (1555), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Abbas.]]. So what is our position on this hadith, O Shaykh, when we now have the Saudi army more than many times over, and it has military equipment of more than twelve thousand?
* The Shaykh: Yes, but its meaning (...). But it may be defeated without lack of numbers. It may be defeated from another direction, as we mentioned: the mud wall erected over a pond of water.
* Student: You mentioned, O Shaykh, that now, praise be to Allah, and we heard this (...)?
* The Shaykh: Good. That does not contradict it, but how many? If we assume they are forty, fifty, a hundred (...).

\* \* \*

* Student: I seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿Do not weaken or grieve, and you will be superior if you are (true) believers. If a wound touches you, a similar wound has touched the people, and those days We alternate among the people, and that Allah may know those who believe, and take martyrs from among you. And Allah does not like wrongdoers. And that Allah may purify those who believe and destroy the disbelievers. Do you think that you will enter Paradise while Allah has not yet made evident those of you who fought and made evident those who are patient? And you had certainly wished for death before you encountered it. Now you have seen it, while you were looking on. And Muhammad is not but a messenger; (other) messengers have passed on before him. So if he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels? And whoever turns back on his heels will not harm Allah at all; and Allah will reward the grateful. And it is not for a soul to die except by permission of Allah, at an appointed time. And whoever desires the reward of this world — We will give it to him, and whoever desires the reward of the Hereafter — We will give it to him. And We will reward the grateful﴾ [Al 'Imran 139–145].
* The Shaykh: I seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿If a wound touches you, a similar wound has touched the people, and those days We alternate among the people, and that Allah may know those who believe, and take martyrs from among you. And Allah does not like wrongdoers.﴾

It has already passed for us that the meaning of His words ﴿If a wound touches you, a similar wound has touched the people﴾ is consolation. That is, if you were struck at Uhud, then the people have been struck with a similar wound. In the same battle too, some of the polytheists were killed, and they were defeated, had it not been that Allah, glorified and exalted, in His wisdom, willed that some of the troops would oppose the position the Prophet ﷺ had ordered them to take. So what happened afterward was the opposite of what was intended.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And those days We alternate among the people﴾. ﴿Those days﴾: the indicated object here is distant, but in reality it is near, because the days are time, and so they are near. But since among the days some are distant and some are near, the aspect of distance was given precedence: ﴿those days We alternate among the people﴾, that is, We make them turns among them. Sometimes the turn is for these over those, and sometimes the turn is for these over those. At Badr the turn was against the polytheists, and at Uhud the turn was against the believers. This one time and that one another time, for great wisdoms that Allah, glorified and exalted, explained afterward.

His words ﴿We alternate them among the people﴾ include the alternation between one nation and another, and also include the alternation within a single person. A person finds one day joy and another day sorrow, as the poet said:

*One day is against us and one day is for us,*
*and one day we are made to suffer and one day we are made to rejoice.*

So the world is like this: it does not remain in one state. For this reason it is said: lasting in one state is impossible. Days are turns (*duwal*).

His words ﴿and that Allah may know those who believe among you﴾: the "wa" here is a conjunction particle (*harf 'atf*). What is the thing conjoined to? Is it the sentence that preceded: ﴿and those days We alternate among the people﴾? We say: No, because ﴿and that Allah may know﴾ is a cause-clause (*ta'lil*) for the preceding sentence, ﴿and those days We alternate among the people﴾, and the cause is not the effect, and it is not correct to conjoin it to it, because the cause is the reason for the existence of the effect. So there is something conjoined to, and it is to be estimated according to what suits the context. What suits it here is that we say: the estimate is: "so that by this the complete authority of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, may become manifest; We alternate them among the people, so that by this the complete authority of Allah may become manifest, and that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is the One who has the judgment, judging among His servants as He wills, abandoning some peoples and granting victory to others, bringing hardship and bringing ease, until by this the complete authority of Him, glorified and exalted, becomes manifest. Even among creatures, some have good in them and some have evil in them. All of this so that the complete authority of the Most High, the Great, glorified be He, may appear to people." ﴿and that Allah may know﴾. So the "wa" here is a conjunction particle. And what is the thing conjoined to?

* Student: So that the complete authority of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, may become manifest.
* The Shaykh: It is elided; its estimate is: so that by this the complete authority of Allah may become manifest.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verse 140 (part 2 of 2):

﴿And that Allah may know those who believe﴾ is a knowledge of existence (ʿilm wujūd), and a knowledge that results in recompense. We say this because Allah, exalted is He, already knew those who believe before they believed. Allah's knowledge of things is eternal and pre-existent. He, glorified and exalted, knows what was and what will be until the Day of Resurrection. However, He knows it with knowledge of existence, meaning He knows it as existing. As for prior knowledge, He knows that it will come into existence. There is a difference between His knowing a thing as existing while it exists and His knowing a thing as something that will come into existence. This is the first point. The second point: He knows it with knowledge that results in recompense, which occurs when faith comes into existence or is lost. Allah's prior knowledge does not result in recompense, because the believer did not yet exist, so that he could be rewarded or not rewarded. With this, the objection that arises regarding this sentence is removed, and the answer to the objection is obtained. The objection is: Allah, exalted is He, knew those who believe beforehand, for He, glorified and exalted, wrote in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz) the decrees of everything until the Day of Resurrection, and He knew the believer from others beforehand. So how can He say: ﴿and that He may know﴾? What is the answer? We say: that He may know with knowledge of existence, meaning that the thing has come into being, and the knowledge relating to the existent is different from its relation to the non-existent that will come into being. Is that not so? The second: that He knows it with knowledge that results in recompense, because His prior knowledge that it will come into being does not result in recompense.

And His saying: ﴿And that Allah may know those who believe﴾. How is that? Because the believer is content with this alternation, Allah's alternating of the days among people. He is completely content with it. If adversity befalls him, he is patient, and if ease befalls him, he is grateful. He knows that this is by Allah's decree, so he is content and submits. The non-believer is the opposite. If he is afflicted with ease, he becomes arrogant and insolent, and if he is afflicted with adversity, he becomes distressed and resentful. Allah, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿And among the people is he who worships Allah on an edge﴾ [al-Hajj 11], meaning on a border. ﴿If good befalls him, he is reassured by it, but if trial befalls him﴾, and trial here is meant as the opposite of good. ﴿...if trial befalls him, he turns back on his face; he has lost this world and the Hereafter﴾. How many a person has apostatized because a calamity struck him, may Allah protect us.

So then, ﴿And that Allah may know those who believe﴾, how was this knowledge? We say: because the believer is content with Allah's alternating of the days among the servants. If adversity befalls him, what? He is patient; or if ease befalls him, he is grateful. The non-believer is the opposite. He is not content with Allah's decree and destiny. He says: ﴿If they had obeyed us, they would not have been killed﴾ [Al 'Imran 168], ﴿If they had been with us, they would not have died or been killed﴾ [Al 'Imran 156], and what is similar to that. This is one wisdom. The second wisdom: shall I say the second or the third?
* A student: The second.
* Another student: The third.
* The Shaykh: The third. Did we not say that His saying ﴿and that He may know﴾ is conjoined to an implied clause? The implied meaning is: so that the perfection of His dominion may be manifest, and that He may know.

So the third wisdom: He said ﴿and that He may take from among you martyrs﴾. Look at this expression. He did not say "and that there may be," but He said ﴿and that He may take from among you martyrs﴾. These martyrs, Allah took them and chose them for Himself, exalted is He. Had it not been for such a defeat, they would not have been martyrs. But in order that He might take from among you martyrs, meaning He takes from among you people who were killed in the way of Allah. And how many martyrs did He take at the Battle of Uhud?
* A student: Seventy.
* The Shaykh: Seventy men. Had it not been for this, there would have been no martyrs. ﴿And that He may take from among you martyrs, and Allah does not love the wrongdoers﴾. Regarding His saying ﴿and Allah does not love the wrongdoers﴾: first, who are the wrongdoers? The wrongdoers are those who diminish the right of Allah and the rights of His servants, because the original meaning of injustice (ẓulm) is diminution. The original meaning of ẓulm is diminishing, as in His saying: ﴿Each of the two gardens brought forth its produce and did not fall short therefrom in anything﴾ [al-Kahf 33], meaning it did not diminish. So the wrongdoer is one who diminishes what is due to Allah and what is due to His servants, indeed what is due to himself: ﴿And they did not wrong Us, but they were wronging themselves﴾ [al-Baqarah 57]. So Allah does not love the wrongdoer. But if his wrongdoing is the wrongdoing of disbelief, then he has no share in Allah's love. If his wrongdoing is less than that, he has of Allah's love in proportion to the justice he has, and of Allah's dislike in proportion to the injustice he has.

His saying ﴿Allah does not love the wrongdoers﴾ may seem strange to the reader in its connection with what precedes it: ﴿and that He may take from among you martyrs, and Allah does not love the wrongdoers﴾. How is this? It is answered in two ways. The first way: its meaning, in His saying ﴿and Allah does not love the wrongdoers﴾, is to clarify that those who withdrew from the Battle of Uhud, who were about a third of the army, had no martyrs among them, because they saved themselves. Since they were wrongdoers, Allah did not take martyrs from among them. This is a condemnation of whom?
* The students: Of those who fled.
* The Shaykh: Of whom, O people? There was no fleeing; it is of those who withdrew and turned back midway, namely 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy and those hypocrites who followed him. It is as if He said: He took martyrs from among you, O elite, but He did not take them from those who turned back on their heels, because those are wrongdoers and Allah does not love them. This is one. The second way: those who were killed at Uhud were killed at the hands of the polytheists, and the polytheists are the wrongdoers, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, association [with Allah] is great injustice﴾ [Luqman 13]. Is the victory of the wrongdoers at Uhud, and the martyrdom of those Muslims who were martyred at Uhud, because Allah loves the wrongdoers and dislikes the believers? No. So ﴿and Allah does not love the wrongdoers﴾ is so that no one thinks that the victory of the polytheists in that battle was due to Allah's love for them. So Allah, mighty and majestic, made clear that He does not love the wrongdoers. Have you understood, O people? So there are two answers.

Now we return to the benefits of the noble verse: ﴿If a wound touches you﴾ [Al 'Imran 140].
* Among the benefits of this verse: the demonstration of Allah, glorified and exalted, being compassionate toward the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions, through this great consolation: ﴿If a wound touches you, a wound has touched the other people like it﴾.
* And among its benefits also: a person should console one who is afflicted with something like this, with such consolation. He may say, for example: O brother, you are not the first to be afflicted. How many people have been afflicted with a similar calamity or greater. He may say to him, for example: Imagine the calamity is greater than this, because everything is possible. If you were afflicted with the loss of a thousand, imagine that you were afflicted with the loss of how much? Two thousand, because this is possible. When you imagine that you were afflicted with the loss of two thousand, and the loss was a thousand, the loss of the thousand becomes easy for you. So Allah has taught us how to console the afflicted, by consoling them with mention of similar cases or with mention of what is greater.
* Among the benefits of this verse: Allah, glorified and exalted, made this world a succession of turns, so that a person does not incline to it. For if the world were always comfort and blessing, a person would incline to it and forget the Hereafter. And if it were always trial and affliction, it would be a continuous punishment. But Allah made it alternating states, in which people take turns over one another, and events alternate for a person between good and evil.
* Among the benefits of this verse: the perfection of Allah's dominion, glorified and exalted, over His creation, and that He has absolute disposal. Based on what? Based on the decree we have determined, so that the perfection of Allah's dominion may thereby become manifest, or be made clear.
* Among its benefits: Allah, glorified and exalted, may test the servant in order to know whether his faith exists or not. With what? He tests him with various kinds of trials: sometimes with calamities and sometimes with sins. So here the trial is with what? With calamities. And if Allah makes available to a person the means of disobedience, this is a trial through facilitating sins, like His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, Allah will surely test you with something of game which your hands and spears can reach, that Allah may make evident who fears Him in the unseen﴾ [al-Ma'idah 94].
Among the benefits of this verse, from the benefits of this verse: the perfection of Allah's dominion, glorified and exalted, over His creation, and that He has absolute disposal, based on what? Based on the determined decree that we have determined, so that the perfection of Allah's dominion may thereby become manifest, or be made clear.
* Among its benefits: Allah, glorified and exalted, may test the servant in order to know whether his faith exists or not. With what? He tests him with various kinds of trials, sometimes with calamities, and sometimes with sins. So here the trial is with what? With calamities. And if Allah eases for a person the means of disobedience, this is a trial through facilitating sins, like His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, Allah will surely test you with something of game which your hands and spears can reach, that Allah may make evident who fears Him in the unseen﴾ [al-Ma'idah 94].
What do you say about this verse? What is this trial?
* A student: It is a trial so that He may know who transgresses the limits of Allah, glorified and exalted.
* The Shaykh: So what is the story?
* The student: The story is, meaning His saying, glorified and exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, Allah will surely test you with something of game which your hands and spears can reach, that Allah may make evident who fears Him in the unseen. And whoever transgresses after that will have a painful punishment﴾ [al-Ma'idah 94].
* The Shaykh: What is the story?
* The student: It means that hunting was forbidden to the believers while they were in the state of ihram.
* The Shaykh: Correct. Allah forbade hunting to the believers while they were in ihram, so He tested them with game that their hands and spears could reach, meaning a person can seize game with his hand and his spear without needing an arrow. ﴿That Allah may make evident who fears Him in the unseen﴾.
* Among the benefits of this verse: that Allah's knowledge, glorified and exalted, is of two kinds. His knowledge of things is of two kinds: knowledge that they will come into existence, which is eternal, and knowledge that they have come into existence, which occurs at the time of existence. For this reason He said: ﴿And that Allah may know those who believe﴾ [Al 'Imran 140].
* Among the benefits of this verse: that Allah, exalted is He, may decree what is disliked for many wise purposes, as in His saying: ﴿that Allah may know those who believe and take from among you martyrs﴾ [Al 'Imran 140].
* Among its benefits: the virtue of martyrdom. From where is it derived? From His saying: ﴿and that He may take from among you﴾. It is as if He, glorified, chose these martyrs and took them for Himself.
* Among the benefits of this verse: the virtue of the martyrs of Uhud, because His saying ﴿and that He may take from among you martyrs﴾ first includes the martyrs of Uhud, may Allah be pleased with them.
* Among its benefits: affirmation of love for Allah, that Allah loves. The way to show this is that negating it for the wrongdoers indicates its affirmation for their opposites, because if it were negated from both these and those, there would be no benefit in negating it specifically from the wrongdoers.

For this reason, al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, and other scholars, used as evidence for the affirmation of the believers' seeing their Lord in the Hereafter His saying, exalted is He: ﴿No! Indeed, they, that Day, will be veiled from their Lord﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 15], meaning the wicked. He said: Since these were veiled from seeing Him in anger, this indicates that the others will see Him in a state of pleasure.
This is without doubt a good inference. So here we say: since He negated love from the wrongdoers, this indicates its affirmation for whom? For those who are their opposites, because if it were negated from both these and those, there would be no point in specifying the wrongdoers.
Does the love of Allah, meaning that Allah loves a person, involve any deficiency with respect to Allah?
No. For this reason, the early Ahl al-Sunnah (People of the Sunnah) affirmed that Allah loves, and affirmed that Allah is loved, as He said, exalted is He: ﴿So Allah will bring a people He loves and who love Him﴾ [al-Ma'idah 54].
The love of Allah, glorified and exalted, when the servant is granted it, nothing equals it and nothing resembles its pleasure. A person finds in the love of Allah a pleasure that can never be described. Some of the early scholars even said: If the kings and the sons of kings knew what we are in, they would fight us over it with swords. Allahu Akbar! The kings are at the peak of worldly bliss, are they not? And their sons likewise. But the beloved ones of Allah and the friends of Allah are greater than them in this bliss. He says: If the kings and the sons of kings knew what we are in, meaning of the pleasure and joy, they would fight us over it with swords.
