Among the benefits of Allah's love for the servant is that Allah, may He be exalted, places His love in the hearts of the servants, as He said: ﴿Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds, the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection﴾ [Maryam 96]. It is also reported in a hadith: "When Allah loves a servant, He calls Jibril: 'I love so-and-so, so love him.' Jibril loves him, then he calls out among the inhabitants of the heaven: 'Allah loves so-and-so, so love him.' The inhabitants of the heaven love him, then acceptance is placed for him on the earth, so he becomes accepted among the people" [agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3209) and Muslim (2637/157), from the hadith of Abu Hurairah].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: Allah, may He be exalted, rewarded those who did good in their words and deeds with what? With the reward of this world and the reward of the Hereafter.

* Among its benefits: Allah's mercy precedes His wrath. He rewards the obedient with two rewards: a reward in this world and a reward in the Hereafter. By contrast, Allah, may He be exalted, does not combine two punishments. If He prescribes a punishment in this world for a sin, He does not punish for it again in the Hereafter, as in the hadith: "The *hudud* (prescribed punishments) are expiation" [agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3892) and Muslim (1709/41), from the hadith of Ubadah ibn al-Samit, with similar meaning]. *Hudud* means the punishments, such as the punishment for fornication and theft, that they are an expiation for those upon whom they are carried out. The Prophet (ﷺ), peace and blessings be upon him, said to the two who performed *li'an* (mutual condemnation): "The punishment of this world is lighter than the punishment of the Hereafter" [recorded by Muslim (1493/4), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Umar]. Indeed, Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And whatever affliction strikes you is for what your hands have earned, and He pardons much﴾ [al-Shura 30]. So Allah will not combine for a person two punishments for one sin, one in this world and one in the Hereafter. But He combines for him two rewards for one act of obedience, a reward in this world and a reward in the Hereafter, because Allah's mercy precedes His wrath.

* Among the benefits of this verse: an indication of the lowliness of this world in comparison with the Hereafter. From where is this derived?

* Students: From ﴿and the good reward﴾.

* Shaykh: From His saying ﴿the reward of this world and the good reward of the Hereafter﴾. It is as if this world is nothing, such that goodness could be found in it, as we have explained. This indicates that the intelligent person should be concerned with what?

* Students: With the Hereafter.

* Shaykh: With the reward of the Hereafter, which is the good.

* Among the benefits of the verse: affirming resurrection and recompense, from His saying ﴿the reward of the Hereafter﴾.

* Among its benefits: affirming love for Allah, which is a real attribute of Allah in a manner befitting Him. Is contentment (*ridha*) affirmed for Allah?

* Students: Yes.

* Shaykh: It is affirmed for Allah. Joy (*farah*) is affirmed for Allah. Wonder (*ajab*) is affirmed for Allah. Likewise, all the attributes that came in the Book and the Sunnah: we must believe in them as true, according to their reality, because Allah addressed us in the Quran in clear Arabic speech. Nothing has come from the Companions or the Imams that they distorted these texts from their apparent meanings. This indicates that they affirmed them as they came, in the form they have. This is the position of the *salaf* (the early pious predecessors) and of the people of the Sunnah and the Community (*Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah*). In it there is comfort and tranquility, because when a person meets his Lord having affirmed for Him the attribute that the Quran and the Sunnah indicate, he meets Him with proof or without proof? He meets Him with proof. But if he meets his Lord having distorted it and said that the meaning of ﴿He loves the doers of good﴾ is "He rewards them," he has no proof, no proof before Allah.

We always discuss those who deny some of Allah's attributes on the basis of rational proof. We respond to them in general terms:

First: This is contrary to the path of the *salaf*, because the *salaf* did not use reason to establish or negate the attributes.

Second: Reason has no place in the matter of Allah's attributes, because Allah's attributes are pure report (*khabar mahd*), and reason has no role at all in pure reports.

Then, if someone says: "Is it not possible for us to analogize the unseen to the seen?"

We say: analogy is not possible, because Allah has negated this analogy and forbidden it. He negated it and forbade it, saying: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾ [al-Shura 11], and He said: ﴿So do not strike examples for Allah﴾ [al-Nahl 74]. Perhaps I may analogize a person I do not know to a person I know and see, but I cannot analogize the Creator to the created, because Allah has negated that, indeed forbidden it.

Third: We say to them: your negation of what you negated on the argument that reason does not indicate it is not sound in reasoning according to rational people. That is because even if we assume that reason does not indicate it, the revealed text (*al-sam'*) has indicated it. The absence of a specific proof does not necessitate the absence of what is proven. That is, if we say: "This does not indicate such and such," we would be saying: "But we have another proof." Suppose reason does not indicate the affirmation of the attributes you negated. The revealed text has indicated it. This applies to rational matters as it does to sensory matters. If you said: "This road does not lead to Mecca," does that mean we cannot reach Mecca at all?

We can reach it by another road. Suppose reason does not indicate the affirmation of what you negated. We prove it by what? By revelation.

Fourth: We say: rather, reason does indicate it, and in a way more compelling than what you have mentioned. That is, we affirm what you negated by the indication of reason, affirming it in a manner that is more evident than what you mentioned. For example, they say that will (*irada*) is affirmed for Allah, indicated by reason. The discussion here is with the Ash'ariyyah. They say that will is affirmed for Allah, may He be mighty and majestic, because reason indicates it. Do you know what the indication of reason for will is?

* Students: Specification (*takhsis*).

* Shaykh: Specification. That is, the sky being sky and the earth being earth is a specification. What specified that the sky be sky and the earth be earth? Will. Allah willed that the sky be sky and it was, and that the earth be earth and it was. So this is a rational proof for the affirmation of will for Allah.

We say: you have negated mercy, and we prove it by reason. Are not Allah's blessings upon you countless? What will they say?

* Students: Yes.

* Shaykh: Yes, countless. So are they signs of mercy or signs of wrath? Signs of mercy. For this reason, even the common folk, when rain comes and fertility spreads, say: "This is from the mercy of Allah." Indeed they say: "We were given rain by the grace and mercy of Allah." So they affirm mercy for Allah by rational proof. Likewise, contentment can also be affirmed by rational proof. Rewarding the obedient indicates Allah's contentment with them, or His anger? If He were angry, He would have punished. But He was content, so He rewarded. This is a rational proof.

Thus those who deny some attributes on the argument that reason does not indicate them are refuted on four grounds we have just mentioned: this argument contradicts the path of the *salaf*, since the *salaf* did not use reason to affirm or negate the attributes, but rather what? Revelation.

Second: reason has no place in them. If they claim analogy, we say analogy is forbidden, because Allah negated and forbade it.

* Student: The negation of (...) reason?

* Shaykh: Third: they say reason does not indicate them. We say: even if reason does not indicate them, they are indicated by what? Revelation. So it is obligatory to affirm them by revelation, because the absence of a specific proof, which is reason, does not necessitate the absence of what is proven, since it may be established by another proof.

Fourth: we say: we do not concede to you that reason did not indicate them. Rather reason has indicated them. Then we bring the example that makes the argument clear.

* From the benefits of this noble verse: encouragement to do good, because goodness is a means to an end that is the goal of every person, namely the love of Allah. When it is a means to this great end, it is commanded and urged.

Furthermore, it shows that love for Allah is the ultimate goal. Allah said in His Book: ﴿Say: If you should love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you﴾ [Ali 'Imran 3:31]. Huh? ﴿Allah will love you﴾. He did not say, "Follow me so that you may be truthful in what you claim." Rather, He said, ﴿Allah will love you,﴾ because the great fruit is that Allah loves you. We are also assured that whoever truly loves Allah, Allah will love him, because Allah says: "Whoever comes to Me walking, I come to him running; and whoever draws near to Me by a span, I draw near to him by a cubit; and whoever draws near to Me by a cubit, I draw near to him by a fathom."[[Agreed upon (Bukhari, 7405; Muslim, 2675/2) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]] So if your love for Allah is sincere, Allah's love for you is guaranteed. But the real calamity is that you claim love while your love is not sincere. This is the calamity: your heart is occupied with other loves, such as love of wealth, love of children, love of palaces, love of vehicles, love of women, and so on. These loves constrict the love of Allah in the heart, unless they follow His love. Pay attention to this. Do not say, "You are closing the door on loving things that human souls are naturally inclined to love." We say: if the love of these things follows the love of Allah, it becomes part of the love of Allah. If someone loves wealth in order to spend it in the way of Allah, does this love compete with the love of Allah or not?

It does not compete; rather, it increases it. If someone loves women in order to increase the Ummah, to guard his chastity, and for the benefits that are established by marriage, this is part of the love of Allah. But if he seeks merely to satisfy his desire, you will find his heart attached to every woman and never settling on one. Then there is competition, and the love of Allah, the Exalted, weakens in the heart. The important thing is that the real matter is that Allah loves you; this is what matters.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: affirmation of Allah's ikhtiyari attributes (attributes related to His will, the Exalted). That is, which are related to what? To His will. So when Allah ties an attribute to an action, we know that it is one of the ikhtiyari attributes related to His will. How is that? Because ihsan (doing good) is the action of the servant, and is the action of the servant created or eternal? Created. If ihsan is the cause of Allah's love, and it is the action of the servant, which is created, then it necessarily follows that love is established, tied to what? To ihsan. Is that clear?

The ikhtiyari attributes were also denied by the Ash'ariyya (the Ash'ari school of kalam) and their like, who said: it is impossible for created, will-related attributes to subsist in Allah. Why? They said: if we affirm for Allah created attributes, it would follow that created things subsist in Him, and created things subsist only in something created, while Allah, the Exalted, is eternal and everlasting.

It is said: Woe to you! This is false. That created things subsist only in something created: did not Allah say, ﴿And Allah does what He wills﴾ [Ibrahim 14:27]? Allah does what He wills. Is it not the case that our will is not dependent on our existence? A human being has wills that renew, and it does not follow that this willer did not exist until the will existed. Rather, he precedes his will. Is that not so? We precede our wills; that is, a person exists before he wills. So it does not follow that a will, or ikhtiyari actions, must coincide with existence. A person performs many renewing actions that did not exist with him when he came into existence. Likewise, the Lord, the Exalted, does what He wills, performing actions that were not with Him, glorified and exalted is He, eternally. Rather, they are created. Yet their type may be created or their individual instances may be created, while their kind is ancient and eternal. So speech, for example, what is it?

* Students: Eternal.

* Shaykh: Ancient and eternal. Allah, glorified and exalted, has never ceased to be speaking. But its individual instances are created, without doubt. ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ [Ya-Sin 36:82]. We know that the willed matters of Allah, the Exalted, occur: ﴿Every day He is in a [new] matter﴾ [Ar-Rahman 55:29]. He gives life and causes death, honors and humbles, provides and withholds, and all of these occur by a will joined with a word: ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ Yet this does not necessitate that He, glorified and exalted, is created. Therefore their reasoning for this denial, which they adopted, is flawed reasoning. If we said that Allah does not act, and that if an action subsisted in Him it would follow that He is created, then how is He incapable of acting?! Is this a deficiency or a perfection?

* Students: A deficiency.

* Shaykh: A deficiency, and what a deficiency! Observe how the people of falsehood flee from what they believe to be false and fall into something even more false and more evil, while they exceed the bounds by distorting the texts and denying Allah what He described Himself with. They are distorters and deniers (muharrifa, mu'attila), falling into a greater evil than what they fled from.

* Student: Shaykh, may Allah reward you with good. In the authentic hadith, when the fighters in the way of Allah obtain spoils, "they have hastened two-thirds of their reward."[[Recorded by Muslim (1906/153) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr.]] I do not know how they mentioned this hadith (...)?

* Shaykh: There must be a reason. The Prophet (ﷺ) said this because of something, so this hadith and its context need to be examined.

* Student: So this does not affect the reward in the Hereafter?

* Shaykh: It does not affect it if the intention is sincere, with the aim that the word of Allah be supreme. But some fighters may give precedence to the aspect of spoils, and from here the reward decreases greatly, according to the emphasis that arises in his heart. So the hadith needs to be examined regarding its cause; perhaps its cause indicates that they had a desire for this world.

* Student: Shaykh, Allah, the Exalted, in some verses, such as regarding those who wage war against Allah, the highway robbers, at the end of the verse, mentioned two punishments. Is that...?

* Shaykh: What is it?

* Student: Allah, the Exalted, mentioned in this regard, if this warring against Allah and the highway robbers, He prescribed for them two punishments, in this world and the Hereafter?

* Shaykh: Yes. Like what?

* Student: Like the saying of the Exalted: ﴿The penalty for those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and strive upon earth in corruption is only that they be killed﴾ up to the verse, then He mentioned at the end: ﴿That is for them disgrace in this world; and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 5:33].

* Shaykh: Yes. This disgrace is indeed a disgrace they are humiliated by in this world. But perhaps, because of the magnitude of their deeds, they receive the hadd (prescribed punishment) in this world and the punishment in the Hereafter. Otherwise, it is established in the Two Sahihs and others: "Whoever commits any of these sins and is punished for it in this world, that punishment is an expiation for him."[[Agreed upon (Bukhari, 4894; Muslim, 1709/41) from the hadith of Ubadah ibn al-Samit.]] And we have heard the verse: ﴿And whatever affliction strikes you is for what your hands have earned, and He pardons much﴾ [Ash-Shura 42:30]. And Allah does not combine two punishments for a person. So either it is said that this is due to the severity of their crime and sin, and both are combined for them.

Student: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed. ﴿O you who have believed, if you obey those who disbelieve, they will turn you back on your heels, and you will turn about [as] losers. Rather, Allah is your protector, and He is the best of helpers. We will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve because they associated with Allah that for which He had not sent down any authority; and their refuge is the Fire, and wretched is the residence of the wrongdoers.﴾ [Surah Al-Imran 149–152]

* The Shaykh: All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and all his companions. To proceed: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿O you who have believed, if you obey those who disbelieve, they will turn you back on your heels, and you will turn about [as] losers.﴾

Allah has opened this verse with the vocative address, and opening with the address indicates concern for what will be directed to the one addressed, because the address serves to alert, and a person is only alerted to something that concerns him. So when Allah directs the speech, or when speech is opened with the address, it is a sign of attention to it because of its importance.

Then He addressed the servants by the title of faith: ﴿O you who have believed﴾. The purpose of this is, first: to encourage and motivate acceptance of what is conveyed, because faith is what moves a person to accept what Allah has commanded and to abandon what Allah has forbidden. For this reason Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "When Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, then prick up your ears to it, for it is either good that you are commanded to do or evil that you are forbidden from."[[Narrated by Ibn al-Mubarak in al-Zuhd (36), and Sa'id ibn Mansur in al-Sunan (50), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud.]]

It also serves a second benefit: that acceptance of what is mentioned is among the requirements of faith. Just as if you addressed a generous person and said: "O generous one, give to the poor and help the needy," this indicates that giving to the poor and helping the needy is among the requirements of his generosity. Thus, accepting what comes after this address is among the requirements of faith.

The third benefit or purpose: that not accepting it is a deficiency in faith, because if the address is directed to a person with the word of faith, yet he does not comply, this is a deficiency in his faith. For what comes after ﴿O you who have believed﴾ is either something commanded, or something forbidden, or something reported. So abandoning what is commanded is a deficiency in faith, falling into what is prohibited is a deficiency in faith, and denying the report is a deficiency in faith.

Let us listen to this report from Allah, the Exalted, the report of One who is Knowing of everything: ﴿if you obey those who disbelieve﴾. Here ﴿in﴾ is conditional, and the verb of the condition is ﴿تُطِيعُوا (tuti'u)﴾, but it was not apocopated. Shall we say so?

* Students: Apocopated (majzum).
* The Shaykh: Apocopated. By what?
* The students: By the deletion of the nun.
* The Shaykh: By the deletion of the nun, and the waw is the subject, because it is one of the five verbs. As for the response of the condition, it is His saying: ﴿يَرُدُّوكُمْ عَلَى أَعْقَابِكُمْ (yaruddukum ʿala aʿqabikum)﴾, which is apocopated by the deletion of the nun, and the waw is the subject.

His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, if you obey those who disbelieve﴾. So there is a command directed from the disbelievers to the believers, since obedience corresponds to command; or a prohibition directed from the disbelievers to the believers, when they command them to indecency and forbid them what is good. If you obey them in that, the answer is: ﴿they will turn you back on your heels﴾.

His saying: ﴿if you obey those who disbelieve﴾ is general, encompassing the Jews, the Christians, the polytheists, and the atheists who have no religion and worship nothing. Any one of the disbelievers, if he commands you to something and you obey him, he will turn you back on your heels, and you will turn about as a loser.

His saying: ﴿if you obey those who disbelieve﴾ refers to what is an act of worship to Allah. As for other matters, such as matters of craft for example, there is no doubt that it does not enter the verse. If an engineer from among the disbelievers commanded you to make such-and-such so that the result would be such-and-such, it does not enter the verse. What is intended is what falls under the category of, what? Under the category of worship: he commands you to indecency, drinking wine, theft, bad character, or forbids you from what is good, forbids you from prayer, forbids you from sincerity to Allah, and similar things.

His saying: ﴿they will turn you back on your heels﴾. Al-A'qab is the plural of ʿaqib, which is the back of the foot, and it is called al-ʿurqub (the heel). That is, they make you walk backwards. It is well known that one who walks backwards will fall into pits and step on thorns and pebbles. This is close to His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Is one who walks prone on his face better guided, or one who walks upright on a straight path?﴾ [Al-Mulk 22]. So here: ﴿they will turn you back on your heels﴾.

﴿and you will turn about [as] losers﴾. ﴿Tanqalibu (you will turn about)﴾: inqilab implies a transformation from one state to another, which is why it is said: he turned in his bed from the right side to the left side. So there is a transformation from one state to another if we obey these disbelievers: ﴿you will turn about﴾.

His saying: ﴿khasirin (losers)﴾ is a circumstantial state (hal), a hal from the waw in His saying "tanqalibu". That is: you will be in loss after you were in profit, because faith is profit, as He said, the Exalted: ﴿By time, indeed mankind is in loss﴾ [Al-Asr 1–2]. Which mankind? All of them. And for this the definite article here is for generality; that is, every human being is indeed in loss, ﴿except for those who have believed and done righteous deeds and advised each other to truth and advised each other to patience﴾ [Al-Asr 3]. Those who are characterized by these four qualities are the winners, and whoever else is a loser: a loser of what? A loser of his time. This is the wisdom behind Allah swearing by time rather than anything else, because time is the storehouse of deeds. If a person does not uphold these four qualities, he has lost his time, and his life becomes a loss.

﴿you will turn about [as] losers﴾ because you have shifted from what? From Islam to disbelief. And in another verse that preceded: ﴿O you who have believed, if you obey a party from those who were given the Scripture, they will turn you back to disbelief after your faith﴾ [Al-Imran 100]. Here He said: ﴿those who disbelieve﴾, and there He said: ﴿a party from those who were given the Scripture﴾, because among those who were given the Scripture some are good, as He said: ﴿They are not all alike. Among the People of the Scripture is a community standing [in obedience]﴾ [Al-Imran 113]. This is from the eloquence of the Qur'an: when He said: ﴿if you obey a party from those who were given the Scripture﴾, He said: ﴿they will turn you back to disbelief after your faith﴾, since it is a party of them. As for the disbelievers, all of the disbelievers want from us that we what? That we disbelieve, and that we turn back on our heels as losers.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Rather, Allah is your protector﴾. Is ﴿bal (rather)﴾ here for transitional retraction (idrab intiqali) or nullifying retraction (idrab ibtali)?

* A student: Transitional.
* The Shaykh: No, it is nullifying (ibtali), but it is the nullification of something implied. Because our obedience to the disbelievers is for hope or fear: that is, if we obey the disbelievers, then either we obey them out of hope, or we obey them out of fear. Out of hope that they will help us, give us wealth and similar things; out of fear that they will strike at us, fight and attack us. Here the retraction fits perfectly, so He said: ﴿Rather, Allah is your protector﴾, meaning: do not obey them and take them as allies, for you have one who is better than their alliance, and that is Allah. Therefore this retraction is considered a nullifying retraction of something implied: if you obey those who disbelieve in order that they become your allies, then they will turn you back on your heels and you will turn about as losers.

Then He said: ﴿Rather, Allah is your protector﴾. If Allah, glorified and exalted, is our protector, then no one among creation concerns us, as long as we believe that Allah is our protector with the qualities we possess that make us deserving of His protection. Not every person who says: ﴿Indeed, my protector is Allah﴾ [Al-A'raf 196] has Allah as his protector. But if Allah is our protector with the qualities we possess that make us deserving of protection, then they will never concern us, no matter how strong they are, and no matter their craft or wealth, they will not concern us, because with us is whom?

* A student: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
* The Shaykh: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, who says to a thing "Be" and it is. But Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, commands us to fight with our hands. So when our ability is exhausted while we carry out what is obligatory, then there comes to us a victory from Allah that no human has the power to achieve. This is a truth we must understand: we are commanded to prepare what we can and to fight, but when something beyond our capacity comes, then a victory comes from Allah for which neither we nor others have the power. And there are witnesses in history to what I have said. Mūsā, peace be upon him, when he left Egypt, and Pharaoh had gathered for him all the people of the cities, every city, to finish off Mūsā and his people, and said: ﴿Indeed, these are but a small band﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara 54], to diminish their standing among his people so they would prepare and resolve to destroy them. They reached the sea. Does a person have the power against the sea?

* Students: No.
* The Shaykh: No, he has no power. For this reason his people said: ﴿Indeed, we are to be overtaken﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara 61], because the sea was before them and Pharaoh and his soldiers behind them: how could they escape? He said: ﴿No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara 62]. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, commanded him to strike the sea, and he struck it once with a staff, a staff carried in the hand, just once, and it split into twelve dry paths in an instant. This wet earth that was mud and clay became dry in an instant, and this flowing water became each division like a great mountain, like a mountain standing still, not flowing. Some scholars even say that Allah placed in these masses of water gaps so that the Children of Israel could see one another, because a person in the middle of the water has water to his right and left, and fears that his companions have drowned, so Allah made for them gaps in these mountains where they could see one another in an instant. No human has the power for this. But whoever Allah is his protector is victorious. They came out of the sea safe. Then Pharaoh and his people entered, and when they had entered the sea and were all inside, Allah commanded the sea to close, and it closed in an instant, drowning them in an instant. Pharaoh had terrified the Children of Israel, so Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, brought out his body for them to look at: ﴿So today We will save you in your body that you may be a sign to those after you﴾ [Yunus 92], and they were reassured that he had perished.

It is mentioned in the history of this nation that al-ʿAla' ibn al-Hadrami, when he reached Bahrain and found the sea before him with no ships, called upon Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and he crossed the water on foot, and the horses and camels all walked on the water as if walking on a rock; that is, a stone.[[al-Tabarani in al-Awsat (3495) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, and Ibn Abi Shaybah (30301) abridged from the hadith of al-ʿAla'.]] This is something we have no power for.

Likewise, what is mentioned about Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas at the conquest of al-Mada'in: he reached the Tigris, which was throwing up foam from the force of its current, and the Persians had crossed it with their ships and bridges, and had broken the bridges and sunk the ships, and the Muslims had nothing left to cross with. Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas said to Salman al-Farisi: "Give us from—that is, from your opinions," for he, may Allah be pleased with him, was a man of judgment in war, and he was the one who advised the digging of the trench around Medina in the year of the Confederates. Salman said: "By Allah, I see no stratagem in this. The sea is before us, and we have no ships or bridges. But let me look into the people: if they are upon what is proper and they are worthy of victory, then the Children of Israel are no more deserving of victory than we are, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, split the sea for them and they crossed." He went and found the people to be horsemen by day and monks by night: at night in bowing and prostration, and by day preparing the equipment of war and readying themselves. He returned to him after three days and said: "I have found the people in the best of condition, but put your trust in Allah." Sa'd called out for departure, and that he would cross the river, and said: "I will say Allahu akbar three times, and when I say it the third time, then plunge into the river in the name of Allah." They did so. It is said—glory be to Allah—that they all crossed with their horses, their foot soldiers and their camels, so much so that some historians mention that when the horses grew tired, Allah created for them a mound on which they could stand and rest. This is a victory for which we have no power, but it is from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

For this reason He says here: do not befriend the disbelievers, and do not obey them, seeking victory or out of fear of them, for you have a protector greater than them, the Mighty and Majestic, who is Allah: ﴿Rather, Allah is your protector, and He is the best of helpers﴾. ﴿He is the best of helpers﴾: that is, the best of those who help; rather He is the best of helpers, the greatest of helpers, the most capable and the most powerful, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿If Allah helps you, no one can overcome you; and if He forsakes you, who is there that can help you after Him?﴾ [Al-Imran 160]. No one.

So the retraction here is among the finest that could occur in this context: ﴿Rather, Allah is your protector, and He is the best of helpers﴾, that is, the best of those who help.

* Benefits in these verses:

First: the excellence of faith, in that the address is directed to people with the description of faith in a context of guidance and admonition, and that faith necessitates compliance.

* Among its benefits: it is not permissible for us to obey the disbelievers, because obeying them is a means to disbelief: ﴿if you obey those who disbelieve, they will turn you back on your heels, and you will turn about as losers﴾ [Al-Imran 149].

* And among them: the obligation to beware of the disbelievers, the obligation of caution, and that they can never plan a matter that contains benefit for the Muslims and Islam, never, impossible. Even the allies who have an alliance between them and the Muslims cannot ally with the Muslims except for, what? For their own interest, certainly. Khuza'ah had an alliance with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, but it was for their own interest.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that obeying the disbelievers inevitably results in disbelief; as shown by His saying: ﴿they will turn you back on your heels, and you will turn about as losers﴾. How so? The disbelievers take from us little by little. They want from us things that we obey them in, and they stop at this limit? No, they do not stop; they add things, until we turn back on our heels.

This does not mean that we prostrate to them and bow to them. No. When a person leaves his religion, that is sufficient. For this reason it is mentioned that some of their leaders said: "We strive for missionary work, not so that we bring the Muslim out of his religion into Christianity, because the Christian religion is known, far from the natural disposition (fitrah), and by the Christian religion I mean what they follow now. As for what Jesus brought, it is true, but what Jesus brought has ended and was abrogated by the religion of Islam."

He says: "We do not want to bring the Muslim out of his religion into Christianity; it is enough for us that one of two things happens: either we bring him out of his religion into no religion, so that he becomes like an animal whose only concern is his belly, his private parts and his pleasures; or we make him doubt the religion, we make him doubt. And it is known that faith is not valid with doubt; faith is certainty. If a person has even the slightest hesitation, he is not a believer. There must be faith; there is no faith with hesitation. They say: this is sufficient, that we bring him out to become either an animal or a doubter, perplexed and uncertain. This is a result of disbelief."

Among the benefits of this verse: disbelief is a loss, as His saying shows: ﴿So you will return as losers﴾. And if disbelief is a loss, then faith is gain. For this reason we find no one more profitable than the believer in this world, even if he is poor, and even if he is alone, having neither wealth nor children, he is still more profitable than the disbeliever. This is because the disbeliever has lost both this world and the Hereafter. He has not benefited from his worldly life. In truth, the disbeliever has not benefited from his worldly life; he lives only as cattle live, as the One most knowledgeable of all has said: ﴿And those who disbelieve enjoy themselves and eat as cattle eat﴾ [Muhammad 12]. Subhan Allah! A perfectly matching example: ﴿They enjoy themselves and eat as cattle eat, and the Fire is their abode﴾ [Muhammad 12]. The result is evil: ﴿the Fire is their abode.﴾ They leave this world, in which they were given comfort, for the Fire of Hell, may Allah protect us, and at that time their departure is harsher and more difficult. This is unlike the believer. I ask Allah to make me and you among them.

The believer leaves this world, with its hardship and its troubles, for the abode of bliss, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Those whom the angels take in death while they are good, saying: "Peace be upon you. Enter Paradise for what you used to do."﴾ [An-Nahl 32] at the time of their death.

This verse also indicates the bliss of the grave, because He said: ﴿Enter Paradise﴾ now, from your death. And it is established in the authentic hadith: "His grave is widened for him as far as the eye can see, a door to Paradise is opened for him, and there comes to him of its breeze and its bliss," as is well known. [[Narrated by Abu Dawud (4753) from the hadith of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib.]]

Among the benefits of this verse: extreme caution, or strong warning, against obeying the disbelievers and taking them as allies. With great regret, we today have come to treat loyalty and disavowal (al-wala' wal-bara', (loyalty to the believers and disavowal of the disbelievers)) lightly. The loyalty and disavowal that must come from the believer, and through which he tastes the sweetness of faith, is lacking, except in those whom Allah wills. When we were young, when a Christian was mentioned, a person's skin would crawl. His skin would crawl. "I seek refuge in Allah, a Christian or a Jew!" Now it is said that some Muslims describe a Christian as a brother: "Our brother so-and-so." How is so-and-so your brother?! What did Ibrahim, peace be upon him, and his people say?

* The students: ﴿Indeed, we are free from you﴾..
* The Shaykh: ﴿Indeed, we are free from you and from what you worship besides Allah.﴾ See, they disassociated themselves from them before they disassociated themselves from the idols: ﴿Indeed, we are free from you and from what you worship other than Allah. We have rejected you, and there has appeared between us and you animosity and hatred forever until you believe in Allah alone.﴾ [Al-Mumtahanah 4]. And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿There has already been for you an excellent pattern in Ibrahim and those with him﴾ [Al-Mumtahanah 4]. This excellent pattern is that we disassociate ourselves from the disbelievers, that we hate them, and that we believe they are enemies, however gently they speak to us and however they embellish their words. They are our enemies, and by Allah, this enmity will never turn into loyalty, until the Day of Resurrection.

So it is obligatory upon us to be cautious. Here we address the rulers and the common people, warning them against the disbelievers and their allegiance, and advising them to take them as enemies, real enemies, as is the reality. Likewise, the subjects must keep away from the disbelievers, especially in this peninsula, because this peninsula has a special status in keeping the disbelievers away from it. The Prophet, peace be upon him, during his final illness, at the time of leaving this world, enjoined his community, saying: "Expel the polytheists from the Arabian Peninsula" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3053) and Muslim (1637/20) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]], and he said: "I will surely expel the Jews and the Christians from the Arabian Peninsula until I leave none but a Muslim" [[Narrated by Muslim (1767/63) from the hadith of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab.]]. The first is in the two Sahihs, and the second is in Muslim. He also said, in what is authentically reported from him: "Expel the Jews and the Christians from the Arabian Peninsula" [[Narrated by Ibn Abi 'Asim in al-Ahad wal-Mathani (234) from the hadith of Abu 'Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah.]].

We advise our common brothers to take this injunction of the Messenger, peace be upon him, into careful consideration, and not to bring into this land any Jew, Christian, or other disbeliever except out of supreme necessity and within specific limits. In other words, they should not bring them for permanent settlement; rather they should bring them when necessary and only to the extent of the necessity, for a specific period, not as permanent settlement.

Among the benefits of these two verses: the affirmation of Allah's wilayah (guardianship/loyalty). The guardianship of Allah for the believers is affirmed, because He said: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, then He said: ﴿Rather, Allah is your Protector﴾. This guardianship is specific, because Allah's guardianship over creation is of two types:

A general one, for everyone. Its meaning is managing affairs, whether by granting victory or by abandonment. Pay attention: this is general guardianship. What does it mean? Managing affairs, by victory, abandonment, or otherwise. The point is that the manager of creation is Allah, Mighty and Majestic. This is general guardianship, and among its examples is His saying: ﴿until, when death comes to one of you, Our messengers take him, and they do not fail [in their duty]. Then they are returned to Allah, their true Protector﴾ [Al-An'am 61-62].

As for the specific guardianship, it is exclusive to the believers: ﴿Allah is the Protector of those who have believed; He brings them out of darkness into light﴾ [Al-Baqarah 257], and ﴿And Allah is the Protector of the believers﴾ [Ali 'Imran 68]. He, Mighty and Majestic, is the Protector of the God-fearing. So this guardianship is specific, and its meaning or implication is that Allah, glorified and exalted, takes charge of the one who deserves it with kindness and care, granting him success. This is explained by the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him: that the Prophet ﷺ said, relaying from his Lord: "Whoever shows enmity to a friend of Mine, I have declared war against him. My servant does not draw near to Me with anything more beloved to Me than what I have made obligatory upon him. My servant continues to draw near to Me with voluntary acts until I love him. When I love him, I am his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees, his hand with which he strikes, and his foot with which he walks." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari (6502) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]] That is, Allah guides him in all his conduct. So this is a specific guardianship, restricted to those among the believers and the God-fearing who deserve it.

Here: ﴿Rather, Allah is your Protector﴾, is it meant as general or specific?

* The students: Specific.
* The Shaykh: Specific.

* Among the benefits of this verse: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is the Helper of His allies, because of His saying: ﴿And He is the best of helpers﴾, and this is from His guardianship.

If someone says: How do we answer what Allah has informed us in His Book, that among people are those who killed the prophets without right? How do we answer that?

The answer to this is one of two ways.

The first: the victory meant, or the promise of victory, is for the one who was commanded to fight, for Allah grants him victory, because Allah does not assign him anything except that the outcome is in his favor. As for those prophets who were killed, they were not commanded to fight.

The second: we say that victory is of two kinds. Victory of a person, meaning that a man witnesses it in his own person. And moral victory, meaning that Allah grants victory to whoever brought this message even after his death. For this reason you find the imams of the Muslims, their sayings are as if they were alive among us, are they not? The imams' words are alive, so it is as if they are alive. If you take a book by one of the scholars and read it and benefit from it, it is as if this scholar taught you. So is this victory or not? It is victory: victory for his principle, his goal, and his call. This is victory.

There is also a third way: we distribute victory over time. We say that victory may be in this world and may be in the Hereafter, and those prophets who were killed will have their victory in the Hereafter, when they dispute with their peoples. You should notice, brothers, that the people of truth and the people of falsehood dispute before Allah on the Day of Resurrection. He judges between them concerning what they differed about. Do not think that the disagreement between the people of truth and the people of falsehood ends with this world. No, Allah will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection and grant victory to the people of truth. ﴿Your relatives and your children will not benefit you on the Day of Resurrection; He will separate you﴾ [Al-Mumtahanah 3], ﴿Then to Us is your return, and We will inform you of what you used to do﴾ [Yunus 23].

In any case, many verses indicate this: ﴿Indeed, you will die, and indeed, they will die. Then indeed, on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord you will dispute﴾ [Az-Zumar 30-31]. So if Allah rules in favor of the people of truth against the people of falsehood on the Day of Resurrection, is this victory or not? It is victory. So the answer to this verse is in three ways: either we say that those promised victory are those who were commanded to fight; or we say that victory is of two kinds, victory for a person who is granted victory in his lifetime, and victory for his call and what he brought, which happens even after his death; or we say that the victory meant is the victory on the Day of Resurrection when they dispute before Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, We will surely support Our messengers and those who believed in the worldly life and on the Day when the witnesses will stand﴾ [Ghafir 51].

* Student: Shaykh, may Allah be good to you; meaning, confirming Him, glorified and exalted: ﴿If you obey a faction of those who were given the Scripture﴾. Shall we take it, if we return it to His saying, glorified and exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 51], in the context, do we say Jew or do we say Christian?

* The Shaykh: No, the verse is explicit: ﴿a faction of those who were given the Scripture﴾, because some of the People of the Book are with them (...), but not all of them. Then the People of the Book in reality at the present time, there is not (...), because those among them who have affection for the believers are the nearest people in affection. They are the ones who, when they hear what has been sent down to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of what they recognized of the truth, so... close to the believers. At the least call, they are moved and enter Islam. But the Christians of today, like the Jews of yesterday, are obstinate against Islam, and they do not want Islam to be established.

* The student: Enmity in general; meaning, not among the Jews and Christians?

* The Shaykh: At the present time, this is the apparent situation. For this reason you will not find a Christian who has knowledge but cannot believe. But the ignorant Christians may believe. If there were real callers from among the Muslims, many Christians would enter Islam, the ignorant among them. But those who have knowledge, Allah knows best; hearts are in the hand of Allah, but it is far that they would enter Islam.

* Student: Some exegetes mentioned that the Children of Israel, or that Pharaoh and his people, when they followed Musa, some of them remained who had not entered the sea, so Allah sent angels who threw them into the sea. Is this correct?

* The Shaykh: Allah knows best. But we must know that what is not in the Qur'an, and is among the authentic reports of the Sunnah, is neither believed nor disbelieved, because Allah said: ﴿Has there not come to you the news of those before you: the people of Nuh, 'Ad, and Thamud, and those after them, whom none knows but Allah﴾ [Ibrahim 9]. So we receive their reports only from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, either from His Book or from authentic Sunnah, and whatever else is not like this is withheld from judgment.

* The student: Likewise, the number, Shaykh; he did not specify them by numbers.

* The Shaykh: Never. We do not know their number; all of this we do not know.

* Student: Shaykh, the address directed to the Messenger ﷺ specifically and the Companions; meaning some people..

* The Shaykh: What?

* The student: The address directed to the Messenger, peace be upon him..

* The Shaykh: Where is it?

* The student: ﴿O you who have believed﴾.

* The Shaykh: By Allah, this is a problem. Is this specific to the Messenger and the Companions?

* The student: It was revealed to the Messenger ﷺ.

* The Shaykh: Yes, that is known; the whole Qur'an was revealed to him. But are the addresses in the Qur'an and the calls in the Qur'an only for the Messenger and his Companions?

* The student: And to the common people.

* The Shaykh: ﴿O you who have believed﴾ is a description that applies until the Day of Resurrection.

* Student: But I mean, Shaykh, did something of this kind happen during the time of the Prophet ﷺ among the Companions, or does it have a occasion of revelation?

* The Shaykh: Never. I do not know of anyone except those who apostatized, but those among the Arabs who apostatized were not in the position of disbelievers.

* Student: Shaykh, may Allah be good to you, they say about Pharaoh that he is still mummified until now, still mummified in his body.

* The Shaykh: Allah knows best. They say what is in the pyramids are their bodies, and Allah knows best.

* The student: Would this be a confirmation of what Allah mentioned in the Qur'an?

* The Shaykh: Never. Because His saying: ﴿for those after you﴾ does not mean for those after you until the Day of Resurrection. It is enough that the Children of Israel witnessed him and were certain that the man had died, because he terrorized them; he used to kill their sons and spare their women, a tyrannical oppressor. And a person cannot be convinced and reassured that he has died except by seeing him, because Satan comes and says: No, perhaps he is alive, perhaps he swam to the edge of the sea and escaped.

* Student: Shaykh, on the Day of Resurrection people dispute before Allah and judgment is given between them. Is this dispute between the group of believers and disbelievers, or between any dispute, even between a believer and a believer?

* The Shaykh: The apparent statement of the scholars is that it is general, even between the People of the Sunnah and the People of innovation, as passed by us, I think, in what?

* Student: The Nuniyyah.

* The Shaykh: In the Nuniyyah, we passed that it is general.

* The student: Even between the believers and the disbelievers?

* The Shaykh: Even between... As for those with rights, there is no doubt that Allah will judge between them. Whoever has a right over his brother, this is a known matter. But even in legal matters, if they differ about them and some of them are, for example, obstinate, then Allah judges between them. As for those whose disagreement arose from ijtihad, I do not think there is a dispute between them, because the reality is that their path is one; all of them want the truth.

* The student: But the truth is one?

* The Shaykh: Yes indeed, but each of them is considered rewarded: if he is correct he has two rewards, and if he errs he has one reward.

* The student: Shaykh, in a specific ijtihadi issue, the truth in it is one.

* The Shaykh: There is no doubt.

* The student: There is disagreement?

* The Shaykh: But each of them is upon the truth in what he adopted, because he exerted effort and ruled by what he saw as the truth.

* The student: But it is not clarified?

* The Shaykh: No, no, on the Day of Resurrection they will not dispute.

* Student: Shaykh, ﴿He is the best of helpers﴾. There is a helper, but not... this is from the most general states (...).

* The Shaykh: Yes indeed. Among the benefits also: there exists someone who helps other than Allah, meaning someone exists who helps other than Allah, and this is correct: ﴿And if they seek your help in religion, then you must give help, except against a people between you and them is a treaty﴾ [Al-Anfal 72]. But Allah is the best of helpers, just as there is a creator other than Allah, yet Allah is the best of creators. As we mentioned to you previously, creation attributed to other than Allah is not the creation attributed to Allah, because creation attributed to Allah is origination, while creation attributed to other than Allah is nothing but transformation and changing a thing from one thing into another, from one form into another, for example.

* Student: Shaykh, obedience here, is it general?

* The Shaykh: What?

* The student: Obedience to the disbelievers, is it general here?

* The Shaykh: General?

* Student: Shaykh, in crafts?

Shaykh: No, we said: we restricted it. What did we say?

Students: The acts of worship (al-ta'abbudiyya).

Shaykh: In matters of worship. As for these technical or craft matters, or the means of livelihood, or how to plough the land, these are not included in the verse.
* * *
Student: I seek refuge with Allah from Satan the accursed. ﴿We shall cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved, because they associated with Allah that for which He had sent down no authority. Their abode is the Fire, and wretched is the residence of the wrongdoers. (151) And Allah had certainly fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them by His permission, until, when you lost courage and disputed about the matter and disobeyed after He had shown you that for which you longed. Among you are those who desire this world, and among you are those who desire the Hereafter. Then He turned you away from them to test you. And He has already pardoned you, and Allah is full of bounty toward the believers. (152)﴾ [Al 'Imran 151, 152].

Shaykh: I seek refuge with Allah from Satan the accursed. Earlier verses warned against obeying the disbelievers. In which verse?

Student: In the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, if you obey those who disbelieve, they will return you to your heels, and you will turn back as losers.﴾

Shaykh: Good. What is the purpose of the warning?

Student: (...).

Shaykh: Turning back on one's heels and returning as losers. Does this include every kind of obedience?

Student: We made an exception from it (...). We said: this obedience is only in what one worships Allah the Mighty and Majestic by; as for what is a craft or the like, it is not included in the verse.

Shaykh: It is not included in the verse?

Student: No, it is not included.

Shaykh: It is not included in the verse. We have also mentioned the saying of Allah: ﴿So Allah gave them the reward of this world and the good reward of the Hereafter.﴾ Why did He describe the worldly reward as "reward" and the Hereafter's as "good reward"?

Student: Because the reward of the Hereafter is that Allah either repays the servant's good deed with its like, or...

Shaykh: With its like?!

Student: No, the reward of an evil deed is with its like, but a good deed is multiplied to ten times its like, up to seven hundred times. So Allah the Mighty and Majestic mentioned this good reward to indicate that He will recompense them with this, and that their recompense is not a recompense of mere requital but a recompense of bounty and kindness.

Shaykh: Yes indeed.

Student: That the world has no goodness at all, and that the Hereafter is the good reward.

Shaykh: Yes. Because the reward of this world, however great, is deficient, unlike the reward of the Hereafter. Here He said: ﴿the good reward of the Hereafter﴾, and in it is an indication, as we said, of the expiation of their sins for what they did. Has the affirmation of Allah's love been mentioned in the previous verses?

Student: From His saying: ﴿And Allah loves the good-doers.﴾

Shaykh: ﴿Allah loves the good-doers.﴾ And what is the love of Allah? Is it His reward or something else? Is the love of Allah His reward?

Student: It is an attribute befitting Allah, glorified and exalted be He.

Shaykh: And the reward is from...?

Student: From the causes of love.

Shaykh: From its causes or from its effects?

Student: From its effects.

Shaykh: From the effects of love. Good. Has anyone among the people opposed this?

Student: Yes, the Jahmiyya and the Mu'tazila opposed it.

Shaykh: And the Ash'ariyya too, for they denied the reality of love. How did they interpret it?

Student: By its mujib (cause), I mean...

Shaykh: By its mujib or its mujab?

Student: By what it necessitates.

Shaykh: I say: by the mujib or by the mujab?

Student: By the mujab.

Shaykh: By the mujab.

Student: I mean by what results from it.

Shaykh: No, no, the word you said requires analysis. Shall we say: by the mujab or by the mujib?

Student: By the mujab.

Shaykh: By the mujab. Love now has a cause; the cause is called (mujib, "that which necessitates"), and it has a reward called (mujab, "that which is necessitated"). For example, following the Messenger ﷺ we call a mujib of the love of Allah, ﴿Say: If you love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you﴾ [Al 'Imran 31], and the reward for love is the (mujab). So the mujib is the cause, and the muqtada is the cause; the mujab is the effect, and the muqtada is the effect. Why did they interpret love by its effect, that is, by the reward?

Student: Because the occurrence of love is the inclination of a person toward what...

Shaykh: Toward what brings him benefit.

Student: That is, a benefit, or following His command, and Allah is far above that.

Shaykh: That is one. And another?

Student: And they said love is an accident ('arad).

Shaykh: An accident?

Student: Yes; because love subsists only in a body, or it subsists only...

Another student: They said: love exists only between things of the same kind.

Shaykh: Well said: it exists only between things of the same kind, and there is no likeness between the Creator and the created. Well said. How do we refute this reasoning?

They say: love exists only between two things of the same kind: man and man, woman and woman, man and woman. It does not exist between two things that are utterly different, so it does not exist between the Creator and the created.

Student: Do we refute it?

Shaykh: We refute it.

Student: We refute it by saying that a person loves, for example, apples, and an apple is not like him (...). If love is specific to those of the same kind, how does a person love apples?!

Shaykh: And do you love apples?!

Student: Apples and grapes and others!!

Shaykh: Correct. But is there evidence from the Sunnah for affirming love between two things that are not of the same kind?

Student: Yes, concerning the palm tree?

Shaykh: Concerning the palm tree? They did not mention this.

Student: Mount Uhud.

Shaykh: Concerning Mount Uhud. Good. And likewise he approved of Abu Talha when he said: "The most beloved of my property to me is Bayruha'" [Narrated by al-Bukhari (1461) from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik.] Is it clear?

Their claim that love exists only between things of the same kind is a false claim, refuted by sense and reality. Has the affirmation of wilaya (guardianship) for Allah been mentioned to us, and did we mention that it is divided?

Student: Into specific guardianship and general guardianship.

Shaykh: Example of the specific?

Student: The specific: ﴿And Allah is the Wali of the believers.﴾

Shaykh: Yes, ﴿Allah is the Wali of those who believe﴾ [Al-Baqara 257]; this is specific. And the general?

Student: The general means that Allah is the Mawla of all people.

Shaykh: He manages the affairs of all creation. What is its evidence, or an example of it?

Student: Its evidence is the negation of specific guardianship from them.

Shaykh: No, no. The evidence for establishing general guardianship?

Student: The saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Then they are returned to Allah, their true Mawla﴾ [Al-An'am 62].

Shaykh: Yes, ﴿until when death comes to one of you, Our messengers take him, and they do not fail. (61) Then they are returned to Allah, their true Mawla﴾ [Al-An'am 61, 62]. This is general.

And there is a verse that combined both matters in His saying: ﴿That is because Allah is the Mawla of those who believe, and that the disbelievers have no Mawla﴾ [Muhammad 11]. It affirmed the specific guardianship and negated it from those who disbelieved.

Student: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed. ﴿O you who have believed, if you obey those who disbelieve, they will turn you back on your heels, and you will turn about [as] losers. Rather, Allah is your protector, and He is the best of helpers. We will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve because they associated with Allah that for which He had not sent down any authority; and their refuge is the Fire, and wretched is the residence of the wrongdoers.﴾ [Surah Al-Imran 149–152]

* The Shaykh: All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and all his companions. To proceed: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿O you who have believed, if you obey those who disbelieve, they will turn you back on your heels, and you will turn about [as] losers.﴾

Allah has opened this verse with the vocative address, and opening with the address indicates concern for what will be directed to the one addressed, because the address serves to alert, and a person is only alerted to something that concerns him. So when Allah directs the speech, or when speech is opened with the address, it is a sign of attention to it because of its importance.

Then He addressed the servants by the title of faith: ﴿O you who have believed﴾. The purpose of this is, first: to encourage and motivate acceptance of what is conveyed, because faith is what moves a person to accept what Allah has commanded and to abandon what Allah has forbidden. For this reason Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "When Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, then prick up your ears to it, for it is either good that you are commanded to do or evil that you are forbidden from."[[Narrated by Ibn al-Mubarak in al-Zuhd (36), and Sa'id ibn Mansur in al-Sunan (50), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud.]]

It also serves a second benefit: that acceptance of what is mentioned is among the requirements of faith. Just as if you addressed a generous person and said: "O generous one, give to the poor and help the needy," this indicates that giving to the poor and helping the needy is among the requirements of his generosity. Thus, accepting what comes after this address is among the requirements of faith.

The third benefit or purpose: that not accepting it is a deficiency in faith, because if the address is directed to a person with the word of faith, yet he does not comply, this is a deficiency in his faith. For what comes after ﴿O you who have believed﴾ is either something commanded, or something forbidden, or something reported. So abandoning what is commanded is a deficiency in faith, falling into what is prohibited is a deficiency in faith, and denying the report is a deficiency in faith.

Let us listen to this report from Allah, the Exalted, the report of One who is Knowing of everything: ﴿if you obey those who disbelieve﴾. Here ﴿in﴾ is conditional, and the verb of the condition is ﴿تُطِيعُوا (tuti'u)﴾, but it was not apocopated. Shall we say so?

* Students: Apocopated (majzum).
* The Shaykh: Apocopated. By what?
* The students: By the deletion of the nun.
* The Shaykh: By the deletion of the nun, and the waw is the subject, because it is one of the five verbs. As for the response of the condition, it is His saying: ﴿يَرُدُّوكُمْ عَلَى أَعْقَابِكُمْ (yaruddukum ʿala aʿqabikum)﴾, which is apocopated by the deletion of the nun, and the waw is the subject.

His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, if you obey those who disbelieve﴾. So there is a command directed from the disbelievers to the believers, since obedience corresponds to command; or a prohibition directed from the disbelievers to the believers, when they command them to indecency and forbid them what is good. If you obey them in that, the answer is: ﴿they will turn you back on your heels﴾.

His saying: ﴿if you obey those who disbelieve﴾ is general, encompassing the Jews, the Christians, the polytheists, and the atheists who have no religion and worship nothing. Any one of the disbelievers, if he commands you to something and you obey him, he will turn you back on your heels, and you will turn about as a loser.

His saying: ﴿if you obey those who disbelieve﴾ refers to what is an act of worship to Allah. As for other matters, such as matters of craft for example, there is no doubt that it does not enter the verse. If an engineer from among the disbelievers commanded you to make such-and-such so that the result would be such-and-such, it does not enter the verse. What is intended is what falls under the category of, what? Under the category of worship: he commands you to indecency, drinking wine, theft, bad character, or forbids you from what is good, forbids you from prayer, forbids you from sincerity to Allah, and similar things.

His saying: ﴿they will turn you back on your heels﴾. Al-A'qab is the plural of ʿaqib, which is the back of the foot, and it is called al-ʿurqub (the heel). That is, they make you walk backwards. It is well known that one who walks backwards will fall into pits and step on thorns and pebbles. This is close to His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Is one who walks prone on his face better guided, or one who walks upright on a straight path?﴾ [Al-Mulk 22]. So here: ﴿they will turn you back on your heels﴾.

﴿and you will turn about [as] losers﴾. ﴿Tanqalibu (you will turn about)﴾: inqilab implies a transformation from one state to another, which is why it is said: he turned in his bed from the right side to the left side. So there is a transformation from one state to another if we obey these disbelievers: ﴿you will turn about﴾.

His saying: ﴿khasirin (losers)﴾ is a circumstantial state (hal), a hal from the waw in His saying "tanqalibu". That is: you will be in loss after you were in profit, because faith is profit, as He said, the Exalted: ﴿By time, indeed mankind is in loss﴾ [Al-Asr 1–2]. Which mankind? All of them. And for this the definite article here is for generality; that is, every human being is indeed in loss, ﴿except for those who have believed and done righteous deeds and advised each other to truth and advised each other to patience﴾ [Al-Asr 3]. Those who are characterized by these four qualities are the winners, and whoever else is a loser: a loser of what? A loser of his time. This is the wisdom behind Allah swearing by time rather than anything else, because time is the storehouse of deeds. If a person does not uphold these four qualities, he has lost his time, and his life becomes a loss.

﴿you will turn about [as] losers﴾ because you have shifted from what? From Islam to disbelief. And in another verse that preceded: ﴿O you who have believed, if you obey a party from those who were given the Scripture, they will turn you back to disbelief after your faith﴾ [Al-Imran 100]. Here He said: ﴿those who disbelieve﴾, and there He said: ﴿a party from those who were given the Scripture﴾, because among those who were given the Scripture some are good, as He said: ﴿They are not all alike. Among the People of the Scripture is a community standing [in obedience]﴾ [Al-Imran 113]. This is from the eloquence of the Qur'an: when He said: ﴿if you obey a party from those who were given the Scripture﴾, He said: ﴿they will turn you back to disbelief after your faith﴾, since it is a party of them. As for the disbelievers, all of the disbelievers want from us that we what? That we disbelieve, and that we turn back on our heels as losers.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Rather, Allah is your protector﴾. Is ﴿bal (rather)﴾ here for transitional retraction (idrab intiqali) or nullifying retraction (idrab ibtali)?

* A student: Transitional.
* The Shaykh: No, it is nullifying (ibtali), but it is the nullification of something implied. Because our obedience to the disbelievers is for hope or fear: that is, if we obey the disbelievers, then either we obey them out of hope, or we obey them out of fear. Out of hope that they will help us, give us wealth and similar things; out of fear that they will strike at us, fight and attack us. Here the retraction fits perfectly, so He said: ﴿Rather, Allah is your protector﴾, meaning: do not obey them and take them as allies, for you have one who is better than their alliance, and that is Allah. Therefore this retraction is considered a nullifying retraction of something implied: if you obey those who disbelieve in order that they become your allies, then they will turn you back on your heels and you will turn about as losers.

Then He said: ﴿Rather, Allah is your protector﴾. If Allah, glorified and exalted, is our protector, then no one among creation concerns us, as long as we believe that Allah is our protector with the qualities we possess that make us deserving of His protection. Not every person who says: ﴿Indeed, my protector is Allah﴾ [Al-A'raf 196] has Allah as his protector. But if Allah is our protector with the qualities we possess that make us deserving of protection, then they will never concern us, no matter how strong they are, and no matter their craft or wealth, they will not concern us, because with us is whom?

* A student: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
* The Shaykh: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, who says to a thing "Be" and it is. But Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, commands us to fight with our hands. So when our ability is exhausted while we carry out what is obligatory, then there comes to us a victory from Allah that no human has the power to achieve. This is a truth we must understand: we are commanded to prepare what we can and to fight, but when something beyond our capacity comes, then a victory comes from Allah for which neither we nor others have the power. And there are witnesses in history to what I have said. Mūsā, peace be upon him, when he left Egypt, and Pharaoh had gathered for him all the people of the cities, every city, to finish off Mūsā and his people, and said: ﴿Indeed, these are but a small band﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara 54], to diminish their standing among his people so they would prepare and resolve to destroy them. They reached the sea. Does a person have the power against the sea?

* Students: No.
* The Shaykh: No, he has no power. For this reason his people said: ﴿Indeed, we are to be overtaken﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara 61], because the sea was before them and Pharaoh and his soldiers behind them: how could they escape? He said: ﴿No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara 62]. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, commanded him to strike the sea, and he struck it once with a staff, a staff carried in the hand, just once, and it split into twelve dry paths in an instant. This wet earth that was mud and clay became dry in an instant, and this flowing water became each division like a great mountain, like a mountain standing still, not flowing. Some scholars even say that Allah placed in these masses of water gaps so that the Children of Israel could see one another, because a person in the middle of the water has water to his right and left, and fears that his companions have drowned, so Allah made for them gaps in these mountains where they could see one another in an instant. No human has the power for this. But whoever Allah is his protector is victorious. They came out of the sea safe. Then Pharaoh and his people entered, and when they had entered the sea and were all inside, Allah commanded the sea to close, and it closed in an instant, drowning them in an instant. Pharaoh had terrified the Children of Israel, so Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, brought out his body for them to look at: ﴿So today We will save you in your body that you may be a sign to those after you﴾ [Yunus 92], and they were reassured that he had perished.

It is mentioned in the history of this nation that al-ʿAla' ibn al-Hadrami, when he reached Bahrain and found the sea before him with no ships, called upon Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and he crossed the water on foot, and the horses and camels all walked on the water as if walking on a rock; that is, a stone.[[al-Tabarani in al-Awsat (3495) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, and Ibn Abi Shaybah (30301) abridged from the hadith of al-ʿAla'.]] This is something we have no power for.

Likewise, what is mentioned about Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas at the conquest of al-Mada'in: he reached the Tigris, which was throwing up foam from the force of its current, and the Persians had crossed it with their ships and bridges, and had broken the bridges and sunk the ships, and the Muslims had nothing left to cross with. Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas said to Salman al-Farisi: "Give us from—that is, from your opinions," for he, may Allah be pleased with him, was a man of judgment in war, and he was the one who advised the digging of the trench around Medina in the year of the Confederates. Salman said: "By Allah, I see no stratagem in this. The sea is before us, and we have no ships or bridges. But let me look into the people: if they are upon what is proper and they are worthy of victory, then the Children of Israel are no more deserving of victory than we are, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, split the sea for them and they crossed." He went and found the people to be horsemen by day and monks by night: at night in bowing and prostration, and by day preparing the equipment of war and readying themselves. He returned to him after three days and said: "I have found the people in the best of condition, but put your trust in Allah." Sa'd called out for departure, and that he would cross the river, and said: "I will say Allahu akbar three times, and when I say it the third time, then plunge into the river in the name of Allah." They did so. It is said—glory be to Allah—that they all crossed with their horses, their foot soldiers and their camels, so much so that some historians mention that when the horses grew tired, Allah created for them a mound on which they could stand and rest. This is a victory for which we have no power, but it is from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

For this reason He says here: do not befriend the disbelievers, and do not obey them, seeking victory or out of fear of them, for you have a protector greater than them, the Mighty and Majestic, who is Allah: ﴿Rather, Allah is your protector, and He is the best of helpers﴾. ﴿He is the best of helpers﴾: that is, the best of those who help; rather He is the best of helpers, the greatest of helpers, the most capable and the most powerful, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿If Allah helps you, no one can overcome you; and if He forsakes you, who is there that can help you after Him?﴾ [Al-Imran 160]. No one.

So the retraction here is among the finest that could occur in this context: ﴿Rather, Allah is your protector, and He is the best of helpers﴾, that is, the best of those who help.

* Benefits in these verses:

First: the excellence of faith, in that the address is directed to people with the description of faith in a context of guidance and admonition, and that faith necessitates compliance.

* Among its benefits: it is not permissible for us to obey the disbelievers, because obeying them is a means to disbelief: ﴿if you obey those who disbelieve, they will turn you back on your heels, and you will turn about as losers﴾ [Al-Imran 149].

* And among them: the obligation to beware of the disbelievers, the obligation of caution, and that they can never plan a matter that contains benefit for the Muslims and Islam, never, impossible. Even the allies who have an alliance between them and the Muslims cannot ally with the Muslims except for, what? For their own interest, certainly. Khuza'ah had an alliance with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, but it was for their own interest.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that obeying the disbelievers inevitably results in disbelief; as shown by His saying: ﴿they will turn you back on your heels, and you will turn about as losers﴾. How so? The disbelievers take from us little by little. They want from us things that we obey them in, and they stop at this limit? No, they do not stop; they add things, until we turn back on our heels.

This does not mean that we prostrate to them and bow to them. No. When a person leaves his religion, that is sufficient. For this reason it is mentioned that some of their leaders said: "We strive for missionary work, not so that we bring the Muslim out of his religion into Christianity, because the Christian religion is known, far from the natural disposition (fitrah), and by the Christian religion I mean what they follow now. As for what Jesus brought, it is true, but what Jesus brought has ended and was abrogated by the religion of Islam."

He says: "We do not want to bring the Muslim out of his religion into Christianity; it is enough for us that one of two things happens: either we bring him out of his religion into no religion, so that he becomes like an animal whose only concern is his belly, his private parts and his pleasures; or we make him doubt the religion, we make him doubt. And it is known that faith is not valid with doubt; faith is certainty. If a person has even the slightest hesitation, he is not a believer. There must be faith; there is no faith with hesitation. They say: this is sufficient, that we bring him out to become either an animal or a doubter, perplexed and uncertain. This is a result of disbelief."

Among the benefits of this verse: disbelief is a loss, as His saying shows: ﴿So you will return as losers﴾. And if disbelief is a loss, then faith is gain. For this reason we find no one more profitable than the believer in this world, even if he is poor, and even if he is alone, having neither wealth nor children, he is still more profitable than the disbeliever. This is because the disbeliever has lost both this world and the Hereafter. He has not benefited from his worldly life. In truth, the disbeliever has not benefited from his worldly life; he lives only as cattle live, as the One most knowledgeable of all has said: ﴿And those who disbelieve enjoy themselves and eat as cattle eat﴾ [Muhammad 12]. Subhan Allah! A perfectly matching example: ﴿They enjoy themselves and eat as cattle eat, and the Fire is their abode﴾ [Muhammad 12]. The result is evil: ﴿the Fire is their abode.﴾ They leave this world, in which they were given comfort, for the Fire of Hell, may Allah protect us, and at that time their departure is harsher and more difficult. This is unlike the believer. I ask Allah to make me and you among them.

The believer leaves this world, with its hardship and its troubles, for the abode of bliss, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Those whom the angels take in death while they are good, saying: "Peace be upon you. Enter Paradise for what you used to do."﴾ [An-Nahl 32] at the time of their death.

This verse also indicates the bliss of the grave, because He said: ﴿Enter Paradise﴾ now, from your death. And it is established in the authentic hadith: "His grave is widened for him as far as the eye can see, a door to Paradise is opened for him, and there comes to him of its breeze and its bliss," as is well known. [[Narrated by Abu Dawud (4753) from the hadith of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib.]]

Among the benefits of this verse: extreme caution, or strong warning, against obeying the disbelievers and taking them as allies. With great regret, we today have come to treat loyalty and disavowal (al-wala' wal-bara', (loyalty to the believers and disavowal of the disbelievers)) lightly. The loyalty and disavowal that must come from the believer, and through which he tastes the sweetness of faith, is lacking, except in those whom Allah wills. When we were young, when a Christian was mentioned, a person's skin would crawl. His skin would crawl. "I seek refuge in Allah, a Christian or a Jew!" Now it is said that some Muslims describe a Christian as a brother: "Our brother so-and-so." How is so-and-so your brother?! What did Ibrahim, peace be upon him, and his people say?

* The students: ﴿Indeed, we are free from you﴾..
* The Shaykh: ﴿Indeed, we are free from you and from what you worship besides Allah.﴾ See, they disassociated themselves from them before they disassociated themselves from the idols: ﴿Indeed, we are free from you and from what you worship other than Allah. We have rejected you, and there has appeared between us and you animosity and hatred forever until you believe in Allah alone.﴾ [Al-Mumtahanah 4]. And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿There has already been for you an excellent pattern in Ibrahim and those with him﴾ [Al-Mumtahanah 4].
