This excellent pattern is that we disassociate ourselves from the disbelievers, that we hate them, and that we believe they are enemies, however gently they speak to us and however they embellish their words. They are our enemies, and by Allah, this enmity will never turn into loyalty, until the Day of Resurrection.

So it is obligatory upon us to be cautious. Here we address the rulers and the common people, warning them against the disbelievers and their allegiance, and advising them to take them as enemies, real enemies, as is the reality. Likewise, the subjects must keep away from the disbelievers, especially in this peninsula, because this peninsula has a special status in keeping the disbelievers away from it. The Prophet, peace be upon him, during his final illness, at the time of leaving this world, enjoined his community, saying: "Expel the polytheists from the Arabian Peninsula" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3053) and Muslim (1637/20) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]], and he said: "I will surely expel the Jews and the Christians from the Arabian Peninsula until I leave none but a Muslim" [[Narrated by Muslim (1767/63) from the hadith of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab.]]. The first is in the two Sahihs, and the second is in Muslim. He also said, in what is authentically reported from him: "Expel the Jews and the Christians from the Arabian Peninsula" [[Narrated by Ibn Abi 'Asim in al-Ahad wal-Mathani (234) from the hadith of Abu 'Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah.]].

We advise our common brothers to take this injunction of the Messenger, peace be upon him, into careful consideration, and not to bring into this land any Jew, Christian, or other disbeliever except out of supreme necessity and within specific limits. In other words, they should not bring them for permanent settlement; rather they should bring them when necessary and only to the extent of the necessity, for a specific period, not as permanent settlement.

Among the benefits of these two verses: the affirmation of Allah's wilayah (guardianship/loyalty). The guardianship of Allah for the believers is affirmed, because He said: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, then He said: ﴿Rather, Allah is your Protector﴾. This guardianship is specific, because Allah's guardianship over creation is of two types:

A general one, for everyone. Its meaning is managing affairs, whether by granting victory or by abandonment. Pay attention: this is general guardianship. What does it mean? Managing affairs, by victory, abandonment, or otherwise. The point is that the manager of creation is Allah, Mighty and Majestic. This is general guardianship, and among its examples is His saying: ﴿until, when death comes to one of you, Our messengers take him, and they do not fail [in their duty]. Then they are returned to Allah, their true Protector﴾ [Al-An'am 61-62].

As for the specific guardianship, it is exclusive to the believers: ﴿Allah is the Protector of those who have believed; He brings them out of darkness into light﴾ [Al-Baqarah 257], and ﴿And Allah is the Protector of the believers﴾ [Ali 'Imran 68]. He, Mighty and Majestic, is the Protector of the God-fearing. So this guardianship is specific, and its meaning or implication is that Allah, glorified and exalted, takes charge of the one who deserves it with kindness and care, granting him success. This is explained by the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him: that the Prophet ﷺ said, relaying from his Lord: "Whoever shows enmity to a friend of Mine, I have declared war against him. My servant does not draw near to Me with anything more beloved to Me than what I have made obligatory upon him. My servant continues to draw near to Me with voluntary acts until I love him. When I love him, I am his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees, his hand with which he strikes, and his foot with which he walks." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari (6502) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]] That is, Allah guides him in all his conduct. So this is a specific guardianship, restricted to those among the believers and the God-fearing who deserve it.

Here: ﴿Rather, Allah is your Protector﴾, is it meant as general or specific?

* The students: Specific.
* The Shaykh: Specific.

* Among the benefits of this verse: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is the Helper of His allies, because of His saying: ﴿And He is the best of helpers﴾, and this is from His guardianship.

If someone says: How do we answer what Allah has informed us in His Book, that among people are those who killed the prophets without right? How do we answer that?

The answer to this is one of two ways.

The first: the victory meant, or the promise of victory, is for the one who was commanded to fight, for Allah grants him victory, because Allah does not assign him anything except that the outcome is in his favor. As for those prophets who were killed, they were not commanded to fight.

The second: we say that victory is of two kinds. Victory of a person, meaning that a man witnesses it in his own person. And moral victory, meaning that Allah grants victory to whoever brought this message even after his death. For this reason you find the imams of the Muslims, their sayings are as if they were alive among us, are they not? The imams' words are alive, so it is as if they are alive. If you take a book by one of the scholars and read it and benefit from it, it is as if this scholar taught you. So is this victory or not? It is victory: victory for his principle, his goal, and his call. This is victory.

There is also a third way: we distribute victory over time. We say that victory may be in this world and may be in the Hereafter, and those prophets who were killed will have their victory in the Hereafter, when they dispute with their peoples. You should notice, brothers, that the people of truth and the people of falsehood dispute before Allah on the Day of Resurrection. He judges between them concerning what they differed about. Do not think that the disagreement between the people of truth and the people of falsehood ends with this world. No, Allah will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection and grant victory to the people of truth. ﴿Your relatives and your children will not benefit you on the Day of Resurrection; He will separate you﴾ [Al-Mumtahanah 3], ﴿Then to Us is your return, and We will inform you of what you used to do﴾ [Yunus 23].

In any case, many verses indicate this: ﴿Indeed, you will die, and indeed, they will die. Then indeed, on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord you will dispute﴾ [Az-Zumar 30-31]. So if Allah rules in favor of the people of truth against the people of falsehood on the Day of Resurrection, is this victory or not? It is victory. So the answer to this verse is in three ways: either we say that those promised victory are those who were commanded to fight; or we say that victory is of two kinds, victory for a person who is granted victory in his lifetime, and victory for his call and what he brought, which happens even after his death; or we say that the victory meant is the victory on the Day of Resurrection when they dispute before Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, We will surely support Our messengers and those who believed in the worldly life and on the Day when the witnesses will stand﴾ [Ghafir 51].

* Student: Shaykh, may Allah be good to you; meaning, confirming Him, glorified and exalted: ﴿If you obey a faction of those who were given the Scripture﴾. Shall we take it, if we return it to His saying, glorified and exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 51], in the context, do we say Jew or do we say Christian?

* The Shaykh: No, the verse is explicit: ﴿a faction of those who were given the Scripture﴾, because some of the People of the Book are with them (...), but not all of them. Then the People of the Book in reality at the present time, there is not (...), because those among them who have affection for the believers are the nearest people in affection. They are the ones who, when they hear what has been sent down to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of what they recognized of the truth, so... close to the believers. At the least call, they are moved and enter Islam. But the Christians of today, like the Jews of yesterday, are obstinate against Islam, and they do not want Islam to be established.

* The student: Enmity in general; meaning, not among the Jews and Christians?

* The Shaykh: At the present time, this is the apparent situation. For this reason you will not find a Christian who has knowledge but cannot believe. But the ignorant Christians may believe. If there were real callers from among the Muslims, many Christians would enter Islam, the ignorant among them. But those who have knowledge, Allah knows best; hearts are in the hand of Allah, but it is far that they would enter Islam.

* Student: Some exegetes mentioned that the Children of Israel, or that Pharaoh and his people, when they followed Musa, some of them remained who had not entered the sea, so Allah sent angels who threw them into the sea. Is this correct?

* The Shaykh: Allah knows best. But we must know that what is not in the Qur'an, and is among the authentic reports of the Sunnah, is neither believed nor disbelieved, because Allah said: ﴿Has there not come to you the news of those before you: the people of Nuh, 'Ad, and Thamud, and those after them, whom none knows but Allah﴾ [Ibrahim 9]. So we receive their reports only from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, either from His Book or from authentic Sunnah, and whatever else is not like this is withheld from judgment.

* The student: Likewise, the number, Shaykh; he did not specify them by numbers.

* The Shaykh: Never. We do not know their number; all of this we do not know.

* Student: Shaykh, the address directed to the Messenger ﷺ specifically and the Companions; meaning some people..

* The Shaykh: What?

* The student: The address directed to the Messenger, peace be upon him..

* The Shaykh: Where is it?

* The student: ﴿O you who have believed﴾.

* The Shaykh: By Allah, this is a problem. Is this specific to the Messenger and the Companions?

* The student: It was revealed to the Messenger ﷺ.

* The Shaykh: Yes, that is known; the whole Qur'an was revealed to him. But are the addresses in the Qur'an and the calls in the Qur'an only for the Messenger and his Companions?

* The student: And to the common people.

* The Shaykh: ﴿O you who have believed﴾ is a description that applies until the Day of Resurrection.

* Student: But I mean, Shaykh, did something of this kind happen during the time of the Prophet ﷺ among the Companions, or does it have a occasion of revelation?

* The Shaykh: Never. I do not know of anyone except those who apostatized, but those among the Arabs who apostatized were not in the position of disbelievers.

* Student: Shaykh, may Allah be good to you, they say about Pharaoh that he is still mummified until now, still mummified in his body.

* The Shaykh: Allah knows best. They say what is in the pyramids are their bodies, and Allah knows best.

* The student: Would this be a confirmation of what Allah mentioned in the Qur'an?

* The Shaykh: Never. Because His saying: ﴿for those after you﴾ does not mean for those after you until the Day of Resurrection. It is enough that the Children of Israel witnessed him and were certain that the man had died, because he terrorized them; he used to kill their sons and spare their women, a tyrannical oppressor. And a person cannot be convinced and reassured that he has died except by seeing him, because Satan comes and says: No, perhaps he is alive, perhaps he swam to the edge of the sea and escaped.

* Student: Shaykh, on the Day of Resurrection people dispute before Allah and judgment is given between them. Is this dispute between the group of believers and disbelievers, or between any dispute, even between a believer and a believer?

* The Shaykh: The apparent statement of the scholars is that it is general, even between the People of the Sunnah and the People of innovation, as passed by us, I think, in what?

* Student: The Nuniyyah.

* The Shaykh: In the Nuniyyah, we passed that it is general.

* The student: Even between the believers and the disbelievers?

* The Shaykh: Even between... As for those with rights, there is no doubt that Allah will judge between them. Whoever has a right over his brother, this is a known matter. But even in legal matters, if they differ about them and some of them are, for example, obstinate, then Allah judges between them. As for those whose disagreement arose from ijtihad, I do not think there is a dispute between them, because the reality is that their path is one; all of them want the truth.

* The student: But the truth is one?

* The Shaykh: Yes indeed, but each of them is considered rewarded: if he is correct he has two rewards, and if he errs he has one reward.

* The student: Shaykh, in a specific ijtihadi issue, the truth in it is one.

* The Shaykh: There is no doubt.

* The student: There is disagreement?

* The Shaykh: But each of them is upon the truth in what he adopted, because he exerted effort and ruled by what he saw as the truth.

* The student: But it is not clarified?

* The Shaykh: No, no, on the Day of Resurrection they will not dispute.

* Student: Shaykh, ﴿He is the best of helpers﴾. There is a helper, but not... this is from the most general states (...).

* The Shaykh: Yes indeed. Among the benefits also: there exists someone who helps other than Allah, meaning someone exists who helps other than Allah, and this is correct: ﴿And if they seek your help in religion, then you must give help, except against a people between you and them is a treaty﴾ [Al-Anfal 72]. But Allah is the best of helpers, just as there is a creator other than Allah, yet Allah is the best of creators. As we mentioned to you previously, creation attributed to other than Allah is not the creation attributed to Allah, because creation attributed to Allah is origination, while creation attributed to other than Allah is nothing but transformation and changing a thing from one thing into another, from one form into another, for example.

* Student: Shaykh, obedience here, is it general?

* The Shaykh: What?

* The student: Obedience to the disbelievers, is it general here?

* The Shaykh: General?

* Student: Shaykh, in crafts?

Shaykh: No, we said: we restricted it. What did we say?

Students: The acts of worship (al-ta'abbudiyya).

Shaykh: In matters of worship. As for these technical or craft matters, or the means of livelihood, or how to plough the land, these are not included in the verse.
* * *
Student: I seek refuge with Allah from Satan the accursed. ﴿We shall cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved, because they associated with Allah that for which He had sent down no authority. Their abode is the Fire, and wretched is the residence of the wrongdoers. (151) And Allah had certainly fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them by His permission, until, when you lost courage and disputed about the matter and disobeyed after He had shown you that for which you longed. Among you are those who desire this world, and among you are those who desire the Hereafter. Then He turned you away from them to test you. And He has already pardoned you, and Allah is full of bounty toward the believers. (152)﴾ [Al 'Imran 151, 152].

Shaykh: I seek refuge with Allah from Satan the accursed. Earlier verses warned against obeying the disbelievers. In which verse?

Student: In the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, if you obey those who disbelieve, they will return you to your heels, and you will turn back as losers.﴾

Shaykh: Good. What is the purpose of the warning?

Student: (...).

Shaykh: Turning back on one's heels and returning as losers. Does this include every kind of obedience?

Student: We made an exception from it (...). We said: this obedience is only in what one worships Allah the Mighty and Majestic by; as for what is a craft or the like, it is not included in the verse.

Shaykh: It is not included in the verse?

Student: No, it is not included.

Shaykh: It is not included in the verse. We have also mentioned the saying of Allah: ﴿So Allah gave them the reward of this world and the good reward of the Hereafter.﴾ Why did He describe the worldly reward as "reward" and the Hereafter's as "good reward"?

Student: Because the reward of the Hereafter is that Allah either repays the servant's good deed with its like, or...

Shaykh: With its like?!

Student: No, the reward of an evil deed is with its like, but a good deed is multiplied to ten times its like, up to seven hundred times. So Allah the Mighty and Majestic mentioned this good reward to indicate that He will recompense them with this, and that their recompense is not a recompense of mere requital but a recompense of bounty and kindness.

Shaykh: Yes indeed.

Student: That the world has no goodness at all, and that the Hereafter is the good reward.

Shaykh: Yes. Because the reward of this world, however great, is deficient, unlike the reward of the Hereafter. Here He said: ﴿the good reward of the Hereafter﴾, and in it is an indication, as we said, of the expiation of their sins for what they did. Has the affirmation of Allah's love been mentioned in the previous verses?

Student: From His saying: ﴿And Allah loves the good-doers.﴾

Shaykh: ﴿Allah loves the good-doers.﴾ And what is the love of Allah? Is it His reward or something else? Is the love of Allah His reward?

Student: It is an attribute befitting Allah, glorified and exalted be He.

Shaykh: And the reward is from...?

Student: From the causes of love.

Shaykh: From its causes or from its effects?

Student: From its effects.

Shaykh: From the effects of love. Good. Has anyone among the people opposed this?

Student: Yes, the Jahmiyya and the Mu'tazila opposed it.

Shaykh: And the Ash'ariyya too, for they denied the reality of love. How did they interpret it?

Student: By its mujib (cause), I mean...

Shaykh: By its mujib or its mujab?

Student: By what it necessitates.

Shaykh: I say: by the mujib or by the mujab?

Student: By the mujab.

Shaykh: By the mujab.

Student: I mean by what results from it.

Shaykh: No, no, the word you said requires analysis. Shall we say: by the mujab or by the mujib?

Student: By the mujab.

Shaykh: By the mujab. Love now has a cause; the cause is called (mujib, "that which necessitates"), and it has a reward called (mujab, "that which is necessitated"). For example, following the Messenger ﷺ we call a mujib of the love of Allah, ﴿Say: If you love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you﴾ [Al 'Imran 31], and the reward for love is the (mujab). So the mujib is the cause, and the muqtada is the cause; the mujab is the effect, and the muqtada is the effect. Why did they interpret love by its effect, that is, by the reward?

Student: Because the occurrence of love is the inclination of a person toward what...

Shaykh: Toward what brings him benefit.

Student: That is, a benefit, or following His command, and Allah is far above that.

Shaykh: That is one. And another?

Student: And they said love is an accident ('arad).

Shaykh: An accident?

Student: Yes; because love subsists only in a body, or it subsists only...

Another student: They said: love exists only between things of the same kind.

Shaykh: Well said: it exists only between things of the same kind, and there is no likeness between the Creator and the created. Well said. How do we refute this reasoning?

They say: love exists only between two things of the same kind: man and man, woman and woman, man and woman. It does not exist between two things that are utterly different, so it does not exist between the Creator and the created.

Student: Do we refute it?

Shaykh: We refute it.

Student: We refute it by saying that a person loves, for example, apples, and an apple is not like him (...). If love is specific to those of the same kind, how does a person love apples?!

Shaykh: And do you love apples?!

Student: Apples and grapes and others!!

Shaykh: Correct. But is there evidence from the Sunnah for affirming love between two things that are not of the same kind?

Student: Yes, concerning the palm tree?

Shaykh: Concerning the palm tree? They did not mention this.

Student: Mount Uhud.

Shaykh: Concerning Mount Uhud. Good. And likewise he approved of Abu Talha when he said: "The most beloved of my property to me is Bayruha'" [Narrated by al-Bukhari (1461) from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik.] Is it clear?

Their claim that love exists only between things of the same kind is a false claim, refuted by sense and reality. Has the affirmation of wilaya (guardianship) for Allah been mentioned to us, and did we mention that it is divided?

Student: Into specific guardianship and general guardianship.

Shaykh: Example of the specific?

Student: The specific: ﴿And Allah is the Wali of the believers.﴾

Shaykh: Yes, ﴿Allah is the Wali of those who believe﴾ [Al-Baqara 257]; this is specific. And the general?

Student: The general means that Allah is the Mawla of all people.

Shaykh: He manages the affairs of all creation. What is its evidence, or an example of it?

Student: Its evidence is the negation of specific guardianship from them.

Shaykh: No, no. The evidence for establishing general guardianship?

Student: The saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Then they are returned to Allah, their true Mawla﴾ [Al-An'am 62].

Shaykh: Yes, ﴿until when death comes to one of you, Our messengers take him, and they do not fail. (61) Then they are returned to Allah, their true Mawla﴾ [Al-An'am 61, 62]. This is general.

And there is a verse that combined both matters in His saying: ﴿That is because Allah is the Mawla of those who believe, and that the disbelievers have no Mawla﴾ [Muhammad 11]. It affirmed the specific guardianship and negated it from those who disbelieved.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verse 151–152 (part 1 of 4):

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿We shall cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved, because they associated with Allah...﴾ to the end.

﴿We shall cast﴾: the agent is Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. He referred to Himself with a verb in the plural, intending by it glorification; that is, "We shall cast" (we, meaning Allah alone). This can only be meant that way, because Allah is One and not plural, so no one can be with Him. This differs from others: if you say to a person "we shall come to you," it may mean you intend glorification, or it may mean you intend plurality. But with regard to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, the plurality that means multiplicity cannot be intended; only glorification is intended. This is shown by His saying in Surat al-Anfal: ﴿When your Lord inspired the angels, "I am with you, so strengthen those who believe. I will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved"﴾ [al-Anfal 12]. So Allah, glorified and exalted, is the One who casts. But He mentions Himself sometimes in the singular, because He is One, and sometimes in the plural, because He is Great.

Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah said: It is possible that He mentions Himself in the plural form because of the great hosts He has, which none knows but Him. So this is an indication that He is possessed of greatness, authority, and hosts that carry out whatever He commands, may He be exalted.

And His saying: ﴿We shall cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved﴾. The particle "sa" (sin) enters upon the imperfect verb and conveys two things. The first: nearness. The second: certainty. So it conveys certainty from one aspect and nearness from another aspect, unlike "sawfa," which conveys certainty and also deferral. For this reason "sawfa" is used for postponement, and "al-sin" for near future (tanfis), that is, nearness.

﴿We shall cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved﴾: there are two readings: ﴿ar-ru'b﴾ and ﴿ar-ru'ub﴾. This occurs frequently in the Arabic language; that is, the sukun for lightness and the vowel on the original form, like an-nahr and an-nahar. These are: ﴿ar-ru'b﴾ and ﴿ar-ru'ub﴾, and the meaning is one. Ar-ru'b: the most intense fear. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, mentioned that He casts terror into the heart, because when terror enters the heart, the body cannot remain firm. If the body remained firm, or a person tried to stand firm, his heart, from terror, would lift him off the ground and he would flee, and he cannot remain. For this reason, when Allah cast terror into the hearts of the Banu al-Nadir, what did they do? Each one of them began to save himself. Indeed, from the intensity of their fear they would carry their belongings, that is, goods, and break the houses, meaning they would not uproot the doors calmly and deliberately, because of the intense terror that had struck them. Terror is the strongest weapon against an enemy; so when Allah casts terror into the heart of the enemy, he will not remain.

﴿We shall cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved, because they associated with Allah﴾: the "ba" here denotes cause; that is, because of their associating others with Allah. And "ma" the scholars call masdariyyah, that is, "because of their association," and the sign of masdariyyah "ma" is that what follows it can be converted into a verbal noun (masdar). If what follows can be converted into a verbal noun, then it is masdariyyah. They have mentioned that "ma" has several meanings, ten meanings, collected or indicated in a line of poetry memorized by you, unless you have forgotten it?
* A student:
"You will understand the condition of conjunction, so marvel at its denial, with a kaf and a negation, the verbal noun is intensified."
* The Shaykh:
"You will understand the condition of conjunction, so marvel at its denial, with a kaf and a negation, the verbal noun is intensified."
The last one is the example we have: ﴿because they associated﴾. ﴿Because they associated with Allah﴾, that is: because of their association with Allah, in that they made partners for Allah, the Exalted. But these partners they set up alongside Allah, they made them partners only in worship, not in lordship. For this reason the polytheism of the Arabs was polytheism in divinity, not in lordship: ﴿If you asked them who created the heavens and the earth, they would surely say: "The Mighty, the All-Knowing created them"﴾ [az-Zukhruf 9]; ﴿If you asked them who created them, they would surely say: "Allah"﴾ [az-Zukhruf 87]; ﴿Say: "To whom belong the earth and whoever is in it, if you know?" They will say: "To Allah"﴾ [al-Mu'minun 84–85]. So they acknowledge that Allah is the Creator and that whatever is in the universe is His dominion; they do not deny this, but they associate others in worship, worshipping others alongside Allah. Yet they claim that they worship these idols so that they may be intercessors for them with Allah. They also acknowledge that they are below the rank of Allah, yet they worship them: ﴿And those who take protectors besides Him say: "We only worship them so that they may bring us nearer to Allah in closeness"﴾ [az-Zumar 3].

He says: ﴿Because they associated with Allah that for which He had sent down no authority﴾. "Ma" may be a relative pronoun, that is: "that which He had not sent down authority for," and it may be an indefinite qualified noun, that is: "something for which He had not sent down authority." The meaning does not differ under either reading.

His saying: ﴿for which He had not sent down﴾ has two readings: ﴿yunazzil﴾ and ﴿yunzil﴾, that is, with shaddah and without shaddah.

His saying: ﴿authority﴾, that is: proof and evidence. So they make partners for Allah for which Allah has sent down no authority; that is, they have no proof for them.

His saying: ﴿for which He had not sent down authority﴾: the qualifier here is to clarify the reality, not to exclude. It clarifies the reality; that is, the reality of these partners is that there is no authority for their association and no evidence. The meaning is not that they associate what He had not sent down; had they associated what He had sent down, they would be correct. No, because it is impossible that there could be an authority, that is a proof, that Allah has what? Partners.

If someone says: what is the benefit of mentioning this description which clarifies the reality?

We say: the benefit in it is to establish the proof that they have no evidence for their association with Him. They have no evidence, because they built on something without authority and without proof. If that is so, the purpose of this is to deter from this association. The opposite of that: a description may come to clarify the reality for the sake of urging and encouraging adherence to the ruling, as in His saying: ﴿O you who believe, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life﴾ [al-Anfal 24]. The Messenger ﷺ does not call the creation to that which would kill them, but calls them to that which gives them life. So the qualifier here is to clarify the reality, but it is mentioned to urge and encourage responding to his call, just as the qualifier in this verse, ﴿for which He had not sent down authority﴾, is to show the falsehood of this association and that it has no evidence.

He said: ﴿for which He had not sent down authority﴾. Know that "sultan" is that which has authority. Evidence is called sultan, the ruler over a people is called sultan, a man's authority over his household is sultan, and likewise everything that has authority is called sultan.

Sometimes "sultan" means power over something, as in His saying: ﴿You will not pass through except with authority﴾ [ar-Rahman 33], that is, with power, and you have no power to pass through the regions of the heavens and the earth.

He said: ﴿Their refuge is the Fire, and wretched is the abode of the wrongdoers﴾. ﴿Their refuge﴾, that is, their place of return is the Fire. They, may Allah protect us, are overcome in this world and in the Hereafter. In this world Allah casts terror into their hearts, so they neither hold firm nor settle. In the Hereafter their refuge is the Fire, and the Fire is the abode which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has prepared for His enemies, to punish them with it. It exists now; it was shown to the Prophet ﷺ during the eclipse prayer, to the extent that he drew back for fear that its heat would reach him, peace and blessings be upon him, and he saw in it someone being punished [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1052) and Muslim (907/17), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Abbas.]].

﴿And wretched is the abode of the wrongdoers﴾: "bi'sa" is an invariable verb used to express dispraise, and its opposite is "ni'ma." This verb requires a subject and a specified object. What is its subject? "Mathwa" (abode). And what is the specified object? It is omitted; the estimate is: "it," or "the Fire," so the meaning is: wretched is the abode of the wrongdoers, the Fire.

His saying: ﴿mathwa﴾: the mathwa is the place of settling to which a person returns and in which he dwells, like a dwelling for example.

* In this noble verse there are several benefits:
* The first benefit: the affirmation of voluntary actions for Allah, from His saying: ﴿We shall cast﴾.
Second: that among the perfection of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is the renewal of His actions, which follow His will and wisdom. Is the casting of terror into the hearts of these people something newly originated or eternal?
* Students: Newly originated?
* The Shaykh: Newly originated. How?
* A student: Future.
* The Shaykh: Because "we shall cast" is in the future. Then when did these people come into existence? Are they eternal? They are newly originated, their hearts are newly originated, and the terror cast into them is newly originated. With this we refute those who deny the voluntary actions of Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, and who say that Allah has no newly originated actions, supposing that a newly originated act subsists only in a newly originated thing, which, they claim, would entail denying the attribute of eternity of Allah. This is their claim, but we say: this is a false assertion. Who says that a newly originated act subsists only in something newly originated? We observe our own actions which were not eternal as we are not eternal, is it not so? A person eats his dinner today different from yesterday's dinner. This is a newly originated act in something newly originated. It does not follow that the act must be coeval with the agent at all times. So we say: in this verse there is a refutation of those who deny that voluntary actions subsist in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
* Among the benefits of this verse: the demonstration of Allah's greatness. From where is the greatness of Allah derived?
* A student: The greatness of Allah means (...).
* The Shaykh: The demonstration of Allah's greatness.
* The student: ﴿We shall cast﴾.
* The Shaykh: From His saying: ﴿We shall cast﴾, for this form indicates greatness or plurality, and plurality with respect to Allah is impossible, so it is necessarily for glorification.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the locus of intention and direction of the body is the heart, from His saying: ﴿We shall cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved﴾. The locus is not the brain, as is well known among the philosophers of today. In reality the brain does not direct; the brain conceives, then sends the image to the heart, and the heart decides. The brain is like what they call the "secretary," who prepares the papers and arranges them, then sends them to the king and says: "What do you command?"

In reality the brain does not direct; the brain conceives, then sends the image to the heart, and the heart decides. The brain is like what they call the "secretary," who prepares the papers and arranges them, then sends them to the king and says: "What do you command?"

The proof of this is the saying of the Blessed and Exalted: ﴿Have they not travelled through the earth, so that they would have hearts with which to understand, or ears with which to hear? For indeed it is not the eyes that are blinded, but the hearts within the breasts that are blinded﴾ [al-Hajj 46]. This is a clear text that understanding is through the heart and that the location of this heart is the chest. With this we refute those who said that the intended meaning of His saying ﴿hearts with which they understand﴾ [al-Hajj 46] is the metaphorical hearts, which is the brain. We say: how does Allah say ﴿but the hearts within the breasts are blinded﴾ [al-Hajj 46]? It is an explicit text.

Then the Sunnah confirmed this, when the Prophet ﷺ said: «Indeed, in the body there is a piece of flesh; if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt. Indeed, it is the heart» [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (52) and Muslim (1599/107), from the hadith of al-Nu'man ibn Bashir.]]. So direction belongs to the heart and conception to the brain.

Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Understanding is through the heart, and it has a connection with the brain; its connection is what we mentioned: the brain conceives and sends to the heart, and the heart commands through the brain, and the brain moves the nerves. With this explanation it becomes clear to us that what the Qur'an and Sunnah have brought on this matter does not contradict what was known among physicians today.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that casting terror into the hearts of enemies is among the greatest victories, from His saying: ﴿And He is the best of helpers﴾ [Al 'Imran 150], then He said: ﴿We shall cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved﴾ [Al 'Imran 151]. Terror is among the strongest causes of victory, and this is a well-known matter.

Is this terror specific to the time of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, or does it include what befalls the enemies of his followers until the Day of Resurrection? The second is what is established; for this reason the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said in what is authentically related from him: «I have been helped by terror for a distance of one month» [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (335) and Muslim (521/3), from the hadith of Jabir ibn Abdullah.]].

* Among the benefits of this verse: the affirmation of causes, from His saying: ﴿because they associated﴾, for the "ba" denotes cause. Affirming causes is the truth. Causes are either legislated or perceptible, and denying them is folly in reason and error in religion, for the texts have abundantly converged on affirming causes. Entering Paradise only occurs through a cause, salvation from the Fire only occurs through a cause, a child only comes through a cause, provision only comes through a cause; everything must have a cause. So denying causes is error in religion and folly in reason.

It is strange that the Ash'aris and those who follow their path in this matter say that Allah the Exalted brings things into existence without intermediary, and that things occur by His direct management without intermediary, because they say: if we affirm intermediaries and give them influence, that would be a kind of associating partners with Allah. For example, they say: the knife has no effect in cutting meat, and the stone has no effect in breaking glass. How? That is, a person brings meat and begins cutting it with a knife; they say: the knife has no effect on cutting the meat; who is the cutter? Allah.

A person throws a bottle with a stone and it breaks; the stone has no effect on breaking the bottle; who broke it? Allah. Because if you say that the knife cut the meat, you have associated partners with Allah; if you say that the stone broke the bottle, you have associated partners with Allah. So causes have no influence.

How do they not have influence? Do we not observe this? They said: this was created by Allah with it, not by it. Glory be to Allah! If you brought a stick instead of a knife and wanted to cut the meat, would it cut? No.

If you threw a feather onto a bottle and pressed against it with all the force of your throw, would it break it? No, it would not break it. Therefore it is not possible for us to deny this matter; this is folly in reason.

But we say: these causes do not have the effect in themselves; rather, the effect comes about through the powers Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, created and deposited in them. Is that clear? Is the terror cast into the hearts of those who disbelieved, for a cause or for no cause? For a cause, and that cause is associating partners.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verse 151–152 (part 2 of 4):

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: if terror is cast into the hearts of those who disbelieve because of their associating partners with Allah, then security is cast into the hearts of those who believe because of their monotheism, is it not so? For what is established for a thing, its opposite is established for its opposite. So when terror is established for the disbelievers because of their shirk, security is established for the believers because of their tawhid. This is indicated by the Almighty's saying: ﴿Those who believe and do not mix their belief with injustice, those are the ones who will have security, and they are guided.﴾ [al-An'am 82]. And the injustice (zulm) is shirk, as the Prophet (ﷺ) explained it: "When this verse was revealed, they said: 'O Messenger of Allah, which of us has not wronged himself?' He said: 'It is only that [kind of injustice]: Have you not heard the words of the righteous servant: ﴿Indeed, shirk is a tremendous injustice﴾ [Luqman 13]?'" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3429) and Muslim (124/197), from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud.] Therefore, the more a person is firm in faith in Allah and in monotheism toward Him, the greater his security and stability. This is a tested matter, because whoever is firmer in faith and monotheism toward Allah is stronger in reliance (tawakkul) upon Him. And among the strongest causes of security and of enduring against enemies is what? Reliance upon Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. To the point that some people's reliance upon Allah takes the place of medicine in healing, as Shaykh al-Islam (may Allah have mercy on him) affirmed, and it is a reality: some people have strong reliance upon Allah and are healed without treatment, because of the strength of their reliance upon Allah. Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah (may Allah have mercy on him) pointed to this when he mentioned that treatment with what is forbidden is not necessary, so that it could be said that treatment with what is forbidden is permissible out of necessity. He said: this is not necessary. Why? Because the patient may be cured by another medicine, and may be cured by recitation, and may be cured by the strength of reliance upon Allah. "Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) fell ill, and it was said to him: 'Shall we not call a physician for you?' He said: 'The physician has already seen me,' and said: 'I do what I want.'" [Narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah in his Musannaf (35443), and Hannad ibn al-Sarri in al-Zuhd (382), from the hadith of Abu Bakr.] Who is meant by "the physician"? Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
So the conclusion is that we say: the more a person's faith in Allah strengthens and his tawhid becomes firm, the more his security, tranquility and stability increase, and this is a matter observed and perceived by the senses.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: there is no proof for anyone's shirk, because of His saying: ﴿for which He has sent down no authority﴾.
* Among its benefits: the rebuke and public declaration of the foolishness of these polytheists, because they associated with Allah what He had not sent down authority for. If they had a proof, they would have been excused, but they have no proof, and this is a rebuke against them and a declaration of their foolishness.
* Among the benefits of this verse: the affirmation of recompense, because of His saying: ﴿and their refuge is the Fire﴾.
* Among its benefits: the affirmation that the Fire is the abode of the disbelievers who associated partners with Allah. So we testify that every disbelieving polytheist's refuge is the Fire. But do we testify this for a specific person?
* Students: No.
* The Shaykh: We do not testify it for him. Rather, we say that we treat him in this world as a disbeliever. For example, if one of the leaders of the disbelievers died, such as the leader of the Russians or the leader of America or the like, we judge that he is a disbeliever, and that every disbeliever is in the Fire, and we judge that he is a disbeliever, so we do not pray over him, do not shroud him, do not bury him among the Muslims, and do not invoke mercy for him. But as for the matter of recompense, we include him in the generality and say: every disbeliever is in the Fire.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the censure of the Fire and its abode, may Allah protect us, because of the Almighty's saying: ﴿and wretched is the abode of the wrongdoers﴾. And Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, spoke the truth, for the most wretched, the most ugly and the most evil abode is the Fire, and for this it deserved this description from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, namely His saying: ﴿and wretched is the abode of the wrongdoers﴾.
* A student: O Shaykh, may Allah be good to you, some doctors, O Shaykh (...) the artificial [heart], said that intellect is in the brain and that the artificial heart does not understand?
* The Shaykh: The artificial heart must have, for example, veins entering it and movement occurring from it. This movement can be explained as a matter emanating from the heart, whether (...) by something fixed in Allah's creation or by artificial means.
* A student: O Shaykh, may Allah be good to you! If one of the leaders of the disbelievers died today, why do we not say that he is in the Fire, knowing that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿If only you could see when the angels take the disbelievers, striking their faces and their backs﴾ [al-Anfal 50]?
* The Shaykh: Correct, but this is general.
* The student: But he died upon disbelief now, saying that Allah is the third of three, and a polytheist (...). Why do we not say that this one enters the Fire?
* The Shaykh: We do not say it. The specific is not the general. Now, if one of the people, one of the Muslims, died upon the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, do we testify for him that he is in Paradise?
* The student: No, we do not testify for him that he is in Paradise. But this, may Allah be good to you, has the possibility that he will be punished and the possibility that he will be forgiven. But the disbeliever will definitely enter the Fire?
* The Shaykh: No, he is not in Paradise, even after punishment.
* The student: He will enter Paradise; every Muslim will enter Paradise, definitely.
* The Shaykh: Only every Muslim. Well done. We also say: every disbeliever will enter the Fire. For this reason he said: "It is from the creed of the People of the Sunnah and the Community that we do not testify for a specific person with Paradise or the Fire, except one for whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) testified." Shaykh al-Islam (may Allah have mercy on him) added: "or upon whom the Ummah has agreed in praise, like the four Imams, for example, we testify for them with Paradise, not because the Messenger testified for them, but because the Ummah praised them." And Allah the Most High said: ﴿And thus We have made you a justly balanced nation, that you may be witnesses over the people﴾ [al-Baqarah 143]. "A funeral passed by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was sitting with his companions, and they praised it with good. He said: 'It is incumbent (wajabat).' Then another passed, and they spoke ill of it. He said: 'It is incumbent.' They said: 'What is incumbent?' He said: 'As for the first, Paradise became incumbent for him; as for the second, the Fire became incumbent for him. You are the witnesses of Allah on earth.'" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2642) and Muslim (949/60), from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik.]
* A student: O Shaykh, the hadith in which the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whenever you pass by the grave of a disbeliever, give him the glad tidings of the Fire." Does this not indicate the permissibility of giving glad tidings to specific disbelievers when it is apparent?
* The Shaykh: Wait, is this the wording of the hadith or did you specify it?
* A student: I am mentioning the wording of the hadith.
* The Shaykh: No, verify the wording of this hadith and we will see.
* A student: O Shaykh, may Allah be good to you, we do not testify for the Muslim with Paradise, because he may be as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "he works in what appears to people," but as for the disbeliever, meaning the disbeliever..?
* The Shaykh: Al-Bukhari narrated the hadith: "Indeed a man works the deeds of the people of the Fire in what appears to people, while he is from the people of Paradise, and indeed a man works the deeds of the people of Paradise in what appears to people, while he is from the people of the Fire." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4207) and Muslim (112/12), from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd.] All of them said it.
* The student: O Shaykh (...) tawhid, O Shaykh.
* The Shaykh: We do not testify for any specific person. But it suffices to say: the basic principle regarding this is that he is one of the people of the Fire. The basic principle regarding one who died upon disbelief is that he is one of the people of the Fire. This is the basic principle. But do we assert the basic principle with certainty? It is possible that in the last moment of his life Allah cast faith into his heart.
* A student: O Shaykh, will this benefit them (...)?
* The Shaykh: Yes, yes. If he repented and death did not reach him, then Allah accepts his repentance. We do not know. In any case, note, brothers: our testimony that he is in the Fire does not make the Fire obligatory for him, and our not testifying that he is in the Fire does not prevent the Fire from him. So what is the benefit of obliging ourselves to testify to this specific person being in the Fire? What is the benefit?
* A student: O Shaykh, this hadith is not specific to Muslims; it could be that the Muslim works the deeds of the people of the Fire in what appears to people..
* The Shaykh: He did not say "the Muslim": "Indeed, a man works..."
* The student: Is it specific to the Muslim?
* The Shaykh: No, it is not specified.
* * *
* A student: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed. "And Allah had already fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them by His permission, until, when you lost courage and disputed about the matter and disobeyed after He had shown you that which you love. Among you are those who desire this world, and among you are those who desire the Hereafter. Then He turned you away from them to test you. And He has already forgiven you, and Allah is Bountiful to the believers" [Al 'Imran 152].
* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed. The Almighty said: ﴿And Allah had already fulfilled His promise to you﴾ ... to the end.
In the previous lesson there was what indicates the affirmation of causes. From where?
* A student: From His saying, the Most High: ﴿We will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved, because they associated with Allah﴾.
* The Shaykh: ﴿We will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved, because they associated with Allah﴾. Good. Do you know of any disagreement among the scholars regarding the effect of causes?
* A student: Some say that causes are necessarily tied to matters, that (...) the causes, and some say: no, causes have no bearing on matters.
* The Shaykh: These are two opinions. The third?
* The student: The third: they say we do not say (...) that it has an effect (...).
* The Shaykh: No, no.
* A student: That it has an effect, but not by its own essence, rather by what (...) Allah placed in it.
* The Shaykh: Yes, it has an effect, but by the decree of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and not by its own essence. Good.
Regarding His saying: ﴿for which He has sent down no authority﴾, does it indicate that there is a shirk for which Allah has sent down authority?
* A student: This verse is an explicit statement that every kind of shirk has no authority.
* The Shaykh: Then the restrictive clause is for clarification?
* The student: That every shirk has no authority.
* The Shaykh: Yes, but what do the scholars call such a clause?
* A student: A clarifying qualifier (li-bayan al-waqi').
* The Shaykh: For clarifying the reality: that every shirk cannot have authority.
The Almighty said: ﴿And Allah had already fulfilled His promise to you﴾. This sentence is emphasized with three emphases:
The first emphasis: the implied oath, since the estimate is: "By Allah, indeed."
The second: the lam.
The third: qad. So these are three emphases in this sentence.
﴿Allah fulfilled His promise to you (sadaqakumu Allahu wa'dahu)﴾, meaning: He made it come true for you.
And His saying: ﴿wa'dahu﴾ is in the accusative by removal of the preposition; i.e., Allah was truthful to you in His promise, that is, in what He promised you of victory. It is said: ṣadaqahu, and it is said: ṣaddaqahu, and there is a difference between them. When one says ṣadaqahu, it means he informed him with truth; and when one says ṣaddaqahu, it means he said: what you informed of is true. So the affirmation (tasdiq) comes from the addressee toward the speaker, and the truth (sidq) comes from the speaker toward the addressee. Thus the meaning of His saying, the Most High: ﴿Allah fulfilled His promise to you﴾ is: He made the promise come to pass for you, so that what He informed you of became true.
They said: "wa'dahu" is in the accusative by removal of the preposition, and the estimate is "fī wa'dihi" (in His promise). Accusative by removal of the preposition is regular with anna and an, and outside this context it is not regular. Ibn Malik said in the Alfiyyah:
"..and with anna and an it is regular, with safety from ambiguity, as in 'I wonder that they should...'"
That is: removal of the preposition is regular with anna and an on condition that ambiguity is safe.
﴿And Allah had already fulfilled His promise to you﴾, meaning what He promised you of victory. Then He clarified the place of this truth, saying: ﴿when you were killing them by His permission﴾. So (idh) here is a temporal adverb connected to (ṣadaqa), meaning: His promise came true for you when you killed them by His permission.
And His saying: ﴿idh tahussunahum bi-idhnihi﴾ is a present-tense verb used to refer to a past event, by way of "narration of the state" (hikayat al-hal). The rule is that the past is expressed with the form of what? The past, as in "Zayd stood." But here it expressed the past with the form of the present for narrating the state, to bring the image of the past closer to the mind, because the past has ended and a person may forget it; when it is phrased in the present tense, the past becomes as if what? As if it were present. This is what the grammarians call "narration of the state" (hikayat al-hal): the past is as if it were now occurring, so that its presence in the mind is closer.
And His saying: ﴿tahussunahum bi-idhnihi﴾: al-hass means killing or intense killing; that is, killing or its intensification. ﴿tahussunahum bi-idhnihi﴾ means: you kill them with terrible slaughter by Allah's permission, both the cosmic (kawni) and the legislative (shar'i) permission. By His cosmic permission, since it has occurred, and everything that has occurred has been permitted by Allah cosmically. And by His legislative permission, since Allah has prescribed for us to fight the disbelievers, so our killing of them is permitted by the Shari'ah. So in this verse both kinds of permission are combined, namely the cosmic and the legislative.
And His saying: ﴿idh tahussunahum bi-idhnihi﴾, meaning: you kill them by His permission. This is victory.
If someone asks: Was any of the disbelievers killed on the day of Uhud?
The answer: Yes, more than nine men were killed from them, and they were routed and fled, until women were seen running and climbing the mountain, terrified, with uncovered heads and bare shins, because they had fled, having despaired of capture. The dominance and honor were for the Muslims at the beginning of the day.
Then He said: ﴿until, when you lost courage and disputed﴾ ... to the end. "Until" (ḥattā): it is said that it is inceptive (ibtidā'iyyah), and it is said that it is for the limit (ghāyah), meaning: His promise came true for you, when you were killing them by His permission, up to the point when you lost courage. On this view, "idhā" is not conditional, meaning "until the time of your losing courage." This is one view; "ḥattā" is well known as indicating a limit, and ﴿idhā fashiltum﴾ means "until the time when you lost courage": the fulfillment of the promise and the killing continued until what? Until you lost courage: ﴿you lost courage, disputed about the matter, and disobeyed after He had shown you what you love.﴾
The second view: that "ḥattā" is inceptive, so the sentence is a new one, and "idhā" in this view is conditional, and its answer will be mentioned, God willing.
﴿until, when you lost courage﴾: (al-fashal) means cowardice and weakness; that is, until when you became cowardly, weak, and incapable of gaining victory.
﴿and disputed about the matter﴾: al-munaza'ah means contention and disagreement.
And His saying: ﴿fī al-amr﴾: is the intended meaning "the matter" as affair (sha'n), or is the intended meaning "the matter" as the singular of commands (awamir)?
On the first view, "al-amr" is the singular of "umūr" (affairs); on the second, "al-amr" is the singular of "awāmir" (commands). The meaning: ﴿disputed about the matter﴾, that is, concerning the affair, i.e., your affair, or concerning the matter of the Messenger (ﷺ). The address is directed to the archers, who were fifty men, whom the Prophet (ﷺ) appointed over them 'Abdullah ibn Jubayr, and said to them: "Do not leave your position" [narrated by al-Bukhari (3039), from the hadith of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib]; stay on the mountain whether we are victorious or defeated. When they saw the Muslims had won and the polytheists were routed, and the Muslims began collecting the spoils, they wanted to come down from the mountain. Their commander disputed with them and said: stay, remain firm. But they insisted on descending, and most of them descended. So here "al-amr" is the singular of "awāmir" (commands): you disputed about the command of the Messenger (ﷺ). Some of you said: we will remain, in obedience to his command, and some of you descended, seeking to gain the spoils. Do you understand now?
The two meanings are mutually connected, because when they differed about the Messenger's command, they disputed about their affair; i.e., about their own matter.
﴿and disobeyed after He had shown you what you love﴾. And disobeyed whom? You disobeyed the Messenger. But the object was not mentioned, out of disliking to mention it, since it would be harsher and more reproachful. It is as if Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, wanted to rebuke them in a gentle manner. He said: ﴿you disobeyed﴾, and did not say "the Messenger," because this is lighter than if He had stated it explicitly. And it was said: "and you disobeyed the Messenger," and when it is said "you disobeyed the Messenger," it has a harsher effect in rebuke.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verses 151–152 (part 3 of 4):

And His saying: ﴿from after He showed you﴾. Who is the subject of "showed (أراكم)"? Allah. That is, from after He showed you, with the eye's own vision, ﴿what you love﴾ of victory and the defeat of your enemies.

It remains for us to say: where is the response of the conditional on the second interpretation of (إذا, idha, "when")? ﴿when you lost heart and disputed about the matter and disobeyed, after He had shown you what you love﴾?

Some of them said: the response of the conditional is ﴿you disputed﴾, meaning: until, when you lost heart, you disputed about the matter and disobeyed. On this view, the wāw (و) is extra (zā'idah).

Another said: the response of the conditional is ﴿you disobeyed﴾, meaning: until, when you lost heart and disputed about the matter, you disobeyed after He had shown you what you love. Another said: the response of the conditional is omitted, its estimate being: you split into two groups, some of you desiring the world and some of you desiring the Hereafter. These are three opinions. Another said: it is omitted, its estimate being: victory escaped you, until, when you lost heart and disputed about the matter and disobeyed, to the end; victory escaped you.

Another said: the response is omitted with certainty. The view that the wāw is extra in ﴿you disputed﴾ and that it is the response of the conditional, or that it is extra in ﴿you disobeyed﴾ and is the response, is a weak view, because the particle here is a particle that came for a meaning, and whatever it was brought for is lost when it is lost. So the response is therefore omitted. The benefit of omitting it is that the mind may go in every direction in estimating it, and anything estimated as the response of (إذا) that does not contradict the other estimate is valid. On this basis, we may say: ﴿and disobeyed after He had shown you what you love﴾: victory escaped you, or what you love escaped you, or you were forsaken, or you split into two groups. The point is that all these possibilities are correct and do not contradict one another. Victory did escape them, they did split into two groups, and they were forsaken. This is part of the eloquence of the Qur'an: omission, so that the meaning is more comprehensive and fuller.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Among you are those who desire the world, and among you are those who desire the Hereafter﴾. The (مِنْ, min) here is partitive (تبعيضية): that is, some of you; some of you desire the world and the others desire the Hereafter. Those who came down to collect the spoils were evidently desiring the world, and those who held firm were evidently desiring the Hereafter. This is by way of example. Otherwise the examples are many, of those who desire the world and those who desire the Hereafter. Even in seeking knowledge, some people desire the world, and some people desire the Hereafter. Some desire status, elevation, and leadership, as the poet said:

Knowledge raises a house that has no pillars ∗∗∗ and ignorance demolishes the house of honor and nobility.

And some desire the Hereafter: to preserve the Sharia of Allah, to teach the servants of Allah, to worship Allah with insight, and the like. This is the condition of all people: some of them desire the world and some desire the Hereafter.
* * *
* Student: ﴿And Allah had certainly fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them by His permission, until, when you lost heart and disputed about the matter and disobeyed after He had shown you what you love – among you are those who desire the world and among you are those who desire the Hereafter. Then He turned you away from them to test you. And He has already pardoned you, and Allah is full of bounty toward the believers (152). [And mention] when you ran up [the slope] without looking aside at anyone while the Messenger was calling you from your rear. So He rewarded you with distress upon distress, so that you would not grieve over what had escaped you or what had befallen you. And Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾ [Āl ʿImrān 152, 153].
* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿And Allah had certainly fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them by His permission﴾. We said that this sentence is emphasized with emphatics. Is that right?
* Student: (...) The implied oath's wāw, the lām, and qad.
* The Shaykh: Well done. His saying: ﴿when you were killing them (إِذْ تَحُسُّونَهُمْ)﴾. What is the meaning of (الحس, al-hiss)?
* Student: al-hiss is killing, or intense killing.
* The Shaykh: Yes. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿until, when you lost heart (فَشِلْتُمْ)﴾. The meaning of "you lost heart"? ﴿فَشِلْتُمْ﴾, what does it mean?
* Student: You disputed.
* The Shaykh: How?
* Student: You became cowardly.
* The Shaykh: You became cowardly, yes. Where is the response of (إذا) in His saying: ﴿until, when you lost heart﴾?
* Student: There are opinions on it, O Shaykh. It was said: it is ﴿you disputed﴾, and the wāw is extra. It was said: it is ﴿you disobeyed﴾, and on this also the wāw is extra. It was said: you split into two groups, some of you desiring the world and some of you desiring the Hereafter. It was said: victory escaped you. It was said: it is omitted in any case, and it was omitted only so that the mind may go in every direction regarding it.
* The Shaykh: And every estimate is made.
* Student: And this is the preferred view.
* The Shaykh: Yes, well done.
His exalted saying: ﴿Among you are those who desire﴾. What is (مَنْ, man) here?
* Student: Partitive.
* The Shaykh: Partitive; that is, some of you desire the world and some of you desire the Hereafter.
What is an example of those who desire the world?
* Student: Those who desire the world are these archers who came down from their place...
* The Shaykh: Those who came down from the place where the Messenger (ﷺ) had placed them, for the sake of the spoils. His saying: ﴿Then He turned you away from them﴾. The pronoun in "from them" refers to whom?
...Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Then He turned you away from them﴾. Then, that is, after Allah had fulfilled His promise to you by your killing them, namely their slaying, He turned you away from them. That is: after you lost heart, disputed about the matter, and disobeyed, He turned you away from them. Consider His saying: ﴿turned you away (صَرَفَكُمْ)﴾, for turning away requires a strong approach in which the one approaching exerts great effort until he is turned away, as you say: "I turned the animal away from the fodder," and the like. This conveys that the Muslims were approaching these enemies very eagerly, but they were turned away from them despite their intense desire to finish them off, because victory had been theirs at the beginning, but they were turned away from it.

His saying: ﴿to test you (لِيَبْتَلِيَكُمْ)﴾, that is, to examine you: whether you recognize the worth of obedience to Allah and His Messenger, and so it becomes clear who values this matter and who does not. Trial (الابتلاء, al-ibtila') originally means testing and examination, and it occurs in good and in evil. Allah said: ﴿And We test you with evil and with good as a trial﴾ [al-Anbiyā' 35]. Solomon, when he saw the throne of Bilqis present with him and settled beside him, said: ﴿This is of the bounty of my Lord, to test me whether I will be grateful or ungrateful﴾ [an-Naml 40]. So good is a trial and evil is a trial. A person is tested with evil in order to be patient, and is tested with good for what? In order to be grateful. So all of it is a trial; therefore He said: ﴿to test you﴾.

﴿And He has already pardoned you﴾. This sentence is also emphasized with three emphatics: the implied oath, since the original is "and indeed, by Allah, He has pardoned you," the lām, and qad. The sentence is emphasized here and the sentence there, in His saying: ﴿And Allah had certainly fulfilled His promise to you﴾, because from the events one may readily infer otherwise. For example, the first sentence, ﴿And Allah had certainly fulfilled His promise to you﴾: from the fact that defeat came upon the Muslims at the end of the matter, one may think that Allah did not fulfill His promise to them. So this was emphasized by His saying: ﴿And Allah had certainly fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them by His permission﴾, and this is victory. The second: when they were tested with this trial, one may readily think that Allah would punish them for their disobedience, their disputing, and their cowardice, so He said: ﴿And He has already pardoned you﴾. So the emphasis here and at the beginning of the verse was at the utmost degree of eloquence, because the situation requires what? It requires emphasis.

His saying: ﴿And He has already pardoned you (عَفَا عَنْكُمْ)﴾. Pardon (العفو, al-'afw) means overlooking, and it may be praiseworthy or blameworthy. If it is with power, it is praiseworthy, and Allah's pardon is undoubtedly with power, because Allah is able to take revenge, the Mighty and Majestic, yet He pardons while able, as Allah said: ﴿for indeed Allah is Pardoning and Competent﴾ [an-Nisā' 149]. It is blameworthy if its source is incapacity. If its source is incapacity, it is blameworthy and a person is not praised for it, because this indicates his weakness and his failure to take his right.

His saying: ﴿And He has already pardoned you﴾ includes everyone who committed the violation, and this is from the bounty of Allah toward them.

It is fitting for us here to mention a remarkable story: "A man from the Khawarij came to 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, while he was sheltering in the Ka'bah. He stood before him after asking about him, and said: 'Who is this?' They said: 'This is 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar.' So he stood over him, and he was a Khariji, and asked him about the Commander of the Faithful 'Uthman. He said to him: 'Do you not know that 'Uthman ibn 'Affan stayed behind from the battle of Badr?' He said: 'Yes, he stayed behind.' He said: 'Do you not know that he fled on the day of Uhud?' He said: 'Yes, he fled.' He said: 'Do you not know that he did not pledge the Pledge of Ridwan?' He said: 'Yes.' The Khariji said: 'Allahu Akbar'", he said takbir meaning that he had won, because he only asked these three questions to discredit 'Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him. "The Khariji said takbir, and when he had said takbir, Ibn 'Umar said to him: 'As for now that you have done this, I will inform you. As for his staying behind at the battle of Badr, the Prophet (ﷺ) instructed him to remain to nurse his daughter, the daughter of the Messenger (ﷺ), who was ill, Ruqayyah, the wife of 'Uthman. So he stayed behind to nurse her by the Prophet's (ﷺ) command, and the Prophet (ﷺ) gave him a share and his reward from the spoils.'" So is he blamed for this? He is not blamed. He stayed behind by the Messenger's command to nurse the Messenger's daughter, and the Messenger (ﷺ) gave him a share and his reward.

"As for his fleeing at Uhud, Allah the Exalted said:" ﴿And He has already pardoned you﴾, "after the pardon, does any trace of the sin remain? No."

"As for his absence from the Pledge of Ridwan, there is no one from the clans of Quraysh more honored than the clan from which 'Uthman comes, because his clan is strong among Quraysh. So the Prophet (ﷺ) saw no one more worthy to send to Quraysh to negotiate with them than 'Uthman, so he sent him to Quraysh to negotiate, because he had standing. Then when the Messenger (ﷺ) pledged the believers under the tree, he took his noble hand and placed it upon the other hand and said: 'This is on behalf of 'Uthman's hand.'" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari (3698) from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar.]] "Allahu Akbar". So the Prophet's hand, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, was better than 'Uthman's hand for 'Uthman, is it not so?

Glory be to Allah, who has been given this! This is a great merit. Then he said: 'Go with it to your people,' or words similar to that. That is: you came wanting to discredit the Commander of the Faithful, and now the discrediting has become, praise be to Allah, praise. So such matters require a person to be attentive to some people. Some people may ask a question whose apparent purpose is seeking guidance, but whose real meaning is criticism. If he comes with it in this manner, he silences the critic with a stone, and this is part of his understanding."

It is said that one of the people asked one of the scholars (...).

So let him be cautious. In any case, every situation has its own statement. The meaning is not that we should think ill of everyone, but every situation has its own statement. Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, understood from this Khariji that he wanted to attack and discredit 'Uthman, so he answered him.

﴿And He has already pardoned you, and Allah is full of bounty toward the believers﴾. ﴿And Allah is full of bounty (ذُو فَضْلٍ, dhū faḍl)﴾: dhū means "possessor of," that is, possessor of bounty. ﴿toward the believers﴾, meaning: and you are among them, and you are among them, and therefore He pardoned you. Here in the sentence there is an explicit noun in place of a pronoun, since the context would require him to say: "and Allah is full of bounty toward you." The benefit of this, that is the benefit of the explicit noun in place of the pronoun, has already been mentioned to us, and we said that it has three benefits. The explicit noun in place of a pronoun has three benefits?
* Student: Attaching the ruling to the described attribute (...).
* The Shaykh: No.
* Student: The first benefit: alerting, because when speech is in one pattern it may bore the hearing, but when it changes, one pays attention to that speech.
* The Shaykh: That is for iltifat (the shift of grammatical person).
* Student: The first benefit is that we say: this is the cause of the ruling, because they are believers (...).
* The Shaykh: The first benefit, first: recording on the place of the pronoun, or on the referent of the pronoun, that they are people of this attribute. That is, affirming this attribute of the referent of the pronoun. For example: "And Allah is full of bounty toward you" — if he says "toward the believers" instead of "toward you," it conveys that they are what? Believers. This is one.

Second: generality, because if he had said "and Allah is full of bounty toward you," the bounty would be restricted to the referent of the pronoun. When he says ﴿toward the believers﴾, it includes them and others.

The third benefit is what the brothers pointed to: the cause, the cause of the ruling. The ruling is that Allah is full of bounty, and the cause is faith. Here, in this last verse, this differs according to the context. This is the benefit of the explicit noun in place of the pronoun.

As for here, there is a verbal suitability: the explicit noun in place of the pronoun here is a verbal suitability, namely the harmony of the verse endings, because if he had said "and Allah is full of bounty toward you," it would not have harmonized with what came after it or with what came before it.

﴿And Allah is full of bounty toward the believers﴾. In this noble verse there are several benefits:
* First: Allah, glorified and exalted, gave victory to the believers at Uhud just as He gave them victory at Badr. The evidence is His saying: ﴿And Allah had certainly fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them by His permission﴾.
* Second: part of eloquence is that a report be emphasized when the situation calls for it. From where is this taken? From His saying: ﴿And Allah had certainly fulfilled His promise to you﴾, where there is an oath and emphasis by the lām and qad.
* The third benefit: the strong resolve of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, in pursuing the enemy, because He said: ﴿when you were killing them by His permission﴾, and al-hiss is killing or intense killing; that is, as if a sound is heard from it at the moment of killing. Likewise, the Muslims should confront their warring enemies with intensity and severity, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And do not weaken in pursuit of the enemy﴾ [an-Nisā' 104], meaning do not grow weak in pursuing them. ﴿If you suffer, then indeed they suffer as you suffer﴾. Look at the consolation given to the Companions: ﴿Do not weaken in pursuit of the enemy. If you suffer, then indeed they suffer as you suffer, but you hope from Allah for what they do not hope﴾.
* Among the benefits of this verse: disputing and disobedience are a cause for losing the full victory, because at the beginning of the matter they had gained victory and killed the polytheists, but when this obstacle occurred, the full victory was prevented or ceased.
* Among its benefits: such a matter, disputing and disobedience, is a cause of forsaking. From where is this taken? From the reality of the matter, because His saying: ﴿until, when you lost heart﴾, we said that the response of the conditional is omitted, and the meaning is that you lost this victory and were forsaken. Whoever reads the account of the battle will understand what befell the Companions of great matters, which will come, Allah willing, at His saying: ﴿so He rewarded you with distress upon distress﴾.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: disobedience after a blessing is worse than disobedience before a blessing, because of His saying: ﴿and disobeyed after He had shown you what you love﴾. Otherwise He would have said only: "and you disobeyed." But that disobedience occurs after Allah has shown them what they love is greater, greater than if Allah had not shown them what they love.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the exhortation to unity of word. Its basis? Disputing is a cause of forsaking, so agreement is a cause of victory, and so it is. The gathering of people upon one word is undoubtedly a cause of victory. For this reason, students of knowledge and scholars should not display their disagreement and dispute before the common people. Opinions must exist, but for each of them to criticize the other for disagreeing with him is a very great danger, because after such a dispute the common people will see that they cannot trust any one of them. Moreover, the common people will also scatter, and this one will be with this one and that one with that one. So disputing is undoubtedly a cause of forsaking, failure, and the tearing apart of the community.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: everything depends on what is in the heart, because of His saying: ﴿Among you are those who desire the world, and among you are those who desire the Hereafter﴾. It seems, and Allah knows best, that this contains an indication that the cause of cowardice, disputing, and disobedience was the bad intention of some of those among them, because we may take His saying ﴿Among you are those who desire the world﴾ as a resumptive explanatory sentence (جملة استئنافية تعليلية) for what occurred. There is no doubt that everything depends on what is in the heart, and that whenever the heart is sound, the deed is sound, and whenever it is corrupt, the deed is corrupt.

* Among the benefits of this verse: it is possible that among the best generations there are those for whom an action may be faulted, based on His words: ﴿Among you are those who desire the world﴾. But the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, in particular have virtues, precedence, companionship, and the afflictions and other things that befell them, which expiate what occurred from them. For this reason the Companions have a distinction over others. I mean the general expiations that apply to everyone, such as: "No hardship, nor grief, nor harm befalls a believer, not even a thorn that pricks him, except that Allah expiates some of his sins by it" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5642) and Muslim (2573/52), from the hadith of Abu Sa'id and Abu Hurayrah]. This is general for everyone, but the Companions have special things that necessitate the erasure of the sins that occurred from them. What indicates this is that among the greatest calamities and the gravest faults is espionage for the benefit of the polytheists, and it occurred from Hatib, may Allah be pleased with him. When Umar asked the Prophet ﷺ for permission to kill him, the Prophet ﷺ said to him: "Do you not know that Allah looked upon the people of Badr and said: Do whatever you wish, for I have forgiven you" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3007) and Muslim (2494/161), from the hadith of Ali]. Even though this is a great calamity, espionage for the disbelievers requires execution even if the person is a Muslim, because this is striving in the land to cause corruption. For this reason the Messenger ﷺ did not say, "Do not kill him because he is a Muslim." Rather he said, "Do not kill him, because he took part in Badr, and Allah the Exalted has said: 'Do whatever you wish, for I have forgiven you.'" Therefore the correct opinion, about which there is no doubt, is that the spy is killed even if he is a Muslim; even if he prays night and day, he is still killed. Okay.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of causes, based on His words: ﴿Then He turned you away from them to test you﴾. The cause of Allah turning these people away from the disbelievers was what occurred from them of failure, dispute, and disobedience.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of wisdom in the acts of Allah. This is a refutation of whom? Of the Jahmiyyah and those like them who deny the wisdom of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and say: Allah acts not for any wisdom, but merely by will. We believe that Allah, glorified and exalted, does nothing and legislates nothing except for a wisdom. But among the wisdoms, some are known to humans and some are unknown, beyond the reach of minds.
