As for the statement of the Jalalayn (Tafsir al-Jalalayn, by al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti), may Allah have mercy on him, that the (lā) here is superfluous and that the meaning is: "so that you would grieve over what escaped you and what befell you," this is a very distant view. Rather, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, loves that the believers not grieve, and He consoles them when causes of grief arise. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Secret counsel is only from Satan, to grieve those who believe, but it cannot harm them at all except by Allah's permission﴾ [al-Mujadilah 10]. This is consolation. How then would Allah command them, or how would Allah do something in order that they grieve?! This is very distant. The meaning we have mentioned is, I think, quite clear: these distresses that befell them were so that some of them would make others forgotten, so that they would not grieve over what befell them or what escaped them. Then, when everything is revealed, it has a sweet taste in the souls.

He, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And Allah is Aware of what you do﴾. ﴿Khabir﴾ (All-Aware) is derived from ﴿al-khubr﴾, which means knowledge of the inner realities of matters. From it the farmer is called ﴿khabir﴾, because he buries the grain and conceals it. The root of this word indicates concealment. So the ﴿khabir﴾ is the One who knows the inner realities of matters, and the One who knows inner realities knows outer realities all the more.

His saying: ﴿Aware of what you do﴾: ﴿bi-mā﴾ means ﴿bi-alladhī﴾ (with that which), ﴿you do﴾ of good and evil: action, speech, or whispers in the souls. But here He said ﴿what you do﴾, because what is meant by awareness here is what follows from it of reckoning. It is a declarative sentence conveying a warning, because Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, does not hold anyone accountable except for action. As for inner speech of the soul, one is not held accountable for it. If a person speaks to himself about committing sins or abandoning obligations and then does not carry it out, he is not held accountable. For this reason He said: ﴿Aware of what you do﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: reminding the believers of the disobedience that occurred from them, when He said: ﴿When you were going up [the slope] and not turning back for anyone﴾. This is according to the view that ﴿idh﴾ (when) is connected to an implied verb whose estimate is: "Remember." But according to the view that it is connected to ﴿ʿafā﴾ (He pardoned), the benefit is reminding the believers of Allah's blessing upon them in His pardoning them when, what? When they went up.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the gentle rebuke in His saying: ﴿and not turning back for anyone while the Messenger was calling you from your rear﴾. Courage prevents a person from being in such a state, fleeing without turning back for anyone while the Messenger calls him, saying: "Come to me, O servants of Allah." [Reported by al-Bukhari (3039) from the hadith of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, with the wording: "When they came upon them, I turned their faces and they fled retreating. That is what is meant by: 'when the Messenger was calling them from behind them.'"] In it is a gentle rebuke, what? A gentle rebuke to the Companions for what occurred from them.

* Among the benefits of this verse: the excellent care of the Prophet ﷺ for his Ummah in his great leadership, as he would be at the back of the people. This was his manner, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, to be at the back of the people in order to look after them: if someone lags behind, if someone is in need, he looks after them. He was not like kings who go before the people; rather, he would lag behind. The story of Jabir's camel is not far off: the Prophet, peace be upon him, was at the back of the people, and he reached Jabir, who had a camel that had become exhausted. The Prophet, peace be upon him, reached him, struck the camel, supplicated for him, and the camel walked on. This shows that among the aims of the Prophet, peace be upon him, in lagging behind in such a situation was this care.

* Among the benefits of this verse: a leader ought to be courageous in his leadership, so that he remains steadfast and calls others to steadfastness. From where is this taken? ﴿while the Messenger was calling you﴾. ﴿Calling you﴾: because if he had not stood firm and had fled with them, he would not have been fit for leadership.

* Among the benefits of the verse: the affirmation of the Prophethood of the Prophet ﷺ in His saying: ﴿while the Messenger was calling you﴾.

* Among its benefits: the wisdom and justice of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in His recompense to His servants, from His saying: ﴿so He rewarded you with distress upon distress﴾. Justice is very evident if we take the ﴿bāʾ﴾ (with) to mean exchange, and wisdom is evident if we take it to mean accompaniment or the sense of ﴿ʿalā﴾ (upon). This is because these distresses following one another lighten one another.

* Among the benefits of the verse: affirming wisdom, the affirmation of the wisdom of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in His actions, from His saying: ﴿so that﴾, for the ﴿lām﴾ here indicates causation.

Now this matter, that is, affirming wisdom in the actions and legislative rulings of Allah, is denied by whom? By the Jahmiyyah (followers of Jahm ibn Safwan), they deny it. Indeed the Ash'ariyyah also deny it, and they say that the actions of Allah are not subject to causation, because if they were caused, He would act for a purpose; and because if they were caused, a question could be directed to Him about them, saying: "Why did You do this?" But Allah, glorified and exalted, is not questioned about what He does, while they are questioned. We have already explained earlier that denying causation or denying wisdom in Allah's actions is considered a deficiency attributed to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, because if wisdom were negated in His legislative or decreed rulings, His rulings would become vain and playful. Allah, the Exalted, has refuted this in several verses, the most severe of which is His saying: ﴿And We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in vain. That is the assumption of those who disbelieve, so woe to those who disbelieve from the Fire﴾ [Sad 27].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, loves that His servants not grieve, because He decreed distress upon distress for what purpose? So that they would not grieve. This is because grief causes a person constriction, a constriction that may prevent him from many benefits, and may produce psychological knots. A person should accustom himself to an open heart and a relaxed soul as far as he can, because there is no doubt that when a person's chest is open and his soul relaxed, he is at ease, receptive to understanding and to being understood. When he is grieved, you find that he does not want anyone to speak to him, let alone to be taught or to understand.

* Among the benefits of the verse: the great education of the servants: that they not grieve over what escaped them. If good escapes you that you thought would be good for yourself, say: "This is the decree of Allah, and He does what He wills." Likewise, if something you dislike befalls you, say: "This is the decree of Allah, and He does what He wills." Know that grief never returns what has been lost; it only increases a person's trial.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: affirming the vast knowledge of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, of every object of knowledge, from His saying: ﴿And Allah is Aware of what you do﴾ [Al 'Imran 153].

* Among its benefits: the obligation to beware of disobedience, of opposing Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Its explanation: if He is aware of our deeds, this necessitates for us that we not oppose Him, because if we oppose Him, He knows; if we oppose Him, He knows, and if He knows, He will hold us accountable.

* Among the benefits of the verse: refuting the Jabriyyah (those who hold that man has no real choice), from His saying: ﴿what you do﴾. Its explanation: He attributed the action to them, while the Jabriyyah say that man does not act and does nothing by his own choice.

* Among its benefits: refuting the extreme Qadariyyah (those who deny Allah's foreknowledge of human acts), from His saying: ﴿Aware﴾, because the extreme Qadariyyah deny Allah's knowledge of the servant's actions, and say that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, does not know the servant's actions, but when he does them, He knows of them.

Then He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Then He sent down upon you after the distress a security, drowsiness﴾ [Al 'Imran 154]. ﴿Thumma﴾ (then) indicates sequence with an interval. ﴿He sent down﴾: who? Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

﴿He sent down upon you after the distress﴾: the word ﴿distress﴾ here refers to the category of distress, so it includes distress after distress, all the preceding distresses: ﴿after the distress, a security, drowsiness﴾. ﴿Amanah﴾ (security) may be parsed in two ways:

The first: that it is an object of purpose (a verbal complement of purpose, mafʿūl liajlihi).

The second: that it is a direct object of ﴿anzala﴾ (He sent down). According to the first view, ﴿nuʿāsan﴾ (drowsiness) is the object of ﴿anzala﴾; according to the second, ﴿nuʿāsan﴾ is an apposition or explanatory appositive to ﴿amanah﴾.

﴿Amanah﴾ means ﴿amn﴾ (security); that is, He sent down upon you after distress security, and amanah and amn have the same meaning. What is this security? He said: ﴿drowsiness﴾, and drowsiness is the beginning of sleep, and it is a sign of the tranquility of the heart, because the one who is afraid does not doze off, does he? 

* Student: He does not doze off.

* Shaykh: Then what does he do?

* Student: He dies a thousand deaths in a day.

* Shaykh: There is no power nor might except with Allah! Yes, the one who is afraid cannot doze off, because his heart trembles and is agitated. But the one who is secure and at peace dozes off, and for this reason He said: ﴿drowsiness﴾.

﴿It overcame a group of you﴾ [Al 'Imran 154]. In another reading: ﴿it overcomes a group of you﴾ (with feminine verb). If the reading is ﴿taghshā﴾ (feminine), the pronoun returns to ﴿amanah﴾; if the reading is ﴿yaghshā﴾ (masculine), the pronoun returns to ﴿nuʿāsan﴾.

﴿It overcame a group of you﴾ means it reached a group. ﴿Ghashayān﴾ (overcoming) originally means covering, and from it is His saying: ﴿And over their eyes is a covering﴾ [al-Baqarah 7], and His saying: ﴿He covers the night over the day﴾ [al-A'raf 54]. But it may be used to mean simply reaching, and it may be used to mean reaching with comprehensiveness, that it covered them all. ﴿It overcame a group of you﴾: the address is to the believers.

﴿And a group who were concerned only for themselves﴾ [Al 'Imran 154], meaning drowsiness did not overcome them. Why? Because their own selves had made them anxious: they put them into worry, put them into worry, because they say: "We do not know what will happen!" and they make guesses and calculations. One in such a state does not receive sleep nor is drowsiness near him. For this reason He said: ﴿whose own selves had made them anxious﴾. He omitted mention of their not being overcome by drowsiness, He omitted it, because it is known from their condition: if their own selves had made them anxious, it is impossible that they would doze off.

He says: ﴿whose own selves had made them anxious, thinking about Allah other than the truth﴾ [Al 'Imran 154]. The phrase ﴿yaẓunnūna﴾ (they think) may be a second predicate of His saying: ﴿and a group﴾.

Where is the first predicate? The clause ﴿whose own selves had made them anxious﴾, meaning: "and a group whose selves had made them anxious, and likewise they think about Allah other than the truth." It may also be that ﴿yaẓunnūna﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) from the pronoun in ﴿ahammathum﴾; meaning: their selves made them anxious while they were thinking about Allah other than the truth. That is, they think about Allah, the Exalted, a thought other than the true thought. What is this thought? They think many things. They say, for example: "Do we have any part in the affair?"

* Student: There is no hearing in it (...).

* Shaykh: What?

* Student: It moves with the ear.

* Shaykh: "Ahammathum" (made them anxious), the ha'? 

* Student: "Anfusuhum" (their own selves).

* Shaykh: The ha' after the tā'. ﴿They think about Allah other than the truth, the thought of the Jahiliyyah﴾ [Al 'Imran 154]. They think, for example, that the Messenger, peace be upon him, was actually killed, that there is no victory for Islam after this defeat, that dominance will belong to the disbelievers, and other such corrupt thoughts. There is no doubt that this thought is based on ignorance, and for this reason He said: ﴿other than the truth, the thought of the Jahiliyyah﴾. He began with the falsehood of this thought first, then explained that it issues from ignorance. For this reason He said: ﴿the thought of the Jahiliyyah﴾, meaning the thought of the people of ignorance, because whoever knows Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, through His names, attributes and rulings can never think this thought about Him: that Allah would let falsehood prevail over truth, and that Allah would not help His Messenger. Only one who does not know Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, thinks this thought. For this reason He said: ﴿They think about Allah other than the truth, the thought of the Jahiliyyah. They say: "Do we have any part in the affair?"﴾ [Al 'Imran 154].

The clause ﴿yaqūlūna﴾ (they say): can it be a second or third predicate? A third predicate of ﴿ṭāʾifah﴾. It may also be a circumstantial clause from the ﴿yaẓunnūna﴾ (the waw in ﴿yaẓunnūna﴾), meaning they think while saying.

And His saying: ﴿yaqūlūna﴾ (they say): with their tongues or with their hearts?

* Students: With their hearts.

* Other students: It is possible.

* Shaykh: Yes, it allows both: it is possible that they say within themselves, and it is possible that they say with their tongues, meaning some of them say to others: "Do we have any part in the affair?" Which is closer?

* Student: The second.

* Shaykh: What is the second?

* Student: Shaykh, the second is stronger, which is that they say with their tongues, some saying to others.

* Shaykh: Yes. What is its strength in your view?

* Student: Its strength is that it is widespread among them, meaning they want to spread this among themselves, so Allah wanted to expose them, and to show the hadith of one of the Companions, I think it was Talhah, when he said: "I was dozing off, as in the verse, and I heard the voice of one of them, and [he was saying] such-and-such, and he says this statement: 'Do we have any part in the affair?'"

* Shaykh: Yes, very good. But is there evidence from the verse?

* Student: His saying: ﴿They conceal within themselves what they do not reveal to you﴾ [Al 'Imran 154].

* Shaykh: No.

* Student: They say: the original sense of it is that it is with the tongue.

* Shaykh: Yes, well done. The original sense of "saying," when it is unqualified, is saying with the tongue, and when it is inner saying, it must be qualified, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And they say within themselves: "Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?"﴾ [al-Mujadilah 8]. Is it clear? Answer me.

* Students: Yes.

* Shaykh: Then the verse indicates that this statement issued from them with their tongues. Is it clear?

If someone says: You say that when "saying" is unqualified it means speech of the tongue; then how do you answer His saying: ﴿They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts﴾ [al-Fath 11]?

* Student: It is for emphasis.

* Shaykh: For emphasis, and to match His saying: ﴿what is not in their hearts﴾.

﴿They say: "Do we have any part in the affair?"﴾ Here ﴿hal﴾ (is/do) is interrogative. But is the interrogative meant as a denial, as if they say: "Were we consulted? Were we asked?" Or do they mean that the interrogative is a negation? That is, they say: "We have no part in the affair," and we look at what the context of the verse supports: ﴿They say: "Do we have any part in the affair?" Say: "Indeed the affair is entirely Allah's."﴾ [Al 'Imran 154]. Does it support that ﴿hal﴾ means ﴿mā﴾ (not), or that ﴿hal﴾ means denial? That is, they deny that they were consulted about anything?

* Students: The second.

* Shaykh: The context of the verse indicates the second, and that these people took issue with the leadership in this campaign: they objected that it did not consult them, and said: "Do we have any part in the affair?" Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Say: "Indeed the affair is entirely Allah's."﴾ This is also supported by His saying: ﴿They say: "If we had any part in the affair, we would not have been killed here"﴾ [Al 'Imran 154], meaning: if we had any part in the affair, this defeat would not have occurred, and so on through the rest of the verses. So the apparent meaning here is that the interrogative is not for negation, as some exegetes held, but its meaning is denial: a denial against the leadership that it did not consult them in this matter.

They say: ﴿Do we have any part in the affair, any thing?﴾ Is "the affair" here singular (al-amr) or plural (al-umūr), or is it the singular of "commands" (al-awāmir)?

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verses 153–154 (part 3 of 5):

* Student: The first one.
* Student: One (of the matters).
* The Shaykh: The first one. That is, "Do we have any say in matters of war?" We do not. Nothing about the matter of war was directed to us. It seems they want to disown what happened, and they say: "Because we were not consulted, nor was anything referred back to us, nor was our opinion sought."

Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Say: Indeed, the affair is entirely for Allah.﴾ There are two recitations here: ﴿kullu-hu﴾ and ﴿kulla-hu﴾. Which is more preferable?

* Student: Apparently ﴿kullu-hu﴾, because it is a predicate.
* The Shaykh: No, the predicate is "for Allah," without doubt.
* Another student: Apparently ﴿kulla-hu﴾, because it is an emphasis of the matter.
* Another student: The accusative, O Shaykh.
* The Shaykh: The accusative?
* Student: Yes, "the affair, all of it, is for Allah."
* The Shaykh: Yes, it is as he said: an emphasis.
* Student: No, it is not an emphasis; rather, "yes" is the emphasis.
* The Shaykh: I say: both are preferable, because they are two canonical recitations (qira'at sab'iyya, the seven recognised readings). If it is ﴿kulla-hu﴾, then (kulla) is in the accusative as an emphasis of the matter: ﴿Indeed the affair, all of it, is for Allah.﴾ And according to the nominative reading, ﴿al-amr﴾ is the subject of (inna), (kullu) is a subject (mubtada'), (li-llah) is the predicate, and the nominal clause made of the subject and predicate is the predicate of (inna).

In any case, ﴿al-amr﴾ here, in ﴿the affair, all of it, is for Allah﴾, covers both the cosmic command (al-amr al-kawni) and the legislative command (al-amr al-shar'i). So the affair belongs entirely to Allah the Mighty and Majestic. He disposes of His servants as He wills, according to what wisdom requires, whether this command is cosmic, which is what Allah refers to when He says: "Be, and it is," or legislative, which is the command directed to whom? To the servants: "Do" or "do not do." All of it belongs to Allah, just as all judgment belongs to Allah.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They conceal within themselves what they do not reveal to you﴾ [Ali 'Imran 154]. ﴿They conceal within themselves﴾ means they hide in their souls what they do not reveal to the Messenger ﷺ, but Allah knows it. Without doubt, this is something that occurred among the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them). It is a matter which, had they left it, would have been better. Had they spoken openly to the Messenger ﷺ and been frank with him, that would have been better than their talking among themselves and concealing it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. And this does not apply to all the Companions. To whom? To a group.

* Student: The hypocrites.
* The Shaykh: No, to a group of them, because all the hypocrites turned back before they reached Uhud. If any remained, only a few people remained. But the apparent meaning of the verse, where He says: ﴿a group among you was overcome by drowsiness, and another group was concerned only for themselves﴾ [Ali 'Imran 154], is that this group was from the believers. Yet someone may say to me: "Rather, the verse indicates that this group was not from the believers, because He said: ﴿a group among you was overcome by drowsiness, and another group was concerned only for themselves﴾, and He did not say: 'and another group from among you.'" But what favours the first view is the division, because He said: ﴿a group was overcome by drowsiness﴾ and ﴿another group was concerned only for themselves﴾. The exegetes differ on this, in two views:
The first view: this group is a group of hypocrites.
The second view: it is a group of believers, but weak in faith.

* Student: O Shaykh, regarding His saying: ﴿while the Messenger was calling you from behind you﴾ [Ali 'Imran 153], does it mean he was at the front of the army or...?

* The Shaykh: How?
* Student: That is, when they met (the enemy), was he closer to the Muslims than to the polytheists?
* The Shaykh: The Messenger? Yes?
* Student: It is not in the Qur'an, O Shaykh, but indeed...
* The Shaykh: No, no. After they fled, he was at the rear.
* Student: He returned, then?
* The Shaykh: No, he was in his place. Now imagine they are in a certain area and they fled from it, while the Messenger remained. What happens? He is at their rear.

* Student: O Shaykh, ﴿another group was concerned only for themselves﴾ [Ali 'Imran 154]. It is said that they were not overcome by drowsiness, because they were concerned for themselves and not for the Messenger ﷺ. And this is implied but not mentioned.
* The Shaykh: How?
* Student: That is, one group was overcome by drowsiness, and the second group, which was concerned for themselves, was not overcome by drowsiness, because they did not care about his ﷺ affair and the affair of...
* The Shaykh: Yes. The plain meaning of the verse is: ﴿another group was concerned only for themselves﴾. That is, they were selfish.
* Student: That is, a punishment for them, because they did not concern themselves with the Messenger ﷺ, so drowsiness did not overcome them, because drowsiness is security and victory from Allah the Exalted.
* The Shaykh: Drowsiness indicates, without doubt, tranquillity of heart and the lifting of fear from them.
* Student: It follows for them.
* The Shaykh: And one whose soul has concerned him will not doze off.
* Student: The point, O Shaykh, is that because he did not care for Islam and did not care for him ﷺ, He repaid them in this world by...
* The Shaykh: No, they do not need any repayment. This is a fact. Everyone who is concerned for himself in such situations cannot sleep, and sleep does not approach him.

* Student: O Shaykh, may Allah be good to you, regarding the saying of Allah the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Then He turned you away from them﴾ [Ali 'Imran 152], we said that "turning away" implies that the Companions were advancing with great intensity against the disbelievers. May Allah be good to you. I say: what is the wisdom in Allah turning them away, that is, from fighting the disbelievers, when a Muslim's killing of disbelievers is beloved to Allah the Mighty and Majestic?
* The Shaykh: What?
* Student: I say: what is the wisdom in Allah's turning them away, when their killing of disbelievers is beloved to Allah the Mighty and Majestic?
* The Shaykh: For a wisdom.
* Student: Yes, what is it?
* The Shaykh: The wisdom is that this would be a training for them. The cause of that is that they left their position, as Allah said: ﴿until, when you lost heart﴾, that is, became cowardly, ﴿and disputed about the matter, and disobeyed after He had shown you what you love﴾ [Ali 'Imran 152]. All three of these are causes of abandonment.

* Student: O Shaykh, is the verb in His saying: ﴿so that you would not grieve﴾ governed by the lam or by (kay)?
* The Shaykh: What do you say?
* Students: We did not hear, O Shaykh.
* The Shaykh: He is asking: is the verb in ﴿so that you would not grieve﴾ governed by (kay) or by the lam?
* Student: O Shaykh, there is a disagreement between the Basrans (al-Basriyyun, the grammarians of Basra) and the Kufans (al-Kufiyyun, the grammarians of Kufa). Some estimate an implied (an), and some say it is governed by (kay). According to the Basrans, by the lam; according to the Kufans, by (kay).
* The Shaykh: They say: when both the lam and (kay) are mentioned, the accusative is governed by (kay). When (kay) alone or the lam alone is mentioned, the Kufans say the particle itself is the governing element, while the Basrans say an (an) is implied. That is, if the two come together, the accusative is governed directly by (kay). Clear?
* Student: His saying: ﴿so that you would not grieve over what escaped you, nor over what befell you﴾ [Ali 'Imran 153]. We said: the calamity is the cause of another calamity. Would this not be, O Shaykh, indicating that His saying: ﴿grief upon grief﴾ means the preposition (ba') expresses accompaniment, in the sense that this grief has a cause?
* The Shaykh: Yes. Nothing prevents this, and nothing prevents also that their grief for the Messenger, by opposing his command, was its cause. When they opposed the command, grief occurred. Then grief occurred, then grief occurred.

* Student: O Shaykh, some exegetes mentioned that there is a difference between (amana) and (amn). The difference is that (amana) is a temporary security, after which there is fear, as in the verse, whereas (amn) is continuous security, as in His saying: ﴿For them is security, and they are guided﴾ [al-An'am 82], in Paradise?
* The Shaykh: No, that is not correct, because (amn) is a verbal noun (masdar), and a verbal noun is absolute, covering the little and the much. As for ﴿for them is security﴾, the (al) in it indicates completeness and comprehensiveness. But if you say (amina amnan), it does not indicate that it is lasting, or (amana), which does not indicate that it is lasting. So the apparent view is the second: there is no difference. For this reason, many exegetes explained it by saying: "amana" means "amnan" (security).

* * *

* Student: ﴿Then He sent down upon you, after the distress, security in the form of drowsiness overcoming a group among you, while another group was concerned only for themselves, thinking about Allah other than the truth, the thought of the Jahiliyyah, saying: Do we have any say in the matter? Say: Indeed, the affair is entirely for Allah. They conceal within themselves what they do not reveal to you. They say: If we had any say in the matter, we would not have been killed here. Say: Even if you had been in your houses, those destined to be killed would have gone forth to their resting places. And so that Allah might test what is in your breasts and purify what is in your hearts, and Allah is Knower of what is within the breasts. Indeed, those of you who turned back on the day the two armies met, it was only Satan who caused them to slip because of some of what they had earned. But Allah has pardoned them; indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing﴾ [Ali 'Imran 154–155].

* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. We stopped in the explanation of the verse at His saying, blessed and exalted: ﴿They say: If we had any say in the matter, we would not have been killed here﴾.

His saying: ﴿They conceal within themselves what they do not reveal to you. They say﴾. The clause ﴿They say﴾ is an explanation of what they conceal, and "saying" here is saying with the tongue, because when "saying" is used without qualification, it means speech of the tongue. Clear?

﴿They say: If we had any say in the matter, we would not have been killed here.﴾

The saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿When you were climbing and not looking back at anyone, while the Messenger was calling you from behind you. So He rewarded you with distress upon distress﴾ [Ali 'Imran 153]. We take from here: He said ﴿So He rewarded you with distress upon distress﴾. What is the meaning of "reward" (ithaba) here?

* Student: "Reward" here means recompense.
* The Shaykh: Recompense, that is, He recompensed you. Is the word "reward" (thawab) used for recompense by punishment?
* Student: Yes, it is used. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Have the disbelievers been recompensed for what they used to do?﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 36].
* The Shaykh: It is used, based on His saying: ﴿Have the disbelievers been recompensed for what they used to do?﴾. And when reward and punishment are combined?
* Student: Then "reward" is the recompense for good deeds.
* The Shaykh: So reward is for good deeds, and punishment is for evil deeds.

His saying: ﴿He rewarded you with distress upon distress﴾. The preposition (ba')?

* Student: The preposition (ba') has three uses: either for accompaniment, or for substitution, meaning exchange, or in the sense of (ala), and all of them are suitable here.
* The Shaykh: All of them are suitable here. On the view that it means accompaniment, what is its meaning?
* Student: That is, distress closely following distress.
* The Shaykh: Yes, attached to distress.
* Student: That is, many distresses.
* The Shaykh: Well done. So the meaning is not just two distresses?
* Student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Mention an example of two distresses from that?
* Student: The withdrawal of a third of the army on its march to the battle of Uhud.
* The Shaykh: And other than that?
* Student: And the rumour that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had been killed, and the Messenger of Allah being wounded.
* The Shaykh: The Messenger ﷺ being wounded.
* Student: And that, when they had victory at the beginning of the battle, the tide turned against them.
* The Shaykh: The loss of victory, that is?
* Student: Yes, these are three.
* The Shaykh: We want a fourth.
* Student: What happened to the Prophet ﷺ when his face was cut and his front tooth was broken.
* Another student: He mentioned it.
* The Shaykh: He said it.
* Student: And Hamzah was killed, and many of the martyrs.
* The Shaykh: Yes, a number of the men of the Muslims were killed.
* Student: And the withdrawal of a third of the army: the hypocrites.
* The Shaykh: This (...) was before the ascent. We mentioned it, but it was before the ascent.
* Student: Their opposition to the Prophet ﷺ.
* The Shaykh: Their opposition to the Messenger, is this not... a distress?
* Student: That makes five; we mentioned five.
* The Shaykh: My brother, one remains.
* Student: This is it, O Shaykh.
* The Shaykh: This is the fifth?
* Students: Yes, the fifth.
* The Shaykh: Yes. Well, we may say that the fifth is the victory of the polytheists over them, because the victory was lost to them, and the polytheists did not flee. They prevailed over them, climbed the mountain, and began to speak. "Abu Sufyan says: Is Muhammad among you? Is the son of Abu Quhafah among you? Is 'Umar among you?" until he boasted of his idol and said: "Exalt Hubal!"[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (3039) from the hadith of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib.]] This is without doubt a distress. So the distresses are many.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿so that you would not grieve over what escaped you, nor over what befell you﴾. The lam in ﴿so that you would not grieve﴾?

* Student: The lam of causation.
* The Shaykh: The lam is for causation. And (kay) here?
* Student: It is the verbal (masdariyyah) particle.
* The Shaykh: And it is not suitable for causation?
* Student: (an).
* The Shaykh: In this context?
* Student: No, no.
* The Shaykh: It is not suitable.
* Student: It is not suitable.
* The Shaykh: What do you say?
* Students: Is that correct?
* The Shaykh: Fine. Is it the governing particle itself, or governed by an implied (an)?
* Student: No, it is itself.
* The Shaykh: Why?
* Student: That is, if the lam of genitive precedes it, it is necessarily the verbal particle.
* The Shaykh: It is necessarily verbal, and so it governs the accusative directly. Good. This causal clause, ﴿so that you would not grieve﴾, how does it relate to what precedes it?
* Student: Yes, if it is said: "Do not grieve," that is, if they grieved, then not grieving is required.
* The Shaykh: Yes, because He said: "He rewarded you so that you would not grieve."
* Student: Yes, because grief and distress are of no benefit regarding what has passed.
* The Shaykh: How? ﴿so that you would not grieve﴾?
* Student: Yes, because when calamities come one after another, the greater one lightens the lesser. For example, the killing of the Prophet ﷺ was the greatest calamity for them. When they discovered he had not been killed, it lightened the impact of defeat on their souls.
* The Shaykh: The distress that preceded, so the meaning is that every distress makes one forget?
* Student: The lesser distress.
* The Shaykh: What is below it. On this basis is the saying of the poet:

Perhaps your reproach has a praiseworthy outcome,
and often bodies recover health through illnesses.

His saying: ﴿so that you would not grieve over what escaped you, nor over what befell you﴾. What is it that escaped them, and what is it that befell them?

* Student: What escaped them was victory.
* The Shaykh: And the spoils.
* Student: And the spoils. And what befell them was defeat and abandonment.
* The Shaykh: Correct. His saying: ﴿And Allah is Aware of what you do﴾ [Ali 'Imran 153]. What is the meaning of "Aware" (khabir)?

* Student: "Aware" means: He knows (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: "Aware" is the one who knows the inner realities of matters.
* The Shaykh: He is the one who knows the inner realities of matters, yes. And His knowledge of inner realities necessarily includes His knowledge of outward appearances, all the more so.
What is the benefit of ending the verse with this name?

* Student: Ending the verse, that is, with this name.
* The Shaykh: With His saying: ﴿And Allah is Aware of what you do﴾?
* Student: Yes, because Allah's awareness of their condition is what entails the punishment and the reckoning. So it is like a warning to them; that is, if Allah is aware of your words, then He is the one who will hold you accountable and punish you for what you do.
* The Shaykh: For what occurred from you?
* Student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Then He sent down upon you, after the distress﴾ [Ali 'Imran 154].

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verses 153–154 (part 4 of 5):

﴿They conceal within themselves what they do not disclose to you﴾ [Al 'Imran 154]. They say, (this is what they conceal): ﴿If we had had any say in the matter, we would not have been killed here﴾. Here, "al-amr" (the matter) is the singular of "al-umur" (affairs). That is, if we had had any part in deciding this expedition, and the decision had been returned to us, we would not have been killed here, meaning we would not have gone out and been slain. This is because the Prophet (ﷺ) consulted the Companions when he was about to go out to Uhud, asking whether they should go out or not. The young men advised him to go out, because they, or most of them, had not taken part in the Battle of Badr. They wanted to make up for having missed Badr through this expedition. Some of the Companions said: "Rather, O Messenger of Allah, let us remain in Madinah. If they enter upon us, we will fight them from the rooftops." The Prophet's (ﷺ) view inclined toward this. But he entered his house (ﷺ), then resolved to go out, put on his armour and went out. It seems they wanted him to reverse his resolve, and they said: "We compelled the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." They said this to him, and he said: "It is not fitting for a Prophet who has put on his battle armour to take it off until Allah judges between him and his enemy."[[Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (13281) from the hadith of 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, and by him in al-Dala'il (1142) from the hadith of al-Zuhri.]] Thus, or something similar, and he went out. Those who said, "We would remain in Madinah," are the ones who said: ﴿If we had had any say in the matter, we would not have been killed here﴾, meaning, "We would have stayed in Madinah and not been killed."

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Say: Even if you had been in your houses, those destined to be slain would have gone forth to their resting places﴾ [Al 'Imran 154]. ﴿Say﴾, that is, O Muhammad, to those who said: ﴿If we had had any say in the matter, we would not have been killed here﴾: ﴿Even if you had been in your houses﴾, meaning, had you remained in them and not gone out, not merely in your city but in your houses, in the innermost part of the house: ﴿those destined to be slain would have gone forth to their resting places﴾. Notice that houses imply concealment, while "labaraza" (would have come forth) implies exposure. That is, your hiding and remaining in your houses does not prevent you from being brought forth to your resting places, where death was decreed for you.

As for His saying ﴿fi buyutikum﴾ (in your houses), it has two canonical readings: with a damma on the ba' and with a kasra, ﴿fi buyutikum﴾ and ﴿fi biyutikum﴾. In ﴿kutiba 'alayhimu﴾ there are three readings: ﴿'alayhimi al-qatl﴾, ﴿'alayhumu al-qatl﴾, and ﴿'alayhimu al-qatl﴾. These are: kasra on the ha' and the mim; damma on the ha' and the mim; and kasra on the ha' with damma on the mim. These three are canonical readings. The meaning is: ﴿Had you been in your houses, those destined to be slain would have gone forth﴾. Here "law" is conditional, with "kuntum" as the protasis and "labaraza" as the apodosis.

It has already passed before us that "law" comes as a conditional particle and also to express wishing, as in His saying: ﴿They wish you would compromise, so they would compromise﴾ [al-Qalam 9]. That means: they wish that you would compromise, so "an" (that) is the verbal particle here.

The Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Had you been in your houses, those destined to be slain would have gone forth to their resting places﴾ [Al 'Imran 154]. Death was decreed for them by a decree of divine destiny (qadariyyah), not by a legislative decree (shar'iyyah). Is that right? It is like His saying: ﴿And We had already written in the Psalms, after the Reminder, that the righteous servants shall inherit the earth﴾ [al-Anbiya' 105]. This is a decree of destiny. As for His saying: ﴿O you who believe, fasting is prescribed for you﴾ [al-Baqarah 183], it is a legislative decree in the sense of "obligation (furida)."

As for His saying ﴿ila madaji'ihim﴾ (to their resting places), it means the place of lying down, because the dead are laid down in their graves. But this lying down is for a term, until they are raised on the Day of Resurrection, since lying in graves is not the final state. When a Bedouin heard a man recite the saying of Allah: ﴿The mutual rivalry for worldly gain distracts you, until you visit the graves﴾ [at-Takathur 1–2], he said: "By Allah, the visitor does not remain!" Look how the Bedouins understood! By Allah, the visitor does not remain. He derived from this verse that there must be a departure from these graves, and that is at the Resurrection. As for His saying ﴿ila madaji'ihim﴾, I say: it is the place where they are laid down, where they are buried.

﴿And that Allah may test what is in your breasts﴾ [Al 'Imran 154]. His saying ﴿wa li-yabtaliya﴾: the "wa" is a conjunctive particle, and the "lam" is the lam of purpose (lam al-ta'lil). Therefore it must be kasra, and it is not permissible to make it sukun. That is, it is not permissible to recite "wa liyabtali" with sukun; rather you must say ﴿wa li-yabtaliya﴾, because the lam of purpose is always kasra in every case. This differs from the lam of command, which takes sukun when it follows a conjunction: "wa" (and), "fa" (so), and "thumma" (then). Allah said: ﴿Then let them complete their rites and fulfil their vows﴾ [al-Hajj 29], and ﴿Say: By the grace of Allah and His mercy, so let them rejoice in that﴾ [Yunus 58]. As for the lam of purpose, it is always kasra, even after "wa," "thumma," or "fa." He says: ﴿wa li-yabtaliya Allah﴾.

The "wa" is a conjunctive particle, so where is the thing conjoined to? And "li-yabtali"?
* A student: It is implied.
* The Shaykh: Implied. And what is the implied element?
* The student: "He did that"?
* The Shaykh: "He did that"?
* The student: "He did what He did in order to make clear."
* The Shaykh: The "wa" is a conjunctive particle, so it must have something it conjoins.
* A student: To "kutiba" (was decreed).
* The Shaykh: "Was decreed: ﴿labaraza alladhina kutiba 'alayhimu al-qatl ila madaji'ihim wa li-yabtaliya Allah ma fi sudurikum﴾"? No, that does not work.
* A student: The meaning of the verse (...) so that you may know the completeness of His authority.
* The Shaykh: It must be...
* A student: So that you may know the completeness of His knowledge, and that Allah may test what is in your breasts.
* Another student: "That grief has rewarded you."
* The Shaykh: In any case this is far-fetched; that is, the context is distant, though it has indeed been said.
* A student: It is conjoined to His saying: ﴿So that you may not grieve over what escaped you﴾ [Al 'Imran 153].
* The Shaykh: No, that is far-fetched.
* A student: Shaykh, the "wa" is resumptive (isti'nafiyyah).
* The Shaykh: No. They say that the conjoined element is implied. The implied sense is: "He did what He did so that the consequences of your disobedience would become clear to you, and so that He may test." The implied element here is a cause and its effect, so that the second cause can be conjoined to the first cause, which has been omitted together with its effect.

As for His saying: ﴿li-yabtaliya Allah ma fi sudurikum﴾, "yabtali" means "tests and examines." ﴿Ma fi sudurikum﴾ means the hearts, because of Allah's saying: ﴿For indeed it is not the eyes that are blinded, but it is the hearts within the breasts that are blinded﴾ [al-Hajj 46].

﴿wa liyumahhisa ma fi qulubikum﴾ [Al 'Imran 154]. His saying ﴿wa liyumahhisa﴾ is conjoined to "yabtali." "Tamhis" means "purification (takhlis)." "Mahhasahu" means he purified it, that is, cleansed it. It purifies what is in your hearts of every evil intention, like His saying: ﴿Among you are those who desire the world, and among you are those who desire the Hereafter﴾ [Al 'Imran 152], or of any trace of resentment toward the decree, or anything else that corrupts what is in the heart.

As for His saying: ﴿ma fi qulubikum﴾: if someone says: you mentioned that what is in the breasts is the hearts, and that purification is also for the hearts, how is that?

We say: Yes. Because testing is not the same as purification. Testing is examination, and purification is cleansing. For this reason the expression differs. He said: ﴿li-yabtaliya Allah ma fi sudurikum wa liyumahhisa ma fi qulubikum﴾. He did not say "ma fi sudurikum" for both, but said "yumahhisa ma fi qulubikum," that is, from the harm that damages your religion. This is because aversion to what has happened, or the desire for what should not be desired, where does it occur? It occurs in the heart. For this reason purification applies to what is in the heart, not to the heart itself, whereas testing applies to the heart itself. He tests what is in your breasts and purifies what is in the hearts, that is, cleanses. The point of reference therefore differs: in the first it is the heart, and in the second it is what is in the heart.

﴿And Allah is All-Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾. This sentence is resumptive, to explain the all-encompassing knowledge of Allah concerning what is in the heart. ﴿And We have created man, and We know what his soul whispers to him, and We are nearer to him than his jugular vein. When the two receivers receive, seated on the right and on the left﴾ [Qaf 16–17]. The benefit of ending the verse with this is that, having made clear that Allah has decreed what He decreed for these two wisdoms, testing and purification, He makes clear that afterward He will know what will be in the heart after this testing and this purification.

We now return to the explanation of the benefits. Allah said: ﴿Then after the distress He sent down upon you security in the form of drowsiness﴾ [Al 'Imran 154].
* Among the benefits of this verse: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is the One who brings sleep to a person or removes it from him, because of His saying: ﴿Then after the distress He sent down upon you security in the form of drowsiness﴾. However, Allah, in His wisdom, has made causes for sleep. For example, when a person lies down and relaxes, sleep comes to him; and when his heart is occupied and concerned with some matter, sleep does not come to him. This is like other things that occur by the will of Allah, but which have a cause.
* Among the benefits of this verse: if you are sleepless and sleep does not come to you at night, then turn to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Turn to Allah, ask Him to remove your sleeplessness, and supplicate with the well-known supplication for insomnia that is reported in the Sunnah.
* Among the benefits of this verse: drowsiness may be praiseworthy and considered one of the blessings, because of His saying: ﴿security in the form of drowsiness﴾. The scholars said: drowsiness in battle is a blessing. And drowsiness in knowledge?
* A student: A curse (niqmah).
* The Shaykh: We do not say "curse," but we say it is blameworthy. That is, it is praiseworthy in battle and a blessing, but in knowledge it is blameworthy. Likewise in prayer. However, if it overcomes a person, he is not held accountable for it. Yet the Prophet (ﷺ) commanded that when drowsiness overtakes a person during prayer, he should lie down and rest.[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1150) and Muslim (784/219) from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik.]] He said: [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (212) and Muslim (786/222) from the hadith of 'A'ishah, and the wording is: "When one of you feels drowsy while praying, let him sleep until the sleep leaves him, for when one of you prays while drowsy, he does not know, perhaps he would seek forgiveness and would revile himself."]] "Perhaps he would go to supplicate for himself and it would turn into the opposite."
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the drowsiness that befell them afflicted only the sincere believers, because of His saying: ﴿a group of you was overtaken by drowsiness, while another group was concerned only with themselves﴾ [Al 'Imran 154].
* Among the benefits of the verse: there may exist among the perfected believers some faults, such as selfishness. His saying: ﴿while another group was concerned only with themselves﴾ indicates their self-concern, and that they had no concern except themselves. What befits a believer in such situations is that his concern should be the support of Islam and the honour of Islam, and that he should sell himself to Allah.
* Among the benefits of this verse: a person who has no concern except himself in such situations may be afflicted, may Allah protect us, with this great trial, which is that they think of Allah other than the truth: ﴿They think of Allah other than the truth﴾. Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned in Zad al-Ma'ad many kinds of thinking of Allah other than the truth. Among them: they thought that this defeat would have no victory after it. This is an evil assumption. Whoever thinks that Allah will allow falsehood to prevail over truth permanently has thought an evil thought about Allah. Whoever wishes to return to Ibn al-Qayyim's words in Zad al-Ma'ad, it is excellent material, which is not found in the books of tafsir or the books of history.
* Among the benefits of this verse: the condemnation of those who think of Allah other than the truth, because Allah mentioned this in the context of condemning those who had no concern except themselves. If thinking of Allah other than the truth is blameworthy, then thinking of Him in the truth is praiseworthy.
* Among the benefits of the verse: no one thinks of Allah other than the truth unless he is ignorant, because of His saying: ﴿the thoughts of the Jahiliyyah﴾. So whoever thinks of Allah other than the truth is, without doubt, ignorant, one who has not measured Allah with His true measure.
* Among the benefits of this verse: these people denied what the Messenger (ﷺ) did when he went out to Uhud, but in a hidden way, because of their saying: ﴿Do we have any say in the matter?﴾, for in their view, if they had any say in the matter, they would not have been killed.
* Among the benefits of this verse: the clarification that the entire matter belongs to Allah, the legislative command and the cosmic command, all belong to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. No one has any share in the command alongside Allah. All the command belongs to Allah, because of His saying: ﴿Say: Indeed, the entire matter belongs to Allah﴾.
* Among the benefits of this verse: a person is obliged to forbid wrong by mentioning the truth, because Allah said: ﴿Say: Indeed, the entire matter belongs to Allah﴾, and the imperative in His saying ﴿Say﴾ is, at minimum, for recommendation.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the Prophet (ﷺ) does not know the unseen, because of His saying: ﴿They conceal within themselves what they do not disclose to you﴾. For if he knew the unseen, he would have known what they conceal even if they did not disclose it. But the Prophet (ﷺ) does not know the unseen, neither during his life nor after his death. If he did not know the unseen in his life, then his not knowing it after his death is all the more so. Allah has stated this clearly, when He commanded him to say: ﴿Say: I do not tell you that I possess the treasures of Allah, nor do I know the unseen, nor do I tell you that I am an angel﴾ [al-An'am 50]. Allah commanded him to announce this, and he announced it, (ﷺ), openly before the assembly. He did not conceal anything that Allah revealed to him, and this is among it.
* Among the benefits of this verse: the denunciation of those who object to the decree, because of His saying: ﴿They say: If we had had any say in the matter, we would not have been killed here﴾, to the end [Al 'Imran 154].
* Among the benefits of this verse: "law" (if only) after the decree is of no use, because of His saying: ﴿Say: Even if you had been in your houses, those destined to be slain would have gone forth to their resting places﴾.
* Among its benefits: that Allah's decree cannot be escaped, because of His saying: ﴿Say: Even if you had been in your houses, those destined to be slain would have gone forth to their resting places﴾.
* Among the benefits of this verse: it may contain an indication that martyrs are buried in the place where they were martyred, because of His saying: ﴿would have gone forth to their resting places﴾, that is, to the places where they were slain. And if this verse does not convey it, it has been derived from the Sunnah: some of the Companions carried their dead from Uhud to bury them in Madinah, so the Prophet (ﷺ) ordered that they be returned to the places where they fell, to be buried there, and they were buried at Uhud.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of wisdom in the acts of Allah. From where is this derived? ﴿And that Allah may test what is in your breasts﴾. The texts affirming the wisdom of Allah are beyond count, and indeed even the cosmic matters, which have no limit, all indicate the affirmation of the wisdom of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the lesson and the pivot are the hearts that are in the breasts, because of His saying: ﴿And that Allah may test what is in your breasts﴾.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verses 153–154 (part 5 of 5):

We have already explained that the rulings of this world are based on outward appearances, while the rulings of the Hereafter are based on inner realities. The evidence for this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Does he not know that when the contents of the graves are scattered and what is in the breasts is made apparent?﴾ [al-'Adiyat 9–10], and His saying, blessed and exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, He is Able to return him. The Day when secrets are examined﴾ [at-Tariq 8–9]. Also, the Prophet (ﷺ) did not kill the hypocrites even though he knew some of them, and he said: "People should not say that Muhammad kills his companions" [agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3518) and Muslim (2584/63), from Jabir]. He did this to treat them according to what? According to their outward state. Also, if the inner state were taken into account in the rulings of this world, chaos would spread among the Ummah, because every person might kill someone, or discipline or punish him, and claim that his heart harbors disbelief and hypocrisy. Such evil would result from this that the Ummah could not live with. But Allah, in His wisdom and mercy, made the rulings of this world based on outward appearances.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: Allah, exalted is He, may test His servants with that which purifies their hearts and frees them from impurities, based on His saying: ﴿and that Allah might purify what is in your hearts﴾. Tamhis (purification/testing) — as we have said — means cleansing.

* Among the benefits of this verse: the affirmation of Allah's knowledge of what is in the hearts, based on His saying: ﴿and Allah is Knowing of that within the breasts﴾.

* Derived from this benefit is a warning against concealing what Allah does not approve of, because if you conceal what Allah does not approve of, He will call you to account for it even if it does not appear to people. So a person must always take account of himself and examine what is in his heart: Does his heart contain goodness and the desire for what pleases Allah, or is the matter the opposite? Then let him correct his state.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, those who...﴾

* Student: ﴿They say, "If there was anything for us in the matter, we would not have been killed here."﴾ So is the word "al-amr" (the matter) here one of the "commands" (awamir), or one of the "affairs" (umur)?

* Shaykh: One of the "affairs."

* Student: Does it come with the meaning of "affair/matter" (sha'n)?

* Shaykh: From the sense of "matter." That is, if the decision had been a matter of consultation and opinion, we would not have been killed here.

* Student: Shaykh, the opinions of the exegetes regarding "those who say," who are thought to be some of the believers but whose faith has some confusion, and the second opinion that they are hypocrites: which is the stronger view?

* Shaykh: The stronger view is the first.

* Student: That they are believers.

* Shaykh: The stronger view is the first: that they are believers whose faith is weak, because He said at the beginning of the passage: ﴿And Allah has already pardoned you﴾, and such a statement would not be addressed to the hypocrites.

* Student: Shaykh, may Allah reward you well. I say, may Allah reward you well, does this not favor the view that those who said this were weak in faith, that they were the ones who were present at Badr and advised the Prophet (ﷺ) to remain in place, and that the people of Badr could not possibly exhibit hypocrisy?

* Shaykh: No. The correct view is that they were weak in faith. But those who said they were hypocrites seemed to consider it too serious for this to come from believers.

* Student: But if we look at those who said this...

* Shaykh: We cannot be certain that those who said it were the people of Badr. It may be them or others.

* Student: But we explained at the beginning, may Allah reward you well, that those who were present at Badr were the ones who advised the Prophet (ﷺ) to remain in place?

* Shaykh: Yes, they were the ones who advised that, that is correct. But when they saw the fighting and the Messenger (ﷺ) resolved upon it, would they have remained the same? That may not be the case.

In any case, we cannot be certain that they were the ones who were present at Badr. It may be that those who were present at Badr, when they saw the Prophet (ﷺ) resolved and determined, had their intentions made firm, because the people of Badr are among the best of the Companions.

* Student: O Shaykh, is it permissible to judge individuals based on dominant assumption (ghalabat az-zann)?

* Shaykh: Based on what?

* Student: Based on dominant assumption.

* Shaykh: The scholars say: it is forbidden to assume the worst about a Muslim whose outward state is one of uprightness. If his outward state is not one of uprightness, and there are indicators, then there is no harm, because Allah says: ﴿Avoid much of [the] suspicion﴾, then He says: ﴿Indeed, some suspicion is sin﴾. He did not say "avoid suspicion entirely," but said "much of it," and He did not say "suspicion is sin," but said "some suspicion is sin."

* Student: O Shaykh, there is a hadith in which the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Allah has overlooked for my Ummah what its souls whisper about, so long as they do not act upon it or speak of it" [agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5269) and Muslim (127/201), from Abu Hurayrah]. We said that there is a benefit in the verse: that a person is obligated to (...)?

* Shaykh: Yes, that is, he is called to account for it. Because the whispering of the soul is not something a person adopts.

* Student: But (...) at the same time.

* Shaykh: Yes, but what he does not adopt. If he adopts it, it becomes an action. As for mere talk and passing thoughts, we do nothing about them; they are nothing.

* * *

* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed. ﴿Indeed, those of you who turned back on the day the two armies met, it was only Satan who caused them to slip because of some of what they had earned. But Allah has already pardoned them. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing. (155) O you who believe, do not be like those who disbelieved and said of their brothers when they traveled through the land or were [on a military expedition], "If they had remained with us, they would not have died or been killed," so that Allah may make that a regret in their hearts. And Allah gives life and causes death, and Allah is Seeing of what you do. (156) And if you are killed in the cause of Allah or die, then forgiveness from Allah and mercy are better than what they accumulate. (157) And if you die or are killed, indeed, to Allah you will be gathered.﴾ [Al 'Imran 155–158].

* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed. Allah, blessed and exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, those of you who turned back on the day the two armies met, it was only Satan who caused them to slip because of some of what they had earned. But Allah has already pardoned them. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing.﴾

Allah, mighty and majestic is He, says: ﴿They say, "Is there anything for us in the matter?"﴾ [Al 'Imran 154]. What is meant by this interrogative?

* Student: It is a denying interrogative (istifham inkari).

* Shaykh: What is the meaning of "denying"?

* Student: That they say: "If there had been anything for us in the matter..."

* Shaykh: ﴿Is there anything for us in the matter? Say, "Indeed, the matter is entirely for Allah."﴾ [Al 'Imran 154].

* Student: Yes, this is part of their speech: ﴿Say, "Indeed, the matter is entirely for Allah."﴾

* Shaykh: Leave aside what came before it. ﴿Is there anything for us in the matter?﴾ What is meant by the interrogative?

* Student: Denying; that is, they deny, saying: "We have no say in the matter."

* Shaykh: That is, negation?

* Student: Yes, negation.

* Shaykh: Negation. If it is negation, how is it valid to say: ﴿Say, "Indeed, the matter is entirely for Allah"﴾? Because if it is negation, then they have acknowledged that they have no part in the matter, and therefore the matter belongs to Allah.

* Student: That is, they do not negate it, but they say: (...) "We have no say in the matter," so Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, said: ﴿the matter is entirely for Allah﴾.

* Shaykh: But if you take it to mean negation, then His saying: ﴿Say, "Indeed, the matter is entirely for Allah"﴾ cannot be a response to them?

* Student: This is a denial; the interrogative is for denial, its cause.

* Shaykh: But what is the meaning of denial? Does it mean negation as you said?

* Student: No, no, it does not mean negation. Rather, they denied that they had not been consulted, so that their opinion would be taken regarding the matter of war.

* Shaykh: Yes, it is as if they wanted to clear themselves.

What is meant by "the matter" in His saying: ﴿Say, "Indeed, the matter is entirely for Allah"﴾? Is it one of the "commands" or one of the "affairs"?

* Student: "The matter" here?

* Shaykh: Yes. ﴿Say, "Indeed, the matter is entirely for Allah."﴾ Is the intended meaning the matter that is the opposite of a prohibition, meaning one of the commands, or is it one of the affairs?

* Student: One of the affairs.

* Shaykh: One of the affairs? What do you all say?

* Student: The meaning of "the matter" is general, whether it is decreed (qadari) or existential (kawni).

* Shaykh: That is, it includes both affairs and commands?

* Student: Yes, it is general.

* Shaykh: But the context requires that it be one of the affairs.

His saying: ﴿They conceal within themselves what they do not reveal to you.﴾ What is it that they conceal?

* Student: ﴿They conceal within themselves what they do not reveal to you.﴾

* Shaykh: Yes, what is it that they conceal?

* Student: That is, their denunciation of the leadership.

* Shaykh: How, denunciation of what?

* Student: The denunciation that nothing of the matter was given to them and that their opinion about the war was not sought.

* Shaykh: Is there not a clarification of this in the verse?

* Student: The saying of Allah, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿They say, "If there had been anything for us in the matter..."﴾

* Shaykh: ﴿They say, "If there had been anything for us in the matter, we would not have been killed here."﴾ If that is so, how is it valid to say that they conceal it within themselves?

* Student: That is, they conceal it within themselves, meaning that they do not reveal it, but rather there is a group among them that denounced the leadership in this matter, so they conceal this matter within themselves, that is, within this group, and do not reveal it to the Prophet (ﷺ), and [they do not reveal it to] the other group that was overtaken by drowsiness.

* Shaykh: That is, among themselves?

* Student: Among themselves.

* Shaykh: Among themselves. They conceal it among themselves, but they speak of it to one another.

The saying of Allah, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿Those decreed to be killed would have gone out to their death beds﴾. Is the "writing" here legislative (shar'i) or existential (kawni)?

* Student: Existential.

* Shaykh: Existential. Good. Now can you give an example of existential writing other than this verse?

* Student: O Shaykh, the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿And We had already written in the Zabur after the Reminder that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants﴾ [al-Anbiya 105].

* Shaykh: Yes, well done. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And that Allah might test what is in your breasts and purify what is in your hearts﴾. What is the meaning of "yabtali" (tests)?

* Student: Ibtila' is testing.

* Shaykh: Yes. And how was it a test, and with what were they tested?

* Student: Allah tested them with defeat.

* Shaykh: Yes. And what is revealed by this test, what becomes apparent?

* Student: The sincerity of the believer becomes apparent.

* Shaykh: The sincerity of the believer becomes apparent from whom?

* Student: From the hypocrite.

* Shaykh: From the hypocrites. ﴿And that He might purify what is in your hearts﴾?

* Student: Tamhis (purification) of the heart; that is, it clears it.

* Shaykh: It purifies it of the impurity and resentment within it regarding what happened and similar things. Well done.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verses 153–154 (part 1 of 5):

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿When you were running away and not turning back for anyone, while the Messenger was calling you from behind you﴾. ﴿Idh﴾ (when): this is an adverb of time (zarf), and an adverb must have something it relates to. So what does ﴿idh﴾ relate to?

The most preferred view is that what it relates to is omitted. The estimated meaning is: "Remember when you were running away." This is the best of what has been said about it. Some of them said that it relates to what precedes it: "And He had already pardoned you when you were running away." Others said: "Then He turned you away from them when you were running away." But the closer view is that the relation is omitted, with the estimate: "Remember when you were running away," so that this situation remains always in your minds.

As for His saying ﴿tus'idūn﴾ with a ḍammah on the tā', it differs from ﴿taṣʿadūn﴾ with a fatḥah on the tā'. The ṣu'ūd (ascent) is climbing upward, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿To Him ascends the good word﴾ [Fāṭir 10]. The ṣu'd (running away), however, is fleeing swiftly across level ground. It is said: "aṣʿada," meaning he went fleeing or hastening across the land. This is what happened to the Companions (Ṣaḥābah), may Allah be pleased with them, although some of them climbed the mountain. The meaning of His saying ﴿idh tus'idūn﴾ is: what? They fled swiftly across level ground. Why? Because ʾaṣʿada is derived from al-ṣaʿīd, and al-ṣaʿīd is the surface of the earth, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿so perform tayammum with clean earth (ṣaʿīdan ṭayyiban)﴾ [al-Nisā' 43].

He said: ﴿idh tus'idūn wa lā talwūna ʿalā aḥad﴾, meaning you do not turn or look back at anyone. He did not say "wa lam talta-futū" (and you did not look), because al-layy is more eloquent. Al-layy is bending toward something. They did not turn back for anyone who fled, out of fear of being killed by the disbelievers. Picture the scene: about seven hundred of the best believers were fleeing, and only a small number remained with the Messenger ﷺ.

Also observe His saying: ﴿while the Messenger was calling you from behind you﴾. The Messenger ﷺ was at the rear of the people, the one facing the enemy from the back, calling out: "O servants of Allah, return! Come back!" But because of the severity of the situation, they did not turn back for anyone. This is a great matter, yet Allah the Exalted has pardoned them. He pardoned them and did not hold them accountable for what occurred.

﴿wa al-rasūlu yadʿūkum fī ukhrākum﴾: ﴿ukhrākum﴾ means "the last of you." It was the habit of the Prophet, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, to be at the rear of the people. He was not like kings who take the front. Rather, he was like a shepherd who is at the rear, checking on his flock. If someone needs help, or someone's camel or horse lags behind, he helps him. This is seen in the story of Jābir, may Allah be pleased with him. When they were returning on their journey, Jābir was riding a camel that had become exhausted (aʿyā). What does aʿyā mean? It means tired, unable to move. He said: "The Prophet ﷺ overtook me." Notice: this camel was exhausted and would be at the back of the people. He says: "The Prophet overtook me," meaning he was behind him too, behind this exhausted camel. "He overtook me, prayed for the camel and struck it." He struck it with an ordinary strike and prayed for it, and it went at a pace it had never gone before. The camel, SubhanAllah, had been exhausted at first and could only walk a little, until Jābir was pulling it by its rope and it was ahead of the people. It was one of the signs of Allah and the signs of His Messenger ﷺ. Then he said to him: "Sell it to me." The Messenger ﷺ asked Jābir to sell it to him: "Sell it to me for an ūqiyyah." How much is an ūqiyyah? Forty or fifty dirhams. But Jābir refused and said: "I will not sell it." Notice that at first he was going to leave it behind, and now the Prophet ﷺ is bargaining with him over it. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Sell it to me," so I sold it to him. He sold it to the Prophet ﷺ, but he stipulated that he could ride it to Madīnah, and the Prophet ﷺ granted his condition. When he reached Madīnah and came to the Prophet ﷺ at the door of the mosque, he said to him: "Have you prayed?" He said: "No." He said: "Enter and pray two rakʿahs." It is the Sunnah for a traveler, when he arrives in his town, to begin before anything else by praying two rakʿahs in the mosque. This is established from the Prophet's action and command ﷺ, and it is a Sunnah that many people miss. Then he gave him the dirhams, and Jābir wanted to give him the camel as well. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Do you think I bargained with you in order to take your camel? Take your camel and your dirhams, for they are yours." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhārī (2097) and Muslim (715/109), from the hadith of Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh.] This is the utmost of generosity. The Prophet, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, did not intend to give him charity. Some scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, said that the Messenger ﷺ wanted to give him the price of the camel and did so through this stratagem. This is an error, a mistake. Rather, the Messenger ﷺ wanted to know how precious this camel had become in Jābir's heart after it had been cheap to him, to the point that he wanted to abandon it. So he asked him to sell it. Otherwise, what appears from his saying "Do you think I bargained with you in order to take your camel?" is that the Prophet ﷺ did not intend to buy it originally, but wanted to know what was in Jābir's heart, may Allah be pleased with him.

* Student: Shaykh, may Allah be good to you. Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿until, when you lost courage and disputed about the matter and disobeyed﴾, then He says: ﴿then He turned you away from them﴾. And "thumma" (then), as you know, indicates sequence with a delay. But they had lost courage and disobeyed before?
* The Shaykh: No, the turning away came after the disobedience.
* The Student: Yes, so when they lost courage and disobeyed, then they were turned away.
* The Shaykh: Allah turned them away.
* The Student: Allah turned them away. Then He says: "Then He turned you away from them." We said that this turning away happened after an intense advance. So how can the turning away come after an intense advance, when they...?
* The Shaykh: Yes, they advanced intensely, but not in the order the Messenger had commanded them. They advanced intensely in order to finish off the polytheists. The speech is not only about those who disobeyed; it is about everyone.
* The Student: So some of them were advancing?
* The Shaykh: Without doubt. Before these ones came down, the Companions were advancing and gathering the spoils, while these others were fleeing. The disbelievers fled too, to the point that women were seen climbing the mountains with their shins exposed, having raised their garments.
* The Student: So according to this, ﴿until, when you lost courage and disputed about the matter and disobeyed﴾ refers to the archers on the mountain?
* The Shaykh: Yes, to the archers on the mountain. And ﴿ṣarafakum﴾ (He turned you away) is general.
* Student: In His saying ﴿thumma ṣarafakum﴾ (then He turned you away), "thumma" is for coordination (ʿaṭf). Coordinated with what? ﴿Thumma ṣarafakum﴾?
* The Shaykh: ﴿idh taḥussūnahum bi-idhnih﴾ (when you were killing them by His permission). The apparent view is that it is coordinated with ﴿taḥussūnahum﴾, then He turned you away.
* The Student: And in the book al-Jumal (...), "then" is coordinated with the response, the response of the conditional clause (...).
* The Shaykh: It is acceptable. I would say: it is permissible.
* The Student: So this would be the response to the condition.
* The Shaykh: No, this is not the response to the condition. The response to the condition is omitted, and this is part of it.
* The Student: Meaning part of it.
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: What is the difference between ʿafw and ghafūr?
* The Shaykh: ʿAfw, when it is not paired with forgiveness (maghfirah), forgiveness is included in it, because it is pardon for punishments. But when it is said ʿafwun ghafūr, ʿafw becomes pardon for abandoning obligations, and maghfirah is for committing prohibited acts.
* Student: Shaykh, we said that pardon has two kinds, blameworthy and praiseworthy. The blameworthy kind is that which is not from ability (...). Two kinds: for example, a man pardons his right until the Day of Judgment (...), while being unable to?
* The Shaykh: This may fall under the first kind, because on the Day of Judgment he will have the ability, and he will be given his right in full.
* Student: Shaykh, regarding His saying ﴿wa ʿaṣaytum﴾ (and you disobeyed). We said that the rebuke, in order to be gentle, did not mention the object. ﴿Wa ʿaṣaytum﴾: can one not say, Shaykh, that it means "you disobeyed the Messenger's command (...)", especially if we say the word here is one of the words "umūr" (matters)?
* The Shaykh: There is no command here. There is no "umūr" (matters) or "awāmir" (commands) here.
* Student: They disputed with the commander.
* The Shaykh: No. They disputed among themselves and disobeyed the Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, or they also disobeyed Allah, because whoever disobeys the Messenger has disobeyed Allah.
* Student: Those among the Companions who opposed the command were few, yet the sin encompassed everyone?!
* The Shaykh: Because He said ﴿ʿaṣaytum﴾ (you disobeyed). And those who disobeyed were fewer than fifty?
* Answer: We have repeated that the action of a group within a party may be attributed to the entire party. Indeed, Allah the Mighty and Majestic rebukes the Children of Israel for something their forefathers did, because they are one group. ﴿And when you said, "O Mūsā, we will never believe you"﴾ [al-Baqarah 55] addresses those in the time of the Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him (...).
* The Shaykh: What is it?
* Student: Without a waw: "sāriʿū" (hasten).
* The Shaykh: Without a waw: "sāriʿū" (hasten).
Does this contradict the view of the scholars that whoever denies a single letter of the Quran is a disbeliever?
* Student: It does not contradict it.
* The Shaykh: It does not contradict it. Why?
* Student: The scholars' statement applies when the text is not a recitation (qirāʾah) that is transmitted.
* The Shaykh: Yes, if it is not a recitation. And on this basis, if a person recites: "wa aṭīʿū Allāh wa al-rasūl laʿallakum tuḥamūn, sāriʿū ilā maghfirah..." (...)
* Student: This is permissible.
* The Shaykh: There is no harm, because it is a recitation. Good.
* * *
* Student: ﴿When you were running away and not turning back for anyone, while the Messenger was calling you from behind you. So He rewarded you with grief upon grief, so that you would not grieve over what had escaped you or what had befallen you. Allah is Aware of what you do﴾ [153]. ﴿Then after the grief He sent down security upon you, drowsiness overcoming a group of you, while another group was concerned only with themselves, thinking about Allah other than the truth, the thought of the Jāhiliyyah. They say: "Do we have any say in the matter?" Say: "Indeed, the matter belongs entirely to Allah." They conceal within themselves what they do not reveal to you. They say: "If we had any say in the matter, we would not have been killed here." Say: "Even if you had been in your houses, those destined to be killed would have gone out to their places of death. And so that Allah may test what is in your breasts and purify what is in your hearts. Allah is All-Knowing of what is in the breasts"﴾ [Āl ʿImrān 153–154].
* The Shaykh: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad and upon his family and all his Companions.
Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: ﴿idh tus'idūn wa lā talwūna ʿalā aḥad﴾. What is the meaning of ﴿tus'idūn﴾?
* Student: It means you walk across the land fleeing.
* The Shaykh: Yes. And what is the difference between it and taṣʿadūn?
* Student: Taṣʿadūn means you ascend upward, rising up high.
* The Shaykh: That is, you climb the mountain, for example, you climb something elevated. And which is the intended meaning?
* Student: Yes, the intended meaning is the first. (...)
* The Shaykh: Yes, well done. His saying: ﴿wa al-rasūlu yadʿūkum fī ukhrākum﴾: this sentence is in what position?
* Student: A circumstantial clause (ḥāl).
* The Shaykh: But in what position of i'rāb (grammatical analysis)? The ḥāl has a place in i'rāb.
* Student: In the accusative position.
* The Shaykh: It is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause. His saying ﴿yadʿūkum fī ukhrākum﴾?
* Student: That is: "in your rear."
* The Shaykh: With what does he call them?
* Student: He calls them so that they return to him, because they had fled, may Allah be pleased with them.
* The Shaykh: So that they return to him. He says: "Come to me, O servants of Allah, come to me, O servants of Allah" [al-Bukhārī (3039), from the hadith of al-Barā' ibn ʿĀzib, with the wording: "When they reached them, their faces were turned, so they came back in flight. That is when the Messenger called them from their rear."]. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿fa-athābakum ghamman bi-ghamm﴾. ﴿Athābakum﴾: the agent is Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and the meaning of ﴿athābakum﴾ is that He gave you a reward (thawāb).
And ﴿ghamman﴾ is the reward that Allah gave them, and it is the second object of athābakum.
And thawāb is the requital for an action, good for good and evil for evil. Even reward for evil is called thawāb. That is, even the recompense for evil is called thawāb. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Have the disbelievers been rewarded (thuwwiba) for what they used to do?﴾ [al-Muṭaffifīn 36]. But when thawāb is paired with ʿiqāb (punishment), ʿiqāb becomes the recompense for misdeeds, and thawāb becomes the recompense for good deeds. Similar examples in the language are many: a word has one meaning when standing alone and another meaning when paired with something else.
And His saying: ﴿athābakum ghamman bi-ghamm﴾: ﴿ghamman﴾ is the second object of athābakum.
﴿bi-ghamm﴾: the bāʾ here has been said to be for accompaniment (muṣāḥabah), and said to be for substitution (badal), and said to mean ʿalā (upon). Each has its viewpoint. Those who said it means accompaniment said: its meaning is "He rewarded you with grief accompanied by grief," that is, joined to it with no separation between them: successive griefs.
Those who said it means ʿalā said: "He struck you with grief upon grief," and it does not necessarily have to be consecutive.
Those who said it is for substitution and exchange say: its meaning is "He struck you with grief in place of the grief that came from you."
When we reflect, we find that the noble verse can carry all three meanings, as will become clear, Allah willing, from explaining what the grief was. The principle in tafsir is that if a verse can carry more than one meaning and there is no contradiction between them, it is interpreted according to all the meanings it can bear, because this is the eloquence of the Quran. So what were the griefs that befell them?
