* The Shaykh: Persian, yes. Do we not have Persian words?
* Student: This is not Persian.
* The Shaykh: It is not Persian. In any case, we have heard that it is arabicized from this; that is, its origin in a language other than Arabic is (kahannam), then through arabicization it became Jahannam.

And His saying: ﴿wa-bi'sa al-masir﴾: (bi'sa) is a performative sentence (jumlah insha'iyyah) for expressing blame, and (ni'ma) is a performative sentence for expressing praise. (Bi'sa) and (ni'ma) require two things: a subject (fa'il) and a specified element (makhsus). Whenever (ni'ma) and (bi'sa) come to you, they require a subject and a specified element. So here ﴿al-masir﴾: "al-masir" is the subject, and the specified element?
* Students: It is omitted.
* The Shaykh: It is omitted; its estimate is: "wa-bi'sa al-masir" is it, i.e., Jahannam; or "wa-bi'sa al-masir masiruhu" (and wretched is the destination, its destination); meaning both are permissible.
* From the benefits of this noble verse: clarification that the one who follows the pleasure of Allah and the one who returns with His anger are not equal; due to His saying: ﴿Afa-man ittaba'a﴾ ﴿ka-man ba'a﴾. And the interrogative here is for what? For negation; the interrogative is for negation.
* And among its benefits: affirmation of the attribute of pleasure for Allah; meaning affirmation that pleasure is one of the attributes of Allah; due to His saying: ﴿ridwan Allah﴾. And it is a principle of the People of the Sunnah and the Community that every attribute with which Allah described Himself, we must believe in it and describe Allah with it, so we say: Allah has ridwan and He is pleased. Is pleasure an attribute of action (sifat fi'l) or an inherent essential attribute (sifah lazimah dhatiyyah)?
* Students: An attribute of action.
* The Shaykh: An attribute of action; because pleasure has a cause, and every attribute of Allah that has a cause is among the attributes of action; have you understood?

Some people denied the attributes of action of Allah. They denied them on two grounds:
The first ground: that attributes of action are originated (hadithah), and originated things cannot subsist except in an originated thing; because the origination of the attribute indicates the origination of the one described, so originated things cannot subsist except in an originated thing.
The second ground: they said: if this attribute is a perfection, it follows that He must be described with it perpetually; and if it is a deficiency, it follows that He must be prevented from being described with it perpetually. Is the second ground clear?
* Students: It is not clear.
* The Shaykh: Not clear. They say: attributes of action that come into being after not having existed, if they are a perfection, it follows that He must be described with them perpetually and not be tied to His will; and if they are a deficiency, it follows that He must be prevented from them perpetually, that He not be described with them perpetually. Is that correct or not?
* Students: Correct.
* The Shaykh: Because deficiency cannot be something Allah is described with.

As for the first, the first ground, we say: your statement that originated things cannot subsist except in an originated thing is incorrect; because originated things are the act of the agent, and the act, rationally, comes after the... after what? After the agent, without doubt; because the act occurs by the will and power of the agent, and it comes after its existence; so the agent precedes the object and also precedes the act. How then can we say that an originated thing cannot subsist except in an originated thing? It is possible that He is eternal and then the act proceeded from Him, just as we now are born, and our actions occur when? After our birth. This is one point.

The second, the second ground, what is it?
* Students: The attribute (...).
* The Shaykh: That if this attribute is a perfection.
* Students: It must be that He is described with it perpetually.
* The Shaykh: If it is a perfection, it must be that He is described with it perpetually; and if it is a deficiency, it must be that He is not described with it perpetually. So we say in answer to this: it is a perfection at the time of its occurrence; at the time of its occurrence it is a perfection without doubt, and at the time of its non-occurrence it is not a perfection; the perfection lies in its non-occurrence. Is it clear, everyone?

Pleasure, take pleasure now: pleasure toward one who deserves pleasure is what? A perfection, and one does not deserve pleasure except after doing what necessitates it; pleasure toward one who does not deserve it?
* Students: Deficiency.
* The Shaykh: Deficiency, because it contradicts wisdom; so when Allah is described with pleasure, He is described with it in the state in which it is a perfection.

Those who restrict themselves to affirming seven attributes explain pleasure as reward or the will of reward; but the correct view is that pleasure is an attribute of essence (sifah nafsiyyah) with which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is described, and it is not reward; because reward is the creation of what one is rewarded with, the creation of what one is rewarded with, which is other than pleasure; and it, i.e., reward, is among the requirements and effects of pleasure, and it is without doubt not pleasure itself. You now, if you are pleased with a person, after you are pleased with him you reward him with what you see as a reward for him; is that not so?
* Students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: If that is so, then it is not valid to explain the necessitating thing by the necessitated thing, because they are two different things; so it becomes clear that the correct view is that of the People of the Sunnah and the Community, may Allah make us and you among them. What is it? That we describe Allah with what He described Himself with, without altering it; "ridwan Allah," yes, Allah is pleased, and what prevents it? And there is no prohibition or deficiency in it.
* Student: The estimate in His saying ﴿afa-man﴾ according to the Basran view, on the second opinion.
* The Shaykh: The second? ﴿Afa-man ittaba'a ridwana Allah ka-man ba'a bi-sakhatin min Allah﴾, meaning the estimate is: do you equate the seeker of pleasure and the one exposed to anger? So whoever follows the pleasure of Allah is like one who returns with anger from Him; and for this reason, the second opinion is far easier; sometimes a person is perplexed and does not know how to estimate.
* Student: As for ﴿afa-man﴾ according to the view that it is conjunctive to what precedes it, the sentence before it sometimes also does not have a connective between the conjunct and what it is conjunct to; is it not difficult?
* The Shaykh: It is for resumption (isti'naf), because the fa' comes for resumption.
* Student: Shaykh, may Allah be good to you, we mentioned that the negation of attributes is the negation of attributes (...) for total perfection.
* The Shaykh: What?
* The Student: Negating an attribute, negating some attributes requires the affirmation of the perfection of its opposite.
* The Shaykh: What, requires? Perfection?
* The Student: The affirmation of the opposite.
* The Shaykh: What perfection?
* Student: The affirmation of the perfection of the opposite.
* The Shaykh: Yes, yes.
* Student: Shaykh, can it be said conversely: that affirming attributes of negation is a negation of the...?
* The Shaykh: No; but he is described with this. For example, if you say: so-and-so is brave; does its meaning mean that stinginess is negated from him, or cowardice is negated from him?
* Student: Cowardice.
* The Shaykh: Yes, cowardice is negated from him; so perhaps we may say this, but I cannot now assert that it is a consistent rule that affirming attributes of perfection is negation of their opposite; but with respect to the attributes of Allah, there is no doubt that it is negation of their opposite.
* Student: Shaykh, we said: the generality of the saying of Allah, the Glorified and Exalted: ﴿Then every soul will be paid in full what it earned﴾ was specified by charity and fasting.
* The Shaykh: From another.
* Student: We preferred: "Actions are only by intentions" over this generality; and here, why did we not say that this generality is specified by these things, so we do not analogize other things beyond charity, such as prayer?
* The Shaykh: Because when what was excluded from its generality was excluded, the generality weakened; indeed I told you: some scholars say that if anything is excluded from its generality, its generality falls entirely.
* Student: The saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Whoever introduces into this affair of ours something that is not part of it..." [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2697), and Muslim (1718/17) from the hadith of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her.]], and "Whoever does an action upon which is not our command, it is rejected" [[Narrated by Muslim (1718/18) from the hadith of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her.]]. These actions, meaning, someone might say: they were not in the time of the Prophet ﷺ nor in the time of the Salaf, nor in the time of...?
* The Shaykh: Yes; because they did not encounter them, but they encountered similar things and the Messenger permitted them.
* Student: Giving the reward (of recitation) to Abu Bakr is permissible.
* The Shaykh: The correct view is that it is permissible, but it is contrary to what is preferable.
* Student: Is it permissible to give some gift to the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, Abu Bakr and 'Umar?
* The Shaykh: It is permissible, but it is contrary to what is preferable, even to your parents; it is preferable not to give them anything.
* * *
* Student: ﴿They are degrees with Allah; and Allah is Seeing of what they do (163). Allah had certainly conferred favour upon the believers when He sent among them a messenger from themselves, reciting to them His verses and purifying them and teaching them the Book and wisdom, although they were before in clear error﴾ [Al 'Imran 163-164].
* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Is one who follows the pleasure of Allah like one who returns with anger from Allah, and whose refuge is Hell? And wretched is the destination﴾. The interrogative here?
* Student: For negation.
* The Shaykh: For negation, meaning this is not like that. And (man) in His saying ﴿afa-man ittaba'a﴾?
* Student: Relative.
* The Shaykh: Relative, meaning "the one who." And by what is following the pleasure of Allah accomplished?
* Student: By obeying Him.
* The Shaykh: By obedience to Allah and avoiding His disobediences. ﴿Ka-man ba'a﴾: who?
* Student: A relative pronoun.
* The Shaykh: A relative pronoun, meaning "like the one who."
* Student: Returned with anger.
* The Shaykh: Returned with anger. What is the meaning of ﴿ba'a﴾?
* Student: Returned.
* The Shaykh: Returned, like one who returned with anger from Allah and earned it. As for His saying ﴿wa-bi'sa al-masir﴾, they say: this sentence is performative, its verb is an invariable verb (fi'l jamid) for expressing blame, and it requires a subject, a what?
* Student: It requires a subject?
* The Shaykh: Bi'sa requires a subject and what?
* Student: And a specified element.
* The Shaykh: And a specified element; where is the subject?
* Student: ﴿al-masir﴾.
* The Shaykh: ﴿al-masir﴾.
* Student: "Bi'sa huwa."
* The Shaykh: The subject is concealed, meaning? The estimate: "bi'sa huwa"?
* Student: Shaykh, a pronoun after...
* The Shaykh: ﴿Bi'sa al-masir﴾.
* Student: "Your destination, yes it is," or "wretched is the destination, your destination," it is one thing.
* The Shaykh: No; we do not want the specified element, we want the subject.
* Student: It exists.
* The Shaykh: Yes, it exists; the subject is al-masir, and the specified element is omitted; the estimate: "bi'sa al-masir masiruhu," or "bi'sa al-masir hiya," i.e., the Fire.
* From this noble verse: the urging to follow the pleasure of Allah, because this interrogative is for negating equality between one who follows the pleasure of Allah and one who follows His anger.
* And among the benefits of this noble verse: affirmation of pleasure for Allah, and that Allah is described with pleasure; and pleasure is a true attribute of Allah, and it is among the attributes of action; is that not so? And you know that among the People of Innovation are those who denied the attributes of action, giving two flawed reasons; what are they?
* Student: That they are originated and cannot subsist except in an originated thing...
* Another student: They said: if they were a perfection, He would be described with them perpetually, and if they were a deficiency, this is impossible, so Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, is not described with what contains deficiency.
* The Shaykh: No; and if it is a deficiency, He is not described with it. They said: if pleasure is a perfection, it must be that He is described with it eternally and everlastingly, and if it is a deficiency, it must be that He is not described with it; it is impossible that He be described with it eternally and everlastingly; because if it is a deficiency, how is Allah described with it? If it is a perfection, it follows that Allah is described with it perpetually. What is the answer to the first doubt?
* Student: The first doubt, I say: meaning, in refutation of them, that the act comes only after the agent; meaning like the act comes after the agent, meaning the act occurs from the agent.
* Another student: We say: this principle of theirs is wrong.
* The Shaykh: Their principle is wrong.
* Student: Meaning the agent...
* The Shaykh: Meaning it does not follow from the origination of an attribute the origination of the one described; right? Because an attribute exists only after the existence of the one described; the act exists only after the existence of the agent; and we perform originated acts while we are preceding them. What is the answer to the second doubt?
* Student: That it is a perfection, that pleasure is a perfection at the time of its act.
* The Shaykh: Yes, it is a perfection when its cause exists and so He is pleased; and it is a deficiency if its cause does not exist; if Allah were pleased with the disbelievers, this would contradict wisdom. Complete.
* From the benefits of this noble verse: affirmation of anger for Allah; due to His saying: ﴿ka-man ba'a bi-sakhatin min Allah﴾; and sakhat and ghadab are close in meaning; the People of the Sunnah say: sakhat is a true attribute established for Allah, and the People of Innovation say: no, it is impossible for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to be angered; rather the intended meaning of sakhat is retribution or the will of retribution; the meaning of Allah's sakhat is not an attribute in Himself, rather its meaning is that He punished and penalized the one who incurred His anger; or what? He intended to take revenge on him; and this is based on the premise that attributes of action do not subsist in Allah, as already mentioned; the reasoning is what was already mentioned.
But we say: retribution is among the effects of sakhat, and the will of retribution is also among the effects of sakhat; and the proof of this is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So when they angered Us, We took retribution from them﴾ [Az-Zukhruf 55]. "Asafuna" means "angered us"; "We took retribution from them"; so He made retribution after the existence of anger. Is it clear? This shows that this is not that.
* From the benefits of this noble verse: warning against exposing oneself to the anger of Allah; due to His saying: ﴿ka-man ba'a bi-sakhatin min Allah﴾.
* And among the benefits of this noble verse: affirmation of the Fire; due to His saying: ﴿wa-ma'wahu Jahannam﴾, and it is established, now existing and never to perish; because Allah mentioned eternity in three places in His speech: in Surat an-Nisa', in Surat al-Ahzab, and in Surat al-Jinn. He said in Surat an-Nisa': ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved and wronged, Allah would never forgive them, nor guide them to a path, except the path of Hell, to abide therein forever﴾ [An-Nisa' 168-169]; and He said in Surat al-Ahzab: ﴿Indeed, Allah has cursed the disbelievers and prepared for them a blaze, abiding therein forever﴾ [Al-Ahzab 64-65]; and He said in Surat al-Jinn: ﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger, then indeed, for him is the fire of Hell, abiding therein forever﴾ [Al-Jinn 23].

ولا قول بعد قول الله عز وجل؛ لأن قوله أصدق الكلام وأبين الكلام وهو الخالق عز وجل.

* من فوائد الآية الكريمة: ذمّ النار والثناء عليها بالقدح؛ من أين تؤخذ؟
* طلبة: ﴿وَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ﴾.
* الشيخ: من قوله: ﴿وَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ﴾.
* ومن فوائدها: التنبّه لأمر يتكلم فيه الناس كثيرًا الآن؛ يقولون: إذا مات الرجل: إنه رجع إلى مثواه الأخير؛ وهذا لو أخذنا بظاهره لكان يتضمّن إنكار البعث، مع أن القبر ليس المثوى الأخير؛ ما هو المثوى الأخير؟
* الطلبة: الآخرة.
* الشيخ: الآخرة، الجنة أو النار؛ القبر مزار؛ سمع أعرابي رجلًا يقرأ قول الله تعالى: ﴿أَلْهَاكُمُ التَّكَاثُرُ (١) حَتَّى زُرْتُمُ الْمَقَابِرَ﴾ [التكاثر ١، ٢] فقال: والله إن الزائر ليس بمقيم[[ينظر تفسير ابن عطية (٥/ ٥١٨) بلفظ: فإن الزائر منصرف لا مقيم.]]؛ شوف إن الزائر ليس بمقيم، من أين فهم هذا؟
من: ﴿زُرْتُمُ﴾. وهذا فهم فطري ما يحتاج إلى دراسة، لكن الأعراب عندهم ذكاء، بعضهم عنده ذكاء، عندهم ذكاء عظيم؛ وهذا كالذي سمع قارئًا يقرأ: (والسارق والسارقة فاقطعوا أيديهما جزاء بما كسبا نكالًا من الله والله غفور رحيم) قال الأعرابي: اقرأ الآية صوابًا. فقال: (والسارق والسارقة فاقطعوا أيديهما جزاء بما كسبا نكالًا من الله والله غفور رحيم)؛ قال: اقرأها، اقرأها صوابًا ما هو هكذا؛ فقال: ﴿وَالسَّارِقُ وَالسَّارِقَةُ فَاقْطَعُوا أَيْدِيَهُمَا جَزَاءً بِمَا كَسَبَا نَكَالًا مِنَ اللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ﴾ [المائدة ٣٨] قال: الآن، عزّ وحكَم فقطَع، ولو غفر ورحم ما قطع[[ينظر خزانة الأدب وغاية الأرب لابن حجة الحموي (١/ ١٧٦)، الكشكول (٢/ ١١٢).]]؛ ولهذا قال في الذين يحاربون الله ورسوله قال فيهم: إنما جزاؤهم ﴿أَنْ يُقَتَّلُوا أَوْ يُصَلَّبُوا أَوْ تُقَطَّعَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَأَرْجُلُهُمْ مِنْ خِلَافٍ أَوْ يُنْفَوْا مِنَ الْأَرْضِ ذَلِكَ لَهُمْ خِزْيٌ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَلَهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ (٣٣) إِلَّا الَّذِينَ تَابُوا مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ تَقْدِرُوا عَلَيْهِمْ فَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ [المائدة ٣٣، ٣٤].
قال العلماء: في هذا دليل على أنهم إذا تابوا قبل القُدرة عليهم خُلّي سبيلهم؛ لأن الله قد غفر لهم ورحمهم؛ فمن أين أخذوا أن الله غفر لهم ورحمهم؟ من ختم الآية: ﴿فَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ لأن مقتضى علمنا بهذا أن نفهم أن الله غفر لهم ورحمهم.

Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿They are of varying degrees in the sight of Allah, and Allah is Seeing of what they do.﴾

﴿They﴾: who? The pronoun refers to those who followed the pleasure of Allah and to those who incurred the wrath of Allah. However, a difficulty arises here: He returned the pronoun in the plural form (*hum*, "they"), although "man" (whoever) and its relative clause are in the singular, ﴿Is one who follows the pleasure of Allah﴾ ﴿like one who has incurred anger from Allah?﴾. The answer to this is easy: the relative noun carries a general meaning, so the pronoun may return to it according to its wording, and it may also return to it according to its meaning. Have you not heard the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And the one who brings the truth and confirms it, those are the righteous﴾ [az-Zumar 33]. He did not say "that one is the righteous," but said ﴿they are the righteous﴾, so He returned the pronoun to the meaning of the relative noun, which is plural. He says: ﴿They﴾, meaning those who followed the pleasure of Allah and those who incurred the wrath of Allah. ﴿They are of varying degrees in the sight of Allah﴾. Degrees: ranks, ranks in the sight of Allah, differing; so whoever followed the pleasure of Allah more closely is higher in the sight of Allah, and whoever was further from Allah is lower. Thus they are of degrees: ﴿They are of varying degrees in the sight of Allah﴾, that is, in standing. What is the measure of these degrees? We have pointed to it: whoever followed the pleasure of Allah more closely is higher in degree before Allah, and the reverse is also true.

﴿And Allah is Seeing of what they do﴾. ﴿Seeing﴾ is an active participle which may be from seeing with the eye, and may be from seeing with knowledge; so *basir* means "knowing" (*'alim*), or it means "one who sees" (*ra'i*). Does Allah have sight?

* Students: Yes.

* The Shaykh: Yes. The Prophet ﷺ said: "His veil is light; were He to remove it, the glories of His face would burn away whatever of His creation His sight reaches" [Narrated by Muslim (179 / 293) from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him]. ﴿And Allah is Seeing of what they do﴾. ﴿What they do﴾: that is, what they do, outwardly and inwardly, good and bad.

* From the benefits of this noble verse: that people are of differing ranks before Allah.

* Branching from this benefit: that faith increases and decreases, because the increase in degrees follows the increase in faith through certainty and righteous deeds. Is the increase in faith an increase in certainty, or an increase in statements, or an increase in actions, or all of them?

* Students: All of them.

* The Shaykh: Yes, all of them. Certainty undoubtedly varies; statements vary, as one who says "There is no god but Allah" ten times is not like one who says it twenty times, for example.

Actions likewise vary: one who prays six rak'ahs is not like one who prays ten rak'ahs; is that not so? This is what the People of the Sunnah and the Jama'ah adhere to: that faith increases and decreases; it increases through certainty, speech and action. How does certainty increase; does certainty vary? Yes, it varies by the text of the Qur'an. Ibrahim, peace be upon him, said to Allah: ﴿My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead. He said, "Have you not believed?" He said, "Yes, but to make my heart at rest"﴾ [al-Baqarah 260]. This is evidence from the Qur'an. Evidence from experience is that a person, whenever those who report the news increase, grows in certainty, and when he witnesses it, grows even more; and for this reason the hadith says: "Hearsay is not like direct witnessing" [Narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad (1842, 2447) and al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (3289) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both]. As for the increase in statements and actions, this is clear and there is no difficulty in it.

* From the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of Allah's highness, the Mighty and Majestic; the affirmation of His elevation, based on His saying ﴿in the sight of Allah﴾, and "in the sight of" means nearness of place; and if they are degrees, then degrees rise gradually, so from this is derived the affirmation of Allah's elevation. This is a matter agreed upon and unanimously accepted among the Salaf, and all five types of evidence point to it: the Book, the Sunnah, the consensus (ijma'), reason, and the fifth, natural disposition (fitrah). That is, the elevation of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is indicated by these five proofs: the Book and the Sunnah...

* Students: And consensus.

* The Shaykh: And consensus...

* Students: And reason.

* The Shaykh: And reason...

* Students: And natural disposition.

* The Shaykh: And natural disposition. The Book and the Sunnah are full of this. As for consensus, Shaykh al-Islam said: "Allah knows that after thorough research and reviewing what I could of the statements of the Salaf, I have not seen any one of them say that Allah is not in the heaven."

As for reason, it indicates Allah's elevation. How? How does it indicate?

* A student: That is, perfection... that elevation is an attribute, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has been established as not (...) the second...

* The Shaykh: That lowness...

* The student: That lowness is an attribute of deficiency...

* The Shaykh: And Allah...

* The student: And Allah is not described with deficiency.

* The Shaykh: Exactly. Reason indicates this. There is no doubt that elevation of place is like elevation of status; so is it perfection or deficiency?

* Students: Perfection.

* The Shaykh: Perfection. And if that is so, then Allah has every attribute of perfection. As for natural disposition, do not ask: every person who has not read the books of the people of innovation, to where does his heart turn when he mentions Allah?

* Students: Toward the sky.

* A student: Toward elevation.

* The Shaykh: Toward elevation. For this reason it is said that Abu al-Ma'ali al-Juwayni used to affirm elevation and say: "Allah was, and nothing was before Him, and He is now as He was." This statement a person does not understand: "Allah was, and nothing was before Him, and He is now as He was," which a person does not understand. But he wanted to deny Allah's istiwa' (rising) over the Throne. So al-Hamdhani, may Allah have mercy on him, said to him: "O Shaykh, leave aside mention of the Throne; tell us about this necessity that a person finds, for no knower has ever said 'O Allah' without finding in his heart a necessity to seek elevation."

Is that correct or not? If you had studied nothing at all, you would say "O Allah," where does your heart go? Up. Then he began striking his head and saying: "Al-Hamdhani has bewildered me, has bewildered me"; he had no answer. Is it clear? So we say: Allah's elevation is established by the five proofs: the Book, the Sunnah, the consensus, reason, and natural disposition. As you have seen, Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, repeats this meaning many times in al-Nuniyyah, because it is among the highest attributes of perfection.

* From the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, encompassing what we do; based on His saying ﴿And Allah is Seeing of what they do﴾. From this follows a behavioral etiquette: that we be wary of opposing it; for if we know that He is Seeing of what we do, we will avoid everything that angers Him, the Majestic, and do everything that pleases Him, especially since the verse came after His saying: ﴿Is one who follows the pleasure of Allah like one who has incurred anger from Allah?﴾.

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verse 164 (part 1 of 2):**

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Allah has certainly conferred a favour upon the believers when He sent among them﴾. ﴿Certainly (laqad)﴾: Whenever you find (laqad) in the Quran, it is an emphatic sentence. With how many emphases?
* The students: With three.
* The Shaykh: With three emphases. Whenever (laqad) appears in the Quran, it is an emphatic sentence with three emphases, namely: the implied oath, the lam, and qad. The original sentence is: "By Allah, Allah has certainly conferred a favour."
Someone may ask: What is the purpose of the oath when the matter is already clear? An oath is only made to one who doubts or denies. For a doubter who wavers, you swear to him, and for a denier, you also swear to him. So why did Allah swear in this verse that He had conferred a favour upon the believers by sending Muhammad (ﷺ)? And if He had said, "Allah has certainly conferred a favour upon mankind," would that not be sufficient? But He said ﴿upon the believers﴾, who recognise that this is a favour.
We say: The reason for the oath is not necessarily denial or doubt on the part of the addressee. The reason for an oath may be the importance of what is sworn to, even if there is no doubt. This verse is of this type. That is, the purpose is to explain the great importance of this favour, which nothing can equal.
* A student: I say: Regarding the pronoun in ﴿Is one who follows the pleasure of Allah like one who has returned with wrath from Allah?﴾, it is known that the place of wrath is Hell, that its levels are (darakat)...
* The Shaykh: What did you say?
* The student: It is known that the place of Allah's wrath is Hell, and that it has levels (darakat). We return to (...).
* The Shaykh: Did you all hear the objection? He says: Hell has levels (darakat) and Paradise has degrees (darajat)? We say: When the word (darajat) comes in a general sense, it includes both this and that, meaning it is suitable for both. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And for each there are degrees according to what they have done﴾ [al-An'am 132]. But when it is restricted to the people of Hell, it is said (darakat), as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire﴾ [an-Nisa' 145].
* A student: Shaykh, that is, whoever says that the attributes of action (al-sifat al-fi'liyyah) are not attributes of perfection for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic...
* The Shaykh: Raise your voice.
* The student: That Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is not described by them as a perfection. The attributes of action?
* The Shaykh: Yes. To whoever says that, we say: You are not perfect, and you are dull. When Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, does something, there is no doubt that perfection lies in doing it. All attributes are perfection. When Allah saves the believers and rewards them, this is an attribute of action. Is it perfection or deficiency? It is perfection. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is free of need from all creation, yet He manifests to them from His perfection that by which His perfection becomes evident. We know that whoever rewards the obedient has perfection, and whoever punishes the criminals has perfection. For this reason He said: ﴿They plot, and Allah plots, and Allah is the best of plotters﴾ [al-Anfal 30].
* A student: It may be said, O Shaykh, that before that, He was not described by it in Himself...
* The Shaykh: No, no, not at all. We say: Before its existence it was perfection, and after its existence it is perfection. Because when wisdom required its existence and it came into existence, it became perfection; and when wisdom required its non-existence and it ceased to exist, it became perfection.
* A student: Shaykh, may Allah bless you. Concerning the saying of Allah, glorified and exalted be He, in Surah an-Nahl, with (...): ﴿Then do those who plot evil deeds feel secure that Allah will cause the earth to swallow them, or that the punishment will come upon them from where they do not perceive? Or that He will seize them in their going back and forth, so they cannot escape? Or that He will seize them with gradual decline? Indeed, your Lord is Kind and Merciful﴾ [an-Nahl 45-47]. So the saying of Allah, glorified and exalted be He, ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Kind and Merciful﴾, in the context of these verses which contain severe punishment for these people, what is your explanation (tawjih) of the verses?
* The Shaykh: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said ﴿Indeed, your Lord﴾, addressing the believers: ﴿is Kind and Merciful﴾. From His mercy and kindness to the believers is that He destroys their enemies, because the destruction of their enemies is undoubtedly kindness and mercy towards them.
* A student: We said that the Fire is everlasting. It is known that out of every thousand who enter the Fire, nine hundred and ninety-nine men enter it, and one enters Paradise, and that Paradise is pure grace.
* The Shaykh: What?
* The student: Pure grace, unlike the Fire. Does not this contradict the saying of Allah in the sacred hadith: "My mercy precedes My wrath"? [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (7553) and Muslim (2751/15), from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]] How, O Shaykh, is there no basis for those who say that the Fire will pass away?
* The Shaykh: Look, may Allah bless you. When a clear (muhkam) text comes to you, interpret all the ambiguous (mutashabih) texts in its light. Although what you cited is not actually ambiguous, it is clear. Because those who deserve eternal abiding are not at all worthy of mercy, such that mercy would precede wrath. They are the object of Allah's wrath and curse. Do you understand? If the matter were one in which wrath precedes mercy, then a person who has good deeds and bad deeds: good deeds may erase bad deeds, good deeds are multiplied tenfold, and a bad deed is counted as one. That is mercy preceding wrath. But these people are not at all worthy of mercy.
* A student: Shaykh, is their deeds equivalent to the punishment?
* The Shaykh: Yes. Because they spent their whole lives in disobedience to Allah, in this worldly life.
* The student: Life is transient, unlike the Fire.
* The Shaykh: Stay with me. They spent their whole lives in Allah's wrath. When they spent their whole lives in Allah's wrath, their entire afterlife became punishment from Allah. They know this; they read the words of Allah. So why did they not save themselves? ﴿A fitting recompense﴾ [an-Naba' 26]. There is no doubt. That is, just as they passed their entire worldly life in disobedience to Allah, although the warner came to them, the signs came to them, and they were informed, and they did not save themselves, the requirement of justice was that their entire afterlife be punishment.
* A student: O Shaykh, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Its veil is light..."
* The Shaykh: "If He were to uncover it, the glories of His face would burn away whatever His gaze reaches of His creation." [[Narrated by Muslim (179/293), from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him.]]
* The student: Do we understand from this hadith that the sight of Allah, glorified and exalted be He, is limited, since it says "whatever His gaze reaches," implying that it ends?
* The Shaykh: What do you all say about this? Our brother says: "whatever His gaze reaches of His creation." Does it indicate that Allah's sight is limited?
* The students: No.
* The Shaykh: It indicates that the creation is limited, and this is not the limit of sight. Because he said: "whatever His gaze reaches of His creation." All that He created, His gaze reaches it. So the limit here is in what is seen, not in the seeing.
* A student: Shaykh, regarding His saying: ﴿And the one who brought the truth and affirmed it﴾ [az-Zumar 33], it is reported in a second narration; in a sound reading it is: "And those who brought the truth" (wa-alladhina ja'u bi-s-sidq).
* The Shaykh: What?
* The student: "Those who brought the truth and affirmed it" (alladhina ja'u bi-s-sidqi wa-saddaqu bihi).
* * *
* A student: ﴿Certainly, Allah conferred a favour upon the believers when He sent among them a messenger from themselves, who recites﴾ (...) ﴿their own similar [calamity]. They say, "From where is this?" Say, "It is from yourselves. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent"﴾ [Ali 'Imran 164-165].
* The Shaykh: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad and upon his family and all his companions.
I think we mentioned to you earlier some general rules concerning the readings (qira'at). Do you remember this? We mentioned general rules concerning the readings, but most of you did not grasp them. Let us read them now.
The reading of general rules says: These are general rules concerning the readings throughout the entire Quran:
The pronoun (huwa) and (hiya): the first with a dammah on the ha' and the second with a kasrah, according to the majority of readers, absolutely. You say (huwa) and (hiya). Al-Kisa'i, Qalun and Abu 'Amr made the ha' sukun in them after waw, fa' and lam: they made the ha' sukun after fa', waw and lam, as in: (fahwa, fahya, huw, lahi, lahw). That is, whenever they occur in the Quran, you may make them sukun or you may make them with dammah. Al-Kisa'i and Qalun also made it sukun in the saying of Allah: ﴿Then, on the Day of Resurrection, he will be among those brought forward﴾ [al-Qasas 61], in this place only, because this occurs after thumma (then): ﴿thumma huwa﴾. But al-Kisa'i made it sukun and said: ﴿thumma hwa﴾, only in this place. That is the first.
Second: the pronoun (alayhim, ilayhim, ladayhim) with a kasrah on the ha' ('alayhim, ilayhim, ladayhim with kasrah on the ha'). Hamzah read it with a dammah on the ha' throughout the Quran. You say: ﴿not of those who have evoked anger ('alayhum)﴾, and you say (ilayhum), and you say (ladayhum).
Third: the mim of the plural in such words as 'alayhim is sukun when followed by a moving letter that is not a pronoun. The mim of the plural in such words as 'alayhim is sukun when followed by a moving letter that is not a pronoun. Ibn Kathir made it with dammah when connected: he reads ﴿'alayhimu ghayri﴾, ﴿'alayhimu ghayri﴾ when connected: ﴿not of those who have evoked anger upon them﴾ [al-Fatihah 7]. Warsh made it with dammah when connected if a hamzat al-qat' follows: he reads ﴿'alayhimu a-andhartahum﴾. But ﴿'alayhim ghayri al-maghdub﴾ is not read like that. If a sakin follows, it is with dammah without connection according to all readers, as in ﴿atayna-humu al-kitab﴾ [al-Baqarah 121]. If a pronoun follows, it is with dammah when connected for all, as in ﴿anulzimukumuha﴾ [Hud 28]; you may not say "anulzimkumha," but there must be the waw. An exception to this is the mim of the plural when it follows a ha' preceded by a kasrah or a ya', and is followed by a sakin. In connected speech there are three readings: dammah on both the ha' and the mim, which is for Hamzah and al-Kisa'i; kasrah on both, which is for Abu 'Amr; and kasrah on the ha' with dammah on the mim, which is for the rest. In pausal form, all of them use kasrah on the ha' and sukun on the mim, as in ﴿bihim al-asbab﴾ [al-Baqarah 166] and ﴿yurihim Allahu a'malahum﴾ [al-Baqarah 167]. They say: (bihim, bihum, bihumu).
Fourth: if the ha' of the pronoun is not followed by a sakin and the letter before it is moving, it is connected for all readers, as in ﴿amatahu fa-aqbarahu﴾ [Abasa 21]. If it is followed by a sakin, it is not connected for all, as in ﴿ya'lamhu Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah 197]. If the letter before it is sakin, it is connected for Ibn Kathir alone, as in ﴿ajtabahu﴾, ﴿'aqaluhu﴾, ﴿'alayhu﴾. Hafs agreed with him in one verse, which is His saying: ﴿therein humiliated﴾ [al-Furqan 69] (fihi muhana). These are general rules, and it is good to write them down.
* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿Certainly, Allah conferred a favour upon the believers when He sent among them a messenger from themselves﴾, to the end. The discussion of the beginning of this verse and of the verses before it has already been covered.
He says: ﴿Certainly, Allah conferred a favour upon the believers when He sent among them a messenger﴾. This sentence is emphasised with three emphases, and we raised a question about it: why is it emphasised when it is already clear?
* A student: To explain the importance... to explain the importance of the thing.
* The Shaykh: You jumped ahead!
* A student: To explain the importance of what is sworn to, or of the emphasised matter, which is the sending of the Messenger (ﷺ).
* The Shaykh: Correct. Among examples of this is His saying: ﴿Then indeed, after that, you will surely die﴾ [al-Mu'minun 15]. It is emphasised although death is certain. But they said: since some people are heedless, as if they will never die, it is emphasised.
﴿Certainly, Allah conferred a favour upon the believers﴾: upon the believers specifically, rather than others, because the disbelievers did not recognise this favour, did not raise their heads for it, did not see any harm in opposing it, so they left it, turned away from it, and were deprived of its good. As for the believers, they are those for whom this favour became clear and who held fast to it.
And His saying: ﴿when He sent﴾: this may be a time clause (zarf) for ﴿conferred a favour﴾, or it may be for causation, meaning "because He sent." Both are compatible. So it explains the locus of the favour, which is the sending, and it is also a cause for the favour.
His saying: ﴿sent (ba'atha)﴾: the original meaning of ba'th is creating, and the message was called ba'th because it brings people out from one state to another. It is as if they were resurrected as a new creation, and created as a new creation.
His saying: ﴿when He sent among them a messenger﴾: (fi) is for location, because the Prophet (ﷺ) was sent among the middle of the believers, and he, peace be upon him, was the noblest of those among whom he was sent in lineage. His saying: ﴿a messenger﴾ means one sent from Allah. His saying: ﴿from themselves﴾ means from their own kind.
In Surah al-Jumu'ah (Surah 62), He said: ﴿It is He who sent among the unlettered a messenger from themselves﴾ [al-Jumu'ah 2], because the Prophet (ﷺ) was among the unlettered, while the general people are not all of them. But he was from themselves, meaning from their kind, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And of His signs is that He created for you from yourselves mates that you might find tranquillity in them﴾ [ar-Rum 21]. So the meaning of ﴿from themselves﴾ is "from their kind." There is no doubt that his being of our kind is more complete as a blessing, because if he were an angel, people would not have become familiar with him or inclined to him, and perhaps they would not accept from him. But when he is of their kind, eating as they eat, drinking as they drink, sleeping as they sleep, and being with them in their markets and their homes, that is more eloquent as a favour.
His saying: ﴿who recites to them His verses﴾: the clause ﴿recites﴾ is a second description of ﴿a messenger﴾, meaning: a messenger from themselves reciting to them His verses. Recitation here includes recitation in words (lafzan), recitation in meaning (ma'nan), and recitation in ruling (hukman). Recitation in words means he reads the Book among them. Recitation in meaning means he teaches them its meanings. Recitation in ruling means he acts upon its rulings, peace be upon him. There is no doubt that all three are encompassed by the word ﴿recites﴾. He, peace be upon him, recites it in words and recites it in meaning. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We have sent down to you the reminder that you may make clear to the people what has been sent down to them﴾ [an-Nahl 44]. And he recites it to them also in ruling. 'A'ishah said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) used to say often in his bowing and prostration: 'Glory be to You, O Allah, our Lord, and praise be to You.' He was interpreting the Quran." [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (817) and Muslim (484/217), from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her.]] That is, he was implementing it.
He said: ﴿His verses﴾. Are His verses the cosmic (kawniyyah) or the legislated (shar'iyyah)?
* The students: The legislated.
* The Shaykh: Apparently the intended meaning is the legislated verses, which are the revelation that Allah sent down to His Messenger (ﷺ).
﴿And purifies them﴾: that is, He purifies them, purifying them physically and spiritually. As for physical purity, He commanded them to perform ablution for prayer, commanded them to perform ritual bathing from major impurity, commanded them to remove impurity, and even urged cleanliness in general. As for spiritual purification, he purified their hearts from shirk, doubt, hypocrisy and bad character, and refined their character, peace be upon him, until their souls and their characters became pure.
His saying: ﴿and teaches them the Book and wisdom﴾: teaching them the Book and wisdom is not a repetition of His saying ﴿recites to them His verses﴾, because the first is recitation and the second is teaching, and teaching is more specific than recitation. When a person recites the Quran in your presence, he is not considered your teacher. He teaches you when he makes you recite it and instructs you in it. The Prophet (ﷺ) taught them the Book. Teaching here includes teaching the wording, teaching the meaning, and teaching the rulings, that is, acting upon them. His saying: ﴿the Book﴾ means the Quran, and it is called a Book because it is written. So it is (fi'al) in the sense of (maf'ul). It has often been repeated to us that (fi'al) comes in the sense of (maf'ul), and we mentioned examples of this. Who recalls (fi'al) in the sense of (maf'ul)?
* A student: (firash) in the sense of (mafrush, spread out).
* The Shaykh: (firash) in the sense of (mafrush), (ghiras) in the sense of (maghrus, planted), (bina') in the sense of (mabni, built), (kitab) in the sense of (maktub, written). This Quran is a written book. In what place was it written?
* A student: In the Preserved Tablet.
* The Shaykh: In the Preserved Tablet? And elsewhere?
* A student: In the hands of the scribes (safarah) as well.
* The Shaykh: The books that are in the hands of the scribes.
* The student: And in our hands.

**Shaykh:** As for the books in our hands. Some scholars said that the word *kitab* here means writing (*kitabah*), because the Arabs were unlettered (*ummiyyun*). When this great Book was revealed, they learned writing and began writing it down for the Messenger ﷺ, writing the Qur'an, and then they began writing some of the hadiths. Then writing spread among them. You know that among the ransom taken from the prisoners of Badr was that they would teach the children of the people of Madinah reading and writing. This speaker supported his view by saying that their being taught the Book is derived from the words ﴿He recites to them His verses﴾. But there is a point to consider in this. We do not prevent the word *kitab* here from meaning both writing and the Qur'an together, because our principle in *tafsir* (Qur'anic exegesis) is that whenever a word can have two or more meanings and there is no contradiction between them, it is obligatory to take it in both senses, since the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, is broad in meaning. So according to this, what does *kitab* mean? The Qur'an and writing.

As for His words ﴿and wisdom (*al-hikmah*)﴾, some scholars said: that is the Sunnah. *Hikmah* means the Sunnah, as Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿And Allah has sent down to you the Book and wisdom﴾ [an-Nisa' 113]. It was also said: the meaning of *hikmah* is that He taught them how to place things in their proper places, because the Islamic Shari'ah teaches a person how to put a thing in its place. Also, He taught them the wisdom which is the secrets of the legislation, because the Shari'ah, as you know, consists of rulings (*ahkam*) and wisdoms (*hikam*). The rulings are apparent, and the wisdoms are the secrets and meanings on which these rulings depend. When a person knows these wisdoms and secrets, it becomes clear to him that the Shari'ah is not frivolity or play, and that the Shari'ah has lofty meanings which no one grasps except those whom Allah has granted understanding. We can also say that *hikmah* includes both of these: that He taught them the Sunnah, which is called *hikmah*, and taught them how to place things in their places and the secrets and wisdoms of the Shari'ah, so that they would increase in insight into the religion of Allah.

He said: ﴿And indeed they had been before in clear error﴾. The particle (*in*) comes in the Arabic language with several meanings, and the context determines the meaning. So (*in*) comes as a conditional particle. (Abdullah), can you give us an example?

**Student:** *In tahdur* (If you attend).

**Shaykh:** If it is from the Qur'an, it is more beloved to us: ﴿If you support Allah﴾ [Muhammad 7].

**Student:** ﴿If you support Allah, He will support you﴾.

**Shaykh:** ﴿He will support you﴾. And it also comes as a negative particle?

**Student:** (...) it becomes negative.

**Shaykh:** Negative, negative.

**Student:** (…).

**Shaykh:** No.

**Student:** The words of Allah, Exalted: ﴿Indeed, for you is that which you judge﴾ [al-Qalam 39].

**Shaykh:** What?

**Student:** ﴿Indeed, for you is that which you judge﴾.

**Shaykh:** No, this is (*inna*). We are talking about (*in*).

**Student:** ﴿This is not but the speech of a human being﴾ [al-Muddaththir 25].

**Shaykh:** Yes. The sign of the negative (*in*), O brothers, is that it is followed by (*illa*): ﴿This is not but a clear magic﴾ [al-Ma'idah 110], ﴿This is not but a fabrication he has invented﴾ [al-Furqan 4], ﴿This is not but the speech of a human being﴾, yes, ﴿This is not but a noble angel﴾ [Yusuf 31]. So what is the sign of the negative (*in*)? That (*illa*) follows it. Good, that is two. And does it come as a lightened form of the heavy one? (…) What is its condition?

**Student:** ﴿In fi sudurihim﴾ [Ghafir 56].

**Shaykh:** No. ﴿In fi sudurihim illa kibr﴾. This is negative, and (*illa*) follows it.

**Student:** The words of the Exalted: ﴿If you doubt, we will not exchange it for any price, even if it were a near relative﴾ [al-Ma'idah 106].

**Shaykh:** No. This *in* is conditional in meaning. ﴿And if they had been before in clear error﴾: this is by its meaning. This (*in*) is the lightened form of the heavy (*inna*), and its origin is: *wa-innahum kanu min qablu* (and indeed they had been before). The sign of *in* as a lightened form of the heavy is that the lam (*lam*) comes in its predicate. If the lam comes after it, it is the lightened form of the heavy. Do you understand? ﴿In kanu min qablu la-fi﴾: the lam comes. Ibn Malik said:

*"And inna was lightened, so its action became rare, and the lam is obligatory..."*

The lam is obligatory, and it is the one here: ﴿la-fi dalalin﴾.

*"...... when it is left without effect."*

There remains a fourth: (*in*) comes as a superfluous particle.

**Student:** What came from..

**Shaykh:** No, this is (*min*). We are talking about (*in*).

**Student:** The words of the poet:

*"Banu Ghudanah, ma in antum dhahab..."*

**Shaykh:** Yes, this is the words of the poet: *"Banu Ghudanah, ma in antum dhahab..."*, meaning: "You are not gold."

**Student:** In the Qur'an, O Shaykh: ﴿When Our messengers came to Lut﴾ [al-'Ankabut 33].

**Shaykh:** (*An*) here is (*an*). We are talking about (*in*).

**Student:** ﴿The judgment is only for Allah﴾ [al-An'am 57].

**Shaykh:** Yes, this is (*inna*). We are talking about the lightened form of the heavy (*in*). In any case, I do not recall an example of it in the Qur'an. In the noble verse here, ﴿And if they had been before in clear error﴾, we say this (*in*) is the lightened form of the heavy. What is its sign? That the lam comes in its predicate, or in its subject if the subject is delayed. The important thing is that the lam comes after it. Did you understand, everyone?

Where is its subject? It was said that its subject is omitted, implied as an apparent noun, and the estimate is: "And indeed the matter was that they had been before in clear error." Others said: rather, it is an omitted subject implied as a suitable pronoun, and this is the correct view. So when the predicate is plural, the implied pronoun becomes plural. Accordingly, the estimate here is: "And indeed they had been before in clear error." So the pronoun of the matter is implied in a way that suits the context.

﴿And if they had been﴾: the pronoun refers to the believers among whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sent. ﴿Before﴾: before what? Before the sending of this Messenger. ﴿In clear error﴾: (*fi*) is for the sense of containment, meaning that error encompasses them as a container encompasses what it contains. ﴿In clear error﴾: ﴿mubin﴾ means clear (*bayyin*).

And as for His words ﴿before (*min qabl*)﴾, we say to the brothers who are beginners in grammar: (*min*) is a preposition, and ﴿qabl﴾ here is not in the genitive. Is that right?

**Student:** Shaykh, here it is cancelled (*mulghah*).

**Shaykh:** No, it is not cancelled.

**Student:** Shaykh, ﴿qabl﴾ is built on the *damma* (indeclinable).

**Shaykh:** ﴿Qabl﴾ is built on the *damma*? And wherever (*min*) governs it?

**Student:** It governs it in position, not in pronunciation.

**Shaykh:** What do you say, everyone?

**Students:** Correct.

**Shaykh:** The built word, even if prepositions enter upon it, does not change; it remains in its built form. Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿We will draw them gradually from where they do not know﴾ [al-A'raf 182]; He did not say "min haythu" with a kasra. Here He said ﴿min qabl﴾ and did not say "min qabli."

But sometimes (*qabl*) is genitive, and it is said: ﴿min qablihim﴾, ﴿Those before them denied﴾ [al-An'am 148]?

**Student:** Because ﴿min qabl﴾ is not annexed, and here it is annexed.

**Shaykh:** Good. Then when is it built on the *damma*? When the annexed noun is omitted and its meaning is intended. Did you understand? This is the statement of the grammarians.

* In this noble verse there are benefits.

First: the great favour of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, upon the believers by sending the Messenger ﷺ. From where is this taken? From the emphasis of this favour by an oath..
﴿In clear error﴾, ﴿mubin﴾ means clear. As for His words ﴿before (min qabl)﴾, we say to the brothers who are beginners in grammar: (*min*) is a preposition, and (*qabl*) here is not genitive, (*qabl*) is not genitive. Who has studied grammar well?

**Student:** Shaykh, here it is cancelled, it has no effect.

**Shaykh:** No, no, it is not cancelled.

**Student:** (*Qabl*) is built on the *damma*.

**Shaykh:** (*Qabl*) is built on the *damma*? And did (*min*) not govern it?

**Student:** It governed it in position, not in pronunciation.

**Shaykh:** Yes. What do you say, everyone?

**Students:** Correct.

**Shaykh:** The built word, even if prepositions enter upon it, does not change; it remains in its built form. Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿We will draw them gradually from where they do not know﴾ [al-A'raf 182]: He did not say "min haythu" with a kasra. Here He said ﴿min qabl﴾ and did not say "min qabli." But sometimes (*qabl*) is genitive, so it is said: "min qablihim", ﴿Those before them denied﴾ [al-An'am 148].

**Student:** Shaykh, because (*min qabl*) is not annexed, and here it is annexed.

**Shaykh:** Then when is it built on the *damma*?

**Students:** When it is cut off.

**Shaykh:** When the annexed noun is omitted and its meaning is intended. Did you understand? This is the statement of the grammarians. Yes indeed.

* In this noble verse there are benefits:

* First: the magnitude of the favour of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, upon the believers by sending the Messenger ﷺ. From where is this taken? From the emphasis of this favour by an oath.

* Among its benefits: that the favour of sending the Messenger was specifically upon the believers, because they are the ones who benefited from it, due to His words ﴿upon the believers﴾.

* Among the benefits of the verse: whoever does not acknowledge the favour is as one who has been deprived of it, or as one from whom it has been taken. Whoever does not benefit from the favour becomes like one from whom it is taken, because He restricted the favour to whom? To the believers.

* Among its benefits: the obligation to thank Allah's blessing for the one whom Allah has favoured with faith. From where is this taken? From His words ﴿Allah has certainly conferred favour﴾, because the purpose of this statement is to thank Allah, Exalted, for this favour, and that a person should not become conceited within himself.

* Among the benefits of this verse: a refutation of the Bedouins who boasted to the Messenger ﷺ of their faith and Islam. Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿They consider it a favour to you that they have accepted Islam. Say: Do not consider your Islam a favour to me. Rather, Allah has conferred favour upon you that He guided you to faith﴾ [al-Hujurat 17].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: seeking refuge with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that He keep you firm in faith, because if He is the Bestower of it, then He is the One who owns its firmness and its removal, so return to Him.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the virtue of the Messenger ﷺ, in that he was sent from whose side? From the side of Allah. A messenger becomes more honoured and esteemed according to whom? According to the one who sent him. For this reason people distinguish between the messenger of a sultan and the messenger of a servant. The messenger of a sultan they regard as greater than the messenger of an ordinary person.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the establishment of the prophethood of the Prophet ﷺ, from His words ﴿when He sent among them a messenger from themselves﴾.

* Among its benefits: the establishment of Allah's favour, Mighty and Majestic, in that this Messenger is of our kind.

* **Students:** ﴿From themselves﴾.

* **Shaykh:** Because of His words ﴿from themselves﴾.

* Branching from this benefit: the refutation of those foolish, obstinate people who said ﴿Why was not an angel sent down to him?﴾ [al-Furqan 7]. Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿And if We had made him an angel, We would have made him a man﴾ [al-An'am 9], because an angel cannot live among humans, and humans cannot accept from him as they accept from one of their own kind.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the great praise of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, in that he recited to them the verses of Allah, purified them, and taught them the Book and wisdom.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse also: the eagerness of the Prophet ﷺ to convey the message, in that he recited to them the verses of Allah and taught them the Book and wisdom.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the Qur'an is inimitable. From where is this taken? From His words ﴿His verses﴾, because *ayat* means signs, and the sign of a thing is that which specifies it and which is not suitable for anything else. It is a sign of Allah which is not suitable for anything else.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the permissibility of attributing a thing to its cause. From where do we take it?

* **Student:** From ﴿His verses﴾.

* **Another student:** ﴿He recites to them﴾.

* **Shaykh:** ﴿And purifies them﴾, although Allah said: ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you love﴾ [al-Qasas 56]. But he ﷺ is a cause, a cause of purification. So in the verse there is the permissibility of attributing a thing to its cause, but on the condition that it is known to be a cause, either through the Shari'ah, or through reason, or through the senses. As for something that is imagined to be a cause and is not a cause, this is not permissible.

* * *

**Student:** I seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿And when a misfortune struck you, although you had struck [the enemy] with twice as much, you said, "From where is this?" Say, "It is from yourselves." Indeed, Allah is over all things competent. (165) And what struck you on the day the two armies met was by permission of Allah, and [it was] so He might make evident the believers. (166) And to make evident those who were hypocrites. It was said to them, "Come, fight in the way of Allah or [at least] defend." They said, "If we knew there would be fighting, we would have followed you." They were nearer to disbelief that day than to faith, saying with their mouths what was not in their hearts. And Allah is most knowing of what they conceal.﴾ [Al 'Imran 165-167].

**Shaykh:** I seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Satan. Earlier, in the verse we just passed, Allah, Exalted, showed His favour upon the believers by sending the Prophet ﷺ, emphasising it with what emphasis?

**Student:** Three emphases.

**Shaykh:** And they are?

**Student:** The oath, the lam, and (*qad*).

**Shaykh:** Where is the oath?

**Student:** Implied.

**Shaykh:** What is the evidence for it?

**Student:** The lam.

**Shaykh:** The lam, well done. What is the meaning of His words ﴿from themselves﴾?

**Student:** That is, from among them, of their kind.

**Shaykh:** That is, of their kind.
What is the difference between this verse and His words, Exalted: ﴿It is He who sent among the unlettered a messenger from among themselves﴾ [al-Jumu'ah 2]?

**Student:** The same, meaning from among them.

**Another student:** That is, he was unlettered like them, from their own selves.

**Shaykh:** From the same Arab people. And "from their own selves"? ﴿From themselves﴾?

**Student:** ﴿From themselves﴾ means from the very same kind.

**Shaykh:** From the kind of the children of Adam. Is it clear, everyone? So ﴿from among them﴾ because he is from the Arabs, and ﴿from themselves﴾ because he is from the kind of the children of Adam, even though the children of Adam who are not Arabs are not his relatives.
What is the meaning of His words ﴿the Book﴾, ﴿He teaches them the Book﴾?

**Student:** *Kitab* means written, and that is the Qur'an.

**Students:** Yes.

**Student:** It means writing.

**Shaykh:** It means writing. On the first meaning, *fi'al* is in the sense of *maf'ul* (passive). Can we say that the verse includes two meanings?

**Student:** (...).

**Shaykh:** It is possible. Do you know a principle regarding this?

**Student:** Because the principle says: when a word can have more than one meaning with no contradiction between them, it is obligatory to take it in all of them, because the Book of Allah, Exalted, is broad.

**Shaykh:** Yes, because the verse is broader and more comprehensive. His words ﴿And if they had been before in clear error﴾: this (*in*) is what?

**Student:** The lightened form of the heavy.

**Shaykh:** What is its sign in this verse?

**Student:** The distinguishing lam.

**Shaykh:** The distinguishing lam: ﴿la-fi dalalin mubin﴾. Do you know any meaning for (*in*) other than lightening?

**Student:** Yes, it has four meanings: it can be negative.

**Shaykh:** Lightened.

**Student:** Lightened and negative, and it can be superfluous, and it can be..

**Shaykh:** It can be conditional. Good. We mentioned a sign for the negative. What is it?

**Student:** That (*illa*) comes after it, I think.

**Shaykh:** That (*illa*) comes after it. You think, but you are not certain.

**Student:** I think, meaning I believe.

**Shaykh:** And believe means know?

**Student:** That (*illa*) comes after it.

**Shaykh:** Like what?

**Student:** Like the words of Allah, Exalted: ﴿This is not but a fabrication invented﴾.

**Shaykh:** ﴿This is not but a fabrication invented﴾, correct.
His words: ﴿la-fi dalalin mubin﴾. Is this error practical, or knowledge-based, or both?

**Student:** Here it includes both meanings.

**Shaykh:** Error of knowledge and error of action. What do you say?

**Students:** Correct.

**Shaykh:** Correct, because the Arabs were ignorant and were misguided in action: ignorant in knowledge, and erring in deeds.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verse 165 (part 1 of 2):

Then Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Why is it that when a calamity struck you, although you had inflicted twice as much (on the enemy), you said, "How is this?"﴾ The hamzah here is followed by a conjunction (waw/fa-type particle). We have often seen that when the interrogative hamzah is followed by a conjunction, the grammarians have two opinions on this:

The first: the conjunction links to something implied that suits the context.

The second: the conjunction links to what came before, and in this case the hamzah is moved forward from its original position, which is after the conjunction. We have said that this is easier for the one analysing the grammar (mu'rib), because it does not require the strain of supplying an implied element, and sometimes it is difficult for a person to supply a suitable element.

As for His saying ﴿lammā﴾ (lamma): this (lamma) here is conditional (shartiyyah). The evidence that it is conditional is that it governs a conditional verb and its response: the conditional verb is in His saying ﴿when a calamity struck you﴾, and its response is ﴿you said, "How is this?"﴾.

Lamma comes in several senses: it comes meaning (illa, "except"), it comes meaning (hina, "when"), it comes meaning (lam, "not"), and it comes as a conditional. In the saying of Allah the Exalted ﴿There is no soul but that over it is a guardian﴾ [al-Tariq 4], it is in the sense of (illa), meaning "there is no soul except that over it is a guardian." In the saying of Allah the Exalted ﴿Nay, they have not yet tasted My punishment﴾ [Sad 8], this lamma is in the sense of (lam), negating; although there are differences between them, it is negating in the sense of (lam). In the saying of Allah the Exalted ﴿Except the people of Yunus; when they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace﴾ [Yunus 98], some scholars said that lamma here means (hina, "when"). These are four senses of lamma as it occurs in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

As for His saying ﴿a calamity struck you, although you had inflicted twice as much﴾: ﴿struck you﴾ means "befell you," ﴿a calamity, although you had inflicted twice as much﴾ means "there befell you the like of its double." And what is this calamity? This calamity is what befell them at Uhud, for seventy men of them were killed, at their head the Lion of Allah and the Lion of His Messenger, Hamzah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, may Allah be pleased with him, the uncle of the Prophet ﷺ.

As for His saying ﴿you had inflicted twice as much﴾, this refers, may He be glorified and exalted, to what occurred on the day of Badr. On the day of Badr, seventy men of the polytheists were killed and seventy were taken captive. So seventy with seventy is two times seventy, and for this reason ﴿you had inflicted twice as much﴾.

If someone says: How did He say ﴿you had inflicted twice as much﴾ when the killed were seventy and the captured were seventy, and capture is not killing?

We say: capture produces the same humiliation as killing, and perhaps more, perhaps more; because the one who is killed is killed and finds rest, but the captive is humiliated. For this reason the ruler is given a choice regarding captives among several matters: between killing them, between enslaving them, between ransoming them with wealth or with a prisoner, and between releasing them. Four matters; the ruler chooses regarding the captives among these four matters. What are they?

* The students: Ransom with wealth.

* The Shaykh: Ransom with wealth, or exchange for a captive Muslim.

* A student: Enslavement.

* The Shaykh: Enslavement.

* The students: Killing.

* The Shaykh: Killing.

* The students: (...).

* The Shaykh: Release without anything in return, ﴿until, when you have subdued them, then tighten the bonds﴾, meaning captivity, ﴿and then either release them as a favour or take ransom until the war lays down its burdens﴾ [Muhammad 4]. So the summary is that captivity involves humiliation like killing; if it is not equal to it, it is worse than it and does not fall short of it.

﴿You had inflicted twice as much, you said﴾: this is the response of ﴿lamma﴾, meaning: when a calamity struck you, ﴿you said, "How is this?"﴾, meaning: how were we struck when we are the soldiers of Allah and with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? How can defeat reach us? Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿How is this?﴾ Here (anna) is interrogative, and it may also be conditional. In your saying "Anna taqum aqum" ("wherever you stand, I will stand"), it is conditional; but in a verse like this it is interrogative, meaning: how can this be? ﴿How is this?﴾ This interrogation is for amazement, and I do not think it is for denial, because the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, do not deny anything of Allah's decree; rather they were amazed: how does this befall us when we are the army of Allah and with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?!

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say﴾, meaning: say to them, O Muhammad: ﴿It is from yourselves﴾. Here Allah commanded His Prophet to say this. He did not say, Mighty and Majestic: "Why, when a calamity struck you... you said, how is this? It is from yourselves," but rather He commanded His Prophet to convey it to them. This command is for specific conveyance. We have said that the entire Qur'an is something the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was commanded to say to all of the people; this is one matter. Some things, rulings or reports exist for which the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, is commanded to convey them specifically. Here He said: ﴿Say﴾, meaning: say to those who say ﴿How is this?﴾: ﴿It﴾, that is, what struck you, ﴿is from yourselves﴾, that is, from you. The ﴿min﴾ here indicates cause (sababiyyah), meaning: by your causing it; you are the cause. And what is the cause that is apparent to us? It is the dispute and disobedience to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, in that he commanded them to remain in the place he had designated for them, whether victory went to the Muslims or to the disbelievers. But they, may Allah be pleased with them and pardon them, when they saw the polytheists had fled and the Muslims began gathering the spoils, thought the matter was over, so they came down from the place the Prophet ﷺ had designated for them, and what happened, happened. What happened was that the cavalry of the polytheists, seeing the gap undefended, that is behind the Muslims who had been protecting them from behind, charged from behind the Muslims and mixed with them, and what Allah the Mighty and Majestic willed came to pass. This is the meaning of His saying ﴿It is from yourselves﴾.

Then He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is over all things competent﴾. Ending the verse with this sentence is most fitting: He is capable of granting victory over these polytheists, but He did not do so for a wisdom, as He said: ﴿And if Allah had willed, He would have taken vengeance upon them, but [He tested] some of you by means of others﴾ [Muhammad 4]; because if Allah had willed, He would have caused them to die, or sunk them into the earth, or sent down thunderbolts upon them, or the like. ﴿But [He tested] some of you by means of others. And those who were killed in the cause of Allah - never will He allow their deeds to be lost. He will guide them and amend their condition. And He will admit them to Paradise, which He has made known to them﴾ [Muhammad 4-6].

As for His saying ﴿Indeed, Allah is over all things﴾: ﴿all things﴾ is general, encompassing everything. What exists, He is capable of annihilating; what does not exist, He is capable of bringing into being. There is no exception in this generality, no exception in this generality.

As for the words of the commentator, may Allah have mercy on him, in Surat al-Ma'idah: ﴿And He is competent over all things﴾ [al-Ma'idah 120], he said: "The intellect restricts His essence, so He is not competent over them." This is a restriction in the wrong place. First: the intellect has no role in the attributes of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Second: we ask: what do you mean by your saying "the intellect restricts His essence"? Do you mean that Allah, may He be glorified and exalted, cannot act, cannot descend, cannot settle upon the Throne, cannot come to judge between His servants? If you mean this, it is an error: Allah is capable of acting, of settling on the Throne, of descending to the lowest heaven, of coming to judge between His servants, as established by transmitted proof. Or do you mean by your saying "restricts His essence" that He cannot do to Himself what is unbefitting of Him, such as dying, for example? If you mean that, it is also an error on your part; because capability relates only to possibilities, while impossibilities are impossible and do not occur. Can we say that a thing is both moving and still? It is not possible. Capability does not relate to this at all. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, cannot be described with imperfection: ﴿And to Allah belongs the highest description﴾. So your supposing that Allah may be described with imperfection but is incapable of it is a grave error. We say: this does not arise with respect to capability at all, as the poet al-Saffarini, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

By a power related to the possible ***.................

So an impossible thing is impossible, and capability does not relate to it at all; because if a thing is still, it cannot be moving, and if it is moving, it cannot be still. Allah is capable of all things; but if He is capable of making it moving, it ceases to be still, and if He is capable of making it still, it ceases to be moving. This does not arise for the intellect at all, does not arise for the intellect. So we say: ﴿over all things competent﴾ in general and absolute terms, without any exception.

* A student: (...) what is with Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

* The Shaykh: Regarding what relates to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

* The student: It is necessary (...) the she-camel of Salih; if he were intelligent he would not become (...).

* The Shaykh: In any case, the matter of Salih's she-camel, that the mountain brought it forth,[[Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim in his Tafsir, no. (10986) (6/2049), and al-Tabari in his Tafsir (10/287), from the report of Ya'qub ibn 'Utbah ibn al-Mughirah ibn al-Akhnas.]] is an Israelite report which may be authentic and may be unauthentic. But there is something, I mean, more eloquent than this: the staff of Musa, peace be upon him, a known staff of a known tree; he throws it on the ground and it becomes a serpent, and he picks it up and it becomes a staff again.

* A student: Is it correct to say (...).

* * *

* The Shaykh: All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and companions and those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgement. As for what follows (...)

* A student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful: ﴿Why is it that when a calamity struck you, although you had inflicted twice as much (on the enemy), you said, "How is this?" Say, "It is from yourselves." Indeed, Allah is over all things competent. (165) And what befell you on the day the two armies met was by permission of Allah, that He might make evident the believers (166), and that He might make evident those who were hypocrites. It was said to them, "Come, fight in the way of Allah or [at least] defend." They said, "If we knew there would be fighting, we would follow you." They were nearer to disbelief that day than to faith, saying with their mouths what was not in their hearts. And Allah is most knowing of what they conceal (167). They are the ones who said of their brothers while they sat [at home], "If they had obeyed us, they would not have been killed." Say, "Then avert from yourselves death, if you should be truthful"﴾ [Al 'Imran 165-168].

* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Why is it that when a calamity struck you, although you had inflicted twice as much, you said, "How is this?"﴾. This (lamma)?

* A student: Conditional.

* The Shaykh: Conditional. And the sign of that?

* The student: It contains a conditional verb and its response.

* The Shaykh: Yes, the sentence contains a conditional verb and its response. Where is the response?

* The student: The response is ﴿you said, "How is this?"﴾.

* The Shaykh: Yes. What is meant by the interrogative ﴿How is this?﴾?

* A student: ﴿How?﴾

* The Shaykh: Yes, what is meant by the interrogative?

* The student: Meaning "why?"

* The Shaykh: What is meant by it?

* The student: "How," I mean?

* The Shaykh: Glory be to Allah! What is meant by it?

* The student: Amazement.

* The Shaykh: Amazement or denial?

* The student: Amazement.

* The Shaykh: Amazement. Why could it not be denial?

* The student: Because this is from the decree of Allah, Glorified and Exalted.

* The Shaykh: Because it is from the decree of Allah, and the Companions could not deny the decree of Allah.

What is the meaning of His saying ﴿It is from yourselves﴾?

* A student: ﴿It is from yourselves﴾ means: from your action on the day when (...) the Messenger of Allah (...), when the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, commanded them to remain above it...

* The Shaykh: The mountain.

* The student: No, when they disobeyed his command, what happened (...) happened.

* The Shaykh: That is: ﴿It is from yourselves﴾ means you were the cause, by your disobedience to the command of the Prophet ﷺ. Good. How do we reconcile this verse with His saying: ﴿Say, "All is from Allah"﴾ [An-Nisa 78]?

* A student: That is, what was decreed is from Allah, Glorified and Exalted, but the occurrence of the cause is from themselves.

* The Shaykh: That is the reconciliation: it is attributed to them with regard to the cause, and attributed to Allah with regard to the decree and predestination. His saying ﴿Indeed, Allah is over all things competent﴾: is this generality on its absolute footing?

* A student: Yes.

* The Shaykh: On its absolute footing.

* A student: Some of them (...) said: (...) indicates the essence (...).

* The Shaykh: It indicates that He is not capable over His essence. And what is the answer to his saying?

* The student: The answer: first, the intellect has no role; it is not among His attributes.

* The Shaykh: Yes.

* The student: (...) we ask them, what do you mean by the saying of (...) if he intended to link (...) what the intellect does not suit (...) on any matter (...) made this error (...) transmitted from him, makes it from him, on things a saying of deficiency (...) things and others, so it would be an error because this would be (...) possible (...).

* The Shaykh: Capability relates to the possible, and it cannot either exist or not exist; so then it needs to...?

* A student: (...).

* The Shaykh: In any case it is an error; because if they meant by his saying "restricts His essence" the attributes of imperfection, these are impossible matters and capability does not relate to them; and if they meant by it voluntary acts, that He cannot descend, nor settle, nor speak, this is an error.

Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿Why is it that when a calamity struck you, although you had inflicted twice as much...﴾ to the end. * The following is derived from this noble verse:

That Allah rebuked those who said: ﴿How is this?﴾

* And it follows from this: the permissibility of rebuking one whose faith is complete if he does what deserves rebuke; that is, we do not say that the completeness of his faith prevents us from rebuking him when he does what calls for rebuke.

* Among the benefits of this verse: it is recommended that a person be reminded of what makes a calamity easier for him; by His saying ﴿you had inflicted twice as much﴾.

* Also among the benefits of the verse: whoever answers another should answer with what prevents his argument; by His saying ﴿Say, "It is from yourselves"﴾, meaning: you are the cause.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of causes; by His saying ﴿Say, "It is from yourselves"﴾.

* Among its benefits: Allah's favour upon the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them; because Allah made through their hands a calamity greater than what had befallen them, indeed twice what had befallen them; by His saying ﴿you had inflicted twice as much﴾.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of the name Al-Qadir (the All-Capable) among Allah's names; by His saying ﴿Indeed, Allah is over all things competent﴾. Capability is an attribute by which the one who possesses it is protected from being described with incapacity, and we have mentioned previously what it entails.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: when we describe Allah with capability, we should describe Him as He described Himself, so we say: Indeed, Allah is over all things competent, contrary to one who says: Indeed, Allah is competent over what He wills; for if he says: Indeed, Allah is competent over what He wills, the implication of the expression may be that what He does not will He is not capable of, whereas He is capable of what He wills and of what He does not will.
