But He made an exception, saying: ﴿but Allah chooses from His messengers whom He wills﴾. ﴿Yajtabī﴾ means He chooses from His messengers whom He wills, so He reveals to him the unseen that He wishes to reveal to him, as He said: ﴿He is the Knower of the unseen, and He does not reveal His unseen to anyone, except to a messenger whom He has approved﴾.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verses 178–179 (part 2 of 3):

﴿But Allah chooses from His messengers whom He wills.﴾ Now this segment of the verse depicts for us the condition of the Prophetic community in the time of the Prophet ﷺ: that among them were people whose affairs were hidden. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made clear that these people whose affairs are hidden must be separated by Allah from the believers through the signs which He manifests. This does not happen through your being given knowledge of the unseen, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does not make anyone acquainted with the unseen except whomever He has approved of from among the messengers. And by what means does this happen? By our being made aware of what is in the hearts of these people, through revelation. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ named a number of the hypocrites to Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, who was known as "the keeper of the secret" (ṣāḥib al-sirr), the secret of the Prophet ﷺ. Observe now: the Messenger ﷺ confided to Hudhayfah the names of men among the hypocrites, and did not confide to Abu Bakr, nor to 'Umar, nor to anyone who was better than Hudhayfah. This reminds us of a principle mentioned by Ibn al-Qayyim in his Nuniyyah which passed by us recently. What is it?
* Student: That excellence in a specific matter does not necessitate absolute excellence.
* The Shaykh: Yes, that being singled out for a specific virtue does not necessitate absolute superiority; and that excellence is of two kinds: absolute and restricted. So here there is no doubt that Hudhayfah, may Allah be pleased with him, was distinguished over the Companions by what the Prophet ﷺ informed him of concerning these hypocrites. But it does not follow from this that he is better than those who possess absolute excellence over him, such as Abu Bakr, 'Umar, and those like them. The point is that we do not know what is in the hearts of these people, but Allah distinguishes them by what He makes His Prophet ﷺ aware of. For this reason He said: ﴿But Allah chooses from His messengers whom He wills.﴾
And who is the one He chose from among the messengers in the era of Prophethood? Who? Muhammad ﷺ, and there is no prophet other than him.
Then He said: ﴿So believe in Allah and His messengers.﴾ That is, make your faith in Allah and His messengers true, by complete affirmation, submission, and yielding, without objection, neither to the decree and destiny nor to the legislated ruling. Believe in Allah and His Messenger. Thus is the state of the truly faithful one: he submits to Allah's cosmic command and is content with it, and submits to Allah's legislated command and carries it out and yields to it, although submission to the cosmic decree encompasses everyone, whether willingly or unwillingly. ﴿So believe in Allah and His messengers.﴾ "Messengers" is the plural of "rasūl." It is well known that the messengers are those whom Allah, Glorified and Exalted, charged with what was revealed to them, to act upon it, call to it, and convey it to the people. For this reason the basic position of the majority of scholars regarding the rasūl is: he is one to whom a law is revealed and who is commanded to convey it. And the nabī (prophet) is one to whom a law is revealed by which he worships, but who is not charged with conveying it to the people. Adam, peace be upon him, was a prophet but not a messenger; he had no one [to convey to]; he was informed and began acting in accordance with what was revealed to him, and his descendants followed him in that. When time elapsed and people differed, they needed a messenger, so Allah sent [messengers] to them, and the first whom He sent to them was Noah.
And His saying: ﴿Believe in Allah and His messengers.﴾ Faith in Allah comprises four matters: belief in His existence, belief in His lordship, belief in His divinity, and belief in His names and attributes. All of this is necessary; whoever lacks any of them has not truly believed in Allah. Belief in what? In His lordship, His divinity, His names, and His attributes.
Belief in the messengers comprises affirming them in what they brought of revelation, and worshipping Allah by the law of those upon whom it was obligatory to follow them. And it is well known that after the sending of the Messenger ﷺ, creation was obligated only to follow the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, for his law abrogated all religions. So how do we believe in Jesus, for example? We believe that he is truly a messenger of Allah, that Allah sent the Scripture down to him, and that he was truthful in what he brought of the message. As for his law, we are not commanded to follow it; we are commanded only to believe in him.
He said: ﴿And if you believe and fear Allah, you will have a great reward.﴾ That is, if you believe with your hearts and fear Allah with your limbs, you will have a great reward.
Belief of the heart is the affirmation that includes acceptance and submission; this is belief of the heart. Taqwā is taking a shield against the punishment of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, by carrying out His commands and avoiding His prohibitions; this is the most comprehensive of what has been said about taqwā. But it should be known that taqwā may be paired with birr (righteousness), and may be paired with iḥsān (excellence): ﴿And if you do good and fear Allah﴾ [an-Nisā' 128], and may be paired with iṣlāḥ (reform). When it is paired with something like this, it is interpreted as meaning avoidance of the forbidden, that is, avoiding what Allah has forbidden. But when it is mentioned absolutely, it includes both commands and prohibitions. This is the case with many terms: when paired with another, they acquire one meaning, and when mentioned alone, they acquire another. But which of the two is more comprehensive and general: when paired or when mentioned alone? When mentioned alone; because when it is paired with something else, that which it is paired with will take a large portion of the meaning.
He said: ﴿And if you believe and fear Allah, you will have a great reward.﴾ The fā' here falls in the response of the condition, to link the response clause to the conditional verbal clause. It is attached with fā' because the response came as a nominal clause, and we have recited to you a line of verse on this topic. Who will memorize it?
* Student: 
Nominal, imperative,
and with the rigid, and with mā, qad, lan, and with tanfīs.
* The Shaykh: Its meaning is that these seven clauses, when they come as the response to a condition, must be joined by fā'.
And His saying: ﴿reward﴾ means a recompense; and Allah called the reward "ajr" out of generosity and grace, as if we were hired workers who performed the work and so demand—what? The wage—although the right is owed to Allah from us. But He, Mighty and Majestic, obligated Himself: ﴿Whoever among you does evil in ignorance, then repents after that and reforms, indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-An'ām 54].
So we say: "ajr" here means what? Recompense. Allah called it ajr as an act of grace from Him, as if we were laborers who did the work and so demand the wage. This is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Who is it that will lend Allah a goodly loan so He may multiply it for him?﴾ [al-Baqarah 245]. Is Allah poor, that we should lend to Him? No, but this is a matter of showing Allah's commitment to fulfilling for His servant when he fulfills his covenant: ﴿And fulfill My covenant; I will fulfill your covenant﴾ [al-Baqarah 40].
And His saying: ﴿great﴾ is a description by Allah, Mighty and Majestic, of this reward, and the description with greatness from "the Great" indicates its magnitude. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ said in the hadith, the hadith of the supplication which he taught Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, he said: "So forgive me a forgiveness from You"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhārī (834), and Muslim (2705/48), from the hadith of Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him.]], attributing it to the "from You" of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Allah would not leave the believers in the state you are in﴾, to the end.
* From this noble verse a number of benefits are derived. Among them: that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, must distinguish the wicked from the good; due to His saying: ﴿Allah would not leave the believers in the state you are in﴾.
If someone asks: By what is the distinction achieved? We say: it is achieved by revelation in the era of Prophethood, and it is achieved by indicators in other than the era of Prophethood, and also in the era of Prophethood, for indicators may show the wicked from the good, so that we observe their deeds and look at how they conduct themselves and how they act, and their wickedness from their goodness becomes clear to us.
* Among the benefits of this verse: the demonstration of Allah's mercy toward His servants, in that He does not leave them thus, with some confused with others, but there must be a distinguishing of this from that.
* Among its benefits: the demonstration of wisdom, the wisdom of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in His acts and legislation as well; due to His saying: ﴿Allah would not leave the believers in the state you are in until He distinguishes the wicked from the good.﴾
Among its benefits: the division of people into wicked and good; due to His saying: ﴿until He distinguishes the wicked from the good﴾, and this is like His saying: ﴿He it is who created you, so among you is a disbeliever and among you is a believer﴾ [at-Taghābun 2], and He mentioned no third category. And He, Exalted, said in Surah Hud: ﴿So among them is wretched and fortunate﴾ [Hūd 105], and He mentioned no third category. So in deeds Allah divided people into two categories, and in recompense also He divided them into two.
If someone says: Is there not in this evidence for the position of the Khawārij, who say that people are either believer or disbeliever, and that it is impossible for anyone to combine faith and disbelief?
The answer is: there is no evidence in it for their position; because a believer who does not do what takes him out of faith, the description "wicked" does not apply to him absolutely; rather he is of which category? The good; but there is wickedness in him. He is of the category of the good, but there is wickedness in him, and this goodness has overcome his wickedness. Likewise the disbeliever: even if he does what is praiseworthy, such as righteousness, generosity, courage, cheerfulness of face, and the like—these are qualities of faith—but his wickedness is greater than these qualities, so he is of the category of the wicked and not of the category of the good. So we say: those believers who have attributes of disbelief, from which of the two categories are they?
* The students: The good, O Shaykh... the good.
* The Shaykh: Of the category of the good that has wickedness in it, but their goodness overcomes their wickedness; and the disbelievers who have qualities of goodness are of the category of the wicked, but the goodness in them has been submerged in the side of wickedness. On this basis there is no third division; rather they are two categories, but whichever of the two descriptions predominates, they are of that group.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: whoever claims knowledge of the unseen is a liar. From where do you derive it?
* Student: ﴿And Allah would not disclose the unseen to you﴾.
* The Shaykh: ﴿And Allah would not disclose the unseen to you﴾. So whoever claims knowledge of the unseen is a liar, indeed he is a disbeliever; due to His saying: ﴿Say: None in the heavens and the earth knows the unseen except Allah﴾ [an-Naml 65], and because whoever claims knowledge of the unseen has denied the content of His saying: ﴿And Allah would not disclose the unseen to you﴾.
But what is meant by the unseen? What is meant by the unseen is what is absolutely hidden, namely what will occur in the future. As for a present thing that is hidden from some people but not others, a person may come to know of it even without witnessing it, through news from the jinn; the jinn roam the earth, going north and south, and they are swift in their movements, so they may travel through the earth, then inform their allies of what they witnessed in distant lands, and this would be unseen—is it real unseen or relative unseen?
* Student: Relative.
* The Shaykh: Relative. And by relative we mean: relative to some people and not others. Those who witnessed it, it is not unseen to them, and those far from it, it is unseen. Now, what is in the street next to the mosque, while we are here, is unseen to us relative to us, which we do not perceive; but if a man entered upon us and said: "I saw such and such in the street," we would say: "We do not know the unseen, but we were informed of an event that its witness informed us of." So the unseen that none knows but Allah is the absolute unseen, which is what will occur in the future; this none perceives except Allah.
If someone says: When we see the sky darkened, the thunder crashing and the lightning flashing, do we not expect rain? Indeed. But when we say, "It will rain," this is not from the knowledge of the unseen; rather it is based on indicators, and our assumption may be mistaken, and Allah may command that cloud so that it disperses and does not rain. But this is according to what? According to what we expect; and we do not say it is knowledge, rather it is assumption based on indicators. The point, lest the matter be confused for you: the unseen is the absolute unseen, which is what will occur in the future; as for the relative unseen, Allah may make it known to whomever of His servants He wills through an intermediary, such as the jinn for example; the jinn know what has happened on earth and inform their allies of it. But who are the allies of the jinn? The allies of the jinn may be righteous and may be criminals. If the jinn's allegiance to them is due to shirk in them, such as sacrifices to the jinn and the like, this is an allegiance of criminality. But Shaykh al-Islam, may Allah have mercy on him, says: the jinn may take as allies a believer because of his faith; they love him for Allah's sake and serve him in his affairs. He said: this is permissible on two conditions: that the means of employing them is not forbidden, and that he does not employ them in something forbidden. Note well: that the means of employing them is not forbidden, and that he does not employ them in what is forbidden. For example, if they say: "We will not serve you until you prostrate to us"?
* Students: That is forbidden, O Shaykh.
* The Shaykh: That is forbidden, it is shirk. "We will not serve you until you have someone imprisoned?" That is forbidden, but it is not shirk; that is, they served him without shirk, without prohibition. But if he employs them in something forbidden, saying to them, for example: "Go to so-and-so and frighten his camels until he flees and runs away." Is that forbidden?
* Students: Employing something forbidden.
* The Shaykh: Yes. "Go to so-and-so and harm him, terrify him in his house, terrify him in his market"; this too is forbidden and not permissible. So if someone said: their employment is forbidden in every case, because Allah, Exalted, says: ﴿And on the day He will gather them all: "O assembly of jinn, you have taken much from mankind." And their allies from mankind will say: "Our Lord, some of us have enjoyed others, and we have reached our term which You appointed for us." He will say: "The Fire is your abode, wherein you will abide eternally, except as Allah wills. Indeed your Lord is Wise and Knowing"﴾ [al-An'ām 128], and this indicates that the enjoyment of a human from a jinn is forbidden in every case.
The answer to that: read the verse that follows, where He says: ﴿And thus We make some of the wrongdoers allies of others for what they used to earn﴾ [al-An'ām 129]. This enjoyment is enjoyment in wrongdoing, and there is no doubt it is forbidden. But if it is an enjoyment of what is beneficial and free of what is forbidden in its means or its employment, then there is no harm in it.
* Student: O Shaykh, what is meant by al-asbāṭ (...), the sons of Jacob?
* The Shaykh: What?
* The Student: al-Asbāṭ.
* The Shaykh: Where are the asbāṭ?
* The Student: The day we spoke about the prophet and the messenger, O Shaykh, you defined the prophet and the messenger; are they prophets or messengers?
* The Shaykh: Some said: al-asbāṭ means the tribes of the Children of Israel, and the asbāṭ, meaning and the prophets are from the asbāṭ; and some say: they are the sons of Jacob.
* The Student: And the correct view?
* The Shaykh: There is disagreement about it.
* * *
* Student: ﴿And let not those who withhold what Allah has given them of His bounty think that it is good for them; rather it is bad for them. They will have hung around their necks that about which they were stingy on the Day of Resurrection. And to Allah belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is Acquainted with what you do. (180) Certainly Allah has heard the statement of those who say, "Indeed, Allah is poor, and we are rich." We will record what they have said and their killing of the prophets without right, and We will say, "Taste the punishment of the Burning. (181) That is for what your hands have put forward, and [because] indeed, Allah is not ever unjust to the servants."﴾ [Āl ʿImrān 180–182].
* The Shaykh: ﴿Allah would not leave the believers in the state you are in until He distinguishes the wicked from the good.﴾ What do the grammarians call this lām?
* Student: Lām al-juḥūd.
* The Shaykh: Lām al-juḥūd. And what is al-juḥūd?
* Student: It is the attempt (...).
* The Shaykh: No.
* Student: It is the opposition (...).
* The Shaykh: What?
* Student: The opposition.
* The Shaykh: No.
* Student: In the sense of negation.
* The Shaykh: Negation. Al-juḥūd here means negation. And its rule?
* Student: That it comes after a negated kawn (state of being).
* The Shaykh: That it comes after a negated kawn; correct. And what is its meaning when you say: "mā kāna li-kadhā" (it was not for so-and-so to do such-and-such)? "mā kāna Allāhu li-kadhā"?
* Student: That it is impossible, in the strongest sense, that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does this thing.
* The Shaykh: Its meaning is that it is impossible in the utmost degree of impossibility that Allah does this thing.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verses 178–179 (part 3 of 3):

His saying: ﴿So that Allah may leave the believers﴾. What is the meaning of ﴿leave﴾? That is, to leave the believers in the state you are in. What is the meaning of leaving them in the state you are in? He says: "Until when?"

* Student: He leaves them in confusion between the hypocrite and the sincere believer.

* Shaykh: In confusion between the hypocrite and the sincere believer, until He distinguishes the evil from the good.

His saying: ﴿And Allah would not disclose to you the unseen﴾. What is the connection of this to what comes before it?

* Student: Istidrak (a correction or contrast introducing a new point).

* Shaykh: Istidrak. What is the meaning?

* Student: The meaning is that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, would not inform you of the unseen, so that you would know what is in people's hearts, whether hypocrite or sincere believer.

* Shaykh: Yes, indeed. That is, to disclose to you what is in their hearts of hypocrisy or otherwise. So there is no istidrak here, there is no istidrak.

* Student: Istidrak here...

* Shaykh: ﴿Allah would not leave the believers in the state you are in﴾.

* Student: ﴿So that He may leave...﴾ (...).

* Shaykh: No, I mean: ﴿And Allah would not disclose to you the unseen﴾.

* Student: There is an istidrak in that these matters are known to Allah alone.

* Shaykh: No.

* Student: Ta'lil (a causal clause explaining the reason).

* Shaykh: Ta'lil. That is: Allah would not disclose the unseen to you, so that He would inform you of what distinguishes this from that.

His saying: ﴿But Allah chooses of His messengers whom He wills﴾?

* Student: This is an exception.

* Shaykh: Or an istidrak. "Lakin" (but) is used for istidrak. Good. What is the meaning?

* Student: The meaning: But Allah chooses from among His messengers whom He wills to inform, and Allah knows best.

* Shaykh: So He discloses the unseen to you through an intermediary?

* Student: The messengers.

* Shaykh: The messengers. The summary is that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made clear in this verse that He has not left the Muslim community in bewilderment and doubt. Rather, He must distinguish, that is, separate the evil from the good by mentioning the attributes that apply to this and that. This does not happen by disclosing to each one of you the unseen, but through the messengers.

His saying: ﴿And if you believe and fear Allah, then for you is a great reward﴾. Allah often pairs faith (iman) with piety (taqwa). So how do we interpret faith when it is paired with piety?

* Student: When faith is paired with piety, how is it explained? Faith is an action of the heart, and piety is intended as an action of the limbs?

* Shaykh: An action of the limbs. So faith is of the heart and piety is of the limbs.

* From the benefits of this verse: Allah may disclose the unseen to creation through the messengers, as in His saying: ﴿But Allah chooses of His messengers whom He wills﴾.

* From its benefits: the messengers are among those whom Allah chose and selected above creation. This is found in the Qur'an, where the prophets are the elite, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And indeed they are with Us among the chosen and the excellent﴾ [Sad 47].

* From its benefits: affirmation of Allah's will in His saying: ﴿whom He wills﴾. But we say: everything that Allah attached to His will must be accompanied by wisdom. It is not a bare will; it must be joined with wisdom. The proof of this is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And you do not will except that Allah wills. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾ [al-Insan 30]. Then He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾, indicating that His will follows His knowledge and wisdom.

* From its benefits, from the benefits of this verse: the obligation of believing in Allah and His messengers in general, as in His saying: ﴿So believe in Allah and His messengers﴾. We have explained in the tafsir how to believe in the messengers: one believes that they are true, that they came from Allah, and that they are truthful. As for following them, that is specific to the Prophet ﷺ.

* From the benefits of this verse: the virtue of faith and piety, and that a great reward follows from them.

* Also from the benefits of this verse: the demonstration of Allah's favor upon His servants, in that He made their reward for action like a wage that is due to them. As if a person hired workers and gave them their wages as an obligation. But who imposed that upon Him? The one who imposed it is Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

* Also from the benefits of this verse: affirmation of recompense, and that it is of the same kind as the deed. Just as faith and piety are a great matter, outward and inward, so the reward is a great reward.

**Student:** I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿Allah would not leave the believers in the state you are in until He separates the wicked from the good. Nor would Allah reveal the unseen to you, but Allah chooses from His messengers whom He wills. So believe in Allah and His messengers. If you believe and are mindful of Allah, you will have a great reward. (179) Let not those who are stingy with what Allah has given them of His bounty think that it is good for them. Rather, it is bad for them. What they withheld will be placed around their necks on the Day of Resurrection. To Allah belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is well aware of what you do. (180) Allah has certainly heard the words of those who said, "Allah is poor and we are rich." We will record what they said and their killing of the prophets without right, and We will say, "Taste the punishment of the burning." (181) That is for what your hands have sent ahead, and because Allah is not unjust to the servants. (182)﴾ [Al 'Imran 179–182].

* **Shaykh:** I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. The Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿And let not those who disbelieve think...﴾

The Exalted said: ﴿And let not those who hasten into disbelief grieve you. Indeed, they will not harm Allah at all﴾, up to the end of the verse. To whom is the address in this verse?

* **Student:** To the Prophet (ﷺ).

* **Shaykh:** To the Prophet (ﷺ). And is it not valid to address whoever can be addressed?

* **Student:** No.

* **Shaykh:** No, it is valid. What does this prohibition convey?

* **Student:** It shows the Prophet's (ﷺ) grief, sorrow and regret over the unbelievers not having faith.

* **Shaykh:** Well done. That is, it conveys the Prophet's grief, peace and blessings be upon him, over these unbelievers not embracing Islam, and over their hastening into disbelief.

The phrase ﴿who hasten into disbelief﴾: why is ﴿yusari'un﴾ followed by (fi, "in") when it is known that it takes (ila, "to")? It is known that sara' takes ila, as in ﴿And hasten to forgiveness﴾. Why is it construed here with fi?

* **Student:** Perhaps, Shaykh, it means that when they reach disbelief they hasten in it, so they increase in it while being unbelievers.

* **Shaykh:** Yes, but how do we explain that it is construed with fi when it is construed with ila?

* **Student:** It is not possible... The intended meaning is that when they reach disbelief they hasten in it, so they increase in it, and they are ﴿hastening into disbelief﴾, meaning they are unbelievers who increase in disbelief.

* **Shaykh:** That is not clear. It seems you mean a meaning, but you have not reached the expression of it.

* **Student:** It was mentioned to us in the lesson that fi means ila.

* **Shaykh:** Fi means ila. Well done, that is one aspect. The second?

* **Student:** The meaning of yusari'un is "they fall into."

* **Another student:** Shaykh, the cause of the hastening is entering into disbelief.

* **Shaykh:** Yes. So the implicit meaning (tadmin, one word carrying the sense of another) here is in the verb, not the particle. On the first meaning, the tadmin is in the particle, which carries the sense of ila. On the second, the tadmin is in the verb. Which is more eloquent?

* **Student:** The one in the verb is more eloquent.

* **Shaykh:** More eloquent.

* **Student:** Because it contains the meaning plus an addition...

* **Shaykh:** It contains the meaning plus an addition. Can you give another example besides this one that clarifies the matter?

* **Student:** His saying: ﴿a spring from which the servants of Allah drink﴾.

* **Shaykh:** Yes, ﴿a spring from which the servants of Allah drink﴾. Yashrabu ("drink") in its original usage takes what particle?

* **Student:** Min ("from")?

* **Shaykh:** Min. Here it is construed with the ba'. Construe it on both aspects?

* **Student:** "A spring from which one drinks."

* **Shaykh:** That is one aspect; that is, the ba' carries the sense of min.

* **Student:** The second: the tadmin is in the verb. It is a spring from which one drinks and is satisfied.

* **Shaykh:** From it.

* **Student:** A spring.

* **Shaykh:** A spring from which one drinks.

* **Student:** One drinks and is satisfied by it.

* **Shaykh:** A spring, yes, from which one is satisfied. When we say "is satisfied by it," the sense of drinking is included, because there is no satisfaction except after drinking. Clear?

* **Student:** It does not need (...).

* **Shaykh:** It does not need (...). How do we reconcile His saying ﴿Indeed, they will not harm Allah at all﴾ with His saying ﴿Indeed, those who harass Allah and His Messenger﴾?

* **Student:** Harm does not necessarily entail harassment, and harassment does not necessarily entail harm.

* **Shaykh:** Harassment does not necessarily entail harm. A person may be harassed by something without being harmed by it. Such as?

* **Student:** Like those who mock the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him.

* **Shaykh:** No, no, we do not want an example concerning Allah and His Messenger. A common, ordinary one?

* **Student:** A person may speak about another and it does not harm him; it harasses him but does not harm him.

* **Shaykh:** It harasses him with his words but does not harm him. Good. This is moral. What about a sensory one? A man who ate garlic sat beside you.

* **Student:** I may be bothered by the smell.

* **Shaykh:** No, "may"?!

* **Student:** I am bothered by the smell, but nothing harms me.

* **Shaykh:** But does not harm, correct. So now we have two examples. A moral one: a person speaks about me and harasses me with his words, but does not harm me. A sensory one: he sits beside me while eating garlic, and I am bothered by it, but I am not harmed. Therefore harassment does not necessitate harm, and thus there is no contradiction between this verse and His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who harass Allah and His Messenger﴾. What is the meaning of ﴿that He will not give them a share in the Hereafter﴾?

* **Student:** A portion.

* **Shaykh:** A portion. The word ﴿hazz﴾ here, is it general or specific?

* **Student:** General.

* **Shaykh:** General. By what means is it general here?

* **Student:** Its manner, you mean, from one aspect...

* **Shaykh:** Generality has its positions, that is, its methods. So what is the method of generality here? That is, what construction gives us the generality?

* **Student:** That is, a generality intended as specific.

* **Shaykh:** No, brother.

* **Student:** Because it is an indefinite noun that came in a negative context.

* **Shaykh:** Because it is an indefinite noun that came in a negative context. And the rule? Do you not know it?

* **Student:** I know it, but I did not understand the question.

* **Shaykh:** Yes, you did not understand the question, that is, by what means did the generality occur? The method is clearly that it is an indefinite noun that came in a negative context. What is the meaning of His saying ﴿They have bought disbelief in exchange for faith﴾?

* **Student:** They exchanged disbelief for faith.

* **Shaykh:** That is, they took disbelief as a substitute for faith. The scholars of rhetoric (balaghah) say that in this sentence there is a figurative usage (majaz) by way of a explicit subordinate metaphor (isti'arah tasrihiyyah tab'iyyah) or an implicit metaphor (isti'arah makniyyah). Do you know that?

* **Student:** You mean in His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who bought disbelief in exchange for faith﴾?

* **Shaykh:** Yes. He says: may you make it a subordinate explicit metaphor or an implicit metaphor? Of course I have not taught you it; let us see who has some knowledge of...

* **Student:** (...) Should I make an effort?

* **Shaykh:** Make an effort. Either you will be wrong or you will be right.

* **Student:** Shaykh, may Allah be good to you, it appears from His saying that disbelief cannot be bought, yet Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Indeed, those who bought disbelief in exchange for faith﴾. So this is a metaphor; that is, it is as if He placed disbelief...

* **Shaykh:** He made a comparison.

* **Student:** He compared disbelief to a thing that is bought.

* **Shaykh:** To a commodity that is bought. Good. Then He borrowed?

* **Student:** He borrowed disbelief in place of faith.

* **Shaykh:** No. He omitted the comparand (mushabbah bih), and indicated it by one of its attributes. Clearly you have no knowledge of rhetoric!

* **Student:** It is an implicit metaphor, Shaykh, because...

* **Shaykh:** Yes. He compared disbelief to a commodity that is sold and bought, and omitted the thing compared to.

* **Student:** And He mentioned the thing being compared.

* **Shaykh:** Yes, but He indicated it by one of its attributes, which is buying. That is the case if it is implicit. If it is an explicit subordinate metaphor, what then?

* **Student:** The comparand is omitted, which is the disbeliever who bought.

* **Shaykh:** No. An explicit subordinate metaphor means that the metaphor is applied to a verb or to an active participle; that is, to a shared thing. Here, ishtaraw means "chose," so He compared choosing to buying, then derived from the word buying, ishtaraw, by way of explicit subordinate metaphor. Do you understand?

In His saying: ﴿Let not those who disbelieve think that Our giving them respite is good for themselves﴾ is there a grammatical difficulty?

* **Student:** That He made khayr nominative.

* **Shaykh:** That He made khayr nominative.

* **Student:** And here it is nominative because it is the predicate of inna.

* **Shaykh:** The predicate of inna. Where is its subject?

* **Student:** The relative pronoun ma.

* **Shaykh:** The relative pronoun ma. Is the writing in the Qur'an here following the rules known now? Does it not follow the rules?

* **Student:** That we separate anna from ma.

* **Shaykh:** That we separate anna from ma, because it is a relative pronoun. Here its writing looks like a restrictive particle. Yes, well done. What is the meaning of the orthography ﴿that We give them respite﴾? And what does numli lahum mean?

* **Student:** We lure them on.

* **Shaykh:** Amla lahu.

* **Student:** We give them time.

* **Shaykh:** We give them time; ﴿that We give them respite﴾ means We give them time. The lam in His saying ﴿so that they may increase in sin﴾: is it for causation (ta'lil) or for consequence (aqibah)?

* **Student:** For causation.

* **Shaykh:** Causation. That is, Allah gave them respite for the sake of increasing sin, so Allah, may He be exalted, has intended evil for them.

* **Student:** The lam is for causation: Allah, glory be to Him, gave them respite so that they would increase in sin; this is causation. Or it is for consequence, in the sense that they did not disbelieve in order to increase in sin, but rather disbelief was (...) a cause of increasing sin. That is, two aspects.

* **Shaykh:** That is, with respect to Allah's action, it is permissible to make it causation. With respect to their own action, what they are upon, it is necessarily for consequence, because they do not wish their lives to be prolonged in order to increase in sin. But Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, may love that for a wisdom that requires it...

So He omitted the comparand and indicated it by one of its attributes...

* **Student:** The noun contains an implicit metaphor, Shaykh.

* **Shaykh:** Yes. He compared disbelief to a commodity that is sold and bought, and omitted the comparand.

* **Student:** And He mentioned the comparand.

* **Shaykh:** Yes, but He indicated it by one of its attributes, which is buying. Now, is this on the basis that it is implicit, or on the basis that it is an explicit subordinate metaphor?

* **Student:** The omission of the comparand, which is the disbeliever who bought.

* **Shaykh:** No. An explicit subordinate metaphor means that the metaphor is applied to a verb or an active participle; that is, to a shared thing. Here ﴿ishtaraw﴾ means "chose," so He compared choosing to buying, then derived from the word buying, ﴿ishtaraw﴾, by way of explicit subordinate metaphor. Do you understand?

In His saying: ﴿Let not those who disbelieve think that Our giving them respite is good for themselves﴾ [Al 'Imran 178], is there a grammatical difficulty?

* **Student:** That He made ﴿khayr﴾ nominative.

* **Shaykh:** That He made ﴿khayr﴾ nominative.

* **Student:** And "ma" is a relative pronoun.

* **Shaykh:** Yes.

* **Student:** And here it is nominative because it is the predicate of "anna."

* **Shaykh:** The predicate of "anna." Where is its subject?

* **Student:** The relative pronoun "ma."

* **Shaykh:** The relative pronoun "ma." Is the writing in the Qur'an here following the rules known now?

* **Student:** It does not follow them.

* **Shaykh:** It does not follow the rules. The rule known now is that...

* **Student:** That we separate "anna" from "ma."

* **Shaykh:** That we separate "anna" from "ma," because it is a relative pronoun. Here its writing looks like a restrictive particle. Well done. What is the meaning of the orthography? ﴿That We give them respite﴾ [Al 'Imran 178]. What does ﴿We give them respite﴾ mean?

* **Student:** We give them time.

* **Shaykh:** Amla lahu: we give him time. ﴿That We give them respite﴾ means We give them time. The lam in His saying ﴿so that they may increase in sin﴾ [Al 'Imran 178], is it for causation or for consequence?

* **Student:** For causation, Shaykh.

* **Shaykh:** For causation. That is, Allah gave them time in order that their sin increase, so Allah, may He be exalted, has intended evil for them.

* **Student:** Here it is for causation: Allah, the Exalted, gave them respite so that they would increase in sin; this is causation. Or it is for consequence, though they did not disbelieve in order to increase in sin, but disbelief was a cause of increasing disbelief. That is, two aspects.

* **Shaykh:** With respect to Allah's action it is permissible to make it causation; with respect to their own action, what they are upon, it is necessarily for consequence, because they do not love that their lives be prolonged in order to increase in sin. But Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, may love that for a wisdom that requires it.

The Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿Allah would not leave the believers as they are until He separates the wicked from the good﴾ [Al 'Imran 179]. ﴿Mā kāna Allāh li-yadhara﴾: ﴿mā﴾ is a negation particle, and ﴿kāna﴾ is a defective past verb. The lam they call "lam al-juhud" (the lam of denial), that is, the lam of negation, which comes after a negative statement, either "mā kāna" or "lam yakun." Its example with "mā kāna" is this verse: ﴿Allah would not leave﴾, and its example with "lam yakun" is: ﴿Allah would not forgive them﴾ [An-Nisa' 137]. It is called lam al-juhud, and juhud means negation, because it occurs in a context of negation. Where is the negation? "Lam yakun" or "mā kāna." It puts the present verb in the subjunctive, either by itself, as is the view of the Kufan school, or by a necessarily implied "an," as is the view of the Basran school.

His saying ﴿Mā kāna Allāh﴾ means that this is impossible in the extreme; whenever such an expression comes in the Qur'an, it means impossibility, that it is impossible for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in the utmost degree, to do such and such. This impossibility is not an impossibility due to inability, for He is able, but it is a legislative impossibility; that is, it is impossible, according to what His wisdom requires, that He leave the believers in their state until He distinguishes the wicked from the good.

His saying ﴿li-yadhara﴾ means: to leave. His saying ﴿al-mu'minīn﴾ means those who believe in Allah, in their state without distinction between the wicked and the good; this is impossible for Allah.

His saying ﴿ʿalā mā antum ʿalayh﴾ means: without clarification. This is because the Prophetic community in the time of the Prophet (ﷺ) was a mixture of pure hypocrites, pure disbelievers, and hypocrites. As for the pure disbelievers, they are distinguished by their open declaration of disbelief and their clear statement of it, and their condition is not hidden from anyone. As for the pure believers, likewise, their matter is clear and evident. The confusion remains between the pure believer and the hypocrite, because hypocrites show faith and claim to be with them: ﴿When they meet those who believe, they say, "We believe"﴾ [Al-Baqarah 14]. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, needs to distinguish between the wicked and the good, and for this reason He said: ﴿in the state you are in﴾, that is, of obscurity and confusion.

﴿Until He distinguishes the wicked from the good﴾: ﴿yamīz﴾ means "separates." That is, He separates the wicked from the good by what He, the Mighty and Majestic, informs of. If the matter is so, He said: ﴿Nor would Allah reveal the unseen to you﴾; that is, Allah would not reveal the unseen to you in distinguishing the good from the wicked. You do not know what is in their hearts, that is, what is in the hearts of these wicked hypocrites, because you do not know the unseen, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, would not reveal the unseen to you. This verse is restricted by the verse of the Jinn: ﴿He is the Knower of the unseen, and He does not reveal His unseen to anyone, except to a messenger whom He has approved. Indeed, He sends before him and behind him guards﴾ [Al-Jinn 26–27]. I say: this verse is exactly like the verse of the Jinn, and for this reason He said: ﴿but Allah chooses from His messengers whom He wills﴾. This is an exception to His saying ﴿Nor would Allah reveal the unseen to you﴾, for this address is general, even to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. But He made an exception, saying: ﴿but Allah chooses from His messengers whom He wills﴾. ﴿Yajtabī﴾ means He chooses from His messengers whom He wills, so He reveals to him the unseen that He wishes to reveal to him, as He said: ﴿He is the Knower of the unseen, and He does not reveal His unseen to anyone, except to a messenger whom He has approved﴾.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verses 178–179 (part 2 of 3):

﴿But Allah chooses from His messengers whom He wills.﴾ Now this segment of the verse depicts for us the condition of the Prophetic community in the time of the Prophet ﷺ: that among them were people whose affairs were hidden. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made clear that these people whose affairs are hidden must be separated by Allah from the believers through the signs which He manifests. This does not happen through your being given knowledge of the unseen, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does not make anyone acquainted with the unseen except whomever He has approved of from among the messengers. And by what means does this happen? By our being made aware of what is in the hearts of these people, through revelation. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ named a number of the hypocrites to Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, who was known as "the keeper of the secret" (ṣāḥib al-sirr), the secret of the Prophet ﷺ. Observe now: the Messenger ﷺ confided to Hudhayfah the names of men among the hypocrites, and did not confide to Abu Bakr, nor to 'Umar, nor to anyone who was better than Hudhayfah. This reminds us of a principle mentioned by Ibn al-Qayyim in his Nuniyyah which passed by us recently. What is it?
* Student: That excellence in a specific matter does not necessitate absolute excellence.
* The Shaykh: Yes, that being singled out for a specific virtue does not necessitate absolute superiority; and that excellence is of two kinds: absolute and restricted. So here there is no doubt that Hudhayfah, may Allah be pleased with him, was distinguished over the Companions by what the Prophet ﷺ informed him of concerning these hypocrites. But it does not follow from this that he is better than those who possess absolute excellence over him, such as Abu Bakr, 'Umar, and those like them. The point is that we do not know what is in the hearts of these people, but Allah distinguishes them by what He makes His Prophet ﷺ aware of. For this reason He said: ﴿But Allah chooses from His messengers whom He wills.﴾
And who is the one He chose from among the messengers in the era of Prophethood? Who? Muhammad ﷺ, and there is no prophet other than him.
Then He said: ﴿So believe in Allah and His messengers.﴾ That is, make your faith in Allah and His messengers true, by complete affirmation, submission, and yielding, without objection, neither to the decree and destiny nor to the legislated ruling. Believe in Allah and His Messenger. Thus is the state of the truly faithful one: he submits to Allah's cosmic command and is content with it, and submits to Allah's legislated command and carries it out and yields to it, although submission to the cosmic decree encompasses everyone, whether willingly or unwillingly. ﴿So believe in Allah and His messengers.﴾ "Messengers" is the plural of "rasūl." It is well known that the messengers are those whom Allah, Glorified and Exalted, charged with what was revealed to them, to act upon it, call to it, and convey it to the people. For this reason the basic position of the majority of scholars regarding the rasūl is: he is one to whom a law is revealed and who is commanded to convey it. And the nabī (prophet) is one to whom a law is revealed by which he worships, but who is not charged with conveying it to the people. Adam, peace be upon him, was a prophet but not a messenger; he had no one [to convey to]; he was informed and began acting in accordance with what was revealed to him, and his descendants followed him in that. When time elapsed and people differed, they needed a messenger, so Allah sent [messengers] to them, and the first whom He sent to them was Noah.
And His saying: ﴿Believe in Allah and His messengers.﴾ Faith in Allah comprises four matters: belief in His existence, belief in His lordship, belief in His divinity, and belief in His names and attributes. All of this is necessary; whoever lacks any of them has not truly believed in Allah. Belief in what? In His lordship, His divinity, His names, and His attributes.
Belief in the messengers comprises affirming them in what they brought of revelation, and worshipping Allah by the law of those upon whom it was obligatory to follow them. And it is well known that after the sending of the Messenger ﷺ, creation was obligated only to follow the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, for his law abrogated all religions. So how do we believe in Jesus, for example? We believe that he is truly a messenger of Allah, that Allah sent the Scripture down to him, and that he was truthful in what he brought of the message. As for his law, we are not commanded to follow it; we are commanded only to believe in him.
He said: ﴿And if you believe and fear Allah, you will have a great reward.﴾ That is, if you believe with your hearts and fear Allah with your limbs, you will have a great reward.
Belief of the heart is the affirmation that includes acceptance and submission; this is belief of the heart. Taqwā is taking a shield against the punishment of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, by carrying out His commands and avoiding His prohibitions; this is the most comprehensive of what has been said about taqwā. But it should be known that taqwā may be paired with birr (righteousness), and may be paired with iḥsān (excellence): ﴿And if you do good and fear Allah﴾ [an-Nisā' 128], and may be paired with iṣlāḥ (reform). When it is paired with something like this, it is interpreted as meaning avoidance of the forbidden, that is, avoiding what Allah has forbidden. But when it is mentioned absolutely, it includes both commands and prohibitions. This is the case with many terms: when paired with another, they acquire one meaning, and when mentioned alone, they acquire another. But which of the two is more comprehensive and general: when paired or when mentioned alone? When mentioned alone; because when it is paired with something else, that which it is paired with will take a large portion of the meaning.
He said: ﴿And if you believe and fear Allah, you will have a great reward.﴾ The fā' here falls in the response of the condition, to link the response clause to the conditional verbal clause. It is attached with fā' because the response came as a nominal clause, and we have recited to you a line of verse on this topic. Who will memorize it?
* Student: 
Nominal, imperative,
and with the rigid, and with mā, qad, lan, and with tanfīs.
* The Shaykh: Its meaning is that these seven clauses, when they come as the response to a condition, must be joined by fā'.
And His saying: ﴿reward﴾ means a recompense; and Allah called the reward "ajr" out of generosity and grace, as if we were hired workers who performed the work and so demand—what? The wage—although the right is owed to Allah from us. But He, Mighty and Majestic, obligated Himself: ﴿Whoever among you does evil in ignorance, then repents after that and reforms, indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-An'ām 54].
So we say: "ajr" here means what? Recompense. Allah called it ajr as an act of grace from Him, as if we were laborers who did the work and so demand the wage. This is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Who is it that will lend Allah a goodly loan so He may multiply it for him?﴾ [al-Baqarah 245]. Is Allah poor, that we should lend to Him? No, but this is a matter of showing Allah's commitment to fulfilling for His servant when he fulfills his covenant: ﴿And fulfill My covenant; I will fulfill your covenant﴾ [al-Baqarah 40].
And His saying: ﴿great﴾ is a description by Allah, Mighty and Majestic, of this reward, and the description with greatness from "the Great" indicates its magnitude. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ said in the hadith, the hadith of the supplication which he taught Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, he said: "So forgive me a forgiveness from You"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhārī (834), and Muslim (2705/48), from the hadith of Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him.]], attributing it to the "from You" of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Allah would not leave the believers in the state you are in﴾, to the end.
* From this noble verse a number of benefits are derived. Among them: that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, must distinguish the wicked from the good; due to His saying: ﴿Allah would not leave the believers in the state you are in﴾.
If someone asks: By what is the distinction achieved? We say: it is achieved by revelation in the era of Prophethood, and it is achieved by indicators in other than the era of Prophethood, and also in the era of Prophethood, for indicators may show the wicked from the good, so that we observe their deeds and look at how they conduct themselves and how they act, and their wickedness from their goodness becomes clear to us.
* Among the benefits of this verse: the demonstration of Allah's mercy toward His servants, in that He does not leave them thus, with some confused with others, but there must be a distinguishing of this from that.
* Among its benefits: the demonstration of wisdom, the wisdom of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in His acts and legislation as well; due to His saying: ﴿Allah would not leave the believers in the state you are in until He distinguishes the wicked from the good.﴾
Among its benefits: the division of people into wicked and good; due to His saying: ﴿until He distinguishes the wicked from the good﴾, and this is like His saying: ﴿He it is who created you, so among you is a disbeliever and among you is a believer﴾ [at-Taghābun 2], and He mentioned no third category. And He, Exalted, said in Surah Hud: ﴿So among them is wretched and fortunate﴾ [Hūd 105], and He mentioned no third category. So in deeds Allah divided people into two categories, and in recompense also He divided them into two.
If someone says: Is there not in this evidence for the position of the Khawārij, who say that people are either believer or disbeliever, and that it is impossible for anyone to combine faith and disbelief?
The answer is: there is no evidence in it for their position; because a believer who does not do what takes him out of faith, the description "wicked" does not apply to him absolutely; rather he is of which category? The good; but there is wickedness in him. He is of the category of the good, but there is wickedness in him, and this goodness has overcome his wickedness. Likewise the disbeliever: even if he does what is praiseworthy, such as righteousness, generosity, courage, cheerfulness of face, and the like—these are qualities of faith—but his wickedness is greater than these qualities, so he is of the category of the wicked and not of the category of the good. So we say: those believers who have attributes of disbelief, from which of the two categories are they?
* The students: The good, O Shaykh... the good.
* The Shaykh: Of the category of the good that has wickedness in it, but their goodness overcomes their wickedness; and the disbelievers who have qualities of goodness are of the category of the wicked, but the goodness in them has been submerged in the side of wickedness. On this basis there is no third division; rather they are two categories, but whichever of the two descriptions predominates, they are of that group.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: whoever claims knowledge of the unseen is a liar. From where do you derive it?
* Student: ﴿And Allah would not disclose the unseen to you﴾.
* The Shaykh: ﴿And Allah would not disclose the unseen to you﴾. So whoever claims knowledge of the unseen is a liar, indeed he is a disbeliever; due to His saying: ﴿Say: None in the heavens and the earth knows the unseen except Allah﴾ [an-Naml 65], and because whoever claims knowledge of the unseen has denied the content of His saying: ﴿And Allah would not disclose the unseen to you﴾.
But what is meant by the unseen? What is meant by the unseen is what is absolutely hidden, namely what will occur in the future. As for a present thing that is hidden from some people but not others, a person may come to know of it even without witnessing it, through news from the jinn; the jinn roam the earth, going north and south, and they are swift in their movements, so they may travel through the earth, then inform their allies of what they witnessed in distant lands, and this would be unseen—is it real unseen or relative unseen?
* Student: Relative.
* The Shaykh: Relative. And by relative we mean: relative to some people and not others. Those who witnessed it, it is not unseen to them, and those far from it, it is unseen. Now, what is in the street next to the mosque, while we are here, is unseen to us relative to us, which we do not perceive; but if a man entered upon us and said: "I saw such and such in the street," we would say: "We do not know the unseen, but we were informed of an event that its witness informed us of." So the unseen that none knows but Allah is the absolute unseen, which is what will occur in the future; this none perceives except Allah.
If someone says: When we see the sky darkened, the thunder crashing and the lightning flashing, do we not expect rain? Indeed. But when we say, "It will rain," this is not from the knowledge of the unseen; rather it is based on indicators, and our assumption may be mistaken, and Allah may command that cloud so that it disperses and does not rain. But this is according to what? According to what we expect; and we do not say it is knowledge, rather it is assumption based on indicators. The point, lest the matter be confused for you: the unseen is the absolute unseen, which is what will occur in the future; as for the relative unseen, Allah may make it known to whomever of His servants He wills through an intermediary, such as the jinn for example; the jinn know what has happened on earth and inform their allies of it. But who are the allies of the jinn? The allies of the jinn may be righteous and may be criminals. If the jinn's allegiance to them is due to shirk in them, such as sacrifices to the jinn and the like, this is an allegiance of criminality. But Shaykh al-Islam, may Allah have mercy on him, says: the jinn may take as allies a believer because of his faith; they love him for Allah's sake and serve him in his affairs. He said: this is permissible on two conditions: that the means of employing them is not forbidden, and that he does not employ them in something forbidden. Note well: that the means of employing them is not forbidden, and that he does not employ them in what is forbidden. For example, if they say: "We will not serve you until you prostrate to us"?
* Students: That is forbidden, O Shaykh.
* The Shaykh: That is forbidden, it is shirk. "We will not serve you until you have someone imprisoned?" That is forbidden, but it is not shirk; that is, they served him without shirk, without prohibition. But if he employs them in something forbidden, saying to them, for example: "Go to so-and-so and frighten his camels until he flees and runs away." Is that forbidden?
* Students: Employing something forbidden.
* The Shaykh: Yes. "Go to so-and-so and harm him, terrify him in his house, terrify him in his market"; this too is forbidden and not permissible. So if someone said: their employment is forbidden in every case, because Allah, Exalted, says: ﴿And on the day He will gather them all: "O assembly of jinn, you have taken much from mankind." And their allies from mankind will say: "Our Lord, some of us have enjoyed others, and we have reached our term which You appointed for us." He will say: "The Fire is your abode, wherein you will abide eternally, except as Allah wills. Indeed your Lord is Wise and Knowing"﴾ [al-An'ām 128], and this indicates that the enjoyment of a human from a jinn is forbidden in every case.
The answer to that: read the verse that follows, where He says: ﴿And thus We make some of the wrongdoers allies of others for what they used to earn﴾ [al-An'ām 129]. This enjoyment is enjoyment in wrongdoing, and there is no doubt it is forbidden. But if it is an enjoyment of what is beneficial and free of what is forbidden in its means or its employment, then there is no harm in it.
* Student: O Shaykh, what is meant by al-asbāṭ (...), the sons of Jacob?
* The Shaykh: What?
* The Student: al-Asbāṭ.
* The Shaykh: Where are the asbāṭ?
* The Student: The day we spoke about the prophet and the messenger, O Shaykh, you defined the prophet and the messenger; are they prophets or messengers?
* The Shaykh: Some said: al-asbāṭ means the tribes of the Children of Israel, and the asbāṭ, meaning and the prophets are from the asbāṭ; and some say: they are the sons of Jacob.
* The Student: And the correct view?
* The Shaykh: There is disagreement about it.
* * *
* Student: ﴿And let not those who withhold what Allah has given them of His bounty think that it is good for them; rather it is bad for them. They will have hung around their necks that about which they were stingy on the Day of Resurrection. And to Allah belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is Acquainted with what you do. (180) Certainly Allah has heard the statement of those who say, "Indeed, Allah is poor, and we are rich." We will record what they have said and their killing of the prophets without right, and We will say, "Taste the punishment of the Burning. (181) That is for what your hands have put forward, and [because] indeed, Allah is not ever unjust to the servants."﴾ [Āl ʿImrān 180–182].
* The Shaykh: ﴿Allah would not leave the believers in the state you are in until He distinguishes the wicked from the good.﴾ What do the grammarians call this lām?
* Student: Lām al-juḥūd.
* The Shaykh: Lām al-juḥūd. And what is al-juḥūd?
* Student: It is the attempt (...).
* The Shaykh: No.
* Student: It is the opposition (...).
* The Shaykh: What?
* Student: The opposition.
* The Shaykh: No.
* Student: In the sense of negation.
* The Shaykh: Negation. Al-juḥūd here means negation. And its rule?
* Student: That it comes after a negated kawn (state of being).
* The Shaykh: That it comes after a negated kawn; correct. And what is its meaning when you say: "mā kāna li-kadhā" (it was not for so-and-so to do such-and-such)? "mā kāna Allāhu li-kadhā"?
* Student: That it is impossible, in the strongest sense, that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does this thing.
* The Shaykh: Its meaning is that it is impossible in the utmost degree of impossibility that Allah does this thing.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verses 178–179 (part 3 of 3):

His saying: ﴿So that Allah may leave the believers﴾. What is the meaning of ﴿leave﴾? That is, to leave the believers in the state you are in. What is the meaning of leaving them in the state you are in? He says: "Until when?"

* Student: He leaves them in confusion between the hypocrite and the sincere believer.

* Shaykh: In confusion between the hypocrite and the sincere believer, until He distinguishes the evil from the good.

His saying: ﴿And Allah would not disclose to you the unseen﴾. What is the connection of this to what comes before it?

* Student: Istidrak (a correction or contrast introducing a new point).

* Shaykh: Istidrak. What is the meaning?

* Student: The meaning is that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, would not inform you of the unseen, so that you would know what is in people's hearts, whether hypocrite or sincere believer.

* Shaykh: Yes, indeed. That is, to disclose to you what is in their hearts of hypocrisy or otherwise. So there is no istidrak here, there is no istidrak.

* Student: Istidrak here...

* Shaykh: ﴿Allah would not leave the believers in the state you are in﴾.

* Student: ﴿So that He may leave...﴾ (...).

* Shaykh: No, I mean: ﴿And Allah would not disclose to you the unseen﴾.

* Student: There is an istidrak in that these matters are known to Allah alone.

* Shaykh: No.

* Student: Ta'lil (a causal clause explaining the reason).

* Shaykh: Ta'lil. That is: Allah would not disclose the unseen to you, so that He would inform you of what distinguishes this from that.

His saying: ﴿But Allah chooses of His messengers whom He wills﴾?

* Student: This is an exception.

* Shaykh: Or an istidrak. "Lakin" (but) is used for istidrak. Good. What is the meaning?

* Student: The meaning: But Allah chooses from among His messengers whom He wills to inform, and Allah knows best.

* Shaykh: So He discloses the unseen to you through an intermediary?

* Student: The messengers.

* Shaykh: The messengers. The summary is that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made clear in this verse that He has not left the Muslim community in bewilderment and doubt. Rather, He must distinguish, that is, separate the evil from the good by mentioning the attributes that apply to this and that. This does not happen by disclosing to each one of you the unseen, but through the messengers.

His saying: ﴿And if you believe and fear Allah, then for you is a great reward﴾. Allah often pairs faith (iman) with piety (taqwa). So how do we interpret faith when it is paired with piety?

* Student: When faith is paired with piety, how is it explained? Faith is an action of the heart, and piety is intended as an action of the limbs?

* Shaykh: An action of the limbs. So faith is of the heart and piety is of the limbs.

* From the benefits of this verse: Allah may disclose the unseen to creation through the messengers, as in His saying: ﴿But Allah chooses of His messengers whom He wills﴾.

* From its benefits: the messengers are among those whom Allah chose and selected above creation. This is found in the Qur'an, where the prophets are the elite, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And indeed they are with Us among the chosen and the excellent﴾ [Sad 47].

* From its benefits: affirmation of Allah's will in His saying: ﴿whom He wills﴾. But we say: everything that Allah attached to His will must be accompanied by wisdom. It is not a bare will; it must be joined with wisdom. The proof of this is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And you do not will except that Allah wills. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾ [al-Insan 30]. Then He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾, indicating that His will follows His knowledge and wisdom.

* From its benefits, from the benefits of this verse: the obligation of believing in Allah and His messengers in general, as in His saying: ﴿So believe in Allah and His messengers﴾. We have explained in the tafsir how to believe in the messengers: one believes that they are true, that they came from Allah, and that they are truthful. As for following them, that is specific to the Prophet ﷺ.

* From the benefits of this verse: the virtue of faith and piety, and that a great reward follows from them.

* Also from the benefits of this verse: the demonstration of Allah's favor upon His servants, in that He made their reward for action like a wage that is due to them. As if a person hired workers and gave them their wages as an obligation. But who imposed that upon Him? The one who imposed it is Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

* Also from the benefits of this verse: affirmation of recompense, and that it is of the same kind as the deed. Just as faith and piety are a great matter, outward and inward, so the reward is a great reward.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verse 180 (part 1 of 2):

Then the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And let not those who withhold what Allah has given them of His bounty think that it is good for them﴾. In ﴿يَحْسَبَنَّ﴾ there are three readings. The first is ﴿وَلَا يَحْسِبَنَّ﴾, the second is ﴿وَلَا يَحْسَبَنَّ﴾, and the third is ﴿وَلَا تَحْسَبَنَّ﴾ in the second person. All of them are canonical readings (qira'at sab'iyyah), and it is recommended for a person to recite with each of them at times. However, one should not recite a reading that is outside the Mushaf in front of the general public, because that may cause trial and confusion (fitnah).

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And let not those who withhold...﴾, meaning: let not those who withhold what Allah has given them think... Al-bukhl (stinginess) is withholding, and al-bukhl is withholding accompanied by miserliness (shuhh), which is why it takes the particle bi (with). He did not say "yabkhaluna ma atahum" but said "yabkhaluna bihi," meaning they withhold it with miserliness and are greedy about it.

His saying ﴿بِمَا آتَاهُمُ﴾ means: what Allah has given them. This indicates that this stinginess is misplaced, because they are stingy with something that is not from their own earning or effort, but is from Allah, and they are stingy about spending it on what Allah has commanded them. This is the utmost foolishness: the One who gave you it and said, "Spend it on such-and-such," and you are stingy. This is extreme foolishness, since the command requires that the One who gave you it, when He commands you to spend it on such-and-such, that you spend it as He commanded, because it is His bounty.

His saying ﴿مِنْ فَضْلِهِ﴾ means: from His goodness, because fadl (bounty) originally means increase. A person may sometimes do a deed in which he hopes to gain a thousand, and he gains two thousand or more from the bounty of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and he may also lose.

His saying ﴿هُوَ خَيْرًا لَهُمْ﴾: ﴿خَيْرًا﴾ is the second object of ﴿يحسب﴾, and the first object is omitted, its implied meaning being: their stinginess is good for them. "And let not those who withhold think that their withholding is good for them, but rather it is evil for them, as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has mentioned."

His saying ﴿خَيْرًا لَهُمْ﴾: ﴿خير﴾ here is an elative noun (ism tafdil), so there must be something preferred and something it is preferred over. What is the preferred and what is the thing it is preferred over? The thing it is preferred over is stinginess; that is, it is better for them than giving. In other words, they should not think that stinginess is better than giving. They think that stinginess is better than giving, and this thinking is mistaken. This is an erroneous assumption, because the Prophet ﷺ said: "Charity does not decrease wealth" [[Reported by Muslim (2588/69) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]]. How many people see their wealth increase through charity, and charity does not diminish wealth when done seeking reward, due to the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And whatever you spend, He will replace it﴾ [Saba' 39]. The meaning of ﴿يُخْلِفُهُ﴾ is that He will bring its replacement.

The Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿But it is evil for them﴾. Evil for them compared to what? Compared to giving. It is worse than giving. Giving has no evil in it, but Allah addressed these people according to their belief, since they think that if they spend, their provision will be reduced. One of them says: "I have a thousand; if I spend a hundred from it, it will decrease and become nine hundred." So they think this is evil, and the Mighty and Majestic says: the one who is evil is the one who withholds. Therefore He said: ﴿But it is evil for them﴾, evil for them compared to what? Compared to giving. So giving is good and withholding is evil. ﴿But it is evil for them﴾.

Then He said: ﴿That which they withheld will be hung around their necks on the Day of Resurrection﴾. The grammarians say that the sin (sa) is for tanfis (near future) and it conveys tahqiq (certainty). Tanfis means that the thing will occur soon, and tahqiq is clear. That is, the word ﴿سَيُطَوَّقُونَ﴾ is more emphatic in certainty than "yuṭawwaqūn," because the sin conveys certainty and also conveys tanfis, which is the thing being near. So ﴿سَيُطَوَّقُونَ﴾ indicates that these people will certainly be punished with this punishment soon. From where do we derive the certainty?

* The students: From the sin.
* The Shaykh: From the sin, which indicates the certainty of occurrence. And we derive nearness because tanfis, which the sin indicates, means nearness. If someone says: its occurrence is known, but how can it be near? We say: the Day of Resurrection is near. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And what will make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near﴾ [al-Ahzab 63], and He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And what will make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near﴾ [al-Shura 17]. So although the Day of Resurrection seems distant in the view of people, in reality it is near. Consider how the days fold up quickly until they end, so that you know that the Day of Resurrection, though its time seems far, is in reality near.

His saying ﴿سَيُطَوَّقُونَ مَا بَخِلُوا بِهِ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ﴾ means: what they withheld will be made a collar (tawq) around their necks. The tawq is well known, like the collar of a shirt that surrounds the neck. The Prophet ﷺ explained how this encircling would be when he said: "Whoever Allah has given wealth but does not pay its zakah, on the Day of Resurrection his wealth will be made into a bald venomous male snake with two black spots over its eyes, which will seize him by his two jowls and say: 'I am your treasure, I am your wealth'" [[Reported by al-Bukhari (1403) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]].

The scholars said: al-shuja' al-aqra' is the male of snakes, and al-aqra' is one with a great deal of venom, because from the abundance of its venom its hair has fallen off around its head, so it is bald. "Lahu zabibatan" means two glands resembling raisins that are filled with venom. "Fa-ya'khudhu bi-lahzimatayhi" means by his two jaws, as explained in detail in the hadith, and it says: "I am your treasure, I am your wealth." It says this as a reproach to him, and thereby his regret increases. This is the explanation of the noble verse as the Prophet ﷺ explained it.

His saying ﴿مَا بَخِلُوا بِهِ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ﴾: ﴿سَيُطَوَّقُونَ مَا بَخِلُوا بِهِ﴾ Allah expresses the recompense by the deed itself, and this is common in the Qur'an. Allah, may He be glorified and exalted, expresses the recompense by the deed itself, such as: ﴿You will only be recompensed for what you used to do﴾ [al-A'raf 180], and here: ﴿That which they withheld will be hung around their necks﴾. This is because the recompense is of the same kind as the deed, so it is as if it were the deed itself. For this reason Allah often expresses it that way: ﴿That which they withheld will be hung around their necks on the Day of Resurrection﴾. The Day of Resurrection is the day when people are raised. It is called the Day of Resurrection (Yawm al-Qiyamah) for how many reasons, four or three?

* A student: Three.
* The Shaykh: Three. People stand on it before the Lord of the Worlds; the witnesses stand on it; and justice stands on it. People stand before the Lord of the Worlds, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Do they not think that they will be resurrected? For a great Day, the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 4-6]. Likewise, justice is established on it, due to His saying: ﴿And We will set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection﴾ [al-Anbiya' 47]. The third: the witnesses stand on it, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believe in the worldly life and on the Day when the witnesses will stand﴾ [Ghafir 51]. Therefore it is called the Day of Resurrection.

He says: ﴿And to Allah belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth﴾. The lam here is for exclusivity (ikhtisas), and the prepositional phrase is a predicate placed first, and placing it first conveys restriction (hasr): that is, it belongs to Him alone, to Allah alone. Inheritance is the transfer of property from one who precedes to one who follows, like its transfer from the dead to the living. Who inherits the heavens and the earth and remains after them? It is Allah. Therefore He said: ﴿And to Allah belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth﴾, its inheritance will transfer only to Him alone, the Mighty and Majestic. The connection of this sentence to what follows is clear: the one who is stingy with his wealth is only stingy so that it will remain for him. So Allah makes clear that it will not remain for him. He must die and his heirs will inherit it, then his heirs will die and their heirs will inherit it, and so on, until the inheritance ends with whom? With Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. So the connection between this sentence and what precedes it is very evident. That is: withhold or do not withhold, you will leave your wealth after you, and your heirs will inherit it, and after them their heirs, until the inheritance ends with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. You will part from all your wealth, and it will belong to those after you.

He said: ﴿And Allah is All-Aware of what you do﴾. There are two readings: ﴿تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ and ﴿يَعْمَلُونَ﴾. Ending the verse with this name, al-Khabir (the All-Aware), has clear relevance, because these people who withhold what Allah has given them of His bounty may not be seen by creatures. A person may have millions and people do not know about him, and he withholds its zakah and nothing is known about it. So Allah, may He be glorified and exalted, makes clear that Allah is All-Aware of their deeds. Generally, the one who withholds the right in his wealth is afflicted with ruin in falsehood; that is, doors of falsehood are opened for him in which he spends his wealth, so he withholds what is obligatory and falls into what is forbidden. For this reason Allah threatened them by saying: "And Allah is All-Aware of what they do."

* Among the many benefits of this verse: a warning to the one who is stingy with what Allah has given him of His bounty. We have already mentioned that stinginess is withholding what is obligatory in wealth. Withholding what is obligatory in wealth is the stinginess for which a threat is made.
* Among the benefits of this verse: Satan may deceive a person. He may deceive him and say: "Do not spend, or your wealth will be ruined." This is due to His saying: ﴿And let not those who withhold what Allah has given them of His bounty think that it is good for them﴾, and there is no doubt that this is the reality. The evidence is that Allah constantly warns us about this Satan, saying: ﴿Let not the worldly life deceive you, and let not the Deceiver deceive you concerning Allah﴾ [Luqman 33], and the first one to deceive us about Allah is Satan.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: blame and reproach are established against those who are stingy. From where is this derived? From His saying: ﴿what Allah has given them of His bounty﴾, meaning: how can they be stingy with something that is not from their own earning or effort, but is from Allah's bounty, and then be stingy with it in obedience to Allah?
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: whatever a person is given of knowledge, wealth, or children, it is from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. A person does not say about a child, "I was given him because I married and went to my wife." Nor does he say about knowledge, "I was given it because I strove for it." Likewise he does not say about wealth, "I was given it because I strove for it," because all of it is from the bounty of Allah. Your success in striving for this matter is from the bounty of Allah, and then the result you hoped for, what? Is from the bounty of Allah. How many people are deprived and do not strive, and how many people strive and do not obtain fruit. So the origin of the striving and the fruit are all from Allah. For this reason He said: ﴿what Allah has given them of His bounty﴾.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: a warning to the stingy against stinginess, due to His saying: ﴿And let not those who withhold what Allah has given them of His bounty think that it is good for them. Rather, it is evil for them﴾.
* Among its benefits: a person may have his evil deed made attractive to him so that he thinks it good. Stinginess is a bad trait and a bad deed. It may be made attractive to a person so that he withholds, even though it is among the evil deeds and evil traits.
* Among the benefits of this verse: the affirmation of recompense, indeed the affirmation of a severe punishment for these stingy people. What is the punishment? That they will be made to wear it around their necks on the Day of Resurrection, when regret will not benefit them and they will have no means of escape.
* Among its benefits: the certainty of the occurrence of the recompense, due to His saying: ﴿They will be made to wear it﴾, and this is by means of what? By means of the sin (sa).
* Among the benefits of this verse also: establishing the proof that this stinginess does not benefit its people, derived from His saying: ﴿And to Allah belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth﴾. Their stinginess will not make them immortal in this world, nor will wealth remain for them forever. Rather, they will be recompensed for it, and the wealth will pass from them to their heirs, and from their heirs to others, until the matter ends with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
* Among the benefits of this verse: the affirmation of the Day of Resurrection, due to His saying: ﴿That which they withheld will be hung around their necks on the Day of Resurrection﴾. Belief in the Day of Resurrection is one of the six pillars of faith, as is well known, and a servant's faith is not complete until he believes in it. If he has doubt about it, his faith is incomplete.
* Among its benefits: the affirmation of the knowledge of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, due to His saying: ﴿And Allah is All-Aware of what they do﴾. ﴿بما يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ and ﴿تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ are two readings. The scholars said that khibrah (awareness) is knowledge of what? Of the inner realities of matters. It is well known that one who knows the inner realities of matters knows their outward aspects all the more.
* Among the benefits of this verse: an allusion to another of Allah's names, for Allah is al-Awwal and al-Akhir (the First and the Last). From where is this derived?
