From His saying: ﴿And to Allah belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth﴾. If His inheritance of them is established, it necessarily follows that He is al-Akhir, the Mighty and Majestic.

* A student: O Shaykh, we said that in His saying ﴿وَلَا يَحْسَبَنَّ﴾ there are three readings, three readings, O Shaykh. What are the meanings?
* The Shaykh: Only the second person and the third person; there are only the second and third person. But is it second person or third person? As for the meaning, it is the same.
* A student: May Allah be good to you. Regarding inheritance and the transfer of wealth from the dead to the living after his death, it may be confusing, O Shaykh, or one may think that ﴿لِلَّهِ مِيرَاثُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ means that they were not before, i.e., denial or death, the denial of the two worlds that they were not...
* The Shaykh: No, no. They belong to Allah, but before that they are in the hands of their owners, who manage them. The final inheritance means that their people do not manage them at all. For example, as long as wealth is in their hands, they manage it according to what is permitted for them by the Shari'ah. But when they die, there is no management at all.
* A student: O Shaykh, may Allah be good to you, regarding stinginess with what Allah has given of bounty in knowledge and wealth, is this...?
* The Shaykh: What is it?
* The student: The one who is stingy with knowledge...
* The Shaykh: Yes, this is included. Stinginess with knowledge is more severe than stinginess with wealth. "Whoever is asked about knowledge he has and conceals it, will be bridled with a bridle of fire" [[Reported by Abu Dawud (3658) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]].

* * *

* A student: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed. ﴿Allah has certainly heard the statement of those who said, "Indeed, Allah is poor, and we are rich." We will record what they have said and their killing of the prophets without right, and We will say, "Taste the punishment of the burning. That is for what your hands have put forth, and [because] Allah is not ever unjust to [His] servants." Those who say, "Indeed, Allah has taken our promise not to believe in a messenger until he brings us an offering which fire [from heaven] devours." Say, "There have already come to you messengers before me with clear proofs and with what you [now] speak. So why did you kill them, if you should be truthful?" And if they deny you, [O Muhammad], [so were] messengers denied before you who came with clear proofs and written statements and the Book of illumination.﴾ [Al 'Imran 181-184].
* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿And let not those who withhold what Allah has given them of His bounty think...﴾.
In His saying ﴿وَلَا يَحْسَبَنَّ﴾ there are two readings?
* A student: (Wa la yahsibanna), (wa la tahsabanna), (wa la yuhsibanna).
* The Shaykh: ﴿يَحْسَبَنَّ﴾.
* The student: ﴿وَلَا يَحْسِبَنَّ﴾.
* The Shaykh: ﴿وَلَا تَحْسَبَنَّ﴾, ﴿وَلَا يَحْسِبَنَّ﴾?
* A student: ﴿وَلَا يَحْسِبَنَّ﴾.
* The Shaykh: Tahsabanna, yes. ﴿يَحْسِبَنَّ﴾, ﴿تَحْسَبَنَّ﴾.
* The students: ﴿يَحْسِبَنَّ﴾.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No no, we have three: ﴿وَلَا يَحْسِبَنَّ﴾, ﴿وَلَا يَحْسَبَنَّ﴾, ﴿وَلَا تَحْسَبَنَّ﴾.
* A student: (tahsabanna) with a kasra on the sin.
* The Shaykh: No.
* The student: With the feminine (second person) letter.
* The Shaykh: No, it is not with a kasra on the sin with the second person letter. You have...
* The students: O Shaykh, tahsibanna.
* The Shaykh: Allah!! It is with the yā' with the sin fatha and kasra, and with the tā' only with fatha.
* Students: yuhsibanna.
* The Shaykh: yuhsibanna, who said this?!
* The students: With a damma on the yā'.
* The Shaykh: The point is, with the yā' with fatha and kasra of the sin, and with the tā' with fatha.
* A student: Is there one with the tā', O Shaykh?
* The Shaykh: Fine, on the reading with the tā'.
* A student: ﴿وَلَا تَحْسَبَنَّ﴾.
* The Shaykh: The address is to whom?

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verse 180 (part 2 of 2):

* Student: It is addressed to the Prophet ﷺ and to the believers in general.
* The Shaykh: How is it addressed to the Prophet and to the believers? If it were for the believers, it would have said: "And let them not think" (wa la tahsabunna).
* Student: "Wa la tahsabunna" (...).
* Another student: This is addressed to the Prophet, or to whoever is fit to be addressed.
* The Shaykh: Or? Yes, indeed. For the Prophet it is clear: ﴿tahsabanna﴾, [addressed to] those who are fit for address, because the Qur'an is an address to all people. Where is the first object of "tahsaba" (taḥsaba)?
* Student: It is omitted.
* The Shaykh: What is the implied reading?
* Student: "Let not the miserliness be [what they think]."
* The Shaykh: "Their miserliness is better for them." What is the meaning of al-bukhl (miserliness)?
* Student: It is withholding combined with stinginess (shuhh).
* The Shaykh: Yes, withholding what must be given out, together with stinginess (shuhh). If both bukhl and shuhh are mentioned together?
* Student: (...) when they are combined.
* The Shaykh: Good. If both are mentioned together, what is meant by bukhl?
* Student: We said: bukhl is withholding.
* The Shaykh: Withholding what is obligatory. And shuhh is greed for what is not one's own. Which of the things they are miserly with is included?
* Student: The saying of the Prophet...
* The Shaykh: That is, among the things they are miserly with, what would be an example?
* Student: Like the wealth that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, gave them, like zakat.
* The Shaykh: Like withholding zakat. Do you remember a hadith from the Prophet ﷺ on this?
* Student: The saying of the Messenger ﷺ: "Charity does not decrease wealth" [[Narrated by Muslim (2588 / 69) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]].
* The Shaykh: No.
* Student: The one that means zakat?
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: The saying of the Messenger ﷺ: "Whoever Allah gives wealth, but he does not pay its zakat... on the Day of Resurrection it will be turned into a bald poisonous snake with two black spots over its eyes, which will seize him by his two jaws..." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari (1403) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]].
* The Shaykh: By what? "By his two cheeks (bi-lihzimatayh)."
* Student: "Bi-lihzimatayh."
* The Shaykh: That means?
* Student: That means his two jaws; it seizes him by his two jaws.
* The Shaykh: That means his two jaws, and it says..
* Student: "And it says: I am your treasure, I am your wealth."
* The Shaykh: Excellent. Now, what is the benefit of His saying: ﴿And to Allah belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth﴾?
* Student: The intended meaning is miserliness.
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: Those who are miserly with wealth (...).
* The Shaykh: That is, its meaning is miserliness; they are miserly so that they may accumulate it, so Allah makes clear that He...
* Student: Allah is the One who bestowed it upon them.
* The Shaykh: He is the One who bestowed it upon them, and He will inherit it after them; if they keep it, they will leave it behind. ﴿And Allah is All-Aware of what you do﴾ — are there two readings in it?
* Student: The reading ﴿bi-mā ya'malūn﴾ and the reading ﴿bi-mā ta'malūn﴾.
* The Shaykh: The reading ﴿bi-mā ya'malūn﴾ and the reading ﴿bi-mā ta'malūn﴾, you know them? What is the meaning of khabīr?
* Student: Khabīr implies knowledge.
* The Shaykh: Knowledge of what?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No, because khibrah (experiential knowledge) is more specific than ʿilm (knowledge).
* Student: Khabīr is one who knows the hidden aspects of matters.
* The Shaykh: The khabīr is the one who knows the hidden aspects of matters. Here there is a difficulty in His saying: ﴿bi-mā ya'malūn﴾. I did not mention it except long ago, namely that it is well known that fronting the object (taqdīm al-maʿmūl) conveys restriction (ḥaṣr), and here He has fronted ﴿bi-mā ya'malūn﴾ before ﴿khabīr﴾ even though it is related to it. Does that mean He is not khabīr except regarding what they do, on the basis of this rule?
* The students: No, Shaykh.
* The Shaykh: Yes, but what is the benefit of fronting what should be delayed?
* Student: The operator was placed before the object.
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: It conveys restriction, Shaykh.
* The Shaykh: Good, restriction of what?
* Student: Threat, Shaykh.
* The Shaykh: What is the aspect of the threat? What is the aspect of the threat?
* Student: That Allah, glorified and exalted, related to them by what they do.
* The Shaykh: By what they do, as a threat to them, and an intensified threat, lest they say: He is aware of what people do except what we do. Clear. For this reason the Qur'an says in another verse: ﴿And Allah is Khabīr of what you do﴾ [Āl ʿImrān 153]. Do you understand, everyone?
So the benefit of fronting the object here is other than restriction; its benefit is what? The threat to these people, and that He knows what they do, especially, and what else by a fortiori. Then, in His saying: ﴿Nay, it is worse for them﴾?
* Student: This means it is an idrāb ibṭālī (rejecting resumption).
* The Shaykh: Idrāb ibṭālī. Is there an idrāb that is not ibṭālī?
* Student: What I have is not correct.
* The Shaykh: Like..
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: This too we did not mention to you, but it seems clear.
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: By Allah, if it is correct, what example?
* Student: ﴿Bal iddāraka ʿilmuhum fil-ākhirah﴾ (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, ﴿Bal iddāraka ʿilmuhum fil-ākhirah﴾, meaning it has gone far. ﴿Bal hum fī shakkin minhā﴾, we seek refuge in Allah. ﴿Bal hum minhā ʿamūn﴾ [al-Naml 66]. The second does not nullify the first; the second reinforces it, and the grammarians call this idrāb intiqālī (transitional rejection). As for the verse before us, it is idrāb ibṭālī.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Allah has certainly heard the statement of those who said, "Indeed, Allah is poor and we are rich." We will record what they have said and their killing of the prophets without right, and We will say, "Taste the punishment of the burning."﴾

First, we speak about the recitations (qira'at) found in the verse. He says: there are recitations for it. The one we have now is ﴿سَنَكْتُبُ﴾ with a nun, and ﴿نَقُولُ﴾ with a nun as well. On the basis of this reading, (ما) is the direct object (maf'ul bihi), and (قتل) is conjoined to the direct object, and what is conjoined to a accusative noun is accusative.

On the second reading, ﴿سَيُكْتُبُ مَا قَالُوا﴾, (ما) is the deputy subject (naib fa'il), in the nominative, built on sukun in a place of nominative. Then (قتل) is conjoined to a nominative word, the deputy subject, so it is in the nominative. Accordingly, ﴿قَتْلَهُمُ﴾ is governed by which reading? By (يُكتب). It is not permissible to read: "We will record what they have said and their killing (qatluhum)," no. (قتل) cannot be nominative unless we read ﴿سَيُكْتُبُ﴾.

As for ﴿الْأَنْبِيَاءَ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ وَيَقُولُ﴾: does ﴿يَقُولُ﴾ agree with which of the two readings, or match which of the two? ﴿سَيُكْتُبُ﴾ or ﴿سَنَكْتُبُ﴾?
* The students: ﴿سَيُكْتُبُ﴾.
* The Shaykh: ﴿سَيُكْتُبُ﴾, and ﴿وَيَقُولُ ذُوقُوا عَذَابَ الْحَرِيقِ﴾.

As for ﴿الْأَنْبِيَاءَ﴾, there are two readings: ﴿الْأَنْبِئَاءَ﴾, and the second: ﴿الْأَنْبِيَاءَ﴾ with a ya, like ﴿النَّبِيِّينَ﴾ and ﴿النَّبِيئِينَ﴾. On the reading ﴿الْأَنْبِئَاءَ﴾, it derives from (النبأ), with a hamza, which means "news." On the reading with ya, it derives from (النُّبُوّة) or (النَّبْوَة), which means "elevation."

Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿Allah has certainly heard the statement of those who said﴾. Allah has emphasized this report with three emphatics. The first is the implied oath, since the lam here falls in the answer to an oath. The second is (قد). The third is the (lam) in His saying ﴿لَقَدْ سَمِعَ﴾. He emphasized it, glorified and exalted is He, only to intensify the threat to these people. As for us, the believers, we know that whenever He informs us of something, it is emphasized, but He does so to threaten those who uttered this shameful statement.

﴿لَقَدْ سَمِعَ اللَّهُ قَوْلَ الَّذِينَ قَالُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ فَقِيرٌ﴾: ﴿سَمِعَ﴾ here means "perceived this statement," i.e., He heard it with hearing. We do not say "with His ear," because hearing does not necessarily imply an ear. This differs from our saying about "He istawa over the Throne" (istawa 'ala al-'arsh), where we say "in His essence," because Allah attributed the act to Himself. Here we do not say "He heard with His ear," and why? Because hearing does not necessarily entail the existence of an ear. Behold, on the Day of Resurrection the earth will ﴿relate its news﴾ [al-Zalzalah 4], meaning it will inform of what people did upon it or what they said upon it, even though it has no ear. The skins, hands and feet will testify on the Day of Resurrection against a person for what he did, and they have no ears. Therefore it is not permissible to say that Allah has an ear, on the basis that Allah affirmed hearing for Himself, because hearing does not necessarily entail an ear.

If someone says: "Did you not affirm for Allah an eye?"
* A student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: We do not say "yes"; we say "bala." Did you not affirm for Allah an eye?
* The students: Bala.
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed. We say "bala." If we say "na'am," it means we did not affirm it. "Bala," we did affirm it. How did we affirm it? Through the fact that He sees, or through the fact that He affirmed two eyes for Himself?
* The students: The second.
* The Shaykh: The second, yes. Had Allah not affirmed two eyes for Himself, it would not have been permissible for us to affirm the eye. For this reason, we believe that Allah speaks, but do we say "with a tongue"? Never, we do not say it, although Allah said: ﴿The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down, upon your heart, in clear Arabic language﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 193–195]. Yet we do not say "Allah has a tongue," nor "Allah has two lips," because Allah did not affirm that for Himself, and speech does not necessarily entail a tongue. The proof is that the earth relates its news, and the skins testify, and the owner of the skin says to his skin: "Why did you testify against us?" It says: ﴿Allah, who made everything speak, has made us speak﴾ [Fussilat 21], and it does not say, "I have a tongue and two lips." Therefore it is not permissible to affirm for Allah a tongue or two lips merely on the basis of affirming speech. Is it clear?

Just as it is not permissible to affirm teeth for Him, because teeth exist only for one who needs them to chew food, and we do not affirm intestines or the like for Him, because these imply deficiency, being instruments for what? For eating, and eating is impossible for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

We say: He hears. Does His hearing necessarily entail the existence of an ear? No. ﴿Allah has certainly heard the statement of those who said, "Indeed, Allah is poor"﴾. They were a group of Jews, among them a man named (Finhas). But Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in His Book, does not mention anything specific except for a reason that requires identifying the person. For this reason, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, did not mention anyone by name in the Qur'an except for one believing man and one disbelieving man only. Who is the believing man?
* Students: Zayd.
* The Shaykh: Zayd ibn Harithah: ﴿So when Zayd had completed his need from her, We married her to you﴾ [al-Ahzab 37]. And the disbelieving man?
* Students: Pharaoh.
* The Shaykh: No, no, no. From this nation?
* A student: Abu Lahab.
* The Shaykh: Abu Lahab. Others were not mentioned, because the description (al-wasf) is more beneficial due to its generality. This is one aspect. The other aspect is that the state of the specified person may change: he may be at first a wicked, rebellious, disbelieving person, then he accepts Islam and Allah accepts his repentance. If he repents and his name had been mentioned, it would remain a shame upon him even though he repented. Is it clear, brothers?

The second: that it is more general, because attaching a ruling to a description is more general than attaching it to a person. For this reason, when a ruling is attached to a specific person, it may admit of particularity. If we say it applies generally, the generality of a ruling attached to a person is not an all-encompassing generality, but an illustrative generality, meaning by analogy (qiyas). Is the speech clear? It is clear.

Therefore, in such matters, we should not identify the specific person. Even if we want to speak about a wicked newspaper, it is better not to identify it. We say, for example, "Some newspapers said," and when we mention the matter, it is understood. First, because the newspaper may change. Second, if we restrict it, the listener may understand that there is no other than this newspaper, but if we generalize and make the ruling attached to the description, it includes others. If we identify it, the listener, especially the layman who does not know how to analogize, may understand that the calamity is specific to this newspaper, for example. He does not know how to analogize. So if we make the matter attached to the description, it becomes more beneficial. This is a matter that the Qur'an indicates, and likewise the Sunnah. The Sunnah also indicates it: the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, did not say, "What is the matter with so-and-so who says such-and-such," but he said: "What is the matter with people who..." (ما بال أقوام), for the two benefits we have pointed out.

﴿Those who said, "Indeed, Allah is poor and we are rich"﴾: these are the Jews. The reason for their saying this is that Allah said: ﴿Who is it that would loan Allah a goodly loan so He will multiply it for him?﴾ [al-Baqarah 245]. "The Jews rejoiced at this, came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Muhammad, indeed your Lord has become poor, indeed your Lord has become poor." [Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim in al-Tafsir (2429) (2/460), from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both.] Because He asks us for a loan, we seek Allah's protection, and these simpletons did not know, even if they were sincere in what they claimed, and they were lying in what they claimed, even their saying that Allah has become poor, they are liars, they do not believe this. But, by way of accommodating them, we say: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, made spending in His cause like a loan to Him, to make the spender aware that he will be recompensed for it, just as the borrower is obliged to repay his loan. Thus Allah, glorified and exalted is He, made the deed for Himself like a loan, out of His grace and kindness to His servants. The Jews should not be considered strange in describing Allah with such a thing. They said: ﴿The hand of Allah is chained﴾ [al-Ma'idah 64], and they described Him with stinginess: the hand of Allah is chained, He does not spend. They also said that Allah created the heavens and the earth in six days, then became tired and rested on Saturday, and for this reason they make Saturday their day of rest. May Allah curse them; they are liars in this. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿And We created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, and no fatigue touched Us﴾ [Qaf 38].

﴿Those who said, "Indeed, Allah is poor"﴾. Would that they had stopped at this. I say: would that they had, given what follows it. Otherwise, describing Him with this description is a denial, one of the greatest denials. They said ﴿and we are rich﴾, so they made themselves more complete than Allah. They made themselves more perfect than Allah. This is the utmost of insolence. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿We will record what they have said﴾. The attribution of recording to Himself is because His soldiers record it. The proof is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿No! But you deny the Recompense. And indeed, over you are guardians, noble and recording, who know what you do﴾ [al-Infitar 9–11], and His saying, which is more explicit: ﴿Or do they think that We do not hear their secret and their private conversation? Yes [We do], and Our messengers are with them, recording﴾ [al-Zukhruf 80]. So is the recording here the recording of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, with His own hand? No, but with His angels. The angels record, and He attributed the recording of the angels to Himself, since they record by His command and they are His soldiers, just as a commander says: "I did such-and-such," while the doer is other than him; the doer is the soldiers. The king and the ruler speak of a thing attributing it to himself, because it occurred by his command and authority. So ﴿We will record what they have said﴾ by what? By Our angels. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sometimes attributes a thing to Himself while intending the angels, like His saying: ﴿Then why, when [the soul] reaches the throat, and you at that time are looking on, and We are nearer to him than you, but you do not see﴾ [al-Waqi'ah 83–85]. Nearer to him by what? By Our angels. For this reason He said ﴿but you do not see﴾, which indicates that the one who is near is in the same place, but we do not see him, and these are the angels. Among this also is His saying: ﴿And We have certainly created man, and We know what his soul whispers to him, and We are nearer to him than his jugular vein﴾ [Qaf 16]. The preponderant view regarding it is that what is meant is "nearer to him by Our angels," as evidenced by His saying: ﴿When the two receivers receive, seated on the right and on the left﴾ [Qaf 17]. This is what Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, verified in his book, in several places of his speech, including his explanation of the hadith of the Descent, which is famous and widely circulated.

He says: ﴿We will record what they have said﴾, merely to be informed of it, or for recompense? For recompense, as is evident from what comes at the end of the verse.

He said: ﴿and their killing of the prophets without right﴾. He mentioned the killing of the prophets without right, although they did not say, "We killed the prophets," but to make clear that these people transgressed against the right of Allah and against the right of His messengers and prophets, so they killed the prophets without right. It encompasses the killing of prophets and messengers, because every messenger is a prophet. His saying: ﴿and their killing of the prophets without right﴾: is the qualifier here a restrictive qualifier (qayd ihtiraz) or a descriptive qualifier (qayd kashif)?
* A student: Descriptive.
* The Shaykh: A descriptive qualifier. That is, their killing of the prophets is without right. It does not mean that the killing of the prophets is divided into right and wrong; all killing of the prophets is without right. Nevertheless, they do not kill the prophets for their persons; they kill them for what they brought of truth. Any person who comes with this prophethood is killed. His saying: ﴿the prophets without right, and We will say: Taste the punishment of the burning﴾: when?
* Students: On the Day of Resurrection.
* The Shaykh: On the Day of Resurrection? Or also in the grave. The saying here, ﴿We will say: Taste the punishment of the burning﴾, is intended as humiliation and degradation. Otherwise they will taste the punishment of the burning whether it is said to them or not, but it is by way of humiliation. Consider the great humiliation and mockery in His saying: ﴿Taste! Indeed, you are the mighty, the noble!﴾ [al-Dukhan 49]. It is said to him while he is being punished in the Fire: ﴿Taste! Indeed, you are the mighty, the noble!﴾ as humiliation for him, meaning: your might and nobility did not benefit you.

﴿We will say: Taste the punishment of the burning﴾. * In this verse there are benefits. First: the affirmation of the hearing of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, by His saying: ﴿Allah has certainly heard﴾ [Al 'Imran 181]. Hearing here means the perception of sound even if it is faint, and what is meant here is threat. It should be known that the scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, divided the hearing of Allah into two types. The first: in the sense of responding (istijabah). The second: in the sense of perceiving sounds. As for hearing in the sense of responding, it is common in the Qur'an, including His saying: ﴿And do not be like those who said, "We hear," but they do not hear﴾ [al-Anfal 21]. "We hear" means with our ears; "but they do not hear" means they do not respond. And He said: ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able, and listen﴾ [al-Taghabun 16]: "listen" means listen in the sense of responding. And among it is His saying about Ibrahim: ﴿Indeed, my Lord is the Hearer of supplication﴾ [Ibrahim 39], meaning the one who responds to supplication. It is known that this kind or type of hearing is one of the attributes of action (sifat fi'liyyah), because it is connected to His will.

The second type of hearing is the hearing of perception. They said that it divides into three categories. This type, which is the perception of sounds, divides into three categories: one intended as threat, one intended as affirmation/support, and one intended to show the comprehensiveness and totality of Allah's hearing.

As for what is intended as affirmation/support, it is like His saying to Musa: ﴿He said, "Fear not. Indeed, I am with you both; I hear and I see"﴾ [Ta-Ha 46]. The meaning of hearing here is support.

One might say: threat is also in relation to Pharaoh. As for what is intended as threat, it is like this verse: ﴿Allah has certainly heard the statement of those who said, "Indeed, Allah is poor and we are rich"﴾ [Al 'Imran 181].

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verses 181–182 (part 2 of 3):

As for the type of statement that is meant to show the comprehensiveness and vastness of God's knowledge, there is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Allah has certainly heard the statement of the woman who argues with you concerning her husband﴾ [al-Mujadilah 1]. 'Aisha said: "Praise be to Allah, Whose hearing encompasses all voices. I was in a corner of the room, and some of her speech was hidden from me. Glory be to Allah! Allah, Exalted is He, is above His Throne, above the seven heavens, and He hears the words of this woman."[[Narrated by al-Nasa'i in al-Mujtaba (3460) and Ibn Majah (188), from 'Aisha.]] ﴿Allah has certainly heard the statement of the woman who argues with you concerning her husband and complains to Allah, and Allah hears your mutual dialogue﴾. The Messenger was conversing, and the woman was hearing him. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing﴾ [al-Baqarah 181].

* Student: ﴿Did they witness their creation? Their testimony will be recorded﴾ [al-Zukhruf 19]; it means the angels (...).
* Shaykh: They conceal it.
* Student: Good. And ﴿and they will be questioned﴾: are the angels the ones (...)?
* Shaykh: That is possible. The matter is that it is the angels, or that Allah questions them, because the questioning is mentioned in another verse, that Allah Himself questions.
* Student: Shaykh, the hadith: "Allah has never given ear to anything as He gives ear to a Prophet with a beautiful voice who chants the Quran aloud",[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (7544) and Muslim (792/233), the wording being Muslim's, from Abu Hurairah.]] how (...)?
* Shaykh: The meaning of "ma adhina" is "ma sami'a" (he did not hear). "Adhina" with the meaning of "sami'a" is what the scholars have said.
* Student: Is there no affirmation in it (...)?
* Shaykh: No, there is interpretation in it, never anything else. That is why it is followed by the preposition "lam" (adhina lahu).
* Student: The killing here, the threat, includes the killing of the Prophets and the Messengers. We have always been taught that every Messenger is a Prophet but not every Prophet is a Messenger, so what is meant by the Prophets?
* Shaykh: Yes indeed. I gave you a rule, my brothers, earlier: the Prophets mentioned in the Quran are Messengers. You will not find a Prophet mentioned in the Quran who is not a Messenger. I also cited to you a proof from the Quran: ﴿And We certainly sent Messengers before you; among them are those We have related to you and among them are those We have not related to you﴾ [Ghafir 78]. If this holds, the matter is clear. If it does not hold, we say that what is meant by the Prophets are those who were not given a new law to convey to the people.
* Student: Regarding the hearing of the earth (...), it hears by itself (...), Allah makes it speak, Glory be to Him?
* Shaykh: Yes, correct.
* Student: Is it not analogizing the affirmation of hearing for a human to Allah, Glory be to Him?
* Shaykh: No, we do not mean analogy. We mean that a thing may hear even if it has no ear, do you understand? And it may see even if it has no eye either, because the earth will report what was done upon it.
* Student: That is to say (...) the Prophets, Shaykh. That is, when it is said "the Prophets" in the Quran, what is meant or intended by (...) the killing of the Prophets (...)? That is, now if it is said "the Prophet was killed," it becomes "the Messenger was killed." But if it is said "the Messenger was killed," does that not necessarily require that the Prophet was killed?
* Shaykh: No. Whoever kills a Messenger kills a Prophet, because the Prophet is of lower rank than the Messenger. But whoever kills the Prophets, if it were said, for example, "those who kill the Prophets" outside the Quran, we would say that it does not include their killing of the Messengers, because the Messenger is more specific.
* Student: Was Idris, peace be upon him, a Prophet before Nuh?
* Shaykh: No, brother. There was no Prophet before Nuh at all. Idris was from the Children of Israel; the apparent meaning from the context of the verses is that he was from the Children of Israel. That is why there exists, I have seen a chart of the Prophets, where it is written "Idris before Nuh," and this is wrong, undoubtedly wrong. ﴿We have revealed to you as We revealed to Nuh and the Prophets after him﴾ [al-Nisa' 163]. And in the hadith of intercession, they come to Nuh and say: "You are the first Messenger Allah sent to the people of the earth."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3340) and Muslim (194/327), from Abu Hurairah.]]
* Student: Many, Shaykh, mention Idris before Nuh.
* Shaykh: That is wrong. Many... not...
* * *
* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿That is for what your hands have put forward, and that Allah is not ever unjust to the servants. (182) Those who said, "Indeed, Allah has taken our covenant that we not believe a messenger until he brings us an offering which fire consumes." Say, "There have already come to you messengers before me with clear proofs and with what you [now] speak. So why did you kill them, if you should be truthful?" (183) And if they deny you, [so were] messengers denied before you who came with clear proofs and written scriptures and the illuminating Book﴾ [Al 'Imran 182–184].
* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Allah has certainly heard the statement of those who said, "Indeed, Allah is poor, and we are rich." We will record what they have said and their killing of the Prophets without right, and We will say, "Taste the punishment of the burning fire."﴾ Do you think we have taken the benefits?
* Student: One benefit.
* Shaykh: Only that, and it is the hearing, and we mentioned its types.
* Among the benefits of this verse: the demonstration of the insolence and aggression of the Jews, in that they transgressed against the Lord, Exalted is He, by describing Him as poor.
* Among its benefits: because of the severity of their arrogance and rebellion, they did not limit themselves to describing Allah as poor, but said, "We are rich." Thus they affirmed perfection for themselves and deficiency for Allah, Exalted is He.
* Among the benefits of this verse: the affirmation of writing for Allah, in His saying: ﴿We will record what they have said﴾. However, we mentioned that what is meant is by His command, and that the angels are the ones who write. We cited a proof for this, which is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Or do they think that We do not hear their secrets and their private conversations? Yes, and Our messengers are with them, recording﴾ [al-Zukhruf 80].
* Among the benefits of this verse: just as the Jews transgressed against Allah, they also transgressed against the Messengers of Allah, killing the Prophets without right. Thus their aggression extended to the station of Tawhid and the station of prophethood. They did not fulfill the testimony that there is no god but Allah, nor that the Messengers of Allah are Messengers of Him.
* Among the benefits of this verse: the affirmation of speech for Allah, Exalted is He, in His saying: ﴿and We will say, "Taste the punishment of the burning fire"﴾. Allah, Glory be to Him, has been established as speaking by the consensus of the Salaf (the early generations): He speaks and utters speech in a real manner, with letters and an audible voice, and this speech is an attribute, one of His attributes, not created. The Mu'tazilah and the Jahmiyyah said: it is a creation of His creations; it is His speech, but it is a created thing among His creations. The Ash'arites and those who resemble them said: He does not speak with a speech that is heard. His speech is the speech subsisting in His essence, and what is heard is an expression of it or a narration, and it is created. The heard is created. Ibn al-Qayyim mentioned that Shaykh al-Islam, may Allah have mercy on him, refuted this view in ninety aspects in a treatise called al-Tis'iniyyah (the Ninety), and I think it is found in al-Fatawa.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that these people will taste the punishment with physical pain and psychological pain. This is from His saying: "and taste the punishment of the burning fire." In the burning there is physical pain, and in His saying "taste" there is psychological pain, because this is rebuke and humiliation. The command here is for rebuke and humiliation.
* Among the benefits of this verse: the refutation of those who say that the people of the Fire do not taste the punishment, because their bodies are affected by the fire and conform to it, so they no longer taste pain. We refute them with His saying: "taste the punishment of the burning fire."
* Among its benefits: the demonstration of the power of Allah, Exalted is He, in that these people are burned and their skins are roasted, and whenever their skins are roasted, they are replaced with other skins, and yet they do not die. Although such burning, if it struck anyone in this world, would destroy him, they do not die, as Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿They will neither die therein nor live﴾ [Ta-Ha 74]. So they do not die and find rest, nor do they live a pleasant life.

Then Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿That is for what your hands have put forward﴾. This is the completion of His saying: "and taste the punishment of the burning fire." That is, it will be said to them, as an increase in rebuke, regret, and anguish: ﴿That﴾, meaning: what has befallen them of punishment and rebuke. The thing referred to is what preceded in His saying: "and taste the punishment of the burning fire." Here He said ﴿That﴾, although He is speaking about a group, and He used the singular second-person kaf (the particle of address). This is because we have already learned that the demonstrative noun (ism al-isharah) is according to what is pointed to, and the kaf is according to the one addressed, in the standard language. Or it is with a fatha on the kaf for a masculine singular, and with a kasra for a feminine singular, or it is with a fatha on the kaf in all cases. All of these are dialects, but the most common is that it follows the one addressed. I think you have not fully grasped this matter, the difference between what is pointed to and what is addressed. Have you fully grasped it? The demonstrative noun follows what?
* Student: It follows what is pointed to, and the kaf of address takes into account the one addressed.
* Shaykh: It takes into account the one addressed. If you address two people, pointing to women, what do I say?
* Student: Dhanikuma.
* Shaykh: Wrong.
* Student: Dhanik.
* Shaykh: No, wrong. Tilkuma.
* Student: No, Shaykh, two, Shaykh.
* Shaykh: Yes. You address two people, pointing to women? Tilkuma, correct. In any case, there is no need to repeat it, because it is well known and only needs to be written down. Someone writes the demonstrative and the kaf, and he himself converts it from this to that.

He said: ﴿That is for what your hands have put forward﴾, that is, because of, so the ba' here is causal, and "ma" is a relative pronoun meaning "alladhi" (that which), that is, "for that which." His saying ﴿your hands have put forward﴾ means in the world. The hands here refer to themselves, but the deed or what was sent forward is attributed to the hands, because the hands are most commonly the place of striking and doing. Otherwise, it is well known that their hands, tongues, and feet, all their powers, have worked in polytheism.

He said: ﴿and that Allah is not ever unjust to the servants﴾. Here "that" is with a fatha, conjoined to "ma" in His saying ﴿for what [your hands] have put forward﴾. That is, "and that is because Allah is not unjust to the servants."

As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿and that Allah is not ever unjust﴾, "dhallam" is in the form of intensification (mubalaghah), but at the same time it is in the form of attribution (nisbah). The difference between them is that the form of intensification indicates abundance, whereas attribution includes both abundance and scarcity. So is the meaning here the form of intensification or attribution?
* Students: Attribution.
* Shaykh: The meaning is attribution. Why? Because if we said the meaning is the form of intensification, then what is negated would be the abundance of injustice, although Allah does not wrong even the weight of an atom.

Based on this, we say that "dhallam" here is attributive, meaning: not one possessed of injustice, not one possessed of injustice, just as you say: so-and-so is not a carpenter, meaning he is not possessed of carpentry, that is, he is not attributed to carpenters.

His saying ﴿to the servants﴾: "'ibad" is the plural of "'abd," and "'abd" is a singular noun, one of the words with the most plurals; it has many plural forms, just as "shaykh" is a singular noun with many plurals, reaching about ten. The servants here refer to the servants in the sense of creation (kawnan), that is, He does not wrong any of the servants in terms of creation. We said "kawnan" to rule out that what is meant is the servants in the legal sense, namely those who worship Allah. This is because Allah does not wrong either the disbeliever or the believer; each is recompensed according to his deeds. So servanthood in this verse is the general servanthood that encompasses both the disbeliever and the believer. Allah does not wrong a disbeliever, nor does He wrong a believer; He recompenses every person according to his deeds.

* Among the benefits of this verse, first: the affirmation of causes. From where is this taken? From His saying: ﴿for what your hands have put forward﴾.
* Among its benefits also: the negation of injustice from Allah, from His saying: ﴿and that Allah is not ever unjust to the servants﴾. Here we pause to clarify that Allah, Glory be to Him, is described by affirmation and by negation. As for affirmation, Allah, Exalted is He, described Himself by affirming every attribute of perfection; every attribute of perfection is affirmed for Allah. And what is the criterion of perfection? Is it our deficient intellects, or is the criterion of perfection the texts of the Book and the Sunnah? The second, the second is the criterion. That is why we do not judge Allah by saying: this is an attribute befitting Him and this is an attribute unbefitting Him. Rather, the reference in this is to the Book and the Sunnah for the details, whereas in general the intellect indicates that the Lord must be perfect. As for the negated attributes, they are not meant as mere negation, but the meaning is the absence of this attribute because the perfection of its opposite is established. So when He negates being unjust to the servants, that is because of the perfection of His justice; when He negates drowsiness or sleep, that is because of the perfection of His life and self-subsistence; when He negates weariness reaching Him, that is because of the perfection of His strength; and so on.

We must know that there cannot be in the attributes of Allah a pure negation. Pay attention to this rule, O people! There is no pure negation in the attributes of Allah. The proof is the saying of Allah, Exalted is He: ﴿And to Allah belongs the highest description﴾ [al-Nahl 60]. A pure negation is not the highest description. The highest description means the most perfect, supreme attribute, and pure negation is nonexistence, and nonexistence is not a thing, let alone a supreme attribute. Second: a bare negation may be due to the incapacity of the one described, or it may be due to his not being capable of the thing negated. It may be due to incapacity, or it may be due to his not being capable of it. That means we negated this thing from him because he is incapable, he cannot do this thing that we negated from him. And it may be because he is not capable of this thing. For example, if someone says: so-and-so is a "huBayyib" man. A huBayyib does not wrong people and does not transgress against them. What do we understand from this statement, that he does not wrong people or transgress against them? It is his incapacity; that is why we said "huBayyib." "HuBayyib" among people is a diminutive word that also carries contempt. This is like the saying of the poet:

A tribe that does not betray a covenant,
and does not wrong people by a grain of mustard.

When Adam hears such a statement, what does he say? Is it praise or blame? You see him saying: they do not betray a covenant; they can never betray an agreement, and they can never wrong people?
* Student: Blame.
* Shaykh: Blame? Subhan Allah! If I say to you: you do not betray agreements and you do not wrong anyone, what would this be?
* Student: This is praise.
* Shaykh: Praise. That is, when it was said about you, it became praise, and when it was said about the tribe, it became blame. Subhan Allah!
* Student: This is blame.
* Shaykh: From where did we take that it is blame?
* Student: (...) his saying: "qubayyilah" (a small tribe).
* Shaykh: Diminutive.
* Student: The second: they do not wrong with their covenant; that they, because of their incapacity, do not wrong people.
* Shaykh: We understood that it is blame only from the diminutive form, and the diminutive in origin indicates belittling. Is that so? In any case, it is not possible for there to be a pure negation in the attributes of Allah. A negation may, if it does not include perfection, be due to lack of capability. That is, what was negated of Him is not this attribute because of its perfection, but because He is unable. The scholars gave an example of this by saying: "my wall does not wrong," the wall does not wrong. Is this praise?
* Students: No.
* Shaykh: Why? Because it is not capable at all. If it wanted to wrong, it could not. Is that so? So take this rule: there is no pure negation in the attributes of Allah, Exalted is He. Rather, everything Allah negates of Himself includes a perfection. This is the rule.
* Among the benefits of this verse: that Allah, Exalted is He, informs about what He informs about of His attributes to reassure creation; from His saying: ﴿and that Allah is not ever unjust to the servants﴾, so that a person may be reassured that he will only be recompensed for his deeds: if good, then good, and if evil, then evil.
* Among its benefits: the permissibility of applying a part to the whole when there is an indication pointing to it. From where do we take it? The permissibility of applying a part to the whole when there is an indication pointing to it? The verse we have before us?
* Student: (...) "to the servants"?
* Shaykh: No.
* Student: His saying: ﴿your hands﴾, perhaps it repels him, for example.

**Shaykh:** Her words, ﴿for what your hands have sent forward﴾, mean "for what you have sent forward." The hand is a part of a person, but the context shows that the intended meaning is the whole, that is, "for what you have sent forward." A parallel to this in the attributes of God is His words: ﴿Do they not see that We have created for them, from what Our hands have made, livestock?﴾ [Yasin 71], such as camels. God said ﴿from what Our hands have made﴾. Shall we say that God created the camels with His hand, as He created Adam? No. We say ﴿from what Our hands have made﴾ means "from what We have made," because God did not create the camels, for example, with His hand. So the intended meaning is "from what We have made." But this does not mean that the verse contains no indication that God has a hand. Rather, it does indicate that God, the Mighty and Majestic, has a hand.

**Student:** Concerning His words, Exalted is He, ﴿and We will say, "Taste the punishment of the burning."﴾ The speaker is not the angels. It is the human being who...

**Shaykh:** Yes. What is the evidence?

**Student:** His words, ﴿and those who disbelieved are driven﴾...

**Shaykh:** ﴿Those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups, until, when they reach it, its gates will be opened, and its keepers will say to them, "Did there not come to you messengers from among you reciting to you the verses of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this day of yours?" They will say, "Yes, but the word of punishment has come into effect upon the disbelievers." It will be said, "Enter the gates of Hell, to abide therein."﴾ [Az-Zumar 71–72].

**Student:** ﴿It will be said, "Enter..."﴾

**Another student:** ﴿And those in the Fire will say to the keepers of Hell, "Call upon your Lord to lighten for us a day of the punishment." They will say, "Did there not used to come to you your messengers with clear evidence?"﴾ [Ghafir 49–50]. The rebuke comes along with the punishment.

**Shaykh:** Even from God, the Mighty and Majestic. In Surat al-Mu'minun: ﴿He will say, "Remain in it [in humiliation], and do not speak to Me."﴾ [Al-Mu'minun 108].

**Student:** (...)

**Shaykh:** Yes, this is our evidence. ﴿We shall record﴾ has evidence, which is His words: ﴿Or do they think that We do not hear their secrets and their private conversations? Yes, and Our messengers are with them, recording.﴾ [Az-Zukhruf 80], and ﴿No! Rather, you deny the Recompense. But indeed, over you are guardians, noble and recording.﴾ [Al-Infitar 9–11]. In any case, investigate. I agree with you that there is a possibility that the intended meaning is the angels, ﴿and We will say, "Taste the punishment of the burning,"﴾ because the angels...

**Student:** "And We will say," with the nun and the ya' (...) in the Hereafter, on the tongue of the angels.

**Shaykh:** Yes, (...) In any case, if evidence is found, it is to be accepted wholeheartedly.

**Student:** Shaykh, did we not say that the Jews transgressed against the messengers just as they transgressed against God?

**Shaykh:** No. Regarding God, the meaning of "against God" is: concerning His right.

**Student:** Shaykh, does this give support to those who say that ﴿That is for what your hands have sent forward﴾ is figurative (majaz) in language?

**Shaykh:** O brother, may God bless you, whoever said it said it, because they hold that words have an inherent meaning (ma'na dhati). As for those who say that words have no inherent meaning, but their meaning depends on the context, they do not have figurative language (majaz). So they say, for example, ﴿Lower to them the wing of humility﴾ contains no figurative language, because it is well known that humility does not have a literal wing. Rather, the intended meaning is: do not raise yourself up. A bird's habit is to rise, but you should be humble toward them until you lower yourself. The context is what determines this.

**Student:** How, Shaykh, do we respond to them (...) they say here some (...)

**Shaykh:** Yes, yes. We say: the Arabic language expresses the part by the whole and the whole by the part. ﴿They put their fingers into their ears﴾, but not every finger goes into the ear.

* * *

**Student:** I seek refuge with God from the accursed Satan. ﴿Those who said, "Indeed, God has taken our covenant that we not believe a messenger until he brings us an offering which fire consumes." Say, "There have certainly come to you messengers before me with clear proofs and with what you [now] mention. So why did you kill them, if you should be truthful?" And if they deny you, [O Muhammad] – [so were] messengers denied before you who came with clear proofs and written scriptures and the enlightening Book. Every soul will taste death, and you will only receive your full compensation on the Day of Resurrection. So whoever is drawn away from the Fire and admitted into Paradise has attained success. And what is the life of this world except the enjoyment of delusion.﴾ [Al 'Imran 183–185].

**Shaykh:** I seek refuge with God from the accursed Satan. God, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿God has heard the saying of those who said, "Indeed, God is poor and we are rich."﴾ to the end of the verse. Who are these speakers?

**Student:** The Jews.

**Shaykh:** Do you remember anything else they said about God that was a defect?

**Student:** Yes. They said, "The hand of God is chained."

**Shaykh:** Meaning what?

**Student:** Stingy.

**Shaykh:** That is, stingy. And anything else?

**Student:** They said that God, Glorified and Exalted, when He created the heavens and the earth, rested.

**Shaykh:** He grew tired and then rested. Good. As for His words, ﴿We shall record what they have said﴾, what is meant by the recording? Does God record it with His hand?

**Student:** The intended meaning is the angels, and it is attributed to God because they are God's soldiers.

**Shaykh:** What is the evidence that the intended meaning is the recording of the angels?

**Student:** His words, Exalted is He: ﴿Or do they think that We do not hear their secrets and their private conversations? Yes, and Our messengers are with them, recording.﴾

**Shaykh:** Well done.

He said: ﴿and their killing of the prophets without right﴾. Is there any right in killing the prophets, so that the qualifier "without right" is needed to exclude it? That is, does the qualifier "without right" mean that killing the prophets sometimes happens with right and sometimes without it?

**Student:** (...)

**Shaykh:** Indeed. Why did He say "without right"?

**Student:** Because it actually was without right.

**Shaykh:** Yes?

**Student:** Because the reality is that it was without right.

**Shaykh:** That is, to state the reality?

**Student:** Yes.

**Shaykh:** Yes.

**Student:** A descriptive qualifier that reveals the reality (sifa kashifa).

**Shaykh:** A descriptive qualifier that reveals the reality. "Revealing" means that it makes the reality clear. Is there also another benefit besides this?

**Student:** Emphasis?

**Shaykh:** No.

**Student:** So that it is not thought that they killed them with right. Lest someone say that they killed the prophets with right, God emphasized that their killing was without right.

**Shaykh:** Yes.

**Student:** It records against these people and confirms that their situation contains no right.

**Shaykh:** Yes. That is, its meaning is to intensify the abhorrence of them, or to censure them harshly, because they killed them without right.

His words: ﴿Taste the punishment of the burning.﴾ What is the command here intended for?

**Student:** It is intended here as rebuke.

**Shaykh:** And humiliation. Do you have evidence that such a command is intended as humiliation?

**Student:** Yes, from His words: ﴿Taste! Indeed you are the mighty, the noble.﴾ [Ad-Dukhan 49].

**Shaykh:** Yes, ﴿Taste! Indeed you are the mighty, the noble.﴾ Some contemporary scholars have said that the Fire does not burn its people, and for this reason they neither die in it nor live. So does the verse contain anything that refutes them?

**Student:** Yes. His words, ﴿Taste the punishment of the burning﴾, and that necessitates that they continue to taste the punishment and do not die.

**Shaykh:** And they are burned.

**Student:** They are burned, and their skins are scorched, then God replaces their skins with other skins.

**Shaykh:** And they do not die, unlike them in this world, for when a person is burned in this world, he dies.

What is the meaning of His words: ﴿for what your hands have sent forward﴾?

**Student:** That is, for what your hands have earned.

**Shaykh:** But the "bi" here?

**Student:** The "ba'" is causal (lil-sababiyya).

**Shaykh:** The "ba'" is causal. Does it follow from the verse that God's acts are accompanied by wisdom?

**Student:** Yes, because the "ba'" is causal.

**Shaykh:** Everything that is causal indicates causation (ʿillah), and the cause is wisdom.

His words: ﴿and that God is not ever unjust to the servants.﴾ Is "ظلام" here an intensive form (sighat al-mubalagha) or an attributive form (nisba)?

**Student:** An intensive form.

**Shaykh:** An intensive form. That means God does a little injustice but not much?

**Student:** "ظلام" is an intensive form in terms of its pattern, that is all.

**Shaykh:** Yes, "ظلام" is an intensive form in its pattern, that is correct. But this pattern also comes in the attributive sense. One says: "نجار" (carpenter), "حداد" (blacksmith), "بنّاء" (builder). So is it attributive here or intensive?

**Student:** Attributive.

**Shaykh:** Attributive, good. Because if we said it was intensive, then what is negated would be the multitude of injustice.

Is "العبيد" (the servants) here in the specific sense or the general sense?

**Student:** The general sense.

**Shaykh:** The general sense. That means God does not wrong even the disbeliever?

**Student:** Yes.

**Shaykh:** Correct?

**Students:** Yes.

**Shaykh:** Good. Then God, Exalted, said: ﴿those who said﴾. This is a qualifier of His words: ﴿God has heard the saying of those who said﴾.

**Student:** The benefits, Shaykh.

**Shaykh:** From where? Benefits of what?

**Student:** From ﴿That is for what your hands have sent forward﴾. We took four benefits yesterday.

**Shaykh:** Where did we stop?

**Student:** The permissibility of ruling on the whole based on a part when (...) comes after it, which is taken from His words: ﴿for what your hands have sent forward﴾.

**Shaykh:** Then complete it.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse, ﴿That is for what your hands have sent forward﴾: the negation of injustice from God, by His words: ﴿and that God is not ever unjust to the servants.﴾

* And among its benefits: the possibility of injustice from God, were it not that God negated it from Himself, by His words: ﴿and that God is not ever unjust﴾. For if injustice were impossible for Him, it would not be proper for Him, the Mighty and Majestic, to praise Himself with it, since one is praised for something only when abstaining from it is a matter of choice. But if it were impossible for Him, there would be no benefit in praising Himself with it. Is this correct?

Based on this benefit, does it contain a refutation of whom?

**Student:** The Ash'arites (al-Ash'ariyya).

**Shaykh:** No.

**Student:** The Jabriyya (those who deny real human choice).

**Shaykh:** No. It refutes the Jahmiyya (a sect that denied God's attributes). The Jahmiyya say that injustice is impossible for God, impossible in its very essence, not because God negated it from Himself. For they say: whatever He does, He does in His own domain, and whoever acts in his own domain may do as he wishes. So injustice, for them, is impossible in its essence, as Ibn al-Qayyim said in the Nuniyya:

*And injustice, to them, is impossible in its very essence* ∗∗∗ .......................

We say: injustice is not impossible for God. If God willed to do injustice, He would do it. But He negated it from Himself, praising Himself by that. For this reason He said in the hadith qudsi: "O My servants, I have forbidden injustice for Myself."[[Recorded by Muslim (2577/55) from the hadith of Abu Dharr.]] This indicates that it is possible for Him, but He does not do it.

If someone says: it has come in a hadith from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "Indeed God, if He were to punish the inhabitants of His heavens and His earth, He would punish them while not being unjust to them."[[Recorded by Abu Dawud (4699) and Ibn Majah (77) from the hadith of Ubayy ibn Ka'b and Zayd ibn Thabit.]]

The answer: We say there is no contradiction between this hadith and the verse. For if God punished them, it would not be possible for Him to punish them while being unjust to them. Therefore He punishes only those who deserve punishment, and so the hadith agrees with the verse. Or another explanation may be given: if God punished the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth, He would punish them while not being unjust to them, if He wished to hold His servants to account strictly. For whoever is strictly held to account is punished, because if God were to hold them strictly to account, one single blessing from His blessings would outweigh all their deeds, and then they would deserve to be punished. So in this hadith there are two interpretations. The first: He punishes them while not being unjust to them, that is, He punishes them only for a sin, and so it agrees with the verse. The second: what is meant is strict reckoning, the strict scrutiny of the account, because if God, Glorified and Exalted, were to scrutinize them strictly, one single blessing from His blessings would encompass all their deeds, and they would be left with no credit.

If someone says: this is a negative attribute, as they call it. Do negative attributes exist among God's attributes?

The answer: No. But what is meant by negative attributes is the affirmation of the perfection of their opposite. He does not do injustice, not because He is unable to do it, but because of the perfection of His justice.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Allah has certainly heard the statement of those who said, "Indeed, Allah is poor and we are rich." We will record what they have said and their killing of the prophets without right, and We will say, "Taste the punishment of the burning."﴾

First, we speak about the recitations (qira'at) found in the verse. He says: there are recitations for it. The one we have now is ﴿سَنَكْتُبُ﴾ with a nun, and ﴿نَقُولُ﴾ with a nun as well. On the basis of this reading, (ما) is the direct object (maf'ul bihi), and (قتل) is conjoined to the direct object, and what is conjoined to a accusative noun is accusative.

On the second reading, ﴿سَيُكْتُبُ مَا قَالُوا﴾, (ما) is the deputy subject (naib fa'il), in the nominative, built on sukun in a place of nominative. Then (قتل) is conjoined to a nominative word, the deputy subject, so it is in the nominative. Accordingly, ﴿قَتْلَهُمُ﴾ is governed by which reading? By (يُكتب). It is not permissible to read: "We will record what they have said and their killing (qatluhum)," no. (قتل) cannot be nominative unless we read ﴿سَيُكْتُبُ﴾.

As for ﴿الْأَنْبِيَاءَ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ وَيَقُولُ﴾: does ﴿يَقُولُ﴾ agree with which of the two readings, or match which of the two? ﴿سَيُكْتُبُ﴾ or ﴿سَنَكْتُبُ﴾?
* The students: ﴿سَيُكْتُبُ﴾.
* The Shaykh: ﴿سَيُكْتُبُ﴾, and ﴿وَيَقُولُ ذُوقُوا عَذَابَ الْحَرِيقِ﴾.

As for ﴿الْأَنْبِيَاءَ﴾, there are two readings: ﴿الْأَنْبِئَاءَ﴾, and the second: ﴿الْأَنْبِيَاءَ﴾ with a ya, like ﴿النَّبِيِّينَ﴾ and ﴿النَّبِيئِينَ﴾. On the reading ﴿الْأَنْبِئَاءَ﴾, it derives from (النبأ), with a hamza, which means "news." On the reading with ya, it derives from (النُّبُوّة) or (النَّبْوَة), which means "elevation."

Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿Allah has certainly heard the statement of those who said﴾. Allah has emphasized this report with three emphatics. The first is the implied oath, since the lam here falls in the answer to an oath. The second is (قد). The third is the (lam) in His saying ﴿لَقَدْ سَمِعَ﴾. He emphasized it, glorified and exalted is He, only to intensify the threat to these people. As for us, the believers, we know that whenever He informs us of something, it is emphasized, but He does so to threaten those who uttered this shameful statement.

﴿لَقَدْ سَمِعَ اللَّهُ قَوْلَ الَّذِينَ قَالُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ فَقِيرٌ﴾: ﴿سَمِعَ﴾ here means "perceived this statement," i.e., He heard it with hearing. We do not say "with His ear," because hearing does not necessarily imply an ear. This differs from our saying about "He istawa over the Throne" (istawa 'ala al-'arsh), where we say "in His essence," because Allah attributed the act to Himself. Here we do not say "He heard with His ear," and why? Because hearing does not necessarily entail the existence of an ear. Behold, on the Day of Resurrection the earth will ﴿relate its news﴾ [al-Zalzalah 4], meaning it will inform of what people did upon it or what they said upon it, even though it has no ear. The skins, hands and feet will testify on the Day of Resurrection against a person for what he did, and they have no ears. Therefore it is not permissible to say that Allah has an ear, on the basis that Allah affirmed hearing for Himself, because hearing does not necessarily entail an ear.

If someone says: "Did you not affirm for Allah an eye?"
* A student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: We do not say "yes"; we say "bala." Did you not affirm for Allah an eye?
* The students: Bala.
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed. We say "bala." If we say "na'am," it means we did not affirm it. "Bala," we did affirm it. How did we affirm it? Through the fact that He sees, or through the fact that He affirmed two eyes for Himself?
* The students: The second.
* The Shaykh: The second, yes. Had Allah not affirmed two eyes for Himself, it would not have been permissible for us to affirm the eye. For this reason, we believe that Allah speaks, but do we say "with a tongue"? Never, we do not say it, although Allah said: ﴿The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down, upon your heart, in clear Arabic language﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 193–195]. Yet we do not say "Allah has a tongue," nor "Allah has two lips," because Allah did not affirm that for Himself, and speech does not necessarily entail a tongue. The proof is that the earth relates its news, and the skins testify, and the owner of the skin says to his skin: "Why did you testify against us?" It says: ﴿Allah, who made everything speak, has made us speak﴾ [Fussilat 21], and it does not say, "I have a tongue and two lips." Therefore it is not permissible to affirm for Allah a tongue or two lips merely on the basis of affirming speech. Is it clear?

Just as it is not permissible to affirm teeth for Him, because teeth exist only for one who needs them to chew food, and we do not affirm intestines or the like for Him, because these imply deficiency, being instruments for what? For eating, and eating is impossible for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

We say: He hears. Does His hearing necessarily entail the existence of an ear? No. ﴿Allah has certainly heard the statement of those who said, "Indeed, Allah is poor"﴾. They were a group of Jews, among them a man named (Finhas). But Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in His Book, does not mention anything specific except for a reason that requires identifying the person. For this reason, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, did not mention anyone by name in the Qur'an except for one believing man and one disbelieving man only. Who is the believing man?
* Students: Zayd.
* The Shaykh: Zayd ibn Harithah: ﴿So when Zayd had completed his need from her, We married her to you﴾ [al-Ahzab 37]. And the disbelieving man?
* Students: Pharaoh.
* The Shaykh: No, no, no. From this nation?
* A student: Abu Lahab.
* The Shaykh: Abu Lahab. Others were not mentioned, because the description (al-wasf) is more beneficial due to its generality. This is one aspect. The other aspect is that the state of the specified person may change: he may be at first a wicked, rebellious, disbelieving person, then he accepts Islam and Allah accepts his repentance. If he repents and his name had been mentioned, it would remain a shame upon him even though he repented. Is it clear, brothers?

The second: that it is more general, because attaching a ruling to a description is more general than attaching it to a person. For this reason, when a ruling is attached to a specific person, it may admit of particularity. If we say it applies generally, the generality of a ruling attached to a person is not an all-encompassing generality, but an illustrative generality, meaning by analogy (qiyas). Is the speech clear? It is clear.

Therefore, in such matters, we should not identify the specific person. Even if we want to speak about a wicked newspaper, it is better not to identify it. We say, for example, "Some newspapers said," and when we mention the matter, it is understood. First, because the newspaper may change. Second, if we restrict it, the listener may understand that there is no other than this newspaper, but if we generalize and make the ruling attached to the description, it includes others. If we identify it, the listener, especially the layman who does not know how to analogize, may understand that the calamity is specific to this newspaper, for example. He does not know how to analogize. So if we make the matter attached to the description, it becomes more beneficial. This is a matter that the Qur'an indicates, and likewise the Sunnah. The Sunnah also indicates it: the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, did not say, "What is the matter with so-and-so who says such-and-such," but he said: "What is the matter with people who..." (ما بال أقوام), for the two benefits we have pointed out.

﴿Those who said, "Indeed, Allah is poor and we are rich"﴾: these are the Jews. The reason for their saying this is that Allah said: ﴿Who is it that would loan Allah a goodly loan so He will multiply it for him?﴾ [al-Baqarah 245]. "The Jews rejoiced at this, came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Muhammad, indeed your Lord has become poor, indeed your Lord has become poor." [Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim in al-Tafsir (2429) (2/460), from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both.] Because He asks us for a loan, we seek Allah's protection, and these simpletons did not know, even if they were sincere in what they claimed, and they were lying in what they claimed, even their saying that Allah has become poor, they are liars, they do not believe this. But, by way of accommodating them, we say: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, made spending in His cause like a loan to Him, to make the spender aware that he will be recompensed for it, just as the borrower is obliged to repay his loan. Thus Allah, glorified and exalted is He, made the deed for Himself like a loan, out of His grace and kindness to His servants. The Jews should not be considered strange in describing Allah with such a thing. They said: ﴿The hand of Allah is chained﴾ [al-Ma'idah 64], and they described Him with stinginess: the hand of Allah is chained, He does not spend. They also said that Allah created the heavens and the earth in six days, then became tired and rested on Saturday, and for this reason they make Saturday their day of rest. May Allah curse them; they are liars in this. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿And We created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, and no fatigue touched Us﴾ [Qaf 38].

﴿Those who said, "Indeed, Allah is poor"﴾. Would that they had stopped at this. I say: would that they had, given what follows it. Otherwise, describing Him with this description is a denial, one of the greatest denials. They said ﴿and we are rich﴾, so they made themselves more complete than Allah. They made themselves more perfect than Allah. This is the utmost of insolence. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿We will record what they have said﴾. The attribution of recording to Himself is because His soldiers record it. The proof is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿No! But you deny the Recompense. And indeed, over you are guardians, noble and recording, who know what you do﴾ [al-Infitar 9–11], and His saying, which is more explicit: ﴿Or do they think that We do not hear their secret and their private conversation? Yes [We do], and Our messengers are with them, recording﴾ [al-Zukhruf 80]. So is the recording here the recording of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, with His own hand? No, but with His angels. The angels record, and He attributed the recording of the angels to Himself, since they record by His command and they are His soldiers, just as a commander says: "I did such-and-such," while the doer is other than him; the doer is the soldiers. The king and the ruler speak of a thing attributing it to himself, because it occurred by his command and authority. So ﴿We will record what they have said﴾ by what? By Our angels. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sometimes attributes a thing to Himself while intending the angels, like His saying: ﴿Then why, when [the soul] reaches the throat, and you at that time are looking on, and We are nearer to him than you, but you do not see﴾ [al-Waqi'ah 83–85]. Nearer to him by what? By Our angels. For this reason He said ﴿but you do not see﴾, which indicates that the one who is near is in the same place, but we do not see him, and these are the angels. Among this also is His saying: ﴿And We have certainly created man, and We know what his soul whispers to him, and We are nearer to him than his jugular vein﴾ [Qaf 16]. The preponderant view regarding it is that what is meant is "nearer to him by Our angels," as evidenced by His saying: ﴿When the two receivers receive, seated on the right and on the left﴾ [Qaf 17]. This is what Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, verified in his book, in several places of his speech, including his explanation of the hadith of the Descent, which is famous and widely circulated.

He says: ﴿We will record what they have said﴾, merely to be informed of it, or for recompense? For recompense, as is evident from what comes at the end of the verse.

He said: ﴿and their killing of the prophets without right﴾. He mentioned the killing of the prophets without right, although they did not say, "We killed the prophets," but to make clear that these people transgressed against the right of Allah and against the right of His messengers and prophets, so they killed the prophets without right. It encompasses the killing of prophets and messengers, because every messenger is a prophet. His saying: ﴿and their killing of the prophets without right﴾: is the qualifier here a restrictive qualifier (qayd ihtiraz) or a descriptive qualifier (qayd kashif)?
* A student: Descriptive.
* The Shaykh: A descriptive qualifier. That is, their killing of the prophets is without right. It does not mean that the killing of the prophets is divided into right and wrong; all killing of the prophets is without right. Nevertheless, they do not kill the prophets for their persons; they kill them for what they brought of truth. Any person who comes with this prophethood is killed. His saying: ﴿the prophets without right, and We will say: Taste the punishment of the burning﴾: when?
* Students: On the Day of Resurrection.
* The Shaykh: On the Day of Resurrection? Or also in the grave. The saying here, ﴿We will say: Taste the punishment of the burning﴾, is intended as humiliation and degradation. Otherwise they will taste the punishment of the burning whether it is said to them or not, but it is by way of humiliation. Consider the great humiliation and mockery in His saying: ﴿Taste! Indeed, you are the mighty, the noble!﴾ [al-Dukhan 49]. It is said to him while he is being punished in the Fire: ﴿Taste! Indeed, you are the mighty, the noble!﴾ as humiliation for him, meaning: your might and nobility did not benefit you.

﴿We will say: Taste the punishment of the burning﴾. * In this verse there are benefits. First: the affirmation of the hearing of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, by His saying: ﴿Allah has certainly heard﴾ [Al 'Imran 181]. Hearing here means the perception of sound even if it is faint, and what is meant here is threat. It should be known that the scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, divided the hearing of Allah into two types. The first: in the sense of responding (istijabah). The second: in the sense of perceiving sounds. As for hearing in the sense of responding, it is common in the Qur'an, including His saying: ﴿And do not be like those who said, "We hear," but they do not hear﴾ [al-Anfal 21]. "We hear" means with our ears; "but they do not hear" means they do not respond. And He said: ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able, and listen﴾ [al-Taghabun 16]: "listen" means listen in the sense of responding. And among it is His saying about Ibrahim: ﴿Indeed, my Lord is the Hearer of supplication﴾ [Ibrahim 39], meaning the one who responds to supplication. It is known that this kind or type of hearing is one of the attributes of action (sifat fi'liyyah), because it is connected to His will.

The second type of hearing is the hearing of perception. They said that it divides into three categories. This type, which is the perception of sounds, divides into three categories: one intended as threat, one intended as affirmation/support, and one intended to show the comprehensiveness and totality of Allah's hearing.

As for what is intended as affirmation/support, it is like His saying to Musa: ﴿He said, "Fear not. Indeed, I am with you both; I hear and I see"﴾ [Ta-Ha 46]. The meaning of hearing here is support.

One might say: threat is also in relation to Pharaoh. As for what is intended as threat, it is like this verse: ﴿Allah has certainly heard the statement of those who said, "Indeed, Allah is poor and we are rich"﴾ [Al 'Imran 181].

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verses 181–182 (part 2 of 3):

As for the type of statement that is meant to show the comprehensiveness and vastness of God's knowledge, there is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Allah has certainly heard the statement of the woman who argues with you concerning her husband﴾ [al-Mujadilah 1]. 'Aisha said: "Praise be to Allah, Whose hearing encompasses all voices. I was in a corner of the room, and some of her speech was hidden from me. Glory be to Allah! Allah, Exalted is He, is above His Throne, above the seven heavens, and He hears the words of this woman."[[Narrated by al-Nasa'i in al-Mujtaba (3460) and Ibn Majah (188), from 'Aisha.]] ﴿Allah has certainly heard the statement of the woman who argues with you concerning her husband and complains to Allah, and Allah hears your mutual dialogue﴾. The Messenger was conversing, and the woman was hearing him. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing﴾ [al-Baqarah 181].

* Student: ﴿Did they witness their creation? Their testimony will be recorded﴾ [al-Zukhruf 19]; it means the angels (...).
* Shaykh: They conceal it.
* Student: Good. And ﴿and they will be questioned﴾: are the angels the ones (...)?
* Shaykh: That is possible. The matter is that it is the angels, or that Allah questions them, because the questioning is mentioned in another verse, that Allah Himself questions.
* Student: Shaykh, the hadith: "Allah has never given ear to anything as He gives ear to a Prophet with a beautiful voice who chants the Quran aloud",[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (7544) and Muslim (792/233), the wording being Muslim's, from Abu Hurairah.]] how (...)?
* Shaykh: The meaning of "ma adhina" is "ma sami'a" (he did not hear). "Adhina" with the meaning of "sami'a" is what the scholars have said.
* Student: Is there no affirmation in it (...)?
* Shaykh: No, there is interpretation in it, never anything else. That is why it is followed by the preposition "lam" (adhina lahu).
* Student: The killing here, the threat, includes the killing of the Prophets and the Messengers. We have always been taught that every Messenger is a Prophet but not every Prophet is a Messenger, so what is meant by the Prophets?
* Shaykh: Yes indeed. I gave you a rule, my brothers, earlier: the Prophets mentioned in the Quran are Messengers. You will not find a Prophet mentioned in the Quran who is not a Messenger. I also cited to you a proof from the Quran: ﴿And We certainly sent Messengers before you; among them are those We have related to you and among them are those We have not related to you﴾ [Ghafir 78]. If this holds, the matter is clear. If it does not hold, we say that what is meant by the Prophets are those who were not given a new law to convey to the people.
* Student: Regarding the hearing of the earth (...), it hears by itself (...), Allah makes it speak, Glory be to Him?
* Shaykh: Yes, correct.
* Student: Is it not analogizing the affirmation of hearing for a human to Allah, Glory be to Him?
* Shaykh: No, we do not mean analogy. We mean that a thing may hear even if it has no ear, do you understand? And it may see even if it has no eye either, because the earth will report what was done upon it.
* Student: That is to say (...) the Prophets, Shaykh. That is, when it is said "the Prophets" in the Quran, what is meant or intended by (...) the killing of the Prophets (...)? That is, now if it is said "the Prophet was killed," it becomes "the Messenger was killed." But if it is said "the Messenger was killed," does that not necessarily require that the Prophet was killed?
* Shaykh: No. Whoever kills a Messenger kills a Prophet, because the Prophet is of lower rank than the Messenger. But whoever kills the Prophets, if it were said, for example, "those who kill the Prophets" outside the Quran, we would say that it does not include their killing of the Messengers, because the Messenger is more specific.
* Student: Was Idris, peace be upon him, a Prophet before Nuh?
* Shaykh: No, brother. There was no Prophet before Nuh at all. Idris was from the Children of Israel; the apparent meaning from the context of the verses is that he was from the Children of Israel. That is why there exists, I have seen a chart of the Prophets, where it is written "Idris before Nuh," and this is wrong, undoubtedly wrong. ﴿We have revealed to you as We revealed to Nuh and the Prophets after him﴾ [al-Nisa' 163]. And in the hadith of intercession, they come to Nuh and say: "You are the first Messenger Allah sent to the people of the earth."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3340) and Muslim (194/327), from Abu Hurairah.]]
* Student: Many, Shaykh, mention Idris before Nuh.
* Shaykh: That is wrong. Many... not...
* * *
* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿That is for what your hands have put forward, and that Allah is not ever unjust to the servants. (182) Those who said, "Indeed, Allah has taken our covenant that we not believe a messenger until he brings us an offering which fire consumes." Say, "There have already come to you messengers before me with clear proofs and with what you [now] speak. So why did you kill them, if you should be truthful?" (183) And if they deny you, [so were] messengers denied before you who came with clear proofs and written scriptures and the illuminating Book﴾ [Al 'Imran 182–184].
