* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Allah has certainly heard the statement of those who said, "Indeed, Allah is poor, and we are rich." We will record what they have said and their killing of the Prophets without right, and We will say, "Taste the punishment of the burning fire."﴾ Do you think we have taken the benefits?
* Student: One benefit.
* Shaykh: Only that, and it is the hearing, and we mentioned its types.
* Among the benefits of this verse: the demonstration of the insolence and aggression of the Jews, in that they transgressed against the Lord, Exalted is He, by describing Him as poor.
* Among its benefits: because of the severity of their arrogance and rebellion, they did not limit themselves to describing Allah as poor, but said, "We are rich." Thus they affirmed perfection for themselves and deficiency for Allah, Exalted is He.
* Among the benefits of this verse: the affirmation of writing for Allah, in His saying: ﴿We will record what they have said﴾. However, we mentioned that what is meant is by His command, and that the angels are the ones who write. We cited a proof for this, which is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Or do they think that We do not hear their secrets and their private conversations? Yes, and Our messengers are with them, recording﴾ [al-Zukhruf 80].
* Among the benefits of this verse: just as the Jews transgressed against Allah, they also transgressed against the Messengers of Allah, killing the Prophets without right. Thus their aggression extended to the station of Tawhid and the station of prophethood. They did not fulfill the testimony that there is no god but Allah, nor that the Messengers of Allah are Messengers of Him.
* Among the benefits of this verse: the affirmation of speech for Allah, Exalted is He, in His saying: ﴿and We will say, "Taste the punishment of the burning fire"﴾. Allah, Glory be to Him, has been established as speaking by the consensus of the Salaf (the early generations): He speaks and utters speech in a real manner, with letters and an audible voice, and this speech is an attribute, one of His attributes, not created. The Mu'tazilah and the Jahmiyyah said: it is a creation of His creations; it is His speech, but it is a created thing among His creations. The Ash'arites and those who resemble them said: He does not speak with a speech that is heard. His speech is the speech subsisting in His essence, and what is heard is an expression of it or a narration, and it is created. The heard is created. Ibn al-Qayyim mentioned that Shaykh al-Islam, may Allah have mercy on him, refuted this view in ninety aspects in a treatise called al-Tis'iniyyah (the Ninety), and I think it is found in al-Fatawa.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that these people will taste the punishment with physical pain and psychological pain. This is from His saying: "and taste the punishment of the burning fire." In the burning there is physical pain, and in His saying "taste" there is psychological pain, because this is rebuke and humiliation. The command here is for rebuke and humiliation.
* Among the benefits of this verse: the refutation of those who say that the people of the Fire do not taste the punishment, because their bodies are affected by the fire and conform to it, so they no longer taste pain. We refute them with His saying: "taste the punishment of the burning fire."
* Among its benefits: the demonstration of the power of Allah, Exalted is He, in that these people are burned and their skins are roasted, and whenever their skins are roasted, they are replaced with other skins, and yet they do not die. Although such burning, if it struck anyone in this world, would destroy him, they do not die, as Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿They will neither die therein nor live﴾ [Ta-Ha 74]. So they do not die and find rest, nor do they live a pleasant life.

Then Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿That is for what your hands have put forward﴾. This is the completion of His saying: "and taste the punishment of the burning fire." That is, it will be said to them, as an increase in rebuke, regret, and anguish: ﴿That﴾, meaning: what has befallen them of punishment and rebuke. The thing referred to is what preceded in His saying: "and taste the punishment of the burning fire." Here He said ﴿That﴾, although He is speaking about a group, and He used the singular second-person kaf (the particle of address). This is because we have already learned that the demonstrative noun (ism al-isharah) is according to what is pointed to, and the kaf is according to the one addressed, in the standard language. Or it is with a fatha on the kaf for a masculine singular, and with a kasra for a feminine singular, or it is with a fatha on the kaf in all cases. All of these are dialects, but the most common is that it follows the one addressed. I think you have not fully grasped this matter, the difference between what is pointed to and what is addressed. Have you fully grasped it? The demonstrative noun follows what?
* Student: It follows what is pointed to, and the kaf of address takes into account the one addressed.
* Shaykh: It takes into account the one addressed. If you address two people, pointing to women, what do I say?
* Student: Dhanikuma.
* Shaykh: Wrong.
* Student: Dhanik.
* Shaykh: No, wrong. Tilkuma.
* Student: No, Shaykh, two, Shaykh.
* Shaykh: Yes. You address two people, pointing to women? Tilkuma, correct. In any case, there is no need to repeat it, because it is well known and only needs to be written down. Someone writes the demonstrative and the kaf, and he himself converts it from this to that.

He said: ﴿That is for what your hands have put forward﴾, that is, because of, so the ba' here is causal, and "ma" is a relative pronoun meaning "alladhi" (that which), that is, "for that which." His saying ﴿your hands have put forward﴾ means in the world. The hands here refer to themselves, but the deed or what was sent forward is attributed to the hands, because the hands are most commonly the place of striking and doing. Otherwise, it is well known that their hands, tongues, and feet, all their powers, have worked in polytheism.

He said: ﴿and that Allah is not ever unjust to the servants﴾. Here "that" is with a fatha, conjoined to "ma" in His saying ﴿for what [your hands] have put forward﴾. That is, "and that is because Allah is not unjust to the servants."

As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿and that Allah is not ever unjust﴾, "dhallam" is in the form of intensification (mubalaghah), but at the same time it is in the form of attribution (nisbah). The difference between them is that the form of intensification indicates abundance, whereas attribution includes both abundance and scarcity. So is the meaning here the form of intensification or attribution?
* Students: Attribution.
* Shaykh: The meaning is attribution. Why? Because if we said the meaning is the form of intensification, then what is negated would be the abundance of injustice, although Allah does not wrong even the weight of an atom.

Based on this, we say that "dhallam" here is attributive, meaning: not one possessed of injustice, not one possessed of injustice, just as you say: so-and-so is not a carpenter, meaning he is not possessed of carpentry, that is, he is not attributed to carpenters.

His saying ﴿to the servants﴾: "'ibad" is the plural of "'abd," and "'abd" is a singular noun, one of the words with the most plurals; it has many plural forms, just as "shaykh" is a singular noun with many plurals, reaching about ten. The servants here refer to the servants in the sense of creation (kawnan), that is, He does not wrong any of the servants in terms of creation. We said "kawnan" to rule out that what is meant is the servants in the legal sense, namely those who worship Allah. This is because Allah does not wrong either the disbeliever or the believer; each is recompensed according to his deeds. So servanthood in this verse is the general servanthood that encompasses both the disbeliever and the believer. Allah does not wrong a disbeliever, nor does He wrong a believer; He recompenses every person according to his deeds.

* Among the benefits of this verse, first: the affirmation of causes. From where is this taken? From His saying: ﴿for what your hands have put forward﴾.
* Among its benefits also: the negation of injustice from Allah, from His saying: ﴿and that Allah is not ever unjust to the servants﴾. Here we pause to clarify that Allah, Glory be to Him, is described by affirmation and by negation. As for affirmation, Allah, Exalted is He, described Himself by affirming every attribute of perfection; every attribute of perfection is affirmed for Allah. And what is the criterion of perfection? Is it our deficient intellects, or is the criterion of perfection the texts of the Book and the Sunnah? The second, the second is the criterion. That is why we do not judge Allah by saying: this is an attribute befitting Him and this is an attribute unbefitting Him. Rather, the reference in this is to the Book and the Sunnah for the details, whereas in general the intellect indicates that the Lord must be perfect. As for the negated attributes, they are not meant as mere negation, but the meaning is the absence of this attribute because the perfection of its opposite is established. So when He negates being unjust to the servants, that is because of the perfection of His justice; when He negates drowsiness or sleep, that is because of the perfection of His life and self-subsistence; when He negates weariness reaching Him, that is because of the perfection of His strength; and so on.

We must know that there cannot be in the attributes of Allah a pure negation. Pay attention to this rule, O people! There is no pure negation in the attributes of Allah. The proof is the saying of Allah, Exalted is He: ﴿And to Allah belongs the highest description﴾ [al-Nahl 60]. A pure negation is not the highest description. The highest description means the most perfect, supreme attribute, and pure negation is nonexistence, and nonexistence is not a thing, let alone a supreme attribute. Second: a bare negation may be due to the incapacity of the one described, or it may be due to his not being capable of the thing negated. It may be due to incapacity, or it may be due to his not being capable of it. That means we negated this thing from him because he is incapable, he cannot do this thing that we negated from him. And it may be because he is not capable of this thing. For example, if someone says: so-and-so is a "huBayyib" man. A huBayyib does not wrong people and does not transgress against them. What do we understand from this statement, that he does not wrong people or transgress against them? It is his incapacity; that is why we said "huBayyib." "HuBayyib" among people is a diminutive word that also carries contempt. This is like the saying of the poet:

A tribe that does not betray a covenant,
and does not wrong people by a grain of mustard.

When Adam hears such a statement, what does he say? Is it praise or blame? You see him saying: they do not betray a covenant; they can never betray an agreement, and they can never wrong people?
* Student: Blame.
* Shaykh: Blame? Subhan Allah! If I say to you: you do not betray agreements and you do not wrong anyone, what would this be?
* Student: This is praise.
* Shaykh: Praise. That is, when it was said about you, it became praise, and when it was said about the tribe, it became blame. Subhan Allah!
* Student: This is blame.
* Shaykh: From where did we take that it is blame?
* Student: (...) his saying: "qubayyilah" (a small tribe).
* Shaykh: Diminutive.
* Student: The second: they do not wrong with their covenant; that they, because of their incapacity, do not wrong people.
* Shaykh: We understood that it is blame only from the diminutive form, and the diminutive in origin indicates belittling. Is that so? In any case, it is not possible for there to be a pure negation in the attributes of Allah. A negation may, if it does not include perfection, be due to lack of capability. That is, what was negated of Him is not this attribute because of its perfection, but because He is unable. The scholars gave an example of this by saying: "my wall does not wrong," the wall does not wrong. Is this praise?
* Students: No.
* Shaykh: Why? Because it is not capable at all. If it wanted to wrong, it could not. Is that so? So take this rule: there is no pure negation in the attributes of Allah, Exalted is He. Rather, everything Allah negates of Himself includes a perfection. This is the rule.
* Among the benefits of this verse: that Allah, Exalted is He, informs about what He informs about of His attributes to reassure creation; from His saying: ﴿and that Allah is not ever unjust to the servants﴾, so that a person may be reassured that he will only be recompensed for his deeds: if good, then good, and if evil, then evil.
* Among its benefits: the permissibility of applying a part to the whole when there is an indication pointing to it. From where do we take it? The permissibility of applying a part to the whole when there is an indication pointing to it? The verse we have before us?
* Student: (...) "to the servants"?
* Shaykh: No.
* Student: His saying: ﴿your hands﴾, perhaps it repels him, for example.

**Shaykh:** Her words, ﴿for what your hands have sent forward﴾, mean "for what you have sent forward." The hand is a part of a person, but the context shows that the intended meaning is the whole, that is, "for what you have sent forward." A parallel to this in the attributes of God is His words: ﴿Do they not see that We have created for them, from what Our hands have made, livestock?﴾ [Yasin 71], such as camels. God said ﴿from what Our hands have made﴾. Shall we say that God created the camels with His hand, as He created Adam? No. We say ﴿from what Our hands have made﴾ means "from what We have made," because God did not create the camels, for example, with His hand. So the intended meaning is "from what We have made." But this does not mean that the verse contains no indication that God has a hand. Rather, it does indicate that God, the Mighty and Majestic, has a hand.

**Student:** Shaykh, does this give support to those who say that ﴿That is for what your hands have sent forward﴾ is figurative (majaz) in language?

**Shaykh:** O brother, may God bless you, whoever said it said it, because they hold that words have an inherent meaning (ma'na dhati). As for those who say that words have no inherent meaning, but their meaning depends on the context, they do not have figurative language (majaz). So they say, for example, ﴿Lower to them the wing of humility﴾ contains no figurative language, because it is well known that humility does not have a literal wing. **Student:** How, Shaykh, do we respond to them (...) they say here some (...)

**Shaykh:** Yes, yes. We say: the Arabic language expresses the part by the whole and the whole by the part. ﴿They put their fingers into their ears﴾, but not every finger goes into the ear.

**Student:** I seek refuge with God from the accursed Satan. ﴿Those who said, "Indeed, God has taken our covenant that we not believe a messenger until he brings us an offering which fire consumes." **Shaykh:** Well done.

He said: ﴿and their killing of the prophets without right﴾. Is there any right in killing the prophets, so that the qualifier "without right" is needed to exclude it? That is, does the qualifier "without right" mean that killing the prophets sometimes happens with right and sometimes without it?

**Student:** (...)

**Shaykh:** Indeed. Why did He say "without right"?

**Student:** Because it actually was without right.

**Shaykh:** Yes?

**Student:** Because the reality is that it was without right.

**Shaykh:** That is, to state the reality?

**Student:** Yes.

**Shaykh:** Yes.

**Student:** A descriptive qualifier that reveals the reality (sifa kashifa).

**Shaykh:** A descriptive qualifier that reveals the reality. "Revealing" means that it makes the reality clear. Is there also another benefit besides this?

**Student:** Emphasis?

**Shaykh:** No.

**Student:** So that it is not thought that they killed them with right. Lest someone say that they killed the prophets with right, God emphasized that their killing was without right.

**Shaykh:** Yes.

**Student:** It records against these people and confirms that their situation contains no right.

**Shaykh:** Yes. That is, its meaning is to intensify the abhorrence of them, or to censure them harshly, because they killed them without right.

His words: ﴿Taste the punishment of the burning.﴾ What is the command here intended for?

**Student:** It is intended here as rebuke.

**Shaykh:** And humiliation. Do you have evidence that such a command is intended as humiliation?

**Student:** Yes, from His words: ﴿Taste! Indeed you are the mighty, the noble.﴾ [Ad-Dukhan 49].

**Shaykh:** Yes, ﴿Taste! Indeed you are the mighty, the noble.﴾ Some contemporary scholars have said that the Fire does not burn its people, and for this reason they neither die in it nor live. So does the verse contain anything that refutes them?

**Student:** Yes. His words, ﴿Taste the punishment of the burning﴾, and that necessitates that they continue to taste the punishment and do not die.

**Shaykh:** And they are burned.

**Student:** They are burned, and their skins are scorched, then God replaces their skins with other skins.

**Shaykh:** And they do not die, unlike them in this world, for when a person is burned in this world, he dies.

What is the meaning of His words: ﴿for what your hands have sent forward﴾?

**Student:** That is, for what your hands have earned.

**Shaykh:** But the "bi" here?

**Student:** The "ba'" is causal (lil-sababiyya).

**Shaykh:** The "ba'" is causal. Does it follow from the verse that God's acts are accompanied by wisdom?

**Student:** Yes, because the "ba'" is causal.

**Shaykh:** Everything that is causal indicates causation (ʿillah), and the cause is wisdom.

His words: ﴿and that God is not ever unjust to the servants.﴾ Is "ظلام" here an intensive form (sighat al-mubalagha) or an attributive form (nisba)?

**Student:** An intensive form.

**Shaykh:** An intensive form. That means God does a little injustice but not much?

**Student:** "ظلام" is an intensive form in terms of its pattern, that is all.

**Shaykh:** Yes, "ظلام" is an intensive form in its pattern, that is correct. But this pattern also comes in the attributive sense. One says: "نجار" (carpenter), "حداد" (blacksmith), "بنّاء" (builder). So is it attributive here or intensive?

**Student:** Attributive.

**Shaykh:** Attributive, good. Because if we said it was intensive, then what is negated would be the multitude of injustice.

Is "العبيد" (the servants) here in the specific sense or the general sense?

**Student:** The general sense.

**Shaykh:** The general sense. That means God does not wrong even the disbeliever?

**Student:** Yes.

**Shaykh:** Correct?

**Students:** Yes.

**Shaykh:** Good. Then God, Exalted, said: ﴿those who said﴾. This is a qualifier of His words: ﴿God has heard the saying of those who said﴾.

**Student:** The benefits, Shaykh.

**Shaykh:** From where? Benefits of what?

**Student:** From ﴿That is for what your hands have sent forward﴾. We took four benefits yesterday.

**Shaykh:** Where did we stop?

**Student:** The permissibility of ruling on the whole based on a part when (...) comes after it, which is taken from His words: ﴿for what your hands have sent forward﴾.

**Shaykh:** Then complete it.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse, ﴿That is for what your hands have sent forward﴾: the negation of injustice from God, by His words: ﴿and that God is not ever unjust to the servants.﴾

* And among its benefits: the possibility of injustice from God, were it not that God negated it from Himself, by His words: ﴿and that God is not ever unjust﴾. For if injustice were impossible for Him, it would not be proper for Him, the Mighty and Majestic, to praise Himself with it, since one is praised for something only when abstaining from it is a matter of choice. But if it were impossible for Him, there would be no benefit in praising Himself with it. Is this correct?

Based on this benefit, does it contain a refutation of whom?

**Student:** The Ash'arites (al-Ash'ariyya).

**Shaykh:** No.

**Student:** The Jabriyya (those who deny real human choice).

**Shaykh:** No. It refutes the Jahmiyya (a sect that denied God's attributes). The Jahmiyya say that injustice is impossible for God, impossible in its very essence, not because God negated it from Himself. For they say: whatever He does, He does in His own domain, and whoever acts in his own domain may do as he wishes. So injustice, for them, is impossible in its essence, as Ibn al-Qayyim said in the Nuniyya:

*And injustice, to them, is impossible in its very essence* ∗∗∗ .......................

We say: injustice is not impossible for God. If God willed to do injustice, He would do it. But He negated it from Himself, praising Himself by that. For this reason He said in the hadith qudsi: "O My servants, I have forbidden injustice for Myself."[[Recorded by Muslim (2577/55) from the hadith of Abu Dharr.]] This indicates that it is possible for Him, but He does not do it.

If someone says: it has come in a hadith from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "Indeed God, if He were to punish the inhabitants of His heavens and His earth, He would punish them while not being unjust to them."[[Recorded by Abu Dawud (4699) and Ibn Majah (77) from the hadith of Ubayy ibn Ka'b and Zayd ibn Thabit.]]

The answer: We say there is no contradiction between this hadith and the verse. For if God punished them, it would not be possible for Him to punish them while being unjust to them. Therefore He punishes only those who deserve punishment, and so the hadith agrees with the verse. Or another explanation may be given: if God punished the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth, He would punish them while not being unjust to them, if He wished to hold His servants to account strictly. For whoever is strictly held to account is punished, because if God were to hold them strictly to account, one single blessing from His blessings would outweigh all their deeds, and then they would deserve to be punished. So in this hadith there are two interpretations. The first: He punishes them while not being unjust to them, that is, He punishes them only for a sin, and so it agrees with the verse. The second: what is meant is strict reckoning, the strict scrutiny of the account, because if God, Glorified and Exalted, were to scrutinize them strictly, one single blessing from His blessings would encompass all their deeds, and they would be left with no credit.

If someone says: this is a negative attribute, as they call it. Do negative attributes exist among God's attributes?

The answer: No. But what is meant by negative attributes is the affirmation of the perfection of their opposite. He does not do injustice, not because He is unable to do it, but because of the perfection of His justice.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Those who said, "Indeed, Allah has taken our covenant that we not believe in any messenger until he brings us an offering consumed by fire."﴾ and so on to the end. This too is one of the lies of these Jews, that they said: ﴿Indeed, Allah has taken our covenant﴾, meaning: He enjoined upon us a binding injunction, confirmed by covenant. It is said: "'ahida ilayhi" (he entrusted him with a firm charge), and from it comes "al-'ahd bil-wilaya" (the appointment of a ruler), meaning the ruler's assignment of authority to his successor, as when he enjoins the rule upon the one who comes after him, like the appointment of Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) of 'Umar. So the meaning of ﴿He covenanted with us﴾ is: He enjoined upon us a firmly established injunction. ﴿That we should not believe in any messenger until he brings us an offering which fire consumes﴾. Thus they said, and this is from their lies, as will come.

He says: ﴿That we should not believe in any messenger﴾, meaning, a messenger from Allah, ﴿until he brings us an offering which fire consumes﴾. That is, we bring an offering of food, animals, meat or garments, and then fire descends from heaven and consumes this offering. They mean that they restricted the signs they demand from the Messenger to his bringing a fire that consumes this offering. In former times, when they took spoils from the disbelievers, they gathered them, and then fire descended from heaven and consumed them, until the spoils were made lawful for this Ummah. These people say: "We will not believe in a messenger unless he brings us this sign alone, that when we offer an offering, fire consumes it." Thus they said. Allah the Exalted said to His Messenger: ﴿Say: "There have certainly come to you messengers before me with clear proofs and with what you speak of. So why did you kill them, if you are truthful?"﴾ meaning: messengers have come to you with more than what you now claim. ﴿With clear proofs﴾, that is, with clear signs which show the truth of their messengership. And the second: ﴿and with what you speak of﴾, that is, with the offering which fire consumes. ﴿So why did you kill them?﴾ meaning: and despite that, you denied them and killed them.

If someone says: Why did Allah, Mighty and Majestic, turn away from demanding the truth of what they claimed?

We say: This is by way of accommodating the opponent (tanazzul ma'a al-khasm), meaning: supposing the matter is as you say, you have transgressed even in what was brought as your demand; you transgressed against the messengers. I hope we pay attention to this. First, whoever makes a claim, we deal with him in stages: the first stage is the soundness of what he says; the second stage is its contradiction to what he says. Here Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not demand from them the soundness of what they said, by way of agreeing with the opponent. I say: by way of agreeing with the opponent (muwafaqat al-khasm), which is better than accommodation (tanazzul), because what we have is the Qur'an. I said at first "tanazzul", based on the well-known expression among the scholars, but here we say "muwafaqat al-khasm": so here He has agreed with the opponent, saying: "Yes, suppose the matter is as you say, and that it was enjoined upon you not to believe in a messenger until he brings you an offering which fire consumes; yet a messenger has come to you with an offering which fire consumes, and still you killed him. Therefore your demand for this specific sign is not out of sincerity, since it has come to you and still you denied the messengers and killed them." Here He turned away from demanding the soundness of the claim by way of agreeing with the opponent, meaning that you do not wish to believe the messengers, but rather wish to deny them.

* Student: Shaykh, may Allah reward you well, when He said: ﴿until he brings us an offering which fire consumes﴾, they demanded an offering (...) which fire consumes, although what we mentioned is that (...)?

* The Shaykh: No, "an offering", but the offering is what they draw near to Allah with; meaning, until he brings us a lawful offering by which we draw near and which fire consumes. It is not that he brings the offering.

* Student: This is the apparent meaning of the verses.

* The Shaykh: Yes, but the scholars interpreted it that way: that they draw near to Allah with an offering which fire consumes.

* Student: Shaykh, may Allah reward you well, in earlier nations, if one drew near with an offering of animals, would fire consume it like goods?

* The Shaykh: Apparently, if it was lawful, fire consumes it; animals and other things, if lawful like animals. As for other than animals, there is no difficulty in the matter.

* Student: Like the spoils.

* The Shaykh: The spoils, they said: in general.

* Student: For the Islamic nation, were the spoils made lawful at the first battle they fought (...)?

* The Shaykh: No, it is well known regarding Badr that they did not divide them except by the division of the Prophet ﷺ; he divided them himself, and they were not distributed as the later distribution. The scholars differed on this: whether the Messenger ﷺ was permitted specifically at Badr to divide the spoils otherwise than what Allah mentioned in Surah al-Anfal, or whether Surah al-Anfal was not revealed until after Badr.

* Student: (...)?

* The Shaykh: By Allah, I do not have its verification now.

* Student: Is the offering from the spoils, or from any (...) of the person?

* The Shaykh: What these people want? No, from anything; that a person draws near to Allah by setting out food, then fire descends and consumes it.

* The Student: Why did we bring up the spoils?

* The Shaykh: The connection is with the spoils: when spoils were taken from the disbelievers in the early period, they were not lawful for them; they would gather them in one place, and fire would descend upon them and burn them.

* Student: Shaykh, we said: the second answer to the hadith is that what is meant is the scrutiny of reckoning. Whoever has his reckoning scrutinized, what is (...)?

* The Shaykh: That is, for example, if He punished them while they were doing a righteous deed, He would be punishing them, and He would not be unjust to them by scrutiny. For example, if they fast, pray, give charity, fast and perform Hajj, then if they were scrutinized, the blessings of Allah would not be matched or would not be matched by prayer; prayer, charity, fasting and everything would be swept away, and if they are swept away, what remains for a person? He has no deed.

* Student: The saying of Allah: ﴿from what our hands have done﴾, meaning (...) how does it indicate the affirmation of a hand for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, the direction of the indication?

* The Shaykh: The direction of the indication is that He affirmed "our hands"; had He not had a hand, it would not be correct to express Himself with it.

* Student: (...) by it about Allah?

* The Shaykh: Yes, but it is impossible for Him to attribute it to a hand while He has no hand at all.

* * *

* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan: ﴿Those who said, "Indeed, Allah has taken our covenant that we not believe in any messenger until he brings us an offering which fire consumes." Say: "There have certainly come to you messengers before me with clear proofs and with what you speak of. So why did you kill them, if you are truthful?"﴾ (183) ﴿And if they deny you, messengers before you were denied who came with clear proofs, scriptures and the illuminating Book﴾ (184) ﴿Every soul will taste death, and you will only be given your full rewards on the Day of Resurrection. So whoever is drawn away from the Fire and admitted to Paradise has triumphed. And the worldly life is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion.﴾
* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. I think we begin the discussion. ﴿Those who said, "Indeed, Allah has taken our covenant"﴾: what is the grammatical position of the phrase ﴿Those who said, "Indeed, Allah has taken our covenant"﴾?

* Student: It has no grammatical position.

* The Shaykh: No, a noun must have a grammatical position.

* Student: A relative clause complement (silat al-mawsul).

* The Shaykh: No, (alladhina).

* Student: Conjunction (atf).

* The Shaykh: There is no conjunction particle.

* Student: Apposition (badal).

* The Shaykh: It cannot be an apposition.

* Student: Adjective (sifa).

* The Shaykh: An adjective of the first ﴿alladhina﴾. Apposition, my brothers, is that which takes the place of the one it replaces; it is the intended element of the ruling. Do you understand? For example, if you say: "I ate the loaf, its third" ("thuluth" is an apposition), so the thing eaten is the third. "Take a sharp knife" (nabalan mudan): this is apposition of error or forgetfulness; "mudan" means knives; what is intended? Take the knives. So apposition means that it stands in the place of what it replaces, not that it is additional to it.

Your statement: ﴿He covenanted with us﴾, what does it mean?

* Student: It means He enjoined upon us.

* The Shaykh: He enjoined upon us, like that? Good.

Your statement: ﴿until he brings us an offering which fire consumes﴾, what does it mean?

* Student: That they do not believe until the messenger brings them an offering of garments or food or anything which fire consumes; Allah sends fire upon it and consumes it.

* The Shaykh: Is their statement true?

* Student: Not true; a lie from themselves; they lied against Allah and the Messenger.

* The Shaykh: Did Allah refute what they claimed?

* Student: He did not come with a refutation of what they claimed, but He brought something: that messengers had come to them with what they said, but they killed them.

* The Shaykh: The main point: did they speak the truth?

* Student: They are liars.

* The Shaykh: Yes, but did they speak the truth that if a messenger came to them with an offering which fire consumes, they would believe?

* Student: No, they did not speak the truth.

* The Shaykh: What is the evidence?

* Student: The evidence is the saying of Allah: ﴿So why did you kill them, if you are truthful?﴾

* The Shaykh: No.

* Student: The preceding: ﴿with clear proofs﴾, ﴿There have certainly come to you messengers before me with clear proofs and with what you speak of, so why did you kill them?﴾

* The Shaykh: From where do you take that from these words? 

* Student: ﴿There have certainly come to you﴾.

* Another student: "Say, there have certainly come to you messengers with what you said.."

* The Shaykh: In my copy it is: ﴿Say: There have certainly come to you messengers before me with clear proofs and with what you speak of﴾. From where do we take that they lied in what they claimed?

* Student: When Allah sent to them something, they killed the prophets; their killing of the prophets indicates their non-acceptance (...). So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said, in agreement with the opponent: ﴿So why did you kill them, if you are truthful?﴾

* The Shaykh: Yes?

* Student: From His saying: ﴿and with what you speak of﴾.

* The Shaykh: From His saying: ﴿and with what you speak of﴾, meaning that they came with clear proofs and with what you speak of.

The saying: ﴿if you are truthful﴾, what have we explained? Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Say: There have certainly come to you messengers before me with clear proofs﴾, that is, with the clear signs indicating their messengership and truthfulness; ﴿and with what you speak of﴾, meaning and with what you speak of, apart from the clear proofs they brought, as evidenced by His putting ﴿with clear proofs﴾ first. This indicates that what they said, though a sign, is less than the clear proofs they brought, because they brought something greater than this. For example, Moses, peace be upon him, brought a greater proof than that: he would throw down the staff and it would become a serpent, and he would take it back and it would become a staff; he would put his hand into his pocket and it would come out white, yet without defect, without leprosy. Likewise Jesus, peace be upon him, would bring the dead out of graves alive, or stand over a dead person before burial and he would live by the permission of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; he would create from clay the likeness of a bird by Allah's permission, then breathe into it, and ﴿it becomes a bird﴾ [Al 'Imran 49], a flying bird; there are two readings: ﴿fa-yakunu tayran﴾ and ﴿fa-yakunu ta'iran﴾, meaning it becomes a bird that flies in fact. Which is greater: this, or that fire descend from heaven to consume the offering? The first is greater, and that is why He mentioned it first.

﴿and with what you speak of﴾, which is that he brings an offering which fire consumes; ﴿so why did you kill them?﴾ The fa' is conjunctive; "li" is a preposition, and "ma" is interrogative. From the rules of orthography, when a preposition enters upon interrogative "ma", its alif is dropped, as in: "'amma", "bima", "lima", "ghayr"? "mimma", "kayma"; the important point in any case is that when a preposition enters upon "ma", its alif is dropped.

﴿So why did you kill them, if you are truthful﴾ in that you accept messengers when they bring this sign. The clause with ﴿if you are truthful﴾ is conditional, as you have seen; does it need an answer? Some scholars held that it needs no answer, because the meaning is understood without it, and the answer is only given to complete the meaning. Others said: rather, its answer is omitted, indicated by what precedes it; on this view the sense is: "If you are truthful, why did you kill them?" Ibn al-Qayyim (may Allah have mercy on him) followed the first view, that such a construction does not need an answer.

* Benefit drawn from this verse: the demonstration of the obstinacy of these Jews who rejected the clear proofs brought by the Prophet ﷺ, on the basis of what they claimed from this verse.

* Among the benefits of this verse: when disputing, it is proper to silence the opponent with what he himself claims, so that this is more decisive in refuting his argument. This is taken from His saying: ﴿Say: There have certainly come to you messengers before me with clear proofs and with what you speak of﴾; for when he is confronted with what he says, he has no argument left. Among examples is Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah's (may Allah have mercy on him) disputation with the Rafidah and the people of ta'til (denial of divine attributes): he disputes with them using what they themselves acknowledge. For example, the Ash'aris and Mu'tazilah, the people of ta'til in general, said: the intended meaning of the verses of attributes is other than the apparent, because reason prevents taking their apparent meaning. The philosophers, the people of takhyil (imagination), said: the intended meaning of the texts on the Return is other than the apparent, because it is impossible to hold their apparent meaning, for there is no resurrection, no Lord, no Paradise and no Fire in it. How then did the people of ta'til refute them? The people of ta'til affirm resurrection and the Last Day. They said: your statement is not acceptable; rather, resurrection is a true reality, because we know that the messengers brought it, and that the doubt preventing it is false. The doubt preventing it is the saying of the speaker: ﴿Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?﴾ [Ya Sin 78], so it is necessary to affirm it. We say to them: likewise, the verses of attributes, we know the messengers brought them, and we know the doubt preventing them is false, so it is obligatory to affirm them. Indeed Shaykh al-Islam (may Allah have mercy on him) said: the texts on attributes in the Book and the Sunnah are far more numerous than the texts on the Return; for you scarcely find a verse in Allah's Book without finding in it one of Allah's names or one of His attributes. In short, silencing the opponent with his own argument is more damaging and more powerful against him, meaning that we confront him and he cannot dispute after that.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the messengers, peace be upon them, came with clear proofs indicating their messengership, and this is necessary by reason as it is actual in the Sharia. Why, O people? Because if a human messenger came saying: "I am Allah's messenger to you; I call you to such and forbid you from such, and whoever opposes me I will fight," would that be accepted from him? It is not accepted unless with a proof attesting to what he says. This is why there came in a hadith from the Prophet ﷺ: "There is no prophet, or he said: no messenger, whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sends, except that He gives him signs by which mankind believes in the like of him, and what I have been given is a revelation Allah has revealed to me; so I hope to be the most followed of them on the Day of Resurrection." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4981), Muslim (152/239), from Abu Hurayrah.] He said: "There is no messenger except that Allah gives him what mankind believes in on the like of it." This is necessary, for no one accepts that a person comes and says: "I am Allah's messenger to you; do this and leave that, and if you do not, I will fight you," unless with a proof.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the establishment of the proof against those who claimed this claim, that they killed the prophets who brought what they said.

Then Allah the Exalted said, consoling His Messenger ﷺ: ﴿And if they deny you, [O Muhammad], then (already) have messengers before you been denied, who came with clear proofs and written scriptures and the illuminating Book.﴾ In it there is a reading: ﴿وَبِالزُّبُرِ وَالْكِتَابِ الْمُنِيرِ﴾ (with the particle bāʼ added), i.e., with an added bāʼ.

He, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And if they deny you﴾ — the address is to the Messenger ﷺ, and the subject (the doer) is the Quraysh and the People of the Book, everyone who denied the Messenger. ﴿then (already) have messengers been denied﴾ — here the fa' (فقد) is in response to the conditional, because it is accompanied by qad (قد). As for His saying ﴿كُذِّبَ رُسُلٌ﴾ (kudhdhiba rusulun), in another verse it is ﴿فَقَدْ كُذِّبَتْ رُسُلٌ﴾ [Fatir 4]. Why, then, the masculine and the feminine? We say: because rusul is a broken (collective) plural (jam' taksir), and in a broken plural it is permissible to have the tāʼ marker present or absent. Ibn Mālik, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

*And the tāʼ with a plural other than the sound plural of the masculine*
*is like the tāʼ with the word "one of the bricks" (iḥdā al-labin).*

The word al-labin's "one of them" (iḥdāhā) is labina, so labina is both masculine and feminine. All plurals may be treated as masculine or feminine, except the sound masculine plural according to the view of Ibn Mālik; Ibn Hishām adds to these the sound feminine plural. Opposed to them is the one who said that all plurals may be treated as masculine or feminine, even the sound plural of masculine or feminine nouns; from this is the saying of al-Zamakhshari, responding to his enemies: "I do not care about their group; every group (jam') is feminine (mu'annath)." The feminine does not correspond to men. The evidence is his saying "every group is feminine." What appears to be correct, and Allah knows best, is the view of Ibn Hishām: the sound masculine plural must be masculine, and the sound feminine plural must be feminine; but the broken plural may be either masculine or feminine. Here: ﴿فَقَدْ كُذِّبَ﴾, and in another verse: ﴿فَقَدْ كُذِّبَتْ﴾.

As for His saying ﴿messengers before you﴾ — the messenger, as we have often mentioned, is the one to whom a law (sharʻ) was revealed and who was commanded to convey it. These messengers came with clear proofs. The clause ﴿came with the clear proofs﴾ may be a description (ṣifah) of ﴿messengers﴾, or it may be a circumstantial clause (ḥāl). That it may be a description is obvious, since rusul is indefinite, and what comes after an indefinite is a description. That it may be a circumstantial clause, though the preceding noun is indefinite, is because this indefinite noun has been described, and when an indefinite is described, it may be the subject of a circumstantial clause, since once described it becomes specified.

﴿with the clear proofs﴾ — al-bayyinat are the signs (āyāt), both the legislative (sharʻiyyah) and the cosmic (kawniyyah). The legislative signs are the scriptures they brought, and the cosmic signs are what are called the sensory miracles (al-muʻjizat al-ḥissiyyah).

﴿and the scriptures (zubur)﴾ — the plural of zabūr, meaning that which contains admonitions and warnings; this is the zubur, and for this reason the Psalms given to Dawud consisted mostly of admonitions and warnings.

﴿and the illuminating Book﴾ — kitab here means "the written thing," and munir means "that which gives light to the darknesses." This conjunction, ﴿and the zubur and the illuminating Book﴾, is the conjoining of one description to another description, because the zubur include the illuminating Book. Conjoining descriptions to one another is found in the Qur'an, including the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Exalt the name of your Lord, the Most High, who created and proportioned, and who determined and guided, and who brought out the pasture﴾ [al-A'la 1–4]. His saying ﴿who determined﴾ is conjoining of descriptions, and ﴿who brought out﴾ is also conjoining of descriptions; so the difference here is a difference of description, not a difference of particle.

* Among the benefits of this verse: consoling the Messenger ﷺ.

* Branching from it: a person may console himself with whatever has befallen others. For example, one who enjoins good and forbids evil is harmed; let him console himself — with what? With the harm done to others; for when a person knows that others have been struck by the same as what struck him, he surely forgets his grief, as al-Khansa' said lamenting her brother Sakhr:

*Were it not for the great number weeping around me*
*over their brothers, I would have killed myself.*
*They do not weep like my brother, but I console myself regarding him*
*with consolation (al-ta'assi).*

The evidence here is her saying: "I console myself regarding him with consolation." So when a person looks right and left, and sees this one afflicted in his mind, this one afflicted in his body, this one afflicted in his family, this one afflicted in his wealth, he is consoled. Likewise, the Messenger ﷺ, when Allah tells him "messengers before you were denied," the calamity is surely made easier for him and he is consoled thereby, since he is a human being who is subject to what befalls human beings.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the messengers, peace be upon them, are harmed by denial. I do not think anything is harder on the soul than denial of one who brings the truth. A person nearly breaks apart when he reports something true and is told, "You lied." How much more so when they, being supported by the signs of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, are denied! It is surely hard for them, but they bear patiently, peace be upon them, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And messengers were certainly denied before you, but they were patient over what they were denied and harmed﴾ [al-An'am 34]. That is, "and were harmed"; the particle (aw) is conjoined to ﴿were denied﴾, meaning: harm also befell them, and they were patient over what they were denied and harmed, until Our help reached them.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse, and consider whether it can be derived from it: that the Messenger ﷺ is the last of the messengers. Can this be derived?

* A student: (...) it is possible.

* The Shaykh: It is possible, but weak; for if you said, for example, "a man visited me before you," does that mean no one visits me after him? No. The apparent meaning is that it does not indicate this.

* Among the benefits of this verse: the messengers must be supported with clear proofs, based on His saying ﴿came with the clear proofs﴾.

* Also among its benefits: all the earlier messengers came with a book; every messenger had a book with him. This is supported by the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿We certainly sent Our messengers with clear proofs and sent down with them the Book and the Balance, that people may uphold justice﴾ [al-Hadid 25]. This is because every messenger必须 has a law (shari'ah), and by what is a law carried? By what is written, whether it was revealed as inspiration and then written down, or revealed in written form like the Torah, for Allah wrote it with His own hand and sent it down, Mighty and Majestic.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the earlier books, like our book, all illuminate the path for whoever wishes to walk it, but the greatest of them in illumination is this noble Qur'an; for this reason it is the guardian (muhaymin) over what preceded it of books; all the books that came before it have been abrogated (mansukhah) by it.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 3, verse 185 (part 1 of 2):

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Every soul shall taste death, and you will only be paid your full rewards on the Day of Resurrection﴾, to the end of the verse. "Every soul" (kull) is one of the forms of generality. The word "soul" (nafs) may refer to the spirit (ruh), and it may refer to the body together with the spirit. Both meanings are correct: the body tastes death, and the spirit tastes it.

His saying ﴿shall taste death﴾ means: shall taste its flavour, that is, shall certainly die. Allah used the word "taste" because it is more emphatic in attainment, since through tasting one reaches the certainty of the truth (haqq al-yaqin). The scholars divided certainty (yaqin) into three degrees: knowledge ('ilm), sight ('ayn), and truth (haqq). Knowledge comes through report, sight through observation, and truth through tasting. If someone tells you, "This is an apple," and he has hidden it in a bag, and the speaker is truthful, what do you call this? You call it knowledge of certainty ('ilm al-yaqin). When he uncovers it, it is sight of certainty ('ayn al-yaqin). When the one who was informed eats it, it is truth of certainty (haqq al-yaqin). For this reason, the Mighty and Majestic used the word "tasting," because death is a truth, and every living being must die except the Living, the Self-Subsisting, the Mighty and Majestic.

As for His saying ﴿every soul﴾, is the intended meaning the souls of the children of Adam and the jinn who are on the earth, such that we would say that the angels do not die? The answer is no: everyone dies. ﴿And the Trumpet will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall dead, except whom Allah wills﴾ [az-Zumar 68]. The scholars mentioned that exempted from this are those who do not die and who were created for permanence: the youths (wildan) of Paradise and the maidens (hur) of Paradise, for they were created for permanence and do not die. As for the angels and all other creatures, they will die.

His saying ﴿and you will only be paid your full rewards on the Day of Resurrection﴾ is a restriction: that is, your rewards will not be paid in full except on the Day of Resurrection. The intended meaning of "paying in full" here is complete payment, for otherwise a person may be paid his reward in this world and additionally have more stored up for him. The disbeliever, too, may be paid his reward in this world, meaning that whatever good he did is repaid to him in this world, but in the Hereafter he has no share.

His saying ﴿and you will only be paid your full rewards on the Day of Resurrection﴾, after His saying ﴿every soul shall taste death﴾, may suggest that the intended meaning of "the Day of Resurrection" here is something more general than the Great Resurrection, encompassing the lesser resurrection that occurs for every existing soul.

He said: ﴿So whoever is drawn away from the Fire and admitted into Paradise has indeed succeeded﴾. "Zuhzih" means: pushed away with difficulty. This is because the Fire, may Allah protect me and you from it, is surrounded by desires, and souls incline towards desires. A person hardly turns away from these desires except by being pushed away, because he is advancing towards them with force. For this reason He said ﴿drawn away from the Fire﴾, meaning: pushed away from it with hardship and severity. ﴿And admitted into Paradise has indeed succeeded﴾, because he has escaped what is feared and attained what is sought.

﴿And the life of this world is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion﴾. The "ma" here is negating and does not act like "laysa", because the negation has been annulled (intaqada), and when the negation is annulled its function is nullified, as Ibn Malik said: "... with the negation remaining..." So if the "in" has been annulled, it is inoperative (muhmalah).

His saying ﴿the life of this world﴾: He described it as "of this world" (dunya) for two reasons. The first reason: its nearness in time. The second reason: its nearness in status (qadr). As for its nearness in time, it is clear, because it comes before the Hereafter. As for its nearness in status, the Prophet ﷺ said: «The place of a whip of one of you in Paradise is better than this world and all that is in it»[[al-Bukhari (2793), and Ahmad (2862), the wording being his, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]. The place of the whip: the whip may be said to be a metre long, is better than the world and what is in it. "The world" is not your world in which you are, nor is it your own private world; rather, the world from its beginning to its end. So this life, in relation to the Hereafter, is base and low, from "dunuww", which is lowliness.

His saying ﴿except the enjoyment of delusion﴾ means: except an enjoyment that deceives its possessor and cheats him. How many people have been adorned by the world and were deceived by it, and their end was to the abyss, may Allah protect us, because they were deluded by it.

* In this noble verse there are several benefits.
First: that death is a truth that cannot be avoided; from His saying ﴿every soul shall taste death﴾.
* Among the benefits: urging a person to hasten in righteous deeds, because if he is certainly going to die and does not know when he will die, reason, like the Sharia, requires that he hasten, especially in fulfilling obligations and abandoning wrongdoing. Do not neglect, do not delay, for delay has afflictions. Often a person says, "I will do this tomorrow," but he is lax, then tomorrow and the day after come and his time is wasted.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the full reward is only given on the Day of Resurrection; from His saying ﴿and you will only be paid your full rewards﴾, and "payment" implies that there is something previously given that is then increased, and so it is. A person may be rewarded in this world for his deed, especially for kindness to people and meeting their needs, for it is established from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: «Allah is in the aid of the servant as long as the servant is in the aid of his brother»[[Narrated by Muslim (2699/38) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]], and he said: «Whoever is in the need of his brother, Allah is in his need»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2442) and Muslim (2580/58) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Umar.]].
* Among the benefits of this verse: the establishment of the Day of Resurrection; from His saying ﴿the Day of Resurrection﴾. Why is the Day of Resurrection so named?
* Student: Because people (...) in it.
* The Shaykh: Because people stand in it before the Lord of the worlds; that is one reason.
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No.
* Student: All of them are included in it.
* The Shaykh: Included in it.
* Student: And the witnesses stand.
* The Shaykh: And the witnesses stand.
* Student: And the scale stands.
* The Shaykh: And justice is established in it. The evidences for this are well known. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 6], and He the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believe in the worldly life and on the Day when the witnesses stand﴾ [Ghafir 51], and He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And We will set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection﴾ [al-Anbiya 47].
* Among the benefits of this verse: success is not complete except by two things: that a person be drawn away from the Fire and that he be admitted into Paradise. It is known that whoever is drawn away from the Fire must enter Paradise, because in the Hereafter there are only two abodes, either the Fire or Paradise. The Prophet ﷺ, peace and blessings be upon him, explained in a sound hadith what brings about this great reward, the drawing away from the Fire and admission into Paradise. He said: «Whoever wishes to be drawn away from the Fire and admitted into Paradise, let his death come to him while he believes in Allah and the Last Day, and let him treat people with what he would like to be treated with»[[Narrated by Muslim (1844/46) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As.]]. He mentioned the right of Allah and the rights of the servants. So whoever finds in himself these two qualities, faith in Allah and the Last Day, and that he treats people with what he would like to be treated with, let him rejoice in this.
* Among the benefits of this verse: that it shows Allah will not be seen in Paradise, correct?!
* Students: It has nothing, it has nothing.
* The Shaykh: It contains neither negation nor affirmation. But al-Zamakhshari in his tafsir said: What success is greater than a person being drawn away from the Fire and admitted into Paradise? What success is greater! He intends by this the negation of vision. We say to him: when a person enters Paradise, he will see his Lord, and seeing Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will be the greatest of bliss. So there is nothing in the verse that indicates the negation of vision at all. And if there is no evidence in it for the negation of vision, then there are texts from the Qur'an and Sunnah that establish the affirmation of vision. The believer is one who does not pursue the ambiguous (mutashabih) verses of the Qur'an; he pursues the clear (muhkam) and refers the ambiguous to it.
* Among the benefits of this verse: discouraging attachment to this world; from His saying ﴿and the life of this world is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion﴾.
* Among its benefits: it is obligatory for a person to beware of the consequences of this world and its deceptions. For this reason it is established from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: «By Allah, it is not poverty that I fear for you, but I fear that the world will be opened to you, and you will compete for it as those before you competed for it, and it will destroy you as it destroyed them»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3158), and Muslim (2961/6), from the hadith of Amr ibn Awf.]]. The Messenger ﷺ spoke truly that this is the fear. Look now: when the world was opened to people, what happened? Destruction occurred, and even those to whom it was not opened, when they heard of those to whom it was opened, they were destroyed. Now we hear in some lands of the earth that there is fighting, fighting over bread and food, even though they are poor; they fight over it because they hear that there are those who are satisfied with bread, not in their lands but in other lands. So when a person turns towards this world, may Allah keep us safe, and it becomes his concern, it will delude him and deceive him: ﴿And the life of this world is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion﴾.
I think that al-Hariri in his Maqamat has a great poem warning against this world and its consequences. It is a great poem on one hand, and on the other hand it can be recited in two metres: the long metre (al-tawil) and another metre below it. I do not know the metres, but in it there is the long metre and there is a metre lesser than this; you can read it in both ways. Yes, and this is from his ability in speech, may Allah have mercy on him. His book is called Maqamat al-Hariri, and it is well known.
I will mention two verses in praise of... :
"I swear by Allah and His signs, and the sacred place of the Hajj and its meeting-place, that al-Hariri is worthy that we should write his maqamat in gold."
(In gold) what is "tibr"? Tibr means gold. But are these two verses sound? "I swear by Allah and His signs and the sacred place of the Hajj and its meeting-place": the second half is shirk, swearing by other than Allah. But perhaps he is among those who say, "By the Prophet, I do not swear by the Prophet!"
* Student: The hadith of the Prophet ﷺ: «I hope to be the most numerous of them in following on the Day of Resurrection»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4981) and Muslim (152/239), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]. What is the meaning of this phrase?
* The Shaykh: Its meaning: since it is revelation and will remain, this verse will reach all people until the Day of Resurrection, so they will be most numerous in following. But the sensory signs of the prophets ended with their deaths.
* Student: The criterion for consoling the afflicted with others, because it may be thought that this contradicts the texts indicating that believers are like one body, what afflicts others afflicts them?
* The Shaykh: It is known that if any Muslim is afflicted with a calamity, the believer will be affected by it. But sometimes a believer is afflicted with a similar calamity and is consoled by what befell him, meaning it becomes easier for him to bear what has befallen him.
* Student: What are the muhkam and mutashabih?
* The Shaykh: Do you mean the muhkam and mutashabih in Surat Al 'Imran? The muhkam is that whose meaning is clear, and the mutashabih is that whose meaning is unclear.
* Student: What do muhkam and mutashabih mean, for example?
* The Shaykh: The muhkam: clear verses. For example: ﴿The month of Ramadan in which the Qur'an was revealed﴾ [al-Baqarah 185]. This is muhkam, why? Because it is clear: everyone knows the month of Ramadan, and everyone knows the Qur'an. There are mutashabih verses, for example: ﴿Its penalty is an equivalent of what he killed of livestock, judged by two just men among you, as an offering reaching the Ka'bah, or an expiation: feeding the poor, or the equivalent of that in fasting﴾ [al-Ma'idah 95]. "Equivalent" of what? The equivalent of the game itself, or the equivalent of the penalty? The scholars differ on it. Generally, most matters of disagreement in the Qur'an are from the mutashabih.
* Student: Then (...), O Shaykh, someone says that the attributes are from the mutashabih?
* The Shaykh: To those who say that the attributes are from the mutashabih we say: if you mean that they are mutashabih in meaning, this is wrong, because their meaning is clear. If you mean that they are mutashabih in reality, and that their reality is not known, this is true. So the absolute statement that they are mutashabih is wrong, and the denial that they are mutashabih is also wrong.
* Student: The interpretation given for His saying ﴿and the life of this world is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion﴾, meaning they said it is the rag with which menstruation is wiped.
* The Shaykh: What is the "delusion"?
* Student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: No, that is not correct.
* Student: "Enjoyment of delusion."
* The Shaykh: Yes, that is not correct.
* Student: Shaykh, the meaning of the hadith: «Whoever is in the need of his companion, he is...»?
* The Shaykh: «Whoever is in the need of his brother, Allah is in his need»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2442) and Muslim (2580/58), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Umar.]], meaning that if you care for the needs of your brothers and help them with them, Allah will help you with your needs.
* Student: Shaykh, the meaning of the Prophet's saying ﷺ: «Let him treat people with what he would like to be treated with»[[Narrated by Muslim (1844/46) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr.]].
* The Shaykh: It means that you deal with people with what you would like them to deal with you: with truthfulness, sincere advice, sincerity, help, and other things.
* * *
What is meant by "the clear proofs" (al-bayyinat)?
* Student: The verses.
* The Shaykh: The clear verses that testify to their truthfulness.
Do you know a hadith that indicates a cause, or indicates that if a person acts upon it he is drawn away from the Fire and admitted into Paradise?
* Student: I forgot.

* Sheikh: He should not forget it, neither in memorization nor in practice, because it is important.

* Student: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever loves to be drawn away from the Fire and admitted into Paradise, let his death come to him while he believes in Allah and the Last Day, and let him treat people in the way he loves to be treated." [Recorded by Muslim (1844/46) from ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr.]
* Sheikh: Well done, excellent, this is very important.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿It is only Satan who frightens you of his allies, so do not fear them﴾ [Āl ʿImrān 175]. Does fear of other than Allah contradict faith?

* Student: Fear is divided into categories. Natural fear...
* Sheikh: Does natural fear contradict faith or not?
* Student: No.
* Sheikh: What is the evidence?
* Student: The Prophet (ﷺ) was the most faithful of people, yet he feared. When he wanted to leave Makkah, he left wearing a face covering so that the polytheists would not harm him.
* Sheikh: Concealed.
* Student: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿So Moses sensed fear within himself﴾ [Ṭā-Hā 67].
* Sheikh: Yes.
* Student: His saying, Exalted is He...
* Sheikh: ﴿So he left from there fearful, watching warily﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ 21].

His saying: ﴿And let them not grieve you﴾ [Āl ʿImrān 176]. There are two readings here: ﴿yuḥzinka﴾ or ﴿yaḥzunka﴾? Which is it?

* Student: ﴿yaḥzunka﴾.
* Sheikh: Yes, and the second reading?
* Student: ﴿yaḥzunka﴾.
* Sheikh: ﴿يَحْزُنْكَ﴾ is the same reading.
* Student: With two ḍammas.
* Sheikh: ﴿يَحْزُنُكَ﴾ no. It is jussive (majzūm), because لا is prohibitive.
* Student: ﴿وَلَا يُحْزِنْكَ﴾.
* Sheikh: ﴿يُحْزِنْكَ﴾ is from the quadriliteral (rubāʿī) form? Read: ﴿They rejoice in a blessing from Allah﴾ [Āl ʿImrān 171].

* * *

His saying: ﴿Those who responded to Allah and the Messenger after the wound had befallen them﴾ [Āl ʿImrān 172]. What was the wound (qarḥ) that befell them?

* Student: Grief.
* Sheikh: Grief? No.
* Student: The defeat, O Sheikh.
* Sheikh: When?
* Student: At Uḥud.
* Sheikh: At Uḥud. That is, the wound befell them: the injuries and the killing that occurred at Uḥud.

Was there a battle when the Prophet (ﷺ) called them to go out, or was there not?

* Student: When they returned from the battle...
* Sheikh: No. When he called them after their return from Uḥud and they went out, did a battle take place?
* Student: No, it was not a battle.
* Sheikh: What is the evidence from the verse?
* Student: They did not fight.
* Sheikh: Yes, what is the evidence from the verse?
* Student: ﴿So they returned with a blessing from Allah and bounty; no harm touched them﴾ [Āl ʿImrān 174].
* Sheikh: ﴿No harm touched them﴾, and there is no mention that they were victorious. This indicates that no fighting took place.

* * *

* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan: ﴿Allah has heard the statement of those who said, "Indeed Allah is poor and we are wealthy." We will record what they have said and their killing of the prophets without right﴾ [Āl ʿImrān 181].
* Another student: ﴿...who say, "Allah has enjoined upon us not to believe a messenger until he brings us an offering which fire consumes." Say, "There have already come to you messengers before me with clear proofs and with what you speak of. So why did you kill them, if you should be truthful?"﴾ [Āl ʿImrān 183].
* Sheikh: ﴿Allah has heard the statement of those who said﴾. What is meant by this report?
* Student: The meaning is that someone spoke, and it was said. The narrations differ on this.
* Sheikh: No, my question is what is meant by this report. Why did Allah inform us of it?
* Student: Why did Allah inform us, "He has heard"?
* Sheikh: That He heard, yes.
* Student: That He heard this?
* Sheikh: Yes.
* Student: This is a response to those who said Allah is poor, when the verse ﴿Who is it that will lend to Allah a goodly loan﴾ [al-Baqarah 245] was revealed.
* Sheikh: Yes, but why did Allah inform us of that?
* Student: To console the Messenger (ﷺ)...?
* Sheikh: To threaten these people. It may also include consoling the Messenger (ﷺ), by telling him that Allah will punish them on the Day of Resurrection.

His saying: ﴿We will record what they have said﴾. Does Allah write it, or do the angels?

* Student: The angels, and there are the noble recording angels.
* Sheikh: Yes.

Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan: ﴿You will surely be tested in your possessions and your persons, and you will surely hear from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associate others with Allah much hurt. But if you are patient and mindful of Allah, indeed that is of the matters requiring determination (ʿazm al-umūr). (186) And [recall] when Allah took the covenant of those who were given the Scripture: "You must make it clear to the people and not conceal it." But they cast it behind their backs and exchanged it for a small price. How wretched is what they purchase. (187) Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have done and love to be praised for what they have not done – do not think them safe from punishment; and for them is a painful punishment. (188) And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is over all things competent.﴾ [Āl ʿImrān 186–189].

Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿You will surely be tested in your possessions and your persons, and you will surely hear from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associate others with Allah much hurt.﴾ In this sentence, ﴿لَتُبْلَوُنَّ﴾ is emphasized, as is well known, by three emphatics. What are they?

Student: The nūn of emphasis, the lām, and the implied oath.

Shaykh: And the implied oath, because this lām is a preparatory lām for the oath (lām al-muwaṭṭiʾah lil-qasam), meaning: "By Allah, you will surely be tested."

Al-ibtilāʾ (testing) is examination. Allah, glorified and exalted, sometimes tests with good and sometimes tests with evil, as He said: ﴿And We test you with evil and good as a trial﴾ [al-Anbiyāʾ 35], and as Allah said about Sulaymān: ﴿This is of the favor of my Lord, to test me whether I will be grateful or ungrateful﴾ [al-Naml 40]. That is because a person moves between two states: either something that gladdens and pleases him, and his duty in that is gratitude; or something that grieves and saddens him, and his duty in that is patience. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ said: "How wondrous is the affair of the believer, for all of his affairs are good. If something good happens to him, he is thankful, and that is good for him; if something harmful befalls him, he is patient, and that is good for him. This is not the case for anyone except the believer." [Narrated by Muslim (2999/64) from the hadith of Ṣuhayb.]

Here the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿You will surely be tested in your possessions and your persons.﴾ In possessions: either from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, such as calamities, or from created beings, such as the domination of the polytheists over the wealth of the Muslims. All of this is from the trial that Allah tests His servants with.

His words ﴿and your persons﴾ also include the trial that is connected and the trial that is separate. The connected trial is what befalls a person from Allah in his body, such as illness, disability and the like. The separate trial is what occurs with children, because children are part of ourselves; a person is tested in his offspring, his family, his wife, and other things. This too is part of the testing.

Then, the testing that comes either from Allah the Mighty and Majestic or from created beings: a person is tested in himself by created beings, who sometimes harm him by beating, sometimes by words, and sometimes by killing, as they killed the prophets without right.

﴿And you will surely hear from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associate others with Allah much hurt.﴾

﴿You will surely hear from those who were given the Scripture before you﴾ — they are the Jews and Christians; ﴿and from those who associate others with Allah﴾ — they are the idolaters, such as the Quraysh and others. You will hear from them ﴿much hurt﴾. Hurt by what? By speech, since it is the hearing that perceives it: such as their insulting you or reviling your religion or reviling your Prophet. They said about the Prophet ﷺ that he is a sorcerer and a liar, ﴿Has he made the gods into one God? Indeed, this is a strange thing!﴾ [Ṣād 5]. They said he is mad: ﴿Shall we really abandon our gods for a mad poet?﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt 36]. They said he is a soothsayer, and they described him with every defect. There is no doubt that this hurts the believers and hurts the Prophet ﷺ, but our duty regarding this matter is patience, and for this He said: ﴿But if you are patient and mindful of Allah, indeed that is of the matters requiring determination.﴾ [Āl ʿImrān 186].

His words ﴿much hurt﴾ imply also little hurt, but much hurt is harder on a person than little hurt; nevertheless he is commanded to be patient. For this He said: ﴿But if you are patient and mindful of Allah, indeed that is of the matters requiring determination.﴾ Consider His words "you will hear hurt" and He did not say "harm," because what we hear hurts us but does not harm us. Allah said: ﴿If you are patient and mindful, their plotting will not harm you at all﴾ [Āl ʿImrān 120]. Here there is a difference between being hurt and being harmed: a person may be hurt by something without being harmed by it.

For this reason Allah affirmed that His servants hurt Him, meaning that some of His servants harm Him, and He negated that anyone can harm Him. He said in a sacred hadith: "O My servants, you will never reach My harm so as to harm Me, and you will never reach My benefit so as to benefit Me." [Narrated by Muslim (2577/55) from the hadith of Abū Dharr.] And He said: ﴿Indeed, those who hurt Allah and His Messenger – Allah has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter and prepared for them a humiliating punishment.﴾ [al-Aḥzāb 57]. So He affirmed hurt. And Allah said in a sacred hadith: "The son of Adam hurts Me: he reviles time, while I am time." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhārī (4826) and Muslim (2246/2) from the hadith of Abū Hurayrah.] So He affirmed hurt also. As for harm, it is not affirmed.

So here the believers hear from the People of the Scripture and from the polytheists what hurts them, but it does not harm them.

Then He said: ﴿But if you are patient and mindful of Allah﴾ — be patient over what you hear, and over what you are tested with in your possessions and your persons. Patience (ṣabr) means restraint (ḥabs), and from it comes the saying "he was killed ṣabran," meaning restrained: he is stopped, restrained and killed. In the Sharia it means restraining the heart, the tongue and the limbs from what angers Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

The people of knowledge said: patience is of three types: patience in obedience to Allah, which is the highest type and category; patience in refraining from disobedience to Allah, which is below it; and patience over painful decrees of Allah, which is below both. This is because the first two are patience regarding the Sharia of Allah, while the third is patience regarding the decree of Allah. Patience over the decree of Allah occurs from the believer and the disbeliever, and from the speaking and the animal, but patience over the Sharia of Allah occurs only from the believer.

Then, patience over what is commanded is higher than patience in refraining from what is forbidden, because patience in refraining from the forbidden is merely restraint, while patience over what is commanded is action; it is bringing something into being and doing it, so there is a degree of burden in it, unlike patience in refraining from doing what is forbidden, which is merely restraint.

However, sometimes, with respect to the self, patience in refraining from the forbidden can be harder than patience in performing what is commanded. Prayer may be easy for some people, but it is hard for them to leave what Allah has forbidden of matters to which their souls urge them strongly.

Good. What about the fasting person's patience in fasting? From the first.

And his patience over the pain caused by hunger and thirst?

Student: From the second.

Shaykh: No, from the third: patience over the painful decrees of Allah.

And his patience in refraining from what was forbidden to him by fasting is from the second.

For this reason the month of Ramadan is called the month of patience, because all three types of patience are found in the fasting person. In it (i.e., in fasting) there is patience in obedience, patience in refraining from disobedience, and patience over decrees.

Yusuf's patience over his brothers throwing him into the well?

Students: From the third.

Shaykh: From the third (...).

Student: The patience over being killed.

Shaykh: And his patience in refusing the wife of the ʿAzīz's solicitation?

Students: From the second.

Shaykh: From the second, patience over disobedience.

And his patience in calling to Allah while in prison?

Students: From the first.

Shaykh: From the first, yes.

﴿But if you are patient and mindful of Allah﴾ — mindful of what? Mindful of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, by not transgressing or oppressing others; because the self is naturally inclined to love taking revenge on others, so when it hears hurt, it may take more than its share.

I say: the self is naturally inclined to love revenge on others when hurt comes from them, so a person may transgress and take more than his right. For this He said: ﴿If you are patient and mindful﴾, meaning mindful of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, so do not transgress against those who made you hear hurt.

﴿Indeed, that is of the matters requiring determination﴾ — meaning of the matters that are resolved upon, so ʿazm here is a verbal noun in the sense of the passive participle: matters that are determined, which require resolve, aspiration and persistence, because they are hard on the self.

Determination in affairs is among the praiseworthy qualities with which the perfected among creation are described. Allah said: ﴿So be patient as the messengers of determination were patient﴾ [al-Aḥqāf 35]. Determination is undoubtedly a lofty trait that Allah grants to whomever He wills. When a person has determination in his affairs, he is the one who is granted success; but the person who lacks determination is always found in boredom, laziness and negligence, and such a person is certainly a loser. The determined person in his affairs is the winner in this world and the next: ﴿But if you are patient and mindful of Allah, indeed that is of the matters requiring determination.﴾

* Benefits of this verse:

* First: among eloquence is the emphasis of a matter with what makes one confident about it, as in His saying "you will surely be tested in your persons." The scholars of rhetoric say emphasis may be good, may be obligatory, and may be superfluous if there is no need for it; this is because emphasis must include an addition, and what is the addition? The addition of the letters by which the emphasis is achieved. So if there is no need for it, it becomes superfluous, and it is also superfluous in meaning.

For this reason, if you emphasized to someone something he sees, he would blame you and say: "Am I not seeing? I know!" If you said: "By Allah, I prayed two rak'ahs when I entered the mosque," while he sees you and watches you, what would he say to you? You would say: "How do you swear to me when I am watching you?!" This is superfluous speech.

It is good — i.e., emphasis is good — when the addressee has some hesitation; when the addressee has some hesitation, it is good to emphasize your words to him so that he is reassured.

It is obligatory when the addressee is a denier or one who does the act of a denier.

When is it obligatory?

Student: When the act is a denial.

Shaykh: When the act is a denial?!

Student: Yes.

Shaykh: How do you say "yes"?
